domains.game_engines: Game engines & engine plugins (Unreal, Unity, Godot)
domains.ai_agents_mcp: AI agents & MCP servers for engineering tools
domains.industrial_iot: Industrial IoT, OPC UA & data pipelines

tools.name: godotengine/godot
tools.desc: Godot Engine – Multi-platform 2D and 3D game engine

cls.summary: Godot is a mature, free and open-source cross-platform 2D/3D game engine used to build interactive real-time applications and export them to desktop, mobile, web and consoles.
cls.what_it_does: Godot provides a unified editor, scene/node architecture, renderers, physics, scripting (GDScript/C#/C++), and export pipelines to create interactive 2D and 3D applications and games. It is used by developers to prototype, simulate and deliver real-time visualisations and interactive simulations, and is notable for its permissive MIT license and large community.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository is long-established (created 2014), very widely adopted with large star/fork counts, active development and official releases and ecosystem (docs, demos, asset store), indicating de-facto industry-standard maturity.
student_project_ideas: Build an interactive vehicle dynamics demonstrator in Godot that visualises sensor data and physics behaviour, integrating a Python data stream (e.g. MQTT) for real-time inputs.
Create a robotics simulation scene that tests simple navigation algorithms (path planning/obstacle avoidance) using Godot's physics and export a WebAssembly build for browser-based demonstrations.

tools.name: mrdoob/three.js
tools.desc: JavaScript 3D Library.

cls.summary: three.js is a widely used open-source JavaScript library for creating and displaying 3D graphics in web browsers using WebGL and WebGPU.
cls.what_it_does: three.js provides a high-level API to create scenes, cameras, lights, meshes, materials and renderers so developers can build interactive 3D web applications and visualisations. It is used in-browser (via npm or CDN) to render real-time 3D content and supports multiple renderers (WebGL, WebGPU, SVG, CSS3D) and common asset formats, making it notable for cross-browser, lightweight 3D development and a large example and documentation ecosystem.
cls.trl_rationale: three.js is mature and widely adopted since 2010 with very large community, many stars/forks, active releases and an extensive examples/docs ecosystem, making it a de-facto standard for web 3D.
student_project_ideas: Build an interactive web-based digital twin dashboard that loads a glTF model, overlays telemetry (simulated or MQTT) and visualises state changes in real time using three.js and a time-series backend.

Create a robot simulator front-end that visualises a mobile robot's sensors and planned trajectory in 3D using three.js, integrating with ROS 2 (rosbridge/websocket) or recorded bag data for playback and analysis.

tools.name: bilawalsidhu/gods-eye-view
tools.desc: A spy satellite simulator in your browser, except the data is real. Live open source spatial intelligence on a photorealistic 3D globe.

cls.summary: God's Eye View is a browser-based, photorealistic 3D globe that overlays live public data (flights, ships, satellites, earthquakes, cameras, weather) for interactive situational awareness and exploration.
cls.what_it_does: It aggregates live public spatial feeds and visualises them on a photorealistic 3D globe in the browser, letting users track contacts, follow camera handoffs, play timelines, capture cinematic tours and control the scene by voice. It's used as an analyst-style situational visualiser built on Cesium/WebGL with modular data layers and optional provider keys for higher-resolution imagery.
cls.trl_rationale: The project is actively maintained and widely used (very large star/fork counts, trending, recent pushes), but the repository is under one year old (created 2026-06) so maturity is strong but still young; this fits a beta-level TRL.
prerequisites: familiarity with Cesium and geospatial coordinate systems
optional: API keys for high-resolution imagery (Cesium ion / Google Maps)
student_project_ideas: Build a lab exercise that integrates a student-sourced live AIS or ADS-B feed into God's Eye View to analyse vessel/flight traffic patterns for a coastal region and produce a short report on temporal trends.
Create a digital-twin style demonstrator by combining God's Eye View with a live sensor stream (e.g. earthquake or weather radar) to visualise events and evaluate latency and data-staleness handling.

tools.name: HKUDS/nanobot
tools.desc: Your lightweight open-source personal agent.

cls.summary: nanobot is a lightweight, self-hosted Python framework for running a personal AI agent via browser, terminal or chat apps and connecting it to local or remote LLM providers.
cls.what_it_does: nanobot provides a small core for persistent conversational agents that can run in a WebUI or terminal, connect to chat channels (Telegram, Discord, Slack, etc.), read common document formats, run tools (shell, web fetch, image generation), and keep long-term memory and scheduled automations. It is used by installing the Python package or running the current source, configuring a model provider or local model server, and optionally connecting chat integrations or the bundled WebUI; its notable points are model-provider freedom, multi-channel reach, and an emphasis on a small readable core.
cls.trl_rationale: The project has a large public presence (many stars, active pushes) and installation scripts and docs showing a complete product, but the repository is under one year old so by the stated criteria TRL is capped at 6 (beta): usable with versioned releases and active community but not long-term production track record yet.
prerequisites: access to a supported model provider or local LLM server
basic familiarity with command line and service deployment
student_project_ideas: Build a course assistant that ingests lab reports (PDF/Word) and summarizes experimental results or extracts key metrics using nanobot plus a local LLM.
Create an automation that monitors CI/test outputs and posts summarized alerts to a team chat (Discord/Slack) by integrating nanobot with a CI system or webhooks.

tools.name: janhq/jan
tools.desc: Jan is an open source alternative to ChatGPT that runs 100% offline on your computer.

cls.summary: Jan is a desktop application that runs local LLMs and provides an OpenAI‑compatible chat API so you can use large language models entirely on your computer.
cls.what_it_does: Jan lets you download and run open-source large language models locally (Llama, Gemma, Qwen, etc.), or connect to cloud providers, and exposes an OpenAI‑compatible local server for other apps. It is delivered as a cross‑platform desktop app (Tauri) with binaries for Windows, macOS and Linux and supports engine backends like llama.cpp and MCP integration for agentic workflows.
cls.trl_rationale: The project is well established (created 2023-08, >45k stars, official releases and downloadable executables), active commits and documentation, and provides production-ready installers and an API—evidence of wide adoption and maturity.
student_project_ideas: Create a local development assistant that calls Jan's OpenAI‑compatible API to automatically generate and run unit tests for a small codebase, measuring test coverage improvements.
Build a small tool that uses Jan (running locally with a selected model) to parse lab experiment logs and produce structured reports, comparing results when using different local models.

tools.name: codewhale-hq/Codewhale
tools.desc: An open-source coding agent for your terminal, written in Rust. It works with any model, can split one task across several agents, and every line of it is yours to read.

cls.summary: Codewhale is an open-source terminal coding agent that reads a repository, runs commands and edits files using any LLM provider, and can coordinate multiple sub-agents and plugins.
cls.what_it_does: Codewhale accepts natural-language tasks and inspects the local git repository to propose and apply file edits, run shell commands, and iterate until the task is complete; it supports headless runs for CI and scripted workflows. It is notable for multi-agent orchestration, receipts/undo for traceability, many built-in providers (local and cloud models), and prebuilt binaries for Linux, macOS and Windows.
cls.trl_rationale: The project is actively maintained, has prebuilt binaries, documentation, releases and many stars/forks indicating broad interest, but the repository was created less than one year ago so by the TRL rules it is capped at Beta (TRL 6).
prerequisites: familiarity with LLM provider API keys if using cloud models
optional: Rust toolchain to build from source
student_project_ideas: Build a CI pipeline that runs Codewhale headless to auto-fix lint errors and run tests for a student project repository, and measure changes in test pass rate and developer review time.

Create a study comparing developer productivity when using Codewhale with a local model (Ollama or vLLM) versus a cloud provider (OpenAI/DeepSeek), collecting receipts to analyse what files and commands the agent modified.

tools.name: Donchitos/Claude-Code-Game-Studios
tools.desc: Turn Claude Code into a full game dev studio — 49 AI agents, 72 workflow skills, and a complete coordination system mirroring real studio hierarchy.

cls.summary: Claude Code Game Studios is an open-source template that uses Claude Code AI agents and workflows to prototype, grow and sanity-check playable browser games from a short prompt.
cls.what_it_does: The repo provides a studio-style workflow powered by Claude Code: you give a short game idea, the system asks clarifying questions, produces a one-page brief, generates a first playable browser prototype, runs scripted headless-browser checks and provides change/tweak flows and versioned growth into a full web project. It is notable for its coordinated multi-agent studio model, many reusable 'skills' and hooks to validate builds and automate iterative feature growth.
cls.trl_rationale: The project is active, widely starred and shows a working, documented workflow, but the repository was created ~9 months ago so it lacks the longer real-world track record (multiple releases / independent adopters over years) needed for TRL 7+; the README documents demonstrations and automated checks which support a beta-level maturity.
prerequisites: Node.js (recommended for growing to a web project)
student_project_ideas: Use the template to prototype a simple browser-based simulation game, then extend it by adding telemetry logging and analyse player session data to propose two gameplay balance changes.
Integrate a small physics-based mechanic (e.g. projectile motion) into a generated prototype and add automated headless tests to verify expected behaviours across difficulty settings.

tools.name: AlexsJones/llmfit
tools.desc: Hundreds of models & providers. One command to find what runs on your hardware.

cls.summary: llmfit detects your machine's CPU/GPU/VRAM and recommends which open-source LLMs and quantizations will run well, with benchmarking and an optional web dashboard or TUI.
cls.what_it_does: llmfit inspects system hardware (CPU, RAM, GPU/VRAM, accelerators) and predicts model memory fit and performance across common quantizations, letting users pick models that will run on their machine. It provides a terminal TUI, a web dashboard, a REST API, Docker images and a benchmarking workflow that measures tokens/sec and can contribute results back to the project.
cls.trl_rationale: The project is actively maintained, provides release binaries and Docker images, wide community adoption (many stars) and documentation, but the repository is under one year old so per the assessment rules TRL is capped at 6 despite strong indicators of usage.
prerequisites: familiarity with LLM runtimes and model formats (GGUF, GPTQ, AWQ)
permission to run / install binaries or Docker images
student_project_ideas: Build a reproducible benchmark study comparing real tokens/sec for a set of GGUF-quantized models across two different GPUs using llmfit's benchmarking workflow and visualise results in a web dashboard.
Integrate llmfit's REST API into a CI pipeline to auto-select and deploy an appropriate local LLM runtime (e.g. llama.cpp or localAI in Docker) based on detected hardware on a classroom lab node.

tools.name: FreeCAD/FreeCAD
tools.desc: Official source code of FreeCAD, a free and opensource multiplatform 3D parametric modeler.

cls.summary: FreeCAD is a mature, open-source, cross-platform parametric 3D CAD modeller used for mechanical design, architecture/BIM and producing production drawings.
cls.what_it_does: FreeCAD provides parametric 3D modelling tools that let users create and edit designs by changing parameters and model history, sketch 2D geometry then extrude or constrain it into 3D, and produce technical drawings for manufacture. It is used as a desktop application and scripting platform (Python API) and is notable for being fully open-source, extensible with workbenches, and built on OpenCASCADE for geometry operations.
cls.trl_rationale: FreeCAD is a long-lived (since 2012), actively maintained, widely used open-source CAD application with many stars, frequent releases and broad community and documentation; these facts indicate a mature, widely adopted project (TRL 8) though it is not a single industry de-facto standard.
prerequisites: familiarity with 3D geometry and manufacturing drawings
basic Python for scripting and automation
student_project_ideas: Design a small mechanical assembly in FreeCAD, export STEP files and validate fit/tolerances by combining with a simple FEA run using an open-source solver.
Create an architectural floor plan, extrude to a BIM model using FreeCAD workbenches, and generate annotated production drawings and a bill of materials.

tools.name: ahujasid/mcp-for-blender
tools.desc: Community plugin to control Blender 3D with any LLM of your choice. Not affiliated with the official Blender Foundation.

cls.summary: An open-source Blender addon and local server that lets large language models control Blender to generate and edit 3D scenes, assets and Python scripts.
cls.what_it_does: mcp-for-blender provides a socket-based MCP server and Blender addon so LLMs and MCP-capable clients (Claude, Cursor, VS Code, etc.) can create, modify and inspect Blender scenes; it automates scene assembly, material edits, camera views and executes Blender Python generated by the model. It is notable for broad client support, one-command installers, asset import from online libraries and plugins for AI model-driven 3D generation.
cls.trl_rationale: The project is well-established (created >1 year ago), has a very large star count, active recent commits, a PyPI package, documented installers and many client integrations — evidence of wide adoption and maturity in the community.
prerequisites: basic Python familiarity for scripting in Blender
an MCP-capable LLM client or service (e.g. Claude, Cursor) for full functionality
student_project_ideas: Build a Blender pipeline where an LLM (via mcp-for-blender) interprets textual design requirements and iteratively generates and refines a parametric mechanical part, then export to STL for 3D printing.

Integrate mcp-for-blender with a CAD-to-simulation workflow: use the addon to assemble a scene from assets, auto-generate Blender Python to apply loads/fixtures, render geometry and prepare geometry exports for a separate FEA tool.

tools.name: pmndrs/react-three-fiber
tools.desc: 🇨🇭 A React renderer for Three.js

cls.summary: react-three-fiber is a React renderer that lets you build and control three.js 3D scenes declaratively using JSX and React primitives.
cls.what_it_does: It exposes three.js objects as React components so developers can construct interactive 3D scenes using React's component model, hooks and render loop. It is used as a drop-in way to write three.js scenes in JSX, integrate with React state and ecosystem, and scale complex scenes with React scheduling. The project is notable for a large ecosystem (drei and other helpers), performance claims that match vanilla three.js, and cross-target support including web and React Native.
cls.trl_rationale: The repository is long-lived (created 2019), widely adopted (33k+ stars), actively maintained with recent pushes and a large ecosystem (drei, examples, docs), indicating a mature, widely-used library suitable for production web 3D work.
prerequisites: JavaScript/TypeScript and web development (HTML/CSS/JS build tooling)
student_project_ideas: Build an interactive web-based digital twin dashboard that loads a CAD-derived glTF model with react-three-fiber, overlays telemetry via a WebSocket, and implements camera controls and component highlighting.

Create an interactive robotics simulator front-end where students visualise robot kinematics and planned trajectories in a three-fiber scene and connect it to a ROS/WebSocket backend for live state updates.

tools.name: GraphiteEditor/Graphite
tools.desc: Community-built comprehensive 2D content creation appplication for graphic design, digital art, and interactive real-time motion graphics powered by a node-based procedural graphics engine

cls.summary: Graphite is a free, open-source 2D vector and raster graphics editor with a node-based procedural graphics engine and a nondestructive editing workflow.
cls.what_it_does: Graphite provides tools for vector drawing, raster painting, photo editing and motion graphics that are driven by an underlying node graph for procedural generation and compositing. It runs as a desktop and web editor and is notable for combining layer-based workflows with a programmable, node-based core that supports nondestructive editing.
cls.trl_rationale: The project is several years old, highly starred and actively developed with a live web alpha, showing broad community interest; README and site describe the editor as alpha, so it appears to be beta-level maturity rather than fully production-proven.
prerequisites: Rust knowledge only required for development/contribution
student_project_ideas: Create a short automated SVG asset pipeline that generates variations of an engineering diagram using Graphite's node graph and exports SVG for web documentation.
Extend or contribute a small plugin/feature in the Graphite Rust codebase (for example a new procedural node) to learn real-world Rust GUI/graphics programming and version control workflows.

tools.name: mozilla-ai/llamafile
tools.desc: Distribute and run LLMs with a single file.

cls.summary: llamafile packages open LLMs and related runtimes into a single self-contained executable so models can be downloaded and run locally without installation.
cls.what_it_does: llamafile combines llama.cpp and Cosmopolitan libc to produce a single-file executable (a "llamafile") that embeds an LLM runtime and weights or can load external GGUF weights, letting users run inference locally across platforms. It also provides a matching single-file speech-to-text tool (whisperfile) and aims to make local LLM deployment simple and portable without needing complex installs or container stacks.
cls.trl_rationale: The project is mature and actively maintained (high star count, frequent pushes, documentation site and pre-built releases). It has broad adoption evidence (many stars, published pre-built llamafiles, docs) and stable binaries, supporting a high TRL.
prerequisites: C/C++ build toolchain for building from source (if needed)
Familiarity with LLM formats (GGUF) and command-line usage
student_project_ideas: Create a small demonstrator that packages a fine-tuned GGUF model into a llamafile and compare inference latency and accuracy versus running the same model via llama.cpp directly.
Build a local voice assistant by combining a whisperfile transcription llamafile with a chat llamafile, and evaluate end-to-end latency on a laptop (measure CPU usage and response time).

tools.name: BabylonJS/Babylon.js
tools.desc: Babylon.js is a powerful, beautiful, simple, and open game and rendering engine packed into a friendly JavaScript framework.

cls.summary: Babylon.js is a mature open-source JavaScript/TypeScript 3D rendering and game engine for building interactive Web-based 3D scenes and applications.
cls.what_it_does: Babylon.js provides a high-level API, scene graph, camera and light models, mesh builders, materials, physics and shader tooling to create interactive 3D applications that run in the browser. It is used by importing the library or ES6 modules into web projects and is notable for broad feature support (WebGL/WebGPU, glTF, exporters) and an online playground with many examples.
cls.trl_rationale: The project was created in 2013, has a large community, many stars/forks, active development and extensive docs/demos, indicating a mature, widely adopted library suitable for production-grade visualization.
prerequisites: npm and modern web build tools
student_project_ideas: Build a browser-based digital-twin dashboard that loads a glTF model, overlays time-series sensor data, and visualises operational states with Babylon.js and a timeseries backend (e.g. InfluxDB).

Create an interactive robotics simulation scene (robot arm + environment) in Babylon.js that consumes exported URDF/glTF assets and visualises motion trajectories generated by a simple motion planner.

tools.name: earthtojake/text-to-cad
tools.desc: Design physical products with AI

cls.summary: text-to-cad is an open-source system that lets AI agents generate parametric CAD models, drawings, simulations and manufacturing checks by producing and running Python build scripts that export STEP/STL/GLB and other fabrication files.
cls.what_it_does: It provides agent plugins and skills that translate natural-language requests into Python CAD scripts (using build123d/OpenCASCADE) to create parts and assemblies, run manufacturing and stress checks, produce engineering drawings, renderings, PCB files and robot simulation outputs. Notable features include live CAD viewing, export to common fabrication formats (STEP, STL, 3MF, DXF), integration with KiCad, Blender, CalculiX and slicers, and CLI installers that set up the tools across local agent apps.
cls.trl_rationale: The project is actively maintained, has extensive features, installer scripts and many stars and forks indicating community interest, but the repository is only ~7 months old so it lacks the multi-year production track record or stable v1+ releases required for TRL 7+. README shows integrations and usage but age limits higher rating.
student_project_ideas: Create an automated workflow where an agent generates a parametric bracket from a text brief, runs manufacturing checks, exports a STEP and sliced 3D-print file, and documents the changes needed to meet printability constraints.

Integrate text-to-cad with a ROS simulation: have the agent generate a simple robot gripper CAD model, export URDF/MJCF for simulation, and evaluate grasping performance in a simulated pick-and-place task.

tools.name: mxgmn/WaveFunctionCollapse
tools.desc: Bitmap & tilemap generation from a single example with the help of ideas from quantum mechanics

cls.summary: WaveFunctionCollapse (WFC) is an algorithm and reference C# implementation that generates new bitmaps or tilemaps by recombining locally observed patterns from a single example image.
cls.what_it_does: WFC analyses an example image to extract NxN pixel patterns and then synthesises new images whose local pattern statistics match the input by repeatedly collapsing and propagating constraints across an output grid. It is used as a procedural content generator for textures, tilemaps and levels and is notable for producing coherent outputs from small examples and for many language/platform ports and game integrations.
cls.trl_rationale: The repository is long-lived (created 2016, actively maintained with many stars and forks) and the algorithm has been adopted in commercial games and many ports, indicating broad real-world use and stable maturity.
prerequisites: familiarity with C# and .NET build tooling
student_project_ideas: Integrate WFC into a simple Unity or Godot level generator that converts example room layouts into playable levels and evaluate playability metrics.
Use WFC to generate texture atlases or procedural facades for a small urban modelling task and compare statistical similarity of generated outputs to the input example.

tools.name: pascalorg/editor
tools.desc: Open-source 3D architecture software for AECO, scan-to-BIM. Agent-friendly, browser-first, MCP, CLI.

cls.summary: Pascal Editor is an open-source, browser-first 3D building editor for AECO work that supports IFC/BIM modelling, scan-to-BIM workflows, a local CLI, and agent integration via the Model Context Protocol (MCP).
cls.what_it_does: Pascal Editor provides tools to create and edit buildings, levels, walls, slabs, openings, rooms and furniture in the browser and as embeddable packages; it can import 3D scans as reference layers for scan-to-BIM and store projects locally or in a hosted workspace. It is notable for being local-first, supporting a CLI and self-hosting, and offering first-class integration with AI assistants using the open MCP protocol.
cls.trl_rationale: Repo is >1 year old, has large community interest (25k+ stars, many forks), active pushes and documented real integrations (Cursor marketplace, Claude/Codex plugins, hosted endpoint and CLI), CLI and self-hosting instructions — evidence of production-readiness but not a de-facto industry standard.
prerequisites: WebGPU-capable browser for full feature set
basic React/TypeScript knowledge to embed packages
student_project_ideas: Create a scan-to-BIM workflow: import a small point cloud into Pascal, model walls/rooms over it, export IFC and compare geometric/area metrics with the source scan using a Python script.

Build an agent-assisted modelling pipeline: connect an MCP-capable agent (Cursor or a simple MCP client) to a local Pascal CLI instance and implement an agent skill that automates placement of furniture to satisfy simple space-planning rules.

tools.name: taosdata/TDengine
tools.desc: High-performance, scalable time-series database designed for Industrial IoT (IIoT) scenarios

cls.summary: TDengine is an open-source, high-performance time-series database designed for large-scale IoT and Industrial IoT deployments to ingest, store, query and analyze time-series data in real time.
cls.what_it_does: TDengine provides a distributed, cloud-native time-series database optimized for high-throughput ingestion, compression and fast queries of sensor streams and telemetry. It is used as a backend for IoT, connected vehicle and industrial-monitoring systems and includes features for sharding, compute/storage separation, stream processing and built-in AI agents for forecasting and anomaly detection. It is notable for its scalability claims, Kubernetes support and integrations with common observability tooling.
cls.trl_rationale: The project was created in 2019, is actively maintained with a large userbase and community (many stars/forks and claimed widespread instances), offers production deployment options (Kubernetes, containers, managed cloud), and has mature documentation — evidence of wide adoption and production use.
prerequisites: Linux (preferred) or macOS; limited Windows support
student_project_ideas: Build an IoT telemetry pipeline that ingests sensor data from MQTT into TDengine, then create Grafana dashboards and alerting to demonstrate real-time monitoring and anomaly detection.
Compare ingestion performance and query latency between TDengine and TimescaleDB for a simulated industrial sensor workload, and evaluate compression and storage usage.

tools.name: timescale/timescaledb
tools.desc: A time-series database for high-performance real-time analytics packaged as a Postgres extension

cls.summary: TimescaleDB is a PostgreSQL extension that provides a high-performance time-series database for ingesting, storing and querying large volumes of time-stamped data.
cls.what_it_does: TimescaleDB extends PostgreSQL with hypertables and time-series specific features (compression, time_bucket, columnstore) to enable efficient ingest and fast analytical queries on event and sensor data. It is deployed as a Postgres extension (can run via Docker) and is notable for combining full Postgres functionality with time-series optimisations useful for IoT, monitoring and real‑time analytics.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository is mature (created 2017), widely used (23k+ stars), active maintenance with recent pushes and extensive docs; TimescaleDB is used in production by many organisations so it is a mature, widely adopted project.
prerequisites: familiarity with Docker or Linux for deployment
student_project_ideas: Build an IoT sensor pipeline that ingests simulated sensor telemetry into TimescaleDB via a Kafka connector, then implement dashboards and alert queries in Grafana to demonstrate anomaly detection.

Create a digital-twin style monitoring application that stores machine telemetry in TimescaleDB, implements aggregated time_bucket analytics and evaluates compression and query performance for different chunking/compression settings.

tools.name: thingsboard/thingsboard
tools.desc: All-in-one IoT Platform - Device management, data collection, processing and visualization.

cls.summary: ThingsBoard is an open-source (source-available) IoT platform for device management, scalable telemetry collection, rule-based data processing and real-time dashboards.
cls.what_it_does: ThingsBoard collects telemetry from devices (MQTT/HTTP/CoAP/LwM2M), stores time-series data, provides a rule-engine for processing/alarms and exposes dashboard widgets and SCADA-style visualisations. It is deployed on-premises or as a cloud service and is notable for supporting industrial IoT protocols and scalable back-end integrations (Kafka, SQL/NoSQL stores).
cls.trl_rationale: Repository is mature (created 2016) with many stars, active pushes and a commercial cloud offering; the project is used in production and has a stable feature set, so it matches a widely adopted mature platform rather than an experimental prototype.
prerequisites: Java ecosystem familiarity for custom extensions
student_project_ideas: Build a small telemetry pipeline: connect an ESP32 or Raspberry Pi publishing MQTT sensor data to ThingsBoard, create dashboards and rule chains that trigger alerts sent via email or webhook.

Integrate ThingsBoard with a digital-twin simulation (e.g. a Modelica or Gazebo model) to stream simulated sensor data into ThingsBoard and evaluate dashboard visualisation and alarm behaviour under different simulated fault conditions.

tools.name: img2threejs/img2threejs
tools.desc: Rebuild the object in a reference image as a code-only, procedural, quality-gated, animation-ready Three.js model. Token-efficient image-to-3D.

cls.summary: img2threejs converts a single reference image into a procedural, code-only Three.js model that runs in the browser and is animation-ready.
cls.what_it_does: Given one reference image, the project generates a TypeScript factory that reconstructs the subject using primitives, procedural shaders and generated geometry rather than exported mesh files. It is notable for producing compact, editable source code (a THREE.Group factory), a quality-gated detail inventory, and a live demo gallery where generated models run directly in the browser.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository is 125 days old (younger than 1 year) so it cannot be rated above TRL 6 by the project's rules, but it shows strong evidence of maturity: large star count (~21k), frequent pushes, a live demo gallery, versioned demo records and an active showcase repo, which indicate beta-level readiness.
student_project_ideas: Build a web viewer that imports img2threejs-generated TypeScript factories and assembles multiple procedurally-generated parts into an interactive mechanical assembly, comparing editable procedural parts vs static mesh parts for animation and pivoting.

Evaluate perceptual likeness by using img2threejs to reconstruct a set of photographed objects, measure region-by-region confidence reported by the pipeline, and compare fidelity against a mesh-based photogrammetry pipeline.

tools.name: nats-io/nats-server
tools.desc: High-Performance server for NATS.io, the cloud and edge native messaging system.

cls.summary: NATS Server is a high-performance, open-source messaging broker (pub/sub, request-reply, streaming patterns) used to connect services, devices and edge nodes in distributed systems.
cls.what_it_does: NATS provides a lightweight, secure and low-latency message bus for cloud, edge and on-premise deployments, supporting multiple messaging patterns (publish/subscribe, request/reply and streaming). It is typically deployed as a standalone server or clustered service and is notable for its performance, small footprint, broad client-language support and CNCF-backed ecosystem.
cls.trl_rationale: The project is mature and widely adopted (created 2012, >21k stars, CNCF project, documented adopters and recent security audit) indicating significant real-world use and stability consistent with TRL 8.
prerequisites: optional: Go toolchain to build from source
student_project_ideas: Build a sensor-to-cloud pipeline where Raspberry Pi sensors publish telemetry to a NATS cluster and a backend service aggregates and visualises time-series data (combine with Prometheus/Grafana).

Implement a multi-service robotics coordination demo where separate ROS nodes or microservices communicate via NATS for command distribution and telemetry, and evaluate latency and reliability under load.

tools.name: Unity-Technologies/ml-agents
tools.desc: The Unity Machine Learning Agents Toolkit (ML-Agents) is an open-source project that enables games and simulations to serve as environments for training intelligent agents using deep reinforcement learning and imitation learning.

cls.summary: Unity ML-Agents is an open-source toolkit that turns Unity games and simulations into environments for training and evaluating intelligent agents using reinforcement and imitation learning.
cls.what_it_does: ML-Agents provides a runtime Unity package and a Python training API to create simulated environments, collect observations and rewards, and train agents with reinforcement learning or imitation learning algorithms. It is used by researchers and engineers to prototype control policies and behaviour in physically simulated or game-like environments and supports headless training and curriculum learning, making it notable for interactive, transferable simulation-based RL experiments.
cls.trl_rationale: The project is long-lived (created 2017), has many stars, active maintainers, regular releases and documentation, and is widely used in research and industry experiments, indicating a mature and broadly adopted toolkit.
prerequisites: basic Unity editor usage and C# scripting
Python and machine learning fundamentals (RL concepts)
student_project_ideas: Train a mobile-robot navigation policy in a Unity environment using ML-Agents and then evaluate transfer by exporting the policy to a ROS or simulated robot stack (e.g., ROS 2 + Gazebo).

Create a simulated assembly task in Unity and use imitation learning with ML-Agents to teach a manipulator to perform the task, measuring success rates under sensor noise and comparing RL vs imitation approaches.

tools.name: mlc-ai/web-llm
tools.desc: High-performance In-browser LLM Inference Engine

cls.summary: WebLLM is an open-source engine for running large language models entirely in the web browser using WebGPU and WebAssembly.
cls.what_it_does: WebLLM loads LLMs into the browser and runs inference with hardware acceleration (WebGPU) so applications can call an OpenAI-compatible API without a server. It's used as an npm/CDN library or example apps (including a chat demo) and supports streaming, JSON-mode, and many model families via the MLC model format.
cls.trl_rationale: The project is mature and actively maintained (created 2023, >13k stars, recent pushes, docs, examples and a peer-reviewed paper), showing wide adoption and stability suitable for production-grade browser LLM deployment.
prerequisites: familiarity with npm/CDN packaging and WebAssembly concepts
student_project_ideas: Build a browser-based engineering assistant that loads a compact LLM with WebLLM and integrates it into a simple CAD viewer to answer usage and API questions about geometries.
Compare latency and privacy trade-offs by measuring inference time and memory for the same quantized model run locally in WebLLM (browser) versus a server-side deployment, and write a short report.

tools.name: louis-e/arnis
tools.desc: Generate any location from the real world in Minecraft with a high level of detail.

cls.summary: Arnis converts OpenStreetMap and elevation data into detailed Minecraft/Minetest/Hytale worlds that reflect real-world geography and buildings.
cls.what_it_does: Arnis fetches geospatial data (OpenStreetMap, elevation) and processes it into large, accurate Minecraft-compatible worlds with configurable scale and generation settings; it runs as a desktop app or from the command line and supports multiple editions (Java, Bedrock, Minetest/Luanti, Hytale). It is notable for handling large areas, producing architecturally-informed building geometry, and having strong documentation, releases and community adoption.
cls.trl_rationale: The project is mature and actively maintained (created 2022, frequent pushes in 2026), has many stars and forks, official releases, documented usage and press/academic recognition; this indicates broad community adoption though it is not an industry standard.
prerequisites: Rust toolchain to build from source (or use provided releases)
Minecraft or compatible game for loading generated worlds
student_project_ideas: Generate a scaled Minecraft model of a local flood-prone neighbourhood using Arnis and combine it with simple hydrology simulations to create an interactive flood-visualisation demo.
Compare building footprints and heights inferred by Arnis from OpenStreetMap against local cadastral or LiDAR-derived models to quantify generation accuracy and identify common failure modes.

tools.name: microsoft/AirSim
tools.desc: Open source simulator for autonomous vehicles built on Unreal Engine / Unity, from Microsoft AI & Research

cls.summary: AirSim is an open-source, high-fidelity simulator for drones, cars and other autonomous vehicles built as an Unreal (and experimental Unity) plugin to support research and development of perception, control and learning algorithms.
cls.what_it_does: AirSim provides a physics- and photo-realistic simulation environment where developers can run vehicles, collect sensor data (RGB, depth, segmentation, IMU, LiDAR), and control vehicles programmatically via cross-platform APIs (C++, Python, C#, Java). It supports software-in-the-loop (SITL) and hardware-in-the-loop (HITL) workflows with common flight stacks (PX4, ArduPilot), and is notable for being an extensible Unreal Engine plugin used widely in autonomous systems research and ML data generation.
cls.trl_rationale: AirSim is a long-lived (created 2017), actively maintained project with large community interest (18k stars), extensive documentation, published papers and known real-world users; it has been used in research and teaching for years, indicating maturity and adoption beyond initial development.
prerequisites: Unreal Engine (or Unity for experimental builds)
Python or C++ for client/API usage
familiarity with ROS/PX4/ArduPilot for SITL/HITL integration (optional)
student_project_ideas: Build and evaluate a vision-based quadrotor obstacle-avoidance controller by training a neural policy in AirSim (Python + TensorFlow/PyTorch) and validating it with SITL using PX4.

Create a simulated autonomous-car perception pipeline that logs camera and lidar data in AirSim, implements sensor fusion and object detection, and measures detection performance under varied weather/lighting conditions.

tools.name: gfx-rs/wgpu
tools.desc: A cross-platform, safe, pure-Rust graphics API.

cls.summary: wgpu is a production-grade, cross-platform graphics API in Rust that exposes the WebGPU-style GPU programming model for native (Vulkan/Metal/D3D12/OpenGL) and web (WebGPU/WebGL2) platforms.
cls.what_it_does: wgpu provides a safe Rust API for GPU programming and rendering, letting developers create shaders, pipelines, buffers and textures that run on Vulkan, Metal, D3D12, OpenGL and WebGPU/WebGL2. It is used as the graphics core in projects such as Firefox, Deno and other Rust projects and is notable for being a Rust-first, WebGPU-compatible implementation with broad platform support and an active ecosystem (wgpu-native, naga).
cls.trl_rationale: Repository is long-lived (created 2018), widely used and highly starred, and the README states it powers Firefox and Deno; it has stable releases, broad platform support, and an active community—evidence of mature, widely adopted software.
prerequisites: native GPU drivers and toolchains for target backends
student_project_ideas: Build a real-time physically based renderer demo in Rust using wgpu that loads glTF models and implements basic PBR and image-based lighting.
Create a hardware-accelerated simulation visualiser (e.g., particle system or fluid field) that runs both natively and in the browser via wasm using wgpu and compare performance across backends.

tools.name: xming521/WeClone
tools.desc: Build a portrait of your life. Assistants that know you better. Clones that sound more like you.

cls.summary: WeClone builds a personal 'life portrait' from your chat history and other message exports, then uses that portrait to train or drive personalised AI chat clones you can deploy to messaging platforms.
cls.what_it_does: WeClone extracts facts, domains and a speaking-style profile from your exported chats to create a reviewable, source-traced life portrait that acts as long-term memory for personal assistants. It supports fine-tuning (LoRA) of open models or real-time driving of clones, and connects those clones to platforms such as Telegram, Discord and Slack via bots and MCP-style memory interfaces. Notable features include speaking-style analysis, per-fact privacy controls and encrypted local storage by default.
cls.trl_rationale: The repository is over two years old, highly starred (18k+ stars), actively maintained with recent pushes and documented installation and deployment flows, and shows features for real-world use (fine-tuning, bot connectors), which points to production-ready maturity.
prerequisites: Optional NVIDIA GPU for fine-tuning (16GB+ VRAM recommended)
OpenAI-compatible API or Codex CLI for extraction (or compatible local model/runtime)
student_project_ideas: Build a privacy-aware pipeline that imports Telegram chat exports into WeClone, inspects the extracted life-portrait, and implements filters that automatically redact or tag sensitive facts before fine-tuning.

Compare speaking-style analysis outputs by running WeClone on two different users' chat histories and visualise the 179 style features to study stylistic differences and their effect on a small fine-tuned chatbot.

tools.name: google-deepmind/mujoco
tools.desc: Multi-Joint dynamics with Contact. A general purpose physics simulator.

cls.summary: MuJoCo is a high-performance physics simulator for articulated bodies and contact used in robotics, biomechanics and learning research.
cls.what_it_does: MuJoCo simulates multi-joint dynamics with contact to predict motion and forces of articulated systems; it is used via a C API with official Python bindings and has viewers for native and web (WASM) use. It is notable for fast, accurate contact dynamics, support for differentiable physics (JAX/MJX), and wide adoption in robotics and reinforcement learning research.
cls.trl_rationale: The repo is maintained by Google DeepMind, has many stars and active monthly releases, official bindings (Python, JS, Unity) and many downstream projects, indicating wide adoption and maturity beyond initial research prototypes.
student_project_ideas: Implement and compare a PID and an LQR controller for a simulated robotic arm in MuJoCo, using the Python bindings to log performance and visualise trajectories.

Build a simulated mobile manipulator in MuJoCo and integrate a learned policy (RL or imitation learning) to complete a pick-and-place task, then evaluate robustness under perturbed contact/friction parameters.

tools.name: questdb/questdb
tools.desc: QuestDB is a high performance, open-source, time-series database

cls.summary: QuestDB is an open-source, high-performance time-series database that ingests and queries telemetry and event data with low latency using SQL.
cls.what_it_does: QuestDB captures, stores and queries high-throughput time-series data with a SQL interface and specialized time-series extensions (SAMPLE BY, ASOF JOIN, materialized/live views). It is used for real-time ingestion, stream processing and tiered storage (native columnar partitions and Parquet) and is notable for very high ingest/query throughput and a zero-GC Java engine with hot-path code in C++/Rust.
cls.trl_rationale: QuestDB is a mature project (created 2014) with a large community (17.5k stars), ongoing active development and production-facing features (Parquet, QWP, enterprise tiering) and published performance benchmarks, indicating wide adoption and stable engineering maturity.
student_project_ideas: Build an IoT telemetry pipeline: collect sensor data with MQTT, ingest into QuestDB, and create real-time dashboards demonstrating alerting and downsampling to Parquet for cold storage.
Compare query latency and ingestion throughput between QuestDB and TimescaleDB using a synthetic telemetry workload, and visualise the trade-offs in storage and query performance.

tools.name: playcanvas/engine
tools.desc: Powerful web graphics runtime built on WebGL, WebGPU, WebXR and glTF

cls.summary: PlayCanvas Engine is an open-source, browser-based 3D engine for building interactive WebGL/WebGPU applications, games and visualisations.
cls.what_it_does: PlayCanvas provides a runtime for rendering and interacting with 2D/3D scenes in the browser, including graphics, animation, physics, input and asset streaming (glTF, Draco, Basis). It is used by importing via npm or scaffolding a project and is notable for first-class WebGPU/WebGL support, WebXR integration and a lightweight, modular API suited to real-time web visualisation.
cls.trl_rationale: The repository is long-lived (created 2014), has many stars and forks, active recent commits and documented users/companies, showing broad adoption and maturity across projects—consistent with a mature, widely-used engine.
student_project_ideas: Build an interactive web-based digital twin dashboard that streams glTF models and time-series data to visualise component states (combine PlayCanvas with a timeseries backend like InfluxDB or MQTT).
Create a WebXR-enabled robotics simulator scene where a simple robot arm (rigged and animated) executes trajectories and students implement control logic in JavaScript for visual verification.

tools.name: emqx/emqx
tools.desc: The most scalable and reliable MQTT broker for AI, IoT, IIoT and connected vehicles

cls.summary: EMQX is an industrial‑scale MQTT broker and IoT platform for connecting, routing and processing messages from millions of devices in real time.
cls.what_it_does: EMQX provides a high‑performance MQTT server (with support for MQTT v5/v3.1.1/v3.1 and related protocols like CoAP, LwM2M and MQTT‑SN) that routes, queues and transforms IoT messages and integrates them with backend systems. It is used as a clustered, highly available infrastructure component (on‑prem or cloud) and includes features such as a rule engine, data bridges, schema registry and flow designer to process and forward telemetry to databases, message queues and AI services.
cls.trl_rationale: The project is long‑running (created 2012), widely used and actively maintained with many stars, forks and recent commits; README documents production features and integrations indicating broad adoption and maturity.
prerequisites: networking (TLS, ports) and familiarity with message queues/databases
student_project_ideas: Build a campus sensor network prototype: deploy EMQX in Docker, connect ESP32 sensors via MQTT, and forward telemetry to InfluxDB + Grafana for a monitoring dashboard.
Integrate EMQX with a machine‑learning pipeline: route device telemetry to Kafka via EMQX bridges, consume it to train a predictive maintenance model and visualise results in a dashboard.

tools.name: tangency-labs/solidcraft
tools.desc: SolidCraft: an open-source parametric 3D CAD application built in pure Rust. Desktop, web, and automation through MCP.

cls.summary: SolidCraft is an open-source, parametric 3D CAD application written in Rust that runs on desktop and in the browser and supports a feature timeline, assemblies, sheet-metal and file import/export (STEP, IGES, STL, etc.).
cls.what_it_does: SolidCraft provides parametric sketching, constraint solving and a feature-based modelling timeline to create and edit solids and assemblies; it exports and imports common CAD formats and supports headless automation and AI-driven modelling through an MCP server. It is notable for being implemented in pure Rust with desktop installers, a browser build (WASM), and an experimental plugin runtime using WebAssembly.
cls.trl_rationale: The project is clearly functional (desktop installers, notarized mac build, AppImage, browser WASM demo, file import/export and many features documented) which indicates alpha use, but the repository is very young (≈40 days) so there is not yet a long track record or stable release history — TRL 5 (alpha in use) reflects that.
prerequisites: basic CAD modelling knowledge (sketches, constraints, feature timeline)
Rust toolchain if building from source (cargo) — not required to use prebuilt apps
student_project_ideas: Create a parametric enclosure for a small electronics board in SolidCraft, export STEP and perform a simple interference and mass-properties study; optionally drive parameter changes from a Python script using the CLI to demonstrate design variants.
Integrate SolidCraft-produced URDF and STEP exports into a robotics simulation pipeline (e.g. Gazebo/ROS) to test assembly kinematics and collision interactions for a simple manipulator.

tools.name: ArduPilot/ardupilot
tools.desc: ArduPlane, ArduCopter, ArduRover, ArduSub source

cls.summary: ArduPilot is a mature open-source autopilot firmware stack that runs on many types of unmanned vehicles (planes, copters, rovers, subs and more) and is used for flight control, navigation and vehicle automation.
cls.what_it_does: ArduPilot provides firmware, drivers and control algorithms to operate a wide range of unmanned vehicles, solving vehicle control, navigation, telemetry and mission automation. It is used by flashing supported flight-controller hardware or running in software-in-the-loop (SITL) for testing and development, and is notable for broad vehicle support, a large community and long track record in real-world deployments.
cls.trl_rationale: The project has been actively developed since 2010/2013, has many stars and forks, an active maintainer list, extensive documentation and real-world deployments across vehicle types; this indicates a mature, widely adopted codebase (TRL 8).
prerequisites: familiarity with flight controllers and hardware toolchains (e.g. Pixhawk/STM32)
basic understanding of MAVLink/telemetry and control theory
student_project_ideas: Build and evaluate an autonomous waypoint-following mission on a small quadcopter using ArduPilot on a Pixhawk, and log telemetry for a control-performance report.
Integrate ArduPilot SITL with ROS to prototype and test a sensor-based obstacle-avoidance behaviour in simulation and compare against logged flight data.

tools.name: lemomo-ai/lemo-opuscar
tools.desc: A toolbox of film styles made in code for Claude Code: 99 ready to use, and your own. Each style is a style prompt plus a demo film made entirely in code by Claude Opus 5.5, with no video model. By Lemomo. · 一套用代码做片的风格工具箱：99 种现成风格，也能做出你自己的

cls.summary: A Claude Code skill and code library that provides 99 ready-made film style prompts and frame-by-frame code demos so an agent can generate short films (rendered with canvas/WebGL, TTS and ffmpeg) without a video model.
cls.what_it_does: Lemo-Opuscar is a prompt-and-code toolbox for Claude Code that directs an agent to produce short, stylised films entirely in code: each style includes a STYLE.md, demo film source, and rendering pipeline using canvas/WebGL, TTS and ffmpeg. Users pick a style, supply a brief story (and optionally voice/music/images), and the skill generates frames, audio and assembles the final video; it is notable for being an agent skill tailored for Claude Fable/Opus and for providing many ready-made, inspectable style projects.
cls.trl_rationale: The repository is feature-rich with install instructions, an interactive gallery, plugin integration and many examples, indicating early adoption; however it is only 52 days old so by the TRL rules maturity is limited and it should be rated at most TRL 5.
student_project_ideas: Create a 60-second short film using one of the provided styles and extend a STYLE.md to add a custom soundtrack produced with an open-source audio library.

Build a small web UI that lets users pick a style and topic, invokes the Claude skill (locally or via Claude plugin) to generate the film project, then preview frames rendered with three.js or canvas and export via ffmpeg.

tools.name: tracel-ai/burn
tools.desc: Burn is a next generation tensor library and Deep Learning Framework that doesn't compromise on flexibility, efficiency and portability.

cls.summary: Burn is an open-source Rust tensor library and deep-learning framework that runs the same model code across CPU, GPU and web backends for training and deployment.
cls.what_it_does: Burn provides a PyTorch-like API for building neural networks and performing automatic differentiation, while JIT-compiling and fusing tensor kernels for multi-backend execution (CUDA, ROCm, Metal, Vulkan, WebGPU and CPU). It is used to train and run models in a single Rust codebase so the exact code used for training can be deployed for inference on-device or in different runtimes, and it includes tooling for model import/export and ecosystem crates for datasets and benchmarks.
cls.trl_rationale: The project is over three years old, has a large community (16k stars), active development and multiple backend implementations and companion crates, showing production readiness beyond an experimental prototype; however it is not yet a de-facto ecosystem standard.
prerequisites: basic machine learning concepts (neural networks, autodiff)
GPU toolchains for desired backends (CUDA/ROCm/Metal/Vulkan/WebGPU) when using accelerated backends
student_project_ideas: Implement a small image-classification training pipeline in Burn and deploy the trained model to a WebGPU backend to run inference in the browser, comparing latency and accuracy with a PyTorch/ONNX baseline.

Build an on-device personalization demo where a pre-trained Burn model is fine-tuned on-device (or simulated edge device) and measure the performance and resource usage across CPU, Vulkan/Metal and WebGPU backends.

tools.name: CoplayDev/unity-mcp
tools.desc: Unity MCP acts as a bridge between AI assistants and your Unity Editor. Give your LLM tools to manage assets, control scenes, edit scripts, and automate tasks within Unity.

cls.summary: MCP for Unity lets LLMs and AI assistants control the Unity Editor to create and modify scenes, assets and scripts, automate tasks, run tests and build projects.
cls.what_it_does: It exposes ~50 MCP tool entrypoints to control the Unity Editor from any Model Context Protocol client, so LLMs can create GameObjects, edit C# scripts (with Roslyn validation), manage assets, run tests, profile and build projects. It is used as a bridge between LLMs/assistant clients (Claude, OpenAI, Gemini, local LLMs, VS Code, etc.) and Unity to automate game-development workflows and editor tasks.
cls.trl_rationale: The project has a sustained release history (v10.x releases in 2026), high community adoption (many stars/forks), active maintenance and documentation, and a cited 2025 conference paper; these indicate production-ready maturity rather than an experimental prototype.
prerequisites: C# and Unity editor scripting knowledge
Basic MCP client / LLM usage and optional Python (3.10+) for server setups
student_project_ideas: Build an LLM-driven playtesting pipeline that uses MCP for Unity plus the Autopilot tester to generate and run test scenarios, then analyse failure cases and coverage.
Create an assistant that automatically refactors Unity C# scripts (using Roslyn validation) to enforce architectural patterns, then measure code quality and build reliability before/after.

tools.name: CesiumGS/cesium
tools.desc: An open-source JavaScript library for world-class 3D globes and maps :earth_americas:

cls.summary: CesiumJS is an open-source JavaScript library for building high-precision, interactive 3D globes and maps in the web browser.
cls.what_it_does: CesiumJS streams and renders large geospatial datasets (terrain, imagery, 3D Tiles, glTF, GeoJSON) using WebGL so developers can visualise and interact with world-scale maps in the browser. It is used as a client-side engine for web-based digital twins, mapping applications and geospatial analysis, and is notable for supporting standards (3D Tiles, glTF) and large, tiled datasets at high precision.
cls.trl_rationale: CesiumJS is a long-established project (created 2012) with large community adoption (many stars, active repo, frequent commits) and widely used in production for web 3D mapping; this history and ecosystem support a mature TRL of 8.
prerequisites: npm and modern web build tools
basic WebGL / 3D concepts and geospatial coordinate systems (WGS84)
student_project_ideas: Build a web-based digital twin that visualises sensor time-series over a 3D city model by streaming 3D Tiles and plotting telemetry as animated overlays.
Create an interactive hazard-mapping tool that combines elevation (terrain) and flood simulation output (GeoJSON raster/vector overlays) and visualises inundation scenarios in CesiumJS.

tools.name: yihui-dev/awesome-opus5-5-videos
tools.desc: A growing collection of viral videos made with Claude Opus 5.5 and the prompts behind them. Watch each original next to a live remake on Skillry. Updated regularly.

cls.summary: A curated, regularly updated collection of prompts and examples showing videos produced by Claude Opus 5.5 where the model writes animation code (HTML, Canvas, SVG, Three.js) and links to originals and live remakes.
cls.what_it_does: This repository collects prompts and links to viral videos created with Claude Opus 5.5 that produce animation code (HTML, Canvas, SVG, Three.js and related tech). Users can copy prompts and study or rerun the generated code, and many entries point to live remakes hosted on Skillry for side-by-side viewing. It is notable as a large, curated prompt library focused on creative coding and web-based animation examples rather than engineering simulation.
cls.trl_rationale: The repo is a curated collection with many examples and live remakes, but it is very new (created 51 days ago) so it lacks the long track record or stable releases needed for higher TRL; evidence is the README and dataset folders but short age limits the rating.
student_project_ideas: Pick a prompt from the collection, remake the animation using Three.js and extend it to visualise a simple engineering dataset (e.g. sensor time series) in the same visual style.

Create an interactive web-based explainer that adapts one of the prompts to illustrate a systems engineering concept (requirements traceability or system behaviour) with annotated controls and narration.

tools.name: llmware-ai/llmware
tools.desc: Unified framework for building enterprise RAG pipelines with small, specialized models

cls.summary: llmware is an open-source Python framework for building retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) applications and running many small, optimized local models on Windows, macOS and Linux.
cls.what_it_does: llmware provides a model catalog (300+ models) and an integrated RAG pipeline for ingesting, parsing and indexing documents, running embeddings, and querying knowledge libraries; it abstracts multiple runtimes (GGUF, ONNX, OpenVINO, PyTorch, etc.) so the same code can use CPU/GPU/NPU-optimized backends or cloud APIs. It is notable for focusing on local and edge deployment with prepackaged quantized models and connectors to vector DBs and common inference runtimes.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository is mature and active (created 2023, many stars and forks, frequent pushes) with extensive README, examples and a large model catalog suggesting production-ready usage; community adoption (stars ~14k) supports TRL 7 rather than experimental status.
prerequisites: basic familiarity with LLMs and embeddings
optional GPU/NPU drivers for optimized runtimes
student_project_ideas: Build a searchable knowledge assistant for a course repository by ingesting lecture notes and lab manuals into an llmware Library and evaluating retrieval quality using two different embedding models and Milvus vs Chroma.
Integrate a domain-specific small quantized model from the llmware catalog into an automated document Q&A pipeline and measure latency and accuracy on-device (CPU) versus using ONNXRuntime-GPU.

tools.name: cactus-compute/cactus
tools.desc: Sub-50mb agentic, voice and vision intelligence for consumer devices.

cls.summary: Cactus is a Python package for running compact on-device language, speech and vision models and building agentic workflows with tool-calling and fine-tuning support.
cls.what_it_does: Cactus provides a unified API to run text, voice and image models locally on consumer/edge devices, offering an agent framework (Needle) with tool-calling, a speech recogniser (Whistle) and an image understanding model (Mirage). It downloads and caches model runtimes and weights for local inference, supports model fine-tuning and provides an MLX adapter for certain macOS checkpoints.
cls.trl_rationale: The project is actively maintained, well-documented, provides runtime binaries and model checkpoints and has many stars and recent commits, indicating a functioning beta; however the repository is under one year old (≈266 days), which limits it to TRL 6 under the stated rules.
prerequisites: familiarity with Python packaging and basic ML model concepts
(optional) Apple silicon / macOS 26 for MLX CQ checkpoints
student_project_ideas: Build an edge voice assistant for a Raspberry Pi (microphone input -> Whistle transcription -> Needle agent -> actuator control) to demonstrate on-device agent workflows and tool-calling.

Compare local image understanding: run Mirage on a dataset of inspection photos and create a small dashboard that extracts structured findings and evaluates accuracy against hand-labelled ground truth.

tools.name: tonhowtf/omniget
tools.desc: A local MCP server that gives your coding agent a desktop toolbox: downloads from YouTube, torrents and every site yt-dlp supports, media conversion, files, chats and system cleanup. One line connects Claude Code, Codex, Cursor or Gemini CLI, and sensitive actions wait for your click. Free and open source for Windows, macOS and Linux.

cls.summary: OmniGet is a local MCP server that exposes desktop tools (downloaders, media conversion, file operations, developer utilities and controlled system actions) to coding agents via a secure, tokenised HTTP MCP interface.
cls.what_it_does: OmniGet runs a local MCP-compatible HTTP server that gives coding agents controlled access to desktop functionality such as downloading media (yt-dlp, gallery-dl, torrents), file conversion and inspection (FFmpeg, chunked downloads), developer utilities (folder-to-prompt, HTTP/JSON helpers) and system actions that require a user click. It is used by running the server locally and connecting agents (Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI, Cursor, etc.) via the provided MCP snippets or the omniget-mcp bridge; results are returned as structured data and sensitive actions pause for manual approval.
cls.trl_rationale: The project is under one year old (created 2026-02-11, ~279 days) so TRL is limited to beta; however it shows strong community interest (large star/fork counts), active maintenance (recent pushes) and shipped tooling (omniget-mcp), consistent with a TRL 6 assessment.
prerequisites: basic knowledge of MCP-compatible agent clients (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor) and tokens
student_project_ideas: Build an agent workflow that uses OmniGet to download a video playlist, convert audio to text with FFmpeg, and produce a searchable index of lecture transcripts for a course.

Create a safe agent-driven data-collection pipeline where an agent queues scientific datasets (HTTP/FTP/magnet links) through OmniGet, logs errors and requires manual approvals for any network or system-level actions.

tools.name: heroiclabs/nakama
tools.desc: Scalable open-source game backend server: multiplayer, matchmaking, leaderboards, chat, and social features for games.

cls.summary: Nakama is an open-source scalable game backend server that provides multiplayer, matchmaking, chat, leaderboards and social features for games and apps.
cls.what_it_does: Nakama provides a production-ready server to handle user accounts, storage, social graphs, chat, realtime and turn-based multiplayer, leaderboards and tournaments, and extensible server logic via Lua/TypeScript/Go. It is used as a drop-in backend for games and apps (with client SDKs for Unity, Unreal, Godot, web and mobile) and notable for its scalability, Docker support, and support for CockroachDB/Postgres.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository created in 2017, with many stars, forks, active recent commits and an established releases page and customers referenced in docs, indicating a mature, widely adopted project suitable for production use.
prerequisites: experience with client SDKs (Unity, Unreal, web) for integration
student_project_ideas: Build a simple multiplayer game in Unity that uses Nakama for matchmaking, realtime chat and leaderboards to demonstrate client-server integration and session management.
Integrate Nakama as a telemetry and user-management backend for a small robotics or IoT prototype, using its storage and presence APIs to collect and visualise runtime metrics.

tools.name: xszyou/Fay
tools.desc: fay是一个帮助数字人（2.5d、3d、移动、pc、网页）或大语言模型（openai兼容、deepseek）连通业务系统的agent框架。

cls.summary: Fay is an open-source agent framework that connects large language models, ASR/TTS and digital-human (2.5D/3D) front-ends to application backends for multi-platform interactive avatars.
cls.what_it_does: Fay provides a complete stack to drive interactive digital humans by linking LLMs (OpenAI-compatible and others), ASR, TTS and avatar drivers, exposing text/voice and control APIs for apps, web, embedded devices and game engines. It is notable for its focus on end-to-end digital-person scenarios (virtual teachers/anchors), configurable pipelines (models can be swapped) and support for fully-offline deployments and multi-user concurrency.
cls.trl_rationale: The repository is mature (created 2022) with many stars/forks, active maintenance and documentation links; it provides runnable code, platform instructions and a web management UI, indicating production-ready capability rather than a one-off prototype.
student_project_ideas: Build a campus virtual assistant that uses Fay to connect an OpenAI-compatible LLM, a TTS engine and a simple Unity avatar to provide voice answers about timetables and campus maps.

Integrate Fay with an IoT sensor stream to create a talking dashboard: use sensor data to trigger the digital human to announce anomalies and provide suggested actions (combine with a basic rules engine).

tools.name: makerspet/oomwoo
tools.desc: Open-source vacuum robot cleaner

cls.summary: OOMWOO is an open-source robot vacuum project that provides ROS2-based software, Gazebo simulation, and hardware/firmware plans to build a hackable, 2D-LiDAR-enabled vacuum running on Raspberry Pi and microcontrollers.
cls.what_it_does: OOMWOO provides a full-stack reference design for a home robot vacuum: ROS2 packages, Gazebo simulation, bill-of-materials and community-driven modules for navigation, mapping (2D LiDAR / SLAM), and integration with Home Assistant. It is used by running the simulator or deploying on Raspberry Pi + microcontroller hardware and is notable for its open modular approach, heavy ROS2 integration and emphasis on local, no‑cloud operation.
cls.trl_rationale: The project provides runnable ROS2 packages, a Gazebo simulation, a BOM and active community contributions and maintainers (high stars and recent activity), indicating a beta-level project; however the repository is only ~160 days old so it lacks a long production track record, which limits TRL to 6.
student_project_ideas: Extend the Gazebo simulation with a new sensor model (e.g. depth camera) and implement a SLAM-based map-merging node using ROS2 to evaluate multi-robot cleaning strategies.

Build a simple hardware prototype by connecting an inexpensive 2D LiDAR and motor drivers to a Raspberry Pi/ESP32 and port the provided navigation stack for real-world mapping and obstacle avoidance testing.

tools.name: alicevision/Meshroom
tools.desc: Node-based Visual Programming Toolbox

cls.summary: Meshroom is an open-source, node-based photogrammetry application that converts collections of photographs into 3D models, camera poses and textured meshes.
cls.what_it_does: Meshroom provides a visual, nodal workflow for multi-view 3D reconstruction (structure-from-motion, dense stereo, meshing and texturing) and supports local or distributed execution on render farms. It is used by loading image sets into a graph of processing nodes, adjusting node attributes, and executing the pipeline while reusing cached intermediate results; notable features include its nodal UI, built-in AliceVision algorithms and plugin system for extending pipelines.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository created in 2015, large user base (13k stars), pre-built releases and active development with many plugins and documented manuals indicate mature, widely adopted software; production-grade AliceVision backend and long track record support TRL 8.
prerequisites: collections of overlapping calibrated or uncalibrated photographs
basic familiarity with photogrammetry concepts (SfM/MVS) and 3D file formats
sufficient disk space and a reasonably powerful CPU/GPU for dense reconstruction
student_project_ideas: Build a small photogrammetry pipeline that captures a physical prototype, reconstructs a textured 3D model in Meshroom and compares mesh accuracy against ground-truth dimensions measured by hand or a laser scanner.

Integrate Meshroom outputs into a digital twin demo by exporting reconstructed geometry and textures to a WebGL viewer (three.js) and streaming metadata (camera poses, timestamps) to a time-series database for visualization of asset provenance.

tools.name: altic-dev/FluidVoice
tools.desc: Fastest and only macOS Dictation app with on-device STT and custom trained AI enhancement model. Windows, iOS testflight!  Android, Linux waitlist open! A local Wispr Flow alternative. Follow https://x.com/fluidvoiceapp for more

cls.summary: FluidVoice is an open-source macOS dictation app that performs on-device speech-to-text and local text cleanup to provide private, searchable meeting transcripts.
cls.what_it_does: FluidVoice captures audio from meetings or the microphone, runs local speech recognition models to transcribe speech to text, and optionally applies local AI-based text cleanup to remove fillers and format the transcript. It is distributed as a native macOS app (with beta builds for other platforms), installs via Homebrew or releases, and is notable for running models locally to preserve privacy and work offline.
cls.trl_rationale: The project is more than a prototype: it has packaged releases, a Homebrew cask, active development, many stars/forks, cross-platform betas and named model distributions; the repository is over one year old and the README references regular releases and production installers, supporting a production-ready TRL.
prerequisites: sufficient local disk space for speech and cleanup models (hundreds of MB per model)
student_project_ideas: Measure latency, CPU/GPU usage and transcription accuracy of FluidVoice's on-device models (Pro/Mini/Pico) versus a cloud ASR (e.g., Whisper API) for meeting recordings and prepare recommendations for deploying local STT in privacy-sensitive environments.
Extend or prototype an export pipeline that takes FluidVoice meeting JSON transcripts and performs automatic requirements extraction or action-item detection using an open-source NLP toolchain.

tools.name: PX4/PX4-Autopilot
tools.desc: PX4 Autopilot Software

cls.summary: PX4 is an open-source autopilot firmware and middleware stack used to control drones, rovers and other unmanned vehicles.
cls.what_it_does: PX4 provides flight-control firmware, a publish/subscribe middleware (uORB) and integrations for simulation, ground control and vehicle hardware to run autonomous vehicles. It is used by developers to build and test autopilot behaviour on real flight controllers or in SITL simulation, and is notable for wide hardware support, MAVLink/ROS2 integration and a modular architecture.
cls.trl_rationale: PX4 has existed since 2012, has a large community, many stars and forks, broad hardware and simulation support, and is used across industry and research—evidence of mature, widely adopted software (TRL 8).
prerequisites: basic control systems and avionics concepts
Linux toolchain and familiarity with MAVLink/ROS concepts
student_project_ideas: Build and tune a quadrotor controller by running PX4 in SITL (Gazebo) and comparing logged flight data to simulated behaviour.
Port and test a custom sensor driver on a Pixhawk-compatible board using PX4 firmware and evaluate state estimation improvements in ROS 2.

tools.name: jrouwe/JoltPhysics
tools.desc: A multi core friendly rigid body physics and collision detection library. Written in C++. Suitable for games and VR applications. Used by Horizon Forbidden West and Death Stranding 2.

cls.summary: Jolt Physics is a high-performance, multi-threaded C++ rigid-body physics and collision detection library used in commercial games and VR.
cls.what_it_does: Jolt simulates rigid bodies, constraints, collision detection and related features (vehicles, characters, soft bodies, hair, buoyancy) for real-time applications. It's used as a library integrated into games or simulators and is notable for its multicore-friendly design, determinism options and wide platform support including a WebAssembly port.
cls.trl_rationale: The project is mature and actively maintained (created 2021, recent pushes in 2026), has many stars and forks and is used in commercial games (Horizon Forbidden West, Death Stranding 2), indicating wide adoption and production use.
prerequisites: C++ development and build tool familiarity (CMake, compilers)
linear algebra and rigid-body dynamics concepts
multithreading fundamentals for integration and performance tuning
student_project_ideas: Integrate Jolt Physics into a simple C++ game or Unity/Unreal plugin to implement and compare vehicle dynamics and suspension models against theoretical models.
Build a hardware-in-the-loop robot arm collision simulator using Jolt for collision detection and ROS for robot control to test motion planners safely.

tools.name: autowarefoundation/autoware
tools.desc: Autoware - the world's leading open-source software project for autonomous driving

cls.summary: Autoware is an open-source, production-focused software stack for autonomous vehicles that implements perception, localization, planning and control components and runs on ROS/ROS2.
cls.what_it_does: Autoware provides a full autonomous driving software stack—from multi-sensor perception and localization to behavior planning and vehicle control—so researchers and companies can run autonomy software on simulated or real vehicles. It is used via source builds or Docker images and integrates with rosbag replay, simulation environments and vehicle interfaces. Notable features include multi-sensor fusion, NDT-based localization, behavior planning modules and an active foundation-backed ecosystem with extensive documentation.
cls.trl_rationale: The repository is mature (created 2015), has large community adoption (12k stars, many forks), detailed documentation and ecosystem repositories, and is described and used in production by industry partners; these indicate a well-established project beyond beta.
student_project_ideas: Integrate a low-cost LiDAR and camera on a differential-drive platform and use Autoware perception + planning modules to implement and evaluate obstacle avoidance in a lab environment using rosbag-recorded scenarios.
Use Autoware with a simulator (e.g., CARLA or AWSIM) to develop and compare two behavior planners (rule-based vs ML-based) and measure performance on intersection and lane-change scenarios.

tools.name: keplergl/kepler.gl
tools.desc: Kepler.gl is a powerful open source geospatial analysis tool for large-scale data sets.

cls.summary: kepler.gl is an open-source, high-performance web mapping and geospatial visualisation tool for exploring large-scale location datasets.
cls.what_it_does: Kepler.gl renders and interactively explores large geolocation datasets (millions of points, trip data, aggregated spatial layers) in the browser and as an embeddable React component. It is used to create configurable map layers, filters, camera tours and spatial aggregations on the fly and is notable for its performance (built on deck.gl and MapLibre/Mapbox) and easy embedding into React-Redux applications.
cls.trl_rationale: kepler.gl is a mature, actively maintained project created in 2018 with >12k stars, recent commits and documentation, and public demos; these indicators support a high maturity rating though it is not an industry-wide standard (hence TRL 8).
prerequisites: familiarity with MapLibre/Mapbox concepts (optional Mapbox token)
student_project_ideas: Build an interactive dashboard that ingests city GPS traces, creates trip layers and spatial aggregations in kepler.gl, and analyses peak movement patterns combined with a simple time-series analysis in Python.

Embed kepler.gl in a React app to visualise IoT sensor geolocated data (e.g. air quality nodes), implement custom layer styling and a camera tour that demonstrates a digital-twin style operational view.

tools.name: maplibre/maplibre-gl-js
tools.desc: MapLibre GL JS - Interactive vector tile maps in the browser

cls.summary: MapLibre GL JS is an open-source JavaScript library for rendering GPU-accelerated interactive vector-tile maps in web pages and webview apps.
cls.what_it_does: MapLibre GL JS displays interactive vector-tile basemaps and overlays using WebGL in browsers, enabling pan/zoom, styled layers and custom map interactions.
