It is used by including the library in a web app and pointing it at a tile/style source; notable features are GPU-accelerated rendering, a Mapbox GL JS-compatible API surface and broad community support following its fork from Mapbox GL JS.
cls.trl_rationale: The project is a mature, actively maintained fork of Mapbox GL JS with a large community (12k stars), long history since 2020 and recent activity; it shows broad adoption and stability consistent with a mature library.
student_project_ideas: Create a web-based digital twin demo by combining MapLibre GL JS with a time-series backend (InfluxDB/Timescale) to visualise live IoT sensor telemetry on a city map.

Develop an interactive infrastructure inspection tool that overlays GeoJSON asset data and annotated imagery on vector tiles and implements filtering, styling and export using MapLibre GL JS and a simple Express backend.

tools.name: Edge0-AI/Edge0
tools.desc: Device-native foundation models: 145B on a laptop, 35B on a phone. Latent MoE, SSD-streamed weights, a router that predicts loads a step ahead. Mac, iPhone, Android, Windows.

cls.summary: Edge0 is an open-source C++ inference framework for running large sparse (Mixture-of-Experts) foundation models on consumer and edge hardware (laptops, phones, desktops) using streaming/SSD weight loading and platform-specific backends.
cls.what_it_does: Edge0 provides a unified native inference engine and CLI (edge0-infer) that streams sparse MoE model weights from disk, selects among platform engines (GGML/Strata-derived backends) and exposes a local server and chat examples for macOS, iOS, Android, Linux and Windows. It solves running very large foundation models on constrained hardware by combining latent MoE, SSD-streamed weights, and platform-specific backends (CUDA/Metal/CPU) to reduce memory requirements and enable on-device or single-GPU inference.
cls.trl_rationale: The project shows substantial capability (platform builds, published models on Hugging Face, a unified inference CLI and recent large-model releases) and active development, but the repository is only 70 days old so by the project's age it is best classified as 'Alpha in use' (TRL 5) rather than a longer-proven production project.
prerequisites: Platform SDKs for target backends (CUDA for NVIDIA, Metal for Apple, Android NDK)
Large model weights (download from Hugging Face or model registry) and sufficient disk/GPU resources
student_project_ideas: Build a lab that measures latency, throughput and memory use for an Edge0 model across two backends (Metal on Apple Silicon and CUDA on Linux) and report trade-offs for an edge deployment.
Integrate Edge0 as an on-device inference backend for a robotic perception pipeline (ROS bridge) to evaluate real-time model-driven behaviour on a mobile robot.

tools.name: BigBodyCobain/Shadowbroker
tools.desc: Open-source intelligence for the global theater. Track everything from the corporate/private jets of the wealthy, and spy satellites, to seismic events in one unified interface. Hook an AI agent up to have it parse through data and find previously unseen correlations. The knowledge is available to all but rarely aggregated in the open, until now.

cls.summary: ShadowBroker is an open-source, real-time geospatial OSINT platform that aggregates dozens of live telemetry feeds (aircraft, ships, satellites, CCTV, seismic, sensors, etc.) into a single self-hosted map dashboard.
cls.what_it_does: ShadowBroker collects and visualises many public telemetry and OSINT feeds on an interactive map and provides server-side recon tools, searchable telemetry, and an agent command channel for automated analysis. It is deployed as a Next.js frontend with a FastAPI/Python backend and is notable for its many toggleable data layers, optional Shodan connector, and support for agent integration and self-hosted operation.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository is active, popular (many stars/forks) and recently updated, showing a working, documented beta-quality platform; however the project is younger than one year so TRL is capped at 6 despite strong community interest.
prerequisites: API keys for optional providers (Shodan, Sentinel, etc.)
student_project_ideas: Build a course lab where students ingest ADS‑B and AIS feeds into a local ShadowBroker deployment and design map overlays that detect anomalous vessel/aircraft behaviour.

Integrate Sentinel-2 imagery and SAR ground-change alerts from ShadowBroker into a damage-assessment workflow that correlates seismic/earthquake events with observed ground-change, producing automated reports.

tools.name: xinnan-tech/xiaozhi-esp32-server
tools.desc: 本项目为xiaozhi-esp32提供后端服务，帮助您快速搭建ESP32设备控制服务器。Backend service for xiaozhi-esp32, helps you quickly build an ESP32 device control server.

cls.summary: A backend server that provides MQTT/UDP, WebSocket, MCP and management console services to connect and control xiaozhi-esp32 devices and integrate ASR/LLM/VLLM components.
cls.what_it_does: This project implements a device-control backend for the xiaozhi-esp32 hardware platform, offering MQTT+UDP gateway, WebSocket/HTTP APIs, MCP protocol endpoints, voice/ASR/TTS pipeline hooks, user/device management and a web management console. It is used to deploy a local or Dockerised server that connects ESP32 devices, routes commands, and integrates LLM/VLLM/TTS/ASR services; notable points are broad protocol support (MQTT, UDP, WebSocket, MCP), plugin system and multiple deployment modes.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository is >1 year old, has a large star/fork count, active pushes and deployment documentation, and supports production-like deployment modes (Docker and full-stack). The README does include warnings about production security which suggests maturity but not certified industrial use, supporting a production-ready TRL 7 assessment.
prerequisites: Docker or Linux server for deployment
Node.js / Python runtimes (project uses JavaScript, Python and Vue components)
Optional: cloud API keys for external ASR/LLM/TTS providers if not using local models
student_project_ideas: Build an ESP32-based mechatronics demo where students implement device firmware that connects to the xiaozhi-esp32-server via MQTT and demonstrate remote control, OTA updates and telemetry visualization in the provided web console.

Integrate a local open-source ASR model (e.g. FunASR) with the server to create a voice-controlled robotic arm prototype, measuring latency and evaluating voice-identification (speaker recognition) under different network/deployment configurations.

tools.name: PointCloudLibrary/pcl
tools.desc: Point Cloud Library (PCL)

cls.summary: The Point Cloud Library (PCL) is a mature, open-source C++ library for processing 2D/3D point clouds and related algorithms used in perception, mapping and 3D data workflows.
cls.what_it_does: PCL provides algorithms and data structures for acquiring, filtering, registering, segmenting, reconstructing and visualising point cloud data (from LiDAR, stereo, RGB-D sensors, etc.). It is used as a C++ (and some Python bindings) toolkit integrated into perception and 3D processing pipelines and is notable for its breadth of algorithms and wide adoption in research and industry.
cls.trl_rationale: The project is long-lived (repo created 2013), has many stars, regular releases (1.15.1 shown), active CI across OSes, extensive documentation and community — evidence of a mature, widely adopted library.
prerequisites: dependencies such as Eigen, Boost and VTK
student_project_ideas: Use PCL to implement a LiDAR point cloud registration pipeline (ICP + pre-filtering) and evaluate its accuracy on KITTI or an open dataset, visualising results with PCL/VTK.
Build a 3D segmentation and object detection prototype that extracts obstacles from RGB-D scans and publishes results to a ROS node for a small mobile robot to use for navigation.

tools.name: YSGStudyHards/DotNetGuide
tools.desc: 🌈【C#/.NET/.NET Core学习、工作、面试指南】记录、收集和总结C#/.NET/.NET Core基础知识、学习路线、开发实战、编程技巧练习、学习视频、文章、书籍、项目框架、社区组织、开发必备工具、技术前沿周刊、常见面试题、面试须知、简历模板、人才招聘、以及自己在学习和工作中的一些微薄见解。希望能和大家一起学习，共同进步。如果本知识库能为您提供帮助，别忘了给予支持哦(关注、点赞、分享)💖。

cls.summary: A large, curated, and actively maintained one‑stop guide of learning resources, tutorials, tools and interview material for C# and the .NET ecosystem.
cls.what_it_does: DotNetGuide collects and organises links to tutorials, books, project templates, tooling, interview questions and community resources for C#/.NET developers. It is used as a reference and learning roadmap rather than runnable software, notable for its breadth, Chinese-language community orientation and high star count indicating wide awareness.
cls.trl_rationale: The repository is long‑lived (created 2020), actively maintained with many stars and forks and regularly updated; it is a mature, widely adopted community resource rather than experimental code.
student_project_ideas: Follow the guide to implement a small end‑to‑end .NET web application (ASP.NET Core + EF Core) and document the development choices using the guide's recommended resources.
Compare recommended testing and CI/CD workflows from the guide by creating two simple .NET projects and implementing different build/test/deploy pipelines (GitHub Actions vs Azure Pipelines).

tools.name: Orama-Interactive/Pixelorama
tools.desc: Unleash your creativity with Pixelorama, a powerful and accessible open-source pixel art multitool. Whether you want to create sprites, tiles, animations, or just express yourself in the language of pixel art, this software will realize your pixel-perfect dreams with a vast toolbox of features. Available on Windows, Linux, macOS and the Web!

cls.summary: Pixelorama is a free open-source pixel art editor for creating sprites, tiles and animations, available on desktop and the web.
cls.what_it_does: Pixelorama provides a toolkit for drawing and animating pixel art, including layers, timeline animation, tilemap support, palette management and export to spritesheets/GIF/video. It is used as a standalone application (desktop or web) or together with game engines to produce 2D art assets, and is notable for being implemented in Godot, extensible with community plugins, and distributed under an MIT license.
cls.trl_rationale: The project is mature and actively maintained since 2019 with many stars (11k+), regular releases and a wide user base and distribution channels (Steam, Itch, Flathub, GitHub Pages), indicating broad adoption and stability.
prerequisites: Godot 4.7.1 to run or build from source

tools.name: Calinou/awesome-godot
tools.desc: A curated list of free/libre plugins, scripts and add-ons for Godot

cls.summary: A long‑running, community‑curated index of free and open source games, plugins, add-ons and learning resources for the Godot game engine.
cls.what_it_does: This repository collects and organises links to Godot projects: games, demos, plugins, modules, tutorials and tools. Lecturers and students can use it to discover reusable code, learning material and community extensions for prototyping, visualisation and game-like simulations. What makes it notable is its longevity and large community curation rather than being a single software package.
cls.trl_rationale: The repository is mature and actively maintained since 2015 with many stars and recent pushes, indicating a stable, widely used curated resource rather than an experimental project; TRL reflects a production‑ready community resource rather than a single large software product.
prerequisites: ability to use GitHub and follow external project links
student_project_ideas: Select a small open source Godot project from the list and extend it to add an engineering data visualisation (e.g. sensor playback) to demonstrate real‑time UI and interaction.

Use a Godot plugin from the list to build a virtual prototype of a simple mechatronic system (robot arm or vehicle) and compare simulated control performance with a basic controller running on real hardware.

tools.name: CVHub520/X-AnyLabeling
tools.desc: X-AnyLabeling: A lightweight, efficient, and unified cross-platform desktop application for annotating text, image, video, point cloud and multimodal data, combining versatile built-in tools with state-of-the-art AI models and flexible multi-format export.

cls.summary: X-AnyLabeling is a cross-platform desktop application for AI-assisted annotation of images, video, text, point clouds and other multimodal data, supporting many label types and model integrations.
cls.what_it_does: It provides a unified GUI and toolset to create and edit annotations (boxes, polygons, masks, cuboids, rotated boxes, lines, points, etc.) across images, video and 3D point clouds, and can perform automated/batch labeling using integrated deep learning models. Notable features include wide model support (SAM, YOLO family, OCR and many vision foundation models), export/import to many dataset formats, and both local and remote inference via engines like ONNX Runtime, TensorRT and a separate server component.
cls.trl_rationale: The project is mature and widely used: the repository is over three years old, actively maintained with frequent releases and many stars/forks, extensive model integrations and a separate server component; this indicates a stable, well-adopted tool (TRL 8).
prerequisites: familiarity with dataset formats (COCO, VOC, YOLO, MOT, etc.)
GPU and model runtime knowledge for large-model inference (optional)
student_project_ideas: Create a multi-sensor dataset for an autonomous-perception assignment by annotating synchronized camera and LiDAR frames in X-AnyLabeling, then train and evaluate a detection/segmentation model using the exported COCO/point-cloud labels.

Extend X-AnyLabeling by integrating a custom remote inference model (via X-AnyLabeling-Server) to automate annotation for a domain-specific object class and measure annotation time saved versus manual labeling.

tools.name: Agents365-ai/drawio-skill
tools.desc: Agent skill that turns natural language, code, Terraform/K8s, SQL, OpenAPI, AsyncAPI, Protobuf and GraphQL sources into editable, tested draw.io architecture diagrams: incremental sync, multi-view projection, drift diff, CI architecture tests, whiteboard derasterize, interactive HTML/PPTX/Mermaid exports.

cls.summary: A tool that converts natural language and real system sources into editable draw.io architecture models, keeps them in sync, runs CI architecture tests and exports interactive viewers and slides.
cls.what_it_does: drawio-skill generates maintainable .drawio architecture diagrams from prompts, code, Terraform/Kubernetes/docker, OpenAPI/AsyncAPI/Protobuf/GraphQL and images, then synchronises changes incrementally while preserving manual layout. It provides diagram-as-test rules for CI, multi-view projection (C4/system/deployment/data-flow), visual diffs and export options (interactive HTML, PPTX, Mermaid), and can run as a CLI or via an MCP server to integrate with agents.
cls.trl_rationale: The repository is active, well-documented, widely starred and provides CLI, CI integrations and an MCP server, indicating a beta-level project; however it was created under one year ago (259 days), so despite strong interest it lacks the longer track record required for TRL 7+.
prerequisites: optional: Agent Skills-compatible MCP host or agent (e.g. Claude Code)
student_project_ideas: Build a CI pipeline that converts a microservice repository (OpenAPI + Kubernetes manifests) into a multi-page C4/.drawio model and enforces architecture rules using the skill's GitHub Action.

Capture a team whiteboard or legacy PNG of a system, convert it to editable .drawio with raster2drawio.py, then implement incremental sync to detect architectural drift against live Kubernetes/Terraform snapshots.

tools.name: openscad/openscad
tools.desc: OpenSCAD - The Programmers Solid 3D CAD Modeller

cls.summary: OpenSCAD is a mature, script-driven 3D CAD modeller for creating parametric solid geometry using constructive solid geometry (CSG) and 2D extrusion.
cls.what_it_does: OpenSCAD lets users define 3D parts by writing code: primitives, CSG operations and transformations produce models that can be exported as STL, OFF or DXF for printing or manufacturing. It is used as a non-interactive, repeatable modeller notable for parametric, reproducible designs and programmatic control rather than manual sketching.
cls.trl_rationale: Long-lived (created 2010), large user base (10k+ stars), multi-platform releases and extensive documentation indicate a mature, widely adopted project suitable for production workflows.
prerequisites: understanding of CSG and 3D coordinate transforms
C++/build toolchain to build from source (only for developers)
student_project_ideas: Create a parametric mounting bracket generator in OpenSCAD that takes device dimensions as inputs and exports STL for 3D printing; compare hand-modeled vs parametric variations.

Combine OpenSCAD with a simple Python script to auto-generate family-of-parts for a mechanism and run basic interference checks by exporting and loading the STLs into a collision-checking tool (e.g. Blender or a simple mesh library).

tools.name: playcanvas/supersplat
tools.desc: 3D Gaussian Splat Editor

cls.summary: SuperSplat Editor is a browser-based tool for inspecting, editing, optimising and publishing 3D Gaussian splat models derived from photogrammetry or point-cloud capture.
cls.what_it_does: SuperSplat lets users load 3D Gaussian splat datasets, visualise them in the browser using WebGL/WebGPU, edit scene and camera data, optimise splat representations and export results for publishing. It is notable for running entirely in-browser (no install), offering a hosted live editor and developer tools (WebMCP) for scene inspection and authoring.
cls.trl_rationale: The project is actively maintained with a live hosted editor, large GitHub popularity (10k+ stars), recent pushes and documentation/user guide, indicating widespread use and maturity beyond early release.
prerequisites: familiarity with WebGL/WebGPU concepts for advanced use
student_project_ideas: Create a pipeline that converts a photogrammetry-derived point cloud (e.g. from OpenMVG/OpenMVS) into a SuperSplat scene and measure visual quality vs. file size after different optimisation passes.
Implement and evaluate a streaming/level-of-detail system that reduces splat density for web delivery, comparing performance and visual fidelity in the SuperSplat Editor.

tools.name: ultralytics/yolov3
tools.desc: PyTorch implementation of YOLOv3, YOLOv3-SPP, and YOLOv3-tiny for real-time object detection with training, validation, inference, and multi-format export.

cls.summary: Ultralytics YOLOv3 is a mature PyTorch implementation of the YOLOv3 family for real‑time object detection, providing training, validation, inference and multi‑format export tools.
cls.what_it_does: This repository implements YOLOv3, YOLOv3‑SPP and YOLOv3‑tiny for detecting objects in images and video, with scripts for training on custom datasets, running inference on many input sources, validating models and exporting to formats like ONNX, TensorRT and CoreML. It is used by loading pretrained weights or training from scratch in PyTorch and is notable for supporting multiple export targets and real‑time inference use cases on edge and server hardware.
cls.trl_rationale: The repository is long‑lived (created 2018), has many stars and forks, active recent commits, documentation and export/production paths (ONNX, TensorRT, CoreML), indicating broad adoption and production usage rather than an experimental prototype.
prerequisites: basic machine learning and computer vision concepts
student_project_ideas: Build a perception pipeline for a small ground robot that uses YOLOv3 for object detection and ROS (or simple socket communication) to trigger avoidance behaviours, and evaluate detection latency on Jetson or a comparable edge device.

Train YOLOv3 on a custom labelled dataset for an engineering inspection task (e.g. crack or component presence detection), export the model to ONNX/TensorRT and compare inference speed and accuracy across CPU, GPU and an edge accelerator.

tools.name: MakazhanAlpamys/Soup
tools.desc: Fine-tune LLMs from one YAML. Layer streaming trains an 8B model on a 4 GB laptop GPU.

cls.summary: Soup is a command-line tool that automates fine-tuning and post-training of large language models (LLMs) from a single YAML config, including techniques to run large models on very small GPUs.
cls.what_it_does: Soup provides a unified CLI and YAML-driven workflow to prepare data, configure, and run LLM fine-tuning (SFT, DPO, QLoRA/LoRA, etc.) locally or on servers, with features like auto-tuning, quantization, and an experimental layer-streaming mode that reduces VRAM by streaming decoder layers. It is used via the `soup` CLI (installable as soup-cli) and integrates common libraries (transformers, PyTorch, PEFT) to make training reproducible and simpler.
cls.trl_rationale: The repository is active, has extensive docs, benchmarks, releases and many community contributors and stars, showing a mature beta/beta-to-production project; however it is only ~270 days old (<1 year) so by the TRL rules it should be capped at TRL 6.
prerequisites: familiarity with transformers and LoRA/QLoRA concepts
basic CLI and YAML config experience
student_project_ideas: Fine-tune a small open LLM on a course-specific dataset (e.g. engineering FAQs) using Soup and evaluate performance vs a baseline using Hugging Face Transformers + PEFT.

Reproduce and measure the layer-streaming memory/time trade-off: run identical fine-tuning jobs with and without Soup's stream_layers option on a constrained GPU and report VRAM, throughput and model correctness.

tools.name: Turfjs/turf
tools.desc: A modular geospatial engine written in JavaScript and TypeScript

cls.summary: Turf is a mature JavaScript/TypeScript library for performing spatial analysis and working with GeoJSON data in web or Node.js environments.
cls.what_it_does: Turf provides a large collection of spatial operations (buffer, intersect, simplify, clustering, classification, distance calculations, etc.), helpers to construct and manipulate GeoJSON, and statistics tools for geospatial datasets. It is used as a client-side or server-side library to add GIS analysis to web maps or to preprocess geospatial data in Node.js, notable for its modular API and broad set of ready-made spatial functions.
cls.trl_rationale: Turf is a long-running (since 2013), actively maintained project with many stars, frequent updates and broad adoption; this indicates a mature, widely used library appropriate for production use.
prerequisites: GeoJSON concepts and coordinate reference basics
student_project_ideas: Build a web map (Leaflet or Cesium) that calculates and visualises service areas and travel-distance isochrones for campus facilities using Turf spatial functions.
Create a Node.js pipeline that ingests sensor location data, uses Turf to cluster and summarise events into GeoJSON features, and exports results to a time-series database or dashboard.

tools.name: lipku/LiveTalking
tools.desc: Real time interactive streaming digital human

cls.summary: LiveTalking is an open-source real-time streaming digital-human framework that drives virtual avatars (talking heads / full-body) from text or audio and outputs via WebRTC/RTMP or a virtual camera.
cls.what_it_does: It takes text or speech (optionally routed through an LLM and TTS), extracts audio features and runs neural models (Wav2Lip, MuseTalk, er-nerf / Ultralight variants) to generate synchronized lip and facial motion and stream video in real time. It is used as a server with APIs and a web front-end and is notable for supporting multiple avatar models, voice cloning, interruptible speech, multi-concurrency and standard streaming outputs (WebRTC/RTMP/virtual camera).
cls.trl_rationale: The repository is multi-year, has a large community (10k+ stars, active pushes up to 2026) and explicit commercial usage / a paid commercial edition; the README documents deployments, Docker images and performance figures, indicating production-ready capabilities.
prerequisites: Python 3.12 and PyTorch (the README references exact versions)
Basic knowledge of WebRTC/RTMP and model deployment
student_project_ideas: Integrate LiveTalking with a simple knowledge-base chatbot (e.g. RAG over classroom materials) to build an AI teaching assistant that answers student questions with a synchronized digital avatar via WebRTC.
Measure and compare lip-sync quality and latency of two models (Wav2Lip vs MuseTalk) on different GPUs, and produce a report mapping GPU cost, latency and perceptual sync metrics.

tools.name: RunanywhereAI/runanywhere-sdks
tools.desc: Production ready toolkit to run AI locally

cls.summary: RunAnywhere is a multi-platform C++ core and SDK set for running LLMs, VLMs, speech and multimodal AI fully on-device across phones, browsers, desktops and servers.
cls.what_it_does: RunAnywhere provides a single semantic API and language bindings (Python, Swift, Kotlin, Flutter, Web) that discover and route work to the best local engine on a device, enabling on-device LLM inference, vision, speech, TTS, embeddings, RAG and image generation. It is used as an SDK embedded into apps or services to keep AI private and offline while leveraging device accelerators and multiple runtimes. Notable points are broad platform support, an engine capability registry, and production-oriented bindings and distribution (pip/Maven/Swift packages).
cls.trl_rationale: Repository is over one year old with many stars (10k+), active multi-language bindings, published packages (pip/Maven/Swift) and recent pushes, and documentation — indicating production-ready SDK maturity and real-world use; not a de-facto standard, so TRL 7 is appropriate.
student_project_ideas: Build a mobile app that performs offline RAG by ingesting course PDFs, using RunAnywhere for embeddings and local retrieval to answer student questions.
Integrate RunAnywhere into a robotics prototype to run on-device perception (VLM) and local LLM-based instruction parsing for a constrained voice-controlled robot.

tools.name: pmndrs/drei
tools.desc: 🥉 useful helpers for react-three-fiber

cls.summary: A popular collection of ready-made components and helpers for building WebGL/three.js scenes with react-three-fiber, aimed at simplifying common 3D tasks in React apps.
cls.what_it_does: Drei provides reusable React components (cameras, controls, lights, loaders, shapes, performance helpers, shaders and more) that wrap three.js functionality for use with @react-three/fiber, reducing boilerplate when building interactive 3D scenes on the web. It is used as an npm library imported into React projects and notable for its large catalogue of high-level abstractions and active documentation site.
cls.trl_rationale: The project is mature and widely adopted: created in 2020, actively maintained (recent push 2026-10-21), and has a large community (10k+ stars) and documentation site, indicating broad use and a stable API.
student_project_ideas: Build an interactive web-based digital twin viewer for a simple mechanical assembly using react-three-fiber and drei components (cameras, controls, loaders) to visualise parts and animate assembly sequences.

Create a performance comparison demo that loads a complex GLTF model and evaluates optimisations (instances, baked shadows, adaptive DPR) using drei helpers, measuring frame rate and interaction quality across browsers.

tools.name: egametang/ET
tools.desc: Unity3D Client And C# Server Framework

cls.summary: ET is a mature C# server framework with a Unity runtime bridge for building large-scale distributed MMO-style games and AI-assisted development workflows.
cls.what_it_does: ET provides a distributed actor-based server architecture, cloud-native deployment patterns, and a Unity runtime bridge to connect game clients to a scalable backend. It also includes tooling for hot reload, automated gameplay testing, multi-bot test harnesses and analyzers that enforce architecture and safety rules so AI-assisted code changes can be validated before production.
cls.trl_rationale: The repository is long-lived (created 2010), has many stars and forks, frequent recent activity, and a broad feature set (server, Unity bridge, testing/harness tools), indicating a mature, widely used framework rather than an experimental prototype.
prerequisites: Unity Editor and Unity project workflow
student_project_ideas: Create a small multiplayer lobby and matchmaking prototype using ET server components and Unity clients to demonstrate actor-based messaging and service discovery.

Implement an automated multi-bot gameplay test that exercises a simple game feature (e.g. party formation or combat) using ET's test harness and analyze results with the framework's logging/observability tools.

tools.name: cocos/cocos-engine
tools.desc: Cocos simplifies game creation and distribution with Cocos Creator, a free, open-source, cross-platform game engine. Empowering millions of developers to create high-performance, engaging 2D/3D games and instant web entertainment.

cls.summary: Cocos Engine is an open-source, cross-platform runtime game engine focused on high-performance 2D/3D rendering and extensible pipelines, used as the runtime for the Cocos Creator editor on native and web platforms.
cls.what_it_does: Cocos Engine provides the runtime and rendering infrastructure for building and running 2D and 3D interactive applications and games across desktop, mobile and web. It is used alongside the Cocos Creator editor and exposes a TypeScript user API while implementing low-level performance-critical systems in C++; notable features include a customizable render pipeline, PBR support and multi-API graphics backends (Vulkan/Metal/WebGL/WebGPU).
cls.trl_rationale: Repository created in 2015 and actively maintained (recent commits), with ~10k stars and many forks and example projects; demonstrates long track record and real-world use as the runtime for Cocos Creator, so mature and widely adopted in its domain.
student_project_ideas: Create a small interactive physics-based simulation (e.g. vehicle or robot arm) in Cocos Creator using the engine runtime and compare visualization/performance across WebGL and native builds.
Implement a custom render pass or surface shader in the engine's render pipeline to demonstrate PBR materials and measure frame-time impact on desktop and mobile targets.

tools.name: open-pencil/open-pencil
tools.desc: AI-native design editor. Open-source Figma alternative.

cls.summary: OpenPencil is an open-source, AI-enabled design editor and Figma-compatible toolkit that runs in the browser or as a Tauri desktop app and provides a programmable SDK and CLI.
cls.what_it_does: OpenPencil opens and edits .fig and .pen files, offers an AI chat assistant with tools to create and modify design nodes, supports real‑time collaboration, and provides a headless Vue SDK and CLI for embedding or automating editors. It is notable for built‑in AI tooling, Figma file compatibility, a programmable MCP/CLI surface, and both web and small desktop (Tauri) builds.
cls.trl_rationale: The project is active, has downloads/releases, an installable desktop app and a documented CLI/SDK, and a large star count indicating adoption; however the repository is ~8–9 months old (under 1 year), so by the provided TRL rules it should be capped at about TRL 6 (beta).
prerequisites: basic web tooling (Node/npm) for the CLI and SDK
optional: familiarity with Vue to use the headless SDK
student_project_ideas: Build a small product-design workflow that exports OpenPencil design tokens and generates React/Tailwind component stubs, demonstrating design-to-code automation.
Create a headless editor plugin using the OpenPencil Vue SDK to automate accessibility linting and token extraction for a set of design files, then produce a report pipeline (CLI + web).

tools.name: tidwall/tile38
tools.desc: Real-time Geospatial and Geofencing

cls.summary: Tile38 is an open-source, in-memory geolocation data store and realtime geofencing server that indexes GeoJSON, points, bounding boxes and more for fast spatial queries and live notifications.
cls.what_it_does: Tile38 provides a spatial index and geospatial database with commands for Nearby, Within and Intersects queries, realtime geofencing via webhooks or pub/sub, and support for multiple object types (point, bbox, GeoJSON, Geohash, XYZ tiles). It is used as a server you run (binaries, Docker) and accessed via Redis RESP, HTTP, websockets or the provided CLI, and is notable for being lightweight, embeddable, and offering realtime geofencing and Prometheus metrics out of the box.
cls.trl_rationale: Tile38 is a mature, long-lived project (created 2016), with many stars, release binaries, Docker images, client libraries, and production-oriented features (replication, Prometheus metrics), indicating real-world adoption and stability.
prerequisites: familiarity with Redis-style commands or HTTP APIs
basic geospatial concepts (lat/lon, GeoJSON, bounding boxes)
student_project_ideas: Build a realtime vehicle-tracking demonstration that stores GPS points in Tile38, triggers geofence alerts to a dashboard via pub/sub, and visualises vehicle positions on a web map (Leaflet or Mapbox).

Integrate IoT sensor data with Tile38 to detect when assets enter/leave site boundaries and export Prometheus metrics for analysis and alerting, then evaluate performance under load using the tile38-benchmark tool.

tools.name: QwenAudio/SenseVoice
tools.desc: Open-source SenseVoiceSmall model for Mandarin, Cantonese, English, Japanese, and Korean ASR, language ID, emotion recognition, and audio event detection.

cls.summary: SenseVoice is an open-source multilingual speech foundation model that performs ASR, language identification, emotion recognition and audio-event detection with an available small checkpoint and deployment scripts.
cls.what_it_does: SenseVoice provides a single speech model and inference pipeline that converts audio into transcriptions, detects spoken language, tags emotional state and classifies common audio events. It is used via Python/PyTorch code and integrates with the FunASR deployment pipeline and HuggingFace/ModelScope model hubs. Notable points are its multilingual support (Mandarin, Cantonese, English, Japanese, Korean for the released small checkpoint), low-latency non-autoregressive inference, and provided finetuning and deployment examples.
cls.trl_rationale: The repository is over two years old, has many stars and forks, released checkpoints on Hugging Face and ModelScope, online demos and a service/deployment pipeline; these indicate a mature, widely used implementation rather than an early prototype.
prerequisites: familiarity with FunASR (for diarization and deployment)
student_project_ideas: Build a voice-activated data-collection pipeline that uses SenseVoice to transcribe and tag emotion from field audio and feeds timestamps and labels into a time-series database for analytics.
Compare ASR accuracy and latency between SenseVoiceSmall and Whisper on a multilingual in-car voice-control dataset, and evaluate performance trade-offs for edge deployment (CPU vs GPU).

tools.name: xorbitsai/inference
tools.desc: Open-source inference platform for language, vision, embedding, reranking, image, audio, and video models. Deploy with multiple engines across heterogeneous hardware, from a laptop to a distributed cluster. Serve models through OpenAI-compatible APIs.

cls.summary: Xinference is an open-source distributed model inference platform that serves LLMs and multimodal models via OpenAI‑compatible APIs and a Web UI, running from a laptop to multi-node clusters.
cls.what_it_does: Xinference installs and serves 300+ built-in language, vision, embedding, audio and video models and lets you register custom models; it manages deployments, runtimes and heterogeneous hardware (CPU, GPU, Apple Metal, supported MLU) and exposes OpenAI‑compatible REST endpoints, a Python SDK, CLI and Web UI. It is notable for supporting multiple inference engines (vLLM, llama.cpp, Transformers, TRT‑LLM, SGLang, MLX), distributed/multi‑node deployments and hardware-specific runtime recommendations.
cls.trl_rationale: The project is multiple years old (created 2023-06), has active maintenance, extensive documentation, releases, large community interest (9.6k stars) and production‑focused features (Web UI, multi-node support), indicating production readiness rather than an early prototype.
prerequisites: familiarity with GPUs and model runtimes
student_project_ideas: Deploy a small LLM locally with Xinference and compare latency and throughput across two engines (e.g. vLLM vs llama.cpp) on CPU and GPU, reporting tradeoffs and runtime configuration effects.

Build a simple multimodal application (text + image) that uses Xinference as the backend API and integrates model outputs into a web dashboard to demonstrate an engineering data pipeline and monitoring.

tools.name: LearningCircuit/local-deep-research
tools.desc: ~95% on SimpleQA (e.g. Qwen3.6-27B on a 3090). Supports all local and cloud LLMs (llama.cpp, Ollama, Google, ...). 10+ search engines - arXiv, PubMed, your private documents. Everything Local & Encrypted.

cls.summary: Local Deep Research is an open‑source, locally‑run research assistant that performs retrieval‑augmented and agentic literature search across web, academic sources and private documents with encryption and support for many local or cloud LLMs.
cls.what_it_does: It automates deep literature and web research by searching multiple engines (arXiv, PubMed, Semantic Scholar, web, and private docs), downloading and indexing sources into an encrypted local knowledge base, and synthesising answers with citations using configurable agent strategies. It is used via a web UI or Docker/pip installs and is notable for strong local performance on constrained GPUs (examples cite Qwen3.6-27B on a 3090) and for supporting many local/cloud LLM backends and searchable engines.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository is >1 year old, widely starred (~9.5k stars), actively maintained with Docker and pip installation paths, detailed docs and real-world benchmark claims; these indicate production‑ready software used by a community rather than a fragile prototype.
prerequisites: SQLCipher (bundled wheels provided) and optional NVIDIA GPU for local large models
student_project_ideas: Build a reproducible literature review pipeline for a systems-engineering topic by configuring LDR to index a curated arXiv/PubMed query set and evaluate the quality of generated summaries against hand labels.

Integrate LDR with a private data corpus (project reports) and implement automated citation traceability: show provenance from synthesised claims back to indexed documents and visualise the citation graph.

tools.name: databendlabs/databend
tools.desc: Data Agent Ready Warehouse : One for  Analytics, Search, AI, Python Sandbox.  — rebuilt from scratch. Unified architecture on your S3.

cls.summary: Databend is an open-source, Rust-built cloud-native data warehouse that combines SQL analytics, vector and full-text search, and sandboxed Python UDFs on object storage.
cls.what_it_does: Databend provides a single warehouse for analytics, vector search and search-driven AI/agent workloads by running queries and sandboxed Python user-defined functions directly on tables stored on object storage (S3, Azure, GCS). It is used via SQL (and a cloud console or self-hosted Docker images) and is notable for combining vector search, full-text search and analytics in one system with branching (data versioning) and an execution architecture that supports agent sandboxes.
cls.trl_rationale: The project is mature and actively maintained (repository created 2020, large community with ~9.5k stars, regular pushes and published benchmarks and a cloud offering), and it is used in production/Cloud; this indicates broad adoption and stable APIs consistent with TRL 8.
prerequisites: familiarity with Docker or Linux for self-hosting
student_project_ideas: Build a small retrieval-augmented search and analytics pipeline: ingest sensor or document data into Databend, create vector embeddings (using Python UDFs or external embedding service), and implement a simple RAG query interface that ranks documents and runs SQL analytics on results.

Evaluate performance trade-offs for time-series and vector queries by benchmarking data ingestion and query latency on local object storage vs. cloud object storage (S3/GCS) using provided TPC-like datasets and the project's benchmark queries.

tools.name: crynta/terax-ai
tools.desc: Lightweight (7MB) terminal-first AI-native development environment

cls.summary: Terax is a lightweight, terminal-first AI-native development workspace that combines a GPU-accelerated terminal, a code editor, source-control UI and an agent side-panel for local or cloud LLMs.
cls.what_it_does: Terax provides a desktop development environment focused on terminal workflows and integrated AI agents: a native PTY-backed terminal with a WebGL/WebGPU renderer, a CodeMirror-based editor with inline AI-assisted edits and a side-panel for agent orchestration. It is used as a local app (Tauri) for coding, previewing local dev servers, interacting with models (cloud or local) and automating editing and shell tasks.
cls.trl_rationale: The project is actively developed, has official installers/releases and thousands of stars indicating real-user interest, but the repository is only ~210 days old (under one year), so demonstrated production maturity is limited to a beta-level (TRL 6).
prerequisites: basic Node.js and Rust toolchain for building from source (optional)
student_project_ideas: Create an automated coding-agent pipeline that uses a local LLM (Ollama or LM Studio) in Terax to generate, run and test small programs, then report results via the terminal and git commits.

Integrate a simple CI-like workflow: use Terax to host a development workspace that auto-runs tests in a preview pane and uses an agent to suggest and apply fixes, demonstrating human-in-the-loop verification.

tools.name: ai-collection/ai-collection
tools.desc: The Generative AI Landscape - A Collection of Awesome Generative AI Applications

cls.summary: A large, curated 'awesome' list of generative AI applications and projects across many categories.
cls.what_it_does: This repository collects and organises links to generative AI applications, tools and demos (text, image, audio, video, agents and more) as a curated reference for discovery. It is used as a directory to find existing projects rather than as a runnable engineering tool, notable for its broad coverage and high community visibility.
cls.trl_rationale: The repository is long-lived (created 2023-01-03), actively maintained and widely starred, which shows community adoption as a reference resource rather than a software product; it functions as a mature curated directory rather than production engineering software.

tools.name: XINCGer/Unity3DTraining
tools.desc: 【Unity杂货铺】unity大杂烩~

cls.summary: A long-standing collection of Unity example projects, patterns and third‑party plugin samples for learning Unity game development and engine features.
cls.what_it_does: This repository collects many small Unity projects, demos and code samples (UI, pathfinding, physics experiments, editor extensions, performance tips, mobile push, hot update, ECS, etc.) to teach and demonstrate Unity techniques. It is used by browsing example folders or importing individual sample scenes into the Unity editor and running or adapting them. Its notable feature is breadth — a large curated catalogue of practical Unity snippets and community links rather than a single packaged library.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository created in 2016, actively maintained with many stars and forks and a wide set of example projects; demonstrates long-term community interest and practical use (stable examples rather than a research prototype), consistent with a mature, widely adopted learning resource.
prerequisites: Basic game development concepts (scenes, prefabs, components)
student_project_ideas: Build a simple robot simulation in Unity using the Pathfinding and PhysicsStudy examples, then instrument and visualise sensor data in the scene for a mechatronics lab.
Use the UGUI and PerformanceOptimization samples to create a mobile prototype with pooling and assetbundle hot‑update support, then measure and optimise frame time on a target device.

tools.name: BepInEx/BepInEx
tools.desc: Unity / XNA game patcher and plugin framework

cls.summary: BepInEx is an open-source plugin and modding framework that injects code into Unity, XNA and .NET games to enable mods and runtime patching.
cls.what_it_does: BepInEx patches game runtimes (Unity Mono, Unity IL2CPP, XNA/.NET) to load and manage plugins that extend or modify game behaviour at runtime. It is used by dropping the framework into a game's folder and installing plugins; notable points are broad compatibility with Mono and IL2CPP Unity builds and an ecosystem of loader plugins and interop libraries.
cls.trl_rationale: The project is mature and well-adopted (created 2018, ~9k stars, active commits and releases, ecosystem of loaders and interop libraries), indicating widespread use; this supports a TRL of 8 rather than experimental levels.
prerequisites: familiarity with Unity game builds (Mono / IL2CPP)
basic knowledge of runtime injection/modding concepts
student_project_ideas: Create a BepInEx plugin that instruments a Unity game's frame timing and sends performance metrics to a local dashboard (combine with a simple time-series DB or Grafana).
Develop a mod that extends a Unity game's UI to visualise internal state (game object positions, physics parameters) and export the data for offline analysis.

tools.name: MrNeRF/awesome-3D-gaussian-splatting
tools.desc: Curated list of papers and resources focused on 3D Gaussian Splatting, intended to keep pace with the anticipated surge of research in the coming months.

cls.summary: A curated, regularly updated index of papers, implementations, viewers and tools for 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) and related neural rendering technologies.
cls.what_it_does: This repository collects papers, reference implementations, tutorials, datasets and viewer/plugins related to 3D Gaussian Splatting so researchers and practitioners can find implementations and learning resources in one place. It is used as a pointer/index rather than a runnable library, notable for comprehensive coverage and links to community and official implementations, viewers and engine plugins.
cls.trl_rationale: The repository is a curated index with many community and official implementations linked, high star count and active updates over multiple years, indicating community adoption; it is not itself a single production library but connects to several projects that range from research demos to production-ready tools.
prerequisites: basic familiarity with neural rendering / NeRF concepts
student_project_ideas: Reproduce a 3D scene reconstruction using one of the linked PyTorch/CUDA implementations and compare render quality and training time against a NeRF baseline.
Integrate an exported Gaussian Splatting scene into Unity or Godot using a listed plugin and build an interactive viewer to evaluate real-time rendering performance on desktop and mobile.

tools.name: AssetRipper/AssetRipper
tools.desc: GUI application to analyze game files

cls.summary: AssetRipper is a GUI tool that inspects and extracts assets from Unity game files to help users recover, convert and analyse embedded game content.
cls.what_it_does: AssetRipper opens Unity game files to list, extract and convert included assets (textures, models, code metadata and other resources) and helps identify missing or redundant dependencies. It is used as a desktop GUI application for reverse‑engineering or recovering game assets and supports a very wide range of Unity engine versions; a paid ‘Premium’ edition offers extra features.
cls.trl_rationale: The project is several years old, widely used (high star count ~8.9k), actively maintained with recent pushes and a public downloads page plus a paid premium edition; this indicates maturity and broad adoption rather than a one‑off prototype.
prerequisites: familiarity with Unity asset types and game project structure
student_project_ideas: Use AssetRipper to analyse a student-built Unity game to produce a report on included asset dependencies and propose a reduced build by removing unused assets.
Create a pipeline that extracts models and textures with AssetRipper and imports them back into a Unity project to evaluate how third‑party assets affect build size and load time.

tools.name: gamedev-skills/awesome-gamedev-agent-skills
tools.desc: Make games with your AI coding agent: 79 game-dev skills and a router for Godot, Unity, Unreal, Roblox, three.js, Phaser and 6 more engines. Checked on the real engines.

cls.summary: A curated collection of 79 AI agent 'skills' plus a router that lets coding agents generate game engine code for many engines (Godot, Unity, Unreal, three.js, Phaser, Roblox, etc.).
cls.what_it_does: This repository provides small, engine-specific capability files (skills) and a router that detects the target game engine and task, then loads the appropriate skills so an AI coding agent writes or edits game code in the user's chosen engine. It is notable because it covers 12 engines, reports tests against real engine toolchains, and advertises high compatibility with many agent runtimes (Claude Code, Cursor, Copilot, Gemini CLI and others).
cls.trl_rationale: Repository is 146 days old (<1 year) so by the stated TRL rules it cannot be >6 unless enterprise usage is shown; README shows extensive testing on real engines, pinned engine versions, and large community interest (≈8.9k stars) indicating beta-level maturity (versioned installs, CLI integration, compatibility matrix and eval results).
prerequisites: Node.js (for the skills CLI) and familiarity with the target game engine
student_project_ideas: Use the router + Godot skill bundle to implement a gameplay feature (e.g. double jump or inventory) and compare the agent-generated code to a human-written reference, reporting issues and required edits.

Extend the skill catalog with a new engine or genre skill (e.g. physics-based puzzle) and measure router selection accuracy on a set of prompts; integrate with automated test builds for the target engine.

tools.name: 0xFA11/MultiplayerNetworkingResources
tools.desc: A curated list of Multiplayer Game Network Programming Resources

cls.summary: A long-running, high-quality curated list of articles, blog posts and links about multiplayer game networking (netcode), focusing on latency, prediction, reconciliation and related techniques.
cls.what_it_does: This repository collects and organises links to articles, tutorials and resources for multiplayer game network programming so developers and students can learn about netcode approaches such as client-server, rollback, prediction and interpolation. It is used as a learning and reference hub rather than executable software, notable for its wide coverage and sustained community interest (many stars and frequent updates).
cls.trl_rationale: The repository is long-lived (created 2018), actively maintained and widely used (many stars), indicating a mature, stable resource; it is a curated link collection rather than runnable software, so maturity corresponds to documentation and community value rather than release artefacts.
student_project_ideas: Implement a simple client-server multiplayer prototype in Unity or Godot and compare latency mitigation strategies (interpolation, prediction, lag compensation) using links from the repository as guidance.
Build a small C++ prototype demonstrating rollback vs delay-based netcode for a deterministic 2D game and measure perceived latency and correctness under simulated packet loss and jitter.

tools.name: isaac-sim/IsaacLab
tools.desc: Unified framework for robot learning with multi-physics/renderer support

cls.summary: Isaac Lab is an open-source, GPU-accelerated framework for robot learning and simulation that provides physics backends, sensor simulation, and ready-to-train environments for reinforcement and imitation learning.
cls.what_it_does: Isaac Lab bundles simulation environments, robot models, sensor plugins and training workflows to accelerate research in robot learning (RL, imitation learning, multi-agent). It runs with multiple physics/rendering backends (including NVIDIA Isaac Sim / Omniverse Kit) and connects to common RL libraries so users can train and evaluate policies with realistic sensors and GPU acceleration. The project is notable for its large community, extensive documentation and production-grade examples for sim-to-real workflows.
cls.trl_rationale: The repository is mature (created 2022, >8600 stars, active pushes in 2026), has detailed docs, a published arXiv paper and wide community use; these indicate production-grade, widely adopted software though not an industry-wide standard like ROS 2.
prerequisites: NVIDIA GPU (CUDA) and compatible driver stack
Familiarity with Isaac Sim / Omniverse concepts and RL frameworks
student_project_ideas: Train a quadruped locomotion policy in Isaac Lab using Stable Baselines or RLlib and evaluate sim-to-sim transfer to a lightweight PyBullet model to study domain transfer strategies.

Create a perception-to-control pipeline by simulating RGB-D and LIDAR sensors in Isaac Lab, training a depth-based obstacle avoidance policy, and validating performance with recorded real sensor data for sim-to-real analysis.

tools.name: opengeos/GeoLibre
tools.desc: A lightweight, cloud-native GIS platform for visualizing, exploring, and analyzing geospatial data. It runs in the web browser, on the desktop, on mobile, and inside Jupyter notebooks.

cls.summary: GeoLibre is an open-source, cloud-native GIS platform that runs in browsers, desktop, mobile and Jupyter, providing 1,000+ in-browser geoprocessing tools and multiple rendering engines for visualising and analysing geospatial data while keeping data local.
cls.what_it_does: GeoLibre lets users visualise, explore and analyse raster and vector geospatial data in a web or native app without a server by running geoprocessing tools in WebAssembly; it supports cloud-native formats (COG, GeoParquet, PMTiles, FlatGeobuf, STAC) and multiple renderers (MapLibre, Mapbox, Cesium, ArcGIS). It is notable for shipping 1,000+ browser-side geoprocessing tools, DuckDB-WASM spatial integration, and being usable inside Jupyter and R environments.
cls.trl_rationale: The project shows strong evidence of production use (hosted web app, desktop/mobile store listings, Python and R packages, many stars and active pushes), but the repository is only ~173 days old so under the policy it should be capped at TRL 6 despite apparent real-world deployments.
prerequisites: familiarity with web-mapping (MapLibre/Leaflet/Cesium) for advanced use
Node.js/npm to run from source; Rust for desktop builds (optional)
student_project_ideas: Build an interactive flood-risk dashboard that loads COG terrain and LandSat data into GeoLibre, computes flood extents with the browser-side hydrology tools, and publishes the project file for reproducible analysis.

Integrate GeoLibre in a Jupyter lab workflow to demonstrate a data-to-visualisation pipeline: ingest GeoParquet vector data, run spatial queries using DuckDB-WASM, and produce synchronized 2D/3D visualisations (MapLibre + Cesium) for an urban analysis case study.

tools.name: qualcomm/GenieX
tools.desc: Run frontier LLMs and VLMs locally on Qualcomm devices across NPU, GPU, and CPU with a few lines of code

cls.summary: GenieX is an on-device inference runtime for running large language and vision models locally on Qualcomm Snapdragon devices using NPU, GPU or CPU.
cls.what_it_does: GenieX loads GGUF models or Qualcomm pre-compiled bundles and runs them on Hexagon NPU, Adreno GPU or CPU with CLI, Python, Android and C SDK interfaces. It is notable for providing an OpenAI-compatible local server, multi-language bindings, and optimized paths for Qualcomm hardware so models can run on-device without cloud APIs.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository is over two years old, has many stars/forks, active recent commits, documented installers, multi-language SDKs and device-specific guides; these indicate production-ready software maintained by Qualcomm and a community rather than an experimental prototype.
prerequisites: familiarity with Linux or Android build/deployment
access to Qualcomm Snapdragon hardware for NPU/GPU acceleration
student_project_ideas: Deploy a small GGUF language model to a Snapdragon dev board using GenieX and measure latency, throughput and power consumption across CPU, GPU and NPU paths.
Build an Android app that performs on-device visual-language inference (image + text) using GenieX to prototype an edge inspection/demo system for a simple fault-detection task.

tools.name: HeyPuter/everything
tools.desc: We're rebuilding and open-sourcing the world’s software from scratch.

cls.summary: A very large mono-repository that aims to re-create open-source alternatives to many proprietary desktop and web applications, including CAD, parametric modelling, circuits and building design tools.
cls.what_it_does: Everything is a single mono-repo project that develops open-source replacements for a broad set of commercial applications (office, creative, collaboration and engineering tools). It is used by cloning the repo, installing Node.js and running individual app folders; what makes it notable is its ambition to reimplement many categories (including CAD, parametric modelling, circuits and building design) in one coordinated project.
cls.trl_rationale: The repository is very new (created 34 days ago) and is a large mono-repo with many app placeholders; README shows intent and runnable demos per-app via Node.js but no evidence of long-term real-world use or stable releases, so maturity is early-alpha.
student_project_ideas: Fork and extend the repository's CAD app to add a simple IFC/STEP exporter and benchmark interoperability with a standard CAD viewer.
Integrate the Circuits app with an ESP32 firmware build pipeline to create a full hardware-in-the-loop demo that simulates a simple sensor circuit and displays results in the web UI.

tools.name: carson-katri/dream-textures
tools.desc: Stable Diffusion built-in to Blender

cls.summary: Dream Textures is a Blender add-on that generates and projects AI-created textures and images into Blender scenes using Stable Diffusion models.
cls.what_it_does: The add-on lets users create textures, concept art and background assets from text prompts, produce seamless tiling textures, inpaint/outpaint existing images, project generated images across 3D scene depth, and re-style animations using Blender's Cycles passes. It runs models locally (CUDA or Apple Silicon) or can use cloud processing, and exposes a node-based render engine and history tools inside Blender.
cls.trl_rationale: The project is mature and widely used: created in 2022, actively maintained with recent pushes, many releases, a large star count and community (Discord, issues), and documented installation and usage guides—evidence of broad adoption rather than just an experimental prototype.
prerequisites: Familiarity with Stable Diffusion concepts (prompts, inpainting)
GPU with CUDA or Apple Silicon recommended; PyTorch dependencies
student_project_ideas: Integrate Dream Textures into a Blender scene to create procedural, seamless materials for a small product-design prototype and evaluate visual quality and tiling performance compared with hand-made textures.

Build a pipeline that uses Dream Textures to generate environment textures for a digital-twin visualisation, then measure render-time and perceived realism when used with Cycles and real scene depth maps.

cls.summary: A collection of Unity DOTS (Data-Oriented Tech Stack) sample projects demonstrating ECS, the C# Job System, Burst, physics and netcode for high-performance, multicore real-time simulations.
cls.what_it_does: This repository provides runnable sample projects and tutorials that show how to build high-performance entity-component-system (ECS) applications in Unity using the Jobs System, Burst compiler, Physics and Netcode packages. It is used as a learning and reference resource to compare traditional Unity approaches with DOTS patterns and to prototype scalable simulations and multiplayer demos.
cls.trl_rationale: The repo is maintained by Unity Technologies, created in 2018 and actively updated (last push 2026), has many stars and contains extensive documented samples tied to official Unity packages, indicating a mature, widely adopted teaching and reference resource.
prerequisites: C# programming and familiarity with Unity concepts
Basic knowledge of ECS/Jobs concepts is helpful
student_project_ideas: Compare performance and memory use between a MonoBehaviour-based prototype and an ECS DOTS implementation using the included samples and the Burst compiler.
Extend the Netcode sample into a small distributed simulation (multiple clients + server) to study networked state synchronization and latency effects on deterministic physics.

tools.name: PixiEditor/PixiEditor
tools.desc: PixiEditor is a Universal Editor for all your 2D needs

cls.summary: PixiEditor is an open-source, cross-platform 2D image and sprite editor with raster, vector and node-based workflows for painting and animation.
cls.what_it_does: PixiEditor provides tools for pixel art, painting and vector drawing in a single canvas, plus a node-based render system and a timeline for animations. It is used to create and export images, sprite sheets and animations (png, jpg, svg, gif, mp4) and is notable for combining raster and vector toolsets with a node graph for procedural effects.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository is mature (created 2018) with many stars (8k+), active development (recent pushes) and a full-featured README and build instructions, indicating wide adoption and stable use.
student_project_ideas: Create a complete sprite sheet and frame-by-frame animation for a simple game, then import it into a student game project (Unity/Godot) to demonstrate asset pipelines.
Extend the node-based render system with a custom procedural shader node (C#) and demonstrate procedural texture generation for use in a game or simulation.

tools.name: Osmantic/ODS
tools.desc: ODS V3 Pre-Release: Public testing and refinement ahead of the official V3 launch. Turn your PC, Mac, or Linux box into a private AI server.

cls.summary: ODS is an open-source installer and runtime that turns a PC, Mac or Linux machine into a self-hosted AI server for local model inference, chat UIs, agents, workflows and related services.
cls.what_it_does: ODS automates installation, orchestration and management of a local AI stack (models, web UI, workflow/agent services, RAG/search, voice and image generation) so users can run LLMs and agent workflows without cloud dependence. It is used via provided installers and a control dashboard/CLI that bring up Docker containers, select models for available hardware and expose a browser-based Portal for interaction. Notable aspects are the all-in-one installer approach, emphasis on privacy/offline operation, and integration with common tools like ComfyUI, Open WebUI and n8n.
cls.trl_rationale: The project is feature-rich with installers, a dashboard, CI and many stars indicating active interest, but the repository is a V3 pre-release and is under 1 year old so it fits a beta-level maturity rather than long-term production provenance.
prerequisites: Docker (or Docker Desktop / WSL2 on Windows)
basic Linux command-line and shell (bash or PowerShell)
40+ GB disk and optionally a compatible GPU/driver for local inference
student_project_ideas: Create a course lab where students install ODS on a VM and build a RAG pipeline that searches a repository of design documents to answer requirements questions via a local LLM.
Integrate ODS-hosted agents with a simulated IoT sensor feed to implement and evaluate automated maintenance alert workflows and document privacy/security implications.

tools.name: visuallyjs/visuallyjs
tools.desc: VisuallyJs releases and issue tracking

cls.summary: VisuallyJs is a commercial, web-first library for building interactive node-based diagrams, BPMN editors and linked real-time dashboards that integrates with React, Angular, Vue and Svelte.
cls.what_it_does: VisuallyJs provides components and a unified data model for creating interactive diagrams (flowcharts, BPMN, custom shapes) and charts that stay in sync with node/edge interactions. It is used as a front-end library (SVG/HTML-based) and notable for first-class framework integrations and built-in layouts and chart types that let diagrams drive live visualisations.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository is long-lived (created 2011), has many stars/forks and recent activity, and provides production-grade framework integrations and documentation; these indicate a mature, widely adopted library though it is commercial and not an industry standard on the level of e.g. Draw.io.
student_project_ideas: Build a systems-architecture viewer where selecting a component in a BPMN/flow diagram updates performance charts (use VisuallyJs for diagrams and D3 or chartjs for advanced charts).
Create an interactive digital-twin dashboard for a small manufacturing process: model machines as nodes, simulate simple sensor data and visualise real-time KPIs linked to node interactions.

tools.name: mob-sakai/UIEffect
tools.desc: UIEffect is an open-source package that allows you to intuitively apply rich UI effects directly from the Inspector or via code. Combine various filters, such as grayscale, blur, and dissolve, to decorate your UI with a unique visual style!

cls.summary: UIEffect is an open-source Unity package that provides inspector-driven visual effects (blur, grayscale, dissolve, etc.) for Unity UI elements and supports URP/HDRP, TextMeshPro and runtime presets.
cls.what_it_does: UIEffect lets developers and designers apply and combine a variety of shaders/filters to Unity UI elements directly from the Inspector or via code, with runtime/editor presets and tweening support. It is distributed as a Unity package (OpenUPM/UPM) and integrates with TextMeshPro, ShaderGraph and optional SoftMaskForUGUI, making it easy to enhance UI visuals and animate effect transitions.
cls.trl_rationale: The repository is long-lived (created 2017), has many stars and forks, active recent commits and releases, cross-render-pipeline support and documentation, indicating broad adoption and maturity beyond early production.
prerequisites: basic familiarity with Unity UI and Unity Editor
student_project_ideas: Create a Unity-based interactive HMI prototype that uses UIEffect to highlight alarm states and animate transitions, combined with a simple state machine or ROS/ROS2 bridge to simulate live data.

Build a small game UI polish project where students design multiple preset themes (retro, dystopia, clean) using UIEffect and ShaderGraph, and implement runtime switching with Timeline and AnimationClips.

tools.name: veloren/veloren
tools.desc: [mirror of https://gitlab.com/veloren/veloren] An open world, open source voxel RPG inspired by Dwarf Fortress and Cube World. This repository is a mirror. Please submit all PRs and issues on our GitLab page.

cls.summary: Veloren is an open-source, multiplayer voxel action‑RPG written in Rust with procedural terrain and cross‑platform builds for Windows, macOS and Linux.
cls.what_it_does: Veloren provides a complete open world voxel RPG game: engine, assets, networking and tools to run multiplayer servers and play locally. It is used by contributors and players to build, extend and host the game (modding, art, server administration) and is notable for being a mature, community-driven Rust game with procedural generation and a multiplayer stack.
cls.trl_rationale: The repository is long-lived (created 2018) with a large community (thousands of stars, active pushes and multi-platform builds), public servers and contributors, indicating a mature, widely used open-source project rather than an experimental prototype.
prerequisites: basic game development and graphics concepts
student_project_ideas: Extend Veloren's procedural terrain generator to add a new biome type and measure its performance impact on world generation (combine with profiling tools).
Implement or benchmark a new network optimisation for multiplayer state updates and compare bandwidth/latency against the existing implementation using a small test server.

tools.name: microsoft/TinyTroupe
tools.desc: LLM-powered multiagent persona simulation for imagination enhancement and business insights.

cls.summary: TinyTroupe is a Python library that simulates many human-like agents (personas) using LLMs to generate interactions for research, product feedback, synthetic data and offline testing.
cls.what_it_does: TinyTroupe creates configurable simulated agents (TinyPerson) that live in simulated TinyWorlds and interact via LLMs to produce realistic conversations and behaviours. It is used from Python/Jupyter notebooks to run scenarios, generate synthetic user responses, run focus-group style simulations and evaluate content or systems under simulated audiences. What makes it notable is its emphasis on highly customisable personas, experimental features (vision modality, empirical validators) and built-in utilities for LLM cost tracking and validation.
cls.trl_rationale: The project is an active, well-starred research library with multiple releases (0.5.x–0.7.0), example notebooks, a linked preprint, and ongoing development, indicating beta maturity; it is not yet a production standard and README warns the API is still evolving.
prerequisites: access to an LLM provider (e.g., OpenAI API) or a local runtime (Ollama)
student_project_ideas: Build a simulated focus group using TinyTroupe to evaluate different UI copy for a campus service and compare the simulated feedback to a small real-user survey.
Use TinyTroupe to generate synthetic conversational test cases for a chatbot, then measure how those cases exercise intent classification compared with existing test suites.

tools.name: agmmnn/awesome-blender
tools.desc: 🪐 A curated list of awesome Blender add-ons, extensions, AI/MCP tools, tutorials, and 3D resources.

cls.summary: A long-standing, community-curated list of Blender add-ons, tools, tutorials and 3D resources focused on open-source and free material.
cls.what_it_does: This repository gathers and organises links to Blender add-ons, standalone 3D tools, tutorials and other resources so users can discover relevant plugins and learning material. It is used as a reference index rather than runnable software and is notable for its breadth, curation and popularity in the Blender community.
cls.trl_rationale: The repository is mature (created 2020), actively maintained with many stars and recent activity, and serves as a stable community reference rather than experimental code; however it is a curated list, not an application, so TRL reflects resource maturity rather than production software.
student_project_ideas: Survey and compare three open-source Blender add-ons from the list to evaluate their suitability for automating a particular modelling or visualization task, reporting on installation, workflow and limitations.
Build a small pipeline that uses a listed Blender add-on (e.g. for photogrammetry or point-cloud import) to convert real-world scan data into a simplified model and document the reproducible steps.

tools.name: google/draco
tools.desc: Draco is a library for compressing and decompressing 3D geometric meshes and point clouds. It is intended to improve the storage and transmission of 3D graphics.

cls.summary: Draco is an open-source library for compressing and decompressing 3D meshes and point clouds to reduce storage and transmission costs for 3D graphics and geospatial datasets.
cls.what_it_does: Draco implements compact on-disk and on-wire encodings for polygonal meshes and point clouds, and provides C++, JavaScript and WASM decoders/encoders. It is commonly used to shrink 3D assets for real-time web visualization (glTF/three.js) and for storing/transferring large scan or model datasets efficiently.
cls.trl_rationale: The project is long-lived (created 2016), actively maintained by Google, has many stars/forks, stable releases, WASM/JS decoders and explicit glTF integration (draco_transcoder), and is widely used in production pipelines, supporting a high TRL.
student_project_ideas: Build a web viewer that loads glTF models with and without Draco compression (using the WASM/JS decoder) and measure load time, bandwidth and visual fidelity trade-offs for scanned assets.

Integrate Draco compression into a LiDAR scan pipeline: ingest PLY point clouds, compress with Draco, and implement a server-side decompression + streaming demo showing reduced storage and faster streaming to a simple visualization front-end.

tools.name: drumih/turbo-fieldfare
tools.desc: Gemma 4 26B-A4B inference in ~2 GB of RAM on any M-series MacBook

cls.summary: TurboFieldfare is a Swift + Metal runtime that runs Gemma 4 26B-A4B on Apple Silicon Macs by streaming model expert weights from disk to keep RAM usage near 2 GB.
cls.what_it_does: TurboFieldfare enables on-device inference of the Gemma 4 26B-A4B instruction-tuned LLM on Apple Silicon by keeping a small shared core and KV cache resident and streaming expert weights from SSD as needed. It provides a native macOS app, CLI, and an experimental OpenAI-compatible local server, and is notable for custom Metal kernels and an installer/repacking pipeline that make large-model inference possible on 8 GB Macs.
cls.trl_rationale: The repo is young (<1 year) so higher TRL is limited, but the README documents a working native macOS app, CLI, a server, measured benchmarks and community results; the project is actively maintained and widely starred, consistent with a beta-stage (TRL 6) runtime.
prerequisites: Swift 6.2+ toolchain and Xcode/Command Line Tools
~15 GB free disk for the model
student_project_ideas: Build an offline macOS chatbot using TurboFieldfare's loopback OpenAI-compatible server and evaluate latency/throughput and token-cost trade-offs on M1 vs M2 hardware.
Extend the TurboFieldfare CLI to add a simple tool-execution layer (authorize/execute model-suggested function calls) and test safety/validation workflows for local models.

tools.name: htdt/godogen
tools.desc: Autonomous game development with Claude Code and Codex

cls.summary: Godogen is an open-source autonomous game-generation system that uses agent models (Claude Code or Codex) to scaffold, generate assets for, build and run small games in Godot, Bevy, Babylon.js or three.js.
cls.what_it_does: Godogen accepts a short game description and an engine choice, then the agent scaffolds a fresh game repository, generates art/3D/sound assets, compiles or runs the engine, and produces a live preview or a short proof video. It is notable for integrating multiple game engines and an asset-generation skillset so the agent can iterate on visible proof (a running game or recording) rather than only on compile-time checks.
cls.trl_rationale: The repo is active, well-documented, demonstrates end-to-end demos and has many stars indicating real interest, but it is under one year old (created 2026-02-06) so it lacks the multi-year production track record required for TRL 7+.
prerequisites: familiarity with Godot (and optionally .NET for C# builds)
Node.js and npm for browser engines
student_project_ideas: Have the agent generate a simple Godot or three.js game from a classroom brief, then measure and report how many iterations the agent required to achieve a visually acceptable proof video.
Extend the asset-generation skill to swap in a different TTS or image backend (e.g. a local open model vs a paid API) and compare quality, cost and runtime for produced game assets.

tools.name: Serial-Studio/Serial-Studio
tools.desc: Open-source telemetry dashboard. Supports UART, BLE, MQTT, Modbus, CAN Bus and more.

cls.summary: Serial Studio is an open-source cross-platform telemetry dashboard that reads data from serial ports, BLE and industrial/network protocols and visualises and logs live sensor and bus data.
cls.what_it_does: Serial Studio connects to devices over UART/serial, Bluetooth LE, TCP/UDP/WebSocket and many industrial buses (MQTT, Modbus, CAN, OPC UA, Siemens S7, EtherNet/IP etc.), parses frames into named channels and displays them with plots, gauges, maps and 3D views. It logs to CSV/SQLite (and can sink to InfluxDB), supports scripting (JavaScript/Lua) for parsing and transforms, and offers a Project Editor to build dashboards; a Pro edition adds many industrial drivers and advanced features.
cls.trl_rationale: The repository is long-lived (created 2020, actively maintained with recent pushes), has a large user base (7.3k stars, many forks), mature feature set and documented user guides; official binaries and a Pro/commercial edition indicate real-world use and adoption.
prerequisites: basic familiarity with serial/UART and common industrial protocols (MQTT, Modbus, CAN, OPC UA)
comfort installing desktop software on Windows/macOS/Linux or Raspberry Pi
student_project_ideas: Build a sensor-to-dashboard pipeline: connect an ESP32 publishing JSON over serial/MQTT and create a Serial Studio project that parses, visualises and logs the data to SQLite and InfluxDB for later analysis.

Integrate CAN bus data from a microcontroller or CAN-to-USB adapter into Serial Studio, parse a DBC file (Pro or simulated), and build a dashboard that correlates vehicle signals with logged GNSS position data.

tools.name: MengTo/threeui
tools.desc: Open-source ThreeUI Community catalog with live interactive components and complete Community source.

cls.summary: ThreeUI Community is an open-source catalog of live Three.js-powered UI components and page shells for building interactive web 3D interfaces with React.
cls.what_it_does: ThreeUI provides a library and a browsable app of reusable, live-rendered WebGL components built on Three.js and React so developers can embed interactive 3D UI elements and preview them in a component-driven website. It is used by installing the npm package or running the local dev site; notable features include live renderers, component variants, controls and an integrated source/code tab for each example.
cls.trl_rationale: The repository is popular (many stars and forks) and includes installable packages and a runnable dev site, but it is only 88 days old so it lacks the multi-release, long-term track record required for TRL 6+. Popularity suggests early adoption (alpha) rather than proven production history.
student_project_ideas: Build a web dashboard that visualises real sensor time-series on 3D components (e.g. animated gauges or scene overlays) by integrating ThreeUI components with a small backend that serves simulated telemetry.

Create an interactive product configurator where students extend a ThreeUI component to load different 3D models and material variants, demonstrating integration between ThreeUI, Three.js model loaders and a simple UI state store.

tools.name: open-multi-agent/open-multi-agent
