cls.summary: FUXA is an open-source web-based SCADA/HMI platform for building real-time industrial dashboards and connecting to devices using standard protocols like Modbus, OPC-UA and MQTT.
cls.what_it_does: FUXA provides a browser-based visual editor and runtime for SCADA/HMI dashboards, a built-in data historian and protocol drivers so you can connect PLCs, sensors and IoT services. It is used by running a Node.js backend (or Docker image) and an Angular frontend, and is notable for supporting many industrial protocols and headless/embedded deployments (Docker, Raspberry Pi, Electron builds).
cls.trl_rationale: The repository is several years old, has a large community (5k+ stars, many forks), active recent commits and documentation, Docker images and published releases, and offers production-ready deployment options (Docker, headless builds), indicating a mature, widely adopted open-source project.
prerequisites: basic knowledge of industrial protocols (Modbus/OPC-UA/MQTT) and networking
student_project_ideas: Build a lab demonstrator that connects a simulated PLC (or Node-RED) to FUXA via Modbus and design an HMI to monitor and control a small process, logging data to InfluxDB for analysis.
Create an edge-deployed monitoring system by running FUXA on a Raspberry Pi that collects MQTT sensor data, implements simple alarms, and visualises time-series data with a historian backend.

tools.name: dotnet/Silk.NET
tools.desc: The high-speed OpenGL, OpenCL, OpenAL, OpenXR, GLFW, SDL, Vulkan, Assimp, WebGPU, and DirectX bindings library your mother warned you about.

cls.summary: Silk.NET is a mature, high-performance set of C# bindings and utilities that let .NET applications use low-level graphics, compute, audio and input APIs (Vulkan, OpenGL, WebGPU, OpenCL, OpenAL, GLFW/SDL, OpenXR, DirectX, Assimp).
cls.what_it_does: Silk.NET exposes low-level native multimedia and GPU APIs to .NET languages so developers can write cross-platform graphics, compute and audio code with minimal overhead. It is used as a bindings library plus convenience wrappers for windowing, input and asset loading, notable for performance-focused generated bindings and broad API coverage across modern graphics and compute backends.
cls.trl_rationale: The project is several years old (created 2019), has a large community (5k+ stars), active recent commits, example folders and .NET Foundation backing — evidence of wide adoption and stability rather than a small prototype.
prerequisites: basic knowledge of graphics or compute APIs (OpenGL/Vulkan/WebGPU/OpenCL) and native interop concepts
student_project_ideas: Create a cross-platform 3D model viewer in C# using Silk.NET for windowing/input and Assimp bindings to load models, then add basic camera controls and shading.
Implement a simple GPU-accelerated particle or heat simulation using Silk.NET bindings to OpenCL or WebGPU and visualise results with a Silk.NET rendering pipeline.

tools.name: dbrizov/NaughtyAttributes
tools.desc: Attribute Extensions for Unity

cls.summary: NaughtyAttributes is a free Unity Editor extension that adds many convenient attributes to simplify and customise the Unity Inspector without writing custom editors.
cls.what_it_does: It provides a set of C# attributes (e.g. Button, Dropdown, ShowNonSerializedField, Scene, ReorderableList) that change how fields and methods are displayed and edited in the Unity Inspector, reducing the need to write custom property drawers or editors. You use it by adding attributes to MonoBehaviour or serialisable types in your Unity project; most attributes are implemented as CustomPropertyDrawers and work in both runtime and custom editors when used with the project's helper APIs. It is notable for broad adoption, active maintenance, and compatibility with Unity 2022.3+.
cls.trl_rationale: The project is long-lived (created 2017), has many stars and forks, is actively maintained with recent pushes, and is widely used in Unity projects; this indicates a mature, widely-adopted tool rather than an experimental prototype.
student_project_ideas: Create a Unity-based robot parameter tuning scene that exposes controller gains and diagnostics with NaughtyAttributes buttons and reorderable lists to run and log experiments.
Build a small simulation demo where designers use custom inspector attributes (dropdowns, scenes, asset previews) to configure and compare multiple vehicle variants and record results to a CSV.

tools.name: Orillusion/orillusion
tools.desc: Orillusion is a pure Web3D rendering engine which is fully developed based on the WebGPU standard.

cls.summary: Orillusion is a WebGPU-based, TypeScript rendering engine for high-quality 3D graphics in the browser.
cls.what_it_does: Orillusion provides a Web3D rendering engine built on the WebGPU standard so developers can render complex, desktop-like 3D scenes in modern browsers. It is used as a client-side graphics library (importable via npm or CDN) with examples and documentation and is notable for leveraging WebGPU/WGSL for higher performance and modern GPU features in web environments.
cls.trl_rationale: The project is active, well-starred and has documentation and examples, and the README explicitly calls it a beta; these indicators fit a beta-stage TRL (6) rather than production-ready because the README warns against commercial use.
prerequisites: basic WebGPU and GPU shader (WGSL) concepts
student_project_ideas: Build an interactive browser-based digital-twin viewer that streams time-series sensor data and visualises it on a 3D model using Orillusion and a simple WebSocket backend.
Create a WebGPU shader study: implement and compare a physical-based rendering (PBR) material and a custom post-processing effect in Orillusion, documenting performance across browsers.

tools.name: apache/calcite
tools.desc: Apache Calcite

cls.summary: Apache Calcite is a Java framework that provides an extensible SQL parser, planner/optimizer and adapters to query heterogeneous data sources without providing its own storage layer.
cls.what_it_does: Calcite parses and validates SQL, converts SQL to logical and physical algebra, and applies pluggable optimization rules and cost models to produce query plans. It is used as an embeddable query planning and federation layer so applications can run SQL over diverse backends (Kafka, Cassandra, Druid, Elasticsearch, MongoDB and others). What makes it notable is its modular optimizer, adapter architecture and widespread production use in other data systems.
cls.trl_rationale: Project is long-lived (repo created 2014), actively maintained with many stars/forks and numerous adapters mentioned in the README; these indicate broad adoption and production use rather than an experimental prototype.
student_project_ideas: Implement a Calcite adapter for a time-series database (or MQTT-based sensor store) and compare federated query performance against direct queries.
Use Calcite to build a small digital-twin ingestion pipeline that rewrites and optimises SQL queries across Kafka and a document store, measuring latency and resource usage.

tools.name: NVIDIAGameWorks/kaolin
tools.desc: A PyTorch Library for Accelerating 3D Deep Learning Research

cls.summary: Kaolin is an NVIDIA-maintained PyTorch library that provides GPU-optimized building blocks for 3D deep learning, including differentiable rendering, physics for meshes/point clouds/splats, fast conversions, and USD I/O.
cls.what_it_does: Kaolin collects GPU-accelerated modules for 3D deep learning workflows: differentiable renderers, representation-agnostic physics (Simplicits), structured point clouds (SPC), Gaussian splat support, and conversion/IO utilities (including USD). It is used as a developer library within PyTorch to build research prototypes, simulations and interactive visualisations, notable for NVIDIA-grade GPU implementations and direct support for advanced 3D primitives like Gaussian splats and SPC octrees.
cls.trl_rationale: Kaolin is a multi-year NVIDIA project (created 2019) with thousands of stars, active recent commits, formal docs and conference presence (SIGGRAPH), and is used in research and labs — evidence of maturity and adoption beyond a prototype.
prerequisites: familiarity with 3D geometry and rendering concepts
student_project_ideas: Implement a differentiable rendering-based shape optimisation pipeline that trains a neural implicit representation using Kaolin's differentiable renderers and evaluates results with a learned loss.

Build an interactive capture-to-simulation demo converting a small set of RGB-D scans to Gaussian splats, run a simple Simplicits physics simulation, and export the scene as USD for web visualisation.

tools.name: AienTech/dossier
tools.desc: A self-hosted job search and resume builder app that writes tailored resumes and cover letters from your profile.

cls.summary: Dossier is a self‑hosted web app that stores your career profile and generates tailored resumes and cover letters for job postings using a local or hosted LLM.
cls.what_it_does: Dossier keeps a single-person profile (experience, projects, certifications, publications) and reads job postings to score matches and draft tailored resumes and cover letters that only use facts from your profile. It runs as a web app or desktop app, supports local LLMs (Ollama, LM Studio) or hosted APIs, and includes job search, application tracking and optional Google/Claude integrations.
cls.trl_rationale: The repository is very active and already has desktop releases and many stars, showing rapid adoption, but it was created 45 days ago so lacks the months/years of field-proven track record required for TRL 6+; therefore TRL 5 (alpha in use) is appropriate.
student_project_ideas: Evaluate how well a chosen local LLM (Ollama or LM Studio) tailors resumes by running a set of job postings and measuring factuality and hallucination rates compared to human-edited resumes.
Build an extension that exports Dossier resume data into a machine‑readable portfolio (JSON/Markdown) and visualises skill gaps across applications using a simple web dashboard.

tools.name: mavlink/qgroundcontrol
tools.desc: Cross-platform ground control station for drones (Android, iOS, Mac OS, Linux, Windows)

cls.summary: QGroundControl is a mature, cross-platform ground control station that provides mission planning, live telemetry, vehicle setup and parameter tuning for MAVLink-enabled drones such as PX4 and ArduPilot.
cls.what_it_does: QGroundControl lets operators plan and execute autonomous missions (waypoints, surveys, structure scans), monitor live flight telemetry and video, and configure or calibrate vehicle sensors and parameters. It runs on desktop and mobile platforms and includes MAVLink tooling (inspector, console, log download) and GStreamer-based video streaming, making it notable as a complete open-source GCS for UAV development and testing.
cls.trl_rationale: The project is long-lived (created 2011), has many stars, active recent pushes and formal releases, and is widely used with mature documentation; this indicates a mature, widely adopted tool (TRL 8) rather than an experimental prototype.
prerequisites: familiarity with MAVLink and UAV flight concepts
platform-specific build toolchains (Android/iOS SDKs for mobile builds)
student_project_ideas: Integrate a custom MAVLink-enabled sensor payload with PX4 and extend QGroundControl to visualise and log the new telemetry stream.
Develop and evaluate autonomous survey missions by configuring mission parameters in QGroundControl and running PX4 SITL simulations to measure coverage and mission timing.

tools.name: ros-navigation/navigation2
tools.desc: ROS 2 Navigation Framework and System

cls.summary: Navigation2 (Nav2) is the ROS 2 navigation stack that provides path planning, localization integration, and motion control for mobile robots.
cls.what_it_does: Nav2 implements the software components needed for autonomous mobile robot navigation (map servers, costmaps, planners, controllers, behavior trees and lifecycle management). It is used as a ROS 2 package set that runs on a robot or in simulation and integrates with sensors, SLAM, and visualization tools. It is notable for being the community-maintained, production-grade navigation framework for ROS 2 with plugin-based algorithms and extensive documentation.
cls.trl_rationale: Nav2 is a mature, community-backed ROS 2 navigation framework (repo created 2018) with extensive documentation, CI, sponsors and wide adoption in the ROS ecosystem, indicating long-term use beyond experimental prototypes.
student_project_ideas: Build a simulated mobile robot in Gazebo that uses Nav2 for autonomous waypoint navigation and evaluate planner performance under different costmap and obstacle scenarios.

Integrate a SLAM package (e.g. SLAM Toolbox) with Nav2 on a small differential-drive robot to implement map-building, localization and autonomous exploration, and measure localization error during repeated runs.

tools.name: xiangechen/chili3d
tools.desc: A browser-based 3D CAD for AI-assisted, parametric and direct modeling.

cls.summary: Chili3D is an open-source, browser-based 3D CAD application that provides AI-assisted, parametric and direct modelling by compiling OpenCascade to WebAssembly and rendering with Three.js.
cls.what_it_does: Chili3D brings near-native CAD modelling to the browser by compiling the OpenCascade geometry kernel to WebAssembly and using Three.js for rendering. It supports parametric feature-tree modelling, direct geometry edits, 2D sketches and a built-in browser-based AI assistant that can read and modify the document and feature tree.
cls.trl_rationale: The project is over three years old, has a large user interest (≈5k stars), an official live site and active recent development, indicating production-ready software; however it is not a de-facto standard across industry so TRL 7 is appropriate.
prerequisites: basic CAD modelling concepts (feature trees, sketches, constraints)
familiarity with CAD kernels (OpenCascade/OCCT) is helpful but not required
student_project_ideas: Create a parametric flange generator in Chili3D that takes standardised bolt patterns and variable dimensions, then export STEP/GLTF for downstream analysis in a FEA tool.

Integrate Chili3D with a local agent (using the provided local bridge) to build an automated workflow that translates natural-language change requests into scripted parametric edits and then runs geometry checks.

tools.name: onehumanbeing/esp32-iphone-agent
tools.desc: Let an AI model use a real iPhone with a $7 ESP32: AirPlay eyes, USB HID hands, any OpenAI-compatible vision model. No Mac, no developer account, no jailbreak.

cls.summary: An open-source system that uses a cheap ESP32-S3 board plus an iPhone app so an AI model can see the phone via AirPlay and control it via USB-HID without a Mac or jailbreak.
cls.what_it_does: The project turns a Seeed XIAO ESP32-S3 into an AirPlay receiver and USB-HID device so an iPhone can mirror its screen to a local agent app and accept pointer/keyboard actions; the app sends screenshots to OpenAI-compatible vision models and runs a planner to perform taps, swipes and typing. It is notable because it removes the need for a developer Mac/Xcode pairing — the board acts as the tether — and supports audio input via AirPlay plus replayable action traces.
cls.trl_rationale: The repo is very active and popular (many stars, media coverage) and provides firmware + an iPhone app and TestFlight builds, indicating early adopter usage; however the project is only 37 days old so it lacks the longer track record and stable releases needed for TRL 6+.
prerequisites: Seeed XIAO ESP32-S3 (or compatible board) and USB cable
an iPhone (iOS) and familiarity with TestFlight/app installation
basic comfort flashing firmware and configuring hotspot/AirPlay
(optional) API key for an OpenAI-compatible vision model if free shared model is unavailable
student_project_ideas: Build a lab exercise that flashes the ESP32 board, sets up AirPlay mirroring and records an agent run, then analyse the exported run trace to measure perception/action latency and failure modes.

Extend the agent by integrating a local lightweight vision pipeline (e.g. edge-optimized object detector) on a Raspberry Pi or cloud function to compare on-device vs cloud model performance for a constrained phone automation task.

tools.name: tidwall/buntdb
tools.desc: BuntDB is an embeddable, in-memory key/value database for Go with custom indexing and geospatial support

cls.summary: BuntDB is an embeddable, in-memory key/value database written in Go that provides persistence, transactions, custom indexes and multi-dimensional spatial indexing.
cls.what_it_does: BuntDB provides a fast, embeddable key/value store for Go applications with ACID transactions, an append-only persistence file, custom index support and built-in spatial indexing up to many dimensions. It is used by importing the Go package and opening a DB instance (including :memory:), then performing reads and writes inside transactions; notable features are JSON-field indexing, multi-value and custom indexes, and geospatial queries.
cls.trl_rationale: The repository is long-lived (created 2016), has a large star count and active recent commits, documented API and examples, and is an established embeddable DB in the Go ecosystem; this indicates mature, production-ready software.
prerequisites: basic knowledge of transactions and key/value databases
understanding of indexing and geospatial concepts if using spatial features
student_project_ideas: Build an embedded sensor data collector in Go that stores geolocated telemetry in BuntDB and exposes simple spatial queries for nearby events, then visualise results on a web map.

Create a prototype digital-twin cache that uses BuntDB as an in-memory layer to aggregate device state and time-windowed readings from MQTT, demonstrating fast reads for a dashboard and durable persistence to disk.

tools.name: dgiot/dgiot
tools.desc: Open Source Industrial IoT Platform | 300+ protocols | 6-min deploy | Modbus OPC UA MQTT | 12K Stars

cls.summary: DGIOT is an open-source industrial IoT platform that collects, processes and routes device data (Modbus/OPC‑UA/MQTT etc.), provides a device shadow/ontology engine and stores time-series for monitoring and digital‑twin style workflows.
cls.what_it_does: DGIOT aggregates data from many industrial protocols at the edge or cloud, provides a device shadow and rule engine (ontology-based), and writes time-series to databases for dashboards and alarms. It is used as a full IoT stack (edge agent, brokers, parsers, rule engine, connectors) and is notable for wide protocol support, an ontology/shadow architecture and ready Docker deployment for evaluation.
cls.trl_rationale: The repository is multi-year (created 2021), actively maintained with deployment recipes (Docker compose, bootstrap scripts), substantial community interest (thousands of stars) and documentation, indicating production readiness for many users; however it is not a de-facto industry standard across all sectors, so TRL 7 is appropriate.
prerequisites: Erlang/OTP knowledge for building/extending server modules
Docker / Docker Compose for quick deployment
Familiarity with MQTT, OPC‑UA, Modbus and time-series DBs (TDengine/Postgres)
student_project_ideas: Build a small digital twin pipeline: connect a simulated Modbus device (or gateway simulator) to DGIOT, ingest data into TDengine and create a dashboard and alarm rule to demonstrate closed-loop monitoring.

Extend or add a protocol bridge: implement a simple sensor protocol adapter (or an OPC‑UA client) as a dgiot_bridge module and evaluate latency and throughput under load using the provided station-simulation tools.

tools.name: CloudCompare/CloudCompare
tools.desc: CloudCompare main repository

cls.summary: CloudCompare is a mature open-source desktop application for processing, comparing and visualising large 3D point clouds and triangular meshes.
cls.what_it_does: CloudCompare provides tools to load, visualise, register, compare and process large 3D point clouds and meshes (including distance computation and octree-based workflows). It is used as a standalone desktop app on Windows, macOS and Linux and supports plugins and many file formats; it is notable for handling very large point clouds and for an extensive set of point-cloud editing and analysis utilities.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository is long-lived (created 2012) with many stars and forks, active recent commits, cross-platform releases and a public homepage; this indicates a mature, widely adopted project rather than a prototype.
prerequisites: basic familiarity with 3D point clouds and mesh concepts
for building from source: CMake, C++ toolchain and dependencies (OpenGL, Qt when required)
student_project_ideas: Use CloudCompare to register and compare UAV photogrammetry point clouds from two surveys to quantify terrain change and visualise results in an interactive lab assignment.
Integrate CloudCompare with Potree (or export formats) to build a web-based viewer that demonstrates large point-cloud streaming and level-of-detail techniques for a capstone project.

tools.name: vinta/pangu.js
tools.desc: Opinionated paranoid text spacing in JavaScript, with on-device AI semantic judgment

cls.summary: pangu.js is a JavaScript/TypeScript library and Chrome extension that automatically inserts whitespace between CJK (Chinese/Japanese/Korean) characters and ASCII letters, numbers and symbols, with an optional on-device AI step for ambiguous cases.
cls.what_it_does: The project spaces text by inserting appropriate whitespace between full-width CJK characters and half-width ASCII (letters, digits, symbols) for improved readability on webpages and plain text. It is provided as a Node/browser library, CLI and Chrome extension, and the extension can optionally use Chrome's Prompt API (Gemini Nano) on-device to resolve semantic spacing ambiguities. Notable points are its long history, broad language support across many ports, and a DOM-aware build for automatic spacing of web pages.
cls.trl_rationale: The repository is long-lived (created 2012), widely used (several thousand stars, multiple language ports, Chrome extension and npm package) and actively maintained, which indicates maturity and broad adoption consistent with TRL 8.
prerequisites: Chrome (for the extension) if using AI-spacing feature
student_project_ideas: Build a small web accessibility tool that integrates pangu.js with a browser extension or bookmarklet to automatically re-flow mixed CJK/ASCII content on selected pages, and measure user reading speed improvements.

Create a CI pre-commit hook for a multilingual documentation repository that uses pangu.js to enforce consistent spacing rules and generate a report of automated corrections (combine with git hooks and a static site generator).

tools.name: Fractal-Compute-Orchestrations/FractalAndroid
tools.desc: A human-centric, resource-aware Android node for edge computing and federated learning. Orchestrates distributed intelligence with privacy-first localization and empathetic hardware management.

cls.summary: FractalAndroid is an Android client and on-device execution runtime that turns smartphones into resource-aware edge compute nodes for privacy-preserving federated learning and distributed inference.
cls.what_it_does: FractalAndroid monitors device telemetry (SoC temperature, battery, RAM, network) and gates or schedules machine-learning workloads (TFLite-based training/inference) to avoid user impact while participating in a decentralized Fractal compute network. It provides an MVVM Android app with telemetry dashboards, checkpoint upload/transfer logic, and a bandwidth-credit rewards mechanism for running quantized model slices on-device.
cls.trl_rationale: The repository is active (last push recently) and the README describes a full-featured client with telemetry, gating, and network integration, and it has a large star count indicating community interest; however the project is under one year old (created 361 days ago) which limits demonstrated long-term production maturity to about TRL 6.
student_project_ideas: Build a lab exercise that measures and compares on-device ML energy and thermal behaviour by running a TFLite model under FractalAndroid's gating policies and plotting telemetry time-series to evaluate impact on battery and temperature.

Extend the client to integrate a simple simulated FractalCore server (or use Flower) to run a mini federated learning experiment across several Android emulators and analyse convergence and network bandwidth/reward accounting.

tools.name: thunderbird/thunderbolt
tools.desc: AI You Control: Choose your models. Own your data. Eliminate vendor lock-in.

cls.summary: Thunderbolt is an open-source, cross-platform AI client and agent platform designed for self-hosting and on-prem use so organisations can choose models and retain their data.
cls.what_it_does: Thunderbolt provides a desktop and mobile AI chat/agent client that can connect to frontier, local, or on‑prem models and MCP/agent servers; it includes a backend, sync service and CLI to run locally or in self-hosted deployments. It is notable for multi-device sync, embedding interactive widgets and an explicit focus on self-hosting, model choice and data ownership.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository is over one year old, has substantial stars and forks, active recent pushes, extensive documentation (self-hosting, deployment, CLI) and multi-platform build instructions, indicating production-ready maturity and an active community.
prerequisites: Postgres (or running via provided docker compose)
student_project_ideas: Deploy Thunderbolt locally and connect it to an on‑prem LLM (e.g. LocalAI) to build a secure engineering knowledge assistant that answers project documentation queries.
Create a custom agent/skill that automates requirements lookup and traceability by integrating Thunderbolt with a project repository or issue tracker and demonstrate workflows in a lab.

tools.name: TokisanGames/Terrain3D
tools.desc: A high performance, editable terrain system for Godot 4.

cls.summary: Terrain3D is a high-performance, editable terrain system implemented as a Godot 4 GDExtension for creating large, LOD-enabled heightmap terrains and foliage in Godot projects.
cls.what_it_does: Terrain3D provides a terrain engine for Godot 4 that supports very large heightmaps, multiple LODs, texture painting, sculpting, foliage instancing and imports from common heightmap tools. It is used as a Godot addon (GDExtension) callable from GDScript, C# or other Godot-supported languages and is notable for its C++ performance and extensive documentation and tooling for terrain workflows.
cls.trl_rationale: The project is mature and actively maintained (created 2023-01-22, frequent recent pushes, many stars and forks), has extensive documentation and a user community and is widely used in Godot projects; these indicate a well-adopted, production-ready addon.
prerequisites: basic familiarity with GDScript or C#
C++ knowledge to build or extend the GDExtension
student_project_ideas: Create a virtual test site in Godot using Terrain3D to visualise sensor placements and simulate line-of-sight for a robotics navigation task, integrating simple ROS2 messages for robot position.
Build an interactive terrain editor tool that imports real-world DEM/heightmap data and allows students to test different erosion or texture-painting workflows and export scenes for simulation.

tools.name: cyberbotics/webots
tools.desc: Webots Robot Simulator

cls.summary: Webots is a mature, open-source robot simulation environment for modelling, programming and testing robots, vehicles and mechanical systems.
cls.what_it_does: Webots lets users build virtual robots and environments, run physics-based simulations, and control robots using languages like C++, Python and interfaces to ROS/ROS 2. It is used to prototype robot behaviours, validate controllers and run repeatable experiments; notable aspects are its beginner-friendly tutorials, cross-platform prebuilt binaries and cloud-hosted example simulations.
cls.trl_rationale: Webots has a long track record (origin at EPFL in 1996), was open-sourced in 2018, has thousands of stars, regular releases and active maintenance; this indicates a mature, widely-used simulator suitable for production research and teaching.
student_project_ideas: Create and validate an autonomous navigation stack for a wheeled robot in Webots using ROS 2 and compare performance of PID vs MPC controllers in simulation.
Develop a perception-to-control pipeline: simulate a robot with a camera in Webots, run a neural network for object detection (PyTorch) and implement closed-loop control to follow detected objects.

tools.name: google-deepmind/dm_control
tools.desc: Google DeepMind's software stack for physics-based simulation and Reinforcement Learning environments, using MuJoCo.

cls.summary: dm_control is DeepMind's Python library that provides MuJoCo-based physics simulation, a suite of continuous-control RL environments, and tools for composing and viewing articulated models.
cls.what_it_does: dm_control supplies Python bindings and helper libraries for the MuJoCo physics engine, a set of ready-made continuous-control Reinforcement Learning environments (dm_control.suite), tools to compose and modify MJCF models, and an interactive viewer for rendering simulations. It is used to develop and evaluate control algorithms, simulate articulated mechanisms and robots, and build custom RL tasks; its notable aspects are tight MuJoCo integration and a curated environment suite used in research.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository is long-lived (created 2017), actively maintained with many stars and forks, a cited publication and stable releases (semantic versioning from 1.0.0), and is widely used in research—evidence of mature, widely adopted software.
prerequisites: MuJoCo runtime / mujoco Python package and native libraries
OpenGL / EGL / GLFW / OSMesa system libraries for rendering
student_project_ideas: Implement and compare a PID controller and an RL controller for a MuJoCo pendulum task using dm_control.suite and evaluate performance across disturbance scenarios.
Build a simulated mobile manipulator in dm_control (using MJCF composer), then integrate with a motion planner (e.g. OMPL) to test path-following and collision avoidance in simulation.

tools.name: praydog/UEVR
tools.desc: Universal Unreal Engine VR Mod (4.8 - 5.4)

cls.summary: UEVR is an open-source mod and injector that enables VR support for games built with Unreal Engine 4 and 5 by providing stereo rendering, input emulation and runtime integration with OpenVR/OpenXR.
cls.what_it_does: UEVR injects a VR runtime into Unreal Engine games to provide 6DOF stereoscopic rendering, motion control emulation, in-game VR menus and per-game configuration; it is used by running a Windows injector and selecting the target process and runtime. It is notable for supporting a wide range of UE versions (4.8–5.4), multiple rendering modes (native stereo, synchronized sequential, AFR) and a plugin/Blueprint system for modders to extend functionality.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository is multi-year (created 2022), actively maintained with many stars, published stable and nightly releases and user documentation which indicates production-ready mod tooling for its community rather than an experimental prototype.
prerequisites: Windows system administration (running injectors, admin privileges)
Familiarity with Unreal Engine games and modding concepts
Basic C++ / plugin development or Blueprint knowledge for extending the plugin
student_project_ideas: Extend UEVR with a small Unreal C++ plugin that maps a custom controller to in-game actions for an existing UE4 game and evaluate usability and latency.

Build a lab exercise that compares the three rendering modes (Native Stereo, Synchronized Sequential, AFR) in a sample UE5 demo, measuring perceived latency and visual artefacts and reporting trade-offs.

tools.name: focus-creative-games/luban
tools.desc: luban是一个强大、易用、优雅、稳定的游戏配置解决方案。luban is a powerful, easy-to-use, elegant and stable game configuration solution.

cls.summary: Luban is an open-source, cross-platform tool that validates tabular/source data and generates game configuration data and language-specific code from spreadsheets and other input formats.
cls.what_it_does: Luban ingests spreadsheets (csv/xls/xlsx) and other data sources (json, xml, yaml, lua) and validates, transforms and generates runtime configuration data and language bindings (C#, C++, Java, Lua, Python, TypeScript, etc.). It is used as a build/CI tool or CLI to create fast, schema-driven game configuration pipelines and supports many serialization formats (protobuf, flatbuffers, msgpack) and engine targets (Unity, Unreal, Godot).
cls.trl_rationale: The repository is mature (created 2020), has many stars and forks, and active recent development including tests and documentation; it appears production-ready for game projects, which supports a TRL of 7 (production-ready).
prerequisites: familiarity with C# and CLI tools
student_project_ideas: Create a small Unity prototype that loads runtime configuration generated by Luban from Excel sheets and demonstrates changing gameplay parameters without recompiling Unity code.
Build an automated pipeline that validates and converts level or item data from spreadsheets into protobuf and flatbuffer outputs using Luban, and compare runtime load performance between formats.

tools.name: tomlooman/ActionRoguelike
tools.desc: Project Orion - Co-op Action Roguelike in Unreal Engine C++

cls.summary: A large, actively maintained Unreal Engine 5 C++ sample project demonstrating a cooperative action-roguelike with gameplay systems, AI, multiplayer and example subsystems.
cls.what_it_does: Project Orion is a complete sample game built in UE5 and C++ that demonstrates character movement, an action/ability system, AI with behavior trees, multiplayer networking, asset management and various performance techniques. It is used as a teaching/example project for learning Unreal C++ and to illustrate how to combine C++ and Blueprints, async loading, Niagara VFX, UMG UI and optimization techniques.
cls.trl_rationale: The repository is long-lived (created 2020), very active (recent push 2026), widely used (≈4.6k stars, forks) and explicitly tied to a professional course; these indicate mature, well-adopted example code rather than a fragile prototype.
prerequisites: Basic game engine concepts (actors, Blueprints, networking)
student_project_ideas: Extend the sample game's AI by implementing a new behavior tree-driven enemy type and measure its performance and network replication effects using Unreal's profiling tools.

Create a mod or mission that adds a persistent SaveGame-driven progression mechanic integrating the project's SaveGame system and a simple backend (e.g. SQLite or a REST service) to analyse save/load consistency in multiplayer.

tools.name: IvanMurzak/Unity-MCP
tools.desc: AI Skills, MCP Tools, and CLI for Unity Engine. Full AI develop and test loop. Use cli for quick setup. Efficient token usage, advanced tools. Any C# method may be turned into a tool by a single line. Works with Claude Code, Gemini, Copilot, Cursor and any other absolutely for free.

cls.summary: Unity-MCP connects LLM-based agents to the Unity Editor and built games so agents can inspect and modify scenes, run tests, call C# tools and automate the full develop/test loop.
cls.what_it_does: Unity-MCP registers C# methods and editor operations as MCP tools or generated Skills so an external LLM agent (Claude Code, Gemini, Copilot, etc.) can query and modify Unity projects, run EditMode/PlayMode tests, compile C# via Roslyn, and take screenshots from the Editor or runtime. It is distributed as a Unity package and a CLI for CI/automation, and supports running a local MCP server or using a cloud relay to simplify setup.
cls.trl_rationale: The project has many stars and forks, an explicit release and changelog, CI that runs Editor/PlayMode tests across Unity versions, and active recent commits — indicating production-ready maturity (TRL 7). The repository age (~1.6 years) and visible community activity support this rating.
prerequisites: Basic C# and Unity Editor familiarity
Node.js (for optional CLI) / npm for unity-mcp-cli
student_project_ideas: Build an LLM-driven automated test agent that uses Unity-MCP to create randomized scenes, run PlayMode tests, and report failures as part of a CI pipeline.

Create an intelligent level-authoring tool where an LLM (via Unity-MCP) generates and modifies level geometry and NPC behaviours, and evaluate playability metrics using Unity analytics or a physics plugin.

alternatives_to: other in-editor automation or scripting tools

tools.name: hepengwei/visualization-collection
tools.desc: 🌈 一个专注于前端视觉效果的集合应用，包含CSS动效、Canvas动画、Three.js3D、人工智能应用等上百个案例（持续更新）

cls.summary: A popular open-source collection of front-end visual effects and demos including CSS animations, Canvas scenes, Three.js 3D examples and small AI-powered demos, intended as examples and inspiration for web developers.
cls.what_it_does: This repository collects hundreds of front-end visual effect examples (CSS, Canvas, Three.js, plus some AI demo pages) that run in the browser and can be launched locally or viewed online. It is used as a learning and demo resource: developers clone the repo, run the dev server, and inspect or adapt example code; its notable points are the breadth of curated visual examples and an online live demo.
cls.trl_rationale: The project is several years old, actively maintained with many stars (4599) and a public live demo, indicating real-world use and stability; it is an examples/demos collection rather than a formal production platform, so TRL 7 (production-ready demos and resources) is appropriate.
prerequisites: basic familiarity with React/Three.js to modify examples
student_project_ideas: Fork an existing Three.js example from the collection and extend it to visualise time-series sensor data streamed from a simple Node.js server to demonstrate real-time web visualization.
Re-implement a Canvas animation from the collection using WebGPU or a physics library (e.g. integrate with matter.js) and compare performance and code structure.

tools.name: moshang-ax/lottery
tools.desc: 🎉🌟✨🎈年会抽奖程序，基于 Express +  Vue + Three.js的 3D 球体抽奖程序，奖品🧧🎁，文字，图片，抽奖规则均可配置，😜抽奖人员信息Excel一键导入😍，抽奖结果Excel导出😎，给你的抽奖活动带来全新酷炫体验🚀🚀🚀

cls.summary: A web-based 3D raffle/lottery application (Vue + Three.js front end and Express back end) for running event prize draws with Excel import/export of participants and results.
cls.what_it_does: This project provides a configurable raffle/lottery web app that renders a 3D sphere of participant names using Three.js (CSS3D) and runs prize draws; administrators can configure prizes, import participant lists from Excel, and export results to Excel. It is delivered as a Vue 3 + Vite front-end and an Express back-end that serves data and persists results.
cls.trl_rationale: The repository is long-lived (created 2019), has many stars/forks, recent activity and a published demo, indicating production-ready maturity for event/utility use rather than early experimental code.
prerequisites: familiarity with Vue.js and Three.js helpful but not required

tools.name: NVlabs/tiny-cuda-nn
tools.desc: Lightning fast C++/CUDA neural network framework

cls.summary: Tiny CUDA Neural Networks is a compact C++/CUDA library that implements extremely fast MLPs and input encodings (including multiresolution hash) for training and inference on NVIDIA GPUs.
cls.what_it_does: It provides a small, self-contained C++/CUDA API to build, train and run highly optimized neural networks (notably a fully-fused MLP and hash-grid encoding) aimed at real‑time applications such as NeRF and rendering. Users integrate the library into C++ projects (or use PyTorch bindings) and can optionally JIT‑fuse models into larger CUDA kernels for further speedups. It is notable for very high GPU performance and explicit support for runtime CUDA compilation to fuse models into single kernels.
cls.trl_rationale: The project is mature and widely used: created in 2021, actively maintained (recent pushes), thousands of stars, and referenced/used by high-profile projects (e.g. Instant NGP). Documentation, benchmarks and bindings indicate production-grade readiness rather than an experimental prototype.
student_project_ideas: Integrate tiny-cuda-nn with a simple NeRF implementation to compare rendering quality and training/inference speed against a PyTorch baseline on an RTX GPU.
Create a CUDA kernel that fuses a tiny-cuda-nn model into a larger real‑time sensor processing pipeline (using the JIT fusion API) and measure latency improvements for an online inference task.

tools.name: maptalks/maptalks.js
tools.desc: A light and plugable JavaScript library for integrated 2D/3D maps.

cls.summary: maptalks-gl is a JavaScript library for building high-performance 2D/3D web maps that support vector tiles, 3D Tiles and glTF for geospatial visualisation and analysis.
cls.what_it_does: maptalks-gl provides a WebGL/WebGPU-driven map engine for rendering integrated 2D and 3D maps in the browser, with built-in layers for vector tiles, 3D Tiles, glTF models, terrain and traffic simulation. It is used by importing the library in web projects or via CDN and adding layers to a Map object; notable features include WebGL performance, support for common geospatial formats and optional transcoders (Draco, KTX2) for compressed assets.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository created in 2016, thousands of stars and active development as of the last push; stable multi-package project with tests and published packages (maptalks-gl) indicating a mature, widely used library for web mapping.
prerequisites: familiarity with GIS concepts (tiles, projections, vector/3D tiles)
student_project_ideas: Build a web map that loads and visualises city-scale 3D Tiles with glTF building models and implements simple traffic simulation overlays using maptalks-gl and a vector tile server.

Create an interactive infrastructure dashboard that streams sensor time-series (via MQTT or a time-series API) and visualises asset locations and statuses on a 3D map built with maptalks-gl and custom glTF markers.

tools.name: crate/crate
tools.desc: CrateDB is a distributed and scalable SQL database for storing and analyzing massive amounts of data in near real-time, even with complex queries. It is PostgreSQL-compatible, and based on Lucene.

cls.summary: CrateDB is an open-source, distributed SQL database designed to store and query large volumes of time-series, IoT, geospatial and full-text data in near real time.
cls.what_it_does: CrateDB provides a horizontally scalable, fault-tolerant SQL interface and HTTP API for ingesting, storing and querying massive datasets (time-series, documents, geospatial and vectors) with low-latency distributed query execution. It is used as a backend database for analytics, IoT telemetry and real-time dashboards and is notable for PostgreSQL wire-protocol compatibility, built-in full-text and geospatial features, and its Lucene-based indexing.
cls.trl_rationale: The project is long-lived (created 2013), has a large community (4.4k stars), frequent activity and documentation, official Docker images and a commercial cloud offering; these indicate a mature, widely adopted product (TRL 8).
prerequisites: understanding of time-series and indexing concepts
student_project_ideas: Build an IoT telemetry pipeline that ingests sensor data via MQTT, stores it in CrateDB, and implements SQL queries and dashboards to detect anomalies over time.
Compare query performance and storage efficiency between CrateDB and TimescaleDB / ClickHouse for a simulated fleet of vehicles producing geospatial time-series data, and report trade-offs.

tools.name: UnityCommunity/UnityLibrary
tools.desc: :books: Library of all kind of scripts, snippets & shaders for Unity

cls.summary: A large, community-maintained collection of Unity C# scripts, editor utilities and shaders that you can drop into Unity projects.
cls.what_it_does: This repository collects reusable scripts, editor tools, script templates and shaders for the Unity game engine so developers can reuse common functionality instead of writing it from scratch. It's used by cloning or importing assets into the Unity editor and browsing examples; its main value is breadth of practical snippets rather than a single integrated product.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository is mature (created 2016), actively maintained with many stars and recent pushes, indicating stable, production-ready examples rather than an experimental prototype.
prerequisites: Familiarity with Unity Editor (importing assets, scenes)
student_project_ideas: Build a small interactive digital-twin style visualization (e.g., a factory cell) using Unity and repository scripts for UI, input handling and simple animations to demonstrate runtime monitoring.
Create a robotics simulation scene combining Unity and ROS/ROS2 (ROS–Unity bridge) using ready-made input and camera scripts from the library to prototype teleoperation and visualization.

tools.name: KilledByAPixel/LittleJS
tools.desc: Tiny fast 2D/3D HTML5 game engine with many features and no dependencies.

cls.summary: LittleJS is a small, fast open-source HTML5 game engine for building 2D and 3D browser-based interactive scenes and games.
cls.what_it_does: LittleJS provides a compact WebGL2 + Canvas2D rendering core with built-in 2D/3D objects, physics (arcade and Box2D integration), audio, input handling, particle systems, level editors and tooling. It is used by embedding the engine in a web page or a module project (TypeScript/Vite examples are provided) and is notable for its small footprint, many live examples and an editable example browser for rapid iteration.
cls.trl_rationale: The project is mature and well maintained (created 2021, active commits as of Nov 2026) with many stars, forks, documentation, examples and published demos, indicating production-readiness for interactive/web projects rather than an early prototype.
student_project_ideas: Create a browser-based interactive dashboard that visualises robot telemetry (pose, sensor data, map) using LittleJS for rendering and a ROS/websocket bridge to stream data.
Build a physics-based 2D control demo that implements and visualises PID or state-feedback controllers for a simulated vehicle or pendulum using LittleJS arcade physics or Box2D integration.

tools.name: google-deepmind/mujoco_menagerie
tools.desc: A collection of high-quality models for the MuJoCo physics engine, curated by Google DeepMind.

cls.summary: A curated library of high-quality robot and system models for the MuJoCo physics engine, packaged for easy download and use in simulation and research.
cls.what_it_does: Menagerie provides ready-to-run MJCF/MJX model files, assets and Python helpers so users can load, view and simulate a wide range of robots and articulated systems in MuJoCo. It is used by installing the Python package or cloning the repo to probe models interactively or as inputs to control, RL training and validation workflows, with an emphasis on well-constructed, community-maintained models.
cls.trl_rationale: The repository is multi-year (created 2022) with thousands of stars, an installable Python package, pinned model releases and active maintenance by DeepMind, indicating broad use and stability; these facts support a mature TRL rather than an experimental prototype.
prerequisites: understanding of MJCF/MJX model structure for advanced edits
student_project_ideas: Use a Menagerie robot model to develop and evaluate a PID or model-predictive controller in MuJoCo, comparing performance across different grades of model realism.
Integrate a Menagerie model with an RL training pipeline (e.g. Stable Baselines3) to study sample efficiency and the effect of model fidelity on learned policies.

tools.name: MichaelGrupp/evo
tools.desc: Python package for the evaluation of odometry and SLAM

cls.summary: evo is a mature Python toolbox for loading, comparing, plotting and computing standard metrics on odometry and SLAM trajectories.
cls.what_it_does: evo reads common trajectory formats (TUM, KITTI, EuRoC, ROS/ROS2 bag topics), computes standard metrics such as absolute and relative pose error, and provides CLI tools and plotting/ export options to compare SLAM/odometry outputs. It is notable for broad format support, configurable alignment/scale options for monocular systems, and a fast, scriptable command-line interface useful in benchmarking experiments.
cls.trl_rationale: The repository is long-lived (created 2017), actively maintained (recent pushes), has many stars/forks and documented CLI, examples and wiki pages; this indicates wide adoption and production use rather than an experimental demo.
prerequisites: optional: ROS / ROS 2 for some features, PyQt6 for enhanced plotting
student_project_ideas: Compare the trajectory outputs of two open-source SLAM algorithms (e.g. ORB‑SLAM2 and RTAB‑Map) on KITTI or EuRoC data using evo metrics and produce a reproducible report with plots and tables.
Integrate a small monocular SLAM pipeline with evo to measure scale-drift and implement an automated alignment/scale-correction step, then evaluate performance across multiple sequences.

tools.name: WebODM/WebODM
tools.desc: User-friendly, commercial-grade software for processing aerial imagery. ✈️ Download it for free!

cls.summary: WebODM is an open-source web application that processes drone/aerial images into georeferenced orthomosaics, DEMs, point clouds, textured 3D models and gaussian splats.
cls.what_it_does: WebODM automates photogrammetric processing of UAV imagery to produce maps, elevation models, point clouds and 3D meshes; it is run as a server/web application (installers and Docker images available) and can use multiple processing engines (ODX, MicMac, LGT). It is notable for being a mature, user-friendly, open-source platform with tiling/delivery capabilities and integrations for geospatial workflows.
cls.trl_rationale: The project is long-lived (created 2016), actively maintained with many stars/forks, regular pushes and downloadable installers and documentation, indicating wide adoption and a stable user base — consistent with a mature, widely adopted tool.
prerequisites: familiarity with server administration or Docker for installation
understanding of geospatial data formats (GeoTIFF, LAS/LAZ, DEM)
student_project_ideas: Process a small UAV dataset in WebODM to produce an orthomosaic and DEM, then use the DEM to perform simple flood inundation or slope analysis in QGIS.

Compare outputs (orthomosaic, point cloud density and DEM accuracy) from the different processing engines supported by WebODM (ODX vs MicMac) for the same flight and report on processing time and geometric accuracy.

tools.name: PurpleDoubleD/locally-uncensored
tools.desc: The all-in-one local AI studio for your desktop: chat, image and video generation and a coding agent in one free, open source app. Windows and Linux. No Docker, no terminal, no cloud required.

cls.summary: Locally Uncensored is a free, open-source desktop AI studio that runs local chat, image and video generation models plus a coding agent without requiring Docker or cloud services.
cls.what_it_does: It packages local LLMs and generative-image/video models into a single desktop application with chat, create (image/video), and an automated coding-agent UI so users can run models on their own machine and manage downloads and runtimes from a GUI. It is notable for shipping pre-built installers for Windows and Linux (AppImage/.deb/.rpm), offering macOS and Android builds, and integrating multiple runtimes and model backends to make local model use simple for non-experts.
cls.trl_rationale: The project has packaged releases (installers for Windows/Linux, AppImage/.deb/.rpm), an active release history and many stars and forks, indicating a beta-quality product; however the repository is under one year old (created 2026-03-24), which limits TRL to at most 6 by the stated rules.
prerequisites: sufficient disk space for downloaded models
GPU drivers for local acceleration (optional but recommended)
student_project_ideas: Compare local code-generation performance and output quality across two small LLMs in Locally Uncensored by scripting equivalent prompts and measuring latency, token usage and correctness on a code-refactoring task.

Create a plugin or workflow that connects Locally Uncensored's coding agent to a Git repo to automatically propose and apply small fixes (showing diffs), then evaluate safety and reliability in an automated lab exercise.

tools.name: solvespace/solvespace
tools.desc: Parametric 2d/3d CAD

cls.summary: SolveSpace is an open-source parametric 2D/3D CAD application for modelling parts and assemblies with constraint-based sketching and basic solid modelling.
cls.what_it_does: SolveSpace provides a parametric sketcher, constraint solver, and solid modelling tools to create parts and assemblies, and it exports common CAD formats. It is used as a desktop application (or CLI) for designing geometric parts and simple assemblies and is notable for a compact codebase, active releases, and availability across Linux, Windows and macOS.
cls.trl_rationale: The project is mature (repository created 2015), has thousands of stars, official release packages and platform builds (Flatpak, Snap, GitHub releases) and active commits in 2026, indicating a long track record and stable user base.
prerequisites: familiarity with CAD concepts (sketches, constraints, assemblies)
for building: CMake and C++ build toolchain, GTK/Qt knowledge and OpenGL dev libraries
student_project_ideas: Design and 3D-print a small mechanism (e.g. a gearbox housing) using SolveSpace for parametric modelling and export STL for printing, demonstrating design iteration and tolerance checks.
Create a simple assembly and use the command-line interface to parameterise variations (e.g. hole positions/sizes) to study change propagation and automated part generation for a factory fixture.

tools.name: torchgeo/torchgeo
tools.desc: TorchGeo: datasets, samplers, transforms, and pre-trained models for geospatial data

cls.summary: TorchGeo is a PyTorch domain library that provides geospatial datasets, samplers, transforms and pre-trained models to support remote-sensing and earth-observation machine learning workflows.
cls.what_it_does: TorchGeo supplies ready-to-use geospatial datasets, patch samplers, data transforms and model tasks so researchers and engineers can train and evaluate deep learning models on satellite and aerial imagery. It is used as a drop-in domain library alongside PyTorch (and Lightning) and is notable for handling geospatial concerns such as coordinate reference systems, multi-source dataset composition (union/intersection) and large-image sampling.
cls.trl_rationale: The repository is multi-year (created 2021) with many stars, active development, published documentation, tutorials and a referenced paper, indicating production-ready maturity and community adoption; this supports a TRL of ~7 rather than experimental levels.
student_project_ideas: Train and evaluate a semantic segmentation model for land-cover mapping using TorchGeo datasets and PyTorch Lightning, then compare performance across different satellite sources (e.g. Landsat vs Sentinel) using the provided samplers.

Build a change-detection pipeline that ingests multi-temporal imagery with TorchGeo datasets, applies appropriate transforms and samplers, and visualises predicted change maps over time in a simple web dashboard (e.g. using Flask or Dash).

tools.name: 0xShug0/audio.cpp
tools.desc: An all-in-one, pure C++ inference engine for audio models, powered by ggml. Supports TTS, STT, VAD, voice conversion, music generation, and more, with highly optimized performance. No Python dependency.

cls.summary: audio.cpp is a high-performance, pure C++ local inference engine for audio models that runs TTS, ASR, separation, voice conversion and music generation across CPUs and GPUs without Python.
cls.what_it_does: audio.cpp provides a shared native runtime (built on ggml) to run hundreds of audio model families for speech-to-text, text-to-speech, voice cloning, separation and music generation, offering a CLI and built-in WebUI. It focuses on highly optimized, portable inference across CUDA, Vulkan, Metal, SYCL and CPU backends so models can run locally with low latency and reduced memory use. Notable features include many pre-integrated model ports, hardware-specific performance presets, validation tooling and a WebUI for model management and interactive workflows.
cls.trl_rationale: The project is actively maintained, has many stars, documented releases (v0.9.4/v0.9.5) and extensive README/validation reports, indicating a beta-level maturity; however the repository is only ~5 months old (under 1 year) so there is not yet the multi-year production track record required for TRL 7+.
prerequisites: GPU drivers and knowledge of CUDA/Vulkan/Metal/SYCL as required
familiarity with ML model formats and basic audio/ML concepts
student_project_ideas: Integrate audio.cpp TTS output into a small mobile or robot demo (e.g. Raspberry Pi/edge device) and compare latency and resource usage across CPU and a supported GPU backend.

Benchmark multiple ASR models from audio.cpp on classroom edge hardware (CPU-only and a consumer GPU) to evaluate WER, latency and memory trade-offs, and produce a report with recommendations for real-time transcription deployment.

tools.name: opengeos/segment-geospatial
tools.desc: A Python package for segmenting geospatial data with the Segment Anything Model (SAM)

cls.summary: SamGeo is a Python package that applies the Segment Anything Model (SAM) to geospatial raster data (GeoTIFFs) to produce vector segmentations and visualise or serve results.
cls.what_it_does: SamGeo downloads map tiles or loads GeoTIFFs, runs SAM / HQ-SAM (and variants) to produce image segmentations, and exports results as common geospatial vector formats (GeoPackage, Shapefile, GeoJSON). It includes interactive marker creation, text-prompt segmentation, a REST API, and a QGIS plugin, making it usable in both scripting and desktop GIS contexts.
cls.trl_rationale: The project is multi-year (created 2023), has many stars, a published citation, PyPI and conda-forge packages, an accompanying QGIS plugin and REST API, indicating production-ready tooling and real-world use; repository activity is recent. These indicators support a TRL of 7 (production-ready) rather than an experimental prototype.
prerequisites: PyTorch / CUDA knowledge for GPU acceleration
GDAL / rasterio and basic GIS concepts
Optional: QGIS familiarity for plugin use
student_project_ideas: Use SamGeo to segment rooftop areas from a time series of Sentinel-2 GeoTIFFs and compare urban expansion metrics by exporting polygons to GeoPackage and analysing area change in QGIS or Python.

Build a small REST service using SamGeo's API stack to accept uploaded GeoTIFFs, run SAM-based segmentation for a target class (e.g. water bodies), and visualise results on a web map (Leaflet or folium).

tools.name: mbloch/mapshaper
tools.desc: Tools for editing Shapefile, GeoJSON, TopoJSON and CSV files

cls.summary: Mapshaper is a JavaScript tool and web UI for editing and simplifying vector GIS files (Shapefile, GeoJSON, TopoJSON, CSV) and preparing them for mapping or analysis.
cls.what_it_does: Mapshaper lets you import common GIS vector formats, simplify and edit geometry, manipulate attribute tables, clip/erase/dissolve features, and export to multiple formats. It is usable either via a browser-based interactive UI or command-line programs (mapshaper, mapshaper-xl) and is notable for handling large files in-browser and providing a concise command reference and scripting workflow.
cls.trl_rationale: Mapshaper has an active repository (created 2013), thousands of stars, maintained docs and a public web UI, and long-term usage in the GIS community, indicating mature, widely adopted software (TRL 8).
student_project_ideas: Create a workflow that ingests large GeoJSON building footprints, uses mapshaper to simplify geometries and dissolve attributes, then visualises results in a web map (e.g. Leaflet) to study performance trade-offs between simplification level and rendering speed.

Compare file size and topology outcomes by converting a detailed Shapefile to TopoJSON with mapshaper and GDAL, then run a small analysis of download times and browser rendering for a city-scale dataset.

tools.name: cdcseacave/openMVS
tools.desc: open Structure-fom-Motion and Multi-View Stereo reconstruction library

cls.summary: OpenMVS is an open-source C++ library that converts camera poses and a sparse point cloud into a dense point-cloud, watertight mesh, refined geometry and textured 3D models from image sets.
cls.what_it_does: OpenMVS performs the dense multi-view stereo steps of a photogrammetry pipeline: it generates dense point clouds, reconstructs meshes, refines geometry to recover fine detail, and produces textured meshes. It is used as a command-line/C++ library (with Python scripts provided for scalable pipelines) that consumes camera poses and sparse SfM output and outputs high-quality textured 3D models suitable for mapping, inspection and visualization.
cls.trl_rationale: The repository is long-lived (created 2015), has many stars/forks, recent active commits and CI/binary artifacts mentioned in the README, and is widely cited/used in the photogrammetry community, indicating a mature, well-adopted project.
prerequisites: familiarity with photogrammetry / SfM outputs (camera poses, sparse point clouds)
student_project_ideas: Use OpenMVG (or COLMAP) to produce camera poses from an image set, then run OpenMVS to produce a textured mesh and evaluate geometric accuracy against a LiDAR scan.

Integrate OpenMVS into a small digital-twin pipeline: capture drone images of a small structure, build a textured mesh with OpenMVS, and deploy a lightweight viewer (e.g. three.js) to visualise changes over time.

tools.name: JohnSnowLabs/spark-nlp
tools.desc: State of the Art Natural Language Processing

cls.summary: Spark NLP is a mature, open-source NLP library that provides scalable, production-ready natural language processing and pretrained transformer models on top of Apache Spark for JVM and Python environments.
cls.what_it_does: Spark NLP solves large-scale text processing and NLP model deployment by providing a wide collection of pretrained pipelines and annotators (tokenization, POS, NER, embeddings, translation, QA, text generation, speech and vision connectors) that run natively in Apache Spark. It is used by importing its Spark/PySpark package and composing annotator pipelines or loading pretrained models; it is notable for multi-language support, extensive pretrained model catalog, and integrations for TensorFlow, ONNX, OpenVINO and llama.cpp model formats.
cls.trl_rationale: The project is long-lived (created 2017), widely used and actively maintained with thousands of stars, many pretrained models and documented production integrations; this indicates a mature, widely adopted library (TRL 8).
prerequisites: Apache Spark (cluster or local) and JVM (Java 8/11/17) knowledge
student_project_ideas: Build a Spark-based pipeline that ingests equipment maintenance logs, applies NER and sentiment analysis with Spark NLP, and correlates extracted entities to failure reports to prioritise maintenance tasks.
Integrate a Spark NLP translation and QA pipeline into a multi-lingual digital twin data ingestion flow to normalise and extract structured events from operator reports for downstream analytics.

tools.name: langroid/langroid
tools.desc: Harness LLMs with Multi-Agent Programming

cls.summary: Langroid is a Python framework for building and coordinating multi-agent applications that use large language models (LLMs) and retrieval tools.
cls.what_it_does: Langroid provides abstractions for Agents, Tasks, LLM adapters, tools/function-calling and vector stores so developers can construct multi-agent workflows and retrieval-augmented applications. It is used as a library in Python projects and supports many LLMs (OpenAI-compatible APIs, local models) and MCP tool adapters to integrate external tool servers. Notable aspects are its multi-agent orchestration primitives, emphasis on developer ergonomics, and explicit support for local LLMs and MCP tool adapters.
cls.trl_rationale: The repository is mature (created 2023-04, actively maintained with recent releases and a 0.68.0 tag), has many stars and public examples, and the README cites companies using it in production and published case studies, indicating production-readiness rather than a research prototype.
prerequisites: familiarity with LLM concepts and APIs (OpenAI, local LLMs)
student_project_ideas: Build a two-agent pipeline that ingests engineering documents (PDFs), uses Langroid's RAG/DocChatAgent to extract structured requirements, and outputs a CSV of traced requirements linked to source passages.

Create an automated multi-agent test harness where one agent generates test cases in natural language for a software module and another agent converts them to executable unit tests (e.g., pytest), integrating Langroid with a CI runner.

tools.name: raullenchai/Rapid-MLX
tools.desc: Rapid-MLX is an open-source (Apache 2.0) OpenAI- and Anthropic-compatible LLM inference server for Apple Silicon, built on MLX, focused on reliable tool calling for coding agents. Up to 4× faster than Apple's MLX (mlx-lm) on the same weights.

cls.summary: Rapid-MLX is an open-source local LLM inference server optimised for Apple Silicon that provides OpenAI- and Anthropic-compatible APIs and focussed tool-calling for coding agents.
cls.what_it_does: Rapid-MLX runs and serves quantised LLMs locally on Apple Silicon, exposing OpenAI- and Anthropic-compatible endpoints so agents and apps can call models without cloud APIs. It focuses on reliable tool-calling, continuous batching and prompt/KV caching for higher throughput and lower latency compared with other MLX-based servers.
cls.trl_rationale: The project is actively maintained, has substantial community interest (4k+ stars), install scripts and documentation, and published performance comparisons, indicating beta-level maturity; however the repository is only ~265 days old so it lacks the multi-year production track record required for TRL 7+.
prerequisites: Apple Silicon Mac (M1/M2/M4/M5 family) or compatible environment
familiarity with CLI and installing model weights
basic knowledge of OpenAI/Anthropic API semantics and MLX concepts
student_project_ideas: Build a small coding-assistant agent that uses Rapid-MLX as the local backend and evaluates tool-calling reliability by integrating a unit-test runner and a code formatter to automatically patch and test student code.

Measure and compare inference latency and throughput of a quantised Qwen model served by Rapid-MLX versus mlx-lm and oMLX on Apple Silicon, then visualise results and investigate effects of different KV-cache strategies.

tools.name: introlab/rtabmap
tools.desc: RTAB-Map library and standalone application

cls.summary: RTAB-Map is a mature open-source RGB-D / LiDAR SLAM library and application for real-time long-term mapping, loop-closure detection and localisation used widely with ROS and mobile/desktop robots.
cls.what_it_does: RTAB-Map performs simultaneous localisation and mapping (SLAM) by processing RGB-D, stereo, monocular or LiDAR sensor streams to produce consistent 2D/3D maps and pose estimates with loop-closure detection. It is used as a library or standalone application and integrates with ROS/ROS2, Docker and common vision/point-cloud libraries; notable features are long-term mapping, multiple sensor support and an extensive C++ API and command-line tools.
cls.trl_rationale: The project is long-lived (created 2014), has many stars/forks, official releases, ROS/ROS2 packages and Docker images and active recent commits, indicating a mature, widely adopted SLAM implementation rather than an experimental prototype.
prerequisites: basic ROS / ROS2 knowledge (for ROS integration)
familiarity with OpenCV and point-cloud concepts (PCL)
student_project_ideas: Build a mobile robot mapping demo using RTAB-Map with a ROS 2 stack and an RGB-D camera to create and visualise 3D maps, then evaluate localisation robustness across repeated runs.

Integrate RTAB-Map with a LiDAR sensor to produce a fused RGB-D + LiDAR map and compare drift and loop-closure performance against an alternative SLAM library (e.g., Cartographer) on an indoor dataset.

tools.name: antvis/L7
tools.desc: 🌎 Large-scale WebGL-powered Geospatial Data Visualization analysis engine.

cls.summary: L7 is an open-source WebGL-based library for large-scale, interactive geospatial data visualization in web applications.
cls.what_it_does: L7 renders large volumes of geographic data (GeoJSON, CSV, raster) using WebGL to produce interactive 2D/3D map visualizations and chart-like map layers (points, lines, polygons, heatmaps, raster). It is used as a data-driven map visualization engine that plugs into different base maps (Mapbox, AMap) and provides many layer types and style mappings for spatial analysis and dashboards.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository created in 2018 with ~4k stars, active recent commits and an ecosystem of related projects (L7Draw, L7Plot, LarkMap), indicating mature, widely adopted open-source software rather than an experimental prototype.
student_project_ideas: Build an interactive web dashboard that loads city open-data (GeoJSON/csv) and uses L7 to compare traffic density (heatmap) against infrastructure locations, integrating a time slider to animate changes.

Create a digital-twin style visualisation combining IoT time-series (MQTT or timestream) with L7 to render real-time sensor data on a 3D city map and evaluate visualization performance for large point clouds.

tools.name: gee-community/geemap
tools.desc: A Python package for interactive geospatial analysis and visualization with Google Earth Engine.

cls.summary: geemap is a mature Python library that provides interactive mapping, analysis and visualization of Google Earth Engine datasets inside Jupyter/Colab and related environments.
cls.what_it_does: Geemap connects the Google Earth Engine (GEE) cloud platform to the Python/Jupyter ecosystem, letting users display GEE image and vector layers, run interactive inspectors and time-series tools, export maps and imagery, and convert GEE JavaScript code to Python. It is used inside Jupyter/Colab/Streamlit and builds on ipyleaflet and ipywidgets to make interactive geospatial exploration and basic analysis straightforward for research and teaching. Notable aspects are large example gallery, notebook workflows, and tooling for exporting and animating satellite-derived outputs.
cls.trl_rationale: The project has a multi-year history (created 2020), thousands of stars, active development with recent commits, published book and NASA grant support, and a large examples/tutorial collection—evidence of broad adoption and maturity.
prerequisites: Google Earth Engine account and basic familiarity with GEE concepts
student_project_ideas: Use geemap and Google Earth Engine to create a land-cover change detection workflow for a region using Landsat/Sentinel time series and validate results against local sample data.
Build an interactive dashboard (Jupyter/Streamlit) that uses geemap to visualise flood extent time-series from SAR data and export animated GIFs and geotiffs for reports.

tools.name: FedML-AI/FedML
tools.desc: FEDML - The unified and scalable ML library for large-scale distributed training, model serving, and federated learning. FEDML Launch, a cross-cloud scheduler, further enables running any AI jobs on any GPU cloud or on-premise cluster. Built on this library, TensorOpera AI (https://TensorOpera.ai) is your generative AI platform at scale.

cls.summary: FedML is an open-source Python library for federated learning, distributed training, and model serving that helps run ML jobs across clouds, clusters and edge devices.
cls.what_it_does: FedML provides APIs and tooling to train and deploy machine learning models in distributed and federated settings, including on-device training for smartphones and multi-node/cloud GPU training. It includes scheduler/MLOps components (branded TensorOpera in the README) to provision resources and run jobs, and notable for combining federated learning primitives with scalable job orchestration for cross-cloud and edge scenarios.
cls.trl_rationale: The repository dates from 2020, has a large community (4k+ stars, many forks), active recent commits, and positions itself as a production-capable ML library and MLOps stack (TensorOpera). These indicators show mature, real-world use and ecosystem adoption consistent with TRL 8.
prerequisites: familiarity with cloud/Kubernetes and Docker for deployment
student_project_ideas: Implement a privacy-preserving federated learning experiment using FedML to train an image classifier across several simulated edge nodes and compare performance and communication cost against centralized training.

Integrate FedML with a Kubernetes cluster to create an automated pipeline that schedules distributed training jobs on heterogeneous GPU nodes and evaluate job throughput and cost across different cluster configurations.

tools.name: atopile/atopile
tools.desc: Design circuit boards with code! ✨ Get software-like design reuse 🚀, validation, version control and collaboration in hardware; starting with electronics ⚡️

cls.summary: Atopile is a code-first toolchain and language for designing electronic circuit boards with reusable, parametric modules that compile to KiCad layouts and BOMs.
cls.what_it_does: Atopile provides a declarative language (.ato), compiler and toolchain that let engineers capture requirements, parametric constraints and reusable modules for PCB design, automatically select parts and update KiCad board files. It is used via a CLI and a VS Code/Cursor extension and notable for combining constraint solving, component picking and KiCad-native layout in a code-centric workflow.
cls.trl_rationale: The project is actively maintained, has many stars and forks, a VS Code extension, published examples and a package registry—evidence of real-world use; it was created in Dec 2023 and has been developed since, supporting a production-ready judgement rather than an early prototype.
prerequisites: Python tooling (editable installs and development workflows)
VS Code or Cursor for the editor extension
student_project_ideas: Create a parametric sensor breakout board library in atopile that automatically selects resistors and connectors and generates KiCad files and a BOM for fabrication.
Develop a CI pipeline that runs atopile builds and automated design checks for a multi-board embedded system, integrating outputs into a simple dashboard or release artifact.

tools.name: HakanSeven12/OpenCADStudio
tools.desc: A CAD application built with Rust — 2D/3D drawing, DWG/DXF support, and GPU-accelerated rendering

cls.summary: Open CAD Studio is an open-source cross-platform 2D drafting and 3D modeling application that reads and writes DWG/DXF and provides GPU-accelerated viewports for desktop and web.
cls.what_it_does: It provides a full CAD application for precise 2D drafting and kernel-backed 3D solid modelling with native DWG/DXF read/write, layout/plot tools, and GPU-accelerated rendering via wgpu. The project ships desktop installers for Windows, Linux and macOS and a web app, and supports plugins, headless conversion and a JSON automation API for extensible workflows.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository is active with published desktop releases, installers and a web app, many stars and recent commits indicating an established beta; however the project is under 1 year old (created ~240 days ago) so TRL is limited to Beta (6) by the age rule.
prerequisites: Rust toolchain to build from source (optional if using releases)
student_project_ideas: Create a lab exercise where students import a DWG site plan into Open CAD Studio, edit layers and annotate dimensions to produce print-ready layouts and PDFs.

Develop a plugin or headless script using the JSON automation API to batch-convert DWG/DXF files to STL/STEP and evaluate geometry fidelity against a reference (combine with a simple mesh-processing script).

tools.name: Nixtla/nixtla
tools.desc: TimeGPT-2.1: production ready pre-trained Time Series Foundation Model  for forecasting and anomaly detection. Generative pretrained transformer for time series trained on over 100B data points. It's capable of accurately predicting various domains such as retail, electricity, finance, and IoT with just a few lines of code 🚀.

cls.summary: TimeGPT is a production-ready foundation model and SDK for time-series forecasting and anomaly detection, available via an API and deployable in customer infrastructure.
cls.what_it_does: TimeGPT provides zero-shot and fine-tunable forecasting and anomaly-detection for time series across domains (retail, electricity, finance, IoT) through a Python SDK and hosted API; it also supports deployments inside environments like Snowflake and integrations with distributed compute frameworks. It is notable for being a pre-trained transformer foundation model trained on very large time-series datasets and for offering prediction intervals, exogenous variables, and multi-series forecasts with minimal code.
cls.trl_rationale: The repository is several years old (created 2021), has many stars and active recent commits, offers an SDK, documented API and Snowflake deployment scripts, and claims production readiness — evidence consistent with production-ready use (TRL 7) though it is not a de-facto standard with large ecosystem (not TRL 8+).
prerequisites: API key / account for hosted model (optional if self-deploying)
student_project_ideas: Compare TimeGPT forecasts against classical methods (ARIMA/Prophet) on an IoT sensor dataset, quantify accuracy and calibration of prediction intervals, and produce a short report on operational implications.
Deploy TimeGPT forecasting in Snowflake for a small retail sales dataset and build a dashboard that uses forecasts and anomaly detection to trigger alerts for inventory planning.

tools.name: TarrySingh/Artificial-Intelligence-Deep-Learning-Machine-Learning-Tutorials
tools.desc: Synapsa Commons: free, hands-on AI courses that run anywhere (Colab, Kaggle, Binder, Codespaces, Jupyter). EU AI Act conformity evidence, model validation, predictive maintenance, document extraction, retrieval and RAG, AI agents and MCP, a simulated humanoid. Every lesson autograded. From the team building Synapsa.

cls.summary: A large, mature collection of runnable, autograded hands-on AI lessons and mini-courses covering model engineering, governance, RAG/retrieval, agents, predictive maintenance and a simulated humanoid.
cls.what_it_does: This repository provides 100+ Jupyter notebook lessons that run on Colab, Kaggle, Binder, Codespaces or locally and teach practical AI engineering tasks such as model validation, predictive maintenance, document extraction, retrieval & RAG, agent loops and MCP patterns.
