Lessons are autograded, designed to be reproducible evidence for audits (EU AI Act, model-risk) and include runnable code, checks and links to launch on common notebook platforms.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository created in 2017, actively maintained and widely used (many stars, recent pushes), with a large, polished set of runnable lessons and completed programmes that indicate production-ready educational maturity rather than an early prototype.
student_project_ideas: Build a small predictive-maintenance pipeline using one of the predictive-maintenance lessons, adapt its sensor-to-alarm economics to a real or simulated dataset, and produce a validation report suitable for an audit.

Extend a document-extraction lesson to add a retriever+RAG pipeline that answers business questions from a set of invoices, measure extraction accuracy and produce uncertainty/calibration plots for a model-risk portfolio.

tools.name: MrNeRF/LichtFeld-Studio
tools.desc: Train, inspect, edit, automate, and export 3D Gaussian Splatting scenes from a single native application.

cls.summary: LichtFeld Studio is a native C++/CUDA application for training, inspecting, editing and exporting 3D Gaussian-splatting reconstructions from COLMAP-style photo datasets.
cls.what_it_does: It trains 3D Gaussian Splatting models from multi-view photo datasets, provides real-time interactive visualisation and editing of Gaussian components, and exports results to common formats or a standalone HTML viewer. The app is notable for integrating training, inspection, editing, Python plugins and automation (MCP) in one workstation with native CUDA performance.
cls.trl_rationale: The project is multi-year (created 2023-07), has a large star/fork count, active development (recent pushes), extensive docs and prebuilt binaries — indicating maturity and adoption beyond prototype. It is not a de-facto standard (TRL 9) but is mature and widely used in its niche.
prerequisites: familiarity with COLMAP-style multi-view datasets and Python for plugins
student_project_ideas: Use LichtFeld Studio to reconstruct a small outdoor scene from photos, then export the result to a standalone HTML viewer and compare reconstruction quality and rendering performance against an Instant-NGP or NeRF reconstruction.

Develop a Python plugin for LichtFeld Studio that automates dataset pre-processing (COLMAP pipeline) and post-processing (sparsification/POPSpa parameters), and evaluate how automated parameter sweeps affect final model size and visual fidelity.

tools.name: NVIDIA/skills
tools.desc: Agent Skills for NVIDIA products — install into Claude Code, Codex, and other coding agents to run Physical AI, robotics, simulation, CUDA, and RAG workflows end to end.

cls.summary: A curated catalog of NVIDIA-verified 'skills' (instruction modules) that teach coding agents how to use NVIDIA software for robotics, simulation, CUDA and RAG workflows.
cls.what_it_does: This repository publishes portable instruction sets (skills) that agents such as Claude Code or Codex can load to run end-to-end NVIDIA workflows (Physical AI, robotics, simulation, CUDA libraries, and retrieval-augmented generation). It is used by installing the skills package via the skills CLI so an LLM-based coding agent can invoke guided API usage and workflows; notable aspects are NVIDIA verification, a large catalog covering multiple products, and an automated sync/mirroring pipeline.
cls.trl_rationale: Active, well-starred NVIDIA repo with daily syncs and published docs indicates a beta-stage, supported project; however the repository is only ~265 days old (under one year), so it lacks the long-term track record required for TRL 7+.
prerequisites: skills CLI (Node/npm) and familiarity with npx
Access to the target coding agent (e.g. Claude Code, Codex) and any required agent accounts
Familiarity with NVIDIA tools (CUDA, Omniverse, cuOpt) and GPUs for practical use
student_project_ideas: Create a reproducible lab where a coding agent uses an NVIDIA skill to construct and run a small CUDA kernel for a numerical method (e.g. matrix multiply) and profile performance on a GPU.
Build an agent-driven pipeline that uses an Omniverse or robotics skill to run a simulated robot task (motion planning + simulation) and automatically collect verification test logs for analysis.

tools.name: nathanhoad/godot_dialogue_manager
tools.desc: A powerful nonlinear dialogue system for Godot

cls.summary: Dialogue Manager 4 is a Godot 4.6+ editor addon and runtime that lets developers create branching, stateless dialogue scripts and integrate them into games.
cls.what_it_does: It provides an in-editor dialogue format, a visual/structured workflow and a runtime for executing branching conversations in Godot games. Developers install it as an addon (GDScript) or use a C# wrapper, then reference the dialogue runtime from game code to present choices, conditions and mutations. It is notable for being a mature, widely used community addon with full documentation and example projects.
cls.trl_rationale: The repository is active since 2022, has a large user base (≈4k stars), recent commits and documentation, and is used in production Godot projects; this demonstrates production-ready maturity rather than an experimental prototype.
prerequisites: basic GDScript or C# usage in Godot

tools.name: mapnik/mapnik
tools.desc: Mapnik is an open source toolkit for developing mapping applications

cls.summary: Mapnik is a mature open-source C++ toolkit for rendering maps and producing map tiles from spatial data sources.
cls.what_it_does: Mapnik provides C++ libraries and bindings (including Python) to read spatial datasources (PostGIS, shapefiles, raster formats via GDAL/OGR) and render styled maps and map tiles for web and server environments. It is used to build map servers and cartographic rendering pipelines and is notable for its performance, multi-threaded design and long history in the open-source GIS ecosystem.
cls.trl_rationale: Mapnik is an established project (created 2011) with thousands of stars, many contributors, and active development; it is widely used for map rendering and tile servers, which supports a mature TRL rating.
prerequisites: GDAL/OGR and common geospatial libraries (PROJ, Freetype, Cairo)
basic GIS concepts (projections, vector/raster data) and optionally Python for bindings
student_project_ideas: Build a small tile server that renders styled map tiles from PostGIS using Mapnik and serve them to a simple Leaflet web client, demonstrating projection handling and layer styling.
Compare rendering performance and visual output between Mapnik and an alternative renderer (e.g. Mapbox GL or rasterized GDAL output) for a local urban dataset, profiling CPU and memory usage.

tools.name: mesa/mesa
tools.desc: Mesa is an open-source Python library for agent-based modeling, ideal for simulating complex systems and exploring emergent behaviors.

cls.summary: Mesa is a mature, open-source Python library for building, visualising and analysing agent-based models of complex systems.
cls.what_it_does: Mesa provides core components (agent schedulers, spatial grids, data collectors) and a browser-based visualization interface to create and run agent-based simulations in Python, and it integrates with Python data tools for analysis. It is notable for offering a NetLogo-like ABM framework in Python with an example model library, documentation and Docker support for running interactive demos.
cls.trl_rationale: Mesa has been actively developed since 2014, has many stars and forks, stable releases and extensive documentation and examples, and is widely used in teaching and research; these indicators support a high maturity rating (TRL 8).
prerequisites: basic modelling concepts (agents, state update rules)
familiarity with pandas/matplotlib or Jupyter for analysis
student_project_ideas: Implement an urban evacuation model in Mesa that couples a pedestrian agent layer with a simple traffic model and visualises results in the browser; analyse evacuation times using pandas.
Build an epidemiological ABM (SEIR agents) with spatial heterogeneity and compare intervention strategies using Monte Carlo runs and uncertainty analysis, producing summary plots in Jupyter.

tools.name: pyvista/pyvista
tools.desc: 3D visualization and mesh analysis for science and engineering

cls.summary: PyVista is a mature Python library for 3D visualization and mesh analysis used in scientific and engineering workflows.
cls.what_it_does: PyVista provides NumPy-native data structures, mesh filters (clipping, smoothing, thresholding, etc.), and a unified plotting API that runs in notebooks, scripts, CI and apps to visualise point clouds, surfaces and volumetric meshes. It wraps and stabilises the VTK graphics stack behind a Pythonic interface, plus a CLI for quick plotting, conversion and validation, making it easy to integrate into analysis and automation pipelines.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository created in 2017 with ~3.8k stars, active recent commits, extensive documentation, tests and NumFOCUS affiliation; these indicate a mature, widely adopted library built on VTK and used in production and research, so TRL 8 is appropriate.
student_project_ideas: Use PyVista to visualise and compare finite-element meshes from an FEA solver (exported to VTK/VTU) and implement a script to compute and plot element quality metrics and filtered views of poorly conditioned elements.

Build an interactive Jupyter application that loads LiDAR point-cloud data, performs terrain segmentation and displays coloured point clouds and surface meshes using PyVista, combining it with PDAL or laspy for preprocessing.

tools.name: Revolutionary-Games/Thrive
tools.desc: The main repository for the development of the evolution game Thrive.

cls.summary: Thrive is an open-source C# game built with Godot that simulates evolution and organism development in a sandbox environment.
cls.what_it_does: Thrive implements a sandbox evolutionary simulation presented as a playable game: users control organisms that evolve and interact in a simulated environment. It is developed in C# with Godot and includes assets, simulation parameters, and tools for contributors; notable for its long-running open-source community and large code + asset base.
cls.trl_rationale: The repository is long-running (created 2012), has many stars and forks, active recent commits, documentation and a community — indicating production-ready, community-driven maturity rather than an experimental prototype.
prerequisites: Git LFS for large asset files
student_project_ideas: Modify Thrive's simulation parameters or organism behaviour to measure and report emergent population dynamics under different selection pressures (combine with data analysis in Python).
Extend or replace a subsystem in the Godot/C# codebase (for example sensory/AI or rendering) and evaluate performance and player-observable effects.

tools.name: MattParkerDev/SharpIDE
tools.desc: A modern, cross platform IDE for .NET, built with .NET & Godot

cls.summary: SharpIDE is an open-source, cross-platform integrated development environment for .NET built with .NET and the Godot engine.
cls.what_it_does: SharpIDE provides editing, code completion, signature help, refactorings and debugging features for .NET/C# projects, with specific support mentioned for Razor syntax and a solution/project picker. It is used as a desktop IDE you build/run locally; notable points are that it is implemented in C# and Godot and targets cross-platform operation as an alternative to commercial .NET IDEs.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository is ~1 year old with active development, many stars and recent pushes, but the README marks the project as WIP and several features (NuGet, Test Explorer) are still 'WIP', so it fits a beta-level maturity rather than proven production usage.

tools.name: Keychron/Keychron-Keyboards-Hardware-Design
tools.desc: Industrial design files for Keychron keyboards and mice. 100+ models with CAD assets in STEP, DXF, DWG, and PDF. Source-available, with commercial use allowed for original compatible accessories within the license terms.

cls.summary: A large, source-available collection of production-grade CAD files (STEP, DWG, DXF, PDFs) for Keychron keyboards and mice useful for studying and remixing real product hardware designs.
cls.what_it_does: Provides downloadable CAD and manufacturing assets for many Keychron keyboard and mouse models so users can inspect dimensions, internal packaging, plates, cases and PCBs. It is used by opening the provided STEP/DWG/DXF files in CAD software to study or remix designs and to produce compatible accessories or prototypes. Notable for its extensive, production-grade model coverage and frequent repository updates, making it a practical reference for learning industrial design and hardware packaging.
cls.trl_rationale: The repository is active, widely starred (3.8k stars) and contains production-grade files with frequent updates, indicating a mature community resource; however the repo is under one year old (created 2026-04-04), so despite strong activity it best matches a Beta/TR L6 level rather than long-term production/adoption TRL 7+.
prerequisites: familiarity with CAD workflows and file formats
understanding of hardware packaging and PCB basics
student_project_ideas: Remix an existing Keychron plate and case to create a custom-layout keyboard, then 3D print the case and validate fit using the STEP files (combine with FreeCAD or Fusion 360).
Integrate a provided PCB model with custom key mapping and build a prototype flashed with QMK/ZMK firmware, documenting mechanical and electrical integration and producing manufacturing drawings.

tools.name: SciSharp/LLamaSharp
tools.desc: A C#/.NET library to run LLM (🦙LLaMA/LLaVA) on your local device efficiently.

cls.summary: LLamaSharp is a C#/.NET library that runs LLaMA-family and other LLMs locally on CPU or GPU, providing higher-level APIs, RAG support and platform-specific native backends.
cls.what_it_does: LLamaSharp lets developers load GGUF-converted LLMs and run inference efficiently on local machines by using native backends (CPU, CUDA, Vulkan, Metal). It is used as a drop-in library in .NET applications (console, ASP.NET, Unity, Blazor) and provides examples, integrations and documentation to build chatbots, agents and RAG-enabled apps without calling cloud LLM APIs.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository is >3 years old, has many stars and forks, active recent commits and full documentation and examples; it provides published backend packages and integrations which indicate production-ready maturity rather than a fragile prototype.
prerequisites: Familiarity with LLM model formats (GGUF, PyTorch/HuggingFace) and basic tokenisation
Appropriate GPU drivers and runtime for chosen backend (CUDA/Vulkan/Metal) if using GPU
student_project_ideas: Build a local, privacy-preserving question-answering web app that uses LLamaSharp with a document RAG pipeline (e.g., index PDF manuals and implement retrieval + LLamaSharp inference in an ASP.NET backend).
Integrate LLamaSharp into a Unity application to create an on-device NPC dialog system that uses quantized GGUF models and evaluates latency and memory trade-offs between CPU and GPU backends.

tools.name: opengeos/leafmap
tools.desc: A Python package for interactive mapping and geospatial analysis with minimal coding in a Jupyter environment

cls.summary: Leafmap is an open-source Python package for interactive mapping and geospatial analysis in Jupyter environments, letting users load, visualise and run common GIS analyses with minimal code.
cls.what_it_does: Leafmap provides a high-level API and GUI components to create interactive maps in Jupyter (Colab, Notebook, Lab) and to visualise vector and raster geospatial data, switch mapping backends, add web map services and produce 2D/3D map views. It integrates common geospatial libraries (e.g. geopandas, rasterio, WhiteboxTools) so users can perform spatial analysis and create interactive map-based workflows without writing low-level mapping code.
cls.trl_rationale: The project is mature and well-adopted: created in 2021, thousands of stars, active recent commits, published on PyPI and conda-forge and integrates with many established geospatial libraries; this indicates wide community use and stability.
prerequisites: basic GIS concepts (vector/raster) and familiarity with geopandas/rasterio for advanced analysis
student_project_ideas: Build an interactive Jupyter dashboard that ingests drone-derived orthophotos and vector boundaries, performs simple WhiteboxTools hydrological analysis, and visualises the results with leafmap.

Create a map-based web notebook that overlays infrastructure datasets (roads, utilities) and runs spatial queries (buffering, intersection) using geopandas and leafmap to support a small asset-management study.

tools.name: scenario-labs/skills
tools.desc: Get production-ready images, video, audio, and 3D from any AI agent: skills that pick the right model, price before spending, and keep characters and brands consistent through the Scenario MCP, plus expert teams that drive Blender, Maya, ZBrush, Unreal, and Unity.

cls.summary: A large collection of Agent Skills that teach AI coding agents how to produce images, video, audio, textures and 3D assets via the Scenario MCP and to drive DCC and game-engine tools on a local machine.
cls.what_it_does: This repository supplies Agent Skills (following the Agent Skills format) that let AI agents call the Scenario MCP server to generate production-ready media (images, video, audio, textures, 3D) and includes expert skill families that drive desktop DCC and game engines (Blender, Maya, ZBrush, Unreal, Unity, Godot, Roblox) when those applications are installed. It is used through an npx installer/skills CLI and requires a Scenario MCP connection (OAuth or API key); notable for its very large collection of pre-built skills and integrations for creative pipelines.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository is active, well-starred and maintained with releases and an installer, indicating beta-level maturity; it is under 1 year old so cannot be rated above TRL 6 by the stated rules.
prerequisites: Scenario account or API key and access to Scenario MCP
Desktop DCC or game-engine installations for expert tool families (Blender, Maya, Unreal, Unity, etc.)
student_project_ideas: Build an automated pipeline that uses a Scenario skill to generate game-ready textures and import them into Blender to texture a simple asset, demonstrating the agent-driven asset pipeline and versioning.

Compare quality and cost by creating the same 2D concept art via two different Scenario image-generation skills and tabulate model choice, price estimate, and final image consistency as a short study on production trade-offs.

tools.name: Tresjs/tres
tools.desc: Declarative ThreeJS using Vue Components

cls.summary: Tres is a Vue-based library that lets you build Three.js 3D scenes using declarative Vue components for web visualisations.
cls.what_it_does: Tres provides a Vue custom renderer that maps Vue components to Three.js objects so developers can compose 3D scenes with familiar Vue syntax and tooling. It is used in web applications for interactive 3D visualisation, demos and front-end digital twin interfaces, notable for being fully typed, Vite-powered and kept up to date with Three.js features.
cls.trl_rationale: The repository is mature and active (created 2022, recent pushes in 2026), has substantial community interest (several thousand stars), an ecosystem of packages and documentation, which indicates wide adoption and stable API for web 3D projects.
student_project_ideas: Build an interactive web visualisation of a mechanical assembly using Tres to load geometry (glTF) and provide animated component states and basic user controls.
Create a browser-based digital twin dashboard that streams mock sensor data and updates 3D object properties in Tres to demonstrate real-time state visualisation.

tools.name: PixelGuys/Cubyz
tools.desc: Voxel sandbox game with a large render distance, procedurally generated content and some cool graphical effects.

cls.summary: Cubyz is an open-source 3D voxel sandbox game written in Zig with procedural generation, large view distances and custom crafting mechanics.
cls.what_it_does: Cubyz provides a Minecraft-like voxel sandbox where worlds are procedurally generated and rendered with level-of-detail and 3D chunks to allow very large view distances and no height/depth limits. It is distributed as source (Zig) with build/run scripts for Windows and Linux and includes gameplay and content contribution guidelines. The project is notable for its Zig implementation, emphasis on rendering/LOD and procedural crafting mechanics.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository is long-lived (created 2019), has many stars and an active maintainer with recent pushes, releases and user-facing binaries — indicating production-ready maturity; high issue count suggests active use and maintenance rather than early-stage.

tools.name: mevdschee/php-crud-api
tools.desc: Single file PHP script that adds a REST API to a SQL database

cls.summary: A single-file PHP script that automatically exposes a RESTful CRUD API for a SQL database (MySQL, PostgreSQL, SQL Server or SQLite), including GeoJSON/spatial support and OpenAPI generation.
cls.what_it_does: PHP-CRUD-API turns an existing SQL database into a ready-to-use REST API by uploading a single PHP file or installing via Composer; it handles CRUD, filtering, pagination, relations and can serve spatial data as GeoJSON and generate OpenAPI docs. It is notable for its single-file deployability, multi-database support and built-in permissions, mapping and middleware facilities.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository created in 2015, widely used (thousands of stars and forks), actively maintained with recent commits and releases; evidence shows a stable, production-capable project and an ecosystem of integrations, so it is mature and widely adopted.
prerequisites: Familiarity with SQL databases and PDO drivers
student_project_ideas: Build a small sensor-data pipeline: store sensor rows in PostgreSQL with PostGIS and use PHP-CRUD-API to publish a GeoJSON endpoint consumed by a web map (leaflet) to visualise device locations and telemetry.

Create a multi-tenant mock backend for a capstone project: deploy api.php to provide CRUD endpoints, implement table/column permission rules, and connect a frontend (React) to exercise authentication, authorization and API filtering.

tools.name: gumyr/build123d
tools.desc: A python CAD programming library

cls.summary: build123d is a Python library for parametric, scriptable BREP CAD modelling built on the Open Cascade kernel for creating precise 2D and 3D parts for manufacturing and 3D printing.
cls.what_it_does: It provides a Pythonic, operator-driven API to construct and modify edges, faces and solids (BREP) and to compose parametric models suitable for 3D printing, CNC and CAD export. Users write scripts or use builder contexts to create maintainable, repeatable geometry and export to common CAD formats or other tools. Notable features are explicit 1D/2D/3D geometry classes, algebraic operators for composability, and deep integration with Python tooling and type hints.
cls.trl_rationale: The repository is multi-year (created 2022) with many stars, active maintainers (recent pushes) and thorough documentation (RTD), showing real community adoption beyond a demo; however it is not a de-facto industry standard so TRL 7 (production-ready) is appropriate.
prerequisites: familiarity with Open Cascade concepts helpful
student_project_ideas: Create a parametric mount or bracket generation script that exports STEP/SLDPRT for manufacturing and integrates with a BOM script to demonstrate CAD-as-code and automated part variation.

Build a geometry-driven simulation pipeline: generate parametric parts with build123d, export meshes or STEP to a FEA tool (e.g. CalculiX or a Python FEA library) and run structural tests over a design sweep.

tools.name: enactic/openarm
tools.desc: A fully open-source humanoid arm for physical AI research and deployment in contact-rich environments.

cls.summary: OpenArm is an open-source 7‑DOF humanoid arm platform (hardware + software + simulation) intended for research and deployment in contact-rich human-robot interaction and teleoperation.
cls.what_it_does: OpenArm provides hardware designs, firmware, ROS 2 drivers, simulation models (MuJoCo, Isaac Lab), and data-collection/teleoperation tooling to enable research in compliant humanoid manipulation, imitation learning and teleoperation. It is used by swapping real and simulated nodes (MoveIt 2, ROS 2, MuJoCo/Isaac) so experiments and datasets can be reproduced across labs, and the project publishes CAD, URDF, motor/CAN control libraries and example dataflows.
cls.trl_rationale: The project is a multi-repository ecosystem with docs, simulation models, ROS 2/MoveIt integration and purchasable hardware; it has substantial community interest (3.7k stars), active maintenance and multiple production-oriented repos, supporting a production-ready TRL. The repository is >1 year old and shows real-world use (hardware sales and datasets), so TRL 7 is justified.
prerequisites: familiarity with CAD/assembly and embedded motor control
student_project_ideas: Implement a ROS 2 node for a compliant impedance controller on OpenArm using the openarm_can stack and validate performance in the provided MuJoCo model comparing simulated vs hardware responses.

Build a teleoperation pipeline that streams hand/arm motion from a VR controller to OpenArm using the dora-openarm nodes, and measure task success and safety metrics for a simple contact-rich pick-and-place task.

tools.name: twinnydotdev/twinny
tools.desc: Open-source AI coding assistant for VS Code. Coding agent, code completion, chat, edits and reviews with local or hosted models. Your models, your infrastructure.

cls.summary: Twinny is an open-source VS Code AI coding assistant that provides local-or-hosted model powered code completion, chat, inline edits and code review while letting teams run models on infrastructure they control.
cls.what_it_does: Twinny plugs into Visual Studio Code to provide streamed code completions, conversational code chat, inline edit diffs, automated code review and workspace search using an LLM model server you choose (local or hosted). It is notable for supporting local model runtimes, a team gateway server (twinny-server) for shared deployments, and a privacy-focused, self-hosted workflow with optional paid team features.
cls.trl_rationale: The project is production-ready: active for multiple years, thousands of stars, published in the VS Code Marketplace, documentation, changelog and a complementary twinny-server with team features; evidence shows real users and commercial team pricing. Repository age (>1 year) and active pushes support TRL 7.
prerequisites: basic knowledge of LLM model servers / APIs (optional for advanced config)
student_project_ideas: Build an automated code-review pipeline for a student project repository using twinny's review feature plus GitHub Actions to run reviews on PRs and report results to students.

Compare completion quality and latency by connecting twinny to two different local model backends (llama.cpp and LM Studio), measure suggestion usefulness on an engineering codebase, and write a short evaluation report.

tools.name: AtomicBot-ai/atomic-agent
tools.desc: Atomic Agent is a local-first AI agent. Runs open-weight models on your own machine via llama.cpp.

cls.summary: Atomic Agent is an open-source, local-first AI agent that runs on your machine (or cloud models) to automate browser actions, edit files, run approved commands and remember context across sessions.
cls.what_it_does: Atomic Agent provides a local agent runtime and CLI/desktop app that drives browsers, edits files, runs shell commands, schedules follow-ups and connects to external tools via an MCP protocol. It is notable for running on local quantized models via llama.cpp (so it works on consumer hardware) and for offering packaged installers, a Tauri desktop, and a fusion mode that can combine local and cloud models.
cls.trl_rationale: The project is a well-starred, actively maintained repository with installers, OS packages and desktop releases, indicating beta-level maturity and real users; however the repository is only ~210 days old so it does not show a longer track record required for TRL 7+.
prerequisites: local model files (gguf) and/or cloud model credentials
student_project_ideas: Build a small automation pipeline where Atomic Agent uses Playwright to crawl a web dashboard, extracts key metrics, and pushes them into a time-series database for monitoring (combine with InfluxDB or Prometheus).

Integrate Atomic Agent with a local digital-twin prototype to automate scenario runs: the agent edits input files, triggers simulation runs, and summarises results into a report (combine with a simple simulation tool or Python scripts).

tools.name: Derpyu520/qq-bridge
tools.desc: Bridge between QQ (SnowLuma OneBot v11) and DeepSeek Harness agents: social simulation, safe MCP tools, slang learning and more.

cls.summary: qq-bridge is a Node.js message bridge that forwards events between a OneBot v11 (SnowLuma) QQ backend and DeepSeek Harness (DSH) agents so QQ users can interact with DSH-powered AI agents.
cls.what_it_does: qq-bridge connects a running SnowLuma OneBot v11 instance to a DeepSeek Harness (DSH) deployment, relaying messages, media and replies and exposing a local web console for management. It is used as a runtime bridge alongside SnowLuma and DSH (both run as separate services) and notable for providing prebuilt presets and a DSH plugin installer script to integrate MCP tools and agent behaviours.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository is 84 days old (younger than 90 days) which limits TRL; it has an active prerelease (v0.2.2-rc1), many stars and installation guidance, but no long production track record—README also documents the project being sunsetted, reducing demonstrated maturity.
prerequisites: A running DeepSeek Harness (DSH) web service
A running SnowLuma OneBot v11 WebSocket/HTTP server
Basic familiarity with editing JSON config files and running npm
student_project_ideas: Extend qq-bridge to add logging and metrics export (Prometheus) to evaluate message throughput and latency between OneBot and DSH and visualise results with Grafana.
Adapt the bridge to connect DSH agents to another OneBot-compatible backend (or a simulated chat frontend) and compare agent behaviours under different DSH model configurations.

tools.name: ramokz/phantom-camera
tools.desc: A Camera addon for Godot 4. Inspired by Cinemachine.

cls.summary: Phantom Camera is a Godot 4 plugin that provides ready-made camera behaviours (follow, framing, third-person, viewfinder and smooth transitions) for Camera2D and Camera3D nodes.
cls.what_it_does: It solves common camera control tasks in Godot games by exposing configurable behaviours (follow modes, group framing, path confinement, third-person spring arm, zoom and look‑at) and smooth transitions between virtual cameras. You use it as an editor plugin and scene nodes inside Godot 4; notable points are its Cinemachine-inspired feature set, example scenes, and an integrated viewfinder for previewing camera output.
cls.trl_rationale: The project is several years old (created 2022), has a large user star count (3.6k stars), active development (recent pushes) and example scenes and documentation, indicating production-ready maturity for Godot projects; it is not a de-facto industry standard so TRL 7 is appropriate.
prerequisites: Familiarity with Godot 4 editor and scene system
Basic knowledge of GDScript (or C# bindings if used)
student_project_ideas: Build a small 3D exploration game in Godot 4 using Phantom Camera to implement third-person and cinematic cutscenes, then evaluate player experience with different follow and framing settings.
Create a multi-character 2D platformer demo where Phantom Camera's group and framed modes dynamically keep multiple players in view and experiment with different dead-zone and damping configurations.

tools.name: vernemq/vernemq
tools.desc: A distributed MQTT message broker based on Erlang/OTP. Built for high quality & Industrial use cases. The VerneMQ mission is active & the project maintained. Thank you for your support!

cls.summary: VerneMQ is a high-performance, distributed MQTT message broker used to connect IoT devices and services with support for clustering, persistence and many back-end integrations.
cls.what_it_does: VerneMQ implements the MQTT 3.1 / 3.1.1 / 5.0 broker protocol to provide scalable, fault-tolerant publish/subscribe messaging for IoT and industrial use cases. It is deployed as a clustered Erlang/OTP service and notable for horizontal scaling, plugin extensibility, offline message storage and integration with databases and caching systems.
cls.trl_rationale: The repository is long-lived (created 2015), has thousands of stars and active development; the README and repo state VerneMQ is deployed in many countries and supports production features, indicating maturity and wide adoption rather than an early prototype.
student_project_ideas: Build a sensor-to-cloud pipeline: deploy a VerneMQ cluster in Docker, connect simulated MQTT sensors (Python) and forward telemetry to a time-series database for dashboarding (Grafana).

Implement and evaluate edge-to-cloud reliability: create a bridge between a constrained device (ESP32) and a VerneMQ broker, measure message delivery and latency under network partitions and demonstrate QoS behaviours.

tools.name: deta/surf
tools.desc: Personal AI Notebooks. Organize files & webpages and generate notes from them. Open source, local & open data, open model choice (incl. local).

cls.summary: Deta Surf is an open-source desktop AI notebook that organizes local files and web content and uses configurable language models to generate searchable notes and small interactive applets.
cls.what_it_does: Surf collects local files, webpages and media into a private library and lets you create 'smart notes' that query that library and the web using LLMs. It runs as a cross-platform desktop app, stores data locally in an open flat-file format, and supports cloud or local LLMs and generated small interactive applets (Surflets).
cls.trl_rationale: The project is over a year old, has a large community (3.6k stars), cross-platform builds, installation docs and active commits, indicating production-ready desktop maturity rather than an experimental prototype.
prerequisites: basic familiarity with LLM APIs or local LLM tooling
ability to install Electron-based apps or build from source
student_project_ideas: Build a Surflet that ingests and visualises CSV sensor logs inside Surf, adding LLM-powered summaries and observations to support a small IoT data analysis workflow.

Integrate a local LLM (e.g. Ollama or a local model) with Surf to create an automated literature-review notebook that extracts and cites key points from a set of PDFs for a systems engineering design assignment.

tools.name: petercorke/robotics-toolbox-python
tools.desc: Robotics Toolbox for Python

cls.summary: Robotics Toolbox for Python is an open-source library that provides kinematics, dynamics, planning and simulation tools for robot manipulators and mobile robots, designed for research and teaching.
cls.what_it_does: The toolbox implements serial-link manipulator and mobile-robot models, fast kinematic and dynamic routines, trajectory generation, inverse kinematics, motion planning and basic localization/SLAM algorithms. It is used as a Python library (pip / editable install) and integrates with plotting and web visualisers (Jupyter, three.js / Swift) for interactive demos; it is notable for its breadth of classical robotics algorithms, educational focus and a large set of supplied robot models.
cls.trl_rationale: The project has existed since 2015, has many stars and forks, active recent commits and extensive documentation and tutorials; it is mature and widely used in teaching and research though not an industry standard like ROS 2.
student_project_ideas: Implement and compare different inverse-kinematics methods (numerical, analytic if available) on a supplied robot model and evaluate speed/accuracy using the toolbox and matplotlib visualisations.

Create a mobile robot navigation lab that uses the toolbox's motion models and planning (RRT/PRM/D*) combined with a simple occupancy grid mapper (EKF) to demonstrate SLAM and path planning in simulation, then visualise results in Jupyter/Swift.

tools.name: gkjohnson/three-mesh-bvh
tools.desc: A BVH implementation to speed up raycasting and enable spatial queries against three.js meshes.

cls.summary: three-mesh-bvh is a JavaScript library that builds bounding volume hierarchies (BVHs) for three.js geometry to speed up raycasting and spatial queries in web 3D scenes.
cls.what_it_does: The library constructs BVH acceleration structures for three.js BufferGeometry (including specialized BVHs for points, lines and skinned meshes) so raycasts, intersection tests, shape casts and spatial queries run much faster. It is used by adding helper functions to three.js geometries or by constructing BVH objects directly, and includes examples for raycasting, point-cloud intersection, SDF generation and WebWorker/WebGPU workflows. Notable features are multiple BVH types (PointsBVH, LineBVH, SkinnedMeshBVH, ObjectBVH), serialization/webworker generation, and integrations to accelerate real‑time rendering, selection and physics queries in three.js apps.
cls.trl_rationale: The project is mature and long‑lived (created 2018) with many stars, forks and active recent commits; comprehensive examples and multiple integrations (WebWorker, WebGPU, specialised BVHs) indicate broad use and stability, consistent with a mature widely adopted library.
prerequisites: familiarity with 3D geometry and raycasting concepts
student_project_ideas: Build a web demo that loads a complex CAD-derived mesh into three.js, uses three-mesh-bvh to accelerate ray-based picking and implements a measurement tool comparing naive vs BVH-accelerated performance.

Create a simple physics/character controller for a 3D scene where collisions and movement use three-mesh-bvh for nearest-triangle queries and compare behaviour/performance with a conventional physics engine (e.g. Ammo.js).

tools.name: Auburn/FastNoiseLite
tools.desc: Fast Portable Noise Library - C# C++ C Java HLSL GLSL JavaScript Rust Go

cls.summary: FastNoise Lite is a portable, high-performance library that generates 2D and 3D procedural noise (Perlin, Simplex, Voronoi, value/cubic, etc.) for use in textures, terrain, domain warping and other procedural content.
cls.what_it_does: The library produces a variety of deterministic noise functions (2D/3D) and fractal combinations for procedural generation and signal synthesis. It is used as a drop-in library or language port (C/C++, Rust, C#, JavaScript, GLSL/HLSL and more) to create noise textures, terrain heightfields, or domain-warped inputs for rendering and simulation. It is notable for many language ports, a small API surface, and emphasis on portability and performance.
cls.trl_rationale: The repository is long-lived (created 2016), has many stars and ports to many languages, an active preview app and recent commits, indicating wide adoption and maturity rather than an experimental prototype.
prerequisites: programming in the target language (C/C++, Rust, JS, etc.)
basic understanding of procedural noise and sampling
student_project_ideas: Create a terrain generator that uses FastNoise Lite (Rust or JS port) to produce heightmaps and combine them with a simple hydraulic erosion filter to evaluate landscape evolution.
Integrate FastNoise Lite (C++ or GLSL) into a WebGL/three.js scene to generate procedural textures and real-time domain-warped animation for a visualization or interactive demo.

tools.name: huangjunsen0406/py-xiaozhi
tools.desc: Open-source AI assistant ecosystem with MCP integrations, multimodal workflows, IoT support, and cross-platform voice interaction.

cls.summary: py-xiaozhi is an open-source Python framework for building cross-platform, multimodal AI voice assistants that integrate with IoT and edge hardware.
cls.what_it_does: py-xiaozhi provides real-time voice streaming, vision-language integration, MCP (JSON-RPC) tool servers, and IoT/GPIO interfaces so developers can connect large language models to sensors and actuators on desktops and edge boards. It is used as a runtime and plugin ecosystem (audio, UI, tools, protocols) for embodied AI and edge deployments, notable for its async architecture, low-latency Opus audio pipeline, and multi-protocol (WebSocket/MQTT) connectivity.
cls.trl_rationale: The project is over one year old, has large community interest (3.5k stars), active maintenance and documented adoption (mentions upstream use by D-Robotics), and cross-platform releases which indicate production-readiness rather than a fragile prototype.
prerequisites: audio and optional camera hardware for multimodal features
student_project_ideas: Build a Raspberry Pi–based voice-controlled robot that uses py-xiaozhi for wake-word detection, LLM-driven commands, and GPIO-controlled actuators, integrating OpenCV for simple vision tasks.
Create an MCP tool plugin that interfaces py-xiaozhi with an MQTT-based sensor network, demonstrating message routing, encrypted MQTT/WSS connectivity, and logging to a time-series database.

tools.name: hi-godot/godot-ai
tools.desc: Production-grade MCP server and AI tools for the Godot engine. A Snap to install. Totally free and fun.

cls.summary: Godot AI is an open-source Godot editor plugin and local MCP server that lets LLM-based MCP clients drive the Godot editor to create and modify scenes, scripts, UI and assets.
cls.what_it_does: Godot AI connects Model Context Protocol (MCP) clients (Claude, Codex, Cursor, etc.) to a running Godot editor via a local Python server and an editor plugin, exposing ~46 tools and 120+ operations to inspect and modify scenes, scripts, signals, materials, animation and environment settings. It is used by installing the Godot add-on and running a small Python MCP server (uv) so external agents can attach and perform editor automation; notable points are strong security controls, signed releases and an in-editor configuration dock.
cls.trl_rationale: The project shows strong, recent usage (large install and tool-call metrics, many stars), releases and active maintenance, indicating beta-level maturity; however the repository is under one year old (219 days), which limits the TRL to at most 6.
prerequisites: an MCP-compatible client (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, etc.)
basic familiarity with Godot project structure and editor plugins
student_project_ideas: Create an automated scene-builder agent that generates a simple robotic simulation environment in Godot from high-level prompts and integrates a physics test-suite to evaluate robot behaviours.
Build a prompt-driven UI prototyping tool that uses Godot AI to generate menus and HUD elements from JSON requirements, then run user interaction tests and collect telemetry for iterative design.

tools.name: alicevision/AliceVision
tools.desc: 3D Computer Vision Framework

cls.summary: AliceVision is an open-source photogrammetric computer-vision framework that produces 3D reconstructions and camera tracking from unordered photos or video.
cls.what_it_does: AliceVision implements a full photogrammetry pipeline (structure-from-motion, multi-view stereo, meshing and texturing) to recover 3D geometry and camera poses from image sets. It is used as a library and a set of command-line tools and is notable for powering the Meshroom UI and for being the result of academic/industry collaboration with published papers.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository active since 2014 with many stars, forks, published papers and an ecosystem (Meshroom) indicating broad adoption and production use; long history and active maintenance justify a mature rating.
prerequisites: dependencies such as OpenCV / Eigen / Ceres (see INSTALL.md)
student_project_ideas: Use AliceVision to reconstruct a small outdoor site from drone imagery and compare resulting point clouds/meshes with terrestrial LiDAR scans to quantify geometric accuracy.

Integrate AliceVision command-line pipeline with a Python script (via Meshroom or subprocess) to build an automated photogrammetry workflow that labels, batches and uploads textured meshes to a web viewer.

tools.name: PrismML-Eng/Bonsai-demo
tools.desc: Bonsai Demo

cls.summary: A local demo and packaging for running the Bonsai 2 family of LLMs (2B–27B) on CPU/GPU with support for GGUF/MLX formats, vision inputs and agentic tool calling.
cls.what_it_does: This repository provides scripts, prebuilt binaries and a demo server to download and run Bonsai 2 models locally across macOS, Linux and Windows (with CUDA/ROCm/Vulkan/Metal support). It packages model format support (GGUF, MLX, PQ2_0/PTQ1_0), vision input support and example agent/tool integrations so users can experiment with local LLM inference, vision and tool-calling workflows.
cls.trl_rationale: The repo is actively maintained, widely starred and contains install scripts, model downloads and example servers indicating a usable beta-quality project; however it is under 1 year old (237 days) so TRL is capped at 6 by the maturity rules.
prerequisites: knowledge of local LLM inference concepts
GPU drivers (CUDA/ROCm) or Metal on macOS for best performance
student_project_ideas: Build an evaluation suite that compares inference speed, memory and output quality of Bonsai 2 models (2B/4B/9B/27B) on different local hardware backends (CPU, CUDA, Metal) and report trade-offs.

Integrate the demo's agentic tool-calling example with a simple simulated system (e.g. a PID-controlled process in Python) to prototype an LLM-driven operator assistant that issues commands and interprets telemetry.

tools.name: nicedreamzapp/claude-code-local
tools.desc: Hit your Claude Code usage limit? Keep going free and offline on a local model: Qwen 3.8, Gemma 4, and Qwen 4 the day it ships. Runs on Apple Silicon Macs (MLX), Linux and Windows (llama.cpp) with no API key. Your code stays home.

cls.summary: A small Python proxy that lets Anthropic Claude Code talk to local LLMs (MLX on Apple Silicon or llama.cpp on Linux/Windows) so you can continue Claude Code conversations without an API key or cloud model.
cls.what_it_does: It runs a local server that implements the Anthropic Messages API and translates model outputs (Gemma, Qwen, Llama builds) into Claude Code tool calls so Claude Code can continue conversations on-device. It is used by installing the project, running the proxy and switching Claude Code to point at the local server; notable points are MLX support for Apple Silicon, llama.cpp support for Linux/Windows, and tooling to repair tool-call JSON and reuse prompt cache between turns.
cls.trl_rationale: The repo is active, well-starred (3.5k+ stars) with documentation, install scripts and many downloads, indicating beta-level maturity; however it is under one year old (created 2026-03-26) so it fits TRL 6 rather than higher.
prerequisites: access to local model weights (Hugging Face or local builds) and knowledge of model memory requirements
student_project_ideas: Build an assignment where students swap a cloud LLM for a local model using this proxy and measure latency, token usage and privacy implications across different model sizes (compare MLX Qwen 3.8 on Mac vs llama.cpp on Linux).
Extend the proxy to log and visualise tool-call patterns from Claude Code conversations, then analyse how often tool calls occur and propose heuristics to reduce unnecessary model tool invocations.

tools.name: patriciogonzalezvivo/lygia
tools.desc: LYGIA, it's a granular and multi-language (GLSL, HLSL, Metal,  WGSL,  WEGL and CUDA) shader library designed for performance and flexibility

cls.summary: LYGIA is a large, multi-language collection of modular shader functions (GLSL, HLSL, WGSL, Metal, CUDA, etc.) designed to be dropped into rendering projects for prototyping and production use.
cls.what_it_does: LYGIA provides a granular library of reusable shader functions for math, geometry, color, lighting, SDFs, filters and more, letting developers compose and port shaders across multiple shading languages. It is used by including the provided files (locally or via the lygia.xyz resolver) into WebGL/WebGPU or engine projects and is notable for broad language support and many prebuilt integrations.
cls.trl_rationale: The repository is several years old, actively maintained (recent pushes), has many stars (3.5k) and documented integrations and an online resolver; this indicates production-ready maturity and real-world use rather than a fragile prototype.
prerequisites: understanding of GPU rendering pipeline and host API (WebGL/WebGPU/DirectX/Vulkan)
familiarity with JavaScript or engine integration (for web/engine examples)
student_project_ideas: Build a WebGL demo (three.js) that implements an interactive procedural material using LYGIA shader functions and adds GUI controls to explore parameter effects.

Create a physics-visualisation for a simple simulation (e.g., fluid or particle system) and replace/customise the lighting and post-processing with LYGIA shader modules to evaluate visual fidelity and performance.

tools.name: opengeos/geoai
tools.desc: GeoAI: Artificial Intelligence for Geospatial Data

cls.summary: GeoAI is a Python library that integrates deep learning with geospatial data workflows for tasks like classification, segmentation, change detection and visualization.
cls.what_it_does: GeoAI provides high-level APIs to search and download remote sensing imagery, prepare datasets (chips/labels), train and run deep-learning models for classification, detection and segmentation, and visualise results interactively. It bundles integrations with PyTorch-based model libraries and geospatial tools (Leafmap, MapLibre, QGIS plugin) to streamline end-to-end geospatial AI workflows.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository is mature and actively maintained (created 2023-08, >3 years old) with >3k stars, recent commits, a published paper and a companion book, and explicit integrations (QGIS plugin, Leafmap). These indicate production-readiness and real-world use but it is not a de-facto standard requiring TRL 8–9.
prerequisites: geospatial libraries (rasterio, GDAL) and basic GIS concepts
QGIS to use the desktop plugin
student_project_ideas: Build a land-cover classification pipeline using GeoAI to download Sentinel imagery, prepare training chips, train a segmentation model (PyTorch) and deploy results to a Leafmap web viewer.
Use GeoAI and the QGIS plugin to implement a change-detection study on a region affected by flooding, combining NAIP/ Sentinel imagery and vector flood extent validation data.

tools.name: hlorus/CAD_Sketcher
tools.desc: Constraint-based geometry sketcher for blender

cls.summary: CAD Sketcher is a Blender add-on that provides constraint-based, parametric 2D sketching so users can create precise editable geometry inside Blender.
cls.what_it_does: It implements a constraint solver and sketching tools inside Blender to create 2D geometry defined by constraints (distance, angle, tangent, equal, etc.), keeping sketches editable for a non-destructive workflow. Users install it as a Blender extension and create parametric sketches to drive CAD-style modelling inside Blender; it is notable for bringing traditional constraint-based sketching to Blender and for its active documentation and update mechanism.
cls.trl_rationale: The project has been maintained since 2021, has a large user interest (3.4k stars), published documentation, installation instructions and update mechanism, and active development — evidence of production-ready maturity for many users. The README's 'experimental' warning suggests the author still considers it evolving, so TRL 7 (production-ready for many workflows but still under active change) is appropriate.
prerequisites: Familiarity with Blender (interface and add-on installation)
student_project_ideas: Create a parametric mechanical part in Blender using CAD Sketcher and export geometry to a mesh-based FEA tool to compare geometry-driven and mesh-driven design workflows.
Develop a small Blender-based workflow where constraint-driven sketches drive a scripted assembly of parts (using Python) to demonstrate parametric design and BOM updates.

tools.name: aras-p/UnityGaussianSplatting
tools.desc: Gaussian Splatting visualization for Unity

cls.summary: A Unity renderer and visualizer for 3D Gaussian Splatting point-based radiance fields that loads PLY/SPZ splat files and renders them in real time on modern graphics APIs.
cls.what_it_does: This project implements real-time rendering of 3D Gaussian Splatting datasets inside the Unity engine, letting users load PLY or Scaniverse SPZ splat files and view them with different transparency and filtering modes. It is used as a visualization/playground for the SIGGRAPH 2023 3D Gaussian Splatting method and is notable for a Unity-integrated renderer with platform-specific graphics API support (D3D12, Metal, Vulkan) and performance-focused implementations (GPU sorting, burst/C# ports).
cls.trl_rationale: The repository is well-established (created 2023, active through 2026), has a large community (3.4k stars, many forks), performance numbers and example scenes, and multiple platform notes—indicating production-ready quality for visualization tasks though not an industry-standard tool; README also notes project is feature-frozen which limits further advancement.
prerequisites: Unity (knowledge of Unity projects and scenes)
familiarity with graphics APIs (D3D12/Metal/Vulkan) and C#
student_project_ideas: Build a Unity scene that loads a custom PLY/SPZ splat file and implements camera-path benchmarking to compare frame-time and memory for different rendering modes (sorted blended vs stochastic).

Integrate a small photogrammetry pipeline: generate a splat dataset from a point cloud (or convert an existing NeRF/point cloud output), import into the UnityGaussianSplatting project and add UI controls to explore level-of-detail and temporal filtering effects.

tools.name: luigifreda/pyslam
tools.desc: pySLAM is a hybrid Python/C++ Visual SLAM pipeline supporting monocular, stereo, and RGB-D cameras. It provides a broad set of modern local and global feature extractors, multiple loop-closure strategies, a volumetric reconstruction module, integrated depth-prediction models, and semantic segmentation capabilities for enhanced scene understanding.

cls.summary: pySLAM is an open-source hybrid Python/C++ Visual SLAM pipeline that supports monocular, stereo and RGB‑D cameras and includes mapping, loop‑closure, depth prediction, semantic segmentation and volumetric reconstruction.
cls.what_it_does: pySLAM provides a modular visual odometry and SLAM framework for localisation and dense/semantic scene reconstruction; it runs in a single Python environment with C++ performance-critical components and supports multiple feature extractors, loop‑closure strategies and volumetric TSDF/gaussian‑splatting reconstruction. It is used by running dataset or live-camera pipelines, selecting front-end features and back-end optimisers (g2o/GTSAM), and can integrate depth‑prediction and segmentation models to produce semantic dense maps.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository is mature (created 2019), actively maintained, substantial community (3.4k stars, recent pushes) and includes integration with real optimisation engines (g2o/GTSAM) and multiple dataset support, indicating production‑ready research use rather than a one-off prototype.
prerequisites: C++ toolchain and pybind11 build basics
OpenCV and optional CUDA/PyTorch for depth/segmentation models
student_project_ideas: Build a stereo visual odometry pipeline using pySLAM to localise a ground robot on recorded dataset and compare trajectory error when using different local feature extractors (e.g. ORB vs a learned descriptor).

Use pySLAM's volumetric reconstruction with an integrated depth‑prediction model to generate a dense semantic 3D map from monocular video and evaluate reconstruction quality against an RGB‑D baseline (combine with ICP or Meshing tools for post‑processing).

tools.name: vrm-c/UniVRM
tools.desc: UniVRM is a gltf-based VRM format implementation for Unity. English is here https://vrm.dev/en/ . 日本語 はこちら https://vrm.dev/

cls.summary: UniVRM is an open-source Unity implementation of the VRM avatar file format (an extension of glTF) that imports and exports VRM and glTF files at editor time and runtime.
cls.what_it_does: UniVRM provides importers and exporters for VRM 1.0 / 0.x and glTF 2.0 inside the Unity engine, enabling developers to load, migrate and save 3D avatar assets and animations both in the Unity editor and at runtime. It supports async runtime import, scripted importers, PBR material conversion and multiple build targets, making it the standard VRM implementation for Unity projects.
cls.trl_rationale: The project is mature: created in 2018, many stars/forks, active commits and released versions, and is the reference implementation for VRM in Unity; this demonstrates broad adoption though it is not an industry standard across engineering domains.
prerequisites: Unity editor experience (2022.3 LTS or later recommended)
C# and Unity asset pipeline familiarity
basic knowledge of glTF/3D asset workflows
student_project_ideas: Build a Unity scene that imports VRM avatars at runtime and evaluates avatar-based human–machine interaction scenarios (combine with simple UX telemetry logging).
Create a WebGL deployment that loads VRM characters exported from Unity and demonstrates material conversion and animation streaming for an interactive visualisation prototype.

tools.name: pafuhana1213/KawaiiPhysics
tools.desc: KawaiiPhysics : Simple Bone Physics for UnrealEngine 4 & 5

cls.summary: KawaiiPhysics is an open-source Unreal Engine plugin that provides lightweight, artist-friendly bone sway physics for characters and cloth-like parts.
cls.what_it_does: KawaiiPhysics adds a single AnimGraph node to drive pseudo-physics on character bones so hair, skirts and other appendages sway naturally without heavy physics engines. It is installed as an Unreal plugin and configured via Animation Blueprints, DataAssets and in-editor collision primitives; the implementation is PhysX-free and designed to be lightweight and easy to tune for artists. The project is notable for its simplicity, active community, and wide compatibility with UE4.27 and UE5.3–5.8.
cls.trl_rationale: The repository is several years old (created 2019), has many stars (3.4k), published releases and active recent commits supporting UE5.8, and provides documentation and a sample project—evidence of production-ready maturity for its niche.
prerequisites: Basic C++ and Unreal Animation Blueprint knowledge
student_project_ideas: Integrate KawaiiPhysics into a UE5 character pipeline to compare artist-tuned pseudo-physics against Unreal's native cloth/physics systems and report on performance and visual fidelity.
Build an interactive visualization where parameter sliders (exposed via Blueprints) let users explore trade-offs between realism and runtime cost for bone-based sway on mobile vs desktop targets.

tools.name: EpicGames/BlenderTools
tools.desc: Blender addons that improve the game development workflow between Blender and Unreal.

cls.summary: A collection of Blender addons that streamline sending assets and animations between Blender and Unreal Engine, including a one‑click 'Send to Unreal' and a UE-to-Rigify retargeting system.
cls.what_it_does: The repo provides Blender addons to export and transfer geometry, materials and animations into Unreal Engine and to retarget Unreal Marketplace animations to Blender's Rigify rigs. It is used inside Blender as installable Python addons and notable for tight integration with Unreal workflows and a focus on game/real‑time asset pipelines.
cls.trl_rationale: The repository is mature and well established (created 2020) with thousands of stars, active recent commits by Epic Games, downloadable releases and documentation pages, indicating wide adoption and stable maintenance.
prerequisites: basic knowledge of 3D asset export concepts (FBX/glTF) and optionally Python for customization
student_project_ideas: Create a small asset pipeline lab where students model a mechanical component in Blender, use Send to Unreal to import it into an Unreal scene, and measure visual fidelity and material conversion differences between FBX and glTF exports.
Implement a retargeting exercise: take an Unreal Marketplace animation, use UE to Rigify to retarget it to a custom Rigify rig in Blender, and evaluate animation quality and joint mapping strategies.

tools.name: mujocolab/mjlab
tools.desc: Isaac Lab API, powered by MuJoCo-Warp, for RL and robotics research

cls.summary: mjlab is an open-source Python framework that combines Isaac Lab's manager API with MuJoCo Warp to run large-scale, GPU-accelerated robotics and reinforcement learning simulations.
cls.what_it_does: mjlab provides composable environment building blocks and direct access to native MuJoCo data structures so researchers can create, train and evaluate RL agents and robot controllers at scale on GPUs. It is used via Python/command-line entry points (examples and uv/uvx commands) and supports multi-GPU distributed training and evaluation workflows. Notable features include tight integration with MuJoCo Warp for GPU acceleration, Isaac Lab-style APIs, and published research using the framework.
cls.trl_rationale: The repo is over one year old, has broad community interest (3.4k stars), full documentation, examples, published research citing mjlab, and active development, indicating production-ready software rather than a fragile prototype; these factors support TRL 7.
prerequisites: familiarity with reinforcement learning and robot simulation concepts
student_project_ideas: Train a quadruped locomotion controller using mjlab and compare single-GPU vs multi-GPU training performance and sample efficiency, reporting results and training curves.
Implement and validate a motion-imitation task where a humanoid follows recorded trajectories (from a motion dataset) using mjlab and evaluate robustness under sensor noise and terrain variation.

tools.name: zcreativelabs/react-simple-maps
tools.desc: Composable SVG map charts for data visualization in React

cls.summary: React Simple Maps is a React library for composing SVG-based maps (TopoJSON/GeoJSON) with built-in panning, zooming and mapping components for data visualisation.
cls.what_it_does: It provides a set of React components to render geographic maps from TopoJSON/GeoJSON and to build choropleths, markers and annotations with pan/zoom behaviour. You use it by installing the npm package and composing provided components (ComposableMap, Geographies, Geography, Marker, etc.) in a React app; it leverages d3-geo and topojson-client rather than the whole d3 bundle. It is notable for a typed TypeScript API, focus on SVG output and being lightweight to combine with other React component libraries.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository is long-lived (created 2017), has many stars, recent commits and an established, typed API and test coverage; these indicate a mature, widely-adopted OSS library rather than an experimental prototype.
student_project_ideas: Build an interactive choropleth map of census or open demographic data using react-simple-maps and a REST API, demonstrating data binding, color scales and projection choices.
Create a live dashboard that plots IoT sensor locations on a map (TopoJSON basemap) using react-simple-maps and a real-time feed (e.g. MQTT or WebSocket) to visualise sensor status and location.

tools.name: arjun988/blender-skills
tools.desc: 94 specialist Blender skills for Cursor, Claude Code, Kiro & Codex -> MCP-powered production pipeline from blockout to engine export.

cls.summary: A pack of 94 agent-executable Blender skills that automate technical-art and production tasks inside Blender via MCP connectors (Cursor, Claude Code, Kiro, Codex).
cls.what_it_does: This repository provides a large library of prewritten 'skills' that agents can execute directly inside a running Blender instance using the Blender MCP addon, automating modelling, retopology, UVs, materials, LOD/export pipelines and style-directed workflows. It is used by copying the skill folders into the agent's skills directory and connecting the agent to BlenderMCP; its notable feature is orchestration via a 'blender-director' skill that chains other skills into production pipelines.
cls.trl_rationale: The project is actively maintained, has extensive documentation and many stars indicating significant user interest, but the repository is only ~135 days old so under the stated guidance its TRL is capped at 6 (beta).
prerequisites: Agent client such as Cursor, Claude Code, Kiro or Codex
Basic familiarity with Blender modelling/UV/texture workflows
student_project_ideas: Create a pipeline that uses the blender-director skill to automate producing a game-ready modular corridor kit (model, UV, materials, LODs) and export it into Unity or Godot for a small interactive scene.

Compare agent-driven retopology and manual retopology on a sculpt: run an agent skill to generate a retopologised mesh, then evaluate geometry quality, tri counts and animation deformation against a hand-made retopo using quantitative metrics.

tools.name: off-grid-ai/OGAM
tools.desc: The Swiss Army Knife of Offline AI. Chat, see, speak, and generate images on your phone or Mac — GGUF LLMs, vision, Whisper speech-to-text, Stable Diffusion, tool calling, and local-network servers. Runs on your CPU, GPU, or NPU. No account, no API key, zero data leaves your device.

cls.summary: Off Grid AI is an open-source, on-device AI suite that runs local LLMs, vision, speech, and image generation on phones and Macs without sending data off-device.
cls.what_it_does: Off Grid AI runs GGUF-format LLMs, vision models, Whisper speech-to-text, and Stable Diffusion image generation locally on mobile and macOS hardware, using CPU, GPU (OpenCL/Metal) or NPUs where available. It provides chat, tool-calling, document knowledge bases, and local-network discovery of OpenAI-compatible servers, notable for its emphasis on privacy (no cloud API required) and support for multiple acceleration backends and model formats.
cls.trl_rationale: The project is actively developed, well-documented and popular (many stars and active releases), showing beta-level maturity; however the repository is under one year old so per the TRL rules it should be capped at TRL 6 despite evident adoption.
prerequisites: basic machine learning and model formats (GGUF/quantisation)
mobile app development or deployment knowledge (React Native / iOS / Android)
familiarity with local LLM tooling and model management
student_project_ideas: Build a lab assignment that measures inference throughput and energy usage of the same GGUF model across CPU, GPU (OpenCL/Metal) and NPU on a flagship phone using Off Grid AI and visualise the trade-offs.
Create a prototype 'document assistant' that uploads course PDFs into Off Grid AI's local knowledge base and evaluates retrieval+answer quality versus cloud-based retrieval systems.

tools.name: 4sval/FModel
tools.desc: Unreal Engine Archives Explorer

cls.summary: FModel is a desktop explorer that opens Unreal Engine (UE4/UE5) game archives to browse, preview and export game assets such as meshes, textures, maps, animations and audio.
cls.what_it_does: FModel parses Unreal Engine archive files to let users inspect package contents as JSON, preview 3D assets in a bundled viewer (Snooper), and export meshes, textures and other assets to common formats. It is a C#/.NET application built on the CUE4Parse library for asset parsing and provides an interactive asset browser and previewer notable for broad game support and active community maintenance.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository created in 2019, large star count (3.4k), active development (recent pushes) and a community of contributors indicate broad, stable use; it appears mature and widely adopted for its niche rather than a one-off prototype.
prerequisites: basic C# / .NET familiarity for building or extending
understanding of Unreal Engine asset/package formats and game archive files
student_project_ideas: Use FModel to extract textures and meshes from a UE game and assemble them into a simple WebGL viewer (three.js) to demonstrate asset pipelines and visualization.
Extend or script FModel/CUE4Parse to convert exported assets into a lightweight CAD-compatible format and evaluate the fidelity of geometry export for reverse-engineering exercises.

tools.name: armory3d/armory
tools.desc: 3D Engine with Blender Integration

cls.summary: Armory is an open-source real-time 3D game engine with tight Blender integration that lets users build and run interactive scenes and games directly from Blender.
cls.what_it_does: Armory provides a full game engine runtime and a Blender add-on that turns Blender into a game development toolchain, enabling creation, scripting and rendering of interactive 3D content. It is used to author scenes in Blender and export/run them across targets, with a scriptable renderer supporting deferred and forward paths. What makes it notable is its direct Blender integration and focus on portability and small footprint.
cls.trl_rationale: The project is long‑lived (created 2015) with active development, many stars and published releases, indicating production readiness; however it is not a de-facto industry standard like Unity/Unreal, so TRL 7 (production-ready) is appropriate.
prerequisites: some Haxe or scripting experience for advanced use
student_project_ideas: Create an interactive vehicle dynamics demonstrator in Blender and export it with Armory to build a real-time visualization for validating control algorithms.
Build an augmented-reality style mobile app that visualises sensor data from a robot or IoT device in a Blender-authored scene exported with Armory.

tools.name: threlte/threlte
tools.desc: 3D framework for Svelte

cls.summary: Threlte is a Svelte library that makes it easy to build interactive 3D web applications by exposing Three.js objects through a declarative, reactive API and offering plugins for physics, animation and XR.
cls.what_it_does: Threlte simplifies creating interactive 3D scenes in Svelte by providing declarative components that map to Three.js primitives, hooks for rendering and animation, and optional packages for physics (Rapier), animation studio integration (Theatre.js), GLTF component generation and XR. It is used as a web frontend framework for interactive visualisation, lightweight physics-driven scenes and VR/AR experiences, notable for combining Svelte reactivity with Three.js and first-class plugin packages.
cls.trl_rationale: The project is multi-year (created 2022), has sizable community interest (3.3k stars), stable documentation and multiple packages (core, extras, gltf, rapier, theatre, xr) and active recent commits, indicating production-ready maturity rather than an experimental prototype.
student_project_ideas: Create an interactive web viewer that loads GLTF CAD exports and adds Rapier-based physics to demonstrate assembly collisions and kinematics, hosted as a Svelte app.
Build a small XR-enabled inspection demo using @threlte/xr that overlays sensor telemetry (simulated IoT time series) onto a 3D model for a digital-twin style visualization.

tools.name: eclipse-zenoh/zenoh
tools.desc: zenoh unifies data in motion, data in-use, data at rest and computations. It carefully blends traditional pub/sub with geo-distributed storages, queries and computations, while retaining a level of time and space efficiency that is well beyond any of the mainstream stacks.

cls.summary: Zenoh is a lightweight, high-performance pub/sub, storage and query protocol and implementation for geo-distributed IoT and edge systems.
cls.what_it_does: Zenoh unifies data-in-motion (pub/sub), data-at-rest (geo-distributed storage/queries) and distributed computation into a single protocol and set of libraries. It is used as a middleware/router (zenohd) and client libraries (Rust reference implementation plus bindings) to build low-latency, efficient data pipelines across edge, fog and cloud. Notable points are its multi-language bindings, a standalone router with plugin support, and focus on time/space efficiency for constrained and geo-distributed environments.
cls.trl_rationale: The project is mature and widely used: the repository is multi-year (created 2020) with thousands of stars, active recent development, multiple language bindings (C, C++, Python, Go, TypeScript), and a router daemon with plugin ecosystem — evidence of production readiness and a community beyond a demo. This history supports a high TRL.
prerequisites: Rust toolchain (Cargo) to build native components
student_project_ideas: Build a small sensor network where microcontroller nodes (using zenoh-pico or C client) publish telemetry to a zenohd router and a cloud client visualises aggregated data, demonstrating latency and bandwidth under different topologies.

Integrate Zenoh with a ROS 2 robot to bridge DDS-based robot topics to a geo-distributed dashboard via a zenohd plugin, then measure end-to-end message latency and reliability under network partitions.

tools.name: neka-nat/freecad-mcp
tools.desc: FreeCAD MCP(Model Context Protocol) server

cls.summary: FreeCAD MCP is an MIT-licensed server and FreeCAD addon that lets external MCP-capable agents (for example Claude Desktop) control FreeCAD to create and edit models, run Python scripts and perform FEM analyses.
cls.what_it_does: FreeCAD MCP exposes FreeCAD functionality over the Model Context Protocol (MCP) so external clients and AI agents can drive modelling tasks, run scripts and inspect documents programmatically. It is used by installing a FreeCAD addon and launching an MCP client (uv/uvx and e.g. Claude Desktop) to connect to FreeCAD; notable features include examples for parametric modelling, FEM runs and integrations with agent frameworks.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository is over a year old, actively maintained with recent pushes, extensive documentation, demos and many stars/forks indicating community use; the README describes installable addon and practical examples, supporting a production-ready TRL.
prerequisites: basic Python knowledge and familiarity with FreeCAD workbenches
student_project_ideas: Build an agent that reads a 2D engineering drawing (image or DXF) and uses FreeCAD MCP to generate a parametric 3D part, then export it as STEP for downstream manufacturing.
Create an automated FEM testbench where a script driven via MCP parametrises a flange geometry, runs a stress analysis in FreeCAD, and logs design-performance trade-offs to a CSV for optimisation.

tools.name: CGCookie/retopoflow
tools.desc: A suite of retopology tools for Blender

cls.summary: RetopoFlow is a Blender add-on that provides interactive, sketch-based retopology tools to generate clean, quad-based meshes that snap to high‑poly surfaces as you draw.
cls.what_it_does: RetopoFlow helps artists and modelers create low‑density, animation- and simulation-friendly topology over high‑resolution meshes by drawing/painting edge loops and polygons directly on the surface inside Blender. It is used as a Blender add-on (Python) and is notable for its workflow-focused tools that speed up manual retopology compared with raw Blender modelling tools.
cls.trl_rationale: The project is long-lived (created 2014), widely used (3.3k stars), has releases and ongoing maintenance and is distributed commercially as an add-on, indicating a mature, widely adopted tool rather than an experimental prototype.
prerequisites: Basic 3D modelling and mesh concepts (faces, edges, topology)
student_project_ideas: Use RetopoFlow to convert a high‑resolution 3D scan (from photogrammetry) into a simulation-ready mesh and then run a simple finite element or CFD study comparing performance/mesh quality.

Integrate RetopoFlow into a pipeline where students retopologise a sculpted CAD concept in Blender and export clean geometry for downstream manufacturing or 3D printing (compare original vs retopologised printability).

tools.name: hbb1/2d-gaussian-splatting
tools.desc: [SIGGRAPH'24] 2D Gaussian Splatting for Geometrically Accurate Radiance Fields

cls.summary: An open-source implementation of 2D Gaussian splatting for high-quality novel-view synthesis and mesh extraction from multi-view images, aimed at fast, geometrically-accurate radiance-field reconstruction.
cls.what_it_does: This repository implements the SIGGRAPH'24 method '2D Gaussian Splatting' which represents scenes as oriented 2D surface elements (surfels) and rasterizes them with a perspective-correct differentiable rasterizer to produce photorealistic novel views and extract meshes. It is used by training on multi-view image datasets (scripts and examples provided), includes options for bounded and unbounded mesh extraction, and links to viewers and CUDA-accelerated rasterizers that make it notable for interactive visualization and practical reconstruction pipelines.
cls.trl_rationale: The project implements a peer-reviewed SIGGRAPH'24 method, has many stars and forks, active updates and community links (viewers, colabs, related rasterizers), and provides training/testing scripts — indicating production-ready code used by practitioners; however it is relatively recent and not yet a de-facto standard, so TRL 7 is appropriate.
prerequisites: basic familiarity with multi-view reconstruction / NeRF-style datasets
student_project_ideas: Compare 2D Gaussian Splatting and a NeRF implementation (e.g. MipNeRF360) on a small multi-view dataset: train both, compare rendering quality, extraction time and final mesh quality.

Integrate the repository's mesh export with a WebGL viewer (e.g. Three.js/GaussianSplats3D) to build a lightweight web-based viewer that streams reconstructed surfel meshes for interactive inspection and annotation.

tools.name: mixelpixx/KiCAD-MCP-Server
tools.desc: KiCAD MCP is a Model Context Protocol (MCP) implementation that enables Large Language Models (LLMs) like Claude to directly interact with KiCAD for printed circuit board design.

cls.summary: KiCAD MCP Server is an open-source MCP server that lets large language models interact directly with KiCad to automate PCB design tasks such as schematic edits, placement, routing, checks and export.
cls.what_it_does: It implements the Model Context Protocol so AI assistants (e.g. Claude) can query and command a live KiCad project: create projects, edit schematics, place components, run routing, perform DRC/ERC and export fabrication outputs. It is notable because it exposes rich, real-time KiCad project state and tool schemas to LLMs and integrates with parts/catalog services and automated freerouting.
cls.trl_rationale: The repository is over one year old, has many stars and forks, active maintenance and recent pushes, documented integrations (JLCPCB, freerouting) and installation instructions; these indicate production-readiness rather than an experimental prototype.
