student_project_ideas: Build a conversational assistant that places and routes a simple microcontroller-based PCB in KiCad via the MCP server and generates fabrication outputs, comparing manual vs AI-assisted routing quality.
Integrate the MCP server with a parts-availability API (e.g. JLCPCB data) to automatically select components for a small sensor board and evaluate BOM cost and lead-time trade-offs.

tools.name: bitbrain/beehave
tools.desc: 🐝 behavior tree AI for Godot Engine

cls.summary: Beehave is an open-source behavior-tree addon for the Godot game engine that helps authors build and debug AI behaviours inside Godot scenes.
cls.what_it_does: Beehave provides node-based behaviour trees you compose inside Godot scene trees to implement NPC and agent logic, along with an editor debug view and performance monitors for runtime inspection. It is distributed as a Godot addon written in GDScript and installs into the /addons folder so designers and developers can attach behaviour trees to scene nodes.
cls.trl_rationale: The project is several years old (created 2022), has many stars and forks, maintained branches for Godot 3.x and 4.x, releases and active recent commits, test coverage and documentation—evidence of production-ready addon maturity.
student_project_ideas: Create an NPC in a Godot-based robotics simulation that uses Beehave behaviour trees to perform waypoint navigation and obstacle avoidance, comparing tree-based logic with a simple state machine.

Implement a multi-agent patrol and intrusion-detection scenario in Godot where agents coordinate via shared blackboard data and use Beehave to manage complex behaviours; measure performance using the built-in monitors.

tools.name: software-mansion/TypeGPU
tools.desc: A modular and open-ended toolkit for WebGPU, with advanced type inference and the ability to write shaders in TypeScript

cls.summary: TypeGPU is a TypeScript toolkit that lets developers write type-safe GPU shaders and WebGPU compute/graphics pipelines using TypeScript with automatic WGSL generation.
cls.what_it_does: TypeGPU provides a type-safe abstraction layer over the WebGPU API that lets you author shader logic in TypeScript, infer types across buffers and shader code, generate WGSL, and run compute/graphics pipelines in the browser. It is used as a foundation or interoperability layer for higher-level WebGPU libraries and can be partially adopted inside existing WebGPU applications. Notable features are advanced TypeScript type inference for GPU data and the ability to fall back to raw WebGPU when needed.
cls.trl_rationale: The repository is multi-year (created 2024-02-17, actively maintained with recent pushes) and has substantial community interest (3.3k+ stars) and a documentation site; several third-party projects list TypeGPU as a dependency, indicating real-world use beyond a single-author prototype.
student_project_ideas: Create a browser-based GPU-accelerated cellular automata simulator: write compute kernels in TypeScript with TypeGPU to generate and visualise large grids, and compare performance to a CPU implementation.

Build a small physics-visualisation demo that computes a particle system on the GPU (TypeGPU) and renders it in a canvas, then integrate simple control parameters to explore real-time parameter sweeps for teaching simulation concepts.

tools.name: Pointcept/Pointcept
tools.desc: Pointcept: Perceive the world with sparse points, a codebase for point cloud perception research. Latest works: Utonia (ICML'26), Concerto (NeurIPS'25), Sonata (CVPR'25 Highlight), PTv3 (CVPR'24 Oral)

cls.summary: Pointcept is an open-source PyTorch codebase for research and development of point-cloud perception models (semantic/instance segmentation, pretraining and backbones) used in 3D vision and robotics tasks.
cls.what_it_does: Pointcept provides implementations, training scripts and pretrained weights for modern point-cloud perception models and self-supervised pretraining methods, consolidating many backbones and recent papers (e.g. Utonia, Concerto, PTv3). It is used by researchers and engineers to train, evaluate and run inference on 3D point cloud datasets and to reproduce published results; notable aspects are the collection of state-of-the-art models, pretrained weights and integrations with common sparse 3D libraries.
cls.trl_rationale: The repository is actively maintained since 2023, has a large community (3.3k stars), hosts official implementations of multiple peer-reviewed papers with pretrained weights and demos, and shows real research use — evidence consistent with production-ready research code (TRL 7).
prerequisites: familiarity with point-cloud datasets (ScanNet, SemanticKITTI, etc.)
student_project_ideas: Compare semantic segmentation performance and runtime of two Pointcept backbones (e.g. PTv3 vs SPVCNN) on a subset of ScanNet and analyse trade-offs between accuracy, latency and memory.

Use Pointcept pretrained representations (Utonia or Concerto) to build a transfer-learning pipeline for a robotics point-cloud object detection task and evaluate sample efficiency versus training from scratch.

tools.name: open62541/open62541
tools.desc: Open source implementation of OPC UA (OPC Unified Architecture) aka IEC 62541 licensed under Mozilla Public License v2.0

cls.summary: open62541 is an open-source C implementation of the OPC UA (IEC 62541) protocol for building OPC UA clients and servers and integrating industrial-automation communication into applications.
cls.what_it_does: open62541 provides a portable C library and plugins to implement OPC UA clients and servers, including features for secure communication, publish/subscribe, and embedded ports. It is used by embedding the library (or its single-file amalgamation) into C projects and configuring plugins for the target platform; notable points are its platform-independent plugin architecture, single-file distribution option, and a certified example server.
cls.trl_rationale: The project is long-lived (created 2013), has many stars, active development as of the last push, and an OPC Foundation certification for an example server—evidence of real-world adoption and maturity beyond beta; the README and release history indicate stable releases and industry use.
student_project_ideas: Implement an OPC UA server on an embedded board using the open62541 single-file distribution to expose sensor data and demonstrate a simple publish/subscribe pattern to a cloud client.

Build a lab exercise that connects an open62541-based OPC UA client to a simulated industrial controller and implements secure data exchange with mbedTLS/OpenSSL, then log and visualise time-series data in a dashboard.

tools.name: ChartGPU/ChartGPU
tools.desc: Beautiful, open source, WebGPU-based charting library

cls.summary: ChartGPU is an open-source WebGPU-based charting library for high-performance, GPU-accelerated 2D and 3D charts, streaming data, and multi-chart dashboards in the browser.
cls.what_it_does: ChartGPU renders large and streaming datasets using the WebGPU API to provide high-performance charts (lines, scatter, heatmaps, candlesticks) and 3D series (point cloud, surface). It is used as a JavaScript/TypeScript library in WebGPU-capable browsers and supports shared GPU devices for multi-chart dashboards, streaming updates, and GPU/CPU sampling strategies for dense time series.
cls.trl_rationale: The project is active, well-documented, and popular (3.2k stars, examples, and extensive docs) showing more than alpha maturity; however the repository is ~10 months old (<1 year) so it fits a Beta (TRL 6) rather than long-term production/standard status.
prerequisites: WebGPU-capable browser and basic GPU concepts
Node/npm for installing the package and examples
student_project_ideas: Create a streaming dashboard that ingests simulated sensor data (MQTT or WebSocket) and uses ChartGPU to visualise multi-channel time series with zoom-synced charts and a shared GPU device.

Build a web-based digital twin frontend that renders a 3D surface or point-cloud dataset (e.g. terrain or bathymetry) with real-time updates and GPU decimation, comparing CPU vs GPU sampling performance.

tools.name: pmndrs/uikit
tools.desc: 🎨 user interfaces for react-three-fiber

cls.summary: A component library for building performant 3D user interfaces in three.js when using React and react-three-fiber, suitable for web, XR and spatial apps.
cls.what_it_does: uikit provides pre-built, themable UI components and layout primitives that render inside three.js scenes (via react-three-fiber) so developers can create interactive 2D/3D UIs for web and XR applications. It is used as an npm library in React projects, offers examples, tutorials and separate pre-styled kits, and is notable for integration with the pmndrs/react-three-fiber ecosystem and attention to performance for spatial interfaces.
cls.trl_rationale: The project is actively maintained, has substantial community interest (3.2k+ stars), published docs, examples and multiple packaged kits, and recent commits—evidence of production readiness. Repository age (~2.75 years) and ecosystem adoption support a production-ready TRL rather than an experimental rating.
student_project_ideas: Build an interactive VR instrument panel (HUD) in a react-three-fiber scene using uikit for layout and UI controls, and connect it to simulated sensor data from a Node.js server.
Create a web-based digital twin dashboard with 3D controls and status panels using uikit components, three.js models and a time-series backend (e.g. InfluxDB) to visualise and manipulate asset state.

tools.name: google/brax
tools.desc: Massively parallel rigidbody physics simulation on accelerator hardware.

cls.summary: Brax is a JAX-based, highly parallel and differentiable rigid-body physics engine used for fast simulation and reinforcement learning research on accelerators (CPU/GPU/TPU).
cls.what_it_does: Brax simulates rigid-body dynamics and collision/constraint resolution with multiple interchangeable pipelines (MJX, generalized, positional, spring) and provides training algorithms (PPO, SAC, ARS, analytic policy gradients) for RL agents. It is designed for high-speed, large-batch simulation on accelerator hardware and notable for being fully differentiable and tightly integrated with JAX for scalable experiments.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository is stable and established (created 2021) with active maintenance, a NeurIPS paper, 3k+ stars and regular releases; parts of the project (training) remain actively maintained while envs are being deprecated in favour of other engines, so it's mature in research use but not a de-facto industry standard.
student_project_ideas: Compare controller performance and sim-to-real transfer metrics by training a gait policy in Brax and evaluating equivalent trajectories on a PyBullet or real robot dataset.

Implement a differentiable parameter identification experiment: use Brax's differentiable pipeline to fit unknown joint/friction parameters from simulated sensor traces and compare optimisation convergence with finite-difference approaches.

tools.name: vasturiano/globe.gl
tools.desc: UI component for Globe Data Visualization using ThreeJS/WebGL

cls.summary: Globe.GL is a JavaScript web component that renders interactive 3D globe visualisations using Three.js/WebGL for mapping and displaying geospatial datasets.
cls.what_it_does: Globe.GL provides a convenience wrapper around the three-globe plugin to display data layers (points, arcs, polygons, heatmaps, tiles, labels, etc.) on a 3D spherical globe in the browser. It is used by developers to build interactive, web-based globe visualisations and includes many examples (arcs, choropleths, heatmaps, satellites) and React bindings for integration into applications.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository created in 2019, many stars (3.2k), numerous documented examples and active maintenance indicate broad adoption and production use; README and published examples show a stable, mature library.
student_project_ideas: Build an interactive web map that visualises real-time earthquake or satellite telemetry on a 3D globe, using Globe.GL for rendering and a public API (USGS, NORAD) for live data ingestion.

Create a comparative visual analysis of global transport links (airline routes or submarine cables) showing flow intensity and perform basic network analysis, exporting results to a web dashboard integrated with Globe.GL.

tools.name: UE4SS-RE/RE-UE4SS
tools.desc: Injectable LUA scripting system, SDK generator, live property editor and other dumping utilities for UE4/5 games

cls.summary: RE-UE4SS is an open-source injectable modding framework that adds a Lua scripting API, C++ modding hooks, SDK/header generators and live property editing for Unreal Engine 4/5 games.
cls.what_it_does: It provides a runtime modding layer for UE4/UE5 games so users can write Lua or C++ mods, load blueprint mods, inspect and edit live object properties, and generate C++/UHT-compatible headers from game binaries. Notable features include a live property viewer/editor, SDK/header dumpers and tooling to create mods without modifying original game files.
cls.trl_rationale: The project is several years old (created 2022), has many stars and forks, frequent activity including recent pushes, releases and extensive documentation which indicate production-ready maturity within the modding community rather than academic proof-of-concept.
prerequisites: familiarity with Unreal Engine internals and build tooling
CMake / Ninja and optionally Rust toolchain for some components
student_project_ideas: Create a small UE5 game sample and implement a Lua mod using RE-UE4SS to add a debug HUD and runtime-tweakable parameters via the live property editor.
Use RE-UE4SS's header dumper to generate C++ headers for a simple UE game and build a C++ mod that exposes a new gameplay feature, documenting the reverse-engineering and integration steps.

tools.name: Open-Cascade-SAS/OCCT
tools.desc: OCCT is an open-source software development platform for 3D CAD, CAM, CAE.

cls.summary: Open CASCADE Technology (OCCT) is a mature open-source C++ platform providing 3D surface and solid modelling, CAD data exchange and visualization libraries for CAD/CAM/CAE software development.
cls.what_it_does: OCCT provides C++ libraries and tools for building and manipulating 3D geometry (B-rep solids and surfaces), importing/exporting CAD data and rendering/visualisation. It is used as the geometry and interoperability core inside CAD, CAM and CAE applications and notable for being a full-featured, production-capable modelling kernel available under an LGPL licence.
cls.trl_rationale: OCCT is a long-running, actively maintained project with many stars, frequent commits and official releases and documentation; it is a mature CAD kernel used by downstream projects, which supports a high TRL. The repository is several years old, has substantial community activity and packaged release assets.
prerequisites: familiarity with CAD/geometry concepts (B-rep, NURBS, topology)
student_project_ideas: Create a small CAD application that uses OCCT to model a parametric mechanical part, export it to STEP, and visualise it with OCCT's viewer (combine with a simple Qt GUI).
Build a mesh-export pipeline that converts OCCT B-rep geometry to a finite-element mesh (e.g. using Gmsh) and run a basic structural simulation to compare geometry-preprocessing issues.

tools.name: ruucm/shadergradient
tools.desc: Create beautiful moving gradients on Framer, Figma and React

cls.summary: ShaderGradient is a React / three.js library that renders customizable, moving 3D gradients for use in web apps, Framer and a Figma plugin.
cls.what_it_does: ShaderGradient provides a lightweight renderer (ShaderGradient and ShaderGradientCanvas) that uses GLSL shaders and three.js to draw animated gradient meshes which can be driven by props or a URL query string. It is distributed with React and Vue adapters and separate stateless UI components for Framer/Figma, making it easy to embed live, dynamic gradient backgrounds in web UIs and design tools. Notable points are its focus on performance, examples for Next/CRA/Vite, and the split between renderer and UI packages for different host environments.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository is long-lived (created 2022), has high community adoption (3k+ stars), active maintenance with recent pushes and multiple example apps, and published packages and integrations; these indicate production-readiness though it is a specialized renderer rather than an industry-wide standard.
student_project_ideas: Create a web portfolio or product landing page that embeds ShaderGradient as an interactive background, adding a UI to let users modify shader parameters and export the chosen configuration to a URL.

Integrate ShaderGradient into a UI prototype built with Framer or Next.js and measure performance across devices while experimenting with different mesh types and shader parameters (combine with simple telemetry logging to analyse frame rate and GPU usage).

tools.name: hello245m/free-stockdb
tools.desc: 面向 A 股日K、分钟K与ETF分钟数据的本地量化引擎，集成增量同步、本地缓存、复权、批量查询、回测与指标计算。

cls.summary: free-stockdb is a local, open-source time‑series data engine for A‑share market minute/day/tick data that provides incremental sync, local storage, fast bulk queries, indicator calculation and backtesting interfaces.
cls.what_it_does: It solves the data‑engineering bottleneck for full‑market quantitative research by synchronising, cleaning, compressing and storing Chinese stock minute/day/tick data locally and exposing fast batch query, indicator calculation and backtest interfaces. Users run a small local service (C++ time‑series core) and call it from Python, HTTP, Excel/HTML or MCP; notable features include incremental sync, Zstd compressed storage, built‑in 39 technical indicators and cross‑platform binary releases.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository is ~6 months old with cross‑platform binary releases, published test releases, active development and 3k+ stars indicating community interest; however age under 1 year limits a TRL >6 per the rubric despite evidence of pressure testing and ready binaries.
prerequisites: familiarity with time‑series market data and backtesting concepts
basic sysadmin (installing local services on Windows/macOS/Linux)
student_project_ideas: Build and evaluate a full‑market minute‑level backtest for a simple momentum strategy using free-stockdb as the local data backend and compare runtime and throughput against a remote API approach.
Implement a custom technical indicator in Python, register it to the local engine or compute it via the SDK, then run a batched experiment across 1000+ stocks and visualise performance differences.

tools.name: projectchrono/chrono
tools.desc: High-performance C++ library for multiphysics and multibody dynamics simulations

cls.summary: Chrono is a mature open-source C++ library for high-performance multi-body and multi-physics simulation, with Python and C# APIs and modules for FEA, granular dynamics, and fluid–solid interaction.
cls.what_it_does: Chrono lets you build and run simulations of rigid and deformable multibody systems, granular materials, and fluid–solid interaction, and includes modules for vehicles, robots and sensors. It is used via C++ (primary) or Python/C# bindings, configured with CMake, and notable for scalable solvers and optional GPU/multi-core acceleration for large simulations.
cls.trl_rationale: Chrono is a long-lived (created 2013), actively maintained project with thousands of stars, extensive API docs (C++ and Python), modular features (vehicle, FSI, granular), and production-oriented capabilities (GPU/ROCm, multi-core). This sustained community, documentation and real-world use supports a TRL of 8.
prerequisites: familiarity with Python if using PyChrono
basic experience with compilers and platform-specific builds (Linux/Windows/Mac)
student_project_ideas: Simulate and validate a simple ground-vehicle suspension model in Chrono, compare multibody results to a reduced-order analytical model, and visualise tyre–terrain interaction using the vehicle module.
Integrate a robot arm model in Chrono with ROS2 sensors (camera and IMU) to test perception-in-the-loop control and run several scenarios to evaluate collision avoidance and dynamic response.

tools.name: KiCad/kicad-source-mirror
tools.desc: This is an active mirror of the KiCad development branch, which is hosted at GitLab (updated every time something is pushed). Pull requests on GitHub are not accepted or watched.

cls.summary: KiCad is a mature open-source electronic design automation (EDA) suite for schematic capture, PCB layout and related tools used to design and produce printed circuit boards.
cls.what_it_does: KiCad provides tools to create electronic schematics, design multi-layer PCB layouts, generate manufacturing outputs (Gerber, drill files, BOMs) and preview 3D models of boards and enclosures. It is used by engineers to go from circuit idea through detailed PCB design and fabrication outputs, and is notable for being a full-featured, actively developed free alternative to commercial EDA packages.
cls.trl_rationale: The repository is long-lived (created 2013) and shows active development with CI, many contributors, wide adoption and comprehensive components (schematic editor, PCB editor, 3D viewer). These indicate a mature, widely used project rather than an experimental prototype.
student_project_ideas: Design and simulate a low-power sensor PCB in KiCad, produce manufacturing Gerber files and assemble a prototype to validate sensor and power circuitry.
Create a PCB and export STEP models from KiCad to integrate with a FreeCAD enclosure, then run a fit-check and prepare documentation for fabrication.

tools.name: SharpAI/DeepCamera
tools.desc: Open-Source AI Camera Skills Platform, AI NVR & CCTV Surveillance. Local VLM video analysis with Qwen, DeepSeek, SmolVLM, LLaVA, YOLO26. LLM-powered agentic security camera agent — watches, understands, remembers & guards your home via Telegram, Discord or Slack. Pluggable AI skills. OpenAI, Google, Anthropic or local AI. Runs on Mac Mini & AI PC.

cls.summary: DeepCamera is an open-source platform that adds local AI (VLM/LLM and detection) skills to CCTV/NVR camera feeds for on-premise video analysis, alerts and automation.
cls.what_it_does: DeepCamera provides a pluggable skills framework that runs computer-vision and vision-language models locally against camera streams to detect objects, recognize faces, anonymise video and trigger automations. It is used by installing skills (detection, segmentation, annotation, training, automation) which communicate via a JSONL stdin/stdout protocol and can be orchestrated from the SharpAI Aegis desktop app or via MQTT/webhooks/HA integrations. Notable aspects are local-only inference for privacy, hardware-aware optimisation (TensorRT / CoreML / OpenVINO / ONNX / Coral), and an agent layer that integrates LLMs for setup, chat and alerts.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository created in 2019 and actively maintained with many stars, multiple documented skills, hardware backends and a desktop companion (SharpAI Aegis). The README and skill catalogue show production-ready features and integration points; evidence of wide real-world deployment is implied but not formally cited, so TRL 7 (production-ready) is appropriate.
prerequisites: familiarity with Linux/macOS and basic system administration
experience with Python and Node.js environments
knowledge of GPU/accelerator setup (TensorRT/CoreML/OpenVINO/Coral) and Docker is helpful
student_project_ideas: Integrate DeepCamera with Home Assistant to implement a privacy-preserving depth-map transform on home cameras and trigger automations via MQTT when human activity is detected.
Build and evaluate a local fall-detection pipeline using DeepCamera skills and compare detection latency and accuracy across hardware backends (CPU, GPU, Coral TPU) as a performance/validation study.

tools.name: containers/ramalama
tools.desc: RamaLama is an open-source developer tool that simplifies the local serving of AI models from any source and facilitates their use for inference in production, all through the familiar language of containers.

cls.summary: RamaLama is an open-source tool that simplifies running and serving AI models locally by packaging models as OCI container images and managing hardware-accelerated runtimes.
cls.what_it_does: RamaLama treats AI models like container images: it detects available accelerators, pulls an appropriate accelerated container image, and runs the model in an isolated, rootless container exposing a REST/chat API. It removes much of the host configuration friction for GPU/CPU/back-end selection and supports multiple model registries so models can be used for inference in development or production-like local environments.
cls.trl_rationale: The project is over two years old, has many stars, regular recent commits, packaged installers (macOS .pkg), distribution in Fedora and PyPI, and clear user-facing docs and binaries—evidence of production-ready tooling rather than an early prototype.
prerequisites: basic understanding of model inference and GPU drivers for hardware acceleration
student_project_ideas: Create a lab where students package a small transformer model into an OCI image, deploy it with RamaLama, and benchmark latency and throughput across CPU and GPU accelerated images.

Integrate RamaLama-hosted model inference with a small robot: stream sensor data from a robot to a local RamaLama model container and use the model outputs to perform simple autonomy or anomaly-detection tasks.

tools.name: jslee02/awesome-robotics-libraries
tools.desc: :sunglasses: A curated list of robotics libraries and software

cls.summary: A long-standing curated list of robotics libraries, simulators and related software that helps researchers and students discover tools across robotics subfields.
cls.what_it_does: This repository collects and organises links to robotics middleware, simulators, kinematics/dynamics libraries, perception/SLAM, motion planning, control and related tools. It is used as a reference to find established open-source projects and compare available software when selecting platforms for research, teaching or development. Its notability comes from being well-maintained, popular (many stars) and broad in scope across robotics subdomains.
cls.trl_rationale: The repository is long-lived (created 2016), actively maintained and widely starred, indicating sustained community value as a reference resource rather than experimental code; it functions as a production-ready curated index rather than a research prototype.
prerequisites: familiarity with common robotics concepts (ROS, simulators)
student_project_ideas: Use the list to select two simulators (e.g. Gazebo and MuJoCo) and implement the same robot task, then compare ease-of-use, performance and sensor integration in a short report.

Create a small survey and hands-on lab where students pick a motion-planning library from the list (e.g. OMPL or MoveIt), implement path planning for a manipulator, and demonstrate results in simulation.

tools.name: hadashiA/VContainer
tools.desc: The extra fast, minimum code size, GC-free DI (Dependency Injection) library running on Unity Game Engine.

cls.summary: VContainer is a small, high-performance dependency injection (DI) library designed for use in Unity projects to provide fast, low‑GC object resolution and lifecycle scoping.
cls.what_it_does: VContainer provides constructor/method/property injection, lifetime scopes, and Unity-specific integrations (PlayerLoopSystem, UniTask, ECS) so Unity developers can register and resolve dependencies with minimal allocations and small code size. It is used as a Unity package (UPM/OpenUPM or .unitypackage) and can be optionally accelerated with a SourceGenerator; its notable aspects are low GC allocation and performance optimisations targeted at game / real-time Unity projects.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository is long-lived (created 2020), has substantial community interest (3k+ stars), active maintenance with recent pushes and releases, and documentation; these indicate a mature, widely used Unity library rather than an experimental prototype.
prerequisites: C# and familiarity with dependency injection concepts
student_project_ideas: Build a small Unity digital twin (simple factory floor or robot arm) and use VContainer to manage scoped lifetimes for subsystems and scene-level dependency graphs.
Create a Unity simulation that loads levels additively and uses VContainer child scopes to manage resource lifetimes and test hot-reload or staged initialization behaviors.

tools.name: gdquest-demos/godot-open-rpg
tools.desc: Learn to create turn-based combat with this Open Source RPG demo ⚔

cls.summary: A polished open-source Godot 4 demo project that teaches how to build a classical 2D turn-based RPG (combat, inventory, maps, UI) using GDScript.
cls.what_it_does: This repository provides a complete demo project and example code for creating a turn-based 2D RPG in Godot 4, demonstrating combat, inventory, progression, maps, dialogues and UI systems. It's intended as a learning resource and code reference you can open in Godot 4.7.2+ and reuse or extend in your own game projects.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository is mature and actively maintained since 2018 with thousands of stars and recent commits, indicating wide community use as a learning/demo project rather than a research prototype.
student_project_ideas: Extend the demo's combat system by adding status effects and a simple AI opponent behaviour, then measure and visualise turn resolution performance.
Replace the tile/asset pack with a custom level and implement a quest system that persists player progress using Godot's save system.

tools.name: rafska/awesome-local-llm
tools.desc: A curated list of awesome platforms, tools, practices and resources that helps run LLMs locally

cls.summary: A community-curated, regularly updated index of platforms, engines, UIs, models and resources for running large language models locally or self-hosted.
cls.what_it_does: This repository collects links and short descriptions of inference platforms, engines, user interfaces, models, tools and tutorials for running LLMs on local machines or private infrastructure. It is used as a discovery resource to compare options and find implementations, benchmarks and tutorials rather than as runnable software itself.
cls.trl_rationale: The repository is a mature, actively maintained curated list with thousands of stars and frequent pushes over more than a year, indicating broad community use and usefulness as a discovery resource rather than experimental code.
student_project_ideas: Compare three open-source local inference platforms (e.g. LocalAI, vLLM, llama.cpp) on latency and resource use for a small retrieval-augmented chatbot and write a short report.

Use an inference engine and a listed web UI from the list to deploy a simple self-hosted question-answering assistant over a course dataset and document the deployment steps and security considerations.

tools.name: LibrePCB/LibrePCB
tools.desc: A powerful, innovative and intuitive EDA suite for everyone!

cls.summary: LibrePCB is an open-source electronic design automation (EDA) suite for creating schematics and PCB layouts on Windows, Linux and macOS.
cls.what_it_does: LibrePCB provides tools to create electronic schematics, manage component libraries, and design printed circuit board layouts for fabrication. It is used as a standalone desktop application (built with Qt/C++) and aims to be a full PCB design toolchain alternative to other EDA packages, notable for being free, actively developed, and cross-platform.
cls.trl_rationale: The project has an established history (created 2015), thousands of stars, active recent commits and official stable releases and documentation, indicating a mature, widely used open-source EDA application.
prerequisites: familiarity with PCB design concepts (schematics, footprints, nets)
CMake and native build toolchain for building from source
Qt development environment if contributing to the GUI
student_project_ideas: Design and fabricate a simple microcontroller breakout PCB: create schematic and PCB in LibrePCB, generate Gerbers, and assemble and test the board with an embedded firmware task.
Compare PCB layout rules by implementing the same circuit in LibrePCB and KiCad, then run DRC checks and produce fabrication outputs to report differences in workflow and manufacturability.

tools.name: greggman/twgl.js
tools.desc: A Tiny WebGL helper Library

cls.summary: TWGL is a small JavaScript helper library that simplifies low-level WebGL calls so developers can write less boilerplate when building WebGL graphics in the browser.
cls.what_it_does: TWGL wraps common WebGL tasks — compiling shaders, creating buffers and textures, setting attributes and uniforms, and creating framebuffers — into concise helper functions so you can implement low-level GPU rendering with far fewer API calls. It is used in browser-based real-time 3D visualisation and demos where developers want direct control over WebGL without the verbosity of the raw API. Its notable point is being minimal and lightweight compared to higher-level engines (the README explicitly contrasts it with three.js).
cls.trl_rationale: The project has a long history (created 2015), thousands of stars, and recent activity, indicating wide adoption and a stable API; the README and examples show production-quality usage rather than an experimental prototype.
prerequisites: basic WebGL concepts (shaders, buffers, attributes, uniforms)
student_project_ideas: Build an interactive browser-based physics visualisation that uses TWGL for rendering simulation results from a simple dynamics solver (e.g. integrate a Modelica or custom JS solver and visualise in WebGL).
Create a WebGL scene editor where students load geometry (glTF), adjust transforms/materials, and use TWGL to manage shaders, buffers and textures for real-time preview.

tools.name: xyproto/algernon
tools.desc: Small self-contained pure-Go web server with Lua, Teal, Markdown, HTTP/2, QUIC, Redis, TypeScript, npm-less React 19, SQLite, and PostgreSQL support ++

cls.summary: Algernon is a small self-contained Go web server that serves static and dynamic content with built-in support for HTTP/2, HTTP/3 (QUIC), Lua/Teal scripting, Markdown, templating engines and several databases.
cls.what_it_does: Algernon provides a single-file native web server binary that can render Markdown, run Lua/Teal scripts, bundle JSX/TypeScript without npm, and serve over HTTP/2 and HTTP/3. It is used to quickly build and host small web apps or sites with optional integrations (Redis, SQLite, PostgreSQL, Ollama LLMs) and live-reload for development. It is notable for bundling many features (Lua VM, Teal, template engines, esbuild, QUIC) into one lightweight executable.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository created in 2015, with thousands of stars, releases and pre-built images, active recent pushes and a Docker image; evidence of long-term use and a stable feature set supports a high maturity rating.
prerequisites: familiarity with web development (HTTP, HTML, JS/TS)
student_project_ideas: Build a small instrument dashboard that serves sensor readings from SQLite/Redis and a simple React/JSX frontend bundled by Algernon, demonstrating live reload and HTTP/2 delivery.

Create a course microservice that uses Lua handlers to implement REST endpoints backed by PostgreSQL and a simple web UI, then deploy it with the provided Docker image and measure HTTP/2 vs HTTP/3 performance.

tools.name: Pinvou/pinvou-agent
tools.desc: Open-source desktop AI agent for tools, files, knowledge, workflows, and real deliverables.

cls.summary: Pinvou Agent is an open-source desktop AI agent workspace that integrates local or cloud LLMs, tools, connectors and workflows to produce persistent deliverables, editable artifacts, and coding assistance inside a single app.
cls.what_it_does: Pinvou provides a local-first desktop workspace where users run multi-session AI agents that can use tools, read and edit project files, manage a local knowledge base, and produce deliverable artifacts (documents, designs, code changes). It connects to local vLLM runtimes or OpenAI-compatible endpoints, supports MCP/ACP tool servers and many third-party connectors, and exposes skills, commands and workflows to automate repeatable tasks.
cls.trl_rationale: The project is active, has many stars and forks, documented features and release downloads, showing a beta-level product; however the repository is only ~116 days old so it lacks a long track record required for TRL 7+.
prerequisites: basic familiarity with LLMs and model endpoints (OpenAI-compatible)
comfort installing desktop apps on Windows/macOS/Linux
optional: running local vLLM or MCP servers for full local capabilities
student_project_ideas: Build a coding-assistant integration that uses Pinvou to load a small Git repository, have the agent generate and run tests using a local vLLM, and then report changes as a pull request.
Use Pinvou's local knowledge base and connectors to create an engineering team wiki that the agent queries to produce requirement summaries and traceability links for a small systems design exercise.

tools.name: headwaymaps/headway
tools.desc: Self-hostable maps stack, powered by OpenStreetMap.

cls.summary: Headway is an open-source, self-hosted maps stack that provides a basemap frontend, geocoding and routing from OpenStreetMap extracts.
cls.what_it_does: Headway lets you build and run your own maps server from OSM extracts, providing a map frontend, search (geocoding/POI) and routing (driving, cycling, walking). It is used by preparing an OSM extract and running the build/serve commands to generate tiles, indices and services for a chosen area; notable for packaging multiple map components into a single, reproducible stack you can host yourself.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository is mature (created 2020, ~3k stars, active maintenance with recent pushes) and provides a complete, working stack; these indicators and the stable feature set (frontend, geocoder, routing) support a high maturity rating.
prerequisites: moderate disk space (50–100 GB) and >=8 GB RAM for build
student_project_ideas: Build a campus-scale self-hosted map with Headway, integrate a custom POI dataset (e.g. buildings and rooms) and create routing between building entrances.

Compare routing results and performance between Headway and an external routing engine (e.g. OSRM) for bike- and pedestrian-friendly routes in a medium-sized city and visualise differences in a web dashboard.

tools.name: tscircuit/tscircuit
tools.desc: Create real electronics with Typescript and React

cls.summary: tscircuit is an open-source toolkit that lets you write PCB schematics and layouts in TypeScript/React, preview them in 2D/3D, and export manufacturing files.
cls.what_it_does: tscircuit turns TypeScript and React components into schematics, PCB layouts, 3D renders and fabrication outputs (Gerber, BOM, Pick-and-Place). It is used by writing circuit code or via a CLI/playground to iteratively preview and export boards for manufacturing. Notable features include a code-first workflow, a web playground, a package registry for reusable components, and built-in export of manufacturing files.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository is over two years old, has substantial community interest (3k+ stars), an online playground, CLI, registry and active development; these indicate production-ready maturity though not yet an industry standard.
student_project_ideas: Create a simple sensor breakout board in tscircuit from TypeScript, generate Gerbers and assemble a prototype, then measure and report on manufacturability and BOM cost compared with a KiCad version.

Build a modular motor controller in tscircuit, publish components to the registry, simulate placement and 3D fit on a motor mount, and produce a Pick-and-Place file to drive a small batch assembly workflow.

tools.name: Luce-Org/lucebox
tools.desc: Lucebox inference engine for heterogeneous hardware & consumer GPUs

cls.summary: Lucebox is an open-source local inference engine that runs large language and multimodal models efficiently on heterogeneous consumer GPUs (AMD R9700 and Ryzen AI MAX+ and NVIDIA via CUDA).
cls.what_it_does: Lucebox provides fast, production-oriented inference for large LLMs and vision models on consumer GPUs by partitioning work across devices, using HIP/CUDA kernels, speculative decoding and paged attention to support long prompts and multi-user batching. It is used by building from source on Linux (ROCm/CUDA) and can expose OpenAI/Anthropic-compatible APIs and integrations for applications and agent frameworks.
cls.trl_rationale: The project is active, well-starred (3000+ stars), supports multiple real models, has CI and platform-specific builds (HIP/CUDA) and regular commits, indicating beta-level maturity; however the repository is only ~7 months old so it lacks the multi-year track record required for TRL 7+.
prerequisites: NVIDIA or AMD GPUs (Radeon AI R9700 / Ryzen AI MAX+ or CUDA-capable GPUs)
Familiarity with model formats (GGUF) and command-line inference servers
student_project_ideas: Benchmark Lucebox against llama.cpp and another local runtime on the same AMD hardware to quantify throughput, latency and memory use for long prompts (include automated scripts and plots).

Build a local agent service for a robot or digital twin that uses Lucebox (deployed on a Ryzen AI MAX+ or cloud GPU instance) to generate planning/dialogue, and measure end-to-end latency and prompt cache hit rates under multi-user load.

tools.name: eProsima/Fast-DDS
tools.desc: The most complete DDS - Proven: Plenty of success cases. Looking for commercial support? Contact info@eprosima.com

cls.summary: eProsima Fast DDS is a mature C++ implementation of the OMG DDS/RTPS publish–subscribe middleware used for real-time distributed systems (widely used as the default middleware in ROS 2).
cls.what_it_does: Fast DDS implements the DDS standard and the underlying RTPS wire protocol to provide configurable, discovery-based publisher/subscriber communications over networks (including unreliable transports like UDP). It is used as a library (and with tools/CLI and Docker images) to build real-time, distributed and interoperable systems, notable for its use in ROS 2 and production deployments across robotics and IoT.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository is long-lived (since 2014), actively maintained, has thousands of stars and forks, documented releases and official adoption (notably as the default middleware in ROS 2), which indicates a mature, widely adopted project.
prerequisites: familiarity with DDS/RTPS concepts and message/topic/pub-sub patterns
student_project_ideas: Build a small ROS 2 robot application that exchanges sensor and command topics between two simulated nodes using Fast DDS and visualize end-to-end latency and reliability under different network loss conditions.

Create a distributed monitoring prototype where several edge devices publish telemetry to a central subscriber via Fast DDS; measure scalability and compare QoS settings (reliability, history, lifespan) and present findings.

tools.name: MaximeVandegar/Papers-in-100-Lines-of-Code
tools.desc: Implementation of papers in 100 lines of code.

cls.summary: A curated collection of short (≈100-line) Python/PyTorch implementations of influential machine learning papers for learning and experimentation.
cls.what_it_does: This repository implements many seminal ML papers as compact, readable Python scripts so readers can study core ideas with minimal code. It's used as an educational resource and drop-in examples for experimentation and learning rather than a production library, notable for breadth and concise implementations.
cls.trl_rationale: The repository is several years old (created 2020), has a large star count (2915) and many implemented examples across well-known papers, and is actively maintained; these indicate it is stable and widely used as an educational resource rather than experimental prototype.
student_project_ideas: Re-implement and compare training behaviour of a specific generative model from the repo (e.g. GAN or diffusion variant) on a small engineering dataset (e.g. CAD renderings) and report differences in sample quality and training stability.

Extend one concise implementation (for example, a NeRF or inverse-rendering example) to add a small engineering feature such as metric scale recovery or integration with simple CAD models and evaluate reconstruction accuracy.

tools.name: mw00/project-maya
tools.desc: Run GLM-5.3 (744B), GLM-5.3-Flash (321B), DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash (748B) and MiniMax-M3.1-Flash (428B) on your own GPUs - one engine, one dashboard, OpenAI- and Anthropic-compatible API.

cls.summary: Project Maya is an open-source local LLM inference engine and web dashboard that runs large models (GLM-5.3 family, DeepSeek V4.1-Flash, MiniMax M3.1-Flash) on consumer and server GPUs with an OpenAI- and Anthropic-compatible API.
cls.what_it_does: Project Maya packages model-specific engines, automated setup, model download/management and a browser UI so you can run and serve large pretrained models on one or more NVIDIA/AMD GPUs and NVMe storage. It manages expert placement between GPU, RAM and SSD, offers quantised versions and a compatible API for coding agents and multi-session serving, and includes monitoring and a chat interface.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository is very new (created 42 days ago) so it cannot be judged beyond early/adopted alpha; however it already has many stars, active pushes and concrete install scripts and benchmarks which indicate early adopters rather than just a paper prototype.
prerequisites: NVIDIA or AMD GPU (modern cards recommended)
sufficient RAM and NVMe storage (see docs/MEMORY.md)
basic Linux or Windows command-line familiarity
student_project_ideas: Benchmark Project Maya's throughput and latency for a chosen model on different GPU configurations and compare results with published numbers, producing a short report and reproducible scripts.

Integrate Project Maya's OpenAI-compatible API with a simple autonomous agent (e.g., a retrieval-augmented QA or tool-using bot) and evaluate its behaviour and resource usage on a single-GPU workstation.

tools.name: leozide/leocad
tools.desc: A CAD application for creating virtual LEGO models

cls.summary: LeoCAD is an open-source desktop CAD application for creating virtual LEGO models on Windows, macOS and Linux.
cls.what_it_does: LeoCAD provides a graphical environment and parts library for assembling virtual LEGO models, letting users place, rotate and connect standard LEGO elements and visualise builds with OpenGL-accelerated rendering. It is used as a hobbyist/modeling CAD tool notable for its large LDraw-compatible parts library, multi-platform installers (AppImage, Snap, Flatpak, native installers) and an active open-source project.
cls.trl_rationale: The project has existed since 2016, is actively maintained with recent pushes and many stars, provides packaged releases for multiple platforms and a managed parts library (LDraw), indicating a mature, widely used open-source desktop application.
student_project_ideas: Design and document a simple mechanical linkage using LEGO parts in LeoCAD, export images and an assembly bill-of-materials, then prototype selected parts by 3D printing.
Use LeoCAD with the LDraw parts library to create and present a modular assembly exercise for a systems engineering class that demonstrates configuration management and versioned assemblies.

tools.name: sahibzada-allahyar/Formal-Verification-RSI
tools.desc: Formal verification for AI: a Lean 4 + Dafny proof checker that catches fake AI proofs (reward hacking), and verified recursive self-improvement (RSI) for coding agents. AI for math, physics and software engineering.

cls.summary: A research-quality Python toolkit that enforces stronger machine-checking of proofs (Lean 4 and Dafny) and implements a verified recursive self-improvement (RSI) loop for coding agents to prevent reward hacking.
cls.what_it_does: The repository provides a 'Millennium Harness' proof-checker that detects weakened or tampered proofs in Lean 4 and Dafny solutions, and a 'Millennium RSI' agent loop that only accepts self-modifications that increase true verified performance on held-out tasks. It is used from the command line (Python modules) to check proof files, run agent-improvement loops with LLM solvers/improvers, and to audit benchmark results; notable features are kernel-level checks, spec-tamper detection, and admission rules for verified lemma libraries.
cls.trl_rationale: The project is over one year old, has a large star count and active development, plus experimental results and documented runs, but it reads like a research-grade toolkit rather than an established production standard; evidence points to a beta research project rather than widely deployed production software.
prerequisites: familiarity with theorem provers (Lean 4 and Dafny)
basic knowledge of formal methods and proof checking
student_project_ideas: Extend the Millennium Harness to add a new tamper-detection rule for a specific Lean construct and evaluate how many accepted benchmark proofs the new rule flags compared to the baseline.
Build a small RSI experiment using an open LLM (or a stub solver) to demonstrate the admission and kernel-checking of proposed lemmas, and report measured improvements on a held-out mini-benchmark.

tools.name: zig-gamedev/zig-gamedev
tools.desc: Dev repo for @zig-gamedev libs and sample applications

cls.summary: A collection of Zig-language libraries and sample applications for real-time rendering, graphics, and game-development that target native GPUs (wgpu, DirectX12) and WebAssembly.
cls.what_it_does: Provides reusable Zig libraries (math, graphics, GUI, physics bindings) and many runnable sample applications that demonstrate PBR, raytracing, procedural meshes, audio experiments and physics integration. It is used by building example targets with the Zig toolchain and runs natively (Windows/Linux/macOS) or as WebAssembly; notable for being a mature, actively maintained community repo for graphics development in Zig.
cls.trl_rationale: The repository is several years old (created 2021), has many stars and forks, active recent commits and a large set of sample apps and libraries indicating production-ready examples; it lacks the footprint of an industry-standard engine but shows stable, real-world use by the community.
prerequisites: knowledge of Zig language and build system
basic GPU / graphics programming concepts (shaders, pipelines, PBR)
familiarity with building native and WebAssembly targets
student_project_ideas: Build a small interactive simulation that visualises dynamic rigid-body physics by combining the repo's Bullet physics sample with a procedurally generated scene and add camera controls for exploration.
Port one of the PBR rendering samples to WebAssembly and measure/optimise performance differences between native wgpu and wasm builds, reporting on shader compilation and resource usage.

tools.name: YarnSpinnerTool/YarnSpinner
tools.desc: The core compiler and engine-agnostic components for Yarn Spinner, the friendly dialogue tool.

cls.summary: Yarn Spinner is an open-source dialogue system for games that compiles and runs interactive conversations and exposes lines, player options and commands to a game engine.
cls.what_it_does: Yarn Spinner lets writers author interactive conversations in a simple screenplay-like syntax and provides a runtime/compiler that delivers dialogue lines, choice options and engine commands to a host game. It is typically used as a library or engine package (notably with Unity) so developers can drive UI and game events from authored conversations. It is notable for being mature, MIT-licensed, and used in several commercial games.
cls.trl_rationale: The project is long-lived (created 2015), actively maintained (recent pushes), widely used in commercial games listed in the README, and has a sizeable community and stars, which indicates mature, real-world adoption.
prerequisites: familiarity with Unity or game engine integration
basic understanding of game event systems and UI
student_project_ideas: Create a Unity demo scene where Yarn Spinner drives NPC conversations and triggers animations and scene events based on player choices.
Integrate Yarn Spinner with a ROS-enabled robot or virtual agent to prototype conversational interactions for a human-robot interaction lab, mapping Yarn commands to robot behaviours.

tools.name: BlueMap-Minecraft/BlueMap
tools.desc: A Minecraft mapping tool that creates 3D models of your Minecraft worlds and displays them in a web viewer.

cls.summary: BlueMap reads Minecraft world files, generates 3D models of the terrain and builds an interactive web viewer so you can explore worlds in a browser.
cls.what_it_does: BlueMap parses Minecraft world data to produce detailed 3D meshes and textures, then serves an interactive web map so users can navigate and inspect the world from any angle. It is distributed as server plugins (Spigot/Paper, Sponge), mods (Fabric, Forge) or a standalone command‑line tool, and uses a WebGL/three.js frontend for viewing. It is notable for asynchronous rendering on game servers and for producing full 3D surface models rather than only top-down tiles.
cls.trl_rationale: Active project since 2019 with many stars (2.8k), regular commits and releases, and multiple distribution formats (plugins, mods, standalone), indicating maturity and an established user base rather than an experimental prototype.
prerequisites: Minecraft world files or running Minecraft server (Spigot/Paper/Sponge/Fabric/Forge)
Basic server administration and web hosting knowledge
student_project_ideas: Create a lab exercise where students export a small Minecraft world, run BlueMap to generate a 3D web map, then annotate and measure features in the viewer to practice geospatial measurement and visualization techniques.

Build a student project that integrates BlueMap with a simple web dashboard (e.g. Node.js) to visualise time-series metadata (players, events) overlaid on the generated 3D map to explore linking operational data to spatial representations.

tools.name: reacher-z/Awesome-REA
tools.desc: Curated tools, case studies and papers for reverse engineering websites, games, apps, binaries, firmware and protocols. Source-reviewed, English and Chinese.

cls.summary: A curated, searchable collection of tools, case studies and papers for reverse engineering websites, games, apps, binaries, firmware and protocols.
cls.what_it_does: This repository aggregates and indexes thousands of resources (tools, case studies and research papers) for reverse engineering across web, game, app, native binary and firmware domains. It is used as a discovery and reference catalogue (website + API + README index) that points users to specific analysis and rebuilding tools, benchmarks and agent workflows, with entries reviewed from source.
cls.trl_rationale: The repository is a well-populated curated index with many stars and an associated website, indicating active interest and initial adoption, but it is only 32 days old so it lacks the multi-release, production-track record required for higher TRL ratings.
prerequisites: familiarity with software reverse-engineering concepts (disassembly, decompilation)
programming (Python/JavaScript) for using many listed tools
student_project_ideas: Use the curated tools to reproduce a published reverse‑engineering case from the list (e.g. a game or firmware analysis), document the workflow, and compare two different toolchains (e.g. Ghidra vs radare2) for the same task.

Build an automated benchmark that uses resources and agent instructions from the repository to evaluate browser-based agents on a small set of website reconstruction tasks, reporting success rates and failure modes.

tools.name: Mininglamp-AI/Mano-P
tools.desc: Mano-P: Open-source GUI-VLA agent for edge devices. #1 on OSWorld (specialized, 58.2%). Runs locally on Apple M4 Mac mini/MacBook — no data leaves your device.Mano-P 是一个开源 GUI-VLA 项目，支持在 Mac mini/MacBook 上或通过算力棒本地运行推理，实现纯视觉驱动的跨平台 GUI 自动化操作。数据完全本地处理，支持复杂多步骤任务规划与执行。

cls.summary: Mano-P is an open-source, on-device visual-language-action (GUI-VLA) agent that automates complex GUI tasks and long multi-step workflows on Apple Silicon edge devices without sending data to the cloud.
cls.what_it_does: Mano-P runs a GUI-aware multimodal agent locally (targeting Apple M4/M-series Macs and compute sticks) to visually perceive interfaces and perform automated GUI operations, allowing end-to-end automation of lengthy workflows, data extraction, and report generation. It is used as an edge-native inference stack with quantization and runtime optimisations (via a companion SDK) and is notable for being built for private, offline execution and for demonstrated benchmark performance on GUI agent benchmarks.
cls.trl_rationale: The project is actively maintained, has many stars and forks, and a detailed README describing deployment and benchmarks, indicating a beta-level maturity; however the repository is under one year old (~237 days), which limits the TRL to at most 6 absent a longer track record or broad production references.
prerequisites: familiarity with Python and ML model deployment
macOS (Apple Silicon) experience and terminal/CLI usage
student_project_ideas: Create an automated GUI regression test pipeline for a university web application using Mano-P to drive browser interactions on a macOS runner and integrate results into a CI dashboard.

Develop a private, on-device data extraction workflow that uses Mano-P to pull structured data from multiple desktop applications and formats the results into an automated report (combine with Pandas or a document-generation tool).

tools.name: mob-sakai/SoftMaskForUGUI
tools.desc: Enhance Unity UI (uGUI) with advanced soft-masking features to create more visually appealing effects!

cls.summary: A Unity (uGUI) plugin that provides soft (anti-aliased / feathered) masking features and shaders to create smoother UI mask effects.
cls.what_it_does: SoftMaskForUGUI adds soft-mask components and soft-maskable shader variants to Unity's UI system so developers can create feathered, nested and inverse masking effects for Text, Image, RawImage, TextMeshPro and Spine. It is installed as a Unity package and used inside the Unity Editor and runtime; notable aspects are integration with the built-in Mask/RectMask2D behaviour, shader support and performance/quality trade-offs (buffer size, AA vs alpha modes).
cls.trl_rationale: The repository is mature (created 2018), has many stars (2.8k), active recent commits and documented installation paths (OpenUPM/UPM), and a demo page, indicating wide adoption and production use.
prerequisites: basic familiarity with Unity UI (uGUI) and shader concepts
student_project_ideas: Create a small interactive Unity app that demonstrates nested soft masks and performance trade-offs (varying buffer size and masking modes) and measure frame-time impact on mobile vs desktop builds.
Integrate SoftMaskForUGUI with TextMeshPro to prototype a UI for an AR/VR heads-up display that uses animated inverse masking effects for transitions.

tools.name: crbnos/carbon
tools.desc: Open-source manufacturing ERP, MES and QMS. Quoting, MRP, inventory, shop floor, quality and lot/serial traceability on one Postgres schema, with a REST API and MCP server. Self-host or use Carbon Cloud.

cls.summary: Carbon is an open-source combined ERP, MRP, MES and QMS platform for manufacturing that provides planning, shop-floor execution, quality management and traceability on a single Postgres schema with a typed REST API and MCP server.
cls.what_it_does: Carbon consolidates quoting, materials planning (MRP), shop-floor execution (MES), inventory and quality management (QMS) into one database and API so engineering, planning and production share the same records. It is used as a self-hosted or cloud service with a typed REST API, event-driven MCP server for agents, realtime subscriptions and integrations to CAD and business tools. Notable points are its single Postgres schema, generated shared types across DB/API/app, and explicit dependency graphs for manufacturing operations.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository is >2 years old, has many stars and forks, active recent development and pushes, published API docs and a managed Carbon Cloud offering, and supports self-hosting; these indicate production-ready software used by real customers rather than a prototype.
prerequisites: containerisation / Docker and Linux host administration
manufacturing domain knowledge (BOMs, routings, MRP/MES concepts)
student_project_ideas: Integrate a small CNC lab with Carbon by connecting machine job completion events (via webhooks or MCP) to update job status, collect actual machine times and produce job cost reconciliation reports.

Build a demo that links CAD revisions from Onshape to Carbon's BOM and routing: fetch part metadata from Onshape, create versioned BOM entries in Carbon via the API, and visualise traceability from order to source part.

tools.name: GDQuest/learn-gdscript
tools.desc: Learn Godot's GDScript programming language from zero, right in your browser, for free.

cls.summary: A free, browser-run interactive course that teaches beginners the GDScript language used in the Godot game engine.
cls.what_it_does: The project is an interactive learning app that teaches the basics of GDScript through short lessons and hands-on exercises accessible in the browser or via desktop builds. It is used as an introductory stepping-stone to help newcomers quickly learn programming fundamentals within the Godot ecosystem and to prepare them for full project-based tutorials.
cls.trl_rationale: The repository has been maintained since 2021, has several thousand stars and forks, a published web demo and downloadable builds, and active community interaction — evidence of a mature, widely used teaching project.
prerequisites: optional: Godot engine to import the project for code study
student_project_ideas: Create a small 2D game in Godot that implements a gameplay mechanic taught in the lessons (e.g. player movement and enemy AI) and document how GDScript features are used.
Extend the learning app with one or two new interactive lessons (e.g. on signals or finite state machines) and add automated checks for student answers.

tools.name: MewPurPur/GodSVG
tools.desc: A vector graphics application for structured SVG editing, available on all major desktop platforms and on web. Currently in late alpha.

cls.summary: GodSVG is an open-source, structured SVG editor built with Godot that lets you edit SVG code and the visual scene in real time while producing clean, optimized SVG files.
cls.what_it_does: GodSVG provides an interactive vector-graphics editor that exposes SVG elements and path commands directly so users can manipulate graphics visually and edit the underlying SVG text simultaneously. It is distributed as desktop builds and a web editor and emphasizes producing compact, metadata-free SVG output and real-time code synchronization.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository is active and has many stars and releases but the README explicitly states the project is in 'late alpha'; it is widely usable but still labelled alpha, so evidence supports an Alpha-in-use TRL (5) rather than beta or production.
prerequisites: familiarity with Godot if running the source/dev build
student_project_ideas: Create a small engineering icon set and optimize it for web dashboards using GodSVG, then integrate the icons into a simple web telemetry dashboard (e.g., with React or plain HTML/CSS) to teach asset creation and web delivery.

Extend or script a GodSVG export pipeline (in GDScript) that converts SVG symbols into an application-ready sprite sheet or a simplified geometry format for inclusion in a digital-twin UI, demonstrating tooling integration between graphics assets and engineering front-ends.

tools.name: opengeos/RustGIS
tools.desc: A fast, free and open-source GIS in pure Rust.

cls.summary: RustGIS is an open-source, cross-platform GIS application written in Rust that runs natively on desktop and in the browser via WebAssembly for mapping, analyzing and sharing geospatial data.
cls.what_it_does: RustGIS provides a GIS user interface with layers, attribute tables, a tool gallery of analysis functions (1,000+ GeoLibre/Whitebox tools), raster and vector data support, a 3D globe, plugins and scripting via commands and a CLI; it is used to view, analyze and export many common geospatial formats and run geospatial workflows locally or in the browser. It is notable for being implemented in pure Rust with native GPU rendering, a WASM web build, sandboxed WebAssembly plugins and an emphasis on local privacy and scriptable commands.
cls.trl_rationale: The README and features list show a wide scope (desktop + WASM, many formats, plugin system) and the project has large community interest (high star count), but the repository is only 37 days old so there is no long track record or stable release history; this supports an alpha/in-use TRL (5) rather than higher.
prerequisites: Rust toolchain to build from source (cargo)
WebAssembly build toolchain for web targets (optional)
student_project_ideas: Build a geospatial workflow that ingests satellite imagery (Cloud-Optimised GeoTIFF or STAC assets), computes a vegetation index time series in RustGIS, and exports results for further analysis in Python.
Create a WebAssembly plugin that adds an automated flood inundation mapping tool (DEM-based) to RustGIS and evaluate its usability in a lab exercise comparing outputs with QGIS results.

tools.name: qiankanglai/LoopScrollRect
tools.desc: These scripts will make your UGUI ScrollRect reusing cells, to improve performance, loading time and draw calls.

cls.summary: LoopScrollRect is a Unity C# library that makes Unity UI ScrollRect lists reuse cells so very large scroll lists render and load efficiently.
cls.what_it_does: It replaces the default behavior of Unity's ScrollRect by reusing (recycling) visible cell GameObjects so only visible items are instantiated, reducing draw calls, memory and load time for large lists. You use it by adding the provided components and implementing small data/source interfaces or using the demo scenes; it is notable for being lightweight, open-source and widely adopted in the Unity community.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository created in 2015 and actively maintained with many stars (≈2.7k) and recent commits; mature, widely used community project for Unity UI components, indicating stable, production-ready use.
prerequisites: basic C# and Unity UI (UGUI) knowledge
student_project_ideas: Create a Unity application that streams and displays thousands of sensor log entries in a performant scrollable UI using LoopScrollRect and a simple local database.
Integrate LoopScrollRect into a robotics simulation dashboard to show large historic telemetry lists and implement filtering and virtualised sorting.

tools.name: bitwes/Gut
tools.desc: Godot Unit Test.  Unit testing tool for Godot Game Engine.

cls.summary: GUT is an open-source unit testing framework for the Godot game engine that lets you write and run tests in GDScript.
cls.what_it_does: GUT provides a test runner, a collection of assertions and test utilities, test doubles (mocks/stubs/spies), parameterized tests and a CLI to run tests for Godot projects. It is installed as a Godot addon and integrates with editor workflows (and a VSCode extension) and can export results in JUnit XML for CI integration.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository is long-lived (created 2016), actively maintained with many releases for Godot 3.x and 4.x, wide adoption (thousands of stars) and documentation hosted on readthedocs — indicating a mature, widely used OSS project.
prerequisites: Godot Engine (3.x or 4.x depending on GUT version)
student_project_ideas: Create a small robotics simulation in Godot and write a GUT test-suite that verifies controller behaviours and sensor data processing; integrate test runs into CI and export JUnit results.
Build an interactive visualization (e.g. a vehicle dynamics demo) in Godot and use GUT to write automated regression tests for physics-related functions and exported scene state.

tools.name: Mobile-Artificial-Intelligence/maid
tools.desc: Maid is a free and open source application for interfacing with llama.cpp models locally, and with Anthropic, DeepSeek, Ollama, Mistral and OpenAI models remotely.

cls.summary: Maid is an open-source React Native Android app that runs local GGUF LLMs via llama.cpp and connects to many remote LLM providers for chat on mobile devices.
cls.what_it_does: Maid lets users run language models locally on-device using llama.cpp and GGUF files, download curated models from Hugging Face, or connect to numerous remote providers (OpenAI, Anthropic, Mistral, Ollama, etc.). It is used as a mobile chat client with conversation management, adjustable generation parameters, and optional TTS integration via a companion app.
cls.trl_rationale: The repository is more than a year old, has many stars/forks, active recent commits and release PDFs, and build instructions for Android—evidence of a production-ready open-source mobile application rather than an experimental prototype.
prerequisites: React Native development environment (Android SDK, Java/Gradle)
Optional API keys for remote providers (OpenAI, Anthropic, etc.)
student_project_ideas: Build a domain-specific on-device chatbot by fine-tuning or prompting a downloaded GGUF model in Maid and evaluate its latency and response quality on an Android device.
Integrate Maid with a simple robot or IoT device (e.g. Raspberry Pi) to provide a local voice-enabled assistant using the Maise TTS companion and measure end-to-end responsiveness and resource usage.

tools.name: itayinbarr/little-coder
tools.desc: A harness optimized to smaller LLMs

cls.summary: little-coder is a command-line coding agent tuned to run with small local language models and built on top of the pi agent substrate.
cls.what_it_does: It provides a pre-bundled, reproducible coding-agent environment (pi plus ~30 extensions and skills) that runs as a single CLI tool and is optimised for smaller local LLMs. Users launch the agent in a project directory to read, edit and run shell commands, use plan/research modes, and swap local or cloud models; notable features are deliberate extension isolation, a launcher that keeps cold-start context small, and explicit support for local model backends like llama.cpp and Ollama.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository is 220 days old (<1 year) so cannot be assigned very high TRL, but it shows strong community interest (2.7k stars), a full installer, active pushes and open issues and a usable CLI; these indicate a beta-level, actively maintained project rather than an early prototype.
prerequisites: familiarity with local LLM runtimes (llama.cpp, Ollama, LM Studio) is helpful
student_project_ideas: Compare coding task throughput and edit accuracy between a small local model (llamacpp/qwen3.6 variant) and a cloud model by scripting identical tasks in little-coder and measuring time-to-complete and patch correctness.
Extend little-coder with a custom extension that integrates a project's unit test runner and measure how different prompt / planning strategies affect test-driven code edits.

tools.name: xavier150/Blender-For-UnrealEngine-Addons
tools.desc: I have created this addons for export asset from Blender to Unreal Engine

cls.summary: A Blender add-on that automates exporting scene assets (meshes, skeletal rigs, animations, cameras, collisions, splines and more) into a structure ready for import into Unreal Engine 4/5.
cls.what_it_does: The add-on batches export of Blender content and organises assets to match Unreal Engine pipelines, creates sockets/collision shapes, checks for common problems and can generate Python import scripts or clipboard data for direct import into Unreal. It is used inside Blender as a plugin and notable for extensive documentation, support for many asset types (static/skeletal meshes, animations, Alembic, cameras, sequencer data) and long-term maintenance.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository is long-lived (created 2018), has many stars and forks, active recent commits and comprehensive docs/wiki, showing wide adoption and a stable plugin used in production pipelines rather than an experimental prototype.
student_project_ideas: Create a small asset pipeline: model and rig a mechanical component in Blender, export it with the add-on, and import into Unreal to demonstrate correct LODs, collisions and a simple animated sequence.

Build a scene-level transfer demo that exports multiple cameras and sequencer cuts from Blender, imports them into Unreal using the generated Python script, and compares camera parameters and animation fidelity.

alternatives_to: Epic Games 'Send to Unreal' / Unreal Live Link

tools.name: syv-ai/HyperQwen
tools.desc: Serve large Qwen models fast on the GPUs you actually own. Qwen3.8-27B on a single 24 GB card with vLLM: 127 tok/s single-user (381 when the answer quotes the prompt), ~1,035 tok/s at 64 concurrent, 150k-262k context. vLLM patches, requant pipeline, benchmarks.

cls.summary: HyperQwen is an open-source project that prepares and serves large Qwen language models efficiently on consumer GPUs using patched vLLM and model requantization.
cls.what_it_does: HyperQwen provides a deployment and model-preparation pipeline that enables serving Qwen family LLMs (e.g. Qwen3.8-27B) on single 24 GB consumer GPUs or multi-GPU setups, with optimisations such as requantized model heads, specialised KV-cache formats and speculative decoding. It is used by running the provided Docker compose setups or native install to produce a local OpenAI-compatible API and high-throughput inference stack; notable points are its measured throughput numbers, vLLM patch series, and GPU-specific optimisations (pth-flash-attn, int8 KV cache).
cls.trl_rationale: The repository shows substantial engineering (Docker images, benchmarks, patches to vLLM, model-prep pipeline) and a large star count indicating community interest, but it is under one year old so lacks the long track-record or multiple stable major releases required for TRL 7+.
prerequisites: CUDA / NVIDIA Container Toolkit and Docker knowledge
familiarity with vLLM and Python environments
student_project_ideas: Compare throughput and latency of Qwen3.8-27B served by HyperQwen vs stock vLLM on a single 24 GB GPU, reporting the effects of different SPEC and CTX settings and measuring token/sec and memory use.

Extend the HyperQwen pipeline to add support for another consumer GPU architecture (e.g. Ampere vs Ada) by creating and testing a requantization profile and integration with pth-flash-attn, then document performance trade-offs.

tools.name: torch-points3d/torch-points3d
tools.desc: Pytorch framework for doing deep learning on point clouds.

cls.summary: Torch-Points3D is an open-source PyTorch framework for training and evaluating deep learning models on 3D point clouds (segmentation, detection, classification and registration).
cls.what_it_does: It provides implementations, datasets, training/evaluation scripts and configuration management to run state-of-the-art point-cloud deep learning methods (PointNet, PointNet++, KPConv, RandLA-Net, VoteNet, etc.) against standard benchmarks. Users run experiments via Hydra configs or the provided train/eval scripts and can extend models/modules through a modular API; notable points are its benchmark focus, many published model implementations and Docker/pip install options for reproducible training.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository created in 2019 and actively maintained with many stars, a paper describing the framework, Docker images, pip packaging and numerous model implementations and benchmarks; this indicates production-ready maturity and use in research/projects rather than an early prototype.
prerequisites: CUDA and GPU for efficient training
familiarity with deep learning and point-cloud concepts
student_project_ideas: Train and compare semantic segmentation performance of KPConv and RandLA-Net on the SemanticKITTI or ScanNet datasets using torch-points3d, and produce a short report analysing accuracy, inference speed and memory use.
Integrate a real-world LiDAR capture pipeline (e.g. using Open3D to preprocess scans) with torch-points3d to build a small object-detection demo (VoteNet) that runs on campus-collected point clouds.

tools.name: yimengfan/BDFramework.Core
tools.desc: Simple and powerful Unity3d game workflow!  简单、高效、高度工业化的商业级unity3d 工作流。

cls.summary: BDFramework.Core is an open-source workflow and framework for building, hot-fixing and automating Unity3D projects to speed game development and deployment.
cls.what_it_does: BDFramework provides an end-to-end Unity editor and build workflow that centralises asset management, automated build pipelines and hot-fix/hot-update support to streamline iteration. It is used as a plugin/framework inside Unity projects to organise project structure, automations and runtime update mechanisms, and is notable for being a mature, widely starred Unity workflow used by many commercial projects.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository is long-lived (created 2017), actively maintained (recent push 2026), and has a large user interest (≈2.7k stars and many forks), indicating a mature, widely used project rather than an experimental prototype.
prerequisites: basic game development concepts (assets, build pipelines, asset bundles)
student_project_ideas: Create a Unity-based interactive digital twin demo for a simple mechatronic device using BDFramework for asset management and hot-update delivery of new control parameters.
Build an automated build-and-deploy lab exercise that uses BDFramework's pipeline to produce platform builds and demonstrate hot-fix delivery across versions.

tools.name: papersgpt/papersgpt-for-zotero
tools.desc: Professional AI research tool for Zotero: chat with PDFs, whole-library search, Literature Radar, AutoPilot. 30+ LLMs or local models; built-in MCP server.

cls.summary: PapersGPT is an open-source Zotero plugin that indexes your entire PDF library and uses cloud or local LLMs to support whole-library search, multi‑PDF chat, literature monitoring and automated extraction into Zotero notes.
cls.what_it_does: It parses and indexes PDFs inside a Zotero library locally, then retrieves and synthesises evidence from across the library with an LLM (cloud or local) to answer natural-language research queries, compare papers and produce structured notes. Notable features include Literature Radar for subscribing to sources (arXiv, PubMed, Semantic Scholar, etc.), an AutoPilot batch-reading mode, and a built-in MCP server for agent integrations.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository is >1 year old, has many stars/forks, active recent commits and benchmark results in the README; features (local LLM downloads, MCP server, scale benchmarks) and cross-platform compatibility indicate production-ready software used by many users rather than an experimental prototype.
prerequisites: basic familiarity with installing Zotero plugins and optionally Hugging Face or local LLM tooling
