student_project_ideas: Build an automated literature-review pipeline that uses PapersGPT to extract methods and key metrics from a collection of engineering papers and visualise trends (combine with a Jupyter notebook and matplotlib).

Integrate PapersGPT's MCP server with an agent or chatbot to create a campus research assistant that answers local-library queries and links back to Zotero entries, then evaluate citation accuracy on a curated corpus.

tools.name: youssofal/MTPLX
tools.desc: The fastest way to run Qwen 3.8 Flash Next, Qwen 3.8 27B and Ternary Bonsai 2 27B on a Mac: 125 tok/s in OpenCode on an M5 Max, and a 27B model on 16 GB Macs. Native MTP speculative decoding on Apple Silicon, exact at any temperature. OpenAI and Anthropic compatible local server.

cls.summary: MTPLX is a native macOS application and CLI that runs high-performance local large language models on Apple Silicon using the models' multi-token prediction (MTP) heads and speculative decoding to speed up inference.
cls.what_it_does: MTPLX runs local LLMs (Qwen family, Prism ML Ternary Bonsai, Gemma, etc.) on Apple Silicon with a native MTP speculative decoder that drafts several tokens ahead and verifies them via rejection sampling, yielding significantly faster token throughput. It is provided as a macOS app and a command-line tool, installs models and dependencies, and exposes an OpenAI/Anthropic-compatible local server for integration.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository is active, well-documented, provides packaged macOS app and CLI, and lists benchmarks and releases, indicating beta-level maturity; however it is younger than one year (created 199 days ago) so TRL is capped at 6.
student_project_ideas: Measure and compare inference throughput and memory usage between MTPLX and another local LLM runtime (e.g. llama.cpp or Ollama) on different Apple Silicon chips, and report trade-offs in latency, quality and RAM usage.
Integrate MTPLX's OpenAI-compatible local server into a small engineering chatbot for retrieving design documentation and evaluate its performance and reliability under realistic query workloads.

tools.name: gridaco/grida
tools.desc: Grida — Open Canvas

cls.summary: Grida is an open-source cross-platform design canvas for creating graphics, images and presentations with integrated AI-assisted asset generation.
cls.what_it_does: Grida provides a desktop canvas (macOS, Windows, Linux) where users combine images, text and vector art, import from Figma, and use AI models to generate or explore visual assets. It ships a CLI for scripted media generation and links to local or cloud model providers, and is notable for being an open-source alternative to commercial design apps with AI integration.
cls.trl_rationale: The repository is mature (created 2021, many stars, active recent pushes and desktop downloads), has cross-platform desktop builds and a CLI, and an ecosystem (FX, AI Gateway), indicating production-ready maturity rather than an experimental prototype.
prerequisites: Node.js and npm/yarn for local development and CLI use
student_project_ideas: Create a workflow that imports Figma designs into Grida, applies programmatic AI image generation via the Grida CLI, and exports SVG assets for a web UI prototype.

Build a small plugin or script that uses Ollama or another local LLM to generate placeholder art and copy for a digital-twin UI, then evaluate the asset quality and iteration speed compared with manual design.

tools.name: cartesiancs/map3d
tools.desc: 🗺️ Generate City 3D map with R3F. Include building and road information.

cls.summary: map3d is a React + React-Three-Fiber project that generates real-world 3D city maps from OpenStreetMap data and can export scenes as GLB files.
cls.what_it_does: The project fetches OpenStreetMap data and builds 3D representations of buildings and roads in a browser using React-Three-Fiber and three.js, allowing users to visualise city geometry and export the scene as a GLB. It is notable for being focused on real-world mapping (OSM) and for providing a free, web-native pipeline suitable as a starting point for digital-twin, drone-surveying, or GPS-marker applications.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository is >1 year old, has high star count and active commits, a working demo and export features but README and metadata do not cite production deployments or formal releases, so it fits a beta-stage (TRL 6).
student_project_ideas: Create a drone-survey simulation that loads a neighbourhood via map3d, simulates a drone flight path, and records virtual imagery for a photogrammetry or SLAM pipeline.

Extend map3d to accept user-corrected building heights (manual editing UI) and produce a workflow that compares OSM-derived heights against corrected values and exports the corrected GLB for use in a digital-twin viewer.

tools.name: maplibre/maputnik
tools.desc: An open source visual editor for the 'MapLibre Style Specification'

cls.summary: Maputnik is an open-source visual editor for MapLibre/Mapbox GL map styles that lets users design and edit vector-tile map styles in a web UI.
cls.what_it_does: Maputnik provides a graphical interface to create, edit and preview MapLibre GL style JSON used with vector tile maps. It runs in the browser (or as a local dev server / Docker image) and is notable for being open-source, actively maintained, and tightly integrated with MapLibre GL JS for live map previews.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository is long-lived (created 2016), has a large community (2.6k stars, active CI, recent commits) and documented release process; evidence shows wide adoption in the MapLibre ecosystem which supports a mature TRL.
prerequisites: Node.js and npm for local development
optional: Docker for running the packaged image
student_project_ideas: Create a thematic infrastructure map by designing custom Maputnik styles and serving vector tiles with a tile server (e.g. TileServer GL) to visualise asset condition data.
Extend Maputnik with a plugin or UI change that imports sensor time-series metadata and styles layers based on thresholds, demonstrating a simple operational dashboard for a digital twin.

tools.name: absmach/magistrala
tools.desc: IoT Platform Framework

cls.summary: Magistrala is an open-source event-driven IoT platform framework that provides device connectivity, identity/access control, messaging and data pipelines for cloud, edge and hybrid deployments.
cls.what_it_does: Magistrala provides a coherent framework for building scalable IoT systems: it runs message brokering, device provisioning and identity, access control, observability and data-processing building blocks and exposes protocol-native connectivity (MQTT, HTTP, CoAP, WebSocket). It is used by deploying the stack (Docker/Kubernetes) and integrating devices, rules and external storage/monitoring; it is notable for being protocol-native, event-driven and designed for edge/cloud hybrid use.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository is mature (created 2015), has many stars, active development and documentation, and a vendor (Abstract Machines) publishing docs and a product page; these indicate production-readiness and real-world use though enterprise features are noted separately.
prerequisites: basic TLS/X.509 and JWT authentication knowledge
student_project_ideas: Build a small edge-to-cloud demo: provision a simulated sensor device that publishes telemetry over MQTT to Magistrala, implement a rule to route messages to a time-series database and visualise results with Grafana/Prometheus.
Integrate a LoRaWAN/CoAP gateway prototype with Magistrala to demonstrate multi-protocol device onboarding, access policies and end-to-end secure device authentication using mTLS or JWT.

tools.name: nanomq/nanomq
tools.desc: An ultra-lightweight and blazing-fast Messaging  Bus/MQTT Broker for Edge & SDV

cls.summary: NanoMQ is an open-source, high-performance MQTT broker and lightweight messaging bus designed for edge and embedded IoT/IIoT deployments.
cls.what_it_does: NanoMQ provides an MQTT v3.1.1 and v5.0 broker optimized for low-latency, high-throughput messaging on constrained and edge platforms; it is used as a local messaging hub or bridge between devices and cloud services. It is notable for a pure-C implementation, actor-style architecture built on NNG, and support for embedded targets (POSIX and Zephyr) and containerised deployments.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository was created in 2016 and is actively maintained with many stars, Docker images, documentation, and industry-facing pages; it is part of LF Edge ecosystem and provides production-ready installers and benchmarks, indicating mature and widely adopted software.
prerequisites: familiarity with MQTT concepts and broker configuration
C toolchain and CMake build experience for building from source
Linux / POSIX environment (or cross-compilation for embedded targets)
student_project_ideas: Build an edge-to-cloud telemetry pipeline: deploy NanoMQ in a Docker container on a Raspberry Pi, connect simulated sensor publishers and forward messages to a cloud MQTT broker or time-series DB for visualization.

Integrate NanoMQ with a simple ROS 2 or Zephyr-based device: use NanoMQ as a gateway to bridge device MQTT traffic into a robot middleware or microcontroller-based telemetry stack and evaluate latency and throughput.

tools.name: CesiumGS/3d-tiles
tools.desc: Specification for streaming massive heterogeneous 3D geospatial datasets :earth_americas:

cls.summary: 3D Tiles is an open specification for streaming, visualising and fusing massive heterogeneous 3D geospatial datasets (terrain, photogrammetry, BIM, point clouds and vector features) across web, desktop and mobile applications.
cls.what_it_does: 3D Tiles defines file formats and a spatial/level-of-detail hierarchy so large, mixed 3D geospatial content can be efficiently streamed, styled, queried and rendered at scales from global terrain down to building interiors. It is used as a data interchange and runtime format (often combined with a viewer like CesiumJS) to convert existing GIS/CAD/BIM/photogrammetry outputs into a single tileset for visualization and analysis.
cls.trl_rationale: 3D Tiles is a long-established, community-maintained open specification (repo created 2015) and version 1.0 was submitted to the OGC and approved as an OGC Community Standard; there are many implementations and an ecosystem (reference cards, converters and viewers), indicating mature, widely adopted status.
prerequisites: basic GIS and coordinate reference systems
familiarity with 3D graphics concepts and glTF
understanding of tile/LOD and streaming concepts
student_project_ideas: Create a pipeline that converts a small photogrammetry-derived point cloud and a BIM model into a 3D Tiles tileset, host it on a simple server and build a web viewer page (using CesiumJS) that supports feature selection and styling.

Compare streaming performance and level-of-detail of a city-scale dataset by generating 3D Tiles with different implicit tiling schemes and measuring bandwidth and frame-rate in a browser-based viewer.

tools.name: Unity-Technologies/Unity-Robotics-Hub
tools.desc: Central repository for tools, tutorials, resources, and documentation for robotics simulation in Unity.

cls.summary: A Unity-maintained collection of packages, tutorials and tools for building robot simulations in the Unity Editor, with ROS 2 integration, sensor simulation and a URDF importer.
cls.what_it_does: Unity Robotics Hub provides example projects, packages and hands-on modules to import robots (URDF), simulate sensors (LiDAR, RGB-D, IMU), and exchange messages with ROS 2 from within Unity. It is used as a training and development resource to build, run and capture data from virtual robot experiments and supports headless Linux builds for parallel/CI execution.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository is long-lived (created 2020), actively maintained by Unity, has many stars/forks, and documents a production-focused package (Simulation Pro) used with Unity 6.x; evidence shows industry backing and stable examples rather than a one-off prototype.
prerequisites: familiarity with the Unity Editor and C#
experience with URDF and robot kinematics helpful
student_project_ideas: Build a simulated autonomous differential-drive robot in Unity using the URDF importer and a ROS 2 node (rclpy) to implement and tune a LiDAR-based navigation stack.

Compare sensor outputs (simulated LiDAR and RGB-D) from Unity against a real dataset by exporting point clouds and images from Unity and evaluating perception algorithms (SLAM or object detection) in Python.

tools.name: rasterio/rasterio
tools.desc: Rasterio reads and writes geospatial raster datasets

cls.summary: Rasterio is a mature Python library for reading, writing and processing geospatial raster files (GeoTIFF and similar) using N‑D arrays.
cls.what_it_does: Rasterio provides a Pythonic API to open, inspect, read and write geospatial raster datasets, manage georeferencing (CRS, affine transforms), read/write windows and bands, and perform file I/O for formats supported by GDAL. It is used as a programmatic layer over GDAL to work with rasters as NumPy arrays and includes a CLI ('rio') and plugin mechanism, making it notable for easy integration into Python geospatial workflows and data pipelines.
cls.trl_rationale: Rasterio is a long-lived (created 2013), actively maintained project with many stars, CI workflows, binary releases on PyPI, broad community use and mentions of Mapbox origins; these indicate mature, widely adopted software.
student_project_ideas: Build a pipeline that reads multispectral GeoTIFFs with Rasterio, computes vegetation indices (e.g. NDVI) using NumPy, and visualises results as web tiles (combine with a web mapping library).

Create a change-detection workflow that aligns and compares time-series raster datasets using Rasterio for reprojection/windowing and then evaluates statistical change metrics for an environmental monitoring case study.

tools.name: simbody/simbody
tools.desc: High-performance C++ multibody dynamics/physics library for simulating articulated biomechanical and mechanical systems like vehicles, robots, and the human skeleton.

cls.summary: Simbody is a mature C++ library for high-performance multibody dynamics simulation of articulated mechanical and biomechanical systems.
cls.what_it_does: Simbody provides APIs to model rigid bodies, joints, constraints, forces and contact, and to run forward/inverse dynamics and time integration for articulated systems. It is used as a simulation engine embedded in other projects (e.g. OpenSim, Gazebo) and offers features like various integrators, contact models and optimizers for engineering-quality simulation.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository created in 2013 and actively maintained with many stars, forks and integrations (explicitly used by OpenSim and Gazebo), plus stable docs and releases; this indicates a mature, widely-adopted library suitable for production research and engineering (TRL 8).
prerequisites: familiarity with numerical integration and rigid-body dynamics
student_project_ideas: Build and validate a Simbody model of a 2-DOF robotic arm, compare forward dynamics results against analytic solutions and visualize trajectories with the Simbody visualizer.
Integrate a Simbody vehicle suspension model with a simple control loop (PID) to study ride dynamics and perform parameter sweeps for damping/stiffness using the library's optimizers.

tools.name: digitalsamba/claude-code-video-toolkit
tools.desc: Make videos with Claude Code: script, AI voiceover, music, video clips and render, on open-source models that cost cents

cls.summary: A toolkit that automates script, voiceover, music, visuals and rendering so Claude Code can produce programmatic videos using open-source models and optional Blender integration.
cls.what_it_does: The toolkit provides skills, templates and commands for Claude Code to create end-to-end videos: it writes scripts, generates TTS voiceovers and music, assembles video clips and renders MP4s, and can drive Blender to produce 3D-character scenes from a JSON spec. It is used by installing the repo, running an interactive /setup then /video inside Claude Code, and it leverages open-source models deployed to cloud GPUs or local runtimes.
cls.trl_rationale: The repository is active, well-documented, has many stars and examples and runs end-to-end demos, indicating a beta-level project; however it is under one year old (created ~343 days ago), so it lacks the multi-year track record or wide production adoption needed for TRL 7+.
prerequisites: uv (Python venv) for optional AI tools
Optional: Blender and a cloud GPU account (Modal / RunPod)
student_project_ideas: Build an automated pipeline that uses the toolkit to generate short explainer videos from structured product-requirement text, then measure time-to-render and cost on a cloud GPU provider.

Integrate the toolkit's Blender JSON character spec into a simple animation assignment: author behaviours in JSON, render a short scene with Blender, and compare manual vs. AI-directed animation outputs.

tools.name: nortikin/sverchok
tools.desc: Sverchok is Node-based visual programming for parametric 3D modeling and computational geometry in Blender

cls.summary: Sverchok is a mature Blender add-on that provides node-based visual programming for parametric 3D modelling and computational geometry.
cls.what_it_does: Sverchok lets users build parametric geometry and procedural models in Blender by wiring together over 600 specialised nodes that handle vectors, meshes, curves, fields and boolean/CSG operations. It is used inside Blender for interactive geometry creation, analysis (areas, volumes, insolation) and for creating custom Python-scripted nodes or export workflows, notable for its large node library and integration with Blender's API.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository is long-lived (created 2013), has many stars and forks, active development into 2026, extensive documentation and a large node ecosystem—evidence of broad adoption and production use (mature).
prerequisites: optional numeric libraries (SciPy, shapely) for some nodes
student_project_ideas: Use Sverchok to create a parametric pedestrian bridge model in Blender where geometry adapts to span and loading inputs, then export cross-sections for structural analysis.
Develop a procedural façade generator that computes solar insolation per panel using Sverchok nodes and visualises performance across different orientations and times of year.

tools.name: ppmpreetham/BUI
tools.desc: Blender's GPU Accelerated UI, Decoupled from it's original codebase. Supports Rust, Python, JS, Lua, C & C++. Twice as good as GPUI

cls.summary: BUI is a standalone, GPU-accelerated library that exposes Blender’s user‑interface widgets and interaction model to multiple languages (C, C++, Python, Rust, JavaScript, Lua, Dear ImGui).
cls.what_it_does: BUI extracts Blender’s UI drawing, layout and interaction code into a small C core (the kit) and provides language bindings so apps can build native widget trees that behave and render like Blender’s interface. It is used to give desktop applications Blender’s look, feel and efficient redraw behaviour across several languages and UI frameworks.
cls.trl_rationale: The project is well documented, multi-language and shows active development and many stars, indicating early adoption; however the repository is only 83 days old so by the stated rules maturity is limited to TRL 5.
prerequisites: Familiarity with target language (Python, Rust, JS, Lua) and native build/bindings
student_project_ideas: Build a Rust-based desktop front-end for a small simulation (e.g. mass-spring visualiser) using BUI for controls and real-time plotting, integrating a physics library for computation.
Port a Python tkinter-based engineering utility to BUI to compare startup time, responsiveness and redraw efficiency, and report performance differences.

tools.name: NASA-AMMOS/3DTilesRendererJS
tools.desc: Renderer for 3D Tiles in Javascript using three.js, Babylon.js, and r3f

cls.summary: A JavaScript library that loads and renders 3D Tiles tilesets in web engines (Three.js, Babylon.js, PlayCanvas/r3f) for geospatial/terrain visualisation.
cls.what_it_does: 3DTilesRendererJS parses and renders the 3D Tiles open specification in browser/webgl engines so developers can display large geospatial tilesets (b3dm, quantized-mesh, point clouds, etc.). It is used as a drop-in renderer or set of engine-specific adapters (Three.js, Babylon.js, PlayCanvas, r3f) and provides plugins for metadata, overlays and additional tile formats. It is notable for broad support of the 3D Tiles spec, example demos (Cesium Ion, Google photorealistic tiles, Mars), and multiple engine integrations.
cls.trl_rationale: The project is mature and long-lived (created 2020) with many stars (≈2.5k), active activity and hosted live demos, indicating wide adoption and stability. The README, multiple engine integrations and plugin system indicate a stable API and production use.
prerequisites: basic knowledge of Three.js or Babylon.js and WebGL
student_project_ideas: Build a web viewer that loads a Cesium Ion or local 3D Tiles tileset using 3DTilesRendererJS and implements custom styling and measurement tools (combine with Mapbox/leaflet for 2D/3D sync).
Integrate 3DTilesRendererJS with a point-cloud pipeline (Potree) to compare visualization performance and implement a LO D selection strategy and streaming benchmark for large urban models.

tools.name: ooolabdev/ooosplat
tools.desc: A local desktop app that turns videos and images into 3D Gaussian Splats in one click.

cls.summary: OOOSplat is a local desktop application that converts videos and image sequences into 3D Gaussian splats (point-cloud-like volumetric representations) with an automated pipeline and built-in preview/editor.
cls.what_it_does: It automates the full photogrammetry-to-Gaussian-splat pipeline: frame extraction, COLMAP camera reconstruction, Brush training, and export of final PLY/SPZ/SOG assets, all performed locally. The app provides a GUI for one-click generation, preview/editing (WebGPU/WebGL2) and multi-format export, and bundles or integrates tools like FFmpeg, COLMAP and Brush so users need not call command-line tools manually.
cls.trl_rationale: The project is actively developed, distributes platform-specific installers (.exe, .dmg, .deb), bundles COLMAP/FFmpeg/Brush, and has many stars and recent pushes, indicating a usable beta; repository age is ~93–94 days which limits claims of long-term production use, so TRL=6 (beta).
prerequisites: NVIDIA/AMD/Intel GPU recommended for Brush training (GPU drivers/Vulkan/Metal)
sufficient disk space for source media and intermediate COLMAP/Brush data
for building from source: Node.js 22.12+, Rust stable, Tauri/WebKitGTK dev deps
student_project_ideas: Compare reconstruction quality and file-size trade-offs by generating Gaussian splats from the same dataset at the three quality presets (quick/balanced/fine), then quantify geometric and visual fidelity against a COLMAP+mesh baseline.

Integrate OOOSplat output into a simple WebGPU viewer or Cesium scene to build a lightweight digital-twin demo that streams/exported SOG/SPZ/PLY assets and measures runtime rendering performance on different client hardware.

tools.name: okalachev/flix
tools.desc: Making an ESP32-based quadcopter from scratch

cls.summary: Flix is an open-source ESP32-based quadcopter project that provides firmware, hardware files, Gazebo simulation and a Python library intended for education and research.
cls.what_it_does: Flix provides a complete stack to build and run a small quadcopter: Arduino C++ firmware for an ESP32 flight controller, schematics and 3D-printable frame parts, a Gazebo-based simulator that runs the same firmware, and a Python library for scripting autonomous flights. It is designed to be built from general-purpose components, communicate over MAVLink (Wi‑Fi/ESP‑NOW), and used for hands-on teaching, research and prototyping of flight control.
cls.trl_rationale: The repository is mature (created 2020) with many stars (2509), active commits as recently as 2026, documented assembly and usage, demo videos and reported use in education (RoboCamp), and a working Gazebo simulator — evidence of production-ready educational use.
prerequisites: experience with Gazebo/ROS or simulation is helpful
student_project_ideas: Build and fly a Flix quadcopter while extending the Python scripting library to implement an autonomous takeoff/landing sequence and log telemetry to a time-series database for analysis.
Integrate the Flix Gazebo simulation with a vision-based position estimator (OpenCV) to develop and test a camera-based position control loop before deploying to hardware.

tools.name: shinyobjectz/raea
tools.desc: Render Anything Engine: tell your AI what to make. Videos, motion graphics, 3D and games as React and TypeScript, rendered on your own GPU. Rust + Bevy, macOS, Linux and Windows.

cls.summary: raea is an open-source engine that lets you author and render videos, motion graphics, 3D scenes and simple games in TypeScript/React and run them on your local GPU.
cls.what_it_does: raea provides a runtime and desktop app that compiles React/TypeScript compositions to GPU-rendered frames and exports video or standalone games; it supports 3D (via Bevy), audio, hardware encoding and tooling for automated checks. It is designed to be driven by AI agents (skills and plugins are provided) so agents can generate, render and verify media automatically, and it emphasises local GPU rendering and an agent-friendly data model.
cls.trl_rationale: The project is feature-rich and already publishes releases and installers, but the repository is very new (created ~30 days ago) so there is not yet a long track record of production use; that limits it to an early 'alpha in use' TRL despite high interest.
prerequisites: basic GPU and graphics drivers (Vulkan / DirectX 12) and TypeScript/React knowledge
student_project_ideas: Create an interactive engineering visualization that renders sensor telemetry from a small robot as a React composition in raea and export a narrated demo video combining 3D models and time-aligned charts.

Build an AI-driven content pipeline where an agent (using the raea skills) generates a short animated explainer from a plain-text specification, then render and run automated checks (raea check) to validate legibility and loudness.

tools.name: tracel-ai/cubecl
tools.desc: Multi-platform high-performance compute language extension for Rust.

cls.summary: CubeCL is a Rust language extension and JIT runtime that lets you write high-performance compute kernels in Rust and run them across CPUs and multiple GPU backends (CUDA, HIP, Metal, Vulkan, WebGPU).
cls.what_it_does: CubeCL provides a #[cube] Rust attribute to author kernels in plain Rust, compiles them Just-In-Time to target different GPU and CPU backends, and exposes runtimes that map a shared parallelism model to each platform. It aims to let one kernel implementation reach near-peak performance on each backend while keeping Rust type- and borrow-checking, enabling testing on CPU and autotuning for hardware-specific paths (e.g. tensor cores).
cls.trl_rationale: The project is active, widely starred (≈2.5k stars), has many forks, cross-backend runtimes, and recent commits which indicate production-readiness beyond an experimental prototype; the repository age (>1 year) and community interest support TRL 7 (production-ready library/runtimes).
student_project_ideas: Implement a parallel finite-difference heat equation solver as a #[cube] kernel and compare performance and numerical correctness across CPU, CUDA (via cudarc), and WebGPU backends, reporting scaling and autotuning effects.

Port a small neural-network training step (forward + backward for one layer) to CubeCL kernels and integrate it with a Rust ML library (e.g. Burn) to measure throughput and test mixed-precision/tensor-core acceleration on different GPUs.

tools.name: nv-tlabs/3dgrut
tools.desc: Ray tracing and hybrid rasterization of Gaussian particles

cls.summary: 3DGRUT implements research-grade Gaussian particle rendering (ray tracing and hybrid rasterization) for high-quality 3D reconstruction and rendering of scenes from multi-view images.
cls.what_it_does: The repository implements 3D Gaussian Ray Tracing (3DGRT) and a rasterization-compatible Unscented Transform (3DGUT) and combines them into a hybrid 3DGRUT pipeline to render Gaussian particle scenes with support for distorted and time-dependent cameras. It is used to train and render Gaussian-splatting based reconstructions, supports exporting assets (USD/PLY) and integrates optimisations for secondary rays (reflections, refractions, shadows) and production features like Vulkan support and dataset compatibility.
cls.trl_rationale: The project is an official NVIDIA research implementation with peer-reviewed papers (SIGGRAPH Asia 2024, CVPR 2025), a tagged stable v1.0.0 release, active development (recent pushes) and many stars/forks, indicating production-ready research software rather than a fragile prototype.
prerequisites: NVIDIA GPU with ray-tracing/CUDA support for best performance
Python and common ML/vision libraries (PyTorch implied)
Familiarity with multi-view reconstruction / Gaussian splatting concepts
student_project_ideas: Compare reconstruction quality and rendering performance between 3DGRUT and a raster-only Gaussian splatting implementation (e.g. gsplat), measuring effects of camera distortion and secondary rays on final images.

Integrate 3DGRUT exports (USD/PLY) into a simple digital twin pipeline: capture a small scene, train 3DGRUT, export a mesh/point representation and build a lightweight web viewer (three.js) to demonstrate interactive visualization and material properties.

tools.name: mlt131220/Astral3D
tools.desc: 基于Vue3 + THREE.JS 免费开源的三维引擎及配套编辑器，包含BIM轻量化、CAD解析预览、粒子系统、插件系统等功能。               A free and open-source 3D engine based on Vue3 + THREE.JS and its accompanying editor, featuring functions such as BIM lightweighting, CAD parsing preview, particle system, and plugin system.

cls.summary: Astral3D is an open-source web-based 3D engine and editor (Vue3 + Three.js) focused on BIM lightweight viewing, CAD preview and scene editing for web visualisation of engineering models.
cls.what_it_does: Astral3D provides a browser-based 3D editor and engine that loads many CAD and BIM formats (GLTF/OBJ/FBX/GLB/RVT/IFC, DWG/DXF), supports model lightweighting, animations, particle and weather systems, and a plugin/script runtime. It is used by running the editor locally or building it for deployment and notable for integrating BIM/CAD preview and editor features on top of a Three.js + Vue3 stack.
cls.trl_rationale: The repository is mature (created 2021, ~2.5k stars, active commits as recently as Oct 2026, few open issues) and provides a full editor, installation instructions and documentation—evidence of production-ready project adoption rather than a prototype.
prerequisites: familiarity with Three.js and Vue3 is helpful
student_project_ideas: Build a web viewer that loads an IFC model, implements lightweighting and measures occupied volumes, then exports a simple report (combine Astral3D with an IFC parser).
Create a plugin for Astral3D that streams sensor/time-series data into a BIM scene to visualise live status (combine with a simple MQTT broker or time-series backend).

tools.name: NVlabs/ProtoMotions
tools.desc: ProtoMotions is a GPU-accelerated simulation and learning framework for training physically simulated digital humans and humanoid robots.

cls.summary: ProtoMotions3 is an open-source, GPU-accelerated framework for physics-based simulation and reinforcement learning of humanoid characters and robots used to train motion and control policies at scale.
cls.what_it_does: It provides an environment, training pipelines and tooling to simulate humanoid/digital-human characters and humanoid robots for motion learning, policy training and retargeting; users run experiments on GPUs, train generative and imitation policies, and deploy or demo trained agents. It is notable for large-scale multi‑GPU training, built-in retargeting (PyRoki) and published pretrained models and browser demos.
cls.trl_rationale: The project is produced by NVlabs, has many stars and active maintenance, published papers, released pretrained weights and browser demos, and documented multi‑GPU training examples — evidence of production‑ready research software; repository age (~2+ years) and visible real-world demos support TRL7.
prerequisites: Familiarity with reinforcement learning and robotics concepts
student_project_ideas: Train a balance-and-recovery policy for a simple humanoid using a small subset of AMASS motions and evaluate sim-to-sim transfer by retargeting to a different skeleton with PyRoki.
Implement a coursework project comparing imitation learning vs RL fine-tuning for a walk-to-goal task using ProtoMotions and analyse sample efficiency and learned motion quality.

tools.name: hawk86104/three-vue-tres
tools.desc: 🎉一款让你的三维可视化项目快速落地的开源框架，天然具备良好的跨平台与🎊国产化适配能力 支持低代码编辑器、Web / 小程序 / App 全端部署，永久免费商用。 融合数字孪生、三维可视化（WebGL / WebGPU / three.js / tres.js / tvt.js），并扩展 AI 能力（Skills / OpenSpec），助力智能化场景快速构建 🚀

cls.summary: TvT.js is an open-source Web 3D ecosystem built on Three.js and Vue that targets digital twins, industrial visualization and online 3D editors with plugin and AI-assisted workflows.
cls.what_it_does: TvT.js provides a framework and tooling to build cross-platform 3D visualisation projects (web, mini-apps, apps) with plugin-based delivery, scene editors and an AI collaboration workflow for requirements-to-delivery. It is used as a frontend foundation for digital-twin and industrial visualisation applications and is notable for integrating TresJS/Vue3/Three.js with plugin contracts, an OpenSpec approach and optional AI skills for content and implementation.
cls.trl_rationale: The repository is over 2 years old, has a large star count (~2.5k), active development and documentation, plugin ecosystem and deployed editors referenced in the README, indicating production-ready maturity but not a de-facto industry standard.
student_project_ideas: Build a small digital twin dashboard that loads sensor time-series (mocked) and visualises asset states in a TvT.js scene, demonstrating two-way configuration between scene objects and a simple backend.

Create a plugin for TvT.js that imports photogrammetry or glTF models (using an existing converter) and exposes editable scene parameters via the framework's plugin contract, then prototype an AI-assisted asset placement workflow.

tools.name: ddalcu/mlx-serve
tools.desc: Native LLM inference server for Apple Silicon. OpenAI + Anthropic API compatible. No Python. Zig backend, Swift frontend macOS app with chat, music, voice, video generation.

cls.summary: MLX-Serve is a native local LLM inference server and macOS app that runs OpenAI/Anthropic-compatible models and media pipelines (chat, code agents, images, video, music and speech) on Apple Silicon and other platforms without Python or cloud accounts.
cls.what_it_does: MLX-Serve hosts and serves open models locally via an HTTP server and a native macOS app, exposing OpenAI/Anthropic/Ollama-compatible APIs so existing clients and tools can use local models. It supports chat and coding agents, multimodal media generation (images, video, music, TTS and 3D), model streaming/flash-loading for models larger than RAM, and has CLI, plugin and performance tuning features.
cls.trl_rationale: The project is actively maintained, widely starred, publishes releases (mac app and Linux builds) and documents builds, plugins and benchmarks, indicating a beta-level maturity; however the repository is under one year old so TRL is capped at 6.
prerequisites: Apple Silicon Mac for full native app experience (macOS 26.2+)
familiarity with CLI, model files (GGUF) and basic system tooling to build or run server
optionally NVIDIA GPU + CUDA for Linux/Windows builds
student_project_ideas: Build a secure local coding-agent demo using MLX-Serve as the inference backend and integrate it with a CI pipeline to perform automated code review and test generation.
Deploy MLX-Serve on an M-series Mac to host a local multimodal assistant that transcribes meetings, generates summaries and links outputs to a small digital-twin dashboard for operations coursework.

tools.name: iamlukethedev/Claw3D
tools.desc: Claw3D is an open source 3D engine built on OpenClaw for creating games, simulations, and high-performance 3D applications.

cls.summary: Claw3D is a self‑hosted web-based 3D workspace that visualises and lets you interact with AI agents working together in a shared virtual office.
cls.what_it_does: Claw3D provides a live 3D 'office' UI where AI agents appear as workers, enabling chat, monitoring, pull‑request review flows and simple training/playground features; it runs as a frontend (Studio) and connects to backends via a gateway protocol (OpenClaw, Hermes, or a custom HTTP/runtime adapter). It is notable for being a visualization and interaction layer that proxies runtime communications and includes an office builder, demo gateway, and runtime adapters so you can self‑host an immersive view of multi‑agent activity.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository is active and popular (many stars/forks and recent commits) but was created ~247 days ago (<1 year), so while it appears feature‑complete and widely used by the community, it lacks the multi‑year track record or ecosystem to rate above TRL 6.
prerequisites: an OpenClaw or Hermes runtime (or use the bundled demo gateway)
student_project_ideas: Build a small local agent runtime (or use the demo gateway) and extend Claw3D to visualise a simple CI/CD pipeline or automated testing agents, adding custom event cues and metrics displayed on desks.
Integrate Claw3D with a toy multi‑agent simulator to study agent coordination patterns and produce a short report comparing visualised behaviours with logged traces.

tools.name: BelfrySCAD/BOSL2
tools.desc: The Belfry OpenScad Library, v2.0.  An OpenSCAD library of shapes, masks, and manipulators to make working with OpenSCAD easier.  BETA

cls.summary: BOSL2 is a comprehensive OpenSCAD library that adds advanced shapes, filleting, attachment-based positioning, texturing and utility functions to simplify parametric 3D CAD modelling for fabrication and prototyping.
cls.what_it_does: BOSL2 extends OpenSCAD with many higher-level primitives (rounded prisms, tubes, metaballs), geometry utilities (path sweeping, NURBS, boolean/offset on point lists), part generators (gears, threads, hinges) and an attachment system to position components relative to each other. It is used by including the BOSL2 modules in OpenSCAD scripts to produce parametric models and to enable operations that are difficult or awkward in native OpenSCAD, notably fillets, complex sweeps and procedural texturing.
cls.trl_rationale: The project is mature and long-lived (created 2019) with many stars (2.4k), active maintenance (recent pushes) and broad community use in OpenSCAD workflows, indicating a stable, widely adopted library rather than an early prototype.
prerequisites: basic 3D geometry and parametric modelling concepts
student_project_ideas: Design and 3D-print a small assembly (hinged box or camera mount) using BOSL2 attachments and custom fillets, then iterate tolerances to achieve a snap-fit.
Implement a parametrised gear train and housing using BOSL2 gear and threading modules, export STL and run a simple strength or motion simulation workflow with a mechanical analysis tool.

tools.name: yomotsu/camera-controls
tools.desc: A camera control for three.js, similar to THREE.OrbitControls yet supports smooth transitions and more features.

cls.summary: camera-controls is a TypeScript library that provides smooth, feature-rich camera orbit/pan/zoom controls for three.js scenes and web-based 3D visualisation.
cls.what_it_does: It replaces or augments three.js built-in controls (like OrbitControls) to provide smoother transitions, advanced gestures, collision handling, animation/easing and utility helpers (fit-to-rect, path animation, focal offsets). It's used by installing it into a three.js app (CameraControls.install({THREE})) and calling cameraControls.update(delta) inside the render loop; it is notable for extensive examples, API documentation and integration with tooling like react-three-fiber.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository created in 2017 and actively maintained with many stars and forks, comprehensive docs and numerous examples, indicating broad adoption and stability; evidence: long history (2017), 2451 stars, published docs and integration examples (R3F/drei), and recent commits in 2026.
student_project_ideas: Create an interactive 3D parts viewer for an engineering design portfolio using three.js + camera-controls that implements fit-to-bounding-sphere, collision prevention and custom easing for guided walkthroughs.

Build a simple virtual robot demo (mesh + animated path) using three.js, camera-controls and meshwalk where the camera follows/orbits the robot and students evaluate UX of first-/third-person camera modes.

tools.name: geoman-io/leaflet-geoman
tools.desc: 🍂🗺️ The most powerful leaflet plugin for drawing and editing geometry layers

cls.summary: Leaflet-Geoman is a mature open-source Leaflet plugin that provides drawing and editing tools for vector geometry layers (markers, lines, polygons, circles, GeoJSON and more) in web maps.
cls.what_it_does: Leaflet-Geoman adds a comprehensive toolbar and API to create, edit, transform (cut, rotate, scale, split), measure and snap vector geometries on Leaflet maps. It is used in-browser as a drop-in Leaflet plugin and is notable for its wide feature set, TypeScript codebase and long track record in the open-source mapping ecosystem.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository created in 2015, many stars (2.4k), active commits as recently as the last push and good documentation and demos; evidence indicates wide adoption and maturity in the Leaflet/GIS ecosystem.
student_project_ideas: Build a web mapping application that allows users to digitise and edit site boundaries and export GeoJSON/TopoJSON, then visualise simple area/time statistics using a small backend (Node.js).

Integrate Leaflet-Geoman with a routing or asset-management dataset to create a tool for tagging and measuring infrastructure features (e.g. road segments or utility poles) and storing attributes in a GeoJSON-based database.

tools.name: apache/sedona
tools.desc: A cluster computing framework for processing large-scale geospatial data

cls.summary: Apache Sedona is an open-source spatial computing engine for large-scale geospatial data processing on cluster systems such as Apache Spark and Apache Flink.
cls.what_it_does: Sedona provides spatial data types, spatial SQL, and distributed spatial operators (joins, indexing, queries) so developers can run scalable geospatial analytics across large datasets. It is used as a library/plugin within cluster compute frameworks (Spark, Flink) and also offers subprojects like SedonaDB (single-node spatial analytical engine) and SpatialBench (benchmarking). Notable points are its integration with mainstream big-data stacks and active Apache project status with high download counts.
cls.trl_rationale: Long-running Apache project (created 2015) with many stars, high monthly download stats and active development and subprojects (SedonaDB, SpatialBench), used in production-grade big-data stacks — evidence of broad adoption and maturity.
prerequisites: familiarity with Apache Spark or Apache Flink
knowledge of Java/Scala or Python and distributed data processing
basic GIS/spatial concepts (projections, geometry types, spatial indexes)
student_project_ideas: Implement a spatial-join pipeline that matches vehicle GPS traces to road network polygons using Sedona on a Spark cluster and visualise results in GeoPandas.
Compare query performance of SedonaDB versus a PostGIS setup for a set of spatial SQL benchmark queries from SpatialBench and report trade-offs in ingestion and query latency.

tools.name: IBM/AssetOpsBench
tools.desc: AssetOpsBench - Industry 4.0: A unified benchmark and framework for building, orchestrating, and evaluating domain-specific AI agents for Industry 4.0 asset operations and maintenance, with 460+ scenarios, 5 specialist agents (IoT, FMSR, TSFM, Work Order,...), and multi-agent orchestration blueprints (MetaAgent, AgentHive) over MCP.

cls.summary: AssetOpsBench is an open benchmark and framework for building, orchestrating and evaluating AI agents for industrial asset operations and predictive maintenance.
cls.what_it_does: AssetOpsBench provides datasets, scenario definitions, MCP-based agent servers, orchestration blueprints and evaluation pipelines to train and measure specialist AI agents (IoT, fault diagnosis, work-order planning) on realistic maintenance scenarios. It is used by researchers and practitioners to run reproducible experiments, leaderboards and competitions, and to connect models to operational evidence (time series, failure rules, workflows).
cls.trl_rationale: Repository is >1 year old, has substantial community traction (2.4k stars, many forks), published peer-reviewed papers and external dataset releases, multiple integrations and reported independent reuse — evidence of production-ready benchmark and active research use.
prerequisites: familiarity with agent/MCP concepts (Model–Context–Protocol) and LLM toolchains
container / cloud basics for running servers and datasets
student_project_ideas: Implement a diagnostic agent that ingests AssetOpsBench time-series scenarios and uses a retriever+LLM pipeline to propose likely root causes, then evaluate its precision/recall against benchmark labels.

Build a multi-agent orchestration blueprint that couples an IoT-collector agent, a fault-detection agent and a work-order planner using the MCP server and compare performance metrics (response time, correctness) across scenarios.

tools.name: harry7557558/spirula-studio
tools.desc: Cross-vendor 3D Gaussian Splatting trainer - video to splat to mesh, Vulkan or CUDA.

cls.summary: Spirula Studio is an open-source, cross‑vendor trainer that converts photos or video into 3D Gaussian Splatting models and textured meshes, running on Vulkan or CUDA without requiring separate Python/PyTorch or COLMAP installs.
cls.what_it_does: Spirula Studio performs end-to-end 3D reconstruction from images or video: it extracts frames, runs a built‑in SfM pipeline, trains large 3D Gaussian Splatting models, and produces textured meshes and web-viewable outputs. It is notable for cross-vendor Vulkan compute (NVIDIA/AMD/Intel/Apple), extreme VRAM efficiency (quantized training for millions of Gaussians), and built-in conveniences like AI masking, fisheye/360° support and a bundled web viewer.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository is over one year old, has many stars (2417), platform binaries/releases for Windows/Linux/macOS, active recent commits and release notes describing new features; this indicates production-ready software used by a community rather than an early prototype.
prerequisites: GPU with Vulkan or CUDA support and driver knowledge
Vulkan SDK / MoltenVK (for macOS) and CMake/Ninja build toolchain
familiarity with command-line builds and basic photogrammetry concepts
student_project_ideas: Capture a small outdoor scene with a consumer 360° camera or drone video, use Spirula Studio to reconstruct a 3D Gaussian Splatting model and textured mesh, then import the mesh into a GIS or game engine to evaluate metric accuracy and visual quality.

Evaluate performance and VRAM usage by training the same dataset with the Vulkan backend and CUDA backend (on appropriate hardware), measuring training speed, memory footprint and final reconstruction quality.

tools.name: Alex-Rachel/TEngine
tools.desc: Unity 商用级别开发框架，原生内置 AI 工作流支持，集成 HybridCLR 高性能热更、Obfuz 代码混淆加固、YooAssets 企业级资源管理方案，构建高效、安全、可扩展的工业化开发底座。

cls.summary: TEngine is an open-source, production-oriented Unity game framework that provides performance-focused modules (resource management, hot-reload, UI, async systems) and a built-in AI development workflow for commercial-style Unity projects.
cls.what_it_does: TEngine provides a modular Unity application framework that integrates high-performance async systems, hot-update support (HybridCLR), commercial-grade asset management (YooAsset), configuration tooling (Luban) and a UI/code-generation workflow to accelerate cross-platform game and interactive application development. It is used by cloning into a Unity project, opening the provided scenes and following the documented editor menus and build steps; notable points are its integration of industry libraries and an AI/CI workflow for automated checks and verification.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository is >4 years old, has substantial community interest (2.4k stars, active recent pushes and few open issues), comprehensive documentation and examples; these indicate a production-ready framework rather than an experimental prototype.
prerequisites: Unity editor (familiarity with Unity project structure)
student_project_ideas: Create a small interactive digital-twin style scene in Unity using TEngine to manage assets and UI, then instrument it to stream telemetry and visualise state changes.
Build a demonstrator that uses TEngine's HybridCLR hot-update pipeline to deploy and test a scripted gameplay or control logic update without rebuilding the full client.

tools.name: h8man/NavMeshPlus
tools.desc: Unity NavMesh 2D Pathfinding

cls.summary: NavMeshPlus is an open-source Unity package that adds 2D-aware NavMesh generation and pathfinding (tilemap, sprites, Collider2D) to Unity projects.
cls.what_it_does: NavMeshPlus extends Unity's NavMeshComponents to collect 2D sources (tilemaps, sprites, 2D colliders), compute world bounds for a navigation surface, and bake a walkable NavMesh usable by Unity agents in top-down 2D scenes. It is installed as a Unity package or by copying scripts into Assets and is notable for bringing automatic NavMesh baking and standard NavMesh features to Unity 2D games and simulations.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository is mature (created 2018), has a large user community (2.3k stars, active commits up to 2026) and documentation/wiki and demo projects; this indicates production-ready quality though it is not an industry standard outside Unity.
prerequisites: understanding of Unity's navigation/agent concepts and 2D scene setup
student_project_ideas: Create a 2D warehouse simulation in Unity where multiple agents use NavMeshPlus to perform pick-and-place tasks, then measure and visualise congestion and travel times (combine with simple task allocator).
Integrate NavMeshPlus with a ROS/ROS2 bridge in a Unity-based simulator to prototype and test 2D navigation algorithms for a differential-drive robot and compare with a global planner implementation.

tools.name: cogentcore/core
tools.desc: A free and open source framework for building powerful, fast, elegant 2D and 3D apps that run on macOS, Windows, Linux, iOS, Android, and web with a single Go codebase, allowing you to Code Once, Run Everywhere.

cls.summary: Cogent Core is an open-source Go framework for building cross-platform 2D and 3D applications that run on desktop, mobile and the web from a single codebase.
cls.what_it_does: Cogent Core provides APIs and runtime support to write GUI and graphics applications in Go and deploy them to Windows, macOS, Linux, iOS, Android and the web (via WebAssembly/WebGPU). It solves the problem of maintaining separate UI/graphics stacks per platform by offering a single codebase and ships documentation and interactive examples that run in the browser.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository created in 2018, substantial star count (2.3k), active recent commits and extensive documentation with runnable web examples indicate a mature, well-used project suitable for production use.
prerequisites: familiarity with WebAssembly/WebGPU if targeting the web
student_project_ideas: Build a cross-platform data-visualisation dashboard in Go that streams sensor data (MQTT) and renders live 2D/3D plots using Cogent Core, deployable to desktop and web via WASM.
Create a simple physics-based simulator (e.g. pendulum or small vehicle) with interactive controls and 3D visuals in Cogent Core, and compare performance across desktop and web builds.

tools.name: spite/THREE.MeshLine
tools.desc: Mesh replacement for THREE.Line

cls.summary: MeshLine is a small JavaScript library that renders wide, textured and variable-width lines in three.js by replacing GL_LINE with a triangle strip.
cls.what_it_does: MeshLine provides a mesh-based replacement for THREE.Line that supports per-segment widths, textures along the line, partial visibility, dashes and an efficient advance() method for trails. It is used as an ES module together with three.js to create THREE.Mesh objects representing lines and exposes a customizable material with GLSL shaders for advanced visual effects.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository dates from 2015, has substantial community interest (2.3k stars), maintained with recent updates and demos; shows production-ready API and compatibility notes but is not a de-facto industry standard, so TRL 7 (production-ready) is appropriate.
student_project_ideas: Create an interactive web viewer that visualises sensor trajectories or vehicle paths using MeshLine with variable width and texture, combined with a simple backend that streams position data.
Build an animated trail effect for a simulated robot arm or drone in a three.js scene using MeshLine.advance(), and compare performance and visual quality against three.js Line2/LineMaterial.

tools.name: JSBSim-Team/jsbsim
tools.desc: An open source flight dynamics & control software library

cls.summary: JSBSim is an open-source, C++ flight dynamics model (FDM) library for nonlinear 6-DoF simulation of aircraft, rockets and other airborne vehicles with bindings for Python and MATLAB and plugins for simulators like Unreal and FlightGear.
cls.what_it_does: JSBSim computes the forces and motions of aircraft and similar vehicles using a nonlinear 6‑DOF physics model configurable via XML files, supporting aerodynamics, propulsion, control systems and earth/atmosphere models. It is used either as a standalone console simulator or integrated into environments such as Unreal Engine, FlightGear, and autopilot SITL frameworks (PX4, ArduPilot). Notable points are its multi-language bindings (Python, MATLAB), wide use in research and simulators, and documented integrations with UAV/autopilot stacks and game engines.
cls.trl_rationale: The repository is several years old with many stars, language bindings (Python, MATLAB), plugin integrations (Unreal, FlightGear), and documented use by projects (PX4, ArduPilot, Project AirSim) and academic citations; this indicates broad adoption and stable maturity consistent with TRL 8 rather than an experimental prototype.
prerequisites: basic flight dynamics and control theory
familiarity with XML configuration and optionally Python or MATLAB for bindings
student_project_ideas: Integrate a small autopilot (PX4 SITL) with JSBSim and design a PID/autonomous controller to perform a waypoint navigation task, logging performance and comparing guidance strategies.

Use the Python bindings to create a reinforcement learning environment (e.g., via gym-jsbsim) and train/test a controller for stall-recovery or aggressive-manoeuvre flight, then analyse stability and control limits.

tools.name: fougue/mayo
tools.desc: 3D CAD viewer and converter based on Qt + OpenCascade

cls.summary: Mayo is an open-source cross-platform 3D CAD viewer and file converter built with Qt and OpenCascade for inspecting, measuring and converting common CAD formats (STEP, IGES, STL, glTF, etc.).
cls.what_it_does: Mayo reads and writes many CAD and mesh file formats and provides an interactive 3D viewer with features like clip planes, exploded views, measurement tools and configurable mesh precision. It is used as a desktop application and a command-line converter for batch format conversion, notable for its broad format support powered by OpenCascade and a polished Qt UI.
cls.trl_rationale: The project is long-lived (created 2016), has many stars and forks, published release packages for major OSes, and shows recent activity; this indicates mature, production-quality software though not a de-facto standard.
prerequisites: basic CAD file format concepts / OpenCascade knowledge
student_project_ideas: Create a batch conversion pipeline that uses Mayo's CLI to convert large STEP assemblies to glTF/GLB with material preservation and validate the output in a web viewer.
Build an automated QA tool that opens STEP/IGES files with Mayo, measures specified dimensions and generates a report comparing parts against nominal CAD dimensions.

tools.name: Unity-Technologies/com.unity.netcode.gameobjects
tools.desc: Netcode for GameObjects is a high-level netcode SDK that provides networking capabilities to GameObject/MonoBehaviour workflows within Unity and sits on top of underlying transport layer.

cls.summary: Netcode for GameObjects is an official Unity package that provides high-level multiplayer networking for GameObject/MonoBehaviour workflows in the Unity engine.
cls.what_it_does: It implements networking primitives (message/scene/actor synchronization, RPCs, ownership and state replication) so developers can add multiplayer behaviour to Unity GameObjects. The package sits on top of low-level transports (for example the Unity Transport Package), is distributed as a Unity package, and is notable for being maintained by Unity with documentation, samples and a test project.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository is maintained by Unity Technologies since 2018, has many stars and forks, active commits and official documentation and samples; evidence of broad use and maturity justifies a high TRL.
prerequisites: Unity engine (experience with Unity Editor and projects)
basic networking concepts (clients, servers, RPC, state sync)
student_project_ideas: Create a multi-user virtual prototype in Unity that synchronises simple sensor and actuator state across clients using Netcode for GameObjects and log network latency impacts on a control loop.

Build a distributed human-in-the-loop simulation where multiple operators interact with the same simulated system over the network (Unity + Netcode + a simple physics model) and evaluate consistency and rollback strategies.

tools.name: walterlow/freecut
tools.desc: FreeCut is a professional-grade video editor that runs entirely in your browser. Professional video editing, zero installation. Create stunning videos with multi-track editing, keyframe animations, real-time preview, and high-quality exports.

cls.summary: FreeCut is an open-source, browser-based multi-track video editor that runs entirely locally using WebGPU and WebCodecs.
cls.what_it_does: FreeCut provides a professional-grade timeline editor in the browser with multi-track editing, keyframe animation, effects, real-time GPU preview and local export. It keeps projects and media on the user's disk (File System Access API / OPFS), performs analysis and on-device AI tasks (transcription, TTS, music generation) in-browser, and targets high-performance playback and GPU-first effects via WebGPU and WebCodecs.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository is about one year old and shows high activity, many stars (2.3k) and recent pushes; README documents extensive features and integrations but there is no evidence in the README of long-term production deployments or formal stable releases, so maturity corresponds to a Beta-stage open-source project.
prerequisites: modern browser with WebGPU / WebCodecs support
basic video editing concepts (timeline, tracks, keyframes)
student_project_ideas: Integrate FreeCut with an automated captioning pipeline: build a lab exercise that imports recorded lab experiments and uses FreeCut's local transcription to generate searchable clips and annotated export videos.

Prototype a WebGPU effect: implement a custom GPU-based filter (e.g., a scientific false-colour mapping) as a FreeCut plugin or patched effect and compare preview vs exported results for visualization of sensor data.

tools.name: espressif/esp-drone
tools.desc: Mini Drone/Quadcopter Firmware for ESP32 and ESP32-S Series SoCs.

cls.summary: ESP-Drone is an open-source firmware for building and controlling small quadcopters using Espressif ESP32-series microcontrollers.
cls.what_it_does: ESP-Drone provides flight-control firmware derived from the Crazyflie project that runs on ESP32/ESP32-S series SoCs, enabling stabilisation, height-hold and position-hold flight modes and control via mobile apps, gamepads or cfclient. It is used to develop, prototype and operate mini drones with simple hardware and extensible architecture, and is notable for being maintained by Espressif with documentation and multiple platform clients.
cls.trl_rationale: The project has been active since 2020, is maintained by Espressif, shows substantial community interest (2.3k stars), has documentation and platform clients (iOS/Android) and supports multiple ESP-IDF branches, indicating production-ready firmware rather than an experimental prototype.
prerequisites: basic electronics and soldering for hardware assembly
student_project_ideas: Extend ESP-Drone firmware to add a simple autonomous waypoint follower using onboard sensors and log telemetry to a companion Raspberry Pi for post-flight analysis.
Integrate an IMU calibration and fault-detection routine into the firmware and validate performance improvements using a hardware-in-the-loop setup or recorded flight logs analysed with Python.

tools.name: jasonwebb/morphogenesis-resources
tools.desc: Resources on the topic of digital morphogenesis (creating form with code). Includes links to major articles, code repos, creative projects, books, software, and more.

cls.summary: A curated, long-running collection of links and brief notes about algorithms, maths, experiments and software used to generate natural-looking form and patterns with code.
cls.what_it_does: This repository collects references, code links, papers and software relevant to digital morphogenesis and procedural form‑generation (e.g. reaction–diffusion, L-systems, DLA, space colonization). Lecturers and students can use it as a single reference to find algorithms, example projects and implementations for teaching, labs or projects in architecture, fabrication and computational design.
cls.trl_rationale: The repo has been maintained since 2019, has many stars and active updates, showing a stable curated resource (not a runnable engineering product). That sustained curation supports a mid-level TRL (beta/documentation maturity) rather than production software.
student_project_ideas: Implement a reaction–diffusion shader in GLSL or Processing using links from the list, and compare pattern parameter effects with a small report.
Use a space‑colonization algorithm from the resources to generate branch-like structures and export geometry to Blender for fabrication or structural analysis.

tools.name: Gforcex/OpenGraphic
tools.desc: Graphic Engine & Game Engine lists

cls.summary: A long-lived curated repository listing open-source and notable graphics and game engines, rendering projects and related tools.
cls.what_it_does: This repository is an organised index (an "awesome" list) of graphics engines, rendering libraries, shaders, tools and tutorials; users consult it to discover projects and learning resources. It is used as a reference rather than runnable software and is notable for its breadth, longevity and large star count that indicate community interest.
cls.trl_rationale: The repository is mature (created 2017, many stars and active updates) and widely used as a reference, but it is a curated list rather than a production software project, so it fits a Beta-level resource rather than a production tool.
student_project_ideas: Pick an open-source engine from the list (e.g. Godot or WickedEngine) and build a small interactive simulation that demonstrates a systems concept such as sensor fusion or control loop visualization.
Compare rendering techniques by implementing the same small scene in two listed projects (e.g. three.js and Filament) and report performance, visual fidelity and integration effort.

tools.name: gaphor/gaphor
tools.desc: Gaphor is the simple modeling tool

tools.name: pixiv/three-vrm
tools.desc: Use VRM on Three.js

cls.summary: three-vrm is an open-source library that adds VRM avatar (glTF-based) support to three.js so you can load, display and interact with humanoid 3D avatars in WebGL/WebGPU scenes.
cls.what_it_does: three-vrm provides a GLTFLoader plugin and utilities to load VRM (avatar) files into three.js scenes, handle VRM-specific materials (MToon), skeletons, and runtime features. It is used as a client-side library in web apps or demos and includes examples and WebGPU compatibility, making it notable for web-based avatar and XR visualisation workflows.
cls.trl_rationale: The project is several years old (created 2019), has many stars and active maintenance with recent commits and examples, documentation and npm packages; this indicates production-ready maturity though it is a niche library rather than an industry-standard platform.
student_project_ideas: Build a web demo that loads multiple VRM avatars with three-vrm, synchronises simple animations or poses across clients using WebSockets, and measures rendering performance differences between WebGLRenderer and WebGPURenderer.

Integrate a VRM avatar loaded with three-vrm into a robotics teleoperation interface, mapping simple joystick inputs to avatar pose or camera control and demonstrating human-in-the-loop visualisation for a mechatronics task.

alternatives_to: three.js (native glTF loaders without VRM extension support)

tools.name: tractorjuice/arc-kit
tools.desc: The Enterprise Architecture Governance Harness — strategy, architecture, delivery, and assurance using AI coding assistants

cls.summary: ArcKit is an AI-assisted toolkit for practising enterprise architecture governance that structures strategy, requirements, risk, vendor selection and assurance into repeatable workflows and artefacts.
cls.what_it_does: ArcKit automates the creation and governance of enterprise-architecture artefacts (principles, stakeholder analysis, requirements, risk registers, HLD/DLD, procurement/RFP outputs and traceability) by running guided commands and research agents against policy overlays and knowledge sources. It is used as a Claude Code plugin / CLI to generate draft documents, Mermaid diagrams and traceable citations, and notable for its large set of jurisdictional/sector overlays and explicit emphasis on auditable provenance for AI-generated content.
cls.trl_rationale: The repository is active (last push within weeks), has a large community (2.2k stars, many forks), extensive README, playlists and overlays, and a production-oriented install path (Claude Code plugins and multiple jurisdiction overlays), indicating production-readiness rather than an experimental prototype. Age (>1 year) supports a TRL above 6.
prerequisites: familiarity with enterprise architecture concepts (TOGAF/arc42 helpful)
experience with AI assistant platforms (Claude Code) and Node.js / JavaScript tooling
student_project_ideas: Use ArcKit to generate an auditable architecture decision record and traceability matrix for a mock e-government service, then evaluate the quality and review overhead compared with a manual process (combine with Git/GitHub and Mermaid diagramming).

Extend an ArcKit overlay to add a domain-specific constraints set (e.g. university IT services) and run case-based automated checks on generated HLD/DLD artefacts to measure false-positive/false-negative rates for compliance rules.

tools.name: future-agi/future-agi
tools.desc: Open-source, end-to-end platform for evaluating, observing, and improving LLM and AI agent applications. Tracing · Evals · Simulations · Datasets · Gateway · Guardrails. Self-hostable. Apache 2.0.

cls.summary: Future AGI is an open-source, self-hostable platform for evaluating, tracing, simulating, guarding and improving LLM-based agents throughout development and production.
cls.what_it_does: It provides an end-to-end stack to run agent simulations, collect OpenTelemetry traces, run automated evaluations and apply runtime guardrails and gateways so teams can observe and close the feedback loop from production traces back to improved agent behavior. It is deployed as a Docker/Helm stack (or managed cloud) and integrates instrumentation libraries and connectors so you can trace real LLM calls, run large-scale simulators/evals, and route or protect requests in real time.
cls.trl_rationale: The repo is active, well-documented, provides installers and a managed cloud offering, and has many stars and forks, indicating adoption; however it was created ~208 days ago (under one year), so per the maturity rules it should be capped at TRL 6 despite production claims and benchmarks.
prerequisites: familiarity with OpenTelemetry and LLM concepts
student_project_ideas: Instrument a simple LLM-based chatbot with Future AGI's OpenTelemetry libraries, run a set of automated evals and produce a report showing common failure modes and suggested guardrails.

Build a small simulator that generates adversarial prompts for an agent, feed traces into Future AGI, and implement a guardrail policy that blocks or corrects hallucinations; evaluate effectiveness before and after.

tools.name: agno-agi/dash
tools.desc: A self-learning data agent built with systems engineering principles. It grounds answers in 6 layers of context and improves with every query.

cls.summary: Dash is an open-source, self-learning data agent that answers English questions by generating grounded SQL and improving over time using layered contextual memory and a feedback loop.
cls.what_it_does: Dash provides a conversational interface (web UI, Slack, terminal) that translates natural-language queries into grounded, read-only or managed SQL against a PostgreSQL knowledge store and learns from query results and errors. It is used by running the Docker-based service, connecting AgentOS or Slack, and supplying an LLM API key; notable features are its six layers of contextual grounding and a self-learning loop that records validated SQL, schema knowledge and error patterns.
cls.trl_rationale: The project is active, well-documented, provides Docker compose, deployment scripts and examples, and has a substantial community (stars/forks), indicating beta-level maturity; repository age is ~291 days (<1 year) which limits a higher TRL without longer production track record.
prerequisites: OpenAI API key (or other LLM provider credentials)
student_project_ideas: Build a course assignment where students extend Dash's knowledge layer with domain-specific business rules for an engineering dataset and evaluate how that improves SQL accuracy and downstream metrics.
Integrate Dash with a simulated IoT telemetry PostgreSQL dataset (e.g. vehicle or sensor logs) and implement queries and automated learnings to detect and explain anomalous behaviour.

tools.name: CrossGL/crosstl
tools.desc: Translate GPU shaders and compute kernels between GLSL, HLSL, Metal, SPIR-V, Slang, CUDA and HIP, and to WGSL, through the CrossGL IR

cls.summary: CrossTL is an open-source Python tool that translates GPU shaders and compute kernels between many shading languages via an intermediate CrossGL IR.
cls.what_it_does: CrossTL imports shader or kernel source from languages like GLSL, HLSL, Metal, CUDA and others into a CrossGL intermediate representation and generates code for targets such as GLSL, HLSL, Metal, SPIR-V and WGSL. It is used as a CLI or Python library to automate large-scale translation, validation and project porting, and it runs reference-tool checks (glslang, DXC, spirv-tools, etc.) as part of CI to measure coverage.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository is >2 years old, has substantial community interest (2.2k stars), active pushes and CI that runs wide validation probes and coverage reports; shows production-level testing and real-world project porting workflows, so it appears production-ready rather than prototype.
prerequisites: installed native GPU toolchains (glslang, DXC, spirv-tools, nvcc/hipcc, Metal compiler)
student_project_ideas: Port a small rendering or GPU-compute submodule from an open-source repo (e.g. HLSL → WGSL) using crosstl, run the provided validation checks and evaluate performance differences in WebGPU vs native runtimes.

Build an automated shader-compatibility scanner for a game or simulation repo that uses crosstl's scan and translate-project commands to produce a report of unsupported constructs and required host-side changes.

tools.name: martin-ger/esp32_nat_router
tools.desc: An AI-enabled NAT Router/Firewall for the ESP32

cls.summary: Firmware that turns an ESP32-family board into a small NAT router/firewall with features like DHCP, WireGuard VPN, PCAP capture and Home Assistant integration.
cls.what_it_does: The project provides ESP32 firmware to route/NAT between an AP network and a STA or Ethernet uplink, optionally tunnelling upstream traffic over WireGuard. It includes DHCP, firewall/ACLs, port forwarding, packet capture, a web UI/CLI, MQTT Home Assistant telemetry and an MCP bridge for AI control, and is installed via prebuilt binaries or built with ESP-IDF.
cls.trl_rationale: The repository is mature (created 2020), has many stars and forks, active recent commits and pre-built binaries and web installer documentation, indicating a stable, widely-used project rather than a short-lived prototype.
prerequisites: experience flashing ESP32 hardware and basic networking concepts (DHCP, NAT, firewall)
student_project_ideas: Build a small IoT guest network using the ESP32 NAT Router, add device-level telemetry published to Home Assistant via MQTT, and visualise network activity in a dashboard.
Implement an automated PCAP-based intrusion detection demo by streaming captured packets from the router to a Raspberry Pi running a lightweight IDS and evaluate detection of simple attacks.

tools.name: antoinezambelli/forge
tools.desc: A Python framework for self-hosted LLM tool-calling and multi-step agentic workflows

cls.summary: Forge is a Python framework and standalone proxy that adds reliability and guardrails to self-hosted LLM tool-calling and multi-step agentic workflows.
cls.what_it_does: Forge accepts a set of tools and runs an agentic loop where the model can call any tool; it provides rescue parsing, retry nudges, response validation and optional workflow constraints (required steps, prerequisites, terminal tool). It can be used as a Python library (WorkflowRunner or middleware) or as a drop-in proxy that speaks OpenAI/Anthropic-compatible APIs to add guardrails to existing clients.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository is active, well-documented and provides a standalone proxy and Python package with an eval suite and versioned releases (v0.7.0), but it is under one year old so track record is recent—best described as beta.
prerequisites: A running LLM backend (llama-server, Ollama, Anthropic, vLLM, etc.)
Basic familiarity with LLM APIs and agent/tool constructs
student_project_ideas: Build a small question-answering assistant that exposes two domain tools (e.g. a document search and a calculator) and use Forge as a proxy to evaluate how its guardrails prevent malformed tool calls compared to a baseline agent.

Integrate Forge with a local llama-server backend to run an experiment comparing success rates and latency across model sizes and backend configurations (llama-server vs Ollama) for a multi-step engineering workflow.

tools.name: postgis/postgis
tools.desc: PostGIS spatial database extension to PostgreSQL [mirror]

tools.name: erichlof/THREE.js-PathTracing-Renderer
tools.desc: Real-time PathTracing with global illumination and progressive rendering, all on top of the Three.js WebGL framework. Click here for Live Demo: https://erichlof.github.io/THREE.js-PathTracing-Renderer/Geometry_Showcase.html

cls.summary: A browser-based real-time path tracing renderer built on three.js that produces physically-based global illumination, reflections, refractions and volumetric effects at interactive frame rates.
cls.what_it_does: This project implements a GPU path tracer in GLSL and JavaScript on top of three.js to render scenes with global illumination, caustics, depth of field and volumetrics progressively in the browser. It is used by loading scenes or GLTF models into the demo pages and runs as a WebGL shader pipeline with BVH acceleration and ray-marching for procedural environments. It is notable for interactive, progressive convergence demos and many ready-made live examples showing advanced rendering effects on commodity hardware.
cls.trl_rationale: The repository is long-lived (created 2016) with many stars, multiple live demo pages and recent activity (last push 2026), indicating production-quality examples and real users; it lacks evidence of wide industrial standard adoption so TRL 7 (production-ready) is appropriate.
prerequisites: basic 3D rendering concepts (BVH, ray tracing, PBR)
student_project_ideas: Implement a small interactive scene that loads a GLTF model and measures convergence/performance when toggling features (depth of field, caustics, BVH) to study renderer performance trade-offs.

Integrate the path tracer with a simple physics simulation (e.g. particle or fluid surface) and compare visual fidelity and performance between rasterized and path-traced renderings for an engineering visualization task.

tools.name: KhronosGroup/UnityGLTF
tools.desc: Runtime glTF 2.0 Loader for Unity3D

cls.summary: UnityGLTF is an open‑source C# library for importing and exporting glTF 2.0 assets inside the Unity engine, supporting both editor and runtime usage across Unity platforms.
cls.what_it_does: UnityGLTF loads and writes glTF 2.0 models, animations and associated extensions into Unity projects so 3D assets can be exchanged between tools and runtime applications. It is used as a package or code library in the Unity Editor or at runtime (including WebGL), and is notable for being pure C#, extensible with plugins, and supporting many glTF extensions.
cls.trl_rationale: The repository is long‑lived (created 2017), has a substantial user community (2.2k stars, many forks), recent commits (2026) and documented installation and compatibility guidance, indicating production readiness rather than an early prototype.
prerequisites: Familiarity with 3D asset concepts and the glTF format
student_project_ideas: Create a Unity scene that loads different glTF digital‑twin models at runtime and visualises telemetry overlays (combine UnityGLTF with a simple MQTT or REST data feed).

Implement a small export pipeline that converts in‑editor GameObjects (with animations) to glTF using UnityGLTF and validates interoperability by importing the exported file into another glTF viewer or glTFast.

tools.name: locationtech/jts
tools.desc: The JTS Topology Suite is a Java library for creating and manipulating vector geometry.

cls.summary: JTS is a mature Java library for creating, analysing and manipulating 2D vector geometry used widely in GIS and spatial engineering software.
