cls.what_it_does: JTS provides data structures and algorithms for constructing and operating on vector geometries (points, lines, polygons), including topology operations, triangulation, Voronoi, buffering and spatial predicates. It is used as a backend geometry engine in GIS stacks and applications and ships with test data and a small GUI (TestBuilder) for visualising geometry and debugging geometry functions.
cls.trl_rationale: JTS has a long public history, many stars and forks, active maintenance under LocationTech/Eclipse, documentation, Javadoc and known downstream ports (GEOS, NetTopologySuite, JSTS). These indicate a mature, widely adopted geometry engine rather than an experimental prototype.
student_project_ideas: Build a small GIS tool that reads shapefiles, applies geometric operations (buffer, intersection, simplify) using JTS and visualises results in a web map (Leaflet or OpenLayers).
Compare polygon simplification and buffering algorithms: implement test cases using JTS and evaluate error and performance on road-network and building footprints datasets.

tools.name: proj4js/proj4js
tools.desc: JavaScript library to transform coordinates from one coordinate system to another, including datum transformations

tools.name: Esri/arcgis-python-api
tools.desc: Documentation and samples for ArcGIS API for Python

cls.summary: ArcGIS API for Python is a mature Python library for working with maps and geospatial data, letting users query, analyse, visualise and manage GIS content programmatically and within Jupyter notebooks.
cls.what_it_does: The library provides tools to access and manage web GIS content (ArcGIS Online / Enterprise), perform vector and raster analysis, geocoding, routing, and integrates with the scientific Python stack for data processing and machine learning. It is used as a programmatic SDK from Jupyter, scripts, or within ArcGIS Pro/Docker environments and is notable for its direct integration with Esri's web GIS ecosystem and extensive sample notebooks.
cls.trl_rationale: The project is mature and long-lived (created 2016), actively maintained by Esri, has many stars and forks, official documentation, examples and integration with ArcGIS Online/Pro—evidence of wide adoption though it is an Esri product rather than an open standard.
prerequisites: optionally an ArcGIS Online/Enterprise account for some services
student_project_ideas: Build a Jupyter notebook pipeline that ingests open spatial datasets, performs spatial joins and raster/vector analysis with the ArcGIS API, and publishes interactive web maps to ArcGIS Online for a civil infrastructure site survey.
Combine the ArcGIS API with a simple IoT timeseries stream (MQTT or CSV sensor logs) to visualise asset telemetry on a web map and implement geofencing alerts for operations coursework.

tools.name: layabox/LayaAir
tools.desc: LayaAir is a fully platform rendering engine with rich 2D/3D rendering capabilities and a mature integrated development platform

cls.summary: LayaAir is an open-source, cross-platform 2D/3D rendering engine and IDE (TypeScript/JavaScript) for building web and native interactive applications, including games, AR/VR and digital-twin style visualisations.
cls.what_it_does: LayaAir provides a rendering engine that targets WebGL/WebGPU and native graphics APIs and an IDE with scene, material, animation and physics editors to build and publish interactive 2D/3D applications across web, mobile and desktop platforms. It solves the problem of creating and deploying interactive visualisations and real-time scenes (games, AR/VR, digital twins) with a single engine and tooling, and is notable for multi-API support (WebGL, WebGPU, OpenGL, Vulkan) and an integrated IDE workflow.
cls.trl_rationale: The repository is multi-year (created 2019) with many stars, active recent commits, multiple maintenance branches and a downloadable IDE and engine used in production scenarios per the README; this indicates production-ready maturity rather than an experimental prototype.
prerequisites: familiarity with 3D graphics concepts (meshes, materials, lighting)
student_project_ideas: Create an interactive web-based digital twin of a simple mechanical system (e.g., a two-link robot arm) using LayaAir for real-time 3D visualisation and a small ROS/ROS‑bridge backend to feed joint telemetry.

Build a cross-platform AR/VR scene that visualises sensor data (time series) in 3D, combining LayaAir rendering with a time-series backend (InfluxDB or MQTT) to demonstrate operational digital twin concepts.

tools.name: floneum/kalosm
tools.desc: Instant, controllable, local pre-trained AI models in Rust

cls.summary: Kalosm is a Rust ecosystem that provides a simple interface to run and integrate local or remote pre-trained AI models (text, audio, image) and includes Fusor, a compiler-backed runtime for quantized inference on CPU and WebGPU.
cls.what_it_does: Kalosm exposes Rust-first APIs to load and run pre-trained language, audio and image models locally or remotely, plus utilities for context extraction, chunking and structured generation. Fusor is the project's backend runtime that loads quantized GGUF models and compiles fused kernels for CPU and WebGPU to accelerate inference without custom shader code. The project is notable for its Rust-native design, structured generation support (derive-based parsers) and explicit focus on local, privacy-preserving inference.
cls.trl_rationale: The repository is multi-year (created 2023) with many stars (2.2k), active commits and worked examples, indicating production-readiness for many use cases; however, Fusor is marked early-development in the README so some backend features are still maturing.
prerequisites: basic ML / LLM concepts and model formats (GGUF, quantization)
familiarity with async (tokio) and optional WebGPU
student_project_ideas: Build a domain-specific chatbot for a systems-engineering course that uses Kalosm to load a local Llama/Mistral model and integrates context extraction from project documents to answer requirements questions.

Compare inference performance and output quality between Fusor (CPU/WebGPU) and an existing runtime (e.g. llama.cpp) by quantizing a medium-size model to GGUF and benchmarking latency, memory and accuracy on a Raspberry Pi or laptop.

tools.name: GammaLabTechnologies/harmonist
tools.desc: Portable AI agent orchestration with mechanical protocol enforcement. 186 agents, zero runtime dependencies.

cls.summary: Harmonist is an open-source multi-agent orchestration framework that enforces mechanical protocol checks (IDE hooks, manifest verification, validated memory) to prevent AI assistants from bypassing required development workflows.
cls.what_it_does: Harmonist orchestrates many specialised AI subagents and enforces project rules through concrete IDE-level hooks and supply-chain verified manifests so code-changing agent turns cannot complete unless required checks (QA reviewers, schema-validated memory, supply-chain hashes) pass. It is used as a drop-in pack next to a codebase (Python and shell hooks) and integrates with coding assistant runtimes such as Cursor and Claude Code; notable features are mechanical gate enforcement, a hashed MANIFEST for supply-chain integrity, and schema-validated memory with secret scanning.
cls.trl_rationale: The repository is well-documented, popular (2.2k stars) and shows a broad agent catalogue and CI/testing notes, indicating active development and user interest; however it was created ~208 days ago (<1 year) so there is not yet a long track record required for TRL 7+, placing it at Beta (TRL 6).
prerequisites: familiarity with AI agent concepts and IDE hooks
student_project_ideas: Create a lab where students configure a Harmonist pack for a small codebase and demonstrate enforced QA workflows by writing a subagent that attempts to modify code and must be blocked until automated checks and a reviewer approve the change.

Implement a supply-chain integrity exercise: extend Harmonist's MANIFEST verification to include a small third-party script repository and measure detection of tampering and the enforced refusal to install altered agent definitions.

tools.name: jiawanlong/Cesium-Examples
tools.desc: CesiumJS2026年最新Examples，200多个原生示例：自定义纹理、地形开挖、可视域分析、洪水淹没、缓冲分析、日照分析、方量分析、通透分析、剖面、单体化、视频融合、视频投射、雨雪雾、天空盒、场景出图、体积云、闪电、视锥体、雷达扫描、水波纹、动态扩散点、电子围栏、粒子效果、物理引擎、克里金、海流、大数据可视化、坐标转换、相机、飞行漫游、瓦片加载、xyz、tms、wms、wmts、天地图、高德、百度、wkt、shp、geojson、pbf、地形、entity、模型、海量数据、Primitive、gif、聚合、czml、字体图标、运动、3Dtiles、模型偏移、等等。。

cls.summary: A large, actively maintained collection of native CesiumJS web examples demonstrating 3D mapping, spatial analysis and visualization techniques.
cls.what_it_does: This repository provides 200+ standalone, runnable CesiumJS examples showing how to load imagery/terrain/3D Tiles, perform spatial analyses (viewshed, flood inundation, buffer, profile), add effects (particles, weather, lighting) and integrate models and data sources. It is used as a learning and reference resource: each example is a small file you can run on a web server to see code patterns and visual outcomes relevant to geospatial visualization and digital-twin style applications.
cls.trl_rationale: The repository is well-established (created 2024-04, ~939 days old), highly starred (2,231) and actively maintained with recent pushes and many runnable examples, indicating production-ready maturity as a demonstration/reference resource rather than a research prototype.
student_project_ideas: Build a small web-based digital-twin demo that loads a city 3D Tileset and implements a simple inundation simulation using the repository's flood examples and a custom UI.
Create an interactive viewshed and route-visibility tool that combines the viewshed examples with path planning (geojson polylines) and evaluates visibility along a corridor.

tools.name: unrealcv/unrealcv
tools.desc: UnrealCV: Connecting Computer Vision to Unreal Engine

cls.summary: UnrealCV is an open-source plugin and Python client that connects Unreal Engine scenes to external programs for computer vision, synthetic data generation and embodied AI experiments.
cls.what_it_does: UnrealCV extends Unreal Engine with a plugin that exposes commands and APIs to control cameras, capture images (including depth and optical flow) and manipulate objects, and a Python client to communicate with the engine from PyTorch/TensorFlow or other programs. It is used to generate labelled synthetic data, run embodied-agent experiments in realistic virtual worlds, and automate rendering and sensor outputs for vision and robotics research.
cls.trl_rationale: This project has been maintained since 2016, has many stars, a citation in the literature and recent updates (supports UE5.2), indicating production-ready status for research and prototyping; it is not a de-facto industry standard so TRL 7 is appropriate.
prerequisites: Familiarity with Unreal Engine (editor and projects)
Basic C++ knowledge to build the plugin into a UE project
Python experience (PyTorch/TensorFlow) to use the client
student_project_ideas: Create a simulated perception pipeline that captures RGB, depth and semantic masks from an UnrealCV scene and trains a semantic segmentation model in PyTorch using the synthetic dataset.

Integrate an autonomous agent (RL or navigation stack) with UnrealCV to evaluate obstacle avoidance and localisation algorithms in varied simulated environments, and compare performance against real-world datasets.

tools.name: Hubs-Foundation/hubs
tools.desc: Duck-themed multi-user virtual spaces in WebVR. Built with A-Frame.

cls.summary: Hubs is an open-source web-based multi-user 3D collaboration client that runs in desktop, mobile and VR browsers using A-Frame and WebXR.
cls.what_it_does: Hubs provides a client-side platform for creating and joining shared 3D rooms where users can interact, communicate by voice and place 3D assets in real time. It is used by running the JavaScript/Node.js client (customisable) alongside the Hubs backend and is notable for being web-first (A-Frame / three.js / WebXR) and supporting VR and mobile without native apps.
cls.trl_rationale: The project is long-lived (created 2017), has substantial community interest (2k+ stars), active recent commits and is deployed in production contexts (Mozilla Hubs / Hubs Cloud references), indicating a mature, widely adopted codebase.
prerequisites: familiarity with A-Frame / WebXR concepts for customisation
student_project_ideas: Deploy a self-hosted Hubs instance and create a customised room that loads glTF CAD models for a collaborative design-review workflow, adding annotations and measuring tools.
Extend the Hubs client to visualise live IoT telemetry (MQTT or WebSocket) inside a shared room so students can explore real-time sensor data in 3D alongside collaborators.

tools.name: z2586300277/three-cesium-examples
tools.desc: WebGL Three.js Cesium.js Examples And Demo - WebGL 的 Three.js 和 Cesium.js 案例 --- Star ---点星星

cls.summary: A large collection of WebGL examples that integrate Three.js and Cesium.js to demonstrate 3D mapping, visualization and interactive Web3D effects in the browser.
cls.what_it_does: This repository collects many browser-based demo projects showing how to combine Three.js (general 3D) with Cesium.js (3D globe / geospatial) to build interactive maps, point-clouds, particles and visual effects. You use it by running the provided index.html / GitHub Pages preview and by copying example folders and config entries into your own site; it is notable for breadth of curated demos and ready-to-run example pages.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository is over one year old, has many stars and active pushes, and provides a large, maintained set of runnable demos (GitHub Pages preview), indicating beta-level maturity as a examples/demo collection rather than a production platform.
student_project_ideas: Create an interactive web map that overlays a simulated sensor dataset on Cesium and uses Three.js to render 3D markers and particle effects, then evaluate performance and GPU load.
Fork one of the point-cloud or buildings demos and integrate a simple server-side GeoJSON feed to visualise live asset locations, adding UI controls to filter by attribute.

tools.name: eclipse-iceoryx/iceoryx
tools.desc: Eclipse iceoryx™ - true zero-copy inter-process-communication

cls.summary: iceoryx is an open-source, zero-copy inter-process communication (IPC) middleware that transfers large data between processes using shared memory with predictable low latency.
cls.what_it_does: iceoryx provides a shared-memory based publish/subscribe and request/response IPC transport that avoids copying payloads between processes, ensuring constant low latency regardless of message size. It is used as a high-performance transport layer inside larger frameworks (e.g. ROS 2) and is notable for its true zero-copy design, multi-platform support and focus on real-time and automotive use-cases.
cls.trl_rationale: The project has existed since 2019, has a large user base (stars, forks) and explicit integrations (ROS 2, Cyclone DDS, commercial users), showing production use and maturity; README notes it's entering maintenance mode and maintainers are moving to iceoryx2, which explains continued development focus.
prerequisites: familiarity with IPC and shared memory concepts
Linux/Unix toolchain and build systems (CMake, compilers)
student_project_ideas: Build a high-throughput sensor pipeline by integrating iceoryx with ROS 2 (rmw_iceoryx) to stream camera or LiDAR data between processes without copies and measure latency and CPU usage.
Create a simulator-to-controller bridge using iceoryx shared memory to stream large state vectors from a physics simulator to a control process and evaluate end-to-end jitter and determinism.

tools.name: thingsboard/thingsboard-gateway
tools.desc: Open-source IoT Gateway - integrates devices connected to legacy and third-party systems with ThingsBoard IoT Platform using Modbus, CAN bus, BACnet, BLE, OPC-UA, MQTT, ODBC and REST protocols.

cls.summary: ThingsBoard IoT Gateway is an open-source Python gateway that connects devices and industrial protocols to the ThingsBoard IoT platform, normalising telemetry and managing device lifecycle.
cls.what_it_does: The gateway collects data from a wide range of sources (Modbus, OPC-UA, CAN, BACnet, BLE, MQTT, ODBC, REST, FTP, SNMP, etc.), converts and maps incoming messages into a unified format, and forwards them to ThingsBoard. It is used as a protocol adapter and edge integration layer with features for local buffering, automatic reconnection, remote configuration and remote logging, and is extensible via custom Python connectors and converters.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository created in 2017 and actively maintained with many connectors, extensive documentation and a large star/fork count, indicating real-world adoption and maturity; these factors support a mature TRL (8) though it is not a de-facto industry standard.
prerequisites: understanding of industrial protocols (Modbus/OPC-UA) for advanced configuration
student_project_ideas: Build a lab that uses the ThingsBoard Gateway to ingest simulated Modbus PLC telemetry into ThingsBoard and implement dashboards and alerting for a simple industrial process.
Create a custom Python connector for a proprietary sensor protocol and demonstrate end-to-end data ingestion, local buffering during outages, and recovery verification using ThingsBoard dashboards.

tools.name: withcatai/node-llama-cpp
tools.desc: Run AI models locally on your machine with node.js bindings for llama.cpp. Enforce a JSON schema on the model output on the generation level

cls.summary: node-llama-cpp provides Node.js/TypeScript bindings to run llama.cpp models locally with GPU support, prebuilt binaries, and features like JSON-schema output enforcement and function-calling.
cls.what_it_does: This library lets developers run LLMs locally from Node.js by wrapping the llama.cpp runtime, providing prebuilt binaries (with CMake fallback) and automatic hardware adaptation (CUDA/Metal/Vulkan). It adds developer-friendly features such as TypeScript APIs, CLI, embeddings, function-calling, and the ability to require model outputs to conform to a JSON schema.
cls.trl_rationale: The repository is multi-year (created 2023-08), widely starred (2.2k+ stars), actively maintained with releases and documentation, and ships prebuilt binaries and a CLI — evidence of production-ready maturity and real-world use.
prerequisites: Local model files (e.g. .gguf) and sufficient hardware (CPU or GPU with CUDA/Metal/Vulkan drivers)
CMake toolchain only if building from source
student_project_ideas: Build a local question-answering assistant for engineering design documents: ingest PDFs, create embeddings with node-llama-cpp and a small vector store, and implement a JSON-schema enforced response format for traceability.

Prototype an offline, privacy-preserving controller or planner test harness where a local LLM suggests control parameters; validate outputs automatically by enforcing JSON schemas and integrate with a simulation (e.g. Gazebo or a simple dynamics model).

tools.name: andrumak/MyBox
tools.desc: MyBox is a set of attributes, tools and extensions for Unity

cls.summary: MyBox is an open-source collection of Unity editor attributes, inspector widgets, helper components and editor utilities that speed up Unity game and application development.
cls.what_it_does: MyBox provides ready-made Unity editor attributes (e.g. conditional fields, read-only, range sliders, buttons), custom inspector types and small runtime/editor components to simplify common tasks and improve workflow inside the Unity editor. It is used by importing the package into a Unity project and applying the attributes/components to scripts and GameObjects to get improved inspector behaviour and small tooling features. The project is notable for being a broad, mature toolbox with many focused utilities rather than a single large framework.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository is long-lived (created 2016), actively maintained with many stars and forks and recent pushes, indicating broad community use and stability; README and wiki show extensive documentation and examples.
student_project_ideas: Create a Unity demo that uses MyBox attributes (e.g. ConditionalField, AutoProperty) to build a configurable simulation dashboard that students can manipulate via the Inspector and record performance metrics.
Integrate MyBox components (GUID, CoroutineGroup) into a small robotics simulation (Unity + ROS bridge) to manage simulated robot behaviours and demonstrate experiment reproducibility.

tools.name: handy-computer/transcribe.cpp
tools.desc: ggml speech-to-text inference for 16+ model families

cls.summary: transcribe.cpp is an open-source C/C++ speech-to-text inference library that runs many GGUF-format ASR models on ggml with CPU and GPU (Metal, Vulkan, CUDA) backends.
cls.what_it_does: It provides fast local inference for 16+ ASR model families (streaming and batch), verified model variants and a queryable model catalog for performance and accuracy. Users run the library in C/C++ applications or command-line tools to transcribe audio locally, with options for diarization, language identification and token/word timestamps; notable features are broad model support and multiple GPU backend optimisations.
cls.trl_rationale: The repository is active, well-starred (2k+ stars), documents many verified model variants and publishes release artifacts (catalog.db), indicating beta-level maturity; however it is younger than one year (≈224 days), so evidence supports TRL 6 rather than a higher production rating.
prerequisites: GPU drivers for CUDA/Vulkan/Metal when using GPU backends
student_project_ideas: Integrate transcribe.cpp with a ROS-based robot to add local voice command recognition and evaluate latency and reliability across CPU and GPU backends.
Benchmark WER and real-time factor of several transcribe.cpp model variants on noisy industrial audio and produce recommendations for on-device deployment (compare tinyBLAS CPU vs CUDA/Vulkan).

tools.name: vvoovv/blosm
tools.desc: Blosm addon for Blender. A few clicks import of Google 3D cities, OpenStreetMap, terrain. Global coverage. Source code is in the branch 'release'.

tools.name: 3D-Vision-World/awesome-NeRF-and-3DGS-SLAM
tools.desc: A comprehensive list of Implicit Representations, NeRF and 3D Gaussian Splatting papers relating to SLAM/Robotics domain, including papers, videos, codes, and related websites

cls.summary: A curated, community-maintained list of papers, code, demos and resources about Neural Radiance Fields (NeRF) and 3D Gaussian Splatting applied to SLAM and robotics.
cls.what_it_does: This repository collects and organises literature, implementations, benchmarks and tutorials that link implicit/NeRF/3D Gaussian Splatting research to SLAM and robotics problems. It is used as a reference resource for researchers and students to find papers, links to code and related websites rather than as runnable software.
cls.trl_rationale: This is a curated bibliography/awesome-list rather than an engineering tool; it is mature as a reference (many stars, long history since 2022) but provides links to external work rather than a production software product, so rate it at a low software-TRL.
student_project_ideas: Perform a literature review and comparison of NeRF and 3D Gaussian Splatting approaches for robotic localisation, producing a short report and reproducible evaluation on an open dataset linked from the list.
Select a referenced NeRF/3DGS SLAM implementation from the list, reproduce its results and integrate it into a simple ROS-based pipeline to demonstrate scene reconstruction and pose estimation.

tools.name: morluto/awesome-reverse-engineering
tools.desc: Curated reverse-engineering tools and learning resources for binaries, apps, firmware, formats, and protocols.

cls.summary: A curated, community-maintained list of tools and learning resources for reverse engineering binaries, firmware, apps, formats and protocols.
cls.what_it_does: This repository is an 'awesome' curated index linking to tools, tutorials and communities for reverse engineering tasks such as static and dynamic binary analysis, debugging, instrumentation and symbolic execution. It is used as a starting point to find specific tools or learning materials rather than being a runnable tool itself, and is notable for its broad coverage and classification of resources across subdomains (native, managed, firmware, web/protocols, AI-assisted analysis).
cls.trl_rationale: This is a curated resource list (not an application) with many linked projects; the repository itself is new (created ~39 days ago) so maturity is limited by age and ongoing curation, although it has strong community interest (stars/forks) which supports early adoption.
student_project_ideas: Assemble and document a small hands-on lab that uses three recommended open-source tools from the list (disassembler, debugger, dynamic tracer) to reverse-engineer a simple firmware or binary and report findings.

Compare and evaluate several static-analysis tools listed in the repository by measuring accuracy and usability on a curated set of benign and obfuscated binaries, and present recommendations for a teaching toolchain.

tools.name: dune3d/dune3d
tools.desc: 3D CAD application

cls.summary: Dune 3D is an open-source parametric 3D CAD application focused on designing parts (especially 3D‑printable enclosures) with STEP import/export, fillets/chamfers and a constraint solver.
cls.what_it_does: Dune 3D provides a parametric modelling environment that performs extrusions, intersections, fillets and chamfers using the Open CASCADE geometry kernel, and uses the Solvespace constraint solver for parametric constraints. It is used as a desktop application (Linux/Windows/macOS) for creating and exporting STEP models and for interactive modelling via a 3D viewport and editor tools.
cls.trl_rationale: The project is active, has documentation and multi-platform build instructions, many stars and an active discussion community, indicating beyond proof-of-concept maturity; however there is no evidence in the README of broad industrial adoption or stable versioned releases that would justify TRL 7+, so TRL 6 (beta) is appropriate.
prerequisites: build tools on target OS (compilers, meson/cmake as documented)
student_project_ideas: Design and 3D-print an electronics enclosure: create a parametric enclosure in Dune 3D that accepts PCB dimensions exported from a PCB tool (e.g. Horizon EDA) and add mounting features; iterate parameters in class to demonstrate design-for-manufacture tradeoffs.

Integrate STEP export with a downstream simulation: model a bracket in Dune 3D, export STEP to a structural FEA tool (e.g. CalculiX or FreeCAD FEM) and run a simple stress test to compare CAD geometry changes against simulation results.

tools.name: emilianavt/OpenSeeFace
tools.desc: Robust realtime face and facial landmark tracking on CPU with Unity integration

cls.summary: OpenSeeFace is an open-source, CPU-optimised realtime face and facial-landmark tracking library with a Unity component for receiving tracking data.
cls.what_it_does: OpenSeeFace runs a MobileNetV3-based facial landmark detector converted to ONNX and provides a Python-based tracker that sends landmark and pose data over UDP. It is typically used alongside Unity (or other engines) where an included Unity component receives the packets and exposes trackingData for avatar animation or visualization. The project is notable for focusing on CPU realtime performance, multiple model speed/quality trade-offs, and practical integration examples (Unity sample, launcher, binaries).
cls.trl_rationale: The repository is long-lived (created 2020), has many stars (2.1k), active recent commits, binary releases and known downstream users (VTube Studio, VSeeFace), and provides production-ready executables and Unity integration, indicating real-world use and production readiness.
prerequisites: basic Python (3.7+) and virtual environment usage
student_project_ideas: Build a Unity avatar that uses OpenSeeFace UDP tracking to drive facial expressions of a VRM model and measure latency and stability under different lighting and resolutions.

Compare landmark stability and expression capture between OpenSeeFace and MediaPipe on a dataset of low-light and noisy webcam recordings, and produce a short report evaluating suitability for teleoperation or HCI.

tools.name: sixtysevenlf/dsh-blender-plugin
tools.desc: DSH × Blender 直连插件 v3.0.6：15 个模型工具让 AI 驱动 GUI Blender（视口 / 自定义视角 / 无头 worker / 作业层 / 事务回滚 / 配方库），34 family / 228 op 契约层；npm 安装 + addon zip，GUI 优先、无头备用；dsh-TUI 选中 chip / @ 提及 / /blender，随包建模 skill，支持 WSL / Windows / macOS。

cls.summary: A Blender addon and DSH plugin that lets an AI agent inspect, modify, validate and run headless jobs in Blender to automate 3D modelling, assembly checks and render-based acceptance gates.
cls.what_it_does: DSH × Blender connects DeepSeek Harness (DSH) to a running Blender session so an agent can interactively or headlessly build and validate 3D scenes, run parametric modelling ops, perform assembly audits and produce exportable assets and rendered frames. It is used as a Blender addon plus a host-side plugin (npm/DSH bundle) and is notable for GUI-first agent interactions, headless job execution, measurement against reference images and a suite of reproducible parametric modelling and validation tools.
cls.trl_rationale: The project is feature-rich with releases and an installer path (npm + bundled addon) and many stars, indicating early adoption; however the repository is only 64 days old so per the rules its demonstrated maturity should be capped at TRL 5.
prerequisites: basic Python/Blender scripting knowledge; Node.js only for source builds
student_project_ideas: Use DSH × Blender to create a parametric part generator: define a spec-driven lofted surface, run parametric sweeps headlessly, and export GLB/FBX with an automated acceptance gate comparing renders to reference images.

Build an automated assembly-validator that imports a multi-part model into Blender, runs the plugin's assembly audit to detect clashes and gaps, applies safe repairs, and produces a delivery manifest and annotated render report.

tools.name: inferstep/ATLAS
tools.desc: Adaptive Test-time Learning and Autonomous Specialization

cls.summary: ATLAS is a self-hosted local coding agent that wraps compact open LLMs with planning, candidate generation, sandboxed testing and automated repair so models can produce and verify code on your hardware.
cls.what_it_does: ATLAS orchestrates an agent pipeline around local GGUF-compatible models to generate code candidates, run them in an isolated sandbox, verify results with tests and repair failures automatically. It is used from a CLI/TUI and a Go-based proxy that enforces grammar, routes tool calls and manages verification, with features for local model support (Vulkan/ROCm/Metal/CPU) and staged releases for reliability.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository is active with multiple named releases (v3.x line), security advisories, and community interest (2k stars) but is under one year old (289 days) so it lacks the long track record required for TRL 7+; README also marks the project as 'experimental' with known verification gaps.
prerequisites: familiarity with command-line tooling and sandboxing
basic knowledge of testing and code verification workflows
student_project_ideas: Build a CI-style lab that uses ATLAS to automatically generate and verify unit tests for a small C/Python codebase, measuring repair success rates and comparing results across two different local GGUF models.

Integrate ATLAS into a software engineering assignment pipeline so students submit tasks and ATLAS proposes edits and runs sandboxed tests; evaluate human review effort and common failure modes and suggest improvements.

tools.name: fikrikarim/parlor
tools.desc: On-device, real-time multimodal AI with features similar to GPT-Live

cls.summary: Parlor is an open-source on-device, real-time multimodal voice AI that runs a local LLM (Gemma via llama.cpp) with streaming audio/video input, VAD-based turn-taking, and TTS for conversational voice assistants.
cls.what_it_does: Parlor packages a real-time browser client and Python FastAPI server to run a fully local multimodal conversational assistant: microphone + camera frames stream to a local LLM (Gemma via llama.cpp) which produces streamed transcripts and sentence-by-sentence TTS; optional background web research can use an external API. It is notable for being designed to run entirely on Apple Silicon or Linux GPUs, supporting hands-free turn-taking, barge-in, separate action JSON heads, and low-latency streaming.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository is 226 days old (younger than 1 year) so TRL is capped below 7. However it shows strong community interest (2k+ stars), an install/run workflow, explicit runtime requirements, and the author reports hundreds of monthly users — evidence of a beta-level, actively used project.
prerequisites: macOS Apple Silicon or Linux with a supported GPU
~6 GB free RAM for default model
student_project_ideas: Extend Parlor to capture structured user intents for an industrial voice-control demo: integrate a simple MQTT broker to send parsed JSON actions to a Raspberry Pi-based actuator and evaluate latency and reliability.

Benchmark different local LLM backends and quantization settings by swapping models (e2b vs e4b), measuring end-to-end latency and memory usage, and produce a report comparing perceived audio quality and responsiveness.

tools.name: ROBOTIS-GIT/turtlebot3
tools.desc: ROS packages for Turtlebot3

cls.summary: TurtleBot3 is an open-source ROS-based mobile robot platform with packages for running on hardware and in simulators (Gazebo) used for development, teaching and research in robotics.
cls.what_it_does: TurtleBot3 provides ROS packages, device drivers and simulation assets to operate a small differential-drive robot (hardware) and run the same stacks in Gazebo for development and testing. It solves the problem of a standard, reproducible robotics platform for learning navigation, SLAM, teleoperation and manipulation and is notable for its integration with ROS, Dynamixel actuators and official simulation/SDK resources.
cls.trl_rationale: The repository is long-established (created 2016) with many stars, forks, ongoing commits and wide community adoption; the TurtleBot family is a de-facto reference platform used in teaching and research, indicating a mature, widely adopted project.
prerequisites: basic ROS (ROS 1 or ROS 2 depending on branch) knowledge
Gazebo simulation familiarity for simulation use; basic electronics for hardware
student_project_ideas: Implement a ROS-based autonomous navigation stack that performs SLAM and path planning on TurtleBot3 in Gazebo, then validate performance on hardware using ROS bag playback and real sensors.
Integrate a lightweight perception module (e.g. depth camera + YOLO) on TurtleBot3 to perform semantic mapping and test obstacle avoidance strategies in simulation and on the robot.

tools.name: ad-si/awesome-3d-printing
tools.desc: A curated list of awesome 3D printing resources

cls.summary: A long-lived curated list of links and resources for 3D printing, covering printers, CAD tools, slicers, firmware, filaments and related services.
cls.what_it_does: This repository collects and categorises useful links, projects and tools related to 3D printing so users can discover printers, CAD software, slicers, firmware, scanners and materials. It is used as a reference index (README links out to projects and commercial sites) and is notable for its breadth, long history and large community interest.
cls.trl_rationale: The repository is long-lived (created 2016), actively maintained and widely starred, showing steady community use as a reference; as a curated index it is mature and production-use as a resource, so TRL 7 is appropriate.
student_project_ideas: Select and document a 3D-printing workflow from the list (CAD -> slicer -> printer) and produce a reproducible guide plus test prints comparing two slicers.
Create a curated subset of resources and an annotated reading list for a course module on additive manufacturing technologies, including recommended tools and example designs.

tools.name: cosmo-wander-ai/cosmo-edge
tools.desc: Production-grade C++ edge AI engine for video analytics and on-device VLM across Sophon, Rockchip RKNN, and x86, with visual orchestration, real-time OSD, events, and reproducible benchmarks.

cls.summary: CosmoEdge is a production-grade C++ engine and console for deploying video analytics and on-device visual-language model (VLM) workflows on Sophon, Rockchip and x86 platforms.
cls.what_it_does: CosmoEdge turns AI models for video and VLM into deployable edge applications with a runtime, visual orchestration console, real-time on-screen display (OSD), alarm/event handling and reproducible benchmarks. It is used by building or installing platform-specific packages (BM1688/CV186X, RKNN targets, or x86 Docker) and configuring visual pipelines, models and alarm rules. Notable points are its multi-target device packaging and validation artifacts, console for visual workflow orchestration, and focus on on-device VLM and event delivery.
cls.trl_rationale: The project publishes a stable v1.2.0 release, has extensive documentation, platform-specific packages and validation reports, and a large community interest (2k+ stars), indicating beta-level maturity. The repository is 161 days old (younger than one year), so while it shows solid release engineering and device packages it lacks the multi-year track record required for TRL 7+.
prerequisites: Docker for host builds or cross-compilation toolchains for target devices
Target SDKs/runtimes (BMRT for Sophon, RKNN/RKLLM for Rockchip) and ONNX runtime knowledge
Familiarity with video protocols (ONVIF/GB28181) and model packaging
student_project_ideas: Build a small edge video analytics demonstrator that runs a YOLO-based detector in CosmoEdge on x86 Docker, adds a simple alarm rule, and feeds event metadata to an MQTT broker for a dashboard.

Evaluate on-device VLM performance by converting a pretrained VLM to the target ONNX/RKNN format, deploying it with CosmoEdge on an RK3576 board, and measuring latency/accuracy trade-offs across model variants using the repository's benchmark tools.

tools.name: wzyn20051216/solidworks-automation-skill
tools.desc: Reliable AI Skill + MCP toolkit for agent-driven desktop CAD automation.

cls.summary: A toolkit that lets LLM agents drive SolidWorks and other CAD software via a verified, auditable execution layer for reliable desktop CAD automation.
cls.what_it_does: The project provides an AI Skill + MCP toolkit that connects agent clients (Codex, Claude, Cursor, etc.) to desktop CAD software (primarily SolidWorks) using COM and backends, executes modelling tasks, and performs result verification and traceability. It is used by installing the skill/MCP or the CAD Studio desktop, then agents call the skill to perform CAD operations while the Execution Core manages capability routing, verification-first completion and recovery.
cls.trl_rationale: The repository is active, has many stars (2k+), named releases (v2.1.1) and detailed docs and examples, indicating beta-level maturity; however it is under 1 year old so lacks the long track record required for TRL 7+, which constrains the rating to TRL 6.
prerequisites: Windows 10/11 x64 for native SolidWorks COM automation
Local SolidWorks installation with valid license for native modelling
student_project_ideas: Build an agent workflow that generates a parametric bracket in SolidWorks from a text specification, exports drawings/PDFs and implements automated dimension verification using the toolkit's verification traces.
Integrate the Skill with a CI pipeline to auto-generate and validate variants of a part (different parameters) and produce a report of which parameter sets pass the verification rules.

tools.name: SubnauticaNitrox/Nitrox
tools.desc: An open-source, multiplayer modification for the game Subnautica.

cls.summary: Nitrox is an open-source modification that adds multiplayer support to the PC game Subnautica.
cls.what_it_does: Nitrox enables multiplayer gameplay in Subnautica by adding client/server communication, player and vehicle syncing, chat, base and furniture syncing, and other multiplayer features. It is distributed as a community mod for the Unity-based game and integrates with common modding libraries so players can host or join multiplayer servers. The project is community-driven, GPL-licensed, and targets players and modders rather than engineering workflows.
cls.trl_rationale: The repository is long-lived (created 2017) with many stars, forks and recent activity indicating an active community, but the README describes the mod as still in early development and the project remains a community mod rather than a proven production platform, so Beta (TRL 6) is appropriate.
prerequisites: basic familiarity with installing game mods and Unity/C# for development

tools.name: ITI/ICS-Security-Tools
tools.desc: Tools, tips, tricks, and more for exploring ICS Security.

cls.summary: A long-standing community-curated collection of tools, scripts, pcaps and guides for industrial control systems (ICS) and SCADA security.
cls.what_it_does: This repository aggregates links, scripts, testbeds, protocol details, captures and vendor/hardware information useful when exploring cyber-security for ICS/SCADA environments. Lecturers and practitioners use it as a discovery catalogue to find analysis tools, simulation/testbed resources and example traffic for hands‑on security, forensics and protocol study. Its value is that it centralises many community-maintained resources rather than providing a single executable tool.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository created in 2015 and actively maintained with many stars and forks, indicating sustained community use; it is a mature curated resource rather than a single deployable product, so TRL 7 (production-ready resource) is appropriate.
prerequisites: basic networking and Linux command-line skills
familiarity with industrial control systems and common ICS protocols (Modbus, DNP3, IEC60870 etc.)
student_project_ideas: Create a lab exercise where students use provided PCAPs and open-source analysis tools from the list to identify and characterise simulated ICS attacks and produce an incident report.

Assemble a small testbed from the repository's testbed/hardware guides and use listed simulation tools to evaluate how a specific industrial protocol (e.g. Modbus) behaves under malformed traffic, documenting mitigation strategies.

tools.name: gkjohnson/three-gpu-pathtracer
tools.desc: Path tracing renderer and utilities for three.js built on top of three-mesh-bvh.

cls.summary: A WebGPU-based GPU path tracer built on three.js and three-mesh-bvh that renders physically based scenes in the browser.
cls.what_it_does: This library implements a GPU path tracer using WebGPU compute shaders and three-mesh-bvh acceleration to produce high-quality, physically based renders of three.js scenes in the browser. It is used by adding the WebGPUPathTracer to a three.js WebGPU renderer, setting the scene and camera, and calling renderSample each frame; the project includes examples, tools (environment blurring, denoising, animation rendering) and documentation. It is notable for integrating with three-mesh-bvh for fast ray traversal and for providing WebGPU examples and utilities for web-based path tracing.
cls.trl_rationale: The repository is multi-year (created 2021), has many stars (2k+), active maintenance and extensive examples/docs and demo pages, indicating production-ready code for web demos; it is not a de-facto industry standard renderer, so TRL 7 is appropriate.
prerequisites: WebGPU-enabled browser and basic GPU knowledge
student_project_ideas: Compare convergence and visual quality between the three-gpu-pathtracer and a rasterized three.js renderer for a furnished room scene, measuring render time and image error with increasing sample counts.

Integrate a simple physics-based material dataset (glTF models with varied PBR materials) and implement an automated renderer pipeline that produces denoised reference images for use in a computer vision training dataset.

tools.name: microsoft/maker.js
tools.desc: 📐⚙ 2D vector line drawing and shape modeling for CNC and laser cutters.

tools.name: axoviq-ai/synthadoc
tools.desc: Synthadoc: An open-source LLM knowledge compilation engine that turns raw documents into structured, local-first wikis. A transparent, human-readable alternative to traditional RAG, which can be self-managed and self-improved without the use of any tools.

cls.summary: Synthadoc is an open-source Python tool that ingests diverse documents and compiles them into a local, structured Markdown wiki backed by semantic search and an LLM-powered maintenance workflow.
cls.what_it_does: Synthadoc reads raw documents (PDFs, PPTs, spreadsheets, web pages, images, video transcripts, etc.) and synthesises them into a persistent, cross‑referenced Markdown wiki where answers cite sources and contradictions are flagged. It runs as a CLI and provides an Obsidian plugin and a web UI, enabling local-first knowledge bases that can be self-maintained and integrated into organisational workflows.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository is active and fairly mature (release v1.5.2, 2k+ stars, recent commits) but is only ~220 days old so it lacks the long track record and broad production citations needed for TRL 7+. README and docs show multiple interfaces and enterprise features, supporting a Beta (TRL 6) judgement.
prerequisites: experience running local LLMs or cloud LLM APIs
knowledge of Markdown/Obsidian for best integration
student_project_ideas: Build a course-specific Synthadoc wiki that ingests lecture slides, lab instructions and research papers, then evaluate retrieval accuracy and citation quality against a baseline RAG pipeline (e.g. LlamaIndex + vector DB).

Integrate Synthadoc with Obsidian and a git backend to create an auditable documentation pipeline for a student robotics project, then measure how automated cross-referencing and contradiction detection help team knowledge sharing.

tools.name: ranuts/document
tools.desc: Local-first browser editor for Word, Excel, PowerPoint and PDF, with an experimental AI assistant. No Office installation or account required.

cls.summary: A local-first, browser-based editor that opens, edits and exports Word, Excel, PowerPoint and PDF files with an optional experimental AI assistant and agent API.
cls.what_it_does: This project provides a full document workspace running in the browser (PWA) that can edit .docx, .xlsx, .pptx and annotate PDFs without requiring Office or an account; core processing runs client-side and can be self-hosted. It includes an experimental AI assistant and support for WebMCP-compatible browser agents to let automated agents open, convert and export files. Notable points are local-first operation (offline cached assets), a demo deployment, Docker image for self-hosting, and explicit integration points for embedding via iframe and agent tools.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository is >1 year old with many stars (2k+), an online demo, Docker image and active recent commits which indicate a Beta-level project used by others, but it lacks explicit formal releases or wide enterprise adoption evidence required for TRL 7+.
student_project_ideas: Create a lab exercise that uses the editor's iframe API to embed the document editor in a web dashboard and automate generation of engineering reports from a CSV timeseries (e.g. sensor data) using the experimental AI assistant.
Extend or prototype a WebMCP agent that scans a set of PDF requirements documents and extracts and pins candidate requirements into a simple traceability table (CSV or spreadsheet).

tools.name: mikbry/awesome-webgpu
tools.desc: 😎 Curated list of awesome things around WebGPU ecosystem.

cls.summary: A curated, community-maintained list of WebGPU resources, libraries, tutorials and demos for building GPU-accelerated graphics and compute apps in the browser.
cls.what_it_does: This repository collects links to specifications, tutorials, libraries, debuggers, demos and articles around the WebGPU ecosystem to help developers learn and adopt the WebGPU API. It is used as a discovery hub (reading material and examples) rather than a code library, notable for its breadth, longevity and large community attention.
cls.trl_rationale: The list is long-lived (created 2020), has many stars, and has been actively updated (last push 2026), indicating stable, widely used documentation/resource status rather than an experimental note; it is a curated index rather than production software.
prerequisites: a WebGPU-capable browser or experimental build
student_project_ideas: Create a browser-based real-time sensor-data visualiser that uses a WebGPU library from the list to render time-series or point-cloud data and compare performance against a WebGL implementation.
Port a small WebGL shader demo (e.g. a glTF viewer or particle system) to WebGPU using an example/tutorial from the list, profile GPU/CPU behaviour and document implementation differences.

tools.name: CoderGamester/mcp-unity
tools.desc: Model Context Protocol (MCP) plugin to connect with Unity Editor — designed for Cursor, Claude Code, Codex, Windsurf and other IDEs

cls.summary: An open-source Unity Editor plugin that implements the Model Context Protocol (MCP) so AI assistants and IDEs can query and manipulate Unity projects and scenes programmatically.
cls.what_it_does: MCP Unity provides a bridge between the Unity Editor and external AI agents/IDEs via a Node.js MCP server, exposing commands to inspect and modify scenes, GameObjects, components, packages and run tests. It is used as a Unity package/plugin installed into a project and notable for enabling AI coding assistants to perform editor actions (select/update GameObjects, create prefabs/scenes, run tests) and for adding Unity's package cache to IDE workspaces to improve code intelligence.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository is >1 year old, has ~2k stars and active recent commits and issues, and documents many usable features and integrations; this indicates production-ready tooling rather than an experimental prototype.
prerequisites: Familiarity with Unity Editor and C#
Node.js to run an MCP server
Basic knowledge of IDEs (VS Code-like) and package installation in Unity
student_project_ideas: Use MCP Unity plus a Node.js MCP server to build an AI assistant that can automatically add a prefab to a scene, configure its components (e.g. Rigidbody), and run EditMode tests to verify behaviour.

Integrate MCP Unity with VS Code and an LLM (e.g. Claude Code or Codex) to create a tool that suggests and applies refactorings across multiple Unity scripts and then runs the Unity Test Runner to validate changes.

tools.name: Sandflow-ai/sand3d
tools.desc: 3D modeling in Python, built for LLMs.

cls.summary: sand3d is a Python code-first CAD library that expresses 3D parts, assemblies and joints as short, deterministic programs and exports to formats like GLB, URDF, USD and IFC.
cls.what_it_does: It lets you write 3D objects as small Python programs (profiles, solids, edits, frames, joints and assemblies) that build deterministic meshes and articulations over Blender's bpy. It is designed to be compact enough for LLM prompting, includes exports to common interchange formats (GLB, URDF, USD, IFC, OBJ, STL) and is notable for part-naming, program-first assembly structure, and explicit joint descriptions.
cls.trl_rationale: The repo is very new (created 14 days ago) so despite good documentation, examples and high star count it lacks a long track record; evidence (install instructions, examples, datasets and exports) supports alpha-in-use level but age limits maturity to TRL 5.
prerequisites: familiarity with Blender or 3D file formats is helpful
student_project_ideas: Create a parametric robotic gripper in sand3d, export URDF and integrate it into a ROS/PyBullet simulation to evaluate workspace and collisions.
Write a small parts library in sand3d for a mechanical assembly (e.g. hinge and latch set), export to USD and GLB, and build a web viewer demo showing articulated joints and named parts.

tools.name: ButzYung/SystemAnimatorOnline
tools.desc: XR Animator, AI-based Full Body Motion Capture and Extended Reality (XR) solution, powered by System Animator Online

cls.summary: XR Animator is a webcam-based, browser and desktop app that uses MediaPipe/TensorFlow.js to perform real-time full-body and face motion capture and drive 3D avatars (VRM/MMD) for XR/VTubing and AR use-cases.
cls.what_it_does: XR Animator captures 2D/3D pose and facial blendshapes from a single webcam using MediaPipe and TensorFlow.js, then maps those motions to 3D avatar formats (VRM/MMD) in real time in the browser or an Electron desktop app. It supports recording and exporting motion (VMD/BVH/glTF/FBX), AR via WebXR/ARCore on mobile, and integrations like VMC protocol for other VMC-enabled applications. Notable points are single-camera full-body tracking, browser and native Electron builds, and support for common avatar/motion formats.
cls.trl_rationale: The repository is long-lived (created 2019), has a large star count (~2000), active recent commits and published releases (Electron app), and working web demos — evidence of production-ready software used by many. The README documents releases and real-world usage (web app, desktop app), supporting a TRL of 7; the missing explicit OSS license in metadata is noted but does not reduce demonstrated maturity.
prerequisites: Node.js / Electron familiarity for desktop builds
understanding of 3D model formats (VRM/MMD/FBX) and webcam APIs
student_project_ideas: Build a lab assignment where students integrate XR Animator's pose outputs with a simple physics simulation (three.js) to control a virtual robot avatar and log latency/accuracy differences between face-only and full-body tracking.

Create a capstone project that records motion via XR Animator, converts/export motion to BVH/FBX and uses the exported data to validate a gait-analysis pipeline comparing key joint trajectories against a reference dataset.

tools.name: Unity-Technologies/com.unity.multiplayer.samples.coop
tools.desc: A small-scale cooperative game sample built on the new, Unity networking framework to teach developers about creating a similar multiplayer game.

cls.summary: Boss Room is an official Unity sample project that demonstrates how to build a small cooperative multiplayer RPG using Unity Netcode for GameObjects and related Unity services.
cls.what_it_does: Boss Room provides a complete example multiplayer game demonstrating common netcode patterns (replicated objects, RPCs, latency-masking animations, session management and authentication) and ships a reusable Utilities package that developers can import into their own Unity projects. It is used as a learning reference and starting point for implementing multiplayer features in Unity games and interactive simulations.
cls.trl_rationale: The repository is maintained by Unity Technologies, has many stars and forks, regular updates and release assets, and is used as an official learning sample—evidence of production-quality maturity rather than an experimental prototype.
student_project_ideas: Extend Boss Room to add a new networked player ability and implement latency compensation and automated tests to compare perceived responsiveness versus a baseline.

Integrate Boss Room with an external analytics pipeline (e.g., send gameplay telemetry to a time-series backend) and build a dashboard that visualises network performance and player behaviour during sessions.

tools.name: AtomicBot-ai/Atomic-Chat
tools.desc: Local AI app and inference engine for agents. Run open-weight LLMs locally — private, 100% offline on your computer. Join our Discord: https://discord.com/invite/8wGSsvmg4V

cls.summary: Atomic Chat is a local, OpenAI-compatible desktop app and inference engine that runs open-weight LLMs on your machine and exposes a local API.
cls.what_it_does: Atomic Chat lets you load and run GGUF and other open-weight LLMs locally (on CPU, Metal, CUDA, Vulkan, and Apple Silicon) and provides an OpenAI-compatible HTTP API at http://localhost:1337/v1 so other tools and agents can use the models. It bundles multiple inference engines, performance optimisations (speculative decoding, TurboQuant, DFlash, Flash Attention toggles) and integrations with cloud providers, MCP tools and agent launchers, making it notable as an opinionated, privacy-focused local LLM runtime and desktop app.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository is active with many stars, desktop packages and multiple engine integrations, indicating a usable beta-level product; however it is younger than one year (created 2026-03-31) so it cannot be judged above TRL 6 without longer production track record.
prerequisites: familiarity with LLM models and quantised formats (GGUF)
basic command-line and local server usage
student_project_ideas: Build a private code-assistant that runs on-campus documentation and model weights using Atomic Chat's local API and integrates with an IDE plugin to answer engineering-specific queries.

Create a lab exercise where students deploy a small local agent via Atomic Chat that monitors simulated sensor data (e.g. MQTT stream) and issues control recommendations, demonstrating local inference and privacy-preserving workflows.

tools.name: mil-tokyo/webdnn
tools.desc: The Fastest DNN Running Framework on Web Browser

cls.summary: WebDNN runs pre-trained ONNX neural network models directly in web browsers using WebGPU, WebGL or WebAssembly to accelerate inference.
cls.what_it_does: WebDNN loads ONNX models into the browser and executes inference using accelerated backends (WebGPU, WebGL, or WebAssembly). It is used as a client-side inference runtime and includes tooling for offline model optimisation and generating operator bundles; notable features are its WGSL-based WebGPU backend and support for loading unoptimized ONNX models directly in the browser.
cls.trl_rationale: The repository is mature (created 2017), has a substantial user base (2k stars), active recent commits (2026) and documented build/test flows, indicating production-ready software; however it is not a de-facto standard like TensorFlow.js or ONNX Runtime Web, so TRL 7 is appropriate.
student_project_ideas: Build a browser-based demo that loads a small ONNX vision model with WebDNN to perform real-time image classification in the browser and visualise predictions on a 3D scene (three.js).

Compare inference latency and memory usage of an ONNX model across WebGPU, WebGL and WebAssembly backends using automated benchmark scripts and report implications for deploying ML in edge/IoT web dashboards.

tools.name: tpaviot/pythonocc-core
tools.desc: Python package for 3D geometry CAD/BIM/CAM

tools.name: protectwise/troika
tools.desc: A JavaScript framework for interactive 3D and 2D visualizations

cls.summary: Troika JS is a JavaScript collection for building high-performance interactive 2D/3D visualisations in the browser, with tight integration with Three.js and WebGL/WebXR.
cls.what_it_does: Troika provides a framework and standalone tools that simplify creating and managing interactive WebGL/Three.js scenes for data visualisation and UI elements. It is used in web projects to render performant text, layout, meshes and scene management, and includes utilities that integrate with Three.js and WebXR to produce rich browser visualisations.
cls.trl_rationale: The repository is long-lived (created 2019), has substantial community interest (nearly 2k stars), recent commits (2026) and documentation; this demonstrates maturity and real-world usage though it's not an industry standard.
student_project_ideas: Build an interactive web dashboard that visualises live IoT sensor time-series in 3D using Troika and a MQTT/HTTP backend to demonstrate real-time visualisation of operational data.
Create a browser-based viewer that imports simplified CAD or glTF models and overlays telemetry/annotation layers (digital-twin style) using Three.js with Troika for rich text and UI elements.

tools.name: c2g-dev/city2graph
tools.desc: Transform geospatial relations into graphs for Graph Neural Networks and spatial network analysis

cls.summary: City2Graph converts urban geospatial data (buildings, streets, transport feeds, OD matrices, POIs) into spatial and heterogeneous graphs suitable for network analysis and Graph Neural Networks.
cls.what_it_does: City2Graph ingests common geospatial sources (OpenStreetMap, GTFS, GBFS, GeoDataFrames) and builds proximity, contiguity, transport and heterogeneous graphs that can be analysed with NetworkX or trained with PyTorch Geometric. It is used as a bridge between geospatial data formats and GNN-ready tensors, notable for built-in support for transport feeds, metapath composition, and round-trip conversion between GeoDataFrame / NetworkX / PyG formats.
cls.trl_rationale: The project is actively maintained, distributed via pip and conda-forge, has comprehensive docs and tutorials, nearly 2k stars and recent activity, and a peer-reviewed paper describing it — evidence of use beyond a demo, supporting a production-ready TRL 7.
prerequisites: familiarity with geospatial data (OSM, GTFS, GeoDataFrame)
student_project_ideas: Build a GNN to predict bike-sharing station demand by converting GBFS feeds and surrounding POIs into a heterogeneous graph with City2Graph and training a PyTorch Geometric model.

Compare urban accessibility metrics by generating street and building graphs from OpenStreetMap for two neighbourhoods and using graph centrality and simulated OD flows to assess walkability and service coverage.

tools.name: rlguy/Blender-FLIP-Fluids
tools.desc: The FLIP Fluids addon is a tool that helps you set up, run, and render high quality liquid fluid effects all within Blender, the free and open source 3D creation suite.

cls.summary: FLIP Fluids is a Blender addon and standalone fluid simulation engine that produces high-quality liquid effects using the FLIP particle-grid method, integrated into Blender for setup, simulation and rendering.
cls.what_it_does: The project provides a FLIP-based fluid solver and Blender addon to set up, run and export realistic liquid simulations directly inside Blender; it exports caches (Alembic) for rendering and post-processing. It is notable for a production-focused, tightly integrated workflow with a custom C++ simulation engine and a paid full-featured addon plus a free demo repository version.
cls.trl_rationale: The project has been developed since 2016/2017, the repository is long-lived and actively maintained with many stars and commercial users (marketplace sales and support), indicating production-ready maturity rather than a prototype.
prerequisites: Familiarity with Blender and its addon system
Experience building C/C++ projects with CMake (if compiling from source)
student_project_ideas: Compare accuracy and performance of FLIP Fluids vs. Mantaflow for a sloshing-tank benchmark by running equivalent scenarios in Blender, exporting results and analysing free-surface height and runtime.

Create an engineering visualisation: simulate a dam-break in FLIP Fluids, export Alembic caches and build a rendered animation that demonstrates energy transfer and flow features for a civil hydraulics lab.

tools.name: arimger/Unity-Editor-Toolbox
tools.desc: Tools, custom attributes, drawers, hierarchy overlay, and other extensions for the Unity Editor.

cls.summary: A collection of Unity Editor extensions (attributes, custom drawers, hierarchy and project overlays) that improve the Unity Editor workflow and inspector UI.
cls.what_it_does: This package provides custom PropertyAttributes, property drawers, editor utilities and UI overlays to make Unity inspectors, hierarchy and project windows more usable and informative. It is installed into a Unity project (via UPM, git URL or copying Assets) and extends the Editor IMGUI workflow to present richer editors, icons, scene overlays and helper utilities for authoring GameObjects and assets.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository created in 2019 with ~2k stars, active maintenance (recent pushes) and documented installation via UPM/OpenUPM; shows a sustained user interest and production-ready editor tooling rather than an experimental prototype.
prerequisites: C# scripting and Unity Editor extension basics
student_project_ideas: Create a Unity scene for a cyber-physical digital twin where you add custom inspector attributes from the Toolbox to display sensor ranges and runtime status, then build a small dashboard that reads those inspector fields.

Implement a tooling exercise where students add hierarchy overlays and custom asset icons to an existing Unity project to improve authoring and navigation of a multi-team scene (combine with version control or scene management).

tools.name: gfxfundamentals/webgl2-fundamentals
tools.desc: WebGL 2 lessons starting from the basics

cls.summary: A mature, open-source set of step-by-step lessons that teach WebGL2, 2D/3D math and shader programming for building interactive web graphics.
cls.what_it_does: Provides a structured series of tutorials and example code that explain WebGL2 concepts (buffers, shaders, transformations, textures, render targets) and the underlying 2D/3D math. Instructors and students use the site and repository examples in a browser to learn how to write low-level WebGL applications rather than rely on higher-level engines. It's notable for being long-standing, thorough, and focussed on correct modern WebGL2 practice rather than legacy OpenGL idioms.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository is long-lived (created 2016), actively maintained with frequent pushes, many stars and forks, and is a de-facto standard learning resource for WebGL2; this indicates a mature, widely adopted educational project.
prerequisites: familiarity with GLSL shaders is helpful
student_project_ideas: Build an interactive web-based visualiser for a robot arm using WebGL2 examples from the lessons to display joint transforms and animate trajectories.
Create a browser-based CFD/flow-field visualisation mock-up that reads simple CSV/vector fields and renders them as textured particles or lines using WebGL2 shaders from the tutorials.

tools.name: georust/geo
tools.desc: Rust geospatial primitives & algorithms

tools.name: DanKE123abc/NoUnityCN
tools.desc: 🔥✅ Unity国际版下载站，可通过直链或者Unity Hub下载例如Unity 6等Unity Editor的国际版，支持添加组件、下载国际版Unity Hub、包含长期支持版、技术支持版、测试版、预览版的Unity。

cls.summary: NoUnityCN is an open-source website that indexes and provides download links for international builds of the Unity Editor and related components.
cls.what_it_does: NoUnityCN queries official Unity interfaces to list Unity Editor releases (including long-term support, tech, preview and other channels) and offers direct-download links or instructions for use with Unity Hub. It is delivered as a web application (Next.js / vinext) that can be deployed to Vercel or Cloudflare Workers and is notable for providing an alternate, Chinese-language index of Unity international releases.
cls.trl_rationale: The repository is over three years old, has a large star count (≈2k), active maintenance (recent pushes) and clear deployment docs for Next.js and Cloudflare Workers, indicating production-ready maturity rather than an experimental prototype.
prerequisites: basic familiarity with Next.js or Cloudflare Workers for deployment

tools.name: Farama-Foundation/Gymnasium-Robotics
tools.desc: A collection of robotics simulation environments for reinforcement learning

cls.summary: Gymnasium-Robotics is a collection of MuJoCo-based robotic simulation environments that implement the Gymnasium API for reinforcement learning and multi-goal tasks.
cls.what_it_does: The project provides a set of robot manipulation and locomotion environments (Fetch, Shadow Dexterous Hand, Franka Kitchen, MaMuJoCo, D4RL mazes and Adroit) that run on the MuJoCo physics engine and expose a GoalEnv multi-goal API useful for HER and RL algorithms. It is used by importing the package into Python, registering the environments with Gymnasium, and running training or evaluation loops; notable points are its multi-goal API, support for MuJoCo bindings, and integration with D4RL and Minari datasets.
cls.trl_rationale: The repository is multi-year (created 2021), actively maintained with many stars, documented website, examples and community (Discord), and integrates with established projects (Gymnasium, D4RL, Minari), indicating a mature and widely adopted codebase rather than an experimental prototype.
prerequisites: familiarity with Gymnasium/OpenAI Gym APIs and reinforcement learning concepts
MuJoCo physics engine and its Python bindings installed
student_project_ideas: Train and compare a reinforcement learning agent (e.g. SAC vs PPO) on the FetchPickAndPlace environment, evaluate sample efficiency using D4RL offline datasets and visualise learned policies.
Integrate a Shadow Dexterous Hand environment with a perception module (camera input using a simple CNN) to implement and test sim-to-sim transfer and evaluate grasp success rates under sensor noise.

tools.name: wy-luke/All-Chinese-Character-Set
tools.desc: 致力于维护一个包含全部中文字符（汉字+符号）的字符集，包罗万象，含3500 / 7000 常用汉字集、常用符号集。A Charater Set contains all Chinese charaters.

cls.summary: A curated collection of Chinese characters and symbols (including 3500/7000 common sets and full character lists) provided as plain text files for use in fonts and text rendering.
cls.what_it_does: Provides plain-text lists of Chinese characters, common symbol sets, and combined files (3500/7000 common characters plus symbols, and a full set) so developers can build or subset fonts and support Chinese text rendering (notably for Unity TextMeshPro). It is used by downloading the text files and using them to generate or subset fonts or feed text-rendering tools. It is notable for being a comprehensive, community-maintained large character collection with high popularity (many stars) and direct examples for TextMeshPro.
cls.trl_rationale: The repository is mature (created 2021, actively maintained with recent pushes and ~1.9k stars) and provides stable data files used by others (TextMeshPro guidance), indicating production-ready utility rather than an experimental prototype.
student_project_ideas: Create a Unity UI localization demo that loads a subset font generated from the repository's 3500+symbols.txt and demonstrates correct rendering of mixed Chinese/English text using TextMeshPro.
Build a small font-subsetting tool (Python or Node) that reads the all+symbols.txt list and produces reduced OTF/TTF files using fonttools, then measure file-size and rendering performance on mobile.

tools.name: MothCocoon/FlowGraph
tools.desc: Design-agnostic node system for scripting game’s flow in Unreal Engine

cls.summary: FlowGraph is an open-source Unreal Engine plugin that provides a node-based editor for scripting game event flow and narrative logic.
cls.what_it_does: FlowGraph supplies a design-agnostic graph editor where each node is a UObject encapsulating asynchronous/latent gameplay logic and data; developers implement reusable Flow Nodes to represent features, events and narrative elements. It is used as an Unreal Editor plugin to author game flow (quests, cinematic sequences, event scripts) and includes editor debugging displays and documentation.
cls.trl_rationale: Established repository (created 2021) with high star count (~2k), maintained active pushes in 2026, published docs and a recorded presentation — evidence of a stable, production-ready plugin though not a de-facto standard.
prerequisites: Basic understanding of node/graph editors and game architecture
student_project_ideas: Create a short Unreal game level that uses FlowGraph to implement a quest chain and compare development speed and maintainability with the same logic implemented in Blueprints.
Integrate FlowGraph with a simple AI dialogue system (e.g., external chatbot or local dialog manager) so nodes trigger dynamic NPC conversations and evaluate debugging/visualisation benefits.

tools.name: tuya/TuyaOpen
tools.desc: Next-gen AI+IoT framework for T2/T3/T5AI/ESP32/and more – Fast IoT and AI Agent hardware integration

cls.summary: TuyaOpen is an open-source C/C++ SDK and framework for building AI-enabled IoT devices that integrates edge hardware (ESP32, Tuya T-series, Pi, etc.) with cloud AI/LLM services and Tuya Cloud features like OTA and device management.
cls.what_it_does: TuyaOpen provides cross-platform libraries, examples and hardware support to connect embedded devices to Tuya Cloud and to integrate speech, vision and LLM-based AI capabilities (ASR, TTS, KWS, multimodal agents). It is used by compiling the C/C++ SDK for target MCUs or Linux hosts and pairing devices with cloud AI backends and third-party models. It is notable for broad hardware coverage (Tuya T2/T3/T5, ESP32, many Wi‑Fi/BT MCUs), built-in OTA/auth/security features and explicit integrations with major LLM providers.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository is multi-year (created 2023-12-25, active pushes as of 2026), has many stars and documented platform support, formal developer guide and example hardware targets, indicating production-ready SDK status; evidence comes from broad hardware lists, docs and active maintenance rather than independent large-scale deployments.
prerequisites: familiarity with ESP32/MCU toolchains (e.g. ESP-IDF) and serial debugging
basic knowledge of cloud IoT concepts and device provisioning
student_project_ideas: Build a voice-controlled prototype using an ESP32 and TuyaOpen that performs keyword spotting locally and calls a cloud LLM for dialogue, demonstrating end-to-end device-to-cloud communication and OTA updates.
Integrate a camera module with TuyaOpen on a Raspberry Pi to perform basic vision-triggered notifications (edge inference or cloud LLM captioning) and log telemetry to Tuya Cloud for dashboarding.

tools.name: Besty0728/Unity-Skills
tools.desc: AI automation skills specifically designed for Unity

cls.summary: UnitySkills is an open-source REST API server that lets AI agents invoke high-level 'skills' to automate and modify Unity Editor scenes, prefabs and project files with governance, auditing and rollback features.
cls.what_it_does: UnitySkills provides a REST-based engine of reusable 'skills' that allow AI systems to control the Unity Editor (create/modify scenes, prefabs, assets) and supports batch transactions, dry-run/plan modes, audit logs and rollback. It is used by running the server alongside a Unity project (Unity 2022.3+ recommended) and calling skill endpoints from LLM-based IDE integrations or other automation. Notable features include three-tier permission modes, per-skill risk metadata, transactional batch operations and multi-instance control.
cls.trl_rationale: The repository is active, well-documented, has many stars and recent commits suggesting community interest and a usable beta, but it was created 303 days ago (under one year) so it lacks the longer track record and stable releases usually needed for TRL 7+.
prerequisites: HTTP/REST familiarity and basic server setup
student_project_ideas: Build an automated scene-assembly pipeline where a trained LLM selects and composes prefabs via UnitySkills REST calls to generate parameterised test scenes, then run PlayMode tests to verify expected behaviours.

Create a permissions and audit study that compares manual Unity edits vs AI-driven edits by instrumenting UnitySkills' audit logs and rollback features to evaluate safety, error rates and recovery time for automated edits.

tools.name: qcad/qcad
tools.desc: QCAD - The Open Source 2D CAD. QCAD is a cross-platform CAD solution for Windows, macOS and Linux. It supports the DXF format and optionally the DWG format (through a proprietary plugin).

tools.name: pioneerspacesim/pioneer
tools.desc: A game of lonely space adventure

tools.name: geotools/geotools
tools.desc: Official GeoTools repository

tools.name: koide3/glim
tools.desc: GLIM: versatile and extensible point cloud-based 3D localization and mapping framework

cls.summary: GLIM is an open-source, GPU-accelerated 3D LiDAR/RGB-D point-cloud localization and mapping (SLAM) framework focused on accurate multi-scan registration using factor graphs.
cls.what_it_does: GLIM performs range-based 3D mapping and localization by minimizing multi-scan registration errors on factor graphs, supporting GPU acceleration for speed and quality. It is usable with a variety of range sensors (spinning LiDAR, solid-state LiDAR, non-repetitive scan LiDAR, RGB-D) and integrates with ROS/ROS2 and GTSAM; it also provides an interactive map correction interface and extension hooks for custom constraints.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository is multi-year (created 2021), has many stars and forks, active maintenance with recent releases (v1.2.2) and published peer-reviewed paper describing the method; these indicate production-ready open-source software used in real projects rather than a fragile prototype.
prerequisites: GTSAM and point-cloud concepts; CUDA knowledge for GPU acceleration
student_project_ideas: Integrate GLIM with a small mobile robot (ROS2) and compare mapping accuracy and runtime with and without GPU acceleration on an NVIDIA Jetson or desktop GPU.

Extend GLIM using its callback mechanism to add an explicit loop-detection constraint (using place-recognition from OpenCV or a learning-based matcher) and evaluate global consistency improvements on an outdoor LiDAR dataset.

tools.name: thorvg/thorvg
tools.desc: A production-ready C++ vector graphics engine supporting SVG and Lottie formats, featuring advanced rendering backends such as WebGPU for high-performance graphics.

cls.summary: ThorVG is a compact, high-performance C++ vector graphics engine for rendering SVG, Lottie and other vector content across desktop, mobile, embedded and web platforms.
cls.what_it_does: ThorVG renders 2D vector graphics and animations (SVG, Lottie, GIF) with CPU- and GPU-backed rendering paths, SIMD acceleration and a retained-mode scene graph. It is used as a library developers embed into applications or devices (including microcontrollers and WebAssembly builds) to draw shapes, text, images and composited scenes with effects and partial redraw optimisations.
cls.trl_rationale: The repository is multi-year (created 2020), has substantial community interest (≈1.9k stars), active recent commits and the README claims production use including microcontroller (ESP32) and WebAssembly targets; these indicate production-ready use though not a de-facto standard.
prerequisites: optional: knowledge of WebAssembly/WebGPU or platform graphics APIs
student_project_ideas: Build a small instrument panel UI for a simulated embedded device using ThorVG on an ESP32 or Raspberry Pi, rendering animated SVG/Lottie gauges and exporting telemetry to a web dashboard.
Integrate ThorVG into a desktop prototype (C++/Qt) to load and play Lottie animations and compare CPU rasterization performance with Skia or Cairo across varied scene complexity.

tools.name: Farama-Foundation/Metaworld
