tools.desc: Collections of robotics environments geared towards benchmarking multi-task and meta reinforcement learning

cls.summary: Meta-World is a mature open-source collection of simulated robotic manipulation environments and benchmarks for evaluating multi-task and meta reinforcement learning algorithms.
cls.what_it_does: Meta-World provides a library of continuous-control robotic manipulation environments (50+ tasks) and predefined benchmarks (MT1/MT10/MT50 and ML1/ML10/ML45) that follow the Gymnasium API for training and evaluating multi-task and meta‑RL algorithms. It is used by creating Gymnasium environments or vectorised variants, running policy rollouts, and comparing learning and adaptation performance across tasks.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository created in 2019, actively maintained with many stars, documentation website, pip install, and public community; widely used as a benchmark in the research community which indicates maturity and adoption beyond prototypes.
prerequisites: MuJoCo or compatible physics engine (and its licence where required)
student_project_ideas: Implement a reinforcement learning agent (e.g., PPO or SAC via Stable-Baselines3) and evaluate few-shot adaptation performance on an ML1 benchmark, comparing adaptation speed across different observation augmentations.

Create a multi-task policy for MT10 using vectorised synchronous environments and measure task interference and transfer, then visualise per-task learning curves and perform a simple ablation study (e.g., with/without one-hot task IDs).

tools.name: WASasquatch/was-node-suite-comfyui
tools.desc: WAS-NS v3 Reborn; Tools for image processing, filters, masking, text, logic, numbers, latents, files, 3D scenes, and animation.

cls.summary: A large open-source collection of 698 custom nodes for ComfyUI that adds image processing, masking, filters, animation, three.js scenes and Llama‑Index/LLM integration to ComfyUI workflows.
cls.what_it_does: WAS Node Suite installs as a pack of ComfyUI nodes to extend image manipulation, filtering, masking, sampling, animation/video and three.js scene creation inside ComfyUI graphs, and it adds Llama‑Index (document loaders, indexes, vector stores and query/chat nodes) accessible on the canvas. It is used by cloning into ComfyUI's custom_nodes folder and enabling optional groups for LLMs, document export and vector stores; notable for its very large node count, optional groups that avoid autoinstalling packages, and claimed wide user adoption.
cls.trl_rationale: The project is multi-year (created 2023) with active development (last push 2026), many stars/forks and the README claims >1M downloads and daily use; that combination indicates production-ready community use rather than an early prototype.
prerequisites: basic familiarity with ComfyUI node graphs
student_project_ideas: Create a ComfyUI workflow using WAS nodes to preprocess and index a folder of engineering diagrams with the Llama‑Index nodes, then build a chat interface that can retrieve relevant images and text from the indexed collection.

Build a pipeline that exports three.js scenes from ComfyUI (using the WAS three.js nodes) and visualise them in a web page, demonstrating automated generation of 3D assets from image processing pipelines.

tools.name: john-rocky/CoreML-Models
tools.desc: Core ML model zoo for iOS/macOS — PyTorch models converted to ready-to-use .mlpackage, each with a conversion script and SwiftUI sample app. Sibling repos cover Apple's Core AI framework (iOS/macOS 27) and on-device LLMs.

cls.summary: A curated model zoo of PyTorch models converted to Core ML (.mlpackage / .aimodel) with conversion scripts and SwiftUI sample apps for on-device iOS/macOS inference.
cls.what_it_does: This repository provides ready-to-use Core ML models converted from PyTorch for tasks such as classification, detection, segmentation, super-resolution and on-device LLMs, plus conversion scripts and SwiftUI example apps. It is used by downloading the .mlpackage/.aimodel and bundling it into an iOS/macOS project for local inference, notable for its breadth of models and example integrations targeting Apple platforms.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository is mature (created 2020), has many stars, active pushes in 2026, conversion scripts and sample apps, and at least one real project (xLights) uses the models; this indicates production-ready assets rather than an early prototype.
prerequisites: understanding of Core ML and coremltools
familiarity with PyTorch if converting models
student_project_ideas: Build an iOS app that performs real-time semantic segmentation using a Core ML segmentation model from the zoo and evaluate latency/energy on different Apple Silicon devices.
Convert a small PyTorch model to .mlpackage with coremltools, integrate it into a SwiftUI app, and measure inference performance and memory use compared with a TensorFlow Lite baseline.

tools.name: genaray/Arch
tools.desc: A high-performance C# based Archetype & Chunks Entity Component System (ECS) with optional multithreading.

cls.summary: Arch is a high-performance C# archetype-and-chunks Entity Component System library for game development and data-oriented programming.
cls.what_it_does: Arch provides an efficient ECS runtime (archetype + chunk storage), high-performance queries, multithreading and utilities for creating and iterating large numbers of entities and components in .NET/C# projects. It is used as a library dependency in game engines or simulation code (Unity, Godot, MonoGame, Stride) and emphasises cache-friendly layouts and minimal API surface for performance.
cls.trl_rationale: The repository is mature (created Oct 2022), actively maintained with many stars and known downstream users (e.g. Space Station 14) and packaged releases, indicating production-ready use in projects.
prerequisites: familiarity with ECS concepts and game-engine integration
student_project_ideas: Build a simple 2D game prototype in MonoGame or Godot using Arch for entity management and compare update throughput and memory use against a naive object-oriented implementation.
Implement a small multi-agent simulation (e.g. flocking boids) using Arch's multithreaded queries and measure scaling with core count and entity count.

tools.name: robocasa/robocasa
tools.desc: RoboCasa: Large-Scale Simulation of Everyday Tasks for Generalist Robots

cls.summary: RoboCasa is an open research simulation framework and multi-task benchmark for training and evaluating generalist robots on hundreds of everyday manipulation tasks in large collections of kitchen scenes and objects.
cls.what_it_does: RoboCasa provides hundreds of simulated everyday tasks, thousands of kitchen scenes and objects, and large human and robot demonstration datasets to train and benchmark robot policies. It is used by creating gym-compatible environments, running rollouts or teleoperation scripts, and evaluating learning-based policies on the provided leaderboard; notable aspects are its scale (365 tasks, thousands of scenes/objects) and integrated benchmarking support.
cls.trl_rationale: The project has an academic origin with published papers, a v1.0 release, a public leaderboard and substantial datasets (365 tasks, thousands of scenes/objects), active maintenance and regular updates — evidence of production-ready research software rather than a fragile prototype.
prerequisites: robosuite (master branch) and its physics backend
student_project_ideas: Train and evaluate a pick-and-place policy (e.g. behaviour cloning or a diffusion policy) on a subset of RoboCasa tasks and measure generalisation across 'pretrain' vs 'target' kitchen splits.
Use the provided subtask annotations and demonstration data to implement a hierarchical policy that uses subtask labels to switch between atomic skills and compare performance to flat policies.

tools.desc: UPBGE, the best integrated game engine in Blender

tools.name: su2code/SU2
tools.desc: SU2: An Open-Source Suite for Multiphysics Simulation and Design

tools.name: thanglequoc/vietnamese-provinces-database
tools.desc: Comprehensive SQL and GIS datasets for Vietnamese administrative units, including provinces, districts, wards, postal codes, and geospatial boundaries.

cls.summary: A maintained open dataset of Vietnam's administrative units with SQL and GIS exports (PostGIS, GeoJSON, MongoDB, Elasticsearch, Redis and more) including provinces, districts, wards and postal codes.
cls.what_it_does: Provides authoritative tables and geospatial boundaries for Vietnam's provinces, districts and wards in multiple database and GIS formats so developers and analysts can import them into PostGIS, MySQL, MongoDB, Elasticsearch or use GeoJSON directly. Notable points are multi-format releases, inclusion of postal codes and readiness for spatial queries and mapping workflows.
cls.trl_rationale: The repository is mature: created in 2021, actively maintained with frequent releases, many stars/forks, multiple format archives (PostGIS, MySQL, MongoDB, Elasticsearch, Redis, GeoJSON) and changelog tied to government decrees, indicating production-ready dataset use.
prerequisites: basic SQL and relational database use
basic GIS concepts and familiarity with GeoJSON/PostGIS
student_project_ideas: Build a web map (Leaflet or Mapbox GL) that visualises province/district/ward boundaries and allows filtering by postal code, using the GeoJSON export and a simple API.

Import the PostGIS dataset into a local PostgreSQL/PostGIS instance and implement spatial queries to calculate service-area statistics (population by ward polygon intersection with sample point data).

tools.name: csdjk/LearnUnityShader
tools.desc: 记录学习Unity Shader过程中实现过的一些Demo。

cls.summary: A large collection of Unity shader demos and examples illustrating lighting, post-processing, geometry shaders and GPU-driven effects for learning and prototyping visual effects in Unity.
cls.what_it_does: This repository collects many small Unity ShaderLab/HLSL examples and scenes that implement lighting models, post-processing (bloom, blur, motion blur), geometry and instance-based effects, depth techniques and simple physics-driven animations (cloth, mass-spring). It's used by opening the Unity project (targeted Unity 2021.3.11f1) and running the included scenes to study or adapt shader code; notable for its breadth of practical, hands-on shader examples and clear scene organisation.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository is multi-year (created 2019) with many stars and active pushes through 2026, showing sustained community interest and runnable example scenes, but it is example/demo code without formal releases or evidence of production deployment, consistent with a beta-level maturity.
prerequisites: basic C# scripting for Unity and familiarity with ShaderLab/HLSL
student_project_ideas: Implement a physically plausible glass material by combining the repo's reflection/refraction and Fresnel demos, then integrate it into a simple Unity scene and evaluate visual realism and performance on target hardware.

Use the GPU instancing grass demo and depth/blur post-processing examples to build a small interactive scene demonstrating LOD and post-process optimization, and measure frame-time and memory use across devices.

tools.name: sammcj/gollama
tools.desc: Go manage your Ollama models

cls.summary: Gollama is a macOS/Linux command-line TUI for listing, inspecting and managing Ollama LLM models on a local machine.
cls.what_it_does: Gollama provides an interactive text user interface and CLI to list, sort, inspect, edit, run, copy, push and delete Ollama models and to estimate vRAM usage. It is used locally against an Ollama API/installation and is notable for its keyboard-driven TUI and convenience features for day-to-day local model management.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository has multi-year history (created 2024-05), many stars (1848), a v2.0.1 release referenced in the README and recent activity, indicating production-ready tooling used by the community rather than an experimental prototype.
prerequisites: basic familiarity with command-line on macOS/Linux
student_project_ideas: Create a small automation that uses Gollama to deploy a selected local Ollama model, run a test prompt set and log latency and memory (vRAM) usage for comparison with llama.cpp.
Extend Gollama or write a wrapper to add custom model tagging and automated cleanup policies (e.g. remove models older than X days) and integrate it with a simple dashboard showing model inventory.

tools.name: sybil-solutions/local-studio
tools.desc: Control panel for VLLM, Sglang, llama.cpp, exllamav3

cls.summary: Local Studio is a desktop control panel and local gateway for running and connecting to self-hosted large language models and inference servers across machines.
cls.what_it_does: Local Studio discovers and aggregates local inference servers (vLLM, llama.cpp, SGLang, exllamav3 and any /v1/models endpoint) and exposes them via an OpenAI/Anthropic-compatible gateway while providing a desktop UI, controller binaries and a Tailscale-based fleet for multi-machine access. It bundles a controller that can launch registry recipes on available GPUs, install controllers over SSH on Linux/macOS machines, and integrates with the upstream T3 Code UI for agents, threads and mobile access.
cls.trl_rationale: The project is under 1 year old, which limits TRL to <=6, but the repository shows production-oriented releases (signed macOS DMGs, Windows installers, AppImages, controller binaries), active development and many stars, indicating a beta-level, usable tool rather than a fragile prototype.
prerequisites: Tailscale account and key-based SSH access to remote machines for automatic controller install
Local models or inference servers (vLLM, llama.cpp, SGLang, etc.) to connect
student_project_ideas: Set up a small multi-machine fleet using Local Studio and Tailscale to host a vLLM instance on one machine and a llama.cpp instance on another, then measure and compare latency and throughput for identical prompts routed through the Local Studio gateway.

Extend or script the Local Studio controller to automate launching a model recipe on GPU nodes and produce a dashboard that reports model load, token usage and per-model request routing for an operational-awareness lab exercise.

tools.name: HaD0Yun/CozyClay
tools.desc: Open source previs software in the browser: block a scene, pose characters, author camera moves and cuts, then take the same shots to an AI video model.

cls.summary: CozyClay is a browser-based previsualisation studio that lets you block scenes, pose characters, author camera moves and cuts, then export structured references for AI video models.
cls.what_it_does: CozyClay provides an in-browser 3D previs editor for staging sets and actors, generating deterministic motion clips and placing camera shots on a timeline. It exports frames, short greybox clips, depth/normal passes and prompts so external AI video models can reproduce the planned shot, and it supports agent-driven workflows via an MCP server.
cls.trl_rationale: The project is active, well-documented, and has many stars and releases, but the repository is only ~112 days old so it lacks the multi-year track record or wide industrial adoption needed for TRL 7+; README and docs show mature features and integration points consistent with a beta-level tool.
student_project_ideas: Build a short virtual-prototyping pipeline that stages a mechanical assembly in CozyClay, captures camera passes and greybox clips, and uses an external AI video model to generate a narrated animatic for stakeholder review.

Integrate CozyClay's MCP server with a simple agent (using OpenAI or an open LLM) to script and compile motion specs automatically, then evaluate the agent's success rate by running QA checks on collisions and foot sliding.

tools.name: pelicanmapping/osgearth
tools.desc: 3D Maps & Terrain SDK (C++)

tools.name: ggml-org/Llama-macOS
tools.desc: A cosy home for your LLMs.

cls.summary: Llama is a small macOS menu-bar app that runs local LLMs (GGUF models) via a local server and exposes a simple WebAPI and WebUI.
cls.what_it_does: Llama runs language models locally on a Mac by using llama.cpp (or a bundled prebuilt binary), exposing a local HTTP server and a built-in WebUI for chat. It simplifies model installation, auto-configures model settings for the host Mac, and lets other apps talk to the running model through a stable local API.
cls.trl_rationale: The project is over one year old, has many stars, distributed releases and a Homebrew cask, and runs as a user-facing macOS app — evidence of production-ready maturity and real users.
prerequisites: optional: llama.cpp (the app can install or use a bundled binary)
student_project_ideas: Create a small desktop tool that forwards logs or telemetry from an engineering experiment to a local Llama instance for automated summarisation and report generation.
Prototype a local coding assistant by connecting the Llama macOS server API to an editor plugin (e.g. a VS Code extension) to provide offline code suggestions and snippets.

tools.name: matlab/matlab-mcp-server
tools.desc: Run MATLAB® using AI applications with the official MATLAB MCP Server from MathWorks®. This MCP server for MATLAB supports a wide range of coding agents like Claude Code® and Visual Studio® Code.

cls.summary: An official MathWorks MCP (Model Context Protocol) server that lets AI coding agents start MATLAB, run MATLAB code, and check MATLAB code style and correctness from external AI tools and editors.
cls.what_it_does: The MATLAB MCP Server exposes a local service that AI applications (Claude Code, GitHub Copilot CLI, Codex and similar) can use to launch MATLAB, execute scripts, and inspect or assess code. It is installed as a separate binary or bundle and integrates with AI agents via the MCP protocol, making MATLAB functionality available to automated coding assistants and editor integrations.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository is published and maintained by MathWorks, has many stars and active releases and instructions for multiple platforms; README documents releases and tested integrations, indicating production-readiness rather than a fragile prototype. Repository age (~13 months) and visible installs/build instructions support TRL 7.
prerequisites: MATLAB (R2021a or later) installed and on PATH
Basic familiarity with command line and configuring AI agents (Claude, Copilot, etc.)
student_project_ideas: Create an automated test harness where an LLM-based coding agent uses the MATLAB MCP Server to generate, run, and validate control-system simulations (Simulink or MATLAB scripts) and report pass/fail results.
Build a VS Code extension workflow that uses the MCP Server to let an AI assistant refactor MATLAB code, run unit tests, and compare performance before and after changes.

cls.summary: Autoware Universe is an open-source collection of ROS/ROS 2 packages implementing perception, planning, control and related components for autonomous vehicles.
cls.what_it_does: Autoware Universe provides a large, modular software stack for building and testing self-driving vehicle functions (perception, mapping, localization, planning, control and simulation). It is used as a set of ROS/ROS 2 packages and launch configurations to integrate sensors, algorithms and simulators into a full autonomous driving pipeline, notable for being a community-driven, production-grade Autoware ecosystem component.
cls.trl_rationale: The repository is multi-year (created 2021, 5+ years old), actively maintained with many stars and forks and an ecosystem used in industry; it shows a mature codebase and integrations typical of widely adopted autonomous-driving stacks.
prerequisites: Familiarity with Docker and robotics middleware
student_project_ideas: Integrate a perception node (camera + lidar) from Autoware Universe with a ROS 2-based simulator (e.g., Gazebo or CARLA) to implement and evaluate object detection and tracking in simulation.
Use Autoware Universe planning and control packages to implement a simple autonomous navigation pipeline on an RC-car platform or in simulation, and analyse system latency and safety margins.

tools.name: Roy3838/Observer
tools.desc: The agent that deploys micro-agents that monitor anything for you. Running completely locally. Open Source.

cls.summary: Observer is a local-first agent framework that runs micro-agents watching screen, camera, audio and other sensors and can trigger actions and notifications using local models.
cls.what_it_does: Observer lets you create small 'micro-agents' that loop: Sensors → Model → Code, so they can watch screenshots, camera frames, audio or clipboard and call notification or automation tools when conditions are met. It is notable for running models locally (llama.cpp / GGUF support), providing built-in notification tools and a web/desktop app so it can run without sending data to the cloud.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository is >1 year old, has active development and recent pushes, many stars (1800+), and publishes desktop releases (macOS/Windows/Linux) — evidence of production-ready packaging and real users, supporting a TRL 7 judgement.
prerequisites: familiarity with local LLM concepts (llama.cpp, GGUF)
basic CLI and desktop app usage
student_project_ideas: Build a monitoring micro-agent that watches a CI/CD console (screenshot or log text) and posts structured failure alerts to Telegram using a local model for error classification.

Deploy Observer on a lab workstation or Raspberry Pi to watch a camera for experimental setup errors (e.g. instrument covers left open) and trigger email/SMS notifications while logging events to a time-series database.

tools.name: netyouli/WHC_ConfuseSoftware
tools.desc: iOS代码混淆工具，Uniapp代码混淆工具，react-native代码混淆, iOS代码混淆助手，Android代码混淆助手，Uniapp代码混淆助手，过机器审核，辅助过4.3, other审核，android、ios、uniapp、u3d、cocos2dx、flutter、代码翻新(WHC_ConfuseSoftware)是一款运行在MAC OS平台的App、完美支持Objc和Swift、U3D、Flutter、Cocos2dx项目代码的自动翻新(混淆)、支持文件夹名称、文件名、修改资源文件hash值、类名、方法名、属性名、添加混淆函数方法体、添加混淆属性、自动调用生成的混淆方法、字符串混淆加密等...功能强大而稳定。

cls.summary: A commercial macOS app that automates code and resource obfuscation/renaming for mobile and game projects (iOS, Android, Unity, Flutter, UniApp, React‑Native and others).
cls.what_it_does: WHC_ConfuseSoftware rewrites and obfuscates source code, resource names and hashes, inserts dummy code, and alters identifiers to reduce similarity for app-store machine review and reverse engineering. It is distributed as a packaged application (macOS app with Windows helper tools) rather than a reusable engineering library and supports many languages and project types via automated transforms.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository is long‑lived (created 2018), actively maintained with many stars and recent commits, downloadable packaged apps and documented features — evidence of production use; however the project is a proprietary commercial tool rather than an open tooling ecosystem.
prerequisites: familiarity with mobile/game project build systems (Xcode, Android/Gradle, Unity/Flutter)
macOS environment for main application; basic knowledge of source control and project structure

tools.name: geocompx/geocompr
tools.desc: Geocomputation with R: an open source book

cls.summary: An open-source, actively maintained book with code examples that teaches geospatial data analysis and mapping using R packages such as sf, terra and tmap.
cls.what_it_does: Geocomputation with R provides a comprehensive, code-first introduction to spatial data handling, raster/vector interactions, mapping and geospatial workflows in R. It is used as a textbook and practical reference: readers run the included R scripts and examples (locally, in Binder or via Docker) to learn common geospatial tasks. It is notable for covering modern R spatial tooling (sf, terra, tmap, mlr3) and for being widely used and actively maintained as a community resource.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository created in 2017 and actively maintained with many stars and forks, a published second edition (CRC Press) and continual updates; the book and code are widely used in teaching and practice which supports a mature TRL.
prerequisites: command of R package management (installing packages, Docker/Binder optional)
student_project_ideas: Use the book's examples to build a reproducible workflow that ingests satellite imagery with terra, performs land-cover classification with mlr3, and maps results with tmap or leaflet.
Extend a chapter exercise to create a small web map app (shiny or leaflet) that visualises routing and network analysis for a local transport study using sf and osm data.

tools.name: software-mansion/react-native-executorch
tools.desc: High-performance, privacy-first on-device AI inference library for React Native, powered by PyTorch's ExecuTorch runtime

cls.summary: React Native ExecuTorch is a library for running on-device machine learning models (LLMs, vision, speech) inside React Native apps, with hardware acceleration and a catalog of pre-exported models.
cls.what_it_does: It enables offline, private AI inference on mobile devices by embedding Meta's ExecuTorch runtime in React Native, providing high-level task hooks for common AI tasks and lower-level TypeScript primitives for custom pipelines. Notable features include native acceleration backends (XNNPACK, Core ML/MLX, Vulkan), a curated catalog of pre-exported .pte models, and tooling to export and run custom PyTorch models.
cls.trl_rationale: The project is mature with many stars (1791), active development (recent pushes), full documentation and a model catalog, and it is used to power at least one production app (Private Mind). Repository age (>2 years) and community activity support a production-ready TRL rather than an early prototype.
prerequisites: React Native new architecture and familiarity with native modules
Mobile development (iOS/Android) and Expo dev builds knowledge
Basic understanding of PyTorch model export (.pte) and ExecuTorch concepts
student_project_ideas: Build a React Native app that performs on-device image classification and local inference logging, comparing latency and battery usage between XNNPACK (CPU) and Vulkan (Android GPU) backends.

Create a privacy-preserving mobile assistant that uses a pre-exported small LLM for offline Q&A and integrates local speech-to-text and text-to-speech models to evaluate end-to-end on-device UX and performance.

tools.name: MengTo/kage
tools.desc: An interactive five-chapter night walk through a Kyoto mountain temple, rendered live in Three.js.

cls.summary: Kage is a single-file interactive web experience that drives a live Three.js camera through a five-chapter night walk set in a stylised Kyoto temple.
cls.what_it_does: Kage renders a procedurally constructed night-temple scene in the browser with camera scroll choreography, particle effects (rain, leaves), lighting and post-processing, and layers generated scene plates and foreground artwork for a collage-like depth. It is delivered as a portable static site (single HTML file plus assets) that runs without a build step and uses a vendored Three.js r149 for rendering.
cls.trl_rationale: The project is a polished single-file demo with many stars and a working live demo, showing interest and reuse, but it is a creative, repository-hosted art piece (created 101 days ago) rather than a versioned, production-grade library or platform, so maturity aligns with early/adopted alpha (TRL 5).
prerequisites: familiarity with Three.js or WebGL concepts
student_project_ideas: Remix the single-file scene to add an instrumented performance overlay (FPS, draw calls, memory) and profile rendering bottlenecks on mobile vs desktop.

Replace or augment the generated scene plates with sensor-derived imagery (e.g. photogrammetry textures) and compare aesthetic and performance trade-offs when compositing raster plates over a live Three.js scene.

tools.name: Unclecheng-li/AI_Animation
tools.desc: 本项目整理了用于生成[炫酷 HTML 动画网页]的 AI Prompts，涵盖动画效果、3D 可视化、PPT 风格演示、UI 美化等多个类别。

cls.summary: A curated collection of AI Agent 'skills' and templates that generate single-file HTML/CSS/JS animations (presentations, diagrams, UI demos and video-shot style scenes) from natural-language prompts.
cls.what_it_does: The repository packages many self-contained 'Skills' (prompt + assets + templates) that let AI agents (WorkBuddy / Claude Code / Cursor etc.) output complete single-file HTML animations for PPT-style slides, flowcharts, dynamic architecture diagrams, protocol visualisations, UI demos and more. It is notable for a large gallery of specialised templates, an offline GSAP motion library and integration recipes (Node renderers, export to video) that make generating polished, recordable web animations repeatable.
cls.trl_rationale: The repo is well-developed with extensive README, many example skills, assets and templates, active pushes and significant community interest (≈1.8k stars), indicating beta-level maturity; however it is younger than one year (created 220 days ago) so a production-level track record is not yet demonstrated.
student_project_ideas: Build an animated TCP/IP packet flow visualiser for a networking class using the network-protocol-viz skill and extend it to animate custom lab captures (combine with Wireshark export).

Create an automated 'lecture-to-HTML' pipeline: feed slide content and narration into the ppt-animation skill and produce recordable single-file HTML videos, adding a Node.js batch renderer to export MP4.

tools.name: TriAxis-Games/RealtimeMeshComponent
tools.desc: Unreal Engine 5 plugin component for rendering runtime generated content.

tools.name: google-deepmind/mujoco_mpc
tools.desc: Real-time behaviour synthesis with MuJoCo, using Predictive Control

cls.summary: MJPC is a C++ framework and GUI from DeepMind that runs real-time model-predictive control (MPC) experiments and planners on MuJoCo simulated robots.
cls.what_it_does: MJPC provides an interactive application and library to author robotics tasks and run real-time predictive-control planners (derivative-based like iLQG and derivative-free predictive sampling) against MuJoCo simulations. It is used by building the C++ application (with optional Python bindings) to run and visualise control experiments and to prototype planning algorithms for simulation-based robot control.
cls.trl_rationale: The project is a research prototype from Google DeepMind with an established repo, many stars, active maintenance and documented build process; README warns it is a research prototype (not production-quality), so it aligns with a beta-level (6) rather than production (7+). The repo is over a year old and actively updated.
prerequisites: CMake / Ninja and a C++ toolchain (clang recommended)
Familiarity with MPC concepts and MuJoCo models
student_project_ideas: Implement and compare iLQG and predictive-sampling planners in MJPC on a quadruped MuJoCo model, measuring tracking performance and compute/time trade-offs.
Create a Python-driven experiment that uses MJPC's Python API to close the loop on a simulated manipulator performing pick-and-place, and add logging for offline learning of residual dynamics.

tools.name: Unity-UI-Extensions/com.unity.uiextensions
tools.desc: The Unity UI library of controls, components and other useful features for extending the Unity UI solution for Unity

cls.summary: A community-maintained collection of 100+ ready-made UI controls, effects and utilities for Unity's uGUI system to speed up building user interfaces in Unity projects.
cls.what_it_does: Provides a large library of pre-built UI controls (lists, knobs, pickers, line renderers, scroll snap, etc.), example scenes and utilities that extend Unity's built-in uGUI system. It is installed as a Unity package or asset and used inside the Unity Editor to assemble and customise UI without rebuilding common controls from scratch. Notable for being community‑driven, long-lived (assets back to 2015) and frequently updated for new Unity releases.
cls.trl_rationale: The project is long-lived (community code traced to 2015, this repo created 2022), has many stars, regular releases and active maintenance with Unity 6 support and documented release notes, indicating a mature, widely used OSS library.
prerequisites: familiarity with Unity's uGUI (Canvas, RectTransform, EventSystem)
student_project_ideas: Build a simulator UI for a mobile robot in Unity that uses UI Extensions components (e.g. custom gauges, joystick, and telemetry panels) and connects to ROS/ROS2 via rosbridge for live data display.
Create an interactive dashboard for a digital-twin prototype in Unity that visualises sensor time-series and alarms using scrollable lists, segmented controls and line renderers from UI Extensions.

tools.name: cnosdb/cnosdb
tools.desc: A cloud-native open source distributed time series database with high performance, high compression ratio and high availability.

cls.summary: CnosDB is an open-source, cloud-native distributed time-series database designed for high-performance, high-compression storage and queries for IoT, industrial and monitoring workloads.
cls.what_it_does: CnosDB stores and queries time-series data with a distributed, storage/compute-separated architecture that supports SQL and InfluxDB line-protocol ingestion. It is used for high-write, high-throughput scenarios (IoT, industrial telemetry, connected vehicles) and provides features such as sharding, caching of recent data, multi-tenancy, and Kubernetes deployment. Notable points are its Rust implementation, focus on compression and scalability, and integrations for common telemetry ecosystems.
cls.trl_rationale: The project is multi-year (created 2021), has substantial community interest (many stars/forks), active maintenance and documentation, and a cloud offering referenced in the README — indicating production-ready maturity rather than a fragile prototype.
prerequisites: familiarity with Docker / Kubernetes for deployment
Rust toolchain if building from source
student_project_ideas: Set up a CnosDB cluster on Docker/Kubernetes and build a Telegraf->CnosDB pipeline to collect, store and query sensor data from a Raspberry Pi-based IoT sensor, then visualise trends with Grafana.
Compare compression and query performance of CnosDB vs TimescaleDB using a synthetic industrial IoT dataset, measuring storage size, ingest throughput and aggregate query latency.

tools.name: StartLuxLabs/StartLux-Decision
tools.desc: Open decision models from 0.8B to 27B: a calibrated probability for every option in one pass, and a short thought only when unsure. Engine for vLLM, llama.cpp and MLX.

cls.summary: StartLux-Decision provides open decision-focused LLMs and an inference server that returns calibrated probabilities for typed options in one forward pass or with a brief reasoning trace when uncertain.
cls.what_it_does: The project supplies models and an inference engine / HTTP server that take a state (text, JSON or images) plus typed questions and return calibrated probabilities for every option (choice, yes/no, or scored). It is designed to run with local runtimes (vLLM, llama.cpp, MLX) and offers Instant models (single pass) and AutoThink models (produce a short chain-of-thought only when needed). Notable features are calibrated probabilistic outputs for discrete decision tasks and compatibility with local quantised formats (GGUF/MLX).
cls.trl_rationale: The repository shows a released v1.1, Hugging Face model packs, demos and leaderboard results indicating early adoption, but the project is only 49 days old so per the TRL rules its demonstrated maturity should be limited to TRL 5.
prerequisites: experience running local LLM runtimes or quantised model files (GGUF/MLX)
basic knowledge of HTTP APIs and model inference (GPU/CPU deployment)
student_project_ideas: Integrate StartLux-Decision with a small robot simulation (e.g. ROS 2 / Gazebo) so the model makes high-level tactical choices and evaluate decision calibration against ground-truth scenarios.

Build a lab exercise that compares Instant vs AutoThink models on a fault-detection benchmark: feed time-series snapshots and typed questions, then measure accuracy, calibration and latency when running locally with gguf or MLX weights.

tools.name: robin-shaun/XTDrone
tools.desc: UAV Simulation Platform based on PX4, ROS and Gazebo

cls.summary: XTDrone is an open-source UAV simulation platform built on PX4, ROS and Gazebo for developing and validating flight control, perception and multi-vehicle coordination algorithms.
cls.what_it_does: XTDrone provides simulators and models for multirotor, fixed-wing and hybrid aircraft plus other robotic systems (UGV, USV, manipulator) to run algorithms in realistic physics using PX4 autopilot and Gazebo physics with ROS integrations. It is used to test perception (SLAM, detection), planning, control and multi-UAV coordination in simulation before deploying to hardware, and is notable for direct compatibility with PX4 and published papers describing its architecture and multi-vehicle extensions.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository created in 2020 and actively maintained through 2026, with 1.7k stars, peer-reviewed conference/journal papers describing the platform, and use in competitions (Chinese Robotics Competition), which indicates production-ready maturity and real-world adoption rather than a small prototype.
student_project_ideas: Implement and evaluate a vision-based landing algorithm in XTDrone by connecting a monocular SLAM node (ORB-SLAM2) in ROS and testing robustness across wind disturbance scenarios.

Create a multi-UAV formation control lab: use XTDrone's multi-vehicle setup to design a distributed coordination algorithm and measure trajectory tracking and collision avoidance under simulated communication loss.

tools.name: saturday06/VRM-Addon-for-Blender
tools.desc: VRM Importer, Exporter and Utilities for Blender 2.93 to 5.3

cls.summary: A Blender add-on that imports, exports and edits VRM humanoid avatar files and provides a Python API for automation.
cls.what_it_does: The add-on adds VRM import/export, humanoid setup and shader/configuration tools to Blender and exposes a scripting API so users can automate tasks. It is installed into Blender as an add-on and is notable for supporting a common avatar format (VRM) across many Blender versions with tutorials and development guidance.
cls.trl_rationale: The repository is long-lived (created 2019), has a large star count (1.7k), regular recent activity (last push 2026-11-14) and published documentation/tutorials, indicating a mature, widely used community project rather than an experimental prototype.
prerequisites: Blender user experience (installing and using add-ons)
Basic Python for scripting the add-on API
student_project_ideas: Create a Blender pipeline that imports a VRM avatar, rigs it for a simple robot simulation and exports animated poses to be used in a robotics visualization (combine with ROS/ROS2 visualization tools).

Write Python scripts using the add-on's API to batch-convert and standardise a set of humanoid VRM models for use in a human-in-the-loop simulation or VR demonstration (combine with a small Unity or WebGL viewer).

tools.name: GeoNode/geonode
tools.desc: GeoNode is an open source platform that facilitates the creation, sharing, and collaborative use of geospatial data.

tools.name: Maaack/Godot-Game-Template
tools.desc: Godot template with a main menu, options menus, pause menu, credits, scene loader, extra tools, and an example game scene.

cls.summary: A ready-made Godot 4 template and plugin that provides menus, scene loading, music and common game UI features to bootstrap 2D or 3D games.
cls.what_it_does: The repository provides a plugin and project template for Godot (4.4+ / 4.7) that adds a main menu, options menus, pause menu, credits, scene loader, music and UI sound controllers and an example game scene. It is installed either as a new project template or as an addon in an existing Godot project and is aimed at quickly setting up common game scaffolding for jams or small commercial projects. Notable aspects are cross-resolution support, an included setup wizard, and availability via the Godot Asset Library and Asset Store.
cls.trl_rationale: The project is mature: created in 2022, actively maintained with recent pushes (2026-10-29), many stars/forks, documentation and distribution via the Godot Asset Library/Store, and multiple example games using it; this indicates wide adoption rather than an experimental prototype.
prerequisites: basic GDScript and scene workflow knowledge
student_project_ideas: Create a short 2D game for a game-design course using the template's menus and scene loader, then add a new gameplay mechanic and export builds for desktop and web.
Extend the template to implement and evaluate accessibility features (scalable UI, input remapping, audio cues) and document usability improvements as a mini research or capstone project.

tools.name: edgerunners-2/capri-ai-desktop
tools.desc: Cyberpunk AI desktop agent & voice companion for Windows. Supports Claude Code, Ollama, DeepSeek, Discord calls & screen automation.

cls.summary: Capri is a Windows desktop AI companion that speaks, listens, automates desktop tasks and can join voice calls while connecting to various LLMs and voice services.
cls.what_it_does: Capri provides a cyberpunk-themed desktop AI agent that users can talk or voice-chat with, have speak aloud, and use to automate GUI tasks (open apps, click, run scripts). It integrates with multiple assistant backends (Claude Code, Ollama, etc.), voice services (ElevenLabs, Fish Audio) and can join Discord/other voice calls; it also supports a mod system for skins and custom code mods. Notable points are its focus on local/connected LLMs, screen automation and an extendable mod/plugin workflow.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository is active, popular (many stars/forks) with recent commits and releases, showing a maintained beta-quality project; however it is under one year old so lacks the longer track record and stable production adoption required for TRL 7+.
prerequisites: API keys/accounts for supported assistants or voice services (optional)
student_project_ideas: Create a custom Capri code-mod that automates a repetitive lab PC task (file organisation or test-run orchestration) and logs actions to a CSV for analysis.
Integrate a local LLM backend (e.g. Ollama) and extend Capri with a mod that provides simple voice-driven test-case execution for a student-built application.

tools.name: intel/auto-round
tools.desc: PTQ-Level Efficiency, QAT-Level Accuracy | 训练后量化的效率，量化感知训练的精度

cls.summary: AutoRound is an open-source toolkit for post-training and mixed-bit quantization of large language and vision-language models to reduce model size and inference cost while preserving accuracy.
cls.what_it_does: AutoRound provides algorithms and utilities to quantize LLMs and VLMs (including ultra-low-bit schemes such as INT2/INT4 and mixed-bit formats) and export them to common formats (GGUF, AutoAWQ, AutoGPTQ). It is used as a Python toolkit that integrates with Transformer ecosystems (Transformers, vLLM, SGLang) to prepare models for efficient deployment on CPUs, GPUs and accelerators. Notable features include SignRound algorithms, AutoScheme mixed-precision recipe generation, and support for a wide variety of dtypes and backend formats.
cls.trl_rationale: The repository is >2 years old, has substantial community interest (1.7k stars), active recent development and documented integrations with Transformers and vLLM, and is cited as adopted by upstream ecosystems — evidence of production-readiness though not a de-facto standard.
student_project_ideas: Quantize a small open-source LLM with AutoRound to 4-bit and 2-bit mixed precision, measure accuracy vs latency on CPU and GPU, and produce a report comparing trade-offs.
Integrate an AutoRound-quantized model into a vLLM serving stack and evaluate memory footprint and throughput for a simple robotics perception-to-language pipeline.

tools.name: intentee/paddler
tools.desc: Open-source LLM/VLM load balancer and serving platform for self-hosting LLMs (and VLMs) at scale 🏓🦙 Alternative to projects like llm-d, Docker Model Runner, etc but with less moving parts and simple deployments built around ggml ecosystem. Runs on CPU and GPU.

cls.summary: Paddler is an open-source Rust-based load balancer and serving platform to self-host and scale LLM/VLM inference (CPU/GPU) across agents and slots.
cls.what_it_does: Paddler provides a lightweight server and agent architecture to run, load-balance and manage local LLM/VLM inference (using a built-in llama.cpp engine) with features like request buffering, dynamic model swapping, observability and a web admin panel. It is used by deploying a balancer and one or more agents (each hosting inference slots) to serve tokens and embeddings to applications, and is notable for being a single-binary, self-hostable alternative to larger LLM serving stacks.
cls.trl_rationale: The project is more than one year old, has many stars, active pushes (last push recently), public docs, releases and a community (Discord, talks), indicating production-ready maturity rather than an experimental prototype.
prerequisites: familiarity with LLM inference concepts (models, tokens, embeddings)
basic sysadmin/DevOps skills (deploying binaries, networking, monitoring)
optional: knowledge of Rust for building from source
student_project_ideas: Build a small web app that sends inference requests to a local Paddler balancer and compare latency/cost when adding/removing agents (measure scaling behaviour and request buffering).
Integrate Paddler with a simple autoscaling policy (e.g., spawn agents in cloud or local VMs based on queue length) and evaluate reliability and throughput under synthetic workloads.

tools.name: ricosjp/truck
tools.desc: truck - Truck is a RUst Cad Kernel

cls.summary: Truck is an open-source Rust-based CAD kernel that implements B-rep geometry with NURBS, mesh algorithms and visualization support for building CAD and geometry-processing applications.
cls.what_it_does: Truck provides a modular collection of Rust crates implementing geometric primitives (NURBS, B-splines), topological B-rep data structures, meshing algorithms, boolean/shape operations and GPU-backed rendering via wgpu. It is used as a low-level kernel for building CAD tools, converters or visualization pipelines and is notable for being written in Rust, modularised into replaceable crates and offering a JavaScript wrapper for web use.
cls.trl_rationale: The project is multi-year (created 2020) with many stars (1691), active pushes as recently as 2026, modular crates, examples, tutorials and a JavaScript wrapper—evidence of production-grade capability and users; it lacks the very large ecosystem and de-facto standard status required for TRL 8–9.
prerequisites: optional familiarity with GPU programming (wgpu) for rendering
student_project_ideas: Implement a simple CAD viewer that loads a NURBS-based shape using truck, tessellates it with truck-meshalgo and displays it in the browser via truck-js and WebGPU.

Compare boolean-operation robustness by creating a set of parametric parts in truck, performing shapeops (boolean) operations and measuring meshing and topology integrity under geometric perturbations.

tools.name: nasa-jpl/rosa
tools.desc: ROSA 🤖 is an AI Agent designed to interact with ROS1- and ROS2-based robotics systems using natural language queries. ROSA helps robot developers inspect, diagnose, understand, and operate robots.

cls.summary: ROSA is an open-source AI agent that lets developers query and control ROS1/ROS2 robotic systems using natural language and LLMs.
cls.what_it_does: ROSA connects to ROS and ROS2 systems and exposes tools that allow natural-language inspection, diagnosis and control of robots; it is used by instantiating an agent with an LLM backend and invoking natural-language commands. It is notable for being developed by JPL, providing demos (TurtleSim, NeBula-Spot), a research paper and extensibility for custom robot integrations including planned IsaacSim support.
cls.trl_rationale: The project is backed by NASA JPL, has releases, an arXiv paper, demos and an active repository with many stars and recent activity; this indicates production-readiness for experimental use (TRL 7). The repository is over a year old and shows community interest and documentation.
prerequisites: An LLM backend (API or local model) for full functionality
student_project_ideas: Build a lab exercise where students extend a ROSA agent to add a custom tool that inspects robot sensor topics and reports anomalies, integrating with ROS 2 and a simple anomaly detector node.
Create a project that uses ROSA with a TurtleSim or Gazebo/IsaacSim robot to accept natural-language navigation tasks, log the agent decisions, and compare performance using different LLM backends.

tools.name: siddsachar/row-bot
tools.desc: Row-Bot - Personal AI Sovereignty. A local-first AI assistant with integrated tools, a personal knowledge graph, voice, vision, shell, browser automation, scheduled tasks, health tracking, and messaging channels. Run locally via Ollama or add opt-in cloud models. Your data stays on your machine.

cls.summary: Row-Bot is a local-first desktop AI assistant that uses local or cloud models to automate tasks, maintain a personal knowledge graph, run agents and workflows, and interact with files, shell and external services while keeping data on your machine.
cls.what_it_does: Row-Bot provides a conversational assistant that performs real work (creates code folders, decks, mockups, and automations), maintains a local knowledge graph and memory, delegates to goal-directed agents, and connects to services (GitHub, Notion, messaging) via a catalog of apps and skills. It runs with local runtimes (Ollama) or optional cloud APIs, offers installers and Docker deployments, and is notable for its local-first privacy model and integrated tools (voice, vision, browser automation, scheduled workflows).
cls.trl_rationale: The project shows installers, published releases, cross-platform packages and an active repo with many stars and recent commits, indicating beta-level maturity; however the repository is under one year old so TRL is capped at 6.
prerequisites: optional: Ollama or Docker for local model runtimes
familiarity with LLM APIs (OpenAI-compatible) for optional cloud models
student_project_ideas: Build a reproducible workflow where Row-Bot autonomously generates a code project, runs tests in a Docker sandbox, and opens a generated report, then evaluate safety/approval prompts and logging.

Integrate Row-Bot with a local Ollama model and a GitHub repo to prototype an automated commit-and-PR assistant that uses the knowledge graph to maintain traceability between requirements and code changes.

tools.name: libfive/libfive
tools.desc: Infrastructure for solid modeling

tools.name: nobodywho-ooo/nobodywho
tools.desc: NobodyWho is an inference engine that lets you run LLMs locally and efficiently on any device.

cls.summary: NobodyWho is an open-source inference engine for running large language models locally and efficiently on desktop and mobile devices.
cls.what_it_does: NobodyWho runs GGUF-format LLMs locally (CPU/GPU via Vulkan/Metal) and provides bindings for Python, Kotlin, Swift, Flutter, React Native and Godot so apps can do on-device chat, multimodal inputs, speech-to-text and text-to-speech. It is notable for supporting many model sources (Hugging Face or URLs), automatic structured tool-calling grammars, and multi-backend acceleration including llama.cpp and ONNX runtimes.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository is well-established (>1 year), has many stars and active recent commits, multiple language bindings and published mobile apps; these indicate production-readiness and real-world use rather than a narrow prototype.
prerequisites: mobile or desktop development (Kotlin/Swift/Flutter/React Native) and basic Rust toolchain knowledge
understanding of GPU drivers (Vulkan/Metal) and model memory constraints
student_project_ideas: Create an offline voice assistant for a Raspberry Pi or Android device using NobodyWho for local ASR (Whisper), local inference and TTS, and compare latency and privacy against a cloud-based pipeline.
Integrate NobodyWho into a small robot (ROS 2 or custom) to provide on-device natural language interaction and evaluate resource usage and responsiveness across models of different sizes.

tools.name: alexgreensh/anidoodle
tools.desc: Art and animation, written as code. Illustrations, loops, interactive web art, launch-videos and scored films in dozens of styles, identical on every render.

cls.summary: An open-source TypeScript engine for creating deterministic, hand-drawn style illustrations, animated films and music where every stroke and note is produced by code.
cls.what_it_does: Anidoodle generates illustrations, frame-by-frame drawing films, interactive web art and programmatic music using 32 distinct visual styles and 21 music vocabularies; the same source code reproduces identical output on any machine. It is used as a developer library and toolchain (Node + web) to script marks, scores and timelapse films, and it is notable for deterministic reproducibility and a large set of handcrafted stylistic processors.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository is very new (created ~56 days ago) but already popular (many stars) and contains runnable Node/TypeScript code and examples; this indicates early adopters and usable examples but limited track record, so alpha-in-use is appropriate.
student_project_ideas: Create an animated explainer for a systems-design concept by scripting anidoodle to draw the system components step-by-step and export a synchronized score using the built-in music engine.
Extend or design a new visual style that maps time-series sensor data (e.g. temperature or accelerometer) to drawing parameters, producing deterministic diagnostic timelapses for engineering reports.

tools.name: nezvers/Godot-GameTemplate
tools.desc: Template for top-down shooter, with solutions for tough problems.

cls.summary: A ready-to-use Godot Engine project template and addon library for building top-down (including isometric) shooter games, providing common systems like menus, pausing, input rebinding, audio management and enemy spawning.
cls.what_it_does: This repository provides a structured starter project and a set of reusable Godot addons and scripts (in GDScript) to solve common game-development problems such as menus, audio management, input rebinding, threaded loading, instance pooling and AI pathfinding. It is used by copying or importing the template into a Godot project and reusing the included scenes and resources as examples or building blocks. It is notable for its organisation (project placed under an addon folder), a library of general-purpose scripts and a focus on practical solutions for top-down shooter mechanics.
cls.trl_rationale: The repository is mature (created 2019) with many stars (1.6k), active maintenance (recent push in 2026) and a substantial README showing numerous implemented features, indicating production-ready maturity for game development templates rather than a fragile prototype.
student_project_ideas: Create a small top-down shooter level by reusing the template's actor, weapon and projectile scenes and extend enemy AI with a new behaviour (e.g., flanking) while instrumenting performance metrics.
Build a networked two-player prototype by integrating Godot high-level multiplayer APIs into the template, demonstrating synchronization of player actions, projectiles and spawn waves.

tools.name: LibreDWG/libredwg
tools.desc: Official mirror of libredwg. With CI hooks and nightly releases. PR's ok

cls.summary: LibreDWG is an open-source C library for reading and writing AutoCAD DWG files, providing converters and example tools for working with DWG, DXF, SVG and JSON representations.
cls.what_it_does: LibreDWG implements a DWG decoder and writer so applications can parse, inspect, convert and (to an extent) write AutoCAD DWG files. It is used as a C library (with optional bindings) and includes example tools for conversion to DXF, SVG, PostScript and JSON; notable points are wide DWG version support for reading and an active GNU-backed project history.
cls.trl_rationale: The project is several years old (created 2018), actively maintained with nightly releases and CI, many stars and releases, and is part of the GNU ecosystem; this indicates production-ready maturity though not a de-facto industry standard.
student_project_ideas: Implement a DWG -> SVG/DXF batch converter using LibreDWG and demonstrate layer and text extraction for automated drawing quality checks.

Build a small application that extracts geometry and metadata from DWG files and imports them into a simple digital-twin prototype (e.g. a web viewer using three.js) to visualise CAD data in a browser.

tools.name: node-opcua/node-opcua
tools.desc: Unlocking the Full Potential of OPC UA with Typescript and NodeJS - http://node-opcua.github.io/

tools.name: nophead/NopSCADlib
tools.desc: Library of parts modelled in OpenSCAD and a framework for making projects

cls.summary: NopSCADlib is an open-source library of parameterised hardware parts and utilities written in OpenSCAD for making 3D-printed components, electronics enclosures and associated BOM/exports.
cls.what_it_does: The project provides a large collection of reusable, parameterised OpenSCAD modules ('vitamins') for common mechanical and electronic parts (screws, mounts, sockets, hinges, mounts, etc.), example projects, and scripts to produce BOMs, STLs and DXFs. It is used by writing OpenSCAD code that imports the library modules to produce printable parts and documentation; notable features include many tested part definitions, example assemblies, and Python scripts to extract BOMs and generate export files.
cls.trl_rationale: The repository is several years old (created 2019), has a large user base (many stars/forks), active recent commits, comprehensive examples and export scripts, indicating production-ready maturity for CAD libraries rather than an experimental prototype.
prerequisites: basic CAD/3D-printing concepts (tolerances, export to STL)
Python for running the included BOM/export scripts (optional)
student_project_ideas: Design and 3D-print a custom electronics enclosure for a microcontroller board using NopSCADlib modules, generate the BOM with the provided Python scripts, and produce STL/DXF files for fabrication.
Create a small robotic end-effector or mount by combining library 'vitamins' (bearings, pulleys, brackets) in OpenSCAD and validate fit/tolerances through iterative prints and modifications.

tools.name: razzant/ouroboros
tools.desc: Ouroboros — self-creating AI agent. Born Feb 16, 2026.

cls.summary: Ouroboros is an open-source, general-purpose autonomous AI agent that keeps durable memory and can run as a native desktop app or headless CLI while using local or remote LLMs for inference.
cls.what_it_does: Ouroboros provides a persistent, self-reflecting AI agent runtime that coordinates specialist sub-agents, stores durable history and memory on the host, and can modify its own code, prompts and tools. It is used as a desktop application or headless command-line program and supports local GGUF models or remote APIs for inference; notable features include persistent local history, self-modification workflows, and packaged native installers for multiple OSes.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository is 279 days old (<1 year) which limits TRL to at most 6, but the README and release artifacts (native installers, SBOMs, Homebrew tap, verification files) plus high star count indicate a beta-quality project with packaged builds and active distribution.
prerequisites: basic familiarity with command line and desktop app installation
knowledge of LLM APIs or local GGUF models to configure inference
Python familiarity for customization or development

tools.name: gaea-godot/gaea
tools.desc: Procedural generation add-on for Godot 4.

cls.summary: Gaea is an open-source procedural generation add-on for Godot 4 that provides a node-graph system to create 2D and 3D terrains and other generated content inside Godot projects.
cls.what_it_does: Gaea provides a graph-based node system inside Godot to build procedural generation flows for terrains and world content in 2D and 3D. It is installed as a Godot addon (GDScript) and lets users compose and extend generation by authoring custom nodes. Notable points are its focus on an easy-to-extend node graph and integration as an in-engine tool for Godot 4.4.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository has multiple years of history, many stars (1665) and active development, and a v1.x line referenced in the README, indicating community use; however the README notes Gaea 2.0 is still in early development and may not be fully optimised, so beta (TRL 6) is appropriate.
prerequisites: Familiarity with Godot 4 (engine usage and project structure)
student_project_ideas: Create a Godot scene that uses Gaea to procedurally generate varied terrain biomes and add runtime controls to explore parameter effects (combine with Godot's camera and input systems).
Build a small simulation that imports heightmap data (or sensor-derived elevation) and uses Gaea nodes to generate and visualise terrain variations, comparing generated output to the source data.

tools.name: sakalond/StableGen
tools.desc: Transform your 3D texturing workflow with the power of generative AI, directly within Blender!

cls.summary: StableGen is a Blender add‑on that uses diffusion models via ComfyUI to generate, texture, rig and export 3D assets and whole scenes with PBR maps and animations.
cls.what_it_does: StableGen automates creation of meshes, projecting AI‑generated views from scene cameras into consistent textures and estimating PBR maps, and can add skeletons and skin weights to characters for animation. It runs inside Blender and delegates model inference to a ComfyUI server (local or network), then bakes and exports results (glTF/FBX) for game engines or other pipelines. Notable features include TRELLIS.2 mesh generation, Masked Edit for partial texture edits, Marigold PBR estimation and integration with SkinTokens rigging.
cls.trl_rationale: The repository is mature: created >1 year ago, has many stars (1.6k), active pushes and releases, installer ZIPs for Blender and detailed docs, and explicit integrations (ComfyUI, TRELLIS.2, SkinTokens). These indicate production‑ready software rather than a fragile prototype.
prerequisites: Basic understanding of ComfyUI and local model hosting
Access to a capable GPU (recommended) and disk space for models
student_project_ideas: Use StableGen to generate and texture a set of characters, export them as glTF/FBX, and integrate them into a small interactive scene in Godot or Unity to evaluate PBR map fidelity and animation retargeting.

Build an automated pipeline that uses StableGen + ComfyUI to batch‑generate variant props or buildings from prompts and measure consistency, file sizes and polygon counts before and after LATO.2 low‑poly remeshing.

tools.name: kevinraymond/florilegium
tools.desc: Procedurally generated Delft-blue floral page margins for LuaLaTeX, with plants and visitors sampled from genomes and a TikZ library that also draws them under pdfLaTeX

cls.summary: Florilegium is a LaTeX package and TikZ library that procedurally generates decorative Delft‑blue floral page margins and botanical illustrations directly into PDFs.
cls.what_it_does: Florilegium computes and draws plants, flowers, visitors and tracery as parametric curves at document compile time, producing watercolor‑like ornaments without external image assets. It is used as a LuaLaTeX package (with companion Lua scripts) or as a pure TikZ library under pdfLaTeX, and is notable for sampling plant and visitor 'genomes' so species and layouts vary deterministically by seed.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository is very new (created 18 days ago) which caps maturity to an alpha/in‑use level; however it already has releases and CTAN packaging and many stars, indicating interest and some distribution but not a long track record of real‑world use.

tools.name: vasturiano/three-globe
tools.desc: WebGL Globe Data Visualization as a ThreeJS reusable 3D object

cls.summary: three-globe is a JavaScript library that creates interactive WebGL globe visualisations as a reusable Three.js object for plotting points, arcs, polygons and other data layers on a spherical Earth projection.
cls.what_it_does: three-globe provides a Three.js class that renders a textured globe and multiple data layers (points, arcs, polygons, heatmaps, hex bins, tiles, labels, satellites, etc.) in the browser. It is used by importing the module (or a script tag) into a Three.js scene and configuring data and visual options; notable features include many ready-made layer types and example pages demonstrating common geospatial visualisations.
cls.trl_rationale: The project has been actively maintained since 2019, has many stars (1.6k), a published npm package and extensive examples/demos, indicating broad use and stability; documentation and example source files are available. This long history and ecosystem presence justify a mature rating rather than an experimental one.
student_project_ideas: Build an interactive dashboard that visualises IoT sensor locations and time-series summaries on the globe (combine three-globe with a time-series backend like InfluxDB or a simple REST API).
Create a flight-traffic simulator showing aircraft paths and live position updates by integrating three-globe with a small Node.js server that streams ADS‑B-like data and a WebSocket client.

tools.name: LiangliangNan/Easy3D
tools.desc: A lightweight, easy-to-use, and efficient library for processing and rendering 3D data (C++ & Python)

cls.summary: Easy3D is a C++ library (with Python bindings) for efficient geometry processing and rendering of 3D data such as point clouds, surface and polyhedral meshes.
cls.what_it_does: Easy3D provides data structures and common geometry-processing algorithms (normal estimation, Poisson reconstruction, remeshing, simplification, subdivision, etc.) and a high-level OpenGL/GLSL-based renderer with viewers (GLFW/Qt/wxWidgets). It is used as a library in C++ or via Python bindings for research, teaching or building 3D applications and includes tutorials and example applications.
cls.trl_rationale: The project is mature and long-lived (created 2018), has substantial community interest (1.6k stars), active maintenance (recent pushes), Python bindings, tutorials and example applications; these point to production-ready library status rather than an early prototype.
student_project_ideas: Implement a point-cloud-to-mesh pipeline that loads LiDAR scans, estimates normals, runs Poisson reconstruction in Easy3D, and exports the mesh for CAD post-processing (combine with Open3D or Meshlab for comparison).

Develop an interactive viewer plugin using Easy3D and Qt that visualizes sensor data on a robot, includes simple mesh simplification and AO rendering, and measures rendering performance for different datasets.

tools.name: waybarrios/vllm-mlx
tools.desc: High-performance OpenAI and Anthropic compatible LLM inference server for Apple Silicon. Native MLX, continuous batching, multimodal models, MCP tool calling, and Claude Code support.

cls.summary: vllm-mlx is an Apple Silicon native inference server that exposes OpenAI and Anthropic-compatible APIs for running multimodal LLMs with continuous batching, KV and SSD-tiered caches, and MCP tool-calling support.
cls.what_it_does: It provides a high-performance local LLM inference server optimized for Apple Silicon (Metal/MLX) that serves text, vision and audio models via OpenAI- and Anthropic-compatible endpoints. It is used by running the Python package to host models locally and supports continuous batching, prefix/paged KV caching, SSD spillover, TTS/STT, and MCP tool-calling for agent workflows; notable points are native Metal acceleration and integrated multimodal + tool-calling features in one process.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository shows substantial documentation, examples, benchmarks, and many stars, indicating active development and usage; however the project was created ~346 days ago (< 1 year) so it lacks the longer track record required for TRL7+ despite its maturity of features, hence TRL 6 (beta).
prerequisites: Apple Silicon Mac (M1/M2/M3/M4/M5) for native Metal acceleration
Python and familiarity with OpenAI/Anthropic client SDKs
Models and sufficient local disk/RAM for target model sizes
student_project_ideas: Build an autonomous-agent demo that uses vllm-mlx for on-device tool-calling (MCP) to orchestrate simple robotic tasks via a ROS bridge, evaluating latency and reliability for closed-loop interactions.

Create a multimodal maintenance-assistant that combines document embeddings and image QA served by vllm-mlx to answer visual+text queries about machinery manuals, and measure response time under continuous-batching.

tools.name: CraterCrash/godot-orchestrator
tools.desc: Orchestrator: Unleashing Creativity with Visual Scripting

cls.summary: Orchestrator is a visual scripting plug-in for Godot 4 that provides a node-based graph editor and hundreds of nodes to build game logic without writing GDScript or C#.
cls.what_it_does: Orchestrator provides a visual, node-graph scripting environment (OScript) that you can attach to Godot scene nodes to implement game logic, dialogues and behaviours. It installs as a GDExtension for Godot 4.x, exposes many node categories (flow, logic, math, variables, signals) and integrates into the Godot editor for drag-and-drop authoring and reusable custom functions.
cls.trl_rationale: The project is several years old (created 2023), has a large number of stars and active development with releases and branches for multiple Godot versions, indicating production-ready maturity for Godot users; however it is not an industry-wide standard.
prerequisites: Godot 4.6+ editor matching the plugin ABI
C++ toolchain to build GDExtensions (when using source builds)
familiarity with Godot editor concepts (nodes, scenes, resources)
student_project_ideas: Build an interactive systems-visualisation prototype in Godot where telemetry-like values drive a dashboard and animated actors, implemented using Orchestrator graphs to handle behaviour and state transitions.

Create a playable simulation of a simple autonomous agent (navigation and decision logic) using Orchestrator for behaviour scripting and integrate with a physics scene to study state machines and event handling.

tools.name: gustavopsantos/Reflex
tools.desc: Minimal dependency injection framework for Unity

cls.summary: Reflex is a lightweight dependency-injection (DI) library for Unity that helps decouple object creation from usage to make Unity projects more modular and testable.
cls.what_it_does: Reflex provides a fast, minimal inversion-of-control container for Unity projects with features such as scopes, bindings, resolving, source-generated optimisations and AOT-friendly behavior. It is used by adding installers and scopes in a Unity project to register and resolve dependencies at runtime (or during scene load), and is notable for performance comparisons against other Unity DI libraries and using Roslyn source generators to reduce reflection.
cls.trl_rationale: The repository is mature (created 2021), has many stars and active recent commits and releases, clear installation instructions and examples, and appears production-ready for Unity projects; this supports a production-ready TRL rather than an experimental rating.
prerequisites: Unity Editor (knowledge of Unity scenes and MonoBehaviour)
student_project_ideas: Build a small Unity simulation (e.g. a sensor-processing demo) where Reflex manages service lifetimes (sensor interfaces, data pipelines) to demonstrate decoupling and testability.

Create a modular robotics scene where different locomotion or control strategies are swapped via Reflex bindings and compare integration and testing effort between hard-wired and DI-managed implementations.

tools.name: mizorewww/laya-coreml
tools.desc: Local Laya typed decisions on Apple Core ML and Neural Engine. Validated ports, ~5 ms short decisions on M3 Max, reproducible speed and energy benchmarks.

cls.summary: Laya-CoreML runs Laya typed-decision models locally on Apple Silicon (Core ML / Neural Engine) to produce calibrated, token-free choice/score/yes-no answers with very low latency and energy use.
cls.what_it_does: Laya-CoreML loads pretrained Laya decision-model bundles (from Hugging Face) and executes them as Core ML programs on CPU, GPU or the Apple Neural Engine to answer constrained questions (choice/score/noul) in a single bidirectional forward pass. It is used via a Python API or CLI to perform fast, calibrated probabilistic decisions on-device without PyTorch/Transformers, and includes tooling for routing, batching, calibration, serving and conversion.
cls.trl_rationale: The README and repo show polished features, published PyPI package, Hugging Face bundles and performance/energy benchmarks, and the project has many stars demonstrating interest; however the repository is only ~59 days old so there is not yet a long track record of production use, limiting maturity to TRL 5.
student_project_ideas: Build an iOS/macOS prototype that uses Laya-CoreML to triage user support messages (choice/score) on-device and compare latency and energy against a cloud-based classifier.
Benchmark and profile Laya-CoreML bundles (ANE vs CPU/GPU) for a small engineered decision task, and produce a report on inference time, energy and accuracy, comparing FP16 and quantized bundles.

tools.name: outtable/confuse-9live
tools.desc: 🔥🔥🔥 专业版iOS混淆工具，马甲工具包、ipa静态分析工具（相似度对比、敏感词检测），提供试用版本，100%过机器审核，解决 AppStore 4.3，2.3.1问题，支持语言 c、c++、objc、dart、swift 并支持各种资源改名，混淆、傻瓜化操作、一键出包，提供良好的UI界面，支持多包管理一包一特征、支持Unity3d、cocos2d全家桶、swiftUI、flutter、虚幻等各种引擎。支持混淆.a/.framework/.xcframework，混淆比例95%，支持dSYM文件混淆和恢复功能，不影响bugly等各种在线崩溃收集，可持续迭代原工程。

cls.summary: A macOS tool for obfuscating and repackaging iOS apps and libraries (Swift/ObjC/C/C++/Dart), aimed at helping apps pass App Store review and produce multiple branded builds.
cls.what_it_does: This tool performs binary- and resource-level obfuscation and renaming for iOS apps and third‑party SDKs, supports a wide set of engines (Unity, Flutter, cocos, Unreal) and automates packaging (IPA) and signing workflows. It is delivered as a desktop app with a UI and offers both a free trial and paid commercial features (dSYM handling, compile acceleration, support and analytics), notable for its focus on App Store review workarounds and multi‑package 'alias' builds.
cls.trl_rationale: The repository is multi-year (created 2020), has many stars (1.6k), active recent pushes and describes a polished commercial product with free and paid editions, indicating production readiness and real users; README and website references show it is intended for real deployments.
prerequisites: familiarity with Xcode and iOS code signing / provisioning
knowledge of iOS build artifacts (IPA, dSYM, .framework, .xcframework)
basic experience with mobile app packaging and third-party SDKs
student_project_ideas: Compare how obfuscation affects symbol names and crash stacktrace quality by building a small Swift app, obfuscating it, generating dSYMs, and evaluating symbolication with and without the tool.
Integrate the tool into a simple iOS CI pipeline (Fastlane/GitHub Actions) and measure build time, app size and runtime behaviour differences before and after automated obfuscation.

tools.name: rulego/rulego
tools.desc: ⛓️RuleGo is a lightweight, high-performance, embedded, next-generation component orchestration rule engine framework for Go.

cls.summary: RuleGo is a Go-based, componentised rule engine and orchestration framework for building lightweight, high-performance IoT/edge and integration middleware.
cls.what_it_does: RuleGo lets developers define and run configurable 'rule chains' composed of reusable components to filter, transform, route and act on messages and events. It is used as an embedded library or standalone middleware to orchestrate data flows and integrate protocols (HTTP, MQTT, Kafka, gRPC, etc.), with features for dynamic loading, context isolation and high-concurrency execution.
cls.trl_rationale: The repository is over two years old, actively maintained (recent pushes), has substantial community interest (1.6k stars), documentation and many built-in components; this indicates production-ready maturity rather than an experimental prototype.
prerequisites: knowledge of networking/protocols (HTTP, MQTT, gRPC, Kafka)
familiarity with message-based architectures and orchestration concepts
student_project_ideas: Build an IoT data preprocessing pipeline that runs on a Raspberry Pi using RuleGo to filter, enrich and forward sensor data to a cloud Kafka topic, then visualise results in a dashboard.

Create a microservice orchestration lab where students implement a RuleGo rule chain that routes and transforms messages between HTTP, MQTT and a mock backend service, demonstrating hot-reload of rules and fault isolation.

tools.name: BabylonJS/Spector.js
tools.desc: Explore and Troubleshoot your WebGL scenes with ease.

tools.name: yossdotpro/removerized
tools.desc: AI Image Toolkit that runs fully in your browser — free, private, and offline-first.

cls.summary: Removerized is a browser-first AI image toolkit for private, offline background removal and upscaling that runs entirely on the client using ONNX Runtime Web.
cls.what_it_does: Removerized performs image background removal and upscaling in the browser by loading AI models into the client and running inference with ONNX Runtime Web (WASM). It caches models in IndexedDB for offline and repeated use, supports batch processing and quality controls, and requires no server or data uploads, making it notable for privacy-first, client-side image processing.
cls.trl_rationale: The project is over one year old, actively maintained with a significant star count and a live demo, shows an established install/run workflow and caching strategy, but lacks evidence of wide production deployments or formal releases that would justify TRL 7+.
prerequisites: Node.js and yarn for local development
student_project_ideas: Build a simple web photo-studio app that uses Removerized to batch-process product photos and exports transparent PNGs for an e‑commerce front-end.
Integrate Removerized into a small digital-twin or AR prototype to perform client-side background removal and upscaling of user images before texture-mapping them onto 3D models.

tools.name: YGYOOO/WorldX
tools.desc: One sentence creates an AI-driven world — generate maps, characters, and watch stories emerge on their own. 一句话生成一个AI自主驱动的世界.

cls.summary: WorldX is an open-source TypeScript project that generates and runs AI-driven virtual worlds from a single text prompt, producing maps, characters and emergent agent behaviour.
cls.what_it_does: WorldX uses LLMs and image-generation models to procedurally create a world (map, characters, rules) from one sentence and then runs a multi-agent simulation where characters make decisions, talk, remember and evolve over time.
