It is used by running the Node.js server and supplying API keys for the configured LLM/image models; notable aspects are the multi-model pipeline (separate roles for orchestration, image gen, vision review and simulation) and built-in tools to intervene (edit memories, inject events, create timelines).
cls.trl_rationale: The README states the project is in Alpha and 'core usable'; the repo is 7 months old with active development, examples and many stars, but it lacks evidence of long-term production deployments or stable releases, so TRL is in the alpha/early-use range.
prerequisites: API keys for OpenAI/Google/OpenRouter-style LLM and image services
student_project_ideas: Extend WorldX to log and visualise agent interaction graphs over time so students can analyse emergent social networks and behaviours using a graph library (e.g. D3.js) and SQLite exports.

Replace the simulation LLM with a smaller local model (or rate-limited API) and benchmark behaviour/compute trade-offs by running identical worlds with alternative models and comparing metrics (dialogue length, decision latency, memory usage).

tools.name: moonsharp-devs/moonsharp
tools.desc: An interpreter for the Lua language, written entirely in C# for the .NET, Mono, Xamarin and Unity3D platforms, including handy remote debugger facilities.

tools.name: Muesli-HQ/muesli
tools.desc: Muesli: agent-native local meeting transcription + dictation for macOS (Granola + WisprFlow + Littlebird alternative)

cls.summary: Muesli is a native macOS app for on-device dictation and meeting transcription with optional hosted AI summarisation and integrations.
cls.what_it_does: Muesli captures microphone and system audio on macOS, transcribes speech locally by default (with hosted provider options), and provides meeting notes, speaker labels, summaries and an Ask Meetings chat over saved transcripts. It is used as a desktop app (hotkey, press-to-talk, or recording) and notable for its privacy-first, on-device-first speech recognition and multiple provider integrations.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository is ~8.5 months old with active commits, many stars (1.6k) and releases, indicating a beta-level project used by multiple users; age under one year prevents rating above TRL 6 despite popularity.
prerequisites: Microphone and Screen Recording permissions for some features
Optional API keys/accounts for hosted AI providers
student_project_ideas: Build a pipeline that exports Muesli meeting transcripts and uses an NLP library (e.g. spaCy or Hugging Face) to automatically tag action items and assign them to project tasks.

Create an experiment comparing on-device and hosted ASR providers by running identical meeting recordings through Muesli's local ASR and a cloud ASR, then analysing word-error-rate and privacy trade-offs.

tools.name: sideeffects/HoudiniEngineForUnreal
tools.desc: Houdini Engine Plugin for Unreal Engine.

tools.name: pmndrs/react-postprocessing
tools.desc: 📬  Postprocessing for react-three-fiber

cls.summary: react-postprocessing provides React bindings for the postprocessing library to apply GPU-accelerated fullscreen visual effects in react-three-fiber scenes.
cls.what_it_does: It wraps the postprocessing effects library for use with @react-three/fiber so developers can compose effects like bloom, depth of field, noise and vignette as React components. It is used by adding an EffectComposer and effect components inside a three-fiber Canvas to produce high-performance fullscreen shader passes with minimal boilerplate. It is notable for integrating the postprocessing library’s performance optimisations (single-triangle fullscreen passes, MSAA, flexible blending) into a React-friendly API.
cls.trl_rationale: The repository was created in 2020, has strong community interest (1.6k stars), active recent commits and published docs, and is a maintained wrapper around the established postprocessing library; this indicates a mature, widely adopted project.
student_project_ideas: Create an interactive web demo that visualises a robot arm or drone model in three.js and use react-postprocessing to add depth-of-field and motion blur to evaluate how visual effects impact operator perception.
Build a small web-based digital twin dashboard that streams simulation data to a three-fiber scene and use postprocessing effects (bloom, color grading) to highlight system states and alarms.

tools.name: DT42/BerryNet
tools.desc: Deep learning gateway on Raspberry Pi and other edge devices

tools.name: kevinzakka/mink
tools.desc: Python inverse kinematics based on MuJoCo.

cls.summary: mink is a Python library that solves differential inverse kinematics for robots simulated with MuJoCo by formulating and solving a quadratic program for task objectives, limits and constraints.
cls.what_it_does: mink lets you specify tasks (pose, posture, COM, axis alignment), inequality limits (joint/velocity bounds, collision avoidance) and equality constraints, and at each timestep solves a QP for the joint-space velocity that best reduces task error while respecting limits. It is used as a runtime IK solver integrated with MuJoCo models and exposes examples for arms, hands, bipeds and multi-arm setups; notable points are native C code for frame transforms/Jacobians and support for elastic (soft) constraints.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository is over one year old, has substantial community interest (1.6k stars), published documentation and many runnable examples, active recent commits and demonstrated usage with multiple robot models; this indicates production-ready software suitable for real projects (TRL 7).
student_project_ideas: Implement closed-loop Cartesian control for a simulated UR5e in MuJoCo using mink to compute IK and validate tracking performance under joint limits and collisions.

Compare performance and robustness of mink's differential IK against Drake or Pinocchio IK on a dual-arm manipulation task (e.g. coordinated object handover) and report on convergence, constraint satisfaction and computation time.

tools.name: QwenAudio/Fun-ASR
tools.desc: Fun-ASR speech recognition models, with native Hugging Face Transformers support for Fun-ASR-Nano and separate FunASR, vLLM and llama.cpp deployment paths.

cls.summary: Fun-ASR is an open-source family of end-to-end automatic speech recognition models and deployment tooling (including Hugging Face Transformers support, on-device GGUF/llama.cpp and vLLM deployment paths) for multilingual, real-time and long-form transcription.
cls.what_it_does: Fun-ASR provides pretrained ASR checkpoints (including Fun-ASR-Nano and multilingual Fun-ASR-MLT-Nano) and software for running inference, streaming/real-time serving, speaker diarization, and multiple deployment backends (Transformers, FunASR runtime, vLLM, llama.cpp/GGUF). It is used by installing the Python/runtime packages or calling the native Transformers interface and is notable for multi-language and on-device deployment support plus example pipelines for production streaming and diarization.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository is ~11 months old and shows active development, released runtime versions, Hugging Face model checkpoints, runnable examples, and deployment guides; this indicates a beta-level, publicly usable project but not yet a long-established production standard, so TRL 6 is appropriate.
student_project_ideas: Build a realtime voice-command interface for a mobile robot: use Fun-ASR for speech-to-text on-device (llama.cpp/GGUF path) and ROS 2 to trigger robot behaviours.

Evaluate and compare recognition accuracy for regional accents: run batch inference with Fun-ASR-MLT-Nano and Whisper on a curated dataset of regional dialect samples and report error analysis and mitigation strategies.

tools.name: KoBeWi/Metroidvania-System
tools.desc: General-purpose framework for creating metroidvania games in Godot.

cls.summary: A Godot plugin that provides a map editor, map viewer and runtime helpers for building 2D grid-based metroidvania-style games and managing persistent objects and collectibles.
cls.what_it_does: Metroidvania System is an open-source addon for Godot (4.6+) that provides a world/map editor, map viewer, themed visuals and runtime support (object IDs, collectibles, scene linking and save integration) to simplify building grid-based metroidvania games. It is used inside the Godot editor and at runtime to visualise maps, assign scenes to rooms, track collectibles and persist object state; notable points are tight Godot editor integration and a compact VCS-friendly map format.
cls.trl_rationale: The project has been actively maintained since 2022, shows many stars and forks, targets a stable platform (Godot 4.6+), and the author states it evolved from tools used in a released game, indicating production-readiness rather than a throwaway prototype.
prerequisites: Familiarity with Godot engine (editor and project workflow)
student_project_ideas: Create a small 2D metroidvania level in Godot using Metroidvania System, implement room scenes and use the Map Viewer to display and navigate between them.
Extend the plugin's exported JSON map format to drive a procedural level generator or to create a minimap HUD that highlights discovered collectibles and player location.

tools.name: filippocalippo/StykAnimate-App
tools.desc: Free, open-source stick figure animation app for Windows, Linux and the browser. Opens Pivot and Stick Nodes projects.

cls.summary: StykAnimate is a free open-source stick-figure animation editor that runs on Windows, Linux and in the browser and can open Pivot and Stick Nodes projects.
cls.what_it_does: StykAnimate lets users create, pose and animate stick-figure characters with features like inverse kinematics, layered timelines, motion paths, particles and camera moves; it can build figures from basic primitives and export video and frame formats. It runs entirely locally (desktop app or in-browser), includes a Rust engine compiled to WebAssembly for rendering/codec work, and is notable for supporting many export formats and an offline-capable web app.
cls.trl_rationale: The project is active, cross-platform, has CI, packaged releases and a large star count indicating early adoption, but the repository is only 69 days old so by the TRL rules it cannot be rated above TRL 5 despite evident polish.
prerequisites: Rust toolchain (including wasm32 target and wasm-bindgen-cli)
Python 3.11+ for some build/packaging scripts (development only)

tools.name: Haskell-Things/ImplicitCAD
tools.desc: A math-inspired CAD program in haskell. CSG, bevels, and shells; 2D & 3D geometry; 2D gcode generation...

tools.name: Neywa-Labs/nativ
tools.desc: Nativ is an open-source local AI app for Mac. It runs open AI models on Apple Silicon, and nothing leaves your Mac.

cls.summary: Nativ is an open-source macOS app that runs LLMs and multimodal MLX models locally on Apple Silicon and exposes OpenAI-compatible inference endpoints without sending data off-device.
cls.what_it_does: Nativ provides a SwiftUI macOS application plus an embedded inference server (bundled mlx-vlm) to run language, vision and audio models locally on Apple Silicon. It is used as a private chat/vision app, model manager, and local OpenAI/Anthropic-compatible API for other tools and coding agents. Notable features include model discovery/download from Hugging Face, performance and system monitoring, extensions, and developer-facing endpoints for integrations.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository is active with many stars, detailed docs, and releases, and it bundles mlx-vlm for local inference, indicating a beta-level, usable project; however the repo is only 120 days old (under one year) so there's limited long-term production track record, limiting the TRL to at most 6.
prerequisites: Enough unified memory for chosen models
student_project_ideas: Build a small macOS assistant that uses Nativ's local OpenAI-compatible API to summarise engineering meeting notes and tag artifacts, integrating with a Git or Confluence export.

Create a plugin/extension for Nativ that monitors model memory usage and automatically suggests model swaps or quantisation settings for constrained Apple Silicon devices, and evaluate performance metrics.

tools.name: arpanghosh8453/open-dronelog
tools.desc: Drone Log analyzer: A high-performance universal dashboard application for organizing and analyzing DJI/Litchi flight logs privately in one place. Supports plugin for custom flight log formats. Built with Tauri v2, DuckDB, and React.

cls.summary: Open Dronelog is an open-source desktop/web application for importing, storing and analysing drone flight logs (DJI, Litchi, Airdata and similar) with interactive maps, telemetry charts and reporting.
cls.what_it_does: It ingests multiple drone log formats into a local DuckDB database and provides a high-performance React/Tauri dashboard for replaying flights, visualising telemetry, generating reports and tracking battery/maintenance data. It is used as a local-first desktop app (Tauri) or a self-hosted Docker web app and supports plugins for custom parsers and exports (CSV, GPX, KML).
cls.trl_rationale: Repository is actively developed, widely starred and provides desktop builds and a Docker deployment, indicating a beta-level, usable project; however the repo age is under one year (≈284 days), which limits it to TRL 6.
prerequisites: basic familiarity with Node.js/TypeScript and building web apps
understanding of DuckDB or SQL for queries and exports
student_project_ideas: Build a flight-safety dashboard that automatically flags flights exceeding configurable safety thresholds and exports incident reports, combining Open Dronelog with a simple rule-engine and PDF export.

Compare battery health estimation algorithms by extracting per-battery telemetry from Open Dronelog (DuckDB) and implementing capacity fade models in Python to validate against recorded full-charge capacity trends.

tools.name: Auburn/FastNoise2
tools.desc: Modular node graph based noise generation library using SIMD, C++17 and templates

cls.summary: FastNoise2 is a high-performance C++17 library that generates procedural noise via SIMD-optimised node graphs and includes a node editor (WASM and desktop) for building reusable noise pipelines.
cls.what_it_does: FastNoise2 produces coherent procedural noise (Perlin, Simplex, Cellular, fractals, domain warping, blends and modifiers) using a node-graph model that fuses operations into SIMD pipelines for maximum throughput. It is used as a library from C++ (with bindings for other languages) or via the provided Node Editor to design and serialize noise trees for textures, heightmaps, terrain and procedural content.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository is mature (created 2020, ~1.5k stars, active commits as recently as Nov 2026), provides releases and cross-language bindings and has benchmarking — evidence of production-ready use, so TRL 7 is appropriate.
prerequisites: basic understanding of SIMD concepts and build toolchains
student_project_ideas: Build a terrain generator that uses FastNoise2 node graphs to create tiled heightmaps and compare performance and memory usage between fused SIMD node graphs and a naïve per-noise-array approach.
Integrate FastNoise2 via its WASM Node Editor into a small web-based procedural texture tool that exports serialised node trees and applies them to a real-time WebGL/three.js scene.

tools.name: Mapsui/Mapsui
tools.desc: Mapsui is a .NET Map component for: MAUI, Avalonia, Uno Platform, Blazor, WPF, WinUI, Windows Forms, Eto Forms, .NET for Android and .NET for iOS

tools.name: voyager-so/vork
tools.desc: Headless 3D and VFX engine for agents. Research preview.

cls.summary: Vork is a headless, GPU-based 3D and VFX engine that lets AI agents author full scenes (shaders, materials, cameras, physics) as code and renders them via Vulkan/Metal.
cls.what_it_does: Vork provides a compact API that lets programs or agents define scene graphs, GPU shader programs and simulation hooks, then execute high-performance GPU rendering and compositing on Vulkan or Metal. It is notable for being written in Rust and Slang, optimized for agent-driven workflows, and for offering a cloud render option for users without local GPUs.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository is very new (created 12 days ago) and marked as a research preview; it has strong community interest (many stars) but no long track record or stable releases, so maturity aligns with early alpha.
prerequisites: familiarity with Slang (GPU shading language) helpful
student_project_ideas: Create an agent that generates and iteratively refines a short VFX shot in vork, then compare render times and image quality against a Blender EEVEE render.
Use vork to render procedurally generated visualisations of simulated agent behaviour (e.g. flocking) and produce a short film or data-visualisation pipeline that captures agent state per-frame.

tools.name: autonomous-ai/Personal-AI-Computer
tools.desc: Open-source AI computer builds, from 2-GPU desktops to 8-GPU servers: CAD, BOM, BIOS and build guides. Get the case kit with PCIe risers, or ask us for a free fit check.

cls.summary: A collection of open-source hardware designs, CAD, BOMs and step-by-step build and BIOS tuning instructions for multi‑GPU AI workstations and servers.
cls.what_it_does: This repository provides end-to-end build guides, CAD parts, bills of materials, BIOS tuning and GPU testing procedures to assemble 2–8 GPU AI workstations and rack servers for local model inference and training. It is used as a practical manual for sourcing parts, mechanical assembly, firmware/configuration and initial software setup, notable because the project is openly licensed and backed by a company that sells fit‑check and kits.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository is over one year old, has substantial community interest (1.5k stars), detailed build documentation, and the maintainers sell kits and offer fit checks — evidence of production use and real‑world deployments supporting a production‑ready TRL.
prerequisites: basic PC assembly and safety (ESD, power)
experience with Linux and GPU driver installation
student_project_ideas: Modify one of the 2× GPU build designs to add improved airflow or alternative cooling and measure GPU thermal performance and throttling under an LLM inference benchmark (combine with vLLM or llama.cpp).
Create an automated checklist and test script (BIOS settings, GPU link width, stress test) that validates a multi‑GPU build's readiness, and integrate results into a simple dashboard or report.

tools.name: gazebosim/gz-sim
tools.desc: Open source robotics simulator. The latest version of Gazebo.

cls.summary: Gazebo Sim is an open-source, high-fidelity robotics simulator that provides physics, rendering and sensor models for developing and testing robots in virtual environments.
cls.what_it_does: Gazebo Sim runs physics-based simulations of robots and environments, producing realistic sensor outputs and visualisation through a GUI or headless server. It is used via command-line tools, plugins, Python bindings and message/transport interfaces, and supports multiple physics engines and rendering backends. It is notable for its long heritage from Gazebo Classic and tight integration with robotics ecosystems (ROS/ROS 2) and modular Ignition/Gazebo libraries.
cls.trl_rationale: Gazebo Sim is derived from Gazebo Classic (over 16 years of development), the repository is multi-year old with many stars, active maintenance and components (physics, rendering, sensors) and is used widely in robotics research and projects; these facts support a mature, widely adopted tool (TRL 8) though not an absolute single industry standard.
prerequisites: familiarity with Linux and optionally ROS/ROS 2
student_project_ideas: Create and validate a ROS 2 node controlling a differential-drive robot in Gazebo Sim, and run SIL tests comparing expected odometry against simulated sensor outputs.
Build a simulated sensor fusion pipeline by adding IMU, camera and lidar plugins in Gazebo Sim and evaluating state estimation performance with different noise parameters.

tools.name: najmuzzaman-mohammad/gawkbot
tools.desc: open source grok bot. gawk bots automate your menial work via AI models and build you microapps to manage the outcome, so that you have a false sense of control.

cls.summary: gawkbot is an open-source desktop and mobile agent platform that turns described workflows into autonomous micro‑apps which run locally and ask for human approval before taking external actions.
cls.what_it_does: gawkbot discovers agent CLIs on your machine (Claude Code, Codex, Opencode and many others), wraps them as managed bots, and builds small microapps with schedules, approvals, typed data stores and integrations. It is used as a local automation/agent orchestration layer with a UI (Mac app and optional iPhone companion) and sandboxed per-bot directories to keep credentials and actions separate.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository is active with many stars, signed macOS builds and an iOS companion, and provides install/build instructions—evidence of a beta-quality, usable project. However it is under one year old so it lacks a longer track record required for TRL 7+.
prerequisites: Xcode (to build the iOS app / companion)
student_project_ideas: Build a gawkbot that automates weekly data extraction from a public API, stores results in the bot's typed tables, and exposes a dashboard; evaluate reliability and approval latency compared to a cron-based script.

Integrate gawkbot with a local LLM (e.g. Ollama) to prototype an approval-gated CI automation bot that prepares commit messages and opens pull requests, then measure false-positive/negative approval prompts.

tools.name: tin2tin/Pallaidium
tools.desc: PALLAIDIUM — a generative AI movie studio, seamlessly integrated into the Blender Video Editor (VSE), enabling end-to-end production from script to screen and back.

cls.summary: PALLAIDIUM is a free Blender Video Sequence Editor add-on that provides an end-to-end generative-AI movie production workflow from script to images, video, audio and back.
cls.what_it_does: The add-on automates film prototyping inside Blender's VSE: it converts text or media inputs into screenplays, generates images and video frames, synthesises speech and music, and supports batch rendering and refinement. It is used as a Blender plugin that orchestrates local AI models (and model components like ControlNet, LoRA and OpenPose) to produce and manage generative assets and render queues within the Blender environment.
cls.trl_rationale: The repository is several years old, has a large star count (1.5k+), active recent commits and documented install and usage instructions, and targets real users (Blender add-on with dependency installers), indicating production-ready maturity rather than an experimental prototype.

basic Python / Blender add-on installation knowledge
student_project_ideas: Use PALLAIDIUM in a short course project to generate a storyboard and animated proof-of-concept from a written scene, then film a short live-action version and compare timing, shot composition and emotional cues.

Integrate PALLAIDIUM output with additional Blender compositing or a simple CV pipeline to evaluate automated lip-sync accuracy and compare synthetic speech models (use dataset of lines and recorded performances).

tools.desc: Rust bindings for ROS 2

tools.name: livliv-dev/player
tools.desc: A lightweight 2.5D character player for the web, with lip sync and webcam face tracking.

cls.summary: A lightweight, open-source WebGL2-based 2.5D character player for webpages that supports lip sync and in-browser webcam face tracking.
cls.what_it_does: The project renders 2.5D/flat-style characters in a browser canvas and provides APIs for expressions, actions, lip sync (microphone/audio/video) and webcam face tracking. It's provided as a small, dependency-free core (WebGL2) with optional imports for MediaPipe face tracking and adapters for VRM and PNGTuber formats, intended for embedding characters in pages, stream overlays or apps.
cls.trl_rationale: The repository is feature-rich with examples, an npm package and documented API, showing early adopters and a usable demo, but it is only 13 days old so it lacks a longer production track record; this limits the TRL to about 5.
prerequisites: basic WebGL or browser canvas knowledge
optional: familiarity with MediaPipe and three.js for adapters
student_project_ideas: Build a web demo that uses the player with MediaPipe face tracking to drive expression data and stream the character's lip-synced reactions to recorded audio, then evaluate latency and robustness across browsers.
Create a small interactive kiosk or AR overlay that swaps between PNGTuber and VRM bodies using the same Player API and measures memory / performance differences between formats.

tools.name: sail-sg/envpool
tools.desc: C++-based high-performance parallel environment execution engine (vectorized env) for general RL environments.

cls.summary: EnvPool is a high-performance C++ engine that runs many reinforcement-learning environments in parallel and exposes Gymnasium/dm_env Python APIs for fast batched simulation.
cls.what_it_does: EnvPool manages pools of simulated environments (Atari, MuJoCo, Box2D, DeepMind Control, ViZDoom, etc.) and executes them in parallel using a C++ thread-pool and pybind11 bindings to give very high throughput for training RL agents. It is used as a drop-in, vectorized environment backend compatible with common RL libraries and supports synchronous/asynchronous and single/multi-player modes, plus batched rendering and XLA/JAX integration. Its notable features are C++ performance (millions of steps/sec on high-core machines), wide environment coverage, and direct compatibility with Gymnasium and dm_env APIs.
cls.trl_rationale: The project is multi-year (created 2021), actively maintained with recent commits, PyPI wheels for multiple platforms, many stars and documented integrations/examples and an accompanying arXiv paper — indicating mature, production-quality use in the RL community.
prerequisites: C++ development knowledge for custom environments
student_project_ideas: Benchmark parallel training throughput and sample efficiency by integrating EnvPool with Stable-Baselines3 to train a MuJoCo control task and compare wall-clock training time against a subprocess-based vector environment.

Build a reinforcement-learning pipeline where EnvPool supplies parallelized simulated data for a robotics control policy, then validate policy robustness with a noisy simulation-to-reality transfer experiment using domain randomization.

tools.name: fastplotlib/fastplotlib
tools.desc: Next-gen fast plotting library running on WGPU using the pygfx rendering engine

cls.summary: fastplotlib is a Python library for GPU-accelerated interactive plotting and large-scale scientific visualization using the pygfx/wgpu rendering stack.
cls.what_it_does: fastplotlib provides an expressive API for rendering large, interactive plots on the GPU, enabling fast exploration of large datasets and real-time visualisation for scientific acquisition systems. It is used from desktop UIs (Qt/glfw/wx) and JupyterLab, and is notable for leveraging pygfx and WGPU backends (Vulkan/Metal/DX12) to achieve high performance.
cls.trl_rationale: The repository is several years old, has many stars, examples, documentation and listed academic users, indicating active use; however the README explicitly states the project is in a 'late alpha' stage, so it does not yet meet the criteria for fully production-ready TRL 7.
prerequisites: GPU drivers supporting Vulkan/Metal/DX12 or WGPU
student_project_ideas: Build an interactive data-exploration dashboard that streams sensor or simulation time-series and uses fastplotlib for GPU-accelerated real-time plotting, combined with a small Flask or Jupyter front-end.

Compare performance and visual fidelity of large point-cloud or heatmap visualisations by implementing the same dataset views in Matplotlib, VisPy and fastplotlib and measuring frame-rate and memory usage on different GPUs.

tools.name: robotmcp/ros-mcp-server
tools.desc: Connect AI models like Claude & GPT with robots using MCP and ROS.

cls.summary: ROS-MCP-Server lets large language models (Claude, GPT, Gemini, etc.) observe and command ROS robots by exposing ROS topics, services, actions and parameters through the MCP protocol without changing robot code.
cls.what_it_does: The server exposes a ROS (ROS 1 / ROS 2) robot's runtime interface (topics, services, actions, parameters, sensor/state data) over the Model Context Protocol (MCP) so LLM-based clients can both observe and control the robot. It is used by running the rosbridge node alongside an existing ROS system and connecting any MCP-compatible client (Claude, GPT clients, Gemini, etc.). Notable aspects are automatic discovery of custom ROS types and explicit support for multiple ROS distributions and MCP clients.
cls.trl_rationale: The repository is over a year old, has substantial community interest (1.5k stars, active development, recent commits) and published demos showing industrial and simulated robot use (videos), indicating it is production-ready for integration rather than an early prototype.
prerequisites: Familiarity with LLM/MCP clients or basic LLM client usage
student_project_ideas: Build a lab exercise where students connect an MCP-compatible LLM client to a simulated robot (Gazebo or Isaac Sim) via ROS-MCP-Server to implement a natural-language navigation task using Nav2 and evaluate safety checks.
Create a capstone project that logs LLM-driven robot actions through the MCP server and implements automated verification tests comparing commanded actions to sensor data for anomaly detection.

tools.name: ProxyShard/ShardBrowser
tools.desc: Free, open-source anti-detect browser launcher for web scraping and multi-accounting. By the ShardX team (formerly ProxyShard). Engine-level fingerprint spoofing in Chromium 157 (WebGL / WebGPU / Client Hints / fonts / TLS), 220+ device profiles bundled, stable QUIC + WebRTC over SOCKS5.

cls.summary: ShardBrowser is an open-source launcher that runs patched Chromium instances with engine-level fingerprint and networking spoofing for large-scale web scraping and multi-account workflows.
cls.what_it_does: ShardBrowser patches Chromium to apply fingerprint overrides in the browser engine (Blink, V8 and network stack) and manages isolated profiles, proxies and persistent state for many simultaneous browser identities. It is used via a desktop UI, a local HTTP API, an MCP server and language SDKs (Python, Node, Rust), and is notable for engine-level spoofing (not JS shims) plus SOCKS5 UDP relay / QUIC / WebRTC support.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository is active, has many stars/forks and an extensive README showing usable features and SDKs, but it is younger than one year (created 171 days ago) so a maximum TRL of 6 is appropriate; there is no public evidence here of long-term production deployments or stable major-version history.
prerequisites: understanding of HTTP/SOCKS proxies and browser automation
student_project_ideas: Compare and measure fingerprint and bot-detection signals between ShardBrowser and an unmodified Chromium/Playwright instance using automated tests and public detector pages (browserleaks, fingerprint.com) and report which signals differ.

Build a small scraper that uses ShardBrowser's SDK (Node or Python) to manage multiple profiles and proxies, then log and analyse how geolocation, client hints and WebRTC behaviour change with different proxy endpoints.

tools.desc: Building generation addon for blender

tools.name: FrigadeHQ/yogurt
tools.desc: Private AI meeting notes that stay on your computer. A free, open-source alternative to Granola for Mac, Windows and Linux.

cls.summary: Yogurt is a free, open‑source desktop app that records call audio, creates local transcripts and AI summaries, and keeps all data and processing on your computer.
cls.what_it_does: Yogurt captures microphone and system audio from meetings, produces live transcripts using whisper.cpp (and Apple SpeechAnalyzer on supported Macs), and generates summaries and Q&A with a local open-weight model via llama.cpp. It is notable for running transcription and summarisation entirely locally (after model download), offering privacy-by-default and an MCP socket for other local assistant apps to read notes.
cls.trl_rationale: The README and release artifacts show a working cross‑platform Electron app with integrations (whisper.cpp, llama.cpp) and installers, but the repository is only 6 days old so there is not yet a track record of stable releases or production deployments; that age limits the TRL to at most 5.
prerequisites: familiarity with desktop apps and OS permissions (mic, accessibility, calendar)
local model files and runtime for whisper.cpp and llama.cpp
student_project_ideas: Build a small evaluation comparing Yogurt's local transcription accuracy (whisper.cpp) with cloud services on recorded engineering meetings and analyse error types and impacts on meeting minutes.
Extend Yogurt's MCP interface by writing a local assistant that automatically extracts action items and exports them to a lightweight task tracker (e.g. a CSV or simple web service).

tools.name: Vincentqyw/cv-arxiv-daily
tools.desc: 🎓Automatically Update CV Papers Daily using Github Actions

cls.summary: A regularly updated GitHub repository that automatically collects and publishes recent computer-vision and robotics arXiv papers (grouped by topic and year) using GitHub Actions.
cls.what_it_does: The project scrapes arXiv for new papers in computer vision, robotics and related keywords and generates markdown archives organised by year and topic. It runs automatically (via GitHub Actions) to keep lists current and links to PDFs and code when available, making it a convenient curated literature feed for researchers and students.
cls.trl_rationale: The repository is long-lived (created 2021), actively maintained with recent pushes and many stars (1519), and is functionally complete as an automated literature aggregator, matching a beta-level maturity; it lacks evidence of formal production deployments so TRL 6 is conservative.
prerequisites: familiarity with GitHub Actions to run/modify automation
student_project_ideas: Extend the repo to add keyword-based notification emails or Slack alerts for new papers in a selected subfield (combine with GitHub Actions and a simple web service).
Build a mini web app that consumes the markdown archive and visualises trends (publication counts by topic over time) and links to code repositories, using the repo as the data source.

tools.name: thetahealth/mirobody
tools.desc: Mirror your body in data. One standard, every source, one complete picture of you: a self-hosted health record built from lab reports, wearables and genetics, with every number traced to its source and a built-in MCP server. Run it with Docker and one LLM key, or keep every model local on llama.cpp.

cls.summary: Mirobody is an open-source, self-hosted personal health record that ingests lab reports, wearables and genetic files, standardises measurements and exposes the data to AI agents over an MCP server.
cls.what_it_does: Mirobody collects health data from many sources (lab PDFs, wearables, genomics) and normalises names and units to a common standard, keeping each reading traced to its source. It runs as a web app or local Docker stack, offers local or cloud LLM integration (including llama.cpp) for document parsing and question answering, and includes an MCP server so agents can query the record.
cls.trl_rationale: The project is active, well-documented, provides Docker deployment, a live demo and Codespaces instructions, and supports local models (llama.cpp); these indicate a beta-level maturity. The repository is under one year old so per the TRL rules it should not be rated above 6 despite strong community interest (stars and forks).
prerequisites: Docker & Docker Compose (or Python 3.12 and PostgreSQL for no-Docker route)
familiarity with model API keys or local LLM tooling (llama.cpp) for full features
student_project_ideas: Build an extension that imports real-time wearable data (e.g. Garmin) into Mirobody and visualises trends in the web UI, demonstrating data ingestion, unit standardisation and the MCP query flow.

Integrate a local LLM (via llama.cpp) to automate structured extraction from synthetic lab report PDFs and evaluate accuracy against the bundled standardiser, producing a short report on errors and provenance tracing.

tools.name: FreeOpcUa/opcua-asyncio
tools.desc: OPC UA library for python >= 3.10

cls.summary: opcua-asyncio is a Python library that implements an asynchronous OPC UA client and server for connecting, reading, writing and subscribing to industrial devices and systems using the IEC 62541 protocol.
cls.what_it_does: The project provides an asyncio-based implementation of the OPC UA (IEC 62541) binary protocol offering high-level Client, Server, Node and Subscription APIs and low-level access to UA structures. It is used to build OPC UA clients and servers in Python for industrial automation, telemetry and digital-twin workflows, and notable for its async API, test coverage and compatibility with multiple OPC UA stacks.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository is long-lived (created 2018), actively maintained with recent pushes, substantial community (1.5k stars, 460 forks), comprehensive examples and documented testing against many OPC UA stacks; these indicate mature, widely used software rather than an experimental prototype.
prerequisites: Python 3.11+ and familiarity with asyncio and async/await
Basic understanding of OPC UA concepts (nodes, address space, subscriptions, NodeId)
student_project_ideas: Build an OPC UA gateway that reads sensor data from a simulated OPC UA server (using opcua-asyncio) and forwards selected metrics to a time-series database like InfluxDB for dashboarding.

Create an automated testbench that uses opcua-asyncio to run verification scenarios against an OPC UA server implementation (node read/write, subscriptions, certificate authentication) and reports pass/fail results.

tools.name: zalo/CascadeStudio
tools.desc: A Full Live-Scripted CAD Kernel in the Browser

cls.summary: Cascade Studio is a browser-based, scriptable CAD kernel and IDE that exposes the OpenCASCADE modelling kernel (OCCT) for creating, visualising and exporting B-rep 3D models using JavaScript or OpenSCAD-like code.
cls.what_it_does: It provides a live, code-driven CAD environment in the browser (and a standalone 'cascade-core' engine) that supports primitives, CSG, sweeps, lofts, fillets, measurements and STEP/STL/OBJ import-export. Users write JavaScript or OpenSCAD, see realtime 3D results, scrub modelling history, and embed the core engine in other web apps; notable points are full OCCT access, a standard modelling library, URL-sharing of code and an Agent API for automation.
cls.trl_rationale: The project is multi-year (created 2020), has substantial community interest (1.5k stars), active maintenance through 2026, a published reusable package ('cascade-core'), and robust features (OCCT access, import/export, IDE). These indicate production-readiness for engineering prototyping, though not an industry de-facto standard.
prerequisites: basic CAD modelling concepts (B-rep, CSG, sketches)
familiarity with web tooling for building and serving a web app
student_project_ideas: Create parametric mechanical parts (e.g. a mounting bracket) defined in JavaScript, export STEP for CNC or CAD integration, and render with Three.js to produce a parts catalogue.

Integrate cascade-core into a small web dashboard that loads sensor data and generates geometry parametrically (e.g. pipe routing or bracket resizing) to demonstrate a simple digital thread from data to CAD.

cls.summary: dRonin is an open-source autopilot flight-controller firmware for multirotor and fixed-wing UAVs, targeted at racing, acro and autonomous flight and research.
cls.what_it_does: dRonin provides low-level flight control firmware that runs on a variety of flight controller boards to stabilise and navigate multirotor and fixed‑wing vehicles; it is flashed to embedded controllers and configured via companion tools. It is notable for supporting many OpenPilot/TauLabs-era targets and for being positioned as production‑ready GPL firmware for both hobby and research UAV use.
cls.trl_rationale: The README calls the project 'production ready' and it has substantial community interest (many stars), but the repository is only ~8–9 months old so it lacks the multi‑year track record and ecosystem needed for TRL 7+. Evidence is primarily README-supported target list and popularity.
prerequisites: basic electronics and flight controller hardware knowledge
familiarity with UAV concepts and tuning (PID/autotune)
student_project_ideas: Port dRonin to a supported flight controller board and demonstrate closed‑loop altitude hold using an onboard barometer and IMU, documenting the build and tuning process.

Integrate dRonin flight firmware with an external companion computer (Raspberry Pi) to implement and test an autonomy routine (waypoint navigation or vision‑based obstacle avoidance) and evaluate end‑to‑end latency and reliability.

tools.name: iart-ai/motion-skills
tools.desc: 56 open-source skills that teach your AI coding agent to make motion graphics, animation & video — kinetic typography, data-viz, explainers, TikTok/Reels, WebGL, Manim. 19 installable packs. By iart.ai, the AI motion agent.

cls.summary: A collection of 56 open-source 'skills' that teach AI coding agents how to generate motion graphics, animations and short videos using packages for WebGL, Manim, canvas and web animation tooling.
cls.what_it_does: This repository packages reusable agent workflows (called skills) that encode the craft of motion design — timing, easing, safe areas, frame-accurate rendering and render-verify loops — so an AI coding agent can produce animations and video output from prompts. Skills install per-pack (via npx or agent plugin) and are discoverable by many agents; notable features include deliver-and-verify render checks and 19 specialised packs (TikTok, data-animation, WebGL, Manim, etc.).
cls.trl_rationale: The repo is active, well-documented and popular (1.5k stars, frequent pushes) and provides installable packs and integrations, indicating beyond prototype status, but it is only ~5 months old and lacks evidence of long-term production adoption or versioned stable releases, so TRL is limited to Beta (6).
prerequisites: familiarity with AI coding agents (Claude, Cursor, Codex) or plugin MCP integration
basic web animation or Manim knowledge for customizing skills
student_project_ideas: Use the data-animation pack plus a CSV dataset to build an agent-driven pipeline that generates narrated, frame-accurate data-visualisation videos for a course assessment.
Combine the Manim skill pack and an MBSE model export to create short animated explainers of system behaviour (state changes or control logic) for documentation and stakeholder communication.

tools.name: NVIDIA-ISAAC-ROS/isaac_ros_visual_slam
tools.desc: Visual SLAM/odometry package based on NVIDIA-accelerated cuVSLAM

cls.summary: Isaac ROS Visual SLAM is an NVIDIA-accelerated ROS 2 package that performs real-time stereo visual(-inertial) SLAM / odometry on Jetson and other GPU platforms.
cls.what_it_does: The package provides GPU-accelerated visual SLAM and visual-inertial odometry (VSLAM/VIO) using stereo cameras (and optional IMU) to estimate robot pose and build sparse maps for loop closure. It is delivered as ROS 2 nodes and libraries targeting real-time robotics applications, notable for using NVIDIA's cuVSLAM GPU implementations to increase feature extraction and matching throughput on Jetson and CUDA platforms.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository has been actively maintained since 2021, is produced by NVIDIA, has many stars/forks, published documentation and benchmark claims (KITTI) and targets deployed platforms (Jetson), indicating a mature, widely used codebase rather than a prototype.
prerequisites: NVIDIA CUDA-capable GPU or Jetson hardware
student_project_ideas: Integrate Isaac ROS Visual SLAM with a small differential-drive robot (ROS 2) to compare VSLAM odometry against wheel odometry and IMU, quantifying drift and designing a sensor-fusion filter.
Use recorded stereo/IMU datasets to evaluate robustness of cuVSLAM vs ORB-SLAM2 on low-texture indoor scenes, and produce failure-mode analysis and recommendations for sensor placement.

tools.name: lakshaybhushan/vecto3d
tools.desc: A super simple tool to convert your SVG's to 3D models.

cls.summary: Vecto3d is a browser-based tool that converts SVG artwork into editable 3D models and exports them as images, animations, or 3D files (STL/GLB/GLTF).
cls.what_it_does: Vecto3d takes vector SVG files in the browser and generates extruded 3D geometry with adjustable depth, bevel and material properties, previewed using a WebGL viewport. It is used via a web UI (drop/paste/select an SVG), realtime controls, and export options for images, animations and production 3D files; notable for running fully client-side with no account or upload.
cls.trl_rationale: The project is a production web app (deployed, active repo with many stars and recent commits) and provides export formats for downstream workflows, indicating real-world readiness; repository age (~611 days), high star count and active development support a production-ready TRL.
prerequisites: modern web browser with WebGL (Chrome or Firefox recommended)
SVG artwork or vector editor to produce SVG files
student_project_ideas: Convert a vector schematic or logo into a 3D printable part using Vecto3d, then refine and validate the STL in a CAD/printing toolchain (e.g. FreeCAD or PrusaSlicer).

Build a small web portfolio that programmatically imports SVG diagrams of an engineered product, converts them to 3D with Vecto3d, and displays interactive GLB previews using three.js or react-three-fiber.

tools.name: autonomous-ai/openharness
tools.desc: The ultimate harness for coding agents and beyond. All your agents. All your machines. One command center. Start with code, then follow your curiosity and build across disciplines: CAD, circuits, robots, games and music.

cls.summary: OpenHarness is an open-source command-centre and harness for running and coordinating coding agents across machines, designed to connect agents to real tools like CAD, circuit simulators, robots and game engines.
cls.what_it_does: OpenHarness runs agents in isolated harnesses (tmux sessions) on one or more machines, provides a native desktop app and CLI to manage them, and routes encrypted peer‑to‑peer connections (with Cloudflare TURN and a relay fallback). It is used to orchestrate multiple LLM-based agents, link them to local tools (Blender, CircuitJS, device CLIs) and to run local models and agent workflows across heterogeneous hardware.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository is active, popular (≈1.5k stars), provides downloadable desktop apps and clear architecture and build instructions, indicating a beta-level project; however the repo is only ~105 days old so it lacks the multi-year production track record required for TRL 7+.
student_project_ideas: Create an agent workflow that automates a simple CAD design iteration: an LLM agent edits Blender scene parameters via the OpenHarness Blender harness and commits each design variant to a worktree branch, then visualises differences.

Build a multi-machine experimental pipeline where an agent runs a CircuitJS simulation on a remote machine and reports results locally, using OpenHarness to link the machines and record transcripts for verification.

tools.name: qq362946/Fantasy
tools.desc: C # Game Framework, but not limited to games. Can be used for non game business development

cls.summary: Fantasy is a high-performance C# game server framework that provides ECS architecture, multi-protocol networking, service discovery and tools for building distributed multiplayer game backends and related services.
cls.what_it_does: Fantasy provides a zero-reflection, Native AOT-friendly C# framework for building distributed game servers with built-in ECS, multi-protocol networking (TCP/KCP/WebSocket/HTTP), service discovery, control center tooling and AI-oriented developer skills. It is used by writing handlers, entities and systems in C# (optionally integrating with Unity clients) and is notable for compile-time source generation to avoid runtime reflection and for shipping an AI Skill to assist development.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository is multi-year (created 2023-06), has substantial community interest (≈1.5k stars, active pushes up to 2026), comprehensive docs and a CLI, and describes production-focused features (service discovery, deployment guides), indicating production-ready maturity.
prerequisites: familiarity with server-side programming and optionally Unity client development
optional: MongoDB for persistence and Docker/Kubernetes for deployment
student_project_ideas: Build a simple multiplayer lobby and matchmaking server using Fantasy and a Unity client to demonstrate roaming, service discovery and cross-server calls.

Implement a distributed game event (e.g. world-boss announcement) using Fantasy's sphereEvent and persist player state to MongoDB, then deploy locally with Docker to show scaling/replication behaviour.

tools.name: placemark/placemark
tools.desc: A flexible web-based editor, converter, visualization tool, for geospatial data

cls.summary: Placemark is a web-based open-source editor and viewer for creating, converting, visualising and sharing geospatial (GeoJSON) data.
cls.what_it_does: Placemark lets users open, edit, validate and visualise GeoJSON and other common map data formats in a browser-backed web app, with optional routing and geocoding services. It is used as a developer-extendable local app or hosted instance (placemark.io) and notable for integrating MapLibre GL JS basemaps, optional routing providers and AT Protocol sharing for saved maps.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository is over three years old, has substantial community interest (1.4k stars), an active maintainer (recent pushes) and a public production instance (placemark.io) described in the README, indicating production-ready maturity.
prerequisites: familiarity with GeoJSON and map concepts
optional: Geocode Earth token or routing service configuration
student_project_ideas: Build a browser-based tool that imports sensor CSV data, converts it to GeoJSON and visualises time-series tracks in Placemark, adding basic filtering and export functionality.
Integrate Placemark with an open routing service (OSRM or openrouteservice) to create a route-planning demo for civil engineering students comparing shortest vs fastest route across a study area.

tools.name: rohitg00/k8sgames
tools.desc: Learn Kubernetes by playing. Deploy pods, fix CrashLoopBackOff, type real kubectl commands: 3D browser game, no install needed.

cls.summary: K8s Games is a browser-based 3D simulation that teaches Kubernetes and kubectl by letting users deploy resources, diagnose incidents and run real kubectl commands in-game.
cls.what_it_does: It provides an interactive, WebGL/three.js 3D environment where learners place Kubernetes resources, inspect YAML/status, run real kubectl commands, and respond to simulated incidents (CrashLoopBackOff, ImagePullBackOff, node NotReady, etc.). Notable features are a kubectl command bar with tab completion, a 3D architecture whiteboard (K8s Draw) that exports YAML/PNG and sharing via URL, and an Architecture Advisor that scores cluster designs.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository is actively maintained, has a playable public site, many stars and forks and a substantial codebase (no build step) indicating real-world use, but it is under one year old (created ~275 days ago) so demonstrated maturity is best described as beta (TRL 6).
prerequisites: modern web browser with WebGL support
student_project_ideas: Extend the K8s Draw export to generate Helm charts from a drawn architecture and validate them by deploying to a local kind/minikube cluster.
Create an instrumented lab where students solve a sequence of incident scenarios and submit automated logs/commands for grading, integrating the game with an LMS webhook to record progress.

tools.name: ARahim3/mlx-tune
tools.desc: Fine-tune LLMs on your Mac with Apple Silicon. SFT, DPO, GRPO, Vision, TTS, STT, Embedding, and OCR fine-tuning — natively on MLX. Unsloth-compatible API.

cls.summary: mlx-tune is a Python toolkit for fine-tuning language, vision, audio and OCR models natively on Apple Silicon using the MLX backend with an Unsloth-compatible API.
cls.what_it_does: It lets developers run supervised and advanced fine-tuning methods (SFT, DPO, GRPO, ORPO, JEPA, TTS, STT, embeddings, OCR, etc.) locally on macOS using Apple's MLX framework and export models in formats like Hugging Face and GGUF. It is used as a local prototyping bridge so the same training scripts can run on Mac and later be scaled to cloud NVIDIA/Unsloth environments; notable for its Apple Silicon native MLX integration and Unsloth-compatible API.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository is ~318 days old with active development, substantial stars (1.5k), a documented v0.6.0 feature list and examples indicating a usable beta; age under one year prevents assigning TRL >6 despite strong activity.
prerequisites: macOS on Apple Silicon (M1/M2/M3/M4/M5) or MLX-compatible runtime
familiarity with Hugging Face transformers and fine-tuning concepts
student_project_ideas: Prototype fine-tuning a small LLM on a domain-specific dataset locally with mlx-tune, export to GGUF and compare inference speed/accuracy using llama.cpp on a student laptop.
Fine-tune a Whisper-based STT model with mlx-tune on recorded lab demonstrations, then integrate the transcriptions into a simple ROS2 node or data pipeline to automate annotation.

tools.name: codewriter-packages/Tri-Inspector
tools.desc: Free inspector attributes for Unity [Custom Editor, Custom Inspector, Inspector Attributes, Attribute Extensions]

cls.summary: Tri Inspector is an open-source Unity package that provides many custom inspector attributes and editor utilities to improve how fields and objects are displayed and validated in the Unity Editor.
cls.what_it_does: Tri Inspector supplies a large collection of C# attributes and editor UI components so Unity developers can customise inspectors (read-only fields, validation, dropdowns, table lists, dictionaries, info boxes, etc.) without writing custom editor windows. It installs as a git package, integrates with Unity's UI Toolkit, and includes a project-wide validator that can run in CI to report issues as JSON. The package is notable for its extensive sample browser, prefab-aware behaviour and a validator suited for automated pipelines.
cls.trl_rationale: Active repository since 2022 with ~1.5k stars, recent commits in 2026, a documented install path, samples, CI/validator features and an established user base—evidence of maturity and adoption consistent with a widely used tool (TRL 8).
prerequisites: Basic understanding of Unity packages and UI Toolkit
student_project_ideas: Create a Unity simulation (robot, vehicle or interaction) and use Tri Inspector attributes to build polished inspectors for tuning parameters and to validate scene assets using the Tri Validator in a CI pipeline.

Develop a custom tool or editor extension for an engineering visualization (e.g. asset browser or parameter tuning window) that uses Tri Inspector attributes and UI Toolkit styling to improve usability and demonstrate prefab-aware editing.

tools.name: ollaya-dev/ollaya
tools.desc: Jev-compatible API server for open decision models. Ollama for decision models: pull and serve 29 model families (Laya, pplx-decider, Clef, Winnow, coba...) locally or self-hosted behind /v1/systemone. The TypeSafe SDK works unchanged: set its base URL and pick an open model. CLI, desktop app, Docker, MCP server, public bench.

cls.summary: Ollaya is a self‑hosted server that pulls and serves open decision models with a Jev‑compatible API so existing TypeSafe clients and agents can request calibrated decisions locally.
cls.what_it_does: Ollaya runs small, author-published decision model graphs (ONNX or GGUF via llama.cpp) behind a local daemon exposing the TypeSafe/ J ev / /v1/systemone wire format; it returns calibrated probabilities for typed questions about JSON states, designed for fast, local decision-making for agents. It is notable because it is Jev-compatible (drop-in for TypeSafe clients), focuses on decision models rather than free-form text generation, and supports serving to MCP clients and local inference backends (ONNX Runtime, llama.cpp).
cls.trl_rationale: The project is active, well documented and has wide interest (many stars and features), but the repository is only ~55 days old so there is not yet a long track record or stable release history — limiting a conservative TRL to 5 (alpha in use).
prerequisites: familiarity with HTTP APIs and JSON
basic understanding of decision models / calibration and TypeSafe/Jev concepts
experience with running CLI tools or Docker; optional GPU knowledge for performance tuning
student_project_ideas: Integrate Ollaya with a simple agent (e.g. a rule-based or LLM-based assistant) to triage support tickets: compare latency, calibration and downstream action accuracy when using Ollaya decision models vs calling an LLM.
Build an experiment that benchmarks calibration and response time of several open decision models served by Ollaya (ONNX vs GGUF/llama.cpp) on CPU and GPU, and visualise results in a dashboard.

tools.name: ShlkOfTheRa/scarab-osd
tools.desc: MWOSD - UAV HUD

cls.summary: MWOSD is open-source on‑screen display firmware for UAV flight controllers that overlays telemetry (GPS, voltage, RSSI, timers, etc.) onto video feeds.
cls.what_it_does: MWOSD runs on OSD hardware connected to flight controllers and video transmitters to draw flight telemetry and HUD elements on the pilot's video feed. It supports many flight stacks (Betaflight, ArduPilot, PX4, iNav, KISS and more) and is configured via a GUI configurator and firmware install tools, making it notable for broad interoperability across hobby and professional UAV platforms.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository demonstrates a mature feature set and wide interest (many stars) and lists support for many flight stacks, but the repo is only ~8.5 months old so it lacks the longer track record required for TRL 7+; thus it fits a beta-level maturity.
prerequisites: basic embedded C/C++ and toolchain knowledge (cross-compilation, flashing)
familiarity with UAV flight stacks (Betaflight/ArduPilot/PX4) and UART/SPI/I2C connections
basic electronics and soldering for installing OSD hardware
student_project_ideas: Integrate MWOSD with a small quadrotor running ArduPilot and extend the HUD to display a custom sensor (e.g. optical flow or airspeed), demonstrating end-to-end telemetry acquisition, OSD overlay and flight validation.

Build a configurable GUI workflow that automates firmware builds and flashing for different flight stacks and OSD hardware, then evaluate trade-offs in latency and bandwidth for different telemetry update rates.

tools.name: jofizcd/Soul-of-Waifu
tools.desc: 🌌 Give a soul to your favorite characters. Soul of Waifu is a desktop roleplay & AI companion app featuring Live2D/VRM avatars, voice chat & local LLM. Evolve together across immersive chat, RPG adventures, and your desktop.

cls.summary: Soul of Waifu is an open-source desktop AI companion and roleplay app that runs local LLMs and supports Live2D/VRM avatars, voice chat, a tabletop RPG engine, and an autonomous desktop agent.
cls.what_it_does: The project provides a desktop application for creating persistent AI characters that can converse by text and voice, host RPG-style sessions, and act as an autonomous desktop agent with capabilities like screen reading, mouse/keyboard control and sandboxed script execution. It is notable for running primarily locally (supporting local LLM runtimes such as llama.cpp), offering a persistent multi-layer memory architecture, and extensibility via Python plugins and external MCP servers.
cls.trl_rationale: The repository is mature and active (created 2023, many stars and recent pushes), has documented releases and a feature-rich README describing production-like features (desktop agent, plugins, integrations), which indicates production-ready software rather than an early prototype.
prerequisites: local LLM model/runtime (e.g. llama.cpp) and model files
familiarity with desktop OS permissions (mouse/keyboard access)
student_project_ideas: Create a plugin that lets the Soul Companion automatically organise and tag simulation output files (e.g. from CFD runs) and produce a short summary report.

Extend the app with a sandboxed tool that runs automated code-quality or safety checks on an engineering project repository and logs findings to the character's persistent memory for later discussion.

tools.name: 2shady4u/godot-sqlite
tools.desc: GDExtension wrapper for SQLite (Godot 4.x+)

cls.summary: A maintained GDExtension plugin that exposes SQLite databases to Godot 4.x projects so games and apps can store and query data from inside Godot.
cls.what_it_does: This project provides a native C++ wrapper (GDExtension/GDNative) that lets Godot 4.x projects open, query and manage SQLite databases without rebuilding the engine. It is distributed as a plugin/addon with prebuilt binaries and a demo project, and is notable for cross-platform support (desktop, mobile and HTML5) and availability via the Godot Asset Library.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository created in 2019, over 1.4k stars and active development with recent pushes and releases and distribution via the Godot Asset Library indicate a mature, well-used open-source project suitable for production use.
prerequisites: basic Godot Engine familiarity (scene tree, scripting)
student_project_ideas: Build a Godot-based telemetry viewer that logs runtime metrics (FPS, input events) into SQLite and displays charts in-game.
Implement a save/load system for a Godot simulation that stores entity states in an SQLite database and provides query-based report generation.

tools.name: VAST-AI-Research/TripoSplat
tools.desc: TripoSplat converts a single 2D image into high-quality and variable number of 3D Gaussians, developed by TripoAI.

cls.summary: TripoSplat converts a single 2D image into a set of 3D Gaussian splats and exports them for use in 3D viewers and real-time applications.
cls.what_it_does: TripoSplat takes one input image and generates a high-quality, variable number of 3D Gaussians (splat primitives) that represent the scene, with an adjustable trade-off between visual fidelity and rendering cost. It is used as an inference-only Python pipeline: download model checkpoints, run the example or Gradio demo, then export .ply/.splat files for visualization or integration into AR/VR, games and simulation environments. Notable features are support for very large gaussian counts (up to 262,144), minimal code surface (~2 files), near-zero external dependencies, and official ComfyUI workflow support.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository is recent (created ~169 days ago) but shows substantial community interest (≈1.5k stars), clear docs, example scripts, model checkpoints on HuggingFace and explicit integrations (ComfyUI, Gradio), which supports a beta maturity (TRL 6); not yet a long-term production track record so TRL 7+ is not justified.
prerequisites: ability to download model checkpoints from HuggingFace/ModelScope
student_project_ideas: Create a pipeline that takes student photographs, runs TripoSplat to produce .splat exports, and visualises them in a web viewer (SparkJS) while measuring rendering cost vs quality at different Gaussian counts.

Compare TripoSplat-generated splats with a NeRF reconstruction for the same object: evaluate visual fidelity, file size, and rendering performance, and present trade-offs for use in AR/VR applications.

tools.name: benman1/generative_ai_with_langchain
tools.desc: Build production-ready LLM applications and advanced agents using Python, LangChain, and LangGraph. This is the companion repository for the book on generative AI with LangChain.

cls.summary: A companion code repository of Jupyter notebooks and examples that teaches how to build production-ready LLM applications and multi-agent systems using Python, LangChain and LangGraph.
cls.what_it_does: This repository provides runnable notebooks, scripts and worked examples from the book 'Generative AI with LangChain' that demonstrate building RAG pipelines, multi-agent architectures, testing and deployment patterns for LLM applications. It is used as a learning and reference resource (not a standalone engineering product) and is notable for being a maintained, book-aligned collection covering many providers and LangChain/LangGraph patterns.
cls.trl_rationale: The repository is a mature, actively maintained companion to a published book, created in 2023 and still updated in 2026; it has substantial community interest (many stars and forks) and stable example material, which supports a production-ready educational TRL rather than an experimental prototype.
student_project_ideas: Implement a small RAG pipeline using the repository's examples to index a departmental document set and compare retrieval quality across two vector stores (e.g. FAISS vs. Milvus) and two LLM providers.

Build and evaluate a simple two-agent workflow (one assistant for query parsing, one for retrieval/answering) from the notebooks, adding logging/observability and automated tests to demonstrate deployment-readiness.

tools.name: obsei/obsei
tools.desc: Open source, privacy-first Voice of Customer analytics. A self-hosted alternative to Enterpret and Unwrap that strips PII from feedback before any LLM sees it.

cls.summary: Obsei is an open-source, self-hosted platform for extracting, redacting and analysing customer feedback with built-in privacy controls and optional local or cloud LLMs.
cls.what_it_does: Obsei ingests text feedback from many sources (app stores, GitHub, tickets, webhooks, CSV, email, etc.), redacts PII and pseudonymises authors, enriches records with language/sentiment/intent/themes using local or remote models, and routes or stores results to sinks such as webhooks, databases and issue trackers. It is notable for a privacy-first design (PII redaction, encrypted storage, egress controls) and flexible BYO-model support (local classifiers, embeddings and many LLM endpoints).
cls.trl_rationale: The repository was created in 2020, is actively maintained (recent pushes), has substantial community interest (1.4k stars, many integrations and docs) and production-oriented features (encryption, audit, server, Studio), indicating a mature, widely adopted open-source project rather than an experimental prototype.
prerequisites: familiarity with LLM endpoints and API keys
basic devops (Docker, service configuration, environment variables)
student_project_ideas: Build a privacy-preserving pipeline that ingests support tickets, uses Obsei to redact PII and classify issues, then automatically files prioritized bugs in GitHub or Jira.
Compare theme extraction quality by running Obsei with (a) its offline embedder and (b) a multilingual local embedding model, and produce an evaluation report with metrics and example clusters.

tools.name: kitops-ml/kitops
tools.desc: An open source DevOps tool from the CNCF for packaging and versioning AI/ML models, datasets, code, and configuration into an OCI Artifact.

cls.summary: KitOps is an open-source CNCF tool and CLI that packages and versions AI/ML projects (models, datasets, code, configs) as OCI artifacts so teams can store, sign, and distribute them via container registries.
cls.what_it_does: KitOps bundles everything required to reproduce or deploy an AI/ML project into a layered, versioned OCI artifact called a ModelKit (or ModelPack). It provides a CLI to pack, push, pull, inspect and unpack these artifacts, supports cryptographic signing and attestations, and integrates with registries, CI/CD and security tooling to manage model lifecycle and governance. It is notable for using OCI as the storage format and for CNCF governance and ModelPack compatibility.
cls.trl_rationale: The project is governed by the CNCF, has a substantial star/fork community and active recent commits, documentation and integrations (Cosign, ModelPack, registries), and positions itself for production CI/CD use; these indicate production-ready maturity rather than an experimental prototype.
prerequisites: familiarity with container/OCI registries and image concepts
student_project_ideas: Create a CI/CD lab exercise that uses KitOps to pack a trained model into a ModelKit, push it to a registry, and deploy a simple model-serving workload on Kubernetes; evaluate rollback and attestation workflows.
Extend a ModelKit by writing a plugin or script that adds custom security attestations (e.g. automated bias or vulnerability scan reports) and integrates them into the KitOps push/pull pipeline.

tools.name: playcanvas/splat-transform
tools.desc: CLI tool and library for 3D Gaussian splat processing and conversion

cls.summary: SplatTransform is a TypeScript library and CLI for reading, converting, editing and streaming 3D Gaussian splat (point-based) formats and producing outputs suitable for web delivery, GLB, voxel collision data and analysis.
cls.what_it_does: It converts between many Gaussian-splat and point-cloud formats (PLY, SOG/Streamed SOG, SPZ, GLB, etc.), applies transformations/filters/merges, generates LOD/streamed outputs and can produce voxel collision data and WebP renders. It is provided as both a programmatic library (Node/browser) and a CLI, and includes guides, an API reference, a Docker backend for GPU rasterization, and a browser frontend (SuperSplat) for one‑off conversions.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository is >1 year old, has substantial community interest (≈1.4k stars), active recent activity, comprehensive docs, API reference, Docker backend and a browser frontend (SuperSplat) using it — indicating production-ready maturity rather than an experimental prototype.
prerequisites: familiarity with 3D point clouds / Gaussian splats
optional: Docker and GPU/Vulkan for backend rasterization
student_project_ideas: Create a web viewer that converts a large PLY point-cloud to Streamed SOG with multi-LOD using splat-transform, then stream and display it in a PlayCanvas or three.js viewer to evaluate load times and visual quality.

Use splat-transform to convert photogrammetry output to sparse voxel collision (.voxel.bin/.voxel.json) and integrate the collision data into a simple simulation or robotics navigation demo to test collision queries and performance.

tools.desc: On-device LLM execution in React Native with Vercel AI SDK compatibility

cls.summary: A React Native library that runs on-device large language models and other AI primitives (text, embeddings, speech, vision) with compatibility for the Vercel AI SDK.
cls.what_it_does: Provides on-device AI providers and APIs for React Native apps so developers can run text generation, embeddings, transcription, speech synthesis and vision models locally on iOS and Android. It exposes functions compatible with the Vercel AI SDK (generateText, streamText, embed, etc.) and includes provider-specific packages (Apple, Android/ML Kit, Core AI, Llama) and devtools for telemetry profiling.

tools.name: Edgenesis/shifu
tools.desc: Kubernetes-native IoT gateway

cls.summary: Shifu is a Kubernetes-native, protocol‑agnostic IoT gateway that runs device drivers as pods (DeviceShifu) to bring devices into a Kubernetes cluster and enable edge/cloud digital-twin applications.
cls.what_it_does: Shifu provides an open, production-oriented IoT gateway that runs on Kubernetes and represents devices as CRDs and DeviceShifu pods so teams can manage devices, drivers and data using cluster tooling. It supports many industrial protocols (MQTT, OPC UA, LwM2M, RTSP, Siemens S7, etc.), is deployable from Raspberry Pi to cloud clusters, and is notable for treating device drivers as Kubernetes-native workloads (digital twins) rather than separate middleware.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository active since 2021 with many stars (1.4k), recent commits (Nov 2026), CNCF landscape listing and documentation; these indicate production-readiness and community adoption consistent with TRL 7.
prerequisites: familiarity with MQTT/OPC UA or other industrial protocols for device integration
student_project_ideas: Build a small end-to-end digital-twin demo by deploying Shifu on a Raspberry Pi to ingest MQTT sensor data, visualise time-series in a lightweight dashboard, and implement a Kubernetes-native DeviceShifu driver for a simulated sensor.
Integrate an OPC UA industrial device simulator with Shifu running in a minikube cluster and create an automated test suite that validates data collection and edge-to-cloud message flows.

tools.name: emqx/neuron
tools.desc: Open source industrial connectivity server

cls.summary: Neuron is an open-source Industrial IoT connectivity server that bridges shop-floor protocols to modern data platforms (primarily via MQTT) and runs as a small edge-native binary or container.
cls.what_it_does: Neuron connects heterogeneous industrial devices (Modbus, OPC UA, Ethernet/IP, Siemens S7, IEC 60870-5-104, BACnet, etc.) and converts their data into MQTT and other northbound formats, enabling integration with MES/SCADA/historians and analytics. It is used as an edge agent or gateway (native binary or container), supports hot-pluggable plugins and built-in stream processing via eKuiper, and is notable for a tiny footprint and broad protocol coverage.
cls.trl_rationale: The project is multi-year (created 2021), has many stars/forks, active recent commits and published releases, explicit integrations (EMQX, NanoMQ, eKuiper) and a commercial distribution (NeuronEX), indicating production use and maturity beyond beta.
prerequisites: familiarity with Linux and container workflows
basic knowledge of MQTT and industrial protocols (Modbus, OPC UA, etc.)
ability to build C projects with CMake
student_project_ideas: Build an edge gateway lab: deploy Neuron in a container on a Raspberry Pi that collects Modbus TCP data from a PLC simulator and publishes it to an MQTT broker, then visualise the data with a Grafana dashboard.
Implement a small rules pipeline using Neuron + eKuiper to detect anomalies from simulated sensor streams and forward alerts to an MQTT topic consumed by a cloud analytics service.

tools.name: joey-zhou/xiaozhi-esp32-server-java
tools.desc: 小智ESP32的Java企业级管理平台，提供设备监控、音色定制、角色切换和对话记录管理的前后端及服务端一体化解决方案

cls.summary: A Java-based enterprise server and management platform that provides backend services, real-time connectivity, OTA and AI/voice pipelines for ESP32-based IoT devices.
cls.what_it_does: Xiaozhi ESP32 Server Java provides a multi-module, dual-process backend and web UI to manage ESP32 devices, handle WebSocket/MQTT real‑time audio streams, OTA updates, voice STT/TTS pipelines, LLM integrations and a RAG knowledge store. It is deployed as Docker or from source and notable for supporting many AI providers, local models, device orchestration and MCP tool-protocol extensions for large-scale device fleets.

Build an integration that connects ESP32 sensors to the server and a simple dashboard: collect telemetry into the existing stack (MySQL/Redis/Qdrant) and implement a predictive maintenance demo that raises alerts based on simple thresholds or a trained classifier.
