tools.name: BradyAJohnston/MolecularNodes
tools.desc: Toolbox for molecular animations in Blender, powered by Geometry Nodes.

cls.summary: Molecular Nodes is a Blender add-on and Python package that imports molecular structure and trajectory data and produces editable, procedural visualisations using Blender Geometry Nodes.
cls.what_it_does: It reads structural biology files (PDB, mmCIF, AlphaFold models), molecular dynamics topologies/trajectories, oxDNA output and cryo-EM maps, then creates Blender Geometry Nodes-based styles to visualise, animate and render those molecules. It is used either through a Blender GUI extension or programmatically via a Python API (with optional bpy) and is notable for producing fully editable procedural node trees so styles can be combined and animated inside Blender.
cls.trl_rationale: The project has existed since 2022, has many stars (1414), public releases and documentation, CI/tests across Blender versions, and listed academic citations — evidence of production-ready use by others rather than a one-off prototype.
prerequisites: Blender (familiarity with the UI and Geometry Nodes)
basic knowledge of molecular file formats (PDB/mmCIF) and MD concepts
student_project_ideas: Use Molecular Nodes and MDAnalysis to load an MD trajectory, build a Geometry Nodes-driven animation showing conformational change, and render a short annotated video comparing simulation frames with computed measurements (RMSD, distances).

Create a Blender pipeline that imports cryo-EM density maps and fitted models with Molecular Nodes, then produces publication-quality stills and animations to illustrate structural interpretations for a structural biology or bioengineering report.

tools.name: awaescher/OllamaSharp
tools.desc: The easiest way to use Ollama in .NET

cls.summary: OllamaSharp is a .NET client library that wraps the Ollama API to call local or remote LLM models from C# applications with streaming and model-management support.
cls.what_it_does: OllamaSharp provides awaitable .NET bindings for every Ollama API endpoint so developers can generate text, run chats, stream responses, manage models (list, pull, push) and use vision models from C#. It is used as a library in .NET apps and integrates with .NET features like Native AOT and source-generator-based tool support, and is notable for streaming, progress reporting and being recommended/integrated with Microsoft projects.
cls.trl_rationale: The repo is mature (created Oct 2023, >1 year old), has many stars and recent activity, and the README shows adoption/integration in Microsoft projects; this demonstrates production-readiness though it's not an industry-standard platform itself.
prerequisites: access to an Ollama server or remote Ollama API
basic knowledge of LLM concepts (chat, streaming, embeddings)
student_project_ideas: Build a .NET chatbot frontend that uses OllamaSharp to run a local Ollama model with streaming replies and log conversations to a database for later analysis.
Create a structured QA system that indexes engineering documents (PDFs) with embeddings from an Ollama model via OllamaSharp and evaluates retrieval accuracy on engineering queries.

tools.name: alexgaoth/awesome-reverse-engineered
tools.desc: Don't reverse engineer it twice. 17,000+ open-source tools built by reverse engineering closed apps, APIs, devices, protocols, file formats, games and AI tools. Search site + agent skill + MCP server, refreshed nightly.

cls.summary: A large, regularly refreshed curated index of open-source projects that reimplement or reverse-engineer closed apps, protocols, devices, file formats and APIs.
cls.what_it_does: This repository gathers links and metadata for thousands of open-source projects created by reverse engineering proprietary software, hardware and protocols and exposes a searchable website and an agent skill for programmatic access. It helps engineers discover existing unofficial clients, device drivers, protocol implementations and preservation work so they don't repeat previous effort; notable features are the nightly refresh, a browsable web index and an agent skill (npx) for integration with automation/agents.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository is very new (created 37 days ago) so can't be judged as production-proven; however it already aggregates 17k+ projects, has a searchable site and an agent skill which indicate active development and early adoption, supporting an Alpha-in-use rating.
prerequisites: node (for the agent skill) or ability to browse the static site
student_project_ideas: Use the index to find an unofficial client or protocol implementation for an IoT device and create a lab that demonstrates secure integration of that device into an MQTT/OPC UA pipeline.

Pick a reverse-engineered file format implementation from the list and build a converter to an open standard (e.g. convert a proprietary map or config file into JSON or GeoJSON) and compare parsing robustness with an existing tool like ImHex.

tools.name: datadrivenconstruction/OpenConstructionERP
tools.desc: Open-source construction ERP - BOQ, PDF/CAD/BIM takeoff, AI cost matching, 293 guided cases. 120,000+ priced positions, 44 languages, 190+ modules, cost data for 40+ markets. AGPL-3.0. pip install openconstructionerp

cls.summary: OpenConstructionERP is an open-source, self-hosted construction ERP that combines BOQ management, BIM/DWG/PDF takeoff, cost databases and 4D/5D scheduling for estimating and project control.

Evaluate the platform's AI cost-matching by running the same BOQ across two regional cost databases and comparing price differences and quality scores, documenting how LLM connectors affect accuracy.

tools.name: viniciusgerevini/godot-aseprite-wizard
tools.desc: Godot Editor plugin to help import Aseprite animations to AnimationPlayers, AnimatedSprites and SpriteFrames.

cls.summary: A Godot Editor plugin that automates importing Aseprite animation files into Godot AnimationPlayer, AnimatedSprite(2D/3D) and SpriteFrames resources.
cls.what_it_does: The plugin provides importer and inspector docks to convert Aseprite (.ase/.aseprite) files into Godot SpriteFrames, textures, tileset textures and AnimationPlayer tracks, preserving tags, frame timing and layer selection. It is used inside the Godot editor (GDScript plugin) to simplify re-importing and to map Aseprite tags and layers to Godot animation constructs.

student_project_ideas: Build a 2D game prototype in Godot that uses the plugin to import Aseprite character animations and then implement an AnimationPlayer-driven state machine for player actions.
Create an asset-pipeline demo that imports tiled sprites from Aseprite as Tileset/Atlas textures and uses them to assemble a level, showing workflow from Aseprite to Godot tilemaps.

tools.name: tsinghua-fib-lab/AgentSociety
tools.desc: AgentSociety 2 is a modern, LLM-native agent simulation platform designed for social science research and experimental design. It provides a flexible framework for creating and managing intelligent agents in simulated environments.

cls.summary: AgentSociety is an open-source Python platform for running LLM-driven multi-agent simulations and executable social‑science experiments, with a Ray-based scalable runtime and tools for experiment replay and analysis.
cls.what_it_does: AgentSociety provides a framework to create, run and replay simulations of many LLM-powered agents (Silicon Participants) and orchestration agents (AI Social Scientists). It is used by writing agent specifications and environment modules, running them on a Ray-backed runtime, and analysing experiments with built-in replay (JSONL + DuckDB) and skill/tool integrations. Notable features include LLM-native design, multiple reasoning/router patterns, MCP support and a VS Code research workbench.
cls.trl_rationale: The project is over one year old, has active development, published papers, documentation and a pip package (agentsociety2), and substantial community interest (1.4k stars), indicating beta-level maturity; there is not yet evidence of large-scale industrial adoption required for higher TRLs.
prerequisites: familiarity with Ray for scalable execution
student_project_ideas: Implement an experiment comparing different agent reasoning patterns (e.g., ReAct vs Plan‑Execute) in a simulated social space and analyse emergent behaviours using the built-in replay + DuckDB pipeline.
Integrate a simple robotics environment (ROS 2 / Gazebo mock or a gym-like wrapper) with AgentSociety to prototype human–robot multi-agent interaction scenarios and evaluate coordination strategies.

tools.name: m0n0x41d/haft

cls.what_it_does: Haft creates a durable, versioned project memory and governance layer for agent workflows, encoding problems, compared options, human decisions and supporting evidence with decay rules and MCP gates. Build an MCP adapter that connects Haft to a simulated robot-development pipeline (e.g. ROS tools) to capture design decisions and trace them to code and test artifacts for a mechatronics capstone.

tools.name: peterdsharpe/AeroSandbox

Create an MDO workflow that co-optimises airfoil shape (via XFoil integration) and mission trajectory for a solar-electric glider, and validate predicted performance against simple flight-test or high-fidelity CFD results.

tools.name: xtreme1-io/xtreme1
tools.desc: Xtreme1 is an all-in-one data labeling and annotation platform for multimodal data training and supports 3D LiDAR point cloud, image, and LLM.

cls.summary: Xtreme1 is an open-source web platform for creating and managing multimodal annotated datasets including 2D images and 3D LiDAR point clouds, with built-in pre-labeling models and dataset curation tools.
cls.what_it_does: Xtreme1 provides an integrated UI and backend to annotate images, 3D LiDAR point clouds and sensor-fusion datasets, manage ontologies and attributes, run pre-labeling (auto-annotate) models, and inspect/curate datasets and model results. It is typically deployed with Docker Compose and includes connectors / examples using popular perception toolkits and storage services; notable aspects are explicit support for LiDAR-camera fusion workflows and built-in model containers for pre-labeling and visualization.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository is long-lived (created 2022), actively maintained with many stars and recent pushes, provides release packages and Docker-based deployment, and documents built-in model containers and integrations; these indicate production-readiness rather than a small demo project.
prerequisites: optional NVIDIA GPU drivers and NVIDIA Container Toolkit to run model containers
student_project_ideas: Use Xtreme1 to build a labeled LiDAR+camera dataset from open KITTI/nuScenes samples, then train an open-source 3D detection pipeline (OpenPCDet) and compare results before/after manual correction of pre-labels.

Integrate Xtreme1 annotation exports with a ROS2 perception node to create a closed-loop dataset-collection and evaluation workflow for a small mobile robot, demonstrating sensor-fusion annotation and V&V of detection outputs.

tools.name: ngxson/wllama
tools.desc: WebAssembly binding for llama.cpp - Enabling on-browser LLM inference

cls.summary: wllama is a WebAssembly/WebGPU binding around llama.cpp that lets you run LLM inference (including multimodal, speech and tool-calling) directly in a web browser or JS environment.
cls.what_it_does: wllama provides a TypeScript/JavaScript API and WebAssembly binaries that expose llama.cpp models to browser and Node environments, offering OpenAI-compatible endpoints, embeddings, multimodal (image/audio) input, speech (TTS/ASR), realtime sessions and tool-calling. It is used by installing the npm package or building the wasm artifacts and embedding the library into a web app; notable features include WebGPU offload, worker-based inference to avoid UI blocking, and model-splitting for large models.
cls.trl_rationale: The project is >2 years old, actively maintained with many stars, an npm package, demo apps and documented releases, indicating production-ready maturity; evidence includes WebGPU support, multimodal features and prebuilt package on npm.
prerequisites: basic knowledge of WebAssembly and browser security headers
student_project_ideas: Build a browser-based engineering assistant that ingests CAD/technical text and provides searchable embeddings and question-answering using wllama for embeddings and a simple React UI.

Create a realtime voice-controlled data-entry interface for a simulated IoT device where sensor data and voice commands are processed locally in the browser with wllama handling ASR/transcription and intent routing to a mock backend.

tools.name: WooshiiDev/HierarchyDecorator
tools.desc: Lightweight Unity Plugin transforming the Hierarchy into what it should be. Adds headers, styles, icons and more.

cls.summary: A Unity Editor extension that enhances the Hierarchy window with headers, styles, icons and other visual aids to make scene structure easier to read.
cls.what_it_does: Hierarchy Decorator modifies Unity's Hierarchy window to add visual features such as styled headers, breadcrumbs, component icons, layer/tag selectors and alternating backgrounds. It is installed as a Unity package (git or openupm) and configured via a ScriptableObject or Preferences; everything is optional and highly customisable. The plugin is notable for broad feature coverage, UPM support and active community adoption (many stars and releases).
cls.trl_rationale: The repository is mature (created 2020) has many stars and active maintenance (recent pushes, packaged releases and UPM install instructions), indicating production-quality editor tooling used by teams; it lacks evidence of being an industry-standard ecosystem component, so TRL 7 is appropriate.
prerequisites: Basic familiarity with the Unity Editor
student_project_ideas: Create a team Unity project that uses Hierarchy Decorator to enforce and visualise a scene naming/style convention, and extend it by adding custom icons for project-specific MonoBehaviours.
Implement a small tool that reads component state (e.g. enabled/disabled, missing scripts) and uses Hierarchy Decorator to display warnings or health indicators for objects in a simulation scene.

tools.name: TerriaJS/terriajs
tools.desc: A library for building rich, web-based geospatial 2D & 3D data platforms.

tools.name: playcanvas/editor
tools.desc: Browser-based visual editor for building WebGL, WebGPU, WebXR apps

cls.summary: PlayCanvas Editor is a browser-based visual editor for building WebGL/WebGPU/WebXR 3D applications and interactive scenes.
cls.what_it_does: The Editor provides a visual, scene-based environment to author, edit and run real-time 3D/WebXR applications in the browser, with an asset pipeline, scene graph, and code editing hooks. It is used by running a local dev server or the hosted playcanvas.com service and integrates with the PlayCanvas Engine and UI libraries; notable features include WebGPU/WebGL rendering and an MCP integration for AI-assisted workflows.
cls.trl_rationale: The project is several years old (repo created 2020 and actively maintained), has a substantial user base and stars, and powers a public hosted service (playcanvas.com); the README and integrations show a mature codebase and test suite, indicating wide adoption rather than an experimental prototype.
prerequisites: Node.js (for local development) and basic frontend tooling
student_project_ideas: Create an interactive WebXR inspection application that loads a CAD-derived glTF model into a PlayCanvas scene and adds measurement and annotation tools for a digital-twin-style demo.
Build a small sensor-driven dashboard by integrating a simulated IoT data feed with a PlayCanvas scene to visualise live telemetry (combine with a simple Node.js server or a Timeseries DB).

tools.name: szenergy/awesome-lidar
tools.desc: 😎 Awesome LIDAR list. The list includes LIDAR manufacturers, datasets, point cloud-processing algorithms, point cloud frameworks and simulators.

cls.summary: A long‑running, curated GitHub list of LIDAR manufacturers, datasets, point‑cloud libraries, algorithms and simulators useful as a reference for LIDAR-related engineering work.
cls.what_it_does: This repository collects and organises links to LIDAR hardware, datasets, point‑cloud processing libraries, algorithms (segmentation, SLAM, detection), and simulators so users can find existing tools and resources quickly. It is used as a browsable reference (README and GitHub Pages) rather than as runnable software and is notable for its breadth, curation and long history.
cls.trl_rationale: The repository is mature and long‑running (created 2020), has many stars, an active history of updates and a published GitHub Pages view, indicating community interest and curation rather than an experimental toy — appropriate for a TRL ~6 (beta/reference resource).
prerequisites: basic knowledge of LIDAR and point clouds
ability to read and follow links / install referenced projects (varies by item)
student_project_ideas: Use the listed open datasets and a library (e.g. Open3D or PCL) to implement and compare two point‑cloud ground‑segmentation algorithms on urban LiDAR scans.
Build a small simulated sensor pipeline using one of the linked simulators and a ROS 2 driver to collect synthetic point clouds for perception algorithm testing.

tools.name: shner-elmo/TradingView-Screener
tools.desc: A package that lets you create TradingView screeners in Python

cls.summary: A Python library that queries TradingView's official API to build custom market screeners and retrieve many fields (prices, indicators, fundamentals) without web-scraping.
cls.what_it_does: The package provides a Query API to request screener data (stocks, crypto, forex, options, CFDs, etc.) directly from TradingView and returns tabular results (Pandas-friendly). It supports thousands of data fields, multiple timeframes per field, SQL-like filtering, ordering/offset/limit, and optional real-time access when you pass browser session cookies.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository created in 2022 and actively maintained with many stars (1.3k), published docs and clear usage examples; shows production-grade maturity and real users, so it appears production-ready rather than a fragile prototype.
prerequisites: basic familiarity with Pandas and HTTP APIs
(optional) browser session cookies for real-time data
student_project_ideas: Build a small data ingestion pipeline that uses tradingview-screener to collect time-series and indicator fields for a basket of stocks and store them in a time-series database (e.g. InfluxDB) for later analysis.

Implement and backtest a simple technical-indicator-based trading strategy by fetching multi-timeframe indicator columns from tradingview-screener and evaluating performance with a Python backtesting library.

tools.name: joshuafuller/ATAK-Maps
tools.desc: Map sources for ATAK: satellite, topo, street, nautical, aeronautical and overlay maps, each tested the way ATAK loads tiles.

cls.summary: A curated collection of map tile definitions and installers for the ATAK mobile mapping app, with a live explorer and packaged offline releases.
cls.what_it_does: Provides ready-made map sources (satellite, topo, street, nautical, aeronautical and overlay tiles) formatted and tested for use in ATAK, plus a web map explorer to preview and install maps on devices. It is used to add, distribute and package offline maps for ATAK users and developers, notable for its large collection of tested tile sources and automated release packaging.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository is multi-year (created 2020), actively maintained with recent pushes and automated releases, widely starred and used by the ATAK community; this indicates production-ready tooling for its niche rather than an experimental prototype.
prerequisites: ATAK (Android) installed to use the maps
basic familiarity with tile-based map sources and GIS concepts
student_project_ideas: Create a custom ATAK map pack for a local study area by adding new tile sources, packaging them as an offline release, and evaluating download/caching performance on Android devices.
Integrate ATAK-Maps tiles with a UAV mission-planning workflow: produce mission overlays in GIS, add them as ATAK overlays, and demonstrate end-to-end situational awareness in field trials.

tools.name: peonist-ai/halogen-flash-server
tools.desc: Local inference that behaves like a frontier API: Qwen3.8-Flash-Next on AMD Strix Halo plus small NPU models, over the OpenAI and Anthropic APIs on one port.

cls.summary: halogen-flash-server is a specialised local LLM server that runs Qwen3.8-Flash-Next (and compatible GGUF) optimised for the AMD Strix Halo to provide a fast OpenAI/Anthropic-compatible inference API on one port.
cls.what_it_does: It provides a high-performance local inference server that exposes an OpenAI/Anthropic-compatible API while running highly tuned kernels for the AMD Strix Halo GPU and selected small NPUs. It is used to serve long-context agent sessions and large checkpoints (including direct GGUF) with emphasis on throughput and low-latency first tokens; the project ships documentation, measured benchmarks and a prebuilt image for a supported host.
cls.trl_rationale: The repository provides extensive docs, measured benchmarks, a published image and active development (many stars and recent pushes) indicating alpha usage by early adopters; however the project is only 83 days old so it lacks the longer track record and stable releases required for TRL 6+.
prerequisites: AMD Strix Halo (Ryzen AI Max+ 395) or equivalent supported hardware
Linux system administration and GPU runtime (ROCm/HIP) knowledge
familiarity with running local LLMs and managing large model checkpoints
student_project_ideas: Benchmark the latency and throughput of halogen-flash-server versus a general-purpose local LLM runtime (e.g. llama.cpp or vLLM) on identical prompts and report trade-offs for long-context agent workloads.
Integrate halogen-flash-server with an open-source multi-agent harness to measure end-to-end agent turn times and design caching/partitioning strategies for a constrained embedded-like host.

tools.name: Agentshire/Agentshire
tools.desc: OpenClaw / QClaw  plugin that visualizes AI agents as 3D NPCs in a game town — with social simulation, a map editor, and a character workshop.

cls.summary: Agentshire is an open-source OpenClaw/QClaw plugin that visualises AI agents as interactive 3D NPCs inside an editable town with a map editor, character workshop and social simulation features.
cls.what_it_does: Agentshire turns multi-agent AI sessions into living NPCs in a low‑poly 3D town you can watch and interact with, providing a town editor, citizen workshop, day/night and weather systems, audio synthesis and chat mode. It is used as a plugin for OpenClaw CLI or the QClaw desktop app to provide a UGC-enabled visual front end and real-time social simulation for agents, notable for its dual town/chat interface and integrated citizen authoring tools.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository is 243 days old (younger than 1 year) so TRL is capped below 7; however it has many stars, an extended README, demo video and explicit integrations with OpenClaw/QClaw indicating an active beta-quality project used by adopters.
prerequisites: Node.js / npm and TypeScript development experience
Familiarity with OpenClaw or QClaw plugin workflow
student_project_ideas: Extend Agentshire's NPC behaviour templates to log and visualise workplace stress metrics, then evaluate how different scheduling policies change aggregated stress levels in the town (combine with a simple data-analysis notebook).

Build a custom citizen persona workshop profile and integrate a small IoT feed (simulated sensors) to create an interactive digital-twin scenario where agents respond to environmental inputs (e.g. weather changes) and demonstrate observable system behaviours.

tools.name: pablogila/TileMapDual
tools.desc: An automatic, real-time dual-grid tileset system for Godot

cls.summary: TileMapDual is an open-source Godot plugin that provides a real-time dual-grid autotiling TileMapLayer supporting square, isometric and hex grids.
cls.what_it_does: TileMapDual replaces Godot's conventional autotile approach with a dual-grid tileset system that generates filled tiles in real time from a small base set, reducing artwork needs and supporting multiple grid types (square, isometric, hex). It is installed as a Godot plugin and used as a TileMapLayer node in the editor and at runtime; notable features include live in-editor updates, example scenes, and compatibility with workflows that separate display and collision tiles.
cls.trl_rationale: The project is a mature Godot plugin with many stars (1315), multiple major versions (v5 with a legacy compatibility mode), example scenes and active maintainers; the repo is >1 year old and has demonstrated community adoption, supporting a production-ready TRL assessment.
student_project_ideas: Create a small Godot game level that uses TileMapDual for multiple terrain types (ground, water, road) and implement pathfinding using a separate logic tileset to demonstrate separation of display and collision data.

Extend TileMapDual usage by importing hand-drawn minimal tiles, generate the full tileset (using a tool like TileCropper), and compare memory/art asset count and performance versus Godot's built-in autotile on square and hex maps.

tools.name: ciddwd/overlay-translator
tools.desc: 无需 ROOT 的开源 Android 屏幕实时翻译工具，适合游戏、视觉小说和漫画。支持端侧与云端 OCR、离线 LLM、多种翻译服务和文字朗读（TTS），译文可直接显示在画面上。Open-source no-root Android real-time screen translator for games, visual novels, and manga. Supports on-device and cloud OCR, offline LLMs, multiple translation services, on-screen translations, and text-to-speech (TTS).

cls.summary: An open-source Android app that captures the screen (no root), performs OCR, translates detected text using on-device or cloud models/translation services, and displays or reads the translation as an overlay in real time.
cls.what_it_does: Screen Translator captures Android screen or app audio, runs OCR (on-device or cloud), passes text to offline or cloud translation/LLM services, and renders translated text as an overlay or subtitles; it also supports TTS for playback. It is notable for no-root operation, rich options to combine multiple OCR and translation backends (local models like GGUF/llama.cpp, PaddleOCR, ML Kit or cloud providers), and many display/UX optimisations for games, visual novels and manga.
cls.trl_rationale: The repository is active, well-documented and popular (1.3k stars, frequent commits), showing an installable, feature-rich beta-quality application; however it is under 1 year old (created ~148 days ago), so evidence supports a TRL of around 6 rather than production maturity.
prerequisites: Android development / debugging experience (ADB, app permissions)
Familiarity with mobile ML models and optional self-hosted OCR/LLM services
Basic knowledge of configuring cloud API keys if using online services
student_project_ideas: Build a small pipeline that uses the app's local HTTP OCR mode to send screenshots to a student-hosted PaddleOCR server, aggregate translations and evaluate OCR+translation accuracy for a corpus of game screenshots.
Integrate a custom on-device GGUF LLM model into the app's local translation path and measure latency and memory usage across a set of Android devices, proposing optimisations for mobile inference.

tools.name: le5le-com/meta2d.js
tools.desc: Meta2d.js是一个实时数据响应和交互的2d引擎，可用于Web 组态、SCADA，表报、流程图、中控可视化等可视化需求。Meta2d.js is a 2D visualization engine built around data-driven display and dynamic interaction. It can be used to build web SCADA/HMI, reports, flowcharts, control-room dashboards and similar visualizations and so on.

cls.summary: Meta2d.js is a TypeScript-based 2D, data-driven web visualization engine for building SCADA/HMI, dashboards, flowcharts and other interactive control-room style interfaces.
cls.what_it_does: Meta2d.js renders and updates large numbers of 2D graphical elements driven by real-time data and user interaction; it supports data bindings, animations, events, lifecycle hooks and custom graphics. It is primarily used in web pages as a Web Component and supports real-time protocols (MQTT/WebSocket/HTTP/SSE) and extensible plugins so it can power SCADA/HMI, dashboards and flow/diagram editors.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository created in 2021, active development with frequent pushes, a large number of stars and forks, documentation and examples, and explicit use-cases (SCADA/diagram-flow) indicate production-ready maturity suitable for real projects.
prerequisites: basic understanding of realtime data protocols (MQTT/WebSocket/HTTP)
student_project_ideas: Build a small web SCADA dashboard that visualises simulated sensor data via MQTT and uses Meta2d.js to show live gauges, alarms and animated flows.
Create an interactive process-flow editor where users drag-and-drop components, bind simulated data points, and implement condition-based alerts using Meta2d.js extensions.

tools.name: viettranx/3dviz-pro-max
tools.desc: Agent skill for creative 3D visualization: turn an idea into a Three.js/Blender scene worth exploring. Claude Code + Codex plugin, 223 recipes, 440 knowledge records, 22 proved kits, 37 runnable studies.

cls.summary: An open-source agent skill that helps generate and iteratively refine interactive Three.js and Blender scenes from high-level creative prompts.
cls.what_it_does: 3dviz-pro-max provides a ten-step agent workflow, a large catalog of recipes/knowledge records and runnable Three.js templates and Blender kits so an agent can turn a sentence into an explorable 3D scene. It is used by running the skill against supplied kits/templates (headless GPU captures are included) and is notable for its searchable recipe catalog, capture helper that lets the agent inspect rendered frames, and many prebuilt style profiles and kits.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository is very new (created 68 days ago) which caps maturity; README shows extensive data (recipes, kits, runnable examples, headless GPU captures) and many stars, indicating early adopters and a usable alpha, but no long track record or established releases.
prerequisites: basic Blender knowledge for Blender-backed kits
student_project_ideas: Build an interactive walkthrough of a small mechanical assembly by using the project's kits and recipes to generate a Three.js scene and add step-by-step assembly annotations.

Compare visualisation styles for a civil interior (daylight, lantern/night, diorama) by adapting different style profiles and measuring frame captures to support a short study on visual communication of design intent.

tools.name: RiptideNetworking/Riptide
tools.desc: Lightweight C# networking solution for multiplayer games.

cls.summary: Riptide Networking is an open-source, lightweight C# library for building client-server multiplayer networking, suitable for Unity and other .NET applications.
cls.what_it_does: Riptide provides connection management and message send/receive functionality over transports such as UDP and TCP, leaving message design and game logic to the developer. It is used by adding the library to a Unity or .NET project and using its message/connection APIs; notable points are its lightweight focus, built-in transports, and community documentation and ports to other languages.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository has existed since 2021, shows ongoing activity (recent pushes), significant adoption (≈1.3k stars), documentation and multiple transports/ports; this indicates production-ready maturity rather than an experimental prototype.
student_project_ideas: Build a simple multiplayer game prototype in Unity using Riptide for client-server synchronization and measure latency/packet loss effects under different simulated network conditions.
Integrate a Riptide-based .NET server with a small robotic simulator to prototype a remote-control interface and evaluate command reliability over UDP vs TCP.

tools.desc: Main development repository for Rigs of Rods soft-body physics simulator

tools.name: kellyvv/PhoneClaw
tools.desc: PhoneClaw turns phones into local AI agent runtimes with on-device models, native mobile Skills, LiveLand, and optional Mac Gateway inference.

cls.summary: PhoneClaw is an open-source iOS framework that runs on-device LLMs and provides a mobile AI agent runtime with native mobile Skills and an optional Mac gateway for remote inference.
cls.what_it_does: PhoneClaw turns iPhones into local AI agent runtimes by running on-device models (Gemma and MiniCPM variants) via LiteRT, exposing native mobile Skills (calendar, contacts, health, voice, image understanding, LiveLand) and offering an optional Mac Gateway for LAN-based remote inference. It is used as an app and developer framework to build and run local mobile agents that prefer on-device execution for privacy and offline use, and is notable for shipping models, a Skill system, and TestFlight distribution with active releases.
cls.trl_rationale: The project is active, has multiple releases (v1.2.x–v1.4.0), TestFlight distribution, and many stars indicating adoption, which supports a beta-level maturity. However the repository is under one year old (created 2026-04-04, ~227 days), so evidence limits the rating to TRL 6.
prerequisites: basic understanding of local LLMs and model runtimes (LiteRT, Gemma, MiniCPM)
student_project_ideas: Implement a custom mobile Skill (e.g. sensor-data summariser) in PhoneClaw and evaluate latency and privacy trade-offs between on-device inference and using the Mac Gateway.
Build an experiment comparing model response time, memory use and battery impact for Gemma vs MiniCPM on-device using PhoneClaw, and report implications for deploying edge agents.

tools.name: MyoHub/myosuite
tools.desc: MyoSuite is a collection of environments/tasks to be solved by musculoskeletal models simulated with the MuJoCo physics engine and wrapped in the OpenAI gym API.

cls.summary: MyoSuite provides a library of musculoskeletal simulation environments (Gym API) using the MuJoCo physics engine for training and evaluating control policies and biomechanical research.
cls.what_it_does: MyoSuite supplies a suite of musculoskeletal environments and task specifications implemented on top of MuJoCo and exposed via the Gymnasium/OpenAI Gym API so researchers can train and evaluate RL controllers and perform biomechanical experiments. It supports CPU debugging, massively parallel GPU training (mjlab), and an experimental JAX backend, and it ships ready-made tasks, tutorials and baseline checkpoints.
cls.trl_rationale: The project is multi-year (created 2021), actively maintained with recent pushes, has documentation, tutorials, PyPI releases, baseline checkpoints on Hugging Face and a substantial user community (stars/forks), indicating production-ready research software rather than a fragile prototype.
prerequisites: MuJoCo physics engine (or mjlab GPU backend)
familiarity with Gymnasium / OpenAI Gym and reinforcement learning libraries
optional: JAX or PyTorch for GPU backends and training frameworks
student_project_ideas: Train an RL policy in a MyoSuite arm environment (CPU) using Stable-Baselines3 to reproduce a reaching behaviour, then evaluate robustness to motor noise and fatigue wrappers supplied by MyoSuite.

Compare training throughput and final performance for the same MyoSuite task using the CPU Gym backend and the mjlab GPU backend (or experimental JAX path), measuring wall-clock training time and policy quality.

tools.desc: Verilog to Routing -- Open Source CAD Flow for FPGA Research

tools.name: uezo/ChatdollKit
tools.desc: ChatdollKit enables you to make your 3D model into a chatbot

cls.summary: ChatdollKit is a Unity SDK that turns a 3D VRM character into a voice-enabled chatbot by integrating LLMs, STT/TTS and animation/lip-sync.
cls.what_it_does: It connects Unity 3D models (VRM) with LLM backends, speech-to-text and text-to-speech services to produce conversational, voiced virtual agents with facial animation, lip-sync and turn-taking. Developers drop the SDK into a Unity project (including WebGL, mobile and desktop builds) and configure API endpoints and TTS/STT providers; notable features include multi-LLM support, multimodal/function-calling, wakeword and VAD support, and runtime model switching.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository created in 2020 and actively maintained through 2026, with many stars, forks and an example iOS app; README describes production-quality features and multiple real integrations, indicating production-ready maturity rather than an experimental prototype.
prerequisites: API keys for desired STT/TTS/LLM services
student_project_ideas: Build a Unity demo where a VRM robot answers sensor-data queries by combining ChatdollKit (for dialog and TTS) with a simulated IoT data feed, demonstrating multimodal responses and context persistence.

Create an accessible virtual receptionist: integrate ChatdollKit with an external intent-routing service to book appointments and log interactions into a simple backend, evaluating speech latency and turn-taking under noisy conditions.

tools.name: XiaoLuoLYG/GOD
tools.desc: Govern, Observe, Direct - a real-time control room for agent societies

cls.summary: GOD is an open-source browser-based control room for running, replaying and intervening in societies of language agents to inspect behaviour and steer simulations in real time.
cls.what_it_does: GOD runs multi-agent language-model simulations and provides a single-screen web control room where you can replay steps, ask individual agents questions, inject instructions for the next step, edit agent profiles and export/import experiment packs. It is used locally (or via a public demo) with OpenAI-compatible LLM endpoints and is notable for its step-wise pixel-replay UI, no-code setup wizard, and built-in experiment/pack ecosystem for reproducible agent-society runs.
cls.trl_rationale: The project is active with multiple tagged releases (v0.1.0, v0.2.0), a public demo site, and an accepted EMNLP 2026 demo paper, indicating an organised beta-stage maturity; repository age (~190 days) limits TRL to at most 6 per the guidance.
prerequisites: OpenAI-compatible API endpoint or use the provided browser replay (API optional)
student_project_ideas: Compare operator interventions: run the same scenario with different intervention strategies (manual vs scripted vs automated) and measure changes in agent behaviours and emergent metrics.
Extend GOD by adding a custom agent skill or sensor (e.g. simple navigation or local perception) and evaluate its effect on group-level outcomes using exported experiment packs for reproducibility.

tools.name: OpenDCAI/GameFactory-3A

cls.what_it_does: It converts a high-level game requirement into production-ready assets and engine-ready code using a coding agent that orchestrates pipelines for image, 3D object/scene, motion, audio and CG-video generation. tools.name: pnoker/iot-dc3
tools.desc: IoT DC3 — Connect the Physical World to AI. An open-source Industrial IoT Runtime for Physical AI: 36 protocol drivers, edge-to-cloud data delivery, and an MCP tool gateway so AI agents act on devices in a safe, controllable, traceable loop.

tools.name: HelgeSverre/ollama-gui
tools.desc: A Web Interface for chatting with your local LLMs via the ollama API

cls.summary: A browser-based single-page chat interface for interacting with local LLMs through the Ollama API, storing history locally in the browser.
cls.what_it_does: Ollama GUI provides a front-end chat UI that connects directly from the browser to an Ollama server so you can run and manage local LLMs without a separate backend. It supports streaming replies, attachments for vision models, model management (pull/delete/unload), chat history stored in IndexedDB, and exporting/importing chats; notable for being self-hosted, privacy-preserving and usable via Docker or a static build.
cls.trl_rationale: The project is mature and actively maintained (created 2023-10, frequent commits up to 2026-11), has many stars (1270), Docker images and a hosted demo, and documentation for builds and testing, indicating production-ready software rather than a fragile prototype.
student_project_ideas: Create an integration that sends engineering log files (CSV) to a local model via Ollama GUI and builds a prompt pipeline to summarise anomalies and suggest next diagnostic steps.
Extend the GUI to add a custom plugin that forwards model outputs to a CI pipeline or issue tracker, demonstrating a simple local LLM-assisted automation for software/integration tasks.

alternatives_to: Local LLM web clients (various open-source GUIs)

tools.name: Ch1rpys/Mirrai
tools.desc: 不在身边的时候，TA 还在这里。Upload real chat logs, rebuild a digital persona — open-source AI companion with persona distillation, an emotion engine, 11 LLM providers, and a graduation mechanism.

cls.summary: Mirrai is an open‑source AI companion that builds a personalised digital persona from uploaded chat logs, runs an emotion/state machine, supports many LLM backends and channels (web, WeChat, Feishu) and includes a 'graduation' mechanism to retire a persona.
cls.what_it_does: Mirrai ingests real chat histories and distills them into a structured persona using a multi‑stage pipeline, then uses that persona plus a dynamic emotion state machine to generate conversational replies. It is deployed as a TypeScript full‑stack application (server, React frontend) with plug‑and‑play adapters for many LLM providers and channel integrations (WeChat/Feishu), and emphasises local storage and privacy (Ollama/local LLM supported).
cls.trl_rationale: Repository is active, has many stars (1.2k) and integrations, and shows a substantial codebase and tests, but it is under 1 year old (created 2026‑05‑05) so lacks longer track record required for TRL 7+. README claims many features and channels but no large documented production deployments.
prerequisites: environment variables / API keys for cloud LLM providers (optional)
basic familiarity with TypeScript, React and tRPC
student_project_ideas: Compare different persona‑distillation modes (quick/standard/deep) by measuring holdout‑sentence reproduction metrics and analysing memory/anchor injection behaviour.
Deploy Mirrai with a local Ollama backend and evaluate privacy/latency tradeoffs versus a cloud LLM (OpenAI), measuring token costs, response latency and persona fidelity.

tools.name: Jaysmito101/TerraForge3D
tools.desc: Cross Platform Professional Procedural Terrain Generation & Texturing Tool

cls.summary: TerraForge3D is an open-source cross-platform application for procedural terrain generation, advanced node-based texturing and high-resolution texture baking with GPU acceleration.
cls.what_it_does: TerraForge3D generates large, high-resolution terrains using GPU (OpenCL) and CPU pipelines, provides a node-based shader/terrain editor, physically based rendering preview, erosion simulations and texture baking, and exports meshes and heightmaps to common 3D formats. It is used as a standalone desktop tool for creating terrain assets for visualization, simulation or game engines and is notable for its OpenCL GPU acceleration, advanced node editor and many export options.
cls.trl_rationale: The repository is multi-year (created 2021), has many stars and forks, documented releases (v2.3), user tutorials, developer docs and active recent commits, indicating production-ready maturity and real users rather than a one-off prototype.
prerequisites: familiarity with 3D formats (OBJ/GLTF) and shader basics
student_project_ideas: Create a workflow that generates procedurally eroded terrains in TerraForge3D and exports them to Blender for further architectural site modelling and visualization.

Compare hydraulic and wind erosion settings by generating multiple terrains in TerraForge3D, exporting heightmaps and running structural or flood simulations in a separate analysis tool to study landscape effects on runoff.

tools.desc: CadQuery GUI editor based on PyQT

tools.name: TheDuckCow/godot-road-generator
tools.desc: A Godot plugin for creating 3D highways/streets and lane-following traffic

cls.summary: A Godot Engine plugin that procedurally generates 3D roads/highways with lane management and built-in lane-following traffic helpers for use in editor or at runtime.
cls.what_it_does: The Road Generator creates cross-section-based road geometry, intersections, and auto-generated AI paths inside Godot projects, letting designers click-to-draw or procedurally spawn road networks. It provides runtime functions, export to glTF, terrain blending and traffic agent helpers so roads and simple lane-following traffic can be used both in-editor and during gameplay.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository is multi-year (created 2022), actively maintained with many stars, releases and presence on the Godot Asset Store indicating real-world use; README notes production-capable features though some milestones remain incomplete.
student_project_ideas: Build a small traffic simulation in Godot using the road-generator to procedurally create a road network and instrument lane-following agents to measure congestion under different traffic demand scenarios.
Integrate exported glTF road sections from the plugin into a Blender workflow to evaluate different pavement markings and iterate on road geometry linked to simple vehicle dynamics in Godot.

tools.name: Kiri-Innovation/3dgs-render-blender-addon
tools.desc: 3DGS Render by KIRI Engine

cls.summary: A free Blender add-on to import, edit, animate and render 3D Gaussian Splat (3DGS) .ply files inside Blender.
cls.what_it_does: 3DGS Render imports Gaussian-splat point-cloud (.ply) data into Blender and provides editing, rendering and export workflows so splatted scans can be composited with native Blender geometry and animations. It adds tools for switching between editable mesh workflows and a faster splat render mode, baking lighting/shadows (experimental), and exporting edited or animated .ply sequences.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository is >2 years old, has many stars (1.2k), packaged releases and documented install instructions, and shows active recent commits and community maintenance — evidence of production-ready add-on status though some features are marked experimental.
prerequisites: Familiarity with Blender (installing and using add-ons)
Understanding of 3D point-cloud / .ply data and basic GPU/VRAM considerations
student_project_ideas: Create a workflow that imports a 3DGS scan into Blender, composites it with mesh geometry and animated camera, then renders a short scene comparing render performance and VRAM usage between native meshes and Gaussian splats.

Develop an experimental pipeline that converts photogrammetry/mesh data into 3DGS splats, bakes simple lighting or shadows, and evaluates visual fidelity vs. file size and rendering time (compare results with Open3D or MeshLab exports).

tools.name: opengeos/Awesome-GEE
tools.desc: A curated list of Google Earth Engine resources

cls.summary: A curated, regularly updated list of resources, libraries, tutorials and datasets for working with Google Earth Engine (GEE).
cls.what_it_does: This repository collects links to documentation, APIs, tutorials, example scripts, courses and community projects that help users learn and apply Google Earth Engine for remote sensing and spatial analysis. It is used as a discovery hub (clickable links and references) rather than runnable software, and is notable for its broad coverage and long-running curation.
cls.trl_rationale: The repository is a long-lived, actively maintained curated list (created 2020, many stars and recent pushes) which documents mature external tools (GEE, geemap, datasets), but it is not itself deployable software; evidence is the README links and frequent updates.
prerequisites: Google Earth Engine account knowledge (JavaScript or Python API)
student_project_ideas: Use links and example scripts from the list with the geemap Python package to build a Jupyter notebook that maps urban heat island intensity over time for a city and compares surface temperature with land cover.

Use published Earth Engine algorithms and datasets referenced in the list to create an automated time-series deforestation/land-change monitoring pipeline and evaluate detection accuracy against known events.

tools.name: CesiumGS/cesium-unreal
tools.desc: Bringing the 3D geospatial ecosystem to Unreal Engine

cls.summary: Cesium for Unreal is an open-source Unreal Engine plugin that streams and visualises large-scale, high-accuracy 3D geospatial content (terrain, imagery, photogrammetry and 3D Tiles) inside Unreal Engine for simulations and interactive applications.
cls.what_it_does: The plugin connects Unreal Engine to the Cesium 3D geospatial ecosystem, allowing developers to stream global WGS84 terrain, imagery and 3D Tiles content at runtime and integrate it with Unreal physics, collisions and landscaping. It is used as an engine plugin inside Unreal projects and notable for supporting streaming of massive real-world datasets and open standards (3D Tiles) for high-accuracy geospatial visualisation.
cls.trl_rationale: The project is mature and long-lived (created 2020, actively maintained with many releases and an Unreal Marketplace presence) and is produced by Cesium, used in production workflows; these facts support a high TRL short of being an industry standard.
prerequisites: Familiarity with Unreal Engine (editor and plugin workflow)
C++ build toolchain for Unreal (Visual Studio, Xcode, or Linux toolchain)
Understanding of geospatial concepts (WGS84, tilesets) and optional Cesium ion account for cloud content
student_project_ideas: Create an interactive digital twin of a campus by streaming terrain and photogrammetry via Cesium for Unreal and adding simulated sensors/agents to evaluate navigation and line-of-sight scenarios.

Build an infrastructure visualisation that overlays GIS vector data (e.g. utility networks) on streamed 3D Tiles terrain in Unreal and implements a simple analysis tool to query and colour-code assets by attribute.

tools.name: mlightcad/cad-viewer
tools.desc: The world’s first fully web-based DXF/DWG viewer and editor that runs entirely in the browser — no backend server required.

cls.summary: MLightCAD is a browser-only DWG/DXF viewer and editor that parses, processes and renders CAD drawings entirely in the web client and can export self-contained offline HTML viewers.
cls.what_it_does: MLightCAD opens DWG and DXF files in the browser, performs parsing and geometry processing client-side, and renders drawings with high-performance WebGL/three.js. It is used as a drop-in viewer/editor for web apps, offers a plugin system, mobile touch support and one-click export to a single self-contained HTML file for offline sharing.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository is over one year old, has substantial community interest (1.2k stars, forks, active commits within last month) and documents production integrations and apps built on it (Thingraph and others), demonstrating production readiness rather than a small prototype.
student_project_ideas: Create a small web app that integrates MLightCAD to display and annotate DWG/DXF drawings and export annotated drawings as the self-contained HTML artifact for offline review.

Build a pipeline that loads DWG/DXF in the browser with MLightCAD, extracts geometry or layer metadata and exports it to a simple JSON format for downstream analysis (e.g., automated quantity takeoff) using a small Node.js backend.

tools.name: samapriya/awesome-gee-community-datasets
tools.desc: Community Datasets added by users and made available for use at large

cls.summary: A community-curated catalog of geospatial datasets published as Google Earth Engine assets for easy discovery and reuse.
cls.what_it_does: This repository collects and documents community-contributed geospatial datasets that have been prepared as Google Earth Engine assets so researchers and practitioners can find and use them without preprocessing. It is used by browsing the catalog website or by referencing the GitHub listing to load datasets into Earth Engine workflows, notable for its community curation, citation information and a Zenodo-backed release.
cls.trl_rationale: The catalog repository is several years old (created 2020), has substantial community interest (1.2k stars), a public website and a Zenodo release and is cited in the literature, indicating production-ready, community use rather than a toy prototype.
student_project_ideas: Use the catalog to find and load a regional landcover or vegetation time-series asset into Google Earth Engine and produce a change-detection analysis for a class lab, comparing results with a published study.
Create an automated Earth Engine script that ingests a community dataset from the catalog and combines it with Sentinel-2 imagery to build a crop health index dashboard for a small study area.

tools.name: synchopate/llama-modchip
tools.desc: Run 284B DeepSeek-V4-Flash (<59GiB RAM: 41.1 cold pp, 9.1 N=1 tg, up to 25.3 spec tok/s) & 30B MoEs (22.4 N=1 / 111.6 spec tok/s) on 64GB CPU (0 GPUs).

cls.summary: llama-modchip is a CPU-focused local LLM runtime and quantization tool that enables running very large mixture-of-experts and dense models (up to 284B) inside 64 GB-class machines by using custom block-64 quantization formats and memory-aware inference techniques.
cls.what_it_does: It implements custom low-bit block quantization formats (Fractal-64 and LUT-VQ3-64), cache-aware KV management, and speculative decoding to run large MoE and dense language models on CPU-only systems. Users convert or load GGUF-format models and run inference on Linux, macOS (Metal) and Windows, with optimisations for AVX-512/Apple Silicon and detailed memory/throughput trade-offs documented in the README.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository is very new (created 19 days ago) so it cannot be judged production-proven despite a detailed README, benchmarks, and many stars; the README and benchmarks indicate a working, actively developed alpha used by early adopters, consistent with TRL 5.
prerequisites: understanding of CPU architectures and SIMD (AVX/Metal)
basic Python and model inference concepts
student_project_ideas: Quantise a mid-sized MoE or dense model to the project's Fractal-64/VQ3 format, run throughput and memory benchmarks on a 64 GB desktop, and compare signal fidelity (PPL/CosSim) versus BF16.
Integrate llama-modchip inference into a small chatbot web frontend and measure end-to-end latency and resource usage for different load modes (cold/warm, speculative decoding on/off).

tools.name: markaren/threepp
tools.desc: A cross-platform C++20 3D library with Python bindings and the high-level API of three.js.

cls.summary: threepp is a C++20 cross-platform 3D library with a three.js-like high-level API, Vulkan and OpenGL backends, Python bindings, and integrated simulation and sensor tooling for robotics and digital-twin workflows.
cls.what_it_does: threepp provides a scene-graph-driven 3D engine that mirrors three.js semantics but in C++ with portable OpenGL and a deferred Vulkan renderer (with ray-traced effects). It includes loaders, a scene editor, PhysX-based physical simulation, simulated sensors (lidar, cameras, IMU), Python bindings and examples for building simulated environments, HIL flight with ArduPilot and producing labelled ground-truth for perception research.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository is multi-year (created 2021), actively maintained with many stars, a substantial examples folder, prebuilt editor/player applications and Python bindings; README warns APIs change and targets research/prototyping rather than production, supporting a production-ready but research-focused TRL 7 assessment.
prerequisites: familiarity with graphics APIs (Vulkan/OpenGL) and build systems
optional: Python for bindings and simulation scripts
student_project_ideas: Build a simulated sensor rig in threepp (camera + lidar + IMU) and generate labelled datasets to evaluate a SLAM or perception pipeline implemented in ROS or OpenCV.
Integrate an ArduPilot vehicle with threepp for a hardware-in-the-loop flight control experiment and compare closed-loop performance between simulated and real sensors.

tools.name: ASCIT31/Dark-Moon
tools.desc: Open-source autonomous AI penetration testing. 50 specialist agents across web, API, cloud, Active Directory, Kubernetes, CI/CD and AI/LLM (OWASP LLM Top 10). Runs on a local LLM behind a Privacy Gateway. Integrates with GitHub, GitLab, Jenkins, VS Code, JetBrains, n8n, Grafana & Splunk.

cls.summary: DarkMoon is an open-source, autonomous AI penetration testing platform that runs agent-driven security assessments against web, cloud, CI/CD, Active Directory, Kubernetes and LLM endpoints on your own infrastructure.
cls.what_it_does: DarkMoon orchestrates specialist autonomous agents to discover, exploit and document vulnerabilities across multiple surfaces (web, APIs, cloud, AD, Kubernetes, CI/CD and LLMs) and streams every command and raw output as evidence. It runs locally (Docker + local or cloud LLMs) and integrates with CI/CD and observability tools so tests can be triggered from pipelines or developer tools. Notable features include a privacy gateway for tokenizing real secrets, an MCP orchestration layer for running offensive tooling, and explicit support for local LLMs.
cls.trl_rationale: The repository is over one year old, has substantial community interest (1,234 stars), active maintenance (recent pushes), published media coverage and many integrations listed in the README; these indicate production-readiness beyond prototype stage though it's not an industry standard.
prerequisites: LLM API key or local model (Ollama, llama.cpp, etc.)
basic familiarity with CI/CD and pentesting concepts
student_project_ideas: Integrate DarkMoon into a CI pipeline for a student web application and create a lab that analyses and triages the generated findings, producing remediation tickets or PRs.

Build a small local testbed (Juice Shop + Kubernetes) and use DarkMoon to benchmark detection and exploitation of container and API vulnerabilities, then compare results against another tool such as Metasploit or Caldera.

tools.name: hanruihua/ir-sim
tools.desc: A  Python-based lightweight robot simulator designed for navigation, control, and learning

cls.summary: IR-SIM is a lightweight, Python-based robot simulator for navigation, control and learning that uses YAML scenario files and provides built-in collision detection and a Matplotlib renderer.
cls.what_it_does: IR-SIM lets users define robot platforms, sensors and environments in YAML and run multi-agent navigation and control simulations for research and teaching. It is used via a Python API or command-line, renders with Matplotlib, and supports behaviours (RVO/ORCA/SFM), 2D LiDAR sensors and collision handling, making it easy to prototype control and learning algorithms without hardware. Its notable features are simple YAML configuration, multiple kinematic models, and integrations for faster lidar kernels and group behaviours.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository is multi-year (created 2022), has substantial community interest (1,234 stars), active maintenance (recent pushes), documentation (ReadTheDocs) and cites academic publications using it, indicating production-ready maturity for research and teaching (TRL 7).
prerequisites: familiarity with Python programming and basic robotics concepts (kinematics, sensors)
student_project_ideas: Implement and compare RVO, ORCA and a learned RL policy for multi-robot collision avoidance in a cluttered YAML-configured environment and evaluate throughput and safety metrics.
Integrate IR-SIM LiDAR outputs with a SLAM package (e.g. RTAB-Map or a simple EKF) to build and visualise 2D maps, then test robustness with dynamic obstacles.

tools.name: Soulmate-Halo/heterogeneous-gpu-pd-lab
tools.desc: 使用稠密算力卡对稀疏大显存主机进行加速，主机包括 AI Max+ 395、M3 512G、DGX Spark 等。

cls.summary: A C++ experimental repository that implements heterogeneous GPU inference and pipeline-parallel deployment patterns to accelerate large LLMs by splitting work across dense accelerator cards and large-memory hosts.
cls.what_it_does: The project provides deployment patterns, scripts, Docker images and benchmarks for running LLM inference across heterogeneous GPU hosts (e.g. a small 20GB RTX card cooperating with a large-memory server like DGX Spark or AI Max). It is used to split prefill and decode work, coordinate expert requests over RDMA, and measure end-to-end throughput for hybrid MoE / Flash model setups, with reproducible bundles and deployment guides.
cls.trl_rationale: The repository is active and contains Docker images, deployment guides, and measured benchmarks, indicating early real-world use; however it is only 77 days old so it lacks a long track record and formal stable releases, limiting maturity to TRL 5.
prerequisites: Large GPU hardware (RTX, DGX, AI Max) and model assets
student_project_ideas: Reproduce one of the repo's heterogeneous benchmark setups in a lab: deploy the provided Docker image across two virtual machines with a consumer GPU and a multi-GPU host (or simulated resources) and measure prefill/decode throughput, then report how work split ratio affects latency and throughput.

Extend the RDMA-based expert request mechanism to integrate a different local inference engine (e.g. llama.cpp or vLLM) and compare end-to-end token throughput and resource utilisation between the engines.

cls.what_it_does: This project delivers a responsive web application (React + three.js + TypeScript) that lets users rotate, zoom and listen to short narrated exhibit cards for prehistoric animals in English and Simplified Chinese. It is used as an educational, low-pressure exploration experience with accessible controls and static assets (no runtime AI or tracking) and notable for its child-centred design and strong accessibility considerations.

Extend the app to visualise sensor data by adding a digital-twin style exhibit that streams simple time-series telemetry (simulated) and shows how scale/animation changes with input, combining the museum UI with a small Node.js data server.

tools.desc: Open-source AI companions, desktop pets, long-term memory & proactive chat. 人机恋开源项目大全。让你的家机能够脱离官端自主存在，拥有记忆和主动性。

cls.summary: A curated, community-maintained list of open-source AI companion projects, tools and infrastructure for building long-term conversational agents and desktop pets.
cls.what_it_does: This repository collects and categorises open-source projects, clients, libraries and infrastructure related to AI companions (long-term chat agents, desktop pets, memory systems, embodiment, voice, etc.). It is used as a discovery resource and roadmap for developers and hobbyists to find implementations, self-hosting options and integrations; notable for its thorough scanning, language sections and status tags for readiness and security checks.
cls.trl_rationale: This is a well-starred, actively maintained curated index rather than a single runnable engineering product; repository is 137 days old with many entries and regular updates, indicating a mature curated resource but not a production system itself, supporting a beta-level TRL.

tools.name: google/dawn
tools.desc: Native WebGPU implementation. Mirror of https://dawn.googlesource.com/dawn. File bugs here: https://crbug.com/dawn/new

cls.summary: Dawn is an open-source, cross-platform native implementation of the WebGPU API used to run GPU-accelerated rendering and compute on desktop platforms and inside Chromium.
cls.what_it_does: Dawn implements the WebGPU C/C++ API and provides native backends that map WebGPU calls to platform graphics APIs (D3D12, Metal, Vulkan, OpenGL). It is used by embedding projects (for example Chromium) or native applications that want a WebGPU-compatible runtime and includes tooling such as the Tint WGSL shader compiler; it is notable for being a production WebGPU backend maintained alongside the browser ecosystem.
cls.trl_rationale: Dawn is actively maintained, has many stars and forks, extensive developer documentation, and is the underlying WebGPU implementation used in Chromium, indicating wide production use and maturity; the repository is several years old and receives regular updates.
prerequisites: familiarity with GPU concepts and APIs (Vulkan/Metal/D3D12/OpenGL)
CMake and platform SDKs for building native binaries
student_project_ideas: Build a small real-time physics visualisation that uses Dawn as the rendering backend to display simulation results produced by a Python/NumPy simulation pipeline (use a lightweight IPC or file exchange).
Integrate Dawn into a simple sandboxed application demonstrating WGSL shaders via Tint and compare performance across backends (Vulkan, Metal, D3D12) for a basic computational kernel.

tools.name: Dicklesworthstone/coding_agent_session_search
tools.desc: Unified TUI and CLI to index and search your local coding agent session history across 30+ providers (Codex, Claude Code, Gemini, Cursor, Aider, Copilot, and more) into one searchable timeline. Hybrid search plus robot/JSON output for agents.

cls.summary: cass is a Rust command-line and TUI tool that indexes and searches local coding-agent session histories from many providers into a single searchable timeline.
cls.what_it_does: It aggregates conversation and session logs from 30+ coding agent providers into a SQLite-backed archive and provides fast lexical and optional semantic/hybrid search via a CLI and TUI. Notable features include robot/JSON output for programmatic use, local semantic model support (opt-in), and atomic safe publishing of lexical indexes for reliable reads.
cls.trl_rationale: The project is actively maintained, has many stars, packaged installers (Homebrew, Scoop) and an install script, and exposes CLI/TUI and JSON APIs — evidence of a maturing beta. However the repository is under one year old so by the provided rules its TRL should not exceed 6.
prerequisites: familiarity with the command line (Linux/macOS/Windows PowerShell)
basic understanding of search concepts (lexical vs semantic)
optional: knowledge of local model files if using semantic search
student_project_ideas: Create a tool that links cass search results to an automated test runner: detect recent agent-suggested code changes and run targeted unit tests, reporting correlation between agent suggestions and test outcomes.
Build a small dashboard that visualises agent usage patterns across a student cohort by parsing cass's SQLite archive and producing temporal/heatmap analytics (combine with a lightweight web server).

tools.name: awesome-spectral-indices/awesome-spectral-indices

cls.summary: A curated, machine-readable catalogue of spectral indices for remote sensing with cross-language implementations and downloadable CSV/JSON that researchers and practitioners use to compute vegetation, water, soil and radar indices.
cls.what_it_does: This repository collects standardised definitions, formulas and metadata for hundreds of spectral indices used in Earth-observation and remote sensing workflows, and provides generated CSV/JSON tables plus links to language-specific implementations (Python, JavaScript, Julia, R) and a Streamlit app. It is used to look up index formulas, derive inputs/bands and integrate indices into processing pipelines (e.g. Google Earth Engine, local Python workflows), notable for its standardized v1 schema and published peer-reviewed paper.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository is mature (created 2021, active maintenance with recent pushes), has 1.2k stars, a peer-reviewed paper (2023) and language bindings/packages (Python, Julia, JS, R) plus a Streamlit app, indicating wide adoption and stability; therefore assessed as mature and widely adopted (TRL 8).
