familiarity with Python or GIS tools (e.g. Google Earth Engine, QGIS)
student_project_ideas: Implement a processing pipeline that computes a selected set of vegetation and water indices from Sentinel-2 imagery using the spyndex Python package and Google Earth Engine to map seasonal change in a study area.

Compare several spectral indices for burn detection by applying the catalogue formulas to Landsat time series (using the provided CSV/JSON) and evaluate detection accuracy against known fire perimeters.

tools.name: rudrankriyam/Foundation-Models-Framework-Lab
tools.desc: A practical lab for building, testing, and evaluating apps with Apple's Foundation Models framework.

cls.summary: A native iOS/macOS app and workbench for composing, running and inspecting prompts and tool calls against Apple's Foundation Models framework, intended for development and experimentation with on-device and Apple Intelligence model features.
cls.what_it_does: Foundation Lab provides an interactive Playground, a Library of editable recipes and guided labs, and a Runs inspector to persist and analyse prompts, tool calls, transcripts and metrics when using Apple's Foundation Models APIs. It is used as a development and teaching workbench to prototype prompts, configure model/runtime options, exercise tool-calling and speech I/O, compare adapters and export reproducible Swift examples.
cls.trl_rationale: The repository is over a year old, has a large star count and active recent commits, a substantial README, documented labs and multiple example/workspace integrations indicating real-world usage; however it is platform-specific to Apple's ecosystem rather than an industry-standard cross-platform product.
prerequisites: Apple Silicon device for on-device runs
Apple Intelligence enabled / compatible OS (iOS/tvOS/macOS versions noted)
student_project_ideas: Build a guided conversational assistant for a mock device-management workflow that uses Foundation Lab's Playground and a custom tool adapter to call a simulated REST inventory service, and measure response latency and token usage across device and cloud model execution.

Compare model adapter performance by creating two adapters (local on-device and private cloud compute) and use the Adapter Comparison workspace to quantify time-to-first-token, total duration and output quality on a multilingual extraction task.

tools.name: StayLameBro/backburner
tools.desc: Your iPhone helps your Mac run a 27B model: faster prompt reading and more context over a USB-C cable

cls.summary: Backburner splits large local LLM inference across a Mac and an iPhone over USB-C so the pair can run bigger context windows and speed up prompt prefill and decoding.
cls.what_it_does: Backburner offloads later transformer layers and/or attention over old keys to an iPhone connected by USB-C while the Mac runs the remaining work, enabling larger context sizes (measured up to 128k+ tokens) and faster prefill times. It is delivered as a Python project that includes a llama.cpp fork with Mac/Metal kernels and a coordinator to pipeline work between devices; notable features are device-aware scheduling, measured benchmarks, and support for very large contexts by paging to the phone.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository is very recent (created ~47 days ago) but has working code, benchmarks, a llama.cpp fork and multiple reported setups; however it lacks a longer production track record and widespread adoption so TRL is limited to 'Alpha in use'.
prerequisites: Apple Silicon Mac (macOS) with sufficient GPU memory
iPhone with compatible hardware and iOS
USB-C cable and basic build toolchain (Python, compiler for llama.cpp/Metal kernels)
student_project_ideas: Measure and compare end-to-end latency and token throughput of a simple agent using Backburner with different iPhone models and Mac configurations, producing plots and a short report on where split inference helps most.
Integrate Backburner with a small tool-using agent (e.g., a file-reading assistant) to demonstrate multi-device context extension and implement a cache/restore strategy for large-context agents.

tools.name: Bingeljell/image-to-3dlab
tools.desc: AssetFurnace: the most complete open-source image-to-3D pipeline (Oct 2026). Prompt or picture → textured, rigged, animated game character, locally on Apple Silicon or NVIDIA. Pixal3D, TRELLIS.2, Hunyuan3D, SF3D, auto-rig and 21 moves. For indie game devs and 3D artists. Free, Apache-2.0.

cls.summary: AssetFurnace is an open-source pipeline that turns a text prompt or image into a game-ready, textured, rigged and animated 3D character locally (or via an optional paid cloud service).
cls.what_it_does: AssetFurnace automates image/text → 3D asset creation: it generates a mesh, applies textures (Pixel Match), fits a skeleton (auto-rigging) and produces animated GLB exports for game engines. It is used via a local browser 'studio' or CLI and bundles multiple backend models (Pixal3D, TRELLIS.2, Hunyuan3D) with steps for finishing, LODs and license provenance; notable for local-first workflows (Apple Silicon / NVIDIA / AMD) and built-in game-ready optimisations.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository is 107 days old (created 2026-08-02) which limits maturity to beta-level; however the project has many stars, frequent releases (0.5.10 on 2026-11-13), active development and a usable installer and studio, supporting a TRL 6 assessment.
prerequisites: GPU (Apple Silicon, NVIDIA CUDA or AMD ROCm) or cloud credits
student_project_ideas: Use AssetFurnace to generate a set of animated GLB characters and integrate them into a Unity or Godot scene to evaluate animation retargeting and runtime performance (compare LODs and texture sizes).

Compare auto-rigging and skinning quality by running AssetFurnace outputs and refining the same characters manually in Blender, then quantify joint/pose errors and artefacts across a set of test poses.

tools.name: OSGeo/grass
tools.desc: GRASS - free and open-source geospatial processing engine

tools.name: Mastershort/neonplan3d
tools.desc: The original 3D floor plan for Home Assistant: draw your home in the built-in editor and see and control lights, covers, climate, media, sensors and cameras live in neon 3D – panel and dashboard card, runs on old wall tablets too.

cls.summary: NeonPlan 3D is an open-source, in-browser 3D floor‑plan editor and live dashboard card for Home Assistant that visualises and controls smart‑home devices in a spatial digital‑twin style.
cls.what_it_does: NeonPlan lets you draw floor plans inside Home Assistant, furnish them, and link rooms to Home Assistant areas so lights, blinds, sensors and cameras appear and update live in a 3D view. It is used as a Lovelace dashboard card and editor (runs in-browser, designed to work on older wall tablets) and is notable for multi‑building support, user‑customisable visual styles, imports from common formats and a live demo/manual and HACS integration.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository is 50 days old (younger than 90 days) which limits TRL to at most 5; however the project already has a public demo, manual, active releases and many community stars indicating early adoption and practical use, consistent with TRL 5 (alpha in use).
prerequisites: optional: Node.js / TypeScript for local development
student_project_ideas: Build a spatial digital‑twin dashboard by importing a house plan (DXF or RoomPlan) into NeonPlan and connect live energy and temperature sensors from Home Assistant to visualise realtime flows and alerts.
Extend NeonPlan by writing a custom style and an automation that switches visual styles by time-of-day and voice command, then evaluate user usability on a low‑power wall tablet.

tools.name: simpler-env/SimplerEnv
tools.desc: Evaluating and reproducing real-world robot manipulation policies (e.g., RT-1, RT-1-X, Octo) in simulation under common setups (e.g., Google Robot, WidowX+Bridge) (CoRL 2024)

cls.summary: SimplerEnv provides simulated manipulation evaluation environments that reproduce real robot setups to test and compare learned manipulation policies under standardized visual-matching and variant-aggregation protocols.
cls.what_it_does: SimplerEnv packages simulated environments (based on SAPIEN and ManiSkill2/3) that mimic real robot setups (Google Robot, WidowX+Bridge) to evaluate and reproduce behaviour of real-world manipulation policies like RT-1 and Octo. It is used by creating prepackaged environments, running policy inference in simulation, and collecting standardized metrics across visual-matching and variant-aggregation experiments to aid checkpoint selection and failure-mode analysis.
cls.trl_rationale: The project is >2 years old, has an associated CoRL paper, active development, many stars/forks and explicit integrations with SAPIEN/ManiSkill, indicating production-ready research tooling suitable for real experiments and reproducible evaluations rather than a fragile prototype.
prerequisites: Python and typical ML stack (inference libraries for policies)
student_project_ideas: Evaluate a pretrained visual-manipulation policy (e.g., RT-1 checkpoint) across SimplerEnv variant-aggregation scenarios and report how lighting/background/domain randomisation affects success rates.
Integrate a simple RL or imitation-learned policy with SimplerEnv and compare performance between the ManiSkill2 (CPU) and ManiSkill3 (GPU-parallel) backends to study scalability and reproducibility.

tools.name: enable3d/enable3d
tools.desc: 🕹️ Standalone 3D Framework / Physics for three.js (using ammo.js) / 3D extension for Phaser 3

tools.name: openGemini/openGemini
tools.desc: CNCF sandbox project, an open source distributed time-series database with high concurrency, high performance, and high scalability

cls.summary: openGemini is an open-source, cloud-native distributed time-series database intended for high-concurrency telemetry storage, query and analytics at scale.
cls.what_it_does: openGemini stores and queries large volumes of time-series telemetry data using an MPP distributed architecture, LSM-based storage and columnar compression to improve write/read performance and reduce storage. It is used as a backend for observability, IoT and monitoring pipelines and is notable for InfluxDB compatibility, Prometheus/OpenTelemetry integration and CNCF sandbox status.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository is >4 years old, is a CNCF sandbox project, has substantial stars/forks and recent activity, documentation and installation instructions; these indicate production-readiness and community adoption rather than a nascent prototype.
prerequisites: familiarity with time-series concepts (metrics, series, retention)
basic Go toolchain for building from source and Docker/Kubernetes for deployments
student_project_ideas: Build an IoT telemetry pipeline that ingests sensor data (MQTT) into openGemini, then create dashboards and a PromQL/InfluxQL query exercise to explore querying strategies and compression trade-offs.
Compare storage and query performance between openGemini and InfluxDB/TimescaleDB for high-cardinality telemetry by running controlled write/read benchmarks and analysing compression and latency.

tools.name: jamro/tiny-engineer
tools.desc: A small desktop robot that brings an AI coding assistant to life, physically acting out when it reads files, thinks, writes code, and finishes work.

cls.summary: Tiny Engineer is an open-source desktop robot (ESP32 + servos + OLED + speaker + 3D-printed body) that physically acts out the activity of an AI coding agent by receiving pose/control commands over Wi‑Fi HTTP or USB serial.
cls.what_it_does: Tiny Engineer provides a physical embodiment for coding AI agents: the agent sends simple commands (HTTP or serial) and the ESP32 firmware drives servos, an OLED face and a speaker to animate reading, thinking, typing and finishing actions. It is notable because it combines open hardware (KiCad board, 3D-printable body) and ready-made integrations (npx tiny-engineer hooks) for popular agent platforms so software agents can be given a tangible, networked body.
cls.trl_rationale: The repo provides complete firmware, hardware KiCad files, 3D models, detailed build docs and active community interest (many stars and recent commits), indicating use by early adopters; however the repository is only ~88 days old so it lacks a longer track record required for TRL 6+.
prerequisites: experience with Node.js/npm and HTTP APIs
access to a 3D printer or 3D printing service and an ESP32 toolchain
student_project_ideas: Extend the Tiny Engineer firmware to add a new sensor-driven behaviour (e.g. proximity-triggered animations) and demonstrate a closed-loop interaction between a local LLM and the robot using a Raspberry Pi as a gateway.

Design and 3D-print an alternate shell and modify the servo kinematics + control poses, then integrate the modified robot with a CI-based agent hook (npx tiny-engineer) to show custom animations triggered by code repository events.

tools.name: beltromatti/get-it
tools.desc: Read it. See it. Get it. Built at GDG AI Hack Milan 2026 for "Learn Different" track.

cls.summary: Get It. is a desktop study app that turns text PDFs or Markdown files into a concept-level knowledge graph with visualisations and integrated study tools (chat, flashcards, quizzes, Feynman exercises).
cls.what_it_does: Get It. analyses a text PDF or Markdown document to detect concepts that benefit from visual explanation, attaches interactive renderers (Three.js scenes, plots, formula walkthroughs) and builds a small knowledge graph sized by mastery. It provides study instruments (chat, flashcards, forced-choice quizzes, Feynman-style prompts) driven by user-selected LLM APIs that update per-concept mastery scores and store a local journal; notable points are local data storage and support for multiple LLM providers via user-supplied credentials.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository is ~192 days old with many stars, releases and desktop installers described in the README, and a clear user workflow; this indicates a beta-quality project with versioned builds and end-user installers but not yet long-term production track record, so TRL 6 is appropriate.
prerequisites: an AI account or API key for the LLM provider you wish to use
student_project_ideas: Integrate Get It. with an engineering lecture PDF (e.g., dynamics or circuits chapter) and evaluate how its concept-detection maps align with instructor-curated concept lists, measuring gaps and false positives.

Extend a Get It. renderer by adding a custom Three.js visualization for a mechanical component or molecule, and link it to generated flashcards to test whether the visualisation improves application scores in the app's knowledge graph.

tools.name: leap71/PicoGK
tools.desc: PicoGK is a compact and robust geometry kernel for Computational Engineering

cls.summary: PicoGK is a compact open-source geometry kernel (C#) that provides a reduced instruction set for programmatic generation and processing of engineering geometry.
cls.what_it_does: PicoGK exposes a small, deliberate set of geometry operations used to create and manipulate shapes for computational engineering workflows. It is used as a code-driven geometry kernel (library) in C# to generate parts and structures (e.g. for additive manufacturing) and is notable for its focus on a reduced instruction set and integration into a broader computational‑engineering stack.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository is over one year old, has substantial community interest (1.1k stars), and recent active development, indicating a beta-level project; README is promotional but does not show wide independent deployments or formal stable releases, so TRL is limited to ~6.
prerequisites: computational geometry and linear algebra basics
student_project_ideas: Use PicoGK to generate parameterised lattice structures for additive manufacturing and evaluate their mechanical performance by exporting meshes to an FEA tool (e.g. export to a solver or mesh format).

Implement a small code-CAD pipeline that uses PicoGK to procedurally generate cooling-channel geometries for a heat exchanger and compare printability and flow properties by coupling with OpenVDB or a CFD preprocessor.

tools.name: usamahz/cpu-performance-engineering
tools.desc: A reading path for CPU performance engineering, from one instruction to production inference. Primary sources only, with a runnable benchmark for every section.

cls.summary: A curated, source-first reading path and runnable-benchmark collection for understanding and measuring CPU performance from single-instruction behaviour to serving inference on CPU.
cls.what_it_does: This repository collects primary-source readings (papers, vendor manuals, repositories) arranged in an ordered learning path about CPU microarchitecture, memory hierarchy, measurement and optimisation, and includes committed, runnable microbenchmarks for many sections. It is used as a teaching/reference resource and as a reproducible benchmark suite; it also offers an MCP integration (misc/mcp) to surface the collection to AI clients.
cls.trl_rationale: The repository is well-populated with committed benchmarks, detailed README and examples that indicate active use and useful material (evidence: many runnable benchmarks under misc/benchmarks and MCP integration). However the project is only ~61 days old which limits demonstrated long-term adoption, so TRL is capped at 5.
prerequisites: Basic CPU architecture concepts (x86/ARM) and assembly
student_project_ideas: Reproduce and extend one of the repository's microbenchmarks to compare vectorized vs scalar kernels on two different CPU generations, analysing results with roofline and perf counters.
Integrate the MCP index from misc/mcp into a small AI assistant that answers why a specific kernel is slow by citing the repository's primary sources and benchmark evidence.

tools.name: mgonzs13/yolo_ros
tools.desc: Ultralytics YOLOv8, YOLOv9, YOLOv10, YOLOv11, YOLOv12 for ROS 2

cls.summary: yolo_ros is a C++ ROS 2 node that runs Ultralytics YOLO ONNX models for real-time object detection, tracking, instance segmentation and pose estimation (including 3D via depth).
cls.what_it_does: It wraps Ultralytics-exported ONNX YOLO models inside a pure C++ ROS 2 node using ONNX Runtime so you can perform detection, tracking, segmentation and 3D lifting inside ROS 2 without a Python dependency. The package is distributed as a pluginlib-based yolo_node, supports CPU and GPU (CUDA / TensorRT) execution providers, works across many ROS 2 distributions and can be run in Docker for integration into robot software stacks.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository is multi-year (created 2023), actively maintained with many stars and forks, provides build instructions, multi-distro ROS 2 support, Docker images and GPU options; evidence indicates production-ready use in robotics projects rather than a proof-of-concept.
prerequisites: colcon build tool and C++ toolchain
Linux (for CUDA / TensorRT GPU support) and optional CUDA/cuDNN setup
student_project_ideas: Integrate yolo_ros with a mobile robot (ROS 2) to implement autonomous object following and obstacle-aware navigation, combining it with a SLAM stack to test performance in real-world scenarios.

Evaluate 2D vs 3D object detection by running Ultralytics ONNX models through yolo_ros with RGB-D input and compare detection/tracking accuracy and latency on CPU vs GPU (ONNX Runtime) as a performance benchmarking exercise.

tools.name: abarichello/godot-ci
tools.desc: Docker image to export Godot Engine games. Templates for Gitlab CI and GitHub Actions to deploy to GitLab Pages/GitHub Pages/Itch.io.

tools.name: agents-io/PokeClaw
tools.desc: PokeClaw (PocketClaw) — first on-device AI that controls your Android phone. Gemma 4, no cloud, no API key. Poke is short for Pocket.

cls.summary: PokeClaw is an open-source Android app that runs on-device LLMs (notably Gemma 4) to automate and control phone apps and workflows locally without requiring cloud APIs.
cls.what_it_does: PokeClaw turns an Android phone into a local-first AI agent that can observe screen content, choose and call phone-control tools, and chain actions to complete tasks (for example context-aware auto-replies in messaging apps). It is used as an Android application and agent harness combining accessibility/notification observers, a tool layer for phone control, and an on-device LLM runtime; its notable feature is running Gemma 4 locally (LiteRT) so model execution can stay entirely on the device with optional cloud fallback.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository is ~225 days old with many stars and public demos showing real-device capability; README describes working prototypes and device builds but it is a solo-built, actively-developed project without long-term production deployments, so maturity aligns with a beta-stage tool.
prerequisites: understanding of on-device LLM runtimes and model/tool-calling concepts
student_project_ideas: Build an accessibility-focused skill for PokeClaw that automatically reads and summarizes incoming messages for low-vision users, evaluating latency and accuracy across devices (compare local Gemma 4 vs optional cloud model).

Integrate PokeClaw with a simple IoT or home-automation server so the phone agent can observe notifications and trigger external actuators, then measure reliability and failure modes across repeated real-device trials.

tools.name: ManfredCh/Lyapunov
tools.desc: LLM-first, 3D-native robotics and simulation workspace.

cls.summary: Lyapunov is an LLM-first, 3D-native desktop framework that combines scene construction, robot preparation and controlled simulation with an integrated agent, viewer and file/workbench for robotics and simulation workflows.
cls.what_it_does: Lyapunov provides a desktop workbench that unifies a 3D viewer, physics-backed simulation (MuJoCo by default, optional Isaac/Newton), robot and camera tools, and an LLM-driven agent to control and automate tasks in the simulated scene. It is used as a developer and research workspace for building, running and recording robotics simulations and agent interactions, notable for bundling installers, native releases and an "everything-is-a-plugin" composition model (DSH/Cordis).
cls.trl_rationale: The project is actively packaged with platform installers, versioned releases and documented release notes, and is produced by a named company with a sponsor, which suggests early adoption; however the repository is only 46 days old so by the stated policy TRL must be capped at 5.
prerequisites: MuJoCo for physics (installed by default installer)
familiarity with robotics simulation concepts and command-line install
student_project_ideas: Create a simulated robot arm manipulation task in Lyapunov using MuJoCo, record camera streams and build an LLM-based natural-language controller that issues high-level commands to the robot agent.

Compare sensor outputs and collision events between MuJoCo and an optional Isaac Sim setup within Lyapunov by importing the same USD scene and evaluating trajectory repeatability and timing for a mobile robot.

tools.name: emergi-lab/evolving_personality
tools.desc: Dynamic MBTI Personality Simulation for LLM Agents via Carl Jung's Theory. A framework that enables LLM agents' MBTI personalities to naturally evolve and grow through interaction.

cls.summary: A Python framework that models and lets LLM-based agents adopt, adapt and evolve MBTI-style personalities during interaction.
cls.what_it_does: JPAF provides mechanisms (dominant-auxiliary coordination, reinforcement-compensation, reflection) to instantiate, adapt and simulate MBTI personalities in large language model agents. It is used by configuring an LLM backend (OpenAI, Qwen, Llama) and running the provided experiment scripts to evaluate personality alignment and evolution; the README and included experiments report quantitative validation. The framework is notable for its psychologically grounded design and cross-model validation reported by the authors.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository is ~307 days old (under one year) so it lacks a long production track record, but shows strong community interest (1.1k stars), an associated arXiv paper and experimental validation across multiple LLM families; these factors support a beta-level TRL rather than production.
prerequisites: access to an LLM backend (OpenAI/Qwen/Llama) and API keys
basic familiarity with running Python scripts and environment variables
student_project_ideas: Integrate JPAF with a simulated multi-agent environment (e.g. a simple social simulation in Python) to study how different MBTI configurations affect team coordination and task performance.
Adapt JPAF to drive NPC dialogue in a small game prototype using an open-source LLM (local Llama) and measure perceived personality consistency and player engagement.

tools.name: openlayers/ol-cesium
tools.desc: OpenLayers - Cesium integration

tools.name: apache/ofbiz-framework
tools.desc: Apache OFBiz is an open source product for the automation of enterprise processes. It includes framework components and business applications for ERP, CRM, E-Business/E-Commerce, Supply Chain Management and Manufacturing Resource Planning. OFBiz provides a foundation and starting point for reliable, secure and scalable enterprise solutions.

tools.name: EL4CTEO/blender-skills
tools.desc: Professional Blender 5.3 workflows as Agent Skills for Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI, Copilot and Cursor: modeling, UVs, PBR, baking, rigging, animation, export and QA.

cls.summary: A collection of 28 Blender automation scripts packaged as AI 'skills' so coding agents (Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI, Copilot, Cursor) can perform common 3D workflows like modeling, UVs, PBR texturing, rigging, animation, baking, export and QA for Blender 5.2+ (verified on 5.3).
cls.what_it_does: This repository provides tested Python skills that let AI coding agents run professional Blender workflows headlessly or via a local MCP server, automating tasks such as retopology, PBR material setup, baking, rigging, LOD creation and export pipelines for game engines. It is notable because the author packaged discrete, tested workflows as agent-installable skills and includes automated tests (67 headless Blender tests) and an installer for multiple agent platforms.
cls.trl_rationale: The repo is very new (created 34 days ago) which limits TRL despite strong indicators: 1151 stars, a comprehensive README, an installer, and 67 headless Blender tests with verification on Blender 5.3; these suggest early adopters and demonstrable use but not a multi-release production track record.
prerequisites: an AI coding agent or ability to install agent skills (Claude/Codex/Gemini/Copilot/Cursor) if using agent integration
student_project_ideas: Use the blender-skills automation to build a pipeline that takes a sculpt and produces a game-ready asset (retopology, baking, LODs) and exports it to Unity or Godot for performance testing.

Create an automated asset QA tool using the blender-asset-qa skill to detect common issues (bad normals, z-fighting, floating parts) and produce a report and corrected export for a small asset library.

tools.name: wici-ai/inferssd
tools.desc: Run models larger than your RAM or VRAM by streaming MoE experts from SSD. Built on llama.cpp.

cls.summary: InferSSD is an open-source runtime that streams mixture-of-experts (MoE) model weights from SSD so very large LLMs can run on machines with limited RAM/VRAM.
cls.what_it_does: InferSSD lets you run enormous MoE language models by keeping inactive expert weights on SSD and loading active experts on demand, building on llama.cpp and standard GGUF model files. It provides a command-line chat, a browser web UI and an OpenAI-compatible API and supports macOS (Metal), Linux (CUDA) and Windows builds or installers.
cls.trl_rationale: The repository is very new (created 26 days ago) but already provides installers, prebuilt packages and many stars which indicates active early adoption; however the short public track record and recent creation limit it to TRL 5.
prerequisites: Git and Python 3.9+ for source builds
CUDA toolkit and NVIDIA drivers for GPU builds (Linux)
Xcode Command Line Tools for macOS builds
systemd with cgroup v2 on Linux (per README notes)
student_project_ideas: Measure and compare inference throughput and latency for a chosen MoE GGUF model on two hardware setups (e.g., local laptop with SSD vs cloud GPU instance) and document how SSD streaming affects performance and memory usage.

Integrate InferSSD with a simple monitoring dashboard (Prometheus/Grafana) to visualise memory, SSD I/O and model token throughput during inference and evaluate trade-offs for operational deployment of large LLMs.

tools.name: DroneBridge/ESP32
tools.desc: DroneBridge for ESP32. A secure & transparent telemetry link with support for WiFi and ESP-NOW. Supporting MAVLink, MSP, LTM or any other protocol

tools.name: agenmod/immortal-skill
tools.desc: ♾️ 开源数字永生框架 — 从聊天记录蒸馏任何人的七维数字分身。支持微信/飞书/iMessage/Telegram等12+平台，7种角色模板，对齐 OpenClaw Soul Spec 标准。一行指令让你的AI学会蒸馏。

cls.summary: An open-source framework that distills a person's conversational and documentary traces into a loadable AI persona (a digital 'immortality' or digital-twin of an individual) with connectors for many messaging platforms.
cls.what_it_does: It extracts and structures chat logs and other digital traces into a multi-dimensional persona representation that can be loaded by agent runtimes to emulate someone's style, opinions and decision patterns. The project provides a core 'skill' engine plus companion skills for distillation, protection and licensing, and includes integrations for many messaging platforms and prebuilt persona examples. It is notable for packaging a full distillation pipeline and policy/protection components as an ecosystem of skills.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository is ~230 days old (<1 year) but has substantial community interest (1.1k stars), an ecosystem of companion repos and documented workflows; that points to a beta-level project with active development rather than long-term production maturity.
prerequisites: experience with LLM APIs and agent frameworks
access tokens for messaging platforms (WeChat, Telegram, Feishu, iMessage) and possibly vector DBs
student_project_ideas: Build a small persona by distilling a course instructor's public lecture transcripts and deploy it as a Telegram chatbot that answers syllabus and course-policy questions, evaluating fidelity and hallucination rates against ground-truth answers.

Compare privacy-protection strategies by using the project's distill-shield workflow to produce two personas from the same dataset—one protected and one unprotected—and measure information leakage and downstream model behaviour.

tools.name: mlc-ai/web-llm-chat
tools.desc: Chat with AI large language models running natively in your browser. Enjoy private, server-free, seamless AI conversations.

cls.summary: WebLLM Chat is an open-source web chat interface that runs large language models directly in the browser using WebGPU so conversations remain local and private.
cls.what_it_does: WebLLM Chat provides a user-friendly chat UI that runs LLM inference client-side (via WebGPU and the WebLLM runtime), supporting text and image inputs and the ability to point the UI at a locally hosted MLC-LLM REST API. It is used by running the Next.js app locally or deploying the static/site build or Docker container; it is notable for enabling server-free, privacy-preserving LLM use in-browser and for integrating with WebLLM/MLC-LLM.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository is active (last push 2026-11-02), has substantial community interest (1k+ stars) and a public demo (chat.webllm.ai), and documents deployment paths (Docker, Next.js). This indicates production-ready software rather than an experimental prototype.
student_project_ideas: Build a domain-specific, privacy-preserving chatbot by converting a technical model to MLC format, hosting it with MLC-LLM, and connecting it to WebLLM Chat for evaluation against domain queries.
Measure and compare in-browser inference latency, memory use and energy consumption of several LLMs (different sizes) across desktop and mobile browsers using WebLLM Chat as the frontend.

tools.name: icosa-foundation/open-brush
tools.desc: Open Brush is the open source, community led evolution of Tilt Brush! Forked from https://github.com/googlevr/tilt-brush

cls.summary: Open Brush is an open-source, community-maintained VR 3D-painting application (a fork of Google’s Tilt Brush) that runs on Unity and targets VR headsets like Meta Quest and SteamVR.
cls.what_it_does: Open Brush provides room-scale 3D painting and sketching tools for virtual reality, letting users create volumetric brush strokes and export or save sketches. It is distributed as a Unity project and as prebuilt releases for multiple VR stores/platforms; notable aspects are active community maintenance, modern Unity upgrades, and official builds for Quest, SteamVR and other headsets.
cls.trl_rationale: The project is long-lived (created 2021), actively maintained with recent pushes and formal releases, distributed on multiple stores (Quest, Steam) and has substantial community uptake (1k+ stars and official builds), indicating maturity and broad adoption.
student_project_ideas: Extend Open Brush with a custom export plugin that converts brush strokes into a lightweight scene format (glTF) and integrate it with a web 3D viewer to demonstrate VR-to-web visualization workflows.

Create a study that measures usability and motion-sickness metrics for different brush interaction techniques by modifying input mappings in the Unity project and running user tests on Meta Quest or SteamVR headsets.

tools.name: paulmach/orb
tools.desc: Types and utilities for working with 2d geometry in Golang

tools.name: louiszengCN/CarlaAir
tools.desc: CarlaAir: Fly Drones Inside a CARLA World!! A Unified Infrastructure for Air-Ground Embodied Intelligence

cls.summary: CARLA-Air is an integrated simulator that runs multirotor UAVs and urban driving (CARLA) together in a single Unreal Engine process to support joint air-ground embodied intelligence research.
cls.what_it_does: CARLA-Air combines CARLA (urban driving) and AirSim (multirotor flight) into one shared-process Unreal Engine runtime to provide synchronized sensors, exact coordinate alignment and low-latency joint simulations. It is used via provided Python and ROS 2 APIs and prebuilt binaries, and notable features include cross-aligned sensor modalities, binary releases for Ubuntu/Windows, and out-of-the-box ROS 2 examples.
cls.trl_rationale: The project provides versioned releases (v0.1.7), prebuilt binaries for Linux/Windows, a test suite (89/89 CARLA API tests passing) and ROS 2 examples, indicating a beta-level, actively maintained simulator; however the repository is under 1 year old so it is capped at TRL 6 by the stated policy.
prerequisites: familiarity with CARLA or AirSim concepts
Unreal Engine basics (for custom asset work)
student_project_ideas: Develop and evaluate a multi-agent air-ground coordination policy by integrating a ROS 2 planner node with CARLA-Air to command a drone and an autonomous vehicle in a joint urban scenario and measure safety/throughput trade-offs.

Extend CARLA-Air with a custom sensor (e.g. a thermal camera or custom LiDAR plugin) and run experiments comparing perception-based landing or handover strategies between ground and aerial agents using the provided Python API.

tools.name: foxssake/netfox
tools.desc: Addons for building multiplayer games with Godot

cls.summary: Netfox is a collection of Godot engine addons that provide networking and netcode features (timing, rollback, interpolation and prediction) to build responsive online multiplayer games.
cls.what_it_does: Netfox provides client-server networking primitives, consistent timing, rollback-based physics support, client-side prediction and server reconciliation, and integrations (noray) for connectivity; it is installed as Godot addons and used inside Godot 4.x projects. It is notable for shipping multiple example projects (including a sample game 'Forest Brawl'), a rollback debugger, and packaged releases that include dependencies for easy use.
cls.trl_rationale: The repository is several years old, has many stars (1.1k), packaged releases, multiple example projects and a demo game, and recent active commits, indicating production-ready maturity for game development use.
prerequisites: Familiarity with Godot 4.x and the Godot editor
student_project_ideas: Implement a small physics-based multiplayer demo in Godot using netfox to compare smoothness and latency handling with Godot's basic networking API.
Build a networked robot-simulation prototype (simple agents in an environment) using netfox for synchronization and test rollback prediction effects on controller performance.

tools.name: bitbrain/pandora
tools.desc: Godot 4 addon for RPG data management such items, inventories, spells, mobs, quests and NPCs.

cls.summary: Pandora is a Godot 4 editor addon that provides data management and an API for RPG elements such as items, spells, characters, monsters and loot tables.
cls.what_it_does: Pandora centralises RPG game data inside the Godot editor with a dedicated UI for creating and editing entities (items, spells, mobs, quests, etc.) and exposes a runtime API via a Pandora singleton for accessing and instancing those entities in game code. It is intended to simplify content management for Godot-based RPGs and includes unit tests and an accessible API for tool scripts and runtime use.
cls.trl_rationale: The project is several years old, has many stars and active development, but the README explicitly states it is still in alpha and not production-ready; there are unit tests and releases but no evidence of wide production adoption or a stable 1.0 release, so TRL is limited to Alpha-in-use.
prerequisites: Understanding of game entity/data concepts (items, inventories, etc.)

alternatives_to: Godot AssetLib plugins for inventory/item systems

tools.name: openwisp/django-rest-framework-gis
tools.desc: Geographic add-ons for Django REST Framework. Maintained by the OpenWISP Project.

tools.name: FreeCAD/FreeCAD-addons
tools.desc: Legacy index for FreeCAD < 1.0.0

tools.name: manycoretech/aholo-viewer
tools.desc: A high performance 3DGS renderer

cls.summary: Aholo Viewer is a high-performance renderer for 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) and meshes that supports chunked streaming level-of-detail so very large reconstructed scenes can be visualised in the browser and native host.
cls.what_it_does: Aholo Viewer renders 3DGS (Gaussian splatting) and mesh data with a chunked streaming LOD scheme to handle extremely large scenes. It is provided as an npm/TypeScript renderer package plus native C++ tooling for asset conversion and processing (splat-transform) so it can be used in web apps and native pipelines. Notable features are its focus on high-performance streaming LOD for huge point-cloud-like datasets and an associated asset conversion toolchain.
cls.trl_rationale: The project is an active, well-starred open-source repository with TypeScript renderer packages, native C++ tooling, examples and documentation, indicating beta-level maturity. However the repo is under one year old so, per the stated rule, it should be capped at TRL 6 despite strong community interest.
prerequisites: C++ toolchain for native packages (build tools, compilers)
basic WebGL/three.js or web 3D knowledge to integrate renderer
student_project_ideas: Build a web-based viewer that streams a large photogrammetry or LiDAR-derived 3DGS dataset using Aholo Viewer and measure interactive frame rates and bandwidth usage for different chunk/Lod settings.

Create a preprocessing pipeline that converts point clouds (e.g. from Open3D or PDAL) into the ESZ chunked LOD format using Aholo's splat-transform native tools and demonstrate integration with a simple digital-twin web dashboard.

tools.name: deepopen-com/deepopen-3d-webs
tools.desc: Image-driven 3D scene generation system. Users provide a reference image and prompt words, and the system generates previewable, replayable, and traceable scene results according to the camera trajectory; official 3D demonstration assets allow direct viewing of color/depth animations and Gaussian point clouds in the browser 图像驱动的三维场景生成系统

cls.summary: DeepOpen-3d-webs is a Python web app that produces previewable Gaussian point‑cloud 3D scenes and color/depth flythroughs from a single reference image and textual prompts.
cls.what_it_does: The project converts a single image plus prompt into a walk‑around style 3D scene by estimating depth, baking 3D Gaussians and rendering color/depth animations along camera trajectories; it runs as a web service (Gradio/FastAPI) with demo mode that needs no GPU and a full CUDA mode for generation. Notable features include browser preview of Gaussian point clouds, exportable PLY assets for downstream tools, and an end‑to‑end pipeline (preview, bake Gaussians, render video) packaged with Docker images.
cls.trl_rationale: The repository is feature-rich, ships Docker images, and includes demo assets and a runnable web UI, but it is very new (created 22 days ago) so there is no long-term production track record; under the age rule this supports an alpha/in‑use TRL (~5).
prerequisites: Docker (for demo image) and optional CUDA/GPU knowledge for full generation
familiarity with point cloud/PLY and image processing concepts
student_project_ideas: Create a short workflow that takes classroom photos and uses DeepOpen-3d-webs to generate point‑cloud PLY exports, then postprocess them in MeshLab or Blender to evaluate geometry quality versus the input image.

Compare depth and 3D reconstruction quality across different diffusion/backbone models provided by the repo (e.g. SD1.5 vs Realistic Vision) by running batch generations and quantifying depth consistency and rendering artefacts.

tools.name: xiaoiver/infinite-canvas-tutorial
tools.desc: A tutorial on infinite canvas

cls.summary: A hands‑on tutorial repository that implements an GPU-accelerated infinite canvas (2D) using WebGL/WebGPU, an ECS architecture and SDF rendering, aimed at teaching how to build high-performance browser drawing editors.
cls.what_it_does: The project provides lesson-based code and a live app that demonstrates an 'infinite canvas' editor implemented with a hardware abstraction layer for WebGL/WebGPU, an ECS (Becsy) architecture, SDF-based shape rendering and GPU text/Bezier rendering. It is used as a learning course: each lesson is a self-contained step (initialization, shapes, camera, events, optimisation, export, etc.), with runnable packages and a site for interactive exploration.
cls.trl_rationale: The repo is actively maintained, has many stars (1.1k) and an interactive site and multiple lesson packages, indicating more than an ad-hoc demo; it provides install/run instructions and examples. However it is a tutorial/course codebase rather than a widely deployed production library, so it best fits a beta-level TRL rather than production-ready.
student_project_ideas: Extend the tutorial renderer to add a new SDF shape (e.g. star polygon) and evaluate performance impacts when batching vs individual draw calls, measuring FPS and draw-call counts in a browser.

Integrate the infinite canvas with a simple CRDT-based collaborative layer (Yjs) and build a demo where two browser clients concurrently edit shapes and resolve conflicts while profiling network and rendering performance.

tools.name: jaredrhod/barehands
tools.desc: Move things on your screen with your bare hands. A webcam-powered, hand-tracked interface for your AI. No headset. No controllers.

cls.summary: barehands is a browser-based, webcam-powered hand-tracking interface that lets you manipulate notes, images and 3D models on-screen and connect those gestures to an AI via simple file- or HTTP-based hooks.
cls.what_it_does: barehands uses Google MediaPipe in the browser and three.js to present a floating 'board' of cards and 3D props you can pinch, throw, scale and explode with real hand gestures; it runs from a lightweight Python server and exposes simple file/curl protocols so any AI or script can control the stage or reflect state. It is notable for running entirely with a webcam (no headset/controllers), an easy vault-based content system (Markdown/media folders), and simple, safe APIs for wiring in assistants like Claude or local agents.
cls.trl_rationale: The project is active, well-documented and runnable with examples and a simple server, and it has many stars and forks indicating community interest; however the repo is under one year old so there is not yet a long track record required for TRL 7+, so Beta (TRL 6) is appropriate.
prerequisites: Chrome or Chromium-based browser and a webcam
student_project_ideas: Build an assistive AR interface that connects a local LLM to barehands so voice or text queries cause the AI to present and manipulate relevant documents and 3D models on the board.

Integrate barehands with an OBS streaming setup to create a live tutorial system that records instructor hand interactions with exploded views of a CAD model (combine with a simple CAD export pipeline or glTF assets).

tools.name: agi-brain/xuance
tools.desc: XuanCe: A Comprehensive and Unified Deep Reinforcement Learning Library

cls.summary: XuanCe is an open-source Python library that implements a large collection of deep reinforcement learning (DRL) and multi-agent RL algorithms with support for multiple deep learning backends and environments.
cls.what_it_does: XuanCe provides modular implementations of many DRL and MARL algorithms (DQN, PPO, SAC, Dreamer, IQL, etc.), integrates with common environments and backends, and offers tools for distributed training, hyperparameter tuning and logging. It is used by researchers and engineers to train and evaluate RL agents across benchmarks and custom environments, notable for backend compatibility (PyTorch, TensorFlow2, MindSpore) and a broad algorithm zoo.
cls.trl_rationale: The repository is over three years old, has 1,115 stars, an active recent commit history and published documentation and an associated arXiv paper, indicating production-ready maturity and community adoption; however it is not a de-facto standard across industry so TRL 7 is appropriate.
prerequisites: familiarity with PyTorch or TensorFlow (or MindSpore)
student_project_ideas: Compare training stability and sample efficiency of PPO vs SAC on a continuous control task (MuJoCo/Gym) using XuanCe, logging results to TensorBoard/W&B and analysing hyperparameter sensitivity.

Use XuanCe to implement a MARL scenario (e.g. multi-agent navigation or cooperative stacking) and evaluate value-decomposition (VDN) versus independent learning (IQL), then visualise agent behaviours in a simulator.

tools.name: FuJacob/cotabby
tools.desc: Cotabby is local AI autocomplete for your entire Mac. Open source. On device. Everywhere you type.

cls.summary: Cotabby is an open-source macOS app that provides local AI inline autocomplete (ghost-text) across nearly any text field on a Mac.
cls.what_it_does: Cotabby provides AI-powered inline (ghost-text) autocomplete and quick macros while you type on macOS, using on-device models or a configured OpenAI-compatible endpoint. It installs as a menu-bar app, supports multiple local GGUF models via llama.cpp, and offers features like emoji completion, one-key autocorrect and inline conversions.
cls.trl_rationale: The project is actively developed, published to Homebrew, and has a substantial star count and releases, indicating beta-level maturity; however the repository is only ~7 months old so by the TRL rules it should be rated at most 6.
prerequisites: macOS 14.0+ (macOS 26+ recommended for Apple Intelligence engine)
Optional: local GGUF model files to run Open Source engine

tools.name: Sollimann/bonsai
tools.desc: Rust implementation of behavior trees for deterministic AI (now with Python bindings)

cls.summary: Bonsai is an open-source Rust library (with Python bindings) that implements behavior trees for deterministic AI and control in games and robotics.
cls.what_it_does: Bonsai provides an implementation of behavior trees to express decision and control logic as modular, reactive tree structures. It is used as a library in Rust (crates.io) and from Python (bonsai-bt on PyPI), with examples for robotics and game use; notable points are its Rust implementation, Python bindings, and examples demonstrating async/background task patterns for long-running actions.
cls.trl_rationale: The repository is multi-year (created 2022), has substantial community interest (1,110 stars), active recent commits and maintained examples and Python bindings; these indicate production-ready library status rather than a fragile prototype.
prerequisites: basic understanding of behavior trees and concurrency/async concepts
student_project_ideas: Implement a ROS2 node that uses Bonsai to control a mobile robot's navigation behaviours and test it in simulation (Gazebo) to demonstrate modular decision logic and recovery behaviours.

Create a game AI for a simple simulation (Bevy or Unreal) using Bonsai to manage NPC behaviours, then measure robustness by introducing long-running tasks and using the library's async/background patterns.

tools.name: dimartarmizi/map-to-poster
tools.desc: MapToPoster JS is a client-side web app that turns any location into a high-resolution, customizable map poster with various themes, layouts, and export options.

cls.summary: MapToPoster JS is a client-side web app that creates high-resolution, customizable map posters from any location using Leaflet and MapLibre with export options suitable for large-format printing.
cls.what_it_does: It converts searchable geographic locations into stylised, printable map posters by combining raster tile rendering (Leaflet) and procedural vector styles (MapLibre GL), with features like draggable markers, plotted routes, framing effects and high-fidelity PNG export. The app runs entirely in the browser (client-side), supports custom themes and fonts, and can export ultra-high-resolution images for printing.
cls.trl_rationale: The project is well-documented, has Docker support, active commits and many stars indicating community interest, but the repository is under one year old (created 273 days ago) so it lacks the multi-year track record or widespread production deployments required for TRL7+.
prerequisites: optional CARTO API key for some raster basemaps
student_project_ideas: Create a lab exercise where students build a custom thematic poster generator for city infrastructure data by overlaying GeoJSON layers (e.g. bike lanes or utilities) on MapToPoster and exporting printable high-resolution posters.

Develop a student project that integrates MapToPoster with an OSRM-based route planner to visualise and print optimized delivery or inspection routes for a small network, including automated legend and metadata export.

tools.name: opengeospatial/geoparquet
tools.desc: Specification for storing geospatial vector data (point, line, polygon) in Parquet

cls.summary: GeoParquet is an open specification for storing geospatial vector data (points, lines, polygons) inside Apache Parquet files to enable interoperable, cloud-native geospatial workflows.
cls.what_it_does: GeoParquet defines metadata, JSON schema and examples that describe how to encode geospatial vector geometries and coordinate reference system information inside Parquet. It is used by libraries and tools to read/write geospatial tables in a columnar, compressed format suitable for analytics and cloud data warehouses, and is notable for wide multi-language support and formalisation as an OGC working group specification.
cls.trl_rationale: The project is multi-year (created 2021), has substantial community adoption (over 20 implementations noted, many contributors and 1100+ stars) and is maintained as an OGC Standards Working Group item; that track record supports a mature TRL 8 assessment even though it's not yet a de-facto single standard.
prerequisites: experience with Python or other data libraries (e.g. Arrow/GeoPandas) helpful
student_project_ideas: Compare storage size and query performance for a city-scale vector dataset saved as GeoParquet, GeoJSON and Shapefile, using GeoPandas + DuckDB to benchmark read/filter workloads.

Build a simple cloud-native pipeline that ingests GeoParquet files into a data warehouse (e.g. BigQuery or DuckDB + Parquet), performs spatial joins, and visualises results in a web map using a lightweight tile/server stack.

tools.name: linorobot/linorobot2
tools.desc: Autonomous mobile robots (2WD, 4WD, Mecanum Drive)

cls.summary: linorobot2 is an open-source ROS 2 package that provides a complete foundation (URDF, sensors, SLAM, Nav2 and robot_localization) to run and simulate 2WD/4WD/Mecanum autonomous mobile robots in Gazebo and on real hardware.
cls.what_it_does: It bundles pre-configured ROS 2 components (Nav2, SLAM Toolbox, robot_localization) and templated robot URDFs so you can simulate or run an autonomous mobile robot with minimal setup. It includes tools to convert floorplan images or SLAM maps into Gazebo worlds, sensor driver setup, and micro-ROS firmware integration for real hardware, making it notable for matching simulation and physical robot configurations.
cls.trl_rationale: The repository is mature and actively maintained since 2021 with over 1k stars, documented integration with Nav2/SLAM Toolbox/robot_localization and a hardware guide for real robots; this indicates production-ready software used by projects rather than a short-lived prototype.
prerequisites: Linux command-line and package build tools
student_project_ideas: Build and tune a Nav2 navigation stack for a simulated Mecanum robot in Gazebo, then transfer the tuned parameters to a physical robot using the linorobot2 hardware guide.

Create an automated mapping and obstacle-avoidance experiment by converting a real building floorplan into a Gazebo world with image_to_gazebo and evaluating SLAM and path-following performance under different sensor noise models.

tools.name: viblo/pymunk
tools.desc: Pymunk is a easy-to-use pythonic 2d physics library that can be used whenever  you need 2d rigid body physics from Python

tools.name: Pan-Chera/Multi-Agent-CAD
tools.desc: MAC (Multi-Agent CAD): A decoupled multi-agent framework for text-to-CAD generation via constrained test-time compute

cls.summary: MAC is an open-source multi-agent text-to-CAD framework that turns natural-language design briefs into editable CAD geometry (STEP/STL/GLB) and can generate, assemble, verify and export multipart mechanisms including URDF for simulation.
cls.what_it_does: MAC automates generation of parametric engineering geometry from natural-language prompts using a decoupled multi-agent pipeline; it can create single printable parts or decompose and generate multi-part assemblies, perform visual and geometric verification, and export artifacts (STEP, STL, GLB, URDF) for downstream inspection and simulation. It is notable for combining an LLM-driven planning and generation pipeline with CAD kernels (Build123d / OpenCascade), an independent Judge, and documented benchmark results for token/cost efficiency.
cls.trl_rationale: The repository shows substantial functionality, documented benchmarks, example galleries, and active development with many stars, indicating beta-level maturity; however it is only ~110 days old so there is not yet the long track record or stable ecosystem required for TRL 7+.
prerequisites: basic CAD modelling knowledge (parametric geometry, assemblies)
access to an LLM API (for full functionality) and familiarity with command-line workflows
student_project_ideas: Compare CAD outputs and manufacturability of parts generated by MAC from the same prompt using two LLM backends (e.g. Qwen vs another model), then validate geometries in a slicer or FEA tool.
Use MAC to generate a small articulated mechanism from a natural-language brief, export URDF and run physics simulation (e.g. in PyBullet) to evaluate kinematics and collisions.

tools.name: gopcua/opcua
tools.desc: Native Go OPC-UA library

tools.name: kyky2347/ALTA
tools.desc: Autonomous LLM Trading Asterism — a research-only multi-agent trading platform with evidence-first research, an auditable console, Shadow simulation and explicitly authorized broker execution.

cls.summary: ALTA is an open-source, local multi-agent research platform that runs specialised LLM agents to investigate trading opportunities, produce auditable research trails, and optionally route orders to broker APIs or a shadow simulator.
cls.what_it_does: ALTA coordinates specialised LLM agents (Scouts, reviewers, strategy desks) to discover, test and document trading theses, preserving an inspectable evidence trail for each handoff. It provides a local operator console (React frontend), an internal shadow simulator for offline comparison, and an explicit broker-execution boundary for authorised live orders. The project is notable for combining multi-agent orchestration, an auditable record of agent outputs and separate execution modes (Shadow vs Broker API).
cls.trl_rationale: Repository is recent (created ~82 days ago) so maturity is limited despite strong community interest (1000+ stars), a substantial README, architecture docs and recorded audits; evidence indicates an alpha used by early adopters rather than long-running production deployments.
student_project_ideas: Extend ALTA with a new Scout agent that monitors a specific dataset (e.g. economic indicators) and evaluate its signalling performance in the shadow simulator versus other Scouts.

Build an audit analysis tool that ingests ALTA's research trail and produces visual summaries of reviewer disagreement, decision timelines and execution outcomes for a class study on evidence-based automated decision making.

tools.name: marc-shade/world-intel-mcp
tools.desc: 160-tool MCP server for real-time global intelligence from free public APIs: markets, liquidity, prediction markets, SEC filings, conflict, military, aircraft-cohort early warning, migration and border flows, cyber, climate, news and more. Dated observation history, 29 research prompts, cited briefs, geofences, SSE dashboard. MIT, no paid API keys.

cls.summary: A Python-based Model Context Protocol (MCP) server that collects and indexes real-time open-source intelligence across many domains and exposes it via an MCP API, CLI and a Qdrant-backed semantic search dashboard.
cls.what_it_does: The project collects time-stamped observations from many free public APIs (markets, conflict, aviation, migration, cyber, climate, etc.), stores them in a Qdrant vector store for semantic search, and exposes tools and queryable context to AI agents via the Model Context Protocol. It is notable for its broad domain coverage (160 MCP tools across ~30 domains), dated observation history for reproducible research, built-in MCP prompts/resources, and a live ops-dashboard and CLI for exploration.
cls.trl_rationale: The repository is a mature, actively maintained project with many stars, a CLI, dashboard and a Qdrant-backed architecture, indicating an installed base and polish; however it is under one year old so by the provided rules its TRL is capped at 6 (beta).
prerequisites: experience with APIs and JSON data
student_project_ideas: Build a focused monitoring agent that queries the MCP server and issues cross-domain alerts (e.g. correlated market-drop + news spike + air-traffic anomalies) and present a dashboard summarising false positives and precision.
Use the server's Qdrant semantic index to research historical correlations between geopolitical events (ACLED) and regional market movements, producing reproducible dated reports and visualisations.

tools.name: pguso/agents-from-scratch
tools.desc: Build AI agents from first principles using a local LLM - no frameworks, no cloud APIs, no hidden reasoning.

cls.summary: A hands-on, lesson-driven Python repository that teaches how to build an AI agent from first principles using a local LLM and no external frameworks or cloud APIs.
cls.what_it_does: This repo walks learners through 12 incremental lessons that implement a single evolving agent (LLM I/O, prompts, structured output, tools, memory, planning, evals, telemetry) with runnable examples. It is used as an educational codebase: you run the supplied examples against a local GGUF model and read the lessons to learn agent architecture and implementation details. It is notable for its local-first, framework-free approach and clear, lesson-by-lesson code that exposes all logic rather than hiding it behind libraries.
cls.trl_rationale: The repository is active, has a comprehensive README, runnable examples (complete_example.py), lesson files and an evals/telemetry system, and a significant star/fork count indicating community interest; however it was created <1 year ago so lacks the multi-year adoption or stable production references required for TRL7+, limiting it to TRL6.
prerequisites: familiarity with LLM concepts and prompts
student_project_ideas: Extend the provided agent to add a new tool (e.g. a web scraper or a local file search) and write eval cases that measure task success across the agent's decision and planning modules.
Integrate the agent with a simple robot simulator (ROS 2 or a mock environment) so the agent issues high-level commands and you implement an execution layer that logs telemetry and verifies actions.

tools.name: OranAi-Ltd/oransim
tools.desc: Causal Digital Twin for Marketing at Scale · Predict any marketing decision before you spend a dollar.

cls.summary: Oransim is an open-source causal simulation engine that predicts counterfactual marketing campaign outcomes (pre‑launch, mid‑campaign interventions and post‑mortem) using a synthetic consumer population and a transparent causal graph.
cls.what_it_does: Oransim builds a causal digital-twin of a marketing campaign to estimate counterfactual ROI and rollout effects without running real experiments; users run the engine locally or via its API to simulate interventions (do() calls) and inspect the causal graph that produced predictions. It is notable for exposing the causal mechanism (decomposable graph, per-arm counterfactuals) and shipping a small demo dataset while enterprise customers license larger datasets and data refresh.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository is ~7 months old and shows active development, many stars (1k+), example demo data and runnable instructions; the README also claims enterprise use and licensed datasets which supports beta maturity, but the project is still young so TRL is capped at 6.
student_project_ideas: Clone the repo and run the 21k-note demo to reproduce an example pre-launch ranking of creatives × KOLs, then extend the scenario by adding a synthetic new KOL and compare counterfactual ROI.

Build a short study comparing Oransim's counterfactual rollout to a black‑box time‑series predictor (e.g. Prophet) on the same demo corpus and report differences in interpretability and estimated lift.

tools.name: mybigday/llama.rn
tools.desc: React Native binding of llama.cpp

cls.summary: A React Native binding that lets mobile apps run llama.cpp-based LLM inference (with Metal/OpenCL/Hexagon acceleration) on iOS and Android.
cls.what_it_does: llama.rn exposes llama.cpp inference functionality to React Native apps so developers can run local LLMs on-device (chat/completion, embeddings, multimodal inputs and TTS). It provides prebuilt binaries, GPU/NPU acceleration support (Metal, OpenCL, Hexagon), parallel decoding/queueing and helpers for model loading and inference, making on-device LLM integration for mobile apps significantly easier.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository is several years old, has many stars and active development, publishes prebuilt binaries and release downloads, and documents production-oriented features (GPU/NPU, postinstall binary downloader), indicating production-ready software rather than a research prototype.
prerequisites: familiarity with local LLM models / gguf formats
student_project_ideas: Build a React Native mobile chatbot that uses llama.rn with a quantized GGUF model to run fully on-device, measure latency/energy and compare Metal vs OpenCL acceleration.
Integrate llama.rn into a mobile robotics operator app to perform natural-language mission briefing and local inference for command parsing, combined with a ROS 2 backend for robot control.

tools.name: docker/compose-for-agents
tools.desc: Build and run AI agents using Docker Compose. A collection of ready-to-use examples for orchestrating open-source LLMs, tools, and agent runtimes.

cls.summary: A collection of Docker Compose example projects for running and orchestrating open-source LLMs, agent runtimes and tool integrations locally or in cloud contexts.
cls.what_it_does: Provides ready-to-run demo projects that use Docker Compose to orchestrate agent runtimes, local LLMs (via Docker Model Runner) and external Model/Capability Providers (MCPs) such as OpenAI. Each demo is self-contained and runnable by following the provided compose files and environment examples, making it easy to prototype multi-agent and single-agent workflows and mixed local/remote model deployments.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository is over a year old, actively maintained with many stars/forks and numerous runnable example projects and compose files; demonstrates production-oriented orchestration patterns rather than a narrow research prototype.
prerequisites: Docker (Desktop or Engine) and Docker Compose
Optional GPU drivers for local model runtimes or cloud context configuration
Basic familiarity with environment secrets and compose overlays
student_project_ideas: Create a capstone project that composes a multi-agent pipeline using one of the demos, adding a simple sensor/data source (MQTT) and evaluating end-to-end latency and reliability when switching between local model runner and OpenAI as the MCP.

Extend a demo to integrate an engineering toolchain (for example, a small REST-based simulation or database) and implement automated test scenarios to validate agent behaviours and verify outputs against expected rules.

tools.name: drprojects/superpoint_transformer
tools.desc: Official PyTorch implementation of Superpoint Transformer [ICCV'23], SuperCluster [3DV'24 Oral], and EZ-SP [ICRA'26]

cls.summary: Superpoint Transformer is an open-source PyTorch implementation of superpoint-based transformer architectures for fast, scalable semantic and panoptic segmentation of large 3D point‑cloud scenes.
cls.what_it_does: The repository implements Superpoint Transformer (SPT), SuperCluster and EZ‑SP: methods that partition point clouds into hierarchical 'superpoints', run lightweight transformer models over the superpoint graph for semantic segmentation, and perform scalable panoptic instance clustering. It is used as a research and production-ready codebase to train/evaluate 3D segmentation models on large datasets and includes fast GPU preprocessing and graph clustering utilities that make it notable for processing very large scenes on a single GPU.
cls.trl_rationale: The project implements peer-reviewed ICCV/3DV/ICRA papers, has substantial community interest (1k+ stars), active maintenance through 2026 and usable training/inference code and datasets; this indicates production-ready research code used in projects though not an industry de-facto standard.
prerequisites: familiarity with point cloud data formats and 3D datasets
basic experience with training deep learning models
student_project_ideas: Implement a pipeline that uses EZ‑SP partitioning plus SPT to semantic-segment building scans (e.g. S3DIS) and visualise results in Open3D or Potree, comparing accuracy and runtime against a baseline such as PointNet++.

Extend SuperCluster to perform panoptic segmentation on large outdoor lidar tiles (e.g. KITTI-360) and evaluate instance segmentation quality and scalability when processing contiguous tiles on a single GPU.

tools.name: Maran23/script-ide
tools.desc: Transforms the Script UI into an IDE like UI. Multiline Tabs, Splitting, Outline with unique icons that shows all members of the script. Quick search and function override functionality.

cls.summary: A Godot editor plugin that turns the built‑in script editor into an IDE‑like interface with multiline tabs, an enhanced outline, quick search and override popups.
cls.what_it_does: This Godot plugin modifies the Script editor to provide multiline/splittable tabs, a detailed outline of script members with filterable icons, quick file/method search popups, and an override helper for superclass methods. It is installed into the Godot editor and used by GDScript developers to navigate and edit scripts more quickly and with configurable UI behaviour.
cls.trl_rationale: The repository is an actively maintained, popular Godot editor plugin (1k+ stars), has distribution via the Godot Asset Library / Asset Store and regular commits, indicating production readiness and real users; the plugin has existed since 2023 and shows maturity beyond an experimental prototype.
prerequisites: How to install Godot editor plugins
student_project_ideas: Extend the plugin to add a custom linter rule for GDScript and demonstrate automated code quality checks in a Godot project.
Build a small Godot game and document how the Script IDE plugin improves developer productivity; optionally modify the plugin to add a project-specific quick search filter.

tools.name: zhoushoujianwork/easyeda-agent
tools.desc: 嘉立创 EDA 专业版（EasyEDA Pro）开源 AI 自动化：原理图、PCB 布局布线与工程检查，支持 CLI / Agent Skill / MCP。配套 EdaDesk Desktop 内测版可下载体验。Open-source AI schematic and PCB automation for EasyEDA Pro.

cls.summary: easyeda-agent is an open-source AI automation layer that performs schematic authoring, PCB layout/routing and engineering checks inside EasyEDA Pro via a CLI, agent Skill and MCP integration.
cls.what_it_does: It automates electronics design tasks for EasyEDA Pro: from reading datasheets to create symbols/footprints, selecting parts, producing schematics, arranging PCB layout, routing, copper pours and running DRC/DFM checks. It is used as a CLI/daemon, an AI Skill for agent clients (Codex/Claude etc.) or via an MCP connector and is notable for integrating datasheet-driven device creation, automated layout/routing heuristics and built-in verification before writing changes.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository is active with many stars (1k+), releases and a bundled Desktop beta, showing community interest and packaged binaries, but it was created ~145 days ago so lacks the multi-year production track record required for TRL 7+.
prerequisites: familiarity with EasyEDA Pro and enabling external connector
basic PCB and schematic design knowledge (components, footprints, DRC)
comfort with command-line tools and installing CLI/connector
student_project_ideas: Use easyeda-agent to implement a lecture assignment: automatically generate an ESP32 minimal-system schematic and 4-layer PCB, then run DRC and produce a manufacturing-ready report.

Build a datasheet-to-footprint pipeline that feeds PDF/device pages into easyeda-agent to create validated symbol/footprint/device entries and compare the agent's pin↔pad mappings against manual reference designs.

tools.desc: A multi-platform support c++11 library with focus on asio (asynchronous socket I/O) for any client applications.

tools.desc: The Legend of Sword and Fairy 3 (仙剑奇侠传三) & The Legend of Sword and Fairy 3 Gaiden: Wenqing Pian (仙剑奇侠传三外传：问情篇) re-implementation using C#/Unity

cls.summary: A community re-implementation of the classic RPG 'The Legend of Sword and Fairy 3' written in C# for the Unity engine that re-creates game logic and loads original game resources (the repository contains code only, not original game data).
cls.what_it_does: This project rewrites the original game's logic in C# and runs it inside Unity, providing tools (resource browser, effect editor, shaders) to inspect and export original game assets and to run the game if you supply the original game files. It's notable for a mostly code-driven reimplementation, support for URP shaders and editor tooling to index and preview original resources.
cls.trl_rationale: The repository is multi-year (created 2022) with many stars, active commits as recently as Nov 2026, CI for PRs, and the README states the full story and many systems are playable — evidence of a production-ready community project rather than a fragile prototype.
prerequisites: Access to original game data files (not provided)
student_project_ideas: Extend or refactor a subsystem (for example the effect system or resource browser) to add a new export format or UI features and evaluate performance impacts on desktop and mobile builds.

Build an automated tester that runs scripted playthroughs in the Unity build to validate scene loading and resource indexing, and report regressions when game data or code changes (combining the repository with CI tooling).

tools.name: rl-tools/rl-tools
tools.desc: The Fastest Deep Reinforcement Learning Library

cls.summary: RLtools is a high-performance C++ library for training and running deep reinforcement learning algorithms targeting control and robotics applications, including microcontrollers and MuJoCo environments.
cls.what_it_does: RLtools implements common deep RL algorithms (TD3, PPO, SAC, multi-agent PPO) in C++ for fast training and inference on desktop, GPU and embedded targets. It is used by running provided example 'zoo' programs or embedding its algorithms into custom environments, notable for benchmarks showing very fast training and support for microcontroller inference (tinyML).
cls.trl_rationale: The project is several years old, has a large star count (1059), active recent commits, documentation, papers and downstream projects cited in the README (e.g. Learning to Fly), and runnable examples and Docker images, indicating production-ready maturity for research and prototyping.
prerequisites: optional CUDA and MuJoCo knowledge for GPU and physics-based environments
student_project_ideas: Implement an RL controller for a simulated quadrotor using RLtools and MuJoCo, compare training speed and performance against a baseline (e.g. Stable Baselines3) and visualise results in the provided ExTrack UI.

Port a trained small neural controller from RLtools to run inference on a microcontroller (tinyML), measure latency and power on a target board and document the deployment pipeline using the library's tiny inference benchmarks.
