tools.desc: Generic and simple controls framework for ROS 2

tools.name: Dicklesworthstone/swiss_army_llama
tools.desc: A FastAPI service for semantic text search using precomputed embeddings and advanced similarity measures, with built-in support for various file types through textract.

cls.summary: Swiss Army Llama is a FastAPI service that extracts and caches embeddings from text, documents and audio, and provides semantic search and similarity endpoints for local LLMs.
cls.what_it_does: It provides REST endpoints to compute and cache embeddings from plaintext, PDFs, Word, images and audio (via Whisper), and supports semantic search over those embeddings using FAISS plus additional similarity measures. It is used as a local service (Docker or native Python) to expose embedding, similarity and completion functionality from local LLM runtimes such as llama.cpp, with utilities for OCR, document parsing (textract) and advanced similarity metrics.
cls.trl_rationale: The repository is mature (created Aug 2023, actively maintained with many stars and recent pushes) and includes deployment scripts, Docker support and documented installation paths, indicating production-ready software; however it is not a de-facto standard so TRL 7 is appropriate.
prerequisites: basic familiarity with LLM concepts and embeddings
optional: Docker and system-level dependencies (Tesseract, Redis) for full functionality
student_project_ideas: Build a searchable knowledge base for course materials by ingesting lecture slides, papers and recorded lecture audio into Swiss Army Llama and add a web UI that queries the service to return ranked, contextual excerpts.

Compare embedding pooling methods (mean, SVD, ICA, etc.) for domain-specific documents: ingest a corpus of technical reports, run retrieval experiments using FAISS + advanced similarity measures, and evaluate retrieval quality against a labelled relevance set.

tools.name: simplexai-labs/PolyStrata
tools.desc: Run large AI models on your own PC: Qwen3.8-Flash-Next on Strata's engine, and GLM 5.3 Flash, DeepSeek V4 Flash, LFM2.5, Qwen3.6, Ornith 1.5, Gemma 4, Tiel Coder and MiniCPM-V on a second engine written for PolyStrata. One-click install for Windows and Linux, OpenAI/Anthropic API on localhost.

cls.summary: PolyStrata is an open-source local inference server that runs large language and multimodal models on a single PC (Windows or Linux) using GPU acceleration.
cls.what_it_does: PolyStrata provides a one-click installer and inference engine(s) to run many large models (Qwen3.8-Flash-Next and a secondary engine supporting multiple other models) locally on consumer or workstation GPUs, exposing OpenAI/Anthropic-compatible APIs on localhost. It is notable for supporting large multimodal models on desktop GPUs, multi-GPU setups, and for integrating with local agents such as Linger.
cls.trl_rationale: The repository is very new (42 days) which limits demonstrated maturity; the README documents many models and usage tests on single PCs and laptops, and there is active development and many stars, but there is not yet a long track record of production deployments or stable, time-tested releases, so TRL is capped at 5.
prerequisites: NVIDIA or AMD GPU with sufficient VRAM (varies by model)
Windows or Linux familiarity and command-line usage
Large model files (gguf weights) and substantial disk/RAM capacity
student_project_ideas: Build a local coding assistant that uses PolyStrata-hosted Qwen3.8 to generate and unit-test small C++ functions, integrating it with a simple CI script to demonstrate closed-loop code generation and testing.

Measure inference throughput and memory usage for a selected model across different GPU configurations (8 GB laptop card vs 32 GB workstation) and produce a short report comparing performance, latency and resource trade-offs.

tools.name: agiwhitelist/auteur
tools.desc: The Claude Code skill that directs a website like a film. Commit-sheet, generated assets, build, and an executable anti-slop linter that gates every ship.

cls.summary: A Claude Code 'agent skill' that generates cinematic WebGL landing pages from a written commit-sheet and enforces design quality with an executable linter and motion QA.
cls.what_it_does: Auteur is an agent skill and set of Node.js scripts that automates art-directed website production: it profiles reference sites, generates assets, builds a single-WebGL-context landing page (GSAP/three.js), and gates outputs with an executable 'slopscan' linter and Playwright motion tests. It is notable for shipping a reproducible pipeline (SKILL.md) that can be installed into many agent CLIs and for enforcing strict design rules before allowing a site to ship.
cls.trl_rationale: The repository contains runnable scripts, a detailed README, and a live gallery of sites built with the tool, indicating user-facing functionality and examples; however the project is only ~4 months old so it lacks a longer track record required for TRL 7+.
prerequisites: an agent or CLI that reads SKILL.md (optional for full pipeline)
basic web development and WebGL familiarity
student_project_ideas: Build a small portfolio site generator that uses auteur's slopscan to enforce accessibility and motion rules, and extend its commit-sheet format to include project-specific metrics.
Compare performance and motion-quality of two WebGL landing page prototypes by running auteur's motionqa Playwright checks and measuring user-perceived motion on desktop vs mobile (DPR variations).

tools.desc: A comprehensive macromolecular library

tools.name: appsinacup/godot-rapier-physics
tools.desc: Godot Rapier Physics – 2D and 3D physics engine for the Godot game engine. with better stability, performance, liquids, determinism, state serialization and no ghost collisions.

cls.summary: A drop-in 2D and 3D physics plugin for the Godot game engine that replaces Godot's physics with the Rapier engine, offering improved stability, determinism, fluids and state serialization.
cls.what_it_does: Godot Rapier Physics replaces Godot's built-in 2D/3D physics with the Rapier physics engine and Salva fluids support to provide better stability, performance, deterministic cross-platform simulation and save/load of physics state. It is used as a Godot plugin or GDExtension (Rust), configurable via features for 2D/3D, SIMD/parallel builds and web targets, and can be installed via the Godot Asset Store or GitHub releases. Its notable aspects are deterministic simulation across platforms, state serialization for replay/save, and integration with Rust GDExtensions.
cls.trl_rationale: The project is over a year old, has active maintenance (recent pushes), many stars and releases, and explicit installation and CI instructions; these indicate production-ready maturity rather than a fragile prototype. The README notes some 3D features still missing, so it's mature but not necessarily feature-complete in all areas.
prerequisites: Familiarity with the Godot engine (editor and projects)
Basic Rust and GDExtension knowledge for custom builds
student_project_ideas: Build a Godot simulation of a robotic arm using Godot Rapier Physics to implement and test control algorithms and deterministic replay for verification.

Compare stacking and collision stability by reproducing the same scene using Godot's built‑in physics and Godot Rapier Physics, measuring differences in determinism and performance across desktop and web builds.

tools.name: BRL-CAD/brlcad
tools.desc: BRL-CAD is a powerful cross-platform open source combinatorial solid modeling system

cls.summary: BRL-CAD is a mature open-source constructive solid geometry (CSG) modelling system with interactive editing, high-performance ray-tracing, geometric analysis tools and a large library of utilities.
cls.what_it_does: BRL-CAD provides tools to create, combine and analyse solid geometry using CSG and explicit surface representations (NURBS, B‑splines, faceted meshes). It includes an interactive 3D editor, ray-tracer for rendering and geometric analysis, benchmarks and scripting interfaces; it is used for modelling, visualization and physics/geometry analysis of engineering designs.
cls.trl_rationale: The project has a long operational history (development since 1979) and the README and releases describe production use (including military use), a large codebase and regular releases; the GitHub repo is active with releases and a community, supporting a mature TRL.
student_project_ideas: Use BRL-CAD to model a small mechanical assembly in CSG, then run its ray-tracer and geometric analysis tools to compare predicted collision volumes and illuminate design trade-offs.
Integrate a BRL-CAD model with a simple finite-element or CFD preprocessor (export geometry/mesh) to demonstrate geometry-to-simulation workflow and validate mesh export interoperability.

tools.name: K3D-tools/K3D-jupyter
tools.desc: WebGL 3D plotting for Jupyter: meshes, isosurfaces, volumes, voxels and point clouds from NumPy arrays, with a path-traced cinematic renderer.

tools.name: ChiR24/Unreal_mcp
tools.desc: A comprehensive Model Context Protocol (MCP) server that enables AI assistants to control Unreal Engine through the native C++ Automation Bridge plugin. Built with TypeScript and C++.

cls.summary: EngineWire (Unreal_mcp) is a native C++ plugin and MCP server that lets AI assistants control the Unreal Editor to create levels, Blueprints, materials, gameplay, and automate editor workflows.
cls.what_it_does: EngineWire exposes a single MCP tool that drives the Unreal Editor (levels, actors, Blueprints, UI, materials, Niagara, cinematics, Play-In-Editor, packaging and more) via a native C++ plugin and a companion Node.js MCP server. It accepts MCP clients over HTTP or stdio so LLM-based assistants or editor automation tools can script complex editor actions programmatically. Notable points are its native in-editor server, broad coverage (~450 capabilities), and releases with prebuilt binaries and Fab distribution for easy installation.
cls.trl_rationale: The project is over one year old, has a stable 0.6.0 release, large community interest (1k+ stars, active pushes), prebuilt binaries and distribution via Fab and npm, and documented installation — indicating production-ready maturity for editor automation rather than a one-off prototype.
prerequisites: C++ project or ability to install a plugin (or use prebuilt binaries)
Node.js 20.19+ for the stdio server option (optional)
student_project_ideas: Build an automated testbench where an LLM-driven MCP client uses EngineWire to spawn actors, run Play-In-Editor with synthetic input, collect screenshots and logs, and evaluate whether a level meets simple gameplay requirements.

Create a digital-twin-style demonstrator that synchronises simple IoT telemetry (simulated sensor streams) with a visual scene in Unreal via EngineWire and visualises sensor states, then evaluate performance and latency.

tools.name: Natfii/UnrealClaude
tools.desc: Claude Code CLI integration for Unreal Engine 5.7 - Get AI coding assistance with built-in UE5.7 documentation context directly in the editor.

cls.summary: An Unreal Engine 5.7 editor plugin that embeds Claude Code CLI as an AI coding assistant and runs an MCP server to let agents inspect and modify UE projects from inside the editor.
cls.what_it_does: UnrealClaude connects the Claude Code CLI to the Unreal Engine 5.7 Editor, providing a docked chat panel with live streaming responses and editor-aware tooling. It exposes a Model Context Protocol (MCP) bridge that supplies real-time UE5.7 API documentation and over 20 tools for manipulating actors, Blueprints, assets, levels and executing scripts directly in the editor.
cls.trl_rationale: The repository provides a full plugin with build instructions, platform support, and an active community (high stars and forks) showing adoption, but it is younger than one year (created 2026-01-03) which limits the TRL to at most 6.
prerequisites: C++ and basic Unreal plugin development
Anthropic Claude Code CLI (authenticated Claude account)
student_project_ideas: Build an AI-assisted level-design workflow that uses UnrealClaude's MCP tools to programmatically place and configure actors based on high-level prompts and measure resulting performance.
Create an automated Blueprint refactoring tool: use the plugin to have Claude generate, modify and test Blueprint nodes, then validate changes with a simple automated test scene.

tools.name: don-tnowe/godot-resources-as-sheets-plugin
tools.desc: I needed to edit many Resource files, so figured someone would too.

cls.summary: A Godot editor plugin that displays and edits folders of Godot Resource files in a spreadsheet-like table inside the Godot editor.
cls.what_it_does: This plugin adds a tab to the Godot 4 editor that shows resources (one per row) as a strongly-typed table so you can edit text, numbers, colors, booleans and other resource fields directly in a grid. It supports multi-cell selection and editing, CSV import/export, mass operations (e.g. number math, color adjustments, texture atlas chopping), filtering by GDScript expressions and full undo/redo, making bulk editing of many resource files much faster than editing them one-by-one in the inspector.
cls.trl_rationale: The repository is several years old, has a large star count (1k+), active maintenance with Godot 3 and Godot 4 branches and recent commits, and a polished README and features list; these indicate production-ready maturity for its niche as an editor plugin.
prerequisites: basic familiarity with Godot Resources and GDScript
student_project_ideas: Create a Godot project that uses the plugin to bulk-edit and parameterise a set of game object Resource files, then export CSV to drive procedural level generation.
Build a small tool that integrates the plugin's CSV export to feed asset metadata into a data pipeline (e.g. combine with a Python script) for batch conversion or automatic testing of assets.

tools.name: opengeos/streamlit-geospatial
tools.desc: A multi-page streamlit app for geospatial

cls.summary: A multi-page Streamlit web app template for building interactive geospatial dashboards and mapping visualisations using Python libraries.
cls.what_it_does: streamlit-geospatial provides a multipage Streamlit application structure and example pages to visualise geospatial data (real-estate / market trends are given as examples). It is used by forking the repo, editing pages in the pages/ folder and running on Streamlit (locally or on Streamlit Cloud). Notable points are its focus on geospatial data visualisation and the ready-made multipage layout that speeds up creating map-based dashboards.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository is mature (created 2021) with a large number of stars (1k+) and recent activity, indicating real users and community interest; README and examples exist and the project is installable as a Streamlit app, supporting a production-ready TRL 7 judgment.
prerequisites: basic geospatial Python libraries (geopandas, pydeck/folium, pandas)
student_project_ideas: Create a Streamlit dashboard that ingests public building footprint and cadastral data (GeoJSON), computes simple spatial metrics (area, proximity to amenities) with geopandas, and visualises results on interactive maps.
Build a monitoring dashboard that streams time-series sensor locations (simulated) and visualises movement or change over time on maps using pydeck layers and deploy it to Streamlit Cloud.

tools.name: devanshutak25/3d-resources
tools.desc: Curated, CC0 reference hub for 3D, VFX, and game dev. 4,800+ tools, assets, and tutorials across 12 sections. Searchable, filterable, free.

cls.summary: A large, curated, searchable index of free and paid 3D software, assets, plugins and tutorials for artists and game developers.
cls.what_it_does: This repository collects and organises links to 3D tools, asset libraries, HDRIs, textures, tutorials and plugins and exposes them via a searchable/filterable web catalogue. It helps users find free or commercial resources for Blender, Houdini, Maya, Unreal and other DCCs and engines; what makes it notable is its breadth (4,800+ entries) and an interactive site for filtering by license, platform and workflow.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository is actively maintained (last push within weeks), has substantial community interest (1,000+ stars) and an interactive public site linked from the README, indicating a working, versioned project beyond a minimal demo; age (~454 days) supports Beta-level maturity rather than long-term production adoption.
student_project_ideas: Create a small visualisation or game scene for a coursework assignment using only free assets and HDRIs discovered from the catalogue, then document the asset sourcing and licensing decisions.
Extend the catalogue data by writing a scraper or importer that converts selected asset entries into a course asset pack (organised formats: glTF/FBX) and build a simple web viewer to showcase them.

tools.name: kennss/SiliconScope
tools.desc: Sudoless Apple Silicon system monitor (native SwiftUI GUI) with ANE / Media Engine / memory-bandwidth tracking

cls.summary: SiliconScope is an open-source native SwiftUI system monitor for Apple Silicon Macs that exposes Neural Engine, Media Engine, GPU and memory-bandwidth metrics and can aggregate remote machines via a small agent.
cls.what_it_does: SiliconScope visualises low-level hardware telemetry (CPU cores, GPU, ANE/Neural Engine, Media Engine, memory bandwidth, sensors, power) in a native macOS dashboard and menu-bar UI, and can connect to lightweight agents on remote machines (macOS/Linux/cloud) to show their metrics in the same dashboard. It is notable for sudoless ANE and memory-bandwidth tracking on Apple Silicon and for remote 'Fleet' support that preserves detailed Apple-specific metrics.
cls.trl_rationale: Active, well-starred repository with multiple releases and media coverage and a feature-rich v4.0, indicating beta-level maturity; repository age is ~162 days (<1 year) which limits TRL to 6 despite clear real-user interest and published examples.

macOS familiarity (SwiftUI app) or ability to run prebuilt macOS app
Optional: familiarity with Docker/containers for reading remote container metrics
student_project_ideas: Measure token/sec and tokens/Wh for several on-device LLMs (Core ML / Ollama) on different Apple Silicon chips using SiliconScope's benchmark and compare energy efficiency across chips.

Extend the headless agent to export metrics to a time-series database (InfluxDB/Prometheus) and build a dashboard that correlates model inference latency with memory-bandwidth and power on mixed fleets (Mac + Linux GPU box).

tools.name: generative-design/Code-Package-p5.js

tools.name: mni-ml/framework
tools.desc: A machine learning library with a TypeScript API and Rust backend. CUDA and WebGPU compatibility. Built to understand how ML frameworks and models work internally.

cls.summary: A PyTorch-like machine learning library with a TypeScript API and Rust backends that run autograd and neural network training on CPU, CUDA and WebGPU.
cls.what_it_does: Provides tensor operations, automatic differentiation, neural network modules and optimizers accessible from TypeScript while executing compute in a native Rust backend (CPU, CUDA or WebGPU). It is used as an embeddable ML/runtime library for training and inference at GPU speed and is notable for offering both CUDA and WebGPU backends with a Node/npm distribution.
cls.trl_rationale: The project is an actively maintained, well-starred library with builds for multiple backends and an npm package, indicating maturity beyond a fragile prototype; however the repository is under one year old (created 2026-01-08), which limits the TRL to at most 6 in this assessment.
prerequisites: basic machine learning concepts (tensors, gradients, optimizers)
Rust toolchain if building from source and GPU toolkits for CUDA/WebGPU
student_project_ideas: Implement and train a small convolutional neural network for a sensor classification task using @mni-ml/framework with the WebGPU backend and compare training throughput and accuracy to a PyTorch baseline.

Build a realtime inference pipeline in Node that runs a trained model on WebGPU for a robotics perception demo, integrating camera input and publishing classifications to a ROS bridge or simple WebSocket server.

tools.name: Pjbomb2/TrueTrace-Unity-Pathtracer
tools.desc: A High Performance Compute Shader Based Mesh Pathtracer in Unity3d without RT Cores

cls.summary: TrueTrace is an open-source compute-shader path tracer for Unity that enables interactive and offline physically based rendering without requiring hardware ray-tracing cores.
cls.what_it_does: TrueTrace performs path-traced rendering inside Unity using compute shaders and a compressed wide BVH to support high performance software ray tracing on a wide range of GPUs. It is used as a Unity rendering plugin/component to render scenes (including skinned meshes, terrains and emissive geometry) with features such as Disney BSDF, denoising (ASVGF and OIDN), next-event estimation and various post-processing effects.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository is multi-year (created 2022), has a large star count (1021), active development through 2026 and a demo plus documented features, indicating production-ready code suitable for real projects rather than a throwaway prototype.
prerequisites: Basic GPU/graphics concepts (shaders, BVH, path tracing)
Optional: experience with HLSL/compute shaders for customization
student_project_ideas: Integrate TrueTrace into a small Unity scene to compare visual fidelity and performance between rasterization (URP/HDRP) and path-traced renders, measuring frame time and denoising effectiveness with OIDN.

Extend TrueTrace to add a simple material or light sampling strategy (e.g. implement a new BRDF or light importance sampling heuristic) and evaluate its impact on convergence speed for scenes with complex emissive geometry.

tools.name: LibreYOLO/libreyolo

cls.what_it_does: LibreYOLO wraps dozens of detection and vision models behind one consistent Python CLI/API so you can run inference, train models and export to runtimes like ONNX or TensorRT. It supports many tasks (object detection, instance/semantic segmentation, pose, depth and more) and multiple model families, and is notable for providing a lightweight unified interface and packaged extras for export, serving and training integrations.

student_project_ideas: Build a robotics perception pipeline that uses LibreYOLO for real-time object detection on a Raspberry Pi or x86 edge device and stream detections to a ROS2 node for robot navigation.
Compare performance and accuracy of different export backends (ONNX, TensorRT, OpenVINO) for a selected LibreYOLO detection model on CPU vs GPU and report latency/throughput trade-offs.

tools.name: jegly/Box
tools.desc: The most advanced, fully offline client-side AI suite on Android today.

cls.summary: Box is an Android app that runs a wide range of AI models fully offline on-device (LLMs, vision, image generation, TTS, music) with hardware acceleration and model import support.
cls.what_it_does: Box packages on-device machine learning features (local LLMs, image generation, vision tools, speech and music generation, upscaling and inpainting) into a security-hardened Android client that can run models without cloud services and supports GGUF import, llama.cpp, and NPU/GPU acceleration. It is installed as an Android APK and notable for its focus on offline operation, privacy, and compatibility with custom ROMs and device NPUs.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository is active with many stars, releases and claimed 50k downloads indicating real users and polish, but it was created ~214 days ago (<1 year) so a conservative TRL 6 (beta) is appropriate.

basic knowledge of on-device ML models and formats (GGUF, llama.cpp)

Integrate Box's on-device vision pipeline to prototype an offline image-based defect-detection workflow for a manufacturing or inspection use case and measure latency on different phones.

tools.name: scenario-labs/blender-plugin
tools.desc: Scenario for Blender: AI images, video, 3D and PBR materials in the viewport, plus a local MCP server for agents. Blender 5.0+ extension, GPL-3.0-or-later.

cls.summary: A Blender 5+ add-on that connects Blender to the Scenario service to generate images, video, 3D meshes, PBR materials, audio and 360 environments and provides a local MCP server for agent workflows.
cls.what_it_does: The extension lets users author prompts or use scene captures and selected meshes to generate assets (images, video, 3D, PBR texture sets, audio) from the Scenario cloud and import results into Blender; it also runs a local MCP server to expose agentic workflows to the Blender scene. It is notable for combining generative AI asset creation with a Blender UI (sidebar, composer, Studio view) and direct application of generated PBR materials and mesh edits into an active Blender project.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository is recently created (79 days old) and README labels the extension 'Experimental'; it has releases and many stars indicating interest, but the tool depends on a paid cloud service (Scenario) and lacks the long track record or broad production use needed for TRL 6+. Age therefore limits the TRL to about 5.

Basic familiarity with Blender add-ons and asset import/export
student_project_ideas: Create a workflow that uses the plugin to generate PBR textures for a mechanical part, apply them in Blender, and evaluate visual realism and render performance compared with hand-authored textures.

Develop a small pipeline where a written scene brief is converted into a greybox Blockout in Blender via Scenario, then refine geometry and produce a short rendered animation, documenting the human+AI design steps and time savings.

tools.name: nv-tlabs/NKSR
tools.desc: [CVPR 2023 Highlight] Neural Kernel Surface Reconstruction

cls.summary: NKSR is a research implementation that reconstructs high-quality implicit 3D surfaces from large, sparse, and noisy point clouds using a neural-kernel representation optimized for scale and speed.
cls.what_it_does: NKSR takes oriented point clouds and produces an implicit surface field that can be meshed into a watertight surface; it is used via Python/PyTorch with CUDA and provides training and inference pipelines plus pre-trained checkpoints. It is notable for scaling to millions of points, handling large scenes out-of-core, and combining kernel-based neural fields with sparse solvers for fast, memory-efficient reconstruction.
cls.trl_rationale: The project is a published CVPR paper with a project page, pre-trained checkpoints, active maintenance (recent pushes and a news/update about CUDA wheels), and ~1k stars indicating community use; it is research-grade code used to reproduce results rather than a long-standing industrial standard, so TRL ~7.
prerequisites: basic familiarity with point-clouds and mesh extraction
student_project_ideas: Compare NKSR reconstructions to classical methods (e.g. Screened Poisson) on smartphone LiDAR scans and quantify mesh quality and reconstruction time.
Integrate NKSR with a SLAM/photogrammetry pipeline to produce lightweight 3D models of indoor scenes and evaluate how point density and noise affect reconstruction fidelity.

tools.name: Motphys/UniLab
tools.desc: UniLab: Contract-driven infrastructure for robot learning across physics backends and hardware

cls.summary: UniLab is a configurable, contract-driven infrastructure for robot reinforcement learning that lets you describe tasks once and run them across multiple physics backends and hardware targets.
cls.what_it_does: UniLab provides a task-authoring and runtime contract so the same RL task configuration can be executed with different physics simulators, worker topologies, and learner devices; users configure tasks with Hydra and run training/evaluation via a CLI. It is notable for explicit backend support across platforms (CUDA, ROCm, MPS/XPU, Windows/macOS/Linux), overlap of simulation and learner (FlashSAC) for faster off-policy training, and a documented support matrix for tested backend/task combinations.
cls.trl_rationale: The project is active, well documented, has demos, a published support matrix, and significant community interest (1000+ stars and CoRL acceptance), indicating beta-level maturity; however the repository is under one year old so there is not yet the multi-year track record or widespread ecosystem needed for TRL 7+.
prerequisites: familiarity with Hydra and GPU toolchains (CUDA/ROCm/MPS) for advanced setups
student_project_ideas: Use UniLab to compare locomotion policy performance across two simulators (e.g. MuJoCo and Isaac Gym) and quantify differences in learning speed and sim-to-sim transfer.
Integrate a custom robot recipe into UniLab and run an experiment that measures how FlashSAC replay overlap affects wall-clock training time on a multi-GPU setup.

tools.name: ShadowBlip/OpenGamepadUI
tools.desc: Open source gamepad-native game launcher and overlay

cls.summary: Open Gamepad UI is an open-source, gamepad-first game launcher and in-game overlay built with Godot Engine.
cls.what_it_does: It provides a gamepad-native launcher and overlay to browse and launch games, with per-game profiles, automatic artwork downloading and a plugin system. It can remap gamepad input to mouse and keyboard and integrates with companion tools for power control and input plumbing. It is notable for being implemented in Godot 4 and offering an extendable, open-source alternative to proprietary launchers.
cls.trl_rationale: The repository is several years old, has 1k+ stars, published documentation and active recent commits which indicate more than a toy prototype, but the README explicitly states the project is in very early development and there is no evidence of large-scale production deployment, so beta (TRL 6) is appropriate.
prerequisites: basic knowledge of gamepad input and desktop gaming on Linux/Windows/macOS

tools.name: OleksandrChekhovskyi/hax
tools.desc: A minimalist, terminal-native coding agent written in C.

cls.summary: hax is a minimalist, terminal-native coding agent (LLM client/REPL) written in C that runs locally or against hosted LLM providers.
cls.what_it_does: hax provides a lightweight terminal REPL and one-shot CLI for interacting with large language models to assist coding tasks; it auto-discovers local runtimes (eg. llama.cpp) or connects to cloud providers and streams Markdown and tool output into the terminal. It is notable for being a single small native binary with low memory usage, inspectable transcripts/wire traces, and broad provider support while preserving native terminal behaviour.
cls.trl_rationale: The project is active, packaged (Homebrew, AUR), provides prebuilt binaries and install scripts, and has many stars and recent commits, indicating a beta-level maturity; however the repository is only ~7 months old so there is not yet the multi-year track record or broad enterprise adoption required for TRL 7+.
prerequisites: local model runtime (e.g. llama-server/llama.cpp) or API keys for cloud providers
student_project_ideas: Build a lab exercise where students configure hax to use a local llama.cpp model and evaluate its ability to generate unit tests for a small C project, measuring correctness and edit cycles.
Create a small tool that hooks hax transcripts into a CI pipeline to auto-generate changelog or code review suggestions, comparing different providers (local vs cloud) for latency and output quality.

tools.name: cgohlke/geospatial-wheels
tools.desc: Geospatial library wheels for Python on Windows.

cls.summary: A curated collection of unofficial pre-built Windows binary wheels for popular Python geospatial libraries (GDAL, rasterio, pyproj, Cartopy, etc.) to simplify installation and testing on Windows.
cls.what_it_does: This repository publishes compiled Python wheel packages for a range of geospatial libraries targeting Windows (win32, win‑amd64, win‑arm64) so users can install complex native dependencies without building them. It is used by downloading the appropriate wheel release or installing via pip from the release artifacts; notable points are the inclusion of many linked native libraries (GDAL, PROJ, GEOS, HDF5, etc.) and frequent, actively maintained releases.
cls.trl_rationale: The repository is actively maintained since 2023 with many stars, frequent releases (most recent release 2026-11-14) and production-quality binary artifacts used widely by practitioners to avoid building native geospatial stacks on Windows; this indicates production-ready maturity though it is an unofficial packaging distribution rather than a standards project.
student_project_ideas: Build a small geospatial analysis pipeline on Windows that reads satellite or LiDAR data using GDAL/rasterio and visualises results with Cartopy or basemap, demonstrating end-to-end data ingest, reprojection and plotting.

Create a reproducible Windows environment for an urban spatial analysis task (parcel buffering, intersection, and raster aggregation) using Fiona, pyproj and shapely, packaged with a requirements file and documented steps for installation using the repository's wheels.

It also includes Git repository status, commit/branch operations and an asset/template library, notable for combining engine version management with project workflows in one cross-platform app.

tools.name: developmentseed/lonboard

cls.what_it_does: MasterAgent provides a small synchronous C++ SDK and CLI that match inputs to deterministic skills, validate tool names and parameters, and then optionally call a local LLM via an HTTP adapter; it supports durable receipts and SQLite-backed request persistence for replay and recovery. It is designed for edge and embedded deployment (no cloud required), enforces strict tool schemas to avoid guessed calls, and can be embedded into consumer applications via CMake.
cls.trl_rationale: The project is active, has a working CLI, C++ SDK, tests, CI targets and examples (demo, inventory example) which indicate beta-level maturity, but the repository is only ~99 days old so it lacks the long track record and widespread production adoption required for TRL7+.

cls.what_it_does: jev runs a purpose-built decision model locally (no cloud) to give probabilistic yes/no answers, ranked choices or expected scores for a provided text and questions via a small HTTP API or a command-line request. It is notable for being a compact, fast CPU binary with GGUF/llama.cpp and OpenVINO support and a TypeSafe Jev-compatible API so existing Jev clients work unchanged.

tools.name: gkjohnson/three-bvh-csg

cls.summary: three-bvh-csg is a JavaScript library that performs fast constructive solid geometry (CSG) boolean operations on three.js meshes using a bounding-volume-hierarchy for performance.
cls.what_it_does: The library provides CSG operations (union, subtraction, intersection, difference and hollow variants) for three.js Mesh objects by building on three-mesh-bvh to accelerate intersection tests. It is used in web-based 3D workflows to compute boolean combinations of triangle meshes at interactive speeds and includes examples and options for preserving attributes and multi-material groups.
cls.trl_rationale: The repository is over four years old, has a substantial star count (964), active maintenance and hosted interactive examples, which indicates production-readiness for many use cases; the README explicitly notes experimental numerical corner-cases, so while mature and widely used for three.js workflows it is not a hardened CAD kernel.
student_project_ideas: Build a web app that lets users create and export boolean-combined models for 3D printing by integrating three-bvh-csg with a simple three.js UI and an STL exporter.
Compare performance and robustness of three-bvh-csg versus a BSP-based three.js CSG library on complex assemblies, report failure cases and implement pre-processing (mesh repair) to improve results.

tools.name: jame581/GodotPrompter

It is used as a plugin/skill-pack for agent hosts (Claude Code, Copilot CLI, Grok, Cursor, Antigravity) so the agent follows Godot conventions rather than generic programming advice, and includes examples for GDScript and C# targeting Godot 4.3–4.8.

Build an agent-assisted multiplayer setup where the student integrates GodotPrompter's multiplayer skill into a Godot project and measures how much agent guidance speeds up getting a basic client-server demo running.

Compare RAG retrieval performance by deploying the same document corpus to Qdrant and Weaviate inside Selfhost AI, then run benchmark queries from Open WebUI and report latency/accuracy trade-offs.

tools.name: iamaisim/ProjectAirSim
tools.desc: Project AirSim is Microsoft's evolution of AirSim, an advanced simulation platform for building, training, and testing autonomous systems in high-fidelity virtual environments

cls.summary: Project AirSim is an open-source, engine-independent simulation platform for testing and developing autonomous vehicles (drones, fixed-wing, UGVs) with support for realistic sensors, multiple physics backends and integrations with autopilots and ROS 2.
cls.what_it_does: Project AirSim provides a modular simulator that runs vehicle physics, sensor models (cameras, LiDAR, IMU, GPS, radar, etc.), and control APIs for single- and multi-vehicle experiments. It can run headless using a lightweight runtime or with Unreal Engine 5 for rendered worlds, and supports flight dynamics (Fast Physics, JSBSim, Simulink), PX4/ArduPilot workflows and Python/C++/ROS 2 clients. Notable features are multi-vehicle support, multiple physics backends, and a maintained lineage from Microsoft AirSim with packaged releases and prebuilt environments.
cls.trl_rationale: The project is a maintained, publicly released successor to Microsoft AirSim with packaged releases, active commits and many stars/forks; it shows real-world integrations (PX4, ArduPilot, ROS 2, Simulink) and prebuilt environments, indicating production-ready capability rather than an experimental prototype. Repository age (>1 year), frequent activity and release artifacts support TRL 7.
prerequisites: familiarity with Unreal Engine (for rendered scenes) or headless runtime
ROS 2, PX4/ArduPilot or Simulink knowledge for integration use-cases
student_project_ideas: Implement and evaluate an autonomous landing controller in Project AirSim using the Python client and compare performance using Fast Physics vs JSBSim flight dynamics.
Build a multi-vehicle coordination scenario (UGV + UAV) that exchanges position and sensor data over ROS 2, then run V&V tests to measure robustness to simulated sensor noise and wind.

tools.name: alvarobartt/hf-mem
tools.desc: A CLI to estimate inference memory requirements for Hugging Face models, written in Python.

cls.summary: hf-mem is a Python CLI that estimates the GPU/host memory required to run Hugging Face, GGUF or ONNX models without downloading full weights.
cls.what_it_does: hf-mem reads model metadata (safetensors, GGUF, ONNX) via HTTP range requests or local paths and computes inference memory requirements including model weights, KV cache for generative models, and runtime overhead. It is used as a command-line utility to plan deployment (context length, batch size and dtype options) and is notable for estimating memory without downloading full model files.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository is actively maintained, widely starred (950 stars), provides a v1.0.0 example and works with real model formats, indicating maturity beyond prototype; however the repo age is ~330 days (<1 year) which limits TRL to at most 6.
prerequisites: familiarity with Hugging Face model identifiers and model config concepts
student_project_ideas: Compare hf-mem estimates with actual peak GPU memory when running several open-source LLMs (Transformers/ONNX/GGUF) and produce a report explaining discrepancies and recommended safety margins.

Integrate hf-mem into a simple deployment pipeline that selects quantization and partitioning strategies for a given GPU memory budget and demonstrates automated model selection for constrained edge/cloud instances.

tools.name: LottieFiles/dotlottie-web
tools.desc: High-performance Lottie & dotLottie web player powered by Rust + WASM, with React, Vue, Svelte, Solid & Web Components.

cls.summary: dotLottie Web is a high-performance web player for Lottie (.json) and dotLottie (.lottie) animations that uses a Rust+WASM core and provides multiple framework SDKs and GPU-backed renderers.
cls.what_it_does: It loads and plays Lottie and dotLottie animation files in the browser, offering features like theming, state machines, audio, and runtime control. The core rendering is implemented in Rust compiled to WASM (dotlottie-rs) with Software, WebGL2 and WebGPU backends and first‑party SDKs for React, Vue, Svelte, Solid and Web Components, plus an off-main-thread worker mode for high-performance scenarios.
cls.trl_rationale: The project is mature (created 2023-10, active through 2026-11), has substantial stars/forks, multiple framework SDKs, and a Rust/WASM core used across platforms; evidence shows production-quality engineering though it is not an industry-wide standard for engineering domains.
student_project_ideas: Create a web dashboard prototype for an engineering instrument that uses dotLottie animations (via the React SDK) for status indicators and theme switching.
Benchmark and compare main‑thread Canvas rendering vs DotLottieWorker with OffscreenCanvas under heavy UI load to measure frame drops and responsiveness for a web-based HMI.

tools.name: retentioneering/retentioneering-tools
tools.desc: Python toolkit, MCP server, and agent skills for reproducible, auditable clickstream and event log analytics. Helps AI agents, data scientists and analysts build, validate, and cross-check product analytics, quantitative UX, customer journeys, graph-based user flows, behavioral segmentation, A/B tests, process mining models, Markov chain simulation

tools.name: nianticlabs/spz
tools.desc: File format for 3D Gaussian splats. About 10x smaller than the PLY equivalent with virtually no perceptible loss in visual quality. Offered as open source by Niantic Labs. More details at https://scaniverse.com/spz #3dgaussiansplats #gaussiansplatting

cls.summary: spz is an open file format and C++/WASM library for compactly storing and loading 3D Gaussian splats, providing ~10x smaller files than equivalent PLY point clouds with minimal visual loss.
cls.what_it_does: spz encodes 3D Gaussian splats into a compressed .spz file (ZSTD-based) and provides C++ and TypeScript/WASM APIs to save and load Gaussian cloud data. It solves storage, transmission and interoperability problems for dense photo-derived point/splat clouds by independently compressing attribute streams and supporting coordinate-system metadata and extensions. Notable features include a compact multi-stream ZSTD layout, coordinate-system conversion options, and an Emscripten-built Typescript interface for web use.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository is maintained by Niantic Labs, has substantial community interest (≈944 stars), active commits through 2026, and production-focused features (ZSTD multi-stream format, C++ and WASM bindings). These indicators and link to Scaniverse usage support a production-ready judgement rather than an experimental prototype.
student_project_ideas: Build a web viewer that loads .spz files via the provided WASM TypeScript bindings and renders them in three.js, comparing rendering performance and bandwidth to PLY/glTF versions.
Create a pipeline that converts photogrammetry-derived point clouds (PLY) to .spz, measures storage and load-time savings, and evaluates visual fidelity using automated image-based metrics.

tools.name: repalash/threepipe
tools.desc: Next generation toolkit for web3D and photorealistic graphics

cls.summary: Threepipe is a TypeScript web 3D framework built on three.js for creating modular, high-quality model viewers, configurators and editors in the browser.
cls.what_it_does: Threepipe provides a high-level API, plugin system and editor for loading, configuring, rendering and exporting 3D scenes and models (GLTF, OBJ, FBX, etc.) in web pages. It bundles a modular rendering pipeline (deferred rendering, HDR, post-processing), material extension hooks, asset import/export and a browser-based scene editor so developers can build photorealistic, interactive viewers and configurators quickly.
cls.trl_rationale: The project is mature and actively maintained (created 2023, many stars and forks, live website, API docs and examples) which indicates production readiness; however it is not a de-facto industry standard so TRL 7 (production-ready) is appropriate.
student_project_ideas: Build a web-based configurator for a parametric mechanical part: load a GLB model, expose parameters via Threepipe plugins and export configured models and a parts list.
Integrate a Threepipe viewer with a simple IoT data feed (mocked) to visualise real-time sensor values as material/animation changes for an asset-digital-twin demo.

tools.name: rsasaki0109/lidar_slam_ros2
tools.desc: ROS 2 LiDAR SLAM for pointcloud-map authoring, benchmarking, and Autoware-compatible map workflows.

tools.name: sgaofen/humanizer-local-model
tools.desc: Rewrites AI drafts so they read like a person wrote them — runs locally, keeps the facts

cls.summary: Humanizer is a locally runnable 12B LLM and desktop app that rewrites AI-generated drafts (English and Chinese) to read like human prose while attempting to preserve facts such as numbers, names and dates.
cls.what_it_does: Humanizer takes AI-written text (emails, reports, forum posts, essays) and produces rewritten versions that aim to sound human while keeping factual tokens unchanged; it is provided as downloadable GGUF model files and as packaged Mac/Windows apps that run offline. It is notable for quantization-aware training and multiple compressed GGUF variants (including 2-bit and Q8) so the model can run locally with llama.cpp and integrate with local LLM servers.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository is very new (created ~67 days ago) so by the policy its TRL is capped; however the project already provides packaged Mac/Windows apps, GGUF model files, evaluation details and many stars, which indicates early adopter use rather than just a paper prototype.
prerequisites: llama.cpp or compatible local LLM runtime
sufficient local RAM/VRAM for chosen GGUF model
student_project_ideas: Evaluate the model's factual-preservation behaviour on engineering reports by measuring changes to numbers, units and names across a corpus of lab reports and build a dashboard summarising error types.

Integrate Humanizer with a local LM server (llama.cpp or LM Studio) to build a small writing-assistant plugin that preserves selected passages (using the app's 'Create fact' feature) and measure usability for engineering documentation tasks.

tools.name: DomCR/ACadSharp
tools.desc: C# library to read/write cad files like dxf/dwg.

tools.name: QymIs-Tech/QymCAD
tools.desc: Parametric 3D CAD with a real B-rep kernel (OpenCASCADE)

cls.summary: QymCAD is an open-source, parametric desktop CAD application that uses a real B-rep kernel (OpenCASCADE) to create precise mechanical parts and assemblies.
cls.what_it_does: QymCAD lets users create 2D sketches and turn them into exact solid geometry (extrude, revolve, sweep, loft, fillets, booleans, etc.), build parametric parts and assemble them with kinematic joints. It is a desktop application (Windows, Linux AppImage, macOS) that reads/writes STEP, STL and sketch formats and emphasizes associative parametric modelling on a B-rep kernel for accurate CAD exchange and manufacturing workflows.
cls.trl_rationale: The project is a working development build with releases and many stars, but the repository is only 84 days old and the README warns the document format changes frequently and some modules (CAM) are incomplete, so it appears in active early use by adopters rather than a long‑proven production tool.
prerequisites: basic CAD modelling concepts (sketches, constraints, B-rep vs mesh)
familiarity with desktop build tools if building from source (Rust toolchain, Docker or MSVC for kernel builds)
student_project_ideas: Design and parametrize a mechanical bracket in QymCAD, export STEP and validate assembly fits and interference with a simple kinematic joint; document the parametric workflow and revision impact.

Integrate a QymCAD-created part into a small robotics arm simulation by exporting STEP, importing into a simulation tool (e.g. Gazebo or a CAD-to-simulation pipeline) and measuring collision/clearance under motion.

tools.name: orneryd/NornicDB
tools.desc: Nornicdb is a distributed low-latency, Graph+Vector, Temporal MVCC with all sub-ms HNSW search, graph traversal, and writes. Using Neo4j Bolt/Cypher and qdrant's gRPC means you can switch with no changes while adding intelligent features like schemas, managed embeddings, reranking+llm, GPU accel, Auto-TLP, Policy-based Memory Decay, and MCP server.

cls.summary: NornicDB is an open-source, Neo4j-compatible database that combines graph queries, vector search and historical MVCC to support low-latency hybrid retrieval and embeddings-driven features.
cls.what_it_does: NornicDB provides a single server that serves Cypher/Bolt graph queries, HNSW vector search and retained historical reads via MVCC, optionally accelerated on GPU and embeddable in Go applications. It is used as a drop-in graph backend (Neo4j-compatible) that adds vector retrieval, embedding/LLM integration, policy-based memory decay and other AI-oriented features. Notable aspects are hybrid graph+vector retrieval, sub-millisecond HNSW search, historical snapshots, and multi-architecture GPU support (CUDA/Metal/Vulkan).
cls.trl_rationale: The project has substantial documentation, release installers, Docker images, wide community interest (many stars), and active development, indicating a beta-level project; however the repository is under one year old so by the stated TRL rules it should be capped at 6 despite strong activity.
prerequisites: knowledge of graph databases and Cypher/Bolt
experience with Docker and server deployment
familiarity with vector search concepts and embeddings; Go for embedding/embedding-integration
student_project_ideas: Build a small digital-twin prototype for a sensor-equipped device that stores telemetry in NornicDB, uses vector embeddings for fault-diagnosis retrieval, and visualises historical state changes over time.

Compare hybrid retrieval quality and latency by migrating a small Neo4j dataset into NornicDB and benchmarking graph-only vs graph+vector queries (use synthetic dataset and measure retrieval/recall and response times).

tools.name: eclaire-labs/eclaire
tools.desc: Local-first, open-source AI assistant for your data. Unify tasks, notes, docs, photos, and bookmarks. Private, self-hosted, and extensible via APIs.

cls.summary: Eclaire is a self-hosted, privacy-first AI assistant that indexes and lets you search, chat with, and automate tasks over your personal documents, notes, bookmarks and photos.
cls.what_it_does: Eclaire ingests and unifies personal data (documents, notes, bookmarks, images, tasks) and provides an OpenAI-compatible API and web UI for chat, search, classification, OCR and automation using local or hosted LLM backends. It is designed to be run on your own hardware with support for multiple model backends, SQLite/Postgres storage, and integrations such as Telegram and common LLM runtimes.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository is >1 year old with active development, v0.6.0 releases, broad feature list and many stars indicating active users, but README warns it is pre-release and not hardened for public exposure so it is best characterised as beta rather than production-ready.
prerequisites: local LLM runtime (llama.cpp, vLLM, Ollama, etc.)
basic familiarity with self-hosting and configuring services
student_project_ideas: Build a private course-material search assistant by importing lecture notes, slides and papers into Eclaire and implement custom automations to summarise weekly readings.

Integrate Eclaire with a local LLM (llama.cpp or vLLM) to evaluate retrieval + generation performance on a university dataset and compare indexing strategies (SQLite vs Postgres) for latency and relevance.

tools.name: blendi-remade/dioramas
tools.desc: A free, open-source framework for cinematic, interactive 3D websites with AI-generated assets (Nano Banana 2 + Meshy 7.1 on fal). 20 example sites.

cls.summary: Dioramas is an open-source JavaScript framework for building cinematic, interactive 3D web pages that use AI-generated image→3D asset pipelines and a small three.js engine.
cls.what_it_does: Dioramas generates and serves photoreal 3D 'hero' objects (prompt → image → image-to-3D → optimization) and a lightweight three.js-based engine that composes lighting, post-processing and scroll/choreography to make the 3D scene itself the landing page. It is used by dropping in examples or assets, running included Node scripts to generate/optimize models (using fal-based services), and serving the examples locally; notable points are the built-in asset pipeline for AI-generated models and a polished engine tuned for 60 fps.
cls.trl_rationale: The repository is very new (created 48 days ago) so it cannot be judged mature; however it ships 20 complete examples, bundled models (~330 MB), runnable scripts and clear docs which indicate an alpha/in-use level by early adopters rather than a paper prototype.
prerequisites: desktop GPU or GPU-enabled environment for good performance
student_project_ideas: Build a small portfolio site that replaces static images with a Dioramas scene and add telemetry to measure run-time performance across devices, then optimise textures/meshes to meet a 60 fps target.
Integrate a Dioramas example with a simple digital-twin data feed (e.g. simulated sensor values) to drive scene animation and demonstrate visualisation of live system state.

tools.name: metadist/synaplan
tools.desc: Own the flow: one open-source AI platform for your knowledge, models and channels – web, WhatsApp, email, Outlook, Nextcloud & ownCloud. Local and cloud models side by side, with the cost on every answer.

cls.summary: Synaplan is an open-source, self-hosted platform for building AI assistants that serve the same knowledge and policies across web, WhatsApp, email, Outlook and Nextcloud, mixing local and cloud models with per-answer cost visibility.
cls.what_it_does: Synaplan lets teams connect files and knowledge to chatbots and assistant channels (web widget, messaging, email, Nextcloud) and route tasks to local or cloud LLMs while displaying the cost of each answer. It is deployed via Docker/Compose or Kubernetes, supports many model providers and local runtimes (eg. Ollama), and includes admin, policy and plugin mechanisms to control actions and integration.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository is active (last push Nov 2026), has substantial community interest (925 stars), lists real production users and provides deployment options (Docker, Helm, hosted service), indicating production-ready maturity rather than prototype status.
prerequisites: familiarity with LLM provider API keys (OpenAI/Anthropic) and local runtimes (Ollama)
student_project_ideas: Create a course-specific RAG assistant by connecting a set of lecture notes and lab manuals to Synaplan and evaluate answer accuracy and cost when routing different queries to local (Ollama) vs cloud models.

Integrate Synaplan with a CI/CD pipeline to automatically update an assistant's knowledge from a repository of system architecture documents and measure response latency and cost under different deployment modes (Docker vs Kubernetes).

cls.what_it_does: This repository provides a large set of ready-made front-end visual demos and examples (CSS, Canvas, Three.js, AI snippets) implemented with Vue and Vite for learning or reusing visual effects. You run or browse the examples locally or via the author's demo site to inspect implementation patterns and copy components into your own projects. It is notable for its breadth of front-end visual techniques collected in a single Vue project and an active demo site.

tools.name: 0xProbabillity/house-control
tools.desc: Your home as a live 3D model in the Mac menu bar and on iPhone — lights and ACs via Smart Life, Home Assistant, Philips Hue and Apple Home.

cls.summary: House Control is an open-source macOS and iPhone app that shows your home as a live, interactive 3D model and lets you control lights and air conditioners via Smart Life, Home Assistant, Philips Hue and Apple Home.
cls.what_it_does: It renders a 3D floorplan (rooms, furniture, lights, ACs) from a JSON description and links scene items to real devices so you can monitor and control them from the Mac menu bar or iPhone. The UI is a Three.js web app embedded in native Swift shells, supports a visual editor and scenes, and can proxy AI assistants or connect to Home Assistant, Philips Hue and Smart Life/Tuya devices.
cls.trl_rationale: The project has many stars, public releases and CI-built images, showing active interest and that it runs for users; however the repository is only ~34 days old so by the stated TRL rules it should be capped at TRL 5.

basic Node.js and npm knowledge (Vite/web build)
understanding of Home Assistant / Smart Life / Philips Hue device concepts

Build a small research prototype that logs device telemetry from House Control and uses that time-series data to train a simple occupancy or activity detector, visualising results in the embedded Three.js view.

tools.name: microsoft/farmvibes-ai
tools.desc: FarmVibes.AI: Multi-Modal GeoSpatial ML Models for Agriculture and Sustainability

cls.summary: FarmVibes.AI is an open-source framework of data ingestion, preprocessing and multi‑modal geospatial ML workflows focused on agricultural and sustainability use cases.
cls.what_it_does: FarmVibes.AI provides dataset downloaders, configurable preprocessing pipelines and example notebooks to build fusion ML models that combine satellite, radar, weather and other raster data for agricultural insights. It is used via Jupyter notebooks, a local Python client or a local Docker-based cluster and is notable for explicit multi‑modal fusion workflows and published sample notebooks targeted at agriculture tasks.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository is >3 years old, has substantial community interest (900+ stars), published documentation and example notebooks, and a Docker-based local cluster for running workflows; these indicate production-ready software rather than a research prototype.
prerequisites: basic remote sensing / satellite imagery concepts
student_project_ideas: Build and evaluate a crop-type classifier for a chosen region by combining Sentinel-2 optical bands, Sentinel-1 SAR and local weather time series using FarmVibes.AI notebooks and compare fusion vs single-modality models.

Create an automated inference workflow that runs FarmVibes.AI pipelines in Docker to produce seasonal vegetation-health maps for a case-study farm, and deploy a simple dashboard that visualises time-series outputs.

tools.name: XHToken/Spark-X2.6
tools.desc: Spark-x2.6 open model series. Pushing the Limits of Agentic Capabilities in On-Device Models

cls.summary: Spark-X2.6 is an open, compact family of on-device language models (1.7B and 4B) designed for stronger agentic, coding and long-context capabilities and intended for local/offline deployment.
cls.what_it_does: Spark-X2.6 provides compact causal language models tuned for on-device inference and agentic workflows, enabling multi-step planning, tool use and coding tasks with configurable 'thinking' levels. It is distributed as model checkpoints on Hugging Face/ModelScope/Ollama and includes usage examples for transformers, optimized runtime support (e.g. llama.cpp) and containerised runtimes for GPU/NPUs to run locally.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository is recent (created 85 days ago) so lacks a long track record; README and releases show model downloads on Hugging Face/ModelScope/Ollama and benchmark claims indicating early adopter use, consistent with an alpha-in-use TRL rather than production maturity.
prerequisites: basic Docker and container runtime knowledge
access to a capable GPU or on-device runtime (llama.cpp / Ollama)
student_project_ideas: Integrate Spark-X2.6-1.7B into a ROS-based robot prototype to run a local agent for simple multi-step task planning and compare latency and reliability against a cloud LLM.

Benchmark Spark-X2.6-4B against other on-device models (e.g. Qwen3.5-4B, Gemma-E4B) on coding and multi-step reasoning tasks and report trade-offs in throughput, memory and accuracy using llama.cpp and transformers runtimes.

tools.name: shubham0204/SmolChat-Android
tools.desc: Running any GGUF SLMs/LLMs locally, on-device in Android

cls.summary: SmolChat is an Android app and codebase for running GGUF-format small language models (SLMs) locally on-device using llama.cpp and JNI bindings.
cls.what_it_does: SmolChat provides a mobile UI and Kotlin/C++ code to load GGUF models with llama.cpp via JNI and perform on-device inference on Android devices. It lets users add/manage models, change inference parameters (temperature, min-p), and create chat/task prompts, making it notable for enabling fully local LLM inference on commodity Android hardware.
cls.trl_rationale: The project is over a year old, has many stars, active development, published releases and a Google Play listing, and demonstrates real-world distribution — evidence of production-readiness for its specific use case rather than an experimental prototype.
prerequisites: basic C/C++ and familiarity with GGUF/llama.cpp
student_project_ideas: Build an Android app that streams queries from a desktop over Bluetooth/Wi‑Fi to SmolChat for on-device inference and measure latency and energy consumption across different SLMs.
Integrate SmolChat with a small robot's Android controller to run on-device natural language commands and evaluate robustness of local LLM inference in a mechatronics control scenario.

cls.summary: livox_ros_driver2 is an open-source ROS/ROS2 device driver that connects Livox LiDAR units (HAP, MID-360 and others) to ROS ecosystems and publishes pointcloud and related topics for downstream processing and visualization.
cls.what_it_does: This repository provides a C++ driver package to discover, configure and stream point cloud and status data from Livox LiDAR devices into ROS (Noetic/Melodic) and ROS2 (Foxy/Humble/Jazzy). It is used by building the package inside a ROS/ROS2 workspace and launching supplied launch files to publish standard pointcloud2 and custom Livox messages, with example rviz launches included. The project is notable for supporting multiple Livox models, both ROS1 and ROS2, and for integrating with the Livox-SDK2.
cls.trl_rationale: The repository is multi-year (created 2022-08) with large community interest (900+ stars), active recent commits and clear install/build instructions, indicating production-ready maturity for integration and testing; README notes it is intended for test scenarios and suggests code optimisation for mass production, which limits full industrial claims but supports TRL 7.
prerequisites: C++ build tools and colcon / catkin as appropriate
student_project_ideas: Integrate a Livox LiDAR with ROS2 and implement a real-time obstacle detection node that subscribes to the pointcloud2 topic and publishes bounding boxes for a mobile robot navigation stack.

Build a mapping pipeline that fuses Livox point clouds with wheel odometry to produce a 2D/3D map (using Cartographer or RTAB-Map) and evaluate localization accuracy across different sensor placements.

cls.summary: TheWhisper is an open-source, optimized speech-to-text toolkit that provides streaming, low-latency Whisper-based inference for NVIDIA GPUs and Apple Silicon for on-device and cloud deployments.
cls.what_it_does: TheWhisper provides optimized Whisper model weights, inference engines and a simple Python API to run low-latency streaming transcription and translation on NVIDIA GPUs and Apple Silicon (CoreML). It is used for real-time captioning, voice interfaces and edge deployments and is notable for its streaming support, low power on macOS and optimized GPU engines via TheStage ElasticModels.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository is over one year old, has substantial community interest (900+ stars), documented install paths for multiple platforms, benchmarking and an Electron demo app; these indicate production-ready tooling and real deployments rather than an early prototype.

access to supported hardware (NVIDIA GPU or Apple Silicon) for full performance

Evaluate on-device vs GPU transcription trade-offs by benchmarking latency, power and accuracy for a whisper-large-v3 model on Apple Silicon (CoreML) and an NVIDIA GPU (TensorRT) and report implications for edge deployments.

tools.name: hehehai/VoxtMini
tools.desc: Voice input for macOS on local models: transcribe, translate and rewrite in any app. The successor of Voxt.

cls.summary: VoxtMini is an open-source macOS app that lets you press a shortcut, speak, and have local or remote models transcribe, translate or rewrite text directly into any app.
cls.what_it_does: VoxtMini captures speech on Apple Silicon Macs and produces live transcriptions, translations, or rewrites which are inserted at the cursor in any application. It uses local ASR and local/remote language models (defaulting to local Qwen3-ASR/Whisper and MLX-served LLMs) for privacy-first processing and offers features like per-app prompts, history with recordings, and a custom dictionary.
cls.trl_rationale: The project is an active, well-starred repository with releases and recent commits, indicating a beta-level product; however the repository is under one year old which limits the TRL to at most 6 absent longer production track record.
prerequisites: Optional: ~16 GB RAM for recommended local models
student_project_ideas: Measure and compare transcription error rates of VoxtMini's local ASR models (Qwen3-ASR, Whisper) on a prepared dataset of technical speech and produce a report analyzing failures and domain-specific vocabulary handling.

Build a simple accessibility macro that uses VoxtMini's rewrite/translation features to automatically simplify selected text for non-native readers, integrating it with a small UI and testing on target users.

tools.name: OpenDCAI/OpenWorldLib

cls.summary: OpenWorldLib is an open-source Python framework that collects and standardises research code for multimodal world models (video, 3D scene generation, vision-language-action and related tasks).
cls.what_it_does: It provides a unified codebase and wrappers for many world-model research methods so researchers can run, compare and extend models for tasks like video generation, 3D scene generation and vision-language-action. Users install the repository, run included test/inference scripts and plug in individual model implementations; notable aspects are its broad collection of recent research methods and scripted test/inference pipelines.
cls.trl_rationale: The repository is about one year old, has many stars (890), example scripts, a structured codebase and installation scripts which indicate active development and usage beyond a personal proof-of-concept; however it is still research-focused and younger than one year so TRL is capped at 6.
prerequisites: GPU with large VRAM (examples mention 80GB+ and 141GB)
PyTorch / ML libraries (diffusers / transformers often used)
student_project_ideas: Use one included lightweight model from the repo to generate short navigation videos from a dataset, measure basic qualitative metrics and report on compute and memory requirements for deployment.

tools.desc: LSP server leveraging LLMs for code completion (and more?)

cls.summary: llm-ls is an open-source Language Server Protocol (LSP) server that uses large language models to provide code completions and other editor assistance to IDE extensions.
cls.what_it_does: llm-ls acts as a common LSP backend that sends editor context to LLMs and returns model-driven completions, handling prompt construction, tokenisation and heuristics for single- vs multi-line completions. It supports multiple model backends (Hugging Face Inference API, text-generation-inference, ollama, OpenAI-compatible servers) and is intended to be extended by lightweight IDE plugins.
cls.trl_rationale: The project is several years old (created 2023) with substantial community interest (many stars), multiple compatible IDE extensions listed, and active development; however it is still described as a work in progress and not a de-facto standard, so TRL 7 (production-ready but evolving) is appropriate.

basic knowledge of LLM model backends and API keys
comfort building/running Rust binaries for local installs
student_project_ideas: Build an editor extension that integrates llm-ls to provide domain-specific code snippets and measure completion quality on a dataset of student assignments.

Compare latency and suggestion quality by running llm-ls with three backends (local llama.cpp server, Hugging Face Inference API, and an OpenAI-compatible server) and report trade-offs for offline vs cloud models.

tools.name: Belluxx/Aleph
tools.desc: Give satellite imagery, terrain data, buildings, streetview photos to your LLM

cls.summary: Aleph downloads geospatial assets (satellite imagery, terrain tiles, buildings, Street View photos and textured 3D models) for a user-drawn area or specific points and exposes them via a local dashboard and CLI.
cls.what_it_does: Aleph lets you select a rectangle or polygon on an interactive map (or request data for individual points) and then downloads the available world data inside that area: OSM building footprints, elevation/terrain tiles, HD satellite imagery, Street View photos and textured 3D meshes exported as glTF/3D-tiles. It provides a local dashboard to preview layers and explore captures in 3D and a CLI for scripted downloads; notable points are it requires no API keys and aims to produce a portable "piece of the Earth" for local use or for LLMs.
cls.trl_rationale: The project is actively developed and already provides a usable CLI and dashboard (README and install steps), and it has significant community interest (many stars). However the repository is only ~2 months old, uses undocumented/fragile data sources and README warns of breaking changes, so it fits an alpha-in-use TRL rather than production.
prerequisites: internet connection for basemap and remote sources
student_project_ideas: Build a simple digital-twin viewer: use Aleph to capture a city block, then integrate the glTF output into a web viewer (three.js or Cesium) and annotate building metadata from OSM for a visualization assignment.

Compare terrain-derived flood extents: download terrain tiles and building footprints for a small watershed with Aleph, compute simple flow accumulation or flood masking in Python, and visualise results over the captured satellite basemap.

It is used like a SketchUp-style modeller with woodworking-specific features (many joint types, procedural wood grain, routing profiles and cut-plan exports) and is notable for running on WebAssembly/WebGPU and providing live joint previews and workshop-oriented exports.

Build a plugin or script (or modify the source) to export BenchUp assemblies into a CNC-friendly format and validate cut nests using an external nesting library (combine with a simple optimizer).

tools.name: quaadgras/graphics.gd
tools.desc: Runtime for Go + Godot

cls.summary: graphics.gd is a Go-language runtime and bindings that let you write Godot engine games, multimedia apps and gdextensions using Go instead of GDScript, C++ or C#.
cls.what_it_does: graphics.gd provides a cross-platform runtime and Go bindings for the Godot engine (GDExtension), allowing developers to write engine classes, scenes and shaders in Go and build native apps for desktop, mobile and web. It is used as a drop-in development toolchain (including a `gd` CLI) and exposes a ported Godot API with strongly typed variants and documented examples on pkg.go.dev, making fast iteration and cross-compilation straightforward.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository is mature (created 2022, ~3+ years old), has substantial community interest (881 stars), active recent commits and documentation including pkg.go.dev and examples; these indicate production-ready software used by projects rather than a throwaway prototype.
prerequisites: basic knowledge of Godot engine concepts (nodes, scenes, GDExtension)
C toolchain for building native/shared libraries when targeting some platforms
student_project_ideas: Build a desktop and WebAssembly interactive physics demo in Godot where the game logic and custom shaders are implemented in Go using graphics.gd, and compare runtime performance against an equivalent GDScript prototype.

Create a robot teleoperation UI in Godot that visualises sensor data and control inputs, with networking and data decoding implemented in Go (graphics.gd) to demonstrate a real-time HMI for a mechatronics course.

tools.name: torchgeo/terratorch
tools.desc: A Python toolkit for fine-tuning Geospatial Foundation Models (GFMs).

cls.summary: TerraTorch is a Python toolkit for fine-tuning and running geospatial foundation models (remote-sensing ML) built on PyTorch Lightning and TorchGeo.
cls.what_it_does: TerraTorch provides a flexible training and inference framework for image segmentation, classification and pixel-wise regression on geospatial data, including ready-to-use datamodules, model factories, CLI and notebook workflows. It exposes connectors to many open pre-trained geospatial backbones and integrates with common PyTorch model/decoder libraries to simplify fine-tuning and deployment of remote-sensing models.
cls.trl_rationale: The repository is actively maintained, has substantial community interest (≈880 stars), integrates with established projects (PyTorch Lightning, TorchGeo) and lists many supported models and datasets; these indicate production-ready capability rather than a narrow demo. Repository age (>1 year) and active pushes support TRL 7.
prerequisites: CUDA (for GPU acceleration, optional but typical)
student_project_ideas: Fine-tune a pretrained geospatial backbone from TerraTorch on a local land-cover dataset and evaluate segmentation accuracy compared to a baseline UNet implemented with segmentation_models.pytorch.

Build a small operational pipeline that uses TerraTorch to perform inference on satellite tiles, then visualise classification outputs on a web map (combine TerraTorch for model inference and a simple web map stack like Folium or a small backend).

tools.name: esengine/estella
tools.desc: A fast 2D and 3D game engine — TypeScript SDK, C++/WebAssembly core, visual editor. Ship one project to web, desktop, WeChat MiniGames, playable ads, and native Android / iOS.

cls.summary: Estella is an open-source 2D/3D game engine with a TypeScript SDK, C++/WebAssembly core and a visual editor that exposes an MCP server for agent-driven editing and export to web, desktop and mobile targets.
cls.what_it_does: Estella provides a game runtime, editor and toolchain that let developers build, test and export 2D and 3D projects across Web, mini-game platforms, playable ads and native desktop/mobile. It is used via a visual editor plus a TypeScript SDK for game logic, and notable for its Model Context Protocol (MCP) editor surface that lets automated agents drive the editor and perform reproducible edits, playtests and exports.
cls.trl_rationale: The project is active, well-documented and popular (many stars and regular pushes) which indicates maturity, but the repository is under one year old so by the stated TRL rules it should be capped at TRL 6 despite strong community interest.
student_project_ideas: Build a small interactive digital-twin style scene (e.g. a factory cell) in Estella that streams simple telemetry to the game and visualises state changes; combine with a lightweight MQTT broker to simulate live data.

Implement an AI-driven level designer using the MCP interface: have an agent programmatically create scenes, run deterministic playtests and compare rendered frames to reference images to iterate design rules.

tools.name: sipeed/MaixPy
tools.desc: Easily create AI projects with Python on edge device

cls.summary: MaixPy is a Python runtime and SDK for MaixCAM-class edge AI cameras that lets you run vision, audio and lightweight LLM/VLM workloads on embedded hardware.
cls.what_it_does: MaixPy provides a Python API, device drivers and tools to run AI vision and peripheral I/O on MaixCAM devices, enabling rapid prototyping and deployment of edge-AI applications. It is used on-board the MaixCAM / MaixCAM2 / MaixCAM-Pro hardware and integrates with a workstation IDE (MaixVision), online training (MaixHub) and prebuilt models, making it notable for combining embedded firmware/peripherals with higher-level Python AI APIs.
cls.trl_rationale: The project is several years old, has many stars and forks, active recent commits, hardware platforms (MaixCAM family), documentation, IDE and online services, and appears used for real projects; these indicate production-ready maturity (TRL 7).
prerequisites: familiarity with embedded hardware and cross-compilation
knowledge of computer vision / AI model concepts for effective use
student_project_ideas: Build a real-time object detector on a MaixCAM device using a pretrained YOLO model in MaixPy, stream detections to a laptop for logging and evaluation (combine with OpenCV on the host).
Prototype an embedded condition-monitoring sensor that captures images and serial telemetry, runs on-device classification with MaixPy and sends alerts over WiFi for an IoT dashboard.

tools.name: yurineko73/Godot-MCP-Native

It implements the MCP Server using Godot's native HTTP, requires no dependency installation, is ready to use out of the box, and supports invocation by various AI tools.

cls.summary: Godot MCP Native is an open-source Godot plugin that exposes a Model Context Protocol (MCP) server inside the Godot editor so AI agents can read and modify scenes, scripts, nodes and resources directly.
cls.what_it_does: It implements an MCP server natively in Godot (no Node.js dependency) and provides a large set of tools (155 total) to let AI assistants inspect and change a Godot project in real time. It is used as a plugin in the Godot editor or in headless editor mode, and includes a CLI (gdmcp) and connectors/examples for agent platforms (Claude, Cursor, Cline, etc.).
cls.trl_rationale: The repository is actively developed, has many stars and a substantial feature list (CLI, many tools and integrations), indicating more than an experimental prototype, but it was created ~197 days ago (<1 year) so a conservative TRL of 6 (beta) is appropriate until longer-term adoption and release history appear.
prerequisites: Familiarity with Godot engine and editor
Understanding of MCP/AI agent workflows for integrations
