tools.name: genex-games/genex-desktop
tools.desc: Desktop app for game dev with AI: make games in Unreal Engine, Unity, Godot or the browser. The agent sets up the engine, builds your game and play-tests it by itself.

cls.summary: Genex is a desktop app that uses multi-agent AI to create, build and play-test games across engines like Unreal, Unity, Godot and Roblox, and supports local models and plugins (including a Blender plugin).
cls.what_it_does: Genex runs AI agents that scaffold and configure game engine projects, generate assets via plugins (e.g. Blender), orchestrate builds and perform autonomous play‑testing; it can use cloud LLMs (Claude/ChatGPT) or local models and is extensible via a plugin marketplace. It is notable for integrating multiple game engines and model backends into a single desktop app with an agent/plugin system.
cls.trl_rationale: The project is active, provides releases and a runnable desktop app and has significant community interest (many stars), but the repository is very new (created ~46 days ago) so it lacks a long track record or evidence of production deployments, limiting maturity to TRL 5.
prerequisites: Installed target game engines (Unreal, Unity, Godot or Roblox) for full features
macOS on Apple Silicon required for developer build steps
student_project_ideas: Extend Genex with a plugin that exports telemetry from play-tests into a time-series DB and visualises level difficulty progression, integrating with a simple data-plotting library.
Use Genex agents to auto-generate a small physics-based game in Godot, then run automated play-tests to collect failure cases and build a regression test suite for verification.

tools.name: perfanalytics/pose2sim

cls.summary: Pose2Sim is an open-source pipeline that converts 2D pose estimates from video into 3D markerless kinematics and OpenSim-compatible joint-angle outputs for human or animal motion analysis.
cls.what_it_does: Pose2Sim takes pose-estimation keypoints from one or multiple cameras, synchronises and calibrates cameras, triangulates and filters 3D markers, and produces OpenSim-ready kinematics (joint angles) and visualisations in Blender or OpenSim. It is used as a local, privacy-preserving alternative to marker-based motion capture for sports, clinical gait analysis and animation, and supports multiple 2D backends (RTMPose, DeepLabCut, legacy OpenPose).
cls.trl_rationale: The repository is mature (created 2022, >4 years old), has many stars (874), active recent commits and documented, research-validated accuracy in the README; it appears production-ready for real projects though it is not an industry-wide standard, so TRL 7 is appropriate.
prerequisites: familiarity with pose-estimation concepts and camera calibration
OpenSim installation for full kinematics output

cls.summary: DiffusionGS is an open-source method and implementation that uses Gaussian splatting baked into a diffusion denoiser to turn single images into fast 3D point-clouds and exportable meshes.
cls.what_it_does: It performs single-image image-to-3D object and scene generation by combining Gaussian splatting with a diffusion denoiser to produce dense Gaussian point clouds and optional textured mesh exports. Users run the provided demos or command-line scripts on an NVIDIA GPU to generate views, download point clouds or 2K textured meshes, and inspect exported meshes via included assets and Hugging Face Spaces demos. The implementation is notable for fast inference (orders-of-magnitude speed improvement claims versus some prior multi-view diffusion methods) and provided pretrained checkpoints and export tooling.
cls.trl_rationale: The repo provides code, pretrained checkpoints, export tooling, active development with recent pushes and Hugging Face Spaces demos and datasets; it has broad community interest (870 stars). It is more than an experimental prototype and includes mesh export and published paper (ICCV submission), indicating production-readiness although still research-led.

Familiarity with installing/compiling Python C-extensions and managing conda environments

tools.name: Helldez/BigMoeOnEdge

prerequisites: familiarity with llama.cpp and GGUF model formats
experience building/running C++ projects and platform toolchains (Linux/macOS/Windows/Android/iOS)
basic knowledge of LLM inference, quantization and MoE concepts
student_project_ideas: Build a mobile or Raspberry Pi demonstrator that runs a GGUF MoE model via BigMoeOnEdge to perform on-device task planning for a small robot, measuring latency and token throughput under different cache sizes.

tools.name: kytmanov/obsidian-llm-wiki-local
tools.desc: Karpathy’s LLM Wiki, 100% local with Ollama. Drop Markdown notes → AI extracts concepts → your Obsidian wiki auto-links and grows. Zero sharing. Your notes stay yours.

It is designed to run fully locally (Ollama by default) but can be pointed at OpenAI-compatible endpoints, making it notable for privacy-conscious personal knowledge management without requiring cloud vector DBs.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository is actively used and popular (852 stars) with a full-feature README and install paths, but it is under 1 year old (created 2026-04-07) so evidence supports a beta-level maturity rather than long-term production (TRL 6). README also notes the project is in maintenance and points to a successor.
prerequisites: Local LLM runtime (Ollama recommended) or OpenAI-compatible API key
student_project_ideas: Create an extension that links obsidian-llm-wiki outputs with a citation manager (e.g. Zotero) so engineering literature notes become curated wiki articles with source attributions.

Build a comparative experiment that runs the same vault through Ollama and a cloud OpenAI-compatible endpoint to measure differences in extracted concepts and output quality, reporting results as an Obsidian research page.

cls.trl_rationale: The README and examples show a working product with releases and many stars, but the repository is only 47 days old so there is no long track record; this matches an 'alpha in use' stage (TRL 5).

basic knowledge of llama.cpp and GGUF model files

Create a small secure front-end (mobile or web) that authenticates clients and routes requests to PS5LM, demonstrating local-only deployment and basic access control for a private model server.

Build a scene-management tool that validates project scenes at build time (reports Missing/NotInBuild issues) using the SceneReference API and integrates results into a Unity Editor window.

tools.name: AIScientists-Dev/WorldSeed
tools.desc: More is Different. A multi-agent world engine where AI agents live, talk, compete, ally.

tools.name: CHATS-lab/verbalized-sampling
tools.desc: Verbalized Sampling, a training-free prompting strategy to mitigate mode collapse in LLMs by requesting responses with probabilities. cls.summary: Verbalized Sampling is a prompting technique and Python package that asks large language models to output multiple responses with probabilities so you can sample from that distribution to increase output diversity.

tools.name: nace-ai/kapitsa
tools.desc: Blazing fast Apple Silicon inference engine optimized for Qwen & Nemotron. OpenAI + Anthropic API compatible. Built by folks from nace.ai

cls.summary: Kapitsa is a fast local inference engine for running large language models on Apple Silicon that exposes OpenAI/Anthropic-compatible APIs and is built for driving coding agents.
cls.what_it_does: Kapitsa runs and serves LLMs (Qwen, Nemotron/Flint and other packs) locally on Apple Silicon Macs, providing an OpenAI- and Anthropic-compatible API and helper commands to run coding agents. It focuses on high decode throughput and efficient quantisation/streaming (SSD streaming, Neural Engine prefill, KFlash quant flows) so large models can run on smaller Macs and be used by agent workflows.
cls.trl_rationale: The README and benchmarks show a functioning, feature-rich engine and many community stars, but the repository is only ~32 days old so by the TRL rules it cannot be rated above TRL 5 despite strong activity and documentation.
prerequisites: familiarity with LLM model files (GGUF/MLX) and command-line tools
student_project_ideas: Build a coding-agent pipeline that uses Kapitsa locally to run program synthesis tasks and compare developer productivity and latency against a cloud LLM API.

Measure and report model throughput and memory trade-offs by benchmarking different quantised model packs (e.g. Nace quants vs community packs) on a target Apple Silicon machine and document the effects of SSD streaming and Neural Engine prefill.

tools.name: SharpAI/SwiftLM
tools.desc: ⚡ Native MLX Swift LLM inference server for Apple Silicon. OpenAI-compatible API, SSD streaming for 100B+ MoE models, TurboQuant KV cache compression, MACOS + iOS iPhone app.

cls.summary: SwiftLM is a native Swift inference server that runs MLX-format large language models on Apple Silicon with an OpenAI-compatible API and optimisations for SSD streaming and quantised models.
cls.what_it_does: SwiftLM serves MLX models on macOS and iOS devices without a Python runtime, using Metal kernels for GPU acceleration and features such as SSD streaming for Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) models and KV cache compression. It is used as a local, OpenAI-compatible inference endpoint (single-binary server or iPhone app) aimed at maximising Apple Silicon performance for large quantised models.
cls.trl_rationale: The project is active, has releases and a sizeable star count, pre-built binaries and test harnesses, and clear performance benchmarking, indicating beta-level maturity; however the repository is only ~8 months old so there is not yet a long track record required for TRL 7+.
prerequisites: Metal Toolchain and basic Homebrew tools (cmake)
student_project_ideas: Build a privacy-preserving on-device assistant for a robotics lab that uses SwiftLM on a Mac mini to serve an OpenAI-compatible endpoint and integrates with a robot control node (ROS 2) to accept natural-language commands.

Compare inference throughput and energy use by running a quantised MLX model in SwiftLM on different Apple Silicon hardware (M2 vs M6) and produce a report linking performance to model size and SSD streaming settings.

Notable points are single-import task modules, an accompanying demo site, and emphasis on privacy (no data leaves the user's device) and shipping only code under MIT while respecting model licenses.

prerequisites: basic WebGPU / WASM concepts for performance tuning
student_project_ideas: Build a browser-based prototype that captures webcam images and runs runonweb's ObjectDetector and DepthEstimator to create an annotated 3D-like AR overlay, then measure runtime and model download sizes across WebGPU and WASM backends.

Create a privacy-preserving voice-command interface for a simulated IoT dashboard using runonweb/stt and runonweb/translate to process voice locally in the browser and control a Cloudflare-hosted demo dashboard.

tools.name: TylerTemp/SaintsField
tools.desc: A Unity extension for inspector enhancement and data serialization.

cls.summary: SaintsField is a Unity Editor extension that enhances the inspector UI and adds richer data serialization for Unity projects.
cls.what_it_does: SaintsField provides attributes and editor code to customise how fields are displayed in the Unity inspector (including deep-nested fields, grouping, labels and decorative attributes) and extends serialization to types like dictionaries, interfaces and hashsets. It is installed as a Unity package (git, OpenUPM or unitypackage) and works with both IMGUI and UI Toolkit custom drawers, with optional integrations such as DOTween support.
cls.trl_rationale: The repository is mature (created 2023, >3 years old), has substantial community interest (793 stars), recent activity (last push 2026-11-13) and releases, indicating production-ready editor tooling rather than a one-off prototype.
prerequisites: familiarity with Unity package installation (UPM) and editor extensions
student_project_ideas: Create a custom inspector for a simulated robotic sensor component using SaintsField to display nested configuration, then connect it to a runtime simulation in Unity to visualise parameter changes in editor time.

Extend a student game or digital-twin prototype by serialising complex runtime data (e.g. dictionaries of telemetry) using SaintsField and build editor UI panels that group and annotate fields for easier testing.

tools.name: notatestuser/ds4-control

cls.summary: DS4 Control is a macOS menu-bar app that launches, supervises and monitors a local ds4 server and manages downloads and selection of large DeepSeek V4-family models (including V4.1 with up to 1M context).
cls.what_it_does: It runs as a macOS menubar application that starts/stops a local ds4-server process, monitors resource usage, and provides model download, selection and RAM-feasibility gating for DeepSeek V4 variants. It is notable for integrated resumable parallel model downloads, automated RAM/SSD-streaming checks for very large models, and tight macOS-native integration (signed and notarized, Homebrew cask).
cls.trl_rationale: The project is actively developed, signed/notarized, distributed via a Homebrew cask and has many stars, indicating adoption; however the repository is only ~172 days old so demonstrable long-term production track record is limited, capping TRL at 6.
prerequisites: familiarity with macOS terminal and installing Homebrew casks
large local disk and significant RAM for big models (see README RAM table)
student_project_ideas: Measure and report throughput and memory/SSD streaming behaviour by running ds4-server via DS4 Control on different Mac hardware (e.g. M2 vs M3) and plot latency/throughput vs context length.
Extend the app to add automated benchmark scripts that run a set of prompts and record generation speed and resource usage, then visualise the results in a small macOS dashboard.

tools.name: MaiKuraki/UnityStarter
tools.desc: Production-ready modular Unity framework: UE-inspired Gameplay Ability System, zero-GC core, HybridCLR hot-update, Luban config pipeline, data-driven build & atlas workflows. cls.summary: A production-oriented, modular Unity game framework that organises gameplay systems as reusable UPM packages and includes build/CI tooling, a GAS-like ability system, and optional integrations for hot-reload and asset pipelines.

It is used by importing packages into a Unity project or starting from the provided template, and notable features include zero-GC design, HybridCLR hot-update support, and built-in analyzers and project-owned build pipelines.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository is over one year old, actively maintained with recent pushes and CI orientation, large star count (792) indicating adoption; README and module map show production-oriented features (UPM packages, analyzers, build tooling). No evidence of enterprise-wide deployments or formal releases to claim TRL 8–9, so TRL 7 (production-ready) is appropriate.
student_project_ideas: Create a small multiplayer prototype that implements a new gameplay ability using the framework's GameplayAbilities and integrate it with an addressable content pipeline (Addressables/YooAsset) to demonstrate modular packaging and runtime loading.

Use the template to build a deterministic, headless simulation run (no graphics) that exercises AI behavior trees and record deterministic logs for analysis, demonstrating separation of engine-free logic and CI-driven validation.

cls.what_it_does: Vui provides an end-to-end streaming voice assistant: microphone audio is transcribed, passed to an LLM, and replied-to with a conversation-conditioned TTS model (Vui Nano) that supports voice cloning and streaming playback. It is delivered as a Python server with a browser UI, Docker compose option, a pure-C CPU runtime for TTS weights, and pluggable ASR/LLM backends (Ollama, vLLM, OpenAI-compatible). The project is notable for a small (≈219M active parameter) dialogue-conditioned TTS that preserves prosody across turns and a production-oriented streaming pipeline (WebRTC, speculative prefill, barge-in).

tools.name: GameFrameX/GameFrameX
tools.desc: An open-source toolbox that takes a game all the way "from idea → built → live" — Unity/Godot/Cocos/Laya clients + one .NET server. | 开源游戏全流程工具箱：Unity/Godot/Cocos/Laya 客户端 + .NET 服务器，从想法到上线一站搞定。

cls.summary: GameFrameX is an open-source end-to-end toolbox that provides Unity/Godot/Cocos/Laya clients plus a .NET game server and backend tooling to build, deploy and run online multiplayer games.
cls.what_it_does: GameFrameX supplies a ready-made multiplayer server (in .NET), client integrations for multiple engines, data pipelines (MongoDB/Postgres), config tooling and an admin web panel so developers can prototype, deploy and operate online games without building all backend plumbing. It is used by cloning the repository, running the included server and database docker compositions and opening the client project (e.g. Unity) to run a full client↔server loop; notable points are multi-engine client support, built-in packaging/deployment with Docker, and protobuf-based protocol and LuBan Excel-to-data tooling.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository is mature (created 2023, >700 stars, active commits as of 2026) and README lists shipped games that used it; it provides a full server, client integrations and deployment docs, indicating production-ready use rather than a fragile prototype.
prerequisites: MongoDB / PostgreSQL (or use provided docker compose)
student_project_ideas: Build a small multiplayer prototype (lobby + simple gameplay) using the Unity client and GameFrameX server, then measure and report server latency and concurrency behaviour under test clients.
Extend the admin backend to add a simple analytics dashboard (player sessions, retention) by piping server metrics into a timeseries store and visualising them in the provided web panel.

tools.name: zju3dv/LoG
tools.desc: Level of Gaussians

cls.summary: LoG implements gaussian-splatting-based training and real-time rendering for large-scale urban scene novel-view synthesis and immersive visualization.
cls.what_it_does: LoG builds 3D scene models from multi-view images (preprocessed with COLMAP) using gaussian-splatting so you can synthesize novel views and create real-time renderings of city-scale environments. It is used by training on a single high-end GPU (RTX 4090) with PyTorch and provides tooling for dataset preprocessing, training, and interactive/demo rendering; notable points are its focus on large urban scenes and real-time visualization of the reconstructed models.
cls.trl_rationale: The project is linked to a 2024 conference paper, provides full training and demo code, a project webpage with videos, and has substantial community interest (770 stars) with active commits in 2026; these indicate production-ready research software though not an industry standard. It does require high-end GPU hardware which limits turnkey deployment.
student_project_ideas: Compare reconstruction quality and rendering performance between LoG and a NeRF implementation on a small urban dataset preprocessed with COLMAP, and quantify runtime and memory trade-offs.
Integrate LoG outputs into a simple WebGL viewer (three.js) to create an interactive urban-scene visualization that streams precomputed gaussian representations for a digital-twin demo.

tools.name: tetherto/qvac

cls.summary: QVAC is an open-source SDK and local model server for running LLMs, speech, vision and generative models on-device across desktop and mobile platforms without cloud APIs.
cls.what_it_does: QVAC provides JavaScript/TypeScript and Python SDKs plus an OpenAI-compatible HTTP server to run and serve local AI models (GGUF and others), handle inference (text, speech-to-text, image/video generation) and fetch models peer-to-peer. It is used to embed on-device inference in apps or expose local models to other tools via a compatible API and is notable for cross-platform support and P2P model distribution.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository is active with cross-platform SDKs, CLI, documentation and many stars and installs that indicate community interest, but the project was created ~318 days ago (<1 year) so it meets a beta-level maturity (TRL 6) rather than longer-established production status.

Node.js or Python runtime for SDK usage
student_project_ideas: Build a desktop or mobile chat assistant that runs a small local LLM via the QVAC SDK and compare latency and privacy trade-offs against a cloud API.

Create an edge-monitoring prototype that uses QVAC to run on-device speech-to-text for logged audio and forwards anonymised events to a cloud dashboard (combine QVAC with an MQTT broker or time-series DB).

tools.name: autowarefoundation/AWSIM

cls.what_it_does: AWSIM provides a Unity-powered simulation environment that mirrors the ROS 2 topics, messages and vehicle control modes used by Autoware so teams can develop, test and validate autonomous driving software without physical vehicles. It includes simulated sensors (LiDAR, camera, IMU, GNSS), traffic and scenario support (ASAM OpenSCENARIO), and interfaces natively with ROS 2 and Autoware for end-to-end closed-loop testing.
cls.trl_rationale: The repository is mature (created 2022, active maintenance through 2026), has substantial community interest (764 stars), documented tutorials and formal integration with Autoware and ASAM OpenSCENARIO, and has won a Unity industry award — evidence of production-readiness rather than an early prototype.

familiarity with Autoware vehicle topics/messages and sensor concepts

Implement and tune a new vehicle controller in Autoware, then validate control stability and response under different simulated vehicle dynamics and sensor noise models in AWSIM.

cls.trl_rationale: The project is active, public and runnable (Python executable model, Lean library) with many stars and documented papers, indicating more than an experimental prototype; however the repository is only ~10 months old (under one year) so it lacks the long track record, independent production users, or stable releases required for TRL 7+, so Beta (TRL 6) is appropriate.
prerequisites: Lean (Lean 4/the Lean library used in repo)
familiarity with formal proofs and advanced mathematical physics

tools.name: cobanov/awesome-fly

cls.summary: AAS is an open, end-to-end stack for simulating, developing and deploying perception-driven multi‑drone autonomy using PX4/ArduPilot/Betaflight, ROS 2, YOLO and NVIDIA Jetson components.
cls.what_it_does: Aerial-autonomy-stack provides a Dockerised, multi‑vehicle simulation environment (Gazebo + ROS 2 + Gymnasium) tied to common autopilots (PX4, ArduPilot, Betaflight) and perception chains (YOLO, LiDAR odometry). It supports faster‑than‑real‑time and multi‑instance simulation, hardware‑in‑the‑loop with Jetson devices, and provides scripts, example missions and logs/plotting tools to develop and deploy swarm autonomy.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository is >1 year old, has a substantial user interest (661 stars), active recent commits and pre-built container images, detailed docs and end-to-end examples including HITL—evidence of production readiness rather than a throwaway demo.
prerequisites: familiarity with PX4/ArduPilot concepts and JetPack/Jetson hardware
student_project_ideas: Implement and evaluate a formation‑flying controller for a small quadrotor swarm in the AAS simulation, comparing sensor modalities (camera YOLO detections vs LiDAR odometry) for relative localisation.
Integrate a custom perception module (e.g. a TensorRT‑optimised detector) and run Jetson‑in‑the‑loop tests to measure end‑to‑end latency and its effect on offboard control stability.

cls.summary: An open-source Android input method and voice‑input service that runs OpenAI Whisper models locally to provide offline speech recognition and optional translation.
cls.what_it_does: WhisperIME installs as an Android IME and a RecognitionService to capture speech, transcribe it using TFLite versions of Whisper models downloaded on first run, and optionally translate supported languages to English. It is used as a keyboard microphone replacement or system voice input and is notable for running the model entirely on-device after an initial model download to preserve user privacy.
cls.trl_rationale: The repository is over a year old, has substantial community interest (659 stars), active development (recent push), and distribution via F‑Droid/OpenAPK which indicates real‑world use; it runs complete on‑device models but is an app rather than a widely adopted platform, supporting a production‑ready TRL 7 judgement.
prerequisites: basic Android app installation and settings
familiarity with ADB for advanced configuration (optional)
student_project_ideas: Build an Android app that uses WhisperIME as the on-device speech input for a domain-specific data-entry form and evaluate recognition accuracy and latency on different models and devices.

Integrate WhisperIME with a Raspberry Pi based kiosk (Android Things / Android on ARM) to prototype an offline voice-controlled interface and measure CPU, memory and power trade-offs between the compact and multilingual TFLite models.

tools.name: reality-opened/openreality
tools.desc: Open Reality: phone video to AI-queryable 3D scenes. MCP tools for Claude/Codex/Cursor (npm openreality-mcp), the self-hostable broker, and the VGGT-SLAM library, in one repo. BSD-2-Clause.

cls.summary: Open Reality converts phone video into persistent, queryable 3D scenes (gaussian-splatting style) with measurement, path-planning and robot-export tools and an MCP interface for AI assistants.
cls.what_it_does: Open Reality ingests handheld video and produces a persistent 3D reconstruction and camera trajectory, offers measurement and path-planning over the reconstructed scene, and exports robot-training datasets or simulator scenes. It is delivered as a self-hostable server + a 42-tool MCP (Model Context Protocol) npm package so AI assistants (Claude, Codex, Cursor) can call scene tools directly; the reconstruction core builds on the VGGT-SLAM research work and supports gaussian-splatting outputs.
cls.trl_rationale: The repo is feature-rich with a full server, MCP tooling and examples, and many stars indicating strong interest, but it was created only 77 days ago so it lacks the multi-release, long-term production track record required for TRL 6+. README documents self-hosting and an offline simulator, which supports early adopters (TRL 5).
prerequisites: GPU capable machine (CUDA compatible) for reconstruction jobs
student_project_ideas: Create an end-to-end pipeline that scans a small indoor space with a phone, reconstructs the scene with Open Reality, then exports and imports the scene into Isaac Sim to run and evaluate a simple navigation policy.

Build a measurement-and-verification lab: students calibrate a reconstructed scene to real-world distances, then compare automated measurements (from Open Reality) against hand measurements and report errors and sources of scale/pose drift.

tools.name: timmyy123/LLM-Hub
tools.desc: Local LLM, image&video&music generator

cls.summary: LLM Hub is an open-source cross-platform app that runs local large language models and on-device image, video and music generation on mobile and desktop.
cls.what_it_does: LLM Hub lets users run LLM chat, autonomous agents, and multimodal generators (images, video, music) locally on Android, iOS and desktop, with support for multiple model formats and device acceleration. It can also expose OpenAI/Anthropic-compatible APIs to other apps and integrates on-device tools like TTS, transcription and upscaling, making it notable as a privacy-focused, multi-platform local-AI client.
cls.trl_rationale: The project is over a year old, has many stars and published desktop releases (desktop v0.1.3) and a public case study, and provides signed downloads and CI workflows, indicating production-readiness for end users rather than a one-off prototype.
prerequisites: familiarity with local LLM model formats and deployment
mobile/desktop build toolchains (Android/iOS toolchains, native packaging)
basic understanding of model acceleration (CPU/GPU/NPU) concepts
student_project_ideas: Measure and compare on-device latency, memory use and energy consumption of different local LLMs (e.g. Gemma, LLaMA variants) using LLM Hub Desktop and report suitability trade-offs for mobile deployment.
Extend LLM Hub by adding a simple safety-logging plugin that records agent actions and permission use on Android, then evaluate privacy and risk scenarios in a small usability study.

tools.name: wanshuiyin/ARIS-in-AI-Offer
tools.desc: Bilingual (中文+EN) ML / LLM / diffusion / agent interview cheat sheets for AI 秋招 — generated by ARIS /interview-cheatsheet, rendered by /render-html into single-file HTML, reads anywhere — plus a CV→DBLP-fact-checked academic homepage generator and hand-authored long-form blogs 🌱

cls.summary: A bilingual collection of long-form AI/ML interview cheat sheets, runnable PyTorch examples and an automated CV→academic-homepage generator, published as single-file HTML pages for easy reading on any device.
cls.what_it_does: This repository generates and publishes bilingual (Chinese/English) interview preparation materials covering ML, LLMs, diffusion, agents and related topics; each sheet combines derivations, 25 stratified interview questions, and from-scratch PyTorch code. It is produced by an ARIS render workflow into single-file responsive HTML that is downloadable and readable offline, and includes a CV→fact-checked academic homepage generator and hand-authored long-form blog content.
cls.trl_rationale: The project is active, well-documented and widely starred (653 stars) with runnable example code and a public website, indicating more than a proof-of-concept; however the repository is only ~182 days old (under one year) so it lacks the multi-year track record or broad production deployments needed for TRL 7+.
prerequisites: comfort reading technical English/Chinese and LaTeX-formatted math
student_project_ideas: Reproduce and extend one of the 'from-scratch' PyTorch tutorials (e.g. diffusion foundations) to compare training / sampling behaviours and report results in a lab report.

Build a small pipeline that takes a student CV and uses the ARIS homepage generator workflow to produce a fact-checked single-file academic homepage, integrating simple unit tests for extracted bibliographic facts.

tools.name: puran-water/autocad-mcp
tools.desc: MCP server for AutoCAD LT v3.1: freehand AutoLISP execution, 8 consolidated tools, File IPC + ezdxf backends, focus-free dispatch, undo/redo, P&ID symbols, and robust IPC with ESC prefix and UTF-8 fallback. Companion agent skill: puran-water/autocad-drafting

cls.summary: An open-source MCP server that lets MCP clients drive AutoCAD LT or produce headless DXF output for scripted drawing automation and guarded revisioned edits.
cls.what_it_does: The project exposes a single MCP stdio API with eight drawing tools to automate AutoCAD LT (via a Windows File IPC backend and AutoLISP dispatcher) or generate headless DXF output (via ezdxf and matplotlib). It is used to run natural-language driven or programmatic drawing operations, journal revisions, and produce reproducible DXF deliverables; notable features include guarded/journaled revisions, undo/redo semantics, and platform-aware backends.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository is >1 year old with many stars (653), active maintenance (recent pushes) and explicit production use within Puran Water / PuranOS workflows; it provides multiple backends and documented installation, indicating production-readiness rather than an experimental prototype.
prerequisites: Windows 10/11 and native Windows Python for File IPC
familiarity with AutoLISP and DXF concepts
student_project_ideas: Create an MCP client that uses the server to automate placement and tagging of P&ID symbols across a plant layout, then compare AutoCAD LT (File IPC) and ezdxf headless outputs for CI-controlled deliverables.

Build a batch DXF generator that parametrically lays out piping runs from a CSV of equipment positions (using ezdxf) and produces journaled revision receipts to demonstrate guarded edits and traceability.

tools.desc: The public version of the Marching Squares Terrain plugin for godot.

cls.summary: A Godot engine plugin that provides marching-squares based terrain authoring and painting tools for stylized 3D levels.
cls.what_it_does: The toolkit is a Godot addon that lets level designers create and edit chunked terrain using a marching-squares algorithm: elevate/lower cells, smooth, paint multiple textures, place grass via mask maps and draw bridges. It is used as a plugin inside Godot (GDScript) and is notable for being focused on small-to-medium stylized 3D games with an accessible in-editor authoring workflow.
cls.trl_rationale: The project is a maintained, publicly released Godot plugin with documentation, contributors and a substantial star count, indicating community interest; however the repository is under one year old (created ~310 days ago) so it is limited to a beta-level TRL.
prerequisites: Familiarity with Godot engine (scene system and plugins)
student_project_ideas: Create a small procedural level generator that uses the plugin to author chunked terrain and then add gameplay elements (enemy spawns, item placement) to evaluate level flow.
Adapt the plugin to generate simple navigation terrains for a Godot-based robotics simulation and benchmark pathfinding/obstacle avoidance on generated maps.

tools.name: Nehanth/pooled
tools.desc: Peer-to-peer LLM inference in the browser: pool your devices to run big open models, for chat and coding agents.

cls.summary: Pooled runs large open LLMs by splitting model layers across multiple browser tabs/devices using WebGPU and WebRTC so a group of consumer devices can together perform inference without a central server.
cls.what_it_does: Pooled shards a large language model across the GPUs of multiple devices in a browser 'room', passing small hidden states between peers over WebRTC and running custom WGSL kernels on WebGPU. It is used from a web page or CLI to create a peer-to-peer inference cluster for chat and coding agents, notable for running very large models (including SSD-backed 125B MoE experimental mode) entirely in-browser without a server.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository is active and demonstrates full demos and benchmarks, but it is only 77 days old so lacks a longer production track record and stable releases; README shows working demos and CLI usage but age limits maturity to around TRL 5.
prerequisites: Familiarity with LLM concepts and model formats
student_project_ideas: Build a small pooled room that shards a 1–6B open model between a laptop and phone, measure end-to-end latency and token throughput as peers join and leave, and report scaling behaviour.

Integrate Pooled's OpenAI-compatible API gateway with a simple coding-agent that writes and runs small web apps in the host's sandbox, then measure reliability and safety controls when multiple users edit files.

tools.name: codepawl/crucible
tools.desc: 3D engine that AI agents drive

cls.summary: Crucible is a JavaScript 3D engine and MCP server that lets AI agents build, preview and render scenes in the browser or headless Chrome with both a realtime rasterizer and a path tracer.
cls.what_it_does: Crucible provides a lightweight scene format, realtime raster and path-tracing renderers, and an MCP server so an external AI agent can create, edit and render 3D scenes. It is used by running the renderer in a browser (or headless Chrome via the packaged server) and driving scene changes via JSON recipes and MCP commands; it includes addons for terrain, vegetation, characters, liquids and media export. What makes it notable is the explicit agent-driving workflow (MCP), built-in preview/render pipeline for stills and MP4, and support for WebGL2 and WebGPU backends.
cls.trl_rationale: The project is active and well-documented with many stars and weekly minor releases, but the repository is very new (created ~40 days ago) and README notes pre-1.0 API changes, so maturity is limited to early alpha/alpha-in-use (TRL 5).
prerequisites: Headless Chrome for MCP server and WebGL2/WebGPU-capable browser for rendering
student_project_ideas: Create an AI-driven scene authoring lab where students write small agents (using an LLM) that generate JSON scene recipes for Crucible and render PNGs or short MP4s via the MCP server, then compare stylistic differences between agents.

Integrate Crucible with a robotics simulation by exporting simple vehicle or sensor rigs as parts and using an agent to script camera trajectories and rendering to produce a dataset of simulated camera images for perception experiments.

tools.desc: 162 MCP tools for AI-powered Godot 4 development. Scene, animation, 3D, physics, particles, audio, shader, input simulation, runtime analysis, navigation, testing & more. $15 one-time.

cls.summary: Godot MCP Pro is a paid/proprietary MCP server plus a free Godot editor plugin that lets LLM-based assistants (e.g. Claude) interact with Godot Editor through a large set of editor-focused tools.
cls.what_it_does: Godot MCP Pro provides a Godot Editor plugin and an MCP (Model Context Protocol) server that expose editor, scene, scripting and runtime operations as tools for AI assistants. It is used by running a Node.js MCP server (included only in the paid package) which connects via WebSocket to the Godot plugin so LLMs can call JSON-RPC tools to inspect and modify a project in real time. The project is notable for its large set of curated editor tools and modes that accommodate clients with different tool limits.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository is about 8–9 months old with many stars and active commits, and a documented install/usage flow; however the MCP server (required for full functionality) is only distributed in the paid package and not present in this public repo, so demonstrated open-source maturity is limited to the plugin and CLI helpers.
prerequisites: Familiarity with Godot 4 editor and GDScript
Node.js/npm for building/running the MCP server
An LLM client or MCP-capable assistant (optional) and basic JSON-RPC/CLI usage
student_project_ideas: Build a prototype toolchain where an LLM (local or cloud) suggests scene edits via Godot MCP Pro to automatically generate and evaluate simple level layouts and record metrics (combine with a simple playtest bot to gather scoring).

Use the plugin and server CLI to implement automated test scripts that exercise runtime behaviours (input simulation, scene changes) and collect traces for a small physics or control simulation, demonstrating AI-assisted editor automation.

It is used as a teaching and reference resource (not a library) and is notable for being the official, widely starred companion to a published introductory GIS programming book with instructions for MyBinder, Colab and Docker.
cls.trl_rationale: The repository accompanies a published 2025 book, has Docker images, active maintenance with recent pushes, and a substantial community (642 stars), so it is production-ready for teaching; age (>1 year) and book backing support TRL 7 rather than a higher industry-standard rating.

cls.summary: An official Unity plugin that exposes skills for third‑party AI agents to inspect and modify Unity projects, drive the Editor via the Unity CLI, and automate common game‑development tasks.
cls.what_it_does: The repository provides a set of agent 'skills' that let LLM-driven agents (Claude Code, Codex, Grok, Antigravity, GitHub Copilot CLI and others) operate on a Unity project: editing scripts, scenes and assets, running Editor C# through the Unity CLI, and performing build/test tasks. It is notable because it is published by Unity and integrates agent workflows with the Unity CLI and Editor to automate development and debugging tasks.
cls.trl_rationale: The project is an official Unity plugin with many stars and active pushes, showing an organised release and community interest, but the repository is only ~103 days old so it lacks a long track record; that limits it to TRL 6 (beta).

access to an agent platform (Claude Code, Codex, Grok, Copilot CLI) or ability to install skills locally
Unity CLI for full Editor automation
student_project_ideas: Create an automated test workflow where an agent uses the plugin and Unity CLI to run a set of playmode tests, report failures, and open the offending scene for inspection.

Build an agent-driven level‑design assistant that generates a simple tile palette and populates a scene based on high‑level prompts, then compares performance metrics (frame time) before and after changes.

alternatives_to: Editor scripting with custom CLI tools

tools.name: Fast-Editor/Lynkr
tools.desc: Streamline your workflow with Lynkr, a CLI tool that acts as an HTTP proxy for efficient code interactions using Claude Code CLI.

cls.summary: Lynkr is an open-source Node.js CLI that runs an HTTP proxy/gateway to route, cache and compress LLM requests so code-assistant clients use cheaper or local models without code changes.
cls.what_it_does: Lynkr accepts LLM requests (acts as a local proxy) and performs tiered routing, semantic caching and JSON/tool-output compression to reduce token usage and cost; it can 'wrap' AI coding tools (Claude Code, Cursor, Codex) so they call Lynkr instead of an upstream API. Notable features are its tier routing logic, sub-300ms semantic cache hits, and plug-and-play wrap mode that requires no client code changes.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository is active with many stars, CLI installation and extensive docs and benchmarks, indicating a beta-level project; however it is under one year old so by the stated TRL rules it should be capped at TRL 6 despite visible real-world testing and integrations.
prerequisites: familiarity with LLM providers/APIs and basic CLI usage
optional: local model host (e.g. Ollama) for full testing
student_project_ideas: Build a course lab where students deploy Lynkr locally and compare token/cost savings and latency when routing identical coding queries through a local Ollama model vs a paid cloud model.

Create a small integration that uses Lynkr's wrap mode to add semantic caching and routing to an open-source code assistant (e.g. Cursor or a Codex CLI) and measure effects on throughput and cost for an automated test-suite of code-generation prompts.

tools.name: chickensoft-games/GameDemo
tools.desc: The Chickensoft Game Demo — a fully tested, third-person 3D game built with Godot and C#. Now with saving and loading!

cls.summary: A fully tested, third-person 3D game demo built with Godot and C# that demonstrates Chickensoft's architecture patterns, saving/loading, and unit testing for game projects.
cls.what_it_does: GameDemo is a complete third-person 3D example project implemented in Godot using C# that showcases an opinionated, testable game architecture, state machines, dependency injection, and a save/load system. It is distributed as a reference/demo project for Godot C# developers to learn patterns (LogicBlocks, AutoInject, Serialization) and to serve as a starting point for game development.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository is over three years old, has many stars (638), active recent commits, documented CI/testing and a complete project structure; these signs indicate production-ready demo quality rather than an early prototype.
student_project_ideas: Extend the demo to add telemetry and a simple analytics pipeline (e.g., log player actions to a local CSV or time-series DB) to study player behaviour and evaluate the save/load system under different game states.

Refactor a game subsystem (movement or enemy AI) to compare alternative state machine implementations and write unit tests using the project's testing setup to demonstrate test-driven development for interactive systems.

tools.name: Shpigford/nurb
tools.desc: Agentic CAD for 3D printing

cls.summary: nurb is a desktop app that turns a cloud LLM into an interactive parametric CAD partner for designing and exporting 3D-printable parts with live viewer, printability checks and 3MF-ready exports.
cls.what_it_does: nurb lets you describe a printed part in plain language and uses your cloud AI subscription to generate a parametric CAD function that is rendered live as a true B-rep solid (OCCT). It runs a suite of printability checks (overhangs, thin walls, stability, warp risk, etc.), provides sliders for parameters, and exports ready-to-print 3MF (plus STL, STEP, GLB) tuned for common slicers so you can iterate and print quickly. Notable features are live incremental modelling tied to parameter sliders, exact solid-based checks (not meshes), and direct integration with user-owned LLMs and slicers.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository is active, popular (many stars and recent releases including platform binaries) and the README describes a 1.0-style desktop app with end-to-end features; however the project is only ~115 days old (under one year) so it lacks the multi-year production track record required for TRL 7+. Evidence: platform builds and clear feature set in README support a beta-level rating.
prerequisites: knowledge of 3D printing concepts and slicers
understanding of CAD concepts (parametric modelling, units)
student_project_ideas: Build an automated pipeline that takes a measured part photo and asks nurb (via a chosen LLM) to generate a parametric adapter, then export 3MF and run a slicer to compare estimated print time and material before printing.

Extend nurb by adding a new printability check (e.g. lattice strength prediction) that analyses the OCCT B-rep and visualises warnings in the live viewer, integrating an open-source static analysis library.

It runs entirely in the browser using Chrome AI APIs and WebGPU/model caches (or Hugging Face models) so the deck and assets remain local rather than stored on a cloud backend.

Build an automated slide-localisation pipeline that uses LocalStudio's translation features and a small test corpus to compare translation quality and layout preservation across languages.

cls.what_it_does: OlliteRT downloads and runs LLMs on-device using Google's LiteRT-LM runtime and exposes an OpenAI-compatible HTTP API so existing OpenAI clients can use the phone as a private server. tools.name: jzjzzzzzzz/agent-me
tools.desc: Distill your knowledge, memories, and decisions into an open-source, inspectable AI Agent Twin.

cls.summary: Agent-Me is an open-source personal AI 'agent twin' system that stores inspectable, versioned personal knowledge and runs multi-role agent pipelines to produce evidence-grounded responses.
cls.what_it_does: Agent-Me ingests a person's knowledge, memories and decisions into reviewable Markdown (and optional typed SQLite memory), retrieves evidence with a deterministic RAG-style retriever, and runs sequential agent roles (Planner, Researcher, Critic, Writer, optional Verifier) to produce citation-aware answers and an inspectable execution trace. It is notable for its emphasis on provenance, reviewable memory, and an explicit multi-agent architecture rather than a single chat prompt.
cls.trl_rationale: The repo is a runnable FastAPI + React implementation with documented architecture and examples and a substantial star count, suggesting early adopters; however the project is only 82 days old (under 90 days) so it lacks a longer track record and cannot be rated above TRL 5.
prerequisites: optional LLM API credentials for model-backed features
student_project_ideas: Build a course-specific Agent-Me workspace that ingests lecture notes and assignments so students can ask an inspectable agent about course policies and resources.
Integrate Agent-Me with a Git repository to create an agent that answers questions about a codebase using commit messages and source files as reviewable memory.

tools.name: ghbalf/freecad-ai

cls.summary: FreeCAD AI is a FreeCAD workbench that uses large language models to generate and execute Python code to create 3D CAD models from natural-language prompts.
cls.what_it_does: It provides a docked chat interface inside FreeCAD that asks LLMs to produce Python modelling code or call structured modelling tools to build geometry from text (with Plan and Act modes to review or auto-run code). Notable features include tool-calling for safer operations, reusable "skills", vision routing for image inputs, session save/load, and support for many LLM providers.
cls.trl_rationale: The README explicitly labels the project as "Alpha software" and warns of breaking changes; the repository is 270 days old (<1 year) and active but does not show a long production track record or stable 1.0 releases, so it matches an early alpha TRL.

tools.name: Rhoban/bam

cls.what_it_does: BAM fits and provides extended friction models (beyond simple Coulomb-viscous) for servo actuators so simulated robots better match real-world behaviour. Its notable points are support for complex friction phenomena (Stribeck, load dependence, quadratic effects) and published validation in a robotics conference.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository is over two years old, has substantial community interest (619 stars), recent activity, a library of identified real servo models and an associated ICRA 2025 paper; this indicates production-ready research software used for real experiments rather than a fragile prototype.

student_project_ideas: Identify and validate a friction model for an inexpensive hobby servo by recording trajectories, fitting parameters with BAM, and comparing RL policy transfer from simulation to hardware.

Integrate a BAM actuator model into a MuJoCo simulated manipulator and evaluate how using extended friction models affects control performance and sample efficiency of a reinforcement learning algorithm.

tools.name: kunifujiwara/VoxCity
tools.desc: Python framework for integrating geospatial data, 3D city modeling, and urban simulation.

cls.summary: VoxCity generates integrated 3D voxel city models from open geospatial data and runs built-in urban environmental simulations (solar, view indices, microclimate) for any place on Earth.
cls.what_it_does: VoxCity downloads open geospatial layers (buildings, canopy height, land cover, terrain), voxelises and fuses them into a single simulation-ready 3D grid, and runs analyses such as solar irradiance, sky/green view index and microclimate exports. It is used via a Python API or command-line tool, works out-of-the-box with no accounts (optional Google Earth Engine for higher-resolution sources), and exports to many engineering formats (ENVI-met, PALM, OBJ, VOX, GeoTIFF, NetCDF). Compare microclimate impacts of increased street tree planting: use VoxCity to add tree canopy to a voxel model, run view/solar analyses and export ENVI-met inputs to run a microclimate experiment, then compare temperature or shade metrics.

tools.desc: 一款支持godot开源引擎的的mcp插件，支持常见godot引擎操作，一键配置服务。This is an MCP plugin that supports the Godot open-source engine, offering support for common Godot engine operations and one-click service configuration.

cls.summary: A Godot editor plugin that implements a Model Context Protocol (MCP) server so AI assistants can inspect and control Godot projects and editor actions.
cls.what_it_does: The plugin runs inside Godot 4.x and exposes editor operations (scene and node management, script and resource editing, filesystem access, editor control, debugging and animation tools) over an MCP HTTP endpoint so external AI clients can drive the editor. It is used by installing the addon into a Godot project and configuring an AI client (several IDE and CLI clients are supported) to talk to the server; notable for extensive editor coverage and one‑click client configuration.
cls.trl_rationale: The README and feature list are extensive and the repo has significant community interest (555 stars) and cross-platform support, but the repository is under one year old so there is not yet a long track record; this supports a beta (TRL 6) judgement.
prerequisites: basic familiarity with Godot editor and GDScript
ability to configure external AI/CLI clients or IDEs
student_project_ideas: Build an AI-assisted level design workflow where the MCP plugin plus an LLM-based client generate and place scene nodes, then evaluate scene metrics (e.g. pathfinding coverage) using Godot scripts.

Create an automated testbench that uses the MCP server to run scripted editor changes and runtime checks (scene creation, physics setup, basic gameplay tests) to demonstrate editor automation and CI-style validation.

tools.name: RylanBot/threejs-tetris-react
tools.desc: 🎮 3D Tetris game「俄罗斯方块」

tools.name: elodin-sys/elodin
tools.desc: Elodin simulation and flight software monorepo.

cls.summary: Elodin is an open-source monorepo providing drone flight software, embedded firmware, a simulator (Python SDK with JAX/ECS) and a 3D editor for visualising telemetry and simulation data.
cls.what_it_does: Elodin provides a full-stack platform for developing and running UAV flight software and accompanying simulations: embedded firmware and Orin-targeted flight software (time-series DB, sensor bridge, MEKF), a Python simulation SDK with JAX and an editor with 3D visualisation and graphing. It is used to run example simulations, connect live telemetry to the editor, and build or test flight-control algorithms with a reproducible Nix-based development environment.
cls.trl_rationale: The project is a multi-component, actively maintained monorepo (created 2024-02, ~2.7 years old) with 554 stars, documented local setup, validated development notes and example simulations; these indicate production-ready maturity though it's not an industry-wide standard.
prerequisites: Familiarity with Nix or Linux development environments
student_project_ideas: Implement and evaluate an alternative sensor fusion algorithm (e.g. UKF) using the elodin Python SDK and compare attitude estimation against the included MEKF using recorded telemetry.

Extend the simulation to model a simple payload (e.g. camera or lidar) and visualise sensor output in the Elodin editor while running hardware-in-the-loop tests with the serial-bridge and sensor-fw on a development board.

tools.name: r-spatial/mapview
tools.desc: Interactive viewing of spatial data in R

tools.name: anteloc/ldraw-nova
tools.desc: Agent tooling for generative LEGO models building, built with Astra and Opus 5.5, powered by Jev

cls.summary: ldraw-nova is an open-source agent-driven toolkit that generates buildable LEGO models as LDraw source, exports Blender-editable glTF, and provides web/VR viewers and agent traceability.
cls.what_it_does: ldraw-nova lets AI agents take a natural-language model idea and iteratively construct a LEGO model, producing LDraw source files, a Blender-editable glTF (.glb), 3D/VR views, and a record of the agent's chat and reasoning. It is used as a Dockerised web app or local CLI, and notably combines semantic search (optional TypeSafe/Jev reranking) with tooling that constrains agents to produce executable LDraw assemblies.
cls.trl_rationale: The repository is very recent (created ~55 days ago) but already functional with Docker, web app instructions and CLI tools; community interest is indicated by many stars. Age and short track record limit it to an alpha-in-use level rather than production maturity.
prerequisites: optional: TypeSafe (Jev) API key for reranking
student_project_ideas: Build an agent prompt pipeline that generates small mechanical assemblies in LDraw, export to glTF, import into Blender and run a simple kinematics demonstration (compare agent-built vs manually designed assemblies).

Evaluate the impact of semantic reranking vs full-text search on part selection quality by running the same set of model prompts with and without a TypeSafe Jev API key and analysing differences in part usage and structural correctness.

tools.name: playcanvas/react
tools.desc: Build 3D apps with React

cls.summary: A React library that wraps the PlayCanvas 3D engine to build interactive, physics-enabled WebGL/WebGPU scenes inside React applications.
cls.what_it_does: @playcanvas/react provides a React-friendly Scene API, asset loading (with Suspense), input/pointer events, physics, script components and an ECS built on the PlayCanvas engine so developers can compose real-time 3D UIs and visualisations in React. It is used as a lightweight integration layer so you don't have to wire physics, asset management and render loop manually, and it ships examples and documentation for common tasks like model viewing, motion and splatting.
cls.trl_rationale: The project wraps the mature PlayCanvas engine (battle-tested) and the README names real production users (Snap AI, GSplat). The repo is over two years old with many stars, examples and documentation, indicating production-ready maturity.
prerequisites: familiarity with PlayCanvas concepts is helpful but not required
student_project_ideas: Build an interactive model viewer for mechanical components using @playcanvas/react to load GLTF assets, add orbit controls and basic physics-based collision inspection.

Create a web-based digital-twin demo that streams timeseries data to animate actuators in a PlayCanvas scene and visualises sensor health, combining a small backend (Node.js) with @playcanvas/react front end.

tools.name: gazebosim/ros_gz
tools.desc: Integration between ROS (1 and 2) and Gazebo simulation

tools.name: datadrivenconstruction/cad2data-Revit-IFC-DWG
tools.desc: DDC Converters 2.0: RVT/RFA to GLB, IFC4 and JSONL; IFC to Excel; DWG to Excel, DXF and SVG. Offline CLI and desktop apps, n8n workflows and AI-agent instructions.

cls.summary: A suite of converters and a viewer that turn Revit (RVT/RFA), IFC and DWG files into open data (GLB/glTF/OBJ/IFC/Excel/JSONL/SQLite) for offline use and automation without needing Revit or other commercial CAD installations.
cls.what_it_does: cad2data reads proprietary BIM/CAD files (Revit RVT/RFA, IFC, DWG) and exports structured open formats such as glTF/GLB/OBJ, IFC4, Excel, JSONL and SQLite tables; it also includes a desktop Data Viewer for linked table and 3D inspection. It is used via desktop apps or command-line converters, supports batch automation and n8n workflows, and is notable for preserving native element IDs and running offline without Revit installed.
cls.trl_rationale: The project provides released installers and portable binaries for Windows, plus Linux/macOS command-line builds, has an active repo with recent commits and release pages, and ~550 stars indicating community use; these facts and production-oriented features (reports, desktop apps, CLI) support a production-ready TRL 7.
prerequisites: basic command-line skills for CLI usage
Windows for desktop apps (Linux/macOS supported for CLI builds)
student_project_ideas: Build a pipeline that converts a Revit sample model to IFC4 and glTF, then visualises quantities in a web viewer and verifies element-property traceability using the exported ElementId fields.

Compare quantity take-offs from an IFC produced by cad2data against native Revit quantities for several sample models, and produce an automated Excel/Power BI report ingesting the JSONL/SQLite outputs.

tools.name: ibisjp/ibis-office
tools.desc: The next-gen Office suite built with Rust & GPUI. Blazing-fast, memory-safe, and highly accurate editing for DOCX, XLSX, and PPTX with pixel-perfect rendering. Powered by DirectX, Metal, Vulkan & WebGPU for peak performance across Windows, macOS, Linux, and Web (Wasm).

cls.summary: ibisOffice is an open-source, GPU-accelerated office suite written in Rust that views, edits and saves DOCX, XLSX and PPTX with high visual fidelity across desktop and the web.
cls.what_it_does: ibisOffice opens, renders, edits and saves Microsoft Office file formats (Word, Excel, PowerPoint) using a single Rust codebase that draws on the GPU for performance and pixel-accurate rendering. It can run as native desktop apps (Windows, macOS, Linux) and in the browser (WebAssembly + WebGPU), and provides a CLI for headless conversion and benchmarking. It is notable for focusing on visual compatibility with Microsoft Office and GPU-based rendering for responsiveness.
cls.trl_rationale: The project provides downloadable desktop builds, a web playground, and documented CLI options which indicate an alpha/early-adopter usable project, but the repository is only ~43 days old so maturity is limited and the TRL is capped at 5 under the age rule.

tools.name: InvadingOctopus/comedot
tools.desc: Godot template and component-based framework for 2D games.

cls.summary: Comedot is an open-source component-based project template and framework for building 2D games in Godot (GDScript).
cls.what_it_does: Comedot provides a large collection of reusable 'Entity' and 'Component' nodes, example scenes, UI controls, plugins (custom dock) and assets to rapidly prototype and build 2D games in Godot. You use it by cloning the repository into a Godot project or dragging components into your scene tree, and it is notable for a very large, opinionated component library and convenience tools for rapid iteration and game jams.
cls.trl_rationale: The repository is active (last push Nov 2026), has substantial community interest (550+ stars), documented examples and a template intended for real projects, indicating production-ready maturity rather than a fragile prototype.
student_project_ideas: Create a 2D platformer prototype using Comedot's platformer template, then add a custom enemy behaviour by composing existing components and extend it with a new Component script.
Use Comedot to implement a tile-based puzzle game for a term project, integrating a simple level editor and save/load using the framework's Settings/config utilities.

tools.name: cyberbotics/webots_ros2
tools.desc: Webots ROS 2 packages

tools.name: vvhg1/clp-keycaps
tools.desc: MX compatible low profile ergonomic keycaps

cls.summary: A community-maintained collection of low-profile, MX-compatible ergonomic keycap 3D models with Fusion 360 source files and printable STLs.
cls.what_it_does: Provides parametric keycap source files for Autodesk Fusion 360 and pre-exported STL assemblies for 3D printing, letting users produce ergonomic low-profile MX keycaps and combine parts to save on print costs. Notable for offering multiple profile variants (saddle, dished, tilted) and combined assembly STLs intended for printing services.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository is >3 years old with 550 stars, active pushes (last year) and many forks and issues, Fusion 360 source and ready-to-print STLs indicate proven community use; these factors support production-ready (TRL 7) maturity.
prerequisites: basic CAD skills (Fusion 360 or other CAD)
familiarity with 3D printing workflows and slicers
student_project_ideas: Modify the Fusion 360 keycap source to design a custom ergonomic layout for a small keypad and produce a printing-ready STL assembly and bill of materials.

Compare force/comfort predictions by creating CAD variants of a keycap profile and running a simple FEM finger-contact simulation (e.g., in FreeCAD/Calculix or another FEA tool) to evaluate stress and deformation.
