tools.name: Luos-io/luos_engine
tools.desc: Open-source and real-time orchestrator for cyber-physical-systems, to easily design, test and deploy embedded applications and digital twins.

tools.name: AnkleBreaker-Studio/unity-mcp-server
tools.desc: Unity MCP Server — 268 tools for AI-assisted game development. Connect Claude, Cursor, or any MCP client to Unity Editor & Unity Hub. Scene management, GameObjects, components, builds, profiling, Shader Graph, Amplify, terrain, physics, NavMesh, animation, MPPM multiplayer & more. Free & open source by AnkleBreaker Studio.

cls.summary: A Node.js MCP (Model Context Protocol) server that connects AI assistants to Unity Editor/Hub to automate scene authoring, builds, profiling, multiplayer workflows and editor operations.
cls.what_it_does: The project exposes a large catalog of MCP tools that let AI assistants inspect and operate the Unity Editor and Unity Hub (scene creation, GameObjects/components, builds, profiling, shader/terrain/physics tools, multiplayer controls, etc.). It runs as a Node.js server that the assistant or MCP client launches and communicates with while Unity (and optional Unity packages) provide the in-editor bridge; notable features include per-editor queues, agent histories/undo, multiplayer workflow support and discoverable advanced schemas.
cls.trl_rationale: The repository is active, has many stars, demos, installation instructions and documented features indicating a beta-level project with real usage, but it is under one year old (≈265 days) so it lacks the multi-year track record or stable 1.0+ releases required for TRL 7+.
prerequisites: Unity Editor (and optional Unity packages referenced in features)
familiarity with MCP-capable assistant clients and basic Unity tooling
student_project_ideas: Create an automated level-generation workflow where an LLM agent (via the MCP server) iteratively builds and tests a playable Unity scene and records metrics (build time, memory) for comparison.

Build an experiment that uses the MCP server to coordinate multiple AI agents in a simple multiplayer scenario (MPPM) to study agent-driven playtesting and measure how automated changes affect performance and player paths.

tools.name: FluidInference/FluidUse
tools.desc: Local computer use on Apple silicon: on-device typed decisions with laya and form filling with CUA-S1-FORMS, driven through the macOS Accessibility API

cls.summary: FluidUse is an open-source Swift library for macOS that reads UI form fields via the Accessibility API and fills them using small on-device Core ML decision models (e.g. CUA-S1-FORMS and laya).
cls.what_it_does: It captures form fields and labels from running macOS apps or embedded WKWebView pages, queries compact on-device decision models for the best answer for each field, and types or clicks the result back into the real application via the Accessibility API. Notable features are its on-device Core ML model support (runs on the Apple Neural Engine), low per-decision latency, and bundled managers for specific decision models like laya and CUA-S1-FORMS.
cls.trl_rationale: The repository is active and well-documented with benchmarks and demos, demonstrating working functionality and real examples, but it was created only 57 days ago so it lacks a longer track record of production deployments required for higher TRLs.
prerequisites: macOS development and Accessibility API knowledge
student_project_ideas: Build a student tool that uses FluidUse plus a small Core ML model to automatically populate university administrative forms from a student profile, and measure accuracy and latency across different model bucket configurations.

Integrate FluidUse with a browser-based form parser to create an accessibility test harness that verifies correct field mapping and model decisions across different web apps, producing a report for V&V of form-filling automation.

tools.name: OpenGeometry-io/OpenGeometry
tools.desc: Geometry CAD Kernel for Humans and AI Agents

cls.summary: OpenGeometry is an open-source B-rep CAD kernel (Rust + WebAssembly) that builds exact solids, runs booleans and exports STEP, with a TypeScript SDK for Three.js and Node.js.
cls.what_it_does: OpenGeometry provides an exact boundary-representation geometry kernel for the web and server: primitives, extrude/sweep/revolve, boolean operations, shelling, assemblies, parametric rebuild and STEP export. It is used via a Rust core compiled to WebAssembly and a TypeScript SDK that inserts bodies directly into Three.js scenes or runs headless in Node.js. Notable points are deterministic, queryable solids (volume, area, point-inside, validity), STEP/IFC exchange support and features targeted at product configurators, mechanical parts, architecture and agent-driven 'prompt-to-CAD' workflows.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository is over one year old, actively maintained with recent pushes, documented live demos and a 3.0 release line; has several hundred stars and at least one named downstream application (Floorkit), indicating production-ready maturity but not a de-facto industry standard.
prerequisites: understanding of Rust/WASM if building native bindings or contributing
student_project_ideas: Build a parametric part configurator web app that uses OpenGeometry + Three.js to let users change dimensions and export STEP files for manufacturing.
Create an AI 'prompt-to-CAD' agent that translates structured natural-language specs into OpenGeometry API calls, then verifies geometry (volume, validity) and generates STEP for downstream tools.

tools.name: processing/processing4
tools.desc: Source code for Processing, the software sketchbook and Java-based programming language for students, artists, designers, educators, hobbyists, and creative coders. Includes the core library, and editor (PDE)

cls.summary: Processing is a Java-based programming environment and simple language (with the PDE editor) for learning code and creating interactive visuals and sketches.
cls.what_it_does: Processing provides a beginner-friendly programming language, an editor (PDE), and a core library to create interactive graphics, animations and generative art. It is used by students and creatives to prototype visual ideas quickly on desktop platforms and is notable for its long history, extensive examples and community resources.
cls.trl_rationale: Processing is a long-standing project (origin 2001) with large community adoption; the repository is actively maintained and the README and website point to decades of use and learning resources, indicating mature, widely adopted software.
prerequisites: Java toolchain for building from source (JDK, Gradle) if developing the core
student_project_ideas: Create an interactive data-visualisation sketch that reads sensor CSV data and animates time-series traces, then export frames for a report.
Build a generative-design prototype that uses Processing to visualise parametric patterns and integrates a simple optimisation loop (e.g. hill-climb) to explore design variations.

tools.name: partcad/partcad
tools.desc: Package manager for things. Start designing modular hardware! PartCAD is the standard for documenting manufacturable physical products (a.k.a. Digital Thread or TDP). It comes with a set of tools to maintain product information and to facilitate efficient and effective workflows at all product lifecycle phases, boosted by AI.

tools.name: andymai/gridfinity-layout-tool
tools.desc: A web app to plan drawer layouts with Gridfinity, a modular storage system that you 3D print. Design bins, and export baseplates as STL, STEP, or 3MF.

cls.summary: A browser-based parametric planner that lets you design Gridfinity bins and baseplates and export them as STL, STEP or 3MF for 3D printing.
cls.what_it_does: The tool provides a drag-and-drop layout planner and parametric bin designer for the Gridfinity modular storage system, plus an isometric 3D preview and export of baseplates and bins as STL/STEP/3MF. It runs in the browser (PWA), uses a WASM geometry kernel for CAD-style BREP geometry and supports cloud sync, sharing and self-hosting.
cls.trl_rationale: The project is actively developed, has a public deployed site, Docker image, tests and many stars indicating community interest, which supports a beta TRL. However the repository is under one year old so by the provided guidance it should not be rated above TRL 6.
student_project_ideas: Create a custom drawer layout for a specific product (e.g. IKEA Alex) and produce a 3MF/STL baseplate, then slice and print it to validate fit and ergonomics.
Extend the planner to batch-generate parametrised bin sizes from a CSV inventory and produce print-job bundles and a cost/filament optimisation report.

tools.name: koide3/iridescence
tools.desc: Visualization library for rapid prototyping of 3D algorithms [C++, Python]

tools.name: ailev/FPF
tools.desc: FPF (First Principles Framework) Library: methods and pattern languages for open-ended development and a shared culture of thinking and acting among people and AI agents. Use individual methods or combine them to solve difficult problems and expand capabilities.

cls.summary: FPF Library is a collection of pattern-style methods and domain frameworks designed to guide systems thinking, engineering design, decision-making and human–AI collaboration across development activities.
cls.what_it_does: The library documents reusable methods (patterns) for reasoning, investigating, designing and coordinating work so teams and AI agents can tackle difficult, open-ended problems. It is used as a reference canon: practitioners pick one or more methods to structure analysis, design or organisational practice, and the project publishes a linked website and domain frameworks for engineering and management.
cls.trl_rationale: The repository is actively maintained, documented and has significant community interest (stars and forks) and a published website, indicating a beta-level methodology resource; however the project is under one year old so there is not yet a long track record of production use required for TRL 7+.
prerequisites: basic systems thinking and engineering concepts
familiarity with engineering design or project management terminology
student_project_ideas: Use FPF methods to structure a systems engineering capstone: apply a selected pattern to define stakeholder needs, trace requirements and produce an architecture decision record, comparing outcomes with a traditional requirements process.
Combine an FPF decision-design method with a simple simulation (e.g. a Modelica or Simulink model) to show how the method improves identification of missing acceptance conditions and test cases.

tools.name: vladimirrott/mojo-dllm
tools.desc: Local inference for diffusion language models (LLaDA, Dream), written in Mojo

cls.summary: mojo-dllm is an open-source local inference implementation for diffusion language models written in Mojo that runs quantized GGUF checkpoints on CPU and optionally GPU.
cls.what_it_does: mojo-dllm loads quantized GGUF model files (LLaDA, Dream and DiffuCoder variants) and performs inference using a diffusion decoding loop implemented in Mojo, with low-level kernels (quantized matmuls and GPU kernels) also in Mojo. It is used as a standalone binary (with a small Python launcher) for benchmarking and running local diffusion LLMs on CPU or NVIDIA GPUs and is notable for its Mojo implementation and published microbenchmarks versus existing C/C++ implementations.
cls.trl_rationale: The repo (created 44 days ago) includes thorough README content, benchmarks and runnable binaries but is very new (age < 90 days) so despite evidence of functionality and interest it fits an alpha/in-use TRL rather than production-ready.
prerequisites: optional NVIDIA CUDA drivers for GPU use
familiarity with command-line build/run workflows and Python for the launcher
student_project_ideas: Benchmark performance and memory use of a diffusion LLM (eg. LLaDA-8B) on different CPU and GPU hardware using mojo-dllm, then compare results to llama.cpp and diffuse-cpp.
Extend mojo-dllm to add a small REST inference wrapper and evaluate latency and throughput for integration into a lightweight edge-serving prototype (combine with a simple Flask/FastAPI app).

tools.name: iit-DLSLab/Quadruped-PyMPC
tools.desc: A model predictive controller for quadruped robots based on the single rigid body model and written in python. Gradient-based (acados) or Sampling-based (jax)

cls.summary: Quadruped-PyMPC is a Python implementation of model predictive controllers for quadruped robots, offering both gradient-based (acados) and sampling-based (jax) variants and tested on real robots and simulators like MuJoCo.
cls.what_it_does: The project provides an MPC stack for legged robot locomotion built around a single rigid body centroidal model; users can run gradient-based solvers via acados or massively-parallel sampling-based controllers using jax on GPUs. It is notable for real-robot deployments, low-latency CPU performance and extremely fast GPU sampling rollouts, and offers options like foothold optimisation, integrators for model mismatch, and multiple sampling strategies (MPPI/CEM, OT-MPC).
cls.trl_rationale: The repository is actively maintained, has substantial community interest (540 stars), published papers and explicit real-robot deployments and integration with robot stacks (muse, unitree ROS2), which demonstrates real-world use beyond prototype stage; age (~2.7 years) and evidence of deployment justify a production-ready TRL rather than an early prototype.
student_project_ideas: Implement and compare gradient-based (acados) vs sampling-based (jax MPPI) controllers for a simulated quadruped in MuJoCo, measuring tracking performance and computation latency on CPU and GPU.

Integrate the PyMPC controller with a ROS 2-based state estimator (muse) and perform closed-loop experiments in simulation to evaluate foothold optimisation and disturbance rejection, then document transfer considerations for real-robot deployment.

tools.name: opengeos/GeoAgent
tools.desc: A multimodal AI agent for geospatial data analysis and interactive visualization

cls.summary: GeoAgent is an open-source Python agent layer that exposes geospatial library functions and live maps to large language models, with built-in safety hooks and integrations for QGIS, leafmap, STAC and multiple model providers.
cls.what_it_does: GeoAgent provides a consistent agent interface that binds LLM-capable agents to geospatial runtime objects (maps, QGIS iface, STAC catalogs) and exposes package functions as structured tools with metadata and safety/confirmation hooks. It is used by installing the Python package and selecting optional extras (e.g. QGIS, leafmap, provider clients) so downstream projects can reuse a single agent stack rather than building their own.
cls.trl_rationale: The project is active, well-starred (540 stars), and documents multiple real integrations (QGIS plugin demos, leafmap, STAC, NASA Earthdata) indicating early adoption, but the repository was created ~289 days ago (<1 year) so it lacks the longer track record and stable multi-year releases required for TRL 7+.
prerequisites: model provider API keys for some workflows (OpenAI/Anthropic/Gemini/etc.)
student_project_ideas: Build an interactive Jupyter lab exercise that uses GeoAgent + leafmap to let an LLM answer spatial queries and generate map visualisations from a STAC catalog.

Create a QGIS plugin workflow that binds GeoAgent to QgsProject and implements a safe automated layer-cleanup tool requiring confirmation before destructive actions, demonstrating agent safety hooks and provider choice.

tools.name: Kevin-Liu-01/Claude-of-Tanks
tools.desc: A World of Tanks-style armored combat simulator built directly with Three.js and Vite: 220 vehicles, 33 destructible battlefields, and 13 modes, with plate-level armor, ballistics, modules, spotting, and physics. Play in your browser on desktop or mobile. Built end-to-end by a multi-agent Claude/Codex pipeline.

cls.summary: A browser-hosted, Three.js-based World-of-Tanks-style combat simulator with many vehicles, destructible maps, and a Scene Studio for staging and capture.
cls.what_it_does: The project implements a real-time armored combat simulator playable in the browser, including ballistics, plate-level armour, vehicle modules, destructible environments, multiple game modes and a Scene Studio for deterministic captures. It's built with TypeScript, Three.js and Vite and notable for its large content set, procedural vehicle generation and a multi‑agent AI-assisted development workflow rather than being an engineering CAE tool.
cls.trl_rationale: The repository is active, well-documented and playable in-browser with many stars and recent pushes, indicating a beta-level project used by others; however it is younger than one year (111 days) so a TRL higher than 6 is not supported by the age and available evidence.
student_project_ideas: Integrate a simple telemetry export from the game's Scene Studio and build a data dashboard that visualises shot trajectories, damage heatmaps and vehicle states over time (combine with a time-series plotting library).

Modify or extend the ballistics model to add a simplified penetration vs. angle analysis and run automated trade-off experiments across a fleet to compare survivability, then present results as an interactive web report.

tools.name: DSchroer/dslcad
tools.desc: DSLCad is a programming language & interpreter for building 3D models.

tools.name: FrigadeHQ/hob
tools.desc: An easier way to use AI on your own computer. A free, open-source alternative to Claude and ChatGPT that runs open-weight models like Gemma and gpt-oss locally on Mac, Windows and Linux. Private, and works offline.

cls.summary: Hob is an open-source desktop application that runs open-weight local LLMs (e.g. Gemma, gpt-oss) on Mac, Windows and Linux to provide an offline, private AI assistant.
cls.what_it_does: Hob packages and configures frontier open-weight models to run on a user’s personal computer and provides a desktop chat/assistant interface for tasks like filling PDFs and working through documents. It aims to make local LLM usage easy by selecting compatible models and setting up the runtime, notable for being offline, privacy-focused and distributed as native installers for major desktop platforms.
cls.trl_rationale: The repository is very new (created 34 days ago) and the README is short; it appears to be an alpha/early-adopter desktop app that bundles open-weight models for local use, but there is no evidence yet of long-term production use or wide adoption, so TRL is limited to 5.
prerequisites: modern desktop OS (Windows, macOS or Linux)
sufficient CPU and/or GPU resources for local model inference (optional GPU recommended for larger models)
student_project_ideas: Create a small plugin or script that integrates Hob with a course's assignment workflow to auto-fill or annotate PDF lab reports using a specified local model.
Compare inference performance and resource usage of two open-weight models (e.g. Gemma vs gpt-oss) on student laptops by running identical tasks through Hob and measuring latency and accuracy.

tools.name: Visionary-Laboratory/visionary
tools.desc: Visionary: The World Model Carrier Built on WebGPU-Powered Gaussian Splatting Platform

cls.summary: Visionary is an open, web-native WebGPU-based viewer and platform for real-time neural rendering (Gaussian splatting, 4DGS, neural avatars) that runs inference with ONNX in the browser and integrates with three.js.
cls.what_it_does: Visionary provides a WebGPU renderer and TypeScript/three.js integration to load and render Gaussian-splatting assets, dynamic 4D/ML-driven representations and standard meshes in real time inside a browser. It runs per-frame ONNX inference so custom neural generators or post-processing networks can update Gaussians each frame, and includes an online editor and demos for quick experimentation.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository is active, backed by multiple research labs, has a paper, online demos and many stars which shows adoption; however it is under one year old so by the policy TRL is capped at 6 (beta) despite strong evidence of usability.
prerequisites: Discrete GPU recommended for good performance
student_project_ideas: Create a web demo that loads a small 3DGS asset, adds a simple ONNX-based style-transfer post-process and measures frame time and quality differences between mesh and Gaussian rendering.

Build a browser-based pipeline that converts photogrammetry output to the project's supported Gaussian/ONNX format and evaluates rendering performance and occlusion handling across scenes (compare WebGPU-enabled viewer vs a reference three.js mesh viewer).

tools.name: samdauwe/webgpu-native-examples
tools.desc: Collection of C-language examples that demonstrate basic rendering and computation in WebGPU native.

tools.name: faizfahmi77/ScanDot

cls.summary: ScanDot is an experimental Android app and companion workstation pipeline for capturing and viewing 3D point clouds using ARCore depth on supported phones and performing video photogrammetry with COLMAP on a workstation.

prerequisites: familiarity with Three.js or 3D concepts (camera, meshes, lights)
knowledge of browser tooling to run local static pages (optional)
student_project_ideas: Extend the simulator to import GIS building footprints (GeoJSON) and run block-level daylight analysis for an urban block, comparing results to the current image-based import workflow.
Integrate the viewer's sunlight results with a simple thermal model (per façade) to estimate daily solar gains for different orientations and compare heating/cooling implications across units.

tools.name: agargaro/instanced-mesh
tools.desc: Enhanced InstancedMesh with frustum culling, fast raycasting (using a BVH), sorting, visibility, LOD, skinning and more.

cls.summary: InstancedMesh2 is a drop-in enhanced instancing library for three.js that adds dynamic instance capacity, per-instance transforms, frustum culling, BVH-accelerated raycasting, LOD, skinning and per-instance uniforms to improve rendering performance and usability.
cls.what_it_does: The project provides an enhanced InstancedMesh implementation for three.js to manage large numbers of rendered instances more efficiently and ergonomically. It is used in web applications by replacing three.js's InstancedMesh to gain dynamic instance addition/removal, spatial indexing (dynamic BVH) for fast raycasting and culling, sorting/LOD and per-instance visibility/opacity/uniforms; notable features include live examples, integration examples for React/Threlte/Tres and an npm package plus CDN builds.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository is over two years old, has a substantial star count (487), active recent development, published docs and live examples and an npm package, indicating production-ready maturity and real-world use.
prerequisites: JavaScript / TypeScript and web development basics
basic understanding of 3D transforms, LOD and frustum culling
student_project_ideas: Build a web-based digital twin viewer that uses InstancedMesh2 to visualise thousands of sensor-equipped assets and implements BVH-accelerated picking for interactive inspections.

Create a performance comparison lab where students implement the same scene with three.js InstancedMesh and InstancedMesh2 and measure frame-rate, memory and raycasting latency with varying instance counts and LOD strategies.

tools.name: lone-cloud/gerbil
tools.desc: A desktop app for running Large Language Models locally.

cls.summary: Gerbil is a cross-platform desktop application for running local large language and image generation models (KoboldCpp/llama.cpp backends) without an internet connection.
cls.what_it_does: Gerbil provides a GUI (with an optional CLI mode) to download, configure and run GGUF-format models locally using KoboldCpp/llama.cpp, and includes built-in image-generation presets and integrations for browsing HuggingFace model cards. It is used as a turnkey local LLM/image-generation client (portable binaries for Windows, macOS, Linux) notable for offline capability, multi-backend GPU support (CUDA/ROCm/Vulkan/Metal) and integrations with tools like SillyTavern and OpenWebUI.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository is >1 year old with active development, listed pre-built cross-platform releases, integrations and ~482 stars and few open issues; the README documents installers, CLI mode and AUR package — evidence of production-readiness rather than an early prototype.
prerequisites: Node.js (for local development or some integrations)
Locally downloaded GGUF models (HuggingFace or other sources) and optionally GPU drivers (CUDA/ROCm/Vulkan/Metal)
student_project_ideas: Set up Gerbil with two different GGUF models and evaluate latency, memory use and output quality for common engineering prompting tasks (requirements drafting, unit conversion, code snippet generation), reporting differences between CPU and GPU runs.

Integrate Gerbil's CLI mode with a small web frontend (e.g. OpenWebUI) to build a private chat assistant for team documentation and measure its usefulness for drafting system requirements or test procedures.

tools.name: Kai-Jungsthoefel/SOMA
tools.desc: Desktop app for designing parametric 3D models in CadQuery together with the coding agent of your choice

cls.summary: SOMA is a desktop app that uses coding agents to generate and iterate parametric 3D CAD models written in CadQuery, with viewer, export and basic analysis features.
cls.what_it_does: SOMA lets a user describe a part in natural language and works with a separate CLI coding agent to produce and edit CadQuery Python scripts that build the model; the app rebuilds and visualises the model on every change and provides measurement, parameter editing, history, FEM checks and export to common formats. It is notable for combining a terminal/editor/git workspace, agent instructions/skills and an integrated viewer so non‑expert users can drive code‑based CAD via an LLM-powered agent while retaining full access to the generated script.
cls.trl_rationale: The project provides downloadable installers, includes bundled Python/CadQuery/CalculiX and has many stars and releases, indicating active use by early adopters; however the repository is only 38 days old so it lacks a longer track record and wider production adoption, limiting TRL to 5.
prerequisites: a CLI coding agent installed and logged in (Claude Code, Codex CLI, etc.)
student_project_ideas: Create a parametric enclosure for a microcontroller board using SOMA and test 3D‑printability by adding the app's overhang and wall‑thickness analysis, iterating with an agent to meet print constraints.

Integrate a SOMA model with an external FEM workflow: export a generated STEP, run a higher‑fidelity FEA in CalculiX or another solver, and use the agent to modify geometry to reduce a stress hotspot.

tools.name: ducan-ne/remove-bg
tools.desc: Remove background directly in your browser, powered by WebGPU

cls.summary: A browser app that removes image backgrounds using a Hugging Face RMBG model accelerated by WebGPU.
cls.what_it_does: This project runs a background-removal model (RMBG v1.4) entirely in the browser using Transformer.js and WebGPU to accelerate inference. Users open the web app, upload an image, and get a transparent PNG with the background removed; it is notable because it performs model inference client-side via WebGPU rather than a server API.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository is over one year old, has several hundred stars, recent activity and an issue count of 1, and uses a published Hugging Face model; this indicates a beta-level project that runs in-browser but is not a widely adopted production standard.
prerequisites: familiarity with React and browser developer tools
student_project_ideas: Build a small web tool that integrates this client-side background removal with a simple product-image uploader (React frontend + backend storage) to automate transparent PNG generation for an e-commerce mockup.
Compare CPU vs WebGPU performance by modifying the app to benchmark inference time and memory usage across browsers and devices, and produce a short report on practical limits of in-browser ML.

tools.name: apple-aiml-research/ml-facelit
tools.desc: Official repository of FaceLit: Neural 3D Relightable Faces (CVPR 2023)

tools.name: ITomPoland/portfolio-itom
tools.desc: An immersive, interactive 3D Web Developer portfolio built by Tomasz 'ITom' Szmajda using React Three Fiber, GSAP, and advanced WebGL rendering architecture.

cls.summary: An open-source interactive 3D WebGL portfolio built with React Three Fiber and Three.js that demonstrates advanced web rendering and performance techniques for high‑fidelity browser scenes.
cls.what_it_does: This repository provides a complete, production-style 3D web portfolio demonstrating scene composition, shader use, texture management and runtime performance strategies using React Three Fiber, Three.js and GSAP. It is used by running a local Vite dev server or building a production bundle and is notable for bespoke performance architectures (asynchronous shader compilation, adaptive device tiering and baked lighting) and SEO fallbacks for WebGL content.
cls.trl_rationale: The project is a well-executed, actively maintained portfolio with many stars and recent commits, but it is a single-author demo site under one year old (created 2025-12-27) and not a production component library or widely reused framework, so maturity aligns with 'alpha in use'.
prerequisites: familiarity with React and React Three Fiber (r3f)
student_project_ideas: Create a modified version of the portfolio that visualises a small engineering dataset (e.g. sensor time series or FEM result) in the 3D scene and measures performance across device tiers.

Compare rendering performance and memory usage by implementing and measuring the described optimisations (async shader compilation, baked lighting, DPR scaling) against a simple R3F scene and report results.

tools.name: AmyangXYZ/reze-studio
tools.desc: Web-based MMD animation curve editor

cls.summary: Reze Studio is a browser-native, WebGPU-powered timeline and per-channel Bézier curve editor for MMD (.vmd) animations.
cls.what_it_does: Reze Studio lets users load PMX models and VMD animation clips in the browser, edit keyframes on a professional timeline and curve editor, and export VMD files without a server. It uses WebGPU for GPU-accelerated playback and is part of a family of web tools (reze-engine / reze-design) that share files and rendering.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository is active, has a live demo site and many features implemented; created ~235 days ago so under one year which limits TRL to ~6 despite visible polish and community interest.
prerequisites: basic familiarity with MMD concepts (PMX, VMD) and animation keyframing
student_project_ideas: Compare WebGPU rendering performance by instrumenting Reze Studio playback and profiling frame-time across browsers/devices, producing a short report and optimization suggestions.

Build an export/import bridge that converts simple robot arm keyframes between VMD and a robotics-friendly format (e.g. ROS/trajectory messages) to demonstrate motion retargeting and playback on a simulator.

tools.name: SpatiaOS/Procedura
tools.desc: Agentic 3D Modeling with Procedural Control — turns a text prompt into an editable parametric program, with optional per-part materials and articulation.

cls.summary: Procedura converts a text prompt or reference image into an editable, part-based parametric 3D model (OpenSCAD source, meshes, materials and motion/URDF) using an LLM-driven pipeline.
cls.what_it_does: Procedura builds 3D models one part at a time from text or an image, emits editable parametric code (OpenSCAD), generates meshes and painted previews, and can export USD/URDF for articulated parts. It runs as an agentic pipeline inside Codex or Claude Code (via MCP) or via an API, and it is notable for producing editable, procedurally generated CAD-like outputs rather than only opaque meshes.
cls.trl_rationale: The project is active, documented, and provides install scripts and example output (MCP release), indicating early adopters and working examples, but the repo is only ~82 days old so it lacks a longer track record or stable major releases required for TRL 6+.
prerequisites: Codex or Claude Code agent session (or API credentials for model use)
Linux x86_64 recommended for the provided installer
student_project_ideas: Create a parametric robotic gripper from text prompts using Procedura, then validate its kinematics by exporting URDF and simulating pick-and-place in ROS/Gazebo or Isaac Sim.

Compare procedural outputs: feed the same design brief to Procedura and a manual OpenSCAD implementation, then measure editability and printability by exporting meshes and running simple FEA or printability checks in Blender/mesh tools.

tools.desc: Navara is a highly extensible 3D map engine. Load a wide range of GIS data, from satellite imagery and terrain to 3D city models and vector data, then freely layer your own visualizations on top.

tools.name: chengmarc/minecraft-citygen
tools.desc: Minecraft CityGen: Turn your own Minecraft builds into an entire city.

cls.summary: Minecraft CityGen is a Python tool that converts user‑marked Minecraft structures into procedurally generated city layouts inside a Minecraft world.
cls.what_it_does: The project scans regions marked inside a Minecraft Java world (using specific marker blocks) and assembles those building assets into full city maps with roads and stacked building rules. It is used by running the Python package against a world or schematic and is notable for letting authors create modular, stackable building pieces in‑world that the generator will grow into varied city blocks.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository is very new (created ~91 days ago) but shows community interest (475 stars) and runnable code with tests and install instructions; however there is no clear record of production deployments or long-term releases, so maturity aligns with an alpha used by early adopters.
prerequisites: Minecraft Java Edition world or schematic editing tools (World block markers)
student_project_ideas: Extend CityGen to export generated city layouts as georeferenced 3D tiles or glTF for use in a web viewer, demonstrating an asset pipeline from game world to web 3D.

Create rules-based modifications to the generator that encode simple urban design metrics (e.g. block density, road width) and evaluate how authoring different building pieces affects emergent city form.

tools.name: SteveDoyle2/pyNastran

tools.name: databrickslabs/ontobricks
tools.desc: Transforms Databricks Unity Catalog tables into a dynamic knowledge graph, with ontology design and reasoning exposed as tools via MCP.

cls.summary: OntoBricks is a Databricks-native application that turns Unity Catalog tables into an explorable, versioned knowledge graph and exposes ontology design and reasoning tools to LLM agents via the Model Context Protocol (MCP).
cls.what_it_does: OntoBricks automates ontology generation, mapping and materialisation of knowledge graphs from Databricks Unity Catalog tables, runs reasoning and data-quality checks, and provides visual explorers and a chat interface over the graph. It is used inside a Databricks workspace as an app (Python/Spark) and publishes domain contexts to MCP so LLM-based agents can query and act on governed, explainable business semantics.
cls.trl_rationale: The project is active, well-documented and has many stars and frequent releases (current v0.9.2), indicating beta maturity; however the repository is only ~224 days old (<1 year) so there is not yet a multi-year track record or 1.0+ stable release to justify TRL 7+.
prerequisites: Basic knowledge of ontologies (OWL/SHACL) is helpful
student_project_ideas: Build a course demo that maps a small Unity Catalog dataset (e.g. orders/customers) into an ontology with OntoBricks, then implement SPARQL queries and compare answers to equivalent SQL queries to show provenance and explainability.

Integrate OntoBricks-published MCP domain with a simple LLM agent to automate a business task (e.g. classify or enrich entities) and evaluate how ontology-driven context improves agent responses compared to raw table access.

tools.name: LTplus-AG/ifc-lite
tools.desc: Parse, view, query, edit, validate and export building models. Browser-first WebGPU viewer, TypeScript SDK, CLI, MCP server and Rust/WASM core with dual exact-arithmetic & SMlib geometry kernels.

cls.summary: IFClite is an open-source toolkit for parsing, validating, editing, visualising and exporting IFC building models with a WebGPU viewer, TypeScript SDK/CLI and a Rust/WASM geometry core.
cls.what_it_does: IFClite reads IFC files (IFC2X3, IFC4/X3, IFC5) and related formats, produces exact-arithmetic geometry via a Rust/WASM core, offers a browser-first WebGPU viewer and a headless TypeScript SDK/CLI for queries, IDS validation, edits and exports. It is notable for a modular npm package layout, a verified exact CSG geometry kernel, DuckDB-WASM SQL queries and integrations for Three.js/Babylon.js or custom renderers.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository shows a broad feature set (viewer, SDK, CLI, IDS validation), public demo site, many stars and active commits, indicating beta-level maturity; however the repo is under 1 year old so it lacks the longer track record required for TRL 7+.
prerequisites: basic WebGPU or 3D rendering knowledge for viewer integration
student_project_ideas: Build a browser-based IFC model inspector that loads IFC files with IFClite, highlights all load-bearing walls, and exports a CSV of quantities using the SDK and DuckDB-WASM for queries.

Create a small digital-twin demo that streams a parsed IFC to a Three.js or Babylon.js scene via IFClite, overlays sensor time-series data, and demonstrates verification of IDS rules for a subset of components.

cls.what_it_does: Deskworlds renders lightweight, interactive 3D 'world' scenes that react to the cursor and simple inputs, either as a macOS menu-bar wallpaper app or in any WebGL2-capable browser via a local web server. It is notable for running fully locally with Three.js, having multiple pre-built scenes, and providing an installer/uninstaller for macOS alongside a browser demo.

tools.name: kitoweeknd/RFUAV
tools.desc: This is official repository of our paper "RFUAV: A Benchmark Dataset for Unmanned Aerial Vehicle Detection and Identification".  Codes include a two stage model to achieve drone detection and classification using some FFT/STFT analytical method. The Raw data will be free to use after our paper is accept. Star us!!!!, if you think this is useful♥

cls.summary: RFUAV is an open benchmark dataset and accompanying code for RF-based detection and identification of drones using raw IQ data, spectrogram conversion and deep learning models.
cls.what_it_does: RFUAV provides raw IQ recordings from dozens of drone models, signal-processing utilities (FFT/STFT, spectrogram and waterfall generation), SNR estimation/adjustment tools and training/inference code for neural networks (e.g. ViT, ResNet) to detect and classify UAV radio emissions. It is used by replaying raw recordings on SDR hardware or converting them into images/videos for ML pipelines and is notable for being a curated RF benchmark specifically targeted at UAV detection and ID.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository accompanies an arXiv paper, contains dataset, processing and training code, has substantial community interest (466 stars) and active recent commits; however there is no clear evidence of widespread production deployment or industry adoption, so maturity is best judged as beta (TRL 6).
prerequisites: PyTorch and common ML libraries (NumPy, matplotlib)
basic signal processing / SDR concepts (IQ data, STFT/FFT)
access to SDR hardware (USRP) for replay use-cases if needed
student_project_ideas: Build and evaluate a CNN/transformer-based classifier that distinguishes between a subset of RFUAV drone models using spectrogram images, then compare accuracy when using STFT vs. FFT-derived inputs.
Integrate RFUAV raw recordings with GNU Radio to replay signals on a USRP and demonstrate end-to-end detection and classification on a low-cost edge device, measuring latency and SNR sensitivity.

tools.name: john-rocky/coreai-model-zoo
tools.desc: Downloadable models and conversion recipes for Apple's Core AI on iPhone and Mac. Chat, vision, speech and generative models with per-model validation records, Swift examples through CoreAIKit, and a downloadable Mac app.

cls.summary: A community catalog of over 90 models converted to Apple's Core AI format with conversion recipes, validation records, a sample Swift package and downloadable iPhone/Mac apps for running on-device.
cls.what_it_does: This repository collects pre-converted on-device models (chat, vision, speech and generative) for Apple's Core AI, provides conversion recipes and per-model validation, and offers Swift examples and a companion Mac/iPhone app to test models. It is used to download and integrate Core AI-compatible models into Swift/Xcode projects and to benchmark on Apple silicon, notable for its large curated catalog and documented conversion recipes.
cls.trl_rationale: The repo is active (created June 2026, last push Nov 2026), has many models, a downloadable iPhone/Mac app and documented conversion recipes which indicates a beta-level offering; however it is younger than one year so lacks the long track record required for TRL 7+.
prerequisites: iOS 27 / macOS 27 and Apple silicon knowledge
basic ML model concepts and PyTorch familiarity for conversions
student_project_ideas: Build an iOS app that uses a CoreAI Zoo chat model (via CoreAIKit) to provide a voice-controlled assistant, measuring latency and energy use on different iPhone models.

Compare on-device inference throughput and quality between a Core AI-converted model and a PyTorch / CPU alternative (e.g. ggml) using an apples-silicon benchmark and report trade-offs in a systems design assignment.

tools.name: sockmaster27/svader
tools.desc: Create GPU-rendered Svelte components

cls.summary: Svader is a Svelte library for embedding GPU fragment shaders (WebGL and WebGPU) as reusable Svelte components for interactive web visuals.
cls.what_it_does: Svader lets developers write fragment shader code and expose it as Svelte components that run on WebGL or WebGPU, providing built-in uniform values (resolution, time, scale, offset) and an API for passing parameters. It is used to create GPU-accelerated visual effects and interactive visual components in Svelte/SvelteKit web apps and includes example pages and a tests site to preview shaders live.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository has an active history (created 2024-08-18, recent push 2026-11-13), a published package with examples and a live demo site, and a sizeable star count (465), indicating production-ready use by projects; these indicators justify a production-ready TRL 7.
prerequisites: fundamental GLSL / WGSL fragment shader knowledge
student_project_ideas: Create an interactive data-visualisation dashboard in Svelte that uses Svader fragment shaders to render large-scale particle or heatmap visuals from sensor data (combine with a time-series backend like InfluxDB or a mock dataset).

Build a WebGPU shader-based UI widget library (animated buttons, backgrounds) using Svader and integrate it into a SvelteKit app to study performance differences between WebGL and WebGPU implementations.

tools.name: SMBU-PolarBear-Robotics-Team/pb2025_sentry_nav
tools.desc: Shenzhen MSU-BIT University PolarBear Team's Sentry Navigation Sim2Real Package for RoboMaster2025. QQ group: 932119307

cls.summary: A ROS 2-based navigation package for RoboMaster UGVs that provides LiDAR-based odometry, relocalisation, terrain-aware obstacle processing, Nav2 integration and a path-following controller for both simulation and real robot use.
cls.what_it_does: This repository packages a complete sim2real navigation stack built on ROS 2 and Nav2, combining LiDAR drivers, point-cloud odometry (point_lio), GICP relocalisation, terrain analysis, and a custom omni PID pursuit controller to enable autonomous navigation for RoboMaster sentry robots. It is used by launching the provided bringup and launch files in simulation or on the real robot, and is notable for handling LiDAR-to-chassis transform nuances and providing ready-to-run Docker and build instructions for Humble-based systems.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository is >1 year old, has many stars (465), active maintenance with recent pushes and a published Docker image and complete build/run instructions for both sim and real robot, and is explicitly used for RoboMaster competition robots — evidence of production-ready, project-level maturity.
prerequisites: familiarity with colcon and ROS 2 launch systems
student_project_ideas: Integrate the pb2025_sentry_nav stack with a low-cost UGV platform to run Nav2 navigation experiments, compare performance of point_lio vs simulated ground-truth odometry, and report navigation accuracy and failure modes.

Extend the terrain_analysis module to add a traversability cost layer and evaluate path planner behaviour (Nav2 global planner) in varied simulated terrains using the provided Gazebo simulation, measuring success rate and path quality.

tools.name: Esri/arcgis-maps-sdk-dotnet-samples
tools.desc: Sample code for ArcGIS Maps SDK for .NET – WPF, WinUI, .NET MAUI

tools.name: Dicklesworthstone/ntm
tools.desc: Named Tmux Manager: a Go control plane to spawn, tile, and coordinate multiple AI coding agents (Claude, Codex, Antigravity, omp, Grok) across tmux panes - graph-aware work triage, safety policy and approvals, Agent Mail coordination, checkpoints/timelines, and robot JSON + REST/SSE/WebSocket/OpenAPI surfaces.

cls.summary: NTM is a Go-based CLI that turns tmux into a local control plane to spawn, coordinate and manage multiple coding AI agents with session orchestration, approvals, checkpoints and a local API surface.
cls.what_it_does: NTM orchestrates named tmux sessions containing labelled AI agent panes and a human operator pane, providing work triage, mail-style coordination, safety policies/approvals, durable checkpoints and timelines. It exposes machine-readable automation surfaces (robot JSON, REST, SSE, WebSocket, OpenAPI) so scripts and tools can interact with running multi-agent sessions. What makes it notable is the focus on local, tmux-centred multi-agent workflows combined with safety/approval guards and an integrated API for automation.
cls.trl_rationale: The project is an actively maintained, well-documented Go CLI with many stars, a clear install script and a comprehensive README; however the repository is under one year old (≈342 days), so while it shows beta-level maturity (docs, CI-style install, integrations) it lacks the multi-year track record or wide ecosystem required for TRL 7+.
prerequisites: CLIs for any agent you plan to spawn (Claude Code, Grok Build, Codex, omp, etc.)
student_project_ideas: Build a lab exercise where students spawn a small multi-agent session to refactor a legacy code module, using NTM to triage tasks, capture checkpoints, and demonstrate approval workflows.

Integrate NTM's REST/robot API with a CI pipeline (e.g. GitHub Actions) to automatically spawn agent sessions that run static analysis and produce patch suggestions, then record checkpoints and a timeline for review.

tools.name: cselab/aphros
tools.desc: Finite volume solver for incompressible multiphase flows with surface tension. Foaming flows in complex geometries.

tools.name: CuboiLeo/SuperMimic-Reproduced
tools.desc: Independent reproduction of SuperMimic (arXiv:2610.28480) on mjlab/MuJoCo Warp, written from the paper before the official release. For the authors' code see HybridRobotics/supermimic. Kept as a record: experiment log, full BONES-SEED results, checkpoint.

cls.summary: An independent reproduction of the SuperMimic humanoid whole-body control research implementation that trains and evaluates policies on mjlab / MuJoCo Warp for the Unitree G1 using a differentiable world model and BPTT training.
cls.what_it_does: This repository re-implements the SuperMimic research pipeline (world model, differentiable forward kinematics, motion library, training loop and benchmark evaluation) from the paper so readers can reproduce experiments and use the released checkpoint. It is used to run large-scale simulated training and Appendix-F deterministic evaluations on MuJoCo Warp / mjlab, and is notable for publishing experiment logs, full benchmark results and a trained checkpoint produced before the authors' official code release.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository is a working reproduction with experiment logs, checkpoints and measured performance (runs on multi‑GPU), but it is very new (created 26 days ago) and the README states it is no longer actively developed in favour of the official implementation, so demonstrated maturity is alpha/in-use rather than production.
prerequisites: MuJoCo / mjlab (MuJoCo Warp) and GPU hardware (high‑end NVIDIA recommended)
familiarity with reinforcement learning / differentiable simulation concepts
student_project_ideas: Compare anchor-relative vs proprioception-only observation designs by re-running a subset of LAFAN1 clips and measuring yaw drift and normalized returns, producing plots and a short report on limits of proprioceptive-only control.

Use the released world-model and differentiable FK to build a short horizon model‑predictive controller (MPC) for a single Unitree G1 manoeuvre and compare tracking performance and compute cost against the learned policy.

tools.name: Sportinger/MasterSelects
tools.desc: A browser-based media editor and agent-friendly foundation for creative tools. AGPL-3.0-only.

cls.summary: MasterSelects is a browser-based multitrack video/audio/motion-graphics editor with node-based effects, 3D support and an in-app AI agent, implemented with React, TypeScript and WebGPU.
cls.what_it_does: MasterSelects provides a local, web-first timeline editor for video, audio, motion graphics and 3D with a node-graph effects workspace, live previews and an AI assistant for timeline edits. It runs in the browser using WebGPU, WebCodecs and WGSL shaders and can import/export common media and sequence formats; notable features include Gaussian splatting 3D rendering, node-based reusable effect graphs and an AI Studio for content generation.

tools.name: Desert-Ant-Labs/desert-ant-core
tools.desc: On-device AI SDKs for iOS, macOS, Android, and the web. Small, focused models that run fully offline in Swift, Kotlin, and JavaScript with Core ML, LiteRT, and WebAssembly.

cls.what_it_does: The project packages compact models (speech recognition, denoising, PII redaction, emoji suggestion, image understanding, etc.) and platform SDKs so apps can run inference fully offline on iOS, Android, desktop and the web. It is used by embedding the language- and media-focused models into mobile or web apps via provided Swift, Kotlin and JavaScript APIs and supports Core ML, LiteRT and WebAssembly runtimes. What makes it notable is the focus on privacy-preserving, on-device inference across many modalities and target platforms.
cls.trl_rationale: The repository is active and recent (created 131 days ago) with many stars, multi-platform SDKs and model weights published on Hugging Face, indicating a beta-level project; however its short public track record (younger than 1 year) limits TRL to 6.

basic understanding of machine learning inference and model formats (Core ML, TFLite, WebAssembly)
student_project_ideas: Build a mobile app that records meetings, runs on-device diarisation and PII redaction using the Voz and Redact models, then visualises speaker turns and redacted transcripts in a simple UI.

Integrate the Clear audio-enhancement model and an on-device speech recogniser to create a low-latency offline speech-to-text pipeline for a field data-collection app and evaluate transcription quality under different noise conditions.

tools.name: prs-eth/LitePT
tools.desc: [CVPR 2026 Highlight] LitePT: Lighter Yet Stronger Point Transformer

cls.summary: LitePT is an open-source, lightweight point-cloud neural network backbone for 3D semantic and instance segmentation that prioritises lower parameter count, faster runtime and reduced memory usage compared to prior point-transformer architectures.
cls.what_it_does: LitePT provides a family of point-cloud backbone models (small/medium/large) and training/config scripts for semantic and instance segmentation on datasets like ScanNet, NuScenes and Waymo. It is used by installing the Python code and CUDA/PyTorch extensions (PointROPE, optional pointops/pointgroup ops) and running provided training and inference scripts or copying the standalone litept modules into other projects. It is notable for achieving competitive or better accuracy while significantly reducing parameters, latency and GPU memory relative to prior point-transformer backbones.
cls.trl_rationale: The repository provides code, trained model checkpoints, dataset configs, and CUDA extensions and has attracted community attention (454 stars) and a CVPR 2026 paper — evidence of a maintained, usable project; however the repo is under 1 year old so it lacks the long track record and ecosystem required for TRL 7+.
prerequisites: Familiarity with point-cloud datasets and training pipelines
student_project_ideas: Fine-tune LitePT-S on a small, custom-collected indoor point-cloud dataset (e.g. using a handheld LiDAR) to build a semantic segmentation pipeline and evaluate runtime/memory trade-offs on a single GPU.

Integrate the standalone LitePT module into a simple robotics perception stack (ROS) to perform real-time semantic segmentation on LiDAR scans and measure end-to-end latency and segmentation quality versus a baseline (PointNet2 or a voxel backbone).

tools.name: tomyud1/godot-mcp
tools.desc: MCP Server and Godot Plugin for AI-assisted game development

cls.summary: A Godot editor plugin plus a local MCP (machine common protocol) server that lets MCP-compatible AI assistants read and modify Godot projects and provides a browser visualiser for project structure.
cls.what_it_does: Godot MCP connects the Godot editor to MCP-compatible AI clients (Claude, Cursor, etc.) via a local Node.js server so the AI can inspect and change scenes, scripts, project settings and run the game. It includes 69 high-level tools (scene ops, project/runtime control, script/file ops), an undo/batching system and a browser-based project visualiser that edits code live and shows script relationships.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository is actively developed, has many stars, clear install instructions and a working architecture (plugin + Node.js server + visualiser), indicating beta-level maturity, but it is under one year old so lacks the longer track record and broad production adoption required for TRL 7+.
prerequisites: An MCP‑compatible AI client (Claude, Cursor or similar)
student_project_ideas: Build a Godot game prototype where students implement a small feature (e.g. enemy AI or UI menu) by iterating with the MCP agent and measure development speed/bug rates compared to manual development.

Create an automated refactoring lab: use the visualiser and MCP tools to perform scripted refactors across a medium-sized Godot project and verify correctness with unit tests or scene validation scripts.

cls.what_it_does: Shader Skills provides 186 GLSL functions across modules plus templates, an agent-facing skill, a bundler that resolves dependencies into one self-contained shader, and a checker that lints and compiles shaders for WebGL2/Shadertoy. tools.name: BOMWiki/partmode
tools.desc: Open-source, local-first 3D parametric CAD that runs in the browser for people and permissioned typed agents, powered by OpenCascade WASM.

cls.summary: PartMode is an open-source, browser-based parametric mechanical CAD system that runs OpenCascade in WebAssembly to produce exact B-rep geometry, assemblies, drawings and STEP interchange without a desktop CAD installation.
cls.what_it_does: PartMode provides parametric part and assembly modelling in the browser with constrained sketches, editable feature history, exact B-rep evaluation (via OpenCascade WASM), drawing sheets and STEP import/export. It is used by running a local Node.js-based server and opening the web UI; it also supports permissioned typed agents and headless server workflows for automated edits and STEP exports. Notable features are its canonical document model shared between human users and typed agents and an exact kernel (OpenCascade) driving the authoritative geometry.
cls.trl_rationale: The project is feature-rich (parametrics, assemblies, drawings, STEP, agent workflows) and has a polished README and demo, indicating more than an experiment; however the repository is only ~103 days old and there is no public evidence of long-term production deployments or named enterprise users, so maturity is best judged at Beta (TRL 6).

familiarity with web development/TypeScript for contributors

Implement a simple typed-agent workflow that applies design-rule-driven parameter changes to a family of parts (e.g. bolt patterns), then automate headless STEP export and report geometry health using PartMode's inspection APIs.

cls.summary: Code-as-World is a research codebase that discovers executable, simulation-based world representations from video to enable quantitative physical reasoning.

cls.summary: HORUS is a real-time, low-latency distributed middleware for robotics written in Rust with Python and C++ bindings.
cls.what_it_does: HORUS provides a shared‑memory, lock‑free IPC and scheduler for building deterministic robotics and automation software, replacing DDS-style messaging for low-latency use cases. It is used by writing nodes in Rust (with Python and C++ APIs available), defining topics and a scheduler, and running the HORUS runtime to get sub-microsecond IPC and real-time features like watchdogs and execution classes. Notable features include sub-200 ns IPC benchmarks, zero-copy tensor support to NumPy, and built-in RT scheduling and safety hooks.
cls.trl_rationale: The project is over one year old, has substantial documentation, benchmarks, an installer, multi-language bindings (Rust/Python/C++), active commits and community interest (stars/forks), and explicit migration material from ROS2 — indicating production-ready maturity rather than a fragile prototype.

tools.name: Extelligence-ai/bagel

student_project_ideas: Implement an RLHF-style loop using AReno to fine-tune a small open LLM (e.g. Qwen small) on a domain-specific dataset and compare SFT vs RL post-training for task success metrics.

Integrate AReno with a simulated agent environment (a text-based or multimodal simulator) to collect trajectories, train a decision head (JEV), and evaluate the resulting agent's performance against scripted policies.

cls.summary: FusionCore is a C++ UKF-based sensor-fusion library and ROS 2 package for outdoor wheeled-robot localization that fuses IMU, wheel encoders, GPS and optional visual SLAM at 100 Hz and reports which sensor failed when estimates go wrong.
cls.what_it_does: FusionCore implements a 23-state Unscented Kalman Filter to fuse IMU, wheel odometry, GNSS and visual SLAM for outdoor wheeled robots and provides a ROS 2 wrapper for deployment. It is used to produce robust pose estimates at 100 Hz, includes tools to analyse rosbags for sensor/configuration issues, and emphasises explainability by naming the sensor and reason when the filter's estimate becomes unreliable.
cls.trl_rationale: The project is actively maintained, has substantial stars/forks, a ROS 2 wrapper, tests and tooling (bag_report, converters) demonstrating community interest and practical use, but the repository is only ~8 months old so by the repository-age rule it is at most TRL 6 (beta) despite clear real-robot benchmarking and performance claims.

student_project_ideas: Compare FusionCore and robot_localization on a medium-duration rosbag from a wheeled robot: run both filters side-by-side, compute relative ATE/consistency metrics, and produce a report explaining failure modes using FusionCore's bag_report tool.

tools.desc: Godot-MCP — Model Context Protocol (MCP) integration for the Godot Engine. AI tools for the Godot Editor in C#, with cloud connection to ai-game.dev. Apache-2.0.

cls.summary: Godot-MCP is a Godot editor addon that connects MCP-capable AI agents to a Godot project so the agent can read and edit scenes, scripts and resources, run C# builds and capture screenshots.
cls.what_it_does: Godot-MCP exposes editor and runtime tools over the Model Context Protocol so an external AI agent (Claude, Gemini, Copilot-style clients or any MCP client) can inspect and modify Godot projects, run dotnet builds, validate GDScript, take screenshots and optionally access runtime logs. It is distributed as a C# Godot addon plus a companion CLI that can use a local MCP server or the ai-game.dev relay, and is notable for undoable atomic edits and explicit support for Godot .NET builds and multiple Godot versions.
cls.trl_rationale: The repository is active with CI, release notes, cross-version tests and 345 stars indicating community interest, and the README describes stable releases and automated tests; however it is only ~166 days old so by the TRL rules it is assessed at beta (TRL 6) rather than higher.
student_project_ideas: Create an MCP agent that inspects a Godot project and automatically fixes common GDScript issues reported by script-validate, integrating the addon and CI to demonstrate automated code repair.
Build an agent-driven level-authoring tool that places and configures scene nodes (e.g. spawn objects in a pattern) via the Godot-MCP addon and evaluate the produced scenes with automated playtests.

tools.name: op7418/guizang-game-skill
tools.desc: 歸藏 Game Skill：让 AI 从零做出能在浏览器里玩的 3D 动作游戏，附可玩演示《雾锁山门》。Agent skill for Claude Code / Codex that builds a playable browser 3D action game with AI-generated assets (three.js, single-HTML). Playable demo included.

cls.summary: An AI 'skill' (plugin) that guides coding assistants to generate a playable browser 3D action game (three.js single-file or hosted) and includes a working demo and packaging scripts.
cls.what_it_does: This repository provides a skill for AI coding assistants (Claude Code, Codex) that implements a step-by-step workflow, helper scripts and checklists so an agent can produce, validate and package a playable three.js 3D action game for the browser. It bundles examples, packaging scripts (single-file HTML and hosted variants) and a documented process for asset generation, testing and optimisation; notable is a complete playable demo produced using the skill.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository is very new (created 6 days ago) but includes a complete playable demo and reusable scripts; however the skill has only one documented full project run and lacks a track record, so maturity is at early 'in use' alpha level (TRL 5).
prerequisites: access to AI asset tools (optional: Tripo, image-generation tools, Suno for audio)
student_project_ideas: Use the skill to direct an AI assistant to generate a compact single-file three.js demo that visualises a simple engineering concept (e.g. collision response or kinematic chains) and compare agent-generated vs hand-crafted implementations.

Extend the packaging scripts to produce a small offline digital-twin-like scene (single HTML) that streams telemetry from a mock device and visualises it in three.js, integrating the skill's asset pipeline with a time-series emulator.

tools.name: isuzu-shiranui/UnityMCP
tools.desc: Drive the Unity Editor from an AI agent or the terminal. The Editor serves MCP itself over HTTP, so there is no second process to run, and the isuzu-unity-cli command needs no Node or .NET runtime.

cls.summary: UnityMCP exposes the Unity Editor over an HTTP-based MCP endpoint so AI agents and a native CLI can call editor automation and authoring tools.
cls.what_it_does: UnityMCP runs a streamable HTTP MCP server inside the Unity Editor so external AI agents or a native command-line client can invoke editor-side C# tools and automation. It provides a simple attribute-based API for defining tools, a native isuzu-unity-cli for calling those tools, and integrations verified with various agent clients (Claude, Codex, Cursor, Gemini, VS Code). The notable parts are that the Editor is the single process serving MCP and JSON schemas are generated from C# signatures so tools are callable without extra middleware.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository is mature and actively maintained (created 2025-04-16, 580 days old), has substantial community interest (344 stars), documentation and CLI releases, and working client integrations listed in the README — evidence of production-ready tooling rather than a fragile prototype.
prerequisites: basic C# and Unity Editor scripting
Git for package installation (or use VPM)
student_project_ideas: Create an automated Unity scene-authoring pipeline where an LLM-driven agent uses UnityMCP to place, configure and test prefabs, then run the test-suite and collect results.
Build a CLI workflow that triggers batch builds and automated play-mode tests via UnityMCP and visualises test coverage and build metrics in a simple dashboard (combine with a CI system).

tools.name: nathanshankar/terminal_rviz
tools.desc: Terminal RViz is a high-performance 3D visualizer for ROS 2 that runs entirely within a terminal environment. Built using FTXUI and a custom Braille-based software renderer, it provides a feature-rich alternative to standard RViz for headless systems, remote SSH sessions, or resource-constrained environments.

cls.summary: Terminal RViz (TViz) is a terminal-based 3D visualiser for ROS 2 that displays robot models, TF trees, point clouds, maps and other common ROS topics entirely inside a text terminal for headless or SSH workflows.
cls.what_it_does: TViz provides a feature-rich alternative to conventional GUI RViz by rendering 3D scenes using a Braille-character software renderer and an FTXUI-based terminal UI; it subscribes to standard ROS 2 topics (TF, PointCloud2, LaserScan, Odometry, Images, MarkerArray, Nav2/MoveIt messages) and exposes plugins for interaction (Nav2 dashboard, Teleop, Motion Planning). It is used by building the package into a ROS 2 workspace (colcon) and running the terminal_rviz node, and notable for supporting headless/SSH usage, an extensible plugin system, and optional OpenCL-accelerated point-cloud rendering.
cls.trl_rationale: The project is actively developed and shows many features, examples and integration with ROS 2 stacks (Nav2, MoveIt) and has substantial community interest (hundreds of stars), but the repository is only ~8 months old so it lacks the longer track record and releases required for TRL 7+.
student_project_ideas: Integrate TViz with a ROS 2 mobile robot stack (Nav2) over SSH and evaluate teleoperation latency and usability compared with GUI RViz, documenting setup and performance trade-offs.
Extend TViz by writing a plugin that visualises custom sensor data (e.g. simulated multi-beam sonar) and compare CPU vs OpenCL-accelerated rendering performance on point-cloud-heavy scenes.

tools.name: CerealAxis/Nola-Translator
tools.desc: Lightweight, powerful real-time speech translation with multilingual support and a multilingual UI.

cls.summary: Nola Translator is a Windows-focused real-time speech recognition and translation application that produces live bilingual captions and can run local or cloud models.
cls.what_it_does: Nola captures audio (microphone, system or selected device), performs speech recognition and translation in real time, and displays floating or browser-overlay captions with configurable styles. It supports running local ASR and MT models or calling cloud providers, can install models from Hugging Face, and offers history export (TXT/SRT/WebVTT) and a browser extension for bilingual captions.
cls.trl_rationale: The repository is very new (50 days) but shows active development, many stars and a downloadable Windows installer; however it lacks a long track record or versioned stable releases, so it aligns with early alpha/alpha-in-use (TRL 5).
prerequisites: GPU or sufficient CPU for local models if using local inference
Optional API keys for cloud providers (OpenAI-compatible, Anthropic, etc.)
student_project_ideas: Integrate Nola Translator with recorded lab videos to produce bilingual captions and evaluate caption accuracy across noisy laboratory audio using an open ASR model (compare local vs cloud recognition).
Extend the browser extension to add timestamped lecture notes export (WebVTT/SRT) and build a short pipeline that aligns captions with slide timestamps for searchable lecture archives.

tools.name: zju3dv/habitat-gs
tools.desc: [ECCV 2026] Habitat-GS: A High-Fidelity Navigation Simulator with Dynamic Gaussian Splatting

cls.summary: Habitat-GS is an extension of Habitat-Sim that renders photo‑realistic Gaussian Splatting scenes and supports embodied navigation and dynamic Gaussian avatars for training and evaluation of navigation agents.
cls.what_it_does: Habitat-GS replaces the rendering backbone of Habitat-Sim with 3D Gaussian Splatting to produce high‑fidelity RGB and depth sensors in photo‑realistic scenes, and adds support for dynamic Gaussian avatars. It is used as a simulator for embodied navigation tasks (ObjectNav, Multi‑ObjectNav, VLN) and integrates with Habitat‑Lab for agent training and benchmark evaluation; notable features are efficient Gaussian Splatting rendering and tools to convert GS scenes into navigable Habitat datasets (including a web NavMesh editor).
cls.trl_rationale: The project is feature-rich, has a dataset, benchmark, ECCV 2026 paper acceptance and hundreds of stars which indicate active development and early adoption, but the repository is only ~7 months old (created 2026-04-14) so it lacks the long track record and broad production deployments required for TRL 7+.
prerequisites: CUDA toolkit and compatible NVIDIA drivers
student_project_ideas: Use Habitat-GS and Habitat-Lab to train a PointNav agent in Gaussian Splatting scenes and compare learning curves and visual sensor fidelity against a mesh-based Habitat-Sim environment.
Integrate a dynamic Gaussian avatar (from GaussianAvatar) into a multi-agent navigation scenario and evaluate collision avoidance behaviours and perception robustness under photorealistic rendering.

tools.name: wellingfeng/UltraGameStudio
tools.desc: UltraGameStudio - AI coding agent for game development: engine workflows, gameplay code, and asset generation.

cls.summary: UltraGameStudio is an open-source AI coding agent tailored to game development that generates gameplay code and a broad range of game assets and integrates with popular engines.
cls.what_it_does: UltraGameStudio provides a chat-based AI agent primed with game-engine concepts to produce gameplay code, engine integration, shaders, build scripts and to generate assets (images, 3D models, sprites, audio, rigging, video) within the same workflow. It routes requests to multiple model providers (including local runtimes) and supplies engine-specific expert roles and modes to apply generated assets directly into Unity, Unreal, Godot or web projects.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository is active (created ~171 days ago) with substantial stars and recent pushes, documentation and many features described in the README, but it is younger than one year so lacks the multi-year production track record required for TRL 7+.
prerequisites: knowledge of model API keys or local LLM runtimes for advanced features
student_project_ideas: Build an automated workflow that asks UltraGameStudio to generate a Unity gameplay script and corresponding 3D prop, then integrate and test the asset in a small Unity scene to measure iteration speed versus manual creation.

Compare asset quality and pipeline time by routing the same sprite-sheet and audio-generation prompts through two different model backends (one local runtime like llama.cpp or Ollama and one cloud provider) and report on integration effort and performance.

tools.name: RUSEGAL/ruseon-core
tools.desc: Edge video infrastructure in Go for CCTV — RTSP ingest, HLS/WebRTC streaming, fMP4 recording, timeshift and AI metadata pipelines.

cls.summary: RUSEON Core is an open-source Go media server for high-density RTSP ingestion, zero-transcoding transmuxing to HLS/WebRTC/fMP4, and low-overhead gRPC frame streams for edge CCTV and AI pipelines.
cls.what_it_does: RUSEON ingests H.264/H.265 camera streams over RTSP and repackages them in memory into low-latency outputs (WebRTC/WHEP, HLS fMP4/TS, WebSockets) while recording continuous fragmented MP4 archives and providing gRPC streams for real-time AI inference. It focuses on zero-transcoding transmuxing, lock-free ring-buffer distribution to isolate slow consumers, page-cache-aware disk writes for 24/7 recording, and embedded metadata/state storage for robust edge deployments.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository is active, has substantial stars and recent commits and a detailed README describing production-focused features (prometheus, crash recovery, POSIX optimisations), indicating beta-level maturity; however the repo is only ~111 days old so it lacks a long public track-record required for TRL 7+.
prerequisites: knowledge of Go and building Go projects
basic streaming media concepts (RTSP, HLS, WebRTC) and containerisation
student_project_ideas: Build an edge analytics prototype that uses RUSEON to ingest RTSP streams from multiple IP cameras, forward frames via its gRPC StreamFrames API to a YOLO/PyTorch inference service, and display detections in a browser over WebRTC.

Compare storage and CPU efficiency by deploying a small NVR: record the same camera feeds with RUSEON (zero-transcoding fMP4) and an FFmpeg-based recorder, then measure CPU, memory, and disk I/O under increasing camera counts.

tools.name: thushan/olla
tools.desc: High-performance lightweight proxy and load balancer for LLM infrastructure. Intelligent routing, automatic failover and unified model discovery across local and remote inference backends.

cls.summary: Olla is an open-source, high-performance proxy and load balancer that routes and manages requests across self-hosted LLM inference backends to provide failover, model discovery and unified routing.
cls.what_it_does: Olla solves the problem of reliably routing LLM API requests across heterogeneous local and remote inference endpoints by providing priority-based routing, automatic failover, sticky sessions and a unified model catalogue. It runs as a single CLI/configured binary (two proxy engines: Sherpa for simplicity or Olla for high performance), and is notable for low overhead, streaming-first design, many native backend integrations and an embedded read-only admin dashboard.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository is over one year old with active development, 338 stars, many documented integrations and a feature-rich README and docs; README claims production-ready features (rate limiting, circuit breakers, dashboard). This indicates a production-ready tool rather than an experimental prototype.
prerequisites: familiarity with LLM inference endpoints and APIs (OpenAI/Anthropic formats)
knowledge of HTTP proxies, reverse-proxy concepts and basic networking
experience editing YAML/JSON config files and running CLI services
student_project_ideas: Deploy Olla in a small cluster of self-hosted LLM backends (e.g. llama.cpp instances) and evaluate failover, latency and throughput under synthetic load, comparing Sherpa and Olla proxy engines.

Integrate Olla with a simple chatbot web front-end and a vector-search embeddings pipeline to demonstrate sticky sessions, routing of embedding vs. chat requests, and measure end-to-end latency and resource utilisation.

tools.name: GainSec/AutoProber
tools.desc: Hardware hacker’s flying probe automation stack for agent-driven   target discovery, microscope mapping, safety-monitored CNC motion, probe review, and   controlled pin probing.

cls.summary: AutoProber is a Python-based automation stack for controlling a flying-probe CNC setup that discovers PCB targets with a microscope, maps/annotates them, and performs safety-monitored electrical probing under agent or script control.
cls.what_it_does: AutoProber orchestrates hardware (GRBL CNC, USB microscope, oscilloscope, optional network power) to find and map targets on a board, stitch microscope frames into an annotated map, queue probe targets for human approval, and execute bounded probe motions while continuously monitoring an independent safety channel. It is used via a web dashboard, Python scripts, or an agent and is notable for its explicit safety model for live machine control and an end-to-end stack including CAD, docs and device drivers.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository contains a complete Python package, dashboard, CAD and detailed docs and hardware BOM, and has attracted an active community (stars/forks), but it was created ~7 months ago with no long-term release history; maturity looks like a beta-ready project rather than widely adopted production.
prerequisites: familiarity with CNC/GRBL and SCPI oscilloscope control
basic electronics and safe lab practice
student_project_ideas: Build a student-grade flying-probe demonstrator by following the repo BOM, integrate a simple test PCB, and implement an automated pin-test script that records current/voltage traces using the Siglent SCPI interface.

Extend the mapping pipeline to add automated OCR of silkscreen and a feature that cross-references annotated pads with a BOM/Netlist to flag probable net names prior to probing (combine with simple PCB CAD or Gerber parser).
