It is used as an interactive demo (live page included) and as a reference implementation showing how to translate GLSL/WebGL patterns to WGSL/WebGPU resource bindings, pipelines and command encoding.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository provides a working live demo, complete implementation, and active commits but is younger than one year (303 days) so lacks a longer track record; evidence supports a beta-level, usable project rather than a long-term production library.
prerequisites: basic GPU shader concepts and WGSL
student_project_ideas: Extend the heightfield solver to add wind forcing and compare energy spectra over time, then visualise results in the browser and export time-series for offline analysis.
Integrate a simple particle-based debris model (CPU or GPU) to study buoyancy interactions between the sphere and floating objects and measure added damping under different wave conditions.

tools.name: mll-lab-nu/embodied-first-exam
tools.desc: The first exam for code agents in the physical world: frozen robot tasks from many benchmark suites, each answered with a program and verified in a separate sandbox. Runs on Harbor.

cls.summary: A benchmark framework that evaluates code-based agents by running them on frozen robot tasks from multiple suites and verifying their behaviour in sandboxed environments.
cls.what_it_does: Embodied First Exam provides a collection of robotic benchmark suites where an agent writes code, runs it on a robot in a frozen scene, and is automatically verified in an isolated sandbox. It orchestrates many existing simulators and task suites (e.g. dexterous hands, humanoids, manipulation, sim-to-real tests) and runs them using container images on a Harbor-based runner.
cls.trl_rationale: The repository was created 60 days ago (too new for high TRL) but already shows active development, a public release announcement, many stars and multiple bundled benchmark suites; this indicates early alpha/adopted-by-early-users rather than production-proven status.
prerequisites: Docker Engine with Compose v2 / BuildKit (or rootless podman)
NVIDIA driver + NVIDIA Container Toolkit for GPU tasks
Python (3.12-3.14 pulled via uv) and familiarity with environment variables / API keys
student_project_ideas: Integrate a small LLM-based code agent to solve a single RoboPaint or DexHandExam task and compare solution robustness across two simulator backends (e.g. MuJoCo vs Isaac Sim).
Extend one suite with an automated safety-checker: run an agent in the Embodied Safety Exam tasks and implement a monitor that rejects unsafe actions and logs justification for verification.

tools.name: ros-controls/mujoco_ros2_control
tools.desc: ROS2 control package for Mujoco simulation physics simulator, including plugins for various sensors, RGB-D cameras, and lidar.

cls.summary: A ros2_control SystemInterface and supporting packages that let you run ROS 2 controllers against the MuJoCo physics simulator for robot simulation and sensor plugins.
cls.what_it_does: This project wraps the MuJoCo simulator as a ros2_control system interface so standard ROS 2 controllers (controller_manager, controllers, interfaces) can operate on robots simulated in MuJoCo (MJCF or URDF-generated). It includes conversion utilities, sensor and camera/lidar plugins, demo launch files, and integration tests to help develop and validate control software in simulation before deploying to hardware.
cls.trl_rationale: The repository contains a full SystemInterface plugin, demo packages, integration tests, CI Dockerfiles and multi-distribution support indicating a beta-level project. The repo age is under one year (≈362 days), which per the TRL guidance limits the rating to at most 6 despite good community interest (stars/forks) and test assets.
student_project_ideas: Implement a PID and impedance controller using ros2_control with a MuJoCo-simulated manipulator and compare closed-loop performance to a Gazebo simulation.
Extend mujoco_ros2_control by adding a custom sensor plugin (e.g. IMU noise model) and run experiments to evaluate perception-driven control for a mobile robot in simulation.

tools.name: SpikeCalls/FlyDrones
tools.desc: A fruit fly connectome as a drone pilot. Camera -> fly eyes -> spiking brain -> descending neurons -> drone. Live 3D demo in your browser.

cls.summary: FlyDrones runs a spiking-neural connectome of a fruit fly to generate high-level flight stick commands for simulated or real drones, with a live browser demo and Python tools.
cls.what_it_does: FlyDrones maps camera input (or webcam hand gestures) to optic-flow signals, runs a spiking neural-network based on the MaleCNS connectome (or a smaller MiniFly proxy), and decodes descending neurons into high-level drone control commands; it can run a full loop in-browser or from a Python CLI and includes adapters for multiple drone platforms. It is notable for loading a biological connectome as the control policy and for providing an immediate live 3D demo and simulator so the brain/drone loop can be explored without hardware.
cls.trl_rationale: The repository is very new (created 63 days ago) but contains working browser demos, a Python CLI, and example pipelines, indicating early alpha/alpha-in-use maturity; authors note hardware adapters exist but are not flight-tested, so it lacks demonstrated real-world deployment required for TRL 7+.
prerequisites: familiarity with neural simulation / spiking networks is helpful
student_project_ideas: Integrate FlyDrones with a physical Crazyflie (props off / safety governor enabled) to evaluate how different read-out mappings from descending neurons affect closed-loop stability and document safe commissioning steps.

Replace the MiniFly proxy with a small spiking-network variant tuned by students and compare performance in the browser simulator vs using the full MaleCNS connectome to study trade-offs between biological fidelity and control latency.

tools.name: EGSECDA/vocaloid-style-mv-pipeline
tools.desc: Production pipeline and Claude Code skill for Vocaloid-style hand-drawn (手書き) lyric music videos: deterministic Canvas2D/WebGL2 animation engine, JIZURA lyric motion, AI illustration, Blender toon 3D, headless rendering to 16:9 and 9:16.

cls.summary: A production-ready open-source pipeline and Claude Code skill that generates deterministic, hand-drawn style lyric music videos by rendering every frame with Canvas2D/WebGL2 and headless browser + ffmpeg encoding.
cls.what_it_does: This project automates creation of Vocaloid-style 手書き lyric music videos: it analyses audio and lyrics, generates or imports art assets (including AI illustration and Blender toon-3D shots), composes frames deterministically in Canvas2D with WebGL2 post-processing, and uses headless browsers + ffmpeg to render and encode master and vertical cuts. It is notable for being deterministic (frame = pure function of time), having an agent-oriented skill/workflow for Claude Code, and providing a reusable project template and scene library for fast re-rendering and parallel frame production.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository is 44 days old which limits TRL under the provided rules; README demonstrates a working, performance-measured pipeline and a showcase render (≈4 minutes on RTX 3080) so it appears beyond proof-of-concept and used by the author, consistent with TRL 5 (alpha in use).
prerequisites: Blender (for toon-3D shots) and a GPU for reasonable performance
student_project_ideas: Create a short (30–60s) lyric MV from an original or public-domain song using the template, extend a scene parameter to add a custom particle effect, and measure render-parallelism by running worker instances in the cloud.

Integrate the pipeline's Blender toon-3D shot scripts with an existing character rig and produce a vertical 9:16 re-layout, documenting the process of native re-typesetting of lyrics and asset consistency between aspect ratios.

tools.name: Suvitruf/box3d-unity
tools.desc: Box3d Physics bindings for Unity

cls.summary: box3d-unity is a Unity C# wrapper that exposes the native Box3D real-time 3D physics engine for use inside Unity projects, with features for determinism, multithreading, joints, various shapes, replay, and GPU particle water.
cls.what_it_does: It provides Unity bindings for the native Box3D physics engine so you can run high-performance, deterministic 3D physics simulations inside Unity without unsafe pointers or per-frame allocations. It is used by adding the package to a Unity project to create worlds, bodies, shapes, joints and to use features like replay/determinism, debug visualisation and GPU particle water; notable points are its zero-allocation APIs, built-in multithreaded scheduler and a replay system for bit-exact simulation playback.
cls.trl_rationale: The wrapper is actively developed, documented and demonstrably usable (live WebGL demo, performance benchmarks, many features) but the repository and upstream Box3D are both young (<1 year for this wrapper, Box3D noted as v0.1) and the README explicitly calls the status 'early (0.8.x)' and warns of breaking changes, so it best fits an alpha-in-use level.
prerequisites: Unity (familiarity with Unity packages and scenes)
basic physics / dynamics concepts (rigid bodies, joints, collision)
student_project_ideas: Build a Unity scene comparing Box3D and Unity PhysX on a crowd/debris stress test and analyse performance and determinism across worker counts.
Create a kinematic character controller using Box3D's character mover and integrate simple networked rollback logic using the replay/determinism features to demonstrate lockstep netcode concepts.

tools.name: HaD0Yun/Doyunha-Gopeak
tools.desc: GoPeak — The most comprehensive MCP server for Godot Engine. 95+ tools: scene management, GDScript LSP, DAP debugger, screenshot capture, input injection, ClassDB introspection, CC0 asset library. npx gopeak

cls.summary: GoPeak is an MCP server that lets AI assistants interact with Godot 4 projects to edit scenes and scripts, run the game, inspect runtime state, and debug via LSP/DAP.
cls.what_it_does: GoPeak provides an MCP (Model Context Protocol) server for Godot 4 that exposes project control, scene and script editing, resource workflows, LSP diagnostics and DAP debugging, and runtime inspection (screenshots, input injection) to MCP-compatible clients. It is used alongside a Godot project and an MCP client (e.g. Claude Desktop, Cursor) and notable for exposing a gated capability surface (profiles and Godot plugins) to keep powerful runtime operations explicit and secure.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository is active with many stars (273), published releases (v2.4.1) and recent commits, indicating more than an experimental prototype but it is under one year old so a conservative beta TRL 6 is appropriate; README documents installation and integration but long-term production use is not yet demonstrated.
prerequisites: basic TypeScript/Node tooling familiarity and Bun runtime
understanding of MCP clients or LSP/DAP concepts
student_project_ideas: Build an AI-assisted level-creation tool: connect an MCP-capable client to GoPeak and implement prompts that generate scenes and GDScript, then run the game and automatically capture screenshots for evaluation.

Create an automated runtime testbench that uses GoPeak's runtime addon to inject input and capture logs/screenshots, then compare outputs against expected behaviours to exercise V&V of a simple game subsystem.

tools.name: realstrawhat/csakura
tools.desc: A sakura tree with falling petals for your terminal

cls.summary: csakura is a small open-source C program that draws a procedurally grown cherry‑blossom tree with falling petals in a terminal using ncurses.
cls.what_it_does: csakura generates an animated ASCII/Unicode sakura tree with falling petals and interactive keyboard controls; it runs in a terminal and adapts to different terminal sizes. It is used as a visual/entertainment screensaver-style program written in C99 with ncurses and offers multiple tree forms, palettes and a detail mode.
cls.trl_rationale: The project is packaged in popular Linux (AUR) and Homebrew taps and has many stars, an active repo and recent pushes, indicating usable beta maturity; however the repository is only ~4 months old (128 days) so it lacks the longer track record needed for TRL 7+. (README is detailed and installable.)

tools.name: vstorm-co/agenticos
tools.desc: Open-source, self-hosted AI agent platform for your company's AI teammates. Build, run and govern agents on your own servers and models: shared chat, RAG, skills, a real browser, 4,700+ MCP servers, budgets, approvals and an audit trail. An alternative to ChatGPT Enterprise and Grok Bot. Apache-2.0, built on Pydantic AI.

cls.summary: Agenticos is an open-source, self-hosted platform for building, running and governing multi-agent AI teammates on your own infrastructure.
cls.what_it_does: Agenticos provides a server and UI to create, run and manage agent workflows (shared chat, RAG, skills, browser automation, approvals, budgets and audit trails) using local or cloud models. It is used as an on‑premises alternative to hosted agent services and emphasises governance, integrations (chat channels, model providers) and MCP-compatible agent servers. Notable features include a desktop chat with code agents, a real in-chat browser, apps/visuals publishing and audit/approval controls.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository is new (created ~109 days ago) but shows active development (recent pushes), release notes and documentation; community interest (271 stars) suggests early adopters and a beta-stage project rather than long-term production maturity.
prerequisites: basic Python and web service familiarity
knowledge of Docker/containers or server deployment
access to LLM provider credentials if using hosted models
student_project_ideas: Deploy Agenticos locally and create a governance policy that logs and audits automated report generation for a simulated engineering team, then evaluate the policy's effectiveness under different agent behaviours.

Build a small agent that ingests engineering documents (RAG) and produces concise verification checklists, integrating Agenticos with a local LLM and a simple CI pipeline to demonstrate automated V&V support.

tools.name: heyixuan2/bambu-studio-ai
tools.desc: Bambu Lab AI (Bambu Studio AI): agent skill for 3D printing on Bambu Lab. Finds models on MakerWorld & Printables, generates or designs them in CAD, checks printability, hands them to Bambu Studio and reads printer/AMS status. For Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Gemini CLI and any SKILL.md agent. Featured in 我的拓竹 Skill 大赏.

cls.summary: A Python ‘skill’ that lets LLM agents find or generate 3D models, perform parametric CAD and printability checks, and monitor Bambu Lab printers while integrating with Bambu Studio.
cls.what_it_does: This project provides agent-accessible tools to search model repositories, generate or parametric-model parts, run seven automated printability checks and repair meshes, prepare multi-colour AMS projects, and read-only monitor Bambu Lab printer/AMS status. It is used as a skill loaded into existing agents (Claude, Codex, Gemini CLI and others) and hands validated models to Bambu Studio for slicing and printing while keeping the user in control.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository is active, well-documented, and featured by Bambu Lab with many stars, showing real interest and functionality; however it is under one year old (created 2026-03-02), so while it appears beta-ready with working integrations, it lacks a long track record required for TRL 7+.
prerequisites: Bambu Studio (for slicing/viewing and printer profiles)
An LLM agent runtime that supports SKILL.md (e.g. Claude/Codex/Gemini CLI)
Blender (optional, for preview rendering) and network access to the Bambu printer
student_project_ideas: Implement an automated parameter sweep that uses the skill to generate variations of a bracket (different clearances/infill) and evaluates printability scores to recommend the best trade-off between strength and print time.

Integrate the skill with a classroom Bambu printer to build a lab exercise where students submit parametric CAD specs via an agent, verify printability automatically, then monitor and log real print telemetry for a V&V report.

tools.name: mkturkcan/valdrada
tools.desc: Valdrada is a real-time digital twin of New York City built from public data.

cls.summary: Valdrada is a city-scale, real-time digital twin of New York City that streams binary tiles, simulates lane-level traffic and pedestrians, and provides sensor outputs and a Python API for synthetic-data generation and closed-loop scenario simulation.
cls.what_it_does: Valdrada compiles public municipal records into a streamed city-scale digital twin with a WebGL2/three.js client, a simulation server (CARLA-like TCP API) and sensors (RGB, segmentation, depth, instance labels) for synthetic data and scenario testing. It is used by running the server and client or the Python API to control actors, step simulations and export recorded takes to OpenUSD for offline rendering in Blender or Unreal Engine 5.
cls.trl_rationale: The repository is new (created 54 days ago) but already provides binary releases, a Python client API and example workflows; this indicates alpha use by early adopters rather than long-term production maturity, so TRL ~5.
prerequisites: Unreal Engine 5 for optional UE client
Large binary tile/model dataset (download or compile)
student_project_ideas: Use the Python API to script a closed-loop traffic scenario in a defined Manhattan tile, collect RGB and segmentation sensor data, and train/test a computer-vision model for pedestrian detection.
Export a short recorded take to OpenUSD and render it in Blender Cycles to compare photorealism and rendering performance between the WebGL3 client and offline UE5/Blender pipelines.

tools.name: spkane/freecad-addon-robust-mcp-server
tools.desc: The FreeCAD Robust MCP server and MCP Bridge Workbench/Addon

cls.summary: A server and FreeCAD workbench that implements the Model Context Protocol (MCP) to let AI assistants control and inspect FreeCAD models, macros and workbenches for AI-assisted CAD workflows.
cls.what_it_does: This project provides a robust MCP server plus a FreeCAD bridge/workbench so MCP‑compatible AI tools (GPT, Claude and others) can connect to FreeCAD to create, modify, debug and export 3D models and macros. It supports multiple connection modes (XML‑RPC, JSON‑RPC sockets, embedded), GUI and headless operation, and exposes 150+ MCP tools for common CAD operations, making it notable for enabling programmatic/agent control of a parametric CAD system.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository is active, has many stars (270), documented install options (pip, Docker, releases) and ongoing development, indicating a beta-level project; age is ~318 days (<1 year) so TRL is limited to 6 despite strong activity.
student_project_ideas: Build an automated FreeCAD macro generator where an LLM (via the MCP server) creates PartDesign features from high-level design requirements and validate the generated geometry against simple dimensional constraints.

Integrate the MCP server with a CI pipeline (Docker) to run headless regression tests on parametric models: have the agent apply changes and compare exported STEP geometry or key measurements to baseline models.

tools.name: doesthings/FreeFCC
tools.desc: Free FCC unlock for DJI smart controllers. No server, no license, no tracking. Download: freefcc.pages.dev

cls.summary: An open-source Android app that sends DUML command frames to DJI smart controllers to switch radio regulatory mode to FCC and perform related device queries and actions.
cls.what_it_does: FreeFCC runs on DJI smart controllers (RC2, RC Pro 2, RC Plus) and sends plain-JSON DUML frames to switch the radio from CE to FCC, send 4G activation frames (where supported), toggle LEDs and query device info. It is delivered as an Android APK and uses editable JSON profile files containing the raw DUML command frames, and the project intentionally operates locally without a server.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository is functional, provides APK releases and installation guides and has visible user interest (270 stars), but it is only 128 days old so lacks a long track record; age and short history limit the TRL to a beta-level assessment.
prerequisites: familiarity with DJI controllers and DUML command concepts
awareness of radio regulations for your jurisdiction
student_project_ideas: Analyse and visualise the DUML JSON profiles to build a safe simulator that shows what parameter writes would occur on supported controllers without sending radio commands to hardware.

Create a compliance-checking tool that parses FreeFCC profiles and flags command frames that would change regulated radio parameters, combined with a small report generator about legal risks (no hardware required).

tools.name: kytmanov/synto
tools.desc: More than just Karpathy’s LLM Wiki, 100% local with Ollama. Drop Markdown notes → AI extracts concepts → your Obsidian wiki auto-links and grows. Zero sharing. Your notes stay yours.

cls.summary: Synto is a local-first tool that reads your Markdown notes, extracts concepts with local LLMs, and compiles them into an interlinked Obsidian-compatible wiki stored on your machine.
cls.what_it_does: Synto ingests files you drop into a vault, uses a small local model to extract concepts and a larger local model to compile coherent, cross-linked wiki articles, and exports an agent-ready pack without sending data off your machine. It is used as a CLI-driven pipeline (init, add, compile, export) and notable for running entirely locally (Ollama/local models), incremental compilation, draft/verify/publish workflow and per-concept confidence and feedback loops.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository is active, well-documented, has hundreds of stars and recent commits, and describes a complete CLI pipeline; however it is under one year old (created 2026-05-15), so while it appears beta-quality it lacks the longer track record and broad production adoption required for TRL 7+.
prerequisites: familiarity with Obsidian or Markdown vault workflows
local LLM runtime (Ollama or compatible local models) installed
basic CLI and Python environment knowledge
student_project_ideas: Build a course-specific vault where lecture notes and papers are added and Synto automatically compiles a navigable wiki for a subject (e.g. 'control systems'), then evaluate how well the synthesized articles match lecturer-provided summaries.

Create an agent-ready export from a student's lab notebook using Synto and connect it to a local QA agent (e.g. Claude or a file-aware assistant) to answer lab-method questions while tracing answers to source notes.

tools.name: julianmb/q38rocm
tools.desc: Qwen 3.8 27B ROCmFP4 on AMD Strix Halo (Ryzen AI Max+ 395). Up to 36 tok/s via MTP Speculation, TurboQuant & Mesa RADV Wave64.

cls.summary: A specialised deployment and performance package for running the Qwen 3.8 27B GGUF model on AMD Strix Halo APUs using a custom ROCmFP4 quantization and a patched llama.cpp engine to achieve much higher token throughput.
cls.what_it_does: This repository packages a custom-quantized Qwen 3.8 27B model (ROCmFP4) and instructions to run it on AMD Strix Halo (Ryzen AI Max+ 395) APUs, combining block quantization, MTP speculative decoding and TurboQuant KV cache compression to increase generation throughput. It is used by building a pinned fork of the llama.cpp/ROCmFPX engine and running the GGUF weights on ROCm/Vulkan backends; notable points are the hardware-aligned block quant layout and explicit support for Mesa RADV Wave64 cooperative matrix features.
cls.trl_rationale: The project is an active, well-documented deployment with published model weights and a pinned engine fork, showing beta-level maturity and practical performance claims; the repository is 104 days old so it cannot be assumed to have long-term production track record required for TRL7+. Documentation and examples are present, but broader production adoption is not demonstrated in the README excerpt.
prerequisites: Linux with ROCm-compatible stack and Vulkan/RADV support
AMD Strix Halo (Ryzen AI Max+ 395) or similar RDNA 3.5 hardware for best results
Ability to build the pinned llama.cpp / ROCmFPX engine fork
Familiarity with GGUF model weights and local LLM runtimes
student_project_ideas: Benchmark and compare token throughput and memory use for Qwen-3.8-27B using ROCmFP4 vs a standard Q4 quantization on a university AMD GPU, producing reproducible plots and a short report explaining the bandwidth/quant trade-offs.

Extend the pinned llama.cpp ROCmFPX engine to add an automated profiler that measures memory bandwidth, KV cache size and speculative acceptance rates across contexts, and evaluate how TurboQuant parameters affect latency and memory on long-context prompts.

tools.name: 0xMassi/stik_app
tools.desc: Instant thought capture for macOS. One shortcut, post-it appears, type, close.

cls.summary: Stik is a macOS-focused quick-capture note app that summons a floating post‑it with a global shortcut and saves notes as plain Markdown files while providing on‑device AI features.
cls.what_it_does: Stik provides an instant, keyboard-first note capture UI for macOS that saves notes as plain Markdown in a local folder and supports features like voice dictation (on‑device via Apple's frameworks), semantic search, encryption, folder organisation and optional sync via iCloud/Dropbox/Syncthing. It is used as a lightweight, privacy‑focused alternative to heavier note apps and is notable for on‑device NLP, a minimal workflow (one shortcut to capture), and a cross‑technology stack (React frontend with a Rust backend and Tauri packaging).
cls.trl_rationale: Repository is active, has signed releases, Homebrew cask, and visible user-facing features (voice, sync, encryption) indicating a beta/usable app; however the project was created ~285 days ago (under 1 year) so by the provided TRL rules it should be capped at TRL 6.
student_project_ideas: Build a small utility that exports Stik's markdown notes into a searchable dataset and implement a simple NLP analysis (topic modelling or keyword extraction) using Python to visualise capture habits over time.
Create an integration that pushes Stik notes into an Obsidian vault or a Git repo and implement automated tagging or folder suggestions using the on‑device embeddings as a classifier.

tools.name: 122-syf-wcy/PhysicsOS
tools.desc: PhysicsOS 是一个面向初高中物理学习的公益可视化智能体，通过 AI 理解题目并结合物理引擎，将抽象物理过程转化为可交互、可观察、可计算、可验证的真实物理场景。

cls.summary: PhysicsOS is an open-source web platform that turns physics problems into interactive, engine-driven simulations and visualisations for K–12 learning, combining an AI assistant with a browser-based physics engine and a reusable PhysicsCanvas.
cls.what_it_does: PhysicsOS parses physics questions with an AI assistant, runs domain-specific physics engines (mechanics, optics, electromagnetism, circuits, waves, etc.) to compute results and verifications, and renders interactive, reproducible experiments in a React/TypeScript web client. It is notable for integrating question→engine→verifier→visual observation into a single PhysicsScene/PhysicsCanvas workflow and shipping many ready-made experiment templates and automated checks.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository is 89 days old and marked public beta with a production Harness integration, many implemented experiment templates and automated tests; this indicates alpha-in-use maturity but not long-term production track record required for TRL 6+.
student_project_ideas: Extend a PhysicsOS domain engine (e.g. add frictional models to the collision or incline-plane engine) and validate behaviour against analytic solutions and instrumented experiments in the PhysicsCanvas.

Create an automated assessment module that converts textbook optics problems into reproducible PhysicsScene setups and scores student-modified experiments using the built-in verifier, then analyse common error patterns.

tools.name: SahilK-027/Elemental-Serenity
tools.desc: A 3D diorama built with Three.js and custom WebGL shaders. Explore season transitions (spring, summer, autumn, winter), realtime weather (rain, snow, wind and particle effects. 🌱🍁❄️⛈️

cls.summary: Elemental Serenity is an open-source interactive 3D nature diorama built with Three.js and custom GLSL shaders that shows season transitions and realtime weather effects in the browser.
cls.what_it_does: The project renders a stylised 3D diorama in the browser with components for seasons (spring, summer, autumn, winter) and realtime particle-based weather (rain, snow, wind, fireflies) using Three.js and custom WebGL shaders. It's used by running the Vite-based dev server or building a production bundle, and it is notable for its modular shader materials, particle systems and debug controls (lil-gui, three-perf) for tuning performance and visuals.
cls.trl_rationale: The repository is a well-constructed, actively maintained project with many stars, dependencies, and clear build/development instructions, indicating beta-level maturity; however it is under one year old (created 2025-12-28) so lacks the longer track record required for TRL 7+.
prerequisites: JavaScript and basic WebGL / Three.js knowledge
student_project_ideas: Extend the diorama to visualise live sensor or IoT data (temperature, rain sensors) by mapping real-time values to weather/season parameters and hosting the scene as a dashboard front-end.
Replace or augment particle systems with physics-driven effects (e.g. wind fields influencing leaves) and measure performance trade-offs using three-perf, documenting optimisations across devices.

tools.name: VinRobotics/vla.cpp
tools.desc: A unified inference runtime for VLA models.

cls.summary: vla.cpp is a C++ inference runtime that runs vision–language–action (VLA) policies from single-file GGUF models and can drive robots on CPUs, GPUs and embedded accelerators without Python or PyTorch.
cls.what_it_does: vla.cpp loads self-contained GGUF VLA policy models and performs on-device inference to convert images and text prompts into action sequences; it provides CLI, server and library components and supports multiple backends (CPU, CUDA, Metal, ROCm, SYCL, Hexagon, OpenVINO). It is notable for packaging VLA policies as GGUF artifacts, broad hardware support including embedded targets (Jetson/Hexagon/Apple Silicon), and examples showing how to integrate with a robot client.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository is 175 days old and shows prebuilt releases, multi-backend docs, benchmarks and a real-robot client fork (rollout guide), indicating versioned builds and early production usage; age (<1 year) and limited long-term track record cap it at TRL 6 (beta).
prerequisites: basic Linux/macOS cross-compilation and dependency management (ZeroMQ, protobuf)
understanding of GGUF/ggml model artifacts and inference concepts
student_project_ideas: Use vla.cpp and a small robot arm (e.g. URDF-simulated or real SO-101) to implement and evaluate a simple pick-and-place pipeline where a VLA policy infers actions from camera frames and compare closed-loop behaviour between CPU and Jetson inference.

Measure and profile latency and memory use of a chosen GGUF VLA model (SmolVLA or π0) across CPU, CUDA and an embedded backend (Jetson or Hexagon) and propose optimisations (quantization, batching or model selection).

tools.name: Junkz3/wrench-board
tools.desc: A senior microsoldering technician, available to every repair shop from the seasoned pro to the apprentice. Powered by Claude Opus 5

cls.summary: Wrench Board is an agent-driven diagnostic workbench that ingests schematics and boardview files to guide board-level electronics repair with vision, parsers and deterministic diagnostic tools.
cls.what_it_does: The project builds a per-device knowledge pack from schematics and boardview files, runs an Anthropic/Claude-based diagnostic agent that highlights pins/traces, simulates failures and requests microscope images, and provides a replayable repair session. It is used as a technician-facing web workbench (FastAPI backend + JS boardview) and is notable for many boardview parsers, a deterministic sanitizer pipeline to avoid invented refdes, and integration of vision-driven schematic compilation.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository is 210 days old (under 1 year) so by policy TRL is at most 6; nevertheless the project has a live demo site, a 3‑minute demo video, ~2.6k fast tests, many boardview parsers, and a hackathon prize which indicate a beta-level, actively-developed system.
prerequisites: basic electronics and PCB repair knowledge
web development basics (HTML/CSS/JS) for front-end components
student_project_ideas: Build a lab exercise where students feed a known faulty boardview and schematic into Wrench Board, record the agent's diagnostic steps, and compare its recommended measurement points with instructor-provided fault localisation (combine with bench multimeter/oscilloscope measurements).

Extend or add a parser for an additional boardview file format (or KiCad export variant) and validate correctness by running the project's schematic ingestion and ensuring the ElectricalGraph nets and refdes lookups match ground-truth on a small dataset.

tools.name: britcruise9/GrowBot
tools.desc: What's the simplest possible AI robot that learns everything from scratch?

cls.summary: GrowBot is an open-source embodied AI robot project that runs a learning agent on a phone attached to a small printed robot body with Pico firmware, servos and simple sensors.
cls.what_it_does: GrowBot provides firmware, hardware designs, browser app code and trained walk policies so you can build a small mobile robot that learns from experience and runs its brain on a phone or a local computer. It is used by following the build guide (STLs, BOM, Pico installer), pairing the phone app to the body, or running your own agent via the agent harness; notable features include lightweight firmware for the Pico, browser-based visual memory, and published training exports/policies.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository is active, contains firmware, hardware STL files, build guides, and training exports and has community interest (266 stars); however it is only 166 days old (<1 year) so lacks the multi-year production track record required for TRL 7+, placing it at Beta (6).
prerequisites: basic reinforcement learning or agent concepts
student_project_ideas: Modify the GrowBot agent to implement a new reward function (e.g. energy-efficient gait) and compare learning speed using local simulation (PyBullet or MuJoCo) versus on-device trials.
Adapt the hardware and firmware to add a distance sensor and implement obstacle avoidance behaviour, integrating sensor data into the phone-based visual memory and retraining the policy.

tools.name: img2threejs/plugin-interior
tools.desc: Production interior authoring and interactive Three.js delivery plugin for img2.

cls.summary: A Blender+agent-driven workflow that reconstructs an editable interior from a single image and exports an interactive Three.js viewer and GLB assets.
cls.what_it_does: The plugin coordinates an agent-driven authoring pipeline that inspects a single-room reference image, builds an editable Blender scene (geometry, materials, bakes), and produces a hosted Three.js viewer plus portable GLB exports. It is used by installing the skill into the img2 harness and running the agent workflow; notable points are scene-specific manual authoring (not a one-shot image-to-mesh model) and built-in viewer/export integration for web delivery.
cls.trl_rationale: The repository is very new (30 days) but already publishes an npm package, provides a live demo and has community interest (stars), indicating early adopters and packaged releases rather than a paper prototype; its short age prevents a higher TRL.
prerequisites: Node.js / npm (for the published package and viewer tooling)
img2 harness and an agent LLM runtime (Claude/Codex/OpenCode) to run the skill
student_project_ideas: Take a single photograph of a classroom or lab, use the plugin to produce an editable Blender scene and a Three.js viewer, then evaluate geometric and material fidelity against hand-measured dimensions.
Combine the exported GLB from img2-interior with a basic web UI to add runtime controls (material variants, camera presets) and measure performance/load trade-offs for web deployment.

tools.name: bagidea/bagidea-office
tools.desc: A living AI-agent office on your desktop wallpaper — Claude Code agents that walk, work, delegate, learn & hold meetings. Per-agent swappable models (Claude/GLM/DeepSeek/Qwen/Kimi/OpenAI/Gemini/Groq/Ollama…), workflows, plugins, voice & Telegram/Discord/LINE. Open source.

cls.summary: BagIdea Office is an open-source desktop 'office' of cooperating AI agents (2.5D pixel-art) that run as your wallpaper and coordinate work, propose plugins, hold meetings and connect to multiple LLM providers.
cls.what_it_does: It orchestrates multiple AI agents (Claude Code and other LLM backends) as persistent personas that collaborate, learn from work, propose and install plugins, and expose workflows via a desktop wallpaper 'office' UI. You install it locally (one-shot installer or npm) and connect API keys or local model backends; notable features are per-agent swappable models, multi-provider support (Claude, OpenAI, Gemini, Ollama, local LMs), voice/Telegram/Discord/LINE integrations and an extendable plugins/tools hub.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository shows active development, versioned releases (v1.10.0 listed), 265 stars and community contributions but the project is only ~5–6 months old (created 2026-06-03), so while feature-complete and used by early users it lacks the multi-year track record needed for TRL 7+.
prerequisites: Claude Code account (required for core functionality)
API keys for optional providers (OpenAI, Google Gemini) or local model runtimes
student_project_ideas: Build a custom agent plugin that monitors a project Git repository and drafts release notes automatically, integrating the BagIdea Office plugin API and GitHub webhooks.

Create a multi-agent coordination scenario where agents monitor simulated IoT sensor feeds (from a separate simulator) and autonomously propose maintenance tasks, then evaluate the quality of proposals against ground-truth faults.

tools.name: hasso5703/alzeo
tools.desc: Alzeo is an open-source installer that turns an NVIDIA DGX Spark, or any GB10 machine (ASUS, Dell, HP, Lenovo, MSI, GIGABYTE, Acer), into a private AI server in one command: measured model lanes, OpenAI and Anthropic APIs, and a local cockpit.

cls.summary: Alzeo is an open-source installer and runtime that turns an NVIDIA DGX Spark or GB10-class machine into a one-command private AI server that hosts, measures and serves large local models with a browser cockpit and OpenAI-/Anthropic-compatible APIs.
cls.what_it_does: Alzeo automates installing, configuring and running multiple large language and multimodal models (text, image, video) on a single high-memory GPU server, providing lane-based memory management, measured performance, pinned artifacts and a web 'cockpit' for switching lanes and serving models via compatible APIs. It is notable for handling unified-memory pools on GB10/DGX Spark hardware, providing measured throughput benchmarks, and shipping clients and compatibility layers so local models act like OpenAI/Anthropic endpoints.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository is active, well documented, provides a one-line installer, measured benchmarks, and citations from other community projects, indicating a beta-quality project; however it is younger than one year and fairly new (created ~95 days ago), so evidence of longer-term production adoption is limited.
prerequisites: experience with Python and container/system services
familiarity with model serving concepts (vLLM, quantisation, unified memory)
student_project_ideas: Benchmark and compare throughput and latency of a Qwen3.8 lane versus a quantised FP4 lane on a multi-GPU server using Alzeo, reporting effects of context length and concurrent streams.
Adapt Alzeo's cockpit to add an automated V&V test suite that runs smoke tests and correctness checks on model lanes after installation and reports results to a simple dashboard.

tools.name: Quchaosheng/workbench-mobile-home-robot
tools.desc: Evidence-first runtime for a wheeled mobile household robot with bounded actions, replayable events, and fail-closed verification.

cls.summary: Workbench is an evidence-first runtime for wheeled household robots that records append-only event traces, verifies action outcomes from sensor evidence, and provides a replayable dashboard and ROS 2 execution integration.
cls.what_it_does: Workbench provides an offline Python 'evidence plane' that stores append-only task events, runs a verifier that returns confirmed/refuted/insufficient_evidence, and produces deterministic replay artifacts and a read-only dashboard. It pairs with an execution plane implemented for ROS 2 (BehaviorTree.CPP, SocketCAN, MoveIt 2) so planners and device code produce verifiable task events rather than optimistic success claims. The project is notable for its focus on bounded semantic actions, fail-closed policies, strict JSON/Pydantic schemas and an integrity-checked SQLite event store for deterministic replay and assurance traces.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository shows a named v2.0.0 release, active development, CI-style checks and non-trivial feature set (verifier, event store, ROS 2 runtime), but the project is under one year old so demonstrable maturity is limited to a beta-level (TRL 6).
prerequisites: basic knowledge of Gazebo / MoveIt2 and BehaviorTree.CPP
student_project_ideas: Integrate a simple differential-drive robot model in Gazebo with Workbench to record runs, then implement a new verifier rule that uses simulated IMU and odometry to detect slip and validate against the event store.

Extend the evidence plane to export a concise maintenance summary to OmniLink AI and build a student dashboard that correlates verified task outcomes with CAN bus diagnostics for a predictive-maintenance demo.

tools.name: corosolto/client
tools.desc: FPS satírico de navegador: 5 facções brasileiras caricatas, 44 personagens, 5 mapas e 26 armas — rounds e Capture the Flag contra bots, direto na aba, sem instalar nada. Three.js + vanilla JS, zero build. Gerado em par com agentes de IA (Claude, Kimi, Codex/GPT, GLM) — AI generated & AI friendly.

cls.summary: CORO SOLTO is an AI-assisted, browser-based first-person shooter built with Three.js and vanilla JavaScript that runs without a build step and includes singleplayer bots and beta multiplayer.
cls.what_it_does: The repository implements a complete FPS playable in a web browser using vendored Three.js and ES modules, with GLB assets for characters, weapons and props and optional multiplayer handled by client-side networking code. It is notable for a zero-build approach, a large in-repo asset pipeline (gltf-transform, meshoptimizer) and an explicit workflow of being generated and developed in collaboration with AI agents.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository is 123 days old (younger than 1 year) and shows a large codebase, many assets, a public alpha/beta multiplayer and automated pipelines, but it is still an alpha release (versioned as 2.1.0-alpha) without evidence of long-term production adoption, so TRL 5 is appropriate.
student_project_ideas: Extend the game's telemetry to collect anonymised performance metrics and visualise them in a dashboard (use Playwright to run automated sessions and a small Postgres instance to store results).
Modify or replace a weapon's GLB and animation pipeline using gltf-transform and meshoptimizer, then measure FPS and memory differences across browsers as an optimisation lab.

tools.name: raullenchai/esp32-thinks
tools.desc: A multi-model Muse: personal AI voice assistant on ESP32 - wake word or knob, any OpenAI-compatible brain (STT/chat/TTS mix-and-match), streaming replies, out of the box. Built on muse-gadget-sdk.

cls.summary: esp32-thinks is an open-source firmware and supporting agent that turns an ESP32-S3 gadget into a configurable, multi-model voice assistant using OpenAI-compatible speech, chat and TTS backends.
cls.what_it_does: It implements wake-word detection, recording, STT, chat and streaming TTS on an ESP32-S3 device and lets you point each task at any OpenAI-compatible endpoint (or a local agent shipped with the repo). The project is used by applying a patch to the muse-gadget-sdk, building with ESP-IDF, and optionally running the bundled 'openmuse' agent (Docker/Node) to provide local context, memory and proxying.
cls.trl_rationale: The repository demonstrates a working firmware and deployment scripts with many features documented and presets, and has attracted community interest (stars). However it is only 36 days old so lacks the longer track record, stable releases and broad production citations required for higher TRL levels.
prerequisites: familiarity with flashing ESP32 devices and serial consoles
OpenAI-compatible API keys or local model endpoints
basic Docker/Node knowledge for optional agent
student_project_ideas: Build a lab exercise where students modify the wake-word sensitivity and measure false-accept/false-reject rates across noisy conditions, logging results to a Raspberry Pi running the openmuse agent for analysis.

Create a capstone project that integrates a local open-source STT model and an offline TTS to evaluate latency and bandwidth trade-offs for on-device versus cloud processing, and present a cost/latency comparison.

tools.name: kiyoakii/is-gpt-nerfed
tools.desc: Shrinkflation detector for Codex

cls.summary: A macOS menu-bar app and plugin that checks whether Codex actually used the model you requested by probing sessions and fingerprinting short outputs.
cls.what_it_does: IsGPTNerfed reads Codex session records and periodically forks sessions to probe the active model by requesting short random-number answers; it then compares those answers to a calibrated fingerprint bank to detect silent downgrades, swaps, or other discrepancies. It runs locally on macOS (no data uploaded), reports verdicts in the menu bar, notifications and session messages, and provides a CLI for on-demand probes and reports.
cls.trl_rationale: The project is young (created ~63 days ago) but provides a packaged macOS app, install scripts and releases, showing early adoption; repository age limits TRL to <=5 despite apparent working tooling and documentation.
prerequisites: Codex desktop app or CLI with plugin hooks (tested on 0.154)
student_project_ideas: Build an automated test harness that uses IsGPTNerfed to monitor model fidelity over time for an LLM-enabled feature and report drift statistics to a dashboard (combine with Grafana/Prometheus).
Extend the fingerprint bank by collecting probes for additional models and evaluate classifier accuracy across different prompt types and context-window sizes.

tools.name: Meterless/Meterless
tools.desc: Turn your Win, Mac or DGX Spark into an AI hotspot. Nightshift races hundreds of attempts overnight and keeps what passes. Plus the open context engines it runs on.

cls.summary: Nightshift is an open-source system for running and evaluating many local LLM attempts (agents) overnight on a personal or server GPU, keeping verified outputs and provenance.
cls.what_it_does: Nightshift orchestrates many concurrent runs of local models across different personas and temperatures, judges and validates results with automated checks, clusters and synthesises successful approaches, and produces files plus receipts for each verified output. It is used by installing the runtime on Windows, macOS or DGX Spark (or trying the browser demo) and pointing OpenAI-compatible agents at the local provider; notable features include multi-model racing, automated tournament/judge modes, and persistence of successful Methods/Skills for subsequent runs.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository is ~4 months old and actively developed with a polished README, platform installers and a browser demo, and has community interest (stars/forks), indicating beta-level maturity; however it is younger than one year so lacks longer track record required for TRL 7+.
prerequisites: familiarity with local LLMs and model runtimes
access to GPU hardware for heavy workloads (or use demo)
student_project_ideas: Create a lab exercise that deploys Nightshift on a single GPU VM to run a set of automated validation checks on generated engineering reports (e.g. spec templates), measure pass rates across model variants and analyse results.

Build a student capstone that integrates Nightshift with a simple sensor-data pipeline: generate synthetic maintenance reports from time-series inputs, run overnight methods to optimise report quality, and compare automated judge outcomes to human reviewers.

tools.name: engeldlgado/toshllm
tools.desc: Run large language models locally on Intel Macs with AMD GPUs - native macOS app with Metal acceleration

cls.summary: ToshLLM is a native macOS app that runs open large language models locally on Intel Macs with AMD GPUs using Metal-accelerated builds of llama.cpp.
cls.what_it_does: ToshLLM packages a patched, AMD-accelerated build of llama.cpp into a SwiftUI macOS application so users can run and serve LLMs locally (no cloud or per-token costs). It provides a chat UI, local OpenAI-compatible API, model manager, bundled engines (llama.cpp, whisper.cpp, stable-diffusion.cpp), agent tool integrations (SymPy, NumPy/SciPy), multi-GPU/eGPU support and benchmarking targeted at Intel Macs with discrete AMD GPUs.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository is active with releases, many stars and documented features, but it is only ~5 months old (156 days) so it lacks a long track record; evidence (releases, detailed README, benchmarks) supports a beta-level maturity (TRL 6).
prerequisites: Intel Mac with discrete AMD GPU (or eGPU)
macOS development/user privileges to install native app
familiarity with local LLM concepts and model files
student_project_ideas: Build a small RAG (retrieval-augmented generation) pipeline that uses ToshLLM's local OpenAI-compatible API to serve embeddings and answer queries over a course dataset.

Integrate ToshLLM into a lab notebook workflow: create an assistant that inspects code/data files, runs the bundled SymPy/NumPy tools to verify calculations, and logs results for reproducible engineering analysis.

tools.name: yucchiy/UniCli
tools.desc: A CLI tool to control Unity Editor - enabling both humans and AI agents to run compilations, tests, and editor commands from the terminal.

cls.summary: UniCli is a command-line tool and Unity package that lets users and AI agents run Unity Editor commands (compile, build, tests, inspect GameObjects, eval C#) from the terminal.
cls.what_it_does: UniCli provides a standalone CLI plus a Unity package to discover projects, execute 80+ editor commands, run arbitrary C# via an eval command, and produce structured JSON output for automation and AI agents. It is used to automate builds, tests and editor tasks from scripts, CI or agent workflows and is notable for built-in agent integrations (Claude Code plugin, Agent Skills) and cross-platform NativeAOT binaries.
cls.trl_rationale: The repo is active and 279 days old, provides cross-platform NativeAOT binaries, releases and a substantial feature set (80+ commands) and has community interest (258 stars), which indicates beta-level maturity; however it is younger than one year so lacks the longer track record required for TRL 7+.
prerequisites: familiarity with command-line tools and basic C# scripting
a Unity project (Assets folder) for most commands
student_project_ideas: Create a CI pipeline that uses UniCli to automatically run EditMode and PlayMode tests and produce JSON test reports, then visualise pass/fail trends with a small dashboard.

Integrate UniCli with an LLM-based coding agent (using the Claude Code plugin or an open agent framework) to autonomously locate failing tests in a Unity project, propose code changes, and run the tests again.

tools.name: mitcad/Mitcad
tools.desc: Free, open-source parametric 3D CAD for Windows, Linux and macOS. Imports many formats with their feature timeline.

cls.summary: MitCad is an open-source, cross-platform parametric 3D CAD application with a feature history, many import/export formats and a path-traced renderer.
cls.what_it_does: MitCad provides parametric modelling with sketches, constraints, a feature timeline and parameter expressions so models rebuild when dimensions or features change. It is a desktop application (Windows, Linux, macOS) with broad CAD format import/export, assemblies with movable joints, and an integrated renderer and 3D‑printing export workflow. Notable points are its support for many commercial and open file formats and a history‑based parametric model implemented with Rust and C++/OCCT.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository is very new (created 44 days ago) which limits maturity; README and releases show working installers for major OSes and many implemented features (sketches, timeline, assemblies, file formats), indicating early adopters rather than long production use, so TRL ~5 (alpha in use).
prerequisites: CMake, Ninja and vcpkg build systems
student_project_ideas: Create a parametric bracket in MitCad, export to STEP, then run a simple FEA workflow (e.g. in Calculix or another open solver) to compare stress results as parameters change.

Extend or script an import pipeline: write a converter that imports DWG blocks into MitCad and assembles them into a parametric assembly with joints to demonstrate interoperability and assembly kinematics.

tools.name: kevtoe/worldview
tools.desc: Real-time tactical intelligence platform — CesiumJS globe with flights, satellites, earthquakes, traffic & CCTV overlays

cls.summary: Worldview is an open-source real-time situational-awareness dashboard that overlays flights, satellites, vessels, earthquakes, traffic and CCTV on an interactive Cesium 3D globe.
cls.what_it_does: Worldview aggregates multiple live public data sources (ADS‑B, TLE/SGP4, AIS, USGS, OSM, CCTV feeds) and renders them as high-density tactical overlays on a CesiumJS globe for monitoring and exploration. It is used as a web application (React + Resium) with a small Node/Express backend for proxying and caching, and notable features include high-performance primitive rendering for tens of thousands of entities, dead‑reckoning at 60 fps, and GLSL post-processing (CRT / night‑vision / thermal) for tactical display modes.
cls.trl_rationale: The project is a well-implemented full-stack app with many documented features, an active repo with substantial star count and recent commits, which supports a beta-level TRL. However the repository is only ~9 months old, so it lacks a long track record of production deployments that would justify TRL 7+.
prerequisites: basic understanding of CesiumJS and geospatial concepts
API keys for optional tile and data providers (Cesium ion / Google Maps / AISStream etc.)
student_project_ideas: Extend Worldview to add a simple alerts subsystem that flags and logs entities violating geofenced zones (combine with a student-built UI and a test dataset).

Build a course assignment to integrate an additional live data source (e.g. local traffic camera or public transit API) and implement a new Cesium primitive layer with dead‑reckoning and filtering controls.

tools.name: AnkleBreaker-Studio/unity-mcp-plugin
tools.desc: Unity MCP Plugin (UPM) — Editor bridge for AI-assisted game development. Enables Claude, Cursor & MCP-compatible AI to control Unity Editor with 268 tools: scenes, GameObjects, components, builds, profiling, Shader Graph, Amplify Shader Editor, terrain, physics, NavMesh & more. Free & open source.

cls.summary: A Unity Editor package that exposes a Model-Context-Protocol (MCP) bridge so AI agents and compatible MCP clients can inspect and control Unity projects and editor workflows.
cls.what_it_does: The plugin provides an in-Editor UPM package implementing routes and tooling that let MCP-compatible AI agents (Claude, Cursor, etc.) drive scene editing, GameObjects, components, builds, profiling, shaders, terrain, physics and more. It is installed into the Unity Editor, pairs with a companion Node MCP server, and offers a dashboard, history, scheduling and multi-agent fairness for automated or assisted development tasks.
cls.trl_rationale: The repository is active, has widespread usage (257 stars), detailed documentation and a companion server, and demonstrates install and workflow examples; however it is under one year old (created 2026-02-25), so maturity aligns with a beta-stage tool rather than long-term production incumbents.
prerequisites: Node.js and the AnkleBreaker MCP server
basic understanding of MCP/agent workflows and Unity Editor scripting
student_project_ideas: Build an AI-assisted level authoring demo where an MCP agent modifies scene objects and materials to satisfy a design brief, recording iteration history and undo behavior.

Integrate the Unity MCP plugin with a reinforcement-learning agent (or Claude-like agent) to automate simple gameplay tuning tasks (adjust physics or spawn parameters) and measure iteration speedups versus manual tuning.

alternatives_to: Editor scripting / custom Unity Editor tools

tools.name: forgent3d/forgent3d-desktop
tools.desc: Maintenance mode: bug fixes only, no new features. Lighter option, no app to install: forgent3d/forgent3d-skills

cls.summary: Forgent3D is a desktop app that lets AI coding agents and humans generate, build, preview and iterate parametric 3D CAD models locally, producing real geometry (STEP/STL/3MF) from code-driven parts and assemblies.
cls.what_it_does: Forgent3D packages a local CAD runtime, Three.js viewer and agent bridge so models defined by part.py / asm.xml and params.json can be built, previewed and measured without a separate CAD environment. It is designed for AI-agent workflows (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, etc.) to edit code, trigger rebuilds, capture screenshots and bounding-box geometry for verification, and export standard CAD formats. Notable features are parametric-by-default projects, live local preview, agent-facing MCP tooling, and optional MJCF/MuJoCo assembly preview.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository is active with packaged releases, a substantial star count (257), and recent commits, indicating more than an experimental prototype; however the project is only ~208 days old (<1 year) and is described as being in maintenance mode, so beta (TRL 6) is appropriate.
prerequisites: Python 3.13 for the embedded CAD runner
familiarity with code-driven CAD (build123d / OpenSCAD-style workflows)
student_project_ideas: Build a parametric quadrotor arm assembly where students write agent-guided scripts to change motor mount dimensions and export STL for 3D printing, comparing mass/inertia estimates before and after changes.

Create an agent-driven design loop that optimises a planetary gear set's gear ratios and clearances by having the agent modify params.json, rebuild models in Forgent3D, and record bounding-box and mass properties to feed into a simple performance metric.

tools.name: stew675/llama-cpp-rdna-boosts
tools.desc: A set of performant RDNA/HIP patches against llama.cpp focusing on high speed inferencing with numerics assurance

cls.summary: A collection of AMD RDNA-specific performance patches for llama.cpp that improve GPU inference speed and reduce VRAM usage on ROCm/HIP platforms.
cls.what_it_does: This repository provides a set of default-on git patches that modify llama.cpp to add RDNA-targeted optimisations (WMMA flash-attention, BF16 KV, MTP decode, fused MoE paths, hybrid all-reduce, etc.) so large language models run faster and use less VRAM on AMD GPUs. It is applied to a clean llama.cpp checkout as a linear series of commits and includes documentation of environment knobs, supported GPU families, and release manifests. Notable aspects are its RDNA3/4 focus, provided validation notes, and shipping as a reproducible patch series with optional and temporary blocks for testing.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository is actively maintained, has releases and substantial documentation and validation notes, but it is only 84 days old so under the stated rules its demonstrated maturity is limited to an alpha-in-use level (TRL 5) despite community interest (256 stars) and release tags.
prerequisites: familiarity with llama.cpp and ggml internals
Linux development and git (applying patch series)
ROCm/HIP toolchain and GPU driver knowledge
C/C++ build toolchains and cross-compilation basics
student_project_ideas: Apply the rdna-boosts patch series to llama.cpp and benchmark inference latency and VRAM usage across RDNA3 vs RDNA2 GPUs, producing performance reports and tuning environment knobs for different model sizes.

Integrate the patched llama.cpp build into a small edge inference pipeline (containerised ROCm app) and evaluate throughput and energy consumption for on-premise model serving compared with a CPU baseline.

tools.name: Emmi-AI/noether
tools.desc: Deep-Learning framework for Engineering AI. Built on transformer building blocks, it delivers the full engineering stack, allowing teams to build,  train, and operate industrial simulation models across engineering verticals.

cls.summary: Noether is a Python deep-learning framework built on transformer blocks for training and operating physics-informed simulation models across engineering domains.
cls.what_it_does: Noether provides modular transformer-based building blocks, training pipelines, and scaling/cluster support to develop ML models for industrial simulations (examples include aerodynamics/CFD). It is used via a pip package or from-source with recipes and CLI scaffolding, and is notable for GPU/MPS/CPU hardware-agnostic execution and multi-GPU/SLURM readiness for large engineering workloads.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository is 316 days old with active development, examples/recipes, pip packages and documentation which indicates a beta-stage project; because it is younger than one year TRL is capped at 6 despite visible uptake (stars, recipes, benchmarks).
prerequisites: familiarity with machine learning workflows and (for GPUs) CUDA or Apple MPS
basic knowledge of SLURM if using cluster features
student_project_ideas: Train a Noether transformer model on a small CFD benchmark (e.g. DrivAerML subset) to predict pressure fields and compare results with a baseline CNN model, documenting accuracy and inference speed on CPU vs GPU.

Create a pipeline that uses Noether to train a surrogate model for a parameterised aerodynamic shape and deploy a simple inference service (Flask or FastAPI) to demonstrate rapid design-space exploration.

tools.name: ucsandman/marketing-studio
tools.desc: Create product launch assets with Remotion, then review and distribute them through guarded, dry-run-first workflows.

cls.summary: An agent-driven local toolchain that automates creation, review and guarded distribution of product launch assets (videos, demos, audio and social clips) using Remotion, Blender and other tools.
cls.what_it_does: Marketing Studio reads a product repository to generate a validated content brief and then produces a suite of launch assets (logo reveal, recorded product demo, composed launch video, scored voice/music, social clips and OG assets). It is run via agent commands and includes local review gates, a dry-run-first distribution flow, content linting and a mission-control UI to approve or resume runs.
cls.trl_rationale: The README documents a full-featured pipeline with many integrations and a mission-control UI and the repo has community interest (255 stars), but the project is only ~130 days old and lacks evidence of long-term production use or stable releases, so it fits a beta-stage TRL.
prerequisites: API keys for cloud services (e.g. ElevenLabs, posting APIs) for full functionality
student_project_ideas: Use Marketing Studio to produce a launch kit for a student project: adapt the content-brief generation and run /product-demo and /launch-video to create cross-platform assets and document the automated pipeline.

Evaluate and extend the review gates by adding an additional automated quality check (for example color-palette consistency or accessibility captions) and measure how it affects re-render frequency and time-to-ship.

tools.name: jherrodthomas/robotics-skills-suite
tools.desc: 76 audit-ready Claude skills automating the industrial robot, cobot, AMR, ROS2, V&V, AI/ML, and IEC 62443 lifecycle. 38 builder + reviewer pairs anchored to ISO 10218, 13849, 62061, 12100, 9283, 15066, 3691-4, and IEC 62443.

cls.summary: A curated set of 76 Claude 'skills' (38 builder + 38 reviewer) that automate creation and review of standards-driven xlsx deliverables across the industrial-robotics lifecycle (safety, ROS2, AMR, V&V, AI/ML governance, and IEC 62443 cybersecurity).
cls.what_it_does: This repository provides installable .skill files for Claude that generate audit-ready multi-tab XLSX workbooks for tasks such as ISO 12100 risk assessments, ISO 13849/IEC 62061 PLr/SIL determination, ISO 10218 compliance matrices, ISO/TS 15066 biomechanical checks, ISO 3691-4 AMR risk, ROS2 architecture artifacts, FAT/SAT protocols and IEC 62443 assessments. Each 'builder' skill produces a structured xlsx and a paired 'reviewer' skill produces a confirmation checklist and a visual dashboard; skills hand off via stable xlsx contracts so downstream consumers update automatically.
cls.trl_rationale: The project is active, well-documented and installable (provides .skill files and a bundled zip) and has community interest (255 stars) but the repository is only ~198 days old (<1 year), so there is not yet a long track record of broad production deployment—consistent with a beta (TRL 6).
prerequisites: Access to Anthropic Claude (Cowork / Claude Desktop) and familiarity with installing .skill files
Basic knowledge of robotics standards (ISO 12100, ISO 13849, IEC 62061, ISO 10218, ISO/TS 15066, ISO 3691-4, IEC 62443) to interpret outputs
Ability to read/edit Excel xlsx workbooks; Python familiarity helpful for customization
student_project_ideas: Use the iso12100-risk-assessment-builder skill to generate a risk assessment for a cobot cell, then implement a reviewer-driven dashboard that visualises key KPIs and traces changes when upstream inputs are modified.

Integrate the ROS2 architecture/URDF builder skills with a simple Gazebo or ROS2 simulation to generate architecture docs from a simulated robot and validate the generated URDF/TF outputs as part of an acceptance test pipeline.

tools.name: altnautica/ADOSMissionControl
tools.desc: ADOS Mission Control: open-source ground control station for browser and desktop. FC setup, mission planning, flight, 3D simulation and fleet.

cls.summary: ADOS Mission Control is an open-source, browser-first ground control station for drones that supports MAVLink/MSP flight controllers, mission planning, live flight, fleet dashboards and 3D rehearsal on a Cesium globe.
cls.what_it_does: It provides a web and desktop ground control station (GCS) to connect to ArduPilot, PX4, Betaflight and iNav flight controllers over USB or WebSocket, allowing configuration, mission planning (pattern generators, terrain-following), live piloting (gamepad/RC inputs) and telemetry/fleet management. Notable features include an integrated Cesium 3D rehearsal environment, PID tuning with analytics, HMAC-signed MAVLink frames, and an agent architecture (ADOS Drone Agent) that unifies the flight controller and companion computer into a single node.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository is active with many stars, a live demo, documentation and extensions, indicating more than an alpha prototype; however it is under 1 year old (created 2026-02-27) so by the TRL rules it should be capped at ~6 despite visible maturity and usage.
prerequisites: familiarity with MAVLink and common flight controllers (ArduPilot, PX4)
understanding of drone mission concepts and telemetry
student_project_ideas: Build an autonomous survey mission: use ADOS Mission Control to plan a corridor/survey mission, run it in demo mode or with a simulated vehicle, collect telemetry and analyse PID/noise using the built-in tuning tools.

Integrate a perception pipeline: run ADOS Drone Agent on a companion computer (or simulator), stream a simple object-detection node and display detections in Mission Control's live video and mission replay to prototype vision-guided waypoint corrections.

tools.name: jaisurya-dev-art/rigby2d
tools.desc: Open-source 2D skeletal animation editor for games and film. AutoRig layered PSDs, animate with meshes, IK and physics, lip-sync from audio, render video, export JSON/.skel. JavaScript, Rust, Godot and Unity runtimes. Built-in MCP server for AI assistants. Docs: rigby2d.com/docs

cls.summary: Rigby2D is an open-source 2D skeletal animation editor that rigs layered PSD/SVG artwork, provides animation and film workspaces, and exports animations to multiple game runtimes.
cls.what_it_does: Rigby2D turns layered art (PSD/SVG) into editable rigs with bones and weighted meshes, provides keyframe and graph-based animation tools plus camera/film rendering and viseme lip-sync, and exports frame-for-frame runtimes (JSON/.skel, sprite sheets) for engines such as Godot and Unity. It is notable for integrated AutoRig, built-in runtimes across many engines, a browser-capable editor, and a built-in MCP server for AI assistant automation.
cls.trl_rationale: The project is well-documented, has multiple runtimes and notable community interest (stars and featured listings), but the repository is very new (created 35 days ago) so it lacks the multi-release, long-term track record required for higher TRL.
prerequisites: optional: experience with target game engines (Godot, Unity) to use exports
student_project_ideas: Create a short animated character in Rigby2D, export the runtime and integrate the animation into a Godot scene to demonstrate editor-to-engine fidelity.
Build a Python add-on that automates batch lip-syncing using Rigby2D's MCP server and on-device transcription, and evaluate its accuracy on a set of short voice clips.

tools.name: Dicklesworthstone/mcp_agent_mail_rust
tools.desc: Rust MCP server for multi-agent coordination: 45 tools and 25 resources, Git-backed archive, SQLite indexing, advisory file locks, a 16-screen TUI, a server-rendered web UI, and an agent-first robot CLI.

cls.summary: Agent Mail is a Rust implementation of an MCP server that provides mail-like messaging, file reservation leases and tooling to coordinate multiple coding agents working on the same project.
cls.what_it_does: Agent Mail exposes an MCP server and operator CLI/TUI that give AI coding agents identities, threaded inboxes/outboxes, advisory file reservations, a Git-backed archive and SQLite indexing to avoid conflicting edits and preserve an auditable history. It is used by running the server and connecting MCP-compatible agents or via the operator TUI/web UI/robot CLI; notable points are the built-in pre-commit guard, hybrid search bridge (Tantivy + optional semantic routing), and support for many agent CLIs.
cls.trl_rationale: The repository is a feature-rich Rust rewrite of an older Python project (the README cites the 1,700+ star original) with installers, binaries, CI-style assets, an extensive README, video walkthrough and active commits; however the Rust repo is under one year old (285 days) so demonstrated track record limits it to TRL 6 (beta).
prerequisites: familiarity with Git and Git hooks
experience with CLI tools and basic server operation
MCP-compatible agent clients (or configured agent CLIs)
student_project_ideas: Set up Agent Mail for a small team of scripted agents (e.g., GitHub Copilot CLI and an LLM CLI) and evaluate how advisory file reservations and the pre-commit guard prevent merge conflicts compared to a baseline Git-only workflow.

Extend Agent Mail by adding a custom MCP tool that integrates project-specific static analysis results into agent messages and measure how often agents act on the analysis in an automated development workflow.

tools.name: dsh0416/godot-cef
tools.desc: A cross-platform GPU-accelerated CEF-based (Chromium Embedded Framework) WebView Extension for Godot 4

cls.summary: A Rust-written Godot 4 extension that embeds Chromium (CEF) as a GPU-accelerated WebView so web content can be rendered and interacted with inside Godot scenes.
cls.what_it_does: This extension provides a CefTexture node to display and interact with web pages inside Godot 4 applications, supporting GPU-accelerated off-screen rendering with platform-native APIs and a software fallback. It handles CEF subprocesses, typed IPC (CBOR), a listener-based JS bridge and remote debugging, making it notable for high-performance, interactive web UIs inside real-time 3D applications.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository is active with prebuilt releases, cross-platform binaries and a dedicated documentation site, indicating beyond alpha; however the project is under 1 year old (created ~321 days ago) so evidence supports a beta maturity (TRL 6) rather than production-long track record.
prerequisites: Optional: Rust toolchain if building from source
student_project_ideas: Build an in-game instrument panel for a robotics simulation in Godot that embeds a web-based dashboard (e.g. Grafana or a custom React app) via godot-cef and connects it to simulated telemetry via typed IPC.

Create a digital-twin HMI prototype that renders a 3D scene in Godot and embeds WebGPU-based visualisations or control widgets in a CefTexture, demonstrating integrated web UI and real-time 3D data exchange.

tools.name: Comfy-Org/comfy-skills
tools.desc: Comfy Cloud product skills: slash commands for generating images, video, audio, and 3D with Comfy Cloud agents. Single source of truth for the installer and MCP server.

cls.summary: Comfy Skills provides a collection of agent skills and a plugin that connects AI agents (Claude, Cowork) to Comfy Cloud to generate images, video, audio and 3D and to discover/run ComfyUI workflows.
cls.what_it_does: Comfy Skills bundles agent 'skills' and a Comfy Cloud MCP connector so AI coding agents can call image, video, audio and 3D generation, search models/nodes/templates, and run ComfyUI workflows through the hosted Comfy Cloud MCP server. It is distributed as two plugin flavours: comfy-cloud (bundled MCP connector + skills) and comfy-sdk (guidance for building apps using the Comfy SDK and router), and is notable for providing a single source-of-truth plugin manifest and slash/skill commands that work across Claude, Cowork and other agent surfaces.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository is active with CI, documentation and a hosted MCP server workflow, moderate community interest (252 stars) but is younger than one year (created 2026-06) so it fits a beta-stage maturity rather than long-term production adoption.
prerequisites: understanding of MCP/connectors and Comfy Cloud
basic Python or TypeScript for SDK usage
student_project_ideas: Build a small agent-driven pipeline that uses the comfy-cloud skills to generate images from prompts, then post-processes and displays results in a simple web viewer (use Comfy SDK + a three.js viewer).
Create a wrapper that calls the generate-3d skill, converts returned assets to glTF, and integrates them into a lightweight digital-twin prototype displayed in a web-based scene.

tools.name: terryHu7/homecraft
tools.desc: Build your own Minecraft-inspired 3D personal website. 打造“我的世界”风格3D个人网站

cls.summary: Homecraft is an open-source Three.js-based template that turns a personal website into a Minecraft-style voxel 3D world you can navigate in the browser.
cls.what_it_does: Homecraft provides a ready-made, voxel-style 3D website template and example world (Terry's Home) so users can host a navigable, blocky personal site with features like day/night and weather, embedded 2D pages, camera controls and a screenshot mode. It is used by running the included serve script and customizing the example world; it is notable for its mobile-friendly, low-cost voxel visuals and an opinionated, themed portfolio/demo site.
cls.trl_rationale: The project is actively developed and includes example worlds and a simple run command, and it has attracted noticeable attention (many stars) despite being very new; however the repository is only 24 days old so there is limited evidence of long-term usage or stable releases, which constrains the TRL.
prerequisites: Python 3 for the provided serve script
familiarity with Three.js/WebGL helpful for customization
student_project_ideas: Create a customised 3D portfolio by modifying the example world, adding new interactive exhibits that link to GitHub-hosted projects and deploy the site using GitHub Pages or a simple CI pipeline.
Measure and optimise mobile performance by profiling the voxel scene (reduce draw calls, implement LOD or chunking) and report performance improvements across devices.

tools.name: svd-ai-lab/sim-cli
tools.desc: Turn any CAE files into structured text an agent can use

cls.summary: sim is a Python CLI that scans CAE solver input and result files and converts them into bounded, structured JSON summaries an agent or tool can consume without launching the solver.
cls.what_it_does: sim parses a wide range of CAE file formats (Abaqus, Ansys, COMSOL, Fluent, Simulink, etc.) and produces a stable JSON envelope containing summaries or full parsed data, suitable for use by automation/agents. It is used as a command-line tool (example: uv run sim --json scan ...) and notable for faster parsing than simple Python scripts and for producing bounded outputs tuned for agent contexts.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository is active with clear documentation, benchmarks and many stars, indicating an organised project and real users, but it is only ~7 months old (<1 year) so it lacks the long track record and stable ecosystem required for TRL 7+.
prerequisites: familiarity with CAE file types and solvers (Abaqus, Ansys, COMSOL, Fluent, Simulink)
student_project_ideas: Create an agent that uses sim to scan a repository of historical FEA cases and auto-generate a searchable catalogue of problem types, boundary conditions and materials, then visualise trends in a Jupyter notebook.

Integrate sim with a test automation pipeline to automatically parse solver input files and run requirement/consistency checks (e.g., missing boundary conditions or material mismatches) and produce a verification report.

tools.name: int64ago/vistep
tools.desc: Visualize Every Step with AI — bilingual visual explanations, interactive models and synchronized narration.

cls.summary: Vistep is an open-source web platform of short, bilingual interactive visual stories that combine simple computational models, synchronized narration and 2D/3D visualisations for teaching physical and computational mechanisms.
cls.what_it_does: Vistep presents chaptered, pauseable visual explanations driven by small browser-run models so users can watch a mechanism, change inputs and observe outcomes without installing software or needing cloud AI. It combines pre-rendered narration, TypeScript models and Web visuals (SVG, Canvas, Three.js) to make experiments interactive and bilingual (English/Chinese). Notable aspects are a large curated scene catalog, in-browser computations and production CI-driven builds.
