cls.trl_rationale: Repository is 73 days old so TRL is limited by age; however the project publishes production builds via GitHub Actions, includes 301 registered scenes and recording assets, and has active CI and community interest (250 stars), which indicates alpha usage by early adopters rather than mature production deployment.
prerequisites: modern browser (Chrome/Edge/Firefox/Safari) and basic TypeScript/React familiarity
student_project_ideas: Extend a Vistep scene by replacing its numerical model with a more detailed physics model (e.g. improve a pendulum scene to include damping and driving torque) and compare results in-class, using GitHub Pages to publish the modified scene.
Create an accessibility and localisation improvement project that adds another language or audio-captioning pipeline for selected scenes, measuring comprehension with a small user study.

tools.name: mrzh7/scam-with-your-friends-web
tools.desc: Scam With Your Friends Web: unofficial open-source browser remake. Co-op AI call center game with a 3D office, voice chat and daily quotas. React + Three.js; self-host on Cloudflare. Русский язык: кооперативная браузерная игра про колл-центр с ИИ.

cls.summary: An open-source unofficial browser remake of the co-op game 'Scam With Your Friends' built with React, Three.js and Cloudflare Workers that supports multiplayer, WebRTC voice and self-hosting.
cls.what_it_does: This repository provides a playable browser-based co-op party game where up to four players run a fictional AI call centre, manage tasks and talk over WebRTC voice. It is implemented with React and Three.js for the 3D office, Cloudflare Workers for hosting/state, and includes options for local play, self-hosting and optional TTS/AI conversation features.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository is very new (39 days) so TRL is capped by age, but the README and playable demo indicate it is beyond a minimal prototype and used by early adopters; however there is limited long-term production track record.
prerequisites: optional: Cloudflare Workers account for self-hosting
student_project_ideas: Modify the Three.js office to add a new interactive workstation and integrate telemetry to visualise player movement and interactions for a UX study.
Replace or extend the AI caller system with a simple local language-model or scripted FSM to evaluate how caller behaviour affects team performance and quotas.

tools.name: gsamat/amanu
tools.desc: Records and transcribes online meetings. Automatically

cls.summary: Amanu is a free, open-source desktop app that records online meetings on macOS and Windows, produces speaker-attributed transcripts, and can generate summaries using local or cloud models.
cls.what_it_does: Amanu automatically detects when a call app is using the microphone and records the meeting audio, separates speakers, transcribes speech to text with selectable local or cloud engines, and generates summaries and action items. It stores every meeting as ordinary files (audio, transcript, summary, metadata) on the user’s computer and supports local-first operation to avoid sending meeting content to third-party servers.
cls.trl_rationale: The project provides signed installers for macOS and Windows and published release builds, active development (last push Oct 22) and several hundred stars, indicating a beta-level product; the repository is 91 days old so it is still young and lacks the long track record required for TRL 7+.
student_project_ideas: Build a pipeline that ingests Amanu meeting folders and automatically extracts and tags action items into a lightweight issue tracker (e.g., GitHub Issues) using an LLM.

Compare local transcription quality and privacy trade-offs by running the same meeting audio through Amanu configured with Parakeet, Whisper and a cloud service (AssemblyAI) and report on accuracy and latency.

tools.name: Private-Garden-Labs/garden-desk
tools.desc: Private AI on premise

cls.summary: Garden Desk is a privacy-first desktop agent that runs local large language models in an isolated microVM to work with selected folders and files without cloud services or telemetry.
cls.what_it_does: Garden Desk lets a user point to a folder or attach files, then uses a supervised local LLM to propose and run file tools or code inside a network-disabled microVM, keeping the source folder read-only and storing results only where the user chooses. It is notable for its on‑device, privacy-focused architecture (Tauri + Node.js) and published signed builds for macOS and Windows, plus documentation on security and development.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository is 141 days old (<1 year) which limits TRL to at most 6; however it provides signed desktop builds, architecture/security docs, benchmarks, and active commits indicating a beta-stage project used by early adopters.
prerequisites: local model weights (e.g. Bonsai 2 27B) or supported runtime
Node.js and Tauri build toolchain to build from source
Windows: Hyper-V and compatible GPU for Windows builds
student_project_ideas: Build an offline document-processing workflow that uses Garden Desk to extract, summarise and tag engineering requirements from a local project folder and compare outputs when using different local LLMs (e.g. Bonsai 2 vs Qwen).

Evaluate Garden Desk's isolated execution model by adding a new file-analysis tool run inside the microVM, measure safety/privacy guarantees, and document integration steps for reproducible deployment in a lab environment.

tools.name: ayushh0110/ScreenMind
tools.desc: AI-powered screen memory — captures, analyzes, and lets you search/chat your screen history. Powered by Gemma 4 . 100% local, 100% private.

cls.summary: ScreenMind is a local, privacy-first desktop app that continuously captures screenshots, analyses them with multimodal models (Gemma 4), and provides a searchable, chat-able history of your screen activity.
cls.what_it_does: ScreenMind detects meaningful changes on your screen, captures screenshots and audio, extracts multimodal metadata (app/activity detection, scene descriptions, transcripts) using Gemma 4, and stores them in a locally searchable memory that supports semantic search and conversational retrieval. It is used as a personal AI memory and automation platform with an in-app model hub, integrations (Obsidian, Notion, webhooks) and a local API for agent-like automations.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository is active with many features, 249 stars and zero open issues, showing community interest and a workable product; however it is only ~6 months old (179 days) so it fits a beta-level maturity rather than long-term production track record.
prerequisites: familiarity with local LLM/model hosting and GPU/CPU inference
desktop OS configuration (hotkeys, startup services, audio permissions)
student_project_ideas: Build a privacy-preserving meeting analytics plugin that uses ScreenMind's local transcripts to produce meeting minutes and sentiment timelines, then export structured results to an Obsidian vault or Notion database.
Compare semantic search effectiveness by replacing ScreenMind's MiniLM embeddings with another embedding model and measure retrieval precision/latency on a collected day-long screen-capture dataset.

tools.name: fiveoutofnine/whatcanirun
tools.desc: Find the best models and how to run them locally.

cls.summary: A web site and CLI that helps you find which open-source LLMs you can run locally and run standardised performance benchmarks on your hardware.
cls.what_it_does: whatcanirun provides a browsable catalogue of local LLMs with community benchmark results on different devices and a CLI to run standardized local benchmarks and submit results. It is used to compare runtimes and model performance across hardware (eg. Apple Silicon, CPU, GPU) and runtimes such as llama.cpp, and to collect/share results via the hosted site.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository is a public, active monorepo with a working website, CLI published to npm and ~248 stars, showing community interest; however it is younger than one year (created 259 days ago) so lacks the longer track record required for TRL 7+.
prerequisites: access to local hardware for model inference (CPU/GPU/MPS) and optionally model binaries/runtimes
student_project_ideas: Run benchmarks with the whatcanirun CLI on a heterogeneous lab of machines (Intel, AMD, Apple Silicon) and produce a report correlating model size, runtime, and latency; compare results against a hosted dataset from the site.
Extend the CLI to add a new runtime backend (for example a WebGPU or custom WASM backend) and evaluate performance differences for a selected small LLM across backends.

tools.name: sparkgeo/geo-mcp-servers
tools.desc: A curated, tracked list of Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers for geospatial, GIS, mapping, and earth-observation work — geocoding, routing, PostGIS, STAC/imagery, QGIS/ArcGIS, weather, and the commercial location platforms.

cls.summary: A curated, regularly updated catalog of Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers focused on geospatial, GIS, mapping and earth-observation services, plus tooling to generate the catalog and a Claude skill for searching it.
cls.what_it_does: This repository collects and documents MCP-compatible servers for geospatial tasks (geocoding, routing, STAC/imagery, PostGIS, weather, commercial location platforms) and generates the README tables from a single YAML source. It includes scripts to regenerate the catalog, a health-check for entries, and an optional Claude skill to query and recommend servers programmatically. What makes it notable is the curated, categorized listing with health/access metadata and an integrated skill for LLM-based discovery.
cls.trl_rationale: The repo is actively maintained and used to generate a curated catalog and includes scripts and a Claude skill (evidence of practical tooling), but it is only ~107 days old so it lacks the multi-year track record or broad production adoption needed for TRL 7+.
prerequisites: familiarity with geospatial concepts (STAC, PostGIS, geocoding)
optional: using Claude skills / LLM integration
student_project_ideas: Create a small MCP client that queries the catalog for open STAC imagery servers and builds an automated ingestion pipeline into a local PostGIS database.
Extend the repo by adding an evaluation script that benchmarks response time and feature support across a selected subset of MCP geocoding servers, and visualise results on a web map.

tools.name: aivrar/portable-hermes-agent
tools.desc: Hermes Agent made portable desktop for Windows — 100 tools, GUI, local models via LM Studio, TTS, Music, ComfyUI, workflows, tool maker. No install. No Docker. No admin rights.

cls.summary: Portable Hermes Agent is a Windows desktop bundle that runs a Hermes-based AI agent with a Tkinter GUI, local model support (via LM Studio), 100 built-in tools and a workflow engine without requiring installation or admin rights.
cls.what_it_does: It packages the Hermes Agent core into a portable, no-install Windows desktop with a chat GUI, multi-language support, image attachments, toolsets (LM Studio, ComfyUI, TTS, Music, workflows, etc.) and a runtime 'Tool Maker' for creating API or Python tools. It is used by downloading the release ZIP, extracting and running the provided START.bat which auto-installs an embedded Python runtime and optional local extension servers; notable features are offline guided mode, runtime tool creation, and auto-installing portable extension servers.
cls.trl_rationale: The project is an active, public portable distribution with releases and many stars and forks and recent pushes, showing it is beyond a minimal prototype; however the repository is under one year old (created 2026-03-15, ~247 days) so there is limited long-term production track record, capping the TRL at 6.
prerequisites: basic understanding of LLMs / local AI model concepts
optionally Python for advanced tool maker custom handlers
student_project_ideas: Create a workflow that uses the Portable Hermes Agent to automate a data-preprocessing pipeline and integrates a local ComfyUI image-generation step, demonstrating end-to-end automation and logging.

Extend the Tool Maker by writing a custom Python handler that calls a campus lab API and builds a simple experiment-run orchestration tool, then demonstrate scheduling and result retrieval via the agent's workflow engine.

tools.name: codeofaxel/Kiln
tools.desc: From idea to object, and every version in between. Kiln is the open-source MCP server for 3D printing: AI agents (ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, GitHub Copilot, Codex, Cursor, Grok, Hermes Agent, or any MCP client) design, slice and print on Bambu Lab, Creality, Prusa, Elegoo, Klipper, OctoPrint and more. Version control: branch, merge and undo designs.

cls.summary: Kiln is an open-source MCP server that connects AI agents to real 3D printers, providing a design-to-print pipeline with version control, slicing, job queuing and printer monitoring.
cls.what_it_does: Kiln accepts high-level prompts from AI agents and drives a full 3D-print workflow: it can generate or modify designs, run printability checks and slicing, queue and monitor prints on supported printers, and keep Git-style version history of designs. It is notable because it integrates many AI agents (ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, etc.) with a wide range of printers and host software (OctoPrint, Moonraker/Klipper, PrusaLink) to provide an agent-driven end-to-end print loop.
cls.trl_rationale: The project is an actively maintained, installable Python package with releases, broad integrations and several hundred stars, indicating a working beta; however the repository is under 1 year old (created 2026-02-10), so there is not yet a long track record required for TRL 7+.
prerequisites: familiarity with 3D printing concepts (slicing, printers, filament/resin)
understanding of MCP-capable agent clients or how to configure MCP
student_project_ideas: Build an agent-driven print farm demo: configure Kiln to accept prompts from a local LLM or Claude and run a set of automated print jobs on an OctoPrint-connected printer, adding failure recovery and logging.

Compare design branches: use Kiln's version control to implement two parametrised OpenSCAD designs, print both, record print metrics (time, material used, success), and produce a short report that merges the better design branch.

tools.name: Teddy563/realworldmc
tools.desc: Explore real cities, mountains and streets in Minecraft. RealWorldMC brings Google 3D maps and Street View to Java Edition with Fabric. Recommended for 1.21.1; experimental 26.2 available. Requires your own map API keys.

cls.summary: RealWorldMC is a Minecraft Java Edition mod that streams real-world 3D map tiles and Google Street View into Minecraft so players can fly over and walk through approximated real-world locations.
cls.what_it_does: The mod fetches 3D tiles and street-level imagery (via Cesium or Google Maps APIs) and renders them as Minecraft blocks and viewable Street View photos inside the game; it runs as a Fabric mod and provides in-game commands and a local map service. It is notable because it bridges interactive geospatial data and an accessible game engine (Minecraft) for immersive visualisation and exploration, but requires the user's own API keys and can incur map-usage costs.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository is very new (created 39 days ago) but has releases, documentation and downloadable builds; the README and releases indicate early adopters can run it, so it's at an alpha-in-use level rather than production-ready.
student_project_ideas: Create a short interactive lab where students import a local city's 3D tiles into a controlled Minecraft world and annotate infrastructure (roads, bridges) to discuss geospatial data fidelity and limitations.
Build a small extension or script that logs Street View locations visited in-game and compares them to OpenStreetMap building footprints to analyse positional errors and coverage gaps.

tools.name: jammaru/sakutto
tools.desc: A browser extension for easy on-device translation with a local LLM (PLaMo). Private, free, no server needed.

cls.summary: Sakutto is a Chrome/Firefox extension that runs a local LLM (PLaMo via wllama WebAssembly/WebGPU) in the browser to translate web pages, selections, typed text and PDFs on-device without sending data to a server.
cls.what_it_does: Sakutto loads a pinned wllama build and runs PLaMo-3-Translate in the browser (WASM/WebGPU) to translate page content, selected text, typed text and PDFs locally. It is used as a browser extension (Chrome and Firefox) and falls back to the browser translator API only for language pairs the local model doesn't support. Its notable points are completely on-device translation, explicit support for typed-text preview/replace, and a privacy-first workflow.
cls.trl_rationale: The repository is very new (created 12 days ago) so maturity is limited, but the README, published extension listing and active recent commits show an alpha-quality project used by others; that supports an Alpha-in-use (TRL 5) judgement rather than a lower prototype level.
prerequisites: local LLM model weights (PLaMo) and sufficient GPU/CPU resources
student_project_ideas: Measure latency, memory and translation quality of on-device PLaMo (via Sakutto) versus a cloud translation API across multiple languages and report privacy/UX trade-offs.

Extend Sakutto to add usage telemetry (local opt-in only) and build an experiment that compares human evaluation of translations produced by PLaMo vs DeepL/Google for a curated corpus of engineering documentation.

tools.name: morganlinton/Albatross
tools.desc: Open source, terminal-first AI coding agent with fully transparent multi-model routing. Local (Ollama, LM Studio, MLX, llama.cpp) or cloud, your keys, one TUI. No black box.

cls.summary: Albatross is a terminal-first, open-source AI coding agent that runs with local or cloud LLMs and provides session logging, multi-model routing, undo/branching, and an embeddable Rust SDK.
cls.what_it_does: Albatross provides a TUI coding assistant that connects to cloud APIs (OpenAI, Anthropic, OpenRouter) or local models (Ollama, LM Studio, MLX, llama.cpp) to run coding workflows, run tools (edit, grep, tests), and manage sessions with features like routing, planning, undo, and branching. It is used from the terminal or embedded via a Rust SDK and is notable for transparent multi-model routing, per-turn cost reporting, and reproducible session artifacts.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository is active with 244 stars, install instructions (Homebrew/cargo), and detailed README but is only ~7 months old (<1 year), so it appears to be a beta-quality project with real users but not a long track record.
prerequisites: Rust toolchain (for building from source or using the SDK)
access to LLM providers or local model runtimes (Ollama, LM Studio, llama.cpp) if needed
student_project_ideas: Create an assignment where students integrate a local llama.cpp model with Albatross to implement a custom coding 'skill' that runs automated tests and reports a graded rubric, comparing results to a cloud-based provider.
Build a CI-style tool that uses Albatross's Rust SDK to run automated code-fix iterations on a small repository and measure improvement using the agent's /iterate generate→evaluate loop.

tools.name: dbwls99706/ros2-engineering-skills
tools.desc: Agent skill for production-grade ROS 2 development. Progressive-disclosure SKILL.md covering workspace, nodes, executors, QoS, ros2_control, Nav2, MoveIt 2, real-time, and deployment. Works with Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Gemini CLI.

cls.summary: A production-oriented 'skill' that guides coding agents to give operationally correct ROS 2 engineering advice, with validators, tests and client plugins for tools like Claude Code and Codex.
cls.what_it_does: This repository supplies a knowledge/validation skill for coding agents focused on ROS 2 engineering: it encodes best-practice guidance (workspace layout, QoS, lifecycle nodes, ros2_control, Nav2, MoveIt 2, testing and deployment), static validators, regression tests and CI for multiple ROS 2 distributions. It is installed either as a Claude Code/agent plugin or as a knowledge-only skill for other LLM clients and is notable for its emphasis on runtime checks, provenance of installs, and preventing plausible-but-wrong agent recommendations.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository shows multiple releases (source version 1.8.1), active maintenance (recent pushes), CI and 244 stars indicating community interest, but it is younger than one year (created 2026-03-16) so a conservative Beta TRL (6) is appropriate.
prerequisites: basic ROS 2 familiarity (topics, nodes, QoS, rclpy/rclcpp)
familiarity with an LLM client (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Gemini) for full plugin usage
student_project_ideas: Create an automated lab-assistant that uses this skill to inspect a running ROS 2 graph and produce a checklist and minimal code patch to fix a QoS mismatch between a publisher and subscriber, integrating ros2cli output and a small CI test.

Build a CI pipeline for a simple mobile robot package that uses the skill's validators and provenance installer to verify consistent installations and run regression tests across two ROS 2 distributions (e.g. rolling vs long-term) as a course capstone.

tools.name: pasrom/meeting-transcriber
tools.desc: On-device meeting transcriber for macOS — auto-records Teams/Zoom/Webex, transcribes & separates speakers locally. No cloud. Open-source alternative to Otter/Granola/Fireflies.

cls.summary: An open-source macOS menu-bar app that records meetings (Teams/Zoom/Webex), transcribes audio on-device with Whisper/Parakeet, separates speakers, and generates Markdown meeting notes without sending audio to the cloud.
cls.what_it_does: Meeting Transcriber automatically detects and records calls, captures dual audio (app + mic), runs on-device transcription and speaker diarization via CoreML/ANE engines, and produces structured Markdown meeting notes using a local or compatible LLM; it is notable for running the full pipeline locally (no cloud) and supporting multiple transcription engines and diarization modes.
cls.trl_rationale: The project is actively maintained, has many stars (243), a Homebrew cask for easy install and documented features, which indicates more than an experiment; however the repository is ~8 months old (younger than 1 year) so by the stated TRL rules it should be capped at TRL 6 (beta).
prerequisites: macOS with microphone and screen-recording permissions
Optional local LLM or API (Claude CLI, Ollama, LM Studio, OpenAI-compatible) for notes generation
student_project_ideas: Evaluate and compare on-device speaker diarization accuracy (FluidAudio modes) against a labelled meeting audio dataset and report precision/recall for speaker segmentation.

Build a small tool that ingests the Markdown meeting notes from Meeting Transcriber and automatically extracts and traces action items to a simple requirements or issue-tracking spreadsheet (CSV) to demonstrate lightweight traceability.

tools.name: dslsdzc/rev-skills
tools.desc: 122 个逆向工程 AI 技能：恶意软件分析 / 软件逆向 / 固件嵌入式 / 协议逆向 / 移动应用 / 脱壳反混淆 / 软件破解 / 漏洞挖掘 / 托管代码 / 取证情报 / CTF。

cls.summary: A cross-platform collection of 122 AI 'skills' (agent actions) for reverse engineering and malware/firmware analysis that can be installed into multiple AI agent runtimes.
cls.what_it_does: rev-skills packages 122 discrete reverse-engineering workflows and prompts (called skills) covering malware analysis, firmware/embedded, protocol reversing, mobile, unpacking/deobfuscation, vulnerability triage and forensics. It is distributed as an Agent Skills–compatible skillset with an npx installer and adapters for many agent runtimes (Claude Code, Gemini CLI, Cursor, Copilot rules, DeepSeek Harness etc.), so users can load these skills into their preferred AI toolchain for interactive assistance and automation. Notable points are its broad coverage, cross-OS installation guidance and explicit integration paths for many agent platforms.
cls.trl_rationale: The repository is well-documented, provides multiple install routes (npx, skills CLI, marketplace.json), includes tests and an installer and has attracted community interest (243 stars) within three months, indicating beta-level maturity; however it is a recently created, single-repo project without evidence of wide production deployments or long-term releases.
prerequisites: familiarity with an AI agent runtime (Claude Code, Gemini CLI, Cursor, etc.)
basic reverse-engineering tools (Ghidra/IDA/Binary Ninja, debuggers) for practical use
student_project_ideas: Create a lab assignment that uses rev-skills to automate triage of a set of benign binary samples (static indicators, strings, import analysis) and compare the agent-generated reports to manual analysis.
Integrate rev-skills with a firmware emulation workflow (QEMU + Binwalk) to build an agent-driven pipeline that extracts, instruments and reports on embedded firmware components.

tools.name: mlightcad/awesome-cad
tools.desc: A curated list of valuable open-source CAD (Computer-Aided Design) software, libraries, and tools, organized by category.

cls.summary: An open curated list of open-source CAD software, libraries and tools organised by category to help developers and engineers discover projects and resources.
cls.what_it_does: This repository aggregates and categorises open-source CAD projects (2D, 3D, code-driven, kernels, converters, datasets and AI-assisted design tools) so users can find software and libraries for different CAD workflows. It is used as a reference index (an "awesome" list) rather than a runnable tool, notable for its broad coverage and practical focus on reusable projects.
cls.trl_rationale: The repository is a curated index (not production software) created ~320 days ago and has community interest (stars, forks) but no evidence of being a production system; its maturity aligns with an alpha list in use by early adopters.
student_project_ideas: Create a short course reading list by selecting and evaluating three open-source CAD projects from the list, documenting installation, key features and a small modelling demo.
Build an automated dashboard that extracts metadata (license, language, stars) from the listed projects and visualises which CAD kernels, languages and platforms are most common.

tools.name: GoogleCloudPlatform/race-condition
tools.desc: The open source multi-agent simulation from the Developer Keynote at Google Cloud Next '26. A deployable reference architecture for autonomous AI agents using Gemini and ADK.

cls.summary: Race Condition is an open-source reference multi-agent simulation and deployable architecture that runs autonomous AI agents (Planner, Simulator, Runners) communicating over the A2A protocol and demonstrated at Google Cloud Next '26.
cls.what_it_does: It provides a working multi-agent marathon simulation that shows how to architect, run and visualise many AI agents communicating via A2A, with a Go gateway, Python ADK agents and an Angular + Three.js frontend. The repo is notable as a deployable reference architecture that includes cached replay, a deterministic runner variant (zero-API baseline), and multiple planner variants to compare planner features and scaling patterns on Cloud Run / Vertex AI.
cls.trl_rationale: The project is a full reference architecture with deploy scripts, Docker Compose locally and Cloud Run/Vertex AI cloud paths and was demonstrated at Google Cloud Next '26, showing substantial polish and examples, but the repository is only ~8 months old so it lacks the longer track record and broad independent adoption needed for TRL 7+.
student_project_ideas: Extend the deterministic runner to implement a new pacing strategy and compare race outcomes and performance overhead between deterministic, cached-replay and Gemini-powered runners.

Build a scale test that deploys many runner agents to Cloud Run (or local Docker Compose) and measure gateway bottlenecks, experimenting with batching and hub patterns while visualising results in the Three.js frontend.

tools.name: microsoft/XBOX-Godot-Sample
tools.desc: An example implementation binding the Microsoft GDK, XBOX Services, PlayFab and GameInput to Godot 4. Provides GDExtension and Game references for shipping on XBOX on PC.

cls.summary: A Microsoft-authored sample that provides Godot 4 GDExtension bindings to the Microsoft GDK, Xbox Services, PlayFab and GameInput so Godot games can target XBOX on PC.
cls.what_it_does: This repository supplies C++ GDExtension addons and C# facades that wrap Microsoft GDK/Xbox Services, PlayFab and GameInput for Godot 4. Developers build the addons (or drop them into a Godot project) to access Xbox platform services, multiplayer, achievements, leaderboards and controller input from GDScript or .NET. It is notable for covering most Xbox-on-PC surface area and providing modular, reusable integration code and tutorials.
cls.trl_rationale: The repo is a well-documented, actively maintained Microsoft sample with releases and tutorials, but it is only 173 days old (<1 year) so it lacks the longer track record and broad independent adoption required for TRL 7+.
prerequisites: C++ toolchain and optionally .NET/C# for Godot
Installed Microsoft GDK and PlayFab accounts/licenses per their terms
student_project_ideas: Create a small Godot multiplayer prototype that uses the godot_playfab addon for lobby and matchmaking and demonstrates sign-in, leaderboards and cloud saves.
Build a Godot input and UI demo that uses the GameInput binding and Xbox services to show controller mapping, rumble and achievement unlocking, tested via an Xbox sandbox account.

tools.name: cloveric/claude-drawing-skill
tools.desc: Claude paints with code: a Claude Code skill for procedural illustration in 83 styles, from ink wash (水墨), watercolour and ukiyo-e to stained glass, Roman mosaic, Art Deco, shadow puppets, pastel UI, sketchbook doodles, spot illustrations, grainy picture books, dreamy hills, sunlit greenery. No image model: numpy + Pillow on a CPU, draw-on GIFs.

cls.summary: A Python-based procedural illustration library and a Claude Code skill that paints images step-by-step in 83 defined styles using only numpy and Pillow (no image model).
cls.what_it_does: The project generates illustrations programmatically: it plans a composition, renders images with numpy + Pillow on CPU, and can save intermediate stages as GIFs so you can watch the painting process. It is delivered as a Claude Code skill plus a small Python API and example scripts covering 83 stylistic modules and workflow checklists.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository is very new (created 52 days ago) but has a full README, install instructions, many examples and GIFs; community interest is shown by stars, so it's beyond a paper demo but still young—limit TRL to 5.
prerequisites: a CJK font for titles (optional for Chinese text)
student_project_ideas: Build a small toolchain that uses the library to generate staged GIFs for algorithm-illustration in a computing or HCI course, comparing deterministic procedural approaches with stochastic image models.

Create a themed set of procedural illustrations for a course report or website (e.g. engineering concept visualisations) and add per-stroke SVG or layer export for integration with Motion Canvas or Remotion.

tools.name: newideas99/open-dungeon
tools.desc: Open Dungeon — the first easy-to-use, fully local AI roleplay app. Story and inline scene images generated 100% on your machine (Gemma 4 QAT via Ollama(and others) + FLUX). No accounts, no API keys, no cloud.

cls.summary: Open Dungeon is a desktop/web app for fully local AI-driven roleplay that generates story text and inline scene images on your machine without cloud services.
cls.what_it_does: Open Dungeon runs a local narrator (via Ollama or an OpenAI-compatible backend) to generate interactive fiction with streamed narration and calls local image backends (FLUX or ComfyUI) to produce inline scene images. It is used as a privacy-first storytelling app with play controls, long-story memory and saved character portraits, notable for running text and image generation entirely on the user's device.
cls.trl_rationale: The project is a functioning, packaged application with releases (DMG/Windows launcher), documentation and an active repo, but it is only ~5 months old so it lacks a long track record; this supports a beta-level TRL rather than production-proven maturity.
prerequisites: optional: Ollama for bundled Gemma model or a compatible LLM backend
optional: local image backend (FLUX or ComfyUI) for image generation
student_project_ideas: Build a privacy-preserving interactive fiction prototype that integrates Open Dungeon with a custom ComfyUI pipeline to explore character visual continuity and evaluate latency on consumer hardware.
Compare story coherence and memory strategies by swapping local backends (Ollama Gemma vs. llama.cpp) and measuring narrative quality and context-window behaviour across long sessions.

tools.name: h4dex/opc-nexus
tools.desc: 开源的企业版的数字员工工作台, OPC-Nexus（One Person Company Nexus）是一款本地优先的桌面 AI Agent 管理器。它为单人公司 / 独立开发者提供统一的 AI 数字员工管理平台 —— 从 Agent 创建、任务编排、多引擎接入，到消息渠道集成、工作流自动化和专家团协作，一站式覆盖。

cls.summary: OPC-Nexus is a local-first Electron desktop application for creating, orchestrating and managing AI agents and automated workflows targeted at solo studios and small teams.
cls.what_it_does: It provides a desktop workbench (Quest/Hermes) to create AI 'digital employees', plan and approve tasks, and dispatch work to multiple execution engines (Codex, Claude, Pi, Hermes workers, Android workers). Notable features include project-scoped runtimes, secure storage of provider API keys, audit/approval workflows and multi-engine integration for end-to-end agent orchestration.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository shows a packaged desktop release (v2.0.1), CI that runs typechecks, unit tests and smoke checks, and prepared runtime artifacts; however the project is only ~109 days old so it lacks long-term production track record needed for TRL 7+.
student_project_ideas: Create an automated CI task pipeline using OPC-Nexus agents to run unit tests, build artifacts and publish test reports for a student software project, and evaluate the reliability and audit logs of automated deliveries.

Integrate OPC-Nexus with a cloud LLM provider and an Android worker to prototype an end-to-end autonomous assistant that performs a small hardware test workflow (e.g., trigger remote tests and collect screenshots/logs) and document security / provenance concerns.

tools.name: Exploit-Garbage/0day-Rubbish
tools.desc: Redefining vulnerability disclosure in the AI era. We mass-produce exploitable 0days and disclose them directly, using event-driven pressure to elevate vendor security standards and advance the field.

cls.summary: A public, AI-assisted project that discovers, validates and publishes working proof-of-concept 0-day vulnerabilities and technical advisories for real-world software and devices.
cls.what_it_does: The repository documents an automated, LLM-supported pipeline that scans software, produces candidate vulnerabilities, manually verifies findings and publishes full advisories including PoC exploit code. It is used as a reporting/disclosure channel and as a dataset of recent high-impact vulnerabilities; what makes it notable is the combination of multi-LLM discovery plus weekly direct publication of working exploits.
cls.trl_rationale: The project is active and popular (241 stars) and documents an operational disclosure process, but the repository is only ~139 days old (<1 year) so it lacks the multi-year production track record and formal releases needed for TRL 6+.
prerequisites: familiarity with Linux and command-line tools
knowledge of exploit development and PoC testing
understanding of legal and ethical constraints for vulnerability research
student_project_ideas: In a controlled lab, reproduce a single disclosed PoC on an isolated VM and write a short report identifying the root cause and proposing a code-level mitigation.
Mine the advisories to categorise common vulnerability patterns across embedded IoT devices and produce detection signatures for a host-based IDS.

tools.name: ros-claw/rosclaw
tools.desc: Physical AI runtime for embodied agents — governed action, verified experience, physical memory, and skill evolution.

cls.summary: ROSClaw is an open-source runtime that mediates between AI agents and physical robots, providing governed action execution, evidence-bearing execution receipts, and mechanisms for memory and skill evolution.
cls.what_it_does: ROSClaw turns high-level agent intent into governed physical actions on robots or simulators, verifies outcomes, records evidence for memory/skill pipelines, and supports asynchronous evolution of skills. It sits above ROS 2, simulators and vendor SDKs and exposes a runtime that enforces policy, resource arbitration, action leases and verifiable execution receipts.
cls.trl_rationale: The README and maturity section explicitly describe the project as alpha with many component- and system-level verifications but remaining experimental/hardware acceptance tasks; the repository is ~8 months old so it cannot be judged beyond beta/early production (TRL≤6).
prerequisites: Optional simulator knowledge (MuJoCo) and GL backend for rendering
student_project_ideas: Integrate a simple agent with ROSClaw and a simulated UR5e in MuJoCo to implement a verified pick-and-place loop that emits and analyses ExecutionReceipts for V&V.
Extend ROSClaw by adding a small hardware gateway driver for a low-cost mobile base and demonstrate governed action and receipt verification across simulator and real robot transitions.

tools.name: jeantimex/threejs-water
tools.desc: A real-time water simulation with Three.js, featuring raytraced reflections, refractions, caustics, and interactive objects.

cls.summary: A Three.js-based real-time water demo that simulates waves, reflections/refractions, caustics and simple buoyant objects for interactive web scenes.
cls.what_it_does: This project provides a GPU-based water simulation and shader set for Three.js, implementing wave propagation, Fresnel reflection/refraction, caustics and simple gravity/buoyancy for objects. It is used as a web demo or visualization component by loading GLTF models and Three.js geometries into a scene with interactive water effects, and is notable for porting Evan Wallace's WebGL Water to Three.js with extended pool shapes and SDF-based ray intersections.
cls.trl_rationale: The repository is a polished, actively maintained port with a live demo, 239 stars and working examples, indicating a beta-level project; however it is new (<1 year old, created 2026-06-22) so it lacks the multi-year track record or broad production users required for TRL 7+.
student_project_ideas: Create a web-based interactive coastal visualization that loads real coastline geometry (GeoJSON) and uses the water simulation to demonstrate wave interactions with obstacles, comparing qualitative behaviours when changing buoyancy and wave parameters.

Integrate a simple hydrodynamics experiment: export object forces from the simulation and use them to drive a data-logging dashboard (e.g. plot buoyant force vs time) to study stability of floating shapes.

tools.name: Yamz-Labs/kyojin
tools.desc: Kyojin: open-source engine that runs 100 GB-class open models (GLM-5.3, Qwen3.8, DeepSeek V4.1) on one desktop machine. AMD Strix Halo, NVIDIA RTX and Apple Mac. OpenAI API, built on ExLlamaV3.

cls.summary: Kyojin is an open-source inference engine for running very large (100+ GB-class) language models locally on desktop GPUs (AMD ROCm, NVIDIA CUDA, and Apple Silicon).
cls.what_it_does: Kyojin serves large open LLMs from local model packs (Hugging Face) via an OpenAI-compatible API and supports long-context speculative decoding optimisations. It is used by building platform-specific binaries (ROCm/CUDA/macOS) and launching a local server; notable features include support for extremely long contexts, image inputs for some models, and tuning/optimisations for AMD RDNA and NVIDIA GPUs.
cls.trl_rationale: The repository is active, well-documented and has community contributors and benchmarks, indicating early adopters; however it is only 46 days old so by the TRL rules it should be considered at most alpha in use (TRL 5).
prerequisites: GPU platform knowledge (ROCm or CUDA) and drivers
basic Python and Hugging Face model workflow
student_project_ideas: Benchmark and compare throughput/latency of a chosen large model served by Kyojin across two GPU targets (ROCm vs CUDA), report on trade-offs and memory/context scaling.
Integrate a Kyojin-served model with a simple robot or IoT device (ROS node or MQTT client) to prototype an on-premise natural-language interface without cloud APIs.

tools.name: outfox/2dog
tools.desc: 2dog is Godot in .NET 🦴

cls.summary: 2dog packages the Godot engine as a library your .NET application hosts so you can run Godot projects from dotnet on desktop, web (WASM) and inside .NET UIs or test frameworks.
cls.what_it_does: 2dog wraps a modified libgodot so .NET applications can load and host the Godot engine, letting developers run existing Godot projects via dotnet, in browsers (WASM), inside desktop .NET UIs, and under xUnit/NUnit. It is distributed as precompiled NuGet packages and GitHub releases and includes build recipes and tooling to produce platform-specific native packages.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository is under one year old (311 days) so TRL is capped; however the project provides precompiled NuGet packages, GitHub Releases, CI-driven build recipes, documentation site and active pushes, which supports a beta-level (TRL 6) maturity rather than an early prototype.
prerequisites: uv/poe build tooling and optional Nushell
student_project_ideas: Create an interactive digital-twin-style visualization of a simple robot arm by running a Godot scene from a .NET host, adding UI controls in .NET to send commands and log telemetry to a CSV or MQTT broker.

Build an automated test harness that runs headless Godot scenes under xUnit/NUnit via the 2dog host to validate simulation scenarios and capture regression screenshots or output data for verification.

tools.name: giannisanni/pulsar
tools.desc: SSD-streaming inference engine for giant MoE models (Rust + CUDA). GLM 5.2 743B at 2 tok/s and Hy3 295B at 7 tok/s on two consumer 16GB GPUs. Zero-config multi-GPU: measures PCIe bandwidth, places attention and hot experts where they fit.

cls.summary: Pulsar is a Rust + CUDA inference engine that streams experts from NVMe to run very large mixture-of-experts (MoE) language models on consumer GPUs.
cls.what_it_does: Pulsar lets you run huge MoE LLMs by keeping routing and control state in GPU memory while streaming rarely-used expert weights from NVMe per token, enabling multi-GPU zero-config placement and high-throughput decoding on consumer hardware. It is used as a local inference runtime for many modern MoE architectures and is notable for supporting many model formats, automatic multi-GPU placement and SSD-streaming of experts.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository is 127 days old (<1 year) so it cannot be judged as long-track production, but it shows substantial capability (many supported large models, benchmark tables, active commits and issues) consistent with a beta-level, usable inference engine.
prerequisites: Linux GPU environment and NVMe storage
experience with LLM model formats (gguf) and quantization concepts
student_project_ideas: Measure end-to-end latency and token throughput of a mid-sized MoE gguf model on a 2×16GB consumer GPU rig using Pulsar and compare SSD-streaming vs fully-resident runs.
Integrate Pulsar as a backend for a simple chatbot web front-end and implement instrumentation to visualise where experts are resident (GPU vs NVMe) during a long-context conversation.

tools.name: makezur/agenticSTAR
tools.desc: AgentSTAR: Agentic Shape Tracking and Reconstruction from Monocular Videos

cls.summary: AgentSTAR is a harness that uses coding LLMs to build, pose and iteratively refine articulated 3D object models from monocular video by scripting Blender and producing GLB meshes with per-frame poses.
cls.what_it_does: AgentSTAR drives a code-writing agent (e.g. Codex or Claude Code) to generate Blender scenes from video frames, declare jointed parts, render and compare against input frames, and iterate to produce a named-part GLB and per-frame pose/joint state JSON. It is notable because the agent writes and runs Blender scripts inside a sandbox and uses multi-pass render-and-compare sweeps plus temporal analysis to recover articulated shape and motion from monocular captures.
cls.trl_rationale: The README and examples show working runs and outputs (GLB, pose.json) and the repo provides installation and example capture data, indicating early real use; however the repository is only 68 days old so it lacks the longer track record, broad user base and stable releases needed for TRL 6+.
prerequisites: Anthropic/OpenAI API keys for models (Claude Code / Codex)
student_project_ideas: Adapt AgentSTAR to reconstruct and export articulated models of small robotic manipulators from lab-captured monocular video and validate joint angles against encoder ground truth.
Replace the external segmenter with a student-implemented mask model and measure the impact of mask quality on reconstruction accuracy, comparing results to a baseline like COLMAP or a NeRF pipeline.

tools.name: RustingStudio/RustingStrata
tools.desc: Pure-Rust inference engine for Qwen GGUF models (Qwen3 to Qwen3.8, dense and MoE up to 770B+). CUDA and Vulkan (NVIDIA, AMD), hybrid CPU+GPU experts, MTP speculative decoding, OpenAI and Anthropic compatible server. Up to ~1.7x llama.cpp decode on a 12 GB RTX 3060.

cls.summary: RustingStrata is a pure‑Rust local inference engine for Qwen GGUF large models that runs on CPU, CUDA or Vulkan and can host an OpenAI/Anthropic‑compatible server locally.
cls.what_it_does: It provides high‑performance inference for Qwen family GGUF models (dense and mixture‑of‑experts) using Rust with on‑the‑fly CUDA kernel compilation and Vulkan support, allowing experts to run on CPU while GPU handles other work. It is used as a local LLM runtime and server (OpenAI/Anthropic compatible), notable for hybrid CPU+GPU expert placement, MTP speculative decoding and competitive decoding throughput versus llama.cpp.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository is very new (created 38 days ago) but shows working release binaries, benchmarks and documentation which demonstrates early real‑use alpha; age prevents higher TRL until there is a track record of wider adoption and stable releases.
prerequisites: Familiarity with GPU drivers (CUDA NVRTC or Vulkan) and model GGUF files
student_project_ideas: Measure and compare inference latency and throughput of a Qwen model on different GPUs (CUDA vs Vulkan) using RustingStrata and produce a report linking performance to VRAM, batch size and expert placement.

Integrate RustingStrata as a local OpenAI‑compatible backend with a simple robotics control simulation to evaluate using a local LLM for natural language command parsing and generate prompts/logs for safety analysis.

tools.name: developmentseed/deck.gl-raster
tools.desc: Client-side, WebGL2 GeoTIFF & Zarr visualization in deck.gl

cls.summary: A client-side TypeScript library that renders GeoTIFF, Cloud-Optimized GeoTIFF (COG) and Zarr raster data in the browser using deck.gl and WebGL2.
cls.what_it_does: deck.gl-raster lets web applications load large geospatial raster data (GeoTIFF/COG and Zarr) directly in the browser and render it on GPU using deck.gl layers and WebGL2, avoiding a server-side tiling/rendering step. It is used as a deck.gl plugin/renderer for high-performance visualisation of remote-sensed imagery and large raster datasets and is notable for fully client-side operation and demos that show multi-gigabyte COGs rendered in-browser.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository is actively maintained with documentation, demos and 237 stars, and shows practical client-side demos (including a large COG demo). It was created ~348 days ago (under one year), so while it appears beta-ready with releases and examples, it lacks the multi-year track record or wide ecosystem needed for TRL 7+.
prerequisites: familiarity with GeoTIFF/COG/Zarr and geospatial coordinate systems
student_project_ideas: Build a web viewer that overlays Sentinel-2 COGs and NDVI computations using deck.gl-raster and a simple UI to toggle bands and palettes.
Integrate deck.gl-raster with a time-series Zarr store to create an interactive in-browser animation of seasonal land-cover change for a regional study.

tools.name: ueboxai/uebox
tools.desc: Open-source AI agent that operates the Unreal Editor — levels, blueprints, materials, C++.

cls.summary: UE Box is an open-source AI agent that directly operates the Unreal Editor to create and modify levels, blueprints, materials, C++ and other Unreal assets.
cls.what_it_does: UE Box automates common Unreal Editor tasks (level design, blueprints including animation, materials including Substrate, C++, assets, UMG, Sequencer, terrain and PCG) by calling engine tools and verifying results via compile/run checks. It is used as a desktop app and plugin that connects to many LLM providers or local models, shows diffs of edits, supports goal-driven workflows and team/CLI modes, and can be integrated into CI or scripted workflows.
cls.trl_rationale: The project is actively developed, has releases and a usable Windows installer, and a detailed README, indicating early adoption; however the repository is only 61 days old so by the stated TRL rules its maturity is limited to TRL 5.
prerequisites: Unreal Engine (5.0–5.9) and familiarity with editor concepts (levels, blueprints, plugins)
API keys or access to LLM/model providers if using cloud models
student_project_ideas: Use UE Box to implement an automated testbench that spawns a vehicle in an Unreal level, runs PIE, collects telemetry/screenshots and evaluates a controller's performance against requirements (combine with a simple ROS 2 or socket-based controller).

Create a content-pipeline automation that uses UE Box to batch-import assets, generate materials and place prefabs procedurally in levels, then produce a report of changes and optimization suggestions for rendering performance.

tools.name: tanpreetjolly/browser-whisper
tools.desc: In-browser Whisper speech-to-text with WebGPU (WASM fallback). Transcribe audio & video locally, no server.

cls.summary: browser-whisper is a client-side library that transcribes audio and video in the browser using Whisper, Parakeet and other ASR runtimes with WebGPU (WASM fallback).
cls.what_it_does: The library performs speech-to-text locally in the browser: it decodes media files into 16 kHz mono chunks, runs an ASR model (Transformers.js, ONNX or parakeet.js) on WebGPU or WASM, and streams transcription segments back to the page. It is notable for running fully offline in-browser, caching model weights in OPFS, and providing fallbacks for browsers without WebGPU or WebCodecs.
cls.trl_rationale: The project has extensive documentation, a live demo, examples, active commits and several hundred stars, indicating community interest and maturity; however the repository is only ~8 months old so it lacks the multi-year track record or broad production citations required for TRL 7+.
prerequisites: basic knowledge of WebAssembly / WebGPU / WebCodecs
understanding browser security headers (COOP/COEP) for threaded WASM
student_project_ideas: Build a prototype voice-controlled web dashboard that uses browser-whisper to transcribe spoken commands and triggers UI actions (combine with a small front-end framework and simple command parser).
Collect and label short audio samples in the browser using browser-whisper to create a lightweight dataset for a downstream ML task (e.g. keyword spotting), then evaluate model performance offline.

tools.name: SeanWong17/Mammalia-tree
tools.desc: DeepTime Mammalia：交互式哺乳纲演化树，3D 螺旋序幕 + D3.js 动态时间树，跨越 2 亿年 | Interactive mammalian phylogeny with 3D spiral intro & D3.js dynamic timetree spanning 200 Myr

cls.summary: A browser-based interactive visualization that presents a 200 million year timetree of mammals with a Three.js 3D spiral intro and a D3.js dynamic evolutionary tree.
cls.what_it_does: This project renders an interactive, bilingual (Chinese/English) phylogenetic timetree of Mammalia in the browser using D3.js for the tree layout and Three.js (CSS3DRenderer + WebGL particles) for an immersive 3D spiral intro and visual effects. It is used as a science communication / education web-app (open static site or local dev server) notable for its combination of high-performance D3 tree layout, a cinematic CSS3D/particle intro, and responsiveness across desktop and mobile.
cls.trl_rationale: The repository is an almost one-year-old, polished browser project with a live demo, modular code, tests, and 235 stars indicating community interest; however the repo age (created ~339 days ago) is under one year so a conservative TRL 6 (beta) is appropriate rather than higher production ratings.
prerequisites: familiarity with D3.js or Three.js is helpful
student_project_ideas: Extend the tree data to add trait-based filtering and visualise trait evolution (e.g. body mass) by integrating the existing data.js with a small dataset and adding D3-driven color/size encodings.

Port the CSS3D spiral intro into a separate reusable WebGL/three.js component and benchmark performance (particle counts, frame rate) across desktop and mobile, producing a short report and optimisation patches.

tools.name: vibe-stack/ggez
tools.desc: a game framework for threejs for vibe coding maxxing

cls.summary: GGEZ is an opinionated monorepo framework and set of editor tools for building, authoring and running Three.js web games and interactive scenes.
cls.what_it_does: GGEZ provides a world editor, animation editor, orchestration app and runtime packages to author scenes, animation graphs and export runtime bundles for Three.js games. It is used locally (via Bun) to iterate on scenes and push exported content into a Three.js runtime, notable for combining editors, an orchestrator and runtime loaders in one monorepo.
cls.trl_rationale: The README explicitly states this is a public alpha and warns of breaking changes; the repo is 253 days old and shows active development and multiple apps/packages but no long track record or stable 1.0 releases, supporting an alpha-in-use TRL.
student_project_ideas: Build a web-based interactive digital twin prototype by authoring a small scene in GGEZ and loading the exported runtime bundle into a Three.js app that streams simple sensor data.

Create an animated robot demonstration: import a robot model into the GGEZ animation editor, author animation graphs for basic motions, export and integrate into a Three.js simulation that visualises motion planning output.

tools.name: AbrahamPaulJ/nightmare-mobile
tools.desc: On-device, ComfyUI-style node graph for image/video diffusion on Android. Run MiniMax H3 and WAN 2.2 14B on the Qualcomm Hexagon NPU. SD1.5, SDXL, Flux, Z-Image, Anima, Qwen Image 2.1, Krea 2 & MOSS Image. Inpainting, outpainting, ControlNet, LoRA, IP-Adapter & LivePortrait. Fully offline, no server, no account.

cls.summary: Nightmare Mobile is an Android app that provides a ComfyUI-style node graph for running image and video diffusion models entirely on-device, targeting Snapdragon phones with a Hexagon NPU.
cls.what_it_does: It lets users build node graphs on a phone to run text-to-image, image-to-image, inpainting, upscaling and text-to-video flows using local diffusion and DiT models; models are downloaded on demand and many runs execute on the Qualcomm Hexagon NPU or phone GPU/CPU. Notable points are its focus on fully offline operation, support for many quantised models (GGUF/MNN) and mobile-specific UI and performance tooling (NPU test, scheduler, tiled decoders).
cls.trl_rationale: The project provides downloadable APKs, a user guide, active releases and a visible user/tester base (stars, issues) indicating early real use; however the repository is only 71 days old so it lacks the multi-release, long-term track record required for higher TRL levels.
prerequisites: an arm64 Android phone (Snapdragon recommended) and knowledge of on-device model formats (GGUF/MNN)
student_project_ideas: Measure and compare performance and power use of the same diffusion model running on Hexagon NPU vs Adreno GPU vs CPU on a supported Snapdragon device and report implications for mobile deployment.
Build a simplified node-based Android app (using Jetpack Compose) that integrates a small quantised image model (GGUF/MNN) to demonstrate on-device inference and a minimal UI for nodes and outputs.

tools.name: kaichen-z/PAGE4D
tools.desc: [ICLR 2026] PAGE-4D: Disentangled Pose and Geometry Estimation for VGGT-4D Perception

cls.summary: PAGE-4D is a research codebase that infers camera poses, depth maps and dense point maps for dynamic multi-view scenes using a feed‑forward transformer-based model.
cls.what_it_does: PAGE-4D extends a visual-geometry transformer to dynamic 4D scenes, producing disentangled pose and geometry estimates (camera extrinsics/intrinsics, per-frame depth, dense point maps) directly from multi-view images without post-optimization. It is delivered as PyTorch code with training scripts, data-preparation helpers and visualization scripts for feature maps, intended for research and large-scale training on RGB-D / multi-view datasets.
cls.trl_rationale: The repository accompanies an ICLR 2026 paper and provides full training/evaluation scripts, dataset preparation and visualization code, showing a research-grade implementation; however it is younger than one year (created 248 days ago), so while mature for research use it lacks a long track record required for higher TRL.
student_project_ideas: Reproduce a subset of the paper's results using the provided data-preparation scripts and evaluate pose/depth accuracy on a single TUM RGB‑D sequence, comparing performance with COLMAP depth/pose where available.

Integrate PAGE-4D outputs with a simple ROS2 node to build a live point-cloud visualiser for multi-view dynamic scenes and compare reconstruction quality against a NeRF baseline on a small custom dataset.

tools.name: JosssphZhou/groki-bot
tools.desc: Groki Bot desktop robot (M5Stack CoreS3): firmware, a voice and MCP gateway for your computer, and a hand-off to Grok Bot agents

cls.summary: Groki Bot is an open-source firmware and desktop gateway for an M5Stack CoreS3 desktop robot that provides local voice, face-tracking and a bridge to Grok Bot agents.
cls.what_it_does: Groki Bot provides device firmware for an M5Stack CoreS3 robot plus a computer-side gateway that connects the robot to Grok Bot agents and native voice backends. It enables wake-word voice interaction, camera-based face tracking for dual-axis servo steering, expressive on-device animations, and web-based flashing/OTA for deployment. The notable parts are the integrated agent bridge (gateway) and local voice/wake-word handling to avoid requiring cloud voice APIs.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository is very new (created ~55 days ago) so by the policy TRL is capped at 5; the README shows a complete firmware+gateway and active commits/stars which indicate early adopters but no long production track record is documented.
prerequisites: basic command-line and environment setup on macOS (gateway)
student_project_ideas: Extend the Groki Bot firmware to add a sensor (e.g. ultrasonic rangefinder) and modify the gateway to stream sensor telemetry to a simple dashboard to demonstrate embedded-to-cloud pipelines.

Replace or augment the default voice backend by integrating an alternative LLM/voice stack (e.g. local LLM or another cloud model) and measure latency and privacy trade-offs during multimodal interaction.

tools.name: affifuddin-hazam/ghost-infer
tools.desc: Fast local LLM inference for the GPU you already have: one Rust binary, GGUF models, an OpenAI-compatible server and a chat page with a ghost.

cls.summary: ghost-infer is a single Rust binary that runs GGUF LLMs on consumer NVIDIA GPUs, provides an OpenAI-compatible local server and a desktop app for chatting and file-based agents.
cls.what_it_does: It enables fast local inference of GGUF-format large language models on NVIDIA consumer GPUs, using CUDA-optimised kernels and strategies (mixture-of-experts caching, speculative decoding) to run models larger than GPU memory. It exposes an OpenAI-compatible HTTP API for tooling and includes a Windows desktop app with file-agent and voice features so the model can work on local files and audio.
cls.trl_rationale: The project is very new (created 21 days ago) so lacks a long track record, but shows clear working binaries, a Windows installer, benchmarks and a release build which indicate early adopter usage (alpha in use) rather than a mere prototype.
prerequisites: CUDA toolkit (NVRTC) to build from source or use the provided Windows installer; Rust toolchain if compiling
student_project_ideas: Build an editor plugin that uses ghost-infer's OpenAI-compatible API to provide a code-review assistant that runs entirely locally and evaluate latency and privacy trade-offs versus a cloud LLM.
Integrate ghost-infer with a robotics simulation to run a local conversational agent that reads logs and suggests fixes, measuring throughput and GPU memory behaviour with long-context prompts.

tools.name: Stink-O/orbital-laser
tools.desc: A terrestrial orbital laser strike for Horizon: a custom shader, synthesized sounds and a driver that carves the crater.

cls.summary: A Horizon (Rust Minecraft rewrite) mod that lets players call down destructive orbital laser strikes which modify the game world.
cls.what_it_does: Orbital Laser is a game mod for Horizon that provides multiple selectable orbital weapons which produce visual and sound effects and permanently alter the Minecraft world by digging craters and tunnels. It is distributed as a native Horizon mod or as a WebAssembly fork build and includes custom shaders, synthesized sounds and code that edits terrain to create the strike effects. The project is notable for being written in Rust, providing both native and WASM mod variants, and shipping ready-built releases for Linux.
cls.trl_rationale: The repository is very new (26 days old) but already has ready-built releases, multiple features and user interest (233 stars) indicating early adopters; its short age prevents a higher TRL despite functioning builds.
prerequisites: On Linux: C compiler, pkg-config, ALSA and libudev development files

tools.name: SyntheticAutonomicMind/CLIO
tools.desc: An AI-assisted coding agent that runs in your terminal and supports many providers and models.

cls.summary: CLIO is a terminal-native AI coding agent that inspects a codebase, proposes and applies edits, runs tests and Git commands, and can use many cloud and local models.
cls.what_it_does: CLIO provides an extensible agent harness that runs in the terminal and automates end-to-end coding tasks: it reads and searches code, proposes a plan, edits files with undo support, runs tests and git operations, and stores session memory. It is used from the command line and supports many providers (cloud APIs and local models via llama.cpp/LM Studio) and integrates with terminal multiplexers and Docker for sandboxing.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository is active (created ~303 days ago) with many integrations, documented provider list and features, and steady commits; however it's younger than one year so lacks the multi-year track record and broad adoption needed for TRL 7+. README claims self-hosted use and active development which supports a beta-level maturity.
prerequisites: optional: Docker for sandboxing, llama.cpp or LM Studio for local models
student_project_ideas: Integrate CLIO into a small team's CI pipeline to automatically run targeted refactor tasks and report results, measuring how often its edits pass the project's test suite versus require human correction.
Build a course lab where students extend CLIO with a new provider adapter (e.g. a classroom LLM endpoint) and evaluate its performance on automated bug-fixing tasks in a toy codebase.

tools.name: jjang-ai/jangq
tools.desc: JANG — GGUF for MLX. YOU MUST USE JANG_Q RUNTIME. Adaptive Mixed-Precision Quantization + Runtime for Apple Silicon

cls.summary: JANG is an adaptive mixed-precision quantization format and runtime that lets large LLMs run efficiently on Apple Silicon (Metal) by producing GGUF-like quantised model files and a matching runtime.
cls.what_it_does: JANG provides tools and a runtime to convert HuggingFace models into JANG / JANGTQ mixed-precision quantised formats and run them at high performance on Apple Silicon using Metal. It targets very large models (MoE, hybrid attention, long-context) and emphasises keeping models quantised in GPU memory for speed and reduced RAM use; notable features include bfloat16 auto-detection, special support for routed MoE and hybrid attention, and an accompanying macOS GUI (MLX Studio) for conversion and verification.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository is active with many stars and recent commits and provides runnable tooling and a GUI, indicating beyond prototype; however it is under one year old (created 2026-03-15) so TRL is capped at 6 pending longer track record or widespread adoption.
prerequisites: familiarity with HuggingFace model formats and Python tooling
understanding of model quantization and LLM deployment
student_project_ideas: Benchmark and compare memory, throughput and quality (MMLU or other benchmarks) of a midsize model converted to JANG vs MLX and gguf on an Apple Silicon Mac.

Build a small local assistant that uses a JANG-quantized model (converted from HuggingFace) to aid systems-engineering tasks (requirements summarisation or traceability queries) and measure latency and cost benefits.

tools.name: andrisgauracs/whistle-esp32
tools.desc: Whistle speech-to-text running fully on an ESP32-S3: hold a button, say a colour in one of 7 languages, the LED does it. No network.

cls.summary: An on-device speech-to-text demo that runs the Whistle model fully on an ESP32-S3 to recognise colour commands and control an onboard RGB LED without any network.
cls.what_it_does: The repository ports an independent C99 implementation of the Whistle speech model to run entirely on an ESP32-S3 with PSRAM, capturing audio from an I²S microphone, performing on-device transcription and language detection, and mapping recognised colour/command phrases to LED actions. It is used as firmware built with ESP-IDF plus host tools to prepare and flash a trimmed model partition; notable points are the full offline inference on a $10 microcontroller and a tensor-by-tensor reimplementation of Whistle so no external runtime is required.
cls.trl_rationale: The README and repo show a working firmware, hardware wiring, build/flash instructions and host tools, and examples for running on real ESP32-S3 boards, indicating use beyond a minimal prototype. However the repository is only 29 days old so by the policy it should be capped at TRL 5 until a longer track record or broader production adoption is demonstrated.
prerequisites: basic embedded C and ESP32 toolchain experience
Python 3 for host tools and model preparation
familiarity with flashing tools (esptool) and I²S microphone wiring
student_project_ideas: Extend the demo to add new voice commands and a small state machine (e.g. brightness, colour sequences) and evaluate recognition accuracy across languages and SNR conditions, producing a report on robustness.

Integrate the ESP32 Whistle firmware with an MQTT client to publish recognised commands to a local broker and build a dashboard that visualises transcripts and timing for an operations sustainment exercise.

tools.name: GenshinmasterJinHang/Miku-Material-Converter-Blender-to-Unity-
tools.desc: Miku is an open-source material conversion pipeline that translates Blender 5.2 Shader Nodes into editable Unity 6 URP Shader Graph assets. Through its target-neutral MaterialIR 2.0 representation and deterministic .mikubundle workflow, Miku preserves material semantics, texture intent, and structured diagnostics across DCC and game-engine boundary

cls.summary: Miku is an open-source pipeline that converts Blender 5.x Shader Node materials into editable Unity 6 URP Shader Graph assets via a target‑neutral MaterialIR and deterministic .mikubundle workflow.
cls.what_it_does: Miku exports Blender materials to a target‑neutral MaterialIR 2.0 and produces deterministic .mikubundle packages that a Unity package imports as editable Shader Graph assets and material creators. It is used as a Blender add-on plus a Unity package to preserve material semantics and texture intent across DCC and game engine boundaries, with bundled experimental game‑toon shader presets.
cls.trl_rationale: The project is actively released (v3.0.0), provides installable ZIP/TGZ packages, detailed manuals and a validated compatibility matrix, and has community interest (stars). However the repository is only ~108 days old so it lacks a long track record required for TRL 7+.
prerequisites: Basic Unity/URP and Shader Graph knowledge
student_project_ideas: Create a small asset pipeline that exports a set of Blender materials as .mikubundle, imports them into a Unity URP project, and documents texture/bake differences for a visualization study.

Extend or adapt one of Miku's experimental Game Toon presets to implement custom shading (e.g. a simplified technical illustration style) and measure shader performance and visual fidelity across target devices.

tools.name: Jelatine/mockway_robotics
tools.desc: 开源六轴协作机械臂系统，包含机械结构、电路和软件

cls.summary: An open-source 6-axis collaborative robot project providing mechanical designs, electronics BOM and ROS2/MoveIt software to run, simulate and control the arm.
cls.what_it_does: Mockway_robotics supplies a full-stack open robot: parametric CAD models, parts list and firmware/software to run a six-degree-of-freedom collaborative arm. It is used with ROS2 and MoveIt2 for motion planning and includes examples for torque compensation, motor debugging, mock hardware simulation and a MoveIt demo; notable points are tight integration with Pinocchio for dynamics and JellyCAD for parametric CAD sources.
cls.trl_rationale: The repository contains complete hardware BOMs, assembly guides, build and run instructions for ROS2/MoveIt, and example scripts indicating an installable project used by others; however the project is under one year old (created 2025-12-25) so lacks the longer production track record required for TRL 7+, limiting it to TRL 6.
prerequisites: basic Linux command-line, Python and CAN hardware knowledge
student_project_ideas: Build the mockway arm in simulation (use_mock_hardware:=true) and implement a MoveIt-based pick-and-place task with a simple vision pipeline (e.g. OpenCV) to locate parts.

Use the provided dynamics and realtime torque compensation scripts to measure, log and compare computed vs measured joint torques, then tune controller damping and demonstrate improved gravity compensation performance.

tools.name: devnen/qwen3.6-windows-server
tools.desc: One-click Qwen3.6-27B inference on Windows. 158 tok/s on RTX 5090, 72 tok/s on RTX 3090. Native, no WSL, no Docker, no telemetry.

cls.summary: A portable Windows launcher that serves Qwen3.6‑27B locally with an OpenAI‑compatible API and pre-tuned snapshot configs for single‑click inference.
cls.what_it_does: Provides a one‑click Textual TUI launcher that unpacks a patched vLLM wheel and runs Qwen3.6‑27B on native Windows, exposing an OpenAI‑compatible HTTP API for local inference. It bundles measured configuration 'snapshots' tuned for various GPU/context tradeoffs (single and multi‑GPU) and focuses on no‑WSL, no‑Docker, offline privacy and reproducible performance numbers.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository is ~200 days old with substantial stars and measured benchmarks and a working launcher, indicating a beta‑level, usable project; however it is younger than one year and lacks long track record or enterprise adoption evidence for TRL 7+.
prerequisites: Windows 10/11 with supported NVIDIA GPU (drivers installed)
Enough GPU VRAM for chosen snapshot (e.g. 24 GB for RTX 3090)
Basic familiarity with running packaged Windows apps and opening a local HTTP API endpoint
student_project_ideas: Measure and compare inference throughput and context‑window behaviour across the provided snapshots on different GPUs and produce a short report linking hardware, driver settings and observed tok/s.

Integrate the local OpenAI‑compatible API into a simple robotics simulation pipeline to test on‑device prompt engineering for a control or natural language interface component (combine with a simulated robot in Gazebo or a small ROS node).

tools.name: lemonadesaltbagel/airlock
tools.desc: A privacy-first local coding agent that consults frontier AI models without exposing your source code.

cls.summary: Airlock is a privacy-first local coding agent that runs on your machine, scrubs and rewrites questions as minimal examples, and asks cloud 'consultant' models only after deterministic gating and your approval.
cls.what_it_does: Airlock runs a local agent that edits and tests code inside an OS sandbox and, when stuck, rewrites the technical question into a small anonymised example before sending it to a cloud model as a consult. It enforces deterministic gates, crown-jewel blocking, and an approval workflow so sensitive project identifiers and secrets are prevented from leaving the workstation.
cls.trl_rationale: The repo is very new (created 24 days ago) and the README states 'Status: preview' and warns against production use; there is active development and community interest (stars/forks) but no long track record, so maturity is limited to alpha/early-use (TRL 5).
prerequisites: local OpenAI-compatible model server (e.g. llama-server) and optionally a cloud API key for consults
student_project_ideas: Integrate Airlock with an existing local LLM server (llama-server) and evaluate how often consults are triggered on a small test repository, measuring privacy leakage risk by attempting to trigger the gate with synthetic crown-jewel terms.
Extend Airlock's deterministic gate to add a custom corporate policy (e.g. additional regex-based secrets) and run a lab exercise comparing false positives/negatives against a baseline scrubber.

tools.name: skaft-software/octet
tools.desc: fast rust coding agent, extensible in any language, multimodal inputs, deep provider integrations.

cls.summary: Octet is a native, Rust-based terminal coding agent that runs local or cloud models, manages sessions and extensions, and accepts multimodal inputs like audio.
cls.what_it_does: Octet runs a persistent agent loop in a single native Rust process to read and edit code, run tests, manage sessions and invoke external tool extensions via JSON-RPC. It supports local and cloud LLMs, native audio input, resumable sessions, and language-agnostic extensions that run as subprocesses, making it notable for its low resource footprint and extensible architecture.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository is 130 days old with multiple releases (v0.10.4), signed release artifacts, installation scripts, SDKs and documentation which indicate a beta-quality project; age < 1 year prevents assigning higher TRL without long-term production track record.
prerequisites: git and building Rust projects (cargo) for source builds
optional: Node.js for Pi-compat adapter and some extension bundles
student_project_ideas: Build a custom octet extension in Python that runs static analysis (flake8/clang-tidy) on edited files and integrates results into octet sessions.
Create an experiment comparing developer workflow latency and resource use between octet running a local LLM and a cloud LLM for an automated refactoring task, and report trade-offs.

tools.name: Nikolay-Tyulkin/Watti
tools.desc: A desk lamp that's learning to be more than a lamp

cls.summary: Watti is a prototype motorised desk lamp with an RGB‑D camera and a web-based scene editor (Watti Studio) that plays timed light+motion scenes on a Raspberry Pi.
cls.what_it_does: Watti combines a five-joint motorised lamp, a depth camera and a 45‑LED ring to run coordinated light and motion scenes sent from a web editor. The lamp plays scenes locally on a Raspberry Pi at 25 Hz for robust playback and the project emphasises camera-driven behaviours (hand tracking, workspace lighting) and procedural animation. Notable points are the integrated RGB‑D sensing, on‑device playback of complete scenes, and a visual scene editor for non‑firmware authoring.
cls.trl_rationale: The repository documents a working hardware prototype with videos and a web studio, but the source code is not yet published and the project is described as a prototype; the repo is also only ~107 days old, so demonstrated community production use and stable releases are not present.
prerequisites: familiarity with RGB‑D sensors and basic computer vision
web development fundamentals for Watti Studio
student_project_ideas: Build a hand-tracking routine that runs on the lamp's RGB‑D camera to keep a defined workspace region brightly lit, and evaluate latency and reliability compared with a software-only simulation.
Design and implement a simple motion+light scene authoring workflow that exports to the lamp's scene format and add automatic safety limits for joint motion using a Raspberry Pi and mock actuators.

tools.name: Deno2026/comfyui-deno-custom-nodes
tools.desc: ComfyUI custom nodes for RTX Video Super Resolution, NVIDIA VFX/nvvfx, LTX 2.3, Bernini Prompt Guide, Wan2.2 reference video edit, image/video compare, video preview, loaders, resize, and visual workflow helpers.

cls.summary: A collection of custom ComfyUI nodes that streamline image and video production workflows (loading, resizing, comparing, model loaders, NVIDIA VSR and other media helpers) for ComfyUI users.
cls.what_it_does: This repository provides many practical ComfyUI nodes to prepare inputs, control generation, compare results, and finish images and videos (including RTX Video Super Resolution and tiled upscalers). Users install the package into ComfyUI and add nodes on the canvas to perform tasks like multi-image loading, resize/crop with preview, A/B video compare, local-LLM prompts, and NVIDIA VFX integrations. It is notable for covering an end-to-end production loop with many specialised nodes (video preview, tiled samplers, model/LoRA loaders) and for active releases and multilingual docs.
cls.trl_rationale: The repo is active (created 215 days ago) with many stars, frequent releases and an up-to-date changelog, indicating more than an experimental prototype but still younger than one year; evidence supports a beta-level maturity (versioned releases, install via ComfyUI Manager, supported integrations) rather than long-term production ubiquity.
prerequisites: Python runtime (ComfyUI environment) and browser access
NVIDIA GPU for RTX VSR nodes and PyAV for video preview where required
student_project_ideas: Build a ComfyUI workflow that loads a video, applies tiled upscaling and RTX Video Super Resolution nodes, and produces a lossless comparison output to evaluate quality vs. a baseline pipeline.
