Create an automated prompt-and-review workflow using the Local LLM Loader and Image/Video Compare nodes to generate variations, rate them with a local LLM, and export the best results as an assignment demo.

tools.name: panxinmiao/myth
tools.desc: A High-Performance Rendering Engine for Rust

cls.summary: Myth is a cross-platform, high-performance 3D rendering engine in Rust that targets native and WebGPU platforms and provides PBR, advanced post-processing and glTF support.
cls.what_it_does: Myth provides a Rust API and runtime for real-time 3D rendering using wgpu, including physically based rendering, clustered forward lighting, post-processing (SSGI, SSR, SSAO) and built-in support for 3D Gaussian Splatting and glTF assets. It is used by embedding the engine in Rust applications or compiling to WASM for the web, and also exposes Python bindings for prototyping and visualization.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository is active (~317 days old), has examples, a live demo, Python bindings and ~227 stars which indicates community interest; however it is younger than one year so lacks the multi-year track record and wide adoption required for TRL 7+.
prerequisites: basic GPU / graphics concepts (rendering pipeline, PBR)
student_project_ideas: Build a web-deployable scene viewer for engineering CAD exports by loading glTF models into Myth, adding lighting and camera controls, and measuring visual fidelity of PBR materials.
Integrate Myth's Python bindings with a simulation pipeline (e.g., a dynamics simulator) to visualise time-series pose data in real time and record rendered frames for analysis.

tools.name: kaltwrk/spektral
tools.desc: Minimalist framework for modern WebGPU visuals.

cls.summary: Spektral is a small WebGPU runtime for fullscreen WGSL shaders with framework adapters for Svelte, React and Vue, aimed at shader-driven visuals and GPU compute in the browser.
cls.what_it_does: Spektral provides a minimal, framework-neutral runtime that manages the canvas, render loop, GPU resources and scheduling so you can author fullscreen WGSL materials, render/feedback/compute passes and update uniforms/textures easily. It is used as an alternative to full 3D engines when the project focuses on shader-driven visuals, generative art, procedural textures or GPU-based post-processing.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository is 262 days old (<1 year) so maturity is recent; it has substantial documentation, framework adapters, a playground and ongoing commits which supports a beta-level TRL (6) but not long-term production track record yet.
prerequisites: browser with WebGPU support and secure context (HTTPS or localhost)
student_project_ideas: Build an interactive browser demonstrator that visualises CFD/flow-field data by writing WGSL shaders to render fullscreen slices or procedural textures, using Spektral for rendering and a simple server to stream data.

Create a generative-art system that encodes parameterised design variations (e.g. topology-like patterns) into GPU compute passes and exposes controls via a React or Svelte UI using Spektral's adapters.

tools.name: Sudharsanselvaraj/Token-Print
tools.desc: Interactive 3D visualization platform for exploring transformer architectures, tensors, and real-time LLM inference.

cls.summary: TokenPrint is an open-source 3D visual debugger that runs real transformer forward passes and shows attention, KV cache, residual streams and other per-layer tensors in an interactive WebGL/WebGPU interface.
cls.what_it_does: TokenPrint loads real transformer models (local GGUF, browser ONNX/GPT-2 or a Python backend) and visualises per-token tensors, attention patterns, RoPE, KV caches and timings in an interactive 3D scene. It is used as a debugging and inspection tool for model developers and researchers, notable for running real (not simulated) forward passes, CI-backed numeric fidelity, and an integrated frontend+backend for live or recorded traces.
cls.trl_rationale: The project is active, well-documented, has a live demo, CI checks, many stars and contributors, and provides runnable backend/frontend instructions; however the repo is only ~4 months old (123 days) so there is limited long-term production track record, placing it at Beta (TRL 6).
prerequisites: familiarity with transformer models and ML concepts
experience running local models or using GGUF/ONNX
student_project_ideas: Extend TokenPrint to visualise the effect of pruning or weight quantization by comparing traces from a full and a quantized GGUF model and reporting per-layer metric changes.

Integrate TokenPrint traces with an automated testbench that runs synthetic inputs to detect and visualise regression in attention patterns after model fine-tuning (combine with a simple CI runner and diff-reporting).

tools.name: Nathanw1014/strix-halo-llamacpp
tools.desc: Performance-tuned llama.cpp for AMD Strix Halo (gfx1151): FA + MoE-prefill fixes with a bundled current Mesa driver. Vulkan and HIP; portable dir, Docker, and distrobox.

cls.summary: A performance-tuned distribution of llama.cpp that accelerates long-context, quantized KV inference on the AMD Strix Halo (gfx1151) using Vulkan/HIP and bundled driver fixes.
cls.what_it_does: This repository provides a ready-to-run, hardware-tuned build of llama.cpp that applies flash-attention and MoE-prefill fixes plus KV-contiguization to improve prefill throughput on AMD Strix Halo GPUs. It is used by building or running the provided Docker/distrobox images and running local LLM inference; notable aspects are the bundled Mesa driver, Vulkan/HIP optimisations, and an evidence pack of benchmarks showing large speedups for deep-context workloads.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository is 114 days old (under one year) but shows substantive engineering work: many stars, benchmarking evidence, Docker packaging and a runnable payload; however it lacks long-term production adoption or multiple stable releases required for TRL 7+, so a beta-level TRL 6 is appropriate.
prerequisites: familiarity with building native C/C++ projects (make/cmake)
Linux with GPU driver support (Vulkan/RADV/HIP) and AMD Strix Halo or compatible RDNA3 hardware
Docker or distrobox for the provided run environments
student_project_ideas: Measure and reproduce the repository's benchmark results on Strix Halo hardware, then extend the tests to additional models (e.g., other quantisation formats) and present profiling results and optimisation targets.

Integrate this tuned llama.cpp build into a small edge inference pipeline (Docker image + microservice) that serves a quantized model and compare latency/throughput across deployment configurations (driver versions, batch sizes, KV quantisation).

tools.name: AashishH15/Lexicon
tools.desc: The free open source offline writing assistant assist with grammar, rewriting & tone entirely on your machine.

cls.summary: Lexicon is a local-first, offline desktop rich-text editor and writing assistant that provides proofreading, rewrites and tone transforms using bundled local AI models or a local Ollama server.
cls.what_it_does: Lexicon helps users proofread, rewrite, format and export documents without sending text to cloud services; it offers inline grammar checks via LanguageTool and optional local LLM transforms (rewrite, tone, summary, etc.) using a bundled llama.cpp backend or an existing Ollama server. It is delivered as a packaged desktop app for Windows, macOS and Linux and can also be run from source for development.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository is 125 days old with packaged releases (installers) and active development plus a few hundred stars, showing a usable beta-level product; its age (<1 year) and limited track-record constrain it to TRL 6 rather than production-ready.
prerequisites: Node.js, npm, Python 3 and Java (to run from source / LanguageTool)
student_project_ideas: Compare output quality and privacy trade-offs by integrating Lexicon with different local LLMs (bundled llama.cpp vs Ollama) and evaluate performance on drafting technical requirements.
Extend Lexicon with an export plugin that formats editor content into a requirements template (Markdown or SysML-friendly) and preserves traceability metadata for small team workflows.

tools.name: plaxtoris/codehamr
tools.desc: A minimal, local-first coding agent for the terminal.

cls.summary: codehamr is a small terminal-based coding agent that drives local or remote LLMs to inspect and modify a project's files using shell and simple file tools.
cls.what_it_does: codehamr connects to a configurable model endpoint (local model server or API provider) and exposes four tools (bash, read_file, write_file, edit_file) so the agent can read your code, run shell commands, make changes, and report results. It is used from the terminal in a project directory and is notable for its local-first design, streaming Responses API support, and simple installer releases.
cls.trl_rationale: The project is active, has binary releases and installers and a substantial star count which indicates an engaged user base; however the repository is only ~6–7 months old so it lacks a longer track record required for TRL 7+. README documents usage and CI/go.mod exist supporting a beta-level maturity.
prerequisites: comfort with the Unix terminal and shell
knowledge of local model servers or API usage (LLM concepts)
Go toolchain for development or building from source
student_project_ideas: Create a lab where students connect codehamr to a local small LLM (e.g. Ollama) and task the agent with automated refactoring of a small codebase, measuring changes and running test suites to verify correctness.
Build an integration that uses codehamr to generate unit tests for an embedded firmware repository and run those tests in CI, then evaluate the quality of generated tests and failure detection.

tools.name: hanxiao/knowledge-graph-extractor
tools.desc: Turn any document or a whole zip into an interactive knowledge graph, using a self-hosted Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-MTP on a single NVIDIA L4

cls.summary: A self-hosted pipeline that extracts (subject, predicate, object) triples from documents and visualises them as an interactive force-directed knowledge graph, using a local LLM and CPU semantic deduplication.
cls.what_it_does: The tool ingests text, URLs or zipped documents, streams atomic subject–predicate–object triples from a local LLM, deduplicates facts with a CPU embedding model, and displays the results in an interactive force-directed graph in a web UI. It is used by running the provided Docker setup (requires an NVIDIA L4 or similar GPU) and is notable for supporting large local Qwen models, job persistence/resume, and streaming extraction into a graph structure.
cls.trl_rationale: The repository is a working, containerised project with a live demo, installation scripts and active commits, showing a usable beta-quality system; however it is younger than one year (created ~174 days ago) so there is limited long-term production track record.
prerequisites: NVIDIA L4 (or similar GPU) with ~24GB VRAM
Hugging Face/Jina API key for some readers
student_project_ideas: Build a requirements-traceability demo: ingest project documents (specs, meeting notes) and extend the pipeline to tag and filter extracted triples by requirement priority and map them to test cases stored in a CSV.
Integrate the extractor output with Neo4j: convert the JSONL facts into a Neo4j import pipeline and implement simple graph queries to find conflicting requirements or missing links across documents.

tools.name: Dhaiwat10/cricket07-browser
tools.desc: EA Sports Cricket 07 (2006) running in the browser: every function statically recompiled from x86 to C, then WebAssembly, with Direct3D 8 rebuilt on WebGPU. Bring your own copy.

cls.summary: A static recompile of EA Sports Cricket 07 that runs the original Windows executable in the browser by translating x86 code to C and compiling to WebAssembly with Direct3D 8 reimplemented on WebGPU.
cls.what_it_does: This project translates a game's x86 executable into C (via automated translation from Ghidra), compiles that to WebAssembly with Emscripten, and provides browser host shims that reimplement Direct3D8 on WebGPU, DirectSound on Web Audio and DirectInput via browser events so the original game runs in a browser tab. It is notable for performing a full static recompilation of tens of thousands of functions and for re-creating Windows graphics/audio/IO APIs on the web rather than emulating the OS.
cls.trl_rationale: The README documents a working build and run workflow, a browser demo, and detailed toolchain requirements, indicating early adopters can build and use it; however the repository is only 32 days old so it lacks a longer track record and wider production use that would justify TRL 6+.
prerequisites: a legal copy of Cricket 07 (game files)
student_project_ideas: Use the project's translator pipeline to statically recompile a small, open-source x86 Windows demo and compare the generated WebAssembly performance against native execution.
Measure and profile the Direct3D-to-WebGPU translation performance by instrumenting the host WebGPU command replay and produce optimisations or a report on shader translation costs.

tools.name: JorisAR/gaussian-point-splatting
tools.desc: Official implementation of Gaussian point splatting (SIGGRAPH'26)

cls.summary: An open-source CUDA C++ implementation of the SIGGRAPH 2026 'Gaussian Point Splatting' renderer for interactive display of hundreds of millions of Gaussian points from captured 3D scenes.
cls.what_it_does: This project implements a stochastic GPU renderer that displays very large Gaussian-point representations of scenes interactively by sampling and splatting pixel-sized opaque Gaussians and using stochastic transparency to avoid sorting. It is used by building and running a CUDA/OpenGL executable against trained Gaussian models or 3DGS output folders, and is notable for achieving interactive frame rates on consumer RTX GPUs while handling hundreds of millions of points.
cls.trl_rationale: The repository provides a complete implementation, build instructions, example scenes and command-line usage, and accompanies a SIGGRAPH 2026 paper, indicating a mature prototype; however the repo is under 1 year old (≈211 days), so there is limited long-term production track record.
student_project_ideas: Integrate a small photogrammetry capture pipeline (e.g., COLMAP) to produce a point cloud, convert it to the Gaussian format and benchmark rendering performance and memory usage for scenes of increasing scale.
Extend the renderer to add a simple temporal filtering or denoising pass (CPU or CUDA) and evaluate image quality vs. frame time trade-offs on different GPUs.

tools.name: dandacompany/deskrpg
tools.desc: Self-hosted 3D virtual office for Hermes Agent — your profiles become AI employees who sit at desks, chat, hold meetings, work kanban cards and run cron jobs, while your team shares the office in real time.

cls.summary: DeskRPG is a self-hosted 3D virtual office where Hermes Agent profiles act as AI employees that sit at desks, chat, hold meetings, manage kanban cards and run scheduled jobs.
cls.what_it_does: DeskRPG provides a multiplayer three.js-powered virtual office that connects to a Hermes gateway so AI agent profiles appear as NPC employees who can speak, join meetings, operate kanban cards and run cron jobs. It is delivered as a web app with options for npm install, local development (SQLite or Postgres) or Docker/Hostinger one-click deployment, and focuses on social/operational interactions rather than providing an agent runtime itself. Notable features include multi-user real-time presence, meeting controls, kanban integration and Hermes plugin support.
cls.trl_rationale: The project is active, has a live website, an npm package and Hostinger one‑click deployment which indicate adoption beyond a demo; however the repository is only ~8 months old (under one year) so by the provided TRL rules it is best rated as Beta (TRL 6).
prerequisites: a running Hermes gateway to provide agent profiles
PostgreSQL or SQLite for local data
student_project_ideas: Build an HCI lab exercise that compares human–agent interaction metrics (response time, turn-taking, perceived helpfulness) between a text-only Hermes gateway interface and the DeskRPG 3D office front-end.
Integrate telemetry from DeskRPG (agent activity, kanban events) into a small digital‑twins dashboard using a time-series database (Prometheus or InfluxDB) and visualise office activity over time.

tools.name: HackMan3D/HackMan3D-Orbit-Controller
tools.desc: Open-source, fully 3D-printable 6-DOF controller for CAD and slicer navigation, powered by an Arduino Pro Micro and Hall-effect joysticks.

cls.summary: HackMan3D Orbit Controller is an open-source, 3D-printable six-degrees-of-freedom hardware controller that provides native 3D-mouse input for CAD and optional mouse-emulation for slicers, driven by an Arduino Pro Micro and hall-effect joysticks.
cls.what_it_does: The project supplies printable parts, electronics bill-of-materials, wiring diagrams, assembly guides and firmware to build a 6-DOF navigation controller for CAD and slicing software. It is used by printing the enclosure, assembling hall-effect joysticks and an ATmega32U4-based Pro Micro, and uploading provided Arduino firmware to present as a 3Dconnexion-style HID or as a mouse; notable points are full 3D-printability, contactless hall-effect sensing and configurable speed/response profiles.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository is 139 days old (<1 year) so cannot be judged as long-term production but shows evidence of maturity: packaged releases, assembly guides, BOM, wiring diagrams, an assembly video and 222 stars which indicate active interest; these point to a beta-level, usable project (TRL 6) rather than long-term production (TRL 7+).
prerequisites: experience with Arduino IDE and uploading firmware
student_project_ideas: Modify the firmware to add a custom mapping profile and force-feedback-style haptic cues (via added vibration motor) and evaluate usability in a CAD task, comparing performance to a standard mouse.

Integrate the Orbit controller with a ROS-based simulation: publish controller HID inputs as ROS topics and use them to teleoperate a 6-DOF manipulator in Gazebo, demonstrating human-in-the-loop control and logging latency/precision metrics.

tools.name: opengeos/anymap-ts
tools.desc: A Python package for creating interactive maps with anywidget and mapping libraries using TypeScript

cls.summary: anymap-ts is a Python package that creates interactive web maps and 3D globes in Jupyter by bridging Python and multiple JavaScript mapping libraries (MapLibre/Mapbox, Leaflet, OpenLayers, DeckGL, Cesium, KeplerGL, Potree) using a TypeScript frontend and anywidget.
cls.what_it_does: It wraps several web mapping and 3D-visualisation libraries behind a consistent Python API so users can create, control and export interactive maps and point-cloud/3D-tile views from Jupyter notebooks. It is used by instantiating map objects (MapLibreMap, CesiumMap, PotreeViewer, etc.), adding basemaps and layers (GeoJSON, WMS, tiles, point clouds), and exporting to standalone HTML; notable is the bidirectional Python↔JavaScript communication via anywidget and TypeScript-based frontend for type safety.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository is active with a detailed README, multiple supported backends and 222 stars, indicating a usable beta-quality project; however it is under one year old (created 2026-01-07) so a conservative TRL of 6 (beta) is appropriate until longer production usage is demonstrated.
student_project_ideas: Build an interactive Jupyter-based digital twin viewer that overlays building floorplans (GeoJSON) and time-series sensor data on a Cesium globe using anymap-ts for visualization and a small Flask API to serve the data.

Create a LiDAR processing pipeline where students convert raw point clouds into Potree format and use anymap-ts PotreeViewer to visualise and classify point clusters, then export views to standalone HTML for reporting.

tools.name: ultralytics/inference
tools.desc: High-performance Ultralytics YOLO inference in Rust with ONNX Runtime, GPU backends, CLI, and WebGPU/WASM.

cls.summary: A high-performance Rust library and CLI for running Ultralytics YOLO ONNX models (detection, segmentation, depth, pose, classification) without Python, supporting CPU/GPU backends and WebAssembly/WebGPU.
cls.what_it_does: This project provides a pure-Rust inference runtime and command-line tool that loads Ultralytics YOLO ONNX models and runs detection, segmentation, depth estimation, pose and classification across images, video and streams. It is used either as a Rust library integrated into applications or as a standalone CLI, notable for supporting multiple ONNX Runtime backends (CUDA, TensorRT, XNNPACK, CoreML, OpenVINO) and WebGPU/WASM for browser deployment.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository is actively maintained by Ultralytics with many features, multi-backend support, automatic model download and a CLI, indicating beta-level maturity; however the repo age is ~356 days (under one year) which limits TRL to 6 under the guidance.
prerequisites: C build toolchain (compiler) and platform dev headers for building native crates
student_project_ideas: Build a robotics perception pipeline: integrate this Rust inference crate into a ROS2 node (or a simple ROS wrapper) to run YOLO detection on a robot camera stream and publish bounding boxes for downstream planning.
Create a browser-based demo: export a YOLO ONNX model and run real-time detection in the browser using the crate's WASM/WebGPU build to benchmark latency and compare CPU vs GPU backends.

tools.name: saurabhav88/EnviousWispr
tools.desc: Free, on-device AI dictation and meeting notes for macOS. Sub-second dictation with Parakeet and Whisper on Apple Silicon, plus optional AI polish. EnviousMeet (Beta): record calls with no bot, get who-said-what transcripts and AI summaries on your Mac. No account, no subscription, open source. Your audio never leaves your Mac.

cls.summary: EnviousWispr is an open‑source macOS app that does on‑device speech‑to‑text dictation and meeting recording/transcription with optional AI summaries, keeping audio and transcripts local to your Mac.
cls.what_it_does: EnviousWispr provides system‑wide keybind dictation and a meeting recorder (EnviousMeet) that captures call audio, performs speaker diarisation and produces transcripts + AI summaries, all running on the Mac (Apple Silicon) with optional external LLM/API integration. It is notable for on‑device Whisper and Parakeet transcriptions, privacy (audio and data remain local unless you opt to use cloud APIs), and integrations with common meeting apps and local LLM runtimes like Ollama.
cls.trl_rationale: The project is actively maintained, has many stars (221) and recent commits, indicating a working beta, but the repository is only ~9 months old so by the given rules TRL should be capped at 6 (beta); README shows real features and integrations but no long track record or wide production deployments cited.
prerequisites: Apple Silicon recommended for on‑device models
optional: knowledge of Ollama/OpenAI/Gemini API keys if using hosted summaries
student_project_ideas: Build a small tool that exports EnviousMeet transcripts into a requirements tracker (CSV or Jira) and links utterances to requirement IDs to demonstrate capturing stakeholder requirements from meetings.
Create a plugin that post‑processes meeting transcripts to extract action items and automatically populate a project task board (e.g., GitHub Issues) using an on‑device LLM like Ollama.

tools.name: timtoole02/Camelid
tools.desc: Camelid: a Rust-native local inference backend with evidence-gated model compatibility.

cls.summary: Camelid is a Rust-native local inference engine and desktop/web UI for running GGUF-format LLMs on personal hardware with hardware acceleration (Metal/CUDA/CPU).
cls.what_it_does: Camelid runs language, vision and embedding models locally from GGUF files, providing a single Rust binary that serves a browser-based UI, a desktop app and an OpenAI-compatible API. It focuses on privacy and offline use, supports hardware acceleration paths and a curated model catalog with tested compatibility.
cls.trl_rationale: The project is an active, installable product with release artifacts, CI, platform installers and 200+ stars, indicating beyond-proof-of-concept maturity; however the repository is only ~200 days old (younger than one year), so it lacks the multi-year track record or wide ecosystem required for TRL 7+.
prerequisites: familiarity with LLM model files and GGUF format
basic command-line skills (and Rust toolchain if building from source)
student_project_ideas: Build a local assistant for an engineering project repository that indexes project files (PDFs, code, docs) and answers design questions using Camelid as the inference backend and a simple web frontend.

Compare latency, memory use and throughput of a selected GGUF model running in Camelid on CPU vs Metal (Apple Silicon) vs CUDA (NVIDIA) and report implications for deploying local inference in edge engineering tools.

tools.name: PRQELT/Autonomix
tools.desc: AI Developer for Unreal Engine — An autonomous AI agent that creates Blueprints, C++, levels, materials, widgets, and more inside the UE5 editor via natural language.

cls.summary: Autonomix is an Unreal Engine editor plugin that uses agentic AI to create and modify Blueprints, C++ code, levels, materials and other UE assets via natural language inside the editor.
cls.what_it_does: Autonomix lets a conversational AI autonomously plan and execute editor actions (create/edit Blueprints via T3D injection, modify C++ source, manage levels/materials/widgets, run PIE tests, etc.) and provides checkpoints, undo, and auditable tool calls. It integrates with multiple LLM providers and implements context management, tool loops, viewport vision, and a git-based session checkpoint system to operate inside UE5.
cls.trl_rationale: The README describes a wide feature set (T3D injection, multi-provider support, git checkpoints, PIE automation) and the repo has active development and 220 stars, but it was created ~8 months ago so lacks the long-term production track record required for TRL 7+.
prerequisites: familiarity with LLM APIs and keys
student_project_ideas: Use Autonomix to autonomously generate a demo UE level with interactive obstacles and evaluate the quality and timeliness of produced Blueprints and assets compared to a human-built baseline.

Integrate Autonomix with a simple robotics simulation in UE to have the agent create control UIs and run iterative PIE tests that detect and automatically patch common 'Accessed None' Blueprint errors, then report on repair success rates.

tools.name: Video-Rebirth/hyperflow-h3-flash
tools.desc: HyperFlow H3 Flash: Video Rebirth's 13.7B, 4- to 8-step compressed MiniMax-H3 for joint video and audio generation (INT8 and GGUF)

cls.summary: HyperFlow H3 Flash is a compressed, few-step 13.7B multimodal model for joint video and synchronized stereo audio generation, provided with GGUF and INT8 runtimes and ComfyUI integration.
cls.what_it_does: It generates short video clips (≈5–15 s at 24 fps, default 1344×768) together with a 32 kHz stereo soundtrack using 4–8 sampling steps, targeting fast inference via INT8 quantization or GGUF runtimes. The project provides multiple runtime options (ComfyUI, stable-diffusion.cpp, Unsloth Studio, and a Python INT8 package), GGUF and INT8 weight releases on Hugging Face, and integration templates for ComfyUI.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository is very new (created 2026-11-06, ~11 days old) so despite a detailed README, multiple runtimes and hosted weights on Hugging Face, it lacks the multi-month track record and stable-release history needed for TRL7+; README evidence supports usable alpha/early-adopter status (TRL 5).
prerequisites: familiarity with ComfyUI or stable-diffusion.cpp workflows
Hugging Face model downloads and Python packaging (pip)

tools.name: biosshot/easyeda-copilot
tools.desc: AI-powered assistant for EasyEDA — generate schematics from natural language, browse LCSC components, design PCBs with custom DRC configurations, and get interactive circuit design help.

cls.summary: EasyEDA Copilot is an AI-powered extension that automates schematic creation, component resolution and constraint-driven PCB placement and routing inside EasyEDA Pro.
cls.what_it_does: The tool connects MCP-capable AI agents to native EasyEDA schematics and PCB documents to generate or reorganise schematics, resolve parts (LCSC/MPN), perform constraint-driven placement and checkpoint-backed routing, and run native DRC and structured inspections. It is used as an EasyEDA extension plus an MCP skill or server component and is notable because results remain native, editable EasyEDA objects (not static renderings) and it supports transactional checkpoints and recovery.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository is under one year old (created 2025-12-09) so maturity is limited to beta-level despite active demos, releases, 220 stars and recent commits; README documents installation, examples and MCP integration consistent with a beta-stage tool.
prerequisites: Familiarity with PCB design and component libraries
An MCP-capable client (Codex, Claude Code, or similar) for full agent workflows
student_project_ideas: Use EasyEDA Copilot to generate a multi-page schematic and constrained PCB layout for a microcontroller-based sensor board, then validate and repair DRC errors programmatically and produce a BOM with LCSC-sourced components.

Compare human vs agent-driven placement and routing on a constrained RF front-end board: measure routing quality, area, and DRC violations, and extend the Copilot by adding a custom placement constraint script.

tools.name: cyanfish-x/tellux
tools.desc: Open-source 3D Earth Engine built on Three.js for digital globes, digital twins, 3D maps — terrain, 3D Tiles, atmosphere & clouds.

cls.summary: Tellux is an open-source web 3D Earth engine that renders geospatial terrains, imagery, 3D Tiles, models, atmosphere and volumetric clouds in the browser using Three.js.
cls.what_it_does: Tellux provides a unified API and runtime for building browser-based digital globes, digital twins and 3D maps from geospatial sources (Cesium Quantized Mesh terrain, XYZ/WMS imagery, GeoJSON/MVT vectors, 3D Tiles, glTF/GLB and Gaussian splatting). It is used as an ESM library together with Three.js and related peer libraries to compose camera, terrain, imagery, tilesets, atmosphere and post-processing for interactive web applications, and includes documentation, examples and a Sandcastle playground.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository is active with documentation, a demo site and Sandcastle examples and integrates established open-source projects, indicating a usable beta; however it is under 1 year old (created 2026-06-03) so lacks long-term production track record and therefore fits TRL 6.
student_project_ideas: Build a web app that overlays city infrastructure GeoJSON and 3D Tiles models on Tellux to visualize flood-inundation extents and test camera-based storyboards for stakeholder communication.
Create a performance study comparing WebGL and the experimental WebGPU renderer in Tellux by loading a complex 3D Tiles city scene and measuring frame time, memory and tile loading behaviour.

tools.name: patch-gg/trompe
tools.desc: Texture a whole game level from a gray blockout with image models: plan cameras, paint, project, bake. Real shadows, glTF out.

cls.summary: Trompe automates photographing a gray game-level blockout with planned camera views, uses image models to paint those views, projects the paintings back onto the geometry and bakes a single textured glTF for use in games and visualisation.
cls.what_it_does: Trompe plans camera positions over a 3D level, renders view-specific 'clay' passes, calls an image model (via fal) to paint each view to match a textual material/style prompt, projects those images back onto the model and bakes a final texture atlas and textured glTF. It runs the planning, projection and baking in the browser (WebGL / three.js) and uses a remote image model service for the actual painting, producing realistic photo-like albedos with baked shadows left to real-time lighting.
cls.trl_rationale: The repository is runnable with dev server and command-line scripts and has early users/stars, but it is very new (created 23 days ago) so there is no long track record or stable releases; that age limits the TRL to about 5.
prerequisites: familiarity with 3D assets (glTF), UVs and basic lighting
a fal.ai API key for full painting functionality
student_project_ideas: Compare Trompe-produced textures vs manually painted textures by importing the baked glTF into a Unity/Unreal scene and measuring perceived realism and texture memory/performance trade-offs.
Extend Trompe's planner to prioritise views for a specified gameplay path (e.g. first 30 seconds of play) and evaluate cost vs visual coverage when limiting the number of image-model calls.

tools.name: autohandai/code-cli
tools.desc: Open-source terminal coding agent. Use 15+ model providers, local models or your own key. Plan mode before edits. Imports your Codex, Cursor, Claude Code setup.

cls.summary: Autohand Code CLI is an open-source terminal-native AI coding agent that reads a repository, plans edits, runs tools and applies approved changes from the command line.
cls.what_it_does: It helps developers automate coding tasks by scanning project context, producing a plan, editing files, running shell commands and committing changes, while asking for approval before risky operations. It runs locally or against many hosted model providers, supports local runtimes (Ollama, llama.cpp) and integrates with Git workflows and an interactive terminal UI.
cls.trl_rationale: The repo shows a well-documented, cross-platform project with installers, multi-provider support and active development, but it was created less than one year ago so there isn't yet a long track record required for TRL 7+.
student_project_ideas: Build a CI job that uses Autohand Code CLI to run an automated refactoring skill on a small codebase and measure code quality changes using linters and test coverage.
Extend or write a new 'skill' for Autohand that automates updating dependency versions and runs tests, integrating with a local Ollama model for offline inference.

tools.name: boschresearch/3dgeer
tools.desc: [ICLR 2026] The official implementation associated with the paper "3DGEER: 3D Gaussian Rendering Made Exact and Efficient for Generic Cameras"

cls.summary: 3DGEER is an open-source implementation of an ICLR 2026 method for exact and efficient 3D Gaussian rendering that supports generic camera models (pinhole, fisheye) and real-time performance for robotics, AR and autonomous-driving scenes.
cls.what_it_does: It implements an analytical, projectively-exact Gaussian rendering pipeline (forward and backward gradients) and a CUDA rasterizer to remove approximation errors of traditional Gaussian splatting, especially for wide field-of-view and fisheye cameras. The code is used as a drop-in replacement/extension for existing Gaussian-splatting frameworks and includes integrations (DriveStudio viewer, CUDA rasterizer) for training and real-time visualization of dynamic outdoor scenes.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository accompanies an ICLR 2026 paper, provides a CUDA rasterizer submodule, DriveStudio integration and a working codebase with Docker/Conda instructions and many stars, indicating more than an author-only prototype. However the project is under 1 year old (created 2026-03-09), so a beta TRL (6) is appropriate rather than production-ready.
prerequisites: Conda or Docker for environment management
Familiarity with 3D Gaussian splatting / neural rendering concepts
student_project_ideas: Compare 3DGEER and a standard Gaussian-splatting / NeRF implementation on fisheye camera datasets to quantify geometric projection errors and visual fidelity differences, producing quantitative V&V metrics.

Integrate 3DGEER's CUDA rasterizer with a small mobile-robot pipeline (ROS node + DriveStudio dataset) to build a real-time wide-FoV mapping/visualization demo and evaluate runtime and accuracy on outdoor scenes.

tools.name: arikchakma/gpu-time
tools.desc: A small neural model for parsing date & time

cls.summary: gpu-time is a small neural parser that turns English time expressions into concrete dates, time ranges and RFC 5545 recurrence rules and can run locally on CPU or WebGPU.
cls.what_it_does: gpu-time tokenises English date/time text, applies a compact neural model to assign semantic roles to tokens, and resolves those predictions into calendar occurrences and recurrence rules using a provided reference instant and timezone. It ships as a browser/Node package with optional WebGPU acceleration (WGSL kernels) and a training pipeline for regenerating or refining weights.
cls.trl_rationale: The README shows a working, published browser/Node package, test and benchmark commands, and an included training pipeline, but the repository is very new (created 67 days ago) so there is limited track record of real-world production usage; stars show interest but not production maturity.
prerequisites: Chrome with WebGPU (for browser WebGPU testing)
familiarity with JavaScript/TypeScript and npm-style builds
student_project_ideas: Build a browser extension that extracts scheduling information from web pages and inserts standardized RFC-5545 events into a calendar using gpu-time for parsing and a calendar API for storage.

Compare CPU vs WebGPU parsing performance and accuracy on large corpora: run gpu-time benchmark harnesses, measure latency and memory for varying batch sizes, and present optimization recommendations.

tools.name: elithril/blender-kiln
tools.desc: Claude Code plugin: describe an object or show a photo, and Claude builds a clean 3D model in Blender, for games, the web, AR or 3D printing. It animates characters too. New in 3.0: Kiln Studio, a local page to view, check and fix your models with Claude.

cls.summary: Kiln is a Blender plugin and Claude Code skill that generates, cleans, textures, optimises and exports production-quality 3D models (games, web, AR, 3D print) from text or photos and provides a local web 'Studio' for inspecting and annotating models with Claude-driven edits.
cls.what_it_does: Kiln gives the Claude Code agent hands inside Blender via an MCP server to script end-to-end 3D asset creation: sourcing, procedural modelling, cleanup, texturing from CC0 scans, optimisation and multi-format export. It includes Kiln Studio, a local web page to view models, pin notes, and have Claude make targeted fixes, plus quick export paths for GLB/FBX/USDZ/STL and AR preview.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository is active, reasonably starred (217), cited in a 2026 benchmarking paper and shows a rich README and features (Kiln Studio). However the repo is ~230 days old (<1 year) so lacks a long track record required for TRL7+ despite clear beta-level polish and examples.
prerequisites: a running Blender MCP server (e.g. mcp-for-blender or Blender Lab MCP)
Claude / Claude Code runtime or access (claude -p) or compatible MCP connector
student_project_ideas: Build an automated pipeline that converts a set of product photos into printable STL files using Kiln, then validate dimensional accuracy by measuring against a scanned reference and reporting shape scores.
Integrate Kiln-generated GLB assets into a three.js web viewer, add annotation-driven redesign tasks via Kiln Studio, and benchmark turnaround time and file-size optimisation for web deployment.

tools.name: 6wheel/Ortho
tools.desc: Effortlessly generate accurate, configurable orthographic templates for 3D modelling from existing 3D models including mods for Assetto Corsa and beamNG Drive.

cls.summary: Ortho is a Python app that produces clean black-and-white orthographic (blueprint) reference sheets from 3D model files, running locally in a browser with no 3D software required.
cls.what_it_does: Ortho reads common 3D model files (OBJ, STL, glTF, Collada, Assetto Corsa KN5 via an internal parser) and generates orthographic line-art views (front, back, left, right, top, bottom and a cross-section). It runs locally as a small web app (launched with a Python script), offers a part checklist to exclude unwanted geometry, and is notable for being simple, offline, and tailored for vehicle/asset modelling and modding workflows.
cls.trl_rationale: The repository provides a runnable local app, clear install/run instructions and already has community interest (217 stars) which indicates more than a trivial prototype; however it is only ~141 days old and lacks evidence of long-term production deployments, so beta-level TRL 6 is appropriate.
student_project_ideas: Create an automated pipeline that converts vehicle models (OBJ/kn5) into orthographic templates and integrates those images into a parts catalog or BOM viewer (combine Ortho output with a simple web app/Flask or static site).
Extend Ortho to add dimensioning and scale bars to generated views and compare orthographic-derived dimensions against CAD measurements using Blender or FreeCAD as a reference.

tools.name: uncSoft/anubis-oss
tools.desc: Local LLM Testing & Benchmarking for Apple Silicon

cls.summary: Anubis is a native macOS app for benchmarking, comparing and managing local large language models on Apple Silicon, with real-time hardware telemetry and history-exportable results.
cls.what_it_does: Anubis runs repeatable local LLM inference benchmarks against OpenAI-compatible endpoints (Ollama, MLX, LM Studio, OpenWebUI, docker models, etc.), capturing tokens/sec, TTFT and detailed timings while correlating those metrics with live Apple Silicon hardware telemetry. It provides a GUI with a Flow Builder to create multi-model/multi-prompt sweep runs, persistent run history, exportable CSV/MD reports, and server-verified measurement options to improve accuracy and reproducibility.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository is ~9 months old, has releases, 200+ stars, an active README and a public community leaderboard and analysis pages; that indicates beta maturity with documented methodology and installs via Homebrew, but it lacks a multi-year production track record required for TRL7+.
prerequisites: basic familiarity with local LLM hosting (Ollama, MLX, OpenWebUI) and Homebrew
models or endpoints to benchmark (local or networked)
student_project_ideas: Compare performance (tokens/sec, TTFT, memory) of different quantization settings for a chosen LLM on Apple Silicon using Anubis flows, and produce a reproducible report with statistical confidence intervals.
Integrate Anubis-exported benchmark histories with a custom Python notebook to correlate hardware telemetry with model latency and to build a simple performance-prediction regression model.

tools.name: AlysisAi/AlysisCode
tools.desc: Open-source, multi-model agent for coding, research, and everyday workflows. Independently built engine with our own Alysis Sandbox, strict command isolation by default, and local model support.

cls.summary: AlysisCode is an open-source multi-model AI coding agent with a terminal CLI and desktop app that runs local or remote models and enforces sandboxed command execution.
cls.what_it_does: AlysisCode provides a chat-driven coding assistant and workspace for working with code, documents and command-line tasks; it connects to local or remote LLM providers, offers free web search and a built-in sandbox for running shell commands, and includes a desktop app with project/versioning features. It is used from a CLI or native desktop installers and is notable for supporting many model providers, local models, and strict sandboxing by default.
cls.trl_rationale: The project is a working, documented CLI and desktop app with installers, docs, and active commits and issues, indicating a beta-level maturity; the repository is 193 days old (under one year), which limits assigning higher TRL without a longer track record of real-world adoption.
prerequisites: basic knowledge of LLM providers or local model tooling
student_project_ideas: Create a lab exercise where students use AlysisCode to automatically generate and run unit tests for a small Python project, then evaluate sandbox safety by comparing strict and permissive sandbox modes.

Build an integration that routes specific code-review tasks to a local LLM (e.g. Ollama or LM Studio) using AlysisCode's provider configuration and measure differences in suggestions versus a cloud model.

tools.name: oaslananka/kicad-mcp-pro
tools.desc: MCP server for KiCad, connecting AI agents to schematic and PCB workflows, ERC/DRC validation, DFM checks, BOM analysis, and manufacturing preparation—with controlled edits and human-gated release workflows.

cls.summary: KiCad MCP Pro is an open-source Model Context Protocol (MCP) server that connects AI agents to KiCad schematic and PCB workflows to perform reviews, DRC/ERC checks, DFM/BOM analysis and controlled manufacturing handoffs.
cls.what_it_does: It exposes KiCad tools and scripted review/automation operations over an MCP API so LLM-based agents can inspect, run validation (ERC/DRC), perform DFM and BOM analyses, and prepare manufacturing exports with human-gated write/release workflows. It is used as a local or optional cloud-capable server with a browser dashboard and CLI, notable for progressive disclosure profiles (bounded review vs expert write) and explicit privacy/telemetry controls.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository shows an active project with a published PyPI package, npm wrapper, semantic version (4.16.0), 217 stars and regular commits, indicating beta-stage maturity; however the repository is only ~170 days old (<1 year) so it lacks the long track record required for TRL 7+.
prerequisites: understanding of MCP/AI agent concepts and optional API credentials for vendor part sources
student_project_ideas: Build an automated PCB review pipeline that uses KiCad MCP Pro to run ERC/DRC and DFM checks on student KiCad projects, generate a remediation report, and compare results before and after student fixes.

Integrate KiCad MCP Pro with a sourcing API (e.g. JLCPCB or DigiKey) to create a prototype workflow that auto-populates a BOM, checks component availability/pricing, and prepares Gerber/IPC-ready manufacturing output.

tools.name: softdaddy-o/soft-ue-cli
tools.desc: Python CLI + UE plugin that lets Claude Code (AI coding agent) control Unreal Engine in real time. Spawn actors, edit blueprints, call functions, capture screenshots, manage PIE sessions, and more -- all from the terminal. Works with UE5 editor and packaged builds via an in-process HTTP bridge.

cls.summary: soft-ue-cli is a command-line and MCP server plus UE plugin that lets LLMs and developers control Unreal Engine (editor or builds) to spawn actors, edit Blueprints, capture screenshots, profile and inspect assets in real time.
cls.what_it_does: It exposes a discoverable surface of 120+ commands for automating Unreal Engine tasks either live (via an in-process HTTP bridge plugin) or offline (by parsing .uasset/.ini/.uproject files). It is used as a CLI or an MCP server for LLM-driven workflows to mutate projects, run PIE sessions, capture token-efficient screenshots and inspect or patch engine/config assets; its notable feature is AI-native tooling and command-family metadata that help agents discover runtime/plugin requirements.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository is active (created ~8 months ago) with versioned releases (examples: 1.45.0), 216 stars and ongoing pushes, indicating beta maturity; age <1 year prevents assigning TRL 7+ despite a broad command surface and multiple release notes. Solo maintainer noted in README.
prerequisites: Unreal Engine editor and project familiarity (UE5)
understanding of LLM/MCP concepts for agent integration
student_project_ideas: Build an automated test that uses soft-ue-cli to spawn a scene, run a Play-In-Editor (PIE) session, capture token-efficient screenshots and compare them to baseline images to detect regressions.

Integrate soft-ue-cli as an MCP server with a small LLM agent to implement an automated Blueprint-to-C++ assistant that proposes Blueprint edits, applies them via the bridge, and validates runtime behaviour in PIE.

tools.name: godothub/godot-minigame
tools.desc: Godot 4 微信小游戏导出插件，使用 Release 模板分发与版本适配。

cls.summary: A C++ editor plugin for Godot 4 that automates downloading, caching, adapting and exporting project templates for WeChat minigame targets.
cls.what_it_does: This plugin matches the running Godot 4 editor version to a template release, downloads and caches template packages (tpz) from GitHub/Gitee Releases, unpacks them and generates the minigame export directory. It is used inside the Godot editor (installed into res://addons/) and notable for its automated template version matching, release-based distribution and included skills/ folder for AI-assisted adaptation.
cls.trl_rationale: The repo is active, has 216 stars, build scripts for multiple platforms and a clear README, indicating beta-level maturity; however it is only 248 days old (under one year) so evidence for long-term production adoption is limited, capping TRL at 6.
prerequisites: C++ toolchain for building GDExtension modules

tools.name: yuhp/opencode-models-discovery
tools.desc: A universal OpenCode plugin for dynamic model discovery with flexible configuration for OpenAI-compatible providers.

cls.summary: A TypeScript OpenCode plugin that discovers OpenAI-compatible models from provider endpoints and injects them into OpenCode with optional filtering and metadata enrichment.
cls.what_it_does: The plugin queries a provider's model-list endpoint (defaults to /v1/models), applies configurable filters and optional metadata enrichment, and registers discovered models into OpenCode (supports both OpenCode v2 and a legacy v1 adapter). It is used as an OpenCode plugin configured per provider and notable for its provider-agnostic discovery, multiple enrichment formats (models.dev, ollama, vllm, etc.), caching options and CLI/TUI commands for refresh and inspection.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository is well-documented, has active maintenance (recent push), hundreds of stars and a v2 integration with CLI/TUI tools, suggesting Beta maturity; however it is younger than one year (created 2026-04-09), so TRL is capped at 6.
prerequisites: Familiarity with OpenAI-compatible provider APIs and configuring provider credentials
student_project_ideas: Create a small integration that uses the plugin to discover available local and remote models and selects the best-fitting model for a simple course chatbot based on latency and advertised capabilities.
Compare metadata enrichment formats (e.g. models.dev vs provider metadata) across multiple providers and produce a short report showing differences in reported capabilities, limits and modalities.

tools.name: jdilla1277/agentcad
tools.desc: CAD CLI and MCP server for AI agents

cls.summary: agentcad is a Python CLI and MCP server that lets coding agents produce and run build123d/CadQuery scripts to generate, validate, export and preview 3D CAD models (STEP, STL, GLB/OBJ, PNG).
cls.what_it_does: agentcad provides an execution environment and workflow for AI coding agents to author parametric CAD via build123d (with CadQuery compatibility), run builds, measure and validate geometry, produce exports (STEP, meshes, renders), diff versions and serve browser previews. It is delivered as a CLI and MCP server so agents can be given structured JSON commands and responses and automates common CAD build/validation tasks.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository is active, in use and documented (examples, changelog, demo site) with versioned releases noted (v0.7.2) and 216 stars, but it is under one year old (created 2026-06-02, ~168 days) so lacks the multi-year track record required for TRL 7+.
prerequisites: familiarity with build123d or CadQuery and basic CAD concepts
student_project_ideas: Build an agent that generates parametric phone-stand designs with requirements input (angle, dimensions) using agentcad and evaluate outputs by automatically measuring dimensions and exporting printable STL files.

Create a CI pipeline that runs agent-designed CAD scripts with agentcad to validate geometry (dimensions, manifoldness), generate diffs between versions, and produce STEP deliverables for handoff to a downstream tool like FreeCAD or Revit.

tools.name: joeynyc/awesome-microduck
tools.desc: A curated list of software, simulators, policies, agent tools and coverage for the Pollen Robotics / Hugging Face Microduck robot

cls.summary: A community-curated index of software, simulators, trained policies, tools and coverage for the Pollen Robotics / Hugging Face Microduck biped robot ecosystem.
cls.what_it_does: This repository collects links and short descriptions for the Microduck ecosystem: official repos, in-browser simulators, training environments, ONNX policies, community tools and hardware/replica resources. It is used as a discovery hub for students and developers who want to run the Microduck simulator, train or inspect policies, or explore tooling that targets the robot; its notable aspect is that it centralises many disparate repos, spaces and examples for a single open robot platform.
cls.trl_rationale: The repository is a curated collection (not a single production system) and is only 79 days old, limiting TRL by age to at most 5; however it already indexes working simulators, published ONNX policies and official repos indicating early real use in simulation but limited hardware validation.
prerequisites: basic familiarity with robotics concepts (simulator, policy, ONNX)
student_project_ideas: Run the official Microduck in-browser simulator and reproduce a published policy behaviour, then modify observation noise or domain randomisation parameters to study sim-to-sim robustness.
Use the listed microduck_rl training setup to fine-tune an existing ONNX policy in MuJoCo and compare its performance to the published policy in simulation (requires a CUDA GPU).

tools.name: Kayforkind/reimagine-it
tools.desc: Kayforkind Content-Derived Design CLI. HTML in, standalone HTML out from the source's own nouns, dates, numbers, and colors. Not the reimagineit.ai interview SaaS.

cls.summary: A CLI that reads an existing HTML page, extracts its content (headings, facts, dates, colours, numbers) and generates a standalone redesigned HTML artifact with visual layouts and inline SVG/3D assets.
cls.what_it_does: reimagine-it extracts semantic elements from an input HTML file and auto-generates one or more complete, standalone redesigns (HTML + inline SVG/3D) without external dependencies. It is used as an npm CLI (npx reimagine-it) to produce variations, lock brand tokens, and produce audit reports; notable features include multiple generator 'builders' (infographic, landing, 3js, dashboard) and offline artifacts that embed their assets.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository shows many examples, CI-regenerated artifacts, 215 stars and recent activity indicating early adoption, but it is a new project (~90 days) so lacks long-term production track record required for higher TRL.
student_project_ideas: Create a lab exercise where students run reimagine-it on a departmental or government HTML page and critique accessibility, information fidelity, and usability of the generated redesigns.

Compare automated content-derived layouts by instrumenting the tool to produce multiple variations for the same technical document and evaluate which builders (infographic, dashboard, 3js) communicate the same data most effectively using user studies or objective readability metrics.

tools.name: abouchedidxcode/open-source-hands
tools.desc: Make webcam hand games in the browser, or point your coding agent here and have it make one. MediaPipe hand tracking + a gesture engine + a starter game + a playbook.

cls.summary: A browser-first TypeScript kit and starter templates for detecting hand poses and gestures with MediaPipe and building webcam-controlled web games.
cls.what_it_does: It converts MediaPipe Hand Landmarker 21-point outputs into stable, game-ready inputs (poses, motions, two-hand gestures and continuous values) and provides a three.js starter game, demos and a playbook for building hand-controlled browser games. You use it by copying the dependency-free src/kit into a project, loading the MediaPipe model, and registering engine events to drive game logic or UI actions; notable features include synthetic hands for testing, smoothing/hysteresis, a Gesture Lab UI and agent-friendly templates and docs.
cls.trl_rationale: The README shows a working, well-documented codebase with demos, tests and templates, but the repository is very new (created 14 days ago) so there is not yet a track record of production use or long-lived releases, which limits maturity to TRL 5.
prerequisites: basic three.js knowledge for the template game
student_project_ideas: Build a browser-based rehabilitation exercise where hand poses and pinch strength are used to score and track patient progress, storing time-series metrics in a simple backend.
Create a robot teleoperation UI that maps detected hand steering and pinch gestures to remote robot commands, integrating the kit with a ROS 2 bridge or WebSocket control server.

integrates_with: Chromium (headless for e2e with synthetic hands)

tools.name: MONZikWasTaken/Framegen
tools.desc: Real-time neural frame interpolation in the browser: hand-written WGSL runtime on raw WebGPU, 2.9 MB model, 2x-6x any <video> at 3-4 ms per frame. Chrome/Firefox extension.

cls.summary: Framegen is a browser extension that uses a compact neural network and WebGPU to interpolate video in real time, increasing displayed framerates (2x–6x) directly in Chrome/Firefox without servers.
cls.what_it_does: Framegen runs a small neural interpolation model on the user's GPU via WebGPU/WGSL and WebAssembly to generate intermediate video frames in real time inside the browser, letting videos play at higher effective framerates and offering modes like anime-optimized cadence smoothing and neural upscaling. It is used as a browser extension button that attaches to video elements and can auto-adjust quality to match GPU/display headroom; notable points are a hand-written WGSL runtime, a 2.9 MB model, and operation entirely on-device.
cls.trl_rationale: The project is actively developed, published as browser extension releases (Web Store) and shows community interest (213 stars), indicating beta-level maturity; however the repository is only ~139 days old so it lacks the longer track record needed for TRL 7+.
prerequisites: Basic knowledge of installing browser extensions and running Node-based build scripts for development
student_project_ideas: Measure interpolation artefacts and temporal stability by comparing Framegen output to source video across different content types (film, sports, anime) and produce quantitative metrics and visual examples.
Integrate Framegen's WebGPU kernel approach with a simple WebRTC streaming demo to evaluate on-device interpolation latency and quality in a low-latency video conferencing pipeline.

tools.name: Kirakun0328/text-to-vrma
tools.desc: Text-To-VRMA — VRM特化型Text-To-Motionツール

cls.summary: A browser and desktop web app that generates VRM-compatible character motion (VRMA) from text using LLM engines or a local ARDY motion engine and plays/exports the result.
cls.what_it_does: Text-To-VRMA turns plain-language prompts (Japanese/English etc.) into full-body VRM animation files (.vrma) and lets you preview, scrub and export the animation as GIF/video or download the VRMA for use in VRM-capable apps. It runs in the browser or as an Electron desktop app, supports OpenAI/Claude/compatible APIs and an optional local ARDY engine for higher-quality offline motion capture–like results.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository is active and about 4 months old with 200+ stars, desktop releases (Windows zip) and frequent pushes; README documents install, Electron builds and optional ARDY integration. Age is <1 year so TRL limited to beta-level despite good uptake and release artifacts.
prerequisites: OpenAI or Claude API key (optional for cloud LLM engines)
Python 3.10+ and ~20GB disk only if using ARDY local engine (optional)
student_project_ideas: Compare LLM-generated keyframe animations with ARDY-produced motions by building an evaluation pipeline that measures foot contact, joint velocities and perceptual quality for the same textual prompts.
Integrate Text-To-VRMA with a simple Unity or three.js scene to generate and play procedurally authored character behaviours from mission scripts, demonstrating a text-driven animation pipeline.

tools.name: ritesh-kanwar/Cashiro
tools.desc: Cashiro is a comprehensive financial tracking manager that Turn bank SMS and PDF Statements into a clean, searchable money timeline with on-device AI assistance. 100% private, no cloud processing.

cls.summary: Cashiro is an open-source Android app that parses bank SMS and PDF statements to produce a private, searchable transaction timeline with on-device AI assistance.
cls.what_it_does: Cashiro automatically extracts transactions (amount, merchant, date, category) from SMS messages and supported PDF statements and presents budgets, analytics and subscription detection in a timeline UI. It runs entirely on-device (uses MediaPipe's on-device LLM according to the README), targets Android, and is notable for privacy-first, multi‑bank SMS parsing and built-in PDF parsing for UPI statements.
cls.trl_rationale: The project is an active, public Android app with several hundred stars and recent commits, documentation and build instructions, but it is under one year old so lacks a long track record; this supports a beta-level TRL (6).
student_project_ideas: Implement and evaluate a new SMS parser rule for a local bank and measure parsing accuracy across sample messages, producing a short report and demo app build.
Replace or benchmark the on-device LLM assistant (MediaPipe integration) with an alternative lightweight on-device model and compare latency, privacy and answer quality on a phone.

tools.name: openAMRobot/openamr-platform-sw
tools.desc: ROS 2 Jazzy software for the OpenAMRobot mobile base: simulation, Nav2, SLAM, docking, control, drivers, and bringup.

cls.summary: A ROS 2 (Jazzy) software stack providing simulation, navigation (Nav2), SLAM, and AprilTag-based autodocking for the OpenAMRobot mobile base.
cls.what_it_does: This repository supplies a complete ROS 2 software stack for the OpenAMRobot mobile platform including robot description, Gazebo simulation, Nav2 navigation, SLAM and an AprilTag-bundle autodocking pipeline; it can be run via Docker or installed natively and includes launch files, docs and a beginner ROS2 course. It is used to simulate, develop and test navigation and docking behaviours and is notable for its end-to-end example (simulation → Nav2 → docking) and strong documentation aimed at learners and contributors.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository is active with substantial documentation, examples, Docker support and 213 stars, and demonstrates an end-to-end simulated docking workflow; however README marks the project 'experimental' and real-robot bringup is still in progress, and the repo age is ~188 days (<1 year), which limits maturity to TRL 5.
prerequisites: basic ROS concepts (nodes, launch, TF, URDF/Xacro)
student_project_ideas: Implement a robust docking controller by integrating the repository's AprilTag-based docking pipeline with a simple PID or MPC controller and evaluate performance in simulation under sensor noise.

Extend the simulation stack to replay recorded sensor logs and build an autonomous localisation comparison: compare Nav2 AMCL, a SLAM package used in the repo, and a custom particle-filter implementation using the same dataset.

tools.name: yoloshii/ClawMem
tools.desc: On-device memory layer for AI agents. Claude Code, OpenClaw and Hermes. Hooks + MCP server + hybrid RAG search.

cls.summary: ClawMem is an on-device retrieval-augmented memory layer and MCP server that stores, ranks and serves persistent context for AI coding agents (Claude Code, OpenClaw, Hermes) from a local SQLite vault.
cls.what_it_does: ClawMem ingests conversation exports and documents, indexes them with hybrid retrieval (BM25 + vector search + reranking) and maintains evolving memory metadata (recency decay, durability, causal links) to surface relevant context into agent prompts. It runs locally (TypeScript on Bun), exposes hooks and an MCP server for multiple agent clients, and emphasizes safety and contamination guards when injecting memory into sessions.
cls.trl_rationale: The project is active, has many stars and releases of features in the README, indicating a usable beta, but the repository is only ~9 months old so it lacks the multi-year production track record required for TRL 7+.
prerequisites: basic knowledge of LLMs, embeddings and RAG concepts
student_project_ideas: Build an agent workflow that uses ClawMem to mine Slack or exported chat logs, then evaluate retrieval quality and temporal ranking by comparing surfaced context for a set of engineering decisions (combine with a local GGUF model for extraction).

Integrate ClawMem as the memory backend for a small multi-agent system (e.g., Hermes + an OpenClaw plugin) and implement an experiment that measures how quickly decisions propagate between agents and how contradiction detection prevents unsafe merges.

tools.name: MrXujiang/HiCAD
tools.desc: HiCAD,一款AI驱动的CAD建模平台

cls.summary: HiCAD is an open-source, AI-driven web platform that converts natural-language prompts into parameterized JSCAD 3D models with realtime preview and STL/OBJ export for 3D printing.
cls.what_it_does: HiCAD accepts natural-language descriptions and uses AI adapters to generate deterministic, parameterized JSCAD code which is rendered in-browser with Three.js for interactive preview and exported as STL/OBJ for fabrication. It includes a Monaco code editor, a parameter panel for live adjustments, a template marketplace, and multiple AI adapter options (DeepSeek, OpenAI, Qwen) so users can switch models by changing environment variables.
cls.trl_rationale: The project is a working web platform with a public demo, substantial feature set (AI adapters, realtime rendering, export, template market) and 211 stars, indicating active interest; however the repository is only ~6 months old so it lacks the multi-year production track record required for TRL 7+. The README documents install and run steps and shows implemented adapters and components.
prerequisites: an AI API key (e.g. DeepSeek/OpenAI/Qwen) for model-driven generation
basic familiarity with command line and environment variables
student_project_ideas: Build a parameterised part generator: extend HiCAD templates to create a parametric bracket family, then connect exported STL files to a simple slicing pipeline and evaluate tolerance fit with printed prototypes.
Integrate a physics-check: augment the generated JSCAD code with rules that check wall thickness and overhangs, then produce a report and annotated 3D preview flagging manufacturability issues.

tools.name: per-simmons/unreal-agent-harness
tools.desc: AI agents building cities in Unreal Engine 5.8 via the Unreal MCP — free City Sample base + PCG + custom Blender facade kits. Glass city, Paris, Art-Deco, a hand-built Chrysler, and real NYC via Cesium.

cls.summary: An open-source harness that lets an AI agent drive Unreal Engine 5.8 (via the Unreal MCP plugin) to procedurally generate, inspect and play 3D cities including streaming real-world tiles from Cesium.
cls.what_it_does: The project connects an LLM agent (example: Claude) to Unreal Editor using the official MCP plugin so the agent can act (spawn/modify assets), capture viewport images and run a QA loop (act → capture → decode → fix). It provides PCG recipes, Blender headless jobs, cesium streaming support and tooling to decode large viewport captures into compact PNG+JSON for spatial reasoning. Notable features are the MCP tool-layer for serialized scene mutations, documented PCG pipelines, and examples that stream real-world 3D tiles into UE.
cls.trl_rationale: The repo is well-documented, includes multiple example workflows (PCG, Cesium, playable character) and tooling (ue_qa.py, Blender jobs) and has community interest (211 stars). However it is only ~148 days old with no long public production track record, so maturity is beta-level rather than proven production.
prerequisites: Unreal Engine 5.8 (installed and MCP plugin enabled)
student_project_ideas: Create a procedural-city generation lab where students extend towers_jobs.py to implement a new district style and evaluate layout/overlap using the ue_qa QA loop and decoded JSON pose outputs.

Build a small digital-twin demo that streams a chosen city area via Cesium into UE, places sensor actors, and implements an agent-driven inspection routine that captures and analyses viewport images for automated V&V.

tools.name: S4US/Roqer
tools.desc: An open-source AI agent for Roblox Studio. Builds, scripts, and playtests in your place using your ChatGPT/Claude subscription or custom API.

cls.summary: Roqer is an open-source AI agent that automates building, scripting and playtesting inside Roblox Studio using your chosen LLM/API or local models.
cls.what_it_does: Roqer connects to a language or image model to read and edit Roblox places, generate scripts, assets and animations, run multi-client playtests and upload results back into Studio or a Rojo project. It is used as a desktop Electron app and a standalone MCP server and notable for its Blender integration for modelling and automated checks before publishing.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository is very new (53 days) so TRL is limited by age despite active development, documentation and 3rd-party integrations; README and docs show working features and examples but there's not yet a long track record of production use.
prerequisites: Roblox Studio (Windows) or Vinegar on Linux
an LLM/image model subscription or compatible endpoint (OpenAI/Anthropic/Google) for full features
student_project_ideas: Build an automated level-creation pipeline where students prompt Roqer to assemble a small game level, then use Rojo to version-control the generated scripts and assets and run scripted playtests to validate functionality.

Integrate Roqer's Blender modelling pipeline to generate complex props for a Roblox scene, then measure performance and memory impact during multi-client playtests and report optimisation recommendations.

tools.name: griches/EternalDarknessRecomp
tools.desc: Eternal Darkness: Sanity's Requiem static recompilation (DolRecomp + GXRuntime) for Mac, Windows and Linux / Steam Deck. Bring your own disc.

cls.summary: A community project that rebuilds the GameCube game Eternal Darkness as a native application for macOS, Windows and Linux by statically recompiling code from your own disc image.
cls.what_it_does: This repository provides a static recompilation and launcher that translates data from a European GameCube disc image and produces native builds of Eternal Darkness for Mac, Windows and Linux/Steam Deck; it uses components described as DolRecomp and GXRuntime and ships platform-specific installers/releases. It is used by downloading the release, providing a legal disc image and optional HD texture packs; notable points are multi-platform native builds, support for HD textures, and a focus on running from original media rather than distributing game content.
cls.trl_rationale: The repo is young (created 33 days ago) so cannot be rated above TRL 5; however it already publishes releases for multiple platforms and has users (210 stars) which suggests alpha-stage usage rather than a pure prototype.
prerequisites: C toolchain for build/patching if building from source
A legal European GameCube disc image (.iso or .gcm)
Familiarity with platform-specific installation (macOS app, Windows zip, Linux tar)
student_project_ideas: Compare performance and rendering differences between this static recompilation and Dolphin emulator by measuring frame timing and GPU usage on Steam Deck for a set of scenes.

Create a small tool that automates verifying and preparing GameCube disc images (ISO conversion, checksum, required files) and integrates it into the project's launch flow to streamline reproducible builds.

tools.name: escudero/brandpose
tools.desc: Personal project: where shoppers look, estimated from an ordinary security camera and open source AI (YOLO11, Gaze-LLE, Depth Anything V2)

cls.summary: BrandPose estimates where shoppers look from fixed security-camera video by combining person detection/tracking, head-crop gaze heatmaps, single-image depth-to-point-cloud and Blender-based 3D reconstruction to produce attention heatmaps and a rendered 3D scene.
cls.what_it_does: BrandPose processes a fixed-camera retail video to detect and track people (YOLO11 + tracker), produce per-person gaze heatmaps using Gaze-LLE from head crops, estimate metric depth from a single frame with Depth Anything V2 to generate a point cloud, and combine these to assign gazes to store zones and render heatmaps and a Blender 3D reconstruction. It is used as a research/demo pipeline (Python scripts + Blender) and notable for integrating several open-source vision models end-to-end for retail attention analysis from ordinary CCTV footage.
cls.trl_rationale: The repository demonstrates a working end-to-end demo (video, scripts, integrations) and has community interest (stars), but it is very recent (created 33 days ago) so there is not yet a track record of production use or long-term stable releases, limiting maturity to TRL 5.
prerequisites: basic familiarity with machine learning / PyTorch models
student_project_ideas: Adapt the BrandPose pipeline to a different store video: evaluate accuracy of zone assignment by collecting a small labelled ground-truth (manually annotated gazes) and compare attention reports, combining the repo with a simple web dashboard to display results.

Replace the single-frame depth (Depth Anything V2) with multi-view or structure-from-motion (OpenMVG / OpenMVS) for a short surveillance sequence and measure how the improved geometry changes gaze-to-shelf intersection and attention metrics.

tools.name: exoteric33/ps2-native-recomp
tools.desc: Turns a PS2 disc image into a native PC program by static recompilation; builds on ps2-web-recomp (MIT). Work in progress. Bring your own disc.

cls.summary: A project that statically recompiles PlayStation 2 game discs into native Windows or Linux programs by translating the PS2 CPU code to C++ and running the rest of the console in a runtime.
cls.what_it_does: The tool translates the PS2 main CPU code from a disc image into C++, compiles it into a native executable, and emulates the remaining console hardware at runtime using WebGPU (via wgpu-native) for graphics. It is used by selecting a disc image in the app, building, and running — producing a standalone PC program for that game; the project is early-stage and evolving rapidly.
cls.trl_rationale: The README and repository show working functionality (many games tested and some run end-to-end) and the project has attracted interest (stars/forks), but the repo is only 20 days old so it cannot be judged beyond an early alpha-in-use stage.
prerequisites: familiarity with building native projects on Windows and Linux
understanding of emulation/recompilation concepts and graphics APIs (Vulkan/Direct3D12/WebGPU)
student_project_ideas: Measure and report performance differences between static recompilation (ps2-native-recomp) and dynamic emulation (PCSX2) for a short game scene, profiling CPU/GPU hotspots and proposing optimisations.
Extend the tool's runtime to add a simple graphics post-processing effect (e.g. higher-resolution scaling or a shader-based HUD sharpening) and evaluate visual quality and performance trade-offs.

tools.name: Hello-QM/catgo-LRG
tools.desc: AI-driven workbench for computational materials science — interactive 3D structure viewer, natural-language CatBot assistant, visual DAG workflow engine, HPC job submission. Tauri desktop app with SvelteKit frontend and FastAPI Python backend. Drives VASP, ORCA, CP2K, QE, GPAW, DFTB+, SIESTA, LAMMPS.

cls.summary: CatGo is an open-source desktop and web workbench that combines an interactive 3D materials-structure viewer, natural-language assistant (CatBot), visual DAG workflow editor and HPC job submission for running and analysing computational materials simulations.
cls.what_it_does: CatGo helps researchers build, inspect and prepare atomic structures, assemble multi-step simulation workflows (DFT, MD, analysis), and submit/monitor jobs on remote HPC clusters from a single UI. It is notable for integrating a Three.js-based 3D structure viewer, a natural-language agent (CatBot) that calls visible tool operations, and connectors for many electronic-structure and MD codes (VASP, ORCA, CP2K, QE, GPAW, DFTB+, SIESTA, LAMMPS).
cls.trl_rationale: The project is actively developed, integrates many production codes and has a packaged desktop app and web front-end, indicating beta-level maturity; however the repository is under one year old (created 2026-04-29) so there is not yet a long track record required for TRL7+.
prerequisites: basic Linux / HPC and SSH knowledge
familiarity with electronic‑structure / MD concepts (DFT, MD)
developer tooling for Node.js / Python if extending or building
student_project_ideas: Create an automated workflow that builds a slab model in CatGo, runs a small GPAW or CP2K relaxation on a remote HPC node, and visualises the adsorption energy and DOS in the viewer.
Extend CatBot with a custom prompt/tool that validates input settings for ORCA calculations and produces a checklist, demonstrating integration with the CatGo plugin API and ORCA exporter.

tools.name: opengeos/maplibre-gl-lidar
tools.desc: A MapLibre plugin for visualizing LiDAR Point Cloud

cls.summary: maplibre-gl-lidar is a MapLibre GL JS plugin for loading, streaming and interactively visualising large LiDAR point clouds (LAS/LAZ/COPC/EPT) in the browser.
cls.what_it_does: This plugin streams and renders point cloud formats (LAS/LAZ, COPC and EPT) inside a MapLibre map using deck.gl's PointCloudLayer, providing viewport-based streaming, colour schemes, classification controls, point picking and coordinate reprojection. It is used as a drop-in control or React/Vue component to explore, filter and style large point clouds in-browser and supports programmatic APIs for loading and styling.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository is 311 days old (under 1 year) which limits TRL; however README shows a live demo, integrations (React/Vue), a hosted online viewer, active pushes and ~200 stars indicating a beta-quality project used by others, consistent with TRL 6.
prerequisites: familiarity with MapLibre GL JS and deck.gl
basic GIS / coordinate reference systems knowledge
student_project_ideas: Build a web map that streams and compares two COPC point clouds (e.g. pre/post-construction) using maplibre-gl-lidar for visualization and compute simple elevation-change statistics in the browser.
