Create an additional World that demonstrates engineering visualisation patterns (e.g. exploded views, annotations and change-traceability) by integrating portfolio content with a simple MBSE JSON export.

tools.name: ferrumox/fox
tools.desc: A local LLM server built for concurrent work. Drop-in replacement for Ollama and/or OpenAI and Ollama APIs on one port. Requests that share a prompt reuse each other's KV cache instead of each prefilling it. Rust, wrapping llama.cpp.

cls.summary: Fox is a local LLM inference server (Rust) that is a drop-in replacement for Ollama/OpenAI APIs and optimises concurrent requests by reusing prompt KV caches.
cls.what_it_does: Fox runs large language models locally (wrapping llama.cpp) and exposes OpenAI/Ollama-compatible HTTP endpoints so existing clients work without code changes. It is notable for concurrent-request optimisations: requests that share prompts reuse KV cache and can copy live prefixes so many clients can be served more efficiently on the same hardware.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository is ~8 months old with prebuilt installers, release artifacts, benchmarks, examples, and integrations (OpenAI, LangChain, LlamaIndex), indicating a beta-level project; age (<1 year) and lack of long track record limit TRL to 6.
prerequisites: basic knowledge of LLMs and model files (gguf etc.)
Linux experience for prebuilt binaries; Rust toolchain to build on macOS/Windows
GPU drivers (CUDA/ROCm/Metal/Vulkan) for accelerated inference if desired
student_project_ideas: Deploy Fox on a lab server and integrate it with LangChain to build an offline engineering assistant that answers course-specific questions from course materials.
Benchmark Fox vs. another local LLM server (e.g. llama-server) on concurrent prompt workloads and report on latency/throughput trade-offs for different GPUs and model sizes.

tools.name: fanhuayishiy/ai-crew-pass
tools.desc: 万物工牌｜AI 角色、人物特别篇与自定义 3D 工牌，支持拖拽翻面和透明 PNG 下载。微信公众号：风花AI实验室。

cls.summary: A web app that generates interactive 3D 'lanyard' ID badges you can customize, flip and download as transparent PNG or ZIP.
cls.what_it_does: Anything Pass is a React + three.js web project that displays 3D badge/lanyard models with draggable motion, flip animation and client-side generation of PNG/ZIP downloads. Users can pick built-in characters or upload and crop their own images, edit text, and download front/back transparent assets; it also includes progressive texture prefetching and a low-bandwidth mode.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository is very new (created 11 days ago) but contains a working demo, CI for Pages deployment and detailed README; age limits TRL to at most 5 (alpha in use) despite visible interest (stars).
student_project_ideas: Extend the web badge to generate equipment/asset tags that embed QR codes and metadata and export CSV/PNG for a small lab asset-management workflow.
Replace built-in character assets with CAD-derived silhouettes (exported bitmaps) to build an automated badge generator pipeline combining three.js rendering and a lightweight serverless uploader.

tools.name: machinefi/trio-retina
tools.desc: Model-agnostic state layer for world models — turn any detector (YOLO · VLM · DINO) into one standard, queryable stream of events + latent state. numpy-only, runs on CPU at the edge.

cls.summary: Trio Retina is a lightweight, model-agnostic Python library that converts detector outputs (YOLO, VLM, DINO, or scripted detectors) into a standardized, queryable world-state and event stream (zone enter/exit, dwell, line-crossing, counts) suitable for edge deployment.
cls.what_it_does: Trio Retina normalises outputs from arbitrary perception models into a single WorldState record with event messages and an attachable latent vector channel, and provides trackers, rule engines and event producers (zone, line, dwell, count). It runs numpy-only on CPU for edge use, can read video/RTSP or synthetic frames, and is notable for its model-agnostic encoder role that lets different detectors or dynamics be swapped under a stable state interface.
cls.trl_rationale: The project has a polished README, examples, notebooks, a pip package and active repo activity with many stars, indicating a beta-level project; however the repository is only ~5 months old (under one year) so there is not yet a long track record to justify TRL 7+.
prerequisites: numpy; optionally OpenCV and Ultralytics YOLO for full functionality
student_project_ideas: Build an edge camera prototype that uses Trio Retina with a YOLO detector and OpenCV frames to emit zone intrusion events to a dashboard and evaluate latency/CPU usage on a Raspberry Pi-class device.

Combine Trio Retina's latent vec output with a simple dynamics predictor (e.g. an LSTM) to forecast pedestrian trajectories in a lab corridor and compare prediction accuracy with and without the latent embeddings.

tools.name: younghyopark/mjfit
tools.desc: Exact convex collision geometry for MuJoCo assemblies: pegs and holes from any outline, threads, and gears.

cls.summary: mjfit procedurally builds exact convex collision geometry for MuJoCo assemblies (pegs/holes, threads, gears) so MuJoCo can simulate tight-fitting mechanical contacts accurately and efficiently.
cls.what_it_does: mjfit converts outlines and parametric profiles into unions of convex prisms so concave parts (holes, threads, gear teeth) are represented exactly for MuJoCo's convex-only collision engine. It provides command-line and Python generators for pegs, threaded fasteners, and gears, plus sampling utilities to produce many randomized assemblies for training or benchmarking. The output is MJCF XML that can be loaded directly into MuJoCo, and the project emphasises exact clearance control and performance compared with mesh/SDF approaches.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository is actively maintained with a paper, project page, pip install, benchmarks and example scripts, indicating a beta-quality tool used by others; however it is under 1 year old (created 207 days ago) so it is limited to TRL 6.
prerequisites: basic geometry / CAD concepts (outlines, clearance, profiles)
student_project_ideas: Create a MuJoCo manipulation task where a robot arm performs peg-in-hole insertions using mjfit-generated pegs with varying clearances, and compare success rates and contact forces to the same scenes built from mesh+SDF collisions.

Use mjfit.sample_pegs to generate a dataset of randomized assembly configs and train/test a reinforcement learning policy for blind insertion, then evaluate policy robustness across different peg outlines and clearances.

tools.name: Ikunio/Lidar_nav2_ws
tools.desc: 基于 Livox MID-360 3D LiDAR 的 ROS 2 自主导航工作空间，集成 LIO 里程计、重定位、Nav2    导航，支持仿真与实机部署。

cls.summary: A ROS 2 workspace that integrates Livox MID-360 3D LiDAR, LIO odometry, 3D relocalization and Nav2 to provide a complete simulation and real-robot autonomous navigation stack.
cls.what_it_does: Lidar_nav2_ws provides a ready-to-run ROS 2 Humble navigation stack for four-wheeled skid-steer robots using a Livox MID-360 LiDAR and IMU; it runs LIO (FAST-LIO2 or Point-LIO), produces registered point clouds, performs 3D-to-2D slicing and global/local relocalization, and hands pose estimates to Nav2 for path planning. It is notable for supporting both Gazebo simulation and real-hardware deployment with scripted workflows for mapping, saving PCD/2D maps, and switching relocalization strategies (KISS-Matcher + small_gicp, small_gicp, ICP).
cls.trl_rationale: The README shows a full multi-package ROS2 workspace with simulation and real-hardware workflows and concrete scripts for mapping/navigation, indicating functionality beyond a toy prototype; however the repository is only ~190 days old (<1 year) so there is limited long-term production track record, constraining the TRL to beta (6).
student_project_ideas: Use the workspace in Gazebo to build a mapping-and-navigation lab: compare FAST-LIO2 vs Point-LIO odometry performance and final navigation success rates across varied simulated environments, and report on robustness to IMU noise.

Implement and evaluate an improved relocalization pipeline by integrating a learned descriptor-based global matcher (e.g., a lightweight 3D descriptor network) with the provided KISS-Matcher + small_gicp flow and measure recovery time and accuracy on saved PCD priors.

tools.name: iohao/ionet
tools.desc: A Java distributed server framework based on Aeron and Netty, featuring a lock-free, asynchronous, and event-driven architectural design. Suitable for game servers, IoT, high-frequency financial trading, and high-frequency market data pushing.                               基于 Aeron、Netty 的 java 分布式服务器框架，无锁异步化、事件驱动架构设计。适用于游戏服务器、物联网、高频金融交易、高频行情推送。

cls.summary: ionet is a Java-based, lock-free distributed server framework focused on ultra-low-latency messaging for use cases such as game servers, IoT and high-frequency data pushing.
cls.what_it_does: ionet provides an asynchronous, event-driven framework that uses Aeron + SBE and Netty to deliver low-latency, zero-copy message transport and supports multiple connection types (WS, TCP, UDP). It is used to build high-performance distributed services with features like routing, tracing, dynamic binding and easy integration with frameworks such as Spring, Vert.x and Quarkus.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository is under one year old (created 2025-12-03, ~349 days) so maturity is limited; however it has substantial documentation, examples, integration notes and active pushes, indicating a beta-level project rather than a fragile prototype.
prerequisites: familiarity with Aeron/Netty recommended for advanced usage
student_project_ideas: Build a low-latency telemetry collector that ingests sensor streams (UDP/WebSocket) from simulated IoT devices and forwards them to a time-series database, measuring end-to-end latency and throughput.

Create a simple multiplayer game prototype using ionet for server messaging and a web or Unity client to demonstrate connection types, dynamic binding of players to logic services, and scalability under load.

tools.name: lotvulture/lotvulture
tools.desc: Real-time parking lot occupancy detection using existing security cameras and on-device computer vision.

cls.summary: Lot Vulture converts existing IP/RTSP cameras into a real-time, on-device parking occupancy and analytics system with a web dashboard, alerts, and historical scrubbing.
cls.what_it_does: Lot Vulture performs on-device computer-vision inference on camera streams to detect and report parking-space occupancy, provides an interactive polygon editor to define spaces, and offers real-time dashboards, history scrubbing and alerting (MQTT, webhooks, email). It is deployed as a native Windows installer or Docker container and uses an optimized C++ ONNX runtime for edge inference, with a Vue-based web UI for editing and visualization.
cls.trl_rationale: The project is young (created ~76 days ago) which limits TRL despite clear engineering functionality; README and releases show installers, Docker images and a working edge inference runtime indicating early adopters and a usable alpha (community edition) so TRL ~5.
prerequisites: basic Linux or Windows administration (Docker or native installer)
familiarity with IP/RTSP cameras and networking
basic MQTT / webhooks knowledge for integrations
student_project_ideas: Integrate Lot Vulture with a small MQTT dashboard and a Raspberry Pi-driven LED sign to display live lot capacity; evaluate latency and reliability under different network conditions.

Extend the human-in-the-loop correction pipeline: collect flagged misdetections from the UI, build a simple retraining script to fine-tune an ONNX model, and measure accuracy improvement on a held-out parking dataset.

tools.name: CodingFeng101/CanvasAnvil
tools.desc: CanvasAnvil is an open source AI diagram maker and flowchart generator - an infinite-canvas diagram editor and self-hosted drawio alternative that writes editable .drawio files. Text to diagram, then fix nodes, layout and labels in place. Also AI presentations, interior design CAD/BOM, posters and infographics.

cls.summary: CanvasAnvil is an open-source, self-hosted web app that uses AI to generate and edit diagrams, presentations and interior-design drawings (exporting editable draw.io and DXF outputs).
cls.what_it_does: CanvasAnvil converts structured text prompts into editable diagrams, slide decks and interior design drawings, then lets users refine layout, labels and geometry on an infinite canvas. It is used through a web UI and a set of 'skills' that integrate with a host agent (Codex) to produce draw.io XML, PPTX, DXF and exportable assets; notable features include AI-driven text-to-diagram, editable draw.io output and an interior-design delivery pipeline with BOM/exports.
cls.trl_rationale: The project is active with a substantial README, hosted demo, multiple integrated features (diagram, CAD, PPT), and community interest (stars/forks), which indicates beyond early alpha; however the repository is only ~297 days old (<1 year), so there is not yet a long track record or wide adoption required for TRL 7+, limiting it to TRL 6.
prerequisites: optional: PowerPoint/LibreOffice for PPT previews and Python for editable PPTX scripts
student_project_ideas: Build a course activity where students prompt CanvasAnvil to generate system architecture diagrams from requirements, then refine and trace changes back to requirements using the draw.io XML export.

Create a workflow to convert a simple apartment floorplan into editable CAD outputs (DXF + BOM) produced by CanvasAnvil, then validate area and material quantities with a script (e.g. Python) and produce a cost estimate.

tools.name: Zhangweihui666/silver-tourism-digital-twin
tools.desc: Semantic digital twin and 500-agent simulation laboratory for age-friendly research in historic districts.

cls.summary: A browser-based research prototype that builds editable semantic digital twins of historic districts and runs 500-agent pedestrian simulations to evaluate age-friendly interventions.
cls.what_it_does: This project ingests map data, photos, trajectories and GeoJSON to produce an editable 3D semantic scene of a historic district, then runs configurable simulations of up to 500 heterogeneous elderly (silver) agents to evaluate accessibility, wayfinding and environmental-safety interventions. It is used via a prebuilt local Node.js web application (three.js front end) and exports research-ready figures, data ZIPs and GLB scenes for publication or further analysis.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository provides a runnable, prebuilt local web application and research-oriented exports (evidence of early adopters and examples), but it was created 49 days ago so there is limited public track record; README warns it is a research prototype rather than production-grade software.
prerequisites: optional: Python 3 and scientific Python packages for server-side plotting
student_project_ideas: Compare baseline vs redesigned sidewalk interventions in a sampled historic district by running the built-in tasks and producing reproducible accessibility and safety metrics exported as figures and GLB for a short report.

Integrate mobile-collected GPX traces and street photos into the studio to validate and quantify how real pedestrian routes affect agent-based wayfinding performance, combining the tool with simple statistical analysis in Python.

tools.name: ifocus9/PopTrans
tools.desc: PopTrans — Windows 本地离线翻译工具。选中文本 / OCR 截图后一键翻译，基于 Go + Wails + llama.cpp 纯 CPU 推理，无需 GPU。

cls.summary: PopTrans is a Windows desktop app that performs local, offline OCR and translation using llama.cpp so text and screenshots can be translated without sending data to the cloud.
cls.what_it_does: PopTrans captures selected text or screenshots, runs offline OCR and translates text locally using a llama.cpp-backed model (Hy-MT2-1.8B), and exposes a small local OpenAI-compatible API for integration. It is delivered as a Windows native app (Go + Wails UI) with an embedded Python ai_engine executable so end users do not need to install Python, and it supports CPU-only operation as well as GPU acceleration where available.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository shows an active, packaged Windows application with releases, detailed README, and CI-style build instructions; stars and recent activity indicate an active user/maintainer base. The project is 145 days old (under one year) so while it appears feature-complete and usable, it lacks the multi-year track record required for TRL 7+.
prerequisites: optional: GPU drivers for CUDA/Vulkan if using GPU acceleration
model file (Hy-MT2-1.8B GGUF) or network access to download it on first run
student_project_ideas: Extend PopTrans's local API by writing a small script that batch-processes screenshots from a technical document folder and produces a translated PDF with original and translated text side-by-side.

Build a usability study tool that integrates PopTrans's local OCR/translation API to measure translation latency and OCR accuracy on engineering diagrams, comparing CPU vs GPU inference and reporting results in a CSV.

tools.name: kairunwen/Awesome-Robot-Use-Agent
tools.desc: A curated collection of papers, research blogs, open-source tools, benchmarks, and community demos for robot-use agents, including demos powered by GPT-6 Astra. —— Explore our searchable website.

cls.summary: A curated, regularly updated collection of papers, projects, benchmarks and demos about robot-use agents—AI systems that plan and control robots to accomplish user goals.
cls.what_it_does: This repository collects and organises articles, academic papers, open-source projects, benchmarks and demo links focused on robot-use agents (AI agents that reason, plan and act through robots). It is used as a discovery and reference resource to find methods, frameworks, datasets and community demos when building or evaluating agent-driven robotics systems.
cls.trl_rationale: The repository is a curated index (not runnable software) created 67 days ago with active updates and community interest (188 stars), but it lacks a track record as a tool or production deployment; its maturity is that of a useful early-resource list rather than a production library.
student_project_ideas: Use the README's links to pick a recent open-source robot-use agent framework and reproduce a published demo in simulation (e.g. integrate an agent model with Gazebo/Isaac and document limitations).

Create a comparative literature review and benchmark runner that implements a small set of tasks from the listed benchmarks to evaluate two agent approaches (e.g. scripted skill-based vs. learned policy) in simulation.

tools.name: Magnvs7/Promethevs
tools.desc: PROMETHEVS: run the full DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017 (510 GB) on a gaming PC with 64 GB RAM and a 12 GB GPU. PROMETHEVS engine (compress-then-correct), OpenAI-compatible local server, report and logs.

cls.summary: PROMETHEVS is an open-source engine and installer that runs the full 510 GB DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash model on a single consumer gaming PC by using a compress-then-correct method and exposing an OpenAI‑compatible local API.
cls.what_it_does: PROMETHEVS implements a 'compress-then-correct' runtime that runs a 510 GB mixture-of-experts model on a PC with ~64 GB RAM and a 12 GB NVIDIA GPU by first evaluating a highly compressed 2-bit copy and selectively recomputing words with corrections from stored correction planes. It provides installer scripts, a local OpenAI-compatible HTTP endpoint (streaming and tool calls), verification/benchmarking scripts and measured speed/accuracy results to let users run the original model weights locally.
cls.trl_rationale: The repository is young (created 27 days ago) but contains a packaged release, installer scripts, measured benchmarks and many stars, indicating early real use; however the short age prevents TRL>5 despite evidence of functional builds and releases.
prerequisites: NVIDIA RTX 30/40 series GPU with 12 GB and appropriate drivers
student_project_ideas: Reproduce and extend the PROMETHEVS compress-then-correct evaluation by measuring agreement and throughput when varying cache policies and correction thresholds, comparing results to baseline exact decoding.

Build a small OpenAI-compatible client that integrates PROMETHEVS with an agent framework (e.g. LangChain) to evaluate latency and privacy trade-offs when running local LLM-based tools on constrained hardware.

tools.name: pissang/mutracer
tools.desc: WebGPU physically based path tracer

cls.summary: MuTracer is a Web-based physically based path tracer that renders PBR scenes on WebGPU (with a WebGL2 fallback) and integrates with Three.js for interactive, high‑quality imagery.
cls.what_it_does: MuTracer performs progressive, unidirectional path tracing in the browser with support for OpenPBR materials, BVH acceleration, denoising and offline‑quality output. It is used either by converting Three.js scenes via a THREESync helper or by constructing MuTracer scene objects directly, and it is notable for WebGPU-first rendering with a WebGL2 fallback and built-in BVH builders (including a WASM TinyBVH option).
cls.trl_rationale: The README shows a feature-rich library with examples, a live viewer, and WASM/worker builders, and the repo already has community interest (many stars). However the repository is only ~40 days old so it lacks a long track record of stable releases or proven production deployments, limiting maturity to around TRL 5.
prerequisites: familiarity with Three.js (optional) and glTF for scene loading
student_project_ideas: Build a lab exercise that loads a glTF CAD model into Three.js and uses MuTracer via THREESync to compare progressive path-traced renders and denoised outputs under different lighting setups.

Evaluate and benchmark BVH build strategies and denoising options by integrating MuTracer with a set of complex engineering scenes (large triangle counts) to measure build time, render convergence and final quality.

tools.name: game4automation/realvirtual-WEB
tools.desc: Browser-based 3D-HMI for industrial automation — Three.js/TypeScript viewer for realvirtual digital twins

cls.summary: realvirtual is a browser-based 3D HMI and digital twin platform for industrial automation that visualises machine state, runs in-browser simulations and connects to PLCs for virtual commissioning.
cls.what_it_does: realvirtual loads glTF/GLB machine models into a web viewer to provide live 3D HMI, operator dashboards and layout planning, and contains an in-browser discrete-event/physics-lite simulation for transport, collisions and machine sequencing. It connects to real or simulated controllers through realvirtual CONNECT (OPC UA, Siemens S7/TwinCAT, MQTT, EtherNet/IP, etc.), supports WebXR and multiuser collaboration, and is extensible via plugins; notable points are its full-browser runtime (TypeScript + three.js) and community vs commercial module split.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository is active, has a public demo, ~187 stars and a company (realvirtual GmbH) backing it, and the Community edition is runnable from source; however the repo is only ~8 months old so it lacks the multi-year track record and broad adoption required for TRL 7+, limiting it to TRL 6 (beta).
prerequisites: familiarity with three.js / WebGL and basic PLC/industrial protocols
student_project_ideas: Build a small virtual commissioning lab: import a glTF conveyor model, connect simulated PLC signals (e.g. via an OPC UA test server) and implement a LogicStep sequence to validate material flow and KPIs in the browser.

Create an interactive maintenance dashboard: attach technical documents to parts in a factory layout, implement alarm handling and an ECharts-based KPI panel, and demonstrate fault diagnosis workflows during a simulation run.

tools.name: script-gd/gdcc
tools.desc: GDCC is an AOT compiler that compiles GDScript into GDExtension binary module. Run GDScript safely and fast in Godot Engine from now on.

cls.summary: GDCC is an ahead-of-time compiler that turns Godot's GDScript into native GDExtension binary modules so GDScript can run with safety and near-native performance inside the Godot engine.
cls.what_it_does: GDCC compiles GDScript into native GDExtension binaries, allowing projects written in GDScript to run as compiled modules with improved performance and source-code protection. It is installed as a command-line tool or a Godot editor plugin and supports cross-compilation, hot-reload, and mixed typed/weakly-typed code. Notable features include an extensible compiler pipeline, fast incremental compilation, and claims of broad GDScript compatibility for Godot >= 4.5.0.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository is ~9 months old and README states 'beta' with releases and CI; shows substantive functionality and usage but is younger than one year and lacks long-term production track record, so maturity aligns with TRL 5 (alpha in use).
prerequisites: Familiarity with Godot Engine and GDScript
Basic command-line usage and build toolchains
Optional: familiarity with native GDExtension modules and cross-compilation concepts
student_project_ideas: Measure and compare runtime performance and memory usage of a Godot game subsystem (e.g. physics or AI) implemented as normal GDScript versus compiled with GDCC, and produce a report on trade-offs.
Create a small Godot tool/plugin that automates CI builds using GDCC cross-compilation packages to produce platform-specific GDExtension artifacts and demonstrate hot-reload in the editor.

tools.name: satelliteoflove/godot-mcp
tools.desc: Give your AI assistant eyes and hands in the Godot editor: scene editing, input injection, deterministic playtesting, and live game state for agents

cls.summary: godot-mcp is an MIT-licensed Godot editor addon and MCP server that gives AI agents deterministic, programmatic access to a running Godot game for scene editing, input injection, structured runtime observation and playtesting.
cls.what_it_does: It exposes a rich set of tools over the Model Context Protocol so agents can read and edit scenes, run GDScript in a live game, inject precise player inputs, freeze and step game time deterministically, and obtain structured JSON game-state digests and profiler data. It's used by installing a Godot plugin and running the provided MCP server (via npx) so an LLM-based assistant can drive, observe and verify in-editor and in-game changes without relying on screenshots alone.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository is active, has detailed docs, an installation flow and ~186 stars which indicate early community use; however it was created ~331 days ago (under one year) so it lacks the multi-year track record required for TRL 7+.
prerequisites: familiarity with Godot engine and GDScript
basic understanding of MCP / LLM-agent integrations
node/npm toolchain for the npx installer
student_project_ideas: Build an automated regression test that uses godot-mcp to freeze the game, step until an enemy spawn occurs, collect runtime state and assert enemy positions/velocities match expected behaviour.

Create an AI assistant that iteratively edits a scene to fix a reported collision bug: run the game frozen, reproduce the clip via injected inputs, modify collision shapes programmatically, and verify the fix by deterministic replay.

tools.name: HMDSimDev/heartmorrow
tools.desc: AI-powered dating simulator

cls.summary: Heartmorrow is a local-first, browser-playable dating and life simulator that uses a language model running on your machine or a pointed LLM endpoint to drive streamed, in-character conversations and persistent relationship mechanics.
cls.what_it_does: Heartmorrow lets you design characters and a world, then interact with them through streamed dialogue, in-game phone texting, minigames and a living calendar; it runs a small local server that forwards requests to a local or hosted LLM endpoint so the browser never communicates directly with the model. It is notable for being fully local-first (you can explore the UI without an LLM), supporting multiple LLM backends, and combining authored character definitions with model improvisation plus a deterministic rules engine that produces persistent relationship consequences.
cls.trl_rationale: The repo is an active, working project with a sizeable star count, documented features, and recent pushes, indicating a beta-quality product; however it is only ~150 days old (under one year) so there is not yet a long real-world track record to justify TRL 7+.
prerequisites: optional: a local or hosted LLM endpoint (LM Studio, Ollama, llama.cpp, vLLM, OpenAI/Anthropic API key) to enable chatting

tools.name: ceva-ip/DPDFNet
tools.desc: Clean up noisy speech in real time with DPDFNet - open-source streaming speech enhancement for research, audio apps, and edge devices. Includes pretrained models, PyTorch code, ONNX/TFLite inference, 8/16/48 kHz support, and live demos.

cls.summary: DPDFNet is an open-source, real-time speech enhancement library providing pretrained models, a Python/CLI API and edge-friendly ONNX/TFLite runtimes for noise suppression.
cls.what_it_does: DPDFNet removes noise from speech in real time for recordings, live streams and edge devices by running pretrained deep models (8/16/48 kHz) as a CLI, Python API or stateful streaming enhancer. It is notable for low-latency, small model sizes and ready-to-run ONNX and TFLite exports that make deployment on CPU and embedded devices practical.
cls.trl_rationale: The repository provides pretrained models, a PyPI package, CLI/Python APIs, ONNX/TFLite exporters and live demos indicating a ready beta-quality project; however the repo age is ~335 days (<1 year) so it fits TRL 6 rather than higher.
prerequisites: sounddevice or audio I/O libraries for real-time use
student_project_ideas: Build a low-latency voice enhancement pipeline on a Raspberry Pi or Jetson using a DPDFNet TFLite model and measure CPU usage, latency and quality under different noise conditions.
Integrate DPDFNet into a teleoperation link (audio stream in ROS or WebRTC) and evaluate perceived speech intelligibility and end-to-end latency compared to raw audio and an alternative denoiser.

tools.name: Seeed-Studio/kicad-mcp-server
tools.desc: 🔌 MCP server for KiCad EDA - Analyze schematics & PCBs, trace pin-level connections, automate design editing. Works with any MCP-compatible AI tool

cls.summary: A Python-based MCP server that allows AI assistants to inspect KiCad schematics and PCBs, trace pin-level connections, run ERC/DRC, manage parts, and generate embedded-device artifacts.
cls.what_it_does: The server exposes KiCad project information and analysis tools over the Model Context Protocol so language-model assistants can query and edit designs (schematics and .kicad_pcb), trace nets at pin-level accuracy, run ERC/DRC, and generate device-tree or hardware test code. It is installed into a Python environment (preferably KiCad's Python to access pcbnew) and integrates with MCP-capable clients (Claude, Cursor, etc.), making it notable for automating PCB/embedded design workflows via AI.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository is active (created 2026-01-25, recent pushes, 185 stars) with installation instructions, examples and client configuration, but is under one year old so it lacks the multi-year track record or stable 1.0+ releases required for TRL 7+.
prerequisites: an MCP-capable AI client (e.g. Claude, Cursor) for full workflow
student_project_ideas: Create an automated PCB linting pipeline that uses the MCP server to run DRC/ERC on student KiCad projects and produce a structured report (combine with CI like GitHub Actions).
Build an AI-driven pinmux assistant that queries the MCP server to identify pin conflicts and auto-generate device-tree fragments for a microcontroller board.

tools.name: io-eric/webcc
tools.desc: A lightweight C++ toolchain and framework for WebAssembly.

cls.summary: WebCC is a lightweight C++ toolchain and framework that compiles C++ to small WebAssembly binaries and provides a high-performance bridge to HTML5 APIs (Canvas, DOM, WebGL, WebGPU, Audio, etc.).
cls.what_it_does: WebCC generates minimal WASM binaries with generated glue headers and a binary command buffer to batch calls across the C++/JS boundary, reducing overhead and binary size. It is used as a single CLI tool to compile C++ projects for the browser and exposes APIs for DOM, Canvas, WebGL/WebGPU, input and networking, and includes an inline-JS escape hatch for missing APIs.
cls.trl_rationale: The project has substantive documentation, benchmarks, an install/build workflow and a working CLI, and a modest user community (184 stars), indicating a beta-level maturity. The repository is under 1 year old (created 2025-12-15, ~337 days), so there is not yet a longer production track record to justify TRL 7+.
prerequisites: basic web development (HTML/JS) and a browser
student_project_ideas: Build an interactive WebAssembly front-end for a simple physics simulation (e.g. particle system or rigid-body demo) using WebCC for rendering via WebGL/WebGPU and a C++ simulation loop.

Create a web-based teleoperation dashboard for a small robot: compile the robot-side C++ controller to WASM (UI & visualization in browser) and use WebSockets for telemetry, demonstrating low-latency UI updates with WebCC's batching.

tools.name: LeaddeOpenLab/awesome-opus-5-5-video-prompts
tools.desc: Claude Opus 5.5 video prompts for motion graphics, explainers, 3D scenes and interactive demos. Browse by use case, with previews, required inputs and tools.

cls.summary: A curated collection of user-shared prompts, previews and setup notes for creating videos and animations with Claude Opus 5.5 and web/JS toolchains.
cls.what_it_does: This repository collects example prompts for Claude Opus 5.5 targeted at motion graphics, explainers, 3D scenes and interactive demos, with visual previews and practical setup notes. Users browse categories, copy prompt text and follow short instructions to render previews (often as single HTML files) using browser/Node toolchains; the collection emphasises examples and templates rather than providing a runtime engine. It's notable for curated, categorized prompts and ready-to-open previews that lower the barrier to trying Opus 5.5 video outputs.
cls.trl_rationale: The repo is active and contains a public website, many examples and community interest (184 stars) but is only 50 days old, so it lacks a long track record; evidence supports alpha usage by early adopters rather than mature production adoption.
prerequisites: Playwright and FFmpeg for headless rendering/export
student_project_ideas: Use an Opus 5.5 motion-graphics prompt from the collection to produce a short 30s explainer video, integrating a Remotion or three.js scene and exporting via Playwright+FFmpeg.

Create an educational Manim-based lesson prompt from the library, generate narrated video outputs using edge-tts and compare the generated visuals with hand-authored Manim scenes to evaluate prompt-to-code fidelity.

tools.name: EthanChan050430/Saki-Panel
tools.desc: Next-gen AI-native server ops panel with an in-workspace SRE agent. Crash self-healing, safe rollbacks, Docker/game servers, and local Ollama support.

cls.summary: Saki Panel is an open-source web operations panel that combines process/container/game-server management, live logs/metrics and an in-workspace AI SRE agent with support for local LLMs.
cls.what_it_does: Saki Panel provides a unified web console to manage processes, Docker/Compose stacks, game servers (e.g. Minecraft/Steam) and remote Linux nodes, while surfacing live logs, files and resource metrics for incident investigation. It embeds an AI assistant that can inspect logs, propose or execute scoped operations (with approvals and safety controls), supports local LLM endpoints (Ollama/LM Studio) and offers crash self-healing, rollbacks and extensions.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository is ~203 days old (<1 year) but shows releases, active commits, 184 stars and install/run instructions; this demonstrates a beta-level project with community interest but not a long production track record.
prerequisites: SSH access to managed Linux nodes
Optional: local LLM endpoint such as Ollama or LM Studio
student_project_ideas: Integrate Saki Panel with a small fleet of Raspberry Pi nodes and implement a playbook (Skill) that detects a failing service, gathers logs, and performs an automated safe restart with rollback conditions.

Extend Saki with a custom extension that adds specialised telemetry ingestion (e.g. Prometheus exporter) and builds a reliability report dashboard comparing container resource usage before and after a configuration change.

tools.name: jaccen/Awesome-Gaussian-Skills
tools.desc: 1000+ arXiv-verified 3DGS methods · 15 AI agent skills · MCP server (34 tools) · open ebook — the AI-native entry to 3D Gaussian Splatting research

cls.summary: A curated knowledge base, interactive explorer and AI-skill collection for 3D Gaussian Splatting that ships an MCP server and 18 agent skills to make 3DGS research and workflows consumable by AI agents.
cls.what_it_does: This repository collects 1,066 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) methods with metadata, an interactive web explorer, an open technical book, and a set of AI agent skills plus an MCP server exposing 34 tools. It is used to search, compare and automate research and engineering workflows around 3DGS (papers → experiments → figures → experiments) and to let LLM-based agents call domain tools (render, import scene, edit gaussians). It is notable because it combines a large curated literature database with runnable agent skills and an MCP server for cross-client integration.
cls.trl_rationale: The repository is active, has a live interactive demo, many skills, and integrations (MCP server) but is only ~200 days old, so it lacks a long track record and wide independent adoption required for TRL 7+. The README and features indicate beta-level maturity.
prerequisites: familiarity with MCP-capable agent clients (Claude Code, Cursor, DSH) and basic 3D/NeRF concepts
basic TypeScript / JavaScript skills to run the MCP server or integrate skills
student_project_ideas: Use the repo's MCP server and skills to build an agent that automates converting a small photogrammetry dataset into a 3DGS model and produces a comparison report versus a baseline NeRF pipeline.

Create a class assignment where students extend or write a new skill to perform a specific 3DGS quality metric (e.g. PSNR or novel-view RMSE) and integrate the metric into the interactive explorer for dataset benchmarking.

tools.name: shiyao-li/MAGICIAN
tools.desc: [CVPR 2026 (Oral)] MAGICIAN: Efficient Long-Term Planning with Imagined Gaussians for Active Mapping

cls.summary: MAGICIAN is a research codebase implementing an active mapping and long-horizon planning method that uses imagined Gaussian splats to drive exploration trajectories and reconstruct 3D scenes.
cls.what_it_does: MAGICIAN implements an efficient planning algorithm for active exploration that predicts future information gain using imagined Gaussian representations and performs beam search to produce long-term camera trajectories. It is used by running the provided data pipelines, pretrained weights and evaluation scripts on indoor/outdoor scene datasets to generate exploration trajectories, coverage metrics and reconstructed point clouds/meshes, and it integrates with Gaussian reconstruction tools for final mesh extraction.
cls.trl_rationale: The repository accompanies a CVPR 2026 oral paper and includes pretrained weights, datasets, runnable scripts and build instructions, showing a working research prototype; however the project is under one year old (created 2026-03-25, ~237 days) so it is best characterised as a beta-level research codebase rather than long-established production software.
prerequisites: conda and basic CMake / build tools
student_project_ideas: Implement a student project that compares MAGICIAN's imagined-Gaussian planner to a baseline next-best-view planner on a single Matterport3D scene, evaluating coverage and final reconstruction quality.

Extend the pipeline to collect images from a simulated ROS robot (Gazebo or Habitat) and use MAGICIAN to generate real-time exploration trajectories, then reconstruct the scene with MILo and compare point-cloud metrics.

tools.name: cclank/clay-safari
tools.desc: 黏土风格 3D 双语动物世界 · A playful clay-style animal world built with Three.js and Blender.

cls.summary: An open-source, clay-style interactive 3D scene built with Blender-generated models and Three.js that demonstrates procedural modeling, real-time rendering and simple navigation/interaction in the browser.
cls.what_it_does: Clay Safari generates a stylised 3D scene of animals and props by exporting scripted Blender models to glTF and rendering them with Three.js in the browser. It provides interactive behaviours (click reactions, A* navigation, robot tour), procedural materials/noise-based textures, Web Audio/Web Speech synthesis and a live demo deployable to Cloudflare Workers, making it notable as a compact example of a full WebGL content pipeline from Blender scripting → glTF → web runtime.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository is runnable, well-documented, and has a live demo and deployment instructions, but it is only 71 days old so lacks a longer track record; therefore TRL is limited to alpha-in-use level.
prerequisites: basic web development (npm, Vite, ES modules)
student_project_ideas: Extend the scene with a new procedurally-generated animal: write a Blender builder function, export the glTF and add interactivity and synthesized sounds using the repo's audio and animals modules.

Benchmark mobile vs desktop rendering strategies by modifying post-processing, shadow resolution and instancing parameters to measure FPS and memory, and propose optimisations for large instanced scenes.

tools.name: HoppouAI/Breeze-TTS-2.cpp
tools.desc: Bilingual English and Mandarin text to speech in C++ and GGUF. Voice design, cloning, direction and experimental voice conversion. Vulkan backend, streaming HTTP and WebSocket server, web UI and a C API.

cls.summary: Breeze-TTS-2.cpp is a C++ implementation of bilingual (English/Mandarin) text-to-speech that runs GGUF models with a Vulkan (GPU) backend, a streaming server, and a C API for bindings.
cls.what_it_does: It generates speech from text, supporting voice design, voice cloning, voice direction and experimental voice conversion, and can stream audio over HTTP/WebSocket with a web UI. It is used as a local server or CLI and provides prebuilt Vulkan binaries for Windows and Linux and a shared C library for integration. Notable features are a Vulkan backend (with CPU fallback), multi-stream batching for realtime performance, and use of ggml/gguf model formats.
cls.trl_rationale: The repository is functional with prebuilt releases, CLI, server, and documented build steps and performance metrics, indicating early adopters can run it; however it is only 83 days old so by the policy its maturity is capped (no long track record), supporting a TRL ~5.
prerequisites: Vulkan SDK and GPU drivers for Vulkan backend (or CPU build)
AVX2-capable x64 CPU for CPU fallback
student_project_ideas: Build a web-based demo that hosts the Breeze server and adds a simple front-end for multi-user streaming and latency measurement, comparing Vulkan vs CPU performance on available hardware.

Integrate Breeze-TTS-2.cpp with a small robot or virtual agent (ROS/ROS2 or a web-based avatar) to provide voice cloning for human-robot interaction and evaluate perceived voice similarity using recorded reference clips.

tools.name: cortiz2894/flow-shield-effect
tools.desc: A real-time force shield effect built with React Three Fiber, Three.js, and custom GLSL shaders. This repository is a free open-source resource for the creative development community.

cls.summary: A WebGL-based, interactive force-shield visual effect implemented with React Three Fiber, Three.js and custom GLSL shaders for learning and VFX prototyping.
cls.what_it_does: Provides a production-quality, fully parametric shield VFX (hex grid, impact rings, dissolve/reveal, bloom and more) with a live 3D playground to tweak every parameter. It's used as a learning resource and drop-in visual effect for web-based 3D projects, notable for hand-written, well-commented GLSL and ready scene presets.
cls.trl_rationale: The repository is an actively maintained, runnable demo with clear installation and examples and a healthy star count, indicating community interest; however it is only ~9 months old so it lacks long-term production track record required for TRL 7+. README is strong and shows a live playground but no named industrial users.
prerequisites: basic JavaScript/TypeScript and GLSL shader knowledge
student_project_ideas: Integrate the shield effect into a simple WebXR scene to study shader performance and interaction latency on desktop vs mobile browsers.
Extend the hit system to drive sensor-like inputs from an external data stream (e.g. simulated impacts from a physics engine) and visualise damage propagation across a fleet of shields.

tools.name: Mcourtyard/m-courtyard
tools.desc: M-Courtyard: Local AI Model Fine-tuning Assistant for Apple Silicon. Zero-code, zero-cloud, privacy-first desktop app powered by Tauri + React + mlx-lm.

cls.summary: M-Courtyard is a macOS desktop app that provides a zero-code, local workflow for preparing data and fine-tuning LLMs on Apple Silicon using Apple MLX.
cls.what_it_does: M-Courtyard automates document ingestion, dataset generation (either AI-assisted or rule-based), and LoRA fine-tuning of local LLMs with live training visuals, and supports exporting models for local runtimes such as Ollama or MLX/LM Studio. It is used as a privacy-first desktop assistant on Apple Silicon that manages the local Python/MLX environment so users can fine-tune models without writing Python or using cloud GPUs.
cls.trl_rationale: The project is actively developed (recent commits, v0.5.9 changelog) and provides pre-built .dmg releases and documented build steps, indicating a beta-level maturity; however the repository is under one year old which limits TRL to 6 in this assessment.
prerequisites: Basic familiarity with local LLM concepts (LoRA, MLX, Ollama/LM Studio optional)
student_project_ideas: Build a course assignment where students fine-tune a small 3B model on a domain-specific document set (PDFs) using M-Courtyard, evaluate performance on held-out QA prompts, and report on dataset quality and training resource usage.

Integrate exported MLX models from M-Courtyard into a local LM Studio inference pipeline and measure latency and memory usage on different Apple Silicon chips to compare trade-offs between quantisation settings (Q4/Q8/F16).

tools.name: suncityldp/zx-bench
tools.desc: A reproducible local LLM benchmarking platform with versioned datasets, deterministic scoring, and auditable reports.

cls.summary: ZxBench is an open-source, locally runnable benchmarking platform for evaluating large language models with versioned datasets, deterministic scoring and auditable reports.
cls.what_it_does: ZxBench runs candidate LLMs in reproducible Docker-based environments, executes a published benchmark bank of prompts, and produces deterministic scores and reports (optionally using an AI judge). It is used by installing the TypeScript/Node service, preparing runtime images, syncing the released benchmark bank and running evaluations; notable features include frozen image manifests, deterministic scoring and offline deployment support.
cls.trl_rationale: The project is actively maintained with versioned releases (v0.2.13), a published benchmark bank, Docker-based deployment instructions and CI-like commands, and a moderate community (182 stars); repository age (~92 days) and non-1.0 release level suggest beta maturity rather than long-term production track record.
student_project_ideas: Compare evaluation results between two locally hosted LLMs (e.g. Llama-family vs an open instruction-tuned model) using ZxBench and analyse differences in score distributions and failure cases, then present remediation suggestions.
Extend ZxBench by adding a new benchmark dimension (custom prompts and scoring rubric) and integrate an automatic post-processing script that visualises per-task error types using a plotting library.

tools.name: wbc-mjlab/wbc-mjlab
tools.desc: One policy. Any motion. Train universal whole-body tracking in mjlab—swap clips, not checkpoints.

cls.summary: WBC-Mjlab is an open-source training and deployment pipeline that trains a single whole-body control policy in MuJoCo Lab to track many motion clips (humanoid skills) and includes a browser Studio for dataset, training and playback management.
cls.what_it_does: WBC-Mjlab provides a shared MDP, data pipeline and training recipes to train one policy that generalises across multiple motion clips for whole-body humanoid tracking using MuJoCo Lab. It supports PPO or a learned differentiable world model for training, export to ONNX for deployment, and a web-based WBC Studio to manage robots, clips, presets, training jobs and playback.
cls.trl_rationale: The repository is active, has extensive documentation, Docker/devcontainer support, a live demo and sample checkpoints, and many stars, indicating an organised beta-quality project; however it is only ~5–6 months old (<1 year) so it lacks the longer track record needed for TRL 7+.
prerequisites: Python and typical ML toolchain (PyTorch ecosystem implied)
student_project_ideas: Train a single-policy humanoid controller on a small multi-clip dataset (walk/run/crawl) using WBC-Mjlab and evaluate generalisation to unseen clips, comparing PPO vs the world-model recipe.
Integrate a custom URDF humanoid into WBC-Mjlab, create a small motion library from motion-capture or generated clips, and test policy export to ONNX for real-time playback in a lightweight runtime.

tools.name: kisaragi-mochi/stackchan-mcp
tools.desc: MCP gateway for StackChan (xiaozhi-esp32): bridge any MCP client to a CoreS3 + servo + camera robot

cls.summary: stackchan-mcp is an open-source MCP gateway and firmware bundle that lets LLM clients control the M5Stack StackChan robot (CoreS3 + servos + camera) over WebSocket/HTTP/stdio.
cls.what_it_does: It bridges Model Context Protocol (MCP) clients to the StackChan hardware, exposing device operations (head movement, camera capture, touch, LEDs, TTS/STT hooks, avatar control) through a Python gateway and companion ESP32 firmware. Notable elements include a complete firmware subtree for the CoreS3-based StackChan, a Python stdio/WebSocket MCP gateway, and documented integration with local TTS/STT services and remote access playbooks.
cls.trl_rationale: The project is active, has substantial documentation, a full firmware subtree and a working Python gateway, and shows community interest (182 stars). The repo is 201 days old (younger than one year), so while it appears beta-ready with integration docs and examples, it lacks the multi-year production track record required for TRL 7+.
prerequisites: familiarity with ESP32 firmware building and flashing
Python environment and basic web/socket tooling
comfort with command-line tooling and embedded hardware (M5Stack)
student_project_ideas: Build a conversational robot demo where an LLM (MCP client) uses stackchan-mcp to take photos, run an object classifier (e.g. a small PyTorch model) on the gateway, and then respond aloud with contextual behaviour and head movement.

Implement an autonomous interaction mode: use the StackChan camera + faster-whisper STT to detect a spoken keyword, then run an onboard state machine that performs servo gestures, LED animations and TTS responses via the gateway (evaluate latency and robustness).

tools.name: jenissimo/bottleship
tools.desc: Run classic Windows games in your browser. A high-level-emulation engine that boots real x86 Windows executables and reimplements Win32, COM and DirectDraw/Direct3D on WebGPU, WebAudio and OPFS

cls.summary: BottleShip is a browser-based high-level emulator that runs real x86 Windows game executables by reimplementing Win32, DirectDraw/Direct3D and audio on WebGPU/WebAudio without a full OS image.
cls.what_it_does: BottleShip loads a game's PE executable into a WASM x86 runtime (a fork of v86) and intercepts Win32/DirectX calls, translating graphics to WebGPU and audio to WebAudio while storing files in OPFS. It is used to play and preserve late‑90s/early‑2000s Windows games in modern browsers and to develop compatibility fixes for missing Win32/DirectX behaviours.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository is active with a v0.8 release, an online demo site, and many tested titles which show more than prototype maturity, but it is under 1 year old (created ~128 days ago) so it fits a beta-level TRL rather than long-term production maturity.
prerequisites: understanding of WebAssembly and x86 emulation concepts
WebGPU-capable browser and Bun for local development
student_project_ideas: Implement and upstream a missing Win32 or DirectDraw API stub in BottleShip and verify compatibility improvements against a test game from the compatibility list.
Measure and profile Direct3D→WebGPU translation performance for a specific title and optimise WGSL shader generation or resource upload to reduce frame-time spikes.

tools.name: Tim-HW/glass-lio
tools.desc: A transparent LiDAR-inertial odometry for Livox. written to be read :D For more in depth course you can check the website below

cls.summary: glass-LIO is a C++ ROS2 LiDAR–inertial odometry implementation for Livox sensors that emphasises explainable implementation and teaching of Lie-algebra‑based scan-to-map odometry.
cls.what_it_does: It deskews Livox ~100 ms sweeps with gyro integration, voxel-downsamples and registers scans against a local voxel-plane map using a point-to-plane ICP solved by a small Gauss–Newton solver on SE(3), then inserts the aligned scan back into the map to produce an odometry stream. It is distributed as a ROS 2 node with Docker/devcontainer support and extensive documentation and tests intended to make the math and implementation choices readable and auditable.
cls.trl_rationale: The repo is under 1 year old (created 2026-07-14) so TRL is capped; however it contains a working ROS2 node, Docker/devcontainer, tests, documented results on a test bag and an included solver submodule which indicates a beta-level, usable project rather than a throwaway demo.
prerequisites: Eigen / linear algebra (Lie algebra familiarity helpful)
Linux + Docker and colcon build experience
student_project_ideas: Extend glass-LIO to fuse a separate GNSS or wheel-odometry stream and evaluate pose accuracy on the provided bag, comparing RMSE and drift to the base system.
Replace the built-in Gauss–Newton solver with Ceres or GTSAM bindings and benchmark convergence, runtime and sensitivity to Jacobian errors on the test bag.

tools.name: Corebrum/corebrum-synapse
tools.desc: ROS plugin for OpenClaw, Claude (Code,Desktop,Dispatch), Codex, Google Gemini, Hermes, MCP, etc.

cls.summary: Corebrum Synapse is an open middleware layer that connects ROS 2 robots to multiple AI agent platforms so robots can perceive, reason and act from natural-language or multimodal agent prompts.
cls.what_it_does: It provides a platform-agnostic transport and tool contract that exposes ROS2 sensors, actuators and utilities as tools to external AI agents (OpenClaw, Claude, Codex, Gemini, Hermes, Ollama, etc.), letting those agents run skills, teleop, perception queries and missions. It is deployed as ROS2 packages and adapter plugins and is notable for supporting many agent runtimes (including local VLMs) without changing the ROS layer.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository is ~9 months old with active pushes, 180 stars, documentation, hardware guides and multiple adapter packages, showing beta-level readiness and community interest but not yet long-term production track record required for TRL 7+.
prerequisites: Familiarity with LLM / VLM APIs or local runtimes (Ollama) and basic networking
Basic robotics hardware knowledge (teleop, cmd_vel, sensors such as RealSense)
student_project_ideas: Integrate Corebrum Synapse with a small ROS2 mobile robot and a local Ollama VLM to build a voice-driven inspect-and-report robot that captures images and produces natural-language scene summaries.

Extend or write an adapter for a new agent (e.g. local LLM runtime or a custom web agent) and evaluate latency, safety controls and perception accuracy when issuing navigation and object-finding missions.

tools.name: ToxSam/open-source-3D-assets
tools.desc: CC0 3D asset registry: 991+ GLB models from metaverse projects. JSON-based database linking to permanent storage. Medieval props, vaporwave rooms, Egyptian temples, neon streets, and more. API-friendly structure for developers building asset browsers and creative tools.

cls.summary: A curated, JSON-indexed registry of CC0 and open-licensed 3D models (GLB/FBX/OBJ) intended for games, web/VR experiences and creative projects.
cls.what_it_does: The repository provides a machine-readable directory (JSON) linking to permanently hosted 3D model files, preview images and license metadata so developers can programmatically discover and download assets. It is used by fetching the projects.json and per-collection asset JSON files and then loading the referenced GLB/FBX files into three.js, Blender, Unity or other tools; notable is its API-friendly, license-explicit indexing of many CC0/open collections.
cls.trl_rationale: The repository is a working, populated dataset with documentation and examples and a public website, showing more than a basic demo; however it is under one year old (created ~286 days ago) so lacks the long track record or large ecosystem needed for TRL 7+. Activity and stars indicate a small but real user interest.
prerequisites: familiarity with three.js or common 3D tools (Blender/Unity) to load GLB/FBX
student_project_ideas: Build a small WebGL scene using three.js that dynamically queries the registry JSON and loads selected GLB assets into a runtime scene with lighting and interaction.

Create an asset-management pipeline where students convert downloaded GLB files to game-ready prefabs in Unity (apply LOD, colliders, and material tweaks) and track provenance/licenses using the registry metadata.

tools.name: v-modal/physical_ai_stack
tools.desc: SDK and stack for physical AI layer

cls.summary: A curated 'awesome' list of resources, tools and literature for Physical AI and embodied/robotics learning covering simulation, datasets, models and deployment patterns.
cls.what_it_does: This repository collects and organises links to simulators, datasets, benchmarks, foundation models, world models, sim-to-real methods, hardware and pedagogical materials for embodied and physical AI. It is used as a starting map for developers, researchers and educators to find existing tools and papers rather than providing runnable software itself. Notable for its broad, engineering-focused curation of contemporary robotics and embodied-AI resources.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository is a curated, recently created 'awesome' list (created ~103 days ago) with no runnable software in the repo; it is usable as a reference but has no measurable production track record, so maturity is early (README-driven curation rather than a stable software product).
student_project_ideas: Use the curated list to select and compare two simulators (e.g. PyBullet and MuJoCo or Isaac Sim) on a simple manipulation task and report differences in setup, fidelity and sim-to-real considerations.

Build a reproducible reading-and-tools syllabus from the list and produce a tutorial notebook that demonstrates a minimal robot learning workflow (simulation → training → evaluation) using one recommended library.

tools.name: tangency-labs/pcbcraft-gpl
tools.desc: MCP-first Rust EDA with a single-window tabbed editor, KiCad compatibility, and craft-libs

cls.summary: PCBCraft is an open-source Rust-based EDA application providing a single-window tabbed editor for schematic capture, footprint/library editing, basic PCB layout and KiCad-compatible export.
cls.what_it_does: PCBCraft provides schematic editing, library and footprint authorship, SMD/PTH pad support, a simple orthogonal routing tool and design checks, with project persistence and KiCad board export. It is used as a native desktop app (and compiles to WebAssembly) and is notable for its MCP-first command engine, integrated library editing, and explicit KiCad library discovery and export interoperability.
cls.trl_rationale: The README documents a substantial working vertical slice (schematic → PCB → KiCad export, libraries, checks) and runnable instructions, but the repository is very new (36 days) with many open issues, so maturity is at an early-in-use/alpha level (TRL 5).
prerequisites: basic PCB / EDA concepts and KiCad familiarity
student_project_ideas: Use PCBCraft to create, edit and export a simple LED blinker PCB, then import the exported KiCad board into KiCad for fabrication workflow validation.
Extend PCBCraft by adding an obstacle-aware routing heuristic (or integrate a basic A* router) and compare routed results and clearance checks against the built-in orthogonal router.

tools.name: wieslawsoltes/VB6
tools.desc: VB6 Studio Web — a browser-native classic Visual Basic IDE, form designer, source runtime and controls library in HTML, CSS and JavaScript, with a debugger, WebGPU drawing and single-file HTML app export.

cls.summary: VB6 Studio Web is a browser-native implementation of a classic Visual Basic 6 IDE, runtime and form designer built with HTML, CSS and JavaScript that can export projects as single-file HTML applications.
cls.what_it_does: The project provides an in-browser Visual Basic 6-like development environment including a form designer, code editor with IntelliSense, runtime, debugger and controls library. It runs in modern browsers using WebGPU with a Canvas2D fallback, is built with Node.js tooling for local builds/serving, and can export editable projects as standalone HTML apps.
cls.trl_rationale: The repository is new (created ~44 days ago) but contains a working IDE, build scripts, examples and CI-built artifacts, indicating early adopters can run it; its short public track record and young age limit the rating to TRL 5 (alpha in use).
prerequisites: modern web browser with WebGPU or WebGL/Canvas2D fallback

tools.name: mike007jd/voxel-musou
tools.desc: Dynasty Warriors-style voxel action game in the browser: Zhao Yun vs 300 soldiers. Three.js, no build step.

cls.summary: Voxel Musou is a browser-playable voxel action game built with Three.js that recreates Dynasty Warriors–style large-scale battles.
cls.what_it_does: The repository provides a complete, playable voxel action game (campaign, trials and free battles) that runs as plain ES modules in the browser with no build step. It emphasises hundreds of instanced soldiers, voxel characters, procedural WebAudio and performance features (fixed 60 Hz simulation, automatic MSAA reduction) and is notable for using Three.js r186 and a zero-build workflow.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository is recent (created 54 days ago) but contains a complete, playable product without a build step and has community interest (177 stars). Age limits higher TRL levels; there is no long track record or evidence of production deployment, so TRL 5 (alpha in use) is appropriate.
prerequisites: familiarity with Three.js and WebGL concepts
student_project_ideas: Measure and optimise the game's rendering performance by profiling instanced voxel rendering and implementing LOD or culling improvements using Three.js.
Extend the game with a simple physics-based enemy ragdoll or integrate a WebXR view to explore one battlefield in VR, modifying assets and camera controls.

tools.name: soniqo/speech-android
tools.desc: On-device speech SDK for Android — ASR, TTS, VAD, and noise cancellation powered by ONNX Runtime with Qualcomm NNAPI acceleration

cls.summary: An on-device Android SDK providing offline speech capabilities (ASR, TTS, VAD, noise reduction) using ONNX Runtime and Qualcomm NNAPI acceleration.
cls.what_it_does: The repository packages a Kotlin SDK, JNI bridge and demo app that run automatic speech recognition, text-to-speech, voice activity detection and noise cancellation locally on Android devices. It is used by embedding the SDK in Android apps and pulling native inference code and models (via a speech-core submodule and ONNX Runtime) to perform low-latency, offline voice processing with optional NNAPI acceleration on Qualcomm platforms.
cls.trl_rationale: The project is active, provides demo APKs, model links and a linked native engine (speech-core) and shows platform-specific acceleration (NNAPI), which indicates beyond-alpha maturity; however the repository is only ~8 months old so lacks long-term track record required for TRL7+.
prerequisites: familiarity with ONNX Runtime and model lifecycle
student_project_ideas: Build an offline voice-control Android app for a robot or IoT device that uses the SDK for wake-word/VAD, on-device ASR for commands, and Kokoro/Pocket TTS for responses, integrating with a microcontroller over MQTT.

Compare on-device inference performance and energy use on different Qualcomm-based phones by running the SDK with different models (Parakeet vs smaller streaming model) and measuring latency, memory and battery impact.

tools.name: zhbi98/pcb-layout-design
tools.desc: 【Codex PCB Layout Skill】GPT-6  Astra/Sol x KiCad10. PCB 自动布线 Skill（涵盖通用规则，DDR，USB，CAN等各类接口的 ESD 器件泄放路径等专项规则）

cls.summary: A Codex 'skill' that guides an LLM agent to perform PCB component placement, routing, copper pours and manufacture-prep for KiCad projects using a set of engineering rules and checklists.
cls.what_it_does: This repository provides a packaged Skill (markdown, references and examples) that an LLM-based Codex agent can read and apply to automate or review PCB layout tasks after schematic and footprints are ready. It is used by placing the Skill folder where the Codex agent can read it; the agent then follows the documented rules for placement, routing, copper pours, DRC checks and manufacturing data generation. It is notable because it collects interface-specific rules (DDR, USB, CAN, ESD paths) and manufacturing checklists tailored for KiCad workflows.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository is young (created 65 days ago) but shows a structured Skill with reference documents, case study and concrete usage instructions; public interest (stars) suggests early adoption but not a proven production track record, so TRL is limited to 'Alpha in use'.
prerequisites: familiarity with KiCad PCB workflow (pcbnew, stackups, DRC)
ability to run or access a Codex/LLM agent (GPT-6 / Astra/Sol) and point it at local files
basic PCB design knowledge (routing, manufacturing constraints, signal integrity basics)
student_project_ideas: Use the Skill with a local KiCad project to implement and verify DDR routing rules on a simple dev-board: compare agent-produced layout to a manual layout and report DRC/impedance differences.

Integrate the Skill into an automated review pipeline: have the Codex agent run a read-only checklist on several KiCad projects and produce a prioritized list of manufacturing and assembly issues, then implement fixes for one issue set.

tools.name: rubenCodeforges/ardudeck
tools.desc: One GCS to rule them all. ArduPilot, Betaflight, iNav - all in one app. Mission planning, PID tuning, OSD simulator, SITL with FlightGear. Cross-platform (Win/Mac/Linux)

cls.summary: ArduDeck is an open-source, cross-platform ground control station for ArduPilot, Betaflight and iNav that provides mission planning, telemetry, onboard configuration, SITL with FlightGear and tools for fleet operations.
cls.what_it_does: ArduDeck lets users connect to and operate multirotor and fixed-wing vehicles using MAVLink (ArduPilot) or MSP (Betaflight/iNav), offering mission planning, telemetry dashboards, map overlays, OSD tools, RTK/NTRIP support and a SITL integration with FlightGear. It is delivered as an Electron desktop application (Windows/Mac/Linux) and is notable for supporting multiple firmware ecosystems in one unified app and features for multi-vehicle/fleet workflows.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository shows an active project with beta releases (0.1.2), real-world use reported in the README, and ongoing commits, but the repo age is under one year so there is not yet a long track record of stable production releases—appropriate for TRL 6 (beta).
prerequisites: familiarity with drones and flight controllers (ArduPilot/Betaflight/iNav)
Node.js / npm and Electron build tools
student_project_ideas: Integrate a small quad simulated in SITL with FlightGear and implement an autonomous survey mission planner that divides a survey area across multiple vehicles, then visualise and compare flight logs.

Build an extension or plugin that adds an automated RTK correction manager (NTRIP client + fallback logic) and evaluate positioning improvements in logged flights using ArduDeck's fleet log retrieval.

tools.name: raullenchai/twinspark
tools.desc: Production-grade recipe for DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731 (284B MoE) on 2x NVIDIA DGX Spark: self-healing 2-node vLLM cluster, reboot-verified, tuned DSpark speculative decoding (~75 tok/s), full benchmarks, OpenAI Codex CLI integration

cls.summary: Twinspark is a production recipe and deployment guide for running the DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731 large Mixture-of-Experts LLM across two NVIDIA DGX Spark nodes using a vLLM-based serving stack and Ray for orchestration.
cls.what_it_does: It packages a tested deployment and tuning recipe to run a 284B-MoE LLM across a 2-node DGX Spark cluster (TP=2) with RDMA/NCCL optimisations, DSpark speculative decoding, benchmarking, and an OpenAI Codex CLI integration for local inference. It is used as an operations playbook: hardware/fabric preflight, model distribution, container image build, runtime flags and performance tuning, plus end-to-end benchmark results and gotchas specific to DGX Spark and RoCE fabrics.
cls.trl_rationale: The repository provides a detailed, version-pinned, benchmarked deployment recipe and quick-start scripts that go beyond a toy demo, indicating beta-level maturity; however it is very new (created ~98 days ago) and has a small community footprint, so TRL is limited to Beta rather than production-proven at scale.
prerequisites: NVIDIA CUDA / NCCL and RDMA (RoCE) knowledge
familiarity with vLLM and Hugging Face model downloads
student_project_ideas: Reproduce parts of the recipe on a smaller multi-GPU workstation (e.g. 2x A100) with a much smaller model, measure and compare NCCL/RDMA vs TCP performance for token decode throughput.
Implement an experiment comparing DSpark speculative decoding vs standard decoding on a downsized model and report throughput/latency trade-offs and batching behaviour for concurrent agents.

tools.name: ReshefElisha/jarvis-onshape-mcp
tools.desc: Jarvis Onshape MCP — Claude Code plugin for driving real Onshape CAD. Vision-decomposition skill + truth-telling + parametric iteration + FeatureScript.

cls.summary: A Claude Code plugin that lets an LLM drive real Onshape parametric CAD (sketches, features, assemblies) with vision-guided workflows, per-feature truth reporting and FeatureScript escape hatches.
cls.what_it_does: The project provides an MCP plugin that connects Claude Code to the Onshape API so the agent can create and edit Part Studios, features and assemblies, render multi-view PNGs, extract drawing dimensions via OCR, and run parametric iterations via Variable Studios. It adds structured, per-mutation truth (what changed, warnings, hints) and a vision-decomposition skill that walks the agent through reading a reference image before building, plus the ability to emit custom FeatureScript features when primitives are insufficient.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository is 214 days old (<1 year) but shows substantial functionality, a detailed README, many stars (176) and install instructions and dependencies; these signs indicate a beta-quality tool used by early adopters but not yet a long-track production project, so TRL 6 is appropriate.
prerequisites: Onshape account and developer API key
Claude Code with plugin support (desktop or CLI)
student_project_ideas: Build an LLM-driven parametric part configurator: use the plugin to implement a small Claude workflow that re-parameters a bracket (dimensions, hole pattern) and exports DXF/STL for manufacturing, comparing geometry diffs after each iteration.

Evaluate vision-decomposition for CAD-from-image: give students a set of engineering drawing images, have the agent produce feature trees via the vision-decompose skill, then implement and validate the resulting parts in Onshape while measuring error rates and needed human corrections.

tools.name: fatasia/DeepMonkey-Studio
tools.desc: 从 Vibe Coding 到 Vibe World：AI原生的可编程三维世界，面向元宇宙、Science、世界模型的开源底座

cls.summary: DeepMonkey Studio is an open-source WebGPU + Rust/TypeScript platform for building programmable 3D worlds, digital twins and industrial/architectural scenes with model import, simulation, AI workflows and multi‑platform delivery.
cls.what_it_does: DeepMonkey Studio provides a combined editor, rendering engine and data platform to import BIM/CAD/URDF, connect industrial protocols and time-series, run physics/plant/robotic simulations and drive AI agents against a scene. It is used through a web editor, native Windows editor or Docker deployment and exposes SDKs, script APIs and MCP/Skill connectors to automate scene operations and integrate external systems.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository is ~105 days old but already provides releases (v0.2.0), Docker deployment, online demos and extensive docs, indicating more than an alpha; however the project is new so maturity is limited to beta-level (TRL 6).
prerequisites: familiarity with Docker and web deployment
TypeScript or Rust experience for SDK/integration
student_project_ideas: Integrate an IFC model and live OPC UA data stream to build a small digital-twin dashboard showing component status and alarm propagation using DeepMonkey's scene and data APIs.

Create a factory cell simulation that imports URDF robot models, runs a simple plant-lite discrete-event scenario, and compares throughput under two layout variants using the platform's virtual debug and replay features.

tools.name: tubecreate/tubecli
tools.desc: ⚡ TubeCLI — The Ultimate Open Source AI Agents Ecosystem | Agents Browser · Agents Workflow · Agents Studio World

cls.summary: TubeCLI is a self-hosted multi-agent platform that automates operational tasks (video production, browser automation, site deployment and task workflows) from a CLI, web dashboard or messaging clients.
cls.what_it_does: TubeCLI runs teams of AI agents on your machine to perform end-to-end operational workflows such as turning scraped content into narrated videos, driving web apps inside browser profiles, and deploying websites to cloud services. It is used via a CLI, web dashboard (FastAPI + Vue) or messaging integrations and includes a task board, a canvas/flow editor and a render engine for video/storyboard production.
cls.trl_rationale: The project is actively developed (regular pushes, many features described in the README), has a non-trivial user-facing CLI/web stack and 174 stars, but the repository is only ~8 months old so it lacks the long track record or widely documented production deployments required for TRL7+.
prerequisites: familiarity with CLI and basic server setup
(optional) Cloud service accounts for publishing (Cloudflare, YouTube, Google Drive)
student_project_ideas: Create an automated pipeline that scrapes a technical blog, generates a short narrated summary video with TubeCLI's content_video flow, and publishes the result to a personal YouTube channel (using a test account).
Build and document a safe, reproducible 'website agent' that deploys a sample web app to Cloudflare Workers using TubeCLI, and add checks that validate each deployment step and rollback on failure.

tools.name: playopenz/OpenZ
tools.desc: OpenZ: the faithful open-source 3D fan remake of Z (The Bitmap Brothers, 1996) for its 30th anniversary. Free, never sold, 100% original assets.

cls.summary: OpenZ is an open-source 3D fan remake of the 1996 real-time-strategy game Z, published under GPL-3.0 and distributed as playable builds for Windows, Mac and Linux.
cls.what_it_does: OpenZ recreates the classic RTS Z in modern 3D using Unity, providing downloadable builds and source code so users can play, inspect, modify or extend the game. It is used as a standalone game project (no installer required) with features such as multiple difficulty levels, unit editors and platform-specific builds; notable for being a faithful fan remake with free assets and cross-platform experimental builds.
cls.trl_rationale: The repository is very new (created 36 days ago) but already provides downloadable builds (versioned 1.4), an active README and issue tracker; this indicates an early alpha project that runs for users but lacks a long track record, wider adoption, or multi-release history.
prerequisites: familiarity with building/running Unity projects on target OS
student_project_ideas: Profile and optimise OpenZ on a low-power platform (e.g. Steam Deck), measuring CPU/GPU usage and implementing simple changes to improve frame rate.
Extend or mod a game feature (new unit or map) by editing Unity scenes and C# scripts to demonstrate game architecture, asset pipelines and basic AI behaviour.

tools.name: Blackwellboy/model-serving-minefield
tools.desc: Community registry of LLM serving-path traps that produce confidently wrong measurements: templates, tool parsers, reasoning fields, quant kernel paths, CUDA toolchains, KV allocation, eval harnesses, versioning. Symptom-first, with the check that catches each.

cls.summary: A curated registry and CLI tool that detects and diagnoses subtle serving-path bugs that produce confidently wrong measurements from local or hosted LLM deployments.
cls.what_it_does: Model Serving Minefield collects reproducible 'traps' in LLM serving (chat templates, quant kernels, tool parsers, container toolchains, memory/KV allocation, eval harnesses and more) and provides automated checks plus a CLI/doctor to scan configs, logs and live endpoints to find the root cause. It is used as a diagnostic aid during deployment and evaluation to turn hours of debugging into quick checks, with explicit reproduction steps and fixes for each trap.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository provides a packaged CLI, many documented checks, automated scans and a runnable doctor, active pushes and community interest (stars/forks) but is only ~113 days old so lacks long-term production track record required for TRL 7+.
prerequisites: familiarity with LLM serving stacks (Docker, model configs, endpoints)
basic knowledge of GPU/CUDA and container launch flags for advanced checks
student_project_ideas: Create an automated CI check using the project's scan or doctor to run on a student group's LLM deployment pipeline (Docker-compose + model) and report common traps as part of a reproducible engineering exercise.

Compare model evaluation results before and after fixing a reported trap (e.g. chat-template or quantization kernel mismatch) using an evaluation harness such as lm-eval or a custom benchmark to quantify measurement bias introduced by the serving bug.
