tools.name: DingoOz/llm-visuals
tools.desc: Live truecolor terminal dashboard for a locally running LLM: tok/s, TTFT, GPUs, context, MTP acceptance, layer and real expert routing (llama.cpp)

cls.summary: A true‑color terminal dashboard that monitors locally running LLM inference servers and GPU telemetry to show live throughput, latency and model/server internals.
cls.what_it_does: llm-visuals discovers local LLM inference servers (llama.cpp, vLLM, Ollama, etc.), reads their performance counters and GPU telemetry, and renders a live terminal dashboard showing tokens/s, time-to-first-token, GPU load/memory, context fill and routing decisions for mixture‑of‑experts models. It is used as a developer/ops tool from the terminal or as a demo mode; notable features include per‑layer/GPU activity and optional exact expert routing when a small server patch is applied.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository is 67 days old which limits TRL to <=5; README shows active development, releases with prebuilt binaries and a user community (stars), but there is no long track record of production deployments yet.
prerequisites: locally running LLM inference server (e.g. llama-server, vLLM, Ollama) for full functionality
Rust toolchain (1.75+) only required if building from source; otherwise use prebuilt binaries
GPU vendor CLI tools for telemetry (nvidia-smi, xpu-smi, macmon or appropriate drivers)
student_project_ideas: Extend llm-visuals to collect and forward its metrics to a time-series DB (Prometheus/InfluxDB) and build a Grafana dashboard correlating model throughput with GPU metrics.

Implement a small server-side patch and use llm-visuals to visualise and quantify expert routing behaviour for a mixture-of-experts model, then compare runtime performance across different model sharding strategies.

tools.name: hamzaydia/verifyfetch
tools.desc: Your users download a 4GB AI model, the connection drops at 3.8GB, verifyfetch resumes from 3.8GB and verifies every byte. Drop-in integrity verification for Transformers.js, WebLLM, and any large file in the browser.

cls.summary: VerifyFetch is a TypeScript library that performs streaming, chunked integrity verification and resumable downloads of large files (especially AI model weights) directly in the browser and Node.
cls.what_it_does: VerifyFetch solves the problem of downloading very large files in browsers without buffering them into memory, by downloading in verified chunks, persisting progress in IndexedDB, and resuming broken transfers. It is used as a drop-in verified-fetch replacement or via provided integrations (Transformers.js, WebLLM) and as a service-worker to transparently verify fetches. Notable features are constant-memory streaming verification, fail-fast detection of corrupted chunks, chunked manifests and multi-CDN source strategies.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository is under 1 year old (≈296 days) which caps TRL at 6; however it has a published npm package, CLI, WASM build step, direct integrations (Transformers.js, WebLLM) and 160 stars indicating an active beta-stage project suitable for early adopters.
prerequisites: understanding of cryptographic hashes (SRI) and IndexedDB
student_project_ideas: Integrate VerifyFetch into a web demo that loads an ONNX or GGUF model in the browser and measure resilience to simulated network drops while reporting verified-progress and memory usage.

Build a small CI pipeline step that uses the verifyfetch CLI to sign model artifacts and then a service-worker in a deployed web app to validate manifests and demonstrate protection against corrupted CDN responses.

tools.name: Xiaoyangy/novel-studio
tools.desc: 开源、本地优先的 AI 长篇小说创作引擎：多智能体世界推演、按弧规划、RAG 长程记忆、逐章审核与断点恢复 | Open-source AI novel generator for long-form fiction.

cls.summary: An open-source, local-first engine that coordinates multi-agent LLM workflows, RAG memory and checkpointed pipelines to help generate, review and produce long-form novels and serial fiction.
cls.what_it_does: Novel-studio orchestrates multi-agent story production: it initializes a verifiable world and character state, runs arc-level rehearsals and short planning windows where character agents decide actions, builds RAG- backed context, renders chapter drafts, and provides checkpointed audit trails and a read-only dashboard for progress. It is used as a CLI/service (written in Go with a Python dashboard) and notable for its production-oriented features (sealed render packets, SHA-256 digests, restartable pipelines and structured world/ mechanism files) aimed at reliable long-form writing rather than chat-style continuation.
cls.trl_rationale: The project is actively developed, has install scripts, a CLI, dashboard, documented workflow and mentions Releases (v0.3.0), showing beyond prototype status; however the repository is only ~4 months old (134 days) so it lacks the long track record or broad adoption needed for TRL 7+.
prerequisites: At least one LLM/text model provider (OpenAI-compatible or local model)

tools.name: MaxSikorski/jumpstart-3d
tools.desc: Browser-based 3D CAD, community-maintained. No install.

cls.summary: JumpStart 3D is a free, browser-based parametric 3D CAD application that runs as a single HTML file and supports sketch/extrude workflows and a beginner block-building mode.
cls.what_it_does: It provides a no-install, in-browser CAD workspace for creating parametric 3D models (sketch, extrude, fillet, shell, lathe and pattern tools) and exports common formats (STL etc.). It is notable for being a single-file app that runs offline after first load, an embeddable API (window.JS3D) for automation or integration, and a small WebAssembly geometry engine to keep the client lightweight.
cls.trl_rationale: The project provides a working web app and single-file releases and is actively maintained as a community fork, but the repository is very new (≈33 days) so there is not yet a long track record or wide adoption required for higher TRL.
student_project_ideas: Design and 3D-print a small mechanical assembly (e.g. clamp or gearbox housing) in JumpStart 3D, export STL and validate fit by combining with a simple parametric OpenSCAD tolerance test.

Create a web page that embeds JumpStart 3D via the window.JS3D bridge to programmatically generate parts from parametric inputs (e.g. generate customised enclosures from CSV) and export automated STL builds.

tools.name: peva3/SmarterRouter
tools.desc: SmarterRouter: An intelligent LLM gateway and VRAM-aware router for Ollama, llama.cpp, and OpenAI. Features semantic caching, model profiling, and automatic failover for local AI labs.

cls.summary: SmarterRouter is an open-source, local-first LLM gateway that profiles available models, manages VRAM, and routes queries automatically to the best backend (Ollama, llama.cpp or cloud providers).
cls.what_it_does: SmarterRouter sits between an application and multiple LLM backends, profiling models, performing semantic caching, monitoring GPU/VRAM usage and routing requests to the best model with automatic failover. It is deployed as a Docker/FastAPI service and can operate entirely with local models (Ollama, llama.cpp) or mix in external providers (OpenAI, Anthropic), with built-in metrics and an interactive setup wizard.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository is active and has non-trivial adoption (158 stars, Docker deployment, CLI and admin endpoints) and claims production features, but it is younger than one year (created ~274 days ago) so the demonstrated maturity is best described as beta (TRL 6).
prerequisites: Python runtime knowledge for optional CLI usage
familiarity with local LLM backends (Ollama, llama.cpp) and GPU concepts
student_project_ideas: Build a lab exercise that deploys SmarterRouter on a modest GPU VM to compare latency and cost (local vs cloud) when routing identical prompts through local llama.cpp models and an external OpenAI model, and produce a report on trade-offs.

Integrate SmarterRouter with an OpenWebUI frontend and extend its routing policy to prioritise models based on a custom quality metric (e.g. factuality score), then evaluate effectiveness using a small benchmark dataset.

tools.name: manor-os/manor-ai
tools.desc: Source-available, self-hosted AI agent workspace for small businesses and lean teams — with BYOK, workflows, tools, and human approvals.

cls.summary: Manor AI is a self-hosted workspace that runs governed AI agents, tasks and workflows with human approval gates and local data storage.
cls.what_it_does: Manor AI provides a full-stack, deployable workspace for teams to run AI agents against indexed documents and scoped tools while keeping model keys and operational data inside their infrastructure. It is used via a React web UI and a FastAPI backend with a Celery worker runtime, and it is notable for built-in governance (human-in-the-loop approvals), BYOK model support, and integrations for storage and vector search.
cls.trl_rationale: The repo is actively maintained with Docker Compose deployment, documentation, and integrations (Postgres/pgvector, Redis, MinIO) and has community interest (stars/forks), but it is only ~4 months old so lacks a longer track record required for TRL 7+.
prerequisites: familiarity with model provider APIs and keys
student_project_ideas: Build a governed agent that automates creation of lab test reports by indexing experiment notes (pgvector) and routing sensitive actions through Manor AI's human-approval gates.
Integrate Manor AI with a CI pipeline to generate and approve scoped deployment change summaries using workspace documents and a configured model provider.

tools.name: LLCOOLT/paper-cut
tools.desc: Paper Cut: A native port of Paper Mario: The Thousand-Year Door to Windows, macOS, Linux, iOS and Android (AI-assisted)

cls.summary: Paper Cut is a fan-made native rebuild of Paper Mario: The Thousand-Year Door that runs on Windows, macOS, Linux, iOS and Android without an emulator.
cls.what_it_does: Paper Cut rebuilds the game's original code from a decompilation so it can run natively across desktop and mobile platforms, with multiplayer, graphical enhancements and optional content from other ROMs you supply. It is used as a game port and modding platform rather than an engineering tool, notable for cross-platform native builds, high-fidelity graphical options and networked co-op.
cls.trl_rationale: The repository is very new (created 29 days ago) but already has releases and community interest (stars and downloads referenced in the README), indicating early adopters; age limits the TRL to alpha-in-use rather than mature production.
prerequisites: Platform SDKs for target OS (Windows/macOS/iOS/Android) and dependencies (e.g. SDL3)
A legally obtained Paper Mario disc/ROM (no game data included)

tools.name: Oruk-AI/orukeet
tools.desc: Orukeet: multilingual ASR with fitted, frozen Gabor kernels and native inference

cls.summary: Orukeet is an open-source, multilingual automatic speech recognition (ASR) model and Python package that provides local inference runtimes and downloadable weights for offline transcription across 25 languages.
cls.what_it_does: Orukeet replaces part of an encoder with fitted, frozen Gabor kernels and fine-tunes remaining parameters to produce a compact, accurate multilingual ASR model. It is distributed as a Python package with prebuilt native runtimes (ONNX, Metal, CUDA, native Q8/F16) and downloadable weights so users can run offline transcription, batch jobs or integrate the model into desktop and server applications. Notable aspects are its reported WER improvements over the Parakeet baseline and multiple export/runtime targets for on-device inference.
cls.trl_rationale: The repository is young (created 69 days ago) so TRL is limited; however it has a packaged release (v0.1.1), published weights on Hugging Face, a technical report and integrations in several open-source apps, indicating early alpha adoption by others rather than single-author proof-of-concept.
prerequisites: basic familiarity with Python packages and native runtime selection (CUDA/Metal/ONNX)
student_project_ideas: Build a desktop transcription tool that integrates Orukeet (ONNX runtime) with a simple GUI to compare latency and WER between CPU, GPU and Metal backends on a provided multilingual audio corpus.

Create a data-collection and adaptation pipeline that fine-tunes Orukeet on a domain-specific accent or vocabulary (e.g. engineering jargon) and measure WER improvements using Hugging Face-hosted weights and evaluation scripts.

tools.name: zoltanf/extrudo
tools.desc: Parametric CAD for 3D printing, in your browser. Offline version for your Mac, Windows or Linux computer is also available.

cls.summary: Extrudo is an open-source parametric CAD application that runs in the browser (and as an offline app) designed for designing and exporting 3D-printable parts with exact geometry, assemblies and drawings.
cls.what_it_does: Extrudo provides a full parametric CAD workflow (sketch, features, timeline, parameters) in a web app, letting users create solids, assemblies, drawings and export to formats like STL, 3MF and STEP. It is used interactively in the browser or scripted from TypeScript via an API, and is notable for providing exact geometry (not triangle meshes), built-in print analysis and an emphasis on 3D-printing workflows.
cls.trl_rationale: The README and releases indicate a working, stable app and a published release, but the repository is only ~8 weeks old so it lacks a long track record; that supports an alpha-in-use TRL rather than production maturity.
prerequisites: familiarity with a modern web browser; Node/TypeScript for scripting with the API
student_project_ideas: Create a configurable bracket family in Extrudo that exports STEP and STL for automated slicing; demonstrate parameter-driven design changes feeding into a simple print-cost estimator (combine with a slicer or a small Python script).

Use the @extrudo/api to write a TypeScript script that generates parametric mounts for a small robot arm, export the parts as STEP files and assemble them in a simple dynamics simulator or 3D-print the parts to validate fit.

tools.name: dcostenco/prism-coder
tools.desc: Persistent session memory for AI coding agents — local-first, with on-device inference, associative recall, and drift detection. Works with Claude Code, Cursor, and Codex.

cls.summary: Prism Coder is an open-source MCP server that provides persistent, local-first session memory and local inference routing for AI coding agents like Claude, Cursor and Codex.
cls.what_it_does: Prism Coder gives AI coding agents persistent session memory that survives restarts, local-first inference using discovered on-device models, and metered accounting of tokens kept off cloud models. It runs as an MCP (Model Context Protocol) server that integrates with hosts (Claude Code, Cursor, Codex), supports local model selection (oMLX / Ollama), associative recall and drift detection, and includes a dashboard for configuring models and measuring local savings.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository is active (created 2026-02-12, last push 2026-11-14), has substantial feature set and named integrations, and recent versioning (v20.x) suggesting ongoing development and beta stability; however it is under one year old so demonstrated production track record is limited, capping TRL at 6.
prerequisites: Local model runtimes (Ollama or oMLX) for on-device inference if desired
MCP-capable host agents to integrate (e.g. Claude Code, Cursor)
student_project_ideas: Integrate Prism Coder with a small Claude/host demo agent to build a lab exercise showing persistent session memory, then measure and visualise the 'prism savings' token accounting when switching from cloud to local inference.
Extend Prism's drift-detection hooks to flag when recalled code snippets become stale by running automated unit tests on recalled code (combine Prism with a CI runner and a simple test harness).

tools.name: AndrewCTF/velocity
tools.desc: Self-hosted flight and ship tracker that keeps its own history: rewind any moment, every contact with its source and age. No API keys.

cls.summary: Velocity is a self‑hosted web application that ingests public aircraft, ship and satellite feeds, stores full position history locally, and provides a Cesium globe UI with time‑rewind and provenance for each contact.
cls.what_it_does: Velocity pulls public feeds (ADS‑B, AIS, satellite and other sources), writes every position to a local history store (SQLite by default, Postgres/TimescaleDB optional) and presents a 3D globe and 2D console for live viewing and replay. It adds provenance (which feeds reported each contact), an append‑only custody log for evidence exports, and can act as an MCP server so agents can query live/replay data.
cls.trl_rationale: The project is well documented, provides Docker compose, runs multiple components (API, web, nginx), and has active commits and community interest (156 stars), indicating a beta maturity. However the repository was created ~158 days ago (under one year) so it lacks a longer track record or broad production adoption required for TRL 7+.
prerequisites: Node 20+ and pnpm (if running frontend without Docker)
student_project_ideas: Build a small evidence‑reporting pipeline that combines Velocity's recorded history with a simple analytics script to detect and visualise unusual vessel speed/stop events over a chosen port (use TimescaleDB export and a React/Chart frontend).
Integrate a simple autonomous agent (MCP client) that queries Velocity for live traffic in a geographic area and generates periodic summaries or alerts for simulated airspace monitoring.

tools.name: cool-japan/oxigeo
tools.desc: Pure Rust geospatial data abstraction library — the Rust alternative to GDAL (formerly OxiGDAL)

cls.summary: OxiGeo is a pure-Rust, GDAL-compatible geospatial data abstraction library for reading, transforming and processing raster and vector geospatial formats, with WASM, Python and Node.js bindings and cloud-native COG/STAC support.
cls.what_it_does: OxiGeo provides readers, transformers and algorithms for many common geospatial formats (GeoTIFF/COG, GeoJSON, Shapefile, GeoParquet, LAS/LAZ, VRT, GeoPackage, etc.), performs CRS transformations and raster/vector operations, and streams cloud-native tiles via HTTP range requests. It is used as a drop-in Rust alternative to GDAL (with cross-language bindings and Pure‑Rust WebAssembly demos) and is notable for having zero C/C++ dependencies in default features and explicit support for browser-side processing of COGs and STAC searches.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository is <1 year old so TRL capped by age, but shows multiple published releases (v0.2.x), extensive test suite results, cross-platform bindings (WASM/Python/Node), hosted demos and active commits — evidence of beta-level maturity and production hardening.
student_project_ideas: Implement a change-detection pipeline that searches a STAC API for Sentinel-2 COG pairs, streams tiles into a WASM build of OxiGeo, computes NDVI differencing and exports GeoJSON patches of significant change.
Build a web-based viewer that streams elevation or LiDAR tiles (LAS/LAZ or COPC) via OxiGeo WASM, computes slope and aspect on the client and visualises results with a WebGL/three.js front end.

tools.name: cuberact/godot-cuberact-planet-chunked-lod
tools.desc: Procedural Planet - Chunked LOD, Noise terrain by Shader, Atmosphere, Godot engine, GDScript

cls.summary: A Godot 4.6 project that renders a full-scale procedurally generated planet using chunked level-of-detail and GPU shaders, designed as a readable learning resource.
cls.what_it_does: This project implements a chunked LOD planet: the sphere surface is divided into quadtree chunks that split/merge based on camera distance while vertex displacement, coloring and atmosphere are handled by GLSL shaders. It is used by opening the project in Godot and running the scene; the code is pure GDScript with two shaders and is intended for learning and experimentation rather than as a polished engine plugin.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository is ~245 days old and shows a complete, runnable Godot project with documentation and examples (no releases or large user ecosystem), indicating beta-level maturity; age under one year prevents TRL >6 despite healthy star count and clear examples.
student_project_ideas: Extend the planet to visualise real-world elevation data by adding a tile loader that replaces shader noise with heightmaps and export camera flight paths for a geospatial demo.
Integrate the chunked LOD planet into a Godot-based simulation by adding dynamic objects (satellites or UAVs) and measuring performance and LOD split budget effects for an optimisation study.

tools.name: huggingface/cadgenbench
tools.desc: A benchmark for AI-driven CAD generation and editing

cls.summary: CADGenBench is an open benchmark and evaluation toolkit that scores AI-generated or edited 3D mechanical parts (STEP/BREP) against ground-truth parts using geometric, topological and interface metrics.
cls.what_it_does: CADGenBench defines a submission contract and runs an automated scoring pipeline that evaluates validity, shape similarity, interface (mating) correctness and topology of submitted STEP/BREP files for two tasks: generation from a drawing and editing an existing part. It is used both as a leaderboard-backed evaluation (Hugging Face Space) and as a local reference baseline that can produce STEP files via build123d or CadQuery and render them for iterative agent-driven generation.
cls.trl_rationale: The repository is a working benchmark with a scoring engine, documentation, a reference baseline and an active Hugging Face leaderboard; it is 174 days old (<1 year) so it shows beta-level maturity (versioned code, CI/tests, but limited long-term production track record).
prerequisites: optional LLM API keys (OpenAI / Anthropic / Google) for the baseline agent
student_project_ideas: Compare two generative approaches (rule-based build123d script generator vs LLM-driven baseline) on a subset of CADGenBench samples and analyse failure modes by metric (validity, shape similarity, topology).
Extend the baseline to target a different code-CAD backend (e.g. FreeCAD Python API) and evaluate resulting STEP outputs on CADGenBench metrics, reporting integration challenges and metric changes.

tools.name: paul356/KiCad-AI-Assistant
tools.desc: A LLM powered plugin for KiCad 10.0

cls.summary: A KiCad action-plugin that embeds an LLM-powered chat and MCP server to read and edit schematics and PCB layouts from inside KiCad.
cls.what_it_does: KiCad AI Assistant provides an in-editor chat panel backed by a local MCP server so an LLM can inspect, query and modify KiCad schematic and PCB files via natural-language commands. It installs as a KiCad plugin, supports multiple LLM providers, and exposes tools for schematic/PCB querying, editing, routing and DRC-related operations to automate or assist PCB design tasks.
cls.trl_rationale: The project is an actively maintained KiCad plugin with installation instructions, releases, and many stars; it is recent (created ~173 days ago) so it shows beta-level maturity and community interest but lacks the long track record and enterprise deployments required for TRL 7+.
prerequisites: LLM API key for provider (OpenAI/Anthropic/Bedrock) or local Ollama
student_project_ideas: Create a student toolchain that uses the plugin plus a local LLM (Ollama) to implement an automated rule-checker that suggests footprint or netlist fixes for a classroom PCB and measures acceptance rate against manual fixes.

Build an experiment comparing automated placement/routing prompts driven by the plugin vs. human-guided routing on the same PCB and analyse differences in routing length, via count and DRC violations.

tools.name: mustache-dev/Three-VFX
tools.desc: High-performance particle system for Three.js WebGPU, with support for React Three Fiber, TresJS, and Threlte

cls.summary: Three VFX is a GPU‑accelerated particle system built for Three.js WebGPU with adapters for React Three Fiber, TresJS and Threlte, providing high‑performance visual effects for web 3D scenes.
cls.what_it_does: Three VFX runs particle simulation on the GPU using WebGPU compute shaders to produce high‑performance particle effects (sprites, custom geometry, physics, emitters and curve controls). It is used as a component in Three.js-based projects (React Three Fiber, TresJS, Threlte or vanilla Three.js) and notable for its WebGPU native implementation and a WebGL CPU fallback for broader browser support.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository is 295 days old (<1 year) so it lacks a long track record; however the README shows installable packages, multi-framework adapters, a detailed API and active pushes and issues, indicating a beta maturity (versioned package usage and examples but not long-term production adoption).
prerequisites: familiarity with Three.js and 3D concepts (meshes, materials, shaders)
WebGPU-capable browser or knowledge of WebGL fallback
React Three Fiber knowledge for the R3F adapter (if used)
student_project_ideas: Create an interactive web demo that visualises sensor data (e.g. particle trails for vehicle telemetry) by feeding time‑series data into Three VFX in a React Three Fiber scene.
Build a virtual test rig that visualises airflow or smoke approximations using Three VFX emitters and compare performance and visual fidelity between the WebGPU implementation and the WebGL fallback.

tools.name: op7418/guizang-sports-skill
tools.desc: 🚴 Claude Code / Codex skill for FIT & KML sports analysis — cycling, running, hiking, sensor and grade insights, local 3D route reports, PNG & H.264 MP4 exports. 运动轨迹分析与 3D 路线故事

cls.summary: A local Agent 'skill' that ingests FIT/KML activity files to produce automated cycling/running/hiking analyses and a local 3D route report with PNG and H.264 MP4 export.
cls.what_it_does: The project provides a Claude/Codex skill that parses one or more FIT or KML files, computes per-activity and aggregate metrics (distance, cadence, elevation, slope segments, sensor coverage), and launches a local web report (Ride Relief) with interactive 3D route visualisation. It can also export rendered PNGs and H.264 MP4 videos and match photos to the route; notable aspects are the local-first privacy model and built-in three.js-based 3D route rendering.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository is young (~100 days) but has a mature README, sample data, and install/run instructions and a modest star count, indicating early adopters; there are no stable releases or evidence of production deployments, so maturity is around alpha/early-in-use.
prerequisites: local web browser (Chromium recommended) and optional Chromium for exports
student_project_ideas: Build an assignment that compares slope-detection algorithms by importing several FIT/KML files into the skill and extending the analysis to compute additional climb difficulty metrics, then present results in the Ride Relief report.

Integrate the skill's exported route JSON with a simple IoT dashboard (e.g. InfluxDB + Grafana) to visualise time-series sensor data (heart rate, cadence, power) alongside the 3D route and evaluate visualisation strategies.

tools.name: billpwchan/sakura-fantasy
tools.desc: A boat journey through a Japanese river valley, in four seasons and at any hour, rendered live in the browser with three.js.

cls.summary: A high-quality browser-based real-time scene that renders a procedurally-generated Japanese river valley using three.js and photogrammetry assets.
cls.what_it_does: Sakura Fantasy renders a continuous boat journey through multiple handcrafted and procedurally-populated scenes in the browser, using instanced photogrammetry plants, layered water, weather and day/night lighting, and live-composed traditional Japanese music. It's run as a plain JavaScript three.js application with a frame-time governor, worker-based world generation and downloadable 4K wallpapers; notable features are photogrammetry-derived vegetation, multi-tier LOD and a streaming asset/tier system.
cls.trl_rationale: The project is a polished, runnable demo with included assets, a thorough README and example builds, indicating early real use (wallpapers, hosted demo), but the repository is very new (created 44 days ago) so it lacks a long track record or broad adoption—TRL ~5.
prerequisites: familiarity with three.js and WebGL concepts
student_project_ideas: Build a shortened interactive scene that demonstrates LOD and streaming by replacing one river section with a custom scanned plant set and measure frame-time governor behaviour across devices.
Integrate simple sensor-driven controls (e.g. browser gyroscope or mock IoT time/weather input) to drive season/hour/weather parameters and evaluate user perception of real-time rendering changes.

tools.name: yoloyash/overtchat
tools.desc: A simpler self-hosted alternative to Open WebUI. Bring your own API keys or local models. Native Android and iOS clients.

cls.summary: OvertChat is a self-hosted chat front end that connects to local or hosted LLM servers and provides web, desktop and native mobile clients with features like live voice, interactive OpenUI cards, and optional coding-agent sandboxes.
cls.what_it_does: OvertChat hosts conversations for local and cloud models (Ollama, vLLM, llama.cpp, OpenAI-compatible endpoints and more) and synchronises chats, files and accounts across web, desktop and native mobile apps. It bundles speech recognition/synthesis, web search fallbacks, an optional isolated code sandbox for model-driven code runs, and connectors to run coding agents on remote hosts.
cls.trl_rationale: The project is a working, well-documented self-hosted application with an installer, Docker compose options, native clients, and active commits and issues (created 193 days ago). Because the repository is younger than one year it lacks the longer public track record or wide adoption needed for TRL 7+, so TRL 6 (beta) is appropriate.
prerequisites: familiarity with local LLM concepts and API endpoints
student_project_ideas: Set up OvertChat on a campus VM and compare latency, token usage accounting, and response quality across a local llama.cpp model, a vLLM server, and a hosted OpenAI-compatible provider, documenting trade-offs in a lab report.

Build a small coding-agent workflow by connecting a workstation Host Connector and create an assignment where students use the agent to run static analysis and automated refactoring on a shared codebase, then evaluate safety and reproducibility of the sandboxed runs.

tools.name: TilelliLab/atome-lm
tools.desc: A ternary, zero-heap tiny language model that runs inside a $2 microcontroller — bit-exact Python <-> C99 <-> Cortex-M3 (QEMU) parity. Apache-2.0.

cls.summary: Atome LM is an open-source tiny language model and toolchain that trains, exports and runs a ternary (3-valued) LLM on microcontrollers with bit-exact Python ↔ C99 parity.
cls.what_it_does: Atome LM provides training code, a ternary-weight export pipeline and a C99 inference engine so a sub-1M-parameter model can be trained on a desktop and then run on resource-constrained devices (example: ESP32) with bit-exact parity to the Python reference. It targets on-device, offline language inference with extreme memory and compute constraints, notable for its ternary weight packing, token-routing block design and included real-silicon demo and packed weight blobs.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository is 178 days old (<1 year) but contains a complete train→export→C99 inference path, included weights, tests for bit-exact Python↔C parity, and a reproducible real-silicon demo on an ESP32, indicating a beta-level, device-runnable project rather than a fragile prototype.
prerequisites: C toolchain for cross-compiling to Cortex-M/ESP32
familiarity with embedded flashing (ESP32/IDF) and binary packing
student_project_ideas: Port the provided C99 engine and 944k checkpoint to a different MCU board (e.g. STM32) and measure throughput, memory and power to compare against the ESP32 baseline.
Extend the training/export pipeline to quantize and pack a slightly larger Atome configuration (e.g. d_model=128) then evaluate inference latency and model quality trade-offs on-device.

tools.name: simplex-micro/riscv-vector-primer
tools.desc: Read chapters directly from this repo - do not use GitHub Pages link.

cls.summary: An implementation‑focused, openly published technical book that explains the RISC‑V Vector Extension (RVV 1.0) and emerging Matrix Extension for architects, compiler writers and embedded/edge AI developers.
cls.what_it_does: The repository hosts the full chapter‑based online edition of the RISC‑V Vector Primer, presenting both conceptual foundations and implementation details for RVV and matrix acceleration. It is used as a reference and teaching resource to understand vector ISA semantics, hardware mapping (lanes, VRF, ports), instruction behaviour, and performance considerations for AI workloads.
cls.trl_rationale: The repo is a completed, well‑authored technical book with active maintenance and attracted community interest (154 stars) but is under one year old (~292 days), so it lacks a long production track record; documentation and authorship support a beta/TRl-6 judgment.
student_project_ideas: Extend an existing RISC‑V simulator (e.g. Spike or gem5) to implement a subset of RVV instructions from the book and measure performance for a vectorised GEMM kernel.
Use the primer's performance guidelines to design and simulate a 512‑bit RVV lane microarchitecture in an RTL/simulation environment and compare bandwidth/latency tradeoffs described in the book.

tools.name: zymazza/mazzap
tools.desc: Mazzap, part of the Mazzstack: essentials for the Singularity Slowlife

cls.summary: Mazzap is an open-source, self-contained georeferenced 3D digital-twin engine that builds and serves interactive terrain-based twins from open geospatial data in a browser.
cls.what_it_does: Mazzap ingests DEMs, imagery, LiDAR and vector layers to produce a bundled, offline-capable 3D digital twin viewable in a Three.js web viewer. It provides terrain rendering, draped imagery, classified point-cloud display, click-to-identify geolocation, process simulations (hydrology, evapotranspiration, wildfire, solar siting), live telemetry integration and an LLM-backed query/MCP interface—all designed to run locally or in a container without a remote database.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository is 264 days old (<1 year) so TRL is capped; README and examples show a rich feature set (terrain, simulations, MCP chat, QField integration), a runnable demo, Docker support and active commits and stars, which together indicate a beta-level, community-usable project rather than an early prototype.
prerequisites: Python 3 with GDAL (osgeo), numpy, pyproj, Pillow
Familiarity with geospatial formats (DEM, orthophoto, point cloud)
student_project_ideas: Build a local digital twin of a campus area: ingest a DEM and orthophoto, add a vegetation layer from public LiDAR, and implement a simple hydrology runoff scenario to visualise ponding and flows in the viewer.

Integrate Mazzap with a low-cost LoRa tracker (Meshtastic) to stream live positions into the twin, then create an analysis that correlates tracked field observations (QField survey points) with simulated solar-siting suitability.

tools.name: KyosukeIshizu1008/berryscode
tools.desc: Native IDE for the Bevy game engine, built in Bevy + Rust. Scene editor, ECS inspector, AI agent, mobile build, Godot project read-only viewer.

cls.summary: BerryCode is a native desktop IDE built in Rust specifically for developing with the Bevy game engine, providing a scene editor, ECS inspector, system graph and integrated code tooling.
cls.what_it_does: BerryCode provides an integrated development environment tailored to Bevy projects: a visual 3D scene editor with gizmos, live ECS inspection via Bevy Remote Protocol, system dependency graph, event/query visualizers and an integrated Rust code editor with LSP and debugger support. It is used as a desktop application (pre-built binaries or self-build) and is notable because it is implemented in Bevy/WGPU itself and includes local-first AI assistant support (Ollama/Llama) and many engine-aware tools not found in general editors.
cls.trl_rationale: The README is extensive and the project provides pre-built release artifacts and many features, indicating active development and some maturity; however the repository is only ~7 months old so it lacks the longer track record required for TRL 7+, limiting it to TRL 6.
prerequisites: Optional: Ollama or local LLM for AI features
student_project_ideas: Create a small interactive simulation (e.g. wheeled-robot kinematics or particle system) in Bevy and use BerryCode's Scene Editor and ECS Inspector to visualise, instrument and optimise entity queries and system ordering.

Extend BerryCode with a classroom plugin that instruments and visualises student project metrics (frame time, query matches, event traces) and reports them via a simple web UI or CSV export for assessment.

tools.name: dmae97/omk
tools.desc: Open-source multi-agent coding CLI for the terminal (TypeScript, MIT). Switch models mid-session; finish goals only when your test passes.

cls.summary: OMK is an open-source, terminal-based multi-agent coding CLI that runs agents to edit code and only marks goals done when a user-defined test/command passes.
cls.what_it_does: OMK runs AI coding agents in a standalone command-line interface that can read and edit a repository, run commands, and verify progress by re-running a user-specified check (for example tests) before completing a goal. It supports switching models mid-session, adding subagents, and using local or provider-hosted models, making it notable as a multi-agent, model-agnostic CLI with an explicit verification gate.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository is active (created 2026-04-30, last push 2026-11-15) with 153 stars and documented install/run instructions; however it is younger than one year and the README describes a prerelease migration (Rust core incomplete), so maturity aligns with a beta-level tool rather than long-term production evidence.
prerequisites: a git repository with a test/verify command
student_project_ideas: Build an automated CI workflow that uses OMK to run agent-driven fixes on failing unit tests in a small Node.js project and compare agent performance between a local LLM and a hosted provider.
Extend OMK with a custom verification plugin that runs property-based tests and produces a human-readable report, integrating results with Git hooks to block merges until checks pass.

tools.name: Setuav/PyThrust
tools.desc: An Open-Source Framework for Electric Propulsion System Analysis and Optimization in UAV Design

cls.summary: PyThrust is a Python framework for analysing and optimising electric propulsion (motor + propeller + battery) systems for UAVs, with OpenMDAO integration and component databases.
cls.what_it_does: PyThrust provides steady-state propulsion solvers, motor calibration (auto-tuning) tools, and database search utilities to map theoretical designs to real brushless motor and propeller components. It is used from Python and can be embedded in multidisciplinary design/optimization workflows (OpenMDAO) to co-design propulsion and vehicle-level trade-offs.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository is active with documentation, examples and OpenMDAO integration and has community interest (153 stars), but it is only ~6 months old (<1 year) so lacks long-term production track record required for TRL 7+.
student_project_ideas: Use PyThrust with OpenMDAO to co-design a small quadcopter: optimise motor-propeller selection and battery sizing to maximise endurance under a specified payload and flight profile.

Collect test-bench thrust/torque/speed data for a brushless motor and use PyThrust's motor calibration tools to auto-tune a motor model, then compare predicted vs measured hover performance and identify model discrepancies.

tools.name: ingelibre/ingecad
tools.desc: Free 2D DWG/DXF CAD for Linux in the spirit of classic AutoCAD — keyboard drafting with acad.pgp aliases, faithful DWG round-trip, paper space and dimensions, plus surveying and terrain plugins (points, construction chart, contours, profiles, earthworks, UTM georeferencing, global DEM, satellite imagery, Google Earth KML)

cls.summary: IngeCAD is a free, lightweight 2D CAD application for Linux with faithful DWG/DXF round-tripping and surveying/terrain plugins aimed at civil and architectural drafting.
cls.what_it_does: IngeCAD provides a classic command-line driven 2D drafting environment that opens, edits and saves DWG/DXF files while preserving unknown entities; it includes surveying and terrain plugins (points, contours, profiles, earthworks, UTM georeferencing and global DEM/satellite basemaps). It is used as a native Linux CAD for producing plans, layouts and survey-derived geometry and is notable for its focus on faithful file interchange (ezdxf + GNU LibreDWG) and a lightweight, classic CAD workflow.
cls.trl_rationale: The README documents many implemented features (topography/terrain/roads plugins, DWG round-trip, layouts) and there is active recent development, but the project is young (<1 year) and pre-1.0 (v0.8.0) so it fits an alpha-in-use maturity rather than production/stable.
prerequisites: familiarity with 2D CAD concepts and commands
Linux experience (Wayland/X11) and basic system administration
student_project_ideas: Create a lab exercise that imports a CSV survey point cloud into IngeCAD, generates contours and computes earthwork volumes, then exports the DXF for comparison with another CAD tool (e.g. QCAD or FreeCAD).
Develop a small plugin for IngeCAD that reads GPS/RTK point output and automatically creates stationing and alignment tables for a simple road axis, integrating PROJ for coordinate transforms.

tools.name: NVIDIA-Omniverse-blueprints/omniverse-dsx-blueprint-for-ai-factories
tools.desc: For developers, building AI factories demands coordinated planning across systems to optimize AI Factories. NVIDIA Omniverse Libraries and OpenUSD enable developers to to create digital twin solutions for design, simulation and operations of AI Factories.

cls.summary: A reference digital-twin blueprint using NVIDIA Omniverse and USD that demonstrates design, simulation (including CFD) and interactive visualization workflows for AI factory facilities.
cls.what_it_does: This repository provides a developer-focused example digital twin (the DSX Blueprint) that combines SimReady USD assets, a web front-end, and sample simulation data so users can configure AI factory layouts and visualise simulation scenarios such as thermal/CFD and electrical loading. It is used as a template and learning resource to integrate Omniverse libraries, containerised components and frontend code into a realtime digital twin application rather than a production turnkey product.
cls.trl_rationale: The repo is a substantial, well-documented reference blueprint with sample assets, a frontend and containerised components and has community interest (stars/forks). It is younger than one year (created ~276 days ago) so a conservative TRL 6 (beta) is appropriate despite strong vendor backing because there is limited evidence of long-term production deployments in the README.
prerequisites: NVIDIA Omniverse familiarity and USD/SimReady concepts
Modern NVIDIA GPU and drivers (knowledge of GPU requirements)
Linux/Windows development: Docker, NVIDIA Container Toolkit, Node.js/npm
C++ build toolchains (Visual Studio for Windows) and Git LFS for large assets
student_project_ideas: Extend the DSX Blueprint to add an automated HVAC control scenario: import a simple building model from USD, run a parametrised thermal/CFD simulation (or visualise provided sample CFD outputs) and implement a web UI control that adjusts ventilation and shows impacts in the Omniverse viewport.

Build a small digital-twin pipeline that streams time-series sensor data (simulated) into the blueprint scene, visualises live thermal maps in the viewport, and logs configurations to a backend (combine the Omniverse frontend with a lightweight timeseries DB or MQTT broker).

tools.name: raguilar011095/planet_heightmap_generation
tools.desc: Believable worlds from the ground up: a free studio of planet tools in your browser, from tectonic history to climate, geology and more.

cls.summary: World Orogen is a browser-based procedural planet and heightmap generator that models plate tectonics, climate, erosion and related layers and exports high-resolution map data.
cls.what_it_does: World Orogen (Orogen Studio) creates complete, plausible planetary worlds in the browser by simulating plate tectonics, climate, rivers, ice, geology and surface products and then exporting maps and 16-bit height data. It is used from a web page (no install) with interactive controls, import of external heightmaps, and multi-format exports; notable features are named, credited scientific simplifications for each layer, fast generation, and high-resolution export options.
cls.trl_rationale: The project is actively developed, has a public hosted web demo (orogen.studio), 152 stars and recent commits, showing a usable beta; however the repo is under one year old so there is not yet long-term production track record, which limits the TRL to 6.
student_project_ideas: Use World Orogen to generate planetary heightmaps and build a GIS workflow that imports the exported DEM into QGIS to analyse watershed areas and compare predicted river networks with the studio's outputs.
Integrate exported heightmaps from World Orogen with a game engine (Unity or three.js) to create an interactive terrain viewer and evaluate performance and LOD strategies for large planetary tiles.

tools.name: yanun0323/Whallm
tools.desc: DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731  284B inference in ~25 GB of RAM / Qwen3.8-Next-Flash inference in ~15 GB of RAM on any M-series MacBook

cls.summary: Whallm is a macOS application that runs very large language models on Apple Silicon by keeping core weights in RAM and streaming expert weights from an SSD, exposing a chat UI and an OpenAI-compatible local API.
cls.what_it_does: Whallm enables on-device inference of large LLMs that exceed a Mac's RAM by caching common weights in memory and loading expert weights from SSD when needed. It is used as a local macOS app with a chat interface and an OpenAI/Codex‑compatible HTTP API, notable for SSD‑streaming of model experts and explicit support for Apple Silicon and Metal.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository is 102 days old with releases and a downloadable macOS binary, a working server API, benchmarks and documentation, indicating a beta-quality project; age limits the TRL to <=6 and there is not yet evidence of wide production deployment.
prerequisites: Fast SSD (internal, Thunderbolt or USB4) and sufficient free disk space
Large local storage (tens to hundreds of GiB for model files) and recommended 64 GiB RAM
student_project_ideas: Measure and compare inference throughput and memory use of a chosen large model on different Apple Silicon chips using Whallm's Throughput tool and report trade-offs between cache size and latency.

Integrate Whallm's local OpenAI-compatible API into a small engineering tool (e.g., a code-assistant for embedded firmware) to prototype offline prompt workflows and evaluate privacy/latency benefits versus cloud APIs.

tools.name: CarlesRojas/ha-diorama
tools.desc: Home Assistant card that turns your home into a clickable 3D model, with your devices bound to the pieces that stand for them

cls.summary: Diorama is a Home Assistant Lovelace card that renders a clickable 3D model of your home and binds visual pieces to real devices for live control and status.
cls.what_it_does: Diorama displays a small interactive 3D representation of rooms and furniture inside Home Assistant, letting you bind pieces to entities so they reflect device state and accept clicks to control them. It runs as a Lovelace custom card (installable via HACS or manually), uses a built-in full‑screen editor to draw rooms and place pieces, and uses three.js for realtime visuals including lights, shadows and sun movement.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository is new (created ~59 days ago) but provides a working install path, tutorial video, and HACS distribution; active stars show interest but it lacks long-term production track record required for higher TRL.
prerequisites: basic familiarity with Lovelace dashboards and HACS
student_project_ideas: Build a small lab digital twin by connecting a set of MQTT sensor entities to Home Assistant and use Diorama to visualise sensor states and trigger controls from the 3D view.
Extend the Diorama card (TypeScript) to add a custom widget that visualises energy consumption per room and logs events to a timeseries backend for analysis.

tools.name: maximpri/mlxtop
tools.desc: A top for local LLMs: memory, paging, GPU and tokens/s for oMLX, Ollama, llama.cpp, vLLM and more

cls.summary: mlxtop is a command-line / TUI monitoring tool that shows live resource and inference telemetry for local LLM runtimes to help diagnose slowdowns.
cls.what_it_does: mlxtop collects memory, paging, GPU and runtime telemetry (tokens/s, prefill progress, queues, cache reuse) from many local LLM runtimes and displays them in a top-like TUI and text reports. It is used to spot whether slow model responses are caused by memory pressure, swapping, GPU saturation or runtime-specific issues, and it can record and replay sessions for post‑hoc analysis.
cls.trl_rationale: The project provides installers, release artifacts and documented usage and has non-trivial community interest (151 stars), but the repository is only 67 days old so by the stated policy its demonstrated maturity is limited to TRL 5 despite the polished README and multiple install options.
prerequisites: comfort with the command line / TUI
basic knowledge of local LLM runtimes (e.g. vLLM, llama.cpp, Ollama) to interpret telemetry
student_project_ideas: Set up a local inference stack (e.g. vLLM or llama.cpp) and use mlxtop to profile and quantify the impact of different batch sizes, context lengths and GPU memory placements on tokens/s and end-to-end latency.

Record mlxtop sessions while running synthetic workloads, then build a small analysis script to classify slowdowns (paging, GPU saturation, queueing) and propose automated mitigations or configuration changes.

tools.name: pzfreo/build123d-mcp
tools.desc: MCP server for build123d to improve AI cognition when creating 3D CAD models

cls.summary: build123d-mcp is an MCP server that lets LLM-based assistants drive the build123d Python CAD library to create, inspect, measure and export 3D CAD models interactively.
cls.what_it_does: It exposes build123d CAD operations over the MCP tool protocol so an LLM app (Claude, Cursor, VS Code, etc.) can build parts step-by-step, render previews, measure geometry, repair scripts and export STEP/STL/DXF/SVG. Notable features include a stdio/http MCP server mode, tooling for incremental construction and validation, and explicit guidance for integrating into common LLM clients.
cls.trl_rationale: The repository is active, has installation instructions, integration examples for multiple LLM clients and demonstrated benchmark gains on CADGenBench, indicating a beta-level tool with real users; however it is younger than one year (created 201 days ago), which limits TRL to at most 6.
prerequisites: uv (astral-sh/uv) or ability to run the published package
an LLM app/client that supports MCP (Claude, Cursor, VS Code, etc.)
student_project_ideas: Build an LLM-driven CAD workflow that generates parametric mounting brackets with build123d-mcp and validates dimensions automatically against design requirements, then export STEP for downstream FEA in a CAE tool.

Create a lab exercise where students write MCP prompts and small controller scripts to iteratively repair and improve an imported STEP part (detect holes, resize features, re-export) and measure the effect on geometry and mass.

tools.name: akira-init1/ChannelTerm
tools.desc: Shared terminal sessions for humans and AI agents, starting with serial and hardware debugging.

cls.summary: ChannelTerm is a cross-platform tool that shares a live serial or SSH terminal between a human and AI clients to support hardware and firmware debugging with integrated GDB and file transfer.
cls.what_it_does: ChannelTerm creates a shared Session that lets multiple attachments (a human terminal and external AI/MCP clients) read and write the same serial or SSH connection so the AI can follow device output and run debugging commands. It supports managed GDB usage, serial bridging, SCP/SFTP file moves, U-Boot interruption workflows and can export diagnostic evidence for failure analysis. Notable features are MCP-based AI client connectivity, multi-platform prebuilt binaries, and workflows designed for short boot windows and hardware debugging.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository is 87 days old (younger than 90 days) which limits maturity; however the README and release archives show prebuilt binaries, install instructions, cross-platform support and active development with many stars, indicating early adopters rather than a one-off prototype.
prerequisites: Go toolchain (for building from source) and basic CLI skills
access to target hardware (serial or networked device) and optionally GDB
student_project_ideas: Create an automated hardware debugging pipeline where a student-written AI agent (using the MCP protocol) attaches to ChannelTerm to run a predefined set of GDB checks and produce a diagnostic ZIP for failed boot scenarios.

Build a classroom lab that uses ChannelTerm to let pairs of students collaboratively debug a microcontroller board: one student controls the terminal while the other writes a scripted AI client to perform automated tests and file transfers using SCP/SFTP.

tools.name: gaopengbin/cesium-mcp
tools.desc: Protocol-agnostic CesiumJS AI control runtime for MCP, WebMCP, function calling, and browser agents.

cls.summary: cesium-mcp is a protocol-agnostic runtime that lets LLM-driven agents control CesiumJS maps from browser agents, function-calling embeds, or MCP hosts.
cls.what_it_does: It provides a transport-neutral command executor and adapters so AI agents (browser agents, WebMCP, function-calling or MCP runtimes) can inspect and manipulate CesiumJS viewers and geospatial features. It is used as a library and set of examples (browser demo, WebMCP integration, MCP runtime) and is notable for supporting multiple integration paths and a large set of Cesium commands out of the box.
cls.trl_rationale: The project has active development, demos, packaged modules and examples and a moderate star/fork count, indicating a usable beta-level project; however the repo is under one year old (created 2026-03-14) so by the policy it should be capped at TRL 6 in absence of longer track record or documented production deployments.
prerequisites: basic understanding of MCP / WebMCP / function-calling agent concepts
student_project_ideas: Build a browser-based agent that uses cesium-mcp to let a user query and edit building attributes in a 3D city dataset, then export changes to GeoJSON for GIS analysis.
Integrate cesium-mcp with a simple IoT time-series backend to visualise and have an LLM agent annotate hotspots on a Cesium map and generate alerts for anomalous sensor trends.

tools.name: MarkHershey/PSIVG
tools.desc: [CVPR 2026] Physical Simulator In-the-Loop Video Generation

cls.summary: Reference implementation of a CVPR 2026 research pipeline that uses a physical simulator in-the-loop to generate videos conditioned on scene interactions.
cls.what_it_does: PSIVG couples a physics simulator with neural video generation so that rendered videos reflect physically plausible object motion and interactions; the repo provides code to reproduce the paper pipeline and links to data and setup instructions. It is used as a research reference implementation that combines Taichi-based simulation, photorealistic rendering and learned video models to synthesize videos conditioned on simulated dynamics.
cls.trl_rationale: This is a published CVPR 2026 paper with a public reference implementation and several dependencies; the repository is under one year old (created 2026-02-22) so it fits a beta-level maturity (reproducible research code) rather than long-term production use.
prerequisites: experience with ML frameworks (PyTorch) and rendering/simulation libraries (Taichi, Mitsuba)
student_project_ideas: Reproduce a subset of the paper experiments on a simpler scene: integrate a Taichi particle simulation with a learned video generator to show how changing physical parameters affects generated frames.

Extend the pipeline to record simulated telemetry (positions, forces) and build a visualisation dashboard that links simulation state to generated video frames for a study on interpretability of physics-conditioned video models.

tools.name: feng4887/TopoData
tools.desc: TopoData is a C# application, provides PLC/DCS data acquisition , storage and python script capabilities , along with HTTP WebAPI、Mqtt interfaces for data read/write interfaces. Provides flexible recipe definition functionality, allowing users to select different recipes and download parameters to PLCs or devices.

cls.summary: TopoData is a Windows/.NET application for industrial data acquisition that connects PLCs and devices (Modbus, Profinet, OPC UA/DA) to IT systems via WebAPI, MQTT and databases, with scripting and recipe download features.
cls.what_it_does: TopoData collects and stores process data from PLCs and industrial devices using protocols such as Profinet, Modbus TCP/RTU and OPC UA/DA, exposing that data to IT systems through HTTP WebAPI and MQTT and storing it in SQL Server, PostgreSQL or MySQL. It includes Python scripting, configurable storage triggers, recipe management to download parameters to PLCs, and diagnostics for communications; it is notable for targeting IT–OT integration and supporting multiple industrial protocols out of the box.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository is active, has a published v1.3.0 README and multiple protocol implementations (Modbus, OPC UA, Profinet), and a moderate user base (151 stars), indicating a beta-level project with versioned releases and usable features; repository age is ~9 months so TRL is limited to 6 by the <1 year rule.
prerequisites: familiarity with PLCs and industrial protocols (Modbus, OPC, Profinet)
basic SQL/database administration for SQL Server/Postgres/MySQL
student_project_ideas: Build a small proof-of-concept digital twin by connecting TopoData to a simulated PLC (S7 or Modbus simulator) and visualise real-time signals in a web dashboard (e.g., Grafana) while storing historical data in PostgreSQL.

Create an automated recipe management pipeline: use TopoData's recipe download feature and Python scripting to implement and validate parameter changes on a simulated production line, then log and verify changes against requirements in a database.

tools.name: opengeos/maplibre-gl-usgs-lidar
tools.desc: A web-based LiDAR point cloud viewer for USGS 3DEP LiDAR

tools.name: Cai-aa/CAD-Agent-Hub
tools.desc: MCP servers and automation bridges for CATIA, SolidWorks, Siemens NX, and Autodesk Fusion

cls.summary: CAD Agent Hub provides Windows MCP servers and application bridges to automate parametric modelling and CAE workflows in commercial CAD packages like CATIA, SolidWorks, Siemens NX and Fusion.
cls.what_it_does: The project exposes MCP servers, in-process bridges and engineering 'Skills' that let AI agents or scripts control proprietary CAD/CAE applications on Windows for modelling, drawing and analysis automation. It is used by installing the appropriate MCP component next to the target CAD application and running the provided validation tests and example model scripts; notable aspects are multi-vendor coverage (CATIA, SolidWorks, NX, Fusion) and reproducible modeling examples.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository is 112 days old (younger than one year) so TRL is capped; README shows multiple MCP integrations, unit-test guidance, reproducible examples and numerous stars, indicating beta-level maturity with active development but limited long-term track record.
prerequisites: Windows OS and familiarity with Windows COM / application automation
Licensed commercial CAD/CAE software (CATIA, SolidWorks, Siemens NX, Autodesk Fusion, ANSYS as applicable)
student_project_ideas: Build an automated SolidWorks part-and-drawing generation pipeline using the SolidWorks MCP server to create parametric parts from CSV input and export standardized drawings for a manufacturing workflow.

Integrate the Fusion Electronics write bridge with a simple BOM generator to produce PCB enclosure models in Fusion 360 from component lists and run a validation script that checks mounting features via the provided examples.

tools.name: faust-machines/fusion360-mcp-server
tools.desc: MCP Server for Autodesk Fusion 360

cls.summary: A bridge that lets MCP-compatible AI coding agents control Autodesk Fusion 360 to automate CAD editing and feature operations.
cls.what_it_does: The project runs a Model Context Protocol (MCP) server that forwards commands from AI coding agents (Claude Code, Cursor, etc.) to a Fusion 360 add-in which executes Fusion API calls on the main thread. It is used to automate sketching, feature creation and other CAD tasks programmatically from an agent, with a TCP/stdio relay and a list of ~93 available tools for common Fusion operations.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository is 288 days old and marked Beta with active development, a PyPI package, 150 stars and recent commits; this indicates a mature beta/beta-release stage but it is under active development so it lacks the long track record required for TRL 7+.
prerequisites: An MCP-compatible client (Claude Code, Cursor, OpenCode, etc.)
student_project_ideas: Build an agent workflow that takes a parametric part specification (dimensions, holes, fillets) and uses the MCP server to generate the part in Fusion 360, then export a STEP and compare the produced geometry to a reference via bounding-box tests.

Create an automated design-variation script where an AI agent drives a parameter sweep (e.g. varying thickness and fillet radii) via the MCP server and logs geometry metrics to a CSV for simple optimisation and constraint checking.

tools.name: therealMRBK/NextFloor
tools.desc: NextFloor: draw your home in Home Assistant and watch it live in 3D. Free forever – every feature, every furniture pack, no Pro, no shop. Build your own furniture, plugins welcome. No cloud, no account.

cls.summary: NextFloor is a Home Assistant integration that lets you draw or import a floor plan and see a live 3D digital twin of your home that links to real devices and sensors.
cls.what_it_does: NextFloor provides a browser-based editor to draw floors, rooms, walls, doors and roofs (or import scans and CAD/IFC), furnishes them with model packs, and displays a live interactive 3D view that reflects Home Assistant devices, sensors and automations. It is used as a dashboard card or full-screen tablet kiosk and is notable for running locally (no cloud), deep Home Assistant integration (HACS installation) and an included furniture studio and plugin system.
cls.trl_rationale: The project is active, published in the official HACS store with extensive documentation and many features, indicating early real use, but the repository is only ~40 days old so it lacks the longer track record and stable-release history required for higher TRL.
prerequisites: basic familiarity with Home Assistant integrations and Lovelace cards
student_project_ideas: Create a Home Assistant automation that uses NextFloor's 3D view to visualise and replay room-level temperature and HVAC system behaviour over time, exporting data to a time-series DB for analysis.
Import an IFC or Apple RoomPlan scan into NextFloor, extend the model with simulated solar PV and battery elements, and validate room-level energy flows against measured Home Assistant sensor data.

tools.name: Virtastic/openmw-web
tools.desc: Play Morrowind in your browser — the OpenMW engine compiled to WebAssembly, now with multiplayer and a cloud locker for your own game data.

cls.summary: openmw-web is a WebAssembly build of the OpenMW game engine that runs The Elder Scrolls III: Morrowind in a desktop browser and includes a browser-hosted admin dashboard and optional multiplayer server.
cls.what_it_does: It compiles the OpenMW C++ game engine to WebAssembly so the full engine runs client-side in a desktop browser, and provides a Node/Docker-based server and browser admin dashboard for hosting worlds, user accounts, saves and experimental multiplayer. Notable aspects are the prebuilt Docker server image, an in-browser setup/dashboard and a BYO-game-data workflow that streams legally-owned game assets from the user's disk.
cls.trl_rationale: The project provides releases, a hosted demo, prebuilt server Docker images and an active repo with recent pushes, indicating a beta-level, usable build; the repository is 138 days old which supports a TRL up to 6 but is too young for long-term production evidence required for TRL 7+.
prerequisites: Docker for self-hosting and server components
legal access to Morrowind game data to run full game
student_project_ideas: Integrate a simple engineering scene (e.g. 3D procedural environment or interactive visualization of a CAD export) into the WebAssembly engine to compare rendering and input latency between native and WASM builds.

Build a small multiplayer demo using the project's server and WebRTC stack to demonstrate client-server authoritative simulation and measure network-synchronisation strategies for deterministic state updates.

tools.name: Suvitruf/unity-arcanum
tools.desc: A fan-made reimplementation of the engine behind Arcanum: Of Steamworks and Magick Obscura, built from scratch in Unity.

cls.summary: A fan-made clean-room reimplementation of the Arcanum game engine built in Unity that reads the original game's data files at runtime.
cls.what_it_does: This project reimplements the runtime engine of Arcanum inside Unity so the original game's maps, sprites, dialogs and scripts can be loaded and run on a modern engine. It is used by cloning the repository, opening it in the specified Unity editor, and providing a legitimate installation of Arcanum for the engine to read data from. Notable points are the reverse-engineering work on original file formats, a modular Unity architecture, and active documentation aimed at contributors.
cls.trl_rationale: The repository is an active, public fan reimplementation with many subsystems partially working and 149 stars, showing early adoption; it is only 144 days old so it lacks the long track record and stable releases required for TRL 6+. The README warns it is work-in-progress and not a finished product.
prerequisites: familiarity with Unity editor and C#
access to a legitimate copy of Arcanum (to provide original game data)
student_project_ideas: Implement a missing subsystem (e.g. improved AI or pathfinding) in the Unity reimplementation and compare behaviour against the original game's data-driven scripts.
Create a small modding tool that converts or previews Arcanum data files (sprites, maps, dialogs) using the project's reverse-engineering documentation and Unity importer.

tools.name: HilbertraumAI/HilbertRaum
tools.desc: AI, fully local on your computer.

cls.summary: HilbertRaum is a cross-platform desktop app that runs local LLMs entirely offline to let you chat with models and query your private documents and offline Wikipedia on your own machine.
cls.what_it_does: HilbertRaum provides a private, encrypted workspace for running local language and vision models (llama.cpp GGUF models) to perform chat, document Q&A with citations, image understanding, transcription and translation without any cloud service. It installs on Windows, macOS and Linux, benchmarks hardware to recommend compatible models, and offers an optional OpenAI-compatible local API for other local programs to call.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository is 161 days old and README states the app is feature-complete with releases and user-facing installers pending; it runs local models (llama.cpp) and has documentation but lacks a long track record or large user base, fitting a beta-level TRL.
prerequisites: basic familiarity with running desktop applications on Windows/macOS/Linux
understanding of local LLM models (llama.cpp/GGUF) and how to download/install them
student_project_ideas: Build a course project that ingests a corpus of project reports or requirements and uses HilbertRaum's document Q&A and evidence-pack export to produce traceable answers and an audit-ready summary.

Integrate HilbertRaum's local API with a student-built tool (e.g., a requirements tracker or code browser) to provide an offline assistant that answers questions about the codebase and linked documentation.

tools.name: Intellindust-AI-Lab/GTR
tools.desc: GTR: Gated Token Recurrence for Efficient Dense Prediction

cls.summary: GTR is an open-source PyTorch vision backbone that uses gated token recurrence and gated linear attention to provide efficient, high-resolution dense predictions for tasks like detection, segmentation, pose and depth.
cls.what_it_does: GTR implements a softmax-free recurrent vision backbone designed for dense prediction problems (object detection, instance/semantic segmentation, pose and metric depth). It is used as a drop-in backbone in PyTorch training and inference pipelines, provides optimized CUDA/Triton kernels for low-latency FP16 inference, and ships with task-specific configs and checkpoints hosted on Hugging Face. Notable features are gated linear attention, alternating spatial scan directions, a spatially enhanced SwiGLU block and a custom chunkwise CUDA operator for fast inference.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository is 110 days old (younger than one year) so lacks long-term production track record, but shows clear evidence of maturity: working training/inference code, optional fused CUDA operator, active recent commits, a model zoo on Hugging Face and reported bugfixes — consistent with a beta (TRL 6).
prerequisites: basic familiarity with deep learning training/inference pipelines
student_project_ideas: Integrate the GTR backbone into a ROS 2 perception pipeline and evaluate object detection and depth estimation on KITTI or a custom driving dataset, measuring inference latency with and without the fused CUDA operator.
Fine-tune a GTR model for semantic segmentation on Cityscapes and compare accuracy/latency trade-offs against a Swin/DETR-based baseline, profiling GPU memory and FP16 performance.

tools.name: afterimage-lab/Rainform
tools.desc: Rainform / 数据成雨 — an interactive WebGL rainfall data visualization built with Three.js.

cls.summary: Rainform is an interactive Three.js/WebGL demo that maps 25 hourly rainfall values to a real-time particle-based rain scene with draggable curves, water effects and synchronized sound.
cls.what_it_does: Rainform converts 25 hourly rainfall data points into an interactive WebGL particle rain scene where editing the curve updates rain intensity, a peak waterfall, water ripples, axes and audio in real time. It runs in a desktop browser (WebGL2) and is implemented with Three.js and standard web tooling; the project includes a live demo, development and build scripts and bilingual UI. The repository is notable for its data-driven particle effects and responsive editing UI rather than any engineering simulation fidelity.
cls.trl_rationale: The project is a functioning, documented WebGL application with a live demo, development/build scripts, CI and community interest (148 stars). The repository is 119 days old (under one year), so while it is usable and maintained it lacks the longer track record required for TRL 7+.
student_project_ideas: Extend Rainform to visualise other hourly environmental data (e.g. wind speed or temperature) by mapping new channels to particle properties and adding UI controls, then compare visual encodings for clarity.
Integrate Rainform with a small backend (Node/Express) that serves live sensor data (Simulated or real) and implement automated tests to validate data-to-visual mapping and audio sync.

tools.name: Leonxlnx/golden-temple
tools.desc: A golden-hour Japanese temple built entirely in code with three.js. No models, no textures, no HDRIs. Rendered offline into a 70s 1080p60 film

cls.summary: A purely code-driven, procedural Japanese temple scene and short film renderer implemented with three.js and GLSL.
cls.what_it_does: This repository procedurally generates an extensive 3D temple scene in the browser (no imported models or textures) and renders a 70-second, 1080p60 film by driving headless Chrome and piping frames into ffmpeg. It is notable for building a deterministic, high-detail scene entirely from JavaScript and GLSL, with tooling to render single frames, contact sheets and the complete film offline.
cls.trl_rationale: The repository is new (created ~33 days ago) and functions as a polished demo with scripts and instructions, but it lacks a long track record, releases history or broad production use — appropriate for an early-alpha demonstration.
prerequisites: Chrome/Edge for headless rendering (or CHROME env variable)
student_project_ideas: Extend the scene with a new procedural module (e.g. a temple garden or lanterns) and add URL parameters to control its generation, demonstrating procedural modelling and parameterisation.

Use the headless-render pipeline to benchmark GPU shader compilation and rendering performance across settings (spp, shadow map sizes) and report results as a lab assignment combining WebGL profiling and data analysis.

tools.name: LuwuDynamics/rig_omni
tools.desc: Open-source ESP32-S3 robot firmware supporting multiple forms (Puppy & Hover). Features voice AI, EAF emotion animation, IMU balance control, MCP remote tools, OTA updates, and a 240×240 round LCD.

cls.summary: RIG-Omni is an open-source ESP32-S3 firmware that runs multiple small robot forms (Puppy, Hover, ARM, TARS) providing motion control, IMU-based balance, display emote animations, voice AI integration, OTA and remote management tools.
cls.what_it_does: RIG-Omni provides a modular firmware stack for a family of ESP32-S3 robots, combining drivers (IMU, camera, motors), per-board motion logic (servo gaits, wheel balance, arm teach), local wake-word detection and cloud ASR/TTS, display emote animations and an MCP remote management console. It is used by building and flashing board-specific images via ESP-IDF and includes packaging scripts, OTA support and debug tools for motor tuning and remote control.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository shows a full codebase, build instructions, per-board configurations, packaging scripts and active recent commits with community interest (148 stars); however it is only ~161 days old so lacks long-term production track record, limiting TRL to beta (6).
prerequisites: ESP-IDF (5.5.x) and experience with esp32 builds
Access to matching ESP32-S3 hardware (displays, servos, IMU)
Python 3.10+ for utility scripts; FFmpeg for voice asset work
student_project_ideas: Implement and tune a balance controller for the Hover two-wheel robot using the included IMU drivers and compare controller performance (PID vs. simple state-feedback) using serial telemetry and a small test rig.
Extend the Puppy servo gait by adding a new commanded behaviour and use the MCP remote tools to implement voice-triggered actions, demonstrating the end-to-end pipeline from wake-word to motion.

tools.name: JuiceBoxxGames/utsuwa
tools.desc: Utsuwa is an open-source alternative to Grok Companion. This is a platform where you can have a virtual AI waifu that learns and grows with you, bundled with optional mechanics inspired by Japanese dating sim games.

tools.name: off-grid-ai/OGAD
tools.desc: Your private, on-device personal AI assistant for macOS, Windows and Linux. Chat, create, search files, and connect tools with local models. Includes an OpenAI-compatible API. Opt-in Pro sees, remembers, reflects, and acts with your approval, for one payment. No cloud or account.

tools.name: tg-prplx/vellium
tools.desc: Local-first desktop AI workbench for roleplay, multi-character chat, long-form writing, RAG, MCP tools, plugins, and local models.

cls.summary: Vellium is a local-first desktop workbench for multi-character AI chat, roleplay, live voice conversations and long-form writing with support for local and OpenAI-compatible model endpoints.
cls.what_it_does: Vellium provides a desktop Electron interface to run chats, branching roleplay timelines, writing projects and RAG-enabled knowledge collections while connecting to many LLM providers (local and remote). It stores data locally in SQLite, supports plugins and MCP tool integrations, and can run headless as a web service or packaged desktop app.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository is actively developed with desktop release artifacts and a full README, but is under 1 year old (created Feb 2026) so it fits a beta-level maturity (versioned builds and releases present but no long-term production track record).
prerequisites: familiarity with running Electron apps / desktop builds
student_project_ideas: Compare latency, cost and retrieval quality of several local and remote LLM backends (e.g. Ollama, KoboldCpp, OpenAI-compatible endpoints) by building a RAG pipeline in Vellium and measuring end-to-end response times and relevance on an engineering document corpus.

Create a reproducible writing-assistant workflow that ingests course notes as a LoreBook, then evaluates different prompt/block strategies and embeddings configurations to support automated summarisation and chapter drafting.

tools.name: mjasnikovs/pi-task
tools.desc: Deterministic spec-orchestration for local LLMs in the pi coding agent — drives prompts through refine→research→grill→compose→critique, with bundled web/docs/fetch worker tools.

cls.summary: pi-task is a deterministic task-orchestrator that runs a user request through a fixed pipeline of refine→research→grill→compose→critique to produce crash‑safe, verifiable specs for local LLM powered coding agents.
cls.what_it_does: pi-task solves the problem of unreliable single-prompt behaviour in local LLMs by driving requests through a persisted, phase‑based pipeline and isolating noisy work into throwaway child sessions. It is used as an extension/plugin to the Earendil "pi" coding agent to produce reproducible implementation specs, with file-backed state for crash recovery and commands to plan, run, resume or cancel tasks. Notable features include parallel research workers, tooling-claim verification, phase persistence to Markdown files, and safeguards for local model drift.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository is active, has a detailed README, 147 stars and recent commits, indicating community interest and a usable project; however it is ~5.5 months old (younger than 1 year) so lacks the longer track record or stable release history required for TRL 7+.
prerequisites: Earendil 'pi' coding agent (pi >= 0.87) and familiarity with its slash-command workflow
basic knowledge of running local LLMs and configuring model endpoints
