student_project_ideas: Integrate pi-task with a small local LLM (e.g. llama.cpp) to build a classroom demo where students submit feature requests and inspect the generated .pi-tasks Markdown trace to learn about prompt decomposition and verification.

Compare deterministic orchestration vs single-prompt approaches by running the same coding task through pi-task and a baseline agent (e.g. a simple LangChain agent) and evaluate spec quality, hallucination rate, and recoverability.

tools.name: yalun753/moe-l2
tools.desc: MoE expert offload for low-VRAM GPUs — run 100B+ MoE models (DeepSeek, Qwen, Mixtral) on 8 GB cards. Expert cache with LRU hot experts, OpenAI-compatible proxy, GGUF multi-shard.

cls.summary: moe-l2 is an open-source proxy and runtime that offloads and caches Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) model experts so very large MoE LLMs can run on low-VRAM consumer GPUs.
cls.what_it_does: moe-l2 predicts which MoE experts a prompt will need and preloads them into a shared-memory LRU cache, copying only activated experts to GPU to reduce VRAM usage and enable inference of 100B+ MoE models on 10–11 GB cards. It acts as an OpenAI-compatible proxy around existing GGUF/llama.cpp-style runtimes and provides selective pinning, on-demand pin, and multi-shard support to trade off speed, host RAM and GPU VRAM.
cls.trl_rationale: The project is recent (created 2026-07-26, ~114 days old) but shows substantial evidence of functionality: benchmarks, demos, multi-architecture binary releases and active pushes; however it lacks a long track record in production and is younger than one year so TRL is limited to Beta (6).
prerequisites: familiarity with LLM inference concepts and GGUF/llama.cpp-style model formats
comfort building or running native binaries
student_project_ideas: Measure VRAM/throughput trade-offs for a chosen MoE model (e.g. Qwen3.6-A3B) by comparing full-GPU, selective-pin and on-demand modes in moe-l2 and report implications for deploying LLM inference on edge/consumer GPUs.

Integrate moe-l2 with a small downstream application (e.g. a retrieval-augmented QA service) to evaluate latency and cost when serving MoE models from low-VRAM hardware, and implement an automated router-map selection strategy based on domain detection.

tools.name: SquareWaveSystems/opcilloscope
tools.desc: Browse and monitor OPC UA servers from your terminal. Lightweight, cross-platform, keyboard and mouse friendly.

tools.name: believer-oss/Claireon
tools.desc: MCP server for Unreal Editor

cls.summary: Claireon is an Unreal Editor plugin that runs a Model Context Protocol (MCP) server to let AI assistants inspect, search and automate editing of Unreal assets and editor workflows.
cls.what_it_does: Claireon exposes editor automation tools via an MCP server so AI agents can search, read, inspect and modify Unreal assets (Blueprints, Animation, State Trees, Niagara, Data Tables, sequences, etc.) and run Python inside the editor. It is used as an in-editor plugin (or optional proxy) that starts a deterministic per-worktree TCP port and provides a small MCP surface (tool_search + python_execute) with built-in audit logging and session management.
cls.trl_rationale: The repository (created ~160 days ago) documents a feature-rich, actively maintained Unreal Editor plugin with many concrete capabilities and installation instructions; however it is younger than one year so there is limited long-term track record, placing it at Beta (TRL 6).
prerequisites: Familiarity with building Unreal plugins and editor workflows
student_project_ideas: Create an AI-assisted asset-cleanup tool that uses Claireon to search a project for redirectors and broken references, auto-fix them and report changes, integrating with Git for change tracking.

Build an experiment where an LLM (via an MCP client) automatically iterates on a simple Blueprint gameplay mechanic (spawn, movement) using Claireon to modify and test Play-In-Editor scenarios and collect performance/validation traces.

tools.name: wq19901103wq/wechat-mac-rpa
tools.desc: 基于多模态视觉感知与 LLM Agent 的 macOS 微信自动化框架 | Visual RPA for WeChat

cls.summary: A macOS tool that uses computer vision and an LLM-based agent to automate interaction with the WeChat desktop app by treating the app as a black-box GUI.
cls.what_it_does: This project reads WeChat windows with screenshots and OCR / vision models, reasons about messages with a large language model agent, and performs system-level UI actions (AppleScript / System Events) to reply or interact. It is notable for a structured perception→reasoning→action→memory pipeline, options for local OCR fallback and multimodal API fallthrough, and logging for traceability.
cls.trl_rationale: The repository has a detailed README, tests, scripts and active commits with a small user interest (145 stars) indicating a beta-quality project; however it is under 1 year old (199 days), so there is limited public production track record which caps the TRL at 6.
prerequisites: macOS 12+ and familiarity with macOS permissions (screen recording, accessibility, automation)
Python 3.10+ and experience installing Python deps
API keys for multimodal LLMs if using the cloud-backed perception path
student_project_ideas: Build a supervised evaluation that compares local OCR-only replies vs multimodal-API-assisted replies by running the bot against a corpus of exported WeChat chats and measuring reply correctness and latency.

Integrate the perception output with a simple chat-analytics pipeline (store extracted messages to a vector DB and visualise common intents over time) to demonstrate traceability and memory indexing in an RPA context.

tools.name: bandinopla/three-mediapipe-rig
tools.desc: A ThreeJs module to quickly setup a Media Pipe skeletal rig with minimal code.

cls.summary: A JavaScript/TypeScript library that maps Google MediaPipe webcam pose, face and hand landmarks onto Three.js skeletal rigs for real-time avatar control in the browser.
cls.what_it_does: The project connects MediaPipe's browser-based tracking (face, body, hands) to Three.js skeletons, applying angle-based transforms so landmarks drive bones and blendshapes. It's used by installing the npm package, calling setupTracker to load models, binding a Three.js rig, and calling a per-frame update to apply motion; it is notable for an out-of-the-box mapping, demos and recording/export support (.glb).
cls.trl_rationale: Repository has substantial README, demos and npm packaging and moderate community interest (145 stars) but is under one year old (created 2026-03-01) so evidence supports a beta-level maturity rather than long-term production adoption.
student_project_ideas: Create a browser-based ergonomic posture assessor that uses the library to record joint angles from webcam input and flags unsafe postures, exporting motion clips as .glb for offline review.
Integrate the real-time avatar output with a ROS/Gazebo simulation via a simple WebSocket bridge so students can test HRI teleoperation where human motion controls a simulated robot arm or avatar.

tools.name: mamawai/wtfibought
tools.desc: A live arena where LLM agents trade real market data with virtual money — every thought, tool call, thesis and post-mortem is public. Bring your own model and key.

cls.summary: WhatIfIBought is an open-source live arena where LLM trading agents and quant strategies trade on real market feeds with simulated money, exposing full agent reasoning, strategy backtests and a unified ledger.
cls.what_it_does: It runs a multi-process simulator that feeds live Binance and Polymarket market data into a trade simulation and lets LLM agents (bring-your-own-model+key) and quant strategies place simulated trades, backtest, and produce public daily reviews and trade post-mortems. Notable features are a unified margin ledger, real funding and leverage rules matching live venues, walk‑forward evaluation, and a public-to-private transparency model for agent reasoning and tool calls.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository is under 1 year old (created 2026-02-06) so TRL is capped by age, but the README describes a live public deployment, extensive features (simulator, backtests, ledger) and active commits, indicating a beta-level system with working production demo.
prerequisites: Access to an LLM provider key (and exchange API familiarity)
student_project_ideas: Extend the simulator to add a new exchange connector (or a synthetic instrument) and evaluate how an existing LLM agent's performance changes under the new instrument using walk‑forward backtesting.

Implement an explainability module that aggregates agent decision traces and generates concise, structured failure reports for failed trades, then evaluate its usefulness in a lab comparing human vs agent post-mortems.

tools.name: Vottivott/microduck-playground
tools.desc: Reproducible Microduck RL experiments, policies, simulation assets, and hardware add-ons

cls.summary: Microduck Playground provides reproducible MuJoCo-based reinforcement-learning experiments, trained policies, simulation assets and 3D-printable hardware add-ons for the Microduck bipedal robot.
cls.what_it_does: The repository hosts training experiments, policy checkpoints (including ONNX exports), simulation rollouts and parametric 3D-print models and assembly instructions for the Microduck robot. It is used to reproduce and evaluate locomotion behaviours in MuJoCo, run trained policies in simulation and produce hardware add-ons for physical testing; notable aspects are the combination of RL experiments, published runtime artifacts and printable hardware for integration tests.
cls.trl_rationale: The project is an active, well-documented experimental repo with runnable experiments, checkpoints and printable hardware assets, but the repository is only 76 days old so it lacks a longer production track record; that recent age limits the TRL to around 5 despite solid artifacts.
prerequisites: MuJoCo (or compatible physics backend) and simulator setup
basic 3D printing / CAD familiarity to use printable hardware models
familiarity with RL (PPO) and ONNX runtimes
student_project_ideas: Reproduce one of the provided locomotion experiments, convert its ONNX policy to run on a Raspberry Pi or microcontroller-adjacent runtime and report performance differences between local and simulated inference.

Modify a parametric hardware add-on (e.g. stilts or docking station), 3D-print it, and evaluate how the changed geometry affects simulated behaviour and stability using the included MuJoCo experiments.

tools.name: amurgola/LumaBrowser
tools.desc: Local AI desktop app: a Chromium browser with a GPU-aware llama.cpp runtime, OpenAI-compatible API, AI chat and agents, Stable Diffusion image/video, TTS and music, plus an MCP server so Claude Code, Codex and Cline can drive your browser. Windows, macOS, Linux.

cls.summary: LumaBrowser is a desktop Chromium-based app that runs local LLMs, media models and agent automation on your machine and exposes OpenAI/Anthropic-compatible APIs and an MCP server for external tools.
cls.what_it_does: LumaBrowser bundles a browser with GPU-aware runtimes for local language, image, video and voice models so you can run chats, agents and generation without sending data to the cloud. It provides an OpenAI/Anthropic-compatible local API, an MCP/ACP server so external agents and editors can drive your real browser, and integrations to existing model caches and runtimes.
cls.trl_rationale: The repository provides cross-platform releases, detailed documentation and many runtime features which indicate an alpha in use, but it is only 39 days old so it lacks a longer track record or stable ecosystem required for TRL 6+.
prerequisites: familiarity with local LLM concepts and GPU runtimes
understanding of browser automation protocols (CDP, WebDriver) if using agents
student_project_ideas: Build an agent that uses LumaBrowser's MCP server to scrape and summarise engineering standards from logged-in vendor sites, then generate a traceability checklist.
Configure a private local QA system by indexing course documents and using a local LLM runtime in LumaBrowser to answer student questions without using cloud APIs.

tools.name: vprix21/neonblade-ui
tools.desc: Futuristic React UI component library - neon, sci-fi, and futuristic components for modern web apps. Install via CLI.

cls.summary: NeonBlade UI is a TypeScript React component library and CLI that installs futuristic, neon/cyberpunk-styled UI components into web apps.
cls.what_it_does: NeonBlade UI provides a curated set of reusable React components with a neon/sci‑fi visual style and a CLI that copies chosen components into your project. It uses Tailwind CSS v4 for styling, supports TypeScript and Framer Motion for animations, and distributes components from a remote registry.
cls.trl_rationale: The project is an active monorepo with a CLI, a public website, and a visible registry; it has a moderate star count and recent activity but is under one year old (created 233 days ago), so it fits a beta-level maturity rather than long-term production track record.
student_project_ideas: Build a small web dashboard that consumes simulated sensor data and uses NeonBlade UI components and three.js to present a sci‑fi themed monitoring interface.
Create a themed frontend for a digital twin demo (Next.js) using the NeonBlade CLI to install components and Tailwind to adapt styles for an engineering dataset.

tools.name: AIGODLIKE/BlenderAIStudio
tools.desc: An addon to fully enhance Blender's AI workflow, serving as a demonstration for Addon UI-Forge (next-gen Blender Addon UI framework).

tools.name: Shellishack/infinite-pokemon
tools.desc: A Pokémon-style adventure built with Codex, featuring AI-generated maps, NPCs, branching saves, and multiplayer. The adventure never ends.

cls.summary: A TypeScript/Electron procedurally generated Pokémon-style adventure that uses an AI harness (OpenAI Codex) to extend maps, NPCs and story as you play.
cls.what_it_does: Infinite Pokémon is a playable prototype game that procedurally generates new map areas, NPCs and story content using an AI skill harness; it runs as a browser demo and as a local/Electron build and can report minimal progress to a public leaderboard. Notable aspects are the integration with Codex/Skill CLI for on-demand generation, a persistent world snapshot mechanism, and use of Phaser/TypeScript for the game client.
cls.trl_rationale: The repository hosts a working TypeScript/Electron game and a browser demo with published skills and a technical report, indicating early adopters and runnable examples; however the project is only 64 days old so it lacks the multi-release, long-term production track record required for TRL 6+.
prerequisites: Optional OpenAI Codex (or compatible) API access for live generation
student_project_ideas: Compare generated map consistency by running the game with and without Codex integration and report on how persistent-state snapshots affect generation quality.
Extend the game backend to log and visualise NPC behavioural state over time, then analyse how generative suggestions change gameplay balance (combine with simple statistical analysis in Python).

tools.name: PteroLabsAI/PteroSim-UAV-Simulator
tools.desc: UAV simulation platform for development, testing, and research.

cls.summary: PteroSim is a UAV (drone) simulation platform that runs PX4 and ArduPilot SITL, provides accurate 6-DOF flight dynamics and sensors, and exposes a programmatic API and Python SDK for multi‑vehicle orchestration and testing.
cls.what_it_does: PteroSim simulates UAV flight dynamics (6‑DOF), sensors (IMU, GPS, barometer, airspeed, camera) and environmental effects (wind, turbulence) and supports PX4 and ArduPilot SITL so controllers can be tested without hardware. It is used by running the simulator binary or the Python SDK and controlling simulated vehicles via a gRPC API; aircraft are defined by JSBSim XML and glTF assets so users can add or modify aircraft models. Notable aspects are native PX4/ArduPilot SITL support, JSBSim-based dynamics, and a Python SDK for multi-drone orchestration.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository is active with documentation, downloadable releases and a pip-installable Python SDK, demonstrating beta-level maturity and community interest; however the project is only ~7.5 months old so lacks the long track record required for TRL 7+.
prerequisites: basic Linux or Windows system administration
student_project_ideas: Use PteroSim with PX4 SITL and the Python SDK to implement and evaluate an autonomous mission planner (path planning and obstacle avoidance) for a quadcopter and compare performance under varying wind/turbulence profiles.

Create a custom aircraft JSBSim model (new glTF mesh + XML) and integrate a novel control algorithm (e.g. LQR or RL policy) via the gRPC API to assess handling qualities and controller robustness in simulation.

tools.name: IIIIIllllIIIIIlllll/Qwenox
tools.desc: An inference framework customized for AI MAX 395, compatible with both Linux and Windows, and supports deploying only qwen3.8-flash-next. This project is for reference and learning purposes only. 为AI MAX 395定制的推理框架，Linux和Windows通用，只能部署qwen3.8-flash-next。本项目仅供参考学习使用。

cls.summary: Qwenox is an open-source, C++ local inference engine optimized for running the qwen3.8-flash-next large model on AMD Strix Halo (Ryzen AI Max+ 395) systems under Linux and Windows.
cls.what_it_does: Qwenox loads very large model weights (hgn/GGUF variants) from disk and performs GPU-accelerated local inference with OpenAI/Anthropic-compatible HTTP APIs and a web console. It implements disk-resident n-gram tables, speculatively assisted decoding, and memory/prefill strategies to run 177B MoE qwen3.8-flash-next on 128 GiB-class APUs with measured throughput and power numbers.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository is very recent (created ~59 days ago) so it lacks a long production track record; the README contains detailed benchmarks and cross-platform build/run instructions indicating early adopter usage and functioning code, consistent with an alpha-in-use level (TRL 5).
prerequisites: familiarity with building C++ projects on Linux/Windows (compilers, build tools)
ROCm/HIP GPU runtime knowledge for AMD accelerators
substantial disk and memory resources for multi-hundred-GB model files and Hugging Face CLI usage
student_project_ideas: Measure and compare inference latency, throughput and power consumption of qwen3.8-flash-next on Strix Halo with Qwenox versus a CPU-only baseline, and present trade-offs for edge AI deployment.
Integrate Qwenox's OpenAI-compatible API into a robotics or IoT prototype to run on-device high-context conversational agents and evaluate network-offload vs local-inference performance and costs.

tools.name: nathansutton/chad
tools.desc: chad: a coding agent for your macbook pro

cls.summary: chad is a local coding assistant that runs on Apple Silicon Macs using a bundled 27B Qwen model and the MLX runtime to provide fast, offline code-writing sessions in the terminal.
cls.what_it_does: chad provides a command-line, local-LLM coding agent that downloads a specific 27B Qwen model and runs an agent loop owned by the process to perform coding tasks without any cloud API keys. It is used via a CLI (installable as a PyPI package) and is notable for being optimised for Apple Silicon performance using MLX and custom kernels to increase token throughput for interactive coding sessions.
cls.trl_rationale: The project is actively maintained, has documentation, benchmarks, a PyPI package and community interest (143 stars), but the repository is only ~141 days old so it lacks the longer track record required for TRL 7+.
prerequisites: ~30 GB free disk space for initial model download
familiarity with command-line usage and Python packaging

tools.name: delancy827/cad-skills
tools.desc: CAD 自动化设计技能包 — 让 AI Agent 真正学会用 AutoCAD

cls.summary: A repository of AutoCAD automation 'skills' (Python scripts, AutoLISP patterns and workflow guides) that let AI agents or users generate, modify and check engineering drawings from natural language.
cls.what_it_does: cad-skills provides a paired toolkit: cad-automation contains code examples and automation patterns (Python pyautocad/COM, SendCommand, AutoLISP) to drive AutoCAD and compatible Chinese CADs; cad-designer documents drawing standards, layer/annotation conventions and design-check workflows. It is used by placing the skill folders into an AI agent skill directory or running the provided scripts to automate drawing, batch processing and rule-based design checks.
cls.trl_rationale: The repo is active (created 2026-05, last push 2026-10) with a changelog showing multiple numbered releases (v1.0.0 → v1.2.0), 143 stars and detailed docs, indicating beyond prototype but still younger than one year so best-classified as beta (TRL 6).
prerequisites: pyautocad, pywin32 (pip packages) or AutoLISP knowledge
student_project_ideas: Build an AI-driven AutoCAD macro that takes a natural-language part description and generates a fully dimensioned 2D part drawing using pyautocad and AutoLISP, then export a PDF batch; evaluate robustness across parametric inputs.

Implement a rules-based drawing checker (based on cad-designer guidelines) that scans DWG files to validate layer naming, font/annotation sizes and closed dimension chains, reporting non-conformances and suggested fixes.

tools.name: DominikBucko/qwen38-flash-next-2x3090
tools.desc: Qwen3.8-Flash-Next on 2× RTX 3090: with 128 GB RAM up to 4,191 tok/s prefill · 111.5 tok/s decode (131K prompt), full 256K window at 2,865 tok/s; with 64 GB RAM 3,410 tok/s prefill · 84 tok/s decode. New: opt-in uncensored mode (runtime abliteration, no new weights).

cls.summary: A repository of patches, profiles and configuration to run the Qwen 3.8 Flash-Next LLM with very large context windows on consumer GPUs (two RTX 3090s) using CPU offloading and quantised weights for high-throughput local inference.
cls.what_it_does: The project packages a pinned vLLM build, runtime patches and environment profiles to serve a quantised Qwen 3.8 checkpoint with 128K–256K context on dual RTX 3090 systems, using CPU offload and expert caching to trade system RAM, PCIe traffic and GPU memory. It provides prebuilt configs for different host memory sizes, performance-tuned prefill/decode profiles, and an opt-in runtime modification that alters safety/refusal behaviour without changing weights. Notable features are multi‑GPU expert caching, FP8/INT4 support, and documented benchmarked profiles for large prompts.
cls.trl_rationale: The repo contains working code, config profiles, benchmarks and a downloadable checkpoint reference, indicating it is used by adopters; however the repository is very recent (created 79 days ago) so there is limited long-term track record or broad production adoption, capping TRL at 5.
prerequisites: Linux host with CUDA and drivers
One or more NVIDIA GPUs (RTX 3090 recommended)
Familiarity with building/running container images, vLLM and large-model checkpoints
student_project_ideas: Benchmark and compare throughput and memory trade-offs for a quantised Qwen 3.8 model on different GPU+RAM host configurations (single 3090 vs dual 3090) and report impacts of prefill chunk sizes and expert cache sizes.

Integrate the patched vLLM runtime from this repo into a small local LLM service and implement a safe front-end proxy that demonstrates how the repo's opt-in 'uncensored' runtime modification can be constrained and monitored.

tools.name: thomas9120/LLama-GUI
tools.desc: User friendly GUI for configuring and launching llama.cpp

cls.summary: A cross-platform, browser-based GUI that helps users install, configure and launch local llama.cpp backends and models for chat, benchmarking and serving.
cls.what_it_does: Llama GUI provides a lightweight local control panel to install prebuilt llama.cpp binaries (CPU/GPU backends), launch llama-server or llama-cli from quick presets or full configuration, chat with streaming Markdown and benchmarking tools, and manage presets and launch shortcuts. It is used by running the included installer or manual setup; the app runs a local web UI and shells out to llama.cpp binaries and related tools, notable for its multi-backend installer, built-in benchmarking and beginner-friendly quick-launch workflows.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository is actively maintained with an installer, cross-platform support, examples and many stars, indicating adopters and polish; however it is only ~7 months old so lacks the multi-year track record and ecosystem required for TRL 7+.
prerequisites: llama.cpp-compatible model files and runtime binaries
OS-specific GPU drivers for chosen backend (CUDA/ROCm/Vulkan) where needed
student_project_ideas: Build a small local chat assistant for a course dataset by integrating Llama GUI-managed llama.cpp server with a custom frontend, and measure latency and throughput across CPU and GPU backends using the built-in benchmarking tools.

Compare model-perplexity and response latency for two different llama.cpp backends (CPU vs Vulkan/CUDA) using Llama GUI's benchmarking and monitoring, and prepare a short report recommending a backend for low-cost deployment.

tools.name: Scottcjn/legend-of-elya-n64
tools.desc: Legend of Elya — N64 game with a real 6.36M-parameter ternary transformer on the VR4300 MIPS III CPU. Zelda-style dungeon, AI NPCs, byte-level inference at 1.23 tok/s scalar / 2.19 tok/s on the RSP overlay (measured under ares, never on silicon). Built with libdragon.

cls.summary: A homebrew Nintendo 64 game that runs a small transformer LLM entirely on the N64 CPU (and optionally the RSP), demonstrating byte-level inference, ternary quantization and other embedded-AI techniques on vintage hardware.
cls.what_it_does: The project implements a complete 6.36M-parameter transformer that performs live inference on the N64's MIPS R4300i CPU (and an RSP overlay path) inside a Zelda-like demo ROM; weights are stored compressed in cartridge ROM and dequantized on-the-fly for matrix multiplies. It is used as an experimental platform for extreme edge/retro embedded AI, custom numerical tricks (fast exp, inverse sqrt), and performance/quantization research with runnable emulator and EverDrive ROMs.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository is ~9 months old with active pushes, a runnable ROM, emulator demos and EverDrive-backed real-hardware runs for earlier builds; however the largest 6.36M ternary build / RSP overlay have not been fully validated on silicon and the project is experimental, so maturity is consistent with a beta-level project.
prerequisites: knowledge of N64/libdragon toolchain and Rom building
understanding of quantized neural nets and basic MIPS architecture
student_project_ideas: Measure and compare inference speed and memory use of the ternary quantized transformer on emulator vs EverDrive hardware, and produce a short report explaining bottlenecks and possible micro-optimisations (e.g. RSP offload or fixed-point arithmetic).

Modify the sampling strategy or vocabulary to implement a constrained dialog agent for a simple robot simulation, integrating the ROM build with a host-side dataset exporter to evaluate response quality under different quantization schemes.

tools.name: IST-DASLab/GSQ
tools.desc: Gumbel-Softmax post-training quantization for LLMs (1–3 bit scalar, INT/GGUF-compatible).

cls.summary: GSQ is a post-training scalar quantization tool that uses a Gumbel-Softmax relaxation to produce 1–3 bit, GGUF/INT-compatible quantized LLM checkpoints.
cls.what_it_does: GSQ takes pretrained large language models and performs layer-wise post-training scalar quantization by initializing with GPTQ and then refining discrete weight assignments with a Gumbel-Softmax relaxation; it produces compressed checkpoints compatible with GGUF K-Quant and INT inference kernels. It is used as a Python toolchain that offloads per-layer shards, trains logits for discrete grids, and reassembles HuggingFace-compatible checkpoints for low-bit deployment, notable for closing much of the accuracy gap for scalar PTQ at 2–3 bits.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository is ~6 months old with active pushes, a detailed README, example scripts and experimental results, and a modest community (142 stars), indicating beta-level maturity; however it is younger than one year and lacks evidence of broad production adoption, which limits TRL to 6.
student_project_ideas: Apply GSQ to a small open LLM (e.g. Llama-2 7B or a distilled model), compare accuracy and perplexity vs GPTQ/QuIP at 2-bit and 3-bit and report trade-offs in size and latency.
Use GSQ to refine a public GGUF K-Quant checkpoint, then deploy the resulting GGUF with llama.cpp or vLLM and benchmark CPU inference speed and end-to-end task accuracy.

tools.name: andymai/brepjs
tools.desc: CAD in TypeScript with exact solids (B-Rep). AI agents can write parts with it and check them on OpenCascade.

cls.summary: brepjs is a TypeScript library and runtime for creating exact boundary-representation (B-Rep) CAD solids, running in Node or the browser with a WebAssembly geometry kernel and STEP export.
cls.what_it_does: brepjs provides a code-first CAD API in TypeScript that builds exact B‑Rep solids (not triangle meshes), performs precise booleans, fillets, measurements and exports to STEP/IFC. It runs on top of a WASM OpenCascade kernel (occt-wasm) or other kernels, includes a playground and CLI tooling for verification, and is designed for parametric, programmatic part and assembly authoring (including use by AI coding agents).
cls.trl_rationale: The project is active with a published npm package, a live playground, example gallery, CLI verifier and demonstrable examples, indicating a beta-level maturity; however the repository is under one year old (created 2026-02-01) which limits TRL to at most 6 by the guideline.
prerequisites: basic CAD and geometry concepts (B‑Rep, STEP)
student_project_ideas: Create a parametric enclosure for a Raspberry Pi with brepjs, export STEP for manufacturing and validate clearances and center of mass; compare designer-written and agent-generated variants.
Build a six-axis robot arm model in brepjs using DH parameters, simulate kinematic reach and export component STEP files for downstream CAM or FEA processing.

tools.name: steventsvik/Tellurion
tools.desc: Mission control for AI coding agents. Watch Claude Code, Codex, Gemini and a dozen more work live in one macOS terminal: live status, an editor that follows their edits, undo for any turn, approvals from your phone and local models. 20+ built-in tools, all on the site below. Built on Ghostty.

cls.summary: Tellurion is a macOS terminal that monitors and orchestrates multiple AI coding agents, showing live edits, enabling review/undo for agent turns, and providing mission-control style approvals and local-model chat.
cls.what_it_does: Tellurion tracks AI coding agents (Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI, Copilot CLI and others) running in terminal tabs, shows live status and edits as they happen, captures snapshots so any agent turn can be undone, and provides a central Mission Control and review inbox for approvals and hand-offs. It is used as a native macOS terminal (forking Ghostty) to observe, coordinate and interact with multiple agents and local models while developing code.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository is functional and installs via a script, shows many features and agent integrations, and has active commits and stars; however it is only 51 days old so lacks a longer track record of production deployments, which limits the TRL to alpha-in-use.
prerequisites: familiarity with terminal workflows and AI coding agents
student_project_ideas: Build an experiment that runs a set of coding tasks through multiple agents in Tellurion, instrumenting and comparing produced diffs, test pass rates and time-to-fix to evaluate agent quality.
Extend Tellurion to add an automated V&V step: on agent-produced changes, run a CI test suite and automatically annotate the review inbox with test results and coverage diffs.

tools.name: MengTo/towers
tools.desc: A tower builds itself from the ground up in four and a half seconds: a Japanese tenshu, a Chinese pagoda or a Thai prang, in one self-contained HTML file.

cls.summary: A single-file WebGL demo that procedurally generates and animates the staged construction of several East and Southeast Asian tower styles using three.js.
cls.what_it_does: Towers procedurally builds parametric tower models (pagoda, tenshu, prang, prasat, mosque, etc.) and animates a cut-plane construction sequence with lighting, weather and sound entirely in one HTML file. It's used as an interactive visual demo (orbit, timeline scrub, day/night and weather) and is notable for being dependency-free, compact, and for generating geometry and textures procedurally in the browser.
cls.trl_rationale: The repository is a polished, single-file demo with interactive features and 141 stars, showing real interest, but it is a recent project (created ~98 days ago) with no evidence of production deployment or versioned releases, so maturity fits an alpha-in-use level.
prerequisites: familiarity with three.js and WebGL concepts
student_project_ideas: Extend the procedural builders to export parametric geometry (GLTF/OBJ) and integrate with a CAD or 3D-printing pipeline to produce fabrication-ready parts.
Add physics-based validation by coupling the generated towers with a simple structural analysis (e.g. compute centre of mass and load paths) and visualise stability under wind loads in the browser.

tools.name: akawashiro/procinsh
tools.desc: Explore Linux processes in 3D. A real-time process inspector powered by Rust, eBPF and Three.js.

cls.summary: ProcInSh is a web-based, real-time Linux process inspector that uses eBPF and a Three.js frontend to visualise processes and their metadata in 3D from a browser.
cls.what_it_does: ProcInSh captures kernel-level process information using eBPF and exposes it through a web UI rendered with Three.js so you can explore process relationships, memory and environment data in a 3D space. It runs an agent on Linux hosts (x86-64 or AArch64) and can connect multiple agents to a hub for combined views, with privacy masking and recording features for sharing or replay.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository is active with a working demo, install/build instructions and multiple stars, indicating early adopters; however it is only 57 days old so lacks long-term production track record which caps TRL at around 5.
prerequisites: C compiler and clang with BPF backend
bpftool, libelf and zlib dev files, pkg-config
Node.js 22+ and npm for building web assets
student_project_ideas: Build a lab exercise where students extend ProcInSh to visualise inter-process IPC patterns (sockets, pipes) and annotate the 3D view with process start times and resource usage.
Create a multi-host monitoring prototype by deploying ProcInSh agents to several VMs and develop a dashboard that correlates process events across hosts to investigate distributed performance issues.

tools.name: muratozturkdev/homescape
tools.desc: Your Home Assistant home as a live, interactive 3D dollhouse. Fully local, no cloud. Every 3D object is generated by code written by AI: no GLB or other model files.

cls.summary: Homescape is a browser-based, fully local 3D interactive dollhouse that visualises and controls Home Assistant entities and automations in real time.
cls.what_it_does: Homescape automatically builds a 3D floorplan from Home Assistant areas and entities and renders a live, interactive scene in the browser where devices animate and can be controlled. It is used as a local Home Assistant frontend or standalone site (for development) and is notable for generating all 3D geometry in code (no external model files) and for being fully local with no cloud services.
cls.trl_rationale: The repository is very new (created 10 days ago) but has a polished README, examples and active pushes; however there is no long track record or stable releases so maturity fits an early-alpha TRL 4.
prerequisites: Home Assistant instance for full functionality and device data
student_project_ideas: Build a lab exercise that connects a Home Assistant test instance and extends Homescape with a custom device model (e.g. a new sensor or actuator) to demonstrate live state changes and control flows.

Create a capstone mini-project that integrates Homescape with a simulated IoT network (MQTT devices) to visualise occupancy detection and evaluate different sensor fusion strategies for room presence.

tools.name: L-Forster/open-jet
tools.desc: An offline coding agent for local models. One command sets up the best model your GPU can run, and on 24 GB+ RTX 30/40/50-series cards Qwen3.8-27B runs up to 1.9x faster than llama.cpp.

cls.summary: OpenJet is an open-source runtime and coding-agent toolkit for running large local language models (LLMs) efficiently on NVIDIA GPUs and serving them to coding tools and agents.
cls.what_it_does: OpenJet installs and runs local LLMs (notably Qwen3.8-27B) on NVIDIA RTX 30/40/50-series GPUs, providing a prebuilt inference engine tuned for long context and multi-agent decoding. It exposes a CLI agent, a Python SDK and a serving mode compatible with Anthropic/ OpenAI-style APIs so local models can be used by coding assistants and external tools; notable points are its GPU-specific engine (megakernel) and claimed throughput improvements versus llama.cpp.
cls.trl_rationale: The project is active, has documentation, CLI, a Python SDK, and measurable benchmarks, but the repository is under one year old (created 2026-02-16) so there is not yet a long track record of broad production use; this supports a beta-level TRL.
prerequisites: NVIDIA CUDA and GPU driver knowledge
Familiarity with Python and package installation
student_project_ideas: Measure and compare local inference throughput and token-latency of OpenJet vs. llama.cpp on different GPU instances (local RTX vs cloud RTX 3090) and report effects of context length and batching.

Integrate OpenJet's serve mode with a simple automated testing harness to evaluate a coding agent's ability to produce and validate shell commands for a controlled hardware setup (combine with unit tests or a simulated environment).

tools.name: ceresOPA/Alicization-Town
tools.desc: **⚔️ Alicization Town** is a decentralized, multi-agent pixel sandbox world powered by the **Model Context Protocol (MCP)**.    **⚔️ Alicization Town** 是一个基于 **MCP (Model Context Protocol)** 架构的去中心化多智能体像素沙盒世界。

cls.summary: Alicization Town is a decentralised, multi-agent 2D pixel sandbox that lets local AI agents connect via the Model Context Protocol (MCP) to inhabit, move and interact inside a lightweight world server.
cls.what_it_does: It provides a lightweight Node.js world server and a pluginable runtime where AI agents (running locally or via MCP clients) can control characters using CLI commands or an MCP gateway. Notable features include a plugin architecture for gameplay/behaviour, support for AI-driven NPCs, and integrations for local agent runtimes such as OpenClaw and Claude Code.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository is active with deploy/run instructions, plugin architecture, examples and community interest (141 stars). However it was created ~249 days ago (< 1 year) so there's limited long-term production track record; that age constrains the TRL to at most 6.
prerequisites: basic familiarity with MCP clients or CLI-based agent frameworks
student_project_ideas: Extend or modify a plugin to implement a domain-specific NPC behaviour (for example a logistics NPC that moves resources) and evaluate emergent interactions between human-controlled and AI-controlled agents.

Create an MCP gateway adapter that connects a simple local LLM (or llama.cpp) instance to Alicization Town and measure latency and robustness of in-world actions triggered by natural-language prompts.

tools.name: MrXujiang/ApexForge
tools.desc: 一款开箱即用的AI 3D可视化建模平台，支持扩展和二次开发

cls.summary: ApexForge is an open-source, browser-based AI-driven parametric 3D CAD studio that generates and previews editable Three.js models from natural language prompts.
cls.what_it_does: ApexForge converts natural-language prompts into structured parameter sets and produces interactive, parameterized 3D models rendered in the browser using Three.js. It provides a React-based studio UI, multi-vendor LLM adapters, model import (GLB/GLTF/OBJ/STL), real-time property/texture editing and an agented AI generation harness, making it notable for combining an LLM-driven generation pipeline with a live parametric preview workflow.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository is young (created ~132 days ago) but provides extensive README, demos, multi-page developer docs and an integrated frontend/backend demo; however there is limited evidence of broad real-world adoption or stable releases, so maturity aligns with early alpha/alpha-in-use (TRL 5).
prerequisites: familiarity with Three.js and web development
API keys for supported LLM/model providers to exercise generation
student_project_ideas: Build a course lab where students extend the modelFactory to add a new parameterized mechanical part and expose parameters in the property inspector, then validate geometry export (GLB) for downstream use in a simulation.

Integrate ApexForge with a physics engine (e.g. Ammo.js) to create a simple digital twin demo: generate a vehicle body from prompt, import a driveline model, and run browser-based dynamic scenarios to compare design variants.

tools.name: gromacs/gromacs
tools.desc: The GROMACS molecular simulation toolkit.

tools.name: hirokawaguchi/open-genai
tools.desc: デジタル庁のガバメントAI「源内(GENAI)」を完全ローカル(ローカルLLM/OpenAI互換)で動かす非公式プロジェクト。SAML認証(Keycloak)・RAG(Qdrant)・文字起こし(Whisper)・画像生成(SD)・チーム単位ナレッジをローカル完結。

cls.summary: Open GENAI is an unofficial, self-hosted fork that runs a government-oriented AI platform (GENAI) entirely on local infrastructure, replacing cloud services with local LLM endpoints, SAML/Keycloak auth, RAG search and auxiliary AI apps.
cls.what_it_does: It replaces cloud dependencies of the Digital Agency's GENAI web platform with local components so organisations can run an OpenAI-compatible API, RAG (Qdrant), Whisper transcription, and image generation (Stable Diffusion) inside a closed network. The project is packaged as multiple microservices (FastAPI backends, exApps and a modified frontend) and notable for its multi-tenant / team model, SAML (Keycloak) integration and focus on government/closed-network governance features.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository is active, has multiple releases (v0.13.0) and ~140 stars, showing an organised project with Docker/compose and many components; however it is only ~144 days old so lacks a long track record or broad production references, limiting TRL to Beta (6).
prerequisites: experience deploying Keycloak (SAML) and running local LLM servers (e.g. Ollama, vLLM)
GPU or appropriate hardware for local models (optional for image/LLM workloads)
student_project_ideas: Deploy Open GENAI locally in a lab VM using Ollama (or another OpenAI-compatible local LLM) and Keycloak, then evaluate RAG search accuracy by populating Qdrant with municipal documents and measuring retrieval+generation quality.
Extend the backend to add an automated V&V test suite that exercises SAML authentication flows and model-policy enforcement, producing reproducible test reports for an administrative exApp.

tools.name: CUTEPKQ/NEWTON
tools.desc: NEWTON: Agentic Planning for Physically Grounded Video Generation

cls.summary: NEWTON is a research codebase that wraps a learned planner, physics simulator and generative tools into an agentic loop to produce physically-grounded videos from text prompts.
cls.what_it_does: NEWTON treats video generation as one tool inside a Planner→Executer→Verifier agentic loop: a planner LLM composes simulator runs, keyframe/image tools and a video generator to build rich physics conditioning, and a verifier provides feedback for iterative re-planning. It is used by installing the repo, supplying API keys (LLMs, image/video generators) and running the inference loop; notable features are its explicit physics conditioning (Genesis simulator) and on-policy planner optimisation using Flow-GRPO.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository is ~5 months old (157 days) with a well-documented README, examples and ~140 stars indicating interest, but it lacks evidence of stable releases or broad production adoption; README and roadmap show an inference-time release but training code and long-term deployment evidence are not yet present, so TRL is alpha-in-use.
prerequisites: API keys for LLMs / image / video services
familiarity with LLM tool-calling and basic ML workflows
student_project_ideas: Extend Newton's planner to condition a simple open-source physics simulator (e.g. PyBullet) and evaluate how planner-invoked simulations change generated video consistency on a small physics scenario dataset.

Build a lab exercise where students swap the video generation tool (replace Seedance with an open video-diffusion model) and measure verifier-guided improvements in physical plausibility across iterative planning turns.

tools.name: marcopatzelt/brunnfeld-agentic-world
tools.desc: Medieval village economy simulation — up to 1000 LLM agents across multiple villages, driven by supply chains, hunger, tool degradation and market pressure.

cls.summary: Brunnfeld is an open-source agent-based simulation that runs up to 1000 LLM-driven villagers in a constrained medieval economy with supply chains, spoilage, tool degradation and governance.
cls.what_it_does: Brunnfeld builds a structured world state for each agent every simulated hour, calls an LLM for actions, and deterministically resolves those actions against physics-like rules (hunger, production chains, spoilage, markets). It is used by running the Node.js/TypeScript engine locally (or with an LLM backend) to study emergent economic and social behaviours from many simple agents interacting in a constrained environment.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository is active, well-documented, and runnable with examples (npm start) and has community interest (140 stars), but it is younger than one year (created 243 days ago) so it lacks the multi-year production track record and wide adoption needed for TRL 7+.
prerequisites: familiarity with LLM APIs and environment variables
student_project_ideas: Extend the simulation with a web dashboard that visualises market prices and agent trades over time and deploy it to stream live ticks from the engine (combine with D3 or a web framework).

Modify agent memory or perception rules to test how different information-sharing policies affect market stability, then run comparative experiments and analyse metrics (price volatility, starvation events).

tools.name: artokun/comfyui-mcp-panel
tools.desc: The local-first sidebar AI agent for ComfyUI — runs on your own Claude OR ChatGPT subscription (no API keys, no extra LLM costs). Drives your live graph: edits, workflows & installs in natural language. The panel UI for comfyui-mcp, the agent-native control plane for ComfyUI.

cls.summary: A browser-based sidebar panel that embeds an AI agent to drive and edit ComfyUI graphs using a user's Claude or ChatGPT subscription.
cls.what_it_does: The panel connects to a local comfyui-mcp orchestrator and lets an AI agent add, wire, move and manage nodes on a ComfyUI canvas via natural language, load installer packs and perform autonomous install/restart cycles. It is used as a UI extension inside ComfyUI (JavaScript) and is notable for running on the user's own Claude/ChatGPT subscription (no extra LLM API keys) and for local-first, undoable live-graph edits.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository is ~158 days old with active pushes, 139 stars and documented features, but is younger than one year so lacks long-term production track record required for TRL 7+; README shows a polished UI and integrations but not extensive adoption evidence.
prerequisites: a Claude or ChatGPT subscription on the host machine
student_project_ideas: Build an automated workflow dialog where the agent assembles a ComfyUI graph to perform a specific image preprocessing and augmentation pipeline, then validate the graph's outputs against a ground-truth dataset.

Evaluate and document the agent's decision-making and safety guardrails by creating test prompts that request paid-API actions and measuring whether the panel/orchestrator asks for confirmation before incurring costs.

tools.name: mikjee/warpdrv
tools.desc: Local LLM Server Manager + LlaMA.cpp + Chat

cls.summary: warpdrv is a desktop manager and chat UI for running local LLM servers (llama.cpp builds), downloading models, and proxying OpenAI-compatible requests to local backends.
cls.what_it_does: Warpdrv launches and manages local llama-server instances (custom llama.cpp builds), provides a polished chat interface with features like RAG/embeddings, voice (Whisper/Kokoro) and an OpenAI-compatible proxy, and helps download and organise models from Hugging Face. It is used as a desktop app to run, configure and route requests to local LM backends and to integrate tool calling via a built-in MCP server.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository is ~8 months old and explicitly labelled 'Alpha release' in the README; it has installer artifacts (deb/AppImage/msi) and active development but no long track record or stable 1.0+ releases, so it fits an alpha-in-use TRL.
prerequisites: familiarity with command line and desktop app installation
access to local GGUF models and optionally CUDA/ROCm/Vulkan GPUs
basic knowledge of LLM concepts (models, servers, embeddings)
student_project_ideas: Create a small RAG pipeline for a course dataset by running a local warpdrv-managed llama-server, building embeddings for course documents, and demonstrating question-answering in the desktop chat UI.

Compare inference performance and latency across two local backends (e.g. stock llama.cpp vs a custom ROCm/CUDA build) by using warpdrv to launch servers, run benchmark prompts, and visualise results.

tools.name: sixb-ai/sixb
tools.desc: Open-source TypeScript framework for building operational software used by humans and AI agents.

cls.summary: Sixb is an open-source TypeScript framework for defining an application's domain model (ontology), connecting data sources, and building apps and AI agents that operate against that single model.
cls.what_it_does: Sixb lets you define object types and links in TypeScript, ingest and project rows from external systems into versioned datasets, and write typed actions and workflows that can execute changes back to the sources. It includes a built-in agent, a developer console and React app scaffolding so you can run locally without a database and wire LLMs and connectors into a consistent domain model.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository is actively developed with documentation, examples and a reference app and has modest community interest (138 stars), but it was created ~6 months ago and is on 0.1.x (breaking changes warned), so it demonstrates beta maturity rather than long-term production track record.
prerequisites: familiarity with Bun or Node.js runtimes
basic understanding of web apps and LLM concepts
student_project_ideas: Build a small digital-twin for a laboratory asset: define an ontology, create a sync that ingests simulated sensor data into datasets, and implement a projection and simple dashboard using the Sixb scaffolding.

Create an agent-driven maintenance workflow that reads object state from the model and triggers an action (e.g. create a work order) via a connector, integrating with a mock Postgres backend or external API.

tools.desc: WebGPU fluid simulation using Smoothed Particle Hydrodynamics (SPH) and PIC/FLIP methods.

tools.name: GuiYi-Xi/monoform-previs-studio
tools.desc: Browser-based 3D previs workspace for storyboarding, camera blocking, character posing and keyframes

cls.summary: MONOFORM is a browser-based lightweight 3D previsualization workspace for storyboarding, camera blocking, posing skeletal characters and exporting frames or video.
cls.what_it_does: MONOFORM provides an in-browser scene builder with skeletal characters, camera tools, multi-shot management, keyframe timeline and export to PNG/MP4 or portable JSON; it is used to quickly prototype camera composition, character poses and shot sequences without learning full 3D authoring suites. It is notable for running entirely in the browser (Three.js + React), offering built-in character rigs and a runnable GitHub Pages demo plus optional local AI-assisted scene/pose generation.
cls.trl_rationale: The repository provides a working GitHub Pages demo, complete source, tutorials and an included local launcher; it has attracted modest community attention (138 stars) and recent activity. The project is about 105 days old, so while it is a usable beta with examples, it lacks the longer track record and broad adoption needed for TRL 7+.
prerequisites: optional: Node.js and npm for local development
optional: local Python service and compatible model for AI features
student_project_ideas: Create a short automated shot generator that imports a scene (GLB/GLTF) into MONOFORM and programmatically creates camera keyframes to satisfy basic composition rules, then export to MP4.

Extend MONOFORM to export shot metadata (camera, focal length, timings) into a simple production shot-list CSV and build a small viewer that visualises that shot list alongside the source scene (uses MONOFORM export JSON + a Three.js viewer).

tools.name: k-telux/OpticalModeler
tools.desc: Evidence-gated Agent Skill for reconstructing 2D photonics schematics as physically auditable Blender optical tables with CAD, beam-path, mechanics, and render proof.

cls.summary: OpticalModeler is an open-source Agent Skill that reconstructs 2D photonics schematics and photos into auditable, editable Blender scenes containing optical elements, mounts and provenance evidence.
cls.what_it_does: It converts diagrams, photographs and measurement intents into Blender optical-system scenes that include beam paths, real apertures, mounts and a record of evidence and provenance. The tool is delivered as an Agent Skill (installable via an npx installer or copied into an agent's skills folder) and is notable for tying the visual 3D scene to an auditable evidence trail and component identity rather than producing purely presentational renders.
cls.trl_rationale: The project has an official v2.0.0 release, active development (recent pushes) and a noticeable user interest (138 stars), indicating beyond-prototype maturity; however the repository is only about 4 months old, so it lacks a long-term production track record that would justify TRL 7+.
prerequisites: comfort with Python and agent-skill workflows (npx / Node.js installer)
student_project_ideas: Reconstruct a photographed optical bench in Blender using OpticalModeler, then compare beam-path geometry and component placement against hand-measured coordinates to produce an audit report.
Integrate OpticalModeler output with a simple ray-tracing or Python analysis script to evaluate alignment sensitivity for a detector placement change and produce a verified recommendation.

tools.name: AI4Science-WestlakeU/RealPDEBench
tools.desc: [🔥ICLR26 Oral] RealPDEBench: A Benchmark for Complex Physical Systems with Paired Real-World and Simulated Data

tools.name: winchxyz/moon-rover
tools.desc: A 3D lunar rover survey game. WebGL2, no build step, no third-party assets - every texture and sound generated at runtime.

cls.summary: Regolith is a browser-based, single-page 3D lunar-rover survey game that generates all textures, geometry and sounds at runtime and runs with WebGL2 and three.js without a build step.
cls.what_it_does: The project provides an interactive lunar-rover simulation and exploration game you can run in a modern browser; it procedurally generates terrain, rocks, textures, starfields and sounds at load time and implements driving physics, a two-link IK sampling arm, and a ground-penetrating radar sweep. It is used by opening the static site (or running the bundled node server) and playing; notable points are zero runtime asset downloads, minimal size (~380 KB gzipped) and a no-build, no-dependencies delivery model (vendored three.js only).
cls.trl_rationale: The repository is a playable, published static site with a v1.0 demo, a complete codebase and a modest community (137 stars), indicating a beta-quality project; it is younger than one year (created ~98 days ago) so TRL is capped at 6 despite being functional and demonstrable.
prerequisites: modern browser supporting import maps and WebGL2
student_project_ideas: Modify or instrument the ground-penetrating radar code to log detection range and false positives, then run controlled experiments to compare how terrain parameters affect detection performance.

Extend the rover's control code to add a simple autonomous waypoint-following or path-planning routine (A* or RRT) using the existing terrain heightfield and record telemetry for a basic navigation performance study.

tools.name: LucasHJin/react-video-ascii
tools.desc: Video to ASCII React component.

cls.summary: A React component that renders videos or images as ASCII art in the browser using WebGL2.
cls.what_it_does: This library samples video or image media and renders a character-based ASCII representation on a canvas using WebGL2 shaders and a glyph atlas. It is used as a drop-in React component (npm package) and supports options for character sets, effects (mouse, click, reveal), color/brightness controls and passing preloaded HTML media elements.
cls.trl_rationale: The repository provides an npm package, a live demo, detailed API docs and recent activity, indicating a beta-quality library; however it is under 1 year old so there is limited track record in production deployments.
student_project_ideas: Build a small web dashboard that streams a webcam or camera feed and displays it as ASCII with interactive mouse and click effects, adding a control panel to vary character sets and DPR.
Integrate the component with a simple sensor-demo (e.g. Raspberry Pi video stream forwarded to a web app) and measure/perceptually evaluate readability at different resolutions and character sets.

tools.name: HeyPuter/blender-wasm
tools.desc: 🧊 Blender in the Browser

cls.summary: This project builds and runs the Blender 3D content-creation application inside a web browser using WebAssembly.
cls.what_it_does: It compiles Blender to WebAssembly so users can run Blender in-browser without installing the native application; the repository provides build targets and a demo web server to run the result locally. This is notable because it enables lightweight, platform-independent access to a full-featured 3D modelling and visualization tool from the browser.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository is 140 days old with an active demo, build instructions and community interest (137 stars), but it is still recent (<1 year) so it fits a beta maturity rather than long-term production-proof; README is minimal which also limits demonstrated maturity.
prerequisites: WebAssembly build toolchain (Emscripten or equivalent) implied by wasm target
student_project_ideas: Create a lightweight browser-based digital-twin viewer by exporting a Blender scene to glTF and integrating the wasm-built Blender demo with a three.js viewer to allow online model inspection and simple edits.

Develop a browser-based asset-creation workflow where students model parts in the in-browser Blender, export parametric assets, and run automated checks (e.g. simple clearance or mass property calculations) in a small web pipeline.

tools.name: frankchu91/mindbase-llm-wiki
tools.desc: Karpathy's LLM Wiki idea as a product — an AI that builds and maintains a markdown wiki from your notes and sources. MCP server + web UI, runs on free local models (Ollama), no API key needed. MIT.

cls.summary: MindBase is an open-source local-first LLM-powered system that builds and maintains a markdown wiki from your notes and sources, using a MCP server and web UI without requiring cloud API keys.
cls.what_it_does: MindBase ingests documents, synthesises and cross-references them with a local LLM, and writes a persistent markdown wiki on disk that you can review and approve; it provides operations to ingest, build, and lint the wiki and a browser UI for interaction. It is notable for running on free local models (Ollama by default), exposing an MCP server so editor/agent clients can call its tools, and emphasising human approval and auditability (plain markdown files you can git/grep).
cls.trl_rationale: Repository is active, has releases, substantial stars and integrations, and the README documents a working product and install paths, which supports a beta-level maturity; however the repo is ~205 days old (<1 year) so there's not yet a long track record required for TRL 7+.
prerequisites: optional: local LLM runtime like Ollama for best local experience
student_project_ideas: Integrate MindBase with a course reading list to build a class 'knowledge base' that ingests papers and produces a collaboratively maintained syllabus and FAQ, then evaluate how well the wiki supports student queries compared to a RAG pipeline.

Extend MindBase to export structured metadata (e.g. BibTeX tags, topic labels) and build a visualization dashboard (using D3 or three.js) showing concept link graphs and citation networks derived from the wiki.

tools.name: ruashots/open-h3-ir
tools.desc: Open-source local implementation of MiniMax H3 Context-IR. Turn simple prompts into structured, validated H3 video briefs.

cls.summary: OpenH3-IR is a local compiler that turns plain-language prompts into the structured Context-IR briefs required by the MiniMax H3 video model so prompts produce more directed, consistent video.
cls.what_it_does: OpenH3-IR accepts a single prose prompt and produces a validated, sectioned Context-IR document (named reference images, timed cuts on legal frame grids, and other structured fields) that MiniMax H3 expects. It runs as a CLI tool, an HTTP service, or inside ComfyUI and connects to any OpenAI-compatible language+vision endpoint you already run (Ollama, vLLM, llama.cpp, LM Studio, or hosted APIs). The project is notable because it implements the missing "Context-IR" stage locally, removing the need to call MiniMax's hosted service and offering a dial to control how strongly the compiler interprets and transforms prompts.
cls.trl_rationale: The repository provides an installable Python package, a CLI, HTTP service and ComfyUI integration, and has community interest (stars/forks). It was created ~97 days ago and the README warns the project is young and changing, so while it appears usable (beta) it lacks long-term production track record required for higher TRL.
prerequisites: An OpenAI-compatible LLM endpoint (Ollama, vLLM, llama.cpp server, LM Studio or hosted API)
Familiarity with prompt engineering and basic CLI usage
student_project_ideas: Compare outputs of MiniMax H3 with and without OpenH3-IR by building an experiment script that compiles prompts, generates video with fixed seeds, and measures qualitative consistency across runs.

Integrate OpenH3-IR into a ComfyUI workflow to build a GUI tool that allows users to edit the compiled Context-IR (timings, shot labels, intensity dial) and observe its effect on generated video clips.

tools.name: AbrahamPaulJ/facefusion-mobile
tools.desc: FaceFusion for Android. Offline face swap running on the phone's NPU, GPU or CPU. Qualcomm Hexagon (v68 to v81), Vulkan fallback, no server and no upload.

cls.summary: An Android app that performs offline face swaps and optional face animation/lip-sync entirely on-device using the phone's NPU, GPU or CPU.
cls.what_it_does: FaceFusion Mobile runs neural networks on Android phones (preferentially on Qualcomm Hexagon NPUs, with GPU/CPU fallbacks) to swap faces in photos and video and to provide live preview/recording, lip-sync and face-editing features. It is used as a mobile application (Kotlin / Jetpack Compose) and notable for running fully offline on-device and offering NPU acceleration and a live preview mode.
cls.trl_rationale: The project demonstrates a working, performance-measured Android app with many features and active commits and stars, but the repository is only 86 days old (under the 90-day cutoff) so maturity is limited to early alpha/alpha-in-use rather than long-term production evidence.
prerequisites: familiarity with mobile ML frameworks (ncnn) and native build tooling
knowledge of Vulkan/Qualcomm Hexagon or general mobile acceleration concepts
student_project_ideas: Measure and compare performance and energy consumption of the face-swap pipeline across several Android phones (with and without Hexagon NPU) and produce a report explaining trade-offs and bottlenecks.
Integrate the live swap preview into a small user study app to evaluate perceived realism and latency, and correlate results with model choice (hyperswap 1a/1b/1c) and frame resolution.

tools.name: Fratres-X-AI/JamBoy
tools.desc: GPS-denied drone navigation layer: optical flow + offline map geo-match + EKF → MAVLink (sim-validated).

cls.summary: JamBoy is an open-source GPS-denied navigation layer for small drones that fuses optical-flow, map-based geo-matching and a 6-state EKF to produce MAVLink position estimates.
cls.what_it_does: JamBoy takes a downward camera stream, IMU rates, barometer altitude and preloaded GeoTIFF maps to estimate local position and velocity without GPS by combining Lucas–Kanade optical flow, feature-based map homography matching (ORB / optional SIFT) and a 6-state EKF. It outputs MAVLink vision-position messages and includes a simulator gate used in CI; optional GPU acceleration (CuPy) and hardware deployment notes are provided. The project is notable for focusing on GPS-denied map-match fusion and providing a runnable sim-validated stack with MAVLink bridging and hardware checklists.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository is 122 days old (younger than one year) so TRL is capped; the README and CI 'sim gate', example scripts, hardware checklists, and 137 stars indicate an active beta-quality project that runs simulations and has examples, supporting a TRL 6 (beta) judgement.
prerequisites: Linux recommended for full feature set (rasterio/GDAL)
optional CUDA setup for GPU backend
student_project_ideas: Evaluate and tune the 6-state EKF and innovation gating on recorded simulated flights, then compare position error with and without map geo-matching (use PX4 SITL and JamBoy's MAVLink bridge).

Adapt JamBoy's geo-match module to a campus-scale GeoTIFF and test robustness of ORB vs SIFT matches across different altitudes and lighting conditions, reporting detection rates and homography quality.
