tools.desc: open-source ontology platform for operational digital twins

tools.name: Anixapp-Community/anixapp
tools.desc: Быстрый клиент AnixApp для просмотра аниме на базе Anixart API. Anixart на пк

cls.summary: AnixApp is a cross‑platform desktop and Android client for browsing and watching anime using the Anixart API, with built‑in HLS playback, downloads and WebGPU-based Anime4K upscaling.
cls.what_it_does: AnixApp connects to the Anixart API to present release feeds, release pages, user profiles, collections and search, and provides an HLS video player with multiple sources, parallel downloads and FFmpeg-based segment merging. It also offers real‑time image/video upscaling using anime4k-webgpu and features like Discord Rich Presence and synchronous watch‑together rooms.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository is active with cross‑platform builds, multiple features and a beta warning; it demonstrates a working application and distribution artifacts but is under 1 year old (created 2026-03-16) so there is limited long‑term production track record.
prerequisites: FFmpeg (optional, used for merging HLS segments)

tools.name: Leonxlnx/napali
tools.desc: A drone flight over the Na Pali coast, rendered entirely in code. No textures, images or models.

cls.summary: A single-file WebGL2 demo that procedurally renders a drone flight over the Na Pali coast using GLSL shaders and a small JavaScript harness.
cls.what_it_does: Napali procedurally generates terrain, ocean, vegetation, sky and lighting entirely in GLSL and runs the result in a single index.html. It is used as a real-time demo and includes Node-based tools to drive headless Chrome + ffmpeg for high-quality stills and video renders. The project is notable for producing a complex scenic render without external assets and for its shader-driven, self-contained workflow.
cls.trl_rationale: The repo is very new (created 25 days ago) so it cannot demonstrate a long track record; it runs as a polished demo with tooling for video renders and a thorough README, which suggests early-alpha maturity rather than broader production use.
prerequisites: WebGL2-capable GPU and browser (recent Chrome recommended)
Node 22+ and ffmpeg for the provided rendering tools
student_project_ideas: Modify the GLSL terrain and erosion passes to explore how parameter changes affect coastline formation and produce a short video comparing the variants using tools/video.mjs.
Use the shader code as a starting point to implement a runtime UI that exposes more terrain-generation knobs and records parametric variations for a visualisation study.

tools.name: BradyAJohnston/nodebpy
tools.desc: Build node trees in Blender more elegantly with code

tools.name: kkakkkka/awesome-code-as-x
tools.desc: A Curated List of Coding-agent that treat a program as the executable intermediate representation for Policy, World, Editor and beyond

cls.summary: A curated, up-to-date list of papers and projects about 'code-as-X' coding agents that produce executable programs as policies, world models or edit graphs for simulation, robotics and scene generation.
cls.what_it_does: This repository collects papers, benchmarks and projects where agents write or edit executable programs (policy code, scene/world programs, edit graphs) that are run by simulators, renderers or robots. It's used as a literature and project index to discover approaches, benchmarks and example systems that connect LLM/VLM agents to simulators and robotics stacks.
cls.trl_rationale: The repository is a curated literature and projects list with healthy interest (stars) but is only 65 days old, so it lacks a long track record; this supports an early-alpha TRL rather than a mature tooling TRL.
prerequisites: familiarity with large language models and VLM concepts
basic knowledge of robotics or simulation environments (Blender, MuJoCo, USD) and coding
student_project_ideas: Write a short review paper or poster comparing 3 'code-as-policy' papers from the list, highlighting differences in program representation, execution environment (simulator or robot), and evaluation methodology.

Implement a minimal code-as-policy prototype using an LLM to generate high-level robot commands and execute them in a simulator (e.g., MuJoCo or PyBullet), using papers and benchmarks from the list as guidance.

tools.name: xgxgnpu/Physics-informed-vibe-coding
tools.desc: The first open-source repository for Scientific Machine Learning (PINNs, PIELM, RFM, Neural Operators) via Vibe Coding. JAX-GPU implementations with Chinese tutorials. 首个采用 Vibe Coding 进行科学机器学习研究的开源仓库。

cls.summary: A JAX-based collection of reproducible physics-informed machine learning (PINNs, PIELM, random feature methods, neural operators) examples and tutorials for solving PDEs and related research problems.
cls.what_it_does: This repository provides end-to-end JAX GPU implementations of multiple scientific machine learning algorithms (PINNs, PIELM, random feature methods, neural operators) with runnable case scripts, saved checkpoints and Chinese tutorials. It is used to reproduce experiments, compare algorithms on PDE problems, and study training strategies and adaptive weighting methods for physics-informed models.
cls.trl_rationale: The repo (created 2026-03-14, ~8 months old) provides many runnable, self-contained JAX GPU case scripts, saved checkpoints, and tutorials which indicate a beta-level, reproducible codebase; however it is younger than one year and lacks evidence of broad production adoption, so TRL is limited to 6.
prerequisites: JAX (jax, jaxlib) with CUDA GPU support
familiarity with PDEs and ML concepts
student_project_ideas: Compare NTK-PINN and RFM implementations from the repo on a 1D/2D PDE (e.g. Burgers or heat equation) to evaluate training stability and solution accuracy, and produce a report with reproducible experiments and visualisations.

Extend one case (e.g. MultiScale-PINN) to incorporate experimental or synthetic noisy data and quantify robustness to measurement noise, combining the repo code with a data generation script and standard metrics.

tools.name: chisomobanzi/Serpentine3D
tools.desc: Open-source NURBS surface modeller — a Rhino-style freeform modeller on the OpenCASCADE kernel, with AI-native MCP integration

cls.summary: Serpentine3D is an open-source NURBS-based freeform CAD modeller (Rhino-like) built on OpenCASCADE with scripting, file import/export and an AI-driven assistant.
cls.what_it_does: Serpentine3D provides exact NURBS curves, surfaces and solids (not meshes) for creating, editing and exporting engineering geometry; it runs as a desktop app on Linux/Windows/macOS or headless for scripting/batch use. It notabley speaks Rhino-style commands and aliases, supports STEP/3DM/OBJ/GLTF/USD and can be driven by an AI assistant or MCP clients to automate modelling tasks.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository is very recent (created 125 days ago) so it cannot claim long-term production track record; however the project publishes installers/releases, documentation, tests and example use which indicate early adopters and usable builds, consistent with TRL 5 (alpha in use).
prerequisites: familiarity with NURBS / Rhino-like CAD concepts
student_project_ideas: Create a parametric furniture component with Serpentine3D scripting that exports STEP for CNC machining and generates 2D drawing sheets (PDF) for fabrication.

Integrate the assistant/MCP to implement an automated modelling workflow: feed natural-language change requests and verify results programmatically, comparing geometric checks (curvature, draft) before exporting.

tools.name: anviod/edgeCore
tools.desc: EdgeCore is the core runtime of EdgeOS industrial edge platform. 部署于工业现场，支持Modbus、BACnet、OPC-UA、S7、EtherNet等协议接入，通过MQTT、OPC-UA Server、Sparkplug-B连接云端，实现工业数据采集、边缘计算与智能协同(MCP Server)。

cls.summary: edgeCore is an open-source industrial edge gateway written in Go that collects OT device data via many industrial protocols, performs local edge computation and forwards data to cloud/SCADA using MQTT, OPC UA, Sparkplug-B and similar interfaces.
cls.what_it_does: edgeCore provides a lightweight runtime for industrial edge deployments, unifying southbound protocol access (Modbus, S7, BACnet, OPC-UA, etc.), local rule-based processing and northbound connectors (MQTT, Sparkplug-B, OPC UA Server). It is used as a single binary deployment on edge hardware (x86/ARM), with built-in scheduling, device discovery and a UI served by the backend, and notable for its broad protocol support and industrial SLA claims.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository is 264 days old (younger than one year) so TRL is limited to beta-level; however it has substantial documentation, multi-protocol drivers, CI/packaging notes and active commits and stars, which supports a TRL 6 (beta) assessment rather than an early prototype.
prerequisites: familiarity with industrial protocols (Modbus, OPC-UA, MQTT)
Go toolchain for builds and plugins
student_project_ideas: Deploy edgeCore on a Raspberry Pi to collect Modbus TCP data from a PLC simulator and forward it to an MQTT broker, then build a dashboard in Node-RED to visualise and alarm on the data.

Extend or implement a simple driver for a less-common OT protocol (or a simulated sensor) in edgeCore and evaluate end-to-end latency and reliability under load, comparing local rule processing vs cloud processing.

tools.name: lawrence3699/jev-style
tools.desc: JevStyle: local decision models for AI agents. Classify, route and score with a probability per option. systemone-compatible local server, MCP tools, Claude Code guard. Open weights, Apache-2.0.

cls.summary: Jev-Style provides small, local decision models and a toolkit that return calibrated probabilities for multiple-choice, yes/no and rating questions to route or gate agent actions without sending data to an external API.
cls.what_it_does: Jev-Style offers compact decision models (0.8B and 2B variants) and a server/CLI so you can run classification, routing and decision-scoring on your laptop or local server; inputs can include text, JSON and (with the 2B build) images. It is notable for returning calibrated probability distributions for each option in a single forward pass, providing agent skills, an MCP-compatible server and integrations (Claude Code guard) to let agents gate or route calls locally without a cloud API key.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository is very new (created 53 days ago) but supplies runnable models, Hugging Face spaces, an MCP server and CLI; these indicate early real use beyond a paper prototype but not a long production track record, so TRL ~5 (alpha in use).
prerequisites: familiarity with local LLM backends (PyTorch or MLX) and virtual environments
basic knowledge of agent tooling / MCP concepts
student_project_ideas: Build an agent that routes customer support tickets: use Jev-Style locally to classify/ticket-route inputs and compare performance and human-in-the-loop fallback thresholds against an LLM-based router (e.g. using a small fine-tuned classifier vs Jev-Style probabilities).

Integrate Jev-Style as a tool-call guard for an autonomous agent: implement a Claude Code or LangChain agent that only executes potentially risky tool calls when the local Jev-Style model reports probability above configurable confidence, and evaluate safety/false-block rates on synthetic test sets.

tools.name: YIKUAIBANZI/forge-skill
tools.desc: 人格蒸馏引擎 · 蒸馏自己看清自己，蒸馏亲友留住余温与回声 · Claude Code Skill

cls.summary: Forge Skill is a local-first Claude Code 'persona distillation' skill that extracts and structures someone's speaking style and behaviour (including yourself) from chat logs, diaries and guided prompts so Claude can act or reason in that person's tone.
cls.what_it_does: Forge ingests conversational data (chat exports, diaries, notes) and runs local distillation to produce structured persona profiles; those profiles are then used by Claude Code skills to run multi‑variant 'self' decision meetings or to speak in a distilled other‑person's voice. It is notable for providing local‑first tooling (parsers, JSON persona schema, validators and runtime loaders) packaged as Claude Code skills rather than a cloud service.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository has a clear README, installation instructions, multiple example workflows, parsers and tooling and 135 stars, indicating early adopters; it was created 227 days ago (under one year), so while it appears beta with working features, the age prevents assigning TRL >6 and there is no evidence of organisational production deployments.
prerequisites: Claude Code (Anthropic) runtime or compatible Claude Code client
basic familiarity with command line and chat export formats (WeChat/.txt/.html)
student_project_ideas: Build an evaluation study that imports anonymised chat logs, uses Forge to create persona profiles, and compares the persona outputs against human annotations for style and typical responses.

Integrate Forge's persona JSON output with a simple decision‑support web UI (Flask) to let users run 'use-self' multi‑agent decision meetings on realistic case studies and log differences in suggested actions.

tools.name: 0xProbabillity/house-control-android
tools.desc: House Control on Android phones and tablets: your home as a live 3D model — lights, ACs and scenes via Smart Life, Home Assistant and Philips Hue. No Mac needed.

cls.summary: An open-source Android app that shows your home as an interactive live 3D model and controls lights, air-conditioners and scenes via Smart Life (Tuya), Home Assistant and Philips Hue.
cls.what_it_does: House Control renders a floor plan as an interactive 3D model on Android devices and lets users control lamps, air conditioners and scenes by linking 3D items to real devices. It connects to Smart Life (Tuya), Home Assistant and Philips Hue, offers a finger-friendly floor-plan editor and widgets, and simulates devices when none are connected so the UI and flows can be tried offline.
cls.trl_rationale: The project is a working Android app with downloadable APK releases, device integrations and several hundred stars indicating user interest, but the repository is very new (created 26 days ago) so it lacks the longer track record and mature release history required for TRL 6+.
prerequisites: Access to a Home Assistant server / Philips Hue Bridge or Smart Life account to test real integrations
Basic understanding of networking on local Wi‑Fi
student_project_ideas: Extend the app to log device telemetry to a time-series backend (InfluxDB or Prometheus) and build a small dashboard to visualise energy or temperature trends for a digital-twin lab exercise.

Create an experimental interface that maps simple occupancy sensor data to automated scene changes in the 3D model and evaluate usability and latency using a local Home Assistant instance and cheap Wi‑Fi sensors.

tools.name: mohammadijoo/Control_Robotics_Lab
tools.desc: This repository includes codes for comprehensive tutorials in Control / Robotics Engineering. The link of YouTube video tutorials are mentioned in description.

tools.name: NPGameDev/godot-mcp-toolkit
tools.desc: A Godot 4.2+ editor plugin that lets AI coding assistants work inside the editor over the Model Context Protocol. Consolidated tools cover 150+ operations across scenes, scripts, nodes, and playtests, and a GDScript extension API lets any project add its own tools. Pairs with the godot-mcp-server npm bridge; runs locally.

cls.summary: A Godot 4.2+ editor plugin that exposes many editor operations over the Model Context Protocol so AI assistants can inspect and modify scenes, scripts and run playtests from the editor locally.
cls.what_it_does: The toolkit turns the Godot editor into an MCP server, exposing 150+ operations (grouped into up to 113 tools) so MCP-capable AI assistants can create nodes, edit scripts, run playtests and inspect runtime state inside the editor. It is installed as a Godot addon and pairs with a small npm bridge package that the assistant talks to; projects can extend the toolkit via a GDScript extension API to add custom tools.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository is ~7 months old with active pushes, README, architecture docs and a companion npm bridge; it has users and releases but is younger than one year so lacks the multi-year track record needed for TRL7+. Evidence: creation date, activity, 135 stars and explicit release/install instructions in README.
prerequisites: familiarity with GDScript and basic MCP concepts
student_project_ideas: Create a GDScript extension that registers custom MCP tools to automate building a parameterised scene (e.g. procedurally place assets) and evaluate the assistant-driven workflow in a lab assignment.

Build an automated playtest pipeline where an MCP assistant runs playtests, collects runtime state and produces a test-reporting dashboard (combine the toolkit with a simple Node.js server to ingest results).

tools.name: ArtificialAnalysis/aa-agentperf-local
tools.desc: Benchmark local LLM serving by replaying real agent trajectories

cls.summary: A tool to measure throughput and latency when replaying recorded AI agent conversations against local OpenAI-compatible model servers.
cls.what_it_does: agentperf-local replays recorded agent trajectories against a local or managed model server to report throughput and latency (it reproduces a real agent's conversational context per request). It can benchmark an already-running server or download a pinned model, start the server (via supported frameworks) and run a managed benchmark; results focus on performance, not output quality.
cls.trl_rationale: The README and recipes show a fully implemented tool with installation paths, multiple supported frameworks and pinned recipes, and it has community interest (134 stars) but the repository is only 52 days old, so it lacks the multi-release, long-term production track record required for TRL 6+.
prerequisites: access to a local OpenAI-compatible model server (llama.cpp, vLLM, SGLang, Splash, Ollama, etc.)
on Windows: NVIDIA GPU and llama.cpp for managed runs
student_project_ideas: Compare latency and throughput of two model serving stacks (e.g., llama.cpp vs vLLM) on the same hardware using agentperf-local and analyse trade-offs in context window size and batching.

Integrate agentperf-local into a CI pipeline to automatically benchmark performance regressions for a model-serving deployment and produce automated reporting dashboards (combine with a time-series DB or simple CSV + plotting).

tools.name: hh-hang/vid3d-projection
tools.desc: A 3D video projection library for Three.js and CesiumJS

tools.name: Argona7/stampede
tools.desc: STAMPEDE — read-only explorer of observed wallet rotations on Robinhood Chain

cls.summary: STAMPEDE is a read-only explorer that detects and visualises observed wallet 'rotations' (sell A → buy B) on Robinhood Chain and provides live/replay views, ranked boards, flow diagrams and a spatial map with transaction evidence.
cls.what_it_does: STAMPEDE ingests Robinhood Chain trade and transfer events, finds sequences where the same address sold one coin and bought another within a chosen time window, grades those sequences (direct/clean/ambiguous) and exposes the results via a FastAPI backend plus terminal and web visualisations. It is notable for shipping a recorded sample demo (no API keys required) and multiple coordinated views (terminal feed, RADAR, FLOW, MAP) that always link back to the on-chain transactions.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository is young (created 67 days ago) so maturity is limited; it does include a v0.1.0 release, a recorded sample dataset and runnable demo instructions, indicating early alpha/alpha-in-use stage rather than production.
prerequisites: basic Python (uv tool used to install Python 3.13)
student_project_ideas: Extend STAMPEDE to ingest another EVM-compatible chain (e.g. Ethereum testnet) and compare rotation patterns between chains using the existing visualisation pipeline.

Build a simple anomaly detector that flags unusual rotation patterns (high velocity, many distinct wallets) by exporting STAMPEDE's API feed into a time-series analysis notebook and applying clustering or threshold rules.

tools.name: TypeDreamMoon/DreamShader
tools.desc: Unreal Engine Material DSL. Use Dream Shader Lang Write Unreal Material. Simple · Fast · Full syntax · HLSL GLSL Lang Support

cls.summary: DreamShader is an Unreal Engine plugin and domain-specific language that compiles text-based shader source files into Unreal Material, Material Function and Material Layer assets.
cls.what_it_does: DreamShader provides a text-first DSL for authoring Unreal materials (.dsm/.dsf/.dsh etc.) and compiles those sources into UMaterial, UMaterialFunction and material layer assets inside the Unreal Editor. It is used as a plugin you add to an Unreal project so materials are authored as source files and either generated in memory or materialised into uassets; it notably supports both HLSL- and GLSL-shaped syntaxes and includes tooling for migration and auto-compile on save.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository is active with documentation, examples and regular commits and has modest community interest (134 stars), but it was created ~210 days ago (under 1 year) so lacks a longer track record; evidence supports a Beta-level maturity (versioned docs, examples, plugin integration) rather than long-term production adoption.
student_project_ideas: Create a small UE project that replaces several Material Editor graphs with DreamShader source files to demonstrate reproducible material pipelines and version-controlled asset generation.

Implement a custom PBR material using DreamShader that reads runtime parameters from an Unreal actor (or via a simple IoT/MQTT feed) to explore material-driven digital-twin visualisation in a real-time scene.

tools.name: 1homsi/thehumanbox
tools.desc: Civilization sandbox in your browser. Tribes invent their own languages, cultures and wars, from the stone age to computers. Built in Rust and WebAssembly, runs entirely on your device.

cls.summary: The Human Box is an open-source, browser-based agent‑based civilization simulation written in Rust and compiled to WebAssembly where autonomous agents create languages, economies and societies across many eras.
cls.what_it_does: It simulates thousands of autonomous agents on a large tile world so emergent cultures, economies, technologies and conflicts arise without central scripting; the engine runs in Rust compiled to WebAssembly and is viewed through a React/WebGL frontend. Notable features are a deterministic headless mode for batch runs, a desktop Electron wrapper, and extensive docs describing architecture and how to extend actions and behaviours.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository is active and provides a playable browser build, desktop installers, documentation and a headless mode, indicating beyond prototype status; however it is under one year old (created ~194 days ago) so lacks the multi-year track record and broad adoption needed for TRL7+.
prerequisites: basic familiarity with WebAssembly, WebGL and React for frontend work
student_project_ideas: Compare emergent metrics (population, wealth distribution, conflict frequency) under different environmental parameter sets by running deterministic headless sweeps and analysing results with Python (pandas/matplotlib).

Extend the simulation with a new action category (e.g. energy production or automated transport) implemented in the sim-core crate and evaluate its impact on technology diffusion and economy across eras.

tools.name: ChrisChen667788/pixcull
tools.desc: Local-first AI photo culling for professional photographers — 6-axis rubric, XMP/IPTC export, Lightroom & Capture One ready.

cls.summary: PixCull is an open-source, local-first AI tool that automatically sorts and scores photographic shoots into keep/maybe/cull and writes human-readable reasons, while exporting XMP/IPTC metadata for Lightroom and Capture One.
cls.what_it_does: PixCull analyses RAW and other photo files on the user's machine and scores each frame on six rubric axes to decide keep/maybe/cull; it generates a sentence explaining the reason and can export results as XMP/IPTC for integration with Lightroom and Capture One. It runs locally (on-device AI) and uses vision models and heuristics to produce reproducible culls and taste-profile personalisation for photographers.
cls.trl_rationale: The project shows many releases, detailed changelog entries and tests, an active commit history and ~134 stars, indicating a beta-level, installable tool; the repository is ~6 months old so it lacks the multi-year production track record needed for TRL 7+.
prerequisites: PyTorch / on-device ML runtime (Apple Silicon support noted)
familiarity with RAW files and photo metadata (XMP/IPTC)

tools.name: lokutor-ai/oido
tools.desc: Oído: open-vocabulary speech recognition on a $5 ESP32-S3, faster than real time. No cloud, no NPU. English + Spanish.

cls.summary: Oído is an open-source on-device speech-to-text engine that runs streaming English and Spanish ASR in real time on an ESP32‑S3 microcontroller without cloud or neural accelerators.
cls.what_it_does: Oído performs automatic speech recognition on very constrained hardware (ESP32‑S3), using highly quantized models and a C engine that can also be compiled to WebAssembly. It's used to transcribe streaming or utterance audio on-device with low latency and is notable for achieving faster‑than‑real‑time inference on a single 240 MHz core of an ESP32‑S3.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository is very new (48 days) so it lacks a long track record; however the README shows working on‑board measurements, WebAssembly demo and published models which indicate early adopters and functioning alpha-level usage rather than a paper prototype.
prerequisites: ESP32‑S3 development board (8 MB PSRAM, 16 MB flash recommended)
ESP‑IDF build environment and cross toolchain (Xtensa)
C toolchain and familiarity with flashing microcontrollers
student_project_ideas: Build a voice-controlled data-logger: integrate Oído on an ESP32‑S3 to transcribe spoken commands that trigger sensor readings and publish results via MQTT to a time-series database for dashboarding.

Compare on-device ASR performance and energy use: run the provided int8 vs int4 models on hardware to measure latency, word error rate and power consumption, and produce recommendations for low-power voice agents.

tools.name: jsogn/Glint
tools.desc: 面向中文母语者的 macOS 英语学习工具，可切换其他目标语言：读取中文拼音输入法的当前高亮候选，在候选栏旁显示对应译文。

cls.summary: Glint is a macOS app for Chinese-native users that shows translations next to pinyin input candidates so you can see target-language text without interrupting typing.
cls.what_it_does: Glint reads the currently highlighted candidate from Chinese pinyin input methods and displays a nearby translation in the candidate area without replacing the input. It runs translation and dictionary lookup on-device (with optional local models like OPUS‑MT/MLX) and supports insertion and speech playback while emphasising privacy and minimal interruption.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository is very new (created 28 days ago) but already includes installable releases and Homebrew packaging which indicates early adopters; age limits TRL to at most 5 despite a polished README and packages.
prerequisites: Xcode 26 and XcodeGen (for building from source)
familiarity with Homebrew for recommended install
student_project_ideas: Evaluate and compare on-device translation quality and latency by switching Glint between system translation, OPUS‑MT and MLX models and reporting trade-offs in accuracy and performance.

Integrate a simple logging-only extension (respecting privacy constraints) to measure candidate-to-translation latency and visual usability, then propose UI improvements for real-time inline translation in input contexts.

tools.name: KalarisLabs/research-agent-skills
tools.desc: Turn any AI agent into a research co-scientist: 280+ open-source agent skills for literature reviews, hypotheses, experimental design, data analysis, paper writing, citation verification and peer review. Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Gemini CLI and any Agent Skills harness. npx skills add KalarisLabs/research-agent-skills

cls.summary: A collection of 280+ open-source 'agent skills' that let AI agents perform research tasks such as literature review, experiment design, data analysis, writing and citation checks.
cls.what_it_does: This repository provides a modular catalog of agent skills (each a small playbook and scripts) that an AI agent can load to perform stages of scientific research—from hypothesis generation and systematic literature review to analysis and manuscript preparation. It is used by installing the skill pack into an Agent Skills-compatible harness (via npx or embedding the skill URL) and is notable for its large, curated skill set, interactive catalog and automated scanning/benchmarks for reproducibility and safety.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository is active (created 133 days ago) with 134 stars, an interactive catalog, documentation and CI/scans; these indicate an organised beta-stage project but it is younger than one year so lacks a long track record for TRL 7+. README provides benchmark claims but not long-running production adoption evidence.
prerequisites: familiarity with Agent Skills harnesses / npx
basic Python knowledge for some skill scripts
student_project_ideas: Create a reproducible pipeline that uses the literature-review and citation-verification skills to assemble and validate a dataset of papers on a chosen engineering topic, then produce a short systematic-review report.

Integrate an experimental-design skill with a Jupyter-based data analysis workflow (e.g. using scanpy or PyTorch Lightning skills) to run and document a small simulation study, demonstrating reproducibility checks and automated reporting.

tools.name: SyntheticAutonomicMind/SAM
tools.desc: Synthetic Autonomic Mind - An AI assistant for everyone.

tools.name: Sandermage/sndr_core_engine
tools.desc: SNDR Core Engine (Genesis) — vLLM runtime patch-overlay for Qwen3.6 + Gemma4 on consumer NVIDIA (Ampere sm_86, 2× A5000/3090). Qwen3.6-35B-A3B FP8 ~240 tok/s, 27B-int4 hybrid GDN+Mamba, Gemma4 26B/31B AWQ, 256K ctx. 321 patches: TurboQuant k8v4 KV, MTP/DFlash spec-decode, FULL cudagraph, hybrid GDN. vLLM pin dev424 + Control Center GUI.

cls.summary: SNDR Core Engine is a vLLM runtime patch-overlay that enables fast, quantized inference of large open LLMs (Qwen3.6, Gemma4 families) on consumer NVIDIA GPUs and provides a control GUI and persistent neural-memory features.
cls.what_it_does: It applies in-memory runtime patches to vLLM to improve token throughput, enable robust quantized tool-calling, speculative decoding and very long contexts on 24 GB-class NVIDIA GPUs, and ships a CLI + Control Center GUI and a persistent neural-graph memory for tool/agent workflows. It is used by installing via a provided script, then running the sndr CLI to detect the GPU, download supported weights and launch a local server; notable aspects are family-tuned low-level optimizations (TurboQuant KV, hybrid GDN, spec-decode) and support for long (up to ~280K) contexts on consumer hardware.
cls.trl_rationale: The project is actively developed, provides install scripts, a GUI, benchmark docs and a patch registry, and has community interest (133 stars). The repo is 214 days old (<1 year) so it lacks the multi-year production track record required for TRL 7+, but shows beta-level maturity and reproducible tooling.
prerequisites: Linux host with CUDA-capable NVIDIA GPU (24 GiB class recommended)
Familiarity with local LLM concepts and model weights
student_project_ideas: Build a local agent that uses SNDR Core to host a Qwen3.6 model and integrate it with a small web dashboard to run tool-calling chains (e.g. web search + local database) and measure latency/accuracy trade-offs compared to stock vLLM.

Evaluate the effect of different quantization/patch options on long-context retrieval for an engineering knowledge base by combining SNDR Core, pgvector (or another vector DB) and a dataset of technical documents, and report impacts on throughput and answer correctness.

tools.name: bimwright/rvt-mcp
tools.desc: BIMwright — AI-native Revit MCP server (Revit 2022–2027)

cls.summary: rvt-mcp is a local Model Context Protocol (MCP) gateway that lets AI agents call typed Revit tools and run a C# server to automate and extend Revit (supported for Revit 2022–2027).
cls.what_it_does: rvt-mcp provides a .NET 8 MCP server plus a small Revit add-in so agent clients (e.g. Claude Code / Desktop) can talk to a running Revit session via localhost or named pipes; it exposes typed Revit operations and a C# escape hatch for custom calls. It is notable for an all-C#, local-first design, installer scripts for wiring common agent clients, and an optional personal "ToolBaker" workflow to grow reusable agent-driven tools.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository is 214 days old (<1 year) which limits TRL to at most 6, but it has versioned releases (v1.2.2), an installer, documentation, active pushes, and community videos referenced in the README, supporting a beta-level maturity.
prerequisites: Windows OS and familiarity with PowerShell
.NET 8 / C# and basic Revit API knowledge
student_project_ideas: Build an agent that automates placing and parameterising a simple family in a Revit model using rvt-mcp and evaluate time savings compared to manual workflows.

Create a ToolBaker plugin that records a repetitive layout task (e.g. placing lighting fixtures along a corridor) via rvt-mcp and package it as a reusable automation, then test it on multiple floor plans.

tools.name: proyecto26/system-design-skills
tools.desc: A divide-and-conquer wiki of system-design skills for Claude Code — reason about scalable systems, don't memorize architectures.

cls.summary: A composable, agent-runable wiki of system-design building-block 'skills' that guides a reasoning-first workflow to produce scored design documents and diagrams.
cls.what_it_does: This repository provides a collection of modular system-design skills and an orchestrated `/design` workflow that an agent (Claude Code, OpenAI Codex and other Agent Plugins hosts) can run to clarify requirements, estimate scale, compose architectures, evaluate trade-offs and stress-test failure modes. It is delivered as an Agent Plugin/skills package (self-contained HTML+SVG diagrams and docs) and is notable for being authored as composable, justifiable building blocks rather than fixed example architectures.
cls.trl_rationale: The repo is a working, installable Agent Plugin with validated manifests, install instructions for multiple hosts and concrete examples; it has community interest (stars, forks) and recent activity, but is only ~5–6 months old so it lacks the long-term production track record needed for TRL 7+.
prerequisites: an Agent-Plugin host such as Claude Code, OpenAI Codex or the skills CLI
familiarity with installing plugins or copying skills into the agent runtime
student_project_ideas: Use the skills plugin to run the `/design` workflow for a scaled URL-shortener or messaging service, produce the scored design and diagram, then implement a small prototype (API + load test) to validate the back-of-envelope estimates.

Extend the repository by adding a new building-block skill for edge caching or a particular cloud provider variant, then run comparative designs across different provider choices and evaluate trade-offs quantitatively.

tools.name: unable12/codebase-posters
tools.desc: your repository as generative art — npx codebase-posters

cls.summary: A small CLI/browser tool that reads a repository's git history and generates deterministic, high-resolution generative-art posters and an animation of the painting process.
cls.what_it_does: codebase-posters reads a project's git log locally and paints a set of deterministic poster images and an MP4 of the painting animation in the browser; it runs from a one-line npx command or as a dev server. It solves the problem of turning commit history into visual, printable artefacts and notable design points are zero runtime dependencies, deterministic output, and support for high-resolution print export.
cls.trl_rationale: The repository is functional with a CLI and dev server, deterministic output, and a small user base (132 stars). It is 135 days old (<1 year) so it lacks the multi-year track record or wide adoption to justify TRL 6+.
student_project_ideas: Extend the tool with a custom CanvasRecipe that visualises engineering-specific metrics (e.g. test coverage or CI build times) by combining repository commit history with data from a CI server.

Compare visual patterns between multiple project types by scripting batch generation of posters for several repos (use the CLI to produce images and analyse correlations with repo metrics such as contributor count or release cadence).

tools.name: suhaibbinyounis/github-copilot-api-vscode
tools.desc: Unlock GitHub Copilot as a local API Gateway. Use Copilot with Cursor, LangChain, and any OpenAI-compatible tool.

tools.name: ahnafnafee/local-llm-pdf-ocr
tools.desc: Convert scanned PDFs and images into searchable documents with any OpenAI-compatible vision server. Run locally with a Web UI or CLI.

tools.name: therezor/cardputer-ai
tools.desc: Fully offline tiny LLM chatbot on the ESP32-S3 Cardputer ADV - 8M params, Q4 weights baked into the firmware, ~5  tok/s.

cls.summary: Cardputer AI is an open-source tiny LLM chatbot firmware that runs entirely on an ESP32‑S3 Cardputer (512 KB RAM) and provides offline conversational AI at ~5 tokens/s.
cls.what_it_does: Cardputer AI squeezes an 8M‑parameter, Q4 quantised language model and chat runtime into the flash and firmware of an ESP32‑S3 pocket computer so it can hold short, coherent conversations with no internet. It is used by flashing the provided firmware to an M5Stack Cardputer (or running the model on a host via ollama) and interacting via the device keyboard; notable points are extreme model compression, hand‑written SIMD math for the S3 and a model baked into firmware.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository provides firmware releases, demo media, and a working device build with binaries and install instructions, indicating more than a prototype; however the project is only ~5 months old so it lacks long-term production track record, which limits TRL to ~6.
prerequisites: familiarity with C++ and embedded development
experience with ESP32 tooling (PlatformIO or ESP-IDF) and flashing devices
basic understanding of quantised neural nets and constrained memory techniques
student_project_ideas: Modify the firmware to add a sensor-driven prompt (e.g. temperature or accelerometer) so the tiny LLM responds contextually to environmental data and evaluate memory/latency tradeoffs.
Port the runtime optimisations to another low‑cost MCU (e.g. ESP32-C3) and benchmark token throughput, memory usage and energy consumption against the Cardputer S3 implementation.

tools.name: LumioGames/LGUI
tools.desc: Game UI framework for AI agents, made by LumioGames. Build screens, logic and tests in the browser with no game engine, then export to Unity. 给 AI Agent 用的游戏 UI 框架，不依赖游戏引擎。

cls.summary: LGUI is a browser-based game UI framework that lets AI agents design, test and export game interfaces (FairyGUI format) and logic in TypeScript, then export the same UI and code to Unity.
cls.what_it_does: LGUI moves game UI development into the browser so interfaces (stored in FairyGUI format) and TypeScript MVC logic can be authored, previewed, tested (headless or real browser) and verified without opening a game engine. It provides CLI commands for dev, check, test, verify, and a Unity export backend so the same UI and code can be exported to a Unity project; notable features include agent-oriented workflows, automated visual verification, and an editor and asset-splitting tools for preparing art.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository is very new (created 32 days ago) but contains a detailed README, examples, CLI and multiple backends (web, headless, Unity) indicating an installable early-alpha project; the short age and lack of long-term real-world usage evidence limit the TRL.
prerequisites: Chrome or Edge for browser preview
Unity (only for export and final packaging) if using Unity backend
student_project_ideas: Create a playable in-browser inventory UI for a small robot simulation using LGUI for the UI and a headless test harness to run and verify UI flows automatically.

Build an agent-driven UI generator: give an agent a UI spec, have it use LGUI to assemble the interface, run lgui verify to capture screenshots, and export the result to a Unity project for packaging.

tools.name: victor-rong/nexels
tools.desc: The official repository for Nexels: Neurally-Textured Surfels for Real-Time Novel View Synthesis with Sparse Geometries

tools.name: 0nandon/EmbodiedSplat
tools.desc: [CVPR 2026] Official code of "EmbodiedSplat: Online Feed-Forward Semantic 3DGS for Open-Vocabulary 3D Scene Understanding"

cls.summary: EmbodiedSplat is a research codebase that performs online feed-forward 3D Gaussian-splat reconstruction of scenes with open-vocabulary semantic labels from streaming images.
cls.what_it_does: EmbodiedSplat reconstructs whole-scene 3D Gaussian Splat (3DGS) representations from streaming RGB images and produces open-vocabulary semantic 3D segmentation and novel-view rendering. It is used as a research pipeline (training and inference) that runs on a single high-memory NVIDIA GPU and provides pretrained weights and evaluation scripts for ScanNet-style datasets. Notable features include online (streaming) processing at multiple frames-per-second and integration of 2D/3D CLIP features for open-vocabulary semantics.
cls.trl_rationale: The repository accompanies a CVPR 2026 paper and provides released code, pretrained weights and evaluation scripts, indicating a beta-level research release; however it is under one year old so there is limited long-term community or production adoption evidence.
prerequisites: CUDA-capable GPU with large VRAM (e.g. NVIDIA RTX 6000 Ada / 48GB)
student_project_ideas: Integrate EmbodiedSplat's pretrained inference to a mobile robot pipeline to build an online semantic map from an RGB camera stream and evaluate segmentation accuracy in a small indoor environment.

Compare the online 'incremental' vs 'online' reference-frame strategies by running the provided evaluation on ScanNet scenes and measure trade-offs between latency, reconstruction fidelity and semantic accuracy.

tools.name: deskmind-ai/deskmind
tools.desc: Small enough to run on your Mac. Smart enough to ask. An open-source computer use agent for macOS, with local models (MLX) that see, decide and act. 得心，应手。

cls.summary: DeskMind is an open-source macOS agent that uses small local models to read the screen, decide the next desktop action as a multiple-choice step, and either act or ask the user for clarification.
cls.what_it_does: DeskMind runs compact on-device ML models to interpret a macOS desktop (screen "Eyes"), choose the next UI action using a decision-focused model server ("Brain") and optionally perform actions via a macOS helper ("Hands"). It is notable for its two-stage routing (a fast 0.8B model that escalates uncertain steps to a 4B model), local-only inference on Apple Silicon, and a shipped, signed Mac app plus separate model/server components for advanced users.
cls.trl_rationale: The project provides published Mac releases, downloadable models, and documentation, showing practical use; however the repository is only ~52 days old so it lacks a longer public track record and broader adoption, limiting maturity to TRL 5.
prerequisites: macOS 15+ on Apple Silicon for the app
familiarity with running local model servers and command-line tools
basic understanding of LLM/model packaging (Hugging Face or ModelScope)
student_project_ideas: Integrate DeskMind with an automated testing bench to create an agent that performs and grades GUI workflows for a desktop engineering tool (combine DeskMind 'Eyes/Hands' with the project's Bench grader).

Extend the Brain server to add a domain-specific policy for an engineering application (e.g. CAD or simulation app) so the agent can assist repetitive tasks; evaluate routing thresholds and error rates using experiments on local models.

tools.name: WilliamLiu-1997/3D-Tiles-RendererJS-3DGS-Plugin
tools.desc: Gaussian splat tile plugin for 3d-tiles-renderer that streams Gaussian Splats content in Three.js

cls.summary: A Three.js plugin that streams and displays Gaussian Splatting 3D-tiles (glTF/GLB) using WebGPU or WebGL2 for large-scale GIS / ECEF point-cloud visualization.
cls.what_it_does: This plugin integrates Gaussian Splat Lite rendering into the 3d-tiles-renderer pipeline so applications can stream, fade, dispose and render Gaussian-splat tiles in Three.js. It handles loading of uncompressed and SPZ-compressed splat tiles, supports WebGPU and WebGL2 backends (with GPU or worker/WASM sorting), and manages tile transforms and memory accounting for large GIS/ECEF datasets.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository is active with recent pushes, dependency integration and 131 stars indicating community interest, but it was created less than one year ago so there is not yet long-term production track record; README and examples are comprehensive which supports a beta (TRL 6) judgement.
prerequisites: Three.js (>=0.187.0) and familiarity with its renderer/camera
Understanding of WebGPU/WebGL2 and browser deployment
Familiarity with 3D Tiles / point-cloud tiling concepts
student_project_ideas: Build a web viewer that streams a public Gaussian-splat tileset, adds viewpoint-based LOD and fading, and measures rendering performance (FPS, memory) across WebGPU and WebGL2 backends.
Integrate streamed Gaussian-splat tiles with a simple digital-twin dashboard (e.g. overlaying sensor time-series from a CSV or MQTT feed) to visualise changes in a city or site over time.

tools.name: posecode-dev/posecode
tools.desc: An open-source text language, parser, validator and Three.js renderer for inspectable 3D human movement.

cls.summary: Posecode is an open text-based language, parser, validator and Three.js renderer for describing, inspecting and rendering deterministic 3D human motion.
cls.what_it_does: Posecode provides a small domain-specific text format (.posecode) to describe timed joint actions, range-of-motion constraints and grounding rules; a parser and validator turn those documents into an intermediate motion representation; and a Three.js-based renderer and MCP server let you preview, share and programmatically generate or critique movements. It is notable for being human-readable, deterministic (no black-box model required) and agent-friendly (an MCP server and LLM authoring guide are provided).
cls.trl_rationale: Repository contains a working TypeScript parser, IR, Three.js renderer, browser playground, examples and an MCP server with recent commits; project is active and used enough to attract stars but is only ~5 months old, so it fits a beta-level maturity (TRL 6) rather than production-proven TRL 7+.
prerequisites: familiarity with Three.js and web development
student_project_ideas: Integrate Posecode with a ROS 2 humanoid simulation (Gazebo or Ignition) to convert .posecode sequences into robot joint controllers and evaluate repeatability and safety limits.

Build an automated diagnostics tool that validates a library of .posecode exercises against configurable range-of-motion profiles and produces corrective cue suggestions or safety warnings (combine Posecode with a simple web dashboard).

tools.name: jefferysha0627/agent-office-3d
tools.desc: A low-poly 3D office that shows your AI coding agents' live status — idle agents sneak off to play Minecraft (no tokens used).

cls.summary: A local web-based 3D office dashboard that visualises the live status of AI coding agents with low‑poly avatars and optional embedded Minecraft agent demos.
cls.what_it_does: Agent Office 3D runs a Node.js server and a three.js front end to display each AI coding agent as an office worker showing status, recent terminal output (read‑only), and idle animations; optionally it launches a local Minecraft server with mineflayer bots whose first‑person view is embedded into each agent's desk. It is used as a demo/visual dashboard to monitor or showcase agent behaviour and can connect to Herdr or run in a demo mode without real agents.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository is very new (created 19 days ago) but has a substantial README, demo commands and CI; no stable releases or long track record, so it's at alpha/early‑adopter maturity (TRL 5). The short age limits a higher TRL.
student_project_ideas: Extend the dashboard to collect and plot agent runtime metrics (CPU/memory, task durations) and export traces to a time-series database (e.g. InfluxDB) to study agent performance.
Replace the Herdr adapter with a new source adapter that connects the dashboard to a CI system or an LLM orchestration framework, showing live build/test status mapped to office seats.

tools.name: BigStrongSun/ccswitchmulti
tools.desc: CCswitch的全面升级，专门优化codex体验。支持官方订阅和第三方模型混用，自动路由，支持v2subagent使用第三方模型

cls.summary: CCSwitchMulti is a desktop local-proxy and provider-management tool that routes Codex Desktop requests across multiple model providers (official OpenAI/Codex, third‑party APIs and local models) to reduce cost and centralise model metadata.
cls.what_it_does: It provides a local Codex takeover proxy, a provider/model database, and a multi-model routing/workflow (Codex MultiRouter) so a single Codex Provider can dispatch requests to OpenAI, third‑party APIs (Qwen, DeepSeek) or local LLMs. It's used as a desktop Tauri app that compiles provider/model catalogs into files Codex reads and performs per-request routing and protocol conversion.
cls.trl_rationale: The repository is actively maintained with an extensive README, release mention and a sizeable star count which indicates early adoption, but it is only ~100 days old so it lacks the multi‑year track record or ecosystem required for TRL 7+.
prerequisites: familiarity with Codex / ChatGPT Desktop workflows and OAuth
basic knowledge of local LLMs / OpenAI-compatible APIs and networking
comfort installing desktop apps (Tauri) or running Rust binaries for advanced builds
student_project_ideas: Create routing rules that automatically divert batch/low-cost tasks from an official Codex model to a local vLLM and measure token/cost savings across a sample workload.
Integrate a local user-defined model (e.g. vLLM or Qwen local) behind CCSwitchMulti and implement diagnostics to compare latency, success rate and cost versus routing to an external API.

tools.name: gokeshenzhen/TraceWeave
tools.desc: Open-source, evidence-driven MCP server for RTL simulation debugging: correlate VCS/Xcelium logs, VCD/FSDB waveforms, SystemVerilog/UVM source, hierarchy, and connectivity to trace failures to root cause.

cls.summary: TraceWeave is an open-source MCP server that connects simulation logs, waveforms, and RTL source to an AI assistant to help trace RTL/SoC simulation failures to root cause.
cls.what_it_does: TraceWeave ingests simulation artifacts (compile records, VCS/Xcelium/Verilator logs, VCD/FSDB/FST waveforms) and static source information, exposing tools over the Model Context Protocol so an assistant can inspect signals, driver chains, handshakes and provenance to debug failures. It is used as a backend MCP server that an LLM-based client queries to get evidence-backed traces and waveform samples; notable features include multi-format waveform support, hierarchical browsing for large designs, and layered fallbacks (KDB/NPI → Source Graph → static analysis) for driver tracing.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository is a detailed, actively maintained project with many features and examples, non-trivial star/fork counts, and validated-scale claims in the README, indicating beyond prototype; however the repo age is under one year (≈9 months) so demonstrated adoption and long-term production track record are limited, capping TRL at 6 (beta).
prerequisites: understanding of simulation workflows (VCS/Xcelium/Verilator) and waveform formats (VCD/FSDB/FST)
basic Python and server deployment knowledge
student_project_ideas: Integrate TraceWeave with a small Verilator-based RTL testbench to build an LLM-driven debugging assistant that identifies the driver chain for a failed assertion and produces evidence-backed explanations.

Use TraceWeave to compare two simulation runs (golden vs regression) for a pipelined module: automate waveform difference detection and implement a small visualization/reporting front-end that highlights suspected root-cause signals.

tools.name: rvdende/cadrs
tools.desc: A parametric, feature-based CAD app in Rust, with a Bevy UI and rust nurbs b-rep kernel.

cls.summary: cadrs is an open-source, feature-based parametric CAD application written in Rust with its own B-rep kernel, Bevy UI, assembly and drawing tools, and FEA and import/export capabilities.
cls.what_it_does: cadrs provides a full parametric CAD workflow: sketching with geometric constraints and dimensions, building parts from editable features (extrude, loft, fillet, hole, etc.), assembling instances with mates, and producing drawings and BOMs. It includes a pure‑Rust B-rep kernel, import/export for STEP/IGES/STL and Onshape feature-history import, a CPU path tracer for rendering and a linear static FEA module, and can be driven by local AI assistants via an MCP server.
cls.trl_rationale: The README describes a wide set of functioning features (sketcher, feature history, assemblies, FEA, import/export and MCP server) and the project has attracted community interest (131 stars) but the repository is only 48 days old so lacks the multi-release, long-term production track record needed for TRL 6+. This supports an alpha/in‑use rating (TRL 5).
prerequisites: familiarity with parametric CAD concepts (sketches, constraints, features)
Rust toolchain to build from source if not using binaries
student_project_ideas: Implement a design-for-manufacture extension that analyses cadrs part geometry and generates simple CNC toolpaths or export to a CAM-friendly format.

Create an automated testbench that uses the cadrs_mcp server to have an LLM-driven script generate parameterised parts and run the cadrs_fea module to compare stress results across a design variable sweep.

tools.name: luka2chat/awesome-geo
tools.desc: 🚀 A curated list of awesome resources for Generative Engine Optimization (GEO) - optimizing content for AI search engines like ChatGPT, Perplexity, Claude, and Google AI Overviews.

tools.name: LukyVj/GSS
tools.desc: ❴ ● ❵ GSS — GPU Style Sheets. A CSS-like language for 3D scenes: selectors, the cascade, nesting, keyframes and transitions, compiled into one raymarching shader for WebGPU and WebGL2. No Three.js, no meshes. Playground, VS Code extension, and a <gss-scene> tag for any page.

cls.summary: GSS is a CSS-like language that compiles 3D scene declarations into a single raymarching shader for WebGL2 and WebGPU, usable in webpages via a custom tag or runtime.
cls.what_it_does: GSS lets authors declare shapes, materials, animations and scene properties using a CSS-like syntax which a compiler turns into GLSL/WGSL raymarching shaders that run in WebGL2 or WebGPU. It provides a live playground, a VS Code extension, an npm package and a <gss-scene> tag so scenes can be embedded in pages without Three.js or explicit meshes. The notable aspect is its CSS-like selector/cascade model mapped to GPU shader code and single-shader raymarching pipeline.
cls.trl_rationale: The project is young (created ~49 days ago) but provides a working runtime, npm package (0.0.7), playground and VS Code extension which indicates early real-world use; its short age prevents TRL >5 despite good documentation and examples.
prerequisites: familiarity with shaders (GLSL/WGSL) and WebGL/WebGPU concepts
student_project_ideas: Create an interactive web demo of a parametric mechanical part (e.g. flexible bellows or gasket) authored in GSS and export the shader to Shadertoy while documenting the mapping from CSS-like properties to SDF parameters.

Build a small visualization tool that embeds <gss-scene> instances and drives scene parameters from live sensor or time-series data (e.g. animate a dashboard-linked visual) to demonstrate runtime integration of Web data with GPU rendering.

tools.name: DmitriyGolub/threejs-devtools-mcp
tools.desc: Three.js MCP server — inspect and edit scenes, materials, shaders, lights in real time from any AI agent

cls.summary: A local MCP server that lets AI agents inspect, live-edit and convert Three.js and React Three Fiber scenes into ready-to-paste code while running in the browser.
cls.what_it_does: The project provides a meta-control-plane (MCP) server that connects AI clients to running Three.js scenes so you can inspect scene graphs, tweak materials, shaders, lights and capture frames live in the browser. Changes can be previewed without touching source files and then committed back as code (vanilla Three.js or React Three Fiber); it also includes web performance audits and Playwright/Puppeteer helpers for automated testing.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository is well-documented, provides 69 tools, Playwright helpers and integration instructions and has an active commit history and community interest (130 stars). However the repo is under 1 year old (created 2026-03-15), so there is not yet a long track record required for TRL 7+.
prerequisites: familiarity with Three.js and/or React Three Fiber
basic knowledge of web devtools and Playwright/Puppeteer
student_project_ideas: Use the MCP server to build an automated scene-quality auditor that scans a Three.js scene for performance issues (draw calls, large textures, battery drain) and produces a prioritized fix report, integrating with ffmpeg to capture before/after clips.

Create a lab assignment where students connect a simple robotics simulation in Three.js to the MCP, have an AI agent modify robot materials and camera views live, then commit the best visualization changes into React Three Fiber source code.

tools.name: Italink/UnrealClientProtocol
tools.desc: Lightweight UE5 plugin that exposes Unreal Engine's reflection system over TCP+JSON — let AI agents call UFunctions, read/write UProperties, and inspect any UObject in a running editor, zero engine modification required.

cls.summary: UnrealClientProtocol is a lightweight Unreal Engine 5 plugin that exposes UE's reflection (UFunctions and UProperties) over a TCP+JSON protocol so external AI agents can inspect and manipulate a running editor without engine source changes.
cls.what_it_does: It provides an atomic, JSON-over-TCP protocol that lets external AI agents call UFunctions, read/write UProperties, find and introspect any UObject in a running UE5 editor, and extend behaviour via user-authored 'Skills'. It is used as a plugin in the UE editor and notable for exposing the full engine reflection surface (no pre-defined high-level commands) so LLM-driven agents can compose complex editor actions from primitive operations.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository is ~8 months old with active pushes, ~130 stars and open issues which indicates community interest and working code; however it is younger than one year so there's limited evidence of long-term production use, placing it at a beta-level TRL.
prerequisites: Experience with running external AI agents or LLM-based agent frameworks
student_project_ideas: Build an LLM-driven tool that uses UCP to automate level-build tasks (spawn actors, set properties, save levels) and demonstrate a scripted workflow comparing manual vs agent-driven creation.

Create an agent that converts simple ShaderToy snippets into UE material graphs via UCP and validates the result by compiling the material and measuring instruction count, then reports results in a dashboard.

tools.name: Scottcjn/llama-cpp-power8
tools.desc: llama.cpp optimizations for IBM POWER8: vec_perm non-bijunctive collapse, PSE hardware entropy, DCBT prefetch. Sovereign inference. Part of the Proof of Physical AI stack.

tools.name: subhashhhhhh/Lumen
tools.desc: A photo gallery for Android with the smart features of Google Photos and iPhone Photos. Nothing leaves your phone.

cls.summary: Lumen is an open-source Android photo gallery app that provides Google-Photos-like on-device search, text recognition, face grouping and cutout features while keeping all data local to the phone.
cls.what_it_does: Lumen indexes and displays the photos and videos on an Android device and uses on-device machine learning models to find images by description, extract and allow selection of text from images, group faces, and cut out people or objects. It is used as a standalone gallery app (no cloud, no account) and is notable for running smart features entirely offline and targeting degoogled devices.
cls.trl_rationale: The repository is new (created ~24 days ago) but contains a working Android app and documentation; however it lacks a long track record, stable multi-release history and broad production usage, so it fits early-alpha maturity.
prerequisites: familiarity with mobile ML model packaging / deployment
student_project_ideas: Benchmark and compare on-device ML model performance (accuracy, latency, power) used by Lumen across several Android devices, and report trade-offs for model selection.
Extend Lumen to add a simple encrypted cloud backup option and evaluate how the added feature affects privacy guarantees, UX and data flow (demonstrate threat model and mitigations).

tools.name: ABC12345anouys/EvoBot
tools.desc: Agent + reusable skill library for LIBERO manipulation tasks (no RL / VLA / world model; no LLM calls at runtime)

cls.summary: EvoBot is an open-source agent and reusable skill library that runs manipulation tasks from the LIBERO benchmark in MuJoCo/robosuite without reinforcement learning or LLM calls at runtime.
cls.what_it_does: EvoBot decomposes LIBERO benchmark tasks into ordered subgoals offline, then executes those subgoals at runtime using a parameterised skill library (grasp, place, push, open, turn knobs, etc.). It reports classified failure reasons to enable recovery and was evaluated across 30 LIBERO tasks (25/30 success) using robosuite/MuJoCo simulations.
cls.trl_rationale: The repository demonstrates quantitative evaluation on the LIBERO benchmark (25/30 tasks passed) and includes design docs and scripts, but the project is very new (created ~55 days ago) so it lacks a long track record or broad production adoption—appropriate for TRL 5 (alpha in use).
student_project_ideas: Extend EvoBot's failure-recovery logic by adding a perception pipeline (e.g. depth+segmentation) to replace ground-truth poses from LIBERO and measure task success changes across a subset of LIBERO tasks.
Integrate a new parametrised skill (e.g. compliant push or tool use) into the EvoBot skill library and evaluate its effect on success rates for related manipulation tasks in robosuite/MuJoCo.

tools.desc: Gridfinity-compatible baseplate generator with puzzle connectors

tools.desc: QGIS plugin for the SamGeo Python package

tools.name: tg12/phantomtide
tools.desc: Global maritime intelligence platform for real-time vessel tracking, AIS data analysis, sanctions monitoring, shipping routes, port activity, anomaly detection, OSINT analytics, and geospatial insights

cls.summary: Phantom Tide is a geospatial OSINT platform for real-time maritime and airspace intelligence that surfaces prioritized hotspots, supports analyst workflows, and exposes machine-readable feeds for situational awareness.
cls.what_it_does: Phantom Tide ingests open signals (AIS, ADS‑B, HF receivers, thermal detections and other feeds), ranks and correlates cross‑source hotspots, and presents analyst-focused context and timelines instead of raw map clutter. It is used via a hosted web workspace and public API endpoints (e.g. restricted‑airspace crossings) and is notable for emphasising freshness/degraded-state visibility, analyst notebooks and layered geospatial context (tides, coastal elevation, ice, infra).
cls.trl_rationale: Repository is 241 days old (under one year) so TRL is capped at 6; README and metadata show an actively maintained hosted product (v2.2.0), public API endpoints and release notes, but the repo explicitly states it does not contain the full application codebase which limits evidence for higher TRL.
prerequisites: understanding of AIS / ADS‑B and maritime/airspace terminology
experience with REST APIs and JSON
student_project_ideas: Build a reproducible notebook that ingests the public restricted‑airspace feed, visualises crossings on a map, and flags anomalous tracks using simple heuristics (speed, altitude, geofence violations).

Combine open AIS data with publicly available thermal-detection or tide-station layers to produce a short analysis that locates and explains thermal‑vessel gap zones for a selected port or chokepoint.

tools.name: BrettKinny/dotty-stackchan
tools.desc: Self-hosted voice-assistant stack for the M5Stack StackChan desktop robot. Local ASR/TTS, pluggable LLM brain, kid-mode default, no cloud required.

cls.summary: Dotty is a self-hosted voice-assistant stack for the M5Stack StackChan desktop robot that runs local ASR, TTS and a pluggable LLM brain so you can operate a private robot assistant without cloud services.
cls.what_it_does: Dotty integrates firmware on an M5Stack StackChan robot with a pi-hosted agent that handles automatic speech recognition, text-to-speech and a pluggable LLM backend to produce conversational voice responses. It is used to run a fully local voice assistant (kid-mode by default) with swap-out components for ASR, TTS and LLMs, and notable for emphasising privacy, offline operation and hackability.
cls.trl_rationale: The project is a single-maintainer hobby stack that the author says runs end-to-end on their own robot, showing real-use alpha maturity, but the repository is only ~7 months old and has no wide production track record or multiple organisational users, so TRL is limited to alpha-in-use.
prerequisites: M5Stack StackChan hardware (ESP32-S3) and familiarity with flashing firmware
local LLM runtime or access to compatible LLM endpoints (llama-swap, Ollama or OpenAI-compatible API)
installation of ASR/TTS models (FunASR, WhisperLocal, Piper) and audio device configuration
student_project_ideas: Extend Dotty to add a safe-question classifier that flags or redirects questions to a teacher dashboard, integrating the assistant with a simple web UI for supervision.

Replace the default ASR with a small on-device model and benchmark speech-recognition accuracy and latency for children's voices, comparing SenseVoice, WhisperLocal and SenseVoiceOnnx on a Raspberry Pi-class host.

tools.name: ggerman/libgd-gis
tools.desc: libgd-gis is a native GIS and map-rendering engine for Ruby built on top of ruby-libgd. It lets Ruby applications generate map images, tiles, and geospatial visualizations directly from latitude/longitude data — without external map servers or image pipelines.

tools.name: rtmandreyev/construct
tools.desc: Persistent, editable objects for AI agents: researched part by part, honest about what is known, and carried into worlds, film, web, games, CAD and print.

cls.summary: Construct turns natural-language or image descriptions into persistent, part-labelled 3D 'constructs' with provenance that can be exported to models, game engines and printable kits.
cls.what_it_does: Construct has agents research an object or scene, produces a checked, repeatable description of named parts, sizes and joints, and builds a single canonical construct that can be rendered, animated, exported to Blender/Godot/Unity, printed as a kit, or composed into larger worlds. It is used via Python and agent clients (Hermes, Claude, OpenAI-compatible endpoints and MCP clients) and emphasises provenance (what was measured vs guessed) and reusability of parts across exports and worlds.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository is very new (created 2026-10-24, ~24 days old) but has a working Python project, example worlds, and a Hermes plugin; there is evidence of usable functionality and examples but no long track record or stable releases, so TRL is limited to Alpha-in-use.
prerequisites: familiarity with agent clients (Hermes, Claude or OpenAI-compatible APIs)
basic web browser for viewing outputs and 3D models
student_project_ideas: Produce a digital-twin of a simple room from a set of photos using Construct, export it to Godot and create a short interactive walkthrough demonstrating provenance labels on movable parts.

Use Construct with an agent client to generate a construct of a consumer device, then export the part geometry to Blender and produce a 3D-printable replacement part, documenting uncertainty sources for each measured dimension.

tools.name: icesixgod/awesome-astra-blender-characters
tools.desc: An agent skill for Blender character creation and repair, with nine-view references, face and hair workflows, and visual validation.

cls.summary: A distributable Codex/agent skill that documents and automates a Blender-focused workflow for creating and repairing stylised (anime/illustration) character heads and hair using nine-view references and checklist-based validation.
cls.what_it_does: The repository provides a packaged agent skill (blender-character-workflow) that codifies step-by-step instructions, checks and delivery notes for creating and repairing Blender character heads and hair, emphasising nine-view references, local repair steps and visual acceptance criteria for static illustration style characters. It is used by installing the skill into a Codex/agent host and then invoking its prompts; notable points are the workflow documentation, installation/validation scripts and explicit boundaries (it does not include models, training weights or automated reconstruction).
cls.trl_rationale: The repo is young (created ~70 days ago) and distributes an agent skill and documentation rather than exercised production software or datasets; it has installation and validation scripts and CI checks but no bundled models, example assets or demonstrated production users, consistent with an early-alpha level.
student_project_ideas: Integrate the provided skill with a local image-generation pipeline (eg. Stable Diffusion or other image model) to automatically produce the nine-view references and evaluate the agent's guidance quality.

Extend the skill to add automated export and a simple verification script that generates the fixed-camera renders and compares them to reference images to demonstrate repeatable multi-view acceptance checks.

tools.name: Czarnak/tia-portal-mcp
tools.desc: Specialized bridge designed to connect LLMs and AI agents directly to Siemens SIMATIC TIA Portal V21.

cls.summary: A server that exposes a guarded MCP API allowing LLMs and agentic clients to inspect and (optionally) modify Siemens SIMATIC TIA Portal V21 projects via the Siemens Openness API.
cls.what_it_does: The project provides an MCP server which maps the Siemens Openness API into a set of guarded tools for PLC, HMI, VCI (version-control-like) and library operations so agents can read project contents, perform controlled writes (with dry-run support), run compile/check diagnostics and inspect hardware/network configuration. It is used by running the server on a Windows host with TIA Portal V21 available; notable features include per-tool access modes (read-only, read-write, full), batching/paging semantics, structured JSON contracts for responses and documented safety/guard behaviour for write operations.
cls.trl_rationale: The repo is well-documented with detailed operation descriptions and qualification reports and has active pushes and community interest (128 stars), indicating a beta-level project. However it is under one year old (created 206 days ago) so a TRL above 6 is not supported by the age and limited public adoption evidence.
prerequisites: Siemens TIA Portal V21 (commercial software) installed and licensed
Familiarity with Siemens Openness API and PLC/HMI engineering concepts
C#/.NET development and Windows administrative access
student_project_ideas: Build an agent that uses the MCP server to automatically detect mismatches between PLC tag usage and HMI tag declarations, producing a report and suggested remediations, integrating the server with a Git-based VCI workflow.

Create a supervised testing harness that uses the MCP server to run read-only cross-reference and compile diagnostics across multiple TIA projects to evaluate automated regression checks before deploy; compare results with manual checks and measure false-positive/negative rates.

tools.name: Dicklesworthstone/frankenterm
tools.desc: Swarm-native terminal platform for AI coding agents: real-time pane capture, change-point pattern detection, transactional policy-gated automation, a JSON/MCP robot API, and a fail-closed operating envelope — on its own vendored terminal engine, with a native iOS client that attaches to your Macs.

tools.name: sno-ai/llmix
tools.desc: Production LLM call layer for AI agents and tools: keep OpenAI/Anthropic/AI SDK/LiteLLM, hot-swap models with MDA presets, and add cache, retries, circuit breakers, key rotation, singleflight, and Python/TypeScript/Rust parity.

cls.summary: LLMix is a lightweight, config-driven wrapper layer that adds caching, retries, key rotation, circuit breakers and model presets around existing LLM provider SDK calls in Python, TypeScript and Rust.
cls.what_it_does: LLMix wraps individual LLM provider calls so you don't have to change your OpenAI/Anthropic/Gemini/LiteLLM or custom SDK usage; it provides features commonly needed in production such as two-tier caching, retry policies, circuit breakers, key pools/rotation, singleflight and MDA-based model presets. It is used as a thin harness inserted between application code and provider SDKs and is notable for providing parity across Python, TypeScript and Rust runtimes and making model selection a runtime data/config operation rather than a hard-coded value.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository is active and multi-language (Python/TypeScript/Rust) with published packages and 128 stars, documentation and examples, but it is under 1 year old (created ~192 days ago) so it fits a Beta-level maturity rather than long-term production track record.
prerequisites: experience with Python or TypeScript or Rust and basic async programming
understanding of caching and retry patterns (Redis optional)
student_project_ideas: Build a small chat-ops service that uses LLMix to orchestrate model calls with a Redis-backed cache and key-pool rotation to demonstrate reduced latency and resilience under synthetic load.
Integrate LLMix into a TypeScript web backend that can hot-swap between OpenAI and a local LiteLLM instance via MDA presets, and measure failover behaviour and request throughput.

tools.name: dfki-ric/ground_segmentation_ros2
tools.desc: ROS2 wrapper for the ground_segmentation library

tools.name: facebookresearch/Large-Sparse-Reconstruction-Model
tools.desc: LSRM is a SOTA, feed-forward 3D reconstruction model that generates high-fidelity, relightable 3D digital twins from sparse 2D views.

cls.summary: LSRM is a feed‑forward neural model that reconstructs high‑fidelity, relightable 3D object assets from sparse posed RGB views and produces meshes and BRDFs suitable for re‑rendering and downstream digital‑twin use.
cls.what_it_does: LSRM takes a small number of posed 2D images of an object and produces a 3D reconstruction (mesh + textures) and inverse‑rendering outputs (BRDF) that can be re‑lit and re‑rendered. It is distributed as research code with pre‑trained checkpoints and scripts for inference and re‑rendering (using Blender) and is notable for being feed‑forward and designed to work on sparse multi‑view inputs with real‑world evaluation.
cls.trl_rationale: The repo is a recent research code release (created ~6 months ago) from a known research group, includes pre-trained checkpoints on Hugging Face, test scripts and example data, and runs end‑to‑end inference; however it is younger than one year so there is not yet a long track record in production deployments.
student_project_ideas: Collect sparse multi‑view captures of small mechanical parts, run LSRM to produce relightable meshes, and integrate the outputs into a simple Unity or webGL viewer to evaluate visual fidelity and alignment against ground‑truth scans.

Compare reconstructed BRDFs and novel‑view renders from LSRM with outputs from a NeRF or Instant‑NGP pipeline on the same sparse capture set, and quantify differences in render quality and geometry accuracy.

tools.name: b14ckyy/Kite-GC
tools.desc: Kite Ground Control (Kite GC) is a modern, cross-platform ground control station for INAV, ArduPilot and PX4 aircraft — planes, multirotors, VTOL, helicopters, rovers and boats.

cls.summary: Kite GC is a cross-platform ground control station application for INAV, ArduPilot and PX4 vehicles providing mission planning, live telemetry, 3D flight visualization and fleet/flight-log management.
cls.what_it_does: Kite GC connects to UAV autopilots (INAV, ArduPilot, PX4) over USB/serial, Bluetooth, TCP/UDP and MAVLink/MSP to provide live telemetry, mission planning/upload/download, vehicle control and flight logging. It is used as a desktop GCS with a 2D/3D map and Cesium-based 3D globe, fleet and battery managers, live video alongside maps, and telemetry relay features; notable points are its full 3D flight view, terrain-awareness (AGL waypoints, terrain profiles) and multi-autopilot support.
cls.trl_rationale: The project publishes a tagged 1.0 release, platform installers and documentation and is actively developed (recent pushes and release support policy), indicating a beta/near-production maturity; however the repository is under 1 year old so TRL is limited to 6 by the age rule.
prerequisites: familiarity with desktop application deployment (Windows/macOS/Linux) for building from source
optional: Rust/Node/Svelte knowledge if developing or building
student_project_ideas: Use Kite GC to plan and execute automated survey missions for a small multirotor and analyse collected flight logs to evaluate mission accuracy and repeatability, combining with a simple photogrammetry pipeline for mapping.

Develop a telemetry-based anomaly detector: capture flight logs with Kite GC, export telemetry and train a classifier to detect degraded sensor/actuator behaviour, then demonstrate realtime alerts via Kite's telemetry stream and safety widgets.

tools.name: adand-91/gpt-6-astra-skill
tools.desc: Astra Skill Optimizer for GPT-6/Astra project Skill and workflow adaptation

cls.summary: A Python tool that audits and adapts conversational 'Skills' for a GPT-6/Astra agent and provides a focused project-manager workflow called Jarvis to keep goals, requirements and next actions aligned.
cls.what_it_does: Astra Skill Optimizer analyses a selected project and its associated agent Skills to identify outdated constraints, propose minimal authorised changes, and verify those changes in a controlled workflow. It is used as a Codex plugin/CLI to produce evidence-bound audits, next-action recommendations and a project takeover workflow (Jarvis) that restores goals, stages, blockers and an explicit next action.
