cls.trl_rationale: Repository is recent (created 2026-08-17, ~92 days old) but shows structured docs, a quick-start, plugins and release notes; however there is limited evidence of wide production use or enterprise adoption so maturity is around beta with documented workflows.
prerequisites: familiarity with Python and package/plugin installation
understanding of Codex plugin workflow and agent Skills
basic knowledge of conversational agent design and requirements concepts
student_project_ideas: Integrate Astra Skill Optimizer with a simple student-built Codex Skill for an engineering mini-project and demonstrate automated detection and repair of a requirement-change scenario (showing the audit, proposed change and verification).

Compare audit outputs from Astra Skill Optimizer against manual requirements-traceability notes for a small systems design task and measure how suggestions affect task drift and next-action clarity over several simulated iterations.

tools.name: john-rocky/coreai-kit
tools.desc: Swift SDK for running chat, vision and speech models on iPhone and Mac with Apple's Core AI. Model download and caching, FoundationModels integration, and runnable examples with documented OS, SDK and model requirements.

cls.summary: CoreAIKit is a Swift SDK that downloads, caches and runs Apple's Core AI on-device models (chat, vision, speech) for iPhone and Mac and provides runnable examples and simple one-line APIs.
cls.what_it_does: CoreAIKit automates finding, downloading and caching Core AI model builds from Hugging Face and exposes simple Swift APIs and higher-level types (ChatSession, KitLanguageModel, KitVisionModel) to run chat, vision and speech tasks on-device. It is used inside iOS/macOS apps (requires Xcode 27 and macOS/iOS 27 on real hardware) and is notable for its curated model catalog, many example apps and integration with Apple's FoundationModels API.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository has a published version (0.8.0), many example apps, automated catalog checks and device tests; active pushes and 126 stars indicate an active beta-quality project. The repo is 158 days old (under one year), which limits higher TRL despite good documentation and examples.
prerequisites: macOS 27 or iOS 27 on real device
student_project_ideas: Build an iOS app that records short voice memos, uses CoreAIKit to transcribe and summarise them, and indexes results for local search (combine with a simple local database).

Create a multimodal inspection assistant that takes photos, runs object detection and asks a local chat model for inspection checklists and suggested fixes (combine CoreAIKit with device camera and a SwiftUI front end).

tools.name: Aevonix/FlashAlign
tools.desc: ReAlign models instantly, on demand. Per-request alignment for verified users and channels, or Always On. Use directly or with Hermes, OpenClaw and custom harnesses.

cls.summary: FlashAlign is an open-source runtime that applies per-request alignment profiles to LLMs so operators can change refusal and behaviour policies without permanently modifying model weights.
cls.what_it_does: FlashAlign loads a supported base or quantized model and applies alignment profiles on demand, either per-request for verified users/channels or Always On across routed requests. It is used alongside inference engines (vLLM, TensorFold, llama.cpp, SGLang) or via integration harnesses (Hermes, OpenClaw) and emphasises hot-loading profiles without rewriting weights.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository is feature-rich with documentation, multiple compatibility pages, example profiles and a v1.2.0 tag, showing early adopters and organised packaging, but it is only 17 days old so maturity is limited and broader production use is not demonstrated (age limits TRL to at most 5).
prerequisites: Supported inference engine (vLLM, TensorFold, llama.cpp, SGLang)
student_project_ideas: Integrate FlashAlign with a local vLLM deployment to measure how different alignment profiles affect refusal rates and generation quality on a curated test-suite.
Build a simple chat harness that uses FlashAlign to apply per-user profiles and log differences in tool outputs, then visualise differences in a small web dashboard.

tools.name: airesearch-official/Z-Image-Turbo-Windows
tools.desc: One-click Windows installer for Z-Image Turbo AI image generation. Optimized for low-VRAM GPUs (4GB+). Features Gradio web UI, automatic setup, and GGUF model support.

tools.name: jrenaldi79/harness-engineering
tools.desc: Context engineering for coding agents - CLAUDE.md templates, mechanical enforcement, and a field guide to 20+ best practices. Bootstrap with one command.

cls.summary: A reference guide plus a Claude Code plugin that automates 'harness engineering' for coding agents by scaffolding CLAUDE.md, installing enforcement scripts and git hooks, and providing readiness reports and a setup workflow.
cls.what_it_does: This project documents 20+ best practices for running AI coding agents and provides a Claude Code plugin with two main skills: /readiness, which analyses a codebase and produces a scored readiness report, and /setup, which interactively scaffolds CLAUDE.md, enforcement scripts, linters, and git hooks to mechanically enforce rules. It is used as a developer workflow add-on (requires Claude Code, Git and Node.js) to reduce agent drift and automate quality gates for agent-assisted development.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository is 251 days old (under one year) so it lacks the long track record needed for TRL 7+, but it shows demonstrated functionality: a documented plugin, active commits, 126 stars, and usable features (readiness and setup skills), consistent with a beta-level project.
student_project_ideas: Build a CI pipeline that integrates the harness-engineering /readiness report into automated pull request checks and visualises readiness deltas over time using a simple web dashboard.

Extend the /setup skill to add language-specific enforcement (for example, Python project: add pytest colocation and a Bandit security check) and evaluate how the added hooks prevent common agent-generated issues in a staged repository.

tools.name: venkatapgummadi/agentflow
tools.desc: Online-adaptive multi-agent framework for enterprise API orchestration. Adaptive circuit breakers, SLA-driven routing, hybrid LLM+rule intent parser. Apache 2.0.

cls.summary: AgentFlow is a Python framework that uses cooperating AI agents to discover, compose and orchestrate enterprise APIs with adaptive routing and resilience features.
cls.what_it_does: AgentFlow parses natural-language intents into executable API workflows, dynamically discovers and composes candidate endpoints, and routes requests based on latency, cost and capability while providing self-healing behaviour (circuit breakers, adaptive retries and fallbacks). It is used as a runtime orchestrator with connectors (MuleSoft, REST, GraphQL, gRPC) and a hybrid LLM+rule intent parser, notable for its enterprise integration focus and multi-agent execution architecture.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository is ~7 months old with a fairly detailed README, docs/ folder and connectors (shows active development) but is younger than one year and lacks evidence of wide production adoption or long-term stable releases, so beta-level maturity is appropriate.
prerequisites: familiarity with REST/HTTP APIs and API schemas (OpenAPI/RAML)
basic understanding of LLM providers and async API calls
student_project_ideas: Build a lab exercise where students connect AgentFlow to a set of mock REST and GraphQL services and evaluate routing decisions under varied latency and cost settings, measuring how the dynamic router selects endpoints.

Create a student project that extends AgentFlow with a new connector (e.g. a simulated IoT gateway) and implements a workflow that uses hybrid intent parsing to perform automated telemetry ingestion and enrichment.

integrates_with: OpenAI (or other LLM providers via callable adapters)

tools.name: Felix-au/3d-Constructs-Library
tools.desc: A developer library and resource vault for getting pre-compiled 3D particle coordinate distributions to implement interactive 3D particle meshes (like brains, lightbulbs, helixes, and spheres) on thier websites.

cls.summary: A client-side React + TypeScript library and demo app that renders and morphs thousands of particles into 18 predefined 3D mathematical and organic shapes using an optimized HTML5 Canvas physics engine.
cls.what_it_does: 3D Constructs provides precomputed 3D coordinate distributions and a small runtime that simulates particle behaviour (Verlet integration, springs, attraction/repel/ripple/swarm modes) and morphs between shapes in real time in the browser. It is delivered as a developer integration library plus an interactive PWA demo built with React, Vite and TypeScript, notable for implementing 3D-like particle visuals using 2D Canvas math to target low-power devices instead of heavyweight WebGL engines.
cls.trl_rationale: The README is detailed, the project includes a production build and examples, and it has a modest but real user interest (126 stars), indicating a beta-level project; however the repository is only ~142 days old so it lacks a longer track record needed for TRL 7+.
student_project_ideas: Build an interactive web demo that extends 3D Constructs to visualise sensor time-series (e.g. IMU or lidar-derived points) by mapping live data to particle positions and comparing performance against a simple WebGL/three.js implementation.

Create a performance study for low-power devices: vary particle count and physics parameters, measure frame rate and battery use on phones, and propose optimisations or a WebGL fallback for high particle counts.

tools.name: mozihe/z-localization
tools.desc: 2026年 东北大学T-DT实验室 RoboMaster超级对抗赛 哨兵定位开源

cls.summary: Z-Localization is a ROS 2 laser-inertial localization stack for mobile robots that provides odometry, mapping, prior-map localisation, loop-closure/relocalisation and optional UWB assistance.
cls.what_it_does: The project provides a complete LIO (lidar-inertial odometry) front-end (ZLIO) and a localisation back-end that can run on real robots or on rosbag playback to output pose, velocity, covariance and localisation status. It includes tools for map creation/cleanup, generating prior-map bundles (scan-context descriptors), and calibration utilities, and is notable for Livox Mid-360 driver support and an end-to-end ROS 2 launch/interface design.
cls.trl_rationale: The README shows a runnable ROS 2 stack with hardware and bag workflows, map tools and configuration docs indicating it has been used on real robots, but the repository is very new (26 days) with no stable releases — limiting it to an alpha-in-use TRL.
prerequisites: Livox ROS driver / Livox SDK for Mid-360
student_project_ideas: Integrate Z-Localization with a small wheeled robot (Mid-360 sensor or recorded bag) and evaluate localisation accuracy against a motion-capture or ground-truth trajectory, including experiments with and without UWB assistance.

Extend the map-cleaning pipeline by automating CloudCompare post-processing or replacing scan-context descriptors with an alternative (e.g. M2DP) and compare relocalisation robustness in dynamic indoor environments.

tools.name: chiban-org/chiban-oss
tools.desc: Open-source land-use software for small US towns: permits, inspections, Planning Board and ZBA cases, and code enforcement, organized around the parcel.

cls.summary: Chiban is an open-source web application for municipal land-use case management that organizes permits, inspections, board cases and code enforcement around cadastral parcels.
cls.what_it_does: Chiban centralises a town's applications, permits, inspections, board hearings, code-enforcement cases and records by parcel and provides a public parcel portal, staff workflows, payments and exportable records. It is used as a self-hosted web app (Next.js + PostGIS) with vector tiles, background workers and integrations for payments and object storage, notable for its parcel-centric data model and state 'packs' that encode local rules and deadlines.
cls.trl_rationale: The README and documentation indicate a working self-hosted product with a live demo, integration tests and deployment instructions, but the repository is only 7 days old so there is no demonstrated long-term production track record; this supports an alpha-in-use TRL.
student_project_ideas: Extend the demo dataset and build a short analysis that maps permit issuance and inspection frequency by parcel using PostGIS queries and MapLibre visualisation.
Implement a new state pack for a different US state: encode its deadlines, notice text and parcel ID formats, then validate behaviour with integration tests and demo data.

tools.name: glincker/awesome-selfhosted-ai
tools.desc: Curated list of self-hosted open-source AI: local LLMs, chat UIs, agents, MCP servers, RAG, speech and image generation. Health-checked weekly, dead projects removed automatically.

cls.summary: A curated, regularly health‑checked list of open‑source projects you can self‑host for local LLMs, chat UIs, agents, RAG, speech and image generation.
cls.what_it_does: This repository collects and categorises hundreds of self‑hosted open‑source AI projects (LLM runtimes, agent frameworks, MCP servers, RAG/vector stores, interfaces and more) and runs a weekly health check to move stale projects to an UNMAINTAINED list. It is used as a discovery and reference resource rather than a library or runtime, notable for its breadth and automated freshness checks.
cls.trl_rationale: The repository is a curated index with a clear process (weekly health checks) but is very new (created 17 days ago), so it shows early polish and utility but lacks a longer track record or wide adoption to justify a higher TRL.
student_project_ideas: Create a course-specific subset of the list (e.g. for digital twin or robotics) and build a scripted lab environment that deploys a small selection using Docker Compose for student hands‑on exercises.
Reproduce the repository's weekly health‑check pipeline: implement a script that queries GitHub APIs to monitor a set of AI projects, flags stale projects and generates a live status table.

tools.name: twehrbein/ExMR
tools.desc: 3D body, hand and foot motion (SMPL-X) from a single monocular video: world-grounded, with export for Blender, Unity, Unreal and humanoid robots. Official code of ExMR (arXiv 2610.26213).

cls.summary: ExMR is a Python toolbox that reconstructs detailed 3D body, hand and foot motion (SMPL‑X) from a single monocular video and exports results for Blender, Unity/Unreal and humanoid robots.
cls.what_it_does: ExMR refines whole‑body motion estimates with specialised hand and foot refinement modules to produce world‑grounded SMPL‑X sequences from monocular video. It is used via a demo/CLI (python tools/demo.py) to process videos and export SMPL‑X, BVH and FBX outputs for animation, retargeting and robot playback. Notable features include exported world‑frame motions, foot contact estimation, and integration paths for Blender/Unity/Unreal and humanoid retargeting (GMR).
cls.trl_rationale: The repository provides demo code, released model weights, versioned tags and a live Hugging Face Spaces demo, indicating early adoption beyond a toy prototype; however the project is very new (created 28 days ago) and the README states evaluation/training code will follow, which limits maturity to TRL 5.
prerequisites: NVIDIA GPU with CUDA (driver >= 570; ~8 GB recommended)
access to gated SAM 3D Body weights on Hugging Face (manual approval)
student_project_ideas: Integrate ExMR outputs with a ROS 2 and Gazebo pipeline to retarget reconstructed SMPL‑X motion to a simulated humanoid and evaluate foot contact timing against the original video.

Create a Blender add‑on that automates ExMR video processing and imports the exported AMASS/FBX motion into character rigs, then compare animation quality between modes (fast vs accurate) for a small dataset.

tools.name: noumena-labs/Sipp
tools.desc: AI inference, packed simply. A blazing-fast, zero-dependency WebGPU runtime to run GGUF models directly in the browser. Features a symmetric API for seamless local execution and cloud provider routing. Built with Rust & C++.

cls.summary: Sipp is a high-performance, zero-dependency WebGPU runtime and SDK for running GGUF LLM models in the browser, desktop and edge with a unified API for local and cloud inference.
cls.what_it_does: Sipp provides a unified SDK and runtime (Sipp Engine) that runs GGUF-format LLMs locally in WebGPU/WASM or via a cloud gateway, exposing the same client API for local and remote endpoints. It is used to build browser, Node.js, desktop and edge applications that want low-latency on-device inference and seamless routing to cloud providers; notable points are its WebGPU-first runtime, Rust/C++ core and emphasis on minimal memory footprint and fast startup.
cls.trl_rationale: The project is well documented, provides multiple language bindings (browser SDK, Node, Rust, Python) and publishes benchmarks, showing a working runtime and ecosystem; however the repository is only ~8 months old so it lacks the longer track record and wide adoption required for TRL 7+. Active development and examples support a beta-level judgement.
prerequisites: Rust toolchain for native builds (cargo) if building from source
student_project_ideas: Build a web demo that runs a small GGUF model in-browser using Sipp to provide contextual help for a simple engineering CAD viewer and measure latency/UX trade-offs versus server inference.
Integrate Sipp in a data‑logging pipeline (Node.js) to run local model inference on edge-collected sensor text data, then compare privacy and latency against cloud-only inference.

tools.name: rawwerks/VibeCAD
tools.desc: A library of Claude Code skills for teaching coding agents how to use various CAD tools

tools.name: bydtesla1609/intent-debugger
tools.desc: Turn vague product or feature ideas into clear, checkable requirements before planning or coding—mapping rough descriptions to professional terms, exposing ambiguities, and aligning goals, flows, and boundaries. 这是一个需求澄清 Skill：把说不清的想法整理成一份清晰、可核对的需求清单，在执行任务前对齐目标、流程与边界等。

cls.summary: Intent Debugger is an open-source AI 'skill' that turns informal product or feature ideas into a structured, checkable requirements draft by extracting goals, flows, constraints and asking targeted clarification questions.
cls.what_it_does: Intent Debugger takes free‑form, vague descriptions of desired behaviour and produces a structured requirements checklist with identified ambiguities and specific clarification questions; it is used as a skill/plugin for AI clients (Codex, Claude Code, DeepSeek) rather than a standalone modelling tool. It is notable for focusing only on alignment and requirement clarification (not planning or design) and for adapters to multiple AI clients.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository is detailed and provides adapters and packaged skill zip with usage examples, showing early adoption (stars, downloads) and automated checks, but it is only 88 days old so maturity is limited and longer track record is absent; that supports an alpha-in-use TRL 5.
prerequisites: familiarity with the target AI client (Codex, Claude Code or DeepSeek) and how to install user skills
ability to provide clear example scenarios in natural language (Chinese or English)
student_project_ideas: Use Intent Debugger to generate a requirements checklist for a small capstone feature (e.g. team knowledge base UI) and compare the completeness and ambiguity rates against a manually created requirements document.
Create an integration that runs Intent Debugger as a pre-step in a student CI pipeline: automatically generate the requirement draft from a user story, then compare subsequent PRs for scope drift.

tools.name: houmahani/codrops-depth-gallery
tools.desc: A Three.js depth gallery where images shape their own environment, mood-driven GLSL backgrounds, parallax motion, and velocity-reactive effects.

tools.name: xianyu110/awesome-claude-opus-5.5
tools.desc: Best Claude Opus 5.5 video & visual demos, curated with prompts · 149 精选可视化案例 + 1019 完整清单（游戏/3D/动效/讲解/可视化）

cls.summary: A curated, searchable catalogue of video and visual demos made with Claude Opus 5.5, collecting posts, authors, likes and available prompts.
cls.what_it_does: This repository is an 'awesome' curated list that collects 491 highlighted Claude Opus 5.5 visual and video demos (from a larger set of ~1,019 posts) with links, authors, likes and many reproduced prompts. It is used as a discovery and reference resource to inspect examples and copy or adapt the prompts and demos; notable for its large, hand-curated index and links to an archived gallery and a Skilloop preview site.
cls.trl_rationale: The repository is a recently created (≈50 days old) curated index rather than a production tool; it has good README content and an archived gallery but no evidence of production deployments or long-term community adoption, so it matches early-alpha maturity.
student_project_ideas: Recreate one of the listed Three.js/WebGL demos from its prompt and reference, and document the prompt-to-artifact workflow, comparing the prompt variations that appear in the list.

Use the curated motion-graphics prompts as a starting point to produce a short explainer video pipeline (design -> prompts -> assets) and evaluate how well Claude Opus 5.5 + local tools integrate into the media production workflow.

tools.name: antzGames/OpenVAT-for-Godot
tools.desc: OpenVAT for Godot + Animated MultimeshInstance3D support

cls.summary: A Godot 4 plugin that adds OpenVAT Vertex Animation Texture playback and an Animated MultiMeshInstance3D node for efficient GPU-driven instanced mesh animation.
cls.what_it_does: This plugin imports OpenVAT output from Blender (glb, EXR VAT texture and JSON metadata) and provides shaders and an OpenVATMultiMeshInstance3D node to play vertex-animation-texture (VAT) animations on the GPU, including per-instance track selection and alpha control. It is used inside Godot projects to render complex mesh deformations and large numbers of animated instances efficiently, and is notable for adding easy instanced animation support and HTML build compatibility.
cls.trl_rationale: The repository is an active, working Godot plugin with demos, multiple releases in the roadmap, and 124 stars, indicating an engaged user base, but it is under one year old (created 2026-03-30) so it fits a beta-level maturity rather than long-term production track record.
prerequisites: Blender with OpenVAT extension (for baking VATs)
basic shader and Godot scene knowledge
student_project_ideas: Create a Godot scene that visualises instanced debris using OpenVATMultiMeshInstance3D to demonstrate real-time destruction visuals and measure GPU performance versus skinned meshes.

Bake simulated FEA or procedural deformation frames in Blender with OpenVAT, import into Godot and build an interactive viewer that plays different deformation tracks per instance for validation and presentation.

tools.name: striderZA/OpenCodeGameStudios
tools.desc: Agentic game development taken to the next level: plan, build and test across major engines with any coding agent🤖

cls.summary: OpenCode Game Studios is an open-source framework that orchestrates many specialised coding agents to plan, design and build games across multiple agent platforms and game engines.
cls.what_it_does: It provides a structured, plugin‑based pipeline of agents and skills to manage the game development lifecycle (concept, design, architecture, implementation and release) and can run on multiple agent runtimes (OpenCode, Pi, oh-my-pi, Claude Code, Codex). It is used as a local/CLI framework to generate agent files, commands and plugins and to coordinate agent tasks such as GDD creation, asset specs and engine-specific code generation; what makes it notable is the large, role‑divided agent set (~52 agents) and multi‑harness compatibility across several coding-agent platforms and engines.
cls.trl_rationale: The repository is actively developed with ports to several agent runtimes, example/demo game (OCGS-Pong), tests and 124 stars, indicating early community use; however it is under 1 year old (created 2026-04-29) so it fits a beta-level maturity rather than long-term production proven (TRL 6).
prerequisites: familiarity with OpenCode, Pi or other coding-agent runtimes (or Claude Code/Codex)
basic command-line experience and optional knowledge of target engines (Godot/Unity)
student_project_ideas: Use OCGS to generate a simple Pong or platformer project for Godot, then extend/modify an agent's skill to alter gameplay mechanics and evaluate the quality of generated code and assets.

Build a small CI workflow that runs OCGS-driven agent tests to automatically generate, compile and run unit/behaviour tests for a Unity or Godot prototype, measuring how agent changes affect test pass rates.

tools.name: Arcomade/BlendCap
tools.desc: Single video performance capture tool for blender

cls.summary: BlendCap is a Blender add-on that converts a single ordinary video into full-body, hand and facial animation which is retargeted onto Blender rigs.
cls.what_it_does: BlendCap performs markerless single-camera performance capture: it runs body+hand reconstruction and face landmark extraction on a video, post-processes and cleans the motion, and exports/retargets the result to Blender rigs (Rigify, Auto-Rig Pro, Mixamo and custom rigs). It is used as a Blender add-on that runs locally (GPU-accelerated with CPU fallback) and is notable for combining whole-body, finger and facial capture in one pipeline and for producing BVH retargets inside Blender.
cls.trl_rationale: The repository is well-documented, includes full docs, dependencies and an active paid distribution with bundled installer, and shows GPU-accelerated pipelines — indicating beta-level maturity. However the repo is only ~8 months old so it lacks the multi-year track record or wide-adoption evidence needed for TRL 7+.
prerequisites: basic familiarity with installing Blender add-ons and Python environments
GPU (NVIDIA recommended) or willingness to use a slower CPU fallback
student_project_ideas: Compare retargeted motion from BlendCap against keyframe animation in Blender by capturing a short demo clip and quantifying differences in joint trajectories and timing; produce a short pipeline that applies smoothing and foot-lock improvements and evaluates user-perceived quality.

Integrate BlendCap capture outputs with a simple robot simulator (e.g. convert BVH to a robot joint sequence) to evaluate using human performance traces as input for teleoperation or imitation learning experiments.

tools.name: dadwritestech/LlamaForge
tools.desc: Open-source control panel for the real llama.cpp: see where a model lands in your VRAM before loading, every llama-server flag per model, one-click llama.cpp updates, several models at once, and Embers (local agents whose quotes are checked by code). Windows · Linux · macOS.

cls.summary: LlamaForge is an open-source browser control panel that installs, configures and runs upstream llama.cpp servers and helps you discover, benchmark and manage local GGUF models on your machine.
cls.what_it_does: LlamaForge provides a web-based dashboard that discovers models on disk, rates whether they fit your GPU, exposes every llama-server flag per model, and drives upstream llama.cpp builds for chat and inference. It includes features for multi-model placement, Auto-Forge automated performance tuning, blind model Arena comparisons, phone remote access and local agent (Embers) tasks, all while leaving model files and the official engine in place.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository is active with 124 stars, multiple releases referenced in the README (v0.17.0) and CI passing on multiple OSes, indicating a beta-quality project; however the repo is ~134 days old (younger than one year) so it does not yet show long-term production adoption required for TRL 7+.
prerequisites: llama.cpp builds and familiarity with GPU drivers (CUDA/Metal)
comfort running local servers and command-line tools
student_project_ideas: Use LlamaForge to benchmark and compare several GGUF models (from Hugging Face) on a lab's GPU cluster, record Auto-Forge optimisation choices and present a report analysing trade-offs between latency, VRAM footprint and generation quality.

Integrate LlamaForge with an assignment that requires students to deploy a local llama.cpp-based agent (Embers), then measure reliability and safety behaviours by automated tests and compare results across model configurations.

tools.name: syfr512/SweetrollLM
tools.desc: Local-first AI chat client combining SillyTavern-style character cards, LM Studio-style GGUF model management, Ollama/OpenAI-compatible APIs, and an agentic workspace.

cls.summary: SweetrollLM is a local-first desktop/web AI chat client that combines character-based roleplay chat, GGUF model management, Ollama/OpenAI-compatible APIs and an agentic workspace for running automation and file-aware agents.
cls.what_it_does: SweetrollLM lets users run chat-based interactions with local GGUF models, an embedded KoboldCPP fallback, or cloud APIs while managing provider profiles and per-chat memory; it also provides an agentic workspace capable of inspecting and running files, executing terminal commands, and managing background services. It is notable for adaptive inference routing (attempting native llama-cpp-python loading, falling back to a headless KoboldCPP worker), Ollama runtime integration, and local-first storage of models and provider profiles.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository is 165 days old (younger than one year) so TRL is capped; the project shows a functioning product with install scripts, documented features, and >100 stars indicating early adoption, but there are no indications of long-term production deployments or stable versioned releases in the README.
prerequisites: basic command-line experience (Windows .bat used in docs)
local LLM model files (.gguf) or access to cloud API keys
student_project_ideas: Build a lab exercise comparing inference latency, memory usage and output quality between native llama-cpp-python GGUF loading and the KoboldCPP fallback on constrained hardware using SweetrollLM as the frontend.

Extend the agentic workspace with a sandboxed dataset inspection tool that integrates SweetrollLM chats with a simple file-based test harness to evaluate automated code repair suggestions on sample repositories.

tools.name: Sam-AEC/aec-model-bridge
tools.desc: Open-source Revit MCP server: let Claude and other AI assistants read and edit BIM models, with human approval on every change.

tools.name: bakiraa/qyvaria-hardlogic-kernel-engine
tools.desc: Top Open-Source AI Engineering Platform 2026 Qyvaria Kernel

cls.summary: SentinelCore is an oversight engine that enforces deterministic, auditable constraints on agentic AI runtimes and logs decisions to an immutable ledger for governance and compliance.
cls.what_it_does: SentinelCore provides a hard-logic constraint engine (SentinelScript) that compiles to bytecode and runs in an isolated sandbox to enforce rules on AI agents in real time, while recording actions and audits in a tamper-evident ledger. It is used alongside the Qyvaria kernel and local agents to add deterministic vetoes, cross-validation between agent instances, and reproducible governance for decentralized or edge AI deployments.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository is active with many stars and recent commits but is only ~142 days old and lacks evidence of stable releases or broad production deployments; README describes ambitious capabilities but shows a project at early alpha/alpha-in-use stage.
prerequisites: familiarity with agent-based AI concepts and runtimes
basic understanding of cryptographic ledgers and sandboxing concepts
student_project_ideas: Implement a SentinelScript constraint set that enforces GDPR-style data handling for a small Qyvaria agent and measure how constraint enforcement affects model outputs and latency.
Build a lab exercise that integrates a simple agent swarm with SentinelCore instances and demonstrate cross-validation and ledger-based detection of a simulated Sybil attack.

tools.name: jushengzhang/robot-weight-debugging
tools.desc: First release for Can LLMs Debug Robots by Editing Their Weights? Code, 65-row edit, 16 experiment logs and evidence. V2 and real-robot experiments in progress.

cls.summary: Research code that uses large language models to inspect and edit rows of a pretrained robot policy's weights to repair instruction-following failures in simulation.
cls.what_it_does: The repository implements experiments where an LLM proposes sparse edits (65 token-embedding rows) to a pretrained robot policy and evaluates the edited policy via simulator rollouts to repair specific instruction failures without gradient updates or new demonstrations. It provides experiment transcripts, the applied edit payload and scripts to audit the released results, and reproduction notes for running new editing sessions with the required simulator and model assets.
cls.trl_rationale: This is a first research release accompanying an arXiv paper with executed simulation experiments and released transcripts, showing early use by the authors; however the repository is very new (created 8 days ago) and results are simulation-only so maturity is at an alpha/early-adopter research level.
prerequisites: access to pretrained policy model weights (PyTorch-style)
simulator assets and environment configuration (LIBERO-Plus / task simulator)
GPU recommended for running full experiments
student_project_ideas: Reproduce a single editing session from the repository and measure how the 65-row edit changes policy behaviour on a small set of held-out instructions, then visualise differences in action distributions before and after the edit.

Extend the workflow by integrating a different pretrained policy (compatible architecture) and evaluate whether the LLM-proposed sparse edits transfer or need adaptation, reporting successes and regressions across several instruction categories.

tools.name: ringhyacinth/Meow-Generator
tools.desc: A playful procedural 3D kitten generator built with Three.js.

cls.summary: A browser-based procedural 3D kitten generator that creates editable, SDF-built cat models with physics toys, animations and PNG/GLB export.
cls.what_it_does: Meow Generator procedurally builds 3D cat models from a seed and editable parameters using signed distance fields (SDFs), renders them in the browser with Three.js and provides physics-interactive toys, motion sampling and export to GLB/PNG. It is used as a local, client-side creative tool (no backend) notable for SDF-based body generation, integrated Cannon‑es physics, multiple languages and an online demo.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository is a working, publicly demoed web app with tests and active development but is only ~114 days old, has no clear versioned stable releases or known production adopters; this supports an alpha-in-use level (TRL 5). README is detailed which increases confidence but age limits a higher TRL.
prerequisites: Node.js and npm for local development
student_project_ideas: Extend the SDF-based mesh generator to produce other stylised animals and evaluate mesh quality and export (GLB) for use in a simple WebXR scene.
Measure performance and memory of SDF meshing and physics on mobile devices by profiling the app, then optimise LOD or implement GPU-based meshing for better mobile framerates.

tools.name: StarKnightt/operation-ironhold
tools.desc: A complete first-person shooter in a single 290 KB HTML file. No build step, no assets, no dependencies beyond three.js from a CDN.

cls.summary: A single-file, browser-based first-person shooter implemented with three.js and procedurally generated assets and audio.
cls.what_it_does: Operation Ironhold is a complete FPS that runs from one HTML file: it generates all geometry, textures and audio at runtime and uses three.js from a CDN for rendering. It is notable for being self-contained (no external assets or build step) and for demonstrating procedural content, simple AI, and Web Audio synthesis inside a compact demo.
cls.trl_rationale: The repo is a working, playable demo with a hosted demo, active commits and community interest (123 stars), but it is under 1 year old (114 days) and lacks evidence of production use or multiple stable releases, so beta-level maturity is appropriate.
prerequisites: modern desktop browser with WebGL and Pointer Lock support
basic JavaScript and three.js familiarity to modify
student_project_ideas: Modify the procedural level generator to add new obstacle types and measure how spawn/cover changes affect enemy engagement behaviour (combine with simple data logging).
Replace or extend the AI director to implement different combat-director rules (e.g. varying max simultaneous shooters) and evaluate player performance/complexity across runs.

tools.name: poisonxa16/pxa
tools.desc: The set-and-forget LLM engine for Pascal and Volta: PXQ codec + kernels, auto-tuned per card. Ready-to-run PXQ models in MODELS.md; benchmarks vs llama.cpp in the README.

cls.summary: PXA is a local LLM inference engine optimised for older NVIDIA Pascal and Volta GPUs (Tesla P100, V100, GTX 10-series) that provides PXQ/PXQN quant formats, an OpenAI-style local server API and a browser control UI for running and tuning models on those cards.
cls.what_it_does: PXA runs language models on Pascal/Volta-class NVIDIA GPUs using its own PXQ/PXQN quant formats and hand-tuned CUDA kernels to maximise throughput and reduce memory use. It launches a local server with an OpenAI-compatible API (and a browser GUI) that auto-selects per-card settings and supports multi-GPU tensor splits, speculation decoding and on-device quant encoding.
cls.trl_rationale: The project is actively developed with release tarballs, benchmarks and an interface (evidence in the README) and has community interest (stars), but the repository is only 71 days old so it lacks the multi-release, multi-user track record required for TRL 6+.
prerequisites: CUDA-capable driver/runtime (bundled runtimes are provided but familiarity with GPU launch options helps)
basic Linux or container usage; optional knowledge of GGUF model files
student_project_ideas: Measure and compare inference throughput and token-per-second cost between a PXQ-quantized model run with PXA and the same GGUF model run with llama.cpp on a V100, and produce a report explaining the performance differences and how quant choice affects quality.

Extend a simple robotics conversational agent to use a locally hosted PXA server as the language backend, integrating sensor telemetry via a small MQTT broker to demonstrate on-device language-in-the-loop behaviour for constrained GPU hardware.

tools.name: ranrhuang/NAS3R
tools.desc: [CVPR 2026] From None to All: Self-Supervised 3D Reconstruction via Novel View Synthesis

cls.summary: NAS3R is an open-source research codebase that performs self-supervised 3D reconstruction from images using novel-view synthesis and Gaussian splatting without requiring ground-truth 3D labels or camera poses.
cls.what_it_does: NAS3R trains feed-forward models to jointly learn explicit 3D geometry (via Gaussian splats representation) and camera parameters from multi-view images using self-supervision and novel-view synthesis. It is used by preparing datasets, running the provided training and evaluation scripts, and can load pre-trained checkpoints hosted on Hugging Face. The project is notable for being pose-free and prior-free (claims no pretrained 3D priors needed) and for providing reproducible training/evaluation code and checkpoints tied to a CVPR 2026 paper.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository implements a CVPR 2026 method, provides training/evaluation scripts and pretrained checkpoints on Hugging Face, and has community interest (stars). However the project is under 1 year old (created 2026-03-29), so there is not yet a long track record of production use, which limits TRL to ~6 (beta).
prerequisites: familiarity with deep learning and multi-view geometry
student_project_ideas: Compare NAS3R reconstructions with a NeRF and a Gaussian-splatting baseline on a small multi-view dataset (e.g. synthetic or a subset of RealEstate10K) and quantify reconstruction quality and pose estimation accuracy.
Extend NAS3R to fuse sparse LiDAR scans with image inputs (combine with a point-cloud processing library) and evaluate improvements in geometry accuracy on indoor scenes.

tools.name: cvg/VIGS-SLAM
tools.desc: [ECCV'26] VIGS-SLAM: Visual Inertial Gaussian Splatting SLAM

cls.summary: VIGS‑SLAM is a visual‑inertial SLAM system that tracks camera motion from RGB+IMU input while building a high‑fidelity 3D Gaussian‑splat map in real time.
cls.what_it_does: VIGS‑SLAM fuses video frames and IMU readings to estimate camera trajectory and simultaneously reconstruct a dense 3D scene representation using Gaussian splatting. It is used as research / prototype SLAM software with Docker and Conda setups, optional CUDA/TensorRT acceleration and a C++ IMU module for speed; notable for combining visual‑inertial odometry with Gaussian‑splat 3D reconstruction and providing pretrained priors and demo tools.
cls.trl_rationale: The repo accompanies an ECCV'26 paper and provides demos, pretrained models, Docker, and build instructions, indicating beyond-prototype maturity; however the project is only ~4.5 months old so lacks the long track record and wide adoption needed for TRL7+, placing it at TRL6 (beta).
prerequisites: C++ toolchain and CMake for optional IMU module
student_project_ideas: Evaluate VIGS‑SLAM mapping accuracy on a handheld iPhone sequence and compare the resulting Gaussian splat reconstruction against a COLMAP/NeRF pipeline for the same scene.
Integrate the VIGS‑SLAM output with a simple ROS2 node to provide live pose and dense map updates for a small mobile robot, then perform navigation trials in a mapped environment.

tools.name: ybouane/flashraw
tools.desc: Fast, memory-safe camera RAW decoder in Rust: ~40 formats, SIMD, GPU, WebAssembly, ICC colour management. CLI, C, C++, Python and JavaScript bindings.

cls.summary: FlashRaw is a Rust-written, memory-safe camera RAW decoder that provides sensor data, metadata and ready-to-display sRGB images with multi-threading, SIMD and WebAssembly / GPU support.
cls.what_it_does: FlashRaw decodes camera RAW files (about 40 formats) to sensor data, embedded previews or display-ready sRGB images and exposes bindings for C/C++, Python and JavaScript. It focuses on speed and safety using Rust, SIMD, multi-core and optional GPU/WebAssembly acceleration, and includes tools/benchmarks and a browser demo. Notable points are its published packages (crates.io, PyPI, npm), extensive benchmarks vs LibRaw/rawpy/RawSpeed, and claimed use in browser applications.
cls.trl_rationale: The project is young (created 46 days ago) which normally limits TRL, but the README shows published packages (crates.io, PyPI, npm), a live demo and named projects using the WebAssembly package in production (LightFlow, ImageFlow). These indicate it is beyond toy proof-of-concept but still new, so a Beta-level TRL 6 is justified.
prerequisites: basic image processing concepts (RAW, demosaic, colour spaces)
optional: WebAssembly / WebGPU basics for browser use
student_project_ideas: Build a small web application that loads RAW files in the browser using FlashRaw's WebAssembly package and implements interactive exposure/white-balance sliders.

Benchmark and visualise decoding speed and memory usage of FlashRaw versus LibRaw/rawpy on a curated set of camera RAW files, and produce a report explaining differences by format and hardware (CPU vs WASM/GPU).

tools.name: Surajkumar5050/zyron-assistant
tools.desc: ⚡ A local, privacy-focused AI desktop assistant for Windows. Control your PC remotely via Telegram or locally with Voice commands. Powered by Ollama.

tools.name: BrightbeamAI/chap
tools.desc: CHAP, the Collaborative Human Agent Protocol, is a MCP/A2A-compatible runtime for auditable human-agent work: approvals, overrides, handoffs, escalation and verifiable evidence logs.

cls.summary: CHAP is an open protocol and reference runtime that records and governs human decisions (approvals, overrides, handoffs, escalations) over autonomous agents with an auditable, tamper-evident log.
cls.what_it_does: CHAP defines a coordinator-based protocol for structured human–agent interactions so agent outputs, human decisions and their rationales are recorded as verifiable audit entries. It is provided as reference coordinators in Python and TypeScript that you can run as a server or embed in processes to enforce workspace rules, profiles and produce a chained audit log.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository is ~6 months old and README states CHAP is at public draft 0.3 with reference Python/TypeScript coordinators and a differential fuzzer; usable by early adopters but pre-1.0 breaking changes are expected, so it's at an alpha/in-use stage (TRL 5).
prerequisites: understanding of MCP/A2A or multi-agent concepts
basic knowledge of audit logs and cryptographic hashes
student_project_ideas: Build a small agent pipeline (using an LLM agent via LangChain or similar) that routes drafts through a CHAP coordinator and implements approve/override flows, then analyse the audit log to produce metrics on overrides and rationale tags.

Integrate CHAP with a simulated robot control loop (ROS or a Gazebo test) so human operators can approve or override autonomous actions and produce an auditable trace for verification and safety analysis.

tools.name: rlxai/rbot
tools.desc: An open-source end-to-end Autonomous Mobile Robot simulation stack for ROS 2 Jazzy and Gazebo Harmonic.

cls.summary: rbot is an open-source ROS 2 Gazebo simulation stack that provides a complete mapping-to-navigation Autonomous Mobile Robot (AMR) reference workspace for ROS 2 Jazzy and Gazebo Harmonic.
cls.what_it_does: rbot packages a simulation-first AMR reference stack including URDF/Xacro robot description, Gazebo worlds, ros2_control, sensor simulation, EKF/AMCL localization, SLAM Toolbox mapping and Nav2 navigation with example configs and launch files. It is used as a Docker-first ROS 2 workspace to run mapping, teleoperation, and autonomous navigation demos and to serve as a baseline that teams can inspect and adapt. The project is notable for integrating a full mapping-to-navigation path, Docker workflows, and modern Nav2 configurations for ROS 2 Jazzy with Gazebo Harmonic support.
cls.trl_rationale: The repository is active with CI, documentation, Docker workflows, example maps and launch files and a clear workspace layout, indicating a beta-level project; however it is younger than one year (created 192 days ago) so lacks the longer track record required for TRL 7+.
student_project_ideas: Implement and evaluate a custom Nav2 behavior tree and MPPI controller tuning for a warehouse scenario using rbot's Gazebo world and compare path quality and timing against the default configuration.

Extend the rbot workspace to add a ROS 2 node that fuses an additional simulated sensor (e.g. 3-D LiDAR) into the existing SLAM Toolbox/EKF pipeline and measure localization accuracy on generated maps.

tools.name: jinwoolee1230/POLI
tools.desc: [RSS 2026] Learning Point Cloud Geometry as a Statistical Manifold: Theory and Practice

cls.summary: POLI is a self-supervised neural method that predicts a Gaussian ellipsoid per LiDAR point to represent local geometry and improve downstream 3D perception tasks like registration, pose estimation and odometry.
cls.what_it_does: POLI learns per-point local geometry by predicting Gaussian ellipsoids on a statistical manifold using a self-supervised deep network. It is used as a preprocessing / feature module that plugs into existing 3D perception pipelines (registration, object pose estimation, LiDAR odometry) to provide richer geometric descriptors without labelled data. Notable points are its self-supervised training, available pretrained checkpoints, and demonstrated improvements reported in RSS 2026 papers.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository accompanies peer-reviewed RSS 2026 papers and provides pretrained checkpoints and working code, indicating substantial development; however the repo is ~6–7 months old (younger than 1 year) so it lacks the longer track record and broad adoption required for TRL 7+, placing it at TRL 6 (beta).
prerequisites: familiarity with point-cloud processing (e.g. ICP, PointNet++)
student_project_ideas: Integrate POLI's per-point ellipsoid outputs with a standard ICP/NDT pipeline and quantitatively compare registration accuracy on KITTI or nuScenes with and without POLI descriptors.

Build a LiDAR odometry pipeline that uses POLI geometric features for frame-to-frame matching and evaluate drift and robustness on a small outdoor dataset, comparing against a baseline odometry (e.g. LOAM or a point-feature odometry).

tools.name: CapriChooms/CapriCore
tools.desc: Capri — an AI desktop companion for Windows with local/API models, Hugging Face, optional voice, memory and permission-based desktop tools.

cls.summary: Capri is a Windows desktop AI companion that runs local or API LLMs, offers voice I/O, memory, and permissioned desktop automation tools.
cls.what_it_does: Capri provides a desktop chat companion for Windows that can use bundled local models, Hugging Face GGUF imports or OpenAI-compatible APIs, with searchable memory, optional speech recognition/voice, and explicit permissioned desktop tools. It is installed via a Windows installer or run from source with Node.js and connects to local runtimes such as llama.cpp; notable features include resource (CPU/GPU) controls, multilingual voice packs and configurable desktop automation with visible safety controls.
cls.trl_rationale: The README and release notes show an installer, documented setup steps and published releases, indicating early adopters and packaged distribution, but the repository is only 9 days old so it lacks the multi-release, long-term production track record needed for higher TRL.
prerequisites: optional: llama.cpp Vulkan runtime for local models
student_project_ideas: Build a small demo that integrates Capri's desktop tools to automate a repeatable desktop workflow (e.g. opening files, taking screenshots) and log the actions for later analysis.
Compare response latency and resource usage between a bundled local GGUF model and an OpenAI-compatible API using Capri's local/API switching, and report trade-offs in a short lab report.

tools.name: jbang2004/long-wind
tools.desc: 长风 Long Wind — a real-time wuxia action game in the browser (three.js). Every line of code written by Claude Opus 5.5; the first playable version in about a day.

cls.summary: Long Wind is a playable, browser-based real-time wuxia action game implemented with three.js and WebGL and produced largely by an AI (Claude Opus 5.5).
cls.what_it_does: The repository implements a third-person action game (three chapters, enemies, bosses, combat mechanics and procedural environments) that runs in the browser with no install. It is used by opening the hosted demo or running the local dev server (npm install / npm run dev); notable aspects include entirely AI-generated code, procedural content, WebAudio synthesis for all sounds, and a single runtime dependency on three.js.
cls.trl_rationale: The project is a working, playable web application with tests and an online demo, but the repository is only ~52 days old so by the provided age-based TRL rules it is capped at TRL 5; README shows active development (build/test instructions) but lacks evidence of long-term production use.

tools.name: LegedsDaD/Simple-The_Game_Engine
tools.desc: Pro‑Ready Python Game Engine

cls.summary: Simple is a lightweight, Python-first game and animation engine with a C++/OpenGL core and a small standalone editor that lets you script and run 3D scenes from Python.
cls.what_it_does: Simple provides a Python API to create, render and interact with 3D scenes (entities like Cube, camera, input, HUD) backed by a C++/OpenGL 3.3 core for performance, and includes a small editor that can open .sim projects and Play-in-Editor. It is used by installing the package (pip) or downloading prebuilt standalone editor zips and running Python examples; it is notable for combining a Python-first workflow with a native C++ rendering core and an included editor.
cls.trl_rationale: The project provides versioned releases (v1.1.1), prebuilt editor binaries for major OSes and a PyPI package which indicates a beta-level maturity and some user uptake, but the repository is only ~220 days old (under one year) so lacks the longer track record required for TRL 7+.
prerequisites: C++ build toolchain for building from source
student_project_ideas: Build a small interactive physics-free scene (player-controlled cube, camera and HUD) using Simple and add keyboard/mouse controls and screenshot logging for a user-interface study.

Create a simple sensor-visualisation for a robotics mockup: simulate robot poses as scene entities and stream their positions from a Python script (or ROS bridge) into Simple to visualise trajectories in real time.

tools.name: SouthpawIN/turbofit
tools.desc: Adaptive local inference for Hermes — One model provider. Every machine. The best local configuration the hardware can safely sustain.

cls.summary: TurboFit is a local-model provider and runtime coordinator for Hermes Agent that automatically picks, loads and yields the largest model your hardware can safely run across multiple inference engines.
cls.what_it_does: TurboFit scans a machine's hardware and maintains a catalog-driven 'fit' ladder so the best-fitting local checkpoint is resident and served via a gateway; it coordinates multiple runtimes (llama.cpp, vLLM, Strata, media runtimes) and adapts to GPU memory pressure by stepping down model context or model size and releasing the card when other applications need it. It is installed as a Hermes plugin and exposes a local HTTP /v1/models API so local inference clients can use the selected runtime without the user managing model files or engines directly.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository is active with 121 stars, regular pushes and installation instructions, and shows integration with Hermes and multiple runtimes, indicating a beta-capable project; however it is only ~148 days old so it lacks the longer track record and wide adoption needed for TRL7+. README is detailed but truncated here.
prerequisites: familiarity with local LLM concepts and runtimes (llama.cpp, vLLM, Strata)
basic systems administration (GPU drivers, model storage, networking)
Hermes Agent usage and plugin configuration
Python tooling familiarity for installation or development
student_project_ideas: Build a lab exercise that measures GPU memory pressure and demonstrates TurboFit switching between model rungs when a synthetic workload (browser tabs or a game) is launched, capturing logs and timelines for analysis.

Extend TurboFit to add a custom fallback policy or integrate an edge device (Raspberry Pi + Jetson) that reports resource telemetry and triggers remote model swaps, demonstrating adaptive inference for constrained devices.

tools.name: moznoazachem/giga-pisar
tools.desc: Гига Писарь: бесплатная локальная русская диктовка для macOS на GigaAM v3. Зажал правый ⌘, сказал, отпустил. Giga Pisar: offline Russian dictation for Mac

cls.summary: Giga Pisar is a free, fully on‑device macOS push-to-talk dictation app for Russian built on the GigaAM v3 model.
cls.what_it_does: The app captures microphone audio when you hold a configurable modifier key, runs on-device speech recognition with the GigaAM v3 model and inserts punctuated, capitalised text at the cursor in any macOS application. It bundles a Swift inference core using onnxruntime and optionally a local LLM (llama.cpp) to post-edit text, and is distributed as a notarized macOS .dmg or built from source.
cls.trl_rationale: The project publishes notarized macOS builds (dmg), provides scripts to install models and to build the app, and has active commits and community interest, indicating a beta-level maturity; however the repository is under one year old so TRL is capped at 6.
prerequisites: Xcode / Command Line Tools to build from source
~204 MB model download for speech model
student_project_ideas: Compare the transcription accuracy, latency and punctuation quality of GigaAM (via Giga Pisar) and Whisper on a curated Russian speech dataset, and produce a report with example failure modes.

Extend the app to add a simple plugin that logs transcriptions (with user consent) to a local time-series file and visualises word-level timing, demonstrating on-device data pipelines for UX evaluation.

tools.name: Zyphra/ZONOS3-Mini
tools.desc: compact zero-shot voice-cloning TTS with state-of-the-art performance, leading voice control, real-time on-device.

cls.summary: ZONOS3-Mini is an open-source inference runtime and server stack for a compact zero-shot multilingual text-to-speech model that supports on-device and browser playback.
cls.what_it_does: The repository provides HTTP servers, an offline Python API and an in-browser WebGPU runtime to run the ZONOS3-Mini voice-cloning TTS model locally or in the browser. It solves the problem of producing high-quality, real-time voice synthesis and voice cloning on a range of hardware (GPU, Apple Silicon, CPU/ggml, or WebGPU) and is notable for multiple backend implementations (CUDA/PyTorch, ggml/C++, MLX, and a WebGPU studio) and an OpenAI-compatible HTTP API.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository is very new (created 19 days ago) but already provides multiple backend implementations, an API, and downloadable weights; that indicates early alpha/alpha-in-use maturity but not a long production track record, so TRL 5 is appropriate.
student_project_ideas: Build a local web demo that integrates the ZONOS3-Mini WebGPU studio with a simple front-end to demonstrate offline voice cloning and measure latency on different devices.

Integrate the offline Python API with a small robotics or accessibility prototype (e.g., a voice-enabled robot or assistive reader) and evaluate real-time performance and voice-cloning fidelity on edge hardware.

tools.name: IvanMurzak/Unity-AI-Animation
tools.desc: MCP Tools for Unity Animation — create and edit clips and animators with AI.

tools.name: fraisasghar/CAD-and-Simulation-of-Baffled-Shell-and-Tube-Heat-Exchanger
tools.desc: CAD modeling and COMSOL simulation of a shell and tube heat exchanger featuring internal tubes and multiple baffle plates, with fluid flowing through the tubes and across the shell side around the baffles to analyze thermal performance and flow behavior.

tools.name: davide-troiani/moeshift
tools.desc: Memory efficient and high performance Mixture-of-Experts inference for Apple Silicon

cls.summary: MoEShift is a local Mixture‑of‑Experts (MoE) inference runtime optimised for Apple Silicon that runs large GGUF models with reduced memory use so you can perform inference on Macs with ~10 GB of RAM.
cls.what_it_does: MoEShift provides a high‑performance, memory‑efficient inference server for MoE-style LLMs on Apple Silicon, using SSD‑backed expert storage, expert scheduling and Metal execution to reduce peak RAM. It is used as a local OpenAI‑compatible inference endpoint and installs via Homebrew; notable features are its Apple Silicon optimisations and measured benchmarks against alternatives.
cls.trl_rationale: The README states this is an Alpha release and the repository is very new (created 27 days ago). It includes benchmarks and a Homebrew package which indicate early adopters and working runtime, but lacks a long track record or stable releases required for TRL 6+.
prerequisites: knowledge of GGUF models and LLM deployment
student_project_ideas: Build a small local chat application that runs on a Mac mini using MoEShift as the backend and evaluate latency/memory trade-offs for different configuration settings and quantizations.

Compare MoEShift and another local runtime (e.g. Strata or llama.cpp) on an Apple Silicon machine by running benchmark scripts, collecting memory/throughput data, and writing a report on scheduling and SSD caching impacts.

tools.name: mattn/tensai
tools.desc: A tiny neural-network framework in pure Go with AVX2 SIMD kernels (GOEXPERIMENT=simd)

cls.summary: tensai is a compact, pure-Go machine-learning framework with autograd, SIMD-accelerated kernels, optional WebGPU backend, and model utilities (quantization, tokenizers, image/audio/text pipelines).
cls.what_it_does: tensai provides tensors, layers, autograd, optimizers and training loops in pure Go, with optional AVX2/NEON SIMD kernels and an experimental WebGPU backend for acceleration. It includes model loading, quantization, and end-to-end examples (text embeddings, image and audio pipelines), making it notable for being a self-contained Go ML stack without cgo.
cls.trl_rationale: The README and documentation are detailed and the project has active commits and community interest (120 stars), but the repository is very young (~90 days) so there is not yet a long track record or multiple stable releases; this points to an alpha/in-use maturity (TRL 5).
prerequisites: familiarity with basic ML concepts (tensors, autograd, optimizers)
optional: GPU native wgpu library available at runtime for WebGPU backend
student_project_ideas: Implement and train a small transformer for text embeddings using tensai, then build a simple nearest-neighbour search service that serves embeddings over an HTTP API.
Compare CPU SIMD, WebGPU-resident and quantized (int8/int4) performance/accuracy by porting a small image classifier to tensai and measuring throughput and memory/accuracy trade-offs.

tools.name: eliautobot/my-virtual-world
tools.desc: A living 3D city for your AI agents, self-hosted. Bring OpenClaw and Hermes agents, connect a Grok Bot, or build agents on any AI model: they get homes, jobs, a PC and phones in a world you share with them.

cls.summary: A self‑hosted, browser-based 3D city that runs many AI agents which live, work and interact in a shared virtual world.
cls.what_it_does: My Virtual World provides a living 3D city where AI agents are instantiated as residents with homes, jobs, schedules, devices and memories; agents can be connected from existing platforms (OpenClaw, Hermes, MCP apps) or built on any AI model. It is used by running the server (Docker or Node.js) and visiting the WebGL client to observe, interact with and manage agents, and it is notable for integrating multi-agent orchestration with a detailed in-world agent ‘PC’, phones and a large library of ready 3D assets.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository is active with documentation, Docker and native install instructions, and 120 stars, indicating an organised project beyond a minimal demo; however it was created ~157 days ago and lacks a long production track record or versioned releases, so maturity fits a beta-level TRL 6.
prerequisites: Docker and container basics (if using docker compose)
API keys or local model server if connecting external AI models
student_project_ideas: Extend an agent's 'PC' workflow to perform automated data collection and analysis: connect an agent to a sensor data stream (simulated or real) and implement a task that uses the agent to detect an anomaly and notify other agents via the in-world phone system.

Measure emergent behaviour by running experiments with different agent personality parameters: script cohorts of agents with varied decision rules and visualise population-level metrics (traffic, economics, work patterns) over time, exporting results for statistical analysis.

tools.name: Yoosseph/dental-scope
tools.desc: Explore teeth, jaws, nerves, tissues, root canals, cross-sections and layered dental structures in 3D.

cls.summary: Dental Scope is a browser-based interactive 3D explorer of dental anatomy that lets users navigate from whole-mouth views down to layered internal tooth anatomy and cross-sections.
cls.what_it_does: Dental Scope provides an interactive web viewer for dental anatomy allowing selection, dissection, cross-sections and labelled exploration of all 32 permanent teeth and associated jaws, nerves and tissues. It is used as an educational anatomical reference delivered as a static web app (Vite/React/Three.js) with streamed glTF assets and internationalised text. It is notable for a continuous scene (mouth→tooth→tissue), multi-level dissections, per-structure metadata about data provenance, and rich UI features like search, deep links and language support.
cls.trl_rationale: The repository is a well-developed, tested static web app with CI, unit and E2E tests, a production build and Vercel deployment instructions, but it is very new (created 53 days ago) so it lacks the multi-year track record or broad production adoption required for higher TRL.
prerequisites: Node.js / npm for building and running locally
student_project_ideas: Add annotation and assessment layers so students can tag anatomical features and submit a short quiz that grades identification accuracy using the existing selection API.
Integrate the viewer with a simple AR/webXR wrapper (e.g. model placement via WebXR) to explore scaled dental models in physical space and measure anatomical dimensions programmatically.

tools.name: Daturaxoxo/Aurora
tools.desc: Lightweight Mod Manager and Mod Platform for Anime Games.

cls.summary: Aurora is a lightweight, cross-platform mod manager and launcher for Unreal Engine anime games that loads PAK, Lua and DLL mods and provides a desktop UI for managing them.
cls.what_it_does: Aurora helps users install, organize and launch game mods for Unreal Engine 5 games by loading PAK files, Lua scripts and .asi DLL mods and offering features like grouping, bulk actions, automatic updates for GameBanana installs and a built-in screenshot manager. It is a Rust application with a Slint GUI and provides installers/portable builds for Windows and a native AppImage for Linux, plus tools for mod authors such as metadata (mod.json) support.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository is 188 days old, has active commits, releases and a functioning installer/AppImage and a modest user base (120 stars), indicating an active beta-level project; age (<1 year) limits the TRL to 6 despite usable builds and platform support.
prerequisites: familiarity with game modding concepts (PAK, ASI, Lua)
basic Rust toolchain if building from source
student_project_ideas: Create a small mod packaging pipeline that produces mod.json metadata and automated GameBanana-compatible version updates, then integrate it with Aurora to test install/update flows.

Build a UI plugin or addon for Aurora (or fork a small feature) that adds a custom filter or batch operation and demonstrate cross-platform packaging and distribution using the provided AppImage/installer.

tools.name: nickzsche21/AirClaw
tools.desc: Run OpenClaw on a local model. Zero API cost. One OpenAI-compatible endpoint over Ollama, llama.cpp, vLLM or LM Studio — plus AirLLM for models bigger than your GPU.

tools.name: wladimiravila/esp32s3-distributed-ai
tools.desc: Distributed 56M-parameter LLM inference across 3 ESP32-S3 boards via ESP-NOW , Split-PLE + KV cache, fully offline.

cls.summary: A proof-of-concept that runs a 56M-parameter language model distributed across three ESP32‑S3 microcontrollers using ESP‑NOW and a split PLE + KV cache to enable offline LLM inference.
cls.what_it_does: This project partitions a quantized 56M-parameter transformer across three ESP32‑S3 boards so the boards cooperatively perform LLM inference over an ESP‑NOW mesh while one board serves a web UI. It implements split per-layer embeddings (Split‑PLE), an on‑device KV cache in PSRAM, a small HTTP/SSE frontend on one board, and a custom ESP‑NOW protocol to exchange tokens, PLE rows and hidden states. It is notable because it demonstrates multi‑board distributed inference and practical engineering details (memory splits, packet protocol, KV caching) for constrained microcontrollers.
cls.trl_rationale: The README describes a working distributed inference system with end-to-end flow, hardware details and examples; repository is functional and has community interest (120 stars) but is only ~110 days old so it lacks a long track record or multiple stable releases, limiting TRL to beta (6).
prerequisites: knowledge of quantized neural networks and transformer inference
familiarity with ESP‑NOW/WiFi and serial debugging
student_project_ideas: Extend the repository to add a logging and metrics pipeline (over WiFi to a local server) to measure end‑to‑end latency and packet loss effects on generation quality and throughput.
Port the Split‑PLE + KV cache approach to two different ESP32 board variants and compare memory, latency and energy tradeoffs; report design decisions and automated tests for V&V.

tools.name: Abhinesh2004/mirage-cortex
tools.desc: Top Agent Swarm Simulation Tools for LLM World Modeling 2026

cls.summary: RealmForge is an open-source platform for running persistent, LLM-powered swarms of generative agents that interact via a shared Structured World Model to produce emergent narratives and simulated societies.
cls.what_it_does: RealmForge orchestrates large numbers of LLM-driven agents that read from and write to a queryable world graph (the Structured World Model) so that agent actions, memories and relationships persist across ticks and sessions. It is used as a simulation engine: a World Conductor advances epochs, agents act according to persona scripts and state vectors, and a Chronicler records events; notable features include world persistence, perception radii, a narrative market for plot emergence, and configurable backend stores.
cls.trl_rationale: The README describes a substantial, modular architecture and the repo has activity and community interest (120 stars, active pushes), but the project is only ~142 days old, has no indicated stable releases or long track record, so maturity maps to a beta-level TRL.
prerequisites: familiarity with LLM APIs and prompt design
experience with backend services (datastores like SQLite/Redis) and web stacks
comfort with running modular server software (Docker/containers helpful)
student_project_ideas: Build a small persistent world with 10–20 agents that model a resource economy (resources, merchants, consumers) and evaluate emergent market behaviours over simulated epochs, comparing outcomes when agents use different persona parameterisations.

Integrate RealmForge with a lightweight front-end visualiser (three.js or a web map) and a Redis-backed datastore to demonstrate how information propagation and perception radius affect rumor spread and faction formation.

tools.name: PINNeAPPle-Labs/PINNeAPPle
tools.desc: Pinneaple is an open-source Physics AI toolkit for Physics-Informed Neural Networks (PINNs), scientific ML, geometry processing, solvers, and reproducible training pipelines.
