tools.desc: A Godot 4 addon to randomly distribute meshes and decals in a scene in realtime.

tools.name: qwqzhanqwq/Godot-CSG-Blockout
tools.desc: Fast 3D level blockout & prototyping plugin for Godot 4. Features pie menu workflow, array/spreader tools, and one-click mesh baking.

cls.summary: A Godot 4 plugin for fast brush-based level blockout that creates and edits CSG nodes interactively and can bake them to meshes.
cls.what_it_does: CSG_Blockout lets users draw rooms, doors, stairs and other level geometry directly in the Godot 4 viewport using native CSG nodes with a pie-menu workflow, grid snapping and measurement helpers. It is used inside the Godot editor as an addon: build and test level scale with a player reference, then 'freeze' (bake) CSG into regular meshes while keeping the original CSG data for later unfreezing. Notable features include non-destructive CSG editing, one-click baking/unfreezing, procedural spreader/repeater tools and export-friendly frozen meshes.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository is a focused, documented Godot addon with installation options, AssetLib listing and active commits; it has community interest (119 stars) but is only ~98 days old so lacks the long track record needed for TRL 7+. README shows releases and publish channels which support a beta-level maturity.
prerequisites: basic familiarity with the Godot editor and scene system
student_project_ideas: Create a playable architectural walkthrough by blockouting a small building in Godot using CSG_Blockout, then export frozen meshes and add lighting and navigation to evaluate human-scale ergonomics.

Compare level iteration workflows by building the same room set with CSG_Blockout and with static mesh modelling (e.g. Blender), measuring the time to implement changes and demonstrating non-destructive edits and unfreezing.

tools.name: ShadowSafin/AndroLLM
tools.desc: Open-source Android AI using LiteRT-LM with hardware acceleration, cloud providers, memory, and voice.

cls.summary: AndroLLM is an open-source Android app that runs LiteRT-LM .litertlm models on-device with CPU/GPU/NPU acceleration, persistent memory, cloud-provider fallbacks and an offline voice assistant.
cls.what_it_does: AndroLLM enables local inference of LiteRT-LM-format language models on Android devices, using XNNPACK CPU and an OpenCL GPU delegate (with NPU support where available) and providing multi-turn chat, KV-cache persistence and vector-backed memory. It also integrates optional cloud providers via a LiteLLM-compatible proxy, offers offline wake-word/ASR/TTS voice interaction and a capability-based agent tooling system for automating tasks on-device.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository is active but young (created ~108 days ago). The README describes a feature-rich, production-focused project and shows integration with runtimes and hardware delegates, indicating beyond prototype work; however the short public track record and lack of long-term releases limit the TRL to Beta (6).
prerequisites: basic knowledge of LLMs and model formats (.litertlm)
familiarity with mobile hardware acceleration concepts (OpenCL/XNNPACK/NPU)
student_project_ideas: Build a hands-free assistant for factory inspection: deploy AndroLLM on an Android tablet, integrate device camera input and a simple ROS bridge to log inspection notes and voice commands.

Compare on-device vs cloud LLM latency and privacy: measure inference latency, energy and accuracy for the same prompts across local LiteRT models (AndroLLM) and an OpenAI-compatible cloud provider, and present trade-offs.

tools.name: laurent512/opencalque
tools.desc: Open-source 2D architectural editor with a Figma-like interface, a local CLI, and practical workflows for humans and AI agents.

cls.summary: OpenCalque is an open-source 2D architectural floor‑plan editor with a Figma-like interface, a plain JSON file format, desktop/web builds and built-in AI assistant integrations.
cls.what_it_does: OpenCalque lets users draw walls, doors, windows, stairs and annotate rooms with correct geometry and area calculation, using a modern GUI rather than traditional CAD commands. It saves and exchanges drawings as a stable, human‑readable JSON schema, provides a local CLI for scripted edits, and can accept editing commands from AI assistants (Ollama, OpenAI-compatible services, Claude).
cls.trl_rationale: The README and releases claim a 1.0 stable editor, installers for Windows/macOS/Linux, unit and browser tests and example files, which shows substantial implementation; however the repository is only 39 days old so under the stated policy TRL is capped at 5 despite the stable status.
prerequisites: basic CAD or architectural drafting knowledge
Node.js 22+ and pnpm (for running from source)
student_project_ideas: Create a scriptable layout generator that reads a CSV of room requirements and uses the CLI to build and export apartment floorplans in the OpenCalque JSON format, then visualise the results in the web app.

Integrate OpenCalque with a local LLM (Ollama) to implement a natural-language assistant that converts high-level room descriptions into editable floorplan modifications and evaluate usability and error modes.

tools.name: mertgulerx/frontier_exploration_ros2
tools.desc: Modern C++ frontier exploration package for autonomous mobile robots, with a core C++ library for custom integrations alongside ROS 2 Jazzy & Humble, Nav2 support.

cls.summary: A modern C++ ROS 2 package that detects and prioritises frontiers for autonomous exploration on mobile robots and integrates with Nav2 for goal dispatching.
cls.what_it_does: The package detects frontiers on occupancy grids, optimises the decision map, and orders exploration targets using a Minimum Ratio TSP (MRTSP) policy with optional bounded-horizon dynamic programming. It is provided as a reusable C++ library and a ROS 2 node that integrates with Nav2, RViz, and common ROS 2 QoS/parameter setups to run exploration missions on real or simulated robots.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository is active, has CI/tests, benchmarks and a clear integration path with ROS 2 and Nav2, but it was created ~7 months ago and lacks long-term production citations; that supports a beta-level TRL (6).
prerequisites: C++ development and ROS 2 build tools (colcon)
student_project_ideas: Integrate the package with a Gazebo/TurtleBot3 simulation to compare greedy MRTSP vs dynamic programming policies on coverage, path length and CPU use, and produce a report with plots and videos.

Extend the C++ library to add a custom frontier scoring function (e.g. information gain with sensor-modelled uncertainty) and evaluate exploration efficiency in a SLAM scenario using Nav2 for execution.

tools.name: ozcancelik/harfiyen
tools.desc: Tarayıcıda çalışan Türkçe konuşma tanıma ve altyazı aracı. Otomatik noktalama, canlı transkript ve altyazılı video dışa aktarma. Tamamen yerel, WebGPU destekli.

cls.summary: Harfiyen is a browser-based, locally running Turkish-first speech-to-text tool that transcribes, translates, dubs and embeds styled captions into videos using WebGPU and ONNX models.
cls.what_it_does: It runs speech recognition models in the browser (WebGPU / onnxruntime-web) to transcribe audio/video or live microphone input, offers automatic punctuation and editing, can translate and generate synthetic voice dubbing, and exports captioned videos. Notable features are its focus on Turkish (with multiple selectable models for speed/accuracy), entirely local processing in the client, and WebGPU acceleration for larger models.
cls.trl_rationale: The README and repository show a working, feature-rich browser app with multiple model options and export features, and the project already has community interest (stars). However the repository was created only 39 days ago, so there is no long track record or stable releases to justify TRL 6+.
prerequisites: A browser with WebGPU support for GPU-accelerated models (otherwise CPU fallback)
Familiarity with ONNX/onnxruntime-web if extending models
student_project_ideas: Create a lab assignment that uses Harfiyen to auto-generate time-coded transcripts and captions for recorded student presentations, then evaluate caption accuracy across the different bundled models.
Build a small demo that integrates Harfiyen with a video-editing pipeline to automatically produce translated Turkish voice-over and burn-in subtitles for short instructional videos.

tools.name: Heman10x-NGU/Verdict-open-jev
tools.desc: Non-autoregressive decision engine on ModernBERT (151M) with calibrated uncertainty (RLCD), TypeSafe AI Jev benchmark audit, and in-browser WebGPU playground

cls.summary: OpenJev (Verdict) is a non‑autoregressive decision model that returns typed choices and calibrated probabilities in a single forward pass, with a WebGPU playground and hosted weights on Hugging Face.
cls.what_it_does: OpenJev performs fast, single‑pass classification-style decisions (discrete choices, ordinal scores, binary probabilities) for structured software workflows, avoiding token generation and JSON parsing. It is used as an inference engine (byte-identical weights to a published checkpoint) with calibration and an in-browser WebGPU playground; notable features are per-cardinality calibration, NLI-style candidate templating, and sub-35ms forward-pass latency claims.
cls.trl_rationale: The README documents benchmark results across 231 tasks and points to model weights hosted on Hugging Face, indicating early external-use and benchmarking; however the repository is only 61 days old so there is limited public track record and the TRL is capped at 5.
student_project_ideas: Integrate OpenJev into a simulated ticket triage webhook: feed synthetic support tickets and compare latency, calibration and error rates against an autoregressive LLM classifier.

Build a small end‑to‑end automation that uses OpenJev decisions to trigger different simulated downstream services (database writes, alerts) and measure decision calibration and system-level safety when combining deterministic rules with model outputs.

tools.name: endend2003-cmd/Tactical-Matrix-Console
tools.desc: WarMatrix 2026: Next-Gen Tactical Simulation & AI Command Console

cls.summary: Sovereign Core is an event-sourced tactical simulation and AI orchestration platform that provides a responsive web command interface and runtime for building distributed, rewindable digital-twin style simulations of operations and missions.
cls.what_it_does: It provides a backend simulation runtime, an AI orchestration layer and a reactive web command interface to run and visualize large-scale tactical simulations with temporal layering (past/present/future) and replay/checkpoint capability. It is used to run distributed simulation scenarios, attach AI agents or human operators via APIs, and explore speculative ‘what-if’ branches; notable features include an event-sourced lock-free engine, a temporal event bus, and pluggable AI adapters.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository is active with a compiled runtime bundle and multiple components described (backend runtime, AI adapters, frontend) and has community interest (118 stars) but the project is only ~142 days old so it lacks a long track record; README claims a runnable bundle but there is not yet evidence of broad production deployments.
prerequisites: Python and PyTorch for AI backends
experience with FastAPI or web backends
familiarity with three.js / react-three-fiber for visualization
student_project_ideas: Integrate a simple reinforcement-learning agent (PyTorch) with the Sovereign Core API to task and evaluate autonomous route planning for a fleet of simulated drones, and visualise results in the web UI.

Create a disaster-response scenario that uses the temporal event bus to implement rewind-and-replay exercises for multi-agency coordination and measure response metrics across different command strategies.

tools.name: ethicals7s/awesome-local-ai

tools.name: templetongroup/radiant
tools.desc: A local coding harness for Mac. Chat with coding agents across cloud and local models, watch every tool call in a live activity feed, and drive a real terminal — in one window. Free and MIT licensed.

cls.summary: Radiant is a free, open-source macOS app that hosts and orchestrates coding agents across local and cloud LLMs, shows a live activity feed of tool calls, and lets agents read and edit files and run shell commands inside a project folder.
cls.what_it_does: Radiant provides a single-window harness for conversational coding agents that can use local models (Ollama, LM Studio) or cloud APIs (OpenAI, Anthropic, xAI, etc.), run shell commands, edit files, and display a task/kanban board for longer jobs. It is used as a desktop Electron app on macOS and is notable for visible tool calls, sandboxing controls, undo checkpoints for file edits, and workflows like loops and graphs to structure multi-step agent runs.
cls.trl_rationale: The project is actively developed, has a substantive README, many features and community interest (118 stars) but the repository is very new (~90 days) so there is not yet a long track record or stable releases to support a higher TRL.
prerequisites: familiarity with macOS and Electron apps
optional API keys for cloud models (OpenAI, Anthropic, etc.)
student_project_ideas: Create an automated code-fix agent that runs in Radiant to detect failing tests in a repository, propose fixes, apply edits, and create a checklist for a human reviewer.

Integrate a local LLM (via Ollama or LM Studio) with Radiant to build a sandboxed CI helper that triages lint/test failures and generates candidate patches while tracking all changes and undo checkpoints.

tools.name: zorost/alchemylake-databricks
tools.desc: Governed, provenance-sealed creative rendering for Databricks — a Streamlit App + Unity Catalog ai_render() function that turns any governed source (Sample Lakehouse, UC, Genie, or BYO data) into infographics, reports, decks, video briefings, music, and podcasts.

cls.summary: A Databricks Asset Bundle and Streamlit app that calls the AlchemyLake MCP service to produce governance-sealed deliverables (reports, PPTX decks, infographics, video briefings, podcasts, music) directly from governed lakehouse sources.
cls.what_it_does: AlchemyLake for Databricks connects a Databricks workspace to an external MCP rendering service and provides a Streamlit App, a SQL ai_render() function and agent tools so governed tables can be turned into verified deliverables (PDF dossiers, slide decks, infographics, videos, audio) with embedded provenance. It is used by deploying the repository as a Databricks Asset Bundle or registering an MCP endpoint for agents (Genie) so renders are called from SQL, UI or agent flows; notable features are provenance sealing, verification of generated claims against bound rows, and specialised render endpoints for multiple deliverable types.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository is new (created ~135 days ago) but is a runnable Databricks Asset Bundle with a detailed README and deploy instructions; however there is limited public track record or long-term stable releases, so maturity is around alpha/early-use (TRL 5).
prerequisites: Databricks workspace and permission to deploy Asset Bundles
basic Python/Streamlit knowledge and SQL familiarity
student_project_ideas: Build a Databricks notebook workflow that binds a sales table, calls the ai_render() SQL function to produce a pptx deck, then programmatically extracts the provenance seal and compares the reported figures to raw rows.

Create a lab exercise integrating Genie (agent) with the MCP endpoints: have students implement an agent that runs a guided deep-research render on a supplied dataset and produces the sealed PDF + Excel evidence workbook.

tools.name: vLAR-group/PhysInOne

tools.name: YongLD/Multi-UAV-JEV
tools.desc: Camera-observed UAV pursuit in MuJoCo with Jev decisions, RGB/depth HUD, replay and episode collection.

cls.summary: A multi-UAV cooperative pursuit simulation in MuJoCo that runs fleets of 1–4 drones with camera-based shared observations and role-based Jev decision workers, live HUD and replay/recording support.
cls.what_it_does: This repository provides a MuJoCo-based simulation of cooperative UAV pursuit where each drone has onboard cameras, odometry, a controller and a Jev decision worker to choose tactical actions (track, blockade, intercept, support). It is used by running the Python environment with MuJoCo and a local model endpoint (NeoHorse) to test multi-agent decision behaviours, record episodes at 20 FPS and inspect synchronized HUDs and replay; notable features are editable role rules that reload at runtime and inspectable shared, timestamped camera-derived observations.
cls.trl_rationale: The README documents a working simulator with setup scripts, validated platform details, example runs, and recording/replay features, indicating early adopters and usable examples; however the repository is only 39 days old so by the project-age rule it is limited to TRL 5.
prerequisites: Local model endpoint (NeoHorse) for Jev decision queries
student_project_ideas: Integrate the Multi-UAV-JEV simulator with ROS 2 to command simulated drones and log ROS topics for a study comparing centralized vs decentralized decision architectures.

Replace or augment the Jev decision endpoint with a learned policy (RL or imitation) and measure interception success and robustness across the provided P-01..P-04 role scenarios, producing quantitative evaluation and recorded replay.

tools.name: mgurbuz-tr/mapgpu
tools.desc: WebGPU Based GIS Library

tools.name: yui277/ArchViz-Lite
tools.desc: A lightweight WebGL architectural visualization tool powered by Three.js and AI. Developed by lichengfu2003.

tools.name: hassancs91/claude-image-generation
tools.desc: Connect Claude to image generation with Agent Skills. Three levels: a zero-cost code-based design engine, a Three.js 3D renderer, and a real diffusion model on Cloudflare. Plus an AI Storybook pipeline that turns a plain-English story into an illustrated, narrated HTML book.

cls.summary: A collection of Claude Agent Skills and example code that produce images three ways (code-based drawing, headless Three.js rendering, and a Cloudflare-hosted diffusion model) and composes them into an offline HTML 'AI Storybook' pipeline.
cls.what_it_does: This repository provides Claude Code skills that turn plain-English prompts into images using three approaches: a deterministic code-based renderer (Pillow + numpy), a headless Three.js 3D scene renderer, and a Cloudflare Workers-hosted diffusion model. It also demonstrates composing those skills into an illustrated, narrated single-file HTML storybook so a written story becomes a shareable multimedia book.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository is recent (created ~131 days ago) but contains working code, multiple example folders, and published tutorial guides; however it lacks a long track record or production adopters so maturity is around a beta-level.
prerequisites: familiarity with JavaScript/Node.js and web development
basic Python (for the Pillow/numpy code examples)
access to Claude (Anthropic) and optionally Cloudflare Workers credentials for level-3
student_project_ideas: Build a small web app that uses the level-1 code renderer and the level-2 Three.js renderer to create a library of consistent character illustrations for a short interactive story, then package the output as a single HTML storybook.

Extend the storybook pipeline to add simple scene-level metadata and a JSON-based editor so students can author a story and compare outputs from the code renderer, Three.js renderer and the diffusion model for the same prompts.

tools.name: erhanmeydan/kilnframe
tools.desc: Free, open source plugin for Premiere Pro and DaVinci Resolve: turns what you say into animated inserts and music, rendered on your own computer

cls.summary: Kilnframe is an open-source desktop plugin that generates short animated video inserts and music from selected speech for Premiere Pro, DaVinci Resolve Studio and FilmCraft.
cls.what_it_does: Kilnframe listens to speech in a selected timeline range, uses a chosen LLM/vision model to plan scenes, writes each scene as HTML/CSS/JavaScript animations, renders them locally with HyperFrames and places the resulting video and sound on your timeline. It offers multiple visual styles, per-scene approval stills, synthesized sound effects and an optional scored music track using an external model.
cls.trl_rationale: Project is very new (created 37 days ago) but already provides installers and released binaries with active pushes and 100+ stars, indicating early adopters; age limits TRL so it fits 'Alpha in use' rather than a mature production tool.
prerequisites: Adobe Premiere Pro 2026 (26.2+) or DaVinci Resolve Studio 21.1+ or FilmCraft 0.14.0+
GPU-equipped desktop (macOS Apple silicon supported; Intel Macs not yet)
optional paid LLM/vision subscriptions or local vision model for full functionality
student_project_ideas: Build an automated pipeline that uses Kilnframe plus a local LLM/vision model to generate short explainer animations from lab presentation audio and integrate the outputs into a student video report.
Create a custom Kilnframe visual style that renders engineering diagrams (e.g. block diagrams or simple charts) and evaluate how reliably the generated animations match spoken design descriptions.

tools.name: rbc33/Ghostbar
tools.desc: Free macOS-native Cluely alternative. AI chat invisible to screen sharing.  Ollama, OpenAI, Claude. Swift. No Electron. No subscription.

cls.summary: Ghostbar is a native macOS menu‑bar AI chat client that stays invisible to screen capture and can connect to local or cloud LLM backends.
cls.what_it_does: Ghostbar provides a lightweight, native Swift AppKit menu‑bar chat client that is excluded from macOS display capture so its UI does not appear in screen shares or recordings. It connects to multiple backends (local LLMs like Ollama, LM Studio, llama.cpp or cloud APIs such as OpenAI and Anthropic) and supports on‑device voice input via whisper‑cpp. It is notable for being macOS‑native (small footprint), emphasising privacy and local inference options.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository is active and supplies binary releases (DMG), a Homebrew tap and build instructions, showing a functioning beta app and user interest (113 stars). The project is 208 days old (<1 year) so a TRL above 6 is not supported by age alone.
prerequisites: Optional: local LLM servers (Ollama, LM Studio, llama.cpp) or API keys for OpenAI/Anthropic/NVIDIA NIM
For building: Xcode Command Line Tools / Xcode
student_project_ideas: Build a short demo that pairs Ghostbar with a locally hosted Ollama model to show private, on‑device coding assistance during a live coding presentation and measure latency and transcript privacy.

Modify Ghostbar (Swift/AppKit) to add a classroom mode that logs anonymised usage metrics locally and integrates with a simple server to evaluate how students use an on‑device assistant during timed programming tasks.

tools.name: nathaninline/ajean
tools.desc: Run your AI models at home in one binary: chat, persistent memory, web access, browser control, MCP tools, encryption at rest and end-to-end encrypted remote access. Linux, macOS, Windows. FR/EN docs.

cls.summary: AJEAN is a single-file, cross-platform program that runs local LLMs (via llama.cpp) and provides a full AI assistant with chat, persistent memory, tools, web/browser control and encrypted remote access.
cls.what_it_does: AJEAN bundles a local model runtime (llama.cpp) and a web/desktop UI into one binary so you can run an AI assistant entirely on your machine without Docker or Python. It manages models, provides projects and persistent memory, agent tools (browser driving, scheduled tasks, MCP/OpenAI-compatible endpoint) and end-to-end encrypted remote access, notable for shipping prebuilt binaries and automatic engine installation across Linux, macOS and Windows.
cls.trl_rationale: The project is active, provides cross-platform release binaries, and automates installing llama.cpp and engine variants which indicates a beta-level, usable tool; however the repository is only ~5 months old (162 days) so it lacks the longer track record and broad adoption required for TRL 7+.
prerequisites: familiarity with command-line usage and installing binaries
local model files (.gguf) or network access to download them
GPU drivers for accelerated variants (Vulkan/CUDA/ROCm) where used
student_project_ideas: Build an integration that uses AJEAN's OpenAI-compatible endpoint to drive an automated testing pipeline for a simple software project and measure how editable memory and project trackers affect test generation.

Create a small privacy study comparing latency, throughput and data residency between running a .gguf model in AJEAN on CPU vs GPU (Vulkan/CUDA) and produce a report with recommendations for deploying local assistants in an engineering office.

tools.name: mujocolab/mjlab_playground
tools.desc: A collection of tasks built on mjlab

cls.summary: A collection of robot reinforcement-learning tasks and training/playback scripts built on the mjlab MuJoCo-compatible framework for research and sim-to-real robotics experiments.
cls.what_it_does: mjlab_playground provides ready-made robot control tasks (e.g. get-up for Unitree Go1 and Booster T1) implemented on top of the mjlab framework, with commands to train and play policies on GPU. It is notable for offering high-throughput GPU-accelerated RL task setups and short example training recipes that demonstrate fast convergence on modern hardware.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository is ~7.5 months old with 113 stars, runnable CLI examples for training and playback, and a linked mjlab preprint cited in README; these indicate a beta-level project with versioned use and examples but below one year old so a TRL above 6 is not supported by available evidence.
prerequisites: Python development environment and typical RL dependencies
student_project_ideas: Compare sim-to-real transfer strategies by training a Unitree Go1 get-up policy in mjlab_playground, then evaluating robustness under domain randomisation and measuring performance degradation.
Extend an existing task to add a new sensor (IMU or contact) and create a curriculum that improves recovery time, integrating recorded telemetry into a dashboard for analysis.

tools.name: thun-res/vlink
tools.desc: VLink is a high-performance C++ communication middleware for autonomous driving and embodied intelligence, positioned as a full-scenario alternative to ROS 2.

tools.name: WebODM/ODX
tools.desc: Generate maps, point clouds, 3D models and DEMs from aerial and ground images 📷

cls.summary: ODX is an open-source photogrammetry engine that converts aerial and ground images into orthophotos, DEMs, 3D textured models and classified point clouds.
cls.what_it_does: ODX processes collections of images (from drones or ground cameras) to produce georeferenced orthophotos, digital elevation models, 3D textured meshes and compressed point clouds; it is run from the command line or via Docker and is intended for integration into workflows or WebODM. It is notable for GPU acceleration support, OpenSfM 1.0 integration, and output formats that work with common GIS and 3D tools (GeoTIFF, LAZ, OBJ, PLY).
cls.trl_rationale: Repository shows a working, documented tool with Docker images, GPU support and integration with WebODM/OpenSfM, indicating beta-level readiness; the project age is ~225 days (<1 year) which limits the TRL to at most 6 absent a longer track record or wide production citations.
prerequisites: GPU drivers / NVIDIA toolkit for accelerated runs (optional)
student_project_ideas: Use ODX with a small drone image dataset to produce an orthophoto and DSM, then calculate cut-and-fill volumes for a site and compare results to manual survey measurements.
Process time-separated image sets of the same site to generate point clouds and use CloudCompare/QGIS to perform a simple change-detection study (e.g. erosion or stockpile volume change).

tools.name: francescofugazzi/ml-sharp-pinokio
tools.desc: One-click 3D Gaussian Splatting generation from a single image.

tools.name: ChrisVip001/joyczl-agent
tools.desc: Joy — a local-first personal assistant. Rust core (loop / memory / tools / graph / evals), TypeScript gateways + dashboard, Python thin SDK.

cls.summary: Joy is a local-first personal AI agent written in Rust with an inspectable append-only memory ledger, a TypeScript dashboard, and support for multiple LLM providers.
cls.what_it_does: Joy runs a planning-and-execution agent loop locally, keeping a transparent append-only ledger for every conversational turn, and exposes a web dashboard and JSON-RPC gateways for integrations. It is used to run, inspect and extend agent behaviours and tools (file ops, shell, scheduling, delegation) without sending conversation or keys to external servers, and ships prebuilt binaries, Docker images and a thin Python SDK.
cls.trl_rationale: The project is well documented, provides prebuilt binaries, Docker and source builds and lists many features, but the repository is only ~58 days old so it lacks the longer track record, broad production usage and stable release history needed for TRL 6+.
prerequisites: basic Rust toolchain to build from source (optional if using prebuilt binaries)
familiarity with running local services (Docker or CLI) and configuring LLM providers / API keys
student_project_ideas: Extend Joy with a new tool plugin that integrates a course-specific simulator (e.g. a Modelica or Gazebo microservice) and demonstrate agent-driven experiment orchestration and result capture into Joy's ledger.

Create a small secure gateway that connects Joy to an on-premises LLM (e.g. Ollama) and measure privacy and performance trade-offs for local vs cloud providers, reporting results as reproducible experiments.

tools.name: Picom-code/pico-dgx-ds4
tools.desc: DeepSeek V4.1 Flash on 4x DGX Spark: 90/144 tok/s chat/code single-user, 376 tok/s at 16 distinct users, 1M context, images. Fork of blaesus/dsgx10.

cls.summary: A CUDA-based fork of a multi-node LLM inference engine (DeepSeek) optimised to run high-throughput, large-context inference on 4x NVIDIA DGX Spark clusters with RDMA/RoCE.
cls.what_it_does: This project provides a multi-node inference runtime tuned for 4x DGX Spark hardware to increase single-user and multi-user token throughput, support very large contexts (up to 1M), and add image inputs via a side ViT encoder. It is used as a low-level, high-performance inference engine (CUDA kernels, collectives and admission/slot policies) for local LLM deployments and is notable for multi-node optimisations for RoCE/RDMA and measured benchmarking against the upstream dsgx10 implementation.
cls.trl_rationale: The repo is a very recent (12 days old) fork with active benchmarking and modifications but no long-term production track record; it shows measurable performance numbers and CI-style bench scripts, so it appears beyond a throwaway prototype but is still early-stage (TRL limited by age and lack of broad external users).
prerequisites: multi-node DGX / GPU cluster access (RoCE/RDMA-capable network)
familiarity with LLM inference concepts and distributed collectives
student_project_ideas: Port and benchmark a reduced-scale version (1–2 GPUs) of the runtime to measure single-node improvements and compare latency/throughput against an existing open-source inference stack (e.g. a Hugging Face transformer or llama.cpp) on campus GPUs.

Implement a simple admission/slot policy modification and measure multi-user throughput trade-offs on a small cluster or simulated environment, then report how policy changes affect latency and resource utilisation.

tools.name: guzhezao/sandcove
tools.desc: 沙滩小筑 SANDCOVE · 用 AI 打磨的 WebGPU 海滩沙盒：挖沟、筑沙堡、引水与海啸。A WebGPU beach sandbox built on Sandboard.

cls.summary: SANDCOVE is a WebGPU-based interactive beach sandbox that simulates a GPU heightfield for sand and a shallow-water solver so users can dig, build sandwalls and observe water-driven erosion in the browser.
cls.what_it_does: It provides a real-time WebGPU sandbox where sand is represented as a GPU heightfield and water is modelled with a 256×256 shallow-water grid so terrain deformation and simple erosion/flow interactions are simulated and rendered. You run it as a TypeScript/Vite web app (Node.js for local dev) in a WebGPU-capable browser; it is notable for combining GPU heightfield terrain with shallow-water dynamics in an interactive demo derived from the Sandboard project.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository is very recent (created 2026-10-28, ~20 days old) so it lacks a track record despite having tests and a runnable demo; this supports an early-alpha rating rather than production maturity.
prerequisites: familiarity with TypeScript and web development
student_project_ideas: Extend the shallow-water solver to add sediment transport metrics and visualise erosion rates over time, comparing results with parameter variations (e.g. grain size, water viscosity).

Integrate simple agent behaviour so multiple walkers interact with the changing terrain and evaluate how human actions affect flood pathways, then present as an interactive lab on real-time simulation and UX.

tools.name: Hyperiux-Immersion-Labs/hyperiux-components
tools.desc: Animation effects and interactive UI components for Next.js - CLI-installable, 75+ free MPL 2.0 effects and 100+ Pro

cls.summary: A CLI-installable library of animation effects and interactive UI components for Next.js and React, with a mix of free and paid (Pro) effects including WebGL/Three.js scenes.
cls.what_it_does: Hyperiux Vault provides a command-line workflow to add ready-made animation effects and interactive components into Next.js projects (text reveals, particle backgrounds, cursor effects, WebGL scenes, transitions, etc.). It is used by running the npx hyperiux CLI to initialise a project, sign in, and install individual effect source code directly into your repo; notable points are the large catalogue (170+ effects), a free tier plus Pro subscription, and integration with Three.js, GSAP and Tailwind.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository is 6 months old with active commits, a polished README and a working CLI, and has attracted community interest (112 stars), but is younger than one year so it fits a beta-level TRL rather than long-term production maturity.
student_project_ideas: Create a small Next.js digital-twin front-end prototype and use Hyperiux effects (e.g. particle background, WebGL hero) to visualise system state and transitions.

Build a component library catalogue page that demonstrates and compares three different WebGL cursor and image-trail effects (using Three.js and Hyperiux) and measures their runtime performance in the browser.

tools.name: ayingQAQ/McCosmos
tools.desc: McCosmos · 麦门星图｜基于麦当劳 MCP 的餐品营养对比与替代发现 Skill，提供独立运行包、可解释分析与三维星图。

cls.summary: McCosmos is a TypeScript React + three.js web app and Agent Skill that compares McDonald’s menu items by nutrition, finds lower-calorie similar alternatives, and shows results in an interactive 3D 'star' visualization.
cls.what_it_does: McCosmos provides a CLI/Agent Skill and a browser UI to compare nutritional values of McDonald’s menu items, search/filter by nutrient criteria, and explain similarity between items. It ships a standalone Skill package and an offline snapshot plus a three-dimensional WebGL 'galaxy' visualization for interactive exploration; notable features include deterministic explanation algorithms, offline static packaging, and an Agent Skill integration.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository is very new (created ~27 days ago) so it cannot be rated high on maturity; however it provides packaged releases, GitHub Actions checks, a Cloudflare Pages demo and an offline static artifact, indicating usage beyond a single proof-of-concept which supports an alpha-in-use judgement.
student_project_ideas: Adapt the McCosmos visualization to another food dataset (e.g. university canteen menu) and add custom nutrient filters and exportable comparison cards.

Build an Agent Skill that integrates real-time menu APIs (or simulated API) and extends McCosmos's similarity explanation with a simple health-scoring heuristic, then evaluate differences between snapshot and live data.

tools.name: ArkaneFans/servllama
tools.desc: One app for both cloud LLMs and on-device LLMs.

tools.name: AarambhDevHub/aarambh-studio
tools.desc: 🦀 Decoder-only LLM built from scratch in pure Rust using Candle — no Python, no PyTorch. Gated DeltaNet + sparse attention, fine-grained MoE, native video/document understanding, long-horizon tool agents, quantization-aware training. Scales: Tiny (25M) to Large (1.3B).

cls.summary: A from-scratch, Rust-based decoder-only LLM training and serving system (no pretrained weights included) that covers tokenization, training, quantization, multimodal inputs and an OpenAI-compatible server.
cls.what_it_does: aarambh-studio implements a full LLM pipeline in pure Rust using Candle for tensor operations: tokenization, model architectures (including sparse MoE and gated DeltaNet), training (with quantization-aware training), evaluation and an HTTP/SSE inference server. It is used by building and training models locally or on GPUs and by running the included server/agent binaries; notable aspects are its pure-Rust implementation, support for efficient sparse/MoE features, multimodal inputs (image/audio/video/document), and multiple quantized export formats.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository is 146 days old with an apparent v4.0.0 final source release, active commits and 112 stars which indicate a usable beta-quality project; however it ships no pretrained checkpoints and lacks evidence of wide production deployments, so TRL is best judged as 6 (Beta).
prerequisites: Linux or platform supported by Candle
C/C++ build toolchain for optional codecs
Optional NVIDIA CUDA toolchain for GPU features
Familiarity with model training concepts (quantization, LoRA, MoE)
student_project_ideas: Train a tiny (25M) model configuration on a curated engineering dataset and compare inference latency and quality between CPU and CUDA builds, reporting effects of INT8/INT4 quantization.

Integrate aarambh-studio's OpenAI-compatible server with a simple retrieval-augmented pipeline (e.g. SQLite or Weaviate) to build a domain-specific question-answering assistant for systems engineering documentation.

tools.name: LuxAlgo/luxalgo-mcp-server
tools.desc: The LuxAlgo ecosystem as MCP tools: free and keyless.

cls.summary: LuxAlgo MCP is an open-source TypeScript server that exposes LuxAlgo's charting, indicator library and simulation tools as MCP (multi-client protocol) endpoints so clients and AI agents can open and edit live charts and query analytics inside chats and developer tools.
cls.what_it_does: The project provides an MCP server that serves live, interactive charts (via the Vela charting core), a large library of indicators and statistical tools, and prop-firm simulation/statistics to clients and AI agents (ChatGPT plugins, Claude, VS Code, etc.). It is used as a middleware endpoint (HTTP / stdio / Docker) that clients connect to so an agent or app can request charts, indicator source and session analytics without requiring API keys.
cls.trl_rationale: The repository is actively maintained with tests, docs and multiple client integration examples (ChatGPT plugin, Claude connector, VS Code, Cursor) suggesting a beta-quality server; it is only ~99 days old so lacks long-term track record required for TRL 7+.
prerequisites: Basic knowledge of HTTP and OAuth
LuxAlgo account for personal data access (optional for some endpoints)
student_project_ideas: Build a simple MCP client that integrates the LuxAlgo MCP server into a chat UI, allowing users to request and modify live charts from natural language prompts and display them in a web page.

Create a study comparing the library's statistical session outputs (gap fills, weekday effects) against historical data by calling the MCP server programmatically and visualising results in a Jupyter notebook or small web dashboard.

tools.name: laowang-wy/adai-sketchup-skill-mcp
tools.desc: SketchUp MCP + Skill for AI modeling: managed Ruby transactions, geometry readback, source-image review and local edits. Codex/PipClaw on Windows.

cls.summary: An MCP server and Skill that lets AI agents drive editable SketchUp modeling through managed Ruby transactions, geometry readback and visual evidence workflows.
cls.what_it_does: The project provides an MCP (Model Context Protocol) server and a SketchUp Skill enabling prompt-driven, reviewable 3D modelling: agents can create, modify and deliver editable SKP files with managed Ruby write transactions, operation receipts and visual/source-image review. It is notable for integrating agent tooling (Codex/PipClaw) with SketchUp, providing atomic/ recoverable operations, geometry readback for verification and packaged Windows installers for SketchUp 2018/2019 validation.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository is recent (created ~58 days ago) so maturity is limited; however the README and dist/ packages show versioned releases (0.5.39), installer zips, and some validation on SketchUp 2019, indicating alpha-level use by early adopters rather than just a prototype.
prerequisites: Basic familiarity with SketchUp Ruby API and MCP concepts
student_project_ideas: Build an agent-driven pipeline that ingests exterior photos and produces a SketchUp massing model using this MCP Skill, then evaluate geometry-readback accuracy versus manual measurements.

Extend the Skill to add a simple ruleset that enforces dimension constraints (e.g. door/window standards) and create a lab exercise that compares expert vs guided agent workflows when fixing non-conforming elements.

tools.name: auto-agent-protocol/auto-agent-protocol
tools.desc: The open automotive contract for MCP, A2A and Personal Agent Protocol: dealer discovery, inventory, evidence, pricing and consented inquiries.

cls.summary: Auto Agent Protocol is an open specification and TypeScript reference implementation that defines a contract for automotive agent-to-agent (A2A), model-context-protocol (MCP) and personal-agent (PAP) interactions such as dealer discovery, inventory search, vehicle evidence and lead submission.
cls.what_it_does: The project specifies typed JSON schemas, OpenAPI bindings and tooling so brokers, dealerships and agents can discover services, call inventory/search/vehicle-detail skills and exchange authenticated inquiries. It is used as a protocol specification and publishes npm packages, schema artifacts and verification tests so implementers can validate that a deployment conforms to the AAP 3.2 contract.
cls.trl_rationale: The repository supplies a full specification, published npm packages and verification tests and has active commits and community interest, but it is only ~6–7 months old (younger than one year) so it lacks the longer track record and broad production adoption required for TRL 7+.
prerequisites: Familiarity with OpenAPI and JSON Schema
student_project_ideas: Implement a minimal MCP endpoint that serves the AAP 3.2 mcp.json catalog and a simple inventory-search skill, then write a small agent client that discovers the dealer via /.well-known/agent-card.json and queries inventory.

Build a PAP client library that performs delegated Poppy-Session authentication and exercises vehicle-detail and lead-submit skills against the repository's example OpenAPI, and measure how session rotation and recovery behave.

tools.name: opengenesishq/EastGenesis
tools.desc: CaoGen — a vendor-neutral, local-first AI work desktop. Multi-provider agent runtime, GUI automation, MCP, Git worktree, task orchestration, effect ledger, and 3D office workspace. macOS/Windows/Linux.

cls.summary: EastGenesis is a local-first desktop AI workbench that automatically selects and routes tasks to multiple LLM providers and offers a GUI workspace, automation and MCP integration.
cls.what_it_does: EastGenesis classifies user tasks (code, long text, planning, etc.), scores available LLM providers by capability/cost/performance, and automatically routes requests to the best model with failover. It runs as an Electron desktop app, integrates multiple providers (OpenAI, Anthropic, Azure, compatible domestic models), provides developer tools (editor, terminal, Git), office document export and an MCP toolset for plugins and automation.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository is 135 days old and publishes a beta release (v0.1.9-beta) with CI/tests and multiple features implemented; this indicates a beta-stage project but not yet long-term production track record or broad adoption, so TRL=6.
prerequisites: basic familiarity with LLM provider APIs (OpenAI/Anthropic/Azure) for provider configuration
student_project_ideas: Implement and compare custom routing heuristics in EastGenesis (e.g. latency-focused vs cost-focused) and measure task-level cost/latency trade-offs across two providers.
Create an MCP plugin that connects EastGenesis to an institutional LLM or a simulated local model and evaluate failover behaviour and context preservation during provider outages.

tools.name: riponcm/AcadGIS
tools.desc: Make publication-ready study area maps, choropleths, locator insets, terrain & river maps for research papers and theses. Python package + no-code web app on geopandas & matplotlib — no QGIS/ArcGIS, no shapefiles.

cls.summary: AcadGIS is a Python package and companion web app for producing publication‑quality study‑area maps, choropleths, terrain and locator insets without requiring QGIS/ArcGIS or shapefiles.
cls.what_it_does: AcadGIS automates creation of styled thematic maps and multi‑panel study‑area layouts from place names or GeoDataFrames, with built‑in boundary downloads, terrain (DEM) shaded relief, hydrology, basemaps and many map decorations. It is used via a simple Python API (import acadgis as agis) or a no‑code web app and integrates optional extras for live downloads, DEM processing and drainage extraction to produce journal‑ready PNG/PDF/SVG exports.
cls.trl_rationale: The project is young (created ~151 days ago) but demonstrates several maturity signals: PyPI package, website, full docs, an arXiv paper and examples; these point to a beta‑level tool (installable with extras and documented) but it lacks the multi‑year track record or broad ecosystem needed for TRL 7+.
student_project_ideas: Produce a multi‑panel study‑area figure for a civil engineering site assessment: download administrative boundaries with AcadGIS, overlay survey point data from CSV, and export publication‑ready figures comparing landcover and NDVI.

Combine AcadGIS with a DEM and pysheds (via acadgis[drainage]) to extract and visualise a watershed's drainage network, then quantify upstream area and produce annotated maps for a hydrology coursework report.

tools.name: LuxAlgo/prop-firm-sim
tools.desc: Know your odds before you pay the fee: open-source Monte Carlo simulation of prop-firm challenges over each firm's exact ruleset. Pass probability, expected attempts and cost, EV, optimal risk sizing. Engine, CLI, and MCP server. Deterministic, zero telemetry. By LuxAlgo.

cls.summary: A TypeScript Monte Carlo simulator and CLI that estimates pass probability, expected attempts/cost, EV and optimal risk for proprietary trading firm (prop‑firm) challenges using exact rulesets.
cls.what_it_does: Prop Firm Sim runs many deterministic simulated challenge journeys from a trader profile or real trade history against a firm's precise ruleset to produce pass probabilities, phase-level statistics, expected attempts and monetary EV with fees included. It provides a local TypeScript engine, a CLI and an MCP-style server, and can load firm rules from LuxAlgo's public prop‑firm directory or a fully offline ruleset.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository is a well-documented, working TypeScript engine and CLI with examples and 112 stars, but it is only 85 days old so it lacks a long track record or broad production adoption; that age limits TRL to alpha-in-use (5).
prerequisites: basic understanding of trading P&L, win rate and R-multiple statistics

tools.name: gaoypeng/3dcodebench
tools.desc: Benchmarking Agentic Procedural 3D Modeling Via Code

cls.summary: 3DCodeBench is an open benchmark and dataset for evaluating how well LLMs and coding agents can generate Blender 5.0 Python scripts that procedurally build 3D objects across 212 categories.
cls.what_it_does: The project provides reference factory Blender scripts, prompts, tasks and evaluation metrics to measure executability, image similarity and 3D-shape similarity for code-generated procedural models. It is used by running provided runners against models (via API keys) to produce Blender Python outputs and score them against ground truth; notable aspects are the large curated corpus (3DCodeData), multi-view renders, and metric suite (SigLIP/DINOv3, Chamfer/Uni3D, LLM-as-judge).
cls.trl_rationale: The repository includes a published paper, a project website, a sizeable dataset on HuggingFace, and runnable tooling and metrics, which indicates beta-level maturity; however the repo is only ~6 months old so it lacks the longer track record and broad adoption required for TRL 7+.
prerequisites: API keys for provider models if running inference (OpenAI/Anthropic/Gemini)
student_project_ideas: Use 3DCodeBench to evaluate and compare two code-generation models (e.g. OpenAI vs Anthropic) on a small subset of categories, analysing failure modes and common traceback errors; present metrics and visual examples.

Extend one benchmark category by adding parametric variants and create an automated pipeline that converts generated Blender scripts into glTF/GLB assets for integration into a simple Unity or WebGL scene to study procedural asset pipeline robustness.

tools.name: stevyhacker/LokalBot
tools.desc: Your personal context engine for macOS, with Windows and Linux in alpha: on-device meeting notes, screen recall, dictation, and autocomplete that you and your AI agents can search. Free and open source (GPLv3).

cls.summary: LokalBot is an on-device personal context engine for macOS (Windows/Linux alpha) that records and indexes meetings, provides local transcription, searchable meeting memory, dictation and autocomplete across apps, and integrates with local LLMs.
cls.what_it_does: LokalBot records microphone and meeting-app audio, produces local transcripts, summaries, decisions and action items, and provides system-wide features such as dictation, selection-based rewrite actions and inline autocomplete that use a small local model. It is used as a desktop app (macOS primary, Windows/Linux in alpha) and can be searched by keywords or semantic queries, with citations back to the source audio or transcript; notable features include local-first privacy, offline small-model inference, and integration points for MCP clients and local LLM runtimes.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository is 147 days old and actively developed by a single author with 111 stars and alpha/beta platform notes; it provides install options and real-user features (brew cask) but lacks evidence of broad production adoption or long-lived stable releases, so maturity aligns with early adopters/alpha in use (TRL 5).
prerequisites: macOS 15+ (primary); Windows 10/11 or Linux x86_64 supported in alpha
basic familiarity with desktop app installation and keyboard shortcuts
student_project_ideas: Build a small tool that ingests LokalBot meeting transcripts to automatically extract and link action items to project issue trackers (e.g., GitHub) and evaluate accuracy versus manual tagging.

Compare on-device transcription and summarisation quality and privacy outcomes by running the same meeting audio through LokalBot (local model) and a cloud transcription service, and report differences in latency, accuracy and data exposure.

tools.name: maxwhipw/marmalade-tts-android
tools.desc: Native Android TTS app with on-device neural voices and emotion-aware prosody — sister project to marmalade-tts (CLI).

cls.summary: An open-source Android text-to-speech engine that runs neural voices on-device, can be set as the system TTS, and supports offline and optional cloud voices.
cls.what_it_does: Marmalade TTS implements Android's text-to-speech interface so it can replace the system TTS and make any app speak through its neural voices; it bundles a small offline voice and supports downloading larger engines, per-app voice routing, voice effects and accessibility features. Notable points are on-device neural inference for privacy and low latency, optional cloud provider integration via API keys, and availability through F‑Droid for reproducible installs.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository is ~6 months old with active development, GitHub releases and distribution via F‑Droid and installed APKs (shows early real-world use), but it is younger than one year so lacks a longer track record required for TRL7+.
prerequisites: knowledge of Android TTS APIs / Accessibility services
basic understanding of on-device ML model packaging
student_project_ideas: Measure latency, CPU and memory of on-device neural voices across multiple Android devices by integrating Marmalade as the system TTS and reporting results to a small telemetry app.
Create a custom voice-effect preset and evaluate perceptual changes to prosody and intelligibility for accessibility use-cases, comparing on-device vs configured cloud voices (Venice.ai/OpenAI).

tools.name: chayapats/oliv
tools.desc: Thai + English voice typing for Mac. Offline speech-to-text that types Thai-spoken tech words in English. Push-to-talk dictation on Apple Silicon (Whisper + MLX), free & open-source Wispr Flow alternative · พิมพ์ด้วยเสียงภาษาไทย

cls.summary: OLIV is a free, open-source Mac app that performs offline Thai+English speech-to-text and pastes the cleaned text into any application using push-to-talk.
cls.what_it_does: OLIV records speech while you hold a key, runs an on-device Whisper-based Thai model and a small language model to restore English technical terms, applies cleanup and formatting rules, and pastes the result into the current cursor location. It is designed for Apple Silicon Macs, works locally after a one-time model download, and focuses on handling Thai with embedded English jargon.
cls.trl_rationale: The repository hosts a working native Mac app with releases (0.2.2), model downloads, benchmarks, and 111 stars showing community interest, but it is only ~4 months old and under one year (created 2026-07-11), so maturity is best described as beta rather than long-proven production.
prerequisites: familiarity installing macOS apps and downloading model files
optional knowledge of native macOS permissions for accessibility/pasteboards
student_project_ideas: Build an accessibility evaluation comparing OLIV's offline Thai+English dictation to cloud ASR services on a dataset of technical utterances and measure word/meaning accuracy, then visualise errors in a dashboard.

Integrate OLIV with a simple VS Code extension to create a coder-focused voice-typing workflow and evaluate productivity/usability with developers writing mixed Thai-English comments and commit messages.

tools.desc: CLI/GUI tool for efficient and easy safetensors and gguf model conversion

tools.desc: LEARN HOW TO BUILD UP YOUR REVIT MCP

tools.name: matsuoka-601/Particles4All
tools.desc: Unified particle solver for fluid and rigid bodies based on Position Based Dynamics

cls.summary: Particles4All is a WebGPU-based real-time particle solver that simulates fluids and rigid bodies together and renders a smooth fluid surface in the browser.
cls.what_it_does: It implements a unified position-based particle solver that treats fluids and rigid bodies as particles solved in the same constraint loop, with anisotropic-kernel surface reconstruction and screen-space filtering for rendering. The project runs in modern browsers with WebGPU (no build step) and is notable for combining real-time particle physics and GPU-based screen-space fluid rendering in ES modules/WGSL.
cls.trl_rationale: The repository provides a runnable browser demo and references established academic methods, but it is very new (created 89 days ago), has no releases or evidence of production use, so it fits an alpha-in-use level.
prerequisites: familiarity with JavaScript and GPU shading (WGSL)
basic knowledge of particle-based fluid methods (PBF/SPH) and Web server to serve files
student_project_ideas: Extend the solver to couple a simple rigid-body vehicle interacting with the fluid and measure forces on the body, visualising results in the browser and exporting time-series data for analysis.

Compare surface reconstruction and rendering quality/performance by swapping the anisotropic kernel and narrow-range filter for a simpler method, then profile GPU costs and visual differences across browser platforms.

tools.name: ManuelR-T/dockscope
tools.desc: Visual Docker dashboard with a 3D dependency graph, live metrics, logs, terminal, and container actions

tools.name: aablinov/malina
tools.desc: 🍓 Cosy co-op voxel dungeon crawler meets tower defence — defend the raspberry bush with friends online ⚔️🏰 TypeScript + three.js, everything is code.

cls.summary: Malina is an open-source browser-based cooperative voxel action game with tower-defence elements, a built-in level and weapon editor, and a small Node server for online multiplayer.
cls.what_it_does: Malina provides a playable isometric voxel dungeon-crawler / tower-defence game implemented in TypeScript and three.js, with networked multiplayer served by a Node server. It includes an in-game level editor, a large prefab library, tuning data in code, and documentation/wiki intended to make the project easy to modify or extend (including instructions aimed at AI coding agents).
cls.trl_rationale: The repository is very new (created 27 days ago) so it cannot be judged as production-proven; however the README is extensive, there are runnable instructions and a working server/client demo, which supports an early-alpha rating (TRL 4).

tools.name: TheJacksonCode/Agent-Architecture
tools.desc: Visual multi-agent system designer for Claude Code. 60 agents, 62 presets, Five Minds Protocol, HITL gates, cost modelling and Live    Simulation - see the team run before you spend a token. Installable as a Claude Code plugin. Zero dependencies, single HTML file.

cls.summary: A browser-based visual designer and educational reference for building, simulating and exporting multi-agent systems targeted at Claude Code.
cls.what_it_does: It provides a single-file HTML visual canvas where you can drag agents, connect them, run lightweight simulations with human-in-the-loop gates, inspect an encyclopedia for each agent/preset, and export prompts/diagrams for Claude Code. The tool is notable for being zero-dependency, running entirely in the browser (GitHub Pages live demo), and packaging a large curated set of agents (60) and presets (62) with cost-estimation and hook-lifecycle documentation.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository is active, has a live GitHub Pages demo, and an evolving version history (v32→v41) with 110 stars indicating interest; however the project is only ~224 days old so it fits a beta-level maturity rather than long-term production adoption.
prerequisites: familiarity with multi-agent concepts and Claude Code basics
student_project_ideas: Use the designer to compose a multi-agent pipeline for a small robotics task (e.g. perception→planner→monitor) and export a Claude Code prompt, then compare simulated message flows with a simple ROS 2 prototype to study integration patterns.

Extend or curate a new preset that targets a specific engineering workflow (e.g. requirements triage or design review), run cost/latency what-if scenarios in the Cost Command Center, and produce a report that evaluates trade-offs between agent counts and token budget.

tools.name: opengeos/qgis-notebook-plugin
tools.desc: A QGIS plugin for running Jupyter Notebook within QGIS

tools.name: erikzeng2008-del/mcd-dual-budget-coach
tools.desc: 麦门双预算军师 · 麦当劳中国 MCP 参赛作品 | 钱一个预算、热量一个预算，两个闸门同时过才配餐：88,788 种组合本地穷举，给最划算/最扎实/最均衡三档、券后到手价、全息人设卡。Dual-budget (money + calories) McDonald's China MCP Agent Skill with 3-tier meal plans, coupon math and a holographic persona card.

cls.summary: A consumer-facing web agent/skill that suggests McDonald's China meal combinations that satisfy both a money budget and a calorie limit and produces a small holographic-style persona card for each result.
cls.what_it_does: This repository implements an interactive web skill/agent that queries McDonald's China MCP APIs for menu, nutrition and coupon data, locally enumerates feasible meal combinations under two constraints (money and calories), ranks three recommended options (cheapest, most substantial, most balanced), and renders results including a small 3D 'holographic' persona card. It's provided as single-file web pages (demo/lite/party) that run in the browser and can be integrated into the WorkBuddy agent platform using an MCP connector.
cls.trl_rationale: The project hosts working online demos, scripts for fetching MCP data and local combo enumeration, and has community interest (109 stars) but the repository is only 39 days old so it lacks a longer track record and stable releases; that supports an 'alpha in use' TRL.
prerequisites: optional: McDonald's MCP API token to connect live via the MCP connector
basic familiarity with hosting static pages (GitHub Pages) if self-hosting

tools.name: MRCalderon3D/everything-game-dev-code
tools.desc: A universal scaffold for AI-assisted game development. 42 agents, 51 commands, 86 skills. Multi-engine (Unity, Unreal, Godot, HTML). Multi-harness (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, OpenCode, Kiro).
