tools.desc: Your own digital life form — local AI companion with persistent memory, IDE workspace, MCP support, and 30+ tools. Companion-first alternative to Hermes Agent / OpenClaw / Claude Code.

tools.name: olerast67/voice-teleprompter-android
tools.desc: Suflyor (Суфлёр): free voice-following teleprompter app for Android. Scrolls as you speak, floats over Instagram, TikTok and the camera. Speech recognized on the phone in 13 languages, no internet permission. Телесуфлёр по голосу для Android.

cls.summary: Suflyor is an open-source Android teleprompter that follows the speaker's voice using on-device speech recognition and floats over camera and social apps.
cls.what_it_does: The app performs on-device streaming speech recognition and aligns recognized words to a script so the visible text scrolls as the user speaks; it runs entirely offline and can float over other apps (Instagram, TikTok, camera). It is used as a creator tool on Android phones to record videos while reading prompts without network access and notable for its offline sherpa-onnx-based ASR and multi-language downloadable speech packs.
cls.trl_rationale: The README describes a working, full-featured Android app with on-device ASR and multiple language packs and the repo has stars and recent activity, indicating early adopters; however the repository is only ~53 days old so there is no long track record and the project is limited by its young age.
prerequisites: basic familiarity with installing Android apps or building from source (Android development knowledge if modifying)

tools.name: ForestHubAI/edge-agents
tools.desc: The 30 MB open-source edge AI agent runtime. Run AI agents offline on Linux (Raspberry Pi, Jetson). GPIO, UART, MQTT as first-class nodes. Industrial protocols (OPC-UA, Modbus) on the roadmap.

cls.summary: Edge Agents is a small open-source runtime and visual workflow/CLI for running AI agents offline on Linux edge devices (Raspberry Pi, Jetson) with first-class hardware I/O and MQTT integration.
cls.what_it_does: Edge Agents lets you author visual agent workflows with a CLI/builder and run them on resource-constrained Linux edge devices via a ~30 MB container engine. It exposes hardware I/O (GPIO, UART, ADC), MQTT and local SLMs as native workflow nodes so agents can interact with sensors and machines without cloud connectivity.
cls.trl_rationale: The README and examples show a runnable engine, CLI, cross-build instructions and device targets (Pi, Jetson), and the project has community interest (~109 stars) but the repo is ~6 months old so it lacks the multi-year track record and broad production citations needed for TRL 7+.
prerequisites: Docker buildx and container workflow knowledge
familiarity with hardware I/O (GPIO/serial) on target devices
student_project_ideas: Build a privacy-preserving voice assistant on a Raspberry Pi using a local SLM, integrating wake-word/STT/TTS nodes in an Edge Agents workflow and evaluating latency and offline robustness.

Implement a predictive-maintenance prototype: stream vibration sensor data to the agent over MQTT, have an on-device SLM infer anomaly conditions, and publish alerts to MQTT; measure detection and network resilience.

tools.name: SFKislev/Flue
tools.desc: Let agents control many desktop software directly from the cli, with one pip install, and no MCP servers.

cls.summary: Flue is a Python-based bridge that lets coding agents drive and automate desktop applications (Photoshop, Blender, Unity, etc.) from the command line without running a long‑lived MCP server.
cls.what_it_does: Flue exposes desktop applications' native scripting runtimes through a small CLI bridge so LLM-powered coding agents can send scripts to and receive JSON from those apps. It is installed with pip and a setup command and provides adapters for many creative and 3D apps, making it notable for removing the need for separate MCP servers or brittle screenshot-based automation.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository is active with documentation, adapters for many desktop apps and a simple install flow, and has community interest (109 stars), but it is under one year old (created 214 days ago), so it fits a beta-level maturity rather than proven production ubiquity.
prerequisites: installed target desktop applications (e.g. Blender, Photoshop, Unity)
familiarity with agentic harnesses or CLIs (Claude Code, Gemini CLI, etc.)
student_project_ideas: Create an agent workflow that opens a Blender scene, modifies a parameterised model (e.g. adjust link lengths), renders images, and returns results as JSON for an automated design exploration.

Build an agent-assisted asset pipeline that imports artwork into Unity, runs an automated export/optimisation step (LOD, compression), and reports metrics (triangle counts, texture sizes) to a dashboard.

tools.name: csi-dgist/ros2probe
tools.desc: Observe ROS 2 DDS and Zenoh traffic, inspect graphs and topic metrics, and record messages with a CLI or desktop GUI.

cls.summary: ros2probe is a host-level observability tool that uses eBPF to capture ROS 2 DDS and Zenoh traffic, reconstruct the ROS graph, show live topic metrics, and record MCAP bag files via a CLI and desktop GUI.
cls.what_it_does: ros2probe passively captures RTPS/DDS and Zenoh packets at the kernel level using eBPF socket filters, reconstructs participants/nodes/topics and live metrics in userspace, and provides a CLI and GUI to inspect the ROS graph, stream decoded messages, and record MCAP bag files. It is notable for non‑intrusive, single-host capture (including loopback and SHM shadowing), sliding-window topic metrics (hz, bandwidth, delay), and built-in MCAP recording with compression.
cls.trl_rationale: The project is actively maintained, provides prebuilt binaries and an install script, and has a refereed preprint cited in the README, indicating beta-level maturity; however the repository is only ~206 days old so it lacks the multi-year track record or widespread adoption required for TRL 7+.
prerequisites: ROS 2 (Humble or later) for meaningful data
root or elevated privileges for kernel-level capture
Python 3 + rclpy for rp topic echo
student_project_ideas: Measure end-to-end latency and bandwidth of a multi-host ROS 2 demo by using ros2probe to collect live topic metrics and compare results with rosbag2 recordings under different QoS and network conditions.

Integrate ros2probe MCAP recordings with a simple offline analysis pipeline (Python) to detect message loss and compute message inter-arrival statistics for a fault-injection study on DDS QoS settings.

tools.name: migit/verhoBot
tools.desc: VerhoBot is a compact curtain-moving robot designed to automatically close your curtains when you need darkness and open them again when it is time to wake up, no rope,no pulley,deploy and let the bot move your curtain. The goal is simple: improve sleep quality while letting natural sunlight become part of your morning routine.

cls.summary: VerhoBot is an open-source ESP32-based, battery-powered curtain robot (hardware + firmware + 3D-printable enclosure) that automates opening and closing curtains on a schedule or by user command.
cls.what_it_does: VerhoBot provides hardware designs, firmware and a small web dashboard to retrofit existing curtain rails with a compact, rail-mounted robot that drives curtains using a geared DC motor and TB6612FNG motor driver. It is used by flashing the ESP32 firmware, assembling the provided PCB/enclosure and configuring Wi‑Fi/schedules via the device web UI; it is notable for being an accessible, community-oriented open hardware project focused on low-power, battery operation and simple smart‑home integration.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository is 169 days old (<1 year) so cannot be assumed long‑track production; README and metadata describe working firmware and completed basic features (motor control, scheduling, OTA groundwork) and 109 stars indicating community interest, which supports alpha/early-in-use status rather than mature production.
prerequisites: familiarity with ESP32 toolchain (ESP-IDF or Arduino)
basic electronics and soldering; access to 3D printing for the enclosure
student_project_ideas: Integrate VerhoBot with Home Assistant and implement a sunrise-simulation mode that adjusts opening time based on local sunrise data (uses Home Assistant and an HTTP API).

Modify firmware to add position feedback (e.g., magnetic hall sensor or encoder) and implement closed-loop calibration and battery-aware operation, then evaluate battery life under different schedules.

tools.name: Devesh-Shirsath/spotkit
tools.desc: Spotkit — a Claude Code skill that turns a feature description into minimal, abstract SVG product illustrations that all belong to one design system.

cls.summary: Spotkit is an open-source Claude Code skill that generates consistent, production-ready abstract SVG product illustrations from a short feature description.
cls.what_it_does: Spotkit takes a short feature or UI description and produces minimal, themeable SVG 'spot' illustrations that follow a fixed design system and twelve layouts. It is used as a skill for Claude Code / other agents or run locally to output SVG files and a gallery; it emphasizes exact geometry, CSS theming and repeatable family-style illustrations rather than raster images.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository is very new (created ~70 days ago) so it cannot be judged production-stable; README and examples/gallery.html show working examples and install instructions and the project has community interest (stars), which supports an alpha-in-use judgement (TRL 5) rather than lower prototype levels.
prerequisites: familiarity with Claude Code or agent skill workflows to use the skill directly
student_project_ideas: Create a small web UI that queries Spotkit (run locally or via a local agent) to generate themed SVG empty-state illustrations for a mock SaaS product, then integrate them into a simple React component library with light/dark theming.

Extend Spotkit with an additional layout and a script that converts its SVG output into optimized, accessible inline SVG components and measure consistency across a set of 50 generated illustrations (quality checklist + automated checks).

tools.name: HimanshuMohanty-Git24/gitaviswa
tools.desc: GitaViśva (गीताविश्व): the Bhagavad Gita as a living knowledge graph. Explore all 700 verses in 3D, read 20 classical commentaries, listen to recitations, ask a GraphRAG companion with your own free API key, and keep a private journal. Works offline.

cls.summary: GitaViśva is an offline-first web application that presents the Bhagavad Gita as an interactive knowledge graph with 3D and 2D views, commentaries, audio and a GraphRAG-based question companion.
cls.what_it_does: The project builds a searchable, browsable knowledge graph of all verses, concepts and commentaries of the Bhagavad Gita and exposes interactive 3D and 2D visualisations to explore connections. It supports local journaling, offline use, audio playback, and an optional GraphRAG retrieval+LLM companion (via user-supplied API key) that highlights the source subgraph when answering questions. The app is notable for combining a richly annotated humanities dataset with a browser-side graph retrieval pipeline and three.js 3D visualisation.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository is very new (created 13 days ago) so TRL is limited by age; README documents a live demo, a runnable local install, and several features (offline, GraphRAG, Neo4j) which indicates alpha-level use by early adopters rather than mature production adoption.
prerequisites: optional free LLM API key for GraphRAG functionality

tools.name: bbfox0703/UE5CEDumper
tools.desc: A x64 UE Dumper for Unreal Engine 4.11~5.8 runtime data inspector and structure explorer for development. With some tools integrated with CE.

tools.name: AliKarami/MikroMCP
tools.desc: Production-grade MCP server for MikroTik RouterOS routers and SwOS switches, with secure AI-native network automation.

cls.summary: MikroMCP is an open-source Model Context Protocol (MCP) server that exposes MikroTik RouterOS and SwOS devices as typed, auditable tools so LLM-based agents can inspect, diagnose and perform safe network operations.
cls.what_it_does: MikroMCP turns RouterOS routers and SwOS switches into a production-minded MCP control plane exposing 133 typed read/write tools (status, interfaces, routes, firewall, diagnostics, etc.). It is used as a server (stdio, HTTP/SSE or Docker) that MCP-capable agents like Claude or Cursor call to perform idempotent, auditable network changes with dry-run, snapshots, RBAC and rollback-aware workflows. What makes it notable is its focus on agent safety and structured schemas so LLMs interact with network gear without raw CLI improvisation.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository is ~7 months old with active pushes, 108 stars, a detailed README and a wiki; it provides many features (RBAC, audit, dry-run) and deployment modes suggesting a beta-quality project, but it lacks evidence of widespread production adoption required for TRL 7+.
prerequisites: Access to MikroTik RouterOS or SwOS devices (or lab VM)
Familiarity with MCP concepts and basic LLM/agent usage
student_project_ideas: Build a lab exercise where students connect a virtual MikroTik RouterOS instance to MikroMCP and write an LLM-driven workflow that safely audits and suggests firewall rule improvements using dry-run and rollback features.

Integrate MikroMCP with an existing CI pipeline to automatically run diagnostics and generate structured reports (JSON) from routers after configuration changes, then visualise results in a dashboard (e.g. Grafana) to study automated verification and audit trails.

tools.name: robium-ai/robium
tools.desc: Physical AI skills for coding agents, with field-tested robotics guidance, the robium-ai CLI, and a learning engine.

cls.summary: Robium is a Node.js CLI and skill library that gives coding agents runnable, field-tested robotics skills and reference simulation apps for ROS 2, Gazebo, MuJoCo, Isaac Sim and related stacks.
cls.what_it_does: Robium provides a zero-dependency CLI, a catalog of agent 'skills' and runnable reference applications that let coding agents (Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI, Cursor, etc.) inspect, run and adapt robot simulations and workflows. It automates workspace setup, verifies prerequisites, launches example apps (navigation, policy inference, perception assistants) and bundles guidance and troubleshooting tuned for embodied/robotics environments. What makes it notable is the explicit integration with common robotics stacks and an architect that selects small, provable reference behaviours so agents can produce visible, verifiable results quickly.
cls.trl_rationale: The repository (created ~106 days ago) provides an installable CLI, multiple runnable reference apps and examples for ROS 2/Gazebo/MuJoCo/Isaac Sim and shows active development and community interest (stars, issues). Its age (<1 year) and recent pushes suggest beta maturity (versioned examples and CLI) but not the multi-year production track record required for TRL 7+.
prerequisites: Robotics middleware/tools such as ROS 2, Gazebo, Nav2 or MuJoCo for specific apps
student_project_ideas: Use Robium to deploy and extend the 'robot-navigation' reference app: add a new navigation behaviour, run SLAM in simulation, and evaluate success rates for different controller parameters using ROS 2 and Nav2.

Create a perception-to-action pipeline by combining the 'silly-turtlebot' app with a vision model (local or cloud) to detect objects and command guarded navigation, then measure latency and robustness under simulated sensor noise.

tools.name: Ali-Marandi/PyFluidDynamics
tools.desc: A professional Python library for 2D incompressible Navier-Stokes simulations using the Finite Difference Method, with advanced visualization.

cls.summary: PyFluidDynamics is a Python library that solves 2D incompressible Navier–Stokes problems (e.g. lid-driven cavity) using finite difference methods and provides Matplotlib-based visualisations.
cls.what_it_does: The library implements a finite-difference solver for the 2D incompressible Navier–Stokes equations with an iterative Pressure-Poisson solver and utilities for running classic CFD benchmarks such as the lid-driven cavity. It is used by installing the Python package and running the example scripts that produce velocity and pressure plots; it is notable for a clean, modular and educational implementation aimed at teaching and simple research experiments.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository is 109 days old (<1 year) and shows working examples (lid-driven cavity), modular code and active pushes with ~100 stars, indicating a beta-level project; there is no evidence of long-term production use or multiple stable releases, so TRL is capped at 6.
student_project_ideas: Compare numerical convergence and accuracy of the library's finite-difference lid-driven cavity solver against a reference solution (literature or higher-resolution run) and produce error vs mesh-size plots.

Extend the solver to include passive scalar transport (temperature or concentration) and run a project coupling the fluid solution to a simple heat-transfer model, visualising results with Matplotlib or saving data for post-processing in ParaView.

tools.name: ericdrowell/brometal
tools.desc: BroMetal is an LLVM-inspired compiler that transforms TypeScript into highly optimized GPU shaders for WebGPU. Write GPU code in TypeScript, compile to WGSL, and eliminate shader boilerplate

cls.summary: BroMetal is a TypeScript-to-WGSL ahead-of-time shader compiler and small WebGPU runtime that lets you write typed shaders in TypeScript and produce optimized WGSL modules for WebGPU applications.
cls.what_it_does: BroMetal provides a DSL (shader()) in TypeScript to author vertex/fragment shaders with typed attributes, uniforms and varyings, compiles those *.shader.ts files ahead-of-time into dependency-free .shader.gen.ts modules containing WGSL and metadata, and ships a very small runtime to drive the generated shaders in WebGPU. It is notable because it moves shader errors to build time (type-checked TypeScript), produces compact runtime code, and targets modern WebGPU/WGSL workflows rather than in-browser GLSL string compilation.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository shows an active npm package, examples, documentation and an active maintainer with 107 stars and recent commits, indicating beyond prototype stage; however it is pre-1.0 and the repo is only ~4 months old so it lacks a long production track record, limiting it to a beta-level TRL.
student_project_ideas: Create a small WebGPU visualization that uses BroMetal to author a custom procedural material (e.g. water or cloth shading), generate the WGSL, and compare runtime startup and frame cost to an equivalent three.js shader implementation.
Extend a BroMetal example to implement a GPU-based particle simulator and integrate it with a simple physics model, measuring performance and demonstrating build-time type safety for shader inputs.

tools.name: Soul-Brews-Studio/maw-js

tools.desc: 🌌 An interactive, procedurally-generated Milky Way galaxy in the browser — WebGL / three.js, no backend, no build step. MIT licensed.

cls.summary: A single-file, browser-based interactive Milky Way and Solar System demo built with three.js and WebGL for exploration and visualization.
cls.what_it_does: Galaxy Explorer procedurally generates a detailed Milky Way galaxy, a full 3D Solar System and several neighbour galaxies entirely in the browser using WebGL/three.js and GLSL shaders. It is used by opening the demo page (no build or backend) to fly, click beacons and inspect interactive info cards; it is notable for doing rich procedural rendering and particle systems in a compact, dependency-free HTML file.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository is 136 days old and provides a working live demo and polished README, but it's primarily a creative-coding demo repository with modest community uptake (≈100 stars) and no evidence of production deployments or versioned releases, so it fits an alpha-in-use maturity.
prerequisites: familiarity with three.js and WebGL/GLSL recommended
student_project_ideas: Extend the demo to visualise a simple instrument measurement overlay (e.g. simulated telescope FOV and detection limits) and export CSV telemetry for a small analysis pipeline.

Modify the procedural galaxy rules to implement and compare different star-distribution algorithms (e.g. change spiral arm parameters or implement a simple N-body-inspired clustering) and measure rendering/performance trade-offs.

tools.name: hyhy111/game-assets-maker
tools.desc: Turn videos into game-ready animation frames. Extract, remove backgrounds, align & trim locally; optional AI generation and Godot 4 skills.

cls.summary: Game Assets Maker is a desktop tool that converts videos into transparent PNG sprite frames, offers local background removal and alignment, and can optionally generate assets with AI and export to Godot 4.
cls.what_it_does: The tool extracts frames from video, removes backgrounds (using a downloadable U2Net model), lets you clean, align and batch-crop frames, and exports PNG sequences and JSON offsets for game engines. It includes optional AI image/video generation integrations and a set of 'GAM Skills' to automate workflows and export into Godot 4, and provides installers for Windows and macOS.
cls.trl_rationale: The project is an executable desktop application with downloadable installers and documented workflow, indicating early use, examples and releases; however the repository is only ~52 days old so it lacks the long track record required for higher TRLs.
prerequisites: Node.js/npm if using the GAM Skills (agents) features
student_project_ideas: Create a pipeline that converts a short recorded motion into a Godot-ready animated character: extract frames with GAM, apply batch cropping, and import using the gam-export Skill to build an in-engine animated sprite with offsets and audio.

Evaluate background-removal quality on different video materials by running GAM's U2Net-based removal and comparing edge quality and animation stability, then propose and test post-processing fixes (edge cleanup, padding strategies) to reduce visible artefacts in a game prototype.

tools.name: pearjelly/deep-blend

cls.summary: DeepBlend Studio is a DeepSeek Harness plugin that integrates Blender into a web-enabled studio for creating, previewing and delivering product photography and short product animation renders.
cls.what_it_does: DeepBlend provides a DSH plugin and Blender workbench to import models, author editable 'recipes' for product scenes, run real Cycles renders and produce saved revisions or PNG/MP4 deliverables. It is used as a pipeline tool inside DeepSeek Harness (DSH) to prepare, preview and export product-visualisation scenes with repeatable replay inputs and revision management, notable for its DSH integration and prebuilt installation bundles.
cls.trl_rationale: The README and release notes show functioning installs, examples (case films) and npm releases, indicating active alpha use; however the repository is only ~65 days old so by the provided TRL rules the maturity is capped at TRL 5.
student_project_ideas: Create a product-visualisation pipeline that imports a CAD-exported OBJ/FBX into DeepBlend, applies materials and lighting presets, then renders a set of stills and a short MP4 demonstrating reproducible scene recipes.

Extend the DeepBlend workflow to add automated QA: write a script that replays a saved revision, compares rendered frames to a reference image set (pixel-difference threshold) and generates a pass/fail report.

tools.name: htobty/ReadyLLM
tools.desc: Deploy, monitor, and tune LLM through a visual interface — plus image / video generation on top of ComfyUI.

cls.summary: ReadyLLM is an open-source web application to deploy, monitor and auto-tune local LLM inference engines and to run ComfyUI-based image/video generation from a single visual interface.
cls.what_it_does: ReadyLLM helps you register target machines (local or remote), deploy inference engines (llama.cpp, vLLM, SGLang), monitor GPU/VRAM/throughput/latency in real time, and run an automated two‑phase tuning process to improve throughput and latency. It also integrates ComfyUI for text-to-image and text-to-video generation and offers a model store with download and integrity checks; notable points are the executor abstraction for local/SSH targets and engine adapter pattern for adding inference engines.
cls.trl_rationale: The README describes a full-featured system with backend, frontend, adapters and multiple engines and the repo has community interest (102 stars) but is only 78 days old, so there is not yet a longer track record or stable releases; that supports an alpha/early‑in‑use TRL (~5).
student_project_ideas: Benchmark and compare LLM throughput and latency across two different GPU/driver setups using ReadyLLM's monitoring and auto‑tuning, and produce a report explaining the tuning decisions and measured gains.

Extend ReadyLLM with a new EngineAdapter for an additional local inference runtime (or a custom quantized model format) and evaluate tuning integration and deployment automation on a remote test host via SSH.

tools.name: Open-X-Humanoid/BICMap

Build a web dashboard that combines BicMap for map and point-cloud display with a simple MQTT backend to stream live robot poses and demonstrate remote monitoring and path re-planning in a simulated patrol scenario.

tools.name: FreedomIntelligence/BlenderLore

cls.what_it_does: BlenderLore extracts stepwise workflows from tutorial videos, reconstructs editable Blender projects and produces reproduction scripts, renders and validation logs; it packages the recovered methods as a reusable procedural-knowledge library (a "Skill") for coding agents. It is used by running the pipeline with local video files or URLs and requires Blender, Python and FFmpeg for execution, and it is notable for claiming a large, human-reviewed collection (~22k project instances) and tooling to execute and inspect reconstructed assets.
cls.trl_rationale: The repository provides detailed README, install steps and an end-to-end pipeline and claims a large, human-reviewed dataset, indicating more than a bare prototype; however it is only ~91 days old with no clear release history or broad community evidence, so maturity aligns with a beta-stage TRL 6.

student_project_ideas: Build a pipeline that takes a short Blender tutorial video, uses BlenderLore to reconstruct the tutorial into a reproducible Blender Python script, then extend the script to parameterise the model for a small parametric study of geometry variations.

Use the BlenderLore procedural-knowledge library to retrieve a material-creation method and combine it with a student-created rigging workflow to create and render a library of animated assets for use in a simple digital-twin visualization.

tools.name: memovai/mimimodel

The project is designed to run entirely on an ESP32‑S3 (16 MB flash, 8 MB PSRAM) with a tiny C runtime and a host CLI for flashing, managing tool schemas and issuing queries. What makes it notable is the extremely compact, dependency-free C implementation that memory-maps weights from flash and targets a ~$5 microcontroller.

C programming and embedded toolchain familiarity

Compare on-device tool-calling latency and accuracy by running the same Needle 2 prompt set on MimiModel (ESP32) and a host-based runtime (llama.cpp or another local LLM), and analyse trade-offs in power, latency and correctness.

student_project_ideas: Extend or instrument LibreCorsa to record and export telemetry (steering, wheel forces, tyre temps) to a CSV or timeseries DB, then perform data analysis and identify correlations between setup changes and lap time.

Integrate a control algorithm (e.g. simple model predictive controller or PI-based traction control) into the client to evaluate how active control strategies affect lap times and tyre wear across different track/weather conditions.

cls.summary: Jet Studio is a Godot-style 3D editor and C++17 game runtime that can build and run games on desktop and on microcontrollers (ESP32 family) using a custom Jet renderer and JetScript language.
cls.what_it_does: Jet Studio provides a desktop editor (Godot-like UI) and an independent C++ runtime to create, run and flash 2D/3D projects to desktop players and Arduino/ESP32 firmware. It targets constrained devices by pairing a lightweight renderer (Jet Engine) with a scripting language compatible with GDScript, and can build/flash examples directly from the editor.

SDL2 and typical desktop build toolchain
student_project_ideas: Create a simple physics-based interactive demo in Jet Studio and port it to an ESP32 board, demonstrating rendering and input on a constrained microcontroller.
Integrate a sensor (IMU or accelerometer) with an ESP32 flashed by Jet Studio to make a physical controller for a small game, and measure latency and resource use compared to desktop runtime.

tools.name: p0nymc1/cee
tools.desc: Deterministic-first execution engine for agent workflows in Go: the LLM extracts at the edge, a deterministic state machine decides. Zero dependencies, no-code JSON plugins, replayable runs.

cls.summary: CEE is a Go library that runs deterministic, replayable agent/workflow executions where an LLM only extracts structured fields and a state machine controls flow.
cls.what_it_does: CEE provides a deterministic-first execution engine for agent-style workflows: the LLM is used only to extract structured data while a sandboxed, deterministic state machine walks a DAG of steps, supports suspend/resume, probes, and no-code JSON plugins. It is used as a library (not a network service) and can compile to WebAssembly for a browser playground; notable features include zero external dependencies, manifest-based plugins, and run replayability/scorecards for measured decision changes.
cls.trl_rationale: The project is a working Go library with examples, a published playground (WASM), and a v0.2.0 tag suggested in the README; repository age is ~111 days (<1 year) so it shows early adoption but not long-term production track record, which caps TRL around 5.
prerequisites: Basic familiarity with workflows/DAGs and LLM endpoints (optional for draft/serve features)
student_project_ideas: Build a small incident-response workflow using CEE that uses an LLM to extract alert fields and a probe to gate actions, then add a persistent filestore and demonstrate suspend/resume across restarts.

Compare deterministic decision replay: implement two policy manifests and use CEE's diff/replay to measure which past decisions flip when a rule changes, producing a report and visualisation of flipped runs.

tools.name: llros007/lerobot_android
tools.desc: Use a android phone as the controller for a LeRobot mobile robot instead of a Raspberry Pi. It costs less and already has a screen, a USB camera, GPS, Wi-Fi, 5G, and an NPU.

cls.summary: A phone-hosted bridge that runs on an Android device to control LeRobot hardware (servos, cameras, differential base) and stream camera MJPEG to a PC so the phone replaces a Raspberry Pi as the robot controller.
cls.what_it_does: The project provides an Android app and matching Python host code so a smartphone can own USB serial servo adapters and USB cameras, stream MJPEG frames over HTTP, and exchange command/state with a PC at low latency. It is used to teleoperate an arm and drive a differential base, record episodes in the LeRobot dataset format, and reduce Wi‑Fi round‑trip latency by keeping the servo tick local to the phone.
cls.trl_rationale: The README, example commands and a debug APK show a working prototype used by early adopters and integration instructions, but the repository is only 53 days old so it lacks long-term production use and broader adoption — limiting the TRL to about 5.
prerequisites: Android build tools (JDK 17) and ability to install an APK
Access to LeRobot hardware (Feetech servos, USB serial adapters, robot base) and USB OTG on the phone
LAN connectivity between phone and host PC
student_project_ideas: Build a teleoperation lab where students replace a Pi with a phone: record and replay recorded episodes, then evaluate latency and packet loss effects on arm tracking using the provided MJPEG streams and LeRobot dataset format.

Extend the Android bridge to publish ROS 2 topics (camera, joint states, base velocity) and implement a simple autonomy node on the PC that uses the streamed camera for visual servoing or obstacle avoidance.

tools.name: PisenAILab/china-patent-figure-skill
tools.desc: 中国专利附图 Skill：从 3D 装配体（STEP）一步出符合国家知识产权局形式要求的说明书附图。自动标号与引线、13 项质检、PDF/Word/DXF 导出，支持 Skill / MCP / CLI，本地运行。

cls.summary: A Python tool that reads STEP assemblies and automatically generates patent-compliant line drawings (PDF/Word/DXF) with numbering, leader lines and 13 quality checks for China's patent office.
cls.what_it_does: It imports STEP assembly files, computes true geometric hidden-line views using a geometry kernel, auto-allocates figure numbers and leader lines, runs 13 format/quality checks, and exports submission-ready PDF, a Word 'disclosure' version, and DXF source files. It can be used as a local CLI tool, a browser-based workbench, or plugged into AI agents via Skill/MCP; notable points are that all geometric processing happens locally using OpenCascade-style kernels and the tool enforces Chinese patent figure formatting rules.
cls.trl_rationale: The repository has a detailed README, examples and runnable scripts but is very new (created 18 days ago) with no releases or demonstrable production users; that suggests early-alpha maturity rather than established production use.
prerequisites: basic familiarity with CAD concepts (assemblies, views, hidden-line)
student_project_ideas: Build an automated pipeline that takes a student-designed STEP assembly and produces a submission-ready patent figure package, adding an interface to compare agent-suggested part names (using a local LLM) with manual labels.
Integrate the tool's DXF export with a CAD toolchain (e.g. FreeCAD) to produce annotated manufacturing drawings and evaluate how the 13 quality checks map to downstream drawing standards.

tools.name: bpy-dev/blender-mcp
tools.desc: Independent enhanced distribution of Blender Lab MCP: standalone bpy, runtime API documentation, and benchmark tooling

cls.summary: An enhanced developer-preview distribution of a Blender MCP server that lets language-model-driven agents interact with Blender both in a live add-on and headless/saved-file modes for automated 3D/content workflows.
cls.what_it_does: It provides a small MCP (Model Context Protocol) server plus a Blender add-on so LLM-driven clients can query the Blender Python API and issue commands to Blender. Notable features include headless/saved-file CLI tools that run .blend files in subprocesses, selectable backends (Blender executable or standalone bpy), runtime API lookup, process isolation (timeouts/output caps), and benchmark tooling.

prerequisites: Basic understanding of LLM-based agent workflows and environment variables
student_project_ideas: Create an automated pipeline that uses the blender-mcp server and a small local LLM (e.g. llama.cpp) to generate and render parametrised architectural scenes from natural-language prompts, and evaluate output consistency across runs.

Implement a headless benchmarking experiment that compares different LLM prompts or local models on a set of BlenderBench tasks included in the repo and visualise token-efficiency and CLIP-similarity results.

tools.name: chopinregis/CreaBIM
tools.desc: Design-first BIM, modelled like Blender, made for architects. One model for 3D, plans, sections, sheets, schedules, quantities and IFC. Free, open source, offline. By Regis Benoit Brice Nde Tene.

cls.summary: CreaBIM is an open-source, architect-focused BIM modeller that keeps 3D, plans, sections, schedules and IFC exports in sync from a single model on your desktop.
cls.what_it_does: CreaBIM provides a design-first BIM authoring application: you model a building in 3D and plans, sections, sheets, schedules, quantities and IFC exports are generated automatically. It is a desktop application written in Rust, intended to replace the usual split workflow between a modeller and a BIM/drafting tool by keeping every view live and consistent.

for building from source: Rust toolchain and cargo

Create an automated pipeline that imports CreaBIM's glTF export into Blender or FreeCAD to generate rendered visuals and a construction sequencing storyboard, demonstrating model exchange and interoperability.

tools.name: tuallen/GOFish
tools.desc: GOFish reconstructs simulation-ready 3D digital twins directly from fisheye imagery, combining photorealistic Gaussian Splatting over the camera's full field of view with an aligned mesh for collisions.

cls.summary: GOFish reconstructs photorealistic, simulation-ready 3D scenes from fisheye images by performing full field-of-view Gaussian splatting and extracting an aligned collision mesh.
cls.what_it_does: GOFish trains Gaussian splatting models directly on fisheye imagery to render beyond 180° and extracts an aligned mesh suitable for collision and simulation. It is used by preparing scene folders (images, optional LiDAR), running the provided training/benchmark scripts, and requires an NVIDIA GPU and PyTorch; notable features are full-FoV fisheye support and an integrated mesh extraction pipeline so the same model supplies both photorealistic rendering and collision geometry.
cls.trl_rationale: The repository is a recent (25 days old) implementation accompanying a published paper with models and benchmarks; installation and full training/evaluation scripts are provided, suggesting early adopters can run it, but the project is too young to show long-term production use or broad community adoption, so TRL is limited to alpha-in-use.
prerequisites: NVIDIA GPU (compute capability >=7.0) and CUDA toolkit
CGAL (for mesh extraction) and Slang (renderer kernels)
student_project_ideas: Compare collision performance and physics stability by building a simple simulator that uses GOFish-extracted meshes versus LiDAR-derived meshes for robot navigation in a small indoor scene.

Extend GOFish to accept mixed pinhole and fisheye camera setups: prepare a dataset combining standard RGB images and fisheye panoramas and evaluate rendering quality and mesh F-score against the provided benchmarks.

familiarity with MMD (PMX/VMD) or GLB assets

cls.summary: Starling provides local, pure-.NET packaged AI models (embeddings, NER, image/video search and chat) that run on ONNX Runtime and plug into Microsoft.Extensions.AI so hosted-provider code can be swapped for local inference.
cls.what_it_does: Starling packages pretrained models as NuGet libraries that run locally on ONNX Runtime (CPU or CUDA) to provide embeddings, named-entity extraction, multimodal search and chat via Microsoft.Extensions.AI interfaces. It is used by adding the NuGet packages to a .NET project, downloading the pinned ONNX assets once, and calling the provided IEmbeddingGenerator or IChatClient implementations; notable features are model pinning with SHA-256 verification and no Python sidecar or external API key requirement.

tools.name: gokayfem/video-to-blender

cls.summary: A Python skill and node-group library that lets code-driven agents build procedural Blender Geometry Nodes, Shader and compositor graphs from reference media or prompts.
cls.what_it_does: This project provides an agent 'skill' plus a tested library of reusable node-groups and a Python graph builder ('nodekit') that programmatically constructs Geometry Nodes, Shader Nodes and compositor graphs in Blender 5.2+. It is used by agents (Claude Code, Codex, Copilot, Gemini, etc.) or scripts to translate prompts or reference video/images into editable node setups, and includes tools to lint, validate and numerically check groups.
cls.trl_rationale: The repository is very new (created 27 days ago) so lacks a long track record; the README documents a tested node-group library, validation tools and example workflows which indicate early real use beyond a single demo, supporting an alpha-in-use judgement rather than a pure prototype.
prerequisites: Python 3 and familiarity with Blender's Python API
Basic knowledge of Blender Geometry Nodes and shaders
student_project_ideas: Create a reproducible pipeline that converts short reference videos of a simple mechanical scene into editable Geometry Nodes setups and compare rendered outputs with the reference; measure how parameter sweeps change the reconstruction.
Integrate the nodekit-built procedural assets into a small interactive visualization (Blender + glTF export) to evaluate procedural variability and reuse across different input curves or terrains.

tools.name: ruiwang20010702/foursday
tools.desc: Personal-memory-driven AI work twin that uses Codex to work inside real projects.

cls.summary: Foursday is an AI "work twin" agent that runs Codex inside a user's real project workspace, using personal memory and enterprise messaging (DingTalk) to read context, perform edits, run tests and produce evidence-backed replies.
cls.what_it_does: Foursday binds a verified sender identity and an exact project link to provide a scoped AI agent that can read project files and personal memory, plan and execute tasks inside the real workspace via Codex, and persist or pause long-running work with audited evidence. It is used as a Node.js control plane and plugin set (DingTalk integration, workspace sandboxing, MCP control) that enforces safety boundaries and owner-intervention fences while allowing the agent to run tests, edit files and produce read-back evidence.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository has substantial architecture and deployment docs, integrations (Hermes, Codex/Claude, DingTalk) and pilot-test guides, suggesting a beta-capable project; however it is only ~109 days old so lacks a long track record or wide production adoption which limits higher TRL.

Familiarity with agent concepts, sandboxing and security policies

tools.name: legioncodeinc/vibe-coding-tools

cls.what_it_does: The Wasp Nest supplies a Core plus installable plugins (Drones, Stingers, workflows) that extend hosted coding assistants (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, ZCode, Cowork) with project-aware skills, templates for PRDs/IRDs/contracts and automated workflows for planning, coding and verification. It is used by installing the marketplace into a supported assistant host and enabling the Core and selected plugins; notable is its focus on captured project 'Library' knowledge, contract pinning and guided PRD-driven verification paths.

basic Git and project repository workflow knowledge

tools.name: Tylogi/TyloQuant
tools.desc: Get more intelligence from every bit. Better quantization formats and smarter calibration let larger, stronger models run smoothly on the hardware you already own.

cls.summary: MFQ (TyloQuant) is an open-source mixed-precision quantization and native runtime system for running large language models efficiently on local CUDA and Apple Metal hardware.
cls.what_it_does: MFQ produces compact weight formats and per-expert mixed-precision calibration to reduce model size and preserve quality, and provides native CUDA and Metal runtimes to run quantized models locally. It is used to quantize LLMs into MFQ/GGUF-like formats, run them with reduced memory residency (including SSD spill) and expose OpenAI-/Anthropic-compatible inference APIs for applications and agents.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository has active documentation, benchmarks and platform backends (CUDA/Metal) and a modest community (≈95 stars) indicating early adopters, but the project is only ~116 days old so it lacks a long track record and stable releases required for TRL 6+.

familiarity with LLMs, quantization concepts and GGUF model formats
student_project_ideas: Compare downstream task quality and throughput of a small LLM quantized with MFQ versus the same model in llama.cpp, measuring KLD/Top1 agreement and tokens/sec on a student laptop (Metal) or GPU (CUDA).

Integrate MFQ-quantized model serving behind an OpenAI-compatible API and build a small autonomous agent that runs locally, demonstrating end-to-end inference latency, memory residency (VRAM + SSD spill) and cost comparisons.

tools.name: julianmb/halofpx
tools.desc: High-performance Lemonade alternative for AMD Strix Halo & Radeon — latest MoE models (Ling-3.0-Flash, Qwen 3.8 Flash Next, Ornith 1.5), bleeding-edge RDNA 3.5 Wave64/ROCmFP4 kernels, and silicon-tuned profiles.

cls.summary: HaloFPX is a local model server and model zoo optimised for AMD Strix Halo and Radeon GPUs that provides Lemonade-compatible CLI and an OpenAI-style endpoint with silicon-tuned kernels and custom quant formats.
cls.what_it_does: HaloFPX packages pre-quantized large language and MoE models and serves them locally with AMD-targeted acceleration (RDNA 3.5 Wave64 / ROCm kernels) and per-model performance profiles. cls.trl_rationale: The repo is feature-rich and has attracted some community attention (95 stars) and active commits, but it is very new (created 92 days ago) so there is limited real-world track record and no evidence of wide production deployments; this supports an Alpha / early-in-use TRL.

Python runtime and typical Python packaging tools
Familiarity with local LLM model files (GGUF) and command-line model servers

Integrate HaloFPX with a simple IoT data pipeline: deploy the server on a Linux edge device and build a client that sends telemetry to an LLM for on-device summarisation and anomaly explanation.

tools.name: Ropedia/S-Agent
tools.desc: S-Agent: Spatial Tool-Use Elicits Reasoning for Spatial Intelligence

cls.summary: S-Agent is a research agent framework that uses vision-language models plus spatial tools to plan evidence-gathering across multiple views/frames for metric and relational 3D reasoning.
cls.what_it_does: S-Agent frames spatial reasoning as an agentic loop: a planner (VLM) issues evidence requests, calls specialized 2D and 2D→3D tools, and accumulates scene and agent memory across views and time to answer metric, counting, orientation and route reasoning queries. It is notable for combining multi-view persistence, explicit geometric lifting, and trajectory distillation into a compact model (S-Agent-8B) described in the accompanying paper and demos.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository hosts the paper, demo video and project page but the code, checkpoints and tools are not yet open-sourced; the project is a recent research release (~153 days old) and currently functions as a paper/demo release rather than runnable software, so it's at a proof-of-concept research stage.
prerequisites: machine learning and deep learning concepts
student_project_ideas: Build a simplified S-Agent pipeline that uses an off-the-shelf VLM (e.g. CLIP/BLIP) plus an open-source depth estimator to plan a sequence of camera viewpoints and aggregate metric estimates on a small multi-view dataset.

Evaluate how tool-use (2D measurement + 2D→3D lifting) improves counting or distance estimates by comparing a single-view VLM baseline to an evidence-accumulating agent on a curated set of spatial questions.

tools.name: pixijs/3d
tools.desc: A 3D extension for PixiJS

cls.summary: PixiJS 3D is a TypeScript library that adds 3D rendering (WebGL2/WebGPU) and glTF model support to the 2D PixiJS renderer for interactive web visualisations and simple 3D scenes.
cls.what_it_does: PixiJS 3D extends the PixiJS 2D framework with a 3D view, geometry, PBR/Phong/Toon materials, lights, shadows, animations, particles and post-processing; it loads glTF models (with Draco/meshopt) and exposes pointer events on 3D objects. It is used as an npm package alongside pixi.js to create interactive browser graphics and supports both WebGL2 and WebGPU backends, with TypeScript types and example guides.
cls.trl_rationale: The repository is young (created 67 days ago) which limits proven maturity; it already provides documentation, TypeScript types, examples and npm installation which indicates early adoption (alpha in use) but no long track record or stable major releases yet.
student_project_ideas: Build an interactive web demo that loads a glTF mechanical assembly (exported from Blender) and adds camera orbit, lighting controls and part highlighting using PixiJS 3D and PixiJS.

Create a simple lightweight digital-twin-style dashboard that streams sensor data (mocked) to animate object properties (rotation/colour/visibility) in a PixiJS 3D scene and add UI controls for scenario playback.

cls.summary: A small toolkit that claims to decrypt and unpack Unity AssetBundle files for the mobile game 'Girls' Frontline: Fire Control'.
cls.what_it_does: The repository provides tools to decrypt UnityFS/XOR-encrypted AssetBundles, extract schema-less FlatBuffers manifests, handle CDN subpackages and export assets (not including the game assets themselves). It is intended for unpacking and exporting Unity game assets and appears to be a specialist game asset extraction utility rather than an engineering design tool.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository is very new (created 12 days ago) and has no README; the topics indicate working code for asset decryption and extraction but there is no documented track record or releases, so maturity is limited to early adoption/alpha use.
prerequisites: basic command-line skills and knowledge of game asset formats (FlatBuffers, UnityFS)

tools.name: trafficflowhq/ohmail
tools.desc: Consent-first email on your existing IMAP mailboxes. Optional AI assistet screener with local or Cloud models. Full local Clients for MacOS, Windows, Linux + Arch and Omarchy integrationst. Android + iOS (coming soon) Apps. AGPL-3.0.

cls.summary: Ohmail is a privacy-focused, consent-first email client that organizes IMAP mailboxes with a Screener for new senders and optional AI-assisted filing using local or cloud models.
cls.what_it_does: Ohmail connects to existing IMAP mailboxes and automatically files messages into real IMAP folders while holding first-time senders in a Screener for a one-time decision. It optionally uses AI (local models via Ollama or cloud APIs like OpenAI/Anthropic) to suggest filing and draft replies, and can be self-hosted or run as desktop apps for macOS, Windows and Linux with mobile clients.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository is 110 days old but already provides packaged desktop installers, a hosted demo, self-hosting with Docker Compose, and published mobile APK — indicating beta-level maturity; age under one year limits higher TRL.
prerequisites: An IMAP email account (Gmail, iCloud, Fastmail, Microsoft 365 or other IMAP server)
Desktop OS (Windows, macOS, Linux) for desktop clients; optional Docker for self-hosting
Optional API keys for OpenAI / Anthropic or a local Ollama model to enable AI features
student_project_ideas: Evaluate the privacy trade-offs of local vs cloud AI filing by running ohmail self-hosted with Ollama and with a cloud LLM, then measuring latency, privacy-related data exposure, and filing accuracy.
Extend ohmail with a small analytics dashboard (hosted separately) that visualises user filing rules and screening decisions over time, using the IMAP-stored rules as the data source.

tools.name: aaronnat23/disp8ch
tools.desc: Self-hosted AI workspace where chat becomes visual workflows, multi-agent operations, and reviewable automations. Local memory; local or cloud models

cls.summary: Disp8ch is a self‑hosted, local‑first multi‑agent workspace that converts plain‑English chat into inspectable visual workflows, role‑based agent runs, and auditable execution with local or cloud LLMs.
cls.what_it_does: Disp8ch turns chat prompts into editable visual workflows and multi‑agent processes (planners, implementers, reviewers) that are approval gated and auditable; it can run fully local models or connect to cloud providers. Notable features include scoped local memory, delivery briefs, supervised runs with acceptance evidence, an operator dashboard, and installer scripts for quick local deployment.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository is recent (created ~148 days ago) but shows an install script, active pushes, ~94 stars and a detailed README describing tested features and local install; these point to a beta‑stage project rather than long track record, so TRL 6 (beta) is appropriate.
prerequisites: familiarity with Node.js / TypeScript and web apps
basic understanding of LLM providers (local runtimes vs cloud API keys) and agent workflows
student_project_ideas: Build a supervised run that automates acceptance testing for a small software repo: connect disp8ch to a local model and Git repo, have planner propose changes and an implementer create PRs while the reviewer verifies tests and produces an outcome receipt.

Integrate disp8ch with a simulated IoT data source to automate an operations workflow that detects anomalies, assigns a maintenance task, and records evidence for later audit (combine with a time‑series DB or MQTT broker).

tools.name: runboubou/boubou
tools.desc: Run voice AI locally with open-source models. Bring it to any device with one command.

cls.summary: Boubou is a local, open-source CLI tool that runs speech-to-speech AI models on your own Mac or Linux machine so you can talk to an offline voice assistant.
cls.what_it_does: Boubou launches local speech pipelines (recording, speech recognition, LLM inference, and TTS) with a single command and serves the voice over the LAN or locally. It is used as a privacy-first voice assistant/runtime that selects models appropriate for the host hardware and can be run via an npm launcher or built from source in Rust.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository is very new (created 15 days ago) but the README shows runnable examples (npx launcher) and build instructions; however there is no long track record or stable releases yet, so TRL is limited to alpha-in-use.
prerequisites: Node.js / npm for the npx launcher
Rust toolchain (Rust 1.91+) to build from source
student_project_ideas: Integrate Boubou as a voice interface for a small ROS2 robot and demonstrate remote control and status queries over LAN using the serve endpoint.

Measure and compare latency, CPU/RAM usage and audio quality of different local TTS/LLM model combinations on various hardware (M1/M2, x86 Linux) to produce a short report on deployability for embedded/edge devices.

tools.name: MultiX0/ip-nas
tools.desc: Raspberry Pi 5 home NAS: CasaOS apps, Nur Hub and the Nur app (local AI, Fish Audio voice), a 3D-printed case and an ESP32-S3 touch screen

cls.summary: A personal Raspberry Pi 5 NAS project combining CasaOS-managed Docker apps, a local AI assistant service (Nur), 3D-printed enclosure files and ESP32‑S3 touchscreen firmware.
cls.what_it_does: This repository documents and provides files to build a home NAS on a Raspberry Pi 5: hardware parts list, 3D models for a printed case, Pi setup instructions, CasaOS Docker app manifests, a small service called Nur Hub that manages apps and local AI models, and firmware for a 3.5" ESP32‑S3 touchscreen. It's used by cloning the repo, following the Pi and CasaOS setup, importing the provided Docker Compose file for Nur Hub, and flashing the touchscreen firmware; the project bundles maker/homelab instructions rather than a reusable engineering library.
cls.trl_rationale: The README and repo show a working, end-to-end home build with Docker images and firmware, but the repository is very new (created 26 days ago) and appears to be a single-person project without broad adoption or versioned releases, so it matches an experimental prototype TRL.
student_project_ideas: Extend the Nur Hub service to add automated backup and encrypted remote sync (e.g. integrate with Nextcloud or a cloud storage API) and measure throughput and reliability on Raspberry Pi 5.

Create an enhanced touchscreen UI (Flutter + LVGL) that shows drive health and local AI status, and add a small sensor (temperature/humidity) via ESP32‑S3 to demonstrate local monitoring and dashboarding.

tools.name: alebal123bal/khadas_yolov8n_multithread
tools.desc: Real-time YOLOv8n UAV detection on the RK3588S NPU | saturates the sensor at 46 FPS | ~140 MB RAM | fully hardware-accelerated (ISP+RGA+NPU) | on-device LLM scene summaries

cls.summary: A C++ multi-process, hardware‑accelerated pipeline that runs YOLOv8n detection and on‑device LLM summaries on RK3588S boards to detect and track UAVs in real time.
cls.what_it_does: This project captures MIPI camera frames on RK3588S SoCs, runs YOLOv8n inference across all three NPU cores in parallel, performs multi-object tracking and temporal processing, and produces annotated output to HDMI/RTSP; when an object leaves the scene it can generate an on‑device natural language summary using a small LLM. It is implemented as separate processes connected by Unix-domain sockets, uses Rockchip fixed-function blocks (ISP, RGA, NPU) to keep CPU and RAM usage low, and is intended to run on low-memory RK3588S boards like the Khadas Edge2.
cls.trl_rationale: The repository shows a working, hardware-tested implementation (benchmarks, docs, tested on Khadas Edge2) and build instructions including cross‑compile toolchain, indicating beta maturity; however it is under 1 year old (created ~168 days ago) so lacks long-term production track record required for higher TRL.
prerequisites: familiarity with Linux aarch64 and cross-compilation
access to RK3588S hardware (e.g. Khadas Edge2) and compatible MIPI camera
basic knowledge of RK NPU/RKNN and RGA/ISP toolchains
student_project_ideas: Extend the pipeline to add a resource-aware scheduler that dynamically balances NPU time between detection and the on‑device LLM, and evaluate tradeoffs in latency and throughput on a Khadas Edge2.

Replace YOLOv8n with an alternative lightweight detector (converted to RKNN) and compare detection accuracy, FPS and memory footprint across different RK3588S boards; present results and modify buffer pool sizing for optimal RAM use.

tools.name: NoiseGlyph/MELE-Godot-Extractor-resocket
tools.desc: Exports Mass Effect Legendary Edition models, levels, and music to glTF for Godot, from your own install, via Legendary Explorer.

cls.summary: A very new tool that exports Mass Effect Legendary Edition game assets (models, levels, music) to glTF formatted files suitable for importing into Godot using files from a local game install and Legendary Explorer.
cls.what_it_does: The repository aims to extract and convert assets from Mass Effect Legendary Edition into glTF so they can be used in the Godot engine, drawing data from a user's own game installation via Legendary Explorer. It is notable for targeting a specific game and toolchain (Legendary Explorer -> glTF -> Godot) rather than being a general-purpose asset pipeline.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository is very new (created 12 days ago) with no README and no evidence of releases or real-world use; current public metadata suggests a proof-of-concept stage rather than a production-ready project.
prerequisites: Local installation of Mass Effect Legendary Edition game files
Legendary Explorer (tool used to access the game data)
Basic familiarity with Godot and glTF asset import

tools.name: GDPatch/GDPatch
tools.desc: A versatile cross-platform cross-version Godot mod loader

cls.summary: GDPatch is a cross-platform mod loader for the Godot game engine that applies script patches and runtime hooks to enable mods across Godot versions.
cls.what_it_does: GDPatch lets users load and apply mods to Godot-based games by patching GDScript and inserting runtime hooks so mods work across different Godot engine versions. It is distributed as a Rust project with documentation and a community Discord, and reuses reconstruction and patching ideas from earlier Godot reverse-engineering and modding tools.
cls.trl_rationale: The repository is active, has documentation and community links and a noticeable star count, but it is only ~117 days old so it lacks the multi-release, long-term adoption evidence required for TRL 6+.
prerequisites: Familiarity with the Godot Engine and GDScript
Basic Rust toolchain knowledge for building the project
Understanding of modding concepts and runtime patching

tools.name: Dryxio/gta-scout
tools.desc: Create GTA-style 3D models and scenes with your AI and Blender, using models and textures from your game. Early alpha.

cls.summary: GTA Scout helps an AI agent find and inspect models and textures from GTA San Andreas and uses Blender to assemble, modify and export editable 3D scenes in the game's visual style.
cls.what_it_does: GTA Scout searches a user's GTA San Andreas game files for models and textures, exposes those assets to an AI coding agent, and provides scripts and Blender integration so the agent can combine, modify or generate geometry and save .blend files. It is designed as an AI-assisted Blender workflow focused on reusing game assets to create props, vehicles, interiors and small scenes in the GTA style.
cls.trl_rationale: The README labels the project 'Early alpha' and the repo is only 71 days old; it has a working demo and integration instructions but no long track record or stable releases, so maturity is early-alpha (TRL 4).
prerequisites: Blender installed and callable from CLI
Classic PC San Andreas game files (user-provided)
Python runtime and ability for an AI agent to run commands and read/write files
Optional: an AI coding agent or local LLM capable of executing workflows
student_project_ideas: Use GTA Scout and Blender to assemble a themed street market scene from San Andreas assets, then document the pipeline and produce a rendered walkthrough of the scene.

Extend or adapt the asset discovery layer to support another classic game (or a different GTA release) and create an automated Blender script to convert located assets into a standardised .blend asset library.

tools.name: Ariasmaze29819/pc-rpgmaker3-resp
tools.desc: Native PC reimplementation of the RPG Maker 3 (PS2) engine - format documentation and tools (BYOA)

cls.summary: A recently-published open-source effort to reimplement the PlayStation 2 RPG Maker 3 engine for PC and provide format documentation and asset tools.
cls.what_it_does: This repository aims to recreate the RPG Maker 3 (PS2) engine for native PC, exposing file format documentation and conversion/viewer tools so community members can bring assets to PC (BYOA: bring your own assets). It appears to be a collection of tools and an Avalonia/C# application for inspecting and converting game assets rather than a polished end-user product. Notable points from the metadata are support for asset conversion, a Blender addon, and a mun-file viewer, but there is no README or detailed documentation in the repository.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository is very new (created 12 days ago) and contains no README; metadata shows prototype intent (tools, viewers) but no evidence of releases, users or production use, so it is at an early proof-of-concept maturity.

tools.name: benmaster82/writher
tools.desc: 🎙️ Offline voice productivity for Windows - dictate text into any app and control a local AI assistant by voice. Manages notes, to-do lists, appointments & reminders. 100% local: faster-whisper + Ollama + SQLite. No cloud, no telemetry. Free and open source alternative to Wispr Flow

tools.name: duongngocbinh56599-ui/local-llm-lab
tools.desc: Honest local LLM deployment planning and benchmarking for high unified-memory Macs and future Linux/NVIDIA rigs.

cls.summary: A Python CLI that predicts whether a local machine can run a given LLM configuration, generates dry-run deploy scripts, benchmarks and produces reproducible reports for local LLM deployment planning.
cls.what_it_does: local-llm-lab detects and profiles local hardware, estimates memory and runtime requirements for models (weights, KV cache, OS reserve and overhead), ranks quantization and backend options, and generates dry-run deployment scripts and reports. It is used as a planning and benchmarking tool (CLI + local report server) to avoid wasted downloads and to simulate stress and throughput on unified-memory Macs and similar rigs.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository is an actively maintained project with a detailed README, CLI, examples and reporting features, and 93 stars, indicating community interest; however it is younger than one year (165 days), so it fits a Beta-level TRL rather than production-mature.
student_project_ideas: Extend the planner to add CUDA/VRAM-specific heuristics and validate predictions by running small-scale benchmarks on an NVIDIA workstation, then compare predicted vs measured throughput and memory use.

Use the tool to build a teaching lab where students compare quantization and context-length tradeoffs for a 70B model across simulated hardware fixtures and produce a report recommending safe deploy options.

tools.name: FedericoTs/quantprobe
tools.desc: Run a 110B on a 2016 PC with 16 GB RAM. Know your tok/s before you download. Placement beats budget: predicts speed + memory fit for any GGUF on your exact hardware, self-calibrates, emits the exact llama.cpp command — or 'quantprobe auto' does it all. Falsification-tested laws; misses published at full size. pip install quantprobe

cls.summary: Quantprobe predicts whether and how a GGUF local LLM will run on a specific machine, estimates token/s and memory placement, and emits the exact llama.cpp command (or can fetch, build and run the model for you).
cls.what_it_does: Quantprobe measures or models hardware characteristics and a target GGUF model to predict throughput, memory placement (VRAM/RAM/disk) and binding constraints before downloading the model, then produces an exact run command (or runs it with quantprobe auto). It self-calibrates to a machine, validates predictions against bench runs and produces quality and speed checks so you can choose quantization and placement tuned to that exact hardware.
cls.trl_rationale: The repo is actively developed, pip-installable, documented and reports validation results, indicating beta-level maturity; however it is only 119 days old so it lacks a longer track record and broad production adoption, which limits TRL to 6.
prerequisites: local LLM files in GGUF format and basic understanding of llama.cpp flags
student_project_ideas: Build a lab exercise that uses quantprobe to compare predicted vs measured token/s and memory placement for several quantized GGUF models on different student machines, and analyse the sources of prediction error.

Create an integration that automatically runs quantprobe then launches a local inference server (llama.cpp / llama-server) with the recommended flags and measures end-to-end latency and throughput under varying batch sizes.

tools.name: gittensor-ai-lab/sparkinfer
tools.desc: Fastest MoE/LLM inference runtime for consumer and edge Blackwell GPUs. SN74 on Gittensor.

cls.summary: Sparkinfer is a native C++/CUDA inference runtime optimised for NVIDIA Blackwell GPUs to run large LLMs and Mixture-of-Experts models on desktop, workstation and edge-class hardware.
cls.what_it_does: It provides a compact, high-performance OpenAI-compatible server for LLM decoding (including MoE models) that uses Blackwell‑native kernels and ModelOpt quantised checkpoints to achieve much higher throughput and prefill speed than common CPU-based runtimes. It is used as a standalone container or built from source to serve text, images and video inputs with features like speculative decoding, large context sizes and compatibility with common API surfaces (OpenAI/Anthropic/Ollama).
cls.trl_rationale: The repo is a working, actively pushed C++/CUDA project with Docker images, documented runtime flags and model hub integration; it has community interest (stars/forks) but is under 1 year old (created 2026-06-22), so it fits a beta-level TRL rather than long-term production maturity.
prerequisites: NVIDIA Blackwell-class GPU (sm_120) or compatible CUDA device
Linux familiarity (Docker preferred) and CUDA toolchain for building from source
Familiarity with LLM concepts and model quantisation (ModelOpt / NVFP4)
student_project_ideas: Benchmark sparkinfer against llama.cpp and ggml on a Blackwell GPU for different quantisation formats and contexts, then report throughput/latency trade-offs and implications for edge deployment.

Integrate sparkinfer as an on-prem inference service in a simple robotics demonstrator (ROS node or edge gateway) to evaluate real-time response and resource usage when serving multimodal prompts (text+image).

tools.name: Adyansh04/grove-g1
tools.desc: ROS 2 Jazzy autonomy stack for the Unitree G1 humanoid, developed in simulation first on unitree_mujoco: a learned walking policy in ros2_control, Nav2 navigation, MoveIt 2 manipulation and BehaviorTree.CPP missions, with the canopy world model and the NervROS agent you talk to.

cls.summary: Grove-G1 is an open-source ROS 2 autonomy stack that integrates learned walking, Nav2 navigation, MoveIt 2 manipulation, perception and mission-level behaviour for the Unitree G1 humanoid, developed and validated in MuJoCo simulation before hardware transfer.
cls.what_it_does: Grove-G1 supplies a full autonomy stack for a humanoid robot: a learned locomotion policy running as a ros2_control controller, SLAM/AMCL + Nav2 navigation, MoveIt 2 manipulation and BehaviorTree.CPP mission orchestration, plus a world model (canopy) and a conversational agent (NervROS). It is used by running the ROS 2 launches in simulation (unitree_mujoco) that mirror the robot DDS topics so the same code can later run on the real G1; notable points are the learned gait integrated with ros2_control, live octomap collision-checking for MoveIt plans, and language-agent mission execution via NervROS.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository demonstrates a complete stack with demos, multiple subpackages, and active pushes and stars, indicating beta-level maturity; however the project is only 123 days old so it lacks the longer track record or widespread production deployments required for TRL 7+.
student_project_ideas: Integrate a new payload or sensor in the g1_description and evaluate how the learned locomotion policy and Nav2 navigation behave when carrying the payload in simulation, measuring stability and path-following performance.

Extend canopy's world model to add semantic room labels and evaluate NervROS mission success rates for language-specified tasks (e.g. 'fetch the mug in the kitchen') by combining Vision-Language-Action outputs with MoveIt grasp checks.

tools.name: armpro24-blip/cad-cae-copilot
tools.desc: CAD/CAE Copilot — an AI-native CAD/CAE/CAX workbench for AI agents. Text-to-CAD, text-to-CAE, real build123d/OpenCASCADE geometry, editable parameters, stable topology pointers, deterministic critique, and MCP server tools.

cls.summary: CAD/CAE Copilot is an AI-native workbench that lets an MCP-driven agent generate real build123d/OpenCASCADE CAD, produce STEP/STL/GLB outputs, and continue into CAE workflows with reproducible .aieng packages.
cls.what_it_does: It converts a natural-language engineering specification into editable, verifiable CAD models (built with build123d/OpenCASCADE) and associated CAE artifacts, exposing named parts, editable parameters and stable topology pointers. It is driven by an external MCP-capable agent, can export STEP/STL/GLB, run deterministic critiques and benchmarked analytical FEA, and packages all artifacts into a reproducible .aieng bundle.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository is 175 days old (<1 year) but shows signs of maturity: a published alpha release (v0.1.0-alpha.4), Docker images on GHCR, CI that runs benchmark suites, and non-trivial adoption (93 stars). That indicates a beta-level, actively developed project rather than a one-off proof of concept, but it lacks long-term production track record required for TRL 7+.
prerequisites: an MCP-capable client (Claude Code, GitHub Copilot, etc.)
student_project_ideas: Create an agent-driven workflow that reads a spec for a small mechanical bracket, generates parametric CAD with CAD/CAE Copilot, runs the included analytical FEA benchmark, and visualises differences between design iterations.

Integrate CAD/CAE Copilot with a simple CI pipeline to automatically run the repository's analytical FEA benchmark on model changes and produce a reproducibility report (.aieng) comparing solver outputs to closed-form references.

tools.name: Frank-ZY-Dou/awesome-ai-3d-modeling-robotics
tools.desc: Source-linked examples of AI models used for 3D modeling, industrial design and CAD, and robot control, with archived media and the model named for every case

cls.summary: A curated, source-linked index of public demonstrations and examples where AI models are used for 3D modeling, CAD/industrial design and robot control, with archived media and a companion MIT survey.
cls.what_it_does: This repository collects and organises public demonstrations, papers and code links showing how general AI models are applied to 3D modelling, CAD and robot control, and archives demo media so entries remain verifiable. It is used as a reference and survey resource (grouped by application) rather than a runnable tool, notable for its breadth, source-linking and companion MIT CDFG survey.
cls.trl_rationale: This is a curated, actively updated index rather than a production software product; the repository is only ~2 months old so per the TRL rules it cannot exceed TRL 5 despite having many examples and community interest (93 stars). The README and archived media show usefulness but not long-term production use or stable releases.
student_project_ideas: Create a small comparative study that reproduces and evaluates 3–5 demo cases from the archive (e.g. image-to-3D pipelines), documenting inputs, models used and failure modes.
Use the archived demo videos and links to build a searchable dataset and visual dashboard that tags cases by application, model and evaluation metric for a class survey or literature review.

tools.name: xuedai-mayi/dsh-wenshan
tools.desc: 问山：DeepSeek Harness 地理野外实习知识图谱插件与非官方二次开发项目

cls.summary: 问山 (dsh-wenshan) is an open-source DeepSeek Harness plugin that organises geographic fieldwork materials into a reviewable, spatially-aware knowledge graph with guided field-assistant and data ingestion tools.
cls.what_it_does: It collects documents, images, audio and common GIS files, extracts content and builds a provenance-preserving knowledge graph used for on-site Q&A, guided tours and photo-map playback. The project supplies plugins for retrieval, spatial queries, a read-only 'field assistant' agent and interactive 2D/3D graph and map visualisations for inspecting and evolving knowledge.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository is 91 days old and includes runnable installation and startup scripts plus integrated DeepSeek Harness source for reproducible local demos, showing alpha-level use; however there is limited evidence of wider production deployments or long-term stability, so TRL is kept at 5.
prerequisites: familiarity with GIS file formats (GeoJSON, GPX, Shapefile) and basic web/server tooling
student_project_ideas: Build a guided fieldwork app using the dsh-wenshan intake pipeline and a small local dataset (photos, GPX track, PDFs) to demonstrate ingestion, provenance and question-answering with the read-only field assistant.
Extend the photo-map playback by adding weather/time overlays from an external API and evaluate how temporal-spatial visualisation helps students interpret field observations.

tools.name: leehack/llamadart
tools.desc: Cross-platform on-device LLM inference for Dart & Flutter: GGUF via llama.cpp and LiteRT-LM on Android, iOS, macOS, Windows, Linux and web.

tools.name: Zev55555/fragment-universe
tools.desc: 把来不及整理的文字、链接和图片，点亮成一片可以重新打开的私人记忆星空。

cls.summary: Fragment Universe is a browser-first personal note/collection app that saves short text, links and images as clickable ‘stars’ stored locally so you can return to and extend memories without mandatory categorisation.
cls.what_it_does: Fragment Universe captures quick notes, pasted links and uploaded images, stores content locally (IndexedDB/local-first) and represents each saved item as an interactive star in a 3D starfield. It is used as a privacy-focused, no-login web app (Next.js + three.js) with export/restore and background processing for link/image extraction; notable for its local-first storage and a visual 'star' metaphor implemented with Web 3D.
cls.trl_rationale: The project is a working web application with an online demo and local-run instructions, and has modest community interest (92 stars). The repository was created ~113 days ago, so it is still recent and lacks a longer track record or wide adoption, supporting an alpha/in-use TRL rather than beta/production.
student_project_ideas: Extend the app to add optional peer-to-peer sync across devices (e.g. using WebRTC or a small server) and evaluate privacy trade-offs compared with the current local-only design.
Build an accessibility-focused variant that replaces the 3D starfield with alternative visualisations and measure recall/return-rate in a small user study.

tools.name: takeshy/obsidian-local-llm-hub

tools.name: apromisedland/trustworthy-agent-simulation

cls.what_it_does: The project runs an agent-based simulation of a small town where residents, businesses and producers exchange messages, form memories, make decisions, execute contracts and produce/consume resources. It is used from a CLI or dashboard to run baseline, offline and LLM-driven experiments, record authoritative transaction logs and replay committed states for auditability. Notable aspects are explicit resource accounting, configurable policy/ablation experiment suites, run resume/replay semantics and built-in validation tests.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository was created 49 days ago so maturity is limited; README, tests and CI are present and the project is installable and runnable (alpha in use), but there is no long track record or evidence of production deployments.
prerequisites: familiarity with agent-based modelling concepts (agents, ticks, experiments)
basic CLI and virtual environment usage
student_project_ideas: Extend the town scenario with an energy market producer and evaluate the effect of subsidies on energy access and price volatility, using the built-in batch/policy experiment runner to collect metrics.

Integrate a local LLM endpoint (or a constrained rule-based model) for agent decision-making and compare behaviour and resource accounting across baseline, ablation and LLM modes, producing visualisations from the dashboard and statistical summaries.
