tools.desc: Threejs examples of different game genres and features

cls.summary: A browser-based Three.js WebGPU playground with playable prototype scenes demonstrating procedural worlds, vehicle physics, animation and rendering experiments for real-time interactive systems.
cls.what_it_does: The repository provides a collection of prototype, playable scenes and reusable systems (physics, movement, vehicle, streaming terrain, procedural city generators and post-processing) implemented with Three.js (WebGPU) and the Rapier physics engine. It's used as a study and experimentation workspace to explore game-style interaction, procedural streaming, and rendering techniques that can be ported to other projects rather than a finished engine.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository is an active prototype workspace with runnable examples and docs but explicitly described as a prototype rather than a production engine; created 137 days ago so it is younger than one year and lacks the long track record or stable releases required for TRL 6–7.
student_project_ideas: Build a small driving simulation level using the included VehicleSystem and Rapier to study tire-ground interaction and record performance metrics for different terrain blending strategies.

Port the chunked procedural city generator into a digital-twin style viewer: stream chunks, attach simple IoT telemetry overlays (mocked), and evaluate LOD and collision-query performance in the browser.

tools.name: wquguru/fable52-fps-repro

cls.summary: A small repository of four single-file, AI-generated browser 3D demos (including a one-prompt FPS) with the prompts, run scripts and measured API/caching cost data for reproducing them.
cls.what_it_does: This project shows how to use Anthropic's Fable 5.2 via the Claude Code CLI to iteratively generate single-file WebGL/Three.js demos (audio, materials, models, and a full FPS) from prompts, and provides the exact prompts, run scripts, automated metrics and billing/caching data used in five runs. It is notable because it packages runnable demos, per-run cost metrics and scripts that automate headless verification (agent-browser + Chrome) so others can reproduce the same multi-round LLM-driven code-generation workflow.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository contains runnable demos, run scripts and measured data showing the approach works (evidence of early use), but the project is very new (created 6 days ago) so it lacks a track record or broader adoption—limits TRL to alpha/early-use.
prerequisites: Claude Code (Anthropic CLI) with access to claude-fable-5-2
agent-browser (optional, for automated browser checks) and Chrome
Python 3 (for metrics script) and a POSIX shell to run scripts
student_project_ideas: Re-run the provided prompts replacing Fable 5.2 with an open LLM (or a different paid model) and compare artifact quality, iteration counts and reproducible cost metrics using the repository's scripts.

Modify one of the single-file demos to add a simple instrumented test (e.g. automated gameplay scenario) and extend the metrics.py script to record performance and rendering statistics for different hardware (Apple M-series vs Intel).

tools.name: leandrodaf/3d-new-era-ai
tools.desc: Open-source home design and floor plan editor in Rust (a Sweet Home 3D alternative) with a built-in MCP server: your AI agent draws walls, furnishes rooms, checks lighting and ergonomics, and renders photos — live, on your own machine.

cls.summary: An open-source Rust-based home and interior design editor that runs as a desktop app or in the browser and exposes a local Model Context Protocol (MCP) server so AI agents can draw walls, furnish rooms, check lighting/ergonomics and render photos live.

The project includes a built‑in MCP server so external LLM agents (Claude, ChatGPT, Gemini, etc.) can programmatically create and edit designs, check ergonomics and render images; notable features are a local/offline desktop mode, a browser/WebGPU build and explicit integration points for multiple AI clients.
cls.trl_rationale: The repo is young (created 65 days ago) so it cannot be rated beyond an early 'in use' alpha; however there are published binaries, installers, a browser demo and explicit client integrations which show early adopters and usable builds, supporting a TRL ~5.

Rust toolchain if building from source
WebGPU-capable browser or a modern GPU for desktop builds
student_project_ideas: Build an AI-assisted room layout tutor: connect the project's MCP server to a local LLM and implement a lesson that generates multiple layout alternatives constrained by ergonomic standards and compares them (use the app to render photos for each alternative).

Integrate a lighting study: export room geometry from the editor, run simple daylighting/illumination calculations (using an existing Python lighting library), and visualise results in the editor as overlays to evaluate lighting compliance.

tools.name: Arcadia-1/analog-agents
tools.desc: 12 agentic skills for analog IC design — architecture, sizing, verification, cross-model review, knowledge graph, and self-evolution. Works with or without EDA.

tools.name: Morrowmake/glm53-flash-cmp170hx-recipe
tools.desc: GLM-5.3-Flash on 4× NVIDIA CMP 170HX with vLLM: up to 482.6 tok/s single-user, up to 943.7 tok/s at 8 users, 262K context, TP4 or PP4, one-command container install

cls.what_it_does: This repository packages a container image, startup scripts and instructions to deploy GLM-5.3-Flash (a 320B-parameter mixture-of-experts model) on a 4× CMP 170HX GPU machine, including an Ampere-compatible vLLM fork and PCIe peer-to-peer checks. 180+ GiB disk and basic CLI tools (git, curl, jq, Python)
student_project_ideas: Benchmark and compare throughput/latency of GLM-5.3-Flash with tensor-parallel and pipeline-parallel layouts on different PCIe link widths, and report implications for on-premise LLM deployments.

Integrate the running OpenAI-compatible local server with a simple tool-chain (e.g. retrieval over a local documents index) to demonstrate end-to-end tool-calling and reasoning latency for an engineering QA workflow.

tools.name: bayshier/pixelfx-zh
tools.desc: pixelfx 中文版：244 种代码实时生成的顶级游戏像素特效（爆炸/闪电/魔法/连招），MIT 可商用，附 Claude Code 特效师 Skill，汉化自 patch-gg/pixelfx

cls.summary: A JavaScript library of 244 small, code-driven pixel-art visual effects and tools to render them as live animations or sprite sheets for games.
cls.what_it_does: Pixelfx provides a large library of pixel-art visual effects (fire, explosions, magic, UI effects, moves with acting) implemented as small JavaScript modules you can run in-browser or render to sprite sheets. It is used by importing effects into a game loop or using included Node.js tools to export PNG sprite sheets and metadata for engines like Phaser, Godot or Unity. The repo is a Chinese-localised fork with documentation, a catalogue and a Claude Code skill for procedurally drafting new effects.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository is very new (created 16 days ago) which limits demonstrated maturity; README and examples are thorough and there are many stars indicating interest, but no long track record or stable releases yet, so TRL is early-alpha.

student_project_ideas: Integrate several pixelfx effects into a simple Phaser game to implement and tune hit reactions and export sprite sheets for use in Godot.

Build a small tool that uses the repo's render scripts to generate themed sprite atlases (different palettes) and import them into Unity to compare runtime performance of CPU-drawn vs. pre-rendered animations.

tools.name: cavoiie/fluent-cfd-skill
tools.desc: A Codex skill for Ansys Fluent and PyFluent CFD workflows.

cls.summary: A Codex 'skill' that guides Ansys Fluent case setup, convergence diagnosis, and safe PyFluent MCP automation for CFD workflows.
cls.what_it_does: This repository provides an agent-facing workflow and reference guidance for preparing Fluent cases, choosing solvers and turbulence models, checking mesh and convergence, and orchestrating PyFluent MCP automation. It is used as a judgment/decision layer for Codex-style agents (not a Fluent runtime) and supplies prompt templates, checks and conservative defaults to make automated Fluent runs safer and auditable.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository is active with 90 stars, semantic versioning mentioned and recent pushes, indicating community interest and maintained docs; however it was created ~169 days ago (<1 year) and documents a skill rather than a long-established production platform, so beta-level maturity (TRL 6) is appropriate.
student_project_ideas: Implement a student project that pairs this Codex skill with a local PyFluent MCP server to automate a parameter sweep (mesh refinement or inlet velocity) and produce convergence and validation reports.

Create an agent-based case reviewer that uses the skill's convergence and boundary-condition checks to generate a short pre-simulation checklist and suggested solver settings for a small aerospace or turbomachinery case.

tools.name: GroundApprentice/CATIA-Suite
tools.desc: CATIA Suite for Windows — the complete professional build with every module enabled: modeling, drafting, and professional CAD workflows, no edition limits after install.

cls.what_it_does: According to its metadata and topics, the project purports to distribute a Windows build of CATIA with every module enabled so users can perform parametric 3D modelling, technical drawings and professional CAD workflows. There is no README or documentation in the repository, so how it is packaged, installed or licensed is unclear and not verifiable from the repository contents.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository is very recent (created ~70 days ago) and lacks a README, documentation, releases or community evidence; it appears to be a distribution of commercial CATIA rather than a maintained open-source tool, so maturity is low (proof-of-concept/distribution claim only).
prerequisites: commercial CATIA licence or acceptance of third-party distribution (licensing/legal issues may apply)

programming experience (likely Python or JavaScript) and basic WebGPU or rendering knowledge

cls.trl_rationale: The repo contains runnable scripts, install instructions and concrete workflows used by the author, indicating others can install and try it, but the project is very new (created ~23 days ago) and lacks an established user base or versioned releases, which limits maturity to early-alpha.

GPU for Cycles rendering (NVIDIA recommended), ffmpeg

tools.name: luciobaiocchi/heard
tools.desc: Offline group-safety mesh for hikers: ESP32 + GPS + LoRa, with a firmware-in-the-loop simulator and 3D replay viewer

cls.summary: HEARD is an open-source prototype for an offline LoRa/GPS mesh of ESP32 devices that tracks and warns hiking groups when members leave a planned route, with a firmware-in-the-loop simulator and 3D replay viewer.
cls.what_it_does: HEARD provides firmware and a protocol for a multi-hop LoRa mesh of ESP32 devices that share GPS positions and detect off-route hikers against a loaded GPX path; it runs fully offline and supports a Core (leader) and Node roles. The project includes a digital twin where the real firmware ConnectionManager is compiled into a Python simulation (pybind11) and a MapLibre-based 3D replay viewer that visualises runs, radio transmissions and connectivity metrics, which makes it notable for teaching and testing firmware/network behaviour without full hardware deployment.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository is a recent (created 2026-06, ~5 months old at last push) bachelor-thesis prototype that provides working firmware code, a simulator and a 3D viewer but explicitly notes unfinished Node firmware and limited field testing; this indicates early alpha/alpha-in-use maturity rather than production readiness.
prerequisites: Python (pybind11, numpy) and basic web development for the viewer
basic GPS/LoRa networking concepts and electronics assembly
student_project_ideas: Extend the Node firmware to implement full multi-hop relaying and test interoperability by running mixed hardware-simulator experiments, measuring delivery latency and packet loss across terrain scenarios.

Use the simulator and DEM-based terrain obstruction feature to compare simple propagation models (distance-only vs knife-edge diffraction) and quantify their impact on mesh connectivity and safety corridor breach alerts.

tools.name: norio/three-gtvbao
tools.desc: GT-VBAO ambient occlusion for three.js WebGPU and WebGL2 (TSL)

cls.summary: three-gtvbao is a TypeScript implementation of GT-VBAO screen-space ambient occlusion for three.js supporting WebGPU and WebGL2 backends to improve indirect lighting in real-time render pipelines.
cls.what_it_does: The library implements GT-VBAO (visibility-bitmask based voxel/band ambient occlusion) as reusable nodes for three.js's tsl render graph, providing temporal accumulation, denoising, multiple quality presets and debug views. It is used by importing the provided nodes into a three.js WebGPURenderer/RenderPipeline and wiring them into the pre-pass and lit pass to apply AO to materials that use three.js's AO lighting hooks.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository is recent (created 72 days ago) so maturity is limited; however it includes a live demo, integration examples, multiple presets and active commits which show early/adopter use rather than a mere prototype, supporting an Alpha-in-use (TRL 5) judgement.
prerequisites: familiarity with three.js (r184+), tsl render graph and WebGPURenderer
TypeScript and modern ES module usage
understanding of render passes, depth/normals pre-pass and temporal anti-aliasing concepts
student_project_ideas: Integrate three-gtvbao into a three.js WebGPU scene and measure runtime cost and visual quality trade-offs across the provided presets, producing a performance vs perceptual-quality report.

Build an interactive demo that compares temporal (TRAA) accumulation vs denoiser-only AO by switching presets at runtime and recording frame stability and artifact metrics across different camera motions.

tools.name: AgenteMaxo/backrooms-noclip

cls.what_it_does: It exposes a typed Model Context Protocol (MCP) surface of 125 tools and 481 suboperations to drive Revit tasks from natural-language objectives or structured clients, enabling creation, inspection, multi-step workflows, and post-commit verification. It is distributed as a Windows installer that includes the server runtime and Revit add-ins and is notable for its large catalog of typed operations, family authoring support and exports (IFC, FBX, schedules, etc.).
cls.trl_rationale: The project provides packaged Windows installers, multi-year Revit testing evidence (published reports and a stated v1.3.3 test suite) and active releases, indicating a beta-level, versioned product; however the repository is only ~107 days old so there is not yet a long track record to justify TRL 7+.

familiarity with BIM concepts and Revit API / MCP clients for advanced use

cls.summary: Copper is an MCP server that lets AI applications drive KiCad to produce complete, orderable PCB designs including schematic, parts selection, routing, ERC/DRC checks and fabrication files.
cls.what_it_does: Copper connects an AI app to a local KiCad installation so the AI can create real, orderable PCBs: it finds LCSC/JLCPCB parts, imports symbols/footprints/3D models, runs KiCad ERC/DRC with automatic fixes, places and routes boards (including length matching and differential pairs), renders 3D views and exports fab files for board houses. It is used as an MCP server/CLI or plugin for AI hosts (Claude, Cursor, VS Code, etc.) and notable for automating the full KiCad workflow while keeping designs local.
cls.trl_rationale: The README and releases show a feature-rich implementation, install scripts and example boards, but the repository is only a few days old so there is no long track record; under the TRL rules the newness limits it to TRL 5 despite good documentation and examples.
prerequisites: Access to LCSC/JLCPCB parts databases for part lookups
student_project_ideas: Build an AI-driven PCB design pipeline that takes a high-level spec (e.g. USB-powered sensor board) and produces a KiCad project, then validate ERC/DRC results and modify constraints to reduce routability issues.
Integrate Copper with a CI workflow to automatically run ERC/DRC and generate fabrication files for different fab profiles (JLCPCB, OSH Park) and compare BOM cost estimates across suppliers.

cls.what_it_does: This repository packages an Agent Skill that guides and automates steps for extracting protocol formats from game clients (Unity/Unreal/Cocos) and deriving a protocol.spec.yaml plus reference server code to run the original client locally. cls.summary: jev-libero is an open-source Python package that runs a fine-grained, model-based control pipeline (Jev) against LIBERO/robosuite/MuJoCo tasks with local physics previews and configurable task JSONs.
cls.what_it_does: The project provides a layered decision controller that previews candidate actions in a reversible physics branch, scores their effects against task criteria, and executes the selected atomic control. It is used via a CLI or Python API to run, inspect and record episodes for LIBERO tasks, with configurable task definitions and exported features; notable features include per-action physics previews, multi-layer decision structure, and saved inspectable runs.
cls.trl_rationale: The repository contains working demos, CLI, example recordings and configuration files and has an interactive demo site and multiple task examples, indicating use beyond a one-off prototype; however it is very new (created ~59 days ago) so it lacks long-term adoption or stable release history, limiting the TRL to ~5.
prerequisites: LIBERO / robosuite / MuJoCo knowledge and installation
LLM API keys (TypeSafe or OpenRouter) for full runs
student_project_ideas: Create a lab exercise that modifies a bundled LIBERO task JSON to change goals or features, then evaluate how Jev's layered decision choices and physics previews change success rates across seeds and present the findings.

cls.what_it_does: Mica runs a purpose-trained 4B model as an HTTP server that takes an input text, a set of questions and allowed answers, and returns calibrated probabilities for each answer rather than generating text. basic Docker knowledge for container usage

Evaluate Mica's abstention threshold and calibration on an engineering QA task (e.g., pass/fail lab reports) and compare INT8 CUDA and GGUF/llama.cpp runtimes for latency and accuracy on long documents.

cls.summary: TAKTO ONE is an open-source, tendon-driven hand exoskeleton with twelve joint magnetic encoders, Teensy firmware, KiCad PCBs, CAD and a live web 3D twin for recording and control.
cls.what_it_does: TAKTO ONE provides a complete hardware and software package to build or emulate a twelve-joint hand exoskeleton: mechanical CAD, PCB designs, Teensy firmware for sensor reading and motor control, a logging format for sensor/EMG data, and a browser-based live 3D twin and operator console. It is used to measure joint angles directly, drive finger tendons with servos, record synchronized sensor logs to SD, and run an on-device control loop; the web twin can run with simulated or live device data.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository shows a working prototype (encoders read, tendon drives tested, firmware and web twin available) and an installation-ready repo, but the project is very new (created ~79 days ago) and lacks published performance measurements or a longer track record, which limits TRL to around 5.
prerequisites: KiCad for PCB work and Node.js for building the web twin
student_project_ideas: Use the TAKTO ONE hardware or its simulated twin to collect synchronized joint-angle and IMU datasets and train a hand-tracking neural network, comparing joint-encoder ground truth to camera-based estimates.
Extend the Teensy control firmware to add closed-loop force-feedback (safety-limited) and implement experiments to evaluate assist vs transparent modes on task performance and user comfort.

tools.name: CryniflheimNebula/resp-OldenEraExplorer
tools.desc: Interactive data viewer and 3D model explorer for Heroes of Might and Magic: Olden Era - Browse units, heroes, spells, artifacts, and game data

cls.summary: A small web-based interactive viewer for browsing units, heroes, spells, artifacts and other game data from Heroes of Might and Magic: Olden Era.
cls.what_it_does: This repository provides a browser-hosted 3D and data viewer to inspect game assets (models, textures, audio and metadata) from the Olden Era mod of Heroes of Might and Magic. It appears to render assets in the browser (topics and primary language suggest a three.js/WebGL front-end) to let users explore and preview game content.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository is very new (created 17 days ago) and has no README; metadata and topics indicate a browser viewer but there is no documented releases or user-base, so it matches an experimental prototype (TRL 3).

tools.name: wuyhong715/rikkahub-agent-pure
tools.desc: RikkaHub Agent · Pure — an Android AI agent that survives long runs. Independent hardening pass on the rikkahub on-device agent: usage ledger & budgets, on-demand tools, expert sub-agents, cold memory, chained workflows. Kotlin/Compose, Shizuku/Termux/MCP. QQ group 1030362371.

cls.summary: An Android on-device AI agent app (Kotlin/Compose) hardened for long unattended runs with budgeting, on‑demand tools, sub-agents and cold memory.
cls.what_it_does: RikkaHub Agent · Pure runs LLM-driven agents on Android and adds controls to make long autonomous runs survivable: per-call metering and budgets, on‑demand tool loading, expert sub‑agents with isolated memory, disk‑backed large results and chained workflows. It is used as an Android app or built from source and is notable for on‑device operation, cost/usage accounting, and safety fixes for headless/background execution.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository is recent (created 2026-10-01, ~47 days old) but has an APK release, documented features and active development; age limits TRL to ~5 (alpha in use) despite clear functionality and some users.
prerequisites: familiarity with LLM providers and API keys
understanding of on‑device tooling (Termux/Shizuku) if using headless automation
student_project_ideas: Build a proof‑of‑concept Android automation that uses a local LLM model (via the app's Local provider) to run a multi‑step workflow (e.g. fetch data, run tests in Termux, report results) and measure the token/cost ledger for the run.

Extend the agent by creating a new sub‑agent profile that integrates with an external CI endpoint (HTTP API) and implements a capped orchestration that retries failing test steps, demonstrating budget enforcement and headless safety.

tools.name: Dicklesworthstone/frankensim
tools.desc: Plan-first Rust continuum for certified geometry, physics simulation, optimization, and rendering.

cls.summary: FrankenSim is a large Rust workspace implementing deterministic numerics, meshing, physics solvers (notably thermal/airflow FEM), optimization and an evidence/ledger system for reproducible simulation and design studies.
cls.what_it_does: FrankenSim provides a collection of Rust crates that implement certified numerical kernels, geometry representations and conversion hooks, meshing, physics solvers (including a steady P1 FEM conduction kernel and airflow/convection components), adjoint/optimization infrastructure and an evidence-backed design ledger for reproducible campaigns. It is used as a source workspace (Cargo workspaces and many fs-* crates) and notable for integrating determinism, interval/affine numerics, contract/contract-check metadata and an evidence/ledger system alongside simulation kernels.
cls.trl_rationale: The repository is an active, large Rust workspace with extensive crate counts, many integration tests and domain-specific implementations (e.g. conduction, convection, evidence ledger) which demonstrates substantial engineering work; however it is only ~134 days old, has no claimed crates.io release or wide external adoption in the README, so maturity aligns with a Beta-level TRL.
prerequisites: experience with Cargo workspaces and building native/WASM targets
student_project_ideas: Reproduce and document one of the bundled thermal validation cases: run the fs-conduction kernel, compare results to the provided Level-A/B reference, and extend the evidence ledger entries to record the experiment metadata and comparisons.

Integrate a simple geometry (from a CAD export) into FrankenSim's meshing and run a bounded thermal radius or airflow study, then build a small dashboard or report that extracts ledgered evidence and runtime diagnostics.

tools.name: ianTPE/tetra-unfold
tools.desc: Seamless tetrahedral world map with a multi-stop flight trip planner in 9 languages. Also unfolds 360° photos for AI vision and drone attitude. 四面體世界地圖與出差航線規劃。

cls.summary: A single-file web demo that projects the globe onto a tetrahedron to produce a seamless tiled world map, with a multi-stop great-circle flight planner and support for unfolding 360° images.
cls.what_it_does: The project maps the sphere onto a regular tetrahedron then flattens it into a rectangular, seamlessly tileable map useful for visualising global routes and converting equirectangular 360° images into a single flat image. It runs as a client-side HTML/JavaScript demo (no install) that draws the map with D3, shows airports, computes great-circle legs and can reorder stops to minimise total distance.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository is very new (created 16 days ago) but includes a working client-side demo hosted on GitHub Pages and complete source files; there is evidence of an executable demo but no releases or long-term track record, so maturity is limited (alpha in use).
student_project_ideas: Preprocess equirectangular 360° drone images by unfolding them with the tetrahedral projection and feed the flattened images into an object-detection pipeline (e.g. YOLO) to evaluate detection performance across projection types.

Build a student web app extension that compares the map's shortest-distance trip ordering with real flight prices by combining the tetra-unfold planner with a flight-search API and visualising trade-offs between distance and cost.

tools.name: unitedrhino/go-cad
tools.desc: 纯 Go 实现的 DWG/DXF 解析、渲染与写出库。支持 R9～R2018 读取、六代 DWG 容器写出、DXF/JSON 转换、中文 PNG/SVG 渲染、智能拆图与标题栏识别。37 张真实图纸与 LibreDWG 金标准值级对齐 100%。零 cgo，Apache-2.0。

cls.summary: go-cad is a pure-Go library for parsing, rendering (PNG/SVG), and writing Autodesk DWG/DXF files across R9–R2018 with special support for Chinese text and automated sheet-splitting.
cls.what_it_does: go-cad reads and writes DWG and DXF files, renders drawings to PNG and vector SVG (with CJK text handling), extracts text/metadata, and provides CLI tools for sheet splitting and manifest generation. It is designed to be embedded in Go services (zero cgo) and claims bit-for-bit parity with LibreDWG on a test corpus while offering DWG write capability and AI-friendly SVG metadata. Notable features include industrial-scale test validation, high performance compared to LibreDWG, and native Chinese (GBK/UTF-16) text rendering.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository is very new (created 49 days ago) so it cannot be rated above TRL 5 despite extensive README claims and test data; README documents heavy validation, CI-style testdata and examples which support an alpha/in-use judgement but lack long-term production track record.
prerequisites: familiarity with CAD file formats and drawing concepts (layers, blocks, text encodings)
student_project_ideas: Build a pipeline that ingests DWG files with go-cad, extracts text and sheet images, and indexes them into a searchable documentation system combined with a simple web viewer.
Compare automated dimension/text extraction and sheet-splitting results from go-cad against LibreDWG and a commercial CAD viewer on a small corpus to evaluate fidelity and build a converter/QA tool.

tools.desc: A QGIS plugin for searching and visualizing NASA Earthdata

tools.name: tobilg/latlng
tools.desc: Open Source geospatial object engine written in Rust

tools.name: perkel666/MegaCapybara
tools.desc: The fastest inference engine for Qwen3.8-27B on the NVIDIA RTX 5090: up to 500 tokens/s for one agent and up to 2,000 tokens/s for many, contexts up to 1M tokens, and a launcher that shows what every setting costs. Windows and Linux.

cls.summary: MegaCapybara is a high-performance local inference engine for Qwen 3.8 models optimised for NVIDIA RTX 5090 that runs many coding agents concurrently and exposes an OpenAI/Anthropic-compatible HTTP endpoint and a launcher.
cls.what_it_does: MegaCapybara runs quantised Qwen 3.8 models very fast on RTX 5090 GPUs using custom low-bit kernels, speculative decoding and a multi-agent scheduler with a shared paged context pool; it is used locally (Windows/Linux) as a drop-in LLM server that speaks OpenAI and Anthropic-compatible APIs and can download model files from Hugging Face. Notable aspects are card-tuned MXFP4/MXFP6 kernels for high throughput, batched speculative decoding and a launcher that reports the speed/accuracy/memory cost of settings before loading.
cls.trl_rationale: The README and docs show a working product with downloads, a launcher, and usage instructions, and the repo has non-trivial interest (stars). However the repository is very new (created ~45 days ago), so there is not yet a long track record or wide production adoption—this limits the TRL to an alpha/in-use level.
prerequisites: familiarity with running local LLMs and command-line setup
Windows 11 or Linux system administration (drivers, CUDA)
student_project_ideas: Compare inference throughput and token-level agreement between MegaCapybara and a gguf/ggml-based runtime (e.g. llama.cpp) for a coding task, measuring latency, throughput and memory trade-offs on different GPU settings.

Integrate MegaCapybara as a local LLM backend for a multi-agent robotics control simulation: have agents coordinate using the model over the OpenAI-compatible endpoint and evaluate latency and multi-agent scheduling behaviour under load.

tools.name: kouhxp/gutsy
tools.desc: Local decision model with calibrated probabilities: send a state and yes/no, choice or score questions, get a probability for every option. 0.8B GGUF on CPU, Jev-style API.

cls.summary: Gutsy is a small, locally runnable decision model and HTTP runtime that returns calibrated probabilities for yes/no, choice or score questions without text generation or network calls.
cls.what_it_does: Gutsy fine-tunes a 0.8B Qwen model to produce calibrated probability distributions for typed decision questions (yes/no, choice, score) given a state (text or JSON). It runs locally (CPU) via a provided inference server (gutsy-inference) that exposes a Jev-compatible API and browser demos, notable for deterministic, private, and calibrated outputs useful for automated routing, triage and decision automation.
cls.trl_rationale: The repository provides a runnable inference server, model downloads, docs and browser examples which show early real use, but the project is only 47 days old so it lacks a longer track record and broad adoption, limiting it to an alpha-in-use TRL.
prerequisites: familiarity with running local model files (GGUF) and HTTP APIs
student_project_ideas: Build a support-ticket triage prototype that runs Gutsy locally to classify and probabilistically route incoming tickets to 'refund/replace/escalate' and compare outcomes to a rule-based baseline.
Integrate Gutsy with an IoT alert pipeline to make probabilistic decisions (e.g. escalate/ignore/inspect) for sensor anomalies and log calibration and decision thresholds for operational monitoring.

tools.name: gokayfem/gaussian-splat-to-blender-nodes
tools.desc: Agent skill and toolkit for reconstructing Gaussian splats as editable Blender Geometry Nodes meshes and Shader Node materials.

cls.summary: A toolkit and agent skill that reconstructs Gaussian-splat point-rendered captures into editable Blender Geometry Nodes meshes and Shader Node materials with optional calibrated appearance projection.
cls.what_it_does: The project provides an agent-guided workflow that converts Gaussian splat observations into measured, semantic scene parts realized as Blender Geometry Nodes and Shader Nodes, plus tools for camera registration, audits, and calibrated appearance mapping. It is used from the command line or via agent skills/plugins to create editable, inspectable Blender assets and packed blends rather than a one-click mesh decoder. Notable features include a prompt pack, hybrid projection helpers, shared camera manifests, and audit/comparison tooling for strict frame-paired evaluation.
cls.trl_rationale: The README and tooling are comprehensive (install instructions, examples, video, and an included starter pipeline) showing active development and usability, but the repository is only 24 days old so it lacks a track record of stable releases or broad real‑world deployments, which limits maturity to TRL 5.
prerequisites: basic familiarity with Blender Geometry Nodes and Shader Nodes
student_project_ideas: Use the starter pipeline to convert a synthetic Gaussian-splat scene to Geometry Nodes, then extend the Geometry Nodes graph to add a parameterised deformation and evaluate how well the reconstructed parameters match ground truth.

Capture a small multi-view dataset, run the Gaussian-splat-to-Blender workflow to create editable materials, and produce a comparative study (render and metrics) between pure splat renders and the hybrid projected, packed Blender asset.

tools.name: krishkhinchi/AeroTwin-AI
tools.desc: AeroTwin AI is a Physics-Informed Digital Twin platform that uses AI and real-time sensor data to monitor turbojet engine health, predict failures, and optimize maintenance.

cls.summary: AeroTwin-AI is a web-based physics-informed digital twin for turbojet engines that combines AI and real-time sensor data to monitor health and predict failures.
cls.what_it_does: It provides a digital twin platform aimed at monitoring turbojet engine health by ingesting real-time sensor streams and applying physics-informed AI to predict faults and suggest maintenance actions. The project appears implemented as a web application (Next.js) with 3D visualization (three.js) and TypeScript, making it notable for combining real-time visualization and predictive analytics for turbomachinery.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository is 107 days old with limited README text but has public code and some community interest (83 stars). There is evidence of a working web UI stack (Next.js / three.js topics) but no detailed docs, release history or named production users, so maturity appears alpha-in-use rather than production-ready.
prerequisites: basic machine learning / predictive maintenance concepts
understanding of sensor data and time-series processing
student_project_ideas: Build a lab exercise that connects a simulated turbojet sensor stream (CSV or MQTT) to AeroTwin-AI to visualise engine health metrics in three.js and trigger simple anomaly alerts.

Extend the platform by adding a small physics-informed surrogate model (e.g. implemented in TensorFlow.js or Python microservice) and compare ML-only vs physics-informed prediction accuracy on a withheld fault dataset.

tools.name: MistblastClear/UEBulkExport-rpocket
tools.desc: Bulk export of an entire Unreal Engine container (.utoc/.ucas/.pak) into one folder: textures, meshes, animations, audio, levels and properties. A command line front end over CUE4Parse.

cls.summary: A command-line tool that bulk-exports assets (textures, meshes, animations, audio, levels and properties) from Unreal Engine container files (.utoc/.ucas/.pak) into a single folder using CUE4Parse.
cls.what_it_does: UEBulkExport provides a CLI front end to extract all asset types from Unreal Engine container files and write them into a filesystem folder for inspection or reuse. It is used to unpack .utoc/.ucas/.pak/iostore containers so textures, meshes, animations, audio and level data are available as files; it is notable for automating a bulk export over an entire container and for building on the CUE4Parse project.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository is very new (created 17 days ago) and has no README; metadata shows it wraps CUE4Parse and has community interest (stars) but lacks documentation and release history, so it appears at an early 'alpha in use' maturity.
prerequisites: understanding of Unreal asset containers (.pak/.utoc/.ucas) and basic asset formats
Python runtime and ability to install Python packages (CUE4Parse) likely required
student_project_ideas: Use UEBulkExport to extract meshes and textures from a sample Unreal container and convert them into a lightweight glTF pipeline to display in a web 3D viewer (three.js) for an asset-pipeline lab.
Batch-export animations and skeletons from a game .pak, then write a small converter to import them into an open-source engine or robotics simulator to test animation-driven actuator models.

tools.name: kekzl/imp
tools.desc: Run large AI chat models privately on your own NVIDIA RTX 50 or RTX PRO graphics card. On one RTX 5090, Qwen3.8-27B writes about 70 words per second, 1.4x faster than vLLM. Even a model almost four times larger than the card's memory runs. Works with apps made for ChatGPT or Claude. Starts with one docker command.

tools.name: pytraveler/LlamaServerLauncherAvalonia
tools.desc: Corrallama: desktop app to run and manage llama.cpp llama-server instances - launch profiles, llama.cpp build updates, Hugging Face downloads, benchmarks and automatic parameter tuning. Windows, Linux, macOS.

tools.name: MIC-DKFZ/nninteractive-agent
tools.desc: nnInteractive as a tool for AI agents: say what to segment, the agent does the rest (Claude Code, Codex, any MCP client)

cls.summary: nnInteractive Agent lets AI agents (Claude Code, Codex or other MCP clients) drive interactive 3D image segmentation by generating scribbles, checking 3D results and iteratively correcting segmentations.
cls.what_it_does: The project provides an MCP server, an agent 'skill' and an optional web demo so language-model agents can instruct and operate nnInteractive to segment CT/MRI/microscopy and other images. It automates the human-in-the-loop workflow: the agent issues prompts and scribbles, runs the nnInteractive model (locally or via a server), inspects volumetric results and requests corrections until satisfied. Notable points are multi-format image support, an MCP interface for multiple agent platforms, and an accompanying benchmark and technical report.
cls.trl_rationale: The repo is feature-rich, has a benchmark and a linked arXiv technical report, and provides installable Python packages and demos, but it is only 29 days old so (per guidance) maturity is limited to TRL 5 despite evidence of early use and evaluation.
prerequisites: PyTorch (GPU recommended) / CUDA-capable NVIDIA GPU for local inference
familiarity with CLI and basic medical image formats (NIfTI, MHA, TIFF, NRRD)
student_project_ideas: Create a pipeline that uses nnInteractive Agent + nnInteractive to segment a small public CT dataset, evaluate Dice scores and compare agent-driven prompts (Claude Code or Codex) versus human scribbles.

Integrate the MCP server with a simple web viewer to build a demonstrator where students instruct an agent to segment structures, then visualise and quantify volumes over a time series (combine with simple analysis in Python).

tools.name: dashs20/CRAP
tools.desc: CRAP: Cycloidal Reducer Algorithm & Parametrizer. Parametric cycloidal gearbox generator (build123d): give it bearings, motor, ratio and eccentricity; get collision-checked, toleranced STEP/STL parts and a live 3D web GUI.

cls.summary: CRAP is a Python-based parametric generator for cycloidal gearboxes that builds CAD parts, checks collisions through motion, animates the mechanism in a browser and exports toleranced STEP/STL for manufacture.
cls.what_it_does: Given bearings, a motor, ratio and eccentricity (or full dimensions in advanced mode) CRAP generates all solid parts of a cycloidal reducer with build123d, assembles them, performs full-turn collision checks, provides a live three.js web GUI animation and exports toleranced STEP/STL files ready for machining or 3D printing. It includes a solver (simple and advanced modes), an export-time tolerancing system and both fast envelope and exact collision checks, making it notable for producing manufacturable, checked CAD from high-level parameters.
cls.trl_rationale: The repository is a young (38 days) but functional project with a GUI, Python API, tests and export features; that indicates alpha-level use by early adopters but its recent creation prevents assigning higher TRL. The README documents examples and tests but no named production users or formal releases, and the repository has no explicit license metadata.
prerequisites: familiarity with CAD concepts and tolerancing
student_project_ideas: Create a custom cycloidal gearbox variant for a small mobile robot: modify input parameters, add a motor flange adapter, export STEP files and run a simple static strength check in an FEA package.

Integrate CRAP with an automated build pipeline to generate multiple gearboxes with different ratios and tolerances, then compare measured clearances from 3D prints to the exported tolerancing settings (requires a 3D printer and calipers).

tools.name: SahilK-027/Cyber-Ocean
tools.desc: Built with Three.js: MeshSurfaceSampler • 3D flow field particles • Custom post-processing effects, including chromatic aberration, glow, and film grain.

tools.name: remiphilippe/mcp-unreal
tools.desc: MCP server that gives AI coding agents (Claude Code, Cursor, etc.) full control over Unreal Engine 5.7 projects — headless builds & tests, Blueprint editing, actor manipulation, procedural mesh generation, and UE API documentation lookup.

tools.name: itsnik-scrpt/FigmaBridge
tools.desc: Figma-to-Engine UI Pipeline: Figma Auto-Layout → Unity UI Toolkit (UMG & Godot on roadmap) via WebSocket hot-reload and an IR layout compiler

cls.summary: FigmaBridge streams Figma auto-layout designs to game engines (Unity now, Unreal/Godot planned) converting Figma layouts into an intermediate JSON IR and hot-reloading native UI while preserving runtime state.
cls.what_it_does: FigmaBridge extracts an IR from Figma Auto-Layout, sends full-sync and JSON-Patch deltas via a local daemon over WebSocket, and converts the IR into native UI toolkit constructs in receiving engines (Unity UI Toolkit currently). It is used as a live design-to-engine pipeline enabling real-time hot-reload of UI while keeping event handlers and input state intact.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository demonstrates a multi-component implementation (Figma plugin, Node daemon, Unity package), documentation and examples, and has community interest (82 stars) but is only ~110 days old so lacks long-term production track record; this supports a Beta-level TRL.
prerequisites: Figma account and familiarity with Figma Auto-Layout
C# familiarity for Unity package integration
student_project_ideas: Build a Unity UI prototype that live-updates from a Figma page: extend the Unity receiver to add custom component mappings (e.g. sliders mapped to simulated control signals) and demonstrate hot-reload while preserving runtime state.
Add an Unreal UMG receiver plugin that consumes the FigmaBridge IR and implements state-preserving hot-reload for a HUD, comparing integration effort and runtime behaviour between Unity and Unreal.

tools.name: ptahira359-wq/resp-rust-fps-boost
tools.desc: Rust FPS boost: documented client.cfg configs for Rust (Facepunch game). Best Rust settings for 16 GPUs (GTX 1650 to RTX 5070), 4 profiles for low-end PCs, one-click installer with backup. Every setting explained and sourced, no placebo tweaks.

cls.summary: A small repository providing documented client.cfg performance configurations and a one‑click installer to boost FPS for the game Rust (Facepunch Studios).
cls.what_it_does: This project supplies tuned Rust client.cfg settings and an installer that backs up existing configs and applies presets targeted at a range of GPUs and low‑end PCs. It aims to explain each setting and provide ready profiles to improve in‑game frame rates.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository is very new (created ~11 days ago) and lacks a README; the metadata and description show a working installer and presets but there is no evidence of widespread production use or versioned releases, so early alpha (TRL 4) is appropriate.

tools.name: reallygood83/hermes-for-web
tools.desc: A personalized web workbench for Hermes Agent with setup packs, artifacts, memory-aware onboarding, and local+remote model workflows.

tools.name: sergezuber/FABULA-LLM-5
tools.desc: A local-first coding agent that doesn't take "done" on faith: the engine keeps the run going until the project's own tests pass, and every green run leaves a receipt anyone can replay. Built for one small model on one machine (LM Studio, MLX) or any OpenAI-compatible endpoint. No telemetry. macOS · Linux · Windows.

cls.summary: FABULA is a local-first coding agent that drives edits until a project's own tests pass and produces replayable 'proof-of-done' receipts for verification.
cls.what_it_does: FABULA automates code-editing tasks by running a loop that rejects premature "done" claims and forces the agent to continue until the project's tests pass or an explicit NOT DONE is emitted. It records verified runs as replayable receipts (diff, base commit, exact verify command and result, model metadata) so others can reproduce the verification on their machines. It is designed for single-machine small LLM setups (LM Studio / MLX) or any OpenAI-compatible endpoint and prioritises local execution, privacy and reproducibility.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository is active (created 136 days ago) with demos, a readable spec and example replays, and modest community interest (82 stars). It appears alpha/early-adopter quality with working features and real-run receipts but lacks a long track record or 1.0+ stable releases, so TRL ~5.
prerequisites: a local LLM served via LM Studio / MLX or an OpenAI-compatible API key
Node.js / TypeScript runtime (project is TypeScript; README mentions bun/tests)
student_project_ideas: Integrate FABULA with a class CI repo so students create tests that the agent must satisfy and evaluate how often the agent reaches VERIFIED versus NOT DONE.
Compare outcomes (time-to-verify, number of edit cycles) between a local small LLM + FABULA and a remote OpenAI endpoint on the same coding tasks and analyze reproducibility using receipts.

tools.name: Ninnix/q36
tools.desc: Qwen3.8-27B and Qwen3.6-35B-A3B local inference engine for Vulkan and Metal

cls.summary: QuarkStar (q36) is a small native local inference engine for Qwen3.6/3.8 models that runs on Vulkan (AMD BC-250) and Metal (Apple Silicon) with SSD streaming and CPU fallback.
cls.what_it_does: QuarkStar provides a narrow, model-specific runtime to run Qwen3.6-35B-A3B, Qwen3.8-27B and related quantized GGUF weights on low-cost hardware by using tuned Vulkan and Metal graph executors, SSD streaming and compressed KV caches. It includes a CLI, HTTP server, a coding-agent integration, benchmarking/evaluation harnesses and tools for GGUF and quantization, and is intended to be built from source on Linux (Vulkan) or macOS (Metal).
cls.trl_rationale: Repository is active with 82 stars, platform-specific GPU backends (Vulkan/Metal), examples, and an evaluation/benchmark harness; however it was created 119 days ago (under one year) so demonstrated track record is limited, placing it at beta-level maturity.
prerequisites: C programming and building from source (make)
Familiarity with Vulkan or Metal GPU programming/runtime concepts
Comfort working on Linux or macOS command line and managing GPU drivers
student_project_ideas: Measure and compare inference latency and memory residency for a Qwen3.6-35B-A3B GGUF model on an AMD BC-250 (Vulkan) versus Apple Silicon (Metal), reporting bottlenecks and proposing kernel-level optimizations.

Integrate QuarkStar's HTTP server and coding-agent into a small robotics software stack to prototype a local-code-assistant that generates ROS 2 node templates and evaluate reliability and performance on a constrained edge device.

tools.name: routerhubSI/kimi-uncensored
tools.desc: Every uncensored and abliterated Kimi build — Kimi K3.1 Pro Uncensored via API at 0.30/1.50 USD per million tokens, abliterated open-weight checkpoints for K3.1 Pro and K3, license notes and a red-team prompt library. Maintained by RouterHub.

cls.summary: An index and reference for uncensored and 'abliterated' builds of the Moonshot Kimi family, listing hosted API variants, open-weight checkpoints and red-team prompts.
cls.what_it_does: This repository collects and documents uncensored (reduced-refusal) variants of Moonshot's Kimi models, points to hosted API pricing and context limits, and indexes open-weight builds on Hugging Face together with a red-team prompt library and test results. It is used as a reference for researchers or operators who want to find, compare and test uncensored Kimi checkpoints and hosted endpoints.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository is five days old and serves as an index and documentation rather than a mature software product; README is detailed but there is no track record, releases or broad adoption evidence so maturity is early-alpha (TRL 4).

tools.desc: 147 AI tools for Unity game development via MCP (Model Context Protocol). Connect Claude, Cursor, and AI assistants to your Unity editor.

tools.desc: Integrating a custom robot (ANYmal C) with mjlab's velocity task

tools.desc: EMOS - The Embodied OS

tools.name: killop/puerts-unity-mcp
tools.desc: unity-mcp driven by tencent puerts , invoke js/ts  call c#  in your cell phone and unity editor

cls.summary: puerts-unity-mcp lets agents and JavaScript/TypeScript control Unity Editor and built players (phones and standalone) over a JSON‑RPC MCP interface for debugging, automation and profiling.
cls.what_it_does: The project embeds a PuerTS JavaScript VM into Unity Editor and player builds and exposes a Managed Control Protocol (MCP) HTTP/JSON‑RPC endpoint so external agents can run JS/TS that calls C# at runtime. cls.what_it_does: This repository provides a single-file C inference engine, conversion tools, benchmark harness and deployment scripts to quantize GLM‑5.2 to int4, stream inactive experts from disk and serve the model on a machine with ~16 GB RAM. It is notable for implementing expert streaming, custom int4 kernels, a tiering/prefetch system and an OpenAI‑compatible server without relying on a large framework or BLAS.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository is recent (created 125 days ago) and contains a full engine, conversion tools, deployment and benchmarks, but it lacks a long track record, widespread adoption or multiple stable releases; this supports an alpha/early‑in‑use judgement (TRL 5) and limits it to at most TRL 6 given its age.
prerequisites: familiarity with LLM concepts (Mixture of Experts, quantization)
build tools (Make) and basic Python for conversion scripts
student_project_ideas: Rebuild and run the engine on a small MoE toy model, measure memory/IO tradeoffs of streaming experts and compare generation latency against a GPU baseline (use the provided PyTorch reference for validation).
Extend the deployment scripts to add runtime telemetry and a simple scheduler for multiple concurrent requests, then evaluate throughput/latency on a midrange laptop and a small cloud instance.

tools.name: Impressivetravel/wanderer-cad

cls.summary: Wanderer CAD is a Blender add-on that provides precision CAD workflows—command line, object snaps, dimensions, layers, DXF/DWG export and modelling tools—inside Blender for producing engineering drawings and solids.
cls.what_it_does: Wanderer CAD adds CAD-style precision drawing and modelling features into Blender, including a command line, object snaps, dimensions, hatches, blocks, layers, solids/surfaces and layout/export to vector formats. It is used as a Blender add-on by running inside Blender sessions to create dimensioned 2D drawings, parametric curves, solids and sheets suitable for fabrication and documentation, with DXF/DWG export and integration with an ODA converter. The addon is notable for exposing a large set of traditional CAD commands and sheet/layout features inside Blender so artists and engineers can work with millimetre-accurate models and produce CAD outputs without leaving Blender.
cls.trl_rationale: The README documents a rich, polished feature set and a declared stable version, and the repo has attracted many stars quickly, but the repository is only 11 days old so it lacks an independent, long-term track record or evidence of production deployments; that limits the TRL to alpha-in-use.
student_project_ideas: Model and dimension a small mechanical assembly (e.g. a bracket and fasteners) entirely in Blender using Wanderer CAD, export manufacturing drawings to DXF/SVG and compare with the same model created in FreeCAD.

Create a parametrised furniture component (e.g. a table or bracket) that generates 2D layout sheets and cut lists, demonstrating Blender + Wanderer CAD as a lightweight CAD-to-fabrication workflow and exporting to DXF/DWG for CNC or laser cutting.

tools.name: Sam1983Aing/flat-to-3d
tools.desc: Seven ways to turn a flat architectural drawing into 3D as you scroll. Live demos, full code and a starter prompt for each, all in three.js.

cls.summary: A collection of seven scroll-driven three.js demos that turn common flat architectural drawings into interactive 3D walkthroughs for web browsers.
cls.what_it_does: This project demonstrates seven techniques for converting architectural drawings (plans, sections, elevations, exploded axons, schedule sequences and card models) into scroll-triggered 3D experiences using three.js. Each demo is a small, self-contained web page with full source code and a starter prompt so users can adapt the technique to their own drawings; it is notable for producing lightweight scenes entirely in code (no image or model assets) and for showing multiple distinct mapping strategies from 2D drawing to perceived 3D.
cls.trl_rationale: The repository is very new (created 20 days ago) and contains runnable web demos and good documentation, which suggests an early alpha usable by others but without a track record or stable releases. The high star count shows interest but age prevents a higher TRL.
prerequisites: familiarity with three.js concepts (cameras, materials, meshes)
ability to run a local static web server
student_project_ideas: Adapt one demo to take a student-supplied floor plan and produce a scroll-driven walkthrough that annotates structural elements and outputs simple material/area metrics.
Combine the 'Build Time-Lapse' demo with a small sensor-data time series (mocked) to visualise construction progress over time and report schedule-to-work completed comparisons.

tools.name: ederland/Agentes_IA_3D
tools.desc: Oficina 3D con agentes de IA para tu negocio. Funciona con Claude Code: clona el repo, escribe /instalar y Claude lo configura contigo.

cls.summary: A web app and local agent engine that runs AI 'agents' in a 3D office (Three.js) using Claude Code and Firebase to manage tasks and deliverables.
cls.what_it_does: Provides a 3D office UI where you create and assign roles to AI agents that execute marketing/business tasks, manage a Kanban pipeline and deliver results for approval. The system runs a local Node 'motor' that uses a user's Claude subscription to drive agents and a React/Vite web frontend (Three.js) backed by Firebase for state and chats.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository is very new (created ~33 days ago) so lacks a track record; README shows a complete prototype with integration instructions (Claude Code, Firebase, Three.js) and some examples, but there is no evidence of production deployments or long-term usage, so TRL is limited to alpha/in-use.
student_project_ideas: Extend the engine to run engineering-focused agents (requirements authoring, test-case generation) and integrate with a lightweight MBSE tool to demonstrate automated task pipelines for systems engineering.
Replace Claude Code with an open LLM runtime (where licensing permits) and measure latency/costs while adding telemetry to the Firebase backend to study agent orchestration and scaling behaviour.

tools.name: winchxyz/tidewright
tools.desc: A 3D sandcastle simulator that runs entirely on the GPU. No engine, no libraries, no asset files, no build step. Built in one prompt with Claude Code.

cls.summary: Tidewright is a browser-based 3D sandcastle simulator that runs entirely on the GPU using WebGL2 and custom GLSL, letting you build, pour and erode sand with realistic-looking granular behaviour.
cls.what_it_does: Tidewright simulates sand, water and tides on the GPU in real time inside a single WebGL2 context with no external libraries or assets; the user interacts via tools (pail, spade, moulds) and a campaign of nine timed tides. It is notable for implementing granular behaviour (angle of repose, moisture/packing mechanics) and rendering entirely with custom GLSL shaders and JavaScript, with a playable hosted demo.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository is very recent (created ~104 days ago) but includes a working browser demo and complete source; this indicates alpha-in-use maturity rather than long-term production adoption. README shows playable build and instructions but lacks evidence of wide production use or versioned releases.
student_project_ideas: Extend the GPU sand simulation to log and visualise quantitative measures (e.g. erosion rate, deposited volume above a line) and compare results under different tide schedules to explore simple coastal erosion behaviours.

Port or adapt the GPU kernels to WebGPU or integrate the sandbox with a physics engine (e.g. a soft-body solver) to study trade-offs between visual fidelity and physical accuracy in real-time granular simulations.

tools.name: kubai087/pro-threads
tools.desc: Animated WebGL wallpaper: letters woven from threads of light, inspired by the MacBook Pro PROLED XDR wallpaper. Full A–Z thread typeface, palettes, live shader. MIT.

cls.summary: A WebGL-based live wallpaper that draws letters from animated threads of light with a configurable A–Z typeface, palettes, effects and embeddable web component.
cls.what_it_does: PRO Threads renders a full A–Z typeface and hero 3D scenes as a single real-time fragment shader in the browser, producing an animated wallpaper of woven threads of light. It is used by embedding the provided web component or serving the static ES-module site, and is notable for its live shader approach, URL-encoded settings, PNG tile export and a rich settings panel for palettes and effects.
cls.trl_rationale: The README, live demo and feature list show a working project and embed workflow, but the repository is only 18 days old so it lacks a longer track record and broad adoption; this supports an alpha-in-use rating (TRL 5).
prerequisites: static web hosting or npm usage
student_project_ideas: Adapt the PRO Threads shader to visualise time-series engineering telemetry by mapping signal amplitude and frequency to thread colour and motion, and embed it on a dashboard webpage.
Create a customised hero scene for a product landing page that integrates interactive controls (via the settings panel) and records PNG exports for marketing assets.

tools.name: liyupi/binding-of-isaac-webgame
tools.desc: 《以撒的结合》风格的俯视角肉鸽地牢网页游戏：12 层地牢 / 13 个 Boss / 55 件道具，零依赖零构建，全部美术由 Canvas 2D 代码绘制

cls.summary: A zero-dependency, browser-playable top-down roguelike that recreates The Binding of Isaac gameplay with fully programmatic art drawn on Canvas 2D.
cls.what_it_does: This repository implements a 12-floor roguelike web game (55 items, 13 bosses) using vanilla JavaScript and Canvas 2D; all art and sounds are procedurally generated so there are no external assets or build steps. You play it by opening index.html or hosting the folder on a simple web server; the project also includes automated tests and a debug API used for self-play and validation.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository is recent (created ~110 days ago) and contains a complete, playable product with tests and demonstrable use (77 stars, runnable by opening index.html), but it lacks a longer track record, versioned releases, or evidence of production deployments, so assign TRL 5 (alpha in use).
prerequisites: basic familiarity with JavaScript/HTML for local modification
student_project_ideas: Extend or modify the procedural dungeon generator (js/dungeon.js) to add new room templates and balance metrics, then measure effects on player progression using the provided test harness.
Replace or augment the programmatic art in js/art.js with alternative procedural textures or a shader-based renderer and evaluate performance and memory trade-offs across desktop and mobile browsers.

tools.name: midagedev/bloomery
tools.desc: Hybrid GPU + CPU inference for mixture-of-experts models, written in Rust down to the CUDA kernels. A drop-in llama-server.

cls.summary: Bloomery is a Rust-based local LLM inference server that runs mixture-of-experts (MoE) models across GPU, host RAM and NVMe to serve models larger than a single card or host memory.
cls.what_it_does: Bloomery provides hybrid GPU+CPU inference for routed/expert LLMs, moving experts between GPU, host RAM and NVMe so very large MoE models can be served. It is used as a drop-in llama-server compatible HTTP API and is notable for Rust-written CUDA kernels, a Metal backend for Apple Silicon, prebuilt installers/Docker images and tooling to quantize and serve large GGUF and vendor formats.
cls.trl_rationale: The repository is very new (created ~59 days ago) but has functioning releases, installer scripts, Docker images and concrete examples serving large models; this indicates early alpha/alpha-in-use maturity rather than long-term production track record, so TRL 5 is appropriate.
prerequisites: NVIDIA GPU and recent driver (CUDA-capable) or Apple Silicon for Metal backend
familiarity with Linux/Docker and model formats (GGUF, vendor checkpoint folders)
Rust toolchain only needed to build from source (prebuilt releases available)
student_project_ideas: Compare throughput and latency of serving a routed MoE model with bloomery versus a single-device non-MoE model using Docker on a multi-GPU workstation, and report resource usage and scaling behaviour.
Extend bloomery's prompt caching behaviour by instrumenting and measuring cache hit rates across synthetic workloads, then propose and evaluate cache eviction policies to reduce NVMe paging.

tools.name: simd-ai/brae
tools.desc: Runs your OpenFOAM case entirely on GPUs, up to 30x faster than GPU-accelerated OpenFOAM

cls.summary: brae is an open-source CUDA re‑implementation of common OpenFOAM solvers that runs an OpenFOAM case entirely on a single NVIDIA GPU to accelerate CFD simulations.
cls.what_it_does: brae ports OpenFOAM solvers (simpleFoam, pimpleFoam, rhoSimpleFoam, interFoam and others) to run the entire solve on a single GPU, reading a standard OpenFOAM case directory and producing standard OpenFOAM output. It is used by building or installing the binary, then running 'brae' in an existing case; notable points are its high cell-iteration throughput on modern GPUs and a validation suite comparing results iteration-by-iteration with OpenFOAM.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository is 138 days old (younger than 1 year) so TRL is limited; however it has install scripts, documented solvers, benchmark results and active recent commits which indicate a beta-level, usable project rather than a fragile prototype.
prerequisites: NVIDIA GPU (Ampere or newer) and CUDA toolkit (12.4+, 13.x recommended)
Linux toolchain (cmake >= 3.24, MPI/OpenMPI), familiarity with OpenFOAM case structure
student_project_ideas: Compare performance and numerical agreement between brae and native OpenFOAM for a URANS airfoil case at increasing mesh sizes, and produce a report on scaling and error growth.
Integrate brae into a small automated workflow (using SLURM or cloud GPU instances) to run parametric design-of-experiments studies and post-process results with Python for optimisation exercises.

tools.desc: 🚀 Zero-backend, 100% client-side local AI assistant starter template. Powered by WebGPU and Google LiteRT-LM (Gemma 4). Offline-first PWA with multi-language TTS, customizable personas, and GitHub Pages deployment in 5 minutes.

cls.summary: A zero-backend, client-side progressive web app starter that runs lightweight LLMs in the browser using WebGPU and Google LiteRT-LM, with multi-language TTS and persona templates for quick deployment on GitHub Pages.
cls.what_it_does: This repository is a deployable starter template for building a browser-based AI assistant that runs models locally via WebGPU and LiteRT-LM (Gemma 4), supports offline operation as a PWA, and offers configurable personas and multilingual TTS. It is used by forking the repo, editing JSON configuration/persona files, and deploying to GitHub Pages or running locally with the included lightweight Node server. The template is notable for being zero-backend, focused on privacy/offline-first operation, and providing built-in tools for voice I/O, chat export, and quick-action prompt templates.
cls.trl_rationale: The project is functional, has a live demo, CI linting, and several dozen stars which indicate community interest; however the repo is only ~122 days old so it lacks the multi-year track record and wide adoption needed for higher TRL levels.
prerequisites: basic GitHub usage (forking, Pages) and optional Node.js for local server
student_project_ideas: Create a customised persona-based tutoring assistant for a course (e.g. an electronics tutor) that runs entirely in-browser, and extend it to save and visualise student progress using the included IndexedDB storage.

Integrate a small sensor dashboard (simulated or real via Web APIs) with the assistant so it can explain recent measurements and generate summaries, demonstrating edge/embedded-like offline interaction and PWA deployment to GitHub Pages.

tools.name: oxomkbk/Furnish
tools.desc: Web装修设计工具，集 2D 平面布置与 three.js 3D 漫游于一体，内置 12 套户型、多方案管理与自定义家具库，支持多选编辑、对齐吸附、碰撞检查及三语暗色模式。

cls.summary: Furnish is a single-file, browser-based interior floorplan and 3D walkthrough tool that combines 2D layout editing, a furniture library, budgeting and a three.js-powered 3D view without any backend.
cls.what_it_does: Furnish lets users edit floorplans in 2D, place and modify furniture, manage multiple design schemes and instantly switch to a synchronized three.js 3D view for bird's-eye or first-person walkthroughs. It's notable for being zero-dependency and offline (single index.html), with features such as snapping, collision checks, multi-select editing, export/import of designs and a simple cost estimate panel.
cls.trl_rationale: The README describes a working, self-contained application with many features and built-in example data, and the repo has attracted stars quickly; however the project is only 45 days old so it lacks a long track record and wider real-world adoption, limiting the TRL to alpha-in-use.
prerequisites: familiarity with three.js or 3D navigation aids
student_project_ideas: Build a toolchain to import simple IFC/STEP or CSV room geometry into Furnish, map real product price lists to the furniture library, and export a consolidated cost estimate CSV for a client deliverable.
Extend Furnish to log user interactions and produce simple usability analytics (time per task, most-used features) and present results in a small dashboard, comparing desktop vs mobile workflows.

cls.summary: Speedy is a measured, performance-tuned C++ inference engine (a fork of Strata) for running very large mixture-of-experts LLMs with extremely long contexts on consumer NVIDIA GPUs.
cls.what_it_does: Speedy runs Qwen3.8-Flash-Next (125B MoE) and other large models with native support for hundreds of thousands to a million token contexts, optimised for one- or two-GPU consumer RTX cards. It is used as a local inference/runtime engine built in C++/CUDA and notable for measured benchmarks, GPU-specific tuning (presets for RTX 3080 10 GB), and multi-GPU layer-splitting and quantisation presets.
cls.trl_rationale: The repository is a recent, actively developed fork (created 16 days ago) with measured benchmarks and CI, but it lacks a long track record, stable version history or evidence of production deployments; that supports an early-alpha TRL (4). Age limits a higher rating.
prerequisites: NVIDIA drivers and CUDA toolkit (compute capability 7.5+)
Large host RAM (tens of GBs) and significant disk for quantised models
Linux (primary tested OS); optional HIP for AMD builds (untested)
student_project_ideas: Benchmark and compare long-context performance and recall of Speedy versus Strata and llama.cpp on different consumer GPUs, documenting changes needed to run on a single RTX 3090 or a two‑GPU setup.
Integrate Speedy into a small local agent pipeline to test sustained long-context behaviour for a document-retrieval assistant, measuring latency and cache-hit behaviour as conversation length grows.

tools.name: florentPoux/3d-data-materials
tools.desc: Runnable Python behind my 3D data science tutorials. Point clouds, LiDAR, Gaussian splatting, meshing and spatial AI.

cls.summary: A collection of runnable Python scripts that implement 3D data‑science tutorials for point clouds, LiDAR, Gaussian splatting, meshing and spatial AI.
cls.what_it_does: The repository provides one self-contained, commented script per tutorial that demonstrates practical workflows for processing and analysing 3D scan data (point clouds, LiDAR tiles, Gaussian splats, photogrammetry outputs) and producing derived assets such as textured meshes, floorplans and IFC outputs. It is used as teaching/demo material: you run the scripts against external datasets provided on the author's site and read the code to learn concrete processing steps; notable is its emphasis on readable, runnable examples rather than packaging or abstraction layers.
cls.trl_rationale: The repo provides runnable example scripts and many tutorial kits (evidence of working examples) and has attracted community interest (stars), but it is a new repository (created ~56 days ago) so there is limited long-term production track record; that limits maturity to TRL 5.
student_project_ideas: Implement an automated pipeline that ingests a LiDAR tile, performs ground filtering and generates a DTM, comparing the repository's result with PDAL outputs and reporting differences.

Extend the Gaussian-splat-to-mesh script to produce a textured model suitable for BIM import and write a short workflow that exports wall thickness measurements into an IFC file for use in a digital heritage/reuse study.

tools.name: jgsystemsconsulting/jgs-se-knowledge-packs
tools.desc: 74 open systems-engineering knowledge packs + 8 signposts + the /se orchestrator (83 skills) for coding agents: licence-vetted NASA, DoD, UK MoD, FAA, EASA, NIST, FDA, NRC, GAO, SEBoK and more, as on-demand Agent Skills.

cls.summary: A curated, installable catalogue of open systems-engineering 'knowledge pack' skills that coding agents can load on demand to answer SE queries with cited source material.
cls.what_it_does: It converts genuinely open systems-engineering sources (SEBoK, NASA handbook, regulations, etc.) into Agent Skills (markdown 'knowledge packs') that coding agents can install and query. Users install the catalogue with a provided Python installer or a skills CLI and then invoke packs inside supported agents (Claude Code, Copilot CLI, Amp) to get chapter-cited answers. What makes it notable is the strict vetting of source licence status and a single orchestrator skill (/se) that routes queries to the right packs.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository is active with an installer, many packs and documentation, and 75 stars indicating community interest, but it is only ~151 days old (under 1 year) so a conservative TRL 6 (beta) is appropriate; there is evidence of usable tooling and examples but not long-term production track record.
prerequisites: A host/coding agent that supports Agent Skills (e.g. Claude Code, GitHub Copilot CLI, Amp)
student_project_ideas: Build a Claude Code agent that uses the jgs-se knowledge packs to answer SEBoK-based requirements-pattern queries and evaluate answer citation accuracy against the original SEBoK chapters.

Create a small MBSE workflow where student-generated SysML requirements are validated by an agent that consults the packs (e.g. NASA handbook pack) to flag missing rationale or traceability, integrating the agent with a simple modelling tool or a Git repo of requirements.

tools.name: pmndrs/klipp
tools.desc: 📹 A camera toolkit for the web, inspired by Unity Cinemachine.

cls.summary: Klipp is a web-focused camera toolkit (inspired by Unity Cinemachine) that composes virtual cameras, aims and follow behaviours and blends between them for three.js and React Three Fiber scenes.
cls.what_it_does: Klipp solves camera composition and automated shot selection for interactive 3D web scenes: you declare virtual cameras and shots, and the library chooses and blends between them at runtime. It runs core logic framework-agnostic and provides thin integrations for three.js and React Three Fiber, plus DOM input helpers and debug visualisations.
cls.trl_rationale: The repo is young (created 87 days ago) and the README explicitly calls it early-stage/experimental, but it already provides documentation, examples and multiple integrations which indicates early adopter usage consistent with TRL 5.
prerequisites: React Three Fiber to use the React integration
student_project_ideas: Create an interactive web demo that uses Klipp with three.js to visualise a robotic arm performing tasks and automatically switch camera shots to highlight key operations, comparing user-driven vs automated camera behaviours.

Build a small simulation dashboard combining Klipp (React Three Fiber) and a physics model (e.g. cannon-es or a simple kinematic simulator) to record and replay scenarios with cinematic camera sequences for presentation and validation.

cls.summary: A browser-playable, fan-made re-creation of Pokémon Red where every sprite, tile, effect and song is generated procedurally from code rather than image or audio files.
cls.what_it_does: The project reproduces the full Pokémon Red game experience in the browser by procedurally drawing all graphics (sprites, tiles, buildings, effects) and synthesising music from note data; it runs from a single index.html with a 320×180 framebuffer and supports local saves and optional cloud accounts. It is notable because the entire visual and audio content is described and rasterised by code (no image/audio files), produced originally by prompting an AI (Claude Code) and packaged as a playable fan-game.
