tools.name: senjinthedragon/Smart-Memory
tools.desc: A SillyTavern extension providing a multi-tier memory and narrative context system for AI roleplay. Tracks character facts, relationship history, per-character knowledge and secrets, entity state, scene history, story arcs, and rolling summaries - extracted automatically so your AI stays coherent no matter how long the story runs.

tools.name: DaoyuanLi2816/RepoGuardBench
tools.desc: Benchmarking repository-borne prompt injection attacks and lightweight defenses for local coding agents. DL4C @ ICML 2026.

cls.summary: RepoGuardBench is a research benchmark and reproducible pipeline that measures how repository-borne prompt-injection instructions affect local coding agents' bug-fix behaviour and evaluates lightweight defence strategies.
cls.what_it_does: It provides a curated set of controlled tasks, carrier types (README, code comments, rule files, etc.), instrumentation and scoring code to run matched clean/poisoned experiments on local coding agents and measure both utility and safety metrics. The project is designed to run reproducibly on a local machine (GPU optional) with smoke tests and scripts to reproduce paper tables and figures, and it separates local inference from optional remote references.
cls.trl_rationale: The repo is tied to an ICML 2026 workshop paper and provides reproducibility artifacts, smoke tests, and scripts, indicating a mature research prototype; however it is only 141 days old (under one year) so it lacks long-term production use and widespread adoption, limiting TRL to 6.
prerequisites: optionally an Ollama local model or other local LLM runtime for full experiments
student_project_ideas: Extend the benchmark with an additional defence (e.g. a semantic action filter) and evaluate its impact on utility/safety across a subset of the provided carriers using a local Qwen model.

Use the RepoGuardBench smoke pipeline to build a tutorial that demonstrates prompt-injection attacks and mitigations for an undergraduate software-security lab, comparing behaviour with and without sandboxing and action gates.

tools.name: tuff-app/TUFF
tools.desc: The local AI app built for the Mac. Run LLMs like Qwen, Gemma and GPT-OSS on Apple Silicon, including models far bigger than your Mac's memory, by streaming MoE experts from the SSD.

cls.summary: TUFF is an open-source macOS app and inference engine that runs large local LLMs on Apple Silicon by streaming mixture-of-experts (MoE) experts from SSD to enable models larger than system RAM.
cls.what_it_does: TUFF provides a SwiftUI desktop chat app and a local OpenAI-compatible server that runs LLM inference on Apple Silicon using a custom Swift + Metal engine. It streams MoE experts from disk so very large models can be used on machines with limited RAM and includes benchmarking, model management and optional web/file search integration.
cls.trl_rationale: The project is an active, documented open-source app with releases, benchmarks and 75 stars, and the README describes tested behaviour on real hardware; the repository is only ~3 months old so it lacks the long track record required for TRL 7+, placing it at a beta-level TRL 6.
prerequisites: familiarity with local LLM models and model files (GGUF/quantised checkpoints)
student_project_ideas: Build a local agent that uses TUFF's OpenAI-compatible background API to run task-specific pipelines (document search + LLM) and evaluate latency and cost against a cloud-hosted LLM.
Implement an experiment comparing MoE expert-streaming performance on different Apple Silicon Macs by automating TUFF benchmarks and analysing token throughput and SSD I/O characteristics.

tools.name: tinyBigGAMES/VindexLLM
tools.desc: VindexLLM is a pure Delphi, GPU-powered LLM inference engine that uses Vulkan compute shaders to run GGUF models entirely on the GPU. It performs full transformer inference without relying on Python, CUDA, or other external runtimes, requiring only vulkan-1.dll, which is typically included with modern GPU drivers.

tools.name: zju3dv/PointSplat
tools.desc: [ECCV 2026] PointSplat: Compact Gaussian Splatting via Human-Centric Prediction

cls.summary: PointSplat is a research implementation of compact Gaussian splatting for human-centric 3D reconstruction and neural rendering, with code, pretrained weights and inference/training scripts.
cls.what_it_does: PointSplat implements a compact Gaussian-splatting neural representation tailored to human-centric scenes to produce high-quality novel-view rendering and compact 3D reconstructions. It is used by running the provided inference scripts with the pretrained checkpoint or by training/fine-tuning on example datasets; notable points are the provided pretrained weights and dataset-ready example packages and explicit reproducibility instructions.
cls.trl_rationale: The repo is from an ECCV 2026 paper and provides runnable inference and training scripts plus pretrained weights, indicating a working beta implementation; however it is only 141 days old (younger than one year) so it lacks long-term adoption or multiple stable releases required for TRL 7+.
student_project_ideas: Fine-tune PointSplat on a small multi-view capture of a student-built mannequin and compare rendering quality and model size against an off-the-shelf NeRF implementation.

tools.name: composo-ai/DishwasherBench

Notable features are deterministic, replayable episodes, an official (high-accuracy) and fast wash tier and a harness for running scripted players and models to produce verified benchmark records.
cls.trl_rationale: The repository is young (created 36 days ago) which limits TRL; however the README describes working browser and CLI examples, scripted players, an MCP server and reproducible results on at least one platform, indicating alpha-level use by early adopters rather than a paper prototype.
prerequisites: macOS recommended (development and tested on macOS 27)

cls.trl_rationale: Repository is 102 days old with active pushes, packaged standalone releases for macOS and Windows, a substantial README and real-world usage notes (stars and measured examples), indicating a beta-level tool; age limits TRL and there is no evidence of large-scale enterprise deployment yet.
prerequisites: on Windows: installing Everything (es.exe) to get fast discovery
student_project_ideas: Extend the tool to add a configurable CI/CD hook that automatically reports reclaimable build caches on build agents and archives reclamation statistics for storage optimisation.
Create an integration that adapts the Custodian's heuristics to another game engine (e.g., Unity) and compare reclaimed-space strategies and safety trade-offs between engines.

cls.summary: Mnemonic Proxy is a local HTTP proxy that archives full agent conversations to disk and provides an on-demand recall tool so coding agents can continue long sessions despite small model context windows.
cls.what_it_does: Mnemonic Proxy sits between a coding agent and a model server, replacing old tool outputs in the prompt with short receipts while storing the full messages in a local SQLite archive. cls.what_it_does: Neon Zenith procedurally generates a large, deterministic vertical city (9,373 buildings) and renders it in real time in the browser using three.js's WebGPURenderer and TSL shaders. It's used as a playable demo/time-trial game and a technical demonstration of large-scale instancing, LOD, deterministic procedural layout and WebGPU/TSL workflows; notable points include Blender-baked hero districts, seeded determinism across RNG streams, and a WebGPU + WebGL2 fallback via TSL.
cls.trl_rationale: The project is a functioning, playable demo with build/run instructions and an online deployment, showing uptake and polish, but the repository is only 45 days old so it lacks the longer track record, stable releases and community history required for higher TRL.

Blender familiarity helpful for asset edits

It is used as an interactive demo (browser or Electron) for exploring high-performance, real-time fluid and surface rendering techniques and for experimentation with WebGPU/WGSL shader approaches.
cls.trl_rationale: The repository is very new (created 28 days ago) but contains runnable code, a live demo and an architecture design log; however it lacks a long track record, stable releases or evidence of production use, so it sits at early alpha maturity.

Go toolchain to build the CLI (release binaries available)

familiarity with WebRTC and three.js/VRM concepts

cls.summary: macuda is a userspace NVIDIA driver and CUDA-compatibility shim that lets Apple Silicon Macs run CUDA-based inference (e.g. llama.cpp, stable-diffusion.cpp) on an external RTX GPU over Thunderbolt.

cls.trl_rationale: The project provides releases and installers referenced in the README and already ships model download logic, indicating early adopters use; however the repository is only ~12 days old, limiting demonstrated long-term stability and wider production use, so TRL is limited to alpha-in-use.

basic understanding of local model files and GPU/driver requirements

It is used to train and evaluate reinforcement-learning policies (with large-scale parallel environments) and can run a trained policy in the browser via MuJoCo WebAssembly for demo and playback. Notable features include prepackaged tasks, example training commands, integration with W&B for checkpoints, and support for Hugging Face motion datasets.

It provides a read-only browser dashboard for viewing models, training curves and rollouts and includes CLI tools for exporting, rendering, training and evaluation.

C++ build toolchain and experience building native projects on Linux
MuJoCo and OCCT knowledge or willingness to install those dependencies
pixi (project tool) and basic web/dashboard troubleshooting
student_project_ideas: Create a small robot (e.g. a 2-DOF leg or simple gripper) by writing Cadex parametric scripts, export MJCF and evaluate control policies trained in the included training pipeline.

tools.name: sharptoolbox/WorkBuddy-AppBuilderSkill
tools.desc: Ontology-driven WorkBuddy skill for requirements discovery, domain modeling, and app generation | WorkBuddy 需求探索、本体建模与领域应用生成器

cls.summary: An ontology-driven WorkBuddy skill that interactively discovers requirements, generates eleven standard domain models, and produces a self-contained runnable domain skill with SQLite, REST API, HTML forms and a knowledge graph.
cls.what_it_does: Starting from a business idea or requirement document, the skill runs a multi-stage, interactive requirements exploration (with human confirmation), produces eleven YAML/JSON ontology models (M1..M7, ME, MU, MM, MI) and then generates a standalone WorkBuddy domain skill that includes a SQLite schema, CRUD REST API, HTML entry forms and an offline knowledge-graph viewer. It is used inside WorkBuddy as a skill: users provide requirements, confirm model decisions, and the tool outputs a ready-to-run skill directory with engine/run.py to launch the local service.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository is functional with detailed README, examples and a runnable generator, but it is very new (created 77 days ago) so there is limited evidence of wider production use or long-term stability; that supports an Alpha-in-use TRL (~5).
prerequisites: WorkBuddy installed and supporting local skills directory
student_project_ideas: Use the App Builder to model a campus equipment inspection workflow: run the interactive exploration to produce the domain skill, then extend the generated REST API to integrate with a simple React front end that students build.

Compare manual data model design vs generator output by feeding the same requirements into the skill and into a hand-crafted M1 model, then evaluate differences in generated SQLite schema, CRUD behavior and traceability documentation.

tools.name: alchaincyf/seedance-skill
tools.desc: Seedance.skill — 白模驱动的 AI 视频工作台。白模参考视频与提示词出自同一份 scene.json，渲染前做几何体检，还能从一张照片反解出白模。Control AI video with clay renders — and a prompt that can't drift from them.

cls.summary: Seedance.skill is an open-source toolkit that uses simple 'white-model' 3D renders to drive and constrain AI video generation, providing geometry checks, prompt generation and a photo-to-white-model converter.
cls.what_it_does: The project uses a scene.json white-model to specify spatial relationships, camera paths and timing, then produces lightweight renders and prompt text that align strictly with that geometry. It includes pre-render geometric sanity checks, frame-extraction self-tests, and tools to generate stable prompts and reference images so the AI video output matches the intended camera motion and composition.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository provides runnable scripts, examples, integration notes and a clear 3-minute quickstart; it has community interest (64 stars) but is only ~3 months old so lacks long-term production track record, placing it at a beta-level maturity.
student_project_ideas: Build a short pipeline that takes a scene.json, runs the probe checks and renders a white-model video, then feeds frames to a T2V service (e.g. local diffusion front-end) to compare how prompt derivation methods affect output fidelity.

Extend the photo-to-white-model flow by adding automated camera tracking from a single image and evaluate failure modes where the geometric probe flags composition problems, documenting fixes and UX improvements.

tools.name: majidmanzarpour/threejs-procedural-animals
tools.desc: Fully procedural animals for three.js: sculpted from SDFs, auto-rigged and skinned, with fur, feathers and scales, and IK gaits and actions. No models, no textures, no animation clips.

cls.summary: A JavaScript library that generates fully procedural, rigged and animated animals at runtime for three.js scenes, with levels of detail and optional baking for fast loading.
cls.what_it_does: This library sculpts animals from signed distance fields, creates meshes, auto-rigs and skins them (dual-quaternion), adds fur/feathers/scales, and provides IK gaits and action APIs that drive motion. It's used by calling createAnimal(...) in a three.js app (builds run in Web Workers by default) and can bake individuals to binary files for instant load; notable for producing complete animated creatures entirely in code with multiple quality tiers.
cls.trl_rationale: The project is well documented, has a live demo, npm install instructions and examples, and moderate community interest (64 stars), but the repository is very new (created 47 days ago) so it lacks a longer track record or stable releases required for higher TRL.
prerequisites: familiarity with web bundlers (Vite/webpack) and Web Workers
student_project_ideas: Integrate procedural animals into a three.js scene that visualises robot-environment interactions and use the library to produce crowd scenarios for performance testing of a perception pipeline.
Bake several animal variants and build a web demo comparing GPU/CPU performance and LOD strategies in Web Workers, measuring build times and frame rates across quality tiers.

tools.name: Rod292/3d-home-tv-os
tools.desc: Scan your home, turn it into a live 3D model, and make it your TV's home screen — lights wired in. An AI-agent playbook + reference implementation (Google TV, Hue, Home Assistant, iPhone, macOS).

cls.summary: A reference implementation and AI-agent playbook that scans a home into a live low‑poly 3D model and links it to smart‑home devices so the model and real devices stay in sync (used as a Google TV home screen, phone and macOS widgets).
cls.what_it_does: It converts room scans (iPhone LiDAR or drawn plans) into an editable low‑poly 3D 'dollhouse' and exposes a live API that bridges smart‑home devices (Philips Hue, Home Assistant, TVs) so actions in the 3D view affect real devices and vice versa. The repo provides a playbook for AI coding agents, demo apps (TV launcher, web editor, iOS/macOS clients) and a Home Bridge to unify device APIs; notable for combining a live digital twin of a home with a TV launcher UX.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository is very young (created 29 days ago) which limits demonstrated maturity, but the README documents a working reference implementation running daily on a single real setup and contains runnable demo instructions, so it matches an alpha 'in use' level rather than just a paper prototype.
prerequisites: familiarity with smart‑home platforms (Home Assistant / Hue)
(optional) iPhone/iPad Pro with LiDAR for scanning
student_project_ideas: Build a classroom demo that scans a small room with an iPhone LiDAR, imports it into the repo's web editor and maps a set of simulated lights to teach digital twin concepts and device mapping.
Extend the Home Bridge in the repo to add a new device type (e.g. a Zigbee sensor) and evaluate latency and consistency between the physical device, Home Assistant, and the 3D TV view.

tools.name: Squalive/banana-shooter
tools.desc: Official repo of Banana Shooter, a free-to-play FPS game available on Steam

cls.summary: A Unity-based first-person shooter game repository that exposes the project's source for people curious about how the game was made or who want to make derivative works.
cls.what_it_does: Banana Shooter is the source repository for a free-to-play first-person shooter built with Unity; it contains the project's Unity C# code and Editor project structure so others can open it in the Unity Editor and inspect or modify the game. The repo is notable because the game is distributed on Steam, but the README explicitly warns that the code does not follow good Unity best-practices.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository is 55 days old (younger than 90 days) so TRL is capped at 5; however the game is distributed on Steam indicating a production build exists, but the repo appears to be an author release for inspection rather than a long‑running, widely used codebase.
student_project_ideas: Refactor a small subsystem (e.g. player controller or weapon system) to apply Unity best-practices and document improvements in performance and maintainability.
Add a new weapon or enemy AI behaviour in the Unity project and measure gameplay/balance changes, integrating basic telemetry to compare variants.

tools.name: shinbunbun/llama-cpp-p100-patches
tools.desc: llama.cpp performance patches developed and measured on Tesla P100 (GP100, sm_60). Most are not Pascal-specific.

cls.summary: A collection of 43 performance patches for the llama.cpp local LLM runtime, developed and measured on NVIDIA Tesla P100 GPUs to improve inference throughput and kernel efficiency.
cls.what_it_does: This repository provides source patches that modify llama.cpp to improve GPU inference performance, especially on Tesla P100 (sm_60) hardware, by changing kernels, scheduler paths, and launch geometries and by adding optional optimisations gated behind environment variables. It is applied by building a patched fork of llama.cpp (the project supplies Nix build targets) and running existing inference tools (llama-server, llama-bench) to measure throughput improvements.
cls.trl_rationale: The repo contains many measured patches and examples and is being actively developed (pushes and measurements), but it is young (created ~106 days ago) and lacks a long track record, broad adoption or versioned releases that would support TRL 6+.
prerequisites: CUDA programming and GPU performance concepts
student_project_ideas: Benchmark a subset of the patches on multiple NVIDIA GPU architectures (P100, V100, A100) and report which patches are beneficial or neutral across hardware.
Integrate the patched llama.cpp into a small inference server (using llama-server/llama-bench) and quantify end-to-end throughput and latency changes for different model types (dense vs MoE).

tools.name: VANdexj/OmniRisk
tools.desc: OmniRisk: omnidirectional trajectory-risk learning for agile quadrotor dynamic avoidance. One forward pass scores every maneuver onboard; real-world evasion at up to 15 m/s.

cls.summary: OmniRisk is a learning-based onboard planner for quadrotors that scores omnidirectional candidate trajectories to enable fast dynamic-obstacle avoidance on platforms like NVIDIA Jetson.
cls.what_it_does: OmniRisk trains a neural network offline to evaluate risk for many candidate maneuvers and runs a single forward pass onboard to score and select safe evasive trajectories; it is packaged with a ROS planning node, simulator, dataset generator, pretrained models and deployment instructions for Jetson hardware. It is notable because the planning cost does not grow with the number of obstacles and the authors report real-world evasion trials at high speeds with TensorRT acceleration.
cls.trl_rationale: The README documents training code, a simulator, ROS planner, pretrained models and real-world deployment steps, showing the project runs end-to-end, but the repository is only ~64 days old so there is not yet a longer track record or multiple stable releases; that limits the TRL to about 5 (alpha in use).
student_project_ideas: Integrate OmniRisk into a small quadrotor lab platform (PX4 + Jetson Nano/Orin NX) and evaluate real-world avoidance success rates for different thrown objects, comparing TensorRT and CPU inference latency.
Extend the Simulator dataset generator to add new obstacle classes (e.g. irregular shapes or UAVs) and retrain the network to study generalisation and failure modes under varying LiDAR density.

tools.name: KanJieTeam/kjdraw
tools.desc: The open-source CAD engine for AI agents. One-line MCP setup for Kimi Code, TraeCode, WorkBuddy and ZCode. Stable object IDs, undoable transactions, DXF/KJD output. TypeScript + Rust/WASM.

cls.summary: KJDraw is an open-source 2D CAD engine (TypeScript + Rust/WASM) designed to let AI agents generate, propose, review and edit engineering drawings that remain editable and exportable as DXF/KJD.
cls.what_it_does: KJDraw exposes a JavaScript/TypeScript SDK, web editor components and a CLI that perform stable, undoable CAD operations and produce DXF/KJD output. It is intended to be driven by AI agents (MCP/Skill integrations) so a model proposes changes which KJDraw can preview, require human approval for, and commit as single transactions. Notable features include stable object IDs, revision-bound proposals, undoable transactions and an embedded editor for web apps.
cls.trl_rationale: The repository contains a CLI, SDK, web editor, documentation and runnable examples which show working functionality, but it is young (created 71 days ago) and lacks a long track record or stable release history; this supports an Alpha-in-use TRL rather than production maturity.
student_project_ideas: Build an agent-backed part configurator: create a web UI using the KJDraw SDK where a simple LLM proposes dimensional changes to a part and the user approves/exports validated DXF files (combine with a small Node.js/express backend).

Implement an automated review pipeline that reads DXF files with KJDraw, runs geometry checks (clearances, hole sizes) and generates revision-bound proposals for repairs or standardisation, then visualises differences in a web page.

tools.name: nandometzger/metal-gauss
tools.desc: Metal-native differentiable 3D Gaussian Splatting for Apple Silicon: fused forward+backward rasterizer on PyTorch MPS, no CUDA anywhere.

cls.summary: metal-gauss is an open-source implementation of differentiable 3D Gaussian Splatting that trains and renders radiance-field style reconstructions natively on Apple Silicon using Metal/MPS instead of CUDA.
cls.what_it_does: It trains and renders 3D Gaussian-splatting scenes (a NeRF-like radiance field representation) on macOS Apple Silicon by compiling Metal compute kernels at runtime and using PyTorch on MPS. The tool provides training, exporting to .ply, and a renderer for stills and video paths, emphasising fast convergence and practical benchmarks against other 3D-splatting implementations.
cls.trl_rationale: The repository provides an installable package, training and rendering commands, and benchmark comparisons, indicating early real use; however it is only 83 days old so by the project's age it should be rated at most TRL 5 absent a longer track record or multiple external adopters.
student_project_ideas: Reconstruct a small indoor scene from a set of photographs using metal-gauss, compare quality and runtime against msplat or Brush, and analyse PSNR/SSIM vs training time.
Integrate metal-gauss exported .ply scenes with a WebGL viewer (three.js) to build an interactive visualisation pipeline and demonstrate camera path rendering and metric-guided quality assessment.

tools.name: KalenHwei/PaperDuet
tools.desc: Mirror your translation! A lightweight AI paper translator for Mac and Windows. The original PDF and its translation sit side by side, page for page, with formulas, figures and tables in place. Translates into eight languages with a local model: no sign-in, no fees, and papers stay on your computer.

cls.summary: PaperDuet is a desktop PDF reader that runs local translation models to display an original research paper side-by-side with a translated version while preserving layout, figures and formulas.
cls.what_it_does: PaperDuet takes a PDF and produces a page-aligned translation using local or optional online LLM translation models, keeping formulas, figures and tables in place and providing a bilingual navigation, annotations and a small library/knowledge-space. It is used as a researcher-focused desktop app (macOS and Windows) that downloads open-source translation models and runs translations locally so no sign-in or cloud fees are required.
cls.trl_rationale: The repository is very new (created 25 days ago) and contains a detailed README describing features and supported models, but there is no evidence yet of wide adoption, stable releases, or named production users — appropriate for an early-alpha maturity.
prerequisites: A modern macOS or Windows machine
Download of one of the supported local GGUF/LLM model files (from Hugging Face or similar) or an API key for optional cloud translation
student_project_ideas: Create a Zotero/Reference-manager plugin that automatically opens selected PDFs in PaperDuet and synchronises highlights and annotations between the two tools.

Build a pipeline that uses PaperDuet's exported translated Markdown to extract paper summaries and populate a simple knowledge graph (e.g. Neo4j) for literature mapping in a systems-engineering literature review.

tools.name: ewhacc/tandem.cpp
tools.desc: llama.cpp patch: faster MoE offload for models that don't fit in VRAM

cls.summary: tandem.cpp is a patch set for llama.cpp that speeds up inference of Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) models by keeping the most-used experts on GPU and offloading the rest to CPU/RAM to reduce SSD reads and improve throughput on cards with limited VRAM.
cls.what_it_does: tandem.cpp modifies llama.cpp's MoE handling so that heavily-used experts stay resident on the GPU while less-used experts are served from host RAM (or SSD when needed), improving token/sec for single-user decoding of large MoE models that don't fit entirely in VRAM. It is applied as a patch set and includes runtime heuristics, CUDA/HIP kernel changes, and a Python launcher to select flags for a given machine; the README contains benchmark tables comparing it to llama.cpp and Strata.
cls.trl_rationale: The repository is only 16 days old (created 2026-11-01) so it cannot be rated above early alpha; the README shows functioning benchmarks, a launcher and multiple fixes which indicate a working prototype but no long track record or stable releases yet.
prerequisites: familiarity with building native C/C++ projects
CUDA (NVIDIA) or HIP (AMD) toolchains and GPU driver setup
Python for the provided launcher scripts
student_project_ideas: Benchmark tandem.cpp vs stock llama.cpp and Strata on a university GPU workstation using a chosen MoE model (e.g. Qwen3.8) and produce a report analysing throughput, memory usage and SSD activity.

Extend the tandem.cpp launcher to automatically profile a machine (VRAM, RAM, SSD bandwidth) and produce recommended runtime flags, then evaluate how adaptive flag selection impacts first-token latency and steady-state throughput.

tools.name: tonychuhai/Cove
tools.desc: Mac 桌面上的活场景：一个能钓鱼的水族箱，一只追着鼠标扫帚咬的垂耳兔。开源，macOS，Three.js。

cls.summary: Cove is an open-source desktop live-scene application that renders interactive scenes (an aquarium, a rabbit, an interactive dress-up, and hand-drawn critters) locally using Three.js/WebGL and bundled native wrappers for macOS and Windows.
cls.what_it_does: Cove provides several locally rendered interactive desktop scenes (fish that can be 'caught', a mouse‑responsive rabbit, an interactive outfit scene, and procedural line-drawn critters) and installs as a desktop wallpaper app for macOS and Windows or runs in a browser. It is used either by running the bundled native installers (macOS Swift app, Windows WebView2/.NET wrapper) or by launching the browser demo; notable points are fully local rendering (Three.js / WebGL2 + Canvas 2D), no network or special permissions, and scripts to build/install on each platform.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository is a working, installable project with install scripts, tests and vendor Three.js, showing early real use (macOS and Windows installers), but it is very new (created 57 days ago) so it lacks the longer track record and stable releases required for higher TRL.
prerequisites: Xcode command line tools and Swift (for macOS build/install)
student_project_ideas: Modify the aquarium scene to visualise live IoT telemetry (e.g. temperature/humidity mapped to water colour or fish behaviour) by connecting a local MQTT feed and adapting fish parameters.

Replace the Muse character assets with a simple 3D/2D data-driven avatar that reflects system state (e.g. CPU load → character animation) and build a small native wrapper to demonstrate embedding WebGL content in a desktop wallpaper app.

tools.desc: Blender MCP addon for AI agents to model, edit meshes and UVs, rig, build materials and render scenes through typed tools in the DCC-MCP ecosystem.

tools.name: gpillon/ignis
tools.desc: An inference engine for one NVIDIA RTX card, built for a coding agent and its subagents, and a companion that listens, reads and draws: Qwen3.8 27B and 125B Flash-Next MoE, Qwen-Image-2.1, Qwen3-ASR on the CPU. OpenAI-compatible API and Playground in one binary.

cls.summary: Ignis is a single‑GPU inference engine (Rust core with C++/CUDA kernels) that serves Qwen3.8 family and Qwen‑Image models over an OpenAI‑compatible HTTP API, optimised for one NVIDIA RTX card and agent workloads.
cls.what_it_does: Ignis runs large Qwen models (27B, 125B Flash‑Next MoE and Qwen‑Image‑2.1) on a single NVIDIA RTX GPU, providing an OpenAI‑compatible HTTP API, a playground and monitoring in one binary. It is designed for multi‑lane agent workloads (one main agent plus subagents), uses device‑resident CUDA kernels and a paged KV cache to maximise throughput on supported RTX cards, and includes image generation and ASR on CPU.
cls.trl_rationale: The project is feature‑rich with documentation, benchmarks and a hosted docs site and appears to run real models and a single binary (evidence in the README), but the repository is only 77 days old and has many open issues, so it fits an alpha used by early adopters rather than a production‑proven runtime.
prerequisites: NVIDIA RTX GPU with sufficient VRAM (Blackwell/RTX 5090 or RTX PRO 6000 recommended)
Linux build environment (Rust toolchain, C++ compiler, CUDA SDK)
Familiarity with LLM inference, CUDA concepts and model weights (Qwen family)
student_project_ideas: Deploy a small coding agent that uses Ignis on an RTX card to measure latency and throughput for single‑lane vs multi‑lane decoding and compare to another local runtime (e.g. vLLM or ggml).
Integrate Ignis with a simple CI test harness to run automated verification of model responses for a controlled set of prompts (V&V style) and produce Prometheus metrics and dashboards.

tools.name: samuelcardillo/glm-5.3-flash-2x-rtx-pro-6000-blackwell
tools.desc: Validated GLM-5.3 Flash recipe for 2x NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell 96GB: 262K context, EXL3/TR3, adaptive MTP, tools, and vision.

cls.summary: A pinned, validated deployment recipe for running GLM-5.3 Flash with DFlash2 speculative decoding on two RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell 96GB GPUs to achieve million-token context and high-throughput local inference.
cls.what_it_does: This repository provides configuration, build scripts and operational guidance to run a long-context GLM-5.3 Flash model (including a DFlash2 draft) using a pinned runtime on two PCIe-connected RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell 96GB GPUs. It solves the problem of reproducible, high-throughput local LLM inference with million-token contexts and multi-image prompts by providing a validated recipe, pinned runtime image handling, license checks and benchmark methodology. Notable aspects are the exact hardware/profile constraints, safety/license gating for the DFlash2 draft, and performance validation on the specified GPU pair.
cls.trl_rationale: The repo is a working, validated deployment recipe with benchmarks and install scripts and has visible community interest (63 stars), but it is only 81 days old so it lacks a long track record and broad production adoption; under the age rule this supports at most TRL 5.
prerequisites: Two 96GB RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell GPUs with PCIe P2P access
Hugging Face CLI (hf) and ability to manage large model files
student_project_ideas: Compare end-to-end throughput and token-latency of GLM-5.3 Flash with and without DFlash2 speculative decoding on a university GPU cluster and report trade-offs in energy and latency.

Integrate the recipe's runtime service with a small evaluation harness that runs automated verification suites (e.g. prompt robustness, tool-call guard tests) and visualises results in a dashboard (combine with a simple web UI).

tools.name: sygnalinc/Apple-Frameworks-for-TouchDesigner
tools.desc: Apple's on-device frameworks (Vision, Core ML, RealityKit, SpeechAnalyzer, MLX ...) as native TouchDesigner operators. macOS / Apple Silicon.

cls.summary: A collection of native TouchDesigner operators that expose Apple on‑device ML and media frameworks (Vision, Core ML, RealityKit, SpeechAnalyzer, etc.) on macOS / Apple Silicon.
cls.what_it_does: This project provides TouchDesigner plugins (.plugin) that wrap Apple's on‑device frameworks so you can run vision, audio, language and media processing directly inside TouchDesigner without external runtimes or cloud APIs. It is used by dropping the supplied operators into TouchDesigner projects to get pose/hand/face tracking, OCR, object detection, on‑device LLMs and more, with asynchronous inference that doesn't block TouchDesigner cooks. Notable points are macOS/Apple‑Silicon native execution (Neural Engine/GPU) and a demo .toe containing minimal examples for each operator.
cls.trl_rationale: The repo provides a broad, working set of plugins with demos and measurable performance notes and has active commits and stars, indicating a usable beta; however it is only ~4 months old and lacks a long public production track record, so TRL is capped at 6.
prerequisites: macOS developer tools / Xcode knowledge for building plugins
familiarity with TouchDesigner operator concepts and realtime pipelines
student_project_ideas: Use the Vision Pose plugin in TouchDesigner to capture human pose and stream it via OSC to a robotics simulator (e.g. Webots or ROS) to control a robot avatar, evaluating latency and tracking reliability on Apple Silicon.

Combine the CoreML object detection operator with a TouchDesigner scene to build a simple operational digital twin dashboard that logs detected events to a time series (CSV or InfluxDB) and visualises object counts over time.

tools.name: ronitgupta138/Bharat-Spatial-Engine
tools.desc: 🇮🇳 High-Performance Geospatial Administrative Hierarchy & Proximity Query Engine for India's 650k+ Census Settlements (Java 21 Loom, 2D KD-Tree, 38k+ QPS).

cls.summary: A Java-based in-memory spatial search engine for India that provides sub-millisecond reverse geocoding, radius and KNN proximity queries and fuzzy Indic name search over 650k+ settlements.
cls.what_it_does: Bharat Spatial Engine ingests MDDS/LGD census datasets, builds in-memory spatial indices (2D KD-tree, geohash, trigram inverted index) and exposes REST endpoints for reverse geocoding, radius searches and K-nearest neighbours. It is designed for very high concurrency using Java 21 Project Loom virtual threads and includes transliteration-tolerant fuzzy search for Indic place names, making it notable for low-latency national-scale spatial lookups.

student_project_ideas: Extend the engine to index an additional open dataset (e.g. OSM POIs) and compare reverse-geocoding accuracy and latency against Nominatim or Elasticsearch geo queries.
Build a small web map client that queries the engine's REST API to display KNN and radius search results and measure latency/throughput under simulated concurrent users using a load tester (e.g. k6).

tools.name: hongfaqiu/strata-manager
tools.desc: Strata Manager makes Niko1221/Strata, the local LLM inference engine, easier to set up and use. Manage local models and services, monitor hardware and API usage, chat and tune inference. Open-source desktop app for Windows / Linux x64.

cls.summary: Strata Manager is an open-source desktop app that helps set up, run and monitor a local Strata LLM runtime and manage model files, services and usage on a single machine.
cls.what_it_does: Strata Manager guides first-time setup of the Strata local inference engine, installs or updates engine packages, downloads and organises model weights, and provides runtime controls, chat, API verification, monitoring, tuning and benchmarking tools. It is used as a desktop workspace (Windows / Linux / macOS) to simplify installing compatible Strata engines, managing model files and observing runtime resource and API usage, with an optional public leaderboard for benchmarks.
cls.trl_rationale: The README documents many usable features (engine install/update, model management, monitoring and benchmarking) indicating an alpha in-use project, but the repository is only 38 days old so there is no long track record or broad adoption; this limits the TRL to 5.
prerequisites: familiarity with local LLM concepts (models, quantizations, GGUF)
access to a machine with supported GPU/CPU and enough disk space
basic familiarity with installing desktop apps on Windows/Linux/macOS
student_project_ideas: Build a small local web app that queries a Strata runtime managed by Strata Manager to evaluate response latency and throughput for different model quantizations and present results in a dashboard.
Extend Strata Manager with a simple plugin that logs inference metrics to a timeseries store (e.g. InfluxDB) and implements basic alerting for VRAM/CPU saturation during batch workloads.

tools.name: GeekatplayStudio/Meshwright
tools.desc: Know why your model won't print. Fix it. Prove it. — mesh analysis, repair and smart retopology for 3D printing, by Geekatplay Studio

cls.summary: Meshwright analyses, repairs and retopologises 3D meshes with measurements and provenance to make models ready for 3D printing.
cls.what_it_does: Meshwright inspects 3D models with many named checks, locates each problem on the surface, applies a measured multi-stage repair pipeline and re-analyses results so you can see what changed. It preserves UVs and PBR textures through repairs, offers smart retopology (QuadriFlow and other methods), exports multiple formats and provides an MCP server plus a Python API for automation.

cls.summary: A project‑based online book and companion code that teaches ROS 2 by building a complete autonomous mobile robot from modelling through simulation, navigation and deployment.
cls.what_it_does: This repository publishes a step‑by‑step, project-driven ROS 2 book (with a companion robot codebase) that teaches nodes, TF2, URDF/Xacro, Gazebo simulation, ros2_control, SLAM, Nav2, MoveIt2, sensor integration and deployment to Jetson/Raspberry Pi. It is used as a learning resource and worked example to assemble a complete AMR architecture (ARCHO) so readers can progress from toy examples to sim‑to‑real workflows. It is notable for following a single continuous robot project through modelling, simulation, autonomy stacks and real‑hardware integration.
cls.trl_rationale: The repository is a well‑written, substantial learning resource with companion code and examples and has attracted community attention (stars/forks), but it is under 1 year old (created ~102 days ago) and has no evidence of long term production deployments or versioned releases, so maturity is best judged as beta.
prerequisites: Familiarity with Linux and command line
ROS 2 (Jazzy or compatible distribution) and colcon build system
Gazebo / ROS simulation basics; basic Python/C++ for ROS nodes
student_project_ideas: Use the ARCHO companion repository to implement a new sensor (e.g. LiDAR or depth camera) integration, extend the URDF/xacro model, and demonstrate SLAM + Nav2 navigation in Gazebo then deploy to a Raspberry Pi robot.

Extend the book's Nav2/behavior tree chapter by implementing a custom high‑level fleet coordination task (multi‑robot goal assignment) using the provided multi‑robot architecture and test in simulation using Gazebo and Dockerized nodes.

tools.name: connorkapoor/geofield-bracket
tools.desc: One learned latent for geometry + physics + manufacturability: give it a box and a load, get a solver-certified bracket. SE(3)-equivariant field model, immersed FEA, live 3D designer.

cls.summary: GeoField is a Python research codebase that generates shelf brackets from high-level requirements, predicts stress and manufacturability with a learned SE(3)-equivariant field, and certifies designs by re-solving them with an immersed finite-element solver.
cls.what_it_does: GeoField learns a single latent representation that encodes geometry, physics and manufacturability for a family of L-brackets, lets a small design agent propose parameterised designs, predicts stress/deflection quickly via continuous fields, and then verifies chosen designs with a real immersed-FEA solver. It is used as a local demo server or research pipeline (Python, PyTorch-based) and is notable for unit-gradient signed-distance field geometry, SE(3)-equivariant field predictions, and an immersed FEA verifier that avoids meshing.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository provides a complete pipeline, runnable demo, tests and pretrained checkpoints as release assets which indicates early adoption and functionality, but the project is only ~86 days old so it lacks the multi-release, long-running track record needed for TRL 6+.
prerequisites: PyTorch and scientific Python stack (numpy, scipy)
basic FEA and solid mechanics background
student_project_ideas: Extend the GeoField dataset to a different bracket family (e.g. cantilever flange) and compare design outcomes and verification cost against classical topology optimisation using an external solver.
Integrate GeoField's signed-distance CSG geometry export with a fabrication pipeline: export STL, run a slicer or CAM tool, and measure manufacturability checks against the repo's analytic rules.

tools.name: Zane-0x5a/remotion-director
tools.desc: A Claude Code plugin that designs and builds a finished motion piece from a one-line brief — via the 甲乙环 (critic-loop) pipeline, judged on its real rendered frames.

tools.name: manifoldor/jumper-replica
tools.desc: Independent Jumper geometry recovery and assembly references: STL, faceted STEP, Blender exploded views, and pilot-fit 3MF. Physical replica not yet validated.

cls.summary: A repository of recovered geometry, faceted STEP/STL exports, Blender scenes and validation scripts for an independent digital replica of the KingKong Robotics Jumper used as a reference for fit-check slices and assembly annotation.
cls.what_it_does: The project extracts and publishes millimetre-scale geometry from an upstream Jumper source, produces faceted STEP and STL files, an editable Blender exploded scene and pilot-fit 3MF slices, and provides scripts to validate provenance and basic mesh closure. It is used as a reference dataset and reproducible workflow for reverse-engineering and first-fit 3D printing checks, notable for its provenance metadata, annotated exploded poster and included validation tools.
cls.trl_rationale: The repository is recent (created 41 days ago) but contains substantial documentation, data (faceted STEP/STL/3MF/Blender), and validation scripts; however there is no record of physical replica validation or broad external use, so maturity is early alpha.
student_project_ideas: Use the provided faceted STEP and STL files to build and run a tolerance/fit study: compare measured geometry from the repository with fitted 3D-printed prototypes and report likely interference or gap issues.
Integrate the Blender exploded scene and component manifest to create an interactive assembly animation or web-viewer (three.js/glTF) that highlights part provenance and measurement checks.

tools.name: Wilhao-CN/WilhasonOceanMaster
tools.desc: WilhasonOceanMaster V1.0 — A Physics-Based Digital Twin for Marine Surface Systems (NOF Team, SCUT)

cls.summary: WilhasonOceanMaster is a physics-based digital twin platform and ground-station bundle for marine surface systems (USVs) maintained by a university team, providing a runnable Windows simulation package and a GPL-licensed ground-station application that can drive real actuators.
cls.what_it_does: The repository provides a digital-twin environment for marine surface vehicles plus a ground-station application that can communicate with and control real USV hardware (thrusters, rudders, relays). It is delivered as a Windows x64 runnable simulation package and a source-distributed ground-station (Python/Qt) with safety documentation, making it notable for combining a physics simulation, hardware interfacing, and operational safety guidance for field use.
cls.trl_rationale: The project is a runnable package with source for a ground-station and explicit safety and build documentation, and is produced by a university team, indicating early real-world use; however the repository is only ~70 days old so by the TRL rules its demonstrated maturity is limited to an alpha/in-use level (TRL 5).
prerequisites: understanding of embedded hardware and safety before connecting to actuators
Windows experience to run the provided simulation package
student_project_ideas: Extend the ground-station to add a simulated fault-injection mode and run V&V scenarios using the provided physics-based digital-twin to evaluate safety responses (combine with a simple microcontroller firmware testbed).

Integrate the digital-twin package with a ROS 2 node that feeds localization and control commands, and build an autopilot module that is tested in simulation before deployment to a small USV hardware test rig.

tools.name: ChartGPU/chartgpu-react
tools.desc: React bindings for ChartGPU — a WebGPU-powered charting library.

tools.name: ChenKuanSun/openclaw-world
tools.desc: 3D virtual room where AI agents walk, chat, and collaborate as animated lobster avatars

tools.name: souranyp-stack/koi-pond-garden
tools.desc: Interactive Japanese koi pond garden rendered in real time with Three.js — one HTML file, no build step, no assets.

cls.summary: A single-file, browser-based real-time interactive koi pond scene built with Three.js and custom GLSL shaders that procedurally generates all geometry, textures and sounds at runtime.
cls.what_it_does: This project renders an ultra-realistic interactive Japanese koi pond in the browser using Three.js, procedural geometry and custom GLSL shaders; all meshes, textures and audio are generated in code so there are no external asset files. It is used as a creative-coding demo and learning example for real-time WebGL techniques (water simulation, instancing, procedural textures and Web Audio synthesis). Its notable aspects are the single-file distribution and emphasis on fully procedural content so the entire scene is inspectable and reproducible.
cls.trl_rationale: The repository is a polished demo with documentation and a live demo, but it is very new (created 51 days ago) and there is no evidence of production use or broad adoption; this supports an early-alpha TRL.
prerequisites: understanding of GLSL shaders helpful for deeper edits
student_project_ideas: Modify the water shader to implement a simplified Gerstner wave model and measure performance across desktop and mobile browsers, reporting FPS and visual differences.

Extend the scene to add simple telemetry (fish counts, positions) and build a small dashboard that records interactions (feeding, weather changes) to teach event handling and basic analytics in web apps.

tools.name: Leonxlnx/halo-above-the-clouds
tools.desc: A concrete ring restaurant above a sea of clouds: a real-time Three.js scene and a 45 s drone film, built with Claude Code

cls.summary: A real-time Three.js scene and a short rendered film showing a procedural alpine terrain, volumetric cloud sea and a concrete ring structure viewable in the browser and renderable offline.
cls.what_it_does: This repository provides an interactive WebGL2 Three.js scene (and an offline renderer) that assembles multi-scale terrain, volumetric raymarched clouds, sky baking and a designed architectural ring structure to produce both an interactive viewer and a 45 s filmed camera path. It is used by running the Node-based tooling to download baked scene data and then serving the viewer or driving headless Chrome to render frames; notable parts are procedural multi-resolution terrain tools, cloud volume raymarching and a film renderer using puppeteer and ffmpeg.
cls.trl_rationale: The project is runnable with clear install and render instructions and includes baked data and an example film, indicating early adopters can use it (alpha in use). However the repository is only 15 days old so there is no long track record or broad adoption to justify a higher TRL.
student_project_ideas: Adapt the volumetric cloud and sky modules into a small interactive demo that visualises different meteorological conditions over a real DEM, integrating local elevation data and wind vectors.

Use the terrain tiling and multi-resolution pipeline to import another real-world site (DEM + textures) and create an architectural concept visualisation for a proposed structure, then render a short cinematographic flythrough.

tools.name: hridaya423/silkreel
tools.desc: Your KiCad board, as a launch film. silk reel turns a .kicad_pcb into a 12-second film of its real copper and parts.

cls.summary: SilkReel converts a KiCad .kicad_pcb file into a short, stylised video of the board by parsing the PCB data and rendering frames with WebGL2/Canvas2D and ffmpeg.
cls.what_it_does: SilkReel reads KiCad PCB files, builds a board model (copper, pads, footprints and silkscreen), compiles an animated timeline and renders a 10–12 second film (trace or glyph style) of the board using WebGL2/Canvas2D and ffmpeg/Remotion. It is used as a CLI or in-browser studio to produce promotional or documentation films of hardware boards, including optional STEP part models when available.
cls.trl_rationale: The repository is very new (created 24 days ago) so it cannot be judged as mature; however the README and CLI show a runnable tool, demo studio, and documented workflow, indicating early-alpha readiness rather than mere prototype.
student_project_ideas: Use SilkReel to generate a short promotional video for a student-designed PCB, enhancing it by exporting STEP models from Fusion 360 and comparing visual results with and without real part models.
Integrate SilkReel into a CI pipeline to auto-generate a visual changelog video for each PCB revision and build a web dashboard that displays the latest film for stakeholder review.

tools.name: callmemhz/godot-map-builder
tools.desc: TrenchBroom-style brush level editor inside the Godot 4 viewport - draw convex brushes, push/pull faces, clip, texture, and bake to an optimized scene.

tools.name: nautilusbits/skynet-godot
tools.desc: A Godot 4 port of Bethesda's 1996 XnGine shooters SkyNET and Future Shock - plays your own copy of the original game data.

cls.summary: A Godot 4 source port that runs the 1996 XnGine shooters SkyNET and Future Shock using the original game data you provide.
cls.what_it_does: This project rewrites the original XnGine game engine in Godot 4 and decodes the original game's assets (BSA archives, heightmaps, textures, maps, sounds) at runtime so you can play the original campaign, vehicles and deathmatch modes. It is notable because it aims to reproduce the original rules and behaviour by reading data and scripts from the DOS executables rather than guessing, and includes modern graphical options and LAN deathmatch support.
cls.trl_rationale: The repo demonstrates a working, feature-rich port (campaign, multiplayer, asset import and releases) but is only 66 days old and the README states development is frozen in favour of a new port; that combination supports an alpha/in-use level (TRL 5) rather than a more mature rating.
prerequisites: A legally owned copy of the original SkyNET/Future Shock game data
Basic familiarity with running/exporting Godot 4 projects if building from source
student_project_ideas: Analyse and visualise differences between the original XnGine rendering and the Godot port by creating a side-by-side comparison tool that captures frames and metadata from both renderers.
Extend the port to add a small modding example (new weapon or vehicle) and document how original asset formats are decoded and mapped into Godot resources.

tools.name: wanshuiyin/ALIGN-Agentic-Loop-Image-GeneratioN
tools.desc: Agentic loop image generation without diffusion or autoregressive image models. Coding agents draw in p5.js, using iterative refinement and adversarial visual review for high-fidelity art and method figures. Skills for Claude Code and Codex.

cls.summary: ALIGN is an open-source project that uses AI agents to write and iteratively refine p5.js drawing programs through render→review→revise loops to produce high-fidelity images and method figures without diffusion models.
cls.what_it_does: ALIGN runs a coding agent to study a reference image, generate a p5.js program that draws the picture, render the result, and then uses a separate reviewer agent to critique the pixels so the executor can revise the program across iterations. It is notable for emphasising source-code-as-art (every stroke is in readable code), cross-family adversarial review between different model types, and an interactive gallery showing construction stages and replayable programs.
cls.trl_rationale: The repository is an early but functional project (interactive gallery, multiple worked examples and exported assets) showing a working agentic loop, but it is only 73 days old so it lacks a long track record, widespread adoption or stable releases required for higher TRL.
prerequisites: understanding of LLM-based agent workflows (Claude/Codex) to reproduce agent chains
student_project_ideas: Reimplement the ALIGN agentic loop with a different pair of models (open LLM + open-source code model) and compare the quality and failure modes across several reference images.

Extend a p5.js ALIGN pipeline to produce annotated method figures for an engineering report, adding automated traceability from critique comments to code changes and generating a small wiki of decisions.

tools.name: ATLURI0001/BuildSite
tools.desc: 🏡 Your GitHub Builds Your Home. Turn verified commits into a photorealistic, evolving luxury villa inside your profile README.

cls.summary: BuildSite turns your GitHub contribution history into a photorealistic, evolving villa image (SVG/PNG) using a Blender-based asset pipeline and a lightweight GitHub Action or CLI.
cls.what_it_does: BuildSite maps GitHub activity (commits, PRs, issues, reviews) to deterministic architectural changes and renders photorealistic, PBR-styled scenes exported as self-contained SVG (and optional PNG) for inclusion in profile READMEs. It runs as a zero-backend GitHub Action or a local CLI that uses Blender for asset production and a fast compositor in CI to produce the final images.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository is very new (created 11 days ago) so it lacks a track record; README and examples show a working pipeline and CLI but there are no published releases or evidence of broader production use, consistent with an early-alpha project.
prerequisites: Python and pip for the CLI
Familiarity with GitHub Actions and repository-level workflows
student_project_ideas: Modify the BuildSite Blender pipeline to produce simplified, schematic floorplans from the photorealistic assets and export them as vector diagrams for an architecture/engineering portfolio.
Create a GitHub Action that adapts BuildSite's progression rules to visualise team milestone completion for a course project, producing an SVG progress dashboard embedded in the project README.

tools.name: remete618/widemem-ai
tools.desc: Local-first memory layer for LLM apps and agents. Runs offline on Ollama, sentence-transformers and FAISS; OpenAI and Anthropic optional. Importance scoring, contradiction resolution, confidence-aware retrieval.

tools.name: AnkitNayak-dev/llmBench
tools.desc: llmBench is a high-depth benchmarking tool designed to measure the raw performance of local LLM runtimes (Ollama, llama.cpp) while providing deep hardware intelligence.

tools.name: ulyssestenn/omt
tools.desc: Ollama Model Test - Figure out the best model for the task

tools.name: alphastorm/omp-ninfer
tools.desc: Durable local inference for Oh My Pi: NInfer + Qwen3.8 27B on one RTX 3090/4090/5090, with restart-resumable OpenAI Responses state.

cls.summary: OMP NInfer provides a qualified, restart-resumable local inference stack that runs a pinned Qwen3.8 27B model with NInfer to give Oh My Pi long, private, stateful coding-agent sessions on RTX 3090/4090/5090 GPUs.
cls.what_it_does: OMP NInfer binds the Oh My Pi coding agent to NInfer and a hash-pinned Qwen3.8 27B model to keep session continuation state resident on the GPU and durable across restarts. It exposes an OpenAI-compatible Responses interface with checkpointing, rollback, and verification artifacts so long multi-turn sessions can resume privately on a single capable NVIDIA card.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository is 82 days old (younger than 90 days) so maturity is limited; the README and release notes show an end-to-end qualified v0.19.0 with acceptance tests and CI, indicating early use by adopters but not a long track record, supporting TRL 5.
prerequisites: An RTX 3090, 4090 or 5090 GPU with appropriate drivers
Python 3 and familiarity with local LLM tooling and model artifacts
student_project_ideas: Create a reproducible demo that runs Oh My Pi + OMP NInfer on a supported RTX card, measure token retention and latency as context grows, and compare behaviour with a stateless local server.

Implement an experiment to evaluate checkpoint/restore and rollback behaviour by simulating server restarts and verifying session continuity and transcript integrity against the project's verification scripts.

tools.name: ZephnymphBeast/signal-aichat-rpocket-team
tools.desc: An AI chatbot for Signal powered by Google Bard, Bing Chat, ChatGPT, HuggingChat, and llama.cpp

cls.summary: A small project that connects multiple large language model services and local llama.cpp to provide an AI chatbot accessible via Signal.
cls.what_it_does: The repository appears to wire together several LLM backends (Google Bard, Bing Chat, ChatGPT, HuggingChat and local llama.cpp) to let users interact with those models through Signal messages. It is used as a messaging bridge / chatbot frontend rather than a purpose-built engineering analysis tool, notable only for combining multiple hosted and local LLM backends into a Signal-accessible chatbot.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository is only 3 days old with a single push and no README; description indicates a prototype that integrates existing LLM services but there is no evidence of releases, users, or documentation, so this is an early proof-of-concept (TRL 2).
prerequisites: API keys or access to third-party LLM services (Google Bard, OpenAI/Bing as applicable)
Optional local llama.cpp runtime if using local models
student_project_ideas: Build a privacy-focused Signal chatbot that routes engineering-related queries to a locally hosted llama.cpp model and logs anonymised usage for analysis.
Extend the bridge to implement automatic routing: send small queries to a local model and escalate complex queries to a cloud LLM, then evaluate response latency and cost.

tools.desc: Hands-free on-device voice loop for macOS: Apple SFSpeechRecognizer + cloned-voice TTS, continuous listening, zero cloud. Originally built to drive claude-code-local.

tools.desc: On-device speech-to-text for macOS. Hold a hotkey → Whisper transcribes locally via CoreML → text auto-pastes into the focused app. 99 languages, free, open-source.

tools.desc: From-scratch voice agents in Python: end-to-end speech pipelines, runnable chapters, and a small shared library. Local models, explicit streaming behavior.

tools.desc: A LUA telemetry script and widget for Horus X10(S), X12, Taranis X9D+, X9E, QX7 and X-Lite radios using ArduPilot FrSky passthrough protocol modified

tools.name: Artis-98/inventcraft
tools.desc: InventCraft, formerly DATUM: a small parametric CAD application for Windows and Linux. Sketching with a constraint solver, history-based solid modelling on OpenCASCADE, assemblies, drawings with hidden line removal, and 2D CAM.

cls.summary: InventCraft is a small, history-based parametric CAD application (Windows/Linux) with sketch constraints, OpenCASCADE modelling, assemblies, drawings and basic 2D CAM.
cls.what_it_does: InventCraft provides sketching with a numeric constraint solver and a history/feature tree for parametric solid modelling built on the OpenCASCADE kernel; it supports assemblies, drawing generation with hidden-line removal and simple 2D CAM. It is used as a desktop application (Python/PySide6) and is notable for Inventor-style sketch and dimension behaviour, constraint visualisation, and driving dimensions that keep links to expressions.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository is very new (created ~55 days ago) but shows installers, an active README and 50 stars; these indicate early adopters and an alpha usable build rather than just a prototype, so TRL 5 (alpha in use) is appropriate — age prevents higher TRL.
prerequisites: basic CAD concepts (sketches, constraints, feature tree)
student_project_ideas: Create a parametric family of parts in InventCraft and export STEP files to run a simple FEA study in an open-source solver, demonstrating parameter-driven performance trade-offs.
Extend or prototype a CAM post-processor plugin that reads InventCraft's 2D CAM output and generates G-code for a low-cost CNC mill, integrating with a simulator or a GRBL controller.

tools.name: ByPlasmaSky/Microsoft-rpocket-PowerPoint-2026
tools.desc: Standardize your Microsoft PowerPoint 2026 setup and project workflow on Windows with these design, organization, and export best practices.

cls.summary: A very new repository aiming to document and standardise Microsoft PowerPoint 2026 setup, project workflow and export best practices on Windows.
cls.what_it_does: The project intends to collect guidance, configuration and workflow recommendations for Microsoft PowerPoint 2026 on Windows to standardise design, organisation and export steps. It is meant to be used as a how-to / guidelines repository for Windows users working with PowerPoint projects. The repository currently lacks a README or visible content, so exact scope and artifacts (templates, scripts or checklists) are not available from the metadata.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository is only 3 days old and has no README or visible documentation; evidence suggests an early proof-of-concept or placeholder rather than a mature, used project.

tools.name: mbzuai-nlp/ChemLab-Assets
tools.desc: simulation-ready chemistry lab instruments: part-level geometry, joints, executable behaviour models and machine-readable contracts

cls.summary: A collection of 203 simulation-ready chemistry laboratory instrument models that include part geometry, articulated joints, executable behaviour models and a command-line interface for robot or LLM-agent interaction.
cls.what_it_does: ChemLab-Assets provides detailed, instrument-specific 3D models (USD/URDF), joint definitions, grasp points and runtime behaviour models that reproduce documented instrument actions and readings so robots or LLM agents can operate them in simulation. It is used by downloading the assets (Hugging Face dataset), running the provided runtimes and the `chemlab` CLI, or loading the models into NVIDIA Isaac Sim for embodied robot experiments. Notable features are per-instrument machine-readable contracts, front-panel menu simulation for many instruments, and a unified agentic shell that advances lab time deterministically.
cls.trl_rationale: The project ships a large, versioned asset collection (203 instruments), a CLI, examples, and a Hugging Face dataset, showing more than a proof-of-concept, but the repository is very new (created 34 days ago) so it lacks the multi-release, long-track record or broad third-party adoption needed for TRL 6+.
prerequisites: NVIDIA Isaac Sim for embodied mode (optional but required to run full robot scenes)
student_project_ideas: Integrate a ChemLab instrument (e.g. balance + hotplate) into an Isaac Sim scene and implement a robot arm script to perform a simple pipetting and heating workflow, recording sensor readings and validating against the instrument's behaviour model.

Build an LLM agent that uses the `chemlab` CLI to plan and execute a small synthesis (e.g. simple esterification) in agentic mode, then compare textual/logged outputs with the embodied robot execution in simulation.

tools.desc: High-quality, optimized 3D Pokémon models (.glb) served via the Pokemon3D API. Organized by generation and form for seamless web integration.

tools.name: axonyxquantum/novaturbo
tools.desc: AI-Powered Micro Turbojet Engine Design System — Computational engineering for autonomous engine design

tools.name: warhammer50K/WebPointCloud
tools.desc: Web-based 3D point cloud viewer & analysis tool. No install — just open your browser. Supports LAS, LAZ, PLY, PCD, XYZ, PTS.

tools.name: bridge-mind/turbo-kart-rally
tools.desc: Arcade kart racer in the spirit of Mario Kart, built entirely with Three.js. 100% procedural assets, no build step. Built by five Claude Opus 5.5 sub-agents from one prompt.

cls.summary: Turbo Kart Rally is a browser-based, procedurally generated arcade kart racer built with Three.js that runs without a build step and synthesises all assets at load time.
cls.what_it_does: It provides a playable single-page kart-racing game where every mesh, texture, sound and music track is generated in code at runtime, using Three.js and the Web Audio API. You run it by serving the repository folder as a static site and opening the demo in a WebGL2-capable browser; notable is the complete absence of external asset files and the use of procedurally generated audio and visuals.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository is 56 days old (younger than 90 days) but includes a working, playable browser demo and complete source files; this suggests early adopters can run it (alpha in use) though it lacks a long track record or widespread adoption.
prerequisites: familiarity with static servers and WebGL-capable browser
student_project_ideas: Extend the procedural track generator to add new track features (e.g. obstacles or alternate road surfaces) and evaluate how changes affect AI lap times.
Replace or augment the procedural audio with parameterised synthesis (e.g. FM or granular) to explore procedural sound design and its impact on player experience.

tools.name: volkanakyel/vitrum-3d
tools.desc: Turn any icon or logo into a 3D object in glass, metal or colour, right in the browser.

cls.summary: Vitrum is a browser-based tool that converts flat icons, logos or images into true-size 3D objects with glass, metal or colour finishes and can export PNG, GLB or STL.
cls.what_it_does: Vitrum traces an uploaded SVG/PNG/JPG/WebP in a Web Worker, builds an extruded/stacked/inflated 3D solid, applies materials and lights it on a studio stage entirely in the browser. It is used via the web UI (or run locally for development) and exports raster and 3D file formats (PNG, GLB, STL) for downstream use. It is notable for running fully client-side with no server or external API and for being built on Three.js and Nuxt.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository is very new (created 63 days ago) with modest community interest (49 stars) and appears functional with instructions, but lacks evidence of production use or mature releases; this supports an early-alpha TRL.
prerequisites: familiarity with SVG and basic 3D concepts
student_project_ideas: Create a short workflow that takes university branding SVGs, generates STL files with Vitrum and prepares them for 3D printing using Blender or a slicer, documenting adjustments needed for physical tolerances.
Build a simple web portfolio that uses Vitrum to convert user-uploaded logos to GLB and displays them in a three.js scene with selectable materials and lighting presets.

tools.name: Jared-woodruff/OMF-2097-Remastered
tools.desc: One Must Fall 2097, remastered: the 1994 robot fighting classic rebuilt in TypeScript and WebGL2, playing the original game files. HD artwork, widescreen arenas with depth, fight effects, a one-key classic/remastered switch, a training lab, replays, mods and the OMF Studio mod tools. Free, for Windows, macOS, Linux and the browser.

cls.summary: A community remaster of the 1994 DOS fighting game One Must Fall 2097 rebuilt in TypeScript/WebGL2 that runs on desktop platforms or in the browser with HD art, mod tools and the original game data.
cls.what_it_does: This project reimplements the original game engine so it can play the original game files while offering a remastered HD presentation, widescreen arenas, modern input and networking, plus OMF Studio mod tools. It is distributed as native desktop downloads (Tauri/WebView2 wrappers and AppImages) and a browser build that runs offline; notable features include a one-key switch between original and remastered visuals and included modding/studio tooling.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository is only 51 days old but already publishes cross-platform releases and downloadable binaries; this indicates early real-world use (alpha in use) but not a long track record required for higher TRL.

tools.name: TypeDreamMoon/DreamGUI
tools.desc: A 3D UI system for Unreal Engine 5.8: world-space and screen-space widgets, widget Blueprints with a UMG-style designer, a native control library, .dui text authoring and tween animation. A fork of LGUI.

cls.summary: DreamGUI is an Unreal Engine 5.8 plugin that provides a 3D/world-space and screen-space widget system with a .dui text format, a UMG-like designer, control library and animation/tweening.
cls.what_it_does: DreamGUI replaces or complements UMG by offering a widget tree that can be authored as .dui text or with a UMG-style designer, renders widgets in screen or world space with batched draw calls and correct hit-testing, and includes a native control library, per-player input, gamepad navigation and tween animation. It is used as an Unreal plugin (C++/Blueprints) inside UE5.8 projects; notable aspects are the .dui source-as-authoring workflow, editor designer integration, diagnostics and performance benchmarks.
cls.trl_rationale: The README shows a full plugin with editor tools, docs, samples, automated tests and a declared 1.0.0 public release, indicating early adoption; however the repository is only ~89 days old so by the TRL rules it should not be rated above TRL 5.
student_project_ideas: Create an interactive world-space cockpit in UE5 using DreamGUI to display simulated vehicle telemetry and controls, integrating with a ROS/ROS2 bridge or simulated sensors.

cls.what_it_does: CakeCFD provides a graphical environment to import BREP/STEP geometry, drive automated blockMesh/snappyHexMesh meshing, configure and run a range of OpenFOAM solvers and view results with a VTK 3D viewport and live plots. It bundles custom high-order TENO convection schemes as a wmake library and connects to external datasets (JHTDB) for turbulence data, making it notable for combining a full pre-/post-processing GUI with custom numerical schemes on top of OpenFOAM.
cls.trl_rationale: The repository provides a complete application, build scripts, and documented features (solver integration, meshing, GUI), and is being actively pushed; however it is only 88 days old so lacks a longer production track record and broader external adoption needed for TRL 6+. tools.desc: Photographs to a textured mesh on one 8 GB NVIDIA card, offline. Built on TRELLIS.2, with a four view path, and the photographs' own pixels projected onto the texture so printed text stays readable.

cls.summary: LocalMesh Engine converts one to four photographs into a textured 3D glb mesh on a single 8 GB NVIDIA GPU using a TRELLIS.2-based pipeline with explicit texture projection from the source photos.
cls.what_it_does: It runs an image-to-3D pipeline (built on TRELLIS.2) to produce a textured glTF/glb mesh from one or a small set of photographs, handling multi-view fusion, camera pose measurement and per-texel projection of photographed pixels so printed text and fine patterns remain readable. It is used as a Python package / command-line tool that stages FP8 weights, runs on a single 8 GB NVIDIA card, and outputs a ready-to-view textured mesh.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository is very recent (created 68 days ago) and documents a working pipeline with weights on Hugging Face and concrete improvements, suggesting early adoption but limited track record; therefore alpha in use (TRL 5) is appropriate.
prerequisites: disk space for staged model weights
student_project_ideas: Compare textured meshes produced by LocalMesh Engine and Meshroom/Colmap for a small object photographed from 4 viewpoints; evaluate geometry accuracy and texture fidelity (focus on printed text legibility) and report filesize/processing time.

Integrate LocalMesh Engine output into a simple WebGL/three.js viewer and build a small web demo that streams the generated .glb and highlights regions where photograph-projected texels replaced model-drawn texture.

tools.name: manuelgscom/dale

cls.summary: Dale is an offline command-line tool that converts natural-language requests (English/Spanish) into proposed bash commands, explains them, rates their risk, and runs them only after user confirmation.
cls.what_it_does: Dale uses a small, purpose-trained local language model bundled in a single native C++ binary to translate plain-English or Spanish prompts into shell commands, explain the proposed command and classify its risk, and optionally execute it after explicit user approval. It runs fully offline, can use CPU or Vulkan GPU if available, and adapts proposals to installed tools (for example preferring fd over find when present).

optional: Vulkan-capable GPU and drivers for GPU models
student_project_ideas: Evaluate the tool's safety verifier by designing a test suite of ambiguous or dangerous natural-language prompts and measuring false positive/negative classifications, then propose improvements to the verifier.
Integrate dale into a local developer workflow (e.g. a git-hook or CI sandbox) to auto-suggest safe fix commands for common repository maintenance tasks and measure productivity and safety impacts.

tools.name: PRBonn/rko_slam

C++ build toolchain and familiarity with robot sensors (LiDAR, IMU)
Basic knowledge of tf frames, ROS messages (PointCloud2, Imu, Odometry)
student_project_ideas: Record a short LiDAR+IMU ROS2 bag on a small mobile robot and evaluate rko_slam's loop-closure and trajectory accuracy versus ground truth, varying splitting_distance and overlap_threshold parameters.
Integrate rko_lio + rko_slam on a wheeled robot and implement a simple map-based localisation node that replays an aligned multi-session map to perform localisation and path following.

prerequisites: familiarity with running desktop applications on Windows/macOS/Linux
basic knowledge of LLM providers / API keys if using hosted models

basic familiarity with LLM concepts (tokens, embeddings, RAG)

cls.summary: Faltwerk is an open research codec and WebGPU player for compressing and streaming time-varying (4D) Gaussian-splat reconstructions as a compact .falt bitstream.
cls.what_it_does: Faltwerk encodes dynamic multi-view Gaussian-splat reconstructions into a compact, sectioned bitstream using curve-based representations, vector-quantised colour codebooks and spatial/temporal prediction, and provides a bit-exact Python reference decoder plus a WebGPU TypeScript player for streaming playback and side-by-side comparison. It is used to compress and stream 4D scene reconstructions for browser playback and evaluation, notable for its curve-per-attribute time representation, a documented bitstream format, and a WebGPU player that matches the Python reference decoder.
cls.trl_rationale: This is research code with a working Python reference encoder/decoder, tests and a WebGPU player demonstrated in the repo, but the project is very new (created 21 days ago) and lacks a long track record or stable releases, so maturity is limited to early in-use alpha (TRL 5).

Extend the WebGPU player to add analytics (frame-wise bitrate, latency, and progressive refinement metrics) and integrate it with a simple dataset server to study streaming performance for digital-twin use cases.

cls.summary: rfauto is a Python-based automation framework that synthesises, simulates, quality-checks and optimises RF/microwave components across many EM/EDA engines while keeping deterministic physics calculations separate from LLM orchestration.

It is notable for integrating many EM engines behind one CLI/MCP-driven interface, a large registry of deterministic calculators and templates, and strict provenance rules that forbid the LLM from inventing physical numbers.
cls.trl_rationale: The README documents extensive functionality (16 solver adapters, 76 templates, 340 calculators, 28000+ unit tests) and clear engineering practices, suggesting active development and early adopters, but the repository is only 57 days old so it lacks the multi-release, production track record needed for TRL 6+.
prerequisites: working knowledge of RF/microwave engineering (S-parameters, ports, substrates)
access to commercial EM engines only if those adapters are required (not needed to try core features)
