cls.summary: fdop finds faint Doppler tones from propeller aircraft in audio/video, fits their Doppler curves and matches them to archived ADS‑B tracks to produce an estimated latitude/longitude, confidence radius and map.
cls.what_it_does: fdop analyses a media file's spectrogram to detect Doppler-shifted tones from passing propeller aircraft, fits those frequency-vs-time curves to estimate range and speed, then searches archived ADS‑B flight tracks for matching aircraft movements to geolocate the recording. It runs as a Rust CLI, downloads ADS‑B and weather/terrain data, and produces a report that includes coordinates, a confidence radius and nearby place names. The notable aspect is automating the full chain from spectrogram detection through curve-fitting to flight-track matching and geocoding.
cls.trl_rationale: The README and self-test show an end-to-end working CLI with replayed validation runs and a real-recording case, but the repository is only 14 days old so it lacks an established production track record and a wider user/maintenance history, limiting maturity to TRL 5.

tools.desc: GeoCrafter: GeoGuessr meets Minecraft. A Minecraft-style block game inside Google Street View and real 360° street photos: build, dig and blow up real streets in your browser. Formerly Street Craft.

cls.summary: GeoCrafter is a browser-based sandbox that places Minecraft-style voxel building and destruction inside real 360° street photos (Google Street View and other panoramas).
cls.what_it_does: GeoCrafter loads real street panoramas and overlays a voxel sandbox so players can place, dig and explode blocks inside the photographed environment in a web browser. It is used as a recreational/experimental web demo combining street imagery, OpenStreetMap data and three.js rendering, notable for embedding voxel gameplay directly in real-world panoramic tiles.
cls.trl_rationale: The README describes the project as "experimental" and the repository was created 42 days ago; it runs locally with npm and demo locations are provided but there is no evidence of production use or a sustained user community, so it fits early-alpha maturity.
prerequisites: (optional) Google Maps/Map Tiles API key for Street View outside bundled demo locations
student_project_ideas: Extend GeoCrafter to import map layers from OpenStreetMap and compute the volume of removed/added voxels to estimate earthworks quantities for a simple civil engineering case study.

Replace Google Street View tiles with an open imagery source (e.g. Mapillary or a municipal panorama API) and build an exporter that records voxel edits as georeferenced annotations for a geospatial data pipeline.

tools.name: Li-Evan/awesome-opus-5.5-video-prompts
tools.desc: 334 verified prompts people used to make videos with Claude Opus 5.5, copied word for word from each creator's post. Previews, EN/中文 translations, and a director's toolkit.

cls.summary: A curated, bilingual collection of 334 real prompts used with Claude Opus 5.5 to generate programmatic videos, with previews, translations and a director's toolkit.
cls.what_it_does: This repository collects verified prompts copied from creators who used Claude Opus 5.5 to produce videos (Opus outputs code that renders frames). It provides previews, original posts, English/Chinese translations and notes about tools, inputs and costs, plus guidance for directing and adapting prompts. It is notable because every prompt is sourced verbatim from its original creator and the list emphasises practical, reproducible recipes for motion-graphics and explainers.
cls.trl_rationale: The repository is a curated list (not an execution engine) created 51 days ago, with a readable site and examples but limited time and uptake; its young age constrains TRL to an early-alpha level despite useful curation.
prerequisites: access to Claude Opus 5.5 to run prompts
student_project_ideas: Compare a subset of Opus 5.5 prompts from the list by running them through the same renderer (e.g. Remotion) and report on reproducibility, rendering time and asset requirements.

Create a small 'director assistant' script that takes prompts from the list and automates parameter substitution (brand, colours, duration) and batch-renders simple explainer videos with Remotion and ffmpeg.

tools.name: 0xProbabillity/house-control-tv
tools.desc: House Control on Android TV: your home in 3D, controlled straight from the TV through Smart Life, Home Assistant and Philips Hue.

cls.summary: An Android TV app that displays a live 3D model of your home and lets you control Smart Life (Tuya), Home Assistant and Philips Hue devices from the TV.
cls.what_it_does: House Control TV renders your floor plan as an interactive 3D home on Android TV and provides large-TV-friendly controls to switch lights, operate air conditioners and run scenes. It connects directly to Smart Life (Tuya), Home Assistant and Philips Hue on the local network so the TV keeps a live copy of your home and reflects remote changes in near real-time.
cls.trl_rationale: The project is a working Android app with releases and installation instructions, but the repository is very new (created 29 days ago) so it lacks a long track record or broad adoption; that supports an 'alpha in use' TRL 5.
prerequisites: Home Assistant / Philips Hue / Smart Life familiarity
Node.js, JDK 17 and basic command-line skills
student_project_ideas: Build a student project that extends the TV app to log device state changes to a local time-series database (e.g. InfluxDB) and visualise trends on the TV, demonstrating an operational digital twin and simple analytics pipeline.

Create an experiment that integrates a small ESP32 light sensor and publishes MQTT data to Home Assistant, then modify the TV app or plan JSON to visualise sensor-driven automation and evaluate latency from sensor to TV display.

tools.name: Slymaster/masame
tools.desc: A craftsman's Go board, and a teacher that plays like a human. KataGo, macOS & Windows, French & English.

cls.summary: Masame is a desktop Go (baduk) application with a photorealistic three.js goban and an integrated KataGo-based teacher that plays at human-like ranks.
cls.what_it_does: Masame provides a richly rendered 2D/3D Go board, offline play against a KataGo engine tuned to imitate human strength, game study features (tsumego, counting, reviews), OGS online game integration, and downloadable KataGo networks. It is used as a standalone desktop app (macOS and Windows via Tauri) and notable for its visual presentation, offline engine integration and teaching-oriented features.
cls.trl_rationale: The README describes a full-featured desktop app with integration of KataGo, three.js and OGS and has community interest (41 stars), but the repository is only 37 days old so there is no long track record; under the TRL rules a young project without established production users is limited to TRL 5.
prerequisites: Node.js / npm (or pnpm/yarn) and a JavaScript toolchain
Tauri build toolchain for desktop packaging
KataGo networks (downloaded by the app or provided)

tools.name: develop212/agent-floor
tools.desc: A live 3D office for your coding agents. Every agent gets a character and a desk; every team gets an office. Works with Claude Code, Codex, Cursor and anything that speaks HTTP.

cls.summary: Agent Floor is a live 3D office that visualises coding agents as characters at desks, showing their status and tool activity in a browser or desktop window.
cls.what_it_does: Agent Floor receives simple JSON events (or integrates with Claude Code, Codex, Cursor hooks) and renders a persistent 3D office where each agent is represented by a character, desk and monitor that display current activity. It is used as a local desktop or browser app (Electron fallback) for observing multi-agent behaviour and tool calls in real time, notable for its playful, glanceable visual metaphors (paper planes, badges, monitor text) and a live demo that runs in the browser.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository is very new (created 37 days ago) with a working demo, an installable CLI and a short README; this indicates an early alpha that runs for others but lacks a long track record or stable releases, so TRL 4 is appropriate.
student_project_ideas: Extend Agent Floor to log events to a time-series database (e.g. InfluxDB) and create dashboards correlating agent tool use with build/test outcomes.
Integrate Agent Floor with a classroom CI system so student build/test agents spawn desks and visualise concurrent test activity and failures in the 3D office.

tools.name: NewbimAI/NewbimAI-CADViewer
tools.desc: 本地 DWG/DXF 看图与统计工具（AGPL-3.0-only）：WebGL 直读渲染、实体/图层/图块/文字统计、匿名块溯源聚合、PNG/JSON/DXF/PDF 导出，并附带 Agent 命令行 Skill。图纸不出本机。

cls.summary: A local, privacy-preserving DWG/DXF viewer and statistics tool that renders DXF with WebGL, provides layer/block/text/measurement tools, and can export PNG/JSON/DXF/PDF.
cls.what_it_does: It loads DWG (via a local cadcraft converter) and DXF files and renders them in-browser using three.js and a DXF viewer, offering layer/block visibility, anonymous block provenance, measurements, and entity-level drawing comparisons. It is used as a local server + web frontend (Node.js + React) and includes a command-line "Agent Skill" for automated statistics and exports; notable features are on-machine conversion/rendering (no cloud), entity-level diffing, and rich export options.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository is very new (created 28 days ago) but has a detailed README, runnable server/front-end, and multiple features; lacking long-term real-world adoption or stable releases, so it's at an alpha-in-use level (TRL 5).
prerequisites: familiarity with DWG/DXF and CAD concepts (layers, blocks, SHX fonts)
optional: download cadcraft-cli binary; optional: Rust toolchain to build udo-cli for custom objects
student_project_ideas: Build a lab exercise to compare two versions of a building floor plan by automating entity-level diffing and producing a change report (use the Skill CLI to script comparisons), then visualise and filter changes in the web UI.

Integrate the viewer with a simple digital-thread demo: parse DXF statistics to extract component counts and layers, push metadata to a small time‑series or database, and create a dashboard showing changes across revisions.

tools.name: zeikar/iki
tools.desc: The open Live2D alternative that AI can build — a free, MIT-licensed 2D puppet engine for the web, with an open .iki format, an AI auto-rigger and a bundled Claude Code / Codex plugin.

tools.name: RevStudio/Rev2D
tools.desc: Live2D/Spine-style 2D rigging & animation, built for AI agents. A rig is one JSON file; a deterministic headless renderer, a CLI and an MCP server (16 tools) let an agent author, render, measure and fix it, and a live web editor lets the AI see and drive what you are looking at.

cls.summary: Rev2D is an open-source TypeScript toolchain for Live2D/Spine-style 2D rigging and deterministic headless rendering, designed so AI agents can author, render, measure and fix rigs programmatically.
cls.what_it_does: Rev2D stores a complete 2D rig in one JSON file and provides a deterministic headless renderer, a CLI, an MCP server with tools for agents, and a React+WebGL2 live editor. It is notable for making rig authoring machine-readable and automatable (validate → render → inspect → apply atomic ops) so agents can iterate without human pixel inspection.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository is 53 days old (very new) but provides a full CLI, MCP server, deterministic renderer, live editor and a demo; these features and 41 stars show early adoption beyond a toy prototype but the project is too young for production-readiness claims, so TRL ~5 (alpha in use).
prerequisites: familiarity with 2D rigging/animation concepts (bones, IK, keyframes)
student_project_ideas: Build an agent (using the CLI or MCP) that automatically rigs a single portrait image into a Rev2D model and evaluates blink/pose coverage using rev2d inspect/analyze.
Create a reproducible test-suite that measures IK reach and physics stability across parameter sweeps and generates contact-sheet evidence (use the headless renderer and analyze outputs).

tools.name: gregorik/InstantOrganicCaves
tools.desc: An extremely lightweight, purist C++ engine for UE5 to generate procedural cave & rock structures at runtime.

tools.name: LobzyJay/motion-design-with-claude-and-codex
tools.desc: Claude Code & ChatGpt skills for motion designers in Blender and After Effects

tools.name: Ridwannurudeen/hermes-genesis
tools.desc: Autonomous fiction engine — three agents publish a fictional Wikipedia. Hermes-4-70B (canon + critics) + Kimi-K2.6 (prose) + FLUX + ElevenLabs. Constructed-language phonological drift across eras.

tools.name: siftystudio/viv
tools.desc: An engine for emergent narrative.

tools.name: plausibleventures/lattice
tools.desc: Isometric games made easy — an agentic game kit. 12 agent skills over 9 zero-dependency TypeScript packages. Type one sentence, get a playable game.

tools.name: takeshy/obsidian-llm-hub
tools.desc: Obsidian plugin for AI chat, workflow automation, and semantic search — supports Gemini, OpenAI, OpenRouter, Grok, Ollama, and CLI   backends

tools.name: mistval/yozakura
tools.desc: An LLM-powered social simulation and roleplaying engine where NPCs have their own lives too.

tools.name: baker27727/ds4-8gb-cpu
tools.desc: DeepSeek V4 Flash CPU/NVMe research fork: 78.62 GiB GGUF validated on 7.7 GiB RAM, CPU-only, using demand paging.

tools.name: sauravsingla/MemVanta
tools.desc: Low-memory C++20 LLM inference runtime for quantized GGUF models on CPU — mmap-backed weights, paged KV cache, Q4/Q8 kernels, and reproducible llama.cpp benchmarks.

tools.name: jhmeel/bigfoot
tools.desc: An assistant that lives next to your cursor on Windows. It sees your screen, talks with you, draws on things, solves the math you write, and operates your computer. Its AI runs on your PC, so it's private and works offline.

cls.summary: Bigfoot is a Windows desktop assistant that runs a local AI next to your cursor to read the screen, speak, draw annotations, operate the computer and solve handwritten math offline.
cls.what_it_does: Bigfoot runs as an Electron app on Windows and uses local LLMs and on-device speech/vision stacks to let you talk to an assistant, annotate and edit the screen, control apps and terminals, and solve handwritten math with symbolic engines. It is notable for running models and speech entirely on the PC for privacy, integrating whisper.cpp for STT, kokoro/ONNX TTS, and llama.cpp-served local models so it can work offline without sending screenshots or audio to cloud services.
cls.trl_rationale: The README describes a complete, runnable Electron app with local model support and many technical details, but the repository is very new (created 48 days ago) and has limited community traction, so it fits an alpha/in-use TRL rather than production-proven maturity.
prerequisites: Familiarity with installing Electron apps / NSIS installers
Local model hardware (enough RAM and optional GPU) and basic knowledge of model sizes
student_project_ideas: Build a small extension that records Bigfoot actions and produces a reproducible test script to demonstrate automated GUI testing workflows.

Integrate Bigfoot with a local domain-specific model or toolchain (for example add a CAD-aware plugin) to evaluate how a local desktop assistant can aid engineering workflows while preserving privacy.

tools.name: Scottcjn/open-xdna
tools.desc: Open-source bring-up + verified matmul on the first-gen AMD XDNA1 (Phoenix/Hawk Point) NPU on Linux — the gen FastFlowLM/Lemonade skip. RyzenAI-npu1, mlir-aie/IRON, XRT.

tools.name: manjunathshiva/opendecider
tools.desc: Open, calibrated System 1 decision models: typed choice / score / yes-no answers with a probability for every option. 400M to 80B; CPU, NVIDIA, Apple Silicon, LM Studio, Ollama and vLLM.

cls.summary: Opendecider provides lightweight, calibrated LLM decision models that return typed answers (choice, score, yes/no) with calibrated probabilities for each option and can run on CPU, NVIDIA GPUs and Apple Silicon or be served via common model servers.
cls.what_it_does: Opendecider turns a textual or JSON 'state' and typed questions into probabilistic decisions (choice, numeric score, or yes/no) and returns calibrated probabilities for every option. It is used as a Python package or as a served model (LM Studio, Ollama, vLLM, HTTP/MCP servers) to automate or guard decision steps in pipelines and agents, notable for being distilled/calibrated for fast inference and offering GGUF builds for lightweight deployment.
cls.trl_rationale: The repository is very new (created ~51 days ago) but provides runnable packages, examples, a Hugging Face demo and GGUF builds for model servers, indicating early adopters and installable artifacts; however it lacks a long track record or broad downstream adoption, so TRL is limited to alpha-in-use.
prerequisites: familiarity with basic ML/LLM concepts and deployment
optional GPU or Apple Silicon for best performance
student_project_ideas: Build a customer-support triage pipeline that ingests tickets (JSON) and uses opendecider to route tickets to teams and prioritise urgency, then measure automation recall/precision versus human routing.

Integrate opendecider as a guard in a small conversational agent (e.g. RAG chatbot) to allow only high-confidence automated actions and log low-confidence cases for human review, analysing calibration and false accept/reject rates.

tools.name: yusong652/flac-mcp
tools.desc: MCP server connecting AI agents to ITASCA FLAC — run continuum simulations through natural conversation

tools.name: YaoIsAI/SerialRUN
tools.desc: Professional Serial Port Debugging Assistant with Modbus, PLC, CAN, I2C/SPI support and MCP server

tools.name: frankhommers/autodesk-fusion-mcp
tools.desc: MCP server that runs inside Autodesk Fusion (formerly Autodesk Fusion 360) as an add-in, letting AI agents drive your CAD session over Streamable HTTP. Zero external dependencies.

tools.name: lizaixi01/AgentCAD
tools.desc: The CAD runtime built for AI agents: 2D drawings (DXF/DWG) and parametric 3D parts (FreeCAD, STEP) through MCP, CLI and Python, with undo, independent validation and a live viewer.

cls.summary: AgentCAD is a local CAD runtime designed for AI agents to create, edit, validate and export 2D engineering drawings (DXF/DWG) with transactional edits, undo and an MCP server interface.
cls.what_it_does: AgentCAD provides a programmatic CAD engine (MCP server, CLI, Python library and HTTP API) that lets AI agents perform typed drawing operations, checkpoint and undo edits, validate files and export plotted images and common CAD formats. It focuses on 2D engineering drawings (DXF/DWG) and integrates a live viewer and validators so automated agents can safely modify drawings and inspect results.
cls.trl_rationale: The repository is very new (created 20 days ago) but already provides installers, an MCP server, CLI and examples; this suggests an early-alpha project that others can install with effort rather than a proven production tool.
prerequisites: familiarity with MCP clients (Claude Code, Codex) and basic CAD concepts
FreeCAD installed for the live 3D viewer (optional)
student_project_ideas: Create an agent-driven workflow that generates parametric mounting-plate DXFs from JSON requirements and produces a plotted PDF and validation report using AgentCAD's CLI and validator.

Integrate AgentCAD with a simple CI pipeline that runs automated geometry checks and dimension-consistency tests (validator) on DXF artifacts produced by student CAD agents and reports failures to a Git repository.

tools.name: MakeItEzzz555/Gridline
tools.desc: Portable AI agent skills, subagents, and plugins for architecture/AEC workflows across Codex, Claude Code, Gemini CLI, and other compatible agents.

cls.summary: Gridline is a collection of portable AI agent skills and specialist agents that assist architecture/BIM/CAD workflows, producing conceptual drawings, DXF plans, revision comparisons and local verification utilities.
cls.what_it_does: Gridline packages ~30 portable AEC 'skills' and a dozen specialist agents to help with the building project lifecycle from concept through handover; it generates conceptual JSON→SVG/DXF outputs, structured plan sheets, revision-impact reports and local verification checks. It is installed into filesystem-capable AI agent runtimes (Codex, Claude Code, Gemini CLI, skills installer) and exposes an optional local MCP/stdio review server for capability discovery and read-only comparisons.
cls.trl_rationale: The README and changelog show a functional v0.5.x with concrete features (DXF generation, local checks, MCP server) and install scripts, but the repository is only ~48 days old so there is limited track record and it should be considered early-alpha/alpha-in-use rather than production-grade.
prerequisites: familiarity with AI agent runtimes (Codex, Claude Code, Gemini CLI or skills installer)
understanding of BIM/CAD concepts (DXF, sheets, schedules, IFC concepts)
student_project_ideas: Build an automated pipeline that uses Gridline skills to convert a structured building JSON into DXF plan sheets and a schedule, then compare quantities against an external cost-estimating spreadsheet.

Create a small MCP-based review tool that uses Gridline's revision-impact server to detect changes between two BIM JSON exports and visualise changed openings and sheets in a browser (combine with three.js or simple SVG rendering).

tools.name: nanassound/mnft
tools.desc: Text-to-CAD tools in Elixir with build123d, OpenSCAD, replicad, and smlibpy.

cls.summary: mnft is an open-source Elixir framework that converts plain-language prompts into CAD code and generates STEP/STL/GLB outputs using pluggable CAD engines.
cls.what_it_does: mnft uses large language models to translate natural-language descriptions of parts into CAD scripts, runs those scripts in guarded engine runtimes (build123d, OpenSCAD, replicad, smlibpy) and produces manufacture-ready outputs (STL, STEP, GLB) and a web 3D preview. It is notable for a pluggable engine architecture, browser/WASM options, and example reference apps (web, headless, browser) that demonstrate end-to-end text-to-CAD flows.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository is very new (created 36 days ago) but README and examples show a working end-to-end pipeline (build123d worker, browser WASM example, Docker image) and multiple engines; the short age limits proven production use so TRL is capped at Alpha-in-use (5).
prerequisites: Python 3.11/3.12 for build123d worker and optional packages
LLM API key (for fully interactive use)
student_project_ideas: Build a lab exercise where students prompt mnft to generate a simple mechanical part, validate the produced STEP against a CAD reference using geometry checks, and export an STL for 3D printing.

Extend the mnft pipeline to add automated parametric variation: accept a table of dimension inputs, generate multiple CAD variants via the LLM+build123d engine, and run a basic mass/volume comparison script to support a mini trade study.

tools.name: OpenRobOps/oro
tools.desc: OpenRobOps: open-source robot fleet management and operations platform. Real-time   observability and control for AMRs, self-hosted, ROS 2, Open RMF and ISO 21423 native.

tools.name: swift-ros2/swift-ros2
tools.desc: Native Swift client library for ROS 2: publish/subscribe over Zenoh or CycloneDDS without the rcl/rclcpp stack

tools.name: raylanlin/Millwright
tools.desc: Open-source AI automation for SolidWorks — talk to your CAD.

tools.name: jal-co/stampstudio
tools.desc: An online, open source stamp creator.

cls.summary: Stamp Studio is an open-source web app for designing and exporting realistic postage-stamp artwork with perforations, paper shaders and printable exports.
cls.what_it_does: Stamp Studio lets users upload artwork, customise perforation gauges, apply paper ageing and postmarks, and export the result as PNG/GLB/video. It renders a realistic paper shader and die-cut perforations using signed distance fields and three.js, and runs in the browser as a Vite/React application. Notable features include multiple press styles (engraved, offset, photogravure, typeset), procedural paper effects in GLSL, and multi-resolution export.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository was created 79 days ago (younger than 90 days) so maturity is limited; however the README documents a live deployment, bundled templates and build instructions which indicate early adopters and working examples consistent with an alpha-in-use level.

tools.name: NVIDIA/NuRec
tools.desc: NVIDIA Omniverse NuRec provides neural reconstruction APIs and libraries to reconstruct and render interactive simulations from real-world data.

cls.summary: NuRec is NVIDIA's Gaussian-splatting reconstruction and rendering SDK that turns real-world sensor captures (images, LiDAR, radar) into photorealistic, interactive simulations suitable for AV and robotics evaluation.
cls.what_it_does: NuRec provides GPU-accelerated libraries, containerised workflows and APIs to reconstruct scenes from camera/LiDAR/radar captures using Gaussian-based methods and to render those reconstructions for simulator integration and sensor evaluation. It is used as a pipeline component (reconstruction → training → rendering) and notable for integrating Gaussian splatting rendering, support for sensor-specific effects (rolling shutter, fisheye), and container-based development for reproducible benchmarks.
cls.trl_rationale: The project is an active NVIDIA SDK with container images, example workflows and integration notes, but the repository is very new (created 49 days ago) so there is limited public track record; this supports an alpha / early-in-use TRL rather than production readiness.
student_project_ideas: Reconstruct a small indoor scene from a smartphone image sequence, compare Gaussian-splat reconstructions from NuRec with a NeRF implementation and evaluate rendered camera/LiDAR outputs for downstream perception models.

Integrate NuRec rendering with a ROS/Isaac Sim robot simulation to create synthetic sensor streams (camera + LiDAR) and run a perception algorithm to test domain transfer between recorded and simulated data.

tools.name: bluegrassiot/mqttprobe
tools.desc: The MQTT diagnostic tool built for IIoT. Connect to any broker, browse/filter live topics, inspect payloads, chart payload fields. Native Sparkplug B dashboard and MQTT/SpB node emulation.

tools.name: CalamityXeroc/GIS-agent
tools.desc: GIS Agent 是基于 ArcGIS Pro 3.6 的 arcpy（支持 GDAL 双后端）的开源地理空间智能体框架：单一有界「观察-决策-执行」循环 + 多角色模型路由，把自然语言指令变成可验收的 GIS 成果——从数据扫描、处理、符号化到地图导出与可编辑 .aprx，配强制验收、配方记忆、断点续跑和本机 Web 控制台。仍在快速迭代，欢迎指出问题

tools.name: sevecekp/sph
tools.desc: Library and graphical tools for running SPH and N-body simulations.

tools.name: zephel01/Abyss
tools.desc: Run 50-280 GB MoE LLMs (DeepSeek V4/V4.1 Flash, GLM-5.3-Flash, Qwen3.8-Flash-Next, Ornith) on one consumer GPU: experts spread over VRAM, RAM and NVMe SSD. Browser chat + OpenAI/Anthropic APIs. CUDA, ROCm, DGX Spark.

cls.summary: Abyss is an open-source inference engine that runs very large mixture-of-experts (MoE) language models on a single consumer PC by offloading experts across GPU VRAM, system RAM and NVMe SSD.
cls.what_it_does: Abyss lets you run 50–280 GB MoE LLMs locally by keeping hot experts on the GPU, warm experts in pinned RAM and the rest on NVMe, migrating them at runtime to make large models usable on one GPU. It provides a browser chat UI and OpenAI/Anthropic-compatible APIs and supports CUDA, ROCm and DGX Spark deployments; notable features are explicit expert offloading and prepared GGUF model packs on Hugging Face.
cls.trl_rationale: The repo is a recent fork (created 38 days ago) with an extensive README, example model packs and multi-platform support, but it lacks a long track record, stable releases or broad adoption — appropriate for an early-alpha TRL.
prerequisites: NVIDIA CUDA or AMD ROCm-capable GPU and drivers
NVMe SSD with sufficient free space and >=32 GB system RAM for larger models
GGUF model files (downloadable from Hugging Face) and basic command-line skills
student_project_ideas: Measure and compare latency/throughput of a given MoE GGUF model (e.g. Qwen3.8-Flash-Next) across different offloading configurations (vary VRAM/RAM/SSD cutoffs) and plot how token throughput scales with available GPU memory.

Integrate Abyss's OpenAI-compatible API with a small robotics or data-logging pipeline to prototype an on-device natural language interface that queries local telemetry without sending data to external cloud APIs.

tools.name: nvrooijen/KiLeidoscope
tools.desc: Live two-way bridge between KiCad and Blender: real-time 3D view, X-ray/cut-planes, flex folding, multi-board assemblies, LLM-visualizer, solder checks, Cycles renders of your PCB, and more!

cls.summary: KiLeidoscope is a Blender add-on and local bridge that provides a live, bidirectional 3D visualization of KiCad PCBs including X‑ray views, flex folding, multi‑board assemblies and DRC/LLM overlays.
cls.what_it_does: KiLeidoscope connects KiCad to Blender using KiCad's IPC API and a local bridge process to stream board changes in near real time into Blender for interactive visualization and rendering. It supports features useful for PCB designers — live updates of copper/zones/pads/vias, selection sync, X‑ray cross sections, flex folding, multi‑board layouts, and visualised DRC or LLM review findings — and uses Blender's Cycles/EEVEE for realistic rendering.
cls.trl_rationale: The project is an active, functioning bridge with multiple documented features and guides, but the repository is very new (created 52 days ago) and the README states 'early development' and beta features, so it lacks the long track record or wide adoption required for TRL 6+.
prerequisites: basic Blender usage (installing add-ons and using Cycles/EEVEE)
student_project_ideas: Create an automated PCB collision-checking workflow: use KiLeidoscope to import multiple live boards into Blender, script placement scenarios and report collisions to a CSV for design-rule evaluation.

Build a flex‑board visualiser and validator: extend the flex folding pipeline to animate a rigid‑flex assembly and produce a short report that flags coverlay/stiffener violations by combining KiLeidoscope's export with a Python DRC checker.

tools.name: donghaxkim/impasto
tools.desc: Deterministically turns any photo into a palette-knife style painting

cls.summary: Impasto is a TypeScript engine that deterministically converts photos into thick, palette-knife style paintings with per-stroke surface geometry you can relight in the browser or Node.
cls.what_it_does: Impasto analyses a source image to plan and paint strokes layer-by-layer, simulating thick paint that builds up ridges and heaps. It provides an API and a viewer so you can render paintings in Node or the browser, move the light interactively, and export the painted surface.
cls.trl_rationale: The repository is a recent, runnable TypeScript project with usage examples and an npm package, but it was created very recently (14 days) and has a small community and short track record, so it fits an early-alpha TRL.
prerequisites: familiarity with web canvas / WebGL/WebGPU concepts
student_project_ideas: Build a small web app that batches a set of architectural photos and produces relightable impasto renderings, then measure and compare performance for different output resolutions and export formats.

Extend the paint simulation to add custom brush/knife materials or to export the surface as a heightmap/mesh and combine it with a simple real-time renderer (three.js) for a small interactive exhibit.

tools.name: 363045841/KLineChartQuant
tools.desc: High-performance financial charting terminal with Canvas/WebGL/WebGPU backends, 1–3ms GPU time per frame, plugin-based rendering, visual signal annotation, AI-native architecture. Seamlessly supports Vue, React, and Angular.

tools.name: sidmohan0/tesserack
tools.desc: Compiling strategy guides into reward functions for reinforcement learning. Uses Claude Vision to extract unit tests from game   guides, then trains agents with dense, interpretable rewards.

tools.name: vincenzo-afk/browserbrain
tools.desc: Browser-first local AI research workspace with on-device WebGPU and WASM inference, free web context tools, and private local notes.

tools.name: pmndrs/upscaler

Lecturers and students can use it to discover tools for tasks like inversion, geological modelling, drillhole management, geostatistics and prospectivity mapping. It is notable for focusing solely on open-source projects and grouping tools by exploration subdomain.

tools.name: simoneiacomino/xenolith
tools.desc: A pure C inference engine designed for Intel Xe-LP iGPUs and Gemma 4 26B-A4B QAT.

cls.summary: Xenolith is a small, open-source C inference engine that runs local LLM inference on Intel integrated GPUs (Xe family) under Linux using Level Zero.
cls.what_it_does: Xenolith runs transformer model inference on Intel integrated GPUs by splitting work between GPU (prefill) and CPU (decode) to match the memory/compute profile of Xe-LP/Xe3-class iGPUs. It is used from the command line to load gguf-style models and run chat or client modes, and is notable for being specialised and optimised for Intel integrated GPU architectures (Gemma 4 / other Xe devices) rather than being a general-purpose engine.
cls.trl_rationale: The repository is young (≈52 days) but contains a runnable engine, install script, benchmarks and device compatibility matrix, indicating early alpha/alpha-in-use maturity rather than production; age limits it to TRL 5.
prerequisites: Intel Level Zero runtime / intel-compute-runtime drivers
gguf-style model files and sufficient system memory
student_project_ideas: Benchmark and compare inference latency and throughput of a small gguf model on an Intel iGPU using Xenolith versus llama.cpp (CPU and Vulkan) under controlled thermal/power conditions and report trade-offs.

Extend Xenolith to add support for an additional Intel Xe device ID or add basic profiling hooks that log GPU/CPU utilisation during prefill and decode phases, and visualise the results with a simple dashboard.

tools.name: hokindeng/object-permanence
tools.desc: Training Object Permanence in World Models — the codebase

cls.summary: Research code and dataset for training video-based world models that learn object permanence using Blender-rendered simulated scenes and a Trainium-optimised PyTorch training stack.
cls.what_it_does: This repository provides a Blender-based data factory that generates 150 task families of video-to-video samples where objects persist while occluded, plus a native-PyTorch training stack (Cosmos3-Nano on AWS Trainium2) to train and evaluate world models. It is used to produce datasets, encode latents, and run distributed training/sampling on Neuron-enabled instances, and includes links to data, benchmark, model and a leaderboard.
cls.trl_rationale: The repo is a recent research codebase (created 62 days ago) with runnable data generation and training scripts and a public dataset and model, but is very new and primarily in a research/demo stage so it fits an 'alpha in use' level rather than production.
prerequisites: Blender knowledge for rendering task generation
PyTorch and experience with distributed training
Familiarity with AWS Trainium / Neuron to run large-scale training
student_project_ideas: Use the Blender data factory to generate a small subset of object-permanence scenes and train a lightweight world-model on a workstation GPU to evaluate occlusion-aware prediction accuracy, comparing performance with and without occlusion-aware losses.

Integrate the generated dataset with a simple robotics simulator (e.g. a ROS node) to test whether a learned world model can improve short-horizon object-tracking and occlusion handling in a mobile-robot perception pipeline.

Use a Blender-oriented prompt from the catalog and reproduce the scene, then modify the Python animation script to add a parameterised behaviour (e.g. adjustable lighting or animation speed) and report on workflow reproducibility.

tools.name: suanmiao/fly-self-driving
tools.desc: A fruit fly connectome (165k neurons, 25.6M synapses) trained to drive a simulated street from pixels. Code, patches, renderer, results.

cls.summary: This repository trains a full fruit‑fly connectome (165k neurons, 25.6M synapses) as a recurrent neural controller to steer a simulated car from low‑resolution pixels and reproduces recorded drives and visualisations.
cls.what_it_does: The project loads a measured fruit‑fly wiring diagram as a fixed recurrent graph and learns one gain per synapse and one leak per neuron to map pixel inputs to steering actions using behaviour cloning and DAgger. It provides training scripts, baselines, rendering (Blender) and patches to run the sparse connectome core on CUDA and Apple MPS, and reproduces evaluation videos and logged neural activity.
cls.trl_rationale: The README documents full experiments, training recipes, and rendered results, and provides runnable scripts and GPU/MPS patches, showing it is more than a demo; however the repository is only 65 days old so it lacks a longer track record or broad adoption, limiting TRL to about 5.
prerequisites: PyTorch-compatible GPU (CUDA) or Apple MPS for Apple silicon
the MaleCNS (flyhard) connectome dataset (handled by flyhard checkout)
student_project_ideas: Reproduce a simplified street driving experiment by training a reduced-size subgraph of the connectome (or an extracted optic-lobe subset) and compare behaviour cloning vs DAgger performance using GPU or CPU baselines.

Integrate the learned controller into a simple ROS 2 simulation (e.g. gazebo or Webots) to evaluate transfer from the repository's simulator to a robot simulator, and measure robustness to sensor noise and occlusion.

Notable points are the device firmware + matching WASM studio, SysEx editor protocol, and focus on live performance and drone textures.

tools.desc: Offline AI research assistant for Android. Answers from Wikipedia and other reference packs on the phone, with citations. Gemma 4 runs on the Pixel 10's Tensor NPU (first word in about 2 s); other phones use llama.cpp. No INTERNET permission.

cls.summary: Commonplace is an Android app that runs a small LLM on-device to answer questions from downloaded reference packs (Wikipedia, Wikidata, etc.) and shows citations for each answer without requiring network access.
cls.what_it_does: The app provides an offline, retrieval-augmented question-answering assistant: a desktop preprocessor builds searchable passage indexes from reference texts which you download to the phone, and the phone finds relevant passages and generates a cited answer with a local LLM. tools.name: laszapens/Atta
tools.desc: Parametric CAD kernel for LLMs: spec-driven geometry, measured facts, three-state verification, Blender-backed delivery

cls.summary: Atta is a Python parametric CAD kernel designed so language models (or users) can describe parts as reproducible specs, compute exact geometry, measure it, verify three-state correctness, and export or render (Blender optional).
cls.what_it_does: Atta turns a textual/spec description into deterministic parametric geometry, computes measured facts (bbox, volume, topology, wall thickness, etc.), gates results with a three-state verify step (pass/degraded/fail) and only then allows export or render. It is notable for being spec-driven (the spec is the rebuildable model), providing fast perception-like ASCII/metric facts without rendering, and offering exact CAD features (NURBS, analytic fillets/STEP) with Blender used only as an optional backend for visual output.
cls.trl_rationale: The README documents a rich feature set, a beta release tag, and an installable Python package, but the repository is very new (created 14 days ago) and has no visible long-term track record or external adopters; that supports an early-alpha TRL.
prerequisites: familiarity with parametric CAD concepts (NURBS, fillets, assemblies)
optional: Blender for rendering and GLB/BLEND exports
optional: build123d / OpenCASCADE for analytic STEP export
student_project_ideas: Create a small parametric part (e.g. a mounting bracket or cup) defined as an Atta spec, use atta_describe to extract measured facts and then design an automated test that verifies dimensional tolerances across a parameter sweep.

Integrate Atta with Blender (via the optional bridge) to build a pipeline that verifies parts programmatically (verify -> deliver GLB) and produces a lightweight QA manifest for use in a digital-manufacturing workflow.

It is used as a desktop .dmg app or built from source (Xcode) and includes a CLI remote-control interface for scripting and automated workflows.
cls.trl_rationale: The project has a substantial README, binary releases (.dmg) and verification/engine docs and is actively developed, but the repository is very new (created 39 days ago) so it lacks a long track record or broad adoption; that limits maturity to an alpha-in-use level (TRL 5).
prerequisites: Apple silicon Mac (M1 or later) running macOS 26+
familiarity with macOS apps; Xcode 26 to build from source
student_project_ideas: Measure and compare inference speed and memory usage of a chosen diffusion model running in Siliconed on different Apple silicon Macs and report optimisations or configuration changes.
Create a small scripted pipeline using silicontrol to generate annotated image datasets for a computer-vision assignment, then use the dataset with a standard ML training tool.

tools.name: 1314521gjy/cyber-on-strata
tools.desc: 在 8 GB 显存的显卡上跑 35B MoE（Cyber-Tiel-Coder-35B-A3B）：专家权重流式上卡、未命中专家由 CPU 池就地计算。Strata 引擎的 fork（MIT）。RTX 4080S 实测 8 GB 档 57.7–63.5 tok/s、全常驻 134–136 tok/s。Build from THIS repo — upstream does not support this model.

cls.summary: A Strata-engine fork that streams experts from system RAM and computes cache misses on CPU so a 35B Mixture-of-Experts model can run on GPUs with as little as 8 GB VRAM.
cls.what_it_does: This repository is an inference engine fork that pages MoE expert weights from system memory to GPU on demand and runs missed experts on a CPU thread pool, enabling the 22.75 GB Cyber-Tiel-Coder-35B-A3B model to decode on low-VRAM cards. It is used by building the C++/CUDA engine, placing the GGUF model file in /models, and running the provided launchers; the README includes measured throughput and configuration recommendations. It is notable for expert-streaming, adaptive GPU cache sizing, and CPU-side in-place expert computation to trade CPU/RAM for GPU memory.
cls.trl_rationale: The README contains detailed engineering notes, measured benchmarks and example launchers, showing it runs and has practical results; however the repository is only 39 days old so it lacks longer-term adoption or multiple stable releases, limiting maturity to an alpha-in-use level.
prerequisites: NVIDIA GPU (supported SM architectures) and drivers
Large model GGUF file (not included) and ~32+ GB system RAM recommended
Familiarity with building native inference engines and command-line usage

It is used as a library (and includes an example application) to build CAD apps, geometry processing tools and downstream PLM/visualisation workflows. It is notable for being a modern Rust-based BREP implementation split into focused crates within a single workspace.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository is very new (created 50 days ago) and while it contains a full workspace and example app, there is no evidence of long-term releases or industry adoption in the README; demonstrated capability suggests an alpha-level project used by early adopters rather than production-grade maturity.

tools.name: danbiocchi/hermes-vcc-engine
tools.desc: Instant context compaction for Hermes Agent. Builds the compaction summary in milliseconds with no LLM call, keeping the exact commands, exit codes, errors and files, each linked back to its original message. Based on the VCC paper.

cls.summary: A Hermes Agent plugin that produces fast, rule-based conversation compactions (summaries) without calling an LLM, preserving exact commands, exit codes, errors and file references with links to original messages.
cls.what_it_does: This plugin replaces Hermes's LLM-based mid-session summary step with a deterministic, rule-driven compaction engine that runs in milliseconds and emits a structured summary copied from recorded messages. It is installed as a Hermes plugin and configured as the context engine so Hermes triggers it when the conversation reaches the compaction threshold; the output includes linked message IDs, command/error lists and file-change summaries.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository is very new (created 34 days ago) so it cannot be judged as production-mature; however the README shows a comprehensive test suite, CI targets, compatibility matrix with Hermes versions, and real-hardware benchmark claims which support an early-adopter/alpha-in-use assessment (TRL 5).
student_project_ideas: Benchmark and compare Hermes session recall (accuracy and latency) using the VCC engine versus Hermes's LLM compressor across different local LLM backends (e.g. llama.cpp) and report impacts on agent behaviour.

Extend the plugin to add optional lightweight heuristic rationale extraction (e.g. key decisions or short rationale snippets) and evaluate trade-offs between fidelity, size, and recall in compactions.

tools.name: yoslo59/TRELLIS-Studio
tools.desc: Local 3D asset studio powered by TRELLIS.2 and UniRig: image-to-3D, rigging, animation, PBR exports, game preparation, REST API and MCP.

cls.summary: TRELLIS Studio is a local workspace that generates textured 3D meshes from images, provides rigging/animation tools (UniRig), PBR previews and exports prepared assets for games or 3D printing.
cls.what_it_does: The project combines Microsoft TRELLIS.2 image-to-3D generation with UniRig skeleton/weight prediction to create, preview and prepare textured mesh assets locally. It offers a browser-based PBR viewer, queueing, collection management, game/printing preparation (LOD, baking, collisions) and a REST/MCP API for automation, with both single-user desktop and multi-user server modes.
cls.trl_rationale: The repository is very recently created (13 days) but includes a downloadable Windows preview installer and a tested full-installation report by the maintainer; however there is limited public adoption and only preview releases, so it fits an alpha-in-use level.
prerequisites: NVIDIA GPU drivers for GPU inference (recommended)
Windows 11 with WSL2 and Ubuntu 22.04 for some components
student_project_ideas: Create a pipeline that generates a character from a photograph with TRELLIS Studio, refines the rig in Blender and exports an FBX to a simple Unity scene to evaluate deformation and performance across LODs.

Build a REST API automation script that batches image-to-3D generation, runs automated reduction/baking in the Studio, and compares triangle counts and texture sizes for game vs print targets (measure export metrics and create a short report).

tools.name: gokayfem/video-to-physics
tools.desc: Turn a reference video, image or idea into a verified physics reconstruction in Blender: measure the clip, solve and benchmark the real physics, verify it independently, render it in the same scene.

cls.summary: A Blender-oriented toolkit and agent 'skill' that measures a reference video or image, builds a benchmarked physics model (rigid bodies, FEA, CFD, rods, fracture, etc.), verifies it with an independent implementation and bakes solver output back into Blender for pixel-accurate comparison.
cls.what_it_does: Video 2 Physics takes a video/image/idea, extracts measurements and camera information, selects or fits a physical model, runs appropriate solvers (rigid body, elastic, FEA, CFD) with benchmarks and negative controls, and writes solver outputs into Blender so renders can be compared against the original footage. It is distributed as a skill for coding agents (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Copilot, Gemini) and as scripts for local use, notable for its explicit measurement-first workflow, independent verification step, and benchmarked convergence checks.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository is very new (created 22 days ago) but has a detailed README, install instructions and example cases; however there are no stable releases, limited community evidence, and short track record so maturity is early-alpha (TRL 4).
prerequisites: Solver packages as needed (e.g. FEniCSx, Basilisk) and optionally a fal API key for clip generation
student_project_ideas: Reconstruct a simple pendulum video: measure camera and bob motion, fit a rigid-body model, run a solver to correct the dynamics, bake results into Blender and produce side-by-side comparisons with quantitative error metrics.

Benchmark vortex shedding in a short AI-generated clip: measure length scales and time, run CFD (Basilisk or FEniCSx) at multiple resolutions, verify convergence against Williamson's Strouhal curve, and present a reproducible report.

tools.name: uilianks/kiln
tools.desc: Low-poly and voxel 3D game assets as code: a DSL that exports GLB with lights, agent-readable previews, a live viewer and Blender renders, turntables and camera-move videos. Sibling of vex and chirp.

cls.summary: Kiln is a small TypeScript DSL and toolchain that generates low‑poly and voxel 3D game assets as code, exports GLB, produces agent‑readable previews and can hand off scenes to Blender for renders and videos.
cls.what_it_does: Kiln lets you author 3D assets with a concise .kx.js DSL (primitives, voxel layers, lights, animations) and builds flat‑shaded or smoothed meshes, exports GLB for game engines and web, generates four‑view previews for automated checks, and invokes Blender for beauty renders, turntables and camera animations. It is notable for treating assets as code, producing baked PBR textures/UVs for engine compatibility, and including a live viewer and agent‑readable previews.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository is very new (created 27 days ago) but provides runnable tooling, examples and Blender integration; this indicates an early alpha level (others can install with effort) rather than a long track record, so TRL 4 is appropriate.
student_project_ideas: Create a small interactive scene described entirely in kiln (voxel hero + environment), export GLB and load it into a Three.js web viewer to demonstrate asset‑as‑code pipelines and runtime integration.

Build a procedural asset pack in kiln (trees, rocks, props) and produce Blender turntables and a short animation, then measure triangle counts and create a short report on optimization tradeoffs between flat, smooth and subdivided modes.

cls.summary: A community project that adds a WebGPU renderer and an HTML5/WebAssembly target so Unreal Engine 5.8.3 projects can be built to run in a web browser.
cls.what_it_does: The project provides documentation and build support for a modified Unreal Engine that renders via WebGPU (native via Dawn and in-browser via WebAssembly) so packaged Unreal games can run in a browser tab. It is used by building the provided engine fork on a host (macOS/Linux/Windows) and packaging projects for the HTML5/WebGPU target; the README contains step-by-step build and packaging guides. What makes it notable is the aim to run full Unreal Engine content in-browser using modern WebGPU rather than older WebGL or streaming-only approaches.
cls.trl_rationale: The repository is very new (created 32 days ago) and documents a forked engine implementation rather than a drop-in plugin; there is good documentation and demos but the implementation lives in a restricted Unreal fork and lacks a long track record, so maturity is early-alpha.
prerequisites: Unreal Engine development and project packaging experience
C++ toolchains and platform build tool knowledge (Visual Studio, macOS toolchain, Linux)
Familiarity with WebAssembly / Emscripten and WebGPU concepts
student_project_ideas: Port a small Unreal sample (Third Person template) to the WebGPU target and measure runtime performance (frame time, memory) across desktop and mobile browsers, then present optimisations to reduce load time.

Build a simple interactive digital-twin-style scene in Unreal, package it for the browser with WebGPU, and integrate a lightweight web UI to stream telemetry from a simulated IoT sensor (e.g. via MQTT over WebSocket) to demonstrate browser-based visualisation of live data.

tools.name: grizlizora/reverse-cad
tools.desc: ⚙️ Industrial-grade pure TypeScript STL ➔ 100% Watertight Solid STEP AP242 B-Rep & CAD Features JSON engine with built-in MCP server for AI agents. Features exact Gauss-Mirtich 3D inertia, ISO threads (M2–M24), boundary unification (no extra lines), Zero-GC speed, DWRR concurrency & 5-gate RSVS reality verification across macOS, Linux, and Windows.

cls.summary: ReverseCAD is a TypeScript engine and CLI that converts polygonal STL meshes into watertight STEP AP242 B‑Rep solids and structured CAD features JSON, with an optional MCP server for agent integration.
cls.what_it_does: ReverseCAD reverse‑engineers raw STL meshes into production‑grade solid B‑Reps (STEP AP242) and dense CAD features JSON, performing topology repair, profile fitting, ISO thread recognition and exact mass/inertia calculations. It is delivered as a high‑performance pure TypeScript CLI/library (Bun/Node) and includes an MCP server mode to let AI agents interact with the conversion pipeline and outputs. The project emphasises deterministic, watertight output, engineering audit artifacts (heatmaps, reports) and CLI options for quality, thread handling and selective artifact emission.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository is very new (created 52 days ago) but README documents a complete CLI, many engineering features and testing hooks; however there is no public evidence of broad production use or multiple releases, so maturity is limited to early alpha/alpha‑in‑use (TRL 5).
prerequisites: Node.js / Bun runtime and npm tooling
basic knowledge of CAD/STEP concepts and CLI usage
familiarity with mesh and topology concepts (STL, B‑Rep)
student_project_ideas: Create a reproducible pipeline that converts 3D scan STL files into STEP AP242 solids using ReverseCAD, then validate volume and inertia against measured part data and visualise deviations in three.js.

Build an MCP agent that automates batch reverse‑engineering: feed STL parts, apply thread detection and quality presets, collect JSON feature reports and generate a summary dashboard (combine with a simple web UI).

tools.desc: A live, isometric 3D view of your Dokploy. Read-only, self-hosted.

cls.summary: 3Dokploy is a self-hosted, read-only isometric 3D dashboard that visualises the state, metrics and deploy activity of a Dokploy server.
cls.what_it_does: 3Dokploy polls a Dokploy API and renders projects, services and deploys as an isometric three.js scene in the browser while a small Node.js server proxies read-only API calls and strips secrets. It is used as a live operations dashboard to observe status, CPU/memory/network metrics, deploy logs and alerts without giving the UI any ability to change state. What makes it notable is the visual, gamified mapping of deployment concepts (buildings, racks, carts) implemented with React + react-three-fiber and a minimal Hono-based server.
cls.trl_rationale: The project is a working application with a clear README, Docker Compose support and a prebuilt image, but the repository is very new (created ~32 days ago) and has limited community adoption; this suggests early-alpha maturity rather than a production-proven tool.
prerequisites: access to a Dokploy instance and API key

cls.summary: Jatra is an Unreal Engine plugin that provides a data-driven motion-matching locomotion and overlay animation system to get playable biped characters moving quickly.
cls.what_it_does: Jatra packages motion-matching locomotion, data-asset driven configuration, overlay bone blending, aim offsets and a dynamic camera into a drop-in Unreal Engine plugin so developers can get a playable character quickly. It is used as a UE plugin (C++) and extends the Game Animation Sample Project, notable for its data-asset configuration and simple overlay system that eases retargeting and runtime switching of locomotion sets.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository is very new (created 20 days ago) so it lacks a long track record; it has usable docs (wiki), example project integration and multiple stars indicating interest, which suggests early-alpha (installable with effort) rather than a research prototype.
prerequisites: Unreal Engine (familiarity with UE editor and asset pipeline)
C++ and Unreal plugin development basics
Understanding of animation systems and motion matching concepts
student_project_ideas: Integrate Jatra into an Unreal scene and compare motion-matching locomotion vs. blendspace-based locomotion for a biped robot simulation, reporting on responsiveness and animation accuracy.

Build an interactive demo that switches locomotion data-asset sets via gameplay tags to demonstrate context-aware animation (walking, crouch, sprint) and evaluate camera behaviour and retargeting across two character rigs.

alternatives_to: other motion-matching plugins or custom locomotion frameworks

cls.summary: BitLLM is a peer-to-peer system that lets users share and fetch locally hosted LLM servers so your local gateway can route inference requests to whichever peer is serving a model.

It is notable for using libp2p-style discovery and relays to avoid port forwarding and for interoperating with many existing local model servers (vLLM, llama.cpp, Ollama, MLX, etc.).
cls.trl_rationale: The README states the project is 'Beta' and describes a live network at bitllm.org, indicating early real use; however the repository is only 18 days old so longer-term production stability and broader adoption are not yet demonstrated, limiting TRL to around 5.

cls.summary: GradSplat is a research implementation that reconstructs scenes as 3D Gaussians from a few images in a single forward pass and refines those Gaussians via learned gradient-based updates inside the model.
cls.what_it_does: GradSplat performs few-view 3D reconstruction and novel-view synthesis by predicting one Gaussian per input pixel, rendering them into input views, computing photometric gradients through a rasterizer, and applying learned recurrent updates to opacity, color and shape inside the forward pass. It is provided as a PyTorch codebase with pretrained weights, demo scripts (including a Gradio app), evaluation code and an external CUDA rasterizer (gsplat) for inference and visualization.
cls.trl_rationale: Repository is very new (created 28 days ago) so long-term production use cannot be shown; however the README includes pretrained weights, demo scripts, evaluation code and a runnable inference path, which suggests early adopters can run it (alpha in use) but not yet a proven production track record.
